## 3. The exact polynomial, its far part and changing the truncation

Let V=1 on[0,1], V=0 on[2,infinity), as in the source, and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)V(Nd/R).

With Y=U^B the completed tail and its prefix/far split are

    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R)phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y),
    P_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R)phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                                     e^(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L),
    F_R,u(s)=D_R,u(s)-P_R,u(s).                         (F6)

H is the same smooth function equal to one on[0,1], between zero and one, and zero beyond a fixed C. In particular the far coefficient is exactly multiplied by1-H(Nn/L). No sharp pair mask is substituted for it. Terminate genuinely at Nn<=U^(B+1), paying its exponentially small error before any pair expansion. This preserves every required derivative. The complete zero identity gives

    D_R,u(rho_u)=-1+O(U^(-A)).                          (F7)

Choose B after the polynomial costs from t and heights so the contour shift pays A. This is [restricted research revision]'s nonprincipal ordinary-L identity; no L-pole has been discarded.

The alternative t in F1 does not estimate the old R=U^(4/3) far norm by comparison. It supplies a different sufficient detector for the SAME high-row counting problem. For clarity, two truncations have the exact difference

    D_R0-D_R1 =sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(dm)(Ndm)^(-s)e^(-Ndm/Y)
                       [V(Nd/R0)-V(Nd/R1)].            (F8)

The unit coefficient is zero in this difference. At the same actual nonprincipal zero it is O(U^(-A)), with a common B chosen for both fixed truncations. The difference is not asserted small in an ambient norm. Its prefix terms must be retained if comparing the two far polynomials. Our argument instead bounds all original high rows directly from F6--F7 at F1; therefore it also gives the corresponding counting implication for any old far-active subset. No old prefix or old far cross term is silently removed.

For every nonunit ideal n, the full Mobius convolution vanishes, giving

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n)mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)].                 (F9)

Complete multiplicativity preserves F9 at all valuations and shared primes. The unit is excluded throughout. Its nonzero complementary summands have Nd>R. This identity, not a claim of arbitrary-coefficient moment permission, is the new way we retain the unweighted cofactor.

## 4. Exponent return and precise arithmetic gap

For fixed 0<theta<1 take H=floor(X^theta). For every fixed r, 2rH<=X eventually. The last term in (R1) is smaller than every negative power of X, since its logarithm has leading term

    -(1-theta)^2 (log X)^2/(2*tau).

The middle term is O(X^(1-r(1-theta))). Consequently the full hypothesis

    for every epsilon>0 and all large dyadic X:
    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) <<_epsilon X^(e+epsilon)             (OPEN-W)

gives the complete pointwise and dyadic L2 exponent

    gamma_r=max((1-theta+e)/2, 1-r(1-theta)).                 (R3)

The order r may be chosen after fixed theta and a fixed target exponent, then kept fixed as X tends to infinity. There is no theta=1 theorem or silent growing-order substitution. Endpoint equality has the usual every-epsilon interpretation. This is a sufficient return, not an asserted energy equivalence: oscillatory window-null directions can carry other information.

For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with chi any fixed ordinary Dirichlet character including its natural zeros,

    integral_0^infinity F_a(x) x^(-s) dx/x
        = exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi),       Re(s)>1.

The small-x tail is superpolynomial. The complete all-scale bound from (R3), or its dyadic L2 version followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, makes this Mellin transform holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma_r. Multiplying by L and analytic continuation excludes every zero there: the numerator is nonzero at every finite height and multiplicity. The principal pole of L produces a reciprocal zero, not a forbidden pole. No estimate for vertical reciprocal growth, Phragmen--Lindelof assumption, primitive replacement or conductor uniformity is needed for this forward implication.

The family statement needs a COMMON exponent for each fixed chi, with constants allowed to depend on chi. Neither Eisenstein/Hecke families nor a growing conductor nor a replacement f3 source has been proved by this argument.

To improve c6, both strict inequalities are necessary in this interface:

    e < 2*theta6-1+theta = .749722+theta,
    1-r(1-theta) < theta6=.874861.                           (R4)

The absolute energy bound is O(XH)=O(X^(1+theta)); its required arithmetic saving remains

    (1+theta)-(.749722+theta)=.250278=2*c6.

Only the old first-order approximation ceiling theta<theta6 is removed. For example theta=.9 and r=2 pay remainder exponent .8, but still require the unproved energy exponent e<1.649722. Under the hypothetical e=1, examples (theta,r,gamma) are (.26,1,.87), (1/3,1,5/6), (.5,1,.75), (.8,2,.6), (.9,5,.55), (.98,25,.51). These are conditional calibrations, not estimates. A growing r at theta=1 cannot be inferred from them.

statement:
## 4. Reconstructing the enlarged density theorem

Fix a nonempty finite dictionary of natural characters

\[
 c_{\chi_{u,\lambda}}(I)
 =c_{\eta_\lambda}(I)\mathfrak s_{m_0^6u}(I),
 \qquad N\mathfrak q_{u,\lambda}\le K_\lambda N(u).
\]

The literal sextic character includes all ramified/nonunit zeros. The
modulus bound belongs to the natural representative, not the unrelated
existential `RowData.character`; coefficient equality transfers moments
between them. Whole-character conjugation reflects the height and keeps
the modulus; conjugating only `eta` is a different operation. Fixed
orientations may be handled label by label. The finite dictionary and
parent translate are fixed before the scale; unrelated translates are
never put into a single eligibility bin.

Set `K=max(1,max K_lambda)`, `U=KY`. This is fixed multiplicative padding,
not a power loss. Remove the union of fixed-inducing free rows for all
dictionary labels. Their primes lie in a fixed finite support and their
valuations are at most five, with finitely many units; the union is
finite. Every remaining natural character is nonprincipal. The removed
rows contribute `O(1)` to free-row density, without needing witnesses.

Use only the old no-slot inverse moment and PR15's established zero-slot
plain moment (P). The latter requires `m<=3/4`, not a restriction on the
zero bin. Its contradiction hypothesis `beta>=51/100` is automatic when
the current high-zero population is nonempty; if `beta<a`, that population
is empty. The plain source is obtained at the fixed modulus
`Q=q_eta(72)`, with its exact inclusion gates, a fixed small conductor
padding and width `max(1,2m)+padding<=2`. Its zero auxiliary slot has
identically zero profile and the selected product is empty; this does not
impose prime supply on the unmarked family. The omitted finite rows are
bounded absolutely by `|P_n|<=288A sqrt(D)`, uniformly in frequency.

Fix positive detector and moment errors `epsilon_det,epsilon_m`, with
`epsilon_det<=1/1000`. On a supported fiber
`m<=1/2+75 epsilon_det<=23/40<3/4` and `0<=r<=2`.
The inverse and plain inputs have a common fixed polynomial height degree
`J0`, uniform in the zero bin, dyadic choices, scale and actual witness
frequencies. One now chooses the detector auxiliaries and a small positive
`tau_det` AFTER this degree. It can satisfy the witness budget and make
`(J0+1)tau_det` arbitrarily small. There is no dependence of `J0` on the
later chosen witness frequency interval.

For `T<=U^tau_det`, use the actual buffered-bin theorem with
`I=ceil(49/(100e))`. Every nonempty part has

\[
  b>a-e>51/100,\qquad b\le7/8,
  \qquad \delta_b=2b-1\in(0,3/4].
\]

The last upper bound is the incumbent seven-eighths bound, applied to
the actual fixed dictionary. The mesh can put `delta_b` slightly below
`.65`; this is harmless because the actual count and witness gates are
strictly weaker. Set

\[
 t_*=\frac5{5-2\delta_b}
\]

for this bin before selecting witnesses. The cutoff is in `[1,3/2]`
throughout `0<=delta_b<=5/6`. At the proposed density endpoints it is
`50/37` and `10/7`. The source theorem is used at `Z=U,d_min=d_max=d=1`
with frequency allowance `U^(tau_det/2)` and
`H_i=2 pi U^(tau_det/2)+3iU^tau_det`.

Partition by the witness's independent character label and its two dyadic
indices. The cardinality of the latter is `O(log U)` each. Do not require
the witness label to equal a physical numerator/denominator label; the
finite union covers whichever label has the detecting zero.

Here is an independent derivation of the balanced exponent, including the
long inverse branch. With tolerance `gamma` and common moment loss `v`,
the two moment estimates give

\[
 |R|\ll U^{\max(1,(1+5r)/6)-\delta r+v},
 \qquad |R|\ll U^{1-2\delta m+v},
 \quad m\ge t_*-r-\gamma.
\]

For `r<=1`, the unperturbed bounds `1-delta r` and
`1-2delta(t_*-r)` cross at `r=2t_*/3`. The actual second bound adds
at most `2delta gamma`. Choose the inverse bound above the unperturbed
crossing and the plain bound below it, obtaining
`1-(2/3)delta t_*+2delta gamma`. For `r>=1`, the inverse exponent
is `1/6+(5/6-delta)r`; since `delta<=5/6` and `r<=t_*+gamma`, it is
at most `1/6+(5/6-delta)t_*+(5/6-delta)gamma`.
The choice `t_*=5/(5-2delta)` makes both main expressions equal to
`rho(delta)`. Bounding both error coefficients by two gives
`rho(delta)+v+2gamma`. No marked moment or amplitude theorem is used.

This is exactly the broader gate exposed by
`UnmarkedDensity.unmarked_count_bound` and
`count_from_unmarked_raw_moments`: `0<=delta<=5/6`. The concrete inverse
spike incurs `2 epsilon_det`; the squared plain-pair spike incurs
`4 epsilon_det`, while `max(1,2m)<=1+150 epsilon_det`.
Thus both source estimates fit `154 epsilon_det+epsilon_m`, and support
tolerance adds another `2 epsilon_det`, for the displayed
`rho(delta_b)+156 epsilon_det+epsilon_m`.

The source threshold precedes all live characters/height/bin/cutoff
variables in the supported theorem, and precedes those variables in the
count after the fixed source family is supplied. Taking finite maxima
over dictionary moment inputs is valid. Partition costs, the finite bin
count and `(1+H_i)^(J0+1)` consume arbitrarily small allotted powers.
Since

\[
 -\rho'(\delta)=\frac{50}{3(5-2\delta)^2}\le\frac{200}{147}
 \quad(\delta\le3/4),
\]

the rounding costs at most `(400/147)e<3e`. Choose the losses so that
`156 epsilon_det+epsilon_m+3e+dyadic_loss+(J0+1)tau_det<epsilon`.
Auxiliary choices exist in this order: select small detector/moment
errors; obtain their finite `J0`; select `e,kappa_aux,eta_aux` within the
detector budget; then decrease `tau_det` for both height and final loss.
All are fixed before `Y,a,T`.

For `T>U^tau_det`, the lattice bound `N<<U` suffices. Choose an integer
`J>=1/tau_det`; then `U<=T^J` and `rho>=2/7>0`. A single enlarged
constant covers bounded `Y`, uniformly in `a,T`. Consequently

\[
 N(Y,a,T)\ll_{\mathcal D,\epsilon}
 (1+T)^JY^{\rho(2a-1)+\epsilon}
 \quad(33/40\le a\le7/8)
\]

with one threshold before `a,T`. The weighted sixth-power lifting is
uniform because `rho>=2/7>1/6`; the sixth-root convolution converges.
After lifting, even the finite exceptional free cores are paid through
that convolution, not incorrectly declared a finite raw-row population.
Natural holes and orientation survive the lift. At a physical use
`T=Z^tau_out`, choose a DISTINCT `tau_out` after the final density degree
`J`; its polynomial height cost fits the physical loss. This proves the
enlarged source theorem within precisely the accepted fixed-family scope.

## 3. Reconstructing the stronger gain in actual source units

Write c_s,d_s for the genuine first-support widths, distinguishing them from the endpoint constant. On either consistent first-side orientation the literal row is

    w=u0 e F_c G_c V_id h',
    W=M-R-(c_s-d_s)_+ +L_c-6a,
    L_c=log_Z NF_c <=5(R-R0), R<=min(c_s,d_s).       (I1)

The actual enclosing radius is used before dropping its favorable extra -omega. The separate child width M'=M-(c_s-d_s)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2, with the original padding, is unchanged. Active residues 1+t_p and 1-t_p modulo six remain distinct, including their zero-residue punctures. No equality of their F_c is assumed; the opposite first-side orientation is treated separately. Reflected second rows and whole-character conjugation remain within the fixed dictionary.

The actual joint high exponent relative to its target, from LA.13, is

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)+E1+E2+small,
    E1=(1-rho)(c_s-d_s)_+-delta c_s-(1+rho)R
       -E-Bc+rho L_c+R0,
    E2=g2-t2-(1+delta)b2.                            (I2)

There is no additional square root to take after this formula. It has already combined the two normalized sides, the joint row count, the missing radical and the outside power.

For delta in [17/25,7/10], put

    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],
    k=rho+delta-1=delta(5-6delta)/[3(5-2delta)].       (I3)

Here 5rho>1, 4rho-1>0, rho<2/5, and 0<k<delta. Let m=min(c_s,d_s), T=(c_s-d_s)_+, so c_s=m+T. Substituting L_c<=5(R-R0) into (I2) gives

    E1 <= -(rho+delta-1)T-delta m
          +(4rho-1)R+(1-5rho)R0-E-Bc
       <= -(delta-4rho+1)m-kT-E-Bc
       <= -k c_s.                                    (I4)

The last inequality is exactly delta-4rho+1-k=2-5rho>=0. This uses actual valuations and signs, not a finite residue-table enumeration. Since g2<=b2, also E2<=-delta b2-t2. Both coefficients are in the units of (I2).

For the full second projector, retain the B3.65 signed priority allocation. Extracting a selected plain n=d*l keeps psi_w(d), including its zero; l is unrestricted. Selecting a slot freezes that prime. No additional quotient puncture is inserted. For each of the four actual rectangle pairs put

    rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2,
    zbar=(z_1+z_2)/2.                                 (I5)

Every clipped reduction is nonnegative. B3.69 pays the divisor dyad by the two exact extraction scalars. Independently, the physical pointwise plain price contains -delta rbar. It is a shorter-plain saving, not an extraction scalar used a second time. The actual slot products stay inside the joint row sum; Cauchy and the accepted raw weighted bound replace their paired price delta zbar by gamma zbar. The gain there is eta zbar, where

    eta=4delta(5/6-delta)/(5-2delta)=2k.               (I6)

For example, clearing 3(5-2delta) reduces both sides of eta=2k to 2delta(5-6delta). It is an identity throughout the interval, not a numerical endpoint coincidence.

The already reviewed coefficient reduction is essential: freeze the missing first radical before weighted summation; all other apparent moving holes are natural zeros of w. Residual fixed holes have divisor-many subsets, and the finite surviving slot lists retain their original relative characters. The second projector stays outside this row reconstruction. Its count is paid once by B3.69. Common Fourier majorants precede the labels and their diagonal contraction adds no label count. Thus the weighted bound has the actual fixed prime coefficients, natural conductor and same-parent zero maximum; it is not applied to arbitrary moving masks.

The surviving widths satisfy the already established literal incidence bound

    zbar >= z-c_s-b2-rbar-small.                       (I7)

Each genuine frozen incidence divides the relevant complete extracted column, with its multiplicity. The column widths are c_s+c2 and c_s+d2. Newly frozen second-projector slots are included in r_j, and clipping costs only the single aggregate endpoint tolerance. Both the support terms and (I7) refer to the same pair of rectangles.

Set s=c_s+b2+rbar. If s>=z, (I4), E2 and the retained plain reduction already save at least ks>=kz. This uses only the old density, with its supported-window completion; no positive surviving slot width or weighted-width premise is needed. In particular all-slot-exhaustion cases are covered.

If s<z, then c_s<z and (I1) gives W>=M-c_s-6a>M-z-6a. Under the strict condition

    M-6a>22z,                                        (I8)

one has W>21z. Each individual surviving z_j<=z is therefore admissible for the accepted raw weighted theorem. The gain is at least

    ks+eta(z-s)-small =ks+2k(z-s)-small >=kz-small.    (I9)

The weighted theorem's width condition is needed only here. No negative nominal width is put into a nonempty density count: outside this case the old supported-window rule applies, and in this case W is strictly positive. Since k decreases, its endpoint values are

    k(17/25)=391/6825,  k(7/10)=7/135.

This proves the sharper all-configuration gain **k(delta)z**, in paired units. The weaker uniform 7z/135 follows. Exceptional rows remain separate and contribute no part of (I9).

The internal supported-witness zero bin can still have a larger upper endpoint than the physical bin. The accepted weighted lemma supplies its inverse/prime witnesses using that larger bin, but its slot price uses the original physical upper bound. Buffered bins below .70 use their prescribed lower edge with an O(e) upper-price allowance. Bins above .70 can use the old high estimate. Bins crossing .68 use the original low-branch rounding rule. No transform or projector is applied to a zero-bin indicator.

Do not credit an arithmetic energy improvement or any new zero-free constant.** The incumbent remains c6 = 125139/1000000, with b6 = 874861/1000000. # [private research revision]: native translation costs and a fixed-source renewal obstruction

Accept G201-G203 at the scopes below, from the [W64 author](wild64/report.md)
and [independent review](wild64-review/report.md). The review corrects the
moving-stencil normalization and proves a stronger, single fixed synthetic
source obstruction. The [two selection-blind audits](wild64-review/independent-audits.md)
retain complete signed smooth prefixes and complete feedback forcing.
These results redirect particular norm-based attacks. They neither bound
the full signed arithmetic source nor increase c11=.1251459636.

## G201. Exact native carrier spectrum, with normalized stencil cost

Use the literal Eisenstein [JN source](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), not
an ordinary integer surrogate. Freeze the original long-prime pair of
distinct degree-one rational norms p,r, with Q=pr and phi=(p-1)(r-1).
The complete finite group has Q^2 elements and unitary Fourier factor 1/Q.
The row multiplier is m(h)=ell_p(h_p)ell_r(h_r), with quadratic characters
zero at zero. The mark factors vanish off exactly phi mark pairs and have
modulus one on them. The complete coefficient includes the original
b0=b(pi)conjugate(b(pi'))zeta_CRT, which may vanish.

For translation S_t f(h)=f(h+t), the row commutator is

    D_t=diag(m(h)-m(h+t)) S_t.

When t is nonzero in both residue fields, local autocorrelation is -1.
Indeed z^2=y(y+1) is equivalent, by an invertible change of variables over
an odd field, to (2y+1-2z)(2y+1+2z)=1. Counting its p-1 solutions proves
the local identity including the zero sites. CRT gives correlation 1.
There are B=(p-2)(r-2) positions where both row values are nonzero, two
where both vanish, and n1=2(p+r-3) where exactly one vanishes. Thus

    singular value 2: multiplicity n2=(B-1)/2;
    singular value 1: multiplicity n1;
    rank D_t=(Q+2p+2r-9)/2;
    ||D_t||_HS^2=2(phi-1),  ||D_t||_op=2.

For a shift nonzero only at p, replace these multiplicities by
n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2 and n1=2(r-1); the other case is symmetric. The full
carrier repeats each nonzero row singular value phi times and scales
it by |b0|. Unitary Fourier conjugation introduces no further saving.
For rank k<=n2 approximation the squared row Hilbert-Schmidt error is
at least 4(n2-k)+n1, and for k<n2 the operator error is at least 2.

Let P=sum c_j S_j for k distinct integer shifts 0<j<min(p,r). Distinct
matrix diagonals cannot cancel in Hilbert-Schmidt norm, so

    ||[M_m,P]||_HS^2=2(phi-1)||c||_2^2,
    sqrt(2(phi-1)/Q)||c||_2 <= ||[M_m,P]||_op
                             <=2 sqrt(k)||c||_2,
    rank[M_m,P] >= (phi-1)/(2k),  c!=0.

The lower operator bound uses rank<=Q. Moving coefficients require the
displayed normalization: c_1=Q^(-10) defeats the author's unnormalized
prose claim. The correct cost is relative to |b0| ||c||_2, or for stencils
whose normalized size does not vanish. The immutable author report is
retained with this explicit superseding correction.

These are ambient carrier facts. They do not identify the carrier with
the physical mark matrix, make the actual folded W an extremizer, or
bound its signed pairing below. All original projectors, ordered short
pairs including equality, complex gcd core, masks, roots, independent
heights and natural zeros remain. The raw H target is still

    Z^epsilon G K [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig,

followed by N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. None of the .004 full-H deficit is
paid. A source-specific recurrence and its complete observation/residual
estimate remain legitimate targets.

## G202. Centered quotient norm and one fixed cumulative source

Now use a separate ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, with
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), a(1)=1 and literal natural zeros. Write M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n),
psi_chi(y)=sum_(d<=y)Lambda(d)chi(d), and delta=1 for principal chi and
zero otherwise. The exact [[restricted research revision] renewal identity](../[private research revision]/wild55/report.md)
is prior credit:

    R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n,
    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x).

For integer N>=2 and floor-invariant f define the centered functional

    J_N(f)=sum_(d<=N)Lambda(d)chi(d)f_floor(N/d)
                     -delta int_1^N f_floor(N/u) du.

The pole-subtraction measure is du. The restored principal term is exactly
N sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n-M(N); it cannot be dropped. Merge equal quotient states
before taking absolute values:

    J_N(f)=sum_(1<=m<N)c_m f_m,
    c_m=psi_chi(N/m)-psi_chi(N/(m+1))-delta N/[m(m+1)].

The lower interval endpoint is strict. State m=N contributes neither a
nonzero discrete atom nor positive continuous length. The exact norm for
|f_m|<=m^beta and f_m=0 at m<=Y, with 0<beta<1, is

    C_(beta,Y)(N)=N^(-beta) sum_(Y<m<N)|c_m|m^beta.

Set D=floor(min(sqrt(N)/4,N/[4(Y+1)])). Each unramified prime power
2<=d<=D has a distinct cell m=floor(N/d)>Y of length
N/[m(m+1)]<=d^2/(N-d)<=1/8, containing d alone. Therefore

    C_(beta,Y)(N)>=2^(-beta-1)
                    sum_(d<=D,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta)
                  >>_(q,beta) D^(1-beta).

The lower estimate needs only an elementary Chebyshev bound: prime
valuations of binomial(2n,n) give psi(2n)>=2n log 2-log(2n+1), and deleting
the finitely many q-prime-power rays costs O_q(log D). For Y=floor(N^theta),
0<=theta<1, even C/log N grows at least as
N^((1-beta)min(1/2,1-theta))/log N. This is a merged centered norm bound,
not a lower bound for J_N(M), R, or M.

The obstruction survives cumulative inputs with honest natural-zero
increments. For 1/2<beta<1 and 0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta), let

    Q_q(t)=sum_(n<=t)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q t+O_q(sqrt t),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

For each unramified prime power d<=N^alpha, put m_d=floor(N/d),
H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8) and
B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|). The squarefree density formula follows
by inserting sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-units, and paying every square-divisor
error and tail. It places each bump within m_d+O_q(H_d). The support-width
to nearest-center spacing ratio is O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta))=o(1).
Supports and increment boundaries are disjoint. Their inverse images
under u->floor(N/u) have width o(1), so each has exactly the integer
contact d; the floor error O(d^2/N) also tends uniformly to zero.

The compact synthetic sum G_N(n)=sum_d conjugate(chi(d))B_d(n) satisfies
|G_N(n)|<=n^beta and |G_N(n)-G_N(n-1)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1).
Every discrete atom contributes Lambda(d)H_d. For principal chi the full
continuous subtraction costs at most half this for sufficiently large N;
for nonprincipal chi it is absent. Thus

    J_N(G_N) >= c N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)) >0.

Independent strengthening: choose N_j increasingly so that each whole
bump block G_j, including its increment boundary, lies above N_(j-1)
and above the preceding support. If F_old is the earlier sum, choose
z_j=J_(N_j)(F_old)/|J_(N_j)(F_old)| when nonzero and z_j=1 otherwise.
Then |J_(N_j)(F_old+z_jG_j)|=|J_(N_j)(F_old)|+J_(N_j)(G_j).
Later blocks change no state sampled at N_j. Hence ONE locally finite
F=sum_j z_jG_j and b(n)=F(n)-F(n-1) satisfy

    |b(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),  |F(n)|<=n^beta,
    |J_(N_j)(F)|>=c N_j^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).

Any fixed finite zero prefix can be prescribed. For principal chi, the
phases may be +/-1 and b(n) belongs to {-1,0,1}. A growing zero prefix
at infinitely many N_j would force F identically zero and is NOT claimed.
Only the cutoff-dependent construction retains that separate property.
Neither construction has the prescribed Möbius signs, multiplicativity,
or the actual inverse-convolution law. Those are the remaining structures
that a successful arithmetic argument must use.

## G203. A signed inner source does not rescue the outer positive budget

For fixed ordinary chi and y=x^eta, 0<eta<1, split each squarefree n uniquely
into its y-smooth part a and y-rough part b. With S_y the entire signed
smooth prefix, including its unit, exactly

    M_chi(x)=sum_(b<=x,Pminus(b)>y)mu(b)chi(b) S_y(x/b).

The proposed outer absolute budget retains all cancellation inside S_y.
Nevertheless each unramified prime p in (x/2,x] contributes exactly one
to that budget, because S_y(x/p)=1. It is therefore >>_q x/log x by the
ordinary [prime number theorem, DLMF27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
No arithmetic-progression or conductor-uniform theorem is imported.
On shells [X,2X], primes p in (X,3X/2] have the same unit inner prefix
through the common interval [3X/2,2X]. The sum of complete polymer L1 or
L2 norms also costs >>_q X/log X. This does not bound the signed sum or
its full Gram form below. Cross-polymer cancellation remains open.

## Complete feedback and arithmetic return remain explicit

The other blind audit retains a conditional feedback budget. For a fixed
compatible finite map T=[[a,b],[c,D]], let r>||D|| and
Delta=r-|a|-||b||||c||/(r-||D||)>0. The exact Schur denominator
s(w)=w-a-b(wI-D)^(-1)c has no zero at |w|>=r. Its full resolvent formula
gives C_r=K+(1+K||c||)(1+K||b||)/Delta, K=(r-||D||)^(-1), and

    ||T^j||<=C_r r^(j+1),
    ||z_j||<=C_r r^(j+1)||z_0||+C_r sum_(k<j)r^(j-k)||f_k||.

Every forcing term is retained. A contour-only denominator bound without
exterior zero exclusion is insufficient. Varying native Q^2 spaces require
compatible maps, physical observation and all discarded/forced complements;
the stationary lemma alone supplies none of these. G136/G151 retain ancestry.

For actual ordinary coefficients, [restricted research revision]'s exact inverse
M(x)=1-R(x)/log x-int_2^x R(t)dt/[t(log t)^2] shows that a complete
all-real-x every-epsilon bound R=O(x^(gamma+epsilon)log x) is equivalent
to the corresponding Mertens exponent. Mellin continuation then excludes
regular L zeros at Re(s)>gamma, retaining the principal pole, imprimitive
factors and all finite heights for each fixed character. This entire
arithmetic estimate is still OPEN. A first gain requires gamma<.8748540364;
gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 correspond to nearby c=.1252,1/6,1/4 targets.

Root read both full reports, the two blind audits, both finite helpers and
their saved receipts, and the named exact ancestor contracts. The existing
finite checks were not rerun: they establish only their finite convention
checks. Forty-three frozen original files and the prior raw scorecard are
retained with byte hashes. Both writers stopped and normally released.
All 30 seeds, immutable draws, failed tests and corrected claims survive.
No full signed estimate, c improvement, formalization or external admission
is inferred from these scoped mathematical results.

## G112. Coalescence does not lower the independent-defect power cost

For each fixed ordinary character chi preserve all natural zeros and put
R(t,y)=sum_(n<=t,P^-(n)>y)mu(n)chi(n), with P^-(1)=infinity.
Its least-prime recurrence is R=1-sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)R(t/p,p).
For a floor-invariant approximation F let Delta be its full recurrence
defect. G92 gives the exact root identity

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_(N,chi)(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<v<=N/(pm),P^+(v)<p)mu(v)chi(v).    (77.1)

All coefficients are merged by the actual integer state BEFORE absolute
values. The strict lower/inclusive upper endpoints, v=1 and strict prime
ordering matter. For the exact integer collar m<=p^r, fixed integer r>=1,
the independent bounded-defect norm is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.        (77.2)

The earlier real-state exponent-one lower bound did not prove anything
comparable after signed coalescence. The actual cancellation at
(N,p,m)=(20196,17,18), v=65,66 remains valid. Here a new arithmetic
argument proves, for EVERY fixed principal character chi0 modulo q,

    lim_(N->infinity) log B_(r,chi0)(N)/log N=1.        (77.3)

The external input is Tenenbaum's fixed-order friable Mobius expansion,
combining Theorems2-3 in the [original source](headroom/Erdos-Alladi.pdf).
Write omega for the Buchstab function. For fixed K>=1 and a fixed compact
I contained in(K+1,infinity), uniformly for u=log x/log y in I,

    W(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P^+(n)<=y)mu(n)
      =x sum_(j=1)^K a_j omega^(j)(u)/(log y)^(j+1)
        +O_(I,K)(x/(log y)^(K+2)),
    sum_(j>=1)a_j z^j=1/[(1+z)zeta(1+z)], a1=1.        (77.4)

The primary images confirm the sign, derivative index and logarithm power.

Psi(x,y)/L_epsilon(y) is smaller than every needed fixed logarithmic
order. No uniform growing K or u estimate is imported. The published
theorem and ordinary PNT are mathematical premises, not consequences of

statement:
### 2.1 Exact disk theorem and strongest cheap counterexample

Let h be holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk and h(0)=1. Define normalized circle measure dm=dtheta/(2pi),

    u(theta)=Re h(exp(i theta)),
    B(h)=integral max(-u(theta),0) dm.

Write u=u_+-u_-. The mean-value identity gives integral u_+=1+B and integral u_-=B. For |z|=rho<1 the Poisson kernel obeys

    (1-rho)/(1+rho) <= P_z(theta) <= (1+rho)/(1-rho).

Consequently, with k_rho=(1-rho)/(1+rho),

    Re h(z) >= k_rho(1+B)-B/k_rho.                 (W40.1)

This is the full complementary return: the negative part is paid against the largest Poisson weight and the positive part against the smallest. It follows that

    B(h) <= b(r):=(1-r)^2/(4r)
       ==> Re h(z)>0 for every |z|<r.              (W40.2)

At |z|=r a strict hypothesis gives strict positivity; equality only gives nonnegativity there. The open-disk conclusion with non-strict B<=b(r) is valid because b(rho) is strictly decreasing for 0<rho<1. In particular h has no zero in |z|<r. No positivity of the original arithmetic coefficients was used.

For completeness the signed representation is also exact:

    h(z)=integral (exp(i theta)+z)/(exp(i theta)-z)
                       *u(theta) dm.              (W40.3)

Expand the kernel into1+2 sum_(n>=1)z^n exp(-in theta). The Fourier coefficients of Re h give half the positive Taylor coefficients; the constant is h(0)=1. Uniform convergence on compact subdisks proves the identity. This avoids assuming a positive Herglotz measure or an analytic logarithm of h.

The generic budget is sharp in the signed-measure closure. Put B>0 and

    h_B(z)=(1+B)(1+z)/(1-z)-B(1-z)/(1+z).

Its representing measure is (1+B)delta_1-B delta_-1, and h_B(0)=1. It has a zero at

    z=-r_B,
    r_B=(sqrt(1+B)-sqrt B)/(sqrt(1+B)+sqrt B),
    B=(1-r_B)^2/(4r_B).                             (W40.4)

Thus arbitrarily small total negative mass can create a zero arbitrarily close to the boundary. A claim that a small unweighted defect gives the ENTIRE disk is false. A positive collar is essential. The rational h_B has boundary poles, so it is not an equality example in the smooth-boundary class. To verify sharpness there, take h_B(tz), t<1, and choose r_B=tr. It is analytic beyond the unit circle and has its zero at-r. Its boundary real part is the signed Poisson smoothing of the two atoms. Its negative mass tends to b(r) as t increases to1: the two Poisson kernels concentrate on disjoint arcs, and their overlap mass tends to0. For a proposed larger budget at fixed r, first choose r'<r with b(r') below that budget, then use this approximation at r'. Its zero is now INSIDE the target disk. Thus no larger uniform open-disk budget follows in the smooth class either.

This first test corrects the unpriced seed: total negative mass is useful only with the explicit radius-dependent return W40.2. It does not by itself prove any arithmetic bound.
title: 2.1 Exact disk theorem and strongest cheap counterexample

## 7. Uniform independent audit17: optimized contours retain the observed residues

The seed proposes signed endpoint states on a low-resolvent contour. The relevant test must use the actual reciprocal L-function, not an arbitrary rational transfer function.

For fixed ordinary chi define the first logarithmic Riesz sum

    R_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n)log(x/n)
           =integral_1^x M_chi(t)dt/t.                 (R15)

The n=x endpoint has weight0. On a fixed vertical line c>1, the elementary inverse Mellin kernel for log_+(y) is y^s/s^2. It follows by closing left for y>1 and right for y<1, with the double pole at0; at y=1 the vertical integral of1/s^2 is0. Its absolute vertical convergence and sum_n |a(n)|n^(-c)<=zeta(c) justify interchange. Thus the FULL identity is

    R_chi(x)=(1/(2pi i))integral_(c-i infinity)^(c+i infinity)
                         x^s/[s^2 L(s,chi)] ds.         (R16)

No character zero or source coefficient has changed.

Let 0<sigma<c and T>0, with the boundary of the finite rectangle avoiding zeros of L. Write I_(v,T) for the upward integral on Re(s)=v from -T to T, divided by2pi i, and K_x(s)=x^s/[s^2L(s,chi)]. The residue theorem gives EXACTLY

    R_chi(x)=I_(sigma,T)
          +sum_(rho inside rectangle) Res_(s=rho) K_x(s)
          +B_T(x)+E_(c,T)(x),                           (R17)
    B_T=-(1/(2pi i))[
          integral_(c+iT)^(sigma+iT) K_x(s)ds
          +integral_(sigma-iT)^(c-iT) K_x(s)ds],
    |E_(c,T)(x)|<=zeta(c)x^c/(pi T).

The last bound comes only from the omitted RIGHT-line tails and |1/L(c+it,chi)|<=zeta(c). It does not bound the horizontal pieces, the left side or any detours. Principal L's pole at1 is a zero of1/L, not a residue of K_x. The s=0 kernel pole is outside the sigma>0 rectangle. Ramified Euler factors have not been deleted.

If L has a zero rho of multiplicity m, with Re(rho)>0, its contribution has the exact form

    Res K_x(s)=x^rho P_(m-1)(log x),
    leading coefficient of P_(m-1)
       = m! / [L^(m)(rho) rho^2 (m-1)!] !=0.            (R18)

This follows by multiplying the leading Laurent term of1/L by the Taylor series of x^s/s^2. A closed local contour with winding1 around rho and0 around every other pole has integral2pi i times (R18), regardless of its optimized shape. For fixed rho its absolute value is asymptotic to a nonzero constant times x^Re(rho)(log x)^(m-1). Shrinking or moving that local detour cannot turn it into O(x^gamma) when gamma<Re(rho).

This is a scoped obstruction to discarding or underpricing a pole's local contour contribution. It is NOT a lower bound for the complete Mertens or Riesz sum: other residues and boundary integrals may interfere. Nor does it assert that a hypothetical arithmetic zero exists. It shows precisely what a source-correct contour-state construction would have to retain and estimate.

There is a complete conditional return. If, for every fixed chi and epsilon>0, the whole R_chi(x) is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) at all large real x, then

    integral_1^infinity R_chi(x)x^(-s)dx/x
       =1/[s^2 L(s,chi)]   initially Re(s)>1

continues holomorphically to Re(s)>gamma. The numerator1/s^2 is nonzero at every possible zero there, so all finite-height L zeros are excluded exactly as in section2. In particular (R3) implies this Riesz bound by Cauchy--Schwarz in (R15), with a harmless logarithm absorbed by every epsilon.

A contour proposal would therefore be sufficient if it proved a complete signed bound for ALL of (R17), including the right truncation, horizontal/endpoint states, left line, every enclosed residue and any induced numerator. An individual low-resolvent arc, a contour which simply avoids zeros, or a fixed-height check does not prove that assertion. Choosing T=T(x) to make the explicit right tail small still leaves all the other height-dependent costs.

This is standard Perron/Riesz/residue machinery applied to the exact source. F01/W27 weak detectors, W22's filter cautions and W39's all-height return are ancestry. More specifically, [private research revision] G77 ALREADY retains the full Gaussian rectangle, nonzero multiplicity-residue polynomial, right tail, horizontals and a fixed finite-packet shell-norm lower bound. This audit changes to a Riesz kernel and its explicit polynomial right-tail bound; it does not improve that general gluing principle or its packet lower bound. The seed is promising only if it supplies the missing arithmetic signed boundary estimate; contour geometry or an observability toy does not replace it.

                       (log Np/log D) V_D(yz),        (R3)

and P^(-1/2)E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2). There is no unpriced factor P^(1/2).

Apply the literal common-profile lemma B3.3 on an ambient compact box in y,z, with larger individual cutoffs equal to one on the entire current support. This box and its Fourier measure are fixed BEFORE a current row, prime, slot label or coloring is selected. The sharp band membership and every arithmetic hole remain in row-independent outer coefficients. The measure has a finite weighted L1 norm controlled by finitely many common seminorms; no prime-specific Fourier measure is chosen.

For clarity about heights, first write the original witness twist explicitly. If W_P(x)=W_0(x)x^(sigma+i gamma), then

    (yz)^(sigma+i gamma)=y^(sigma+i gamma)z^(sigma+i gamma).

Separate the remaining smooth kernel W_0(yz) log D/log(Dyz), with the bounded real power either retained there or factored as above. Thus high Fourier decay is a property of a kernel whose derivative constants do NOT grow as |gamma|^N. The original gamma appears explicitly in both output tests. The original B0.14--15 contour padding therefore accommodates the retained frequency shift without changing i, a, beta, phi or the chosen zero. Here is an exact way to pay the ENTIRE Fourier complement. Use the source's internal floor T_ht>=U^kappa with fixed kappa>0.     E^(1/2) <=C E^(beta/2)(1+|tau_2|)^J1

on that complement. Bounded nonempty subunit E obey the same inequality by constants. On the retained frequencies use R1. The unconditioned MI already has polynomial cost in tau_1 and the original heights. The extra high derivatives just used belong to the height-free separation kernel; they do not increase this previously fixed MI height degree. Below the internal floor use the dictionary at that floor. Above the original small polynomial range a larger final external height degree pays the absolute source bound. The external physical height exponent is chosen after that degree. The original detector's contour tails retain their accepted B-before-N order. This full-integral implementation supplies the author's separation step without a circular height/decay choice or a new high-height theorem.

For scale differentiation, use log Np/log U as the FIXED prime coefficient and place log U/log D=1/m outside the prime sum. Its derivatives are bounded because m stays in a fixed positive interval. Neither the band membership nor a live arithmetic prime coefficient is differentiated with D. Derivatives of V_D and the cutoff profiles remain in the finite smooth family. Any rowwise real/height/scale evaluation is dominated by tensor Sobolev on fixed rectangles, followed by MI on its derivative profiles.        <=1-1017/100000+8/1000+small

       <=2-2(1017/100000)+4/20+32/1000+small

`abe39a6c4d0845ded15ce77834b9f3b76c60296de4e3e1c4ae3935c6094a7622`.
These finite checks support the written proof; they are not a kernel proof.

## Credit and preserved contracts

Zhongpai Gao, with AI assistance, supplied the local construction and
bridges at PR15 `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`, relative to
PR9 `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`. OpenAI retains credit for
the initial 7/8 theorem and analytic/arithmetic framework; Hailey Collet
for the quartic, variable-moment, detector and source architecture; Akash
Levy for the weighted numerator. [private research revision] supplies the larger-amplifier
specialization. [private research revision] supplies a finite family of amplifiers coupled
to original slot width and its complete endpoint return. This is not a
claim of literature priority or upstream endorsement. Original sources
and licenses remain in the [preserved PR15 record](../external/gao-pr15-ca182b70/README.md).

The local theorem retains the fixed finite ray family, natural sextic
row, original prime pools and common annular profile, relative characters,
natural zeros, fixed original anchor Q_*, row-independent punctures and
non-FixedInducingRow eligibility. With U=Z^M, the window is

    .41M <= n1,n2 <= .44M,  .03M <= z <= .04M,
    n1+n2+(881/200)z <= M.

It gives the original paired squared moment O(Z^(M+epsilon) H_J),
including all four derivative-profile pairs. Descendants use only the
old 9/2 moment or unrestricted zero-slot input. Mesh, dictionary, finite
orders, constants and one eventual threshold precede the same live
scales, masks, subsets and independent heights as in the original source.

## Genuine new local input

Put C=881/200, r=9/2-C=19/200, k=9/40, and
b_j=.03+j/5000 for j=0,...,50. For t=z/M, take j=1 when t=.03 and
otherwise the unique j with b_(j-1)<t<=b_j. Choose the literal prime
amplifier exponent a_j/M=k b_j and sigma_j=3a_j. This is a ceiling
selection, including at the left endpoint. Within the same interval,

    A/M <= 1-(C-1)b_(j-1),   g/M <= r b_j.

Thus the proof does not combine incompatible full-window extrema. The
fifty choices are fixed before the target, rows, transforms or binning.
Both equal-product rectangles use the same j. Its dependence on original
slot width, rather than either plain scale, causes no derivative of a
selection boundary in plain-scale supremum recovery.

The exact PR9 amplification interfaces quantify original data and slot
widths after the eventual threshold, permit fixed positive sigma, and
require a sufficiently fine mesh. A finite maximum over the fifty
choices and four derivative pairs therefore gives the needed simultaneous
threshold. The representation multiplicity remains a fixed constant.
This is a source-level admissibility check, not an inference from the
older global theorem's separate small-sigma induction.

The enlarged actual main radius is K0+(d-c)_++6a_j+omega. Errors retain
their own radii and original canonical source. Exact interval checking
gives low reserve 151/22500000 >= 1/150000 and high reserve 1/43200,
including the actual rounding charge 13/100000. The high-branch
derivative is bounded below by 1548949/4860000>0 over its whole range.
The low/high transition at .7 is paid with the original mesh losses.

The three error reserves are at least 97/80000,1717/80000,1061/40000;
second-zero, main fixed-inducing and error fixed-inducing reserves are
2727/40000,7497/100000,8199/200000. The exact main exception retains
its -4a_j term. Joint row labels, missing radicals, valuations, projector
costs, natural zeros, moving holes, negative actual-width corrections,
both transforms and old-only descendants all remain in the argument.
Choose aggregate small losses below fixed fractions of the least reserve.

## Complete endpoint, not just local capacity

Use

    ell=15673/93750, h=3969737987/5000000000,
    x=5598466039/15000000000, y=6893853961/15000000000,
    kappa=46859/62500.

The actual shortening maxima are .422132747912 for each plain slot and
.036139510427 for the marked slot. Safe upper edges are **.423 and
.0365**; the older .036 edge cannot be reused. Short-slot and short-plain
complements have reserves 19/1000 and 11/4000. The coarse large
Euler-shift reserve is 2747/15858000>1/6000; its actual value is
37375232238487/188618444993538000. The earlier >1/4000 claim is not
reused. Coefficient mass and exhausted/empty-slot cases are retained.

On the complete delta,p rectangle, rational Bernstein subdivision proves
the local upper row, old junction and old lower row with respectively
8,6,1 leaves and savings 10^-6,10^-5,10^-3. The independent implementation
derives its polynomial separately, verifies every box, nonoverlap and
total coverage, and matches the author's exact extrema. No sampled
grid stands in for a continuous inequality.

The retained-row extension has saving 4999/5000000000; local and old
feedback coefficients are below 1/50 and 1/8. The proof also pays the
floor, finite-conductor and small-row cases, original free Euler shifts,
principal/eigenvalue terms, full height range and off-height fields.
Common reserves and the mesh are fixed before a near-extremal target;
the finite amplifier family adds no target-dependent saving. The final
strip iteration and the Eisenstein-to-ordinary-Dirichlet transfer are
part of the complete author and independent review, with the pole at 1
treated separately. No zero-times-pole inference is used.

## Exact limitation and useful next step

The inequality **C>3791/861** is the open range of the displayed
*strictly positive low/high reserve argument*. At equality the two
reserves cannot both be strictly positive. This does **not** prove the
epsilon-loss moment impossible at equality, and does not exclude an
epsilon-dependent construction or different argument there. Any stronger
wording in the frozen author discussion is qualified by this disposition.
The explicit C=4.405 theorem lies strictly inside the proved range and
does not rely on passage to equality.

A finer fixed family can test constants between this boundary and
4.405, with the complete endpoint repriced. A material further gain
requires a better low-bin deletion price, high-bin density loss, radius
increment or useful local window. Raising a lower slot edge must also
pay the enlarged short-slot complement. Neither such an improvement
nor a limiting endpoint is admitted here.

### D: exact but already credited

`V_P=exp(sum_(p<=P)p^-s) product_(p<=P)(1-p^-s)` has

    log V_P=-sum_(p<=P)sum_(j>=2)p^(-js)/j,
    (1-z)e^z=1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)z^j/j!.

These converge normally, with upper and lower modulus bounds on each `Re s>=rho>1/2`, since the first-prime channel was removed. Restoring it is not paid by bounding higher clusters. Under the separate open fixed-power prime-counting error, integration including the prime-2 atom gives

    D(s)=s integral_2^infinity [pi(u)-li_2(u)]u^(-s-1)du,
    1/zeta(s)=(s-1)V(s)exp(-J(s)-D(s)),
    J'(s)=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1),

with J's constant fixed on Re s>1. The displayed derivative is entire after the removable value at 1, and the factor s-1 handles the principal pole. This matches W36 R36.20–22 verbatim in mathematical content, already credited to [private research revision] A12/W21 there. Ordinary PNT is not the missing fixed-power bound. No additional high-ceiling result is awarded to selected07.

## 1. Decision, statement, and evidence class

**ACCEPT both the closed-plane epsilon-loss source theorem and the separate complete endpoint, as written analytic composition relative to the accepted pinned PR9/PR15 framework.** No blocking mathematical discrepancy or changed numerical parameter is required. The physical parent-modulus padding is spelled out in Section 8; it fits the report's existing small-loss budgets. The independent certificate reproduces all 600 amplifier cases, 60 endpoint scalars, 17 closed-plane bounds, and all 204 Bernstein coefficients on the exact 10/6/1 rectangle partitions.

For a fixed admissible natural source family, M>0, and every requested epsilon>0, sufficiently fine fixed original slots give

    sum_eligible |S_1(Z^n1) S_2(Z^n2) Q_I|^2
        << Z^(M+epsilon) H_J

when

    .41M <= n1,n2 <= .44M,
    .034M <= z <= .04M,
    2009(n1+n2)+8379z <= 1995M.

The boundary is included only in this every-epsilon conclusion. It does not have simultaneously strictly positive fixed low/high reserves in the displayed limiting ledger. The proof uses an epsilon-dependent finite atlas, fixed before the asymptotic variable and live data. It never passes to an atlas whose size grows with Z. H_J contains finite smooth seminorms and polynomial costs of the independent plain and slot heights, including the four plain derivative pairs used in scale recovery.

The endpoint uses a different, fixed strictly interior atlas. It gives

    theta5 = 54679/62500 = .874864,
    c5 = 7821/62500 = .125136.

This is an increase of 1/1000000 over the accepted written c4=25027/200000 and 113/5000000 over Gao's c_G=625567/5000000. Relative to the accepted framework, the resulting zero-free region is Re(s)>theta5 for finite-order Hecke characters of trivial infinite type over the Eisenstein field and all ordinary Dirichlet L-functions, including zeta, with the principal pole at 1 excluded. The statement does not extend to the boundary line, angular Hecke characters, arbitrary slot profiles, or uniform growing-parent-conductor moments.

This is not a new Lean endpoint, dependency replay or kernel certificate; old c0 kernel evidence does not verify c5. No open Gaussian/f3, H, Bessel or Hankel estimate is used. statement:
## 4. Common-filter arithmetic payment: full proof audit

For an integer t>=0 put f_t(n)=mu^2(n)t^omega(n)chi(n), using f_0=delta1. Fix p not dividing q and J>=2, independent of x. Let

    Q_p=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    v_(p,J)=Q_p^(*J), P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b_p=Q_p*chi=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)).                       (4.1)

At p^a, the literal filter coefficient is binom(J,a)(-p chi(p))^a for 0<=a<=J. The actual b_p has period pq and mean zero. For nonprincipal chi both period sums vanish; for principal chi the p unrestricted copies cancel the p-multiple contribution, since chi(p)=1. Imprimitive and ramified natural zeros remain. Hence its partial sums are bounded by a constant depending on p,q.

### 4.1 Periodic hyperbola induction with every overlap

For any fixed bounded periodic mean-zero b, set B_t(x)=sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n). For every fixed integer t>=1,

    |B_t(x)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t), x>=1.                       (4.2)

For t=1 this is bounded periodic partial sums. For t>1 let Y=x^(1/t). Every admissible ordered t-tuple has at least one coordinate <=Y. Inclusion-exclusion over these t events is exact. In a term with j<t designated short coordinates, put m=t-j and beta=1-1/m. Their product is at most Y^j<=x, so the remaining summation threshold is >=1 and the induction hypothesis applies. Bounding ONLY the designated short coefficients costs

    C_m x^beta [sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^-beta]^j
       <=C_m(Dm)^j x^beta Y^(j/m)
       =C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t),                             (4.3)

where D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|). The exponent equality follows from m=t-j. For j=t the product cutoff is automatic and the term is exactly (sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t, bounded by D^t. This last cancellation must not be replaced by Y^t. Every sign and overlap remains; real floors and empty initial intervals cause no error.

The resulting recurrence is

    C_1<=D,
    C_t<=D^t+sum_(m=1)^(t-1)binom(t,m)C_m(Dm)^(t-m).

Induction gives C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2: after division by this proposed bound and j=t-m, each summand is <=2^-j/j!, since m!m^j<=t!. Their sum is <e^(1/2)-1, and the remaining D^t ratio leaves a strict margin for t>=2. This is a valid explicit upper bound, not an optimality claim.

### 4.2 Exact squarefree Euler correction and all p shifts

On Re s>1 the literal f_t has Euler product

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.       (4.4)

The product is over primes. Each local polynomial has constant one and zero linear term. Its coefficients g_t therefore satisfy

    Gabs_t(sigma):=sum_n|g_t(n)|n^-sigma<infinity
                                      for every sigma>1/2, (4.5)

for each fixed t. This follows from the absolutely convergent product of the finite local absolute polynomials; ramified local factors are one. No nonvanishing claim about G_t is needed or implied.

For 1<=t<=J the exact coefficient identity is

    v_(p,J)*f_t=b_p^(*t)*v_(p,J-t)*g_t.                   (4.6)

This retains a COMMON filter on the left. It follows from Q_p^t*chi^(*t)=b_p^(*t); it is not a subtraction of estimates obtained with different filters. For t=0 the source is the finite sequence v_(p,J).

Take sigma>1/2 with sigma>=beta_t:=1-1/t. On every real x, (4.2), (4.5) and (4.6) give

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*f_t)(n)|
      <= C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma.    (4.7)

To justify every endpoint, sum only over p^a d<=x, use the bound at y=x/(p^a d)>=1, and replace y^beta_t by y^sigma. The finite shifts have weights binom(J-t,a)p^a and arguments x/p^a, giving exactly the displayed factor. Terms whose argument is below one are empty, not approximated. At t>=3 choose sigma=beta_t>1/2; at t=1,2 choose sigma=1/2+epsilon. This proves the author's individual-color bound and preserves all dependence on fixed J,p,q.

Define a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu^2(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k), k>=1. Finite differences give

    a_k=sum_(t=0)^k(-1)^(k-t)binom(k,t)f_t.

Summing (-1)^k for k<=J gives the exact low-chain combination

    L_J:=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.              (4.8)

Equations (4.7)-(4.8) prove the author's complete common-filter estimate

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*L_J)(n)|
         <<_(p,q,J,epsilon)x^(max(1/2,1-1/J)+epsilon).     (4.9)

It includes every first-J chain sector and every compensator term for all real x. It is a genuine arithmetic estimate, including principal characters; it is not an estimate of an arbitrarily selected signed subsource.

### 4.3 Explicit growth is accounted for but gives no growing-J theorem

The local coefficient c_(t,a) of (1+tz)(1-z)^t obeys

    |c_(t,a)|<=t^a(1/a!+1/(a-1)!), a>=2.

For fixed 1/2<sigma<1, split primes at Y=t^(1/sigma). The tail local logarithm is O(t^2 l^-2sigma), with a universal constant because t l^-sigma<1. Summing over all integers beyond Y costs O_sigma(t^(1/sigma)). On l<=Y, the absolute local polynomial is bounded by (1+t l^-sigma)(1+l^-sigma)^t. Summing its logarithm over all integers up to Y proves

    log Gabs_t(sigma)<<_sigma t^(1/sigma)log(2t).          (4.10)

Together with C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2 and (4.7), this confirms the author's explicit upper price, including all p shifts, all binomial coefficients in (4.8), and the t=0 bound (J+1)(1+p)^J. The condition sigma>=1-1/t must remain: a fixed target sigma cannot be used in (4.7) for arbitrarily large t. The factorial/Euler constants may also grow rapidly. These are failures of the available upper budget, not lower-bound impossibility theorems for a better growing-color argument.

## 3. The actual witness contract

PR9 Lemma1W, paper lines 298--342, chooses a cutoff `t_* in [1,3/2]`
before witnesses. For a nonfloor zero bin it produces one presentation,
one real power and a common height for the inverse/plain pair, and dyadic
length exponents satisfying

\[
 r\le t_*+O(\epsilon),\quad r+m\ge t_*-O(\epsilon),
 \quad 0\le m\le1/2+O(\epsilon),
\]
\[
 |M|^2\gg U^{\delta r-O(\epsilon)},\qquad
 |S|^2\gg U^{\delta m-O(\epsilon)}.
\]

The source's saturation step explicitly uses only `delta >= 1/50`, not
`delta >= .7`. The inverse cutoff is inserted before dyadic selection.
At an actual zero the unit contribution of the Gamma detector forces a
product spike; the two pointwise upper bounds then separately force both
spikes and `m<=1/2+O(epsilon)`. The smooth product separation and tails
are taken with fixed derivative orders, and the cutoff profile derivatives
are uniformly controlled on the same annulus. This is not a separate
row-dependent truncation inside a moment.

The actual theorem `actual_supported_witness_family`, lines 17--30 of
`DetectorSupportedWitness.lean`, is more precise. Fix

\[
 0<d_{min}\le d_{max},\quad 0<\tau<d_{min}/2,
 \quad4\tau<d_{min}\eta,
\]
\[
 \epsilon>0,\quad0<e<1/1000,\quad0<\kappa\le1,
 \quad\eta\ge0,
 \quad288e+8\kappa+2\eta\le\epsilon/2,
\]

and a finite bin bound `I`. It gives `Z0` BEFORE `Z`, every
`d in [d_min,d_max]`, the row type, finite label type, characters, `a`, bin
index and cutoff. The character family must be nonprincipal at every label;
every natural modulus must be at most `Z^d`. The remaining hypotheses are

\[
 i\le I,\quad51/100<a\le1,
\]
\[
 M(3(i+1)Z^\tau)<a+2e,
 \qquad a\le M(3iZ^\tau),\qquad1\le t_*\le3/2.
\]

The result is a supported witness for every row. For application one takes
the row type to be the nonexceptional rows under consideration (or their
subtype); one does not assert nonprincipality or witnesses on the removed
principal rows. The source allows arbitrary finite labels, independently
of later arithmetic source labels.

`WitnessRows.lean` gives, with `U=Z^d`, a chosen label, an actual zero
`L(chi_label,rho)=0`, `rho.re>=a`, `|rho.im|<=3i Z^tau`, two dyadic
indices, and `|nu|<=U^(tau/(2d_max))`. The common witness frequency is

\[
 h_u=2\pi\nu_u-\Im\rho_u,
 \qquad |h_u|\le2\pi U^{\tau/(2d_{max})}+3iZ^\tau.
\]

The two polynomials in a witness share this frequency and `rho.re`.
Different rows need not share either value; the moment count uses its
rowwise/Sobolev bounds. None of these frequencies is identified with an
independent physical source height.

The support theorem gives exact tolerances

\[
 t_*-r-\epsilon\le m,
 \quad r\le t_*+\epsilon,
 \quad0\le m\le1/2+75\epsilon,
 \quad r\ge t_*-1/2-76\epsilon,
\]

and each spike loses `2 epsilon`. Within fixed dyadic indices the base
profiles are common: the inverse profile is the fixed positive annular
profile times its fixed cutoff at `U^t_*`; the plain profile is fixed.
Their real powers remain in `[0,1]` since actual zeros have real part at
most one. The finite smooth orders and polynomial height degree are
available before the later live height and scale variables.

For clarity about paper versus formal coordinates: the paper's coarse bin
description uses geometric heights `3^i T`; the actual theorem and PR15
density assembly use `3iT` and `3(i+1)T`. The latter exact buffered-bin
theorem is what this reconstruction uses. Both give finitely many bins;
their notations should not be mixed in a claimed literal application.

`DetectorZeros.exists_actual_buffered_bin`, lines 134--156, requires
`T>2`, `e>0`, an integer `n>0` with `49/100<=ne`, and returns
`1<=i<=n`, `b=51/100+ek`, the two strict upper maxima, the lower
maximum, and the zero-free buffered disk for every family label. The
fallback is `51/100`. For a counted zero with real part at least
`a>=33/40`, monotonicity yields `b>a-e`; hence with `e<1/1000`
the fallback cannot be selected. Maximum attainment supplies a genuine
zero. No artificial zero or floor population is used as a witness.

The underlying saturation theorem still uses only `51/100<=b<=1`.
It requires `(3+(3i+2)Z^tau)^4 <= (Z^d)^eta` and enough Fourier
allowance; the strict inequalities above imply both beyond a common
threshold. The Gamma detector's terminal and frequency tails have fixed
polynomial growth paid by sufficiently large fixed decay orders. Lowering
`b` to above `.824` stays inside all these closed real-power/strip ranges.
The small auxiliary `kappa` here is not the physical endpoint's capacity
parameter or the proposed split `k`.

## 6. The complementary analytic term is really small

Although D11 is stated directly for the determinant field, D7 helps calibrate what is and is not gained. Write e_chi,delta for the Dirichlet coefficients of E_delta. For delta in I,

    |e_chi,delta(n)| <=4 d_3(n)n^(-delta),
    sum_n |e_chi,delta(n)| n^(-4/5-epsilon)
                                      <=4 zeta(1+epsilon)^3. (D12)

Each product in E has three factors, the least of its shifts is at least delta, and |mu chi|<=1; this proves the first bound, including its multiplicity 1+2+1. Since delta>=1/5, it proves the second uniformly. Therefore its Gaussian physical field obeys

    |E_chi,delta^g(x)| <<_(epsilon,tau) x^(4/5+epsilon)   (D13)

on all positive x after adjusting a fixed constant; the left tail is better. This uses g_tau(v)<=C_(tau,sigma) exp(-sigma v), with sigma=4/5+epsilon, and the D12 weighted coefficient norm. All three signed complementary fields are paid together, not deleted singly by an unproved cancellation.

The cofactor coefficients are absolutely summable with weight r^(-beta), uniformly for delta in I, whenever beta>3/5. D8 and its majorant prove this because beta+2delta>1. Thus the inherited Mertens calibration beta=.8749 gives

    H_chi,delta(x) <<_(chi,epsilon,tau) x^(beta+epsilon)  (D14)

if the corresponding accepted character Mertens bound is supplied. For zeta the current proof supplies that calibration explicitly. D14 is a comparison, not an improvement. The limiting accepted exponent is beta_0=1-c_G=.8748866 with any fixed positive buffer. The required arithmetic gain below remains genuine.

statement:
## G228. The sharp depth of a low-omega-completed inverse column

Fix 0<beta<1. For 1<=T<=beta N and an integer k>=0 define

    F_(T,k)(d)=1_(d<=T OR omega(d)<=k),
    z=E^-T (chi(d) F_(T,k)(d))_d.

The first row of E^-T is mu(d), and multiplying by A_chi cancels chi against
its conjugate. Using sum_(d|a)mu(d)=1_(a=1) gives the exact identities

    z1=sum_(d in S_N)mu(d)chi(d) F_(T,k)(d),
    r(a)=sum_(d|a,d>T,omega(d)>k)mu(d).                     (228.1)

If omega(a)=k+1 and a>T, all proper divisors are included, so r(a)=mu(a).
For a>N/2 its cofactor observation is exactly R_N(a)=chi(a).
Let b_k be the product of the first k primes not dividing q, b_0=1, and put
alpha=max(beta,1/2). Every prime p in (alpha N/b_k,N/b_k] not dividing b_k q
gives a distinct actual coordinate a=b_k p with |R_N(a)r(a)|=1. Thus

    B_N(z)<=W_N(z),
    B_N(z)>=#{alpha N/b_k<p<=N/b_k : p prime, p not|b_k q}. (228.2)

The second line is an exact finite inequality, possibly zero for small N.
For fixed k, the ordinary prime number theorem gives the lower asymptotic
(1-alpha)N/(b_k log N). Correcting primes, semiprimes or any other fixed number
of omega layers has not made this absolute residual small at any exponent<1.

There is also a matching upper bound for growing depth. Set h=k+1,
H_N=sum_(m<=N)1/m and A_N=sum_(p<=N)1/p, including conductor primes if desired.
Taking the absolute value in (228.1) and exchanging the finite divisor sums,

    W_N(z)<=N H_N sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)>=h)1/d
           <=N H_N sum_(j>=h) A_N^j/j!
           <=N H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!.                     (228.3)

An unordered j-prime set occurs j! times in A_N^j. Admitting repeated primes
and products above N only enlarges the positive sum. The last inequality
uses (h+r)!>=h!r!. This pays EVERY residual coordinate and is uniform in T.

Ordinary PNT and partial summation give p_j~j log j and A_N=O(loglog N).
The [NIST reference](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records the prime asymptotics;
the consequences here are derived from them. Removing fixed q's finitely
many primes changes indices by a bounded amount, so log b_k~k log k as k grows.
If k~kappa log N/loglog N for fixed 0<kappa<1, then
b_k=N^(kappa+o(1)), while its largest prime is O(log N). The prime interval
in (228.2) lies above all these factors eventually; its endpoint is
N^(1-kappa+o(1)). PNT on a fixed-ratio interval, together with (228.3) and
log(h!)=h log h-h+O(log h), proves

    B_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)),  W_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)).      (228.4)

These are logarithmic exponents, uniform for 1<=T<=beta N, not fixed-k
logarithmic asymptotic formulas. If k=o(log N/loglog N), both exponents are1.

More generally fix ONE sequence k_N>=0 and ONE cutoff sequence
1<=T_N<=beta N for all sufficiently large N, independently of epsilon. For 0<gamma<1,

    B_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff W_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff liminf_N k_N loglog N/log N >= 1-gamma.             (228.5)

For sufficiency, bound the nonnegative tail in (228.3) at any smaller depth
a log N/loglog N with 0<a<1-gamma and then let a approach1-gamma according
to epsilon. For necessity, if the liminf is smaller, choose such an a above
it. Along infinitely many N the primorial is at most N^(a+o(1)), so (228.2)
has exponent at least1-a, contradicting a sufficiently small fixed epsilon.
No short-interval or growing-modulus prime theorem is used.

Equality in (228.5) is sufficient for the residual bill alone. It does not
pay z1. In fact, with D_N the number of omitted coefficients,

    z1=M_chi(N)-sum_(d in S_N,d>T,omega(d)>=h)mu(d)chi(d),
    D_N<=sum_(n<=N)binom(omega(n),h)
        =sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)=h)floor(N/d)
        <=N A_N^h/h!.                                    (228.6)

Once (228.5) holds, the every-epsilon exponent-gamma estimate on z1 is
equivalent to that on M_chi(N). The retained coordinate still carries the
arithmetic problem. At the c11 benchmark the residual's threshold is
liminf k_N loglog N/log N >= .1251459636; the full certificate is still open.

The lower bounds concern COMPLETE ABSOLUTE bills of this SPECIFIC column
family. They do not lower-bound the complete signed residual, Mertens sum,
any arbitrary approximant or a Gaussian energy. Higher residual layers need
not have a common sign: for k=1,T=11,a=30, r(30)=mu(15)+mu(30)=0.

The ancestry is the first-unpaid-layer argument in W43/[restricted research revision] and [restricted research revision]'s
fixed-layer circle obstruction. W43's Newton defect includes prime powers
and factorial multiplicities; at T=1,k=1 its order-two defect at pq is2,
where (228.1) is1. G78/G83-G85 already paid their own growing-order Gaussian
restoration, so that older obligation is not reopened. The new scoped result
is the cofactor certificate's exact depth threshold and its remaining z1
obligation, rather than a new generic lesson about truncation.

statement:
### T09b. Compact-profile triple-convolution criterion

Let \(P_r(y)\) be the exact [restricted research revision] Z13–Z15 triple convolution, including equal-element projection, fixed good sectors, and all cube/core overlaps. For \(5/6<a<1\), suppose
\[
\int_Y^{2Y}\int_1^2|P_r(y)|^2\,dr\,\frac{dy}{y}
\ll_\epsilon Y^{\,2(3-2a)-\epsilon} \tag{T09.3}
\]
for every sufficiently small dyadic \(Y\) and every \(\epsilon>0\). Then \(\zeta_K^S\), and hence \(\zeta\), is zero-free in \(\Re s>a\).

Take \(H=L^2([1,2],dr)\) and \(P(y)=(P_r(y))_r\). Cauchy gives, on \(\Re s\ge a+\delta\),
\[
\left\|\int_Y^{2Y}P(y)y^{2s-3}\frac{dy}{y}\right\|_H
\ll Y^{2(\Re s-a)-\epsilon/2}.
\]
Choose \(\epsilon<4\delta\). The Bochner Mellin integral is holomorphic; large \(y\) decays exponentially uniformly on the compact \(r\)-interval. Initially its exact value is
\[
J_\bullet(s)
\frac{L^S(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang})}{\zeta_K^S(s)},
\quad
J_r(s)=\int_0^\infty t^{2s}K_{1/3}(\kappa t)^2
K_{1/3}(\kappa rt)\,dt.
\]
For fixed \(\Re s>0\), \(r\mapsto J_r(s)\) is analytic on \(r>0\). [restricted research revision] Z16 proves a nonzero gamma-product limit for \(r^{1/3}J_r(s)\) as \(r\downarrow0\). Therefore \(J_r(s)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere on \([1,2]\); its \(H\)-norm is positive. The angular numerator is nonzero because \(3\Re s-3/2>1\). Continue the identity after multiplication by \((s-1)\zeta_K^S(s)\), and evaluate at a hypothetical zero. The right side is a nonzero vector, contradiction.

This removes the need for estimates uniform as \(r\to0\) or an individual zero-free kernel \(J_1\). It does not supply the arithmetic decay. At \(a=.87449\), the squared \(Y\)-exponent is \(2.50204\); \(N=Y^{-2}\) is a different scale.

**Sources:** BB R06–R07; [restricted research revision] V1–V10; [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18.
title: T09b. Compact-profile triple-convolution criterion

statement:
## 4. Exact two-factor completion with alternating restoration

Fix kappa0>0 with eta+kappa0<1, and let

\[
 Y=\left\lfloor X^{(1-\eta-\kappa_0)/2}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad \mu_{\le Y}(n)=\mu(n)\mathbf1_{n\le Y}.
 \tag{DP20}
\]

The elementary convolution identity

\[
 \mu=2\mu_{\le Y}-\mu_{\le Y}*\mu_{\le Y}*\mathbf1
                         +\mu_{>Y}*\mu_{>Y}*\mathbf1
 \tag{DP21}
\]

follows by expanding (mu-mu_leY)^2*1 and using mu*1=e_1. Convolve with kappa. The new unrestricted factor is the exact periodic sequence

\[
 b=\kappa*\mathbf1,
 \qquad b(\ell)=1-2\mathbf1_{2\mid\ell}=(-1)^{\ell+1}.
 \tag{DP22}
\]

Thus no new random sign or arbitrary bounded coefficient has been inserted. Its period-two mean is zero.

Extend V_delta as a smooth compactly supported function on the real line by zero on nonpositive arguments. For any fixed integer B>=2,

\[
 |\widehat V_\delta(\xi)|
 \le C_B(1+\delta|\xi|)^{-B}.
 \tag{DP23}
\]

This follows from the L1 bound on V_delta and the bound C_B delta^{-B} on the L1 norm of its B-th derivative, with delta<=delta0. Alternating Poisson summation, with the zero extension causing no endpoint terms, gives for 0<t<=delta

\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell\ge1}b(\ell)V_\delta(\ell t)\right|
 \le C_Bt^{-1}(t/\delta)^B.
 \tag{DP24}
\]

There is no zero dual frequency: the dual frequencies are the half-integers divided by t. DP23 sums absolutely over them for B>=2. This is the precise removal of the Type I main term.

On x in [e^{-1}X,2eX], the term 2*kappa*mu_leY has support n<=2Y, eventually outside the narrow profile. For d,e<=Y, t=de/x satisfies t/delta_X<=C X^{-kappa0}. Consequently, for every fixed B,

\[
 \sum_{d,e\le Y}
 \left|\sum_{\ell\ge1}b(\ell)V_{\delta_X}(\ell de/x)\right|
 \le C_B X\left(CX^{-\kappa_0}\right)^B(\log(2Y))^2.
 \tag{DP25}
\]

Choose B after the requested error power, before X and all labels. Combining DP21--25 proves for every R>0

\[
 \boxed{F_{A,\delta_X}(x)
 =\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
       \sum_{\ell\ge1}(-1)^{\ell+1}
                       V_{\delta_X}(\ell de/x)
       +O_R(X^{-R}).}
 \tag{DP26}
\]

This holds uniformly across the entire enlarged shell at its single frozen width. All sums are finite on the kernel support. Their exact ranges imply

\[
 d,e\ll X/Y\asymp X^{(1+\eta+\kappa_0)/2},
 \qquad \ell\ll X/Y^2\asymp X^{\eta+\kappa_0}.
 \tag{DP27}
\]

The floors cause only fixed constants for large X. Both original ordered factor placements remain; neither d and e nor any restoration labels are identified. Repeated primes, shared primes, squarefree zeros and alternating signs remain exactly those of DP26. No conductor, height or primitive-character bound is invoked.

## 6. Signed Taylor completion; proof of the negative main term

Take W=delta L. For |w|<=W and r<=R, the arguments in ([restricted research revision]) obey

    log x+w-log r >= (1-2delta)L > 2rho_1 L.

All derivatives up to order three of phi_t on this corridor satisfy

    |phi_t^(j)(a)|<=C_(rho_0,rho_1,j)L^(-1-j).       ([restricted research revision])

This follows directly by scaling a=L u, t=L rho; the scaled compact
corridor stays a fixed positive distance above u=2rho. The original
cutoff definition phi=0 below 2t is not analytically continued across
its boundary.

Globally phi_t(a), defined by ([restricted research revision]) and zero below 2t, is bounded by
C/t. Therefore the WHOLE discarded |w|>W portion of ([restricted research revision]), even after
the absolute harmonic core sum, is bounded by a fixed power of X,L
times `exp(-c_(delta,tau)L^2)`. This pays both Gaussian ends before
the Taylor argument and does not extend a rational denominator across
a pole or a support boundary.

Set A=log x+w and v=log r in the retained integral. Write

    phi_t(A-v)=phi_t(A)-v phi_t'(A)
                  +(v^2/2)phi_t''(A)+e_A(v).

On 0<=v<=log R, Taylor's theorem and ([restricted research revision]) give

    |e_A(v)|<=C v^3/L^4,
    |e_A'(v)|<=C v^2/L^4.                           ([restricted research revision])

It would be WRONG to sum this error using `sum |f(r)|/r`; that would
erase the useful cancellation. Apply Abel summation instead:

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)e_A(log r)/r
      = A_f(R)e_A(log R)/R
        -integral_1^R A_f(u)
             [e_A'(log u)-e_A(log u)]du/u^2.         ([restricted research revision])

Both the endpoint and the integral are `O_(beta)(L^(-4))`, since
`sup_(v>=0) exp(-(1-beta)v)v^3` and
`integral_0^infinity exp(-(1-beta)v)(v^2+v^3)dv` are finite.
This is uniform in w,rho in the retained corridor. This second signed
Abel step, not a positive Taylor estimate, is essential.

Complete the three polynomial moments before evaluating them. Equation
(C7) gives, for each fixed j=0,1,2,

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)(log r)^j/r|
       <= C_(beta,j) R^(beta-1)[1+(log R)^j].        ([restricted research revision])

After multiplication by phi_t^(j), their combined error is at most
`C R^(beta-1)/L`. Inserting the exact moments ([restricted research revision]), the j=0 and j=1
terms vanish and the surviving term is

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(A-log r)
       = C_f phi_t''(A)+O(L^(-4)+R^(beta-1)/L).      ([restricted research revision])

The positive 2C_f second moment meets the NEGATIVE curvature of the
actual two-prime density. There is no independent-sign premise and no
use of an unknown full energy in this cancellation.

Finally the tilted Gaussian has exact mass exp(tau/2) and finite first
absolute moment. Since log x=L+O(1) and phi_t''' is O(L^(-4)), ([restricted research revision])
and the already paid tails imply

    integral_(-W)^W exp(w)g(w)phi_t''(log x+w)dw
       =exp(tau/2)phi_t''(L)+O_tau(L^(-4)).          ([restricted research revision])

Direct differentiation gives

    phi_t''(A)=2log((A-t)/t)/A^3
                   -2/[A^2(A-t)]-1/[A(A-t)^2],
    phi_(rho L)''(L)=L^(-3)B(rho).                  ([restricted research revision])

Equations ([restricted research revision]), ([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision]) prove (C3), with every core, prime power,
prime diagonal, sharp endpoint and Gaussian end accounted for.

Here is the complete error ledger, before convenient absorption:

| Source | Uniform field cost |
| --- | --- |
| Actual/completed source above U<z^3 | O_A(X^(-A)) for any fixed A |
| All signed cores r>R | O(X^(1-kappa)L) |
| Prime-pair p=q diagonal | O(X/z) |
| Both PNT replacements, N=8 fixed | O(X/L^6) |
| Full omitted tilted-Gaussian ends | O_A(X^(-A)) |
| Signed Taylor remainder | O(X/L^4) |
| Three signed moment completions | O(X^(1-kappa)/L) |
| Frozen-shell/tilted-Gaussian replacement | O(X/L^4) |

All constants are allowed to depend on the fixed compact rho interval,
tau,beta and the fixed accepted PNT constant. This ledger contains no
growing-order estimate or unsupported limit interchange.

## 8. Exact whole-rectangle proof and feedback

On the full closed rectangle 0<=delta<=3/4, 0<=p<=1/2 put

    D=3-p-2p/(3kappa_*), P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa_*)),
    V=5/6-delta, J=VD+delta P,
    R=1-delta+delta P V/(2J), q=delta p.

V>=1/12, D>=D(1/2), P>=0 and J>=924595/5398056>1/10. The complete original w-inversion yields, for d>=1/2>y,

    G(d,c)=(1+delta)/2+13h/75-y/2-ell/2+ell delta p
      +d(1/4+3R/4-17/50)-delta p(2y-d)/(2c).

Below 1/2 the old term is -q min(d,2y-d)/(12kappa_*). Only the physical selection term changes with C; R stays the original detector.

For fixed d,c and saving v the positive-denominator numerator is

    N=J[theta-v-(1+delta)/2-13h/75+y/2+ell/2-ell delta p
          -d(1/4-17/50)+delta p(2y-d)/(2c)]
       -(3d/4)[(1-delta)J+delta P V/2].
