## G183. Literal smaller signed core and complete return

Import the [[private research revision] source and complements](../[private research revision]/square-source-integration.md)
exactly. Fix an ordinary chi modulo q and an unramified prime p. Put
a=lambda chi, h=chi, s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, zero off squares, and

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g=a*a*b0.                           (G183.1)

Here a*h=s and a is completely multiplicative, including its natural
zeros. The p^2 coefficient is -p chi(p)^2. The two complete cofactors

    b0(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r))

are bounded periodic sequences of mean zero, with periods p^3q,pq.
The exact Euler series is

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).

For 3/4<=gamma<1 retain the accepted choices

    L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4),
    B(n)=min(L,X^6/(6000p^3q n^5)),
    U(n)=B(n)^tau, V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau),
    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau))<=(11gamma-3)/8.             (G183.2)

Tau and all cuts are fixed before live x. The exact ordered decomposition
c=Q_U+Q_V-S_tau+R_tau still holds, with both full short slots, the whole
small-double source and the long-long source. No cutoff is differentiated.

In the finite core L<n<=M impose the new condition gcd(d,e)<=G, where
G=X^(1-gamma), on the original long-long tuples. Denote the resulting
full signed shell source by T_small. Its discarded part has EXACT mask

    1_(L<del<=M)1_(d>U(del))1_(e>V(del))

in G182 with the strict gcd>G condition. For b=3/2,k=6 its norm costs
X^(gamma+epsilon), since the second exponent is
1/4+gamma/2<=gamma. All composite common factors, shared cofactors,
squareful outputs, original orders and natural zeros remain accounted for.

The difference C-T_small also includes both old short sources, minus the
full small-double source, the prefix n<=L and the ENTIRE damped high
tail n>M. Their accepted [private research revision] payments remain applicable BEFORE
the gcd restriction. In particular no periodic-mean argument is reapplied
after a new mask that might break it. Norm triangle gives

    ||C-T_small||_(1,2) <<X^(gamma+epsilon).                (G183.3)

The retained merged coefficient is exactly

    sum_(m l=n)a(m)b0(l)
       #{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U(n),e>V(n),gcd(d,e)<=G}.

The merge a(d)a(e)=a(de) uses Liouville complete multiplicativity. It
does not license an unrestricted Mobius merge.

The prior absolute finite-core price required G>=X^((3/2)(1-gamma));
G182 permits G=X^(1-gamma). At the conditional quarter target the
threshold changes from X^(3/8) to X^(1/4), and at1/6 from X^(1/4)
to X^(1/6). At the current gamma11 the exponent is exactly c11.
These describe paid complementary regions, not attained new values of c.

OPEN-LCG is the remaining full signed L1 bound for T_small by
X^(gamma+epsilon), for every epsilon and all sufficiently large dyadic
X, for each fixed ordinary character and each of a fixed covering pair
of unramified primes. One gamma<gamma11 is chosen before characters
and candidate zeros. Tau may vary with epsilon,chi,p,X inside the
allowed corridor, but stays fixed on each real shell. Constants and
thresholds may depend on the fixed data. L2 at that exponent suffices.
A selected cell, sampled x, finite height range or fixed epsilon loss
does not meet this input.

By (G183.3), this hypothesis is equivalent to the corresponding full L1
bound for the FIXED complete source C. It is not claimed equivalent to
zero exclusion. The inherited complete Mellin identity is

    H_p(z)=A0(z)D_c(z)+E_p(z),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6,
    E_p holomorphic on Re z>1/2.                           (G183.4)

The all-shell bound gives holomorphy of H_p on Re z>gamma. The identity
uses C, not the shell-dependent core. A0 has no zero there, J_p vanishes
only on Re z=1/2, and L(2z,chi^2) is finite and nonzero on Re z>1/2.
P_p zeros are on Re z=1. Two distinct fixed primes cannot have a common
P zero at nonzero height; for nonprincipal chi choose one with chi(p)!=1
to cover height zero. The principal pole at1 is retained as the stated
exception. This gives the conditional ordinary-character zero-exclusion
return at every finite height, with no height-uniform or growing-q claim.

The actual coefficient variance still gives only ||C||_2<<X. The prior
fixed logarithmic bound has squared norm X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D)
for every fixed D. Transfer to T_small retains the extra complementary
cost. Neither result supplies any fixed power below1. The entire
gcd-one signed source remains present and unproved.

## 5. Full conditional ordinary-character return

Fix tau>0, 0<theta<1 and e before scale or character selection. Let H=floor(X^theta). The missing arithmetic hypothesis is, for every fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi and every epsilon>0,

    E_{mu*chi}(X,H) <<_{epsilon,chi,tau} X^(e+epsilon)     (A)

for all sufficiently large dyadic X. Here mu*chi denotes the pointwise sequence mu(n)chi(n), not Dirichlet convolution. Its energy must have exactly the full support and weight in Section 4. Constants and the scale threshold may depend on the fixed character. A universal conductor constant is not needed for the resulting qualitative per-character assertion, but the same theta,e must be valid for every character being asserted.

For large X the floor gives H comparable to X^theta. Applying (B) yields, with every epsilon loss,

    F_{mu*chi}(x) << x^(gamma+epsilon),
    gamma = max(theta, (1-theta+e)/2).

Dyadic shells cover every x>=1. The factor 1/2 on the energy accuracy exponent is harmless because (A) holds for every epsilon. The O(H) replacement cost is part of gamma, not discarded. First improvement over b6 requires theta<b6 and

    e < 2b6-1+theta = .749722+theta.

For the literal ordinary-character sequence, absolute Euler products in Re(s)>1 identify its Dirichlet series with 1/L(s,chi). Direct absolute interchange gives

    integral_0^infinity F_{mu*chi}(x) x^(-s) dx/x
       = exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi),      Re(s)>1.

At x->0, bounded coefficients give O_A(x^A) for arbitrarily large A. At infinity, the returned bound with arbitrarily small epsilon makes the integral holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly on compact subsets, including its differentiated integrals. This supplies all imaginary heights. The nonvanishing entire Gaussian factor means the reciprocal L-function cannot have a pole there. Equivalently, after meromorphic continuation, L has no zero in this half-plane away from its principal pole. Nonprincipal s=1 is included; the principal pole at s=1 corresponds to a zero of the reciprocal and is compatible with the identity. The external theorem's explicit principal-(chi=1,s=1) exclusion should therefore remain.

This is an ordinary Dirichlet return for all positive moduli if (A) is supplied separately for all their characters. It is not a Hecke or number-field theorem. The exact external root-LFunction definition and its ordinary-function identification remain an external handoff obligation; they were not proved here. There is no moving Gaussian transform: the growing H occurs only in an estimate of the fixed F. No actual-supremum feedback is needed for this replacement route. Its source estimate directly implies the asserted conditional strip.

The architecture does not import any PR9/PR15 local moment bound in order to prove (A). Accordingly it does not constitute a cheaper version of the old shortening, 29-family/109-child, height, Euler-shift, 9a or physical K^(5/6) ledger. If an eventual proof of (A) uses that route, those costs must be paid in that proof. This review changes none of the accepted old source assumptions, and discharges none of their remaining import-independence or external kernel obligations.

# Post52 Sol High 01: paid heads for a moving rough detector, and an exact finite-sieve trap

## Current checkpoint and evidence class



The mathematical output is two source-specific developments, not an increased constant:

1. **D04:** moving *actual f3* rough-field estimates are required only on cofactor scales U>=X^delta. The lower head is paid at sigma+delta(1-sigma), with complete signs, powers and fixed-character zero extensions. The source moment is open.
2. **D33:** exact finite-sieve correlations and rapid Gaussian cancellation from prime 2. This model has zeta in the numerator; its omitted rough correction restores the full hard field. Marginal-only hidden signs can also attain the opposite coherent extremum. This is a restricted theorem/failure.

No OPEN-F3/OPEN-GC/H estimate, endpoint gain, formalization, kernel replay or literature priority is established. The accepted written analytic incumbent is c4=25027/200000, separately from the old c0 three-kernel evidence. The smallest showcased conditional improvement is c=313/2500=.1252; it is NOT proved.

## Frozen design, screen and first tests

The 60 seeds preceded detailed history. `seeds.md` SHA-256 **9020e85ea4553808943823b8566244f272a1a4adf6c80c80ec52eefeb0679300**, 16366 bytes. Six groups of ten: two uncapped, two p<.03, two p<.001. Labels remain uncalibrated typicality. No extras or matched comparison.

The protocol, [private research revision] decision, current proof, attempt index and relevant actual sources were then read. `selection.json` freezes the screen; its exclusions are scoped, not global impossibility verdicts.

Reservations: strongest bridges S04/S15, highest reach S45/S51, most different S31. Sequential literal-pool draws: S33/S37 at p<.03, S54/S57 at p<.001, wildcard S06. Every numerically qualifying unreserved screened card from ALL prompt groups entered each pool. In particular the .03 draws included the remaining .001 cards. Already selected IDs were removed; no group was removed as a group. No reroll or outcome-based relabel occurred.

`selection.json` SHA-256 **2ed54bc31b66037b5c65e5cedc8e15f0afff034f04e6f265a86984df3c39b18e**. Pools, in draw order:

| Draw | Count | Chosen | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|---|
| rare03_1 | 27 | S33 | 5514446314bcd2e8fb51f2a96eca75e1455fd28786e43a212a75d72be57eb143 |
| rare03_2 | 26 | S37 | e029bd4d23d7ed435eaf98dfe663f389593dfebba3410fd465703384b43d7509 |
| rare001_1 | 15 | S54 | 83984d51c9ffed5977fe1f6a90195933874f4b15b2f4fcde12a07cc3c56645e0 |
| rare001_2 | 14 | S57 | 15185ce5659fb3181505d297f23908054a3bb2d9bc5f8440bb306121af30340c |
| wildcard | 40 | S06 | 38a9fe705cc2a531ba5471b02e48fe53f82fc1ac9afe4b8e4d74ae7be72e0a37 |

Root received seeds before history development; root and the retained Astra critic received selections before deep outcomes. Root owns Sol-then-Astra review, which is not yet claimed completed.

### All ten exact first tests

**S04: small-prime conditioning.** For finite P contained in primes>=5, let f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) and f_P(n)=f(n)1_(gcd(n,product P)=1). The exact Dirichlet-convolution multiplier that reconstructs f from f_P has local series 1-z-z^2-z^3-..., not 1-z. Thus every eliminated prime power is retained. Its positive reconstruction price is product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)^-1. A moving P is affordable in a strict subpower range, but its source estimate must keep the parent cutoff frozen on cofactor shells. **Pass as a source-specific conditional bridge; developed D04.**

**S15: central covariance plus absolute complement.** Current-proof G23 already proves the full actual-f3 far-pair bound X^(2-r^2/(4tau)+o(1)) outside |log(n/m)|<=r sqrt(log X). To pay this below a target 2gamma-eta, choose r^2>=4tau(2-2gamma+eta). The true diagonal is O(X). This merely specializes G23; central signed energy is still open, and no H saving can be added. **Duplicate quantitative split, not a new survivor.**

**S45: weak negative Sobolev proposal.** For the finite actual coefficient measure nu=sum c(n)delta_(log(n/X)), r>1/2 gives

    ||g_tau*nu||_(L2(R))^2
       <= M_(tau,r) ||nu||_(H^-r(R))^2,
    M_(tau,r)=sup_t exp(-tau*t^2)(1+t^2)^r < infinity.

This follows directly from Fourier multipliers. The proposed rational frequency weight is a *stronger sufficient all-height estimate* than the Gaussian weight; it is not a weakening of the needed arithmetic cancellation. It also controls the full line, whereas the original energy is shell-local. A fixed smoothing or primitive multiplier nonzero at s=rho does not change the growth exponent of an e^(rho u) mode. **Valid conditional organization, existing D-GREEN/A-GRAPH ancestry; no new arithmetic norm or relaxed input. Parked after first test.**

**S51: Koszul detector.** Contraction d by the all-one covector and exterior multiplication h by a chosen generator obey dh+hd=I: the augmented complex is acyclic. A sharp mask introduces [d,P]. W37 T15/D28 already supply this obstruction and a paid-boundary repair; finite Euler zeros cannot replace the infinite reciprocal limit. **Duplicate failure.**

**S31: divisor Stokes boundary.** For n=pq with distinct primes p,q<=Y<pq, sum_(d|n,d<=Y)mu(d)=1-1-1=-1. The full Boolean rectangle adds mu(pq)=+1 and sums to zero. Truncation leaves exactly the omitted top face. For the actual Gaussian d,e,ell source W37 D28 supplies the stronger fixed-total-product boundary identity, including the masks. **Exact boundary failure duplicates U-PRIME-CHAIN/W37; no new saving.**

**S33: finite marginal LP.** Retain the actual local sign (-1)^(1_(p|n)), including p=2 and excluding p=3. Chinese-remainder independence on one complete period gives exact pair correlations, but the single-field average is identically zero because of prime 2. Gaussian smoothing makes that periodic field rapidly small. The full f3 field is not that finite local model. **Pass as a restricted source-specific calculation and failure diagnosis; developed D33.**

**S37: complex saddle contour.** For 0<r<1, averaging log|1-r exp(it log p)| over its full height period gives zero, by the absolutely convergent logarithmic series. A fixed imaginary shift leaves this average unchanged. Thus avoiding the finite Euler factor's zeros alone cannot provide a strictly smaller modulus at all heights, even in the one-prime test. An adaptive contour would still need its exact source integral, Jacobian, growth and residue payments. **Scoped failed free-contour gain; broader arithmetic saddle estimates remain untested.**

**S54: smallest missing-prime involution.** The cut top face from S31 survives. A source-compatible pivot is fixed as a function of d*ell and preserves de*ell. W37 D28.6 permits ANY odd-prime pivot, already including “smallest.” **Duplicate boundary mechanism.**

**S57: arithmetic differential forms.** Each d log(1-chi(p)p^-s) is a multiple of ds, so its wedge with another is zero. Independent formal prime coordinates require a new paid diagonal readout. **Scalar wedge fails; broader multivariable constructions remain open.**

**S06: contour index.** B_a(z)=(z-a)/(1-a z), 0<a<1, has a zero, B_a(1)=1 and |B_a|=1 on the whole circle. Winding one coexists with the constant function's boundary L2 norm. Contour detection still needs its reciprocal/background and all edges (F22). **Normalized toy failure, not a native L-function bound.**

Two developments: rare D33's restricted result and D04's high-ceiling return. The selected complex/Sobolev shortcuts stopped after their decisive tests.

## D04. Moving rough f3 detector with a paid cofactor head

### D04.1 Exact object, powers and signs

Fix tau>0 and an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its literal extension chi(n)=0 when gcd(n,q)>1. Constants may depend on this fixed chi; no growing-conductor statement is intended. Define

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    F_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) f(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

The zeta case is chi=1. This is the exact existing f3 field when chi=1; it is not a squarefree surrogate. For a finite prime set P contained in {p>=5:p does not divide q}, define

    f_(P,chi)(n)=f(n)chi(n)1_(gcd(n,product P)=1),
    V_(P,chi)(x)=sum_n f_(P,chi)(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    a_(P,chi)(r)=f(r)chi(r)1_(every prime divisor of r lies in P),
    a_(P,chi)(1)=1.

Unique decomposition n=r v into its FULL P-smooth part r and P-rough part v proves

    f(n)chi(n)=sum_(r|n) a_(P,chi)(r)f_(P,chi)(n/r),
    F_chi(x)=sum_(r P-smooth) a_(P,chi)(r)V_(P,chi)(x/r).   (D04.1)

Only one term is nonzero in the coefficient convolution, but all r occur in the field sum. At a deleted prime the local a-series is

    1-sum_(v>=1)chi(p)^v z^v=(1-2chi(p)z)/(1-chi(p)z).

Repeated powers have coefficient -chi(p)^v, not zero. This is the important difference from the older mu-based D35, whose reconstruction has finite squarefree support. Replacing this factor by 1-chi(p)z would be incorrect.

For any sigma>0 its absolute weighted mass is exactly

    W_P(sigma)=sum_r |a_(P,chi)(r)|r^-sigma
              =product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)^-1.           (D04.2)

The field identity is absolutely justified: use the Gaussian positive integer sum and, for example, sigma>1 in (D04.2). Local convergence, derivatives and shell rearrangements then follow by Gaussian decay. It is an equality of the actual signed field, not domination by a favorable subfamily.

### D04.2 The coarsest sufficient moving-source hypothesis used here

Fix 1/2<gamma<1, 0<sigma<gamma, A>0 and 0<delta<1 such that

    A(1-sigma)<1,
    q_head:=sigma+delta(1-sigma)<gamma.                  (D04.3)

For every large dyadic X, put z_X=(log X)^A and

    P_X={p prime:5<=p<=z_X, p does not divide q}.

This parent X and P_X stay frozen while the argument x varies over [X,2X] and while every cofactor shell is estimated. Assume, for every epsilon>0,

    ||V_(P_X,chi)||_(L2([U,2U],dx/x))
       <= C_epsilon U^(gamma+epsilon)
    for ALL real U with X^delta<=U<=X,                  (OPEN-D04)

with constants independent of X,U. This includes the complete norm of the signed rough source; it is not a norm of only primes or one rough depth. No conclusion is drawn from V_(P_U,chi) at its own changing cutoff. The latter is a different field and is not the premise.

**Conditional return theorem.** OPEN-D04 and (D04.3) imply, for every epsilon>0,

    ||F_chi||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (D04.4)

Proof of the price: for fixed 0<sigma<1, p>=5 implies

    log W_(P_X)(sigma)
       <= C_sigma sum_(p<=z_X) p^-sigma
       <= C'_sigma z_X^(1-sigma)
       =O((log X)^(A(1-sigma)))=o(log X).               (D04.5)

Comparison with ALL integers suffices; no prime-distribution estimate, calibrated random sign or external cancellation claim enters. Thus W=X^o(1), uniformly in the parent X.

Split (D04.1) at R=X^(1-delta), without rounding ambiguity: short r satisfy r<=R, long r satisfy r>R. For r<=R the exact real cofactor shell U=X/r lies in [X^delta,X]. Minkowski and OPEN-D04 give

    ||sum_(r<=R) a(r)V(./r)||_[X,2X]
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)
                       sum_(r<=R)|a(r)|r^(-gamma-epsilon)
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) W_(P_X)(sigma).

The last inequality uses gamma+epsilon>sigma and r>=1. For each arbitrarily small output epsilon, apply the premise with a smaller epsilon and absorb (D04.5).

For r>R, t=x/r<=2X^delta. The positive Gaussian integer sum satisfies

    sum_(n>=1)g_tau(log(n/t)) <<_tau t, t>=1,
    sum_(n>=1)g_tau(log(n/t)) <<_(tau,sigma) t^sigma, 0<t<1.

For the first bound compare the positive profile with its integral and bounded maximum; integral equals t exp(tau/2). For the second use Gaussian left-tail decay (or multiply by t^-sigma and take the bounded supremum on (0,1]). Consequently, uniformly for 0<t<=2X^delta,

    |V_(P_X,chi)(t)|
       <= C_(tau,sigma) X^(delta(1-sigma)) t^sigma.

This estimate uses ONLY coefficient modulus <=1 and includes every small-scale term and every character zero. Hence the entire long-r head is bounded pointwise by

    C X^(delta(1-sigma)) x^sigma
                  sum_(r>R)|a(r)|r^-sigma
       <= X^(q_head+o(1)).                              (D04.6)

The shell has fixed logarithmic length, so this also bounds its L2 norm. Equation (D04.3) gives a fixed positive margin below gamma. Norm triangle proves (D04.4). If the full energy is expanded afterwards, every r,r' interaction is retained; the triangle proof has already paid both mixed terms and the head square. No positivity deletion, inherited masked moment, height truncation, projector commutation or baseline-beta scalar shortcut is needed.

This coarse head price is not optimal or an equality impossibility. It removes the bounded-x source hypothesis at the stated delta/sigma cost.

### D04.3 Complete zero-exclusion return for each fixed ordinary character

Initially for Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    Mellin(F_chi)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) D_chi(s),
    D_chi(s)=sum_n f(n)chi(n)n^-s=H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    H_(chi,p)(s)=(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2, p!=3,
    H_(chi,3)(s)=(1-chi(3)3^-s)^-2.                    (D04.7)

At p|q these are literally 1. At p>=5 the factors begin at degree two and their Euler product converges absolutely, locally uniformly on Re s>1/2. Their numerators have zeros only on Re s=log_p 2<1/2 when chi(p)!=0; denominators only on Re s=0. Prime 2 is separate: its possible numerator zeros lie on Re s=1. Prime 3 has no numerator. Thus H_chi is holomorphic and nonzero throughout 1/2<Re s<1. This accounts for all exceptional local factors instead of discarding them.

The Gaussian left tail is paid uniformly by the bounded coefficient majorant. Equation (D04.4), dyadic Cauchy-Schwarz and summation show that the Mellin integral is holomorphic on Re s>gamma.        =1+sum_(v>=1)2^(v-1)chi(p)^v z^v.

### D33.1 Actual local signs and their complete-period law

    Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2/p)=0,
    Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)e_P(n+h)
       =product_(p in P) c_p(h),
    c_p(h)=1 if p|h; c_p(h)=1-4/p otherwise.            (D33.1)

For p not dividing h exactly the two distinct residues n=0,-h contribute -1 and the other p-2 contribute +1; for p|h both signs are equal at each residue. This proves the formula with no heuristic independence of actual integers outside the completed period. The p=2 factor is -1 for odd h and +1 for even h. The natural p=3 exemption is literal. Both prime powers and h=0 are included.

For P={2,5,7}, all 70 shifts were checked exactly with rational arithmetic. This is an arithmetic periodic identity, not a bound for f3(n)f3(n+h): multiplying the true rough-prime factors before averaging changes the measure and destroys the completed-period factorization.

The marginal-only optimization has a complementary decisive test. Keep every small-prime divisibility pattern fixed, but permit a free hidden rough sign r(n) in {+1,-1}.                               |x(j-k/Q)|^-m

The reindexing r=Qj-k runs over nonzero integers not divisible by Q; their absolute m-series is at most 2zeta(m). The constant is independent of Q,P,x. No arbitrary ell-dependent mask is inserted into G9; this is direct Poisson on the stated periodic coefficient sequence.

All rough valuations, signs and coefficient interactions remain in E_P. Its absolute bound is merely O_tau(x), since |r_P-1|<=2. There is no separately proved power cancellation. With the moving sieve in (D33.3), for any fixed gamma>0 and every epsilon, the norm bound

## 4. The untruncated completion error

### 4.1 Small-radical bound

For every delta>0,

    C_delta := sum_{n>=1} n^(-delta)/r(n)
      = (1-2^(-delta))^(-1)(1-3^(-delta))^(-1)
          product_{p>=5}
             (1 + p^(-1-delta)/(1-p^(-delta)))
      < infinity.                                       (4.1)

For sufficiently large p the denominator is at least 1/2, so the
prime contribution is O_delta(p^(-1-delta)), a summable series.
The finitely many remaining factors are finite and positive.
This proves (4.1) without any uniformity as delta tends to zero.

Using 1_{r(n)<=Y}<=Y/r(n) and the exact Gaussian supremum,

    g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_{delta,tau} x^delta n^(-delta),

gives, uniformly for every x>0 and every integer Y>=1,

    |U_Y(x)| <= C_{delta,tau} C_delta Y x^delta.           (4.2)

This includes all n, however large relative to x, and all powers
of 2 or 3. There is no finite-height replacement hidden in (4.2).

### 4.2 Both-short bound under the fixed pair mask

Extend h(t)=g_tau(log t) for t>0 by h(t)=0 for t<=0.
The Gaussian beats every power at both t=0 and t=infinity after
any fixed number of derivatives, so h is Schwartz and flat at zero.
For Fourier transform hhat(xi)=integral_R h(t)exp(-2 pi i t xi)dt,
Poisson summation with the alternating character gives

    S_tau(y) = -y sum_{k in Z} hhat(y(k+1/2)).             (4.3)

There is no zero frequency. For each fixed M>1, Schwartz decay
and summability of |k+1/2|^(-M) imply

    |S_tau(y)| <= C_{M,tau} y^(1-M),       y>=1.

Equivalently, for each fixed A>0,

    |S_tau(y)| <= C_{A,tau} y^(-A),        y>=1.           (4.4)

Now take X>=1, x in [X,2X], theta=.495 and
Y=Y_X=floor(X^theta). Then

    x/(de) >= X/Y^2 >= X^(.01) >= 1

for d,e<=Y. Taking absolute values only after completing each
alternating l-sum yields

    |B_Y(x)| <= C_{A,tau} Y^2 (X/Y^2)^(-A)
             <= C_{A,tau} X^(.99-.01 A).                 (4.5)

The pair mask (d,e)=1, (de,6)=1 and the Möbius signs are fixed
independently of l, so this argument is valid under that mask.
It does not assert inheritance under an arbitrary l-dependent mask.
For any prescribed N>0, choose A>=100(N+.99); then

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|B_{Y_X}(x)| <<_{N,tau} X^(-N).        (4.6)

### 4.3 Error in the required norm

For delta>0 and N>0, equations (3.2), (4.2) and (4.6) give

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|F_6(x)-R_{6,Y_X}(x)|
       <<_{delta,N,tau} X^(.495+delta) + X^(-N).         (4.7)

The same estimate holds for the L2(dx/x) norm on that shell, up
to the fixed factor sqrt(log 2). For every gamma>=1/2, choose
0<delta<gamma-.495. The error is then O(X^rho) for a fixed
rho=.495+delta<gamma. No estimate for R at a transported or
nonintegral cutoff is needed.

## 4. What the first row Poisson actually does

This section concerns the concrete no-slot, coprime squarefree pair l,l' in S1. It records the exact coefficient change, rather than claiming an estimate for every pair of the full source.

Write a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))*gamma_2(n) as in PR9 B3.1. On good squarefree n, finite Parseval and PR9 B1.10 imply

    gamma_1(n)=mu(n)G(n)*conjugate(a0(n)).            (S7)

The source's G is the fixed ray function, distinct from the two-variable Gauss sum. To check S7, use gamma_1(n)gamma_2(n)=mu(n)alpha(n)G(n), and |gamma_2(n)|=1. Thus the transformed complete column contains

    A_R(n)gamma_1(n)
      =G(n)conjugate(a0(n))*mu(n)A_R(n).             (S8)

Since n is squarefree, mu(n)mu(d)=mu(n/d) for d|n, so

    mu(n)A_R(n)=sum_(m|n) mu(m)V(Nn/(Nm R))
              =-sum_(m|n) mu(m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].    (S9)

The last identity uses n!=1. The cofactor m in its final expression satisfies Nm<Nn/R. Equations S8--S9 move the signed Mobius weight from the original inverse divisor to this complementary cofactor. They preserve the entire signed divisor sum. Applying them independently on both sides of the ordered square retains both cofactors; neither was averaged away.

For orientation, the literal clean row kernel before this coefficient substitution is obtained from PR9 B3.5/B3.52. With q=ll', a compact radial Phi and all six element units, the unrestricted sixth-free row kernel is

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') * sum_b mu(b)/(Nb)^6 1_((b,ll')=1)
       * R(l,l') sum_h Gcal(l,h) conjugate(Gcal(l',-h))
                      F Phi(U Nh/((Nb)^6 Nl Nl')).  (S10)

The b sum is the exact sixth-free projector: retain its finite original range Nb<=(C_Phi U)^(1/6). Nonprincipal zero frequency vanishes. For squarefree l, Gcal(l,h)=gamma_1(l)*conjugate(chi_l(h)); in particular all frequencies sharing a conductor prime are zero. The -h and R(l,l') in S10 are retained; they cannot be replaced by unsigned absolute Gauss factors. Formula S10 is stated for the clean pair with no additional row ray restriction. Fixed ray restrictions require their complete finite expansion, including their b^6 phase. Natural fixed holes require the full d|rad(E) projector and its scale U/((Nb)^6 Nd). Removing the eligible finite fixed-inducing free rows means subtracting their actual finite kernel sum. These operations are exactly the retained [restricted research revision] contract; they are not implicit deletions from S10.

The prefactor is U/sqrt(Nl Nl'), not U/(Nl Nl'). It is the residue-class Poisson factor U/(Nl Nl') multiplied by the two unnormalized Gauss factors. Thus, for Nl,Nl' comparable to L, the dual scale is L^2/U. In the present first high-conductor range L=U^(4/3), that scale is U^(5/3). Merely retaining a high relative conductor therefore does not shorten the first frequency below the column scale.

S10 is an exact transform for this pair class. Its application to the full residual still requires the complete common-support allocation, all valuations, both physical coprimality projectors where relevant, slots, unequal roots/dyads and every outside scalar. That complete transformation was not finished before the stop.

statement:
## Theorem B: exact complete offset-averaged short-window return

Let |a(n)|<=1 for positive integers, and extend a(n)=0 for n<=0. Fix tau>0, X>=1, and integer H>=1. Define

  B_H(k)=sum_{k-H<n<=k}a(n),
  w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4*tau)),
  E_a(X,H)=(1/H)sum_{k>=1}|B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

The sum includes every positive endpoint and all Gaussian tails. It is finite by the Gaussian decay; it is neither a projected rank nor an energy restricted to selected lag terms. Put ell=log2 and

  K_tau=exp(ell^2/(3*tau))
     *[exp(tau/3+4*ell/3)/sqrt(3*pi*tau)+1/(pi*tau)].

Then the complete uniform return is

  sup_{X<=x<=2X}|F_a(x)|
    <= sqrt(K_tau*(X/H+1)*E_a(X,H))+2H*g_tau(0).       (B)

### B1. Proof with all offsets, tails, and mixed terms

For each r in{1,...,H}, partition the integer line into blocks(k-H,k] whose positive right endpoints k are congruent to r modulo H, and use the zero extension on the initial partial block. Set

  V_r(x)=sum_{k>=1,k congruent r mod H} B_H(k)g_tau(log(k/x)).

The total variation of t -> g_tau(log(t/x)) on(0,infinity) is2g_tau(0). On one block, replacing each value at n by its right endpoint value costs at most H times the variation on that block. Summing disjoint blocks proves

  |F_a(x)-V_r(x)|<=2H*g_tau(0)

uniformly in x. This pays the complete replacement error, including the first block and both infinite tails; no summatory cancellation was used.

For u=log(x/X) in[0,ell] and v=log(k/X), the Cauchy weight quotient is

  g_tau(v-u)^2 / exp(-v^2/(4*tau))
    =(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp(-3v^2/(4*tau)+2uv/tau-u^2/tau).

As a function of t=k/X this is positive and unimodal. Its integral over t>0 equals

  exp(tau/3+4u/3+u^2/(3*tau))/sqrt(3*pi*tau),

and its supremum is exp(u^2/(3*tau))/(2*pi*tau). A positive unimodal function sampled on a grid of spacing H/X has sum at most(X/H) times its integral plus twice its supremum: split at the maximum and compare each monotone tail with adjacent grid integrals. Thus the quotient sum on every offset grid is at most K_tau*(X/H+1).

Writing E_r=sum_{k congruent r}|B_H(k)|^2w_X(k), Cauchy gives |V_r(x)|<=sqrt(K_tau*(X/H+1)*E_r). Average the identity F_a=V_r+error over all r and apply Jensen to sqrt(E_r). Since H^(-1)sum_r E_r=E_a, inequality(B) follows. This proves a supremum, so the log-shell L2 norm is also at most sqrt(log2) times its right side. No omitted cross terms are estimated as though positive.

For clarity the EXACT arithmetic content of E is

  E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_{|h|<H}
    sum_{n>=max(1,1-h)} a(n)conjugate(a(n+h))
    *sum_{j=max(0,h)}^{min(H-1,H-1+h)}w_X(n+j).       (L)

Indeed B_H(k)=sum_{j=0}^{H-1}a(k-j); write n=k-j and h=j-l in its square. All sums converge absolutely. Formula(L) includes every diagonal, both signs of every lag, and the exact moving weight. Replacing the inner weight by(H-|h|)w_X(n) would introduce an error not used or hidden here. A bounded exact check accompanies the report solely to guard these indices, not to certify the analytic theorem.

### B2. Exact arithmetic estimate needed for a gain

Choose theta in(0,1), H=floor(X^theta), and suppose that for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

  E_{mu*chi}(X,H) <<_{epsilon,chi,tau} X^(e+epsilon).   (A)

Then(B), after absorbing floors, yields the complete Gaussian estimate with every epsilon loss and limiting exponent

  gamma=max(theta,(1-theta+e)/2).

For a strict first gain over b6=.874861 it suffices that theta<b6 and

  e<2*b6-1+theta=.749722+theta.

At theta=.26, the limiting current threshold is e<1.009722. To reach gamma=.87449, c=.12551, it suffices to prove e=1.00898 with every epsilon loss. This is the upstream source analogue of the .000742 gap between the .249722 baseline and the .24898 target Gaussian moment, but(A) is a different, complete arithmetic estimate and must be proved in its own normalization.

The deliberately coarse square-root averaged energy E<<X^(1+epsilon) would give:

  theta=.26 -> gamma=.87, c=.13;
  theta=1/3 -> gamma=5/6, c=1/6;
  theta=1/2 -> gamma=3/4, c=1/4.

Even the weaker pair theta=.6, e=1.1 gives gamma=.75. These are conditional returns, not established candidates. The rigorous bound available without new arithmetic is only E<=H sum_k w_X(k)<<_tau XH+H, hence exponent e=1+theta. Comparing it with the strict first-gain threshold leaves the fixed power gap2*c6=.250278, independent of theta. Qualitative o(XH), if available in precisely this weighted setting, does not close that gap. The original summatory calibration alone does not give the needed high-frequency window energy; Theorem M makes that failure concrete rather than merely noting a missing proof.

### B3. Zero-exclusion return and family scope

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q, take literally a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including its natural zeros. Its Dirichlet series on Re(s)>1 is1/L(s,chi), so direct absolute Mellin interchange gives

  integral_0^infinity F_a(x)x^(-s) dx/x
    = e^(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

The x->0 estimate in M2 used only |a(n)|<=1 and applies here. If(A) holds, the dyadic-shell estimate gives F_a(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for all x>=1. For every fixed s with Re(s)>gamma, choose epsilon strictly below Re(s)-gamma. The Mellin integral therefore continues holomorphically to that half-plane, locally uniformly on compact subsets. The Gaussian transform is entire and nonzero. By identity with the usual meromorphic continuation, L(s,chi) has no zeros there. The principal-character pole at s=1 is compatible with a zero of1/L and is not a zero-exclusion violation; zero multiplicity causes no cancellation because the numerator never vanishes.

All heights are included by the Mellin transform and absolute x-integrability on compact subsets; no height cutoffs or finite numerical height data are substituted. The H parameter grows only inside the estimate; the returned F is the original fixed Gaussian, so no moving transform is analytically continued. Choose tau,theta,e and the intended strict target before character, scale, epsilon bookkeeping, or data-dependent selection. Constants may depend on the fixed ordinary character and tau. To assert the result for every q and character, hypothesis(A) is needed separately for each such character with the same theta,e. No uniform conductor constant is claimed. This is ordinary Dirichlet scope; no Hecke, arbitrary number-field, or nonordinary Eisenstein extension is inferred. The project's exact guide/root-L-function binding remains controller work; no proof-assistant activity is performed.

This architecture replaces the original source theorem and pays its own complete Gaussian return. It does not reuse old Gao moments, pretend the old29-family/109-child decomposition disappeared, or leave a shortening complement inside an asserted old theorem. Those objects remain valid and untouched in their own route. No extraction error, moving Euler factor, missing radical, physical K^(5/6), 9a exception, or descendant is silently promoted: none of the old local estimates is invoked to prove(A). If(A) is eventually derived from them, each of those costs must be transferred explicitly at that time. The separate full-H .004 requirement is also not met by this report.

### Complete summation

The exact identity
\[
\prod_{p\mid t,\,p\nmid c}(1-Q_p^{-1})
=\sum_{a\mid\operatorname{rad}t}
\left(\prod_{p\mid a}Q_p^{-1}\prod_{p\mid\operatorname{rad}t/a}(1-Q_p^{-1})\right)1_{a\mid c}
\]
has nonnegative coefficients summing to one. Also
\[
I_Y(ct^3)=-\sum_{q_d,q_e\le Y,\,de\mid ct^3}\mu(d)\mu(e).
\]
If a prime divides `(d,e)` outside `t`, its term is impossible because `c` is squarefree. Otherwise divisibility by `de` is exactly one squarefree selector on `c`, formed from primes of `de` outside `t`. Combining the two identities expresses `A_Y(c,B)` as a finite sum of squarefree selectors with absolute coefficient mass
\[
\ll Y^2\sum_{t\mid B}q_t^{-1/2}\ll_\epsilon Y^2q_B^\epsilon.
\]
The selector norms have a fixed polynomial bound in `q_BY`, sufficient for their subpower local costs.

Insert the exact coprime projector `sum_{ell|c,e}mu(ell)` into (T05.2). Apply (T05.3) with forced divisor `[ell,selector]`, whose norm is at least `q_ell`. Choose fixed `1/2<sigma0<5/6<sigma1`, and put
\[
f(X)=\begin{cases}X^{\sigma_0+1/2},&X\ge1,\\X^{\sigma_1+1/2},&X<1.\end{cases}
\]
The two column sums cost at most `Y² q_ell^{-sigma0} f(D/q_B³)` and its `E` counterpart, up to subpowers. Choose those losses below `2sigma0-1`; the `ell` sum converges. The one joint row profile obeys, by ideal counting and Schwartz decay,
\[
\sum_{z\ne0}q_z^\epsilon|\Phi(Uq_{\sigma_*}q_z^3)|
\ll U^{-1/3-O(\epsilon)}.
\]
The fixed-prime cube powers also sum, and fixed unit states give constants. After this row sum the bound becomes
\[
(DKY)^\epsilon Y^4{K^{2/3}\over D^{4/3}}
\left(\sum_Bq_B^3 f(D/q_B^3)\right)^2.
\]
For `q_B<=D^(1/3)`, the summand is `D^(sigma0+1/2) q_B^(3/2-3sigma0)`; this exponent of `q_B` is greater than `-1`, and ideal counting gives total `D^(4/3)`. The tail with `sigma1>5/6` gives the same bound by a convergent sum. Therefore
\[
\boxed{|P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[I,I]|\ll_\epsilon
(DKY)^\epsilon D^{4/3}K^{2/3}Y^4.}
\tag{T05.4}
\]
All originally infinite cube-label sums have now been justified by these positive majorants, after exact row/mask identities were established.

At `K<=D^(1753/2000)` and `Y=D^(1/100)`, the exponent is `5873/3000`, with margin `127/3000` below two. Bilinearity thus gives
\[
P_{\rm cub}(2\Re\mathfrak Q[I,R]+\mathfrak Q[R,R])
=P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[C,C]+O_\epsilon(D^{5873/3000+\epsilon}).
\]
The available principal C–C bound remains `D^(5/3-2c0+epsilon)K^(2/3+epsilon)`, by CP (18). At this geometry it has exponent `2.000773294079928262...`. T05 is an upper-budget comparison, not a lower bound showing that C–C actually attains that size. The nonprincipal generic sieve still has the much larger `D²K^(1/3)` loss.

# A checked hybrid of smoothing, filter banks and numerator phases



**Result.** The forward chain old compact → almost-log compact → Gaussian extends to the full Gaussian-ideal numerator-phase family as a Hilbert-valued operator identity. It can alternate with a simultaneous two-filter bank and a bounded causal recombination. The constants, coefficient mass, tails and zero signal are paid below. This supplies an actual architecture, including an explicit four-channel instance. It does not prove the required arithmetic estimate. All these scalar convolution operators commute, so their rearrangement alone cannot create a saving. A new bound exploiting a complete signed arithmetic source is still necessary.

## 1. Exact source and coefficient contract

The new family in the merged consultation, §8.2 R4V1–R4V8, is over **K=Q(i)**. It is neither the ordinary coefficient A(n)=mu(n)−2·1_(2|n)mu(n/2), nor the original Eisenstein field Q(sqrt(−3)), nor a finite-order twist of either source. The word quartic in the existing endpoint optimization is a separate use of the word. Keep the fixed excluded prime set S, fixed nonzero quartic seed, two ray states, compatible angular character chi2((d))=(d/|d|)^2, and nonconjugated source pairing from merged §3.

Write every good integral ideal uniquely m=c d² with c squarefree; c and d need not be coprime. Fix a bounded real interval I of positive length, H=L²(I,dt), and

    B_m(t)=mu_K(c) chi2(d) N(d)^(1+it),
    F_k(x)(t)=sum_m B_m(t) k(log(Nm/x)).                    (H1)

The coefficient family is fixed before x. No moving mask or pointwise selection of t is included. For each m, ||B_m||_H=|I|^(1/2)N(d). Ideal counting in Q(i), by lattice counting modulo the four units, gives # {Nc<=Y}=O(Y), hence the useful sharper mass bound

    sum_(Nm<=Y) ||B_m||_H
      <= C |I|^(1/2) Y sum_(Nd<=sqrt(Y))1/Nd
      <= C_S |I|^(1/2) Y log(2Y).                          (H2)

Indeed the middle sum is O(log(2Y)) by dyadic ideal counting. This is uniform in the phase; neither cancellation nor a deep coefficient estimate is used. More precisely the absolute Dirichlet majorant is

    sum_(c,d) |mu(c)| Nc^(−sigma) Nd^(1−2sigma)
       = [zeta_K^S(sigma)/zeta_K^S(2sigma)]
           zeta_K^S(2sigma−1) < infinity, sigma>1.         (H3)

Consequently, for the three fixed profiles, the H-valued Mellin identity initially holds absolutely at Re s>1:

    Fhat_k(s)=M_k(s) N_I(s)/zeta_K^S(s),
    N_I(s)(t)=L_K^S(2s−1−it,chi2).                        (H4)

This is an independently checked Dirichlet-series identity. It does not itself identify a bounded automorphic relative-period operator. The merged source supplies finite Schwartz approximations and their arithmetic stabilization; approximation-uniform bounds for the actual coupled restriction remain an additional contract.

## 2. Forward smoothing survives forming the phase family

Use the frozen review §4, [restricted research revision].1–[restricted research revision].4, for the already proved scalar kernel estimates: geometric-width compact k_o, new almost-log compact k_n, and fixed g_tau, with transforms M_o,M_n,M_g=exp(tau s²/2). All are nonzero at Re s>0. There are fixed bilateral kernels h_no,h_gn such that, for every a>0,

    C_h(a):=integral_R |h(v)| exp(a v) dv < infinity,
    M_n/M_o=M_(h_no), M_g/M_n=M_(h_gn).                   (H5)

The same kernels act on H-valued fields, S_hF(x)=integral h(v)F(xe^v)dv. Equation H2/H3, followed by absolute rearrangement first at a line sigma>1, gives literal identities

    F_n=S_no F_o,             F_g=S_gn F_n.               (H6)

The Bochner integrals are justified directly: compact F_o,F_n vanish for x below a fixed positive number and have O_H(x log(2+x)) absolute bounds to the right. For Gaussian output, a dyadic decomposition using H2 shows O_H(x log(2+x)) for x>=1 and O_(H,A)(x^A) as x→0 for every fixed A>0. Thus every positive-weight h tail is paid; nothing has been dropped at shifted scales.

Define the full shell norm

    N_a(F)=sup_(X>0) X^(−a)
        [integral_X^(2X) ||F(x)||_H² dx/x]^(1/2).

Minkowski gives N_a(S_hF)<=C_h(a)N_a(F), exactly, because a shifted shell is still a shell in this definition. The same bound holds on global L²_a=L²(R,e^(−2au)du;H), u=log x. A large-X estimate O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) extends to N_(gamma+epsilon)<infinity using the stated left tails and compact intermediate scales. This establishes all-shell exponent transfer in the forward direction, including vector-valued cross-phase information. Such growth need not give a finite full-line norm at exactly a=gamma. To use the global Hilbert frame from an every-epsilon hypothesis, choose a>gamma and use a smaller epsilon<a−gamma; alternatively use the shell-sup inequalities directly. The limiting global norm is never presumed finite.

The arithmetic phase formation and smoothing commute on finite sums and on H3's absolute half-plane; H2 justifies passing to the physical smoothed fields. Thus one can form the entire phase family and then smooth, or smooth each fixed coefficient family and then form its H-vector. One cannot remove smoothing, assert a bounded raw family at the target line, and use H6 to justify that assertion: the raw measure sum B_m delta_(log Nm) is an algebraic/distributional object, and the raw Dirichlet series is justified here only at Re s>1.

There is also a specific scalar-to-vector construction from the primitive ideal field F_(K,k)(x)=sum_c mu_K(c)k(log(Nc/x)):

    F_k(x)(t)=T_t F_(K,k)(x),
    T_t U(x)=sum_d chi2(d)Nd^(1+it) U(x/Nd²).

It commutes with smoothing on the absolute domain, and its absolute shell operator bound is sqrt(|I|)zeta_K^S(2a−1) for a>1. The absolute majorant series diverges at a<=1; this construction has not supplied boundedness at the target line. Thus the scalar-to-vector identity exists, but its target norm is unpaid. Arbitrary rephasing of an already aggregated completed F_0 or a masked piece is a different operation: equal norms can carry different square parts, and one scalar sample supplies no bounded recovery of those labels. Retain the ideal square-part labels, or the specific primitive-source T_t construction, without identifying this arithmetic transfer with the paid scalar smoothing maps.

There is still no bounded Gaussian→compact or new compact→old compact convolution on a positive weighted L² line. Their inverse multipliers are unbounded; finite-band inversion pays the supremum of the inverse quotient. Phase formation supplies no improvement to that conditioning. The forward theorem applies to the same fixed family only. A moving mask may be carried through as an extra index if its entire fixed indexed family and uniform norms are retained; it cannot silently be recomputed at each shifted scale.

## 3. Two dilation filters, sharp frame constants and causal reconstruction

Fix beta<gamma, preferably with a fixed positive gap. For lambda=2 or 3 set

    D_lambda F(x)=F(x)−lambda^beta F(x/lambda),
    d_lambda(s)=1−lambda^(beta−s).                         (H7)

On Re s=a>beta let r_lambda=lambda^(beta−a), q_lambda=1−r_lambda. Then

    q_lambda <= |d_lambda(a+i y)| <= 1+r_lambda.

Each individual filter is already nonzero in Re s>beta. Its zeros lie on Re s=beta. The common zeros of d_2,d_3 consist only of s=beta, since a nonzero common imaginary part would imply 2^m=3^n for nonzero integers. This common-zero observation is valid, but it adds no zero coverage in our target half-plane: either filter already covers it.

On L²_a define A_beta F=(D_2F,D_3F). Plancherel, including arbitrary H fibers, gives the exact frame inequalities

    A(a,beta)||F||² <= ||A_beta F||² <= B(a,beta)||F||²,
    A=q_2²+q_3²,
    B=(1+r_2)²+(1+r_3)².                                 (H8)

The constants are sharp as operator bounds. The lower symbol value occurs at frequency zero; the upper supremum is B by irrationality of log 2/log 3 and density of the corresponding phases. Equality need not be attained by a nonzero L² function.

There is an explicit left inverse using only past scales, not deconvolution of a smoothing kernel:

    E_lambda G(x)=sum_(j>=0) lambda^(j beta) G(x/lambda^j),
    ||E_lambda||_(L²_a)<=q_lambda^(−1),
    w_lambda=q_lambda²/A,
    R_a(G_2,G_3)=w_2 E_2G_2+w_3 E_3G_3.                  (H9)

Then R_a A_beta=I and ||R_a||_(L²_a(H²)→L²_a(H))=A^(−1/2). The proof is the convergent geometric inverse for each translation, followed by Cauchy–Schwarz:

    sum_lambda |w_lambda/d_lambda(s)|²
       <= sum_lambda q_lambda²/A² =1/A.

At zero frequency equality holds. The multipliers w_lambda/d_lambda(s) are holomorphic for Re s>beta, so this reconstruction also respects the analytic Mellin identity. The frequently used canonical frame inverse, conjugate(d)/sum|d|² on one vertical line, need not furnish this holomorphic extension; H9 does.

For physical fields, the telescoping boundary lambda^(J beta)F(x/lambda^J) vanishes: eventually exactly for compact fields, and rapidly for Gaussian fields. Thus H9 reconstructs them even when global target integrability is what is being proved. On all-shell norms, N_a(E_lambda G)<=q_lambda^(−1)N_a(G); consequently

    N_a(R_a G)<= A^(−1/2)
       [N_a(G_2)²+N_a(G_3)²]^(1/2)
       <= sqrt(2/A) N_a^bank(G).                          (H10)

Here N_a^bank uses the joint H² shell norm. The last sqrt(2) accounts for component suprema possibly occurring at different shells; the sharp global L² constant must not be silently asserted for a shell supremum. This harmless fixed factor does not alter an exponent. Fixed beta and any fixed reconstruction weights summing to one give a causal identity; choosing weights at a chosen a optimizes its global bound.

For delta=a−beta→0+, A=delta²[(log2)²+(log3)²]+O(delta³). Thus the frame inverse costs approximately 1/[delta sqrt((log2)²+(log3)²)]. A product D_2D_3 instead costs 1/(q_2q_3), of order delta^(−2). A fixed bank is better conditioned than this serial product, but no exponent saving follows from that fixed constant. Choosing beta within X^(−kappa) of a would incur an X^kappa bank cost, or X^(2kappa) for the product, and would also change the source with X. Keep beta fixed. At a=.874864 and beta=.75 the receipt evaluates these constants explicitly.

All filters act in scale, independently of t. They preserve the exact coefficients, excluded-prime convention and phase parameter. They do not turn the phase into a Hecke twist on the squarefree factor.

## 4. A concrete alternating chain and another stage

One allowed chain is

    F_o → S_no F_o=F_n → A_beta F_n
        → (S_gn direct-sum S_gn) A_beta F_n
        = A_beta F_g → R_a A_beta F_g=F_g → A_beta F_g.

It uses a bank, forward smoothing of the whole bank, a paid left inverse, and a further bank. S_h,D_lambda,E_lambda commute on the just established domains because they are scalar convolutions in log scale. The causal sums and convolution interchange by their positive-weight absolute bounds. No stage inverts M_g/M_n. Recombination is useful for retaining a simple source for another argument, though the displayed final bank equals the preceding Gaussian bank and is not an independent gain.

A less redundant explicit two-level bank, with smoothing between levels, is

    G_ij = D_i S_gn D_j S_no F_o = D_iD_j F_g,
                     i,j in {2,3}.                      (H11)

Its four channels retain H=L²(I). Applying R_a to either index and then the other reconstructs F_g, with global norm <=A^(−1) and all-shell norm <=2/A. Its global frame bounds are A² and B²: the symbol is d tensor d. This supplies a fully specified alternating construction and a paid route to another stage. Depth m costs A^(−m/2) globally and at most (sqrt(2/A))^m in the stated shell bound; it is not free if depth grows with X.

For a fixed finite composition the product of all C_h(a), frame, shift and reconstruction constants is a fixed constant. If depth depends on X, the whole product must be X^o(1) to preserve an every-epsilon exponent, or its explicit power must be subtracted from a strict gain. For a uniform stage bound C>1, depth o(log X) suffices for subpower cost, while depth proportional to log X generally costs a power. The source/profile choices must also be consistent: the direct chain has only the allowed forward arrows, and growing-depth identities must still reconstruct one fixed source before its Mellin return. Moving profiles cannot simply be assigned the fixed Mellin identity. At beta=a the causal series no longer contracts and A=0; the easy inverse and frame lower bound fail.

For H11 the actual profile, with z=log(Nm/x), is

    kappa_ij(z)=g_tau(z)−i^beta g_tau(z+log i)
       −j^beta g_tau(z+log j)+(ij)^beta g_tau(z+log(ij)).   (H12)

This formula includes repeated indices, whose equal middle terms add. Each kernel has left/right Gaussian decay and Mellin multiplier M_g(s)d_i(s)d_j(s), nonzero at Re s>beta. One can instead stop at the compact bank if that source admits a cheaper arithmetic estimate; H6 carries such an estimate forward. One cannot obtain an old-compact bank estimate back from a Gaussian one by these operators.

For reference, even the one-stage square has the complete expression

    ||D_lambda F(x)||_H²=||F(x)||_H²
      +lambda^(2beta)||F(x/lambda)||_H²
      −2lambda^beta Re<F(x),F(x/lambda)>_H.               (H13)

The last term, all original signed ideal pairs within it, and the integral in t are part of the task. For two stages there are the full sixteen ordered profile cross terms per channel before equal terms are collected. Taking absolute values before a proposed cancellation pays only an upper bound; it cannot be credited with a negative cross term. A weighted signed recombination of different detectors also creates all its cross terms and needs a nonvanishing combined multiplier. H9 avoids that uncertainty by proving its exact left-inverse identity.

## 5. Phase signal, interval width and zero return

Assume the fixed chi2 Hecke numerator has its usual holomorphic continuation (it is a nonprincipal fixed angular character), as required by the underlying source contract. Then N_I(s) is an H-valued holomorphic function and is a nonzero vector at every fixed s: if its norm were zero, continuity in t and the identity theorem would make L_K^S(w,chi2) identically zero. Its far-right Dirichlet series excludes that possibility. Individual numerator zeros, of any finite multiplicity, are allowed.

For a filter word of length m with a common terminal kernel k, the vector signal norm on Re s=a is at least

    |M_k(s)| A(a,beta)^(m/2) ||N_I(s)||_H                (H14)

for the full 2^m bank. The bank supplies a quantitative scale-filter factor; it does not supply a uniform lower bound for the L numerator or for the decaying M_k. On a fixed compact set of s, ||N_I(s)|| has a positive minimum by continuity; this gives a finite constant, not a known explicit numerical bound and not a uniform all-height claim. The fixed compact transforms are nonzero at positive real part and the Gaussian is everywhere nonzero; their high-frequency attenuation remains the conditioning in frozen [restricted research revision].1.

A small fixed phase interval suffices qualitatively. Its quantitative width cost is real. If the center t0 gives a numerator zero of order r, with local leading coefficient C in t, then for centered interval width h,

    integral_I |N(s)(t)|² dt
      = |C|² h^(2r+1)/[(2r+1)2^(2r)] (1+O(h)).          (H15)

The inverse signal cost is of order h^(−r−1/2), or h^(−r) with normalized interval measure. C depends on the relevant derivative. A shrinking interval or an increasing height range needs quantitative derivative/multiplicity and remainder bounds; the identity theorem alone does not pay that loss. Keeping I fixed avoids an X-dependent width cost without asserting numerical stability at every height.

Retain the vector until return. Integrating against one fixed weight in t can annihilate the numerator at a possible denominator zero. Finite samples have no proved common-zero exclusion here. An s-dependent projection onto N_I(s), or division by its norm, is not a fixed bounded arithmetic detector without its own conditioning proof. In particular the compact local projection considered in frozen Part VIII collapses the phase family to a scalar multiple of the old numerator; bounded reconstruction from that rank-one projection is not provided by H9. Scale-filter reconstruction and lost phase information are different issues. Ordinary simultaneous stacking of smoothing kernels or dilation filters at one fixed t has the same common scalar numerator: all channels can still vanish where that numerator does. The retained interval vector supplies the new numerator coverage, independently of the scale-bank frame. Every split and recombination above is the identity on that H fiber.

Suppose, for some fixed gamma>max(beta,1/2), one complete bank has all-shell size O_(epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0, with its established small-scale tails. Dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz makes its H^q-valued Mellin transform holomorphic for Re s>gamma. Continue the exact identity

    zeta_K^S(s) Ghat(s)
       = M_k(s) [filter-symbol vector] tensor N_I(s).    (H16)

At a zero rho of zeta_K^S in that half-plane the left side vanishes and the right side is nonzero by H14. The pole of zeta_K at 1 is irrelevant to this zero contradiction; continuation can first be made off that point. Every finite zero multiplicity is excluded. Fixed removed Euler factors are nonzero at positive real part. Thus zeta_K, and by zeta_K=zeta·L(s,chi_(−4)) also zeta, has no zeros at Re s>gamma. This proves the return conditional on the new arithmetic bound; no uniform-height inverse numerator is used.

## 6. The precise new arithmetic estimate and the limit of the architecture

A fully concrete sufficient target for a first gain is: choose fixed 1/2<gamma<.874864, fixed beta<gamma, fixed tau>0 and fixed I of positive length, and prove, for every epsilon>0,

    [sum_(i,j in {2,3}) integral_I integral_X^(2X)
      |sum_(c,d good) mu_K(c) chi2(d) Nd^(1+it)
          kappa_ij(log(Nc Nd²/x))|² dx/x dt]^(1/2)
            <= C_(I,tau,beta,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (HYB-QFAM)

The inner sum includes the whole Gaussian tail, all repeated-square towers, all signs and all pair cross terms. If the proof passes through a quartic relative-period realization, require constants uniform in finite-prime/valuation Schwartz approximations and a justified passage to this literal family. Preserve the seed, both ray states, angular line, bad places, actual equal-square restriction and both local relative orbit cells. Ordinary local Fourier self-duality or ambient automorphic L² bounds do not establish that relative restriction. The existing fixed-family Eisenstein mixed-moment theorem does not automatically apply to Q(i) with this angular/repeated-square source.

HYB-QFAM gives zeta zero freedom to Re s>gamma and therefore a potential numerical c=1−gamma for that ordinary zeta conclusion. It does **not** automatically extend the original fixed Dirichlet/Eisenstein character family. Such an extension needs its own family construction, numerator continuation, uniform scope and complete norms. No instance of HYB-QFAM at a gaining gamma is proved here.

For this SAME completed arithmetic source and fixed operators, HYB-QFAM is equivalent, up to constants/every epsilon, to OPEN-QFAM(gamma) for F_g. One direction is H7's bounded shifts, the other H10/H11's causal reconstruction. A complete bound on even one channel also returns zeros because its multiplier is already nonzero; the bank is not a weaker hypothesis merely by being vector-valued. Fixed repeated analysis/recombination therefore rephrases the exponent unless a new arithmetic argument can estimate the new representation more efficiently.

Here is an explicit mixed-representation harvesting rule. Choose fixed bounded ideal masks p_1,p_2,p_3 with sum_j p_j(m)=1 and mass bounds as in H2 (multiplying its constant by each mask bound). Retain t and define F_k^(j) by replacing B_m with p_j(m)B_m. Estimate F_o^(1), A_beta F_n^(2), and the four-channel Gaussian bank of F_g^(3). Then

    F_g = S_gn S_no F_o^(1)
        + S_gn R_a(A_beta F_n^(2))
        + (R_a in each index)(Gaussian bank of F_g^(3)).  (H17)

For N_a, this gives the fully paid upper bound C_gn(a)C_no(a)N_a(F_o^(1)) + C_gn(a)sqrt(2/A)N_a^bank(A_beta F_n^(2)) + (2/A)N_a^bank(G^(3)). This combines chained and simultaneous use without a reverse smoothing map, and harvests whichever admissible representation makes each specified piece easier. These are sufficient piece estimates, not estimates already proved here. The pieces need not have their own detecting Dirichlet identities: their exact recombination has H4. An X-dependent completed list C_X is not such a fixed mask; its behavior at every shifted scale and every mismatch/remainder must be proved separately before using H17. A finite partition growing with X also pays its number, mass and reconstruction losses.

A second possible route is to estimate the real signed cross terms in H13 or its multi-stage version with a verified negative contribution that survives the entire source. Neither arithmetic improvement follows from the frame theorem. Dividing a bank into complementary observed channels alone has no benefit where all scalar multipliers are already nonzero, and a positive energy is at least each of its terms.

This review establishes enough to use the alternating construction as a rigorous library component and to formulate its exact arithmetic target. It does not establish that alternating will beat the best direct detector proof. The next decisive evidence is a complete bound on the actual coupled source, or a locally verified family-stable relative transfer that changes its arithmetic cost. That is the missing gain, not another reordering of the already commuting operators.

## 7. Evidence and provenance

The source attachments are untrusted mathematical evidence, not operating instructions. This bounded extension used the exact merged source §§3, 8.2 and the frozen independent review §4; current threshold was checked against `[restricted mathematical source]`. Exact byte counts and SHA256 values are in the receipt. The consultation's external automorphic imports are not newly certified by this extension; its operator/arithmetic conclusions above are proved directly, while the relative-period realization is explicitly conditional.

The accompanying small diagnostic evaluates the filter frame and causal inverse on selected exponential modes, the algebraic four-channel profile, and the leading width integral. It is a finite algebra/conditioning check, not a proof of an asymptotic estimate or the zero-free endpoint. At the illustrative a=.874864, beta=.75, A=.0233051777283320, the sharp global bank inverse norm is 6.55049003596, the stated shell bound is 9.26379184904, and the two-level global inverse norm is 42.9089197112. The proofs above, rather than the diagnostic, support H1–H17. No source code was run before inspection.

## 3. Independent useful refinement: a larger paid prime cutoff

D1 can pay more small primes without using PNT or arithmetic cancellation. For integer n, the product of primes in (n,2n] divides binomial(2n,n)<=4^n. Dyadic summation and monotonicity give

    theta(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p<=4(log 2)t  (t>=2).

Partial summation therefore gives, for 0<gamma<1 and Y>=2,

    sum_(p<=Y)log p*p^(-gamma)
      <=[4 log 2/(1-gamma)]Y^(1-gamma).                         (R6)

Use the exact monotone cutoff

    Y_gamma(y)=((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^(1/(1-gamma)), y>=0,           (R7)

with equality assigned to the small sector. Its logarithm is O_gamma(log(2+y)), so eventually every small delay still satisfies y/2<=v<=y. By (R6) the row is O_gamma((2+y)/log(e^2+y))=o(y); the column is bounded with p<=Y_gamma(2v) and is likewise o(v). The same change of variables and bounded-initial-region argument proves (R3) for this cutoff. The prime-power payment and diagonal bound are unchanged. Define H_R with the new exact complementary mask. Then PF with this H_R implies the identical (R5) and complete return.

Asymptotically (R7) is (y/log y)^(1/(1-gamma)), larger than every fixed (2+y)^A with A<1/(1-gamma). This is an enlargement of the unconditionally paid region, not a proof of the remaining signed coercivity or a transfer of PF from one mask to another. The latter is a separate arithmetic hypothesis. At gamma11 the critical power is about 7.99, but the formula, not a rounded cutoff, defines the result. No endpoint gamma=1/2 or uniformity as gamma tends to 1 is claimed.

Ancestry and usefulness: W35 already gives the Gaussian renewal/heat commutator; G118 has the full logarithmic source, and G79 records the one-sided energy drift. W62's combined paid prime-power sector, moving column, exact finite diagonal and explicit residual coercivity form give a useful source-specific reduction. The refinement (R6)-(R7) modestly strengthens that interface. It does not create a new general renewal method or remove the full arithmetic problem.

statement:
### 3.2 Exact Poisson formula and its signs

For a high output scale N=2^jX, set T=(N/X)^6>=1. Decompose m into dyadic intervals I_M=[M,2M) intersect[1,D]. Define

    beta_h=(1/Q)sum_(r mod Q)b(r)exp(-2pi i hr/Q), h in Z.

Then beta is Q-periodic, bounded by ||b||inf, and beta_h=0 whenever Q divides h. Applying Poisson after extending the smooth positive-support function by zero gives

    sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)=(1/m)sum_(h in Z)beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    I_r(x)=integral w(n/N)exp(-n/x^(3/2))
                         exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.        (R5)

The sign is correct. A Fourier mode exp(2pi i j l/Q), paired with the Poisson integer k, has frequency (j-kQ)/m; it is exactly h/m with h congruent to j modulo Q. Negative aliases and all repeats are present. The h=0 mode vanishes, rather than being estimated away. For each finite row the transformed sum converges absolutely after two integrations by parts in the large-|h| tail.

Write rho=N/(X^(3/2)) and x=Xz,1<=z<=2. The rescaled phase is

    T[2pi (rN/T)t/Q-t^6/z^6], n=Nt.

Choose a fixed positive frequency interval c_Q T/N<=r<=C_Q T/N which contains every possible stationary point on t in[1,4], with a fixed gap outside. The author's explicit constants work: c_Q=3Q/(128pi), C_Q=6Q*4^5/pi. At the lower outside boundary the linear derivative is at most half the minimum nonlinear derivative; at the upper outside boundary it is at least twice the maximum. These strict margins hold uniformly in z.

For a near positive r the unique critical point and phase are

    n_r=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
    Phi_r(n_r)=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5)r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
    Phi_r''(n_r)=-30n_r^4/x^6.                               (R6)

In rescaled variables the critical point remains in a fixed positive compact interval and the second derivative is bounded away from zero. The amplitude and each fixed needed derivative are O(e^(-c rho)): derivative factors are powers of rho, absorbed into a weaker exponential. Uniform smooth stationary phase therefore gives

    I_r=Z_r exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4)
                  +O_Q((N/T)e^(-c rho)),
    Z_r=sqrt(pi/15)x^3 n_r^(-2) w(n_r/N)exp(-n_r/x^(3/2)).    (R7)

The normalization and negative Fresnel sign follow directly from (R6). The deliberately weak T^-1 error is valid; a smooth nondegenerate expansion gives a stronger remainder. Support-edge crossings do not introduce a sharp endpoint: w and its derivatives extend smoothly by zero. The uniform proof and constants are detailed in support.md. No stationary expansion with a discarded sharp cofactor cutoff is used.

statement:
## D. Rare-lane test: nonnegative smoothing and fixed layer deletion retain shrinking zeros

Let w:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity) be a fixed continuous compactly supported function with w(0)>0 and w>=c_w>0 on some fixed interval [a,b], 0<a<b. Smooth functions are included. For a principal character modulo fixed q set

    C_j(X)=sum_(n squarefree,(n,q)=1,omega(n)=j)w(n/X),
    Z_X(z)=sum_(j>=0)C_j(X)z^j.                        (D1)

This is a finite polynomial and its signed endpoint is the exact smoothed Mobius sum. C_0=w(1/X) tends to w(0), and sum_j C_j=O_w(X). Fix an integer ell>=1, then explicitly change the polynomial by deleting its first ell-1 nonconstant layers:

    Z_X^[ell](z)=C_0+C_ell z^ell+sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j.   (D2)

This is coefficient deletion, not exact root deflation. Its changed signed endpoint must retain the correction sum_(1<=j<ell)(-1)^j C_j to recover the original field.

Taking ell distinct primes in [a^(1/ell)X^(1/ell), b^(1/ell)X^(1/ell)] gives squarefree products in [aX,bX], with unique unordered factorizations. Fixed-proportion prime counts therefore imply

    C_ell(X) >>_(w,q,ell) X/log^ell X.                 (D3)

Put R_X=(2C_0/C_ell)^(1/ell), which tends to zero. On |z|=R_X,

    |C_0+C_ell z^ell| >= C_0,
    |sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j| <= O_w(X) R_X^(ell+1)
       =O_(w,q,ell)(X^(-1/ell)log^(ell+1)X)=o(1).     (D4)

For large X, Rouche's theorem gives exactly ell zeros counted with multiplicity in |z|<R_X. In particular the Taylor branch of log Z_X^[ell] about zero cannot have a fixed positive radius. This concerns the actual FULL weighted polynomial: higher degrees are paid together, not discarded. For ell=1 it applies G106's mechanism to every such nonnegative compact smoothing. For every fixed ell it also defeats the proposed finite-degree-deletion repair. Fixed weights vanishing near zero instead have C_0=0 eventually and already lack a logarithm at zero; sign-changing or X-dependent weights are outside this theorem.

The corresponding absolute price of the deleted endpoint layers is at least C_ell0(X)>>X/log^ell0 X for any retained fixed removed degree ell0>=1, hence has exponent 1. Their SIGNED combination could cancel and has not been lower-bounded. Exact deflation, complex paths, signed weights, growing degree and another normalized object remain eligible only with their complete recovery cost. These fugacity zeros are not ordinary L-function zeros.

This test preserves the p<.01 draw by developing its strongest affordable repair. It finds a real obstruction rather than a new parity estimate. It extends the recorded sharp-cutoff/root and prime-clique tests in a specified direction; it makes no claim of literature novelty.

# [private research revision]: coupling the original slot width to a finite amplifier atlas



## 1. New input and complete candidate consequence

**Theorem L4405.** Relative to the accepted PR9 analytic inputs and Gao's signed-row, fixed-dictionary, density and Fourier-transport lemmas, the original natural paired moment has capacity

\[
 C=881/200=4.405
\]

on the SAME local window

\[
 .41M\le n_1,n_2\le.44M,\qquad .03M\le z\le.04M,
 \qquad n_1+n_2+Cz\le M.                       \tag{1}
\]

All descendants use only the OLD 9/2 moment or its unrestricted zero-slot theorem. The proof chooses one of fifty actual prime amplifiers according to the original total slot width, before any row sum or transform. It changes the literal pool, actual main smooth ball and corresponding errors. It is not an endpoint-only retuning of the accepted C=4.44 estimate.

The complete return proved below gives the candidate

\[
 \theta_2=109359/125000=.874872,\qquad
 c_2=15641/125000=.125128.                       \tag{2}
\]

This is a gain of exactly 1/125000=.000008 over the accepted written analytic incumbent c1=391/3125=.12512. The scope is every finite-order Eisenstein Hecke L-function of trivial infinite type and every ordinary Dirichlet L-function, including zeta, in the OPEN half-plane Re s>theta2, excluding the principal pole at 1. There is no claim on the boundary, angular families or a uniformly moving parent conductor.

Zhongpai Gao, with AI assistance, retains credit for the PR15 construction and bridges; OpenAI for the initial 7/8 result and analytic/arithmetic framework; Hailey Collet for the quartic, variable-moment, detector and source architecture; Akash Levy for the weighted numerator. [private research revision] supplied the larger-amplifier specialization. This lane supplies the finite coupled atlas and its complete return. No literature-priority or upstream-endorsement claim is made.

## 2. Sources, accepted scope and quantifiers

I read `[restricted mathematical source]`, `[restricted mathematical source]` and `[restricted mathematical source]` before developing this extension. The accepted [private research revision] author proof and independent critic supply the reviewed parameter-general interfaces. Its prior uncoupled boundary 4961/1121 is not an admissible coefficient.

The PR15 pin is `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`. Under `[restricted mathematical source]`, use `PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex` (LA), `RestrictedCanonicalSource.tex` (RC), `SignedReconstruction.tex` (SR), `FixedDictionaryBridge.tex`, `PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex`, `FourierMaskTransport.tex` (FM), `PhysicalScaleShortening.tex` and `EndpointAssembly.tex` (EA). The PR9 pin is `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`; its retained manuscript is `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`. The actual amplification formulas B3.58--61 were reread here. The [private research revision] reviewed sources additionally include `FirstAmplificationChoice`, `AmplifiedRetainedRadius`, `AmplificationOriginalErrors`, `GaussEnergy`, `SecondActualWidth`, `SecondExceptionalFixedQSource` and the physical empty-slot/continuation interfaces. Their exact pins and blob identities remain in the accepted critic. No provider or remote-source contact was made in this continuation.

The theorem retains the literal fixed finite ray factor times the extended sextic row, without positive-width moving parent support. The ray modulus, original anchor and proper ideal

\[
 Q_* = M_{\rm ray}\cap(72)\cap\mathfrak q_{\eta_0}
\]

are fixed. Original canonical prime pools, one common annular slot profile, allowed individual relative characters, natural coefficient zeros, radial majorant and literal non-FixedInducingRow gate remain. An additional common puncture may depend on frozen outer labels, with polynomial norm, but must be independent of the row being summed. Assume 51/100<=beta_*<=7/8, as in the accepted initialization.

For U=Z^M, the conclusion is the actual natural estimate

\[
 \sum_{k\ {
m eligible}}
 |S_{k,1}(Z^{n_1})S_{k,2}(Z^{n_2})Q_{k,I}|^2
 \ll Z^{M+\epsilon}\mathcal H_J.                 \tag{3}
\]

It includes the same four logarithmic scale-derivative profile pairs. The finite atlas is fixed numerically first. Given a loss, choose a common slot mesh from the normalized geometry BEFORE target/dictionary and finite original slots. Once a family and slot system are fixed, choose finite orders, constant and ONE eventual threshold before every live scale, selected subset, mask, row and independent height. Fixed family dependence remains; there is no new arbitrary-coefficient moment.

## 3. The finite atlas and why it is an analytic change

Set

\[
 t=z/M,\quad r=9/2-C=19/200,\quad k=9/40,
 \quad h_s=1/5000,\quad b_j=3/100+jh_s\ (0\le j\le50).
\]

Choose j=1 at t=b0 and otherwise the unique j with b_(j-1)<t<=b_j. Select the ACTUAL prime amplifier

\[
 a=a_j=kb_jM,\qquad \sigma_j=3a_j.              \tag{4}
\]

Both original rectangles use this same choice. It depends only on the frozen original selected-slot width and M; it does not depend on a summed row, first/second extraction label, height, plain scale within a supremum rectangle, or later low/high bin. Thus no row-dependent prime pool, nonsmooth differentiated indicator, or extra reconstruction label is introduced.

The fifty normalized exponents a_j/M are fixed in advance, between 1359/200000 and 9/1000. After using U as base, every case invokes the SAME original amplifier source with one fixed positive sigma. All thresholds/orders can be maximized over this finite list. This avoids inferring uniformity from an arbitrary continuum of pointwise eventual statements. A moment call uses one j, so there is no factor U^(log 50) or repeated label count; even summing fifty cases would cost only a constant.

On case j the exact parent geometry supplies

\[
 A=n_1+n_2+z\le A_jM,
 \quad A_j=1-(C-1)b_{j-1},\qquad
 g=(n_1+n_2+(9/2)z-M)_+\le g_jM,
 \quad g_j=rb_j.                                \tag{5}
\]

The old coarse proof used incompatible extrema t=.03 for A and t=.04 for g with a single amplifier. Here both bounds are taken within one interval. Rounding a upward from kz loses at most kh_sM, and that loss is paid explicitly below. In particular C=4.405 is STRICTLY BELOW 4961/1121, so no retuning of the old independent-envelope certificate establishes this theorem.

### Actual source admissibility

PR9 B3.58 uses primes in `(Z^a/2,Z^a]`. Its reviewed exact amplification theorem assumes sigma>0, positive prime-count loss, bounded support/row exponents and mesh<sigma/6, with no fixed small upper bound on sigma. Choose normalized mesh less than min_j(a_j/M)/10. All fifty pools are eventually disjoint from original slot annuli. The fixed-field prime ideal theorem supplies cardinality at least Z^(a-loss); omitted row, first-projector, common-puncture and fixed-support primes number O(log Z). The maximum of fifty thresholds works. Representation multiplicity is bounded by a constant determined by the largest row envelope and smallest positive a_j/M.

The literal map is h -> hp^6. Only valuations 1,6,7 change. Their exact pairs (w,w_o) are (lambda,lambda),(6lambda,0),(7lambda,lambda), with lambda=log_Z Np>=3a/4 eventually. Their moving characters, extraction scalars and Euler holes are unchanged; the prime average stays normalized. They undergo no second amplification. Also 7a/M<=63/1000<1/4; combined common extractions still use the original allocation and subunit-scale conventions.

With K0=2A-c-d+R+E-M, the ACTUAL main radius is

\[
 K_{\rm main}=K_0+(d-c)_++6a+\omega,
 \quad \omega=\delta_1+\mathrm{reserve},
 \quad 2\le Z^{\mathrm{reserve}}.                \tag{6}
\]

The reviewed `main_energy_common` constructs this domination before the second transform. Error radii remain their own exact `K0+max(d-c-2w+w_o,0)+3a+delta_1+reserve`. They are not enlarged to (6). `GaussEnergy` accepts every positive physical radial scale. Polynomial caps for all fifty cases have one common bound, even if a logarithmic radius is negative. Nonempty nominal end windows are handled by actual-width padding; unsupported negative windows are empty.

The radial kernels and normalized smooth profiles are unchanged. Euler derivatives of `K(B product y_i^e_i)` are uniform for B>0, so none of the fifty radii creates an unpriced Z^a smoothness loss. Common Fourier majorants precede live labels; all four derivative pairs use the same j. Main density dictionaries and fixed ray moduli are unchanged. Moving primes in extracted errors remain in the old canonical source, not in a supposedly fixed new dictionary.

The original global proof chose its INTERNAL small sigma for recursive terminal errors. This local proof has two transforms, with fixed outer sigma_j and explicitly priced terminal losses. Every descendant invokes the already completed old theorem with its own requested loss and internal parameters. There is no circular local induction. Density's internal tau_det and the later physical tau_out remain distinct; finite atlas selection imposes no positive lower bound on tau_out.

## 4. First transform, comparison and low-bin descendants

The equal-product comparison uses lengths M/4 and n1+n2-M/4, identical masks, whole character and profiles. Delete its exact extra mask and reflect only the long factor. Its old capacity is at most

\[

\]

The old nonempty or unrestricted empty-slot theorem applies. Whole-factor conjugation, redundant Euler coefficient mass, eligibility and two-scale supremum are retained.

For the centered difference, first-transform outside exponent is M-A-R/2-E. Keep first labels INSIDE Hilbert-space Cauchy. The C-side joint target is

\[
 \sum_\lambda\mathcal N_{C,\lambda}
 \ll Z^{p+A-c+R+E+B_c+\eta},\qquad
 B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6,                             \tag{7}
\]

with the exchanged D target. Here the local p is first radical width. Since B_c+B_d<=c+d-2p-R, their geometric mean times the outside factor has exponent

\[
 M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(B_c+B_d)/2+\eta\le M+\eta.
\]

No first-label count is added after that step.

At radius (6) the exact main child formulas are

\[
 M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-\omega-g_2+t_2,
\]
\[
