statement:
# W53: finite-prime log pressure and phase-balanced blocks

**Result: no improved zero-free constant is proved.** Two bounded developments give exact new candidate interfaces: a one-sided subpower log-pressure continuation criterion, including a quantitative `a+kappa` return; and a phase-balanced prime-block criterion with its entire unmatched complement. Their arithmetic estimates remain OPEN. The principal character is included in the first interface and is a decisive obstruction to using the second alone for the common-character objective.

Baseline premise: source-relative c10=3128649/25000000=.12514596, theta10=.87485404. No F0/ancestry, positive-slot uniformity, external root-definition/import/admission or formalization obligation is discharged. No proof-assistant/kernel work was performed. Fixed ordinary characters keep their natural zero extensions and the principal pole. This packet has six first tests and two substantive developments, not six new mechanisms or a proved improvement.

## 1. Frozen selection, provenance and scope

The exact frozen problem and recipe match their supplied hashes. `seeds.md` was completely read and frozen before detailed proof/index/history access: 15098 bytes, SHA-256 `1340d04e32821958b111f1bdf5bee627150ad63cd9fad810497b9958ad6770d8`. It contains all30 cards, six groups, literal numerical p labels, incoherent raw draws and the pre-draw reservations03 strongest,21 most ambitious,16 most different. Root received the freeze notice before history was read.

Each actual random pool contains every eligible unselected card across ALL six groups, ordered by frozen ID. Each full pool was saved, entirely read and hashed in a separate call before its native entropy was consumed. `sample.py` uses an unbiased256-bit native-entropy rejection algorithm; every actual draw accepted its first entropy sample, and there was no redraw.

| Slot | Pool size and SHA-256 | Zero-based index | Card |
|---|---|---:|---|
| strict p<.10 |20; a67f69aa7e743130ddcfff50c9acaacc570fa634acb70b5fd0a7d49b6ffb3ae9|19|30|
| strict p<.01 |10; abf5f80118808e96dd2db40bb391b285d2bfef46cadc2eea5df28411e4b4800e|4|24|
| unrestricted |25; b83101ec4b11e1255a941d69a00af9c735a799bca2f27df156092de41d767008|20|25|

The exact entropy, full cards and result receipts are in `pool-*.json` and `draw-*.json`. The six first tests are03,21,16,30,24,25. No card was replaced or retrospectively re-rated. The p labels are subjective generation typicality, not measured frequencies or success probabilities.

The entire `[restricted mathematical source]` as exposed through [private research revision] was read after freezing. Relevant detailed entries and exact sources were then inspected, especially [restricted research revision]/G49 compact kernels, W27 topology, W33 singleton pressure, W35 fractional-vacuum ancestry, W36 actual finite-prime divergence and centered prime discrepancy, W41's unrenormalized reciprocal, G74/G79 and G76. The newly integrated [private research revision] delta and G108 were subsequently inspected: their cutoff-dependent Mobius prime-block marginal retains signed cofactor interactions, and is not the Euler-logarithm block hypothesis in D2. Large combined history outputs that truncated were not represented as complete reads; source slices supplied the material comparisons below.

**Ancestry correction.** Compact nonvanishing Mellin kernels are already constructed in [restricted research revision]. The squarefree complex, its homotopy, linear unsigned Betti mass and weighted commutator are already W27 and classical Bjorner. W36 C4 already derives the principal continuous-vacuum identity and the classical pointwise prime-discrepancy return. W53 does not claim these as new. The proposed additions are the one-sided local subpower pressure hypothesis with its continuation proof and explicit rate budget, and the precise phase-balanced prime-block plus unmatched-tail contract. No literature-priority claim is made; no arithmetic-gap credit follows from either interface.

## 2. Six first tests

**T03: compact Mellin observation frame — passes, duplicate.** The already retained geometric convolution kernel has multiplier

    M(s)=product_(j>=1) sinh(2^-j s)/(2^-j s).

Every factor has zeros only on Re(s)=0; the locally uniform product is nonzero on Re(s)>0 because its tail differs from1 by O_K(4^-j). Its C-infinity compact kernel and complete zero return are [restricted research revision]/G49. A finite bank does not add numerator coverage when one member already has no zeros. No new arithmetic estimate or substantive development is credited to03.

**T16: squarefree chain contraction — inherited obstruction.** Include the empty face and grade a squarefree set S by |S|, so the finite chain-space supertrace of I is M(x). If d h+h d=I-P and W is an even diagonal weight, graded trace cyclicity gives exactly

    Str(W)=Str(WP)+Str((W d-d W)h).

Character weights are not generally chain maps, so the commutator cannot be removed. Even for W=I, Bjorner's total reduced Betti mass is linear in x: 2x/pi^2+O(x^theta), theta>17/54. Thus this unsigned homology certificate supplies no exponent below1. This is W27 ancestry, not a new lower bound for signed M or a prohibition on a different signed invariant. Primary source: Bjorner, *A cell complex in number theory*, arXiv:1101.5704v1, 29 January2011, equations(1.1),(1.2), Theorems3.1/3.4: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704 .

**T21: finite independent prime gas — the missing limit is real.** At one principal prime p and real sigma>0, weights(1,-p^-sigma) have normalized occupation -p^-sigma/(1-p^-sigma)<0. They are not a positive probability state; a positive mixing theorem cannot be imported. Distinct-site connected correlations vanish algebraically, yet the sum of one-site responses can diverge. More decisively, the zero-free finite products P_y(s)=product_(p<=y)(1-p^-s) cannot be locally bounded on the whole half-plane Re(s)>a for any0<a<1. Otherwise Montel and the known limit on Re(s)>1 give a locally uniform subsequential limit F with zeta F=1 away from1. At1, continuation forces F(1)=0; Hurwitz forces the nonzero limit of the zero-free P_y to have no zero, a contradiction. The simpler wrong-sign real limit and stronger actual-kernel low-height divergence are already W41/W36. D1 retains this obstruction and changes the finite-volume normalization explicitly.

**T30: low-rank bad Schur block — fails without its arithmetic bound.** For any prescribed rho, A(s)=diag(s-rho,I_N) has a perfectly conditioned complementary block, bad rank1, and determinant s-rho. The reciprocal determinant has a pole at rho. This is an exact finite-dimensional countertest to deriving nonvanishing from small bad rank alone. It is not an arithmetic L-function counterexample. The Schur complement must itself be bounded away from zero or given a separate source theorem. This is the existing Schur/complete-complement family; no extended development.

**T24: bulk zero-gas information — finite outlier survives.** If an entire reference function is multiplied by

    P(s)=(s-rho)(s-conjugate(rho))(s-(1-rho))(s-(1-conjugate(rho))),

its zeros gain at most four counted points. P is real under conjugation and satisfies P(1-s)=P(s); the corresponding symmetries and finite order are retained. Every zero-count asymptotic unchanged by an O(1) perturbation is retained, while the new rightmost zero can lie anywhere. Thus such bulk statistics alone cannot exclude a fixed outlier. This tests that precise class, not every possible rigidity statistic. An Euler product is not preserved, so no actual-character counterexample or universal hyperuniformity no-go is asserted. The live escape is a statistic sensitive to every isolated zero together with an actual arithmetic bound.

**T25: pair clusters — quadratic terms do not pay the singleton.** With z=chi(p)p^-s,w=chi(q)q^-s,

    (1-z)(1-w)-1=-(z+w)+zw.

For Re(s)>1/2, the quadratic corrections over a disjoint bounded-size prime partition are absolutely summable. The complete first-order sums therefore remain the issue. For the principal character on real0<sigma<=1, even an arbitrary partition into finite blocks cannot make the positive block activities summable: if A_B=1-product_(p in B)(1-p^-sigma), then0<A_B<1 and sum A_B<infinity would make product_B(1-A_B)>0, whereas the full prime product is0. This strengthens the singleton check to arbitrary finite block sizes only at this literal principal-real scope. D2 gives a useful nonprincipal phase-balanced escape and pays its full complement.

## 3. D1 — a one-sided subpower finite-volume pressure criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Put delta=1 if chi is principal and0 otherwise. Throughout use chi(p)=0 at every ramified prime, without deleting this convention. For y>=2 and Re(s)>0 define the single holomorphic logarithm

    J_y(s)=integral_2^y u^-s/log(u) du,
    H_y(s)=delta J_y(s)+sum_(p<=y) log(1-chi(p)p^-s),       (1)
    Q_y(s)=exp(H_y(s)),

where each log is its absolutely convergent local power series -sum_(k>=1)chi(p)^k p^(-ks)/k. The finite prime sum is holomorphic and Q_y is nonzero on Re(s)>0. These are actual prime factors, not an unrestricted replacement coefficient sequence. The continuous term is explicit; it does not subtract the unknown prime sum.

On Re(s)>1, Q_y converges absolutely to exp(delta J_infinity(s))/L(s,chi). Define the entire nonvanishing function B by

    B(s)=(s-1)exp(J_infinity(s)) on Re(s)>1,
    B'(s)/B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1),                         (2)

with its constant fixed at one real point>1. The quotient on the right is entire after its removable value log2 at1, proving the claimed extension. Equivalently, for z=(s-1)log2,

    B(s)=exp(-gamma_E)/log2 * exp(-sum_(n>=1)(-z)^n/(n n!)).

NIST DLMF6.6.2 confirms the exponential-integral series used in this optional explicit formula: https://dlmf.nist.gov/6.6.E2 . The proof can use(2) alone.

The exact initial identity is

    (s-1)^delta L(s,chi) lim_y Q_y(s)=B(s)^delta.          (3)

For principal chi modulo q, (s-1)L(s,chi) is holomorphic and nonzero at1, with value product_(p|q)(1-1/p). Thus(3) explicitly keeps the original pole; it does not assume it away. For nonprincipal chi delta=0. Imprimitive local factors have their natural zeros on Re(s)=0 and are retained throughout.

### D1.1 One-sided local criterion

**Proposition.** Fix1/2<a<1. Suppose that for every compact K contained in Re(s)>a, every epsilon>0, and all sufficiently large integer k,

    integral_K log^+|Q_(2^k)(s)| dA(s)
           <= C_(chi,K,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).           (LP_a)

Here dA is ordinary planar area and log^+u=max(0,log u). It suffices to assume this on a countable exhaustion by closed rectangles with interior in the half-plane. Then L(s,chi) has no zero in Re(s)>a. If the same a works for each fixed ordinary chi, this gives a common c=1-a, with character-dependent constants and onset. LP_a is OPEN at every proposed a<theta10.

**Proof, including the missing continuation.** Write h_k=H_(2^k). The positive part of the harmonic function Re(h_k) is subharmonic. The area mean inequality on a disk of fixed radius r gives

    (Re h_k(z))_+ <= (pi r^2)^-1
                    integral_(|w-z|<=r) (Re h_k(w))_+ dA(w).

Thus LP_a gives a local upper bound Re h_k=O_(K,epsilon)(2^(k epsilon)). At a fixed real b>1 the exact series in(1) makes h_k(b) bounded, including its imaginary part. The Borel-Caratheodory disk inequality

    sup_(|z-c|<=R/2)|f(z)|
       <=3|f(c)|+2 sup_(|z-c|<=R) Re f(z)

and a finite overlapping-disk chain from b yield

    sup_K |h_k| <= C_(K,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon)             (4)

for every compact K in the connected half-plane. A harmless absolute constant can be added on the right of the disk inequality when the displayed supremum is negative; alternatively use its maximum with0. All chain geometry is fixed before k grows. This step shows why an uncontrolled imaginary additive constant cannot enter: the actual logarithm is anchored at b.

Let f_k=h_(k+1)-h_k. On every compact subset of Re(s)>1, the omitted prime interval and the continuous integral give

    |f_k(s)| <= C_b 2^(-k(b-1)) when Re(s)>=b>1.          (5)

The integer majorant sum_(n>2^k)n^-b suffices; no prime theorem is used. Meanwhile(4) gives local O(2^(k epsilon)) growth for every epsilon>0. These two facts imply exponential decay of f_k on EVERY fixed compact in Re(s)>a. For completeness: start with a disk in Re(s)>1 where(5) has exponent -d<0. A chain of disks with radii r,2r,4r inside the half-plane propagates decay by Hadamard's three-circle inequality. An inner bound2^(-kd_j) and outer bound2^(k epsilon) give a middle bound2^(-k(d_j-epsilon)/2). For a chain of N disks choose epsilon<d/2^(N+1); then every resulting d_j remains positive. Finite covers handle an arbitrary compact. Constants depend on the compact and do not depend on k.

Hence sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly, and h_k has a holomorphic limit H on Re(s)>a. Q=exp(H) is holomorphic and nonzero. On Re(s)>1 it has the required initial value; the identity theorem extends(3) throughout Re(s)>a. Its right side never vanishes, so a zero of L at any fixed height is impossible, with every multiplicity covered. At1 the principal pole has already been canceled by its explicit factor. This proves the proposition.

**What is weaker and what is not.** LP_a allows any fixed logarithmic power in the positive pressure and even arbitrary subpower growth of the finite cutoff. It asks neither for a uniform O(1) finite-volume bound nor a lower pressure bound. The analytic anchor and rapidly converging dyadic increments force actual local convergence. It is nevertheless a complete all-dyadic-cutoff arithmetic hypothesis, not finite evidence, a density-of-good-volumes hypothesis, or a claim that independence proves cancellation. A finite isolated zero is visible to this return, unlike T24's bulk statistic.

### D1.2 A fixed-power quantitative return

There is also a usable budget without an unspecified analytic-continuation loss. Fix a>0,kappa>=0 with a+kappa<1. Assume, for every epsilon>0, some fixed A>=0 and C exist such that for every dyadic y>=2 and all real t,

    |H_y(a+it)| <= C(1+|t|)^A y^(kappa+epsilon).          (P_a,kappa)

A and C may depend on chi and epsilon but not on y,t. This is a separate, two-sided line hypothesis with global height control; it is NOT inferred from LP_a. It implies zero exclusion in Re(s)>a+kappa.

To prove it, choose b>1 and divide f_k(s) by(s+D)^m with D>1 and integer m>A. On the left strip boundary its modulus is O(y^(kappa+epsilon)); on the right it is O(y^(1-b)) by(5). Finite sums in(1) are uniformly bounded in t for each fixed y on the closed strip, so the usual three-lines proof applies after this polynomial denominator; there is no missing horizontal boundary. It gives, locally in t,

    |f_k(s)| << (1+|t|)^m y^E,
    E=((kappa+epsilon)(b-sigma)+(1-b)(sigma-a))/(b-a).     (6)

The exponent is negative when

    sigma > r_b(kappa+epsilon),
    r_b(kappa)=(b kappa+(b-1)a)/(kappa+b-1).

For kappa>0 and a+kappa<1,

    r_b(kappa)=a+kappa+
              kappa(1-a-kappa)/(kappa+b-1) -> a+kappa.   (7)

For any compact with sigma>a+kappa, first fix a sufficiently large finite b and then a sufficiently small epsilon. The dyadic increments sum geometrically; the proof of(3) completes the return. The boundary line is excluded only strictly, as required. The case kappa=0 uses any b>1 and a positive epsilon buffer before its limit.

| Conditional target | a | kappa | Resulting c=1-a-kappa |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| a concrete first gain |3/4|78/625=.1248|313/2500=.1252|
| high-headroom target |3/4|1/12|1/6|
| high-headroom target |2/3|1/12|1/4|

The first row would improve c10 by1351/25000000=.00005404. It requires kappa<theta10-3/4=3121351/25000000=.12485404. This is a conditional target, not an obtained exponent.

**Deliberately coarse actual bound.** Directly from(1), for0<a<1,

    |H_y(a+it)| <= C_a sum_(n<=y)n^-a
                  + integral_2^y u^-a/log2 du
                <= C'_a y^(1-a),                       (8)

uniformly in t. It gives a+kappa=1 and therefore NO improvement. Grouping only the already summable higher-prime-power terms at a>1/2 does not improve(8)'s singleton exponent. The arithmetic saving is precisely what remains open.

**Sharpness of the abstract budget.** For gamma=a+kappa<1 and kappa>0, take the synthetic holomorphic logs

    h_k^*(s)=sum_(j=1)^k 2^(j(gamma-s))/j.

They satisfy the left power budget and the right dyadic-tail budget used above. On Re(s)>gamma their exponentials tend to1/(1-2^(gamma-s)), which has a pole at gamma. Thus these analytic hypotheses alone cannot improve the strict boundary a+kappa. This is not an arithmetic counterexample: the logs are not prime sums. It checks that the return has no hidden unearned saving.

## 4. D2 — phase-balanced prime blocks and a paid complement

This development concerns a fixed NONPRINCIPAL ordinary character. It cannot by itself meet the all-character objective. Let all unramified primes be partitioned into disjoint finite blocks B and an unmatched set U, with finitely many exceptional primes freely moved to U. Assume fixed m,C and common exponents eta>0,delta_U<1 such that

    |B|<=m, r_B=min B,
    max B-r_B <= C r_B^(1-eta),
    sum_(p in B)chi(p)=0 exactly,
    #{p in U:p<=x} <= C x^delta_U for all x>=2.          (PB)

The constants and m may depend on chi; the desired exponent must be common across the characters being covered. Mere short gaps between some primes or approximate phase balance are not PB. It must account for EVERY unramified prime.

**Proposition.** PB implies that L(s,chi) has no zero in

    Re(s)>gamma_B=max(1/2,1-eta,delta_U).                 (9)

Proof. For s in a fixed compact set with sigma>=sigma0>gamma_B, differentiate u^-s along the positive real axis. Exact phase balance gives

    S_B(s)=sum_(p in B)chi(p)p^-s
          =sum_(p in B)chi(p)(p^-s-r_B^-s),
    |S_B(s)| <= m C |s| r_B^(-sigma0-eta).               (10)

Distinct blocks have distinct integer anchors, so their total is absolutely summable when sigma0+eta>1. Also

    sum_p sum_(j>=2) |chi(p)^j p^(-js)|/j
        <= C_sigma0 sum_(n>=2)n^(-2sigma0)<infinity.      (11)

Partial summation of the COMPLETE unmatched counting bound gives absolute convergence of sum_(p in U)p^-s for sigma0>delta_U. Therefore the full series

    sum_B sum_(p in B)log(1-chi(p)p^-s)
      +sum_(p in U)log(1-chi(p)p^-s)                    (12)

converges locally uniformly on Re(s)>gamma_B. Its exponential is nonzero there and agrees with1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. Since nonprincipal L is holomorphic on this domain, multiplying and applying the identity theorem excludes every zero. No reordering of a conditionally convergent series is asserted before(10)-(12); initial agreement uses absolute convergence on Re(s)>1.

For partial products using complete blocks with r_B<=Y and unmatched primes<=Y, the whole omitted logarithm on a fixed compact has the deliberately coarse bound

    O_K(Y^(1-sigma0-eta)+Y^(1-2sigma0)+Y^(delta_U-sigma0)). (13)

Denominators sigma0+eta-1,2sigma0-1 and sigma0-delta_U are positive fixed constants. The three terms price block singleton mass, higher prime powers, and every unmatched prime respectively. Selecting by anchor can include a few primes above Y; it is the defined complete-block cutoff, and(13) already covers its actual complement. Agreement with the natural product is established in the absolute-convergence half-plane, not by dropping boundary blocks.

For a real character, opposite-sign pairs are the m=2 case. For complex characters, two-prime opposition may be impossible, so PB uses exact zero-sum root-of-unity blocks of bounded size. No existence theorem for these blocks is supplied.

**First-gain calibration.** To beat c10 through(9) one needs eta>.12514596 and delta_U<.87485404. The example eta=.1252,delta_U=.8748 would return the same conditional c=.1252 for every covered nonprincipal character. A restricted matching with unmatched counting exponent1 pays no gain, even if its matched sector is perfect. The principal character has no phase-balanced block at all: chi(p)=1 at every unramified prime. Its unmatched set then has exponent1 and its known pole contradicts any purported globally nonvanishing reciprocal continuation through1. The continuous vacuum in D1 is an actual separate repair, not an automatic extension of PB.

**Comparison and next arithmetic action.** W33 already separates the summable higher powers from the singleton; G76 already gives an actual prime-toggle matching for a different completed source. PB instead specifies matching of ordinary prime phases in the Euler logarithm, charges diameter and ALL unmatched primes, and proves its direct natural-L return. It is a candidate arithmetic transport estimate, not a claimed new prime distribution theorem. The next useful test is an actual-character construction proving PB with these common exponents, or a continuous-vacuum analogue for principal chi with its discrepancy paid. A finite matched list, numerical prime gaps, or pair-only formula cannot certify either infinite statement.

## 5. All30 final dispositions

UT means untested: no failure is inferred merely from ancestry. AT means one of the six actual first tests. D1/D2 mark substantive development. Reopen conditions retain the full source and return obligations.

| ID | Disposition and exact remaining work |
|---:|---|
|01|UT; Euler deletion/inverse family, G73/G78. Need the complete multiplier and complementary convolution bound.|
|02|UT; W21/W27 spike and G72 window ancestry. Need actual increment cancellation and the starting value.|
|03|AT duplicate [restricted research revision]/G49; nonzero compact Mellin kernel already exists. New signed arithmetic bound needed.|
|04|UT; G76 matching ancestry. Complex weights and all unmatched vertices remain.|
|05|UT; G18/G60 and observation ancestry. Exact projector tails and cross terms remain.|
|06|UT; W36 finite-prime evolution obstruction is relevant, not an automatic no-go for every resolvent. Need actual source matrix element.|
|07|UT; square-convolution/Liouville ancestry. Need a genuinely stronger lambda estimate and full return.|
|08|UT; logarithmic-derivative and explicit-formula family. Pole competition and all tails remain.|
|09|UT; F22 logarithmic potential. Boundary lower values alone omit winding/zeros.|
|10|UT; fixed phase/cone criterion lacks an actual invariant and complete return.|
|11|UT; renewal/DP/tree ancestry. Need an exact recurrence with a proved contracting arithmetic residual.|
|12|UT; transport family/G76. Complex mass conservation and min-cut price remain.|
|13|UT; W37 finite-prime state/threshold ancestry. Approximate arithmetic compression is still open.|
|14|UT; prime cube/toggle family. Product of(1-chi(p)) replaces unweighted Walsh cancellation.|
|15|UT; F21/dual and signed transport family. Need full signed debt and all boundary terms.|
|16|AT inherited W27/Bjorner unsigned-rank and weighted-commutator obstruction. No new contraction saving.|
|17|UT; exact W27/W31 persistence ancestry. Need a signed invariant beyond total Betti rank.|
|18|UT; raw undefined sheaf draw retained. No topology, source morphism or projection has been constructed.|
|19|UT; Lefschetz label supplies no correspondence. Need an actual operator and trace identity first.|
|20|UT; square-factor transfer remains algebraic until a new estimate is supplied.|
|21|AT+D1; principal finite-volume obstruction plus changed pressure criterion and a+kappa budget. LP/P arithmetic OPEN.|
|22|UT; W27/G74/G79 supertrace ancestry. Positivity is not inherited by a signed trace.|
|23|UT; independent-site mixing does not supply arithmetic continuation; exact KMS object remains undefined.|
|24|AT scoped finite-outlier countertest. Need an outlier-sensitive statistic with actual Euler arithmetic.|
|25|AT+D2; principal block obstruction and nonprincipal PB bridge with three paid tail terms. PB OPEN.|

## 6. Verification, limits and handoff

Proof evidence is the explicit analytic derivation and exact identities above. `checks.py`/`checks.json` independently verify the rational budgets, the complex mod5 block expansion with its ramified zero and unmatched factor, the symmetric four-zero polynomial, and the saved draw/pool consistency. They do not verify an asymptotic arithmetic hypothesis or establish any new zero-free constant. No numerical Mobius/prime sample is used as theorem evidence.

The most useful next action is to seek a real arithmetic estimate for the corrected one-sided pressure, first at a=.87485 under LP_a, or a=3/4,kappa=.1248 under P_a,kappa. The actual coarse bound(8) falls short. PB is a secondary nonprincipal construction problem with an explicit principal-character obstruction. A success on either unproved input must still be independently reviewed and returned through the literal identities.

### E: exact finite decoder obstruction

If a syndrome fibre contains opposite parities x,y, `delta_x-delta_y` lies in the kernel of all unsigned fibre sums but has nonzero signed parity readout. They concern arbitrary inputs on a uniform cube, not a lower bound on the actual detector. A source-specific decoder with a separately paid restricted input class remains open. W38/W41 already require the unexposed arithmetic parity covariance; E does not erase it.

## 7. Uniform S15: retain the resonant scalar, its feedback and the literal H source

This p=1/150 card proposes decimating a resonant mode of the original far-H transfer and controlling the innovation. It was chosen from the original uniform ordering, independently of author outcomes. There is no derived actual scale operator in the seed or author report. I therefore separate the exact native readout from a conditional transfer calculation.

The source remains the same-scale distinct-rational-norm degree-one Eisenstein prime packet, complete bounded short core with every ordered pair including equality, both rooted mark arrays/projectors, natural zeros, ray/unit coefficients, fixed bad places and independent heights. The native transform has factor1/Q, Q=q_pi*q_pi', on a group of size Q^2; its kernel is

    chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4,

with the original CRT phase and angular factors. Its nonzero mask is (h,pi*pi')=1, s!=0 mod pi, s'!=0 mod pi'. The signed short sum is folded into W before taking a norm. These are the [restricted research revision] joint-source contract and G89, not an ordinary-character replacement. No normalization, one-root simplification, favorable height or missing restoration term is allowed.

For the literal counting-measure pairing H_raw=<What,kappa>, kappa=conj(K), use inner product linear in the first slot. For ANY unit vector v let alpha=<What,v>, eta=What-alpha*v and Q_v=I-vv*. Exactly,

    H_raw=alpha*<v,kappa>+<eta,Q_v kappa>.

A small innovation norm controls only the second term; the scalar amplitude and its source coupling remain. The already retained G89 orthogonal projection identity makes the same point for a whole subspace. For the unit/nonunit conditional projection its projected kernel is zero, so generic occupancy does not stand in for native phase contrast. This is full-source bookkeeping, not an H estimate.

Suppose a candidate method actually constructs compatible Hilbert spaces and an exact transfer z_(j+1)=T_j z_j, with all physical scaling and source/tail errors accounted for. Choose unit v_j and write z_j=alpha_j v_j+eta_j, Q_j eta_j=eta_j. Define

    a_j=v_(j+1)* T_j v_j,       b_j=v_(j+1)* T_j Q_j,
    c_j=Q_(j+1)T_j v_j,         D_j=Q_(j+1)T_j Q_j.

The exact two-channel recurrence and its elimination are

    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_j eta_j,
    eta_(j+1)=c_j alpha_j+D_j eta_j,
    eta_j=D_(j-1)...D_0 eta_0
             +sum_(k<j)D_(j-1)...D_(k+1)c_k alpha_k,
    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_jD_(j-1)...D_0 eta_0
             +sum_(k<j)b_jD_(j-1)...D_(k+1)c_k alpha_k.

Empty products are the identity. Every scalar memory term b_j...c_k, initial innovation, sign and phase is retained. Any additive source forcing in an actual T construction must add its corresponding full Duhamel terms; this displayed homogeneous calculation does not silently dispose of them. It is Schur/Feshbach elimination ancestry, not a newly derived arithmetic transfer.

A bounded two-dimensional diagnostic isolates the strongest defect in innovation-only reasoning. Let T=[[1,epsilon],[epsilon,0]], epsilon>0, z_0=(1,0). The innovation propagator D is exactly zero, yet

    alpha_0=alpha_1=1,
    alpha_(j+1)=alpha_j+epsilon^2 alpha_(j-1).

The positive root (1+sqrt(1+4epsilon^2))/2 exceeds1. At epsilon=1/2 the first amplitudes are1,1,5/4,3/2. Replacing the lower-left entry by -epsilon changes the feedback sign; the diagnostic is genuinely sign-sensitive. For a constant two-channel T=[[a,b],[c,d]], the scalar resolvent is 1/[1-a z-bc z^2/(1-d z)], as a local formal/analytic identity. Dropping bc changes the determinant rather than proving stability. None of these ambient examples is asserted to be a native H packet.

**Disposition:** exact elimination is valid; free gain from a small innovation channel is false in the indicated ambient class. The native scale map, its conditioning, scalar source/feedback estimate, complete Gram and all physical error costs remain OPEN. A source-compatible signed feedback bound could still be useful. No native-H lower bound, .004 saving, or exclusion of all resonant-mode methods has been obtained.

## 2. Global asymptotic and the fixed-filter obstruction

The density of squarefree positive integers coprime to d is

    delta(d)=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|d) p/(p+1).

Expanding mu(g)^2=sum_(h^2|g)mu(h), restricting (h,d)=1 and counting the remaining coprime integers gives

    A_d(t)=delta(d)t+O(2^omega(d)sqrt(t)), t>=1.

The main constant is (phi(d)/d)sum_((h,d)=1)mu(h)/h^2, which equals the displayed delta(d). The truncation tail costs O(sqrt(t)); the coprime counting errors cost O(2^omega(d)sqrt(t)). Partial summation, including the boundary term at a real cutoff, gives

    sum_(g>t;(g,d)=1)mu(g)^2 g^(-2r)
      =delta(d)t^(1-2r)/(2r-1)
        +O_r(2^omega(d)t^(1/2-2r)).                       (R2)

Insert this into (R1) when min(a,b)<=N. The error sum is absolutely finite: for a<=b, using 2^omega(abq)<<_q (ab)^(1/4), its summand is at most a^(-1/4)b^(1/4-2r); summing b first leaves O(a^(1-2r)). The region min(a,b)>N contributes O(N^(2-4r)) both to the exact expression and to the proposed main term. This is smaller than N^(1/2-2r) for r>=2. Consequently the author's

    ||R_N||_2^2 = C_r(q)N^(1-2r)+O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r))

and its signed, absolutely convergent formula for C_r(q) are correct.

Parseval on both first bands and the same squarefree count give

    C_r(q)>=2delta(q)(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1)>0.

This positivity is proved without termwise positivity of the signed gcd series. It is independent of the particular chi at the fixed admissible r,q. Subtracting the scalar main term destroys the nonnegative-measure inequality that bounded an arc by the whole period. The half-power error is therefore not an arc estimate and does not give c=1/4.

For fixed 0<lambda_1<...<lambda_J, the author's earliest-nonzero-coefficient band argument is valid with floors. Choose B strictly between that lambda_j and min(2lambda_j,lambda_(j+1)); the positive interval after floor(lambda_j N) and before BN sees only that source. The squarefree count supplies a positive limiting mass. The finite-dimensional compactness argument extends this to all unit vectors of coefficients, including N-dependent ones: the uniformly bounded scaled norms make coefficient convergence imply convergence in scaled field norm. No uniformity as J grows or gaps close is obtained.

An independently derived quantitative strengthening makes this especially explicit. Define

    M_jk=2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      *sum_((a,b)=1;(ab,q)=1) mu(a)mu(b)delta(abq)/(ab)^(2r)
          *max(lambda_j/a,lambda_k/b)^(1-2r).              (R3)

The same summable majorants prove absolute convergence. For fixed scales,

    <R_floor(lambda_jN),R_floor(lambda_kN)>
      =N^(1-2r) M_jk + O_(q,r,lambda)(N^(1/2-2r)).         (R4)

To handle the floors, the exact threshold is max(floor(lambda_jN)/a,floor(lambda_kN)/b). Its difference from N times the threshold in (R3) is O(1/min(a,b)); the induced main-term error sums to O(N^(-2r)). Thresholds below 1 are handled by the same O(N^(2-4r)) outer tail. The matrix M is real symmetric by swapping a,b. It is positive definite by the earliest-band lower bound for every nonzero vector. Thus the scaled Gram matrix tends to a positive definite matrix at rate O(N^(-1/2)); its smallest eigenvalue is eventually at least half that of M. This proves the uniform coercivity with an explicit limiting object, but does not price growing J or colliding scales.

statement:
# Independent square-collision refinement — proof record



## 1. Exact universal collision count

For real D>=1 let W_D(n)=#{d<=D: n/d is an integer square}. Then, uniformly
for Y>=1,

    sum_{n<=Y} W_D(n)^2 << sqrt(Y D).                    (I1)

The implicit constant is absolute. To prove this, write every pair of
possible physical multipliers with the same squarefree kernel as
d1=a u^2,d2=a v^2, a squarefree. Their common square multiples are
n=a l^2 with l a multiple of lcm(u,v). Thus the exact identity is

    sum_{n<=Y} W_D(n)^2
      = sum_{a squarefree; a<=D} sum_{u,v<=sqrt(D/a)}
          floor(sqrt(Y/a)/lcm(u,v)).                    (I2)

Pairs with different squarefree kernels have no common square multiple.
Using floor(t)<=t and then interchanging the nonnegative sums gives

    LHS <= sqrt(Y) sum_{u,v>=1} gcd(u,v)/(uv)
                  sum_{a<=D/max(u,v)^2} a^(-1/2)
        <= 2sqrt(YD) sum_{u,v>=1} gcd(u,v)/(uv max(u,v)).

The last series converges. Write u=g h,v=g k with gcd(h,k)=1 and drop
that last restriction: it is bounded by

    (sum_g g^(-2)) 2 sum_{k>=1} k^(-2) sum_{h<=k} h^(-1),

which is finite by H_k<=1+log k. This proves (I1), including all repeated
physical multipliers, exact diagonal collisions and nonintegral cutoffs.
It imports no arithmetic cancellation or outside counting theorem.

## 2. Application after the exact row-dependent removals

Use the author's Q_D, with arbitrary shell-fixed |u_d|<=1 and arbitrary
shell-fixed root prefixes, retaining both e=1,p rows and q1(e). Remove
precisely each low prefix r<=c0(X/(ed))^(6/11), as in the author's proof.
Its full norm is O(D). Let z(n) be the complete merged remaining coefficient.
Every contributing physical multiplier ed is <=pD and has at most two
e-label realizations, so

    |z(n)| <= C_p W_{pD}(n),
    sum_{n<=Y}|z(n)|^2 <<_p sqrt(YD).                  (I3)

This remains true after arbitrary row-dependent prefix masks because it is
coefficient domination by a positive multiplicity count. It does not invoke
domination of one signed norm by a signed subset. The strict support
n>N0=c0^2 p^(-1/11)X^(12/11)D^(-1/11) is unchanged.

In a comparable dyadic block n,m~N, let H=X^6/N^5. The smooth-shell kernel
is bounded by exp(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,(H/|n-m|)^2), with diagonal value1.
For every n, the full unweighted integer row sum is O(1+H). Indeed the
off-diagonal sum over integer distances is O(H) if H>=1, and O(H^2)<=O(H)
if H<1. Applying 2|z(n)z(m)|<=|z(n)|^2+|z(m)|^2 and (I3) pays the COMPLETE
block by

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) sqrt(ND)(1+H).                   (I4)

The author's independent multiplicity-local-count bound for the same
complete block is

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) [H D+sqrt(ND) E_N],
    E_N=min(N^(1/3),D).                              (I5)

Both bound the same positive expansion, including its diagonal. Taking
their minimum, then using min(A+B,C)<=A+min(B,C) for nonnegative A,B,C,
gives an upper bound by a constant times

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) [H D+sqrt(ND)(1+min(E_N,H))].     (I6)

No intersection of signed subsets is involved. Differences in fixed kernel
constants are absorbed into a common fixed constant and weaker exponential.

Sum H D over N>=N0 to obtain X^(6/11)D^(16/11). The isolated1 in (I6)
costs X^(3/4)D^(1/2) by actual damping over the entire infinite dyadic sum.
The remaining dyadic sum can be extended to all N>=1 and bounded without
damping. Its summand is

    sqrt(ND) min(N^(1/3),D,X^6 N^(-5)).

It grows geometrically until the decreasing third entry meets the first
two, and then decays as N^(-9/2). If D<=X^(3/8), the meeting occurs at
N=X^(6/5)D^(-1/5), where its value is X^(3/5)D^(7/5). If D>=X^(3/8),
it occurs at N=X^(9/8), where the value is X^(15/16)D^(1/2). Thus its
sum is bounded by the smaller of those two expressions. All geometric
exponents are separated from zero, so there is no logarithmic loss.

Far pairs retain the author's O(D^2) total: on max(n,m)~N the full gap
kernel is O(X^12 N^(-12)), while both the shell mass and cumulative mass
are O(sqrt(ND)); summing from N0 gives X^12 D N0^(-11)=O(D^2).
Both orientations are included. The triangle inequality between complete
low and high sources pays their mixed term.

Consequently the full source satisfies the strengthened uniform estimate

    ||Q_D||_2^2 << D^2 + X^(6/11)D^(16/11)
                    + X^(3/4)D^(1/2)
                    + min(X^(3/5)D^(7/5),X^(15/16)D^(1/2)). (I7)

All quantifiers of the author's short-source theorem are preserved.

## 3. Complete-core consequence and limits

For D=X^alpha the norm exponents are

    alpha, (3+8alpha)/11, 3/8+alpha/4,
    min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4).

For every fixed gamma in[3/4,1), all are <=gamma whenever

    alpha <= (11gamma-3)/8.                           (I8)

Indeed alpha<gamma; the third exponent is at most(11gamma+9)/32;
the last is <=9/16 when alpha<=3/8 and otherwise at most
(11gamma+12)/32<=gamma. The first two conditions hold by construction.
Endpoint equality is allowed. Thus the complete replacement-source theorem
and its conditional all-height return hold on the larger closed corridor

    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= (11gamma-3)/8.

This agrees with the author's corridor for gamma>=17/21 and improves it
for 3/4<=gamma<17/21. At gamma=3/4 it gives alpha<=21/32 and
tau in[1/8,7/8], in place of alpha<=1/2 and tau in[1/3,2/3]. At gamma=5/6
and at the nearer first-gain target the author's endpoints are unchanged.
Every small-double, low-core, high-core and Mellin term remains as in the
original complete theorem. The actual signed OPEN-LC estimate remains open.

The refinement is a completed restricted source bound, not a zero-free gain
and not a claim that the Liouville core is easier than the Mobius core.
Novelty is relative to the inspected project record; no literature priority
is asserted. Root review must adjudicate the proof before acceptance.

The Gamma integral yields, for r>0,

    E_(r,nu)(z)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity
       q^(r-1)e^-q g_(2(nu+q))(z)dq,
    E_(0,nu)(z)=g_(2nu)(z).

Its Fourier multiplier is exactly `e^(-nu*t²)(1+t²)^-r`, with the `(2pi)^-1` inversion factor already in the Gaussian. Consequently

    N_r² = sum_(n,m) a(n)conj(a(m)) b_n b_m
               E_(r,nu)(alpha log(n/m)).               (R5)

The double series converges absolutely since `E(z)<=E(0)<=g_(2nu)(0)` and `sum |a|b<infinity`. All ordered pairs, powers and natural character zeros remain. E is positive, but this does not make the coefficient products nonnegative or authorize removal of negative cross terms. For bounded coefficients the true diagonal is `O(X)` uniformly in r; divisor-bounded coefficients permit the stated epsilon allowance. The diagonal can be paid below `X^(2eta)` only with the corresponding eta>1/2 buffer; positivity is not a substitute for cancellation at smaller eta.

For `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)` the character twist is pointwise. The symbol `*` in later coefficient identities denotes Dirichlet convolution. Mellin Fubini first on Re s>1 gives

    integral_0^infinity F(x)x^-s dx/x = e^(tau*s²/2)/L(s,chi).

R4 plus dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz gives absolute locally uniform Mellin convergence on `Re s>gamma=eta+d/2`; the small-x Gaussian bound handles zero. Multiplying the meromorphic identity by L excludes any zero in that half-plane. A principal pole at 1 is handled by the usual cancelling zero of the reciprocal, not treated as an L-zero. This proof covers arbitrarily large finite heights without requiring an unproved uniform reciprocal growth estimate on a continued line. No X-dependent source was Mellin transformed.

For the literal f3 twist, an explicit scope check is useful. Its prime-power values are `f3(p^j)=-1` for p!=3,j>=1, and `f3(3^j)=1`. With `z_p=chi(p)p^-s`, the numerator in `D_(f3 chi)=W_chi/L(s,chi)` is

    W_chi = (1-2z_2)/[(1-z_2)²(1-z_3)²]
               product_(p>=5) (1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)².        (R6)

Zero-extended ramified factors mean z_p=0. The p>=5 product converges normally and is nonzero for Re s>1/2; the p2 factor can have zeros on Re s=1, not in `1/2<Re s<1`. Thus the paid f3 return is valid in the open target strip, with the already known right boundary retained. One must not claim that W_chi is nonzero everywhere on the line Re s=1. This qualification agrees with the established G28/G53 source returns and requires no modification to A's useful claim.

For the original ideal Möbius coefficient, the analogous Mellin identity has numerator 1 and its own Hecke L-function. A separately proved full ideal moment is required; an ordinary f3 estimate does not imply it. Fixed ordinary characters and the originally specified fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke family are the available scopes. No angular, growing-conductor, or generic-character uniformity follows from notation alone.

**Verdict A:** accept R1–R6 and A1–13/A10 as a conditional analytic interface. The exact complete R5/A13 arithmetic bound remains open. Fixed-order negative norms and Gaussian spectral localization are prior; the useful increment here is the exact localized source, arbitrary moving order and explicit `d/2` budget, not a new negative-norm mechanism or a proved weaker arithmetic exponent. The Sol01 S45 norm was on a raw finite atomic measure over the full line; it is not this already smoothed and localized norm.

statement:
## 2. Full fixed-phase theorem

Let b>1, integer k>=4, and bounded mean-zero Q-periodic h be fixed. For any finite real D>=1 and any complex |A_m|<=A, frozen before x, put

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k),
    H_D(x)=sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1) h(l) f_x(ml).

Then, uniformly in D and the entire bounded bank,

    ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2 << A(D+X^(b/2)) log^4(2X).            (H)

There is no arbitrary joint mask in (m,l), live-x bank, growing period or undamped infinite bank in this statement. Divisor losses become X^epsilon only when the relevant m range is bounded by a fixed power of X.

### 2.1 Exact output partition and low source

Choose a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi equal to one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity), and set w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t). For every n>0,

    1=phi(n/X)+sum_(N=2^j X,j>=0) w(n/N).

This is an exact telescoping identity, with w supported in [1,4]. For each finite D all rearrangements first follow from the original exponential damping. The final bounds also prove summability of the block norms.

On the low part, expand h(l)=sum_(1<=j<Q) beta_j exp(2pi i j l/Q). For m<=delta X, the phase derivative in l is

    j/Q - (k/(2pi))(m/x)^k l^(k-1).

On the entire low support ml<=2X, including an extra integer for the last discrete increment, its correction is O_k(m/X). Choose fixed delta sufficiently small relative to Q,k. The derivative is monotone, lies between two consecutive integers with a fixed gap, and the reciprocal discrete-increment factor has bounded total variation. Discrete summation by parts gives O_(Q,k)(1) for every undamped prefix. Abel summation with phi(ml/X) exp(-ml/x^b), a bounded monotone weight, pays the actual damped low row. For m>delta X any nonempty low row has m<=2X and at most 2/delta terms. Hence the entire low source costs O(A min(D,X))<=O(AD). No D<X hypothesis was used.

### 2.2 Exact Poisson transform and uniform stationary term

Fix a high output block N and put T=(N/X)^k>=1. Remove exactly empty rows m>4N before transformation. Group the remaining m into frozen dyadic intervals [M,2M) intersect [1,D] intersect [1,4N]. Thus m/N<=4 and M<=4N. Extend the smoothly supported summand by zero to all real n and apply Poisson to the periodic Fourier expansion. With the appropriate periodic Fourier coefficients beta_h,

    sum_l h(l) w(ml/N) f_x(ml)
      =(1/m) sum_(h in Z) beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    beta_(Qj)=0,
    I_r(x)=int_0^infinity w(n/N)e^(-n/x^b)
                          exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^k]) dn.      (2.1)

The integer alias h here is distinct from the original periodic sequence h(l). Both alias signs and every nonzero Fourier residue occur. Mean zero deletes every beta_(Qj), not just the single zero alias.

For r>0 the unique critical point is

    n_r=(2pi r/(kQ))^(1/(k-1)) x^(k/(k-1)),
    Phi_r=(k-1)(2pi r/(kQ))^(k/(k-1)) x^(k/(k-1)),
    Z_r=sqrt(2pi/[k(k-1)]) x^(k/2) n_r^(-(k-2)/2)
                                      w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^b).

Fix a near range cT/N<=r<=CT/N, with constants depending only on Q,k, wide enough to contain every critical point meeting the smooth output support for all x in [X,2X]. Write x=Xz, n=Nt, rho=N/X^b and R=rN/T. The normalized phase is

    T psi_(R,z)(t), psi=2pi Rt/Q-t^k/z^k.

Here z in [1,2], R in a fixed positive compact interval, and the critical point t0 lies in another fixed positive compact interval. Its second derivative is negative and bounded away from zero there. Every fixed derivative of the damped amplitude w(t)e^(-rho t/z^b) is O_j(e^(-c rho)) on the positive support, with a smaller fixed c after absorbing powers of rho.

For completeness, choose a uniformly small smooth neighborhood of t0. Away from it, two integrations by parts give O(T^-2 e^(-c rho)). Near it, the one-dimensional Morse coordinate

    y=sign(t-t0) sqrt(psi(t0)-psi(t))

has uniformly bounded derivatives and inverse derivatives. The transformed compact amplitude B has the same derivative bounds and B(0)=a(t0)sqrt(2/|psi''(t0)|). Write B(y)=B(0)kappa(y)+y C(y), with a fixed even bump kappa equal to one near zero. The y C term is O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)) by one integration by parts; the kappa term is the Fresnel integral plus a smaller nonstationary error. This gives, after restoring N,

    I_r=Z_r exp(i Phi_r-i pi/4)
                  +O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^b)).                   (2.2)

The argument is uniform even when t0 crosses either endpoint of w's smooth support: the amplitude, extended smoothly by zero, remains in the same bounded family. No sharp output truncation was substituted inside a stationary formula. No derivative of the remainder is needed later.

### 2.3 Every alias remainder is paid

Put H_m=mT/N. The near integer bank has O(1+H_m) aliases, and if nonempty then H_m is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. Thus the sum of (2.2)'s remainders after the original factor 1/m is O(e^(-cN/X^b)). This includes the case of an empty near bank.

For nonstationary positive aliases below the near range, at most O(H_m) terms occur, each bounded by O(N T^-2 e^(-cN/X^b)). Negative aliases have the stronger bound O(N(T+N|h|/m)^-2 e^(-cN/X^b)); summing them after 1/m costs O(T^-1 e^(-cN/X^b)). The full positive tail above the near range costs

    e^(-cN/X^b) (m/N) sum_(h>cH_m,h>=1) h^-2
       << e^(-cN/X^b)(T^-1+m/N).

Because m/N<=4, every complete row remainder is O(e^(-cN/X^b)), uniformly in the original finite D. Summing the entire row-block error costs O(AM e^(-cN/X^b)) in either norm. Its interaction with the stationary bank is paid by the norm triangle, before any Gram estimate.

### 2.4 Complete reduced-frequency bank and shell Gram

Reduce the positive near alias r=h/m=u/v, (u,v)=1. Since the ENTIRE Z_r and Phi_r depend only on r,N,x, exact grouping gives

    C_(u/v)=sum_(vj in the original row block) A_(vj) beta_(uj)/(vj).

It is frozen before x, includes every collision and Fourier zero, and satisfies |C_(u/v)|<<A/v by summing 1/j on the truncated ratio-two interval. Moreover u>=1 and r<=CT/N force the essential lower denominator floor v>=N/(CT). Consequently

    sum_r |C_r|^2
      << A^2 sum_(max(1,N/(CT))<=v<=2M) (vT/N+1)/v^2
      << A^2 (T/N) log(2M).                               (2.3)

If the lower floor exceeds 2M, the bank is empty. If the floor is at most one, T/N is already bounded below, so the +1 count still has the stated price. Dropping this floor would introduce an unpaid term.

On the fixed real z interval, the explicit amplitudes satisfy

    |Z_r|+|dZ_r/dz| << (N/sqrt(T))e^(-cN/X^b).

By the mean value theorem and the near-range bounds,

    |d_z(Phi_r-Phi_s)| is comparable to N|r-s|,
    |d_z^2(Phi_r-Phi_s)| << |d_z(Phi_r-Phi_s)|.

One integration by parts in the entire sharp shell, retaining both endpoints and the weight 1/z, therefore bounds the full inner product by

    (N^2/T)e^(-cN/X^b) min(1,1/(N|r-s|)).                 (2.4)

The diagonal uses minimum one. Distinct reduced fractions with denominators <=2M are separated by 1/(4M^2). Their number is J<<M+M^2T/N, and log(2+J)<<_k log(2N) since M<=4N, X>=2 and k is fixed. The complete positive kernel row sum is O(1+(M^2/N)log(2N)). Applying 2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 to every pair and using (2.3) yields

    ||whole (M,N) block||_2^2
      << A^2 e^(-cN/X^b)(N+M^2) log^2(2N).               (2.5)

This includes the already paid entire row error by norm triangle. No diagonal, close frequency, or either off-diagonal orientation is omitted.

### 2.5 Infinite completion and arbitrary D

Sum WHOLE block norms. For fixed N there are O(log(2N)) row blocks; the M terms sum to O(min(D,N)). Thus the high source is bounded by

    A sum_(N=2^jX) e^(-cN/X^b)
           [sqrt(N)log^2(2N)+min(D,N)log(2N)].

For each fixed b>1 the first sum is O(X^(b/2)log^2(2X)); the second is O(D log^2(2X)). The tail beyond N comparable to X^b is exponentially summable, with all differentiated damping already absorbed. Adding the low source proves (H), with the stated conservative log^4. This norm-triangle completion pays all cross terms between low/high sources, distinct row blocks and distinct output blocks. Finite-measure Cauchy gives L1. Arbitrarily large finite D creates no log D because rows m>4N were removed exactly first.

## 8. Uniform independent audit W49-20

The seed asks whether cutoff/prime-factor commutators telescope into a small boundary. Here the final observation functional decides what the boundary means.

Let P_Y project integer coefficient vectors to n<=Y, with integer Y>=1, and S_p e_n=e_(pn). Exactly

    [P_Y,S_p]e_n=-1_(Y/p<n<=Y)e_(pn).                   (R16)

Every nonzero output is above Y. Consequently P_Y S_p(I-P_Y)=0 and P_Y[P_Y,S_p]=0. For A_p=I-chi(p)S_p and any finite ordered list of distinct primes,

    P_Y A_(p1)...A_(pk) P_Y
      =P_Y A_(p1) P_Y A_(p2) P_Y ... A_(pk) P_Y.        (R17)

Every path is a forward integer dilation, so a path that leaves the prefix never returns. This proves (R17) including every expanded cross term, not by estimating each commutator separately. Also the compressed S_p commute: P_Y S_p P_Y S_q P_Y=P_Y S_p S_q P_Y. The assertion uses a divisor-closed integer prefix; it is false for arbitrary projections.

If every prime<=Y is present, applying either side to e_1 gives precisely mu(n)chi(n) for all n<=Y, with character zeros and squarefree signs. Summing the output still gives the original M_chi(Y). Thus the proposed sharp-cutoff commutator correction is killed by the final projection exactly; it does not make the remaining arithmetic output small. This is a stronger prefix form of the G69 causal mechanism used by first test16, rather than an independent cancellation theorem.

For the physical Gaussian readout the same boundary is NOT killed. Write

    g_tau(u)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2tau)), tau>0,
    ell_x(v)=sum_n v_n g_tau(log(n/x)).

Then the literal boundary readout is

    ell_x([P_Y,S_p]v)
      =-sum_(Y/p<n<=Y)v_n g_tau(log(pn/x)).              (R18)

The multiplier -chi(p) must be retained when replacing [P_Y,S_p] by [P_Y,A_p], as must the signed input v and all interactions from the other prime factors. A sharp-output zero is not a Gaussian zero.

There is a fully paid way to remove a distant integer tail. For |a_n|<=1 and integer Y>=x, monotonicity beyond x and completing the square give

    sum_(n>Y)|a_n|g_tau(log(n/x))
      <=integral_Y^infinity g_tau(log(t/x))dt
      =x exp(tau/2) barPhi((log(Y/x)-tau)/sqrt(tau)).     (R19)

Here barPhi is the upper standard-normal distribution tail. Fix a dyadic X and take

    Y_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))).

Uniformly X<=x<=2X, (R19) is at most X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). Choosing C>sqrt(2tau(1-gamma)) puts it below any desired fixed gamma<1 with a buffer. The finite Euler product over primes<=Y_X agrees with the actual mu*chi coefficients through Y_X; its remaining difference from the full coefficients has modulus<=1 and lies beyond that cutoff. Thus (R19) also pays the COMPLETE finite-Euler-to-fixed-Gaussian return, with no coefficient replacement at small integers. It promises no computational economy: the finite Euler product can have a huge support.

The surviving open input is still a bound for the complete signed retained output. Neither (R17) nor (R19) provides it. No transfer to native H's noncausal arithmetic projectors is claimed. This audit preserves the seed's potentially useful distinction between a terminal functional and an operator commutator, while locating its sharp-cutoff version within G69 and its tail payment within the existing Gaussian-tail contracts. Original uniform choice20 is unchanged; there was no redraw after seeing test16.

## 6. Reviewer extension: exact polynomial-hole and Gram transfers

For each fixed finite radical Q, the complete field satisfies

    U_Q(x)=sum_(d Q-smooth) eta(d) U(x/q_d),
    U(x)=sum_(d|Q) mu(d)eta(d) U_Q(x/q_d).                (R19)

These follow coefficientwise from the finite Euler factors and are
absolutely convergent Gaussian identities. For every sigma,delta>0,

    prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-sigma)^(-1) <<_(sigma,delta) q_Q^delta.

Thus if the ONE original U has every-epsilon shell Lp exponent gamma>0,
p=1 or2, all its polynomial-sized holes q_Q<=X^A have the same shell
exponent, uniformly with an arbitrarily small extra loss. Small shifted
scales are included through the Gaussian left tail. Q is frozen during
each convolution; no moving family is falsely identified across scales.

It follows that, whenever(R8), or the appropriate one-sided error gate,
is paid, the complete averaged POSITIVE cofactor energy bound
B_FE<<X^(2gamma+epsilon) is equivalent to U's complete shell-L2 exponent
gamma. The reverse direction is Jensen, fixed-source approximation and
the fixed inverse(R6). This equivalence does not identify the L1 and L2
hypotheses. It identifies where the same unresolved arithmetic survives.

There is also an exact full limiting Gram for the f-only average.
Let K_X(a,b)=integral_X^(2X) g_tau(log(q_a/x))g_tau(log(q_b/x)) dx/x
and p_F(d)=N_F^-1 #{f in Fset:(f,d)=1}. The finite positive energy is

    B_F^sf=sum_(a,b) mu(a)mu(b)eta(a)bar(eta(b))
                           K_X(a,b) p_F(rad(ab)).        (R20)

All a,b are S-coprime. The averaged FIELD squared instead uses
p_F(a)p_F(b); confusing these loses label covariance. In the fixed
limit, p_F(rad(ab))->A(rad(ab)), and

    A(rad(ab))=A(a)A(b) sum_(d|gcd(a,b)) q_d^-1

on the actual squarefree a,b support.

Consequently its full limiting energy is

    sum_(d squarefree,(d,S)=1) q_d^-1
       ||sum_(d|a) mu(a)eta(a)A(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x))||_2^2. (R21)

The d=1 term is ||W_A||_2^2; all other terms are the positive label
variance. Absolute Gaussian majorants justify the complete identities.
They do not bound that variance or its signed inner arithmetic.

Replacing(R20) by(R21) at a GROWING shell costs
O(X^2 F^-1/2 log(2F)) over K, or
O(X^2 F^-1/2(1+log(2+X))^2) over Z. To pay this ENERGY approximation
at exponent2-2c requires v>=4c, not the v>=2c needed for the FIELD
return(R16). This is a concrete guard against an apparently free limit

## A rigorous positive part of the critical-window profile

Completing the Gaussian square gives

    J_tau(v)=exp(tau/2) integral_0^infinity
                   t g_tau(t+v-tau)dt.

If v>=3tau and h>=0, its pointwise integrand comparison gives

    J_tau(v+h)/J_tau(v)
       <= exp(-(v-tau)h/tau-h²/(2tau)) <= exp(-2h).              (CT7)

For q>=exp(3tau), the r=1 term is J_tau(logq)>0 and the absolute total
of all r>=2 terms is at most

    J_tau(logq) sum_(r>=2) r^-3 <= (1/4)J_tau(logq),

using1/8+integral_2^infinity t^-3 dt=1/4. Since f(1)=1 and |f(r)|=1,
CT2 follows. On the compact q interval[kappa²/2,kappa²], this lower
bound is a fixed positive constant. Thus CT1 is eventually positive
uniformly over the entire shell, even if its constant is small.

# W40 — signed boundary budgets, the cost of positivity, and long projector cycles

Unreviewed frozen-author mathematics for independent review. This packet proves no larger zero-free constant and does not change the accepted written analytic c4=25027/200000=.125135. That premise retains its stated PR9/Gao dependencies and pending endpoint/kernel work. The older c0 has its separate completed kernel evidence.



## Outcome and compact checkpoint

The highest-reach development is an explicit **signed-boundary negative-mass criterion**, followed by a decisive arithmetic failure of its bare normalization. The sharp generic disk budget is (1-r)^2/(4r), and its complete conditional returns include c=.125136, 1/6 and 1/4. However, a primary-source universality theorem proves that the actual bare pole-removed zeta boundary has UNBOUNDED negative mass as height varies. That all-height hypothesis is impossible. A genuinely changed, zero-preserving normalization has an exact return but an OPEN estimate. No moment/H gaps are combined. A finite-height quadrature/height-net certificate has a stated error budget; no numerical certificate was executed.

The rare selection15 gives an exact **minimum positive-repair theorem for the literal f3 source**: retaining its entire prime-presence algebra forces positive correction mass asymptotic to exp(tau/2)x/2. Thus a correction of order X^gamma with gamma<1 cannot make that signed functional positive. This is a source-specific consequence of an elementary Jordan-decomposition dual, not a new general GNS theorem. W38 and W39 already supply related parity and total-variation facts; their credit is retained.

The wildcard25 gives a quantitative **rank-one projector holonomy theorem** and an exact long-cycle counterexample. A fixed phase pi is compatible with cyclic product magnitude tending to1. The loss is only O(1/N) on an N-cycle. This refines the old U-FLUX warning by pricing cycle length; no embedding of native H into these rank-one chains is proved.

All six frozen first tests were completed. Developments20,15,25 protect the highest-reach, rare and wildcard selections. The strongest-bridge11 test fails for the proposed whole-operator majorant of the actual critical split, using a canonical rough-block lower bound. Tests29 and28 give a phase-occupancy obstruction and an exact arithmetic bar-differential defect. These failures do not disprove changed architectures.

Remaining: independent mathematical review, then only a changed boundary normalization with an actual reason to survive Section2.4, or an admissible restricted operator system. The bare boundary criterion is rejected as an all-height route. No new c is authorized by this handoff.

## 1. Frozen generation and selection
