# PR15 local physical moment review — pinned head ca182b70



## Current disposition and exact scope

The local physical-moment argument is **proved relative to the named accepted [private research revision]/PR9 analytic inputs**, with the transfers described below. I found no mathematical obstruction in the six assigned analytical supplements. The crucial new steps are the joint count of actual signed rows and first labels, the unmarked density with a threshold before height, and the post-transform low-bin use of the old moment. These are substantive written arguments; their status does not follow merely from the supporting Lean component checks.

This disposition is limited to the local estimate with coefficient `C = 2249/500 = 4.498`, in the stated narrow length window and for the stated fixed natural family. The proposed endpoint `b = 4374433/5000000` and `c = 0.1251134` require the separately owned endpoint/continuation argument. The accepted research baseline remains `c0 = 0.125113352960035869...` unless the controller accepts the complete new proof. In particular, this review does not transfer acceptance to `[restricted mathematical source]`, which is a different Gaussian proposal with open signed covariance.

The source author is **Zhongpai Gao (Gaozhongpai), with AI assistance**. Credit for the new local-moment refinement and its written bridges belongs to Gao as submitted. The imported quartic moment, unrestricted zero-slot input, detector, natural Hecke machinery, and old endpoint framework retain their distinct upstream OpenAI / Hailey Collet / Akash Levy attribution. I make no claim of literature priority beyond this submission and our existing record.

Completed: read the concise paper and all six assigned full analytical supplements; inspected the relevant new Lean components; fetched and inspected exact upstream constructors at the PR9 pin; checked signed rows, both transforms, natural conductor, fixed exclusion, low-bin restrictions, joint labels, height order, compact uniformity, and source-relative local assembly. Final independent challenges found no additional obstruction. Endpoint assembly and overall acceptance remain with their assigned owners. The full readback and SHA-256 are reported in the external controller handoff; no self-referential hash is embedded here.

## Evidence and pin discipline

PR15: [GTimG/QuasiRiemannTracker #15](https://github.com/GTimG/QuasiRiemannTracker/pull/15), pinned head `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`. The controller's immutable receipts are `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]` and `source-verification.json`: 57 selected added files reconstructed from complete GitHub patches and matched to their Git blob identities. I treated these receipts as source provenance, not as mathematical validation. I did not use the submission's internal AI reviews as proof.

Main structural source: [paper.tex](https://github.com/Gaozhongpai/QuasiRiemannTracker/blob/ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef/proofs/gao-local-moment-20261011-paper/paper.tex), blob `5b45d826f98a7e307de7511447201229a5524c7d`, local SHA-256 `549b5e12802c61c3030606b89d7a05726c3b2e231c4b9f253f5092504a55aeae`.

Assigned analytical sources, all beneath `proofs/gao-local-moment-20261011-v3/` at this head:

- `PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex` (PLA below), especially lines 20–64 (statement/quantifiers), 135–156 (joint first target), 164–210 (actual main radius), 212–293 (low rows), 295–379 (joint high rows), 381–438 (errors/exceptional), 439–488 (heights/recovery/scope).
- `SignedReconstruction.tex` (SR), especially lines 10–50 (signs and natural zeros), 52–94 (complete frequency), 96–148 (two projectors and arbitrary valuations).
- `FixedDictionaryBridge.tex` (FD), blob `88007f82e9f4160d82db7e731d305ab30d958b08`, especially lines 11–63, 65–149, 151–184.
- `RestrictedCanonicalSource.tex` (RC), the literal arbitrary-keep allocated-child bridge and its scope restrictions.
- `PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex` (PD), especially lines 49–117 (actual empty-slot plain input), 130–224 (height-uniform density and two different height exponents).
- `FourierMaskTransport.tex` (FM), blob `8130671b2094388dbc6c2d35eba32f4b366a4236`, especially lines 12–75 (Euler holes), 77–159 (joint Fourier transport), 161–173 (height order).

The exact PR9 source pin is `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`. Its manuscript is `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, blob `ae5d0488c155d35f10b39038f7b9b9f2d5e00071`, SHA-256 `2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8`. I compared B3.41–B3.79 and the surrounding natural-family/old-moment statements. The local absence of the whole advertised 3232-source archive was not replaced by the unrelated older 4/33 archive. Missing exact constructors were obtained read-only from the PR9 GitHub pin. Full source URL and blob list is at the end of this report.

The baseline independent maintainer receipt summarized in `[restricted mathematical source]` supports only the accepted PR9 source. New PR15 claims of 15 compiled components and 48 standard-axiom checks remain component evidence; I neither reran a clean dependency build nor an independent kernel check. The controller reported passing rational replays in `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`; those confirm numerical inequalities, not any character or analytic interface.

## Exact local theorem under review

Work over the Eisenstein integers with the accepted nontrivial contradiction branch `51/100 <= beta_* <= 7/8`. Fix the natural parent family of PR9 B3.4: fixed finite ray factor times the literal extended sextic row character, fixed ray modulus, fixed slot anchor, literal nonzero proper fixed exclusion ideal `Q_*`, and the original canonical prime pools with one common annular slot profile and their original allowed relative ray characters. The parent has no moving support of positive width. A further common puncture of norm at most `U^B` may depend on frozen outer labels but is independent of the row currently being summed. The smooth source radial majorant and the literal `not FixedInducingRow` gate are retained.

Put `U = Z^M`, `A = n1+n2+z`, and `C = 2249/500`. The local window is

`0.41 M <= n1,n2 <= 0.44 M`, `0.03 M <= z <= 0.04 M`, `n1+n2+Cz <= M`.

For each requested loss `epsilon>0`, sufficiently fine canonical slots give the exact natural moment bounded by `Z^(M+epsilon) H_J`, where `H_J` is a finite smooth-seminorm/polynomial-height control for the two independent plain profiles and the original slot heights. The same estimate holds for all four logarithmic scale-derivative profile pairs used in two-variable supremum recovery. The finite dictionary may affect the constants, height/seminorm orders and eventual threshold. It does not set the initial mesh or slot widths.

The genuine local improvement is `9/2 - C = 1/500`. This is not a claim of a global `C`-moment for all lengths. All descendant mean values used in this proof are the **old** `9/2` moment or its separate unrestricted zero-slot theorem. No strengthened descendant induction is assumed.

## 1. The actual source family, signs, zeros and fixed ideal

**Classification: compatible after a proved source transfer; no change to the accepted family.**

The ideal convention is important: `Q subseteq m` means that `m` divides `Q`, not a numerical norm inequality. For the source family `F` and slot anchor `eta0`, the fixed ideal is literally

`Q_* = internalQ(F.modulus intersect (72), eta0)
      = F.modulus intersect (72) intersect q_eta0`.

This remains fixed after extraction; the moving child whole-product character `tau` is not substituted for the anchor in `internalQ`. The source theorem `NaturalFixedRaySourceCharacters.relativeCharacter_fixedQ` gives the required containment for `nu_theta = chi_theta eta0^(-1)`. `AllocatedRayDictionary.originalImage_fixedQ` preserves it for surviving original slots. Its `both_common_rectangles` keeps their original relative characters, profiles, and heights. No arbitrary new slot coefficient or ray twist is substituted.

At an active common prime of net exponent `1 <= t <= 5`, using the source's zero-extended coefficients and reciprocity phase `q(pi,n)`, the two exact identities are

`c_n(pi) c_pi(n)^t = q(pi,n)^t c_n(pi)^(1+t)`,

`c_n(pi) conjugate(c_pi(n)^t) = q(pi,n)^(6-t) c_n(pi)^(7-t)`.

They hold off units as well, since both products are then zero. Thus the formal left residue is `1+t mod 6`, and the formal right residue is `1-t mod 6`. Side names may be exchanged only consistently. A resulting exponent six is the coprimality indicator `1_(n,pi)=1`; it is not the constant one. Canceled active primes therefore remain genuine holes. These signs agree with `FirstColumns.leftCoefficient/rightCoefficient`, not merely with a proposed valuation table.

The generator of an ideal can differ by a sixth-root unit from the product of the chosen primary prime generators. Retain this unit `u0` in the row or in the fixed six-unit dictionary. No equality between these generator conventions is needed.

On the second transform the genuine correlation vanishes unless its frequency has the form `j = G V h'`: `G` is the common gcd generator and `V` the forced nonunit radical. The normalized partition scalar has modulus at most one, including its zero extension. Multiplicativity gives the complete nonzero integer row

`w = u0 e F G V h'`.

The full residual coefficient on every ideal is

`c_eta_lambda(I) s_(m0^6 w)(I) 1_(I,R)=1`, with `m0=2(1-omega)`.

On unsupported ideals the `m0` factor supplies zero; on supported ideals the signed identity supplies the coefficient; canceled-prime holes are in `R`. The reflected rectangle has row `-w`. If a whole rectangle is conjugated, its entire character is conjugated and its height reflected. Replacing `conjugate(eta s_w)` by `conjugate(eta) s_w` is not justified and is not used here.

The first projector `s` really divides both genuine second common parts, hence `G` and `w`; `SecondSourceMask.source_pair_divisor_common/divisor_dvd_common` verify this. The second projector `t` is different: terms in the artificially separated off-coprime extension need not have `t|w`. The proof retains its original signs and pays that label through allocation/scalars, never through this divisibility claim. For an assigned plain divisor `d`, `psi_w(dv)=psi_w(d)psi_w(v)` is the exact identity; the possibly zero outside scalar remains. There is no invented restriction `(d,v)=1` on the quotient plain sum.

The exceptional/nonexceptional bridge is literal. `FixedRowMask.fixedInducingRow_mul_mask_iff` removes a nonzero extra mask from the *predicate*, not from the coefficient sum. `FixedRayInducingTransport.fixedInducingRow_product_iff` proves invariance under a permitted `Q_*`-character twist; its reverse implication uses the inverse twist and a restored modulus mask, so does not divide by a possibly zero coefficient. `SecondExceptionalFamily.Family.inducing_iff` identifies the actual reduced row; `paired_inducing_iff` identifies the reflected row with the **same** fixed ideal. Their hypotheses include the genuine nonzero row and the good-lambda and 2 divisibility of the bad mask, satisfied by `m0` and its retained products.

## 2. Fixed dictionary and natural conductor

**Classification: proved relative to exact natural constructors and the preceding signed transfer.**

The primary reciprocity phases are fixed ray characters modulo `(12)`, the unit phases modulo `(36)`, and the surviving relative characters have modulus dividing `Q_*`. Since `Q_* subseteq (72)`, their products on ideals prime to `Q_*` belong to one finite ray group. Arbitrarily many active primes multiply inside this same finite group. They do not generate a scale-dependent list. Products with each fixed original parent form a finite union of translates of this group; finite zero-extension choices give finitely many presentations.

For eligibility and buffered zero maxima, keep each parent translate separate. An eligible row for one translate need not make an unrelated translate nonprincipal. The proof uses the union only to select simultaneous constants and to partition fixed outer labels. Within the actual translate, the fixed-inducing gate excludes every principal allowed twist by `sector_nonprincipal` and the mask/twist equivalences above. Whole-character inversion can use the reflected-height symmetry instead of falsely adding a different fixed-factor translate.

Choose the **natural** representative of `c_eta_lambda(I)s_(m0^6w)(I)`. Its source constructor proves

`N q_(lambda,w) <= N q_eta_lambda * N(m0) * N(72) * Nw <= K Nw`,

with one fixed `K`. Its coefficients equal those of `momentData eta_lambda`; the new `natural_row_moment_dictionary` supplies that equality. The abstract choice `RowData.character` has no stated conductor bound, so cannot be used as the source of this estimate. The primitive inducing conductor is no larger. Polynomial common holes enter neither `K` nor the finite dictionary: their Euler factors are restored separately.

Removing sixth powers `w = u b^6` creates only further Euler holes in the literal row. These factors have no positive-real zero, so buffered zeros belong to the same primitive character. For a maximum over one finite permitted translate, some fixed label attains the lower edge, whereas its upper edge bounds every surviving slot character. Density may therefore count the fixed finite union of possible attaining labels. Moving arithmetic labels are reconstructed from `w` and the missing radical rather than added to that finite dictionary.

## 3. The unmarked density and quantifiers before height

**Classification: proved written theorem relative to the accepted zero-slot moment, inverse moment and actual supported-witness theorem. The general density assembly is not independently formalized by the component receipt.**

For a fixed finite dictionary of natural row characters and free rows `u` (nonzero, all prime valuations <6), PD proves the detector plain estimate

`sum_u |P_j(chi; U^m,sigma,t) P_k(chi; U^m,sigma,t)|^2
 <= C (1+H)^J U^(max(1,2m)+epsilon)`

for `m<=3/4`, `j+k<=2`, `sigma in [0,1]`, `|t|<=H`. The constants, degree and threshold precede `H` and all fiber parameters. The actual adapter uses the old empty-slot theorem, with `d=min(epsilon/4,1/4)` and initial width `1+d+max(0,2m-1)`. The fixed modulus fits `U^d` at a common eventual threshold. The legacy interface is filled by a dummy slot of width `7/37` with zero profile while the selected set is empty; it imposes no prime supply on the original unmarked family. This was checked in the actual new `PlainUnmarkedAdapter.lean`/`ActualUnmarkedInputs.lean` source, not inferred from the theorem name.

Rows omitted by the old `initialKeep` gate are a fixed **finite** exceptional set: all their prime factors divide fixed `Q`, and the free-row valuations are at most five, with six possible units. Absolute counting gives `|P_n| <= 288 A sqrt(D)` for the detector profile. Hence each exceptional paired squared term is at most a fixed multiple of `D^2 = U^(2m)`, which is absorbed by `U^max(1,2m)`. This proves the estimate without a lower row-norm cutoff. A finite maximum over dictionary labels makes the constants simultaneous.

For `17/20 <= a <= 7/8`, let `N(Y,a,T)` count free rows of norm at most `Y` having a zero of real part at least `a` and height at most `T` for some dictionary label. The density is

`N(Y,a,T) <= C (1+T)^J Y^(rho(2a-1)+epsilon)`,

`rho(delta) = 1 - 10 delta/[3(5-2 delta)]`.

Its threshold is fixed before both `a` and `T`. The argument actually produces that order:

1. Use `U=K Y` with fixed `K` large enough that both natural conductor and row norm are at most `U`. Discard the fixed finite exceptional union by absolute counting. The remaining characters are nonprincipal.
2. The accepted inverse moment and the plain estimate above give a common height degree `J0`, uniform in all detector bins, dyadic indices and `U`. Actual detector fibers have `m <= 1/2+75 epsilon_det <= 23/40`, so the plain estimate applies.
3. Choose the *internal* `tau_det>0` after `J0`, small enough that `tau_det(J0+1)` fits the requested error. For `T<=U^tau_det`, the finite buffered-bin lemma gives one of boundedly many `(i,k)` with step `U^tau_det`, fallback `51/100`, and `b>a-e`, `b<=7/8`. The upper/lower adjacent zero boxes are the hypotheses of the actual supported-witness theorem. Set its cutoff `t_*=5/(5-2 delta_b)` before constructing witnesses.
4. The actual source `Hecke/DetectorSupportedWitness.lean` supplies witnesses uniformly in the nonprincipal characters, modulus bound, buffered bin and cutoff. Witness height is at most `2 pi U^(tau_det/2)+3i U^tau_det`. The no-slot balance gives the fiber count `U^(rho(delta_b)+156 epsilon_det+epsilon_m)` times `(1+H_i)^(J0+1)`. There are only the fixed label/bin counts and two dyadic counts, paid by arbitrarily small power.
5. On the compact range, `rho(2b-1) <= rho(2a-1)+3e`. Choose detector/moment/mesh/dyadic errors and then `tau_det` so the sum fits `epsilon`. None is selected from the live height.
6. For `T>U^tau_det`, the trivial lattice count `N<<U` is paid by `(1+T)^J` with `J>=1/tau_det`. Bounded `Y` are filled by a finite row ball. Thus there is one threshold for all heights, not a family of uncontrolled thresholds `Y0(T)`.

When this density is used physically, choose a **different external** exponent `tau_out` after its final height degree `J`, with `J tau_out` below the preallocated power margin. Reusing `tau_det` externally would indeed be circular because of `J>=1/tau_det`; the written proof explicitly does not do so.

For `delta in [7/10,3/4]`, `2/7 <= rho <= 19/54`, so the raw sixth-power lift is uniformly summable: `6rho >= 12/7>1`. With `w=u b^6`, the sum of `(Nb)^(-6rho)` converges (six units only add a fixed factor). This proves the needed raw integer-row count for all supported `H>=1`, with the same height order and arbitrarily small exponent loss. No scale-dependent dictionary is covered by this result.

## 4. Both transforms and the actual main radius

**Classification: inherited source identities, combined with a proved new local ledger.**

Use `a=M/2000`, `sigma=3a`, `k0=7/10`, and old deficit

`g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-M)_+`.

The window implies `g<=M/12500<M/10000`, `0.85M<=A<=44753M/50000<0.9M`. The loss budget is chosen below a fixed fraction of both requested `epsilon` and `4M/225000`. This is possible before the fixed arithmetic dictionary.

The comparison rectangles have lengths `M/4` and `n1+n2-M/4`, with the exact same total product, character, original slot coefficients, masks and independent profiles. Uniform deletion of common masks followed, when needed, by the old reflection gives plain lengths at most `M/4` and `M/2+xi`. The old capacity is at most `0.93M+xi<M`. The literal eligible rows remain nonprincipal; deleting slots only restricts the permitted family. The old zero-slot theorem covers a fully exhausted set. This establishes the comparison without changing the centered expression before its transforms.

The first exact transform retains common widths `c,d,p,R,E,s0`: `p` is first common radical width; `R` its active net-residue radical; `E` the mask divisor; `s0` the first projector. Define `B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6`, and exchange `c,d` for `B_d`. The first outside exponent is `M-A-R/2-E`. Joint Cauchy, with all first labels still inside the direct sum, needs

`sum_lambda N_(C,lambda) << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+eta)`

and its D-side counterpart. PR9 B3.56 then yields exactly

`M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(B_c+B_d)/2 <= M`.

For per-label branches, the original `-s0` in their allowance is canceled once by the label count `Z^(p+s0+eta)`. For the high branch, joint reconstruction directly proves this target; a later factor `Z^p` or `Z^s0` would be a double count and is absent.

The amplifier uses actual good primes in `(Z^a/2,Z^a]`, excluding the finitely many live support/mask primes. Removing `O(log Z)` primes is negligible for fixed `a>0`. The main term has density `Z^(-a+eta)`; each extracted error retains a normalized prime average, with no new prime count.

The **actual smooth radius** in the second transform is

`Kmain = K0+(d-c)_+ +6a+omega`,

`K0 = 2A-c-d+R+E-M`.

This is the pinned source `AmplifiedRetainedRadius.mainCommonRadius`, with `sigma=3a` and `omega=delta+reserve`. The source's `main_energy_common` proves domination of the retained amplified frequency range including fixed support doubling (`2<=Z^reserve` eventually). It is not an attempt to relabel the old ball by a more convenient upper bound. The Poisson identity is used with this chosen ball; the extracted error terms keep their old radii.

For second common widths `c2,d2`, gcd width `g2`, the unit-part radical width `t2`, and the mean `b2=(c2+d2)/2` (exactly PR9 B3.62–B3.64), its nominal child has

`M' = M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2 <= M-6a-omega`,

`A'=A-c-c2`,

`(A'-M')-(A-M) = 6a+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <= 6a+omega`.

The exact second extraction normalizers give nominal allowance `M'+Delta`, with

`Delta=b2-p2+B_c+a >= a`.

These substitutions agree with the source two-transform ledger. If a fixed parent-modulus logarithmic width is displayed, use the total width `M=m+q` and the physical row width `m` in the initial `K0`; the same total formula results. For a fixed target `q` is absorbed by eventual arbitrarily small padding. It is not permission to allow a positively growing parent conductor in the density dictionary.

## 5. Low bins and the canonical actual-width correction

**Classification: proved source transfer; this disposes of the strongest possible low-bin objection.**

The low-bin indicator is introduced only **after both transforms**, on a positive child energy. The exact pinned `Energy.AllocatedChildren.commonChild_energy`, `AllocatedNaturalRadial.allocated_radial_bound`, and `AllocatedRayDictionary.common_clipped_energy` permit an arbitrary extra `keep` predicate. They retain the canonical row, masks, relative characters and normalizers. Thus the bin need not be hereditary through a subsequent transform: no subsequent Poisson transform of that bin is used.

On such rows, first bound and remove a greedy prefix of surviving prime slots of total width `dz`. Their actual nonprincipal natural characters lie in the common buffered bin, so their squared pointwise cost is `Z^((0.7+O(e))dz+eta)`, including restoration of polynomial-size holes. Each removed slot releases old capacity `4.5 dz`. Stop when the old capacity holds, or when all slots are exhausted. After this **pointwise** removal, drop the row restriction by positivity and apply the old canonical moment to the whole remaining eligible family. If empty, use the separate unrestricted zero-slot theorem, which does not demand plain total length below the width. This is not a bootstrap of the improved moment.

Actual canonical width can be below the nominal `M'`, because moving support may cancel. Write `d_* = M_actual-M'`, with upper bound `delta2` but no lower bound. If `F` is the nominal affine defect then actual defect is at most `(F-d_*)_+`. For `0<=r<=1`, the elementary inequality

`d_* + r(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2 + r F_+`

holds: `x -> x+r(F-x)_+` is nondecreasing and at `x=delta2` is at most `delta2+rF_+` when `delta2>=0`. Equivalently, split at `x=F`. This covers negative `d_*` instead of assuming it is nonnegative. PR9 extraction gives `F<=g+6a+eta`. With `r=(0.7+O(e))/4.5`, the combined width/removal exponent is at most

`M' +(7/45)(g+6a)+eta`.

It is strictly inside the available `M'+a` because

`a-(7/45)(g+6a) >= M/2000 -(7/45)(M/10000+3M/1000) = 4M/225000 > 0`.

The one greedy mesh overshoot, `omega`, bin upper-edge error and support padding are selected within a smaller budget. A bin straddling `0.7` is assigned low and uses its upper edge `0.7+O(e)`. Thus neither the cutoff endpoint nor the possibly negative actual-width correction is hidden.

## 6. Joint high count and exact label costs

**Classification: proved written reconstruction/density application relative to the fixed-family inputs above.**

For one first-side orientation let `L_c=log_Z NF_c`, `T_c=(c-d)_+`, and let `R0` be the active radical width whose signed row residue cancels. The actual support of the complete row gives

`log_Z Nw <= W+O(eta)`, `W=M-R-T_c+L_c-6a`, `L_c<=5(R-R0)`.

The extra `-omega` is favorable and may be dropped. Every genuine second common prime and the first projector divides `w`. The first radical absent from `w` has width at most `p-R-E+R0`: this includes the inactive net-zero primes and the canceled active ones. Count that missing radical explicitly. Once it and `w` are fixed, all remaining first and second common labels, first projector, valuations and bounded allocation choices are divisor-many.

This last statement does not rely on bounded valuations. Uniformly for `NQ<=Z^B`, `NI<=Z^T`, Rankin gives

`#{I: rad(I)|Q, NI<=Z^T} <= Z^(sT) product_(p|Q) (1-(Np)^(-s))^(-1)`.

Choose `sT` small. For any `b>0`, all sufficiently large prime factors in the product are at most `(Np)^b`; the finitely many smaller factors give a constant. Choosing `bB` small gives `O(Z^epsilon)`. Counting the missing radical itself costs exactly its norm exponent, since the fixed field has `O(X)` ideals of norm at most `X`. Fixed finite slot assignments can increase the eventual constants but not this exponent. This proves the arbitrary-valuation reconstruction needed by the source family.

Density therefore bounds the **joint** rows and first/common labels by

`Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+eta) (1+T_h)^J`.

If the supported bound is negative the row set is empty. A nonempty slightly negative nominal `W` is at least `-O(eta)`; fill the bounded row ball and charge that same tolerance. No population below one is asserted for a nonempty integral window.

The second projector label is deliberately outside this reconstruction. In each dyadic sector PR9 B3.67–B3.69 pays its count together with **both** exact extraction scalars. After that cancellation the remaining pointwise clipping reductions are nonpositive: paired cost is `delta(alpha1+alpha2-rclip1-rclip2)/2+O(thetaN)`. One may consequently use the pre-reduction paired size `Z^(delta(A-c-b2)+eta)` without incorrectly claiming `t|w`. Signs lost by a triangle inequality cost only the scalar masses that were paid; no unrestricted new arithmetic coefficient is substituted into a moment theorem.

The outside second-transform exponent at the actual main radius is

`A-min(c,d)+R+E-M+5a+g2-t2-b2+O(eta)`.

Subtracting the joint target `p+A-c+R+E+B_c` gives exactly PLA LA.13:

`M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)`

`+(1-rho)T_c-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c+rho L_c+R0`

`+g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+O(eta)`.

I independently expanded this expression, retaining the missing-radical and first-radical terms; the controller independently reported the same result. To bound its second line use `c=min(c,d)+T_c`, `min(c,d)>=p>=R`, `L_c<=5(R-R0)`, `rho+delta>1`, `5rho>1`, and `4rho-1>0`. It is at most

`(4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c <= -79p/270-E-B_c`.

The third line is at most `-delta b2-t2` since `g2<=b2`. On `delta in [0.7,0.75]` the weaker `A/M<=113/125` gives

`1-rho-delta A/M >= 259/16875`, `5-6rho<=23/7`.

With `a=M/2000`, even adding total high losses `M/1000` leaves excess below `-M/100`. Every genuinely high bin has lower `delta>=0.7`, hence zero-real-part threshold at least `17/20`, precisely the density range. The low side handles bins crossing the threshold. The joint proof already paid the first labels; no additional label factor is charged afterward.

## 7. Error, zero and fixed-inducing branches

**Classification: already established source mechanisms, with proved numerical compatibility at this radius.**

The three extracted amplifier errors have `(w,w_o)=(lambda,lambda),(6lambda,0),(7lambda,lambda)`. For actual primes in `(Z^a/2,Z^a]`, eventually `lambda>=sigma/4` because `a=sigma/3`. Their nominal defect is at most `g+sigma+w-w_o+eta`; their allowance is at least `w`. Use global squared slot cost `3/4` and old capacity `9/2`, removal rate `1/6`, with the same actual-width correction. The three reserves are respectively at least

`13M/120000`, `193M/120000`, `119M/60000`.

For example the first is `lambda-(g+sigma)/6`, minimized at `lambda=sigma/4`; the others retain their displayed powers and outside shifts. The normalized prime average stays normalized. No extra prime count, low-bin heredity, or density is used here.

The artificially added zero Gauss row remains unamplified with the direct old `-s0` allowance. The second zero-frequency excess at the new radius is at most `A-M+5a+O(eta)<0`.

For genuinely fixed-inducing nonzero rows, preserve the paired exceptional predicate, forced congruences, masks and extraction scalars. The exact substitution into PR9 B3.75 yields

`F1=(c+5d+R+E)/6+B_c-4a` when `c>=d`,

`F1=c+(R+E)/6+B_c-4a` when `c<=d`,

before the padding correction `-5omega/6`. Thus `F1>=2c/3-4a-O(eta)` and `F2>=2b2/3`. The sometimes quoted `-5a` is a valid weaker inequality, not the equality; the exact formula includes the positive amplifier density `ell=a`.

For `v=c+min(c2,d2)` and `L=M/4`,

`max_(v>=0) [A-5M/6-2v/3-(L-v)_+] = A-M`.

The expression increases up to `v=L` and decreases thereafter. Main exceptional excess is therefore at most `A-M+4a+O(eta)<0`; unchanged error radii have `A-M+3sigma+O(eta)<0`. The old common-lattice leading terms cancel because the centered rectangles retain the same product, whole-product character, mask and norm power. Independent input heights reside in the two shared profiles, so do not invalidate equality of the leading terms. This is a paid estimate despite the fixed positive amplifier length; the amplifier error has not been called arbitrarily small.

## 8. Euler holes, Fourier transport and all height costs

**Classification: the general analytic lemmas are elementary/proved; their use is compatible after the literal coefficient and joint-norm transfers.**

For a squarefree ideal `q`, `Nq<=Z^B`, and `|a_p|<=1`,

`E_q(s)=product_(p|q)(1-a_p(Np)^(-s))`

has no zeros for `Re s>0`. On `Re s>=sigma0>0`, `E_q`, `1/E_q` and every fixed derivative are `O(Z^epsilon)` uniformly in `q`, coefficients and height. Bound by the positive product at `sigma0/2`, put each sufficiently large factor below `(Np)^b`, and use a Cauchy disk of radius `sigma0/2`. This proves uniform deletion/restoration only after the exact Euler identity has been established. It does not provide conductor bounds or remove a principal pole, which is why the natural constructor and eligibility gates above are necessary.

For a normalized prime polynomial of scale `P>=1`, removal of primes dividing `q` costs at most `O(P^(-1/2) log(2Nq))`. This is `O(Z^epsilon)` on polynomial scales and is compatible with squared pointwise cost `P^delta Z^epsilon` for `delta>=0`. Logarithmic profile derivatives add only fixed log powers; imaginary heights have unit modulus. Arithmetic masks have not been discarded by positivity.

On a fixed compact box in logarithmic coordinates, uniformly bounded Euler derivatives of order `2r>J+d` give Fourier densities dominated by `C(1+|t|)^(-2r)`. Their `J`-weighted total mass is uniformly bounded. Minkowski is applied in the **joint** Hilbert space `directsum_lambda ell2(rows_lambda)`, possibly with nonnegative weights, after proving a joint arithmetic bound. Thus it costs the common measure's mass and no factor equal to the number of labels.

If the smooth continuous parameter varies as `A_lambda`, the individual densities need not be equal. Choose their common positive majorant `dmu=C(1+|t|)^(-2r)dt` first and write `f_(A_lambda)dt=a_lambda(t)dmu`, `|a_lambda|<=1`. Multiplication by these scalars is a diagonal contraction in the joint Hilbert space. This proves the claimed extension. It is used only for labels frozen outside the particular sum being Poisson-transformed. Discontinuous row, valuation, coprimality and zero-bin indicators stay inside the arithmetic vector and are never differentiated or inserted before a transform.

For actual kernels `K(A product y_i^e_i)`, Euler differentiation acts on `K` with fixed multipliers. Uniform source kernel seminorms, fixed compact cutoffs and normalized norm powers therefore provide the common profile control. Large frequency tails are paid by sufficiently high integration-by-parts order, using raw polynomial arithmetic bounds before an enlargement. These orders are finite and can be chosen after the density height degree.

For bounded physical input heights retain Fourier frequencies inside a still smaller portion of the `Z^tau_out` zero-height buffer. For arbitrary larger input heights, absolute counting gives a fixed polynomial `Z^D` on the bounded exponent geometry; a sufficiently large fixed polynomial in the largest height absorbs it. This avoids applying a detector at an uncontrolled height. Choosing derivative and height orders backward through the finite graph (two transforms and calls to old moments), then Fourier orders and finally the threshold, supplies a uniform statement for all independent heights and the four scale-derivative profile pairs.

## 9. Endpoint interface: mesh before target, uniformity in live scales

**Classification: the required local uniformity is supported by the proof, subject to retaining the exact fixed-family scope. It does not prove the separate endpoint continuation.**

The potentially fatal order would be to choose the physical slot mesh only after the eventual target character's density height degree. The written proof does not need that order. Its low-branch positive margin `4M/225000`, high margin `M/100`, all three error margins and the comparison/exceptional margins are uniform on the fixed local window and contain no dictionary size or height degree. Choose a numerical error budget from these margins and `epsilon`, then the physical bin/slot mesh and canonical support reserves, before the eventual target family and finite slot list. One greedy prefix overshoot uses one mesh allowance. After the finite slot list is fixed its aggregate support tolerance tends to zero as `Z` grows; it is not a permanent loss charged per slot.

Only afterward fix the finite target dictionary and slot system, choose their density/profile height degrees, choose `tau_out` sufficiently small for those degrees and the fixed minimum positive width, choose Fourier-tail orders and the eventual threshold. All of these may depend on that fixed target/system. None changes the earlier positive slot widths or the final continuation strip. The density's *internal* detector mesh/exponent are auxiliary to its proof; they do not require resetting the original physical slots. A very small eventual `tau_out` merely raises the threshold and allowable finite orders.

For the endpoint lane's moving row exponent `d`, shift `t`, selected subsets, actual plain scales and relative slot widths `ell_i/d`, normalize the local theorem at `U=Z^d`, so `M=1`. The endpoint's retained `d` lies in a fixed compact interval bounded away from zero, the original finite positive slot widths are fixed, and therefore each surviving normalized `ell_i/d` lies in a compact positive interval. There are finitely many subsets, and the plain exponents and free shift range remain in the asserted bounded geometry. The source moment statements already quantify over profiles and scales with a common seminorm control. Natural fixed conductor padding, uniform polynomial-mask Euler bounds, common ambient Fourier boxes, bounded bin counts and bounded-exponent raw counts supply constants/orders/thresholds uniformly over these compact choices. Fix them **before** the live `d,t`, subsets, scales, masks and heights. A common `U0` translates to the common original threshold `Z>=U0^(1/d_min)`.

A pointwise assertion with one uncontrolled `Z0(d,t)` for each live pair would not suffice. This review does not endorse such an assertion: the normalization and the displayed uniform compact ranges are necessary. Likewise, the dictionary cannot grow with `Z`, `d`, a common-support label, or `w`; the signed-row reconstruction must keep all such arithmetic movement in the literal integer row and masks. The endpoint may choose constants after the target family, but cannot recompute its fixed exclusion ideal from a moving child anchor or select its original minimum width from that target.

## Decisive objections tested and limits of the conclusion

| Potential objection | Assessment at the pinned sources |
| --- | --- |
| A new arbitrary prime coefficient family replaced the natural slots. | No: relative characters, canonical pools, common profile and exact zero extensions survive allocation. |
| Low bins are transformed by Poisson, or require heredity after deleting slots. | No: attach them only to positive energy after both transforms, remove slots pointwise, then enlarge and call the old theorem. |
| The height-uniform density is only proved for each fixed height. | No: the internal small-height construction and large-height absolute count produce one threshold before all heights; external exponent is distinct. |
| Abstract character choice has no conductor bound. | True objection to that shortcut; resolved by the natural constructor and coefficient equality, not by using `RowData.character` for conductor. |
| Fixed dictionary silently includes principal twists from another translate. | No: bins remain inside the actual parent translate; fixed union is only for constants/outer partition. |
| Signed exponent zero was replaced by one. | No: its coprimality hole is retained; primary-generator units are also retained. |
| Both projectors were called divisors of the row. | No: only the first is; the second count is paid with both allocation scalars. |
| Finite valuation checks do not cover arbitrary multiplicities. | Correct concern, answered by the support Rankin bound and explicit missing-radical count. |
| Smaller actual canonical width invalidates the nominal defect budget. | Resolved by the inequality in Section 5, valid also for negative width difference. |
| Fourier separation independently repeats each label count. | No: common majorant and diagonal contractions preserve the joint norm. |
| The advertised main radius is only an upper-bound change. | No: the exact pinned `mainCommonRadius/main_energy_common` constructs and dominates the chosen smooth ball. |
| Amplification errors are absorbed as an arbitrarily small power despite fixed `a`. | No: their positive numerical margins, normalized average and exceptional margins are explicitly paid. |
| Mesh depends on the target's height degree, destroying the common endpoint strip. | No such dependence is necessary; only the later height exponent/orders/threshold do. The compact normalized interface in Section 9 must be preserved. |
| Supporting component checks establish the endpoint. | They do not. This is a written source-relative local proof; endpoint assembly and formal replay have distinct statuses. |

No narrow mathematical repair was required for the head reviewed. Some invalid shortcuts above are already explicitly corrected in that head, including the second-projector distinction and the exact `-4a` exceptional equality. Those corrections should not be reverted during integration. A rigorous acceptance of the new **global constant** still requires the endpoint lane's complete weighted/shortened-scale/continuation bridge, source-preserving integration, and the controller's overall assessment. A clean full formalization/checker receipt would be stronger independent evidence, but its current absence is not a refutation of this written proof.

The next mathematical action is to compose this exact local theorem with the endpoint lane's fixed original slot system and target-uniform continuation, keeping Section 9's quantifier order explicit. There is no justification to generalize the local theorem to growing parent conductor, arbitrary coefficients, arbitrary global length geometry, or a union of unrelated translates in one eligibility bin.

## 8. Evidence, limits and final handoff

The reproducible arithmetic checks are in checks.py / checks-result.json and check-hard.py / check-hard-result.json. The first checks verify word-fiber norms, finite inverse prime tails, all twelve exact renewal partitions for N=233,509, q=1,4,5 and r=1,2, the actual 20196 merged fiber, and the bare character squares. The additional N=20196 cases exercise a genuinely nonzero hard contribution: at r=1 its value is14-i for q=1, -5-11i for q=4 and-2+14i for q=5, with22 hard states and192 short states. The total error equals root+short+small+hard exactly in all six added cases. These deliberately arbitrary F have large root defects and do not satisfy W16; they test the identity, not cancellation.

The small-prime price W12 is analytic and does not depend on those finite checks. At these modest N, a log-power cutoff with A=7 would be larger than the eventual hard prime range; the asymptotic theorem has no implied practical threshold. The samples use a separate literal Y=3 to exercise the partition. There is no finite-range extrapolation to all N.

## 7. Independent uniform audit13: entropy price of the actual word

Let Omega be a finite coefficient-pattern space containing the actual word w*, with prior pi(w*)>0. For t>0 and a specified COMPLETE energy E(w), define Z_t=sum pi(w)exp(tE(w)). A single positive summand gives

    E(w*) <= [log Z_t+log(1/pi(w*))]/t.                  (A13)

The sign of the entropy price is positive. Neither a small typical energy nor exponentially rare high-energy words removes it. Applied to E(w*)=|M_chi(N)|^2, a joint bound on the numerator by t*N^(2gamma+epsilon), for every N/epsilon/fixed chi with common gamma, gives the full ordinary-character all-height return just described. This is a valid criterion only after actual-pattern mass and the partition function are both paid. A complete Gaussian-energy version additionally needs its literal full tails and coefficients.

A concrete relaxed model shows the cost. For the principal real source keep its actual K_N squarefree support but allow independent signs there, with uniform prior2^(-K_N). The actual Möbius sign word is present. Its entropy bill is K_N log2. If S is the sum of K independent signs and t=a/K,0<a<1/2, the elementary Gaussian identity and cosh(u)<=exp(u^2/2) give

    E exp((a/K)S^2) <= (1-2a)^(-1/2).

At a=1/4 this partition function is at most sqrt2, yet(A13) gives only

    E(w*) <=4K[K log2+(log2)/2]=O(K^2).

An all-plus word with energy K^2 and the SAME prior mass actually lies in that relaxation. Thus the generic model cannot give the desired subquadratic bound. One may fix the n=1 sign, changing the entropy to(K-1)log2; the exponent obstruction remains. These comparison words are not asserted to satisfy all Möbius relations. Finite enumerations at K4/6/8 verify the exact second moment K and maximum K^2; the Gaussian inequality above, not those enumerations, proves the displayed all-K partition bound.

At the opposite extreme, imposing every exact multiplicative relation, square-zero condition and prescribed prime value -chi(p) determines the single actual word. The admissible space is a singleton, pi(w*)=1 and logZ=tE(w*); the criterion then restates the original problem. The potentially useful middle ground is an arithmetic class/prior that keeps enough correlations to control Z without making the actual word exponentially underweighted. That construction remains OPEN. With complex chi its natural zero set and fixed phases must remain part of the word space; the principal relaxation alone makes no all-character impossibility claim.

statement:
## 4. Survivors03/20: actual Gaussian forcing defeats an uncut prime resolvent

### 4.1 The exact high-ceiling certificate and all its costs

Let P>=5 and retain all primes<=P. Let f_P(n)=f3(n) if every prime factor of n is<=P and0 otherwise, and

    V_P(u)=sum_n f_P(n)g_tau(log n-u),
    E_P(s)=(1-3^-s)^-1 product_(p<=P,p!=3)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s). (R1)

Unlike a squarefree-only partition function, this includes every prime power. For sigma>0 it has an absolutely convergent finite-prime Dirichlet series and

    ||exp(-sigma u)V_P(u)||_L2(R)^2
      =exp(tau sigma^2)/(2pi) integral_R exp(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2dt. (R2)

This is Parseval after absolute Mellin Fubini. Let P_X>=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)). All integers n<=P_X occur with their exact original f3 coefficient, while missing nonsmooth n lie in a full Gaussian tail. The elementary |f3|<=1 Gaussian estimate gives

    sup_(log X<=u<=log2X) |F(u)-V_(P_X)(u)|
       <=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).                      (R3)

Thus a global source norm in R2 bounded by P^kappa would yield shell exponent sigma+kappa (P_X=X^(1+o(1))), with R3 paid by choosing C. At sigma=.6, the weakest first-gain budget is kappa<.274861; c=1/6 allows kappa<.233333..., and c=1/4 allows kappa<.15. These are honest full-return headrooms, not isolated Euler-factor savings. For other sigma>.5, the budget is gamma-sigma.

### 4.2 Source-sensitive obstruction at shrinking height

For each fixed1/2<sigma<1 and sufficiently large P, R2 instead grows faster than EVERY power of P. The obstruction occurs at heights t approximately pi/log P, which approach0, so Gaussian frequency suppression does not help.

For p>=5 the uniformly convergent local logarithm gives

    log|(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)|=-Re(p^-s)+O_sigma(p^-2sigma).

The sum of errors is bounded independently of P and small t. The finite p=2,3 factors are bounded above and away from zero near t=0 for fixed sigma in(1/2,1). Hence

    log|E_P(sigma+it)|=-Re sum_(p<=P) p^(-sigma-it)+O_sigma(1). (R4)

The ordinary PNT, verified in [Johnston–Yang, arXiv:2204.01980v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), supplies pi(y)~y/log y. Stieltjes partial summation or the substitution y=P exp(-v) gives, uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6],

    sum_(p<=P) p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =(P^(1-sigma)/log P)[exp(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o_sigma(1)]. (R5)

For completeness, one may first restrict y>=P^b for fixed b in(0,1), where the PNT error is uniform; the omitted y<=P^b is O(P^(b(1-sigma))) and is negligible. In the main integral, v=log(P/y) has limiting density exp(-(1-sigma)v); a/log P tends to0 uniformly, which yields R5 by a bounded tail split. No zero-free conjecture is used.

Since cos a<=-sqrt3/2 on that interval, R4–5 imply for all sufficiently large P and all those t=a/log P,

    log|E_P(sigma+it)| >= [1/(2(1-sigma))] P^(1-sigma)/log P. (R6)

The t-interval has length pi/(3log P) and its Gaussian factor tends uniformly to1. Consequently

    ||exp(-sigma u)V_P||_2
      >= c_(sigma,tau)(log P)^(-1/2)
           exp([1/(2(1-sigma))]P^(1-sigma)/log P).    (R7)

For rigor one can reduce the positive constant in R7 slightly when absorbing finite factors; the stated R6 already has fixed slack relative to sqrt3/2. Every polynomial allowance in R3 fails for this uncut global norm, including the large c=1/4 budget. This is an ACTUAL f3 finite-prime/Gaussian-source obstruction, stronger than a generic operator-norm example. It does not lower-bound the true full field on x~P: the global norm can be dominated by remote smooth-number scales. It does not disprove a causal, physically restricted signed resolvent.

### 4.3 Protected rare20 and the viable changed object

On H_sigma=L2(R,exp(-2sigma u)du), each prime dilation has norm p^-sigma. The weighted prime factor is (I-2D_p)(I-D_p)^-1. In finite multiplicative truncations D_p is nilpotent and every factor has spectrum{1}; therefore the finite spectrum does not price physical transient growth. On the full space the Fourier multiplier in R2 records precisely the missing norm. R7 shows that merely retaining signs and replacing a singular-value bound by an uncut resolvent bound cannot fit the actual source budget.

The viable changed target is the causal readout

    ||1_[log X,log2X] V_(P_X)||_2 << X^gamma,          (R8)

or a finite signed transfer whose output is exactly this restriction and whose discarded remote-scale feedback is explicitly paid. R3 gives its complete return without a global-norm hypothesis. R8 remains an open actual arithmetic estimate; no spectral-radius claim pays it. A useful next calculation is a Schur/compression identity for this exact output, retaining the two off-block feedback terms, to determine whether the obstruction R7 lives wholly in a removable remote-scale block or couples back at power cost. The previous Schur-complement lower-bound warning remains in force.

The R7 calculation is a distinct source-sensitive failure bound in this record. Its ancestry is W41-28's unrenormalized Euler failure, U-FUGACITY/U-DETERMINANT and finite nilpotent resolvent attempts. It does not claim a general no-go theorem for renormalized Euler products or nonnormal arithmetic operators.

### 3.3 A large actual isolated set exists on every sufficiently large shell

Fix q, C>0, an integer d>=1, and 0<=theta<1. Precisely, every graph edge {n,m} must satisfy the displayed distance bound and delete at most d prime factors from EACH squarefree endpoint when passing to the other endpoint. This condition is independent of a flow's orientation; an incoming edge cannot bypass the source-side budget. Squarefree Hamming radius<=d satisfies it, and optional zero-mass integer vertices are allowed subject to the same endpoint rule. Choose an integer

    k > d/(1-theta),   y=(2X)^(1/k).                            (C6)

Let V_X contain all products of k DISTINCT primes in

    (X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)].

Each n in V_X is squarefree, X<n<=2X, and for large X is coprime to the fixed q. All its primes are<=y. Since1-theta-d/k>0, inequality C5 holds for every n in V_X once X is sufficiently large. Hence every such vertex is isolated in the entire short-move graph, including possible neighbors outside this shell or cutoff.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives, for this FIXED k,

    t_X=#primes in the displayed interval
       ~ k(2^(1/k)-1) X^(1/k)/log X.

Unique factorization counts distinct vertices exactly as binomial(t_X,k). Therefore

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.                                (C7)

Only fixed-relative-width intervals are used, not a primes-in-short-interval theorem or a growing-k substitution. For the external input, the published PNT was checked in the official [NIST DLMF27.12, equations4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12). All deductions C3-C7 are given here. The constants can be tiny and the onset large; both are permitted and neither changes the power obstruction.

It follows that ANY disjoint matching in this graph leaves at least A_k X/(2(log X)^k) actual unit-modulus source coefficients unmatched on [X,2X], for every sufficiently large X. The absolute unmatched mass cannot be O(X^delta) for ANY delta<1. Thus the fixed-radius candidate cannot meet M2, at a near gain,1/6,1/4, or any other power-saving target.

This extends beyond integral matching. For an arbitrary complex edge flow F supported on the same graph, let div F(n) be its net outgoing mass, whenever defined. In any exact source decomposition a=div F+r, an isolated vertex satisfies r(n)=a(n). Hence

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.                               (C8)

No choice of complex flow weights, linear combinations of codewords, or repeated local steps removes an isolated vertex. Chaining cannot start there. The result still holds for any uniformly bounded family of radii and for subpower inflation of C, by first replacing theta by a fixed slightly larger number below1. It does NOT cover growing radii, genuinely long edges, nonlocal auxiliary states with a different exact transfer, or a bound retaining signed cancellation among the isolated states.

| Intended exponent theta | Fixed radius d | k used | Strict isolation exponent1-theta-d/k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|17497/20000=.87485|3|24|3/20000|
|5/6|3|19|1/114|
|3/4|3|13|1/52|

The first row has about X/(log X)^24 isolated24-prime products, all with principal coefficient+1. The next two rows use19- and13-prime products, with principal coefficient-1. This is a lower bound for the absolute residual and for those particular signed subcollections. It is NOT a lower bound for the complete signed residual or M_chi: different prime-count layers can cancel, and that cancellation remains an eligible arithmetic input.

## 3. Full physical covariance after the new core and gcd results

### F04.C — The new hard sector

Use the actual fully compensated field \(S_c\) containing every completed column \(A=cn^3\) with squarefree core \(c\), all descendants, marks and embeddings. With
\[
Q=q_{b_*}XY,\quad P_a=Y^2/Q,\quad L=Z^\ell,
\quad \mathcal F_A=1+P_a^{1/6}+LP_a^2/Y,
\]
T06 proves
\[
\mathcal D_{\rm core}=\sum_c\|S_c\|_2^2
\ll (Z^\epsilon/Y)\mathcal F_A.
\]
This is the actual square function, not a bound on \(\|\sum_cS_c\|_2^2\). For a smooth true-gcd dyad,
\[
\mathcal C(G)=\sum_{c\ne c'}w(q_{(c,c')}/G)\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle,
\]
T07 gives, relative to the stronger inherited finite-order Hecke inputs,
\[
|\mathcal C(G)|\ll {Z^\epsilon\over Y}\mathcal F_A
 {Z^{1+b_0/2}L^{1+3b_0/2}\over G^2}.
\]
The actual product-slot structure is essential. Thus dyads above
\[
G_0=Z^{1/2+b_0/4}L^{1/2+3b_0/4}
\]
are affordable; at the saved .12551 geometry \(\log_ZG_0=.91621058\ldots\). A rigorous proof works first at a fixed \(b>b_0\), then allocates the final small loss. Rational \(b=7/8\) gives \(G_0=Z^{23/32}L^{37/32}\). The result does not follow from rational-zeta nonvanishing alone.

The exact remaining target is a one-sided upper bound, or the stronger absolute bound,
\[
\boxed{\ \sum_{G<G_0}\mathcal C(G)
\ll {Z^\epsilon\over Y}\mathcal F_A\ }
\tag{CORE}
\]
with a smooth complete partition and all inherited uniformities. At the saved geometry \(LP_a^2/Y\) is harmless and \(\mathcal F_A\asymp P_a^{1/6}\) up to allowed losses. This leaves a large arithmetic sector; the tail exponent .9162 is a useful reduction, not evidence that only a negligible set remains.

For \(c=gu,c'=gv\) and embedded products \(D=G_*d,E=G_*e\), the live common-core character is
\[
\psi(g)=\vartheta_g(ve)\overline{\vartheta_g(ud)}.
\]
The exact collision masks \((u,e)=(v,d)=1\), together with the two gcd decompositions, make every surviving off-core good character nonprincipal. A marked prime enters the squarefree Euler identity through
\[
f_s(p)={t_p\over1+t_p},\qquad t_p=\psi(p)q_p^{-s};
\]
a same-slot coincidence contributes \(f_s-f_s^2\). The first two powers carry nonprincipal cubic characters; the first possible principal power is paid by its cubic decay. This is the mechanism already exploited in the large-gcd tail. A small-gcd proof must improve its averaging order or its use of the remaining cofactors.

### F04.N1 — New pass 1: switch the averaging order where the tail stops

The proposed object is the exact gcd-one kernel obtained from \(\langle S_u,S_v\rangle\), with \((u,v)=1\), before absolute values in the row, prime slots or cube descendants. Fix dyads for the *relative character conductor*, distinct from \(q_uq_v\) and the full additive period. Expand mask-only primes as divisibility conditions; preserve the actual \(f_s\) factors at live slots. Try row completion for small relative conductors and column/slot averaging first for large ones. The switching inequality must include the original two product profiles and quotient-square embeddings.

The first missing lemma is a coefficient-specific bound on this switched sum giving the CORE budget after its conductor dyads are summed. The cheapest decisive test is one coprime pair with two unequal embedded products and one genuine marked slot. Print its minimal arithmetic period and transformed phase. If the proposed transform becomes a long individual character sum, it has not exploited the new reduction. A fallback is a thin band of small \(g\) for which a true relative-conductor saving can be summed; record the uncovered region explicitly.

### F04.N2 — New pass 1: core-frame calibration and exact mark cumulants

T06 supplies a useful normalization absent from the earlier raw-Gram proposals. On a finite truncation let \(d_c=\|S_c\|_2\) and
\(\Gamma_{c,c'}=\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle/(d_cd_{c'})\) for nonzero entries. The full target is a bound on the **actual weighted direction** \(d^*\Gamma d\), not an arbitrary-vector spectral bound. Pairing the physical field with the theta witness may require still less than this energy. Compute an independently defined residual subspace of \(\Gamma\) only after its coefficient vectors and principal calibration are explicit.

A complementary arithmetic test centers two actual mark slots *inside* the common Euler identity. The second cumulant must retain \(f_s-f_s^2\), cross-slot collisions and all addback terms. One may seek cancellation in the centered block while pricing its lower moments by T06/T07. An apparent saving that simply drops an addback carrying the original signal fails. This differs from the supplied primewise tail proof: the proposed averaging is across two slots and the remaining small-gcd cofactors simultaneously. First output: a two-slot identity and its full norm/principal terms, then an aggregate estimate. Neither the normalized frame nor the cumulant identity supplies cancellation by itself.

### F04.N3 — New pass 1: merge paid sectors only through an exact common partition

There are two legal decompositions:

- Core decomposition: full physical energy = same-core square function + large-gcd off-core covariance + small-gcd off-core covariance.
- Frequency decomposition: full physical energy = complete zero mode + coherent-unembedded pairwise zero-subtracted remainder + all other pairwise zero-subtracted remainders.

These cannot be combined by declaring their overlapping “paid pieces” positive. A01 controls the coherent principal-good-character pair condition \(aA'/(bA)\in\mathcal I^6\), after subtracting each pair's zero contribution. It does not control a nonprincipal character evaluated on a sixth-power frequency. A15 shows that gcd masks need not preserve positive semidefiniteness, even on a two-column Gram.

The concrete new bookkeeping/lemma task is to express both decompositions on one finite pair index set, enumerate intersections, and price the resulting addbacks before removing truncation. A useful extension would transport the coherent divisibility-discrepancy proof to one mixed embedding: derive coherence after substituting the true rows \(e^2r,d^2r\), then prove the CRT/Jacobian/profile statement. Merely reusing the unembedded ratio is wrong. This is an enabling theorem worth a bounded attempt because it could remove an additional portion of CORE; it is not H or a full saving.

# [private research revision]: local small-value sets recover a complete Gaussian exponent

The W39 [author](../[private research revision]/wild39/report.md) and
[independent critic](../[private research revision]/wild39-review/report.md) prove a conditional
analytic return for actual complete arithmetic Gaussian fields. Root
read both complete arguments and independently replayed the finite
identity checks. The hypothesis is open: no new zero-free constant,
arithmetic small-value bound or kernel verification is claimed.

## 1. The local-set theorem

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character, let

    F(z)=sum_n mu(n)chi(n) g_tau(log n-z),   tau>0 fixed.

All natural zeros remain. The complete series is entire and satisfies
|F(u+iv)|<=C exp(u+v^2/(2tau)) for u>=0, with a Gaussian real left tail.
Fix 0<gamma<1 and 0<=kappa<1/2. Suppose for EVERY epsilon>0 there are
constants c_epsilon,C_epsilon>0 such that for EVERY sufficiently large
integer j a measurable E_j subset [j,j+1] satisfies

    |E_j|>=c_epsilon j^-kappa,
    ess sup_(y in E_j)|F(y)|<=C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j). ([restricted research revision]-V1)

Then the full field is O_epsilon(exp((gamma+epsilon)y)) on the real
axis and L(s,chi) has no zero in Re(s)>gamma. The converse follows
from the full-field bound; this is an equivalent observation criterion,
not a proof that the arithmetic hypothesis holds. Fixed positive-length
intervals also work. Arbitrarily shrinking intervals need another proof.
No missing logarithmic intervals, density-one substitute, finite sample
or selected signed subfield is permitted.

Here is the mechanism, including the errors. A complex polynomial of
degree N on a unit interval obeys

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N ess sup_E |P|,  |E|>=delta.

Quantile Lagrange interpolation proves this for complex values. Given
a prior complex bound C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), expand to
N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j) on Cauchy radius sqrt(tau(N+1)). Both Taylor
remainders are multiplied by the interpolation factor. The resulting
single-step exponent is h=gamma+2kappa(b-gamma), with subexponential
loss. The calculation at kappa>=1/2 gives no improvement by THIS
method; it is not an impossibility theorem for other sampling arguments.

The bilateral Mellin identity

    integral_R F(y)exp(-sy)dy = exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi)

first excludes zeros to the right of h. Only AFTER this exclusion is
the improved complex bound replenished. Ordinary character summation
gives polynomial growth of L on fixed positive half-planes. Regularize
the principal pole by (s-1)L, choose a zero-free logarithm on a disk
centered at2+it, and use Borel--Caratheodory with a positive fixed disk
gap. This proves polynomial reciprocal growth on every fixed line
b>h. Gaussian Mellin inversion then restores the complex bound at b.
Thus h_m=gamma+(2kappa)^m(B-gamma). For each output epsilon choose a
FINITE m and positive intermediate buffers; no infinite limiting
constant or circular reciprocal assumption is used.

## 2. Exact fixed-family and f3 extensions

For each fixed finite-order Eisenstein Hecke character of trivial
infinity type, use the ideal Gaussian with its presented ray modulus
and fixed omitted primes. The Euclidean lattice count is

    sum_(Na<=X) psi(a)=c_psi X+O_f(sqrt X+1).

The Eisenstein covering radius1/sqrt3 and six units give the required
count with the actual periodic residue weights. Nonprincipal c_psi=0;
the principal density has factor pi/(3sqrt3). The ideal count O(X)
pays the entire Gaussian estimate, while the error gives the required
polynomial continuation in Re(s)>1/2. The same theorem follows for
gamma>1/2, separately for EACH fixed member. No angular or growing-
conductor uniformity and no unsupported ordinary-to-Hecke transfer
is asserted.

For the literal f3 field, its actual Dirichlet series is B(s)/zeta(s),
where

    B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^-s)^-2(1-3^-s)^-2
          product_(p>=5)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)^2.

H and its inverse are bounded on each Re(s)>=b>1/2. The zeros of B
on Re(s)=1 are retained. The Mellin return excludes zeta zeros in
gamma<Re(s)<1; the known zero-free edge completes that return. The
zeta reciprocal and B replenish the complex bound in the required
order. This f3 conclusion concerns zeta; the ordinary and Hecke fields
need their OWN hypotheses.

The complete f3 square moment, full pointwise field and local-set
condition have the same exponent through Mellin continuation and
dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz with the paid left tail. This is not an arbitrary
L2-to-supremum estimate. The new exact target is

    OPEN-F3-VALLEY(gamma,kappa): [restricted research revision]-V1 for the complete f3 field,
    1/2<gamma<.874865 and fixed 0<=kappa<1/2.                 ([restricted research revision]-V2)

The strict numerical boundary here is CURRENT c4. Historical .874872
examples in the frozen W39 source are not represented as current gains.
Near gains, gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 remain possible conditional targets.
The W21 smooth-bump countermodel lacks this entire-Gaussian structure;
the W38 sparse-bad-interval countermodel fails the EVERY-interval
hypothesis. Both older failures remain correct in their stated scopes.

## 3. Other reviewed W39 developments

The selected C04 one-path importance sampler has optimum variance
V^2-|Z|^2, attained by probabilities proportional to the absolute
weights. For the actual ordinary Gaussian,
V=d_q exp(tau/2)exp(y)+O(exp(y/2)), where
d_q=zeta(2)^-1 product_(p|q)p/(p+1). Conditional on a desired small
mean of exponent gamma<1, an independent sample mean needs order
exp(2(1-gamma)y) samples for comparable RMS error. This is limited to
that estimator, not all algorithms, arithmetic grouping or control variates.

C01 preserves the signed tensor boundary. The exact rank is the number
of distinct nonzero row-prefix counts; distinct Gaussian logs give full
exponential-matrix rank. The analytic rank-r approximation has paid
error C(w)exp(Z)Z^r/r! times BOTH weighted coefficient l1 masses,
Z=UV/tau, with the corresponding operator l2 bound. On O(sqrt(log X))
bins, r=C3 log X can pay any prescribed fixed negative power for the
stated finite exponential masses. Actual signed growing-degree
contractions and the complete cross-Gram remain open. Sol wave01 A34
and W35 ancestry are credited; this adds no paid arithmetic sector.

F05's natural divisor normal operator squares conditioning; it does
not rule out every Hodge construction. D02's translated Gram determinant
misses a rank-one dangerous exponential; the two-mode/coalescing formula
requires nonzero amplitudes, distinct shifts and positive weighted
variance. B05's mask defect is 2Re(U,V)+||V||^2 and needs a LOWER bound
to inherit an upper estimate; its two-label Gaussian test is scoped.
The independent C05 heat audit preserves boundary flux; the raw kernel
adds E/tau to the normalized energy identity. A dangerous exponential
restores the old growth term. These are precise reopening conditions,
not blanket rejections of related methods.

## 4. Sampling, scope and evidence

All30 seeds froze at21:34:55UTC before portfolio history at21:35:01.
Pools froze AFTER history/deduplication, before draws and development.
Six first tests were A02,C04,F05,D02,C01,B05. Literal all-group rarity
eligibility was preserved, with base pool sizes23 and14. The critic's
protected E03 and uniform C05 were frozen before outcomes. E03 overlaps
the A02 proof; it is not a seventh author test or an extra discovery.
The [[private research revision] index](../[restricted mathematical source] research revision].md) retains every card and its
individual independent disposition. Both author and critic froze,
read back and stopped; only their own claims were released.

| Frozen artifact | Bytes | SHA256 |

| Author report | 38739 | df8115dede9dd0f06fcf5d3146ef71823800008f99d77450713fe9fdeb1ebab9 |
| Author manifest | 2823 | c838ac105f9a7f793b407834f387c0e4a7b9e966fb08d1b069e5b7dd6e8d7ce6 |
| Independent report | 39606 | 2065f4f1495b7dba146392b340673424e66e1187bdb758489616aed0ac482ef7 |
| Independent freeze | 4183 | 2b151382cf16029d66f55e539ebc5120ac3eb00b5052ac3f2b100ec4d1ca2ba6 |

Immutable mathematical source bindings matched. Mutable proof/index
observations changed as c4 and H were integrated, and are explicitly
identified in the controller receipt. The independent finite evidence
replay matches after removing only timestamps and those source
observations; full-byte equality of changing evidence is not claimed.
Analytic acceptance comes from the complete written arguments. No
arithmetic small-value estimate, full signed moment or increased c follows.

Extract E(s)=L_K^S(s+1,eta) and the literal sixth-power series
V6(s)=product_(p notin S)(1-R)^-1. Their coefficients and inverse coefficients
have finite absolute mass at sigma>2/3. With h=E V6 Rhat,

    rhat_p-1=[t(1-t)D^2-tR+t^2DR]/(1-D).              ([restricted research revision]-P3)

Both Rhat and its inverse converge in absolute coefficient mass for sigma>1/2.
The COMPLETE omitted-prime product obeys

    ||Rhat_>P-1||_sigma << P^(-2sigma)+P^(3-6sigma).  ([restricted research revision]-P4)

The product majorant includes every interaction among omitted primes. E and
V6 retain every prime; the finite Rhat product retains every valuation.
For the inherited beta=.8749, define W with transform exp(s^2)h/L and
What_P with transform exp(s^2)E V6 Rhat_<=P/L. Then

    ||W-What_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(-2beta).         ([restricted research revision]-P5)

The inherited beta norm is justified from the accepted fixed-family premise:
lattice residue counting gives polynomial L growth, the zero-free buffered

the complete U beta norm. Holomorphy alone is not used as a growth estimate.

At P=max(2,X^theta), a full signed What_P gamma norm with

## 3. Trying a signed repair that annihilates the leading mean

Taking absolute values was the proposed norm improvement; theoremA defeats
it even after exact integer coalescence. A more plausible repair gives the
residual a signed quotient profile chosen to cancel the leading mean.
Here that construction can be tested completely rather than guessed.

Let g(v)=(v-1)^3*(2-v)^3 on [1,2] and0 elsewhere, and set

    h(v)=v^2*g'(v),
    m0=integral_1^2 h(v)/v^2 dv=0,
    m1=integral_1^2 h(v)*log(v)/v^2 dv
         =-integral_1^2 g(v)/v dv <0.                    (6)

The extension g is C^2; h is C^1 with h(1)=h(2)=0 and |h|<=3/4.
This is an actual signed profile with its complete leading mean removed.
At each integer N prescribe the residual

    Delta_N(m,p)=1_(P<p<=2P)*h(m/p^r),
    Delta_N(N,1)=0,

and zero at all other states. It vanishes on the entire exact collar
m<=p^r. The finite recurrence

    F_N(m,y)=1-sum_(y<ell<=m,ell prime)
                    chi0(ell)F_N(floor(m/ell),ell)+Delta_N(m,y)          (7)

constructs the approximation and its defect, with all child states smaller
than m. Set Delta=0 unless y is a prime or the root as above. This defines
F_N without using an unknown value of M in its construction. Its exact
collar values are the genuine rough sums, not an imposed constant1.
The root error is the full G92 scalar, with no complementary residual.

THEOREM B. Fix u>3 with omega''(u)!=0, P=N^(1/(u+r+1)), and fixed q,r.
For (7), the exact signed root error satisfies

    F_N(N,1)-M_chi0(N)
      ~ (q/phi(q))*m1*omega''(u)*kappa_r
                         *N*P^(-r)/(log P)^4.            (8)

Thus the leading cancellation in (6) earns one logarithm but no fixed
power. For any gamma<1 choose a sufficiently large fixed u with omega''(u)
nonzero and (u+1)/(u+r+1)>gamma. Then this bounded, signed, exact-collar
residual has root error larger than N^gamma. This is a fully induced
defect calculation, not just a formal subtraction from a bound.

Proof. Put L=log p, A=N/p^(r+1), u_p=log A/log p, and v_m=m/p^r.
Let S_m=W_q(N/(pm),p-). Exactly C_m=-(S_m-S_(m+1)). Because h vanishes
at the endpoints and outside [1,2], discrete summation by parts gives

    sum_m C_m*h(v_m)=-sum_m S_m*(h(v_m)-h(v_(m-1))).     (9)

There are no omitted terms at either sharp support endpoint. Apply (2)
with K=2 uniformly on v in [1,2], using a fixed compact near u>3:

    S_m=A/v_m*[ b1*omega'(u_p-log(v_m)/L)/L^2
                +b2*omega''(u_p-log(v_m)/L)/L^3]
                          +O_(q,r,u)(A/L^4).

The total variation of the fixed h is bounded, so the remainder stays
O(A/L^4) in (9), rather than being multiplied by the number of m. Replacing
the main smooth sum by its integral has error O(A/(p^r*L^2)), which is
smaller. Taylor expansion and integration by parts give

    integral h'(v)/v dv=m0=0,
    integral h'(v)*log(v)/v dv=m1-m0=m1.

Hence the COMPLETE prime block is

    sum_m C_m*h(v_m)=b1*m1*omega''(u_p)*A/L^3
                 +O(A/L^4+A/(p^r*L^2)).                 (10)

The b2 term also vanishes by m0=0; no value or sign of b2 is needed.
Now u_p=u+O(1/log P), and PNT sums (10) over the entire prime band to
give (8). The principal natural zeros were already included in (2).

To justify arbitrarily large u with omega''(u)!=0, if omega'' vanished
on a tail then omega would be affine there. Substitution into
u*omega'=omega(u-1)-omega(u) forces its slope to vanish. The constant-tail
contradiction from theoremA applies. Thus the theorem is nonvacuous beyond
every prescribed target threshold, without a floating-point derivative
test or a conjecture about oscillations.

This construction is root-adapted through P and N, as the independent
error-norm question allows. It is an obstruction for a fixed-shape
annihilation certificate, not a claim that all source residuals are free
to vary this way. Its recurrence is finite but no economy of computing
the exact collar is asserted.

## 3. B1–6: actual occupations and the complete unexposed covariance

Let P be any finite prime set containing2 and excluding3, Q=product P,
a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)), and r_P(n)=f(n)a_P(n).
The identity f=a_P r_P is pointwise. Both factors retain all valuations;
r_P consists of exactly the primes outside P other than3. The complete
period mean of a_P is product(1-2/p)=0. No squarefree probability law
is used.

For any Q-periodic a of mean0 and |a|<=1, let its discrete Fourier
coefficients be b_k, k=1,...,Q-1. They satisfy |b_k|<=1. With
h(t)=g_tau(log t), zero-extended to t<=0, ordinary Poisson and m>=2
integrations by parts give

    |sum_n a(n)h(n/x)|
       <=2 zeta(m)(Q/(2pi))^m x^(1-m)||h^(m)||_1.       (R41-B1)

Indeed the reindexing r=Qj-k is one-to-one over nonzero integers not
divisible by Q. Its absolute m-series is bounded by2zeta(m); there is
no lost extra factor Q. Flatness of h at0 pays every boundary term.
This is a direct periodic-source calculation, not a masked application
of a completed alternating field.

For fixed0<delta<1 and Q<=X^(1-delta), even one fixed sufficiently large
m proves any prescribed negative power uniformly on [X,2X]. The stronger
displayed bound with m=2+floor(delta log X/tau) is also valid, because
the *explicit* G7 contract bounds its growing derivative order:

    ||h^(m)||_1<=K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau(m-1)^2/2).

Substitution bounds the logarithm by
-delta^2(log X)^2/(2tau)+O_(delta,tau)(log X loglog X).
Constants are independent of the actual list P, but depend on the fixed
delta and tau. Thus F_P=sum a_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x)) is O_A(X^-A) for every
fixed A. Shrinking delta with X or changing tau is not part of the theorem.

Put Z=sum g_tau(log(n/x))=exp(tau/2)x+O_A(x^-A), by period1 Poisson,
and use the actual positive all-integer measure mu_x(n)=g_tau(log(n/x))/Z.
Each prime-occupation pattern indicator is Q-periodic, with CRT mean

    pi_P(s)=product_(s_p=1)1/p *product_(s_p=0)(1-1/p).

Apply R41-B1 to indicator-minus-mean, of absolute size at most1. The
normalization is exact: its Gaussian sum divided by Z is the difference
between actual pattern probability and pi_P(s). Summing over all patterns
costs at most2^|P|<=Q<=X. Increasing the prescribed negative power once
pays this factor, so the full L1 pattern error is O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A),
uniformly over the full shell and every permitted P. No rare pattern was
discarded and no division by a possibly tiny individual pi_P(s) was used.
This is an absolute joint-law error, not a relative conditional-law estimate.

W38 used a squarefree Gaussian measure, giving occupation1/(p+1) and a
logarithmic partial-parity bias. W41's measure is on all integers, giving
1/p and the prime-two zero mean. Both statements are valid at their
different sources; W41 does not repair or disprove W38's result.

Define the explicit bilinear covariance

    C_P=E[a_P r_P]-E[a_P]E[r_P].

Then, without approximation,

    F=Z C_P+F_P E[r_P].                                  (R41-B2)

Since |E r_P|<=1 and Z is comparable to X throughout the shell, for any
chosen permitted family P_X the complete field estimate is equivalent to

    integral_X^(2X)|C_(P_X)(x)|^2 dx/x
                       <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon). (R41-B3)

Both directions follow from the norm triangle with the uniform rapidly
small F_P error; the gamma>.5 restriction is needed for the existing
zero return, not for this elementary covariance identity. Keeping P={2}
already yields the equivalence. For example, with p_j=Pr(1_(2|n)=j) and
m_j=E[r_{2}|1_(2|n)=j], direct expansion gives
C_{2}=2p0p1(m0-m1). The exposed even/odd probabilities are close to1/2;
their *conditional rough means* still carry the full problem.

More generally, m_P(s)=E[r_P|s] satisfies

    C_P=sum_s Pr(s)(a_P(s)-E[a_P])m_P(s).                (R41-B4)

All these conditional means and signed interactions remain. The accurate
unconditional product law bounds none of their needed cancellation.
For a fixed ordinary chi replace r_P by chi r_P, including zero values.
The positive law stays unchanged, the explicitly bilinear formula stays
valid, |r|<=1 still pays the error, and R41-A9 supplies the exact return.
No character independence, pair-mask domination or ideal-norm transfer
is implied. The covariance target uses the fixed F for Mellin continuation,
not the moving periodic field.

**Attribution correction:** [private research revision] gaussian-signed S24–29 already derives
the all-valuation prime-divisibility product, its mean zero at2, and rapidly
small periodic Gaussian remainder in a priced radical/ray range. More
directly, post52 Sol D33.1–5 has the same finite-prime f3 field, the same
Fourier reindexing, a growing period, and the exact full rough correction
whose exponent bound is equivalent to F's. That independent batch and
its Sol/Astra reviews were frozen before this W41 final review. D33's
formula R41-B1 already implies arbitrary Q<=X^(1-delta), even though its
worked sieve is z_X=a log X/loglog X. Therefore general-Q cancellation is
an explicit extension of presentation, not a new analytic mechanism.
W41's all-pattern L1 statement and normalized conditional covariance are
useful refinements of that same source contract. The covariance is a
reorganization of the full rough correction, not a weaker estimate.

The author correctly credits W34/W35 Poisson and W38's different law, but
its phrase “distinct f3 consequence” needs the [private research revision]/D33 qualification.
This is a record-relative mathematical deduplication. It does not assert
that the author saw an unavailable contemporary packet, copied it, or
