## 6. Reviewer consequence: a nearby band and the actual decaying tail

The following are consequences of (R17) and the existing source tail rule, not a new full R4 estimate or an independent mathematical cycle.

First, let Y=U^kappa. Using E_K>=rho, the raw margin is at least

    (delta+1/3)(r+s)+rho-1-kappa.

Its derivative in delta is at least 217/100-625/486=21481/24300>0 on the physical box. Thus its lower endpoint is at delta=17/25 and r+s=217/100, giving

    kappa_* =268943/170625,
    margin >= kappa_*-kappa.                           (R19)

For example kappa=39/25=1.56 pays not just the author's cutoff but its adjacent band, with raw margin 2768/170625>.0162. A margin 1/100 remains after sufficiently small combined losses. This merely spends some of the already proved room; it supplies no new cancellation input.

Second, PR9's rule following B3.4 requires discarding tails on the genuine arithmetic expression before extending a coprime sum or taking an absolute Fourier integral. A direct raw estimate suffices. Fix a bounded-overlap dyadic partition q_a~A before live labels, and write L_A=A^6N0^2/U. Each copy has at most O(H_J N0 U^epsilon) original inverse/slot tuples by ideal counting. The two central roots and the primitive Poisson factor together are O(U/(q_a^6 N0^2)) on their original supports. Primitive Gauss factors have modulus one; masks can only reduce this absolute bound. Thus the genuine coprime sector, for q_ell~H, satisfies

    |R_(A,H)| <= sum |genuine source terms in that dyad|
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) A^(-5) H
                    [1+H/L_A]^(-B).                  (R20)

This uses O(A) possible a and O(H) frequencies. It keeps the full kernel, every original mask and both heights; no mutual-gcd extension or common Fourier separation is used in this tail bound. All derivative orders and raw-factor powers are fixed before choosing B.

For fixed tau>0, summing the dyadic frequencies H>U^tau L_A in (R20) costs at most

    H_J U^epsilon A N0^2 U^(-tau(B-1)).               (R21)

Here L_A>>1 throughout the actual box, so no small-radius lattice term is missing. Summing A<<U^(1/6), and using r+s<47/20 and v<=1/20, bounds all these tails by

    H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1)).                   (R22)

The exponent 149/30 is a deliberately coarse raw-factor budget:
1/6+2(r+s)+2v<=149/30. For any desired M, a finite B>1+(149/30+M+1)/tau makes (R22) O(H_J U^(-M)), taking epsilon<1. Fixed support factors are absorbed in the tail threshold or a small geometric pad. This is the existing B3.4 tail principle applied to this literal source, not a new arithmetic estimate. Only after this tail is paid do we use the algebraic extension and common-profile separation on the retained finite region.

Consequently the full high term may be replaced, up to this proved rapidly decaying tail, by the exact middle region

    U^(39/25)<q_ell<=U^tau A^6 N0^2/U                 (R23)

inside each original a-dyad. The upper threshold depends only on its nominal dyad and original scales. This keeps the prior common-profile separation valid. The lowest natural dual scale has exponent 2(r+s+v)-1>3.34, so (R23) remains a very large unpaid region. For the largest a-dyads its cap can approach U^(4.8+tau). Nothing in (R20)-(R22) bounds that central high-frequency mass.

The exact complementary statement is therefore R4=R_nonunique+R_middle+R_low+R_far, with R_low paid by (R19), R_far paid by (R22), and the SUM R_nonunique+R_middle still open. These pieces can have either sign. This refinement closes only the decaying infinite tail and states precisely which finite middle remains.

      *product_(p>=5)(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2.   (D48.5)

At ramified primes chi(p)=0 the factor is exactly1. The infinite
product and inverse converge normally for Re s>.5, since their
nonconstant terms start at p^-2s and2p^-sigma<1 at p>=5,sigma>.5.
Denominators have zeros only at Re s=0; prime2 numerator zeros
are on Re s=1. Hence W_chi is nonzero and holomorphic in.5<Re s<1.
Gaussian Mellin transformation gives exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi/L.
D48.3 plus dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz continues that FIXED transform to
Re s>gamma. Multiplication by L and the identity theorem exclude
zeros gamma<Re s<1. The principal pole is excluded; usual right-edge
facts complete zero exclusion. Constants depend on each fixed chi;

## 2. Independent development: cofactor-resolved residual transfer

For squarefree a,b in S put g=(a,b), l=[a,b], and define the literal cofactor sum

    M_{chi,lq}(y)=sum_{m<=y,(m,lq)=1} mu(m)chi(m).

Writing d=lm in (1), squarefreeness forces (m,l)=1. Since mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g), exact complete entries are

    (A_chi^{-1})_ab = mu(g)chi(l) M_{chi,lq}(N/l).             (3)

The right side is zero when l>N. In particular the entire first row is

    R_chi,N(a)=chi(a) M_{chi,aq}(N/a),     |R_chi,N(a)|<=N/a.  (4)

This is an identity for finite coprimality masks, not a claim of uniform estimates for growing-conductor L-functions. Large labels are short cofactor sums; small labels can retain the original hard arithmetic.

For any proposed approximate column z on S, with its COMPLETE residual r=e_1-A_chi z, the exact reconstruction is

    M_chi(N)=z_1 + sum_{a in S} R_chi,N(a) r_a,
    |M_chi(N)-z_1| <= N sum_{a in S} |r_a|/a.                 (5)

No projection or residual coordinate can be omitted. If r is supported on a>N/H, H>=1, (5) is at most H||r||_1. Thus a full global inverse norm is an unnecessarily expensive default bill for residuals concentrated at large labels. The stronger exact signed residual sum in (5) remains available; its absolute majorant is only a sufficient certificate.

A precise sufficient open input is: for every fixed ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer N, construct z=z_{chi,N,epsilon} on the ACTUAL S such that

    |z_1| + N sum_{a in S} |(e_1-A_chi z)_a|/a
       <<_{chi,epsilon} N^{gamma+epsilon}.                  OPEN-RES

This implies the pointwise Mertens bound and the same all-height zero exclusion as above. First improvement requires gamma<.8748540364; gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 are the conditional 1/6 and 1/4 targets. No vector satisfying this budget is constructed. An algorithm computing the exact inverse is not evidence that its observed coordinate is small. The criterion remains hard even though its residual payment is more precise.

The cheapest candidate demonstrates the danger. Set

    z_T=E^{-T}(chi(d) 1_{d<=T})_{d in S},   1<=T<=N.

Then z_T,1=M_chi(T) and

    r_T(a)=1_{a=1}-sum_{d|a,d<=T}mu(d)
          =sum_{d|a,d>T}mu(d).                               (6)

Residual support is indeed confined to a>T. But for T<=N/2 and primes p in (N/2,N] not dividing q, r_T(p)=-1 and R_chi,N(p)=chi(p). Therefore

    sum_a |R_chi,N(a)r_T(a)| >= #{N/2<p<=N : p does not divide q}
                               ~ N/(2 log N).               (7)

The weaker explicit budget in (5) is at least as large. The ordinary prime number theorem suffices; only finitely many excluded primes divide fixed q. [DLMF 27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records this classical asymptotic. The same conclusion holds for a cutoff <=beta N with any fixed beta<1 after shortening the prime interval. Equation (7) is an absolute-price obstruction for this specified truncation, NOT a lower bound for the signed residual, M_chi, or a general certificate. This preserves the real opportunity: construct a residual aligned with the actual signs, or eliminate the prime residual through a new complete arithmetic correction while paying every new coordinate.

Six finite exact matrix cases, q=1 and the quartic character modulo 5 at N=2,12,24, independently verify the literal displayed convention, (3), and (6)'s reconstruction for T=1,floor(N/2),N. Arithmetic values are small Gaussian integers, exactly represented; the algebra above supplies the general proof. No unchanged author diagnostic was rerun.

## Exact coefficient and valuation audit

For J=[U^eta,U^(2eta)), the ordered pair weight is sum_{p,q in J,pq|b} logNp logNq/(logNb)^2. At p=q it requires v_p(b)>=2 and counts that pair ONCE, regardless of higher valuation. Expanding the square of the radical logarithm removes precisely the v_p(b)=1 diagonal. Hence the author's (8) is exact. Since J is disjoint from the old closed band, omega<=ell_J(b)^2/(logNb)^2<=(1-theta)^2<=1-theta. This is a coefficient inequality only.

For every extracted L and d=pq, put h=d/gcd(d,L). At each prime the remaining divisibility requirement is max(v_p(d)-v_p(L),0), so d|Lc iff h|c. Substituting c=h c' preserves all remaining valuations and gives the exact phase phi(h), normalization (Nh)^(-1/2), and length E/Nh. It does not divide by a character. If p=q, h=p^2,p,1 for v_p(L)=0,1,>=2. If p!=q, h contains exactly the missing primes. Natural zeros are multiplicative through this substitution, even when primes occur simultaneously in L, the inverse puncture and the cofactor. The logarithmic profile is exact: NL*Nc=D*(Nc/E). This verifies author (15), including the most dangerous middle valuation.

A useful independent refinement is available without any new analytic input. Write s=(1+beta)/2, w_p=logNp/logD, I=sum_{p|L}w_p, V=sum_{p not|L}w_p(Np)^(-s). The EXACT positive pair mass after the shortened plain estimate is

  A_L=sum_{p,q in J} w_p w_q N(pq/gcd(pq,L))^(-s)
     =(I+V)^2-sum_{p in J,v_p(L)=1}w_p^2[1-(Np)^(-s)].

Proof: all distinct pairs factor as products of the single-prime weights; their diagonal removal is restored by p^(-2s) when v_p(L)=0, p^(-s) when v_p(L)=1, and1 when v_p(L)>=2. Thus only valuation1 differs from the diagonal of (I+V)^2. This identity includes p=q and every shared-prime equality. In particular A_L<= (I+V)^2; no extra diagonal loss is needed. It is a sharper label-specific absolute block mass, not a signed norm contraction or a new global power saving.

Nonempty support gives NL<=CD, so I<=1+O(1/logD). Ideal counting gives V<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2), A=U^(2eta). Therefore A_L<<U^epsilon A^(1-beta). The original whole profile contributes only its declared common derivative/height envelope. ## Full product, collisions and both gates

For p!=q, dyadic lengths lambda_i<=2eta give total added width<=4eta. The exact product normalization is P1^(-1/2)P2^(-1/2)E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2). Common profile separation precedes live primes or colors; the arithmetic coefficients logNp/logU stay fixed when D is differentiated. G137 gives r+2v<=1-.01017 before losses. Thus r+2(v+lambda1+lambda2)<=1-.00217 at eta=.001. From 2r+8v<=2-.02034+4v, the second enlarged gate has margin at least .78834=39417/50000. When a distinct new prime equals an old slot prime, that old slot is removed and its actual normalizers have bounded absolute dyadic mass: the two prime scales are comparable and there are O(P) ideals at scale P against normalization O(P^-1). The plain shortening still yields the full (P1P2)^(-beta/2). Two new distinct primes cannot both equal the same old prime, since the old slots have disjoint supports. On the surviving all-distinct variables, h^h times the NORMALIZED random-color expectation is exactly the indicator that all h prime IDEALS differ. For p=q, retaining the complete old Q and inverse before extracting the phase gives norm mass sum_p (Np)^(-1-beta) times bounded logarithmic coefficients. Its dyadic sum is O(P^-beta). Squaring yields Z^-2beta, including p=q equal to an old slot prime. The off-diagonal gives (P1P2)^-beta<=Z^-2beta as well. ## Full removed source and complementary signal

G198's complete blocks have L=lcm(q0,k^2), not q0*k^2 when primes overlap. Their absolute coefficient mass after the shortened plain bound and every q0-smooth inverse restoration is T^-beta/2 U^epsilon. Pure large-prime plain columns paired with coprime squarefree inverse tuples still have F=1 and theta=omega=0. This is an actual coefficient example, not evidence of any high-zero row or lower bound. The three-coordinate separation factors the original witness twist first, leaving a height-free smooth kernel. Its Fourier measure is fixed before rows, extracted primes or coloring. ## 5. Moving finite twists, natural zeros, and masked Möbius sums

Insert the finite unit-neutral projector. For each dual ideal
`mathfrak n` and unit component `u0`,
\[
\eta(\lambda u_0)\bar\eta(\mathfrak n)
=\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(c)
 \overline{\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(e)},
\qquad
\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(c)
=\vartheta_c(\lambda u_0)
 \overline{\vartheta_c(\mathfrak n)}.
\tag{BC12}
\]
Cubic reciprocity makes this a finite-order character in the good core
variable. Its primitive good conductor consists of the primes for
which `v_p(mathfrak n)` is nonzero modulo three, hence has norm at
most `q_mathfrak_n`.

**Primes dividing `mathfrak n` to a multiple of three still impose
natural zeros.** They remain finite deletions even when absent from
the primitive conductor. The supplementary twist at `lambda u0` has
fixed conductor. Arbitrary fixed-S valuations of the dual ideal do
not create a moving good conductor.

Let `h=1/2-z`. I-HECKE gives
\[
\sum_{\substack{m\\(m,M)=1}}
\mu(m)\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(m)q_m^hF(q_m/U)
\ll
(q_{\mathfrak n}q_M)^\delta T^A
U^{b+\Re h+\delta}\mathcal S(F).
\tag{BC13}
\]
Here `S(F)` uses finitely many Euler derivatives on a fixed norm
annulus. The reciprocal series is `1/L^S(s,chi*)` with the additional
deleted Euler factors required by `M` and the natural zeros at
`rad(mathfrak n)`. Unramified deleted primes contribute factors
`(1-chi*(p)q_p^(-s))^(-1)`, bounded by a subpower of the deletion
norm on the fixed line `b>0`. The primitive reciprocal costs a
subpower of its actual conductor and height by I-HECKE. Buffered
Perron bounds and partial summation also permit a sharp interval
endpoint. All preliminary losses can be decreased independently.

No subpower bound for a moving angular L-function is used. The only
moving reciprocal functions in (BC13) have finite order.

## 2. New exact conductor geometry

Fix an original ordered long-prime pair. Set M=pi*pi', Q=q_M asy N^2. Fold the ENTIRE actual short-source sum and its complete bounded core into W(R,P,P'). It includes both projector indicators and all retained profile/component coefficients; it may depend on the prime pair. Its row support is inside the original O(K)-point disk, and the two mark supports have O(L) points. The original support injects modulo each long prime for sufficiently large Z in the pressure box. These properties survive the signed short-source recombination.

The accepted exact JN4--JN9 transform, with both character inversions and their Gauss factors, has native kernel

    chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4

times b(pi) conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_(pi,pi'), where b retains alpha and fixed ray data and the exact CRT root zeta is not set to one. The finite group is (O/M) x (O/pi) x (O/pi'), with Q^2 elements; its unitary transform has factor 1/Q and phases -Rh/M -Ps/pi +P's'/pi'. This already accounts for the two local 1/q factors. No new physical factor arises.

The kernel is zero unless

    U = {(h,M)=1, s nonzero mod pi, s' nonzero mod pi'}.

Choose integral representatives in bounded fundamental parallelograms, so q_h<=C Q and q_s,q_s'<=C N. For each nonzero h let a2(h) be the product of GOOD prime ideals at which v(h) is odd. For nonzero s let a3(s) be the product of good prime ideals at which v(s) is nonzero modulo 3. These are ideal products; neither integer squarefree kernels nor rational norms are factored in their place.

By JN17/JNR5 the first prime-variable good local exponent is 3v(h)+2v(s) modulo 6 and the second is 3v(h)+4v(s') modulo 6. The exact elementary equivalences are

    3A+2B=0 (mod 6) iff A=0 (mod 2) and B=0 (mod 3),
    3A+4B=0 (mod 6) iff A=0 (mod 2) and B=0 (mod 3).

Consequently the two GOOD primitive finite conductor ideals are exactly

    f1_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s)),
    f2_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s')).                         ([restricted research revision].1)

In particular a2(h) divides both. A cubic mark factor cannot cancel the quadratic row factor, even at a shared good prime. At canceled conductor primes the original natural zero of the imprimitive character remains; ([restricted research revision].1) does not turn it into an unrestricted constant. Fixed bad-place and angular data are retained separately. This is not an ordinary-Hecke prime-sum estimate.

Each conductor declaration freezes the chosen integral indices and takes the reciprocal finite-kernel character in that prime variable. The pair-dependent Fourier coefficient still samples h/(pi*pi'), s/pi and s'/pi'. Nothing here supplies a common prime-independent weight after regrouping by conductor; the original angular alpha factor also remains.

Let a frequency selector, allowed to depend on h,s,s', the prime pair and all coefficients, retain only points of U where AT LEAST ONE of q_f1_good or q_f2_good is <=D. It is pointwise contained in

    E_D x (O/pi) x (O/pi'),
    E_D={h !=0: q_a2(h)<=D}.                          ([restricted research revision].2)

This containment, rather than commutation of the adaptive selector itself, is what permits the row-only uncertainty bound.

Here D denotes a conductor cutoff only; it is not the mark-collision divisor D in JSR11, or the Type I factor length D in SF2. No D*Omega factor from those different variables has been dropped. Their roots and complete projectors are inside the actual tensor before this Fourier statement is applied.

For 1<=D<=C Q, write the ideal of a chosen h as a_S*a*b^2, where a is good squarefree, q_a<=D, and a_S ranges over the finitely many squarefree products of fixed bad primes. The ideal class number is one and each principal ideal has six generators, so there are only a fixed number of possible representatives for each factorization. Elementary Eisenstein ideal counting gives

    #E_D <= C_S sum_(q_a<=D) sqrt(Q/q_a)
          <= C_S sqrt(QD).                            ([restricted research revision].3)

The last inequality follows by partial summation from #ideals(q<=x)<=C x. Arbitrary powers at bad primes are already in b^2; their parity contributes only the finite a_S choice. For D beyond the stated range one uses #E_D<=Q. This estimate is uniform in the orientation of the chosen fundamental cell.

For every fixed physical mark pair, Cauchy on the O(K) rows gives squared Fourier mass <=C K #E_D/Q times its physical squared norm. Plancherel in both mark variables preserves this inequality because E_D is independent of those variables. The original signed short sum remains inside W throughout. Therefore ([restricted research revision].2)--([restricted research revision].3) imply

    ||1_U 1_{min(q_f1_good,q_f2_good)<=D} W_hat||_2^2
       <= C_orig K sqrt(D)/N ||W||_2^2.               ([restricted research revision].4)

This holds for arbitrary further adaptive sub-selection. Accepted JNR5 independently gives

    ||1_U W_hat||_2^2
       >= [1-O_orig((1+L)/N)] ||W||_2^2.              ([restricted research revision].5)

Thus, when the denominator is nonzero, the eligible-mass fraction in ([restricted research revision].4) is at most C K sqrt(D)/N divided by the bracket in ([restricted research revision].5). If W is zero, no nonvanishing is claimed.

At the pressure point D=Z^d, the upper fraction is O(Z^(-.003+d/2)). In particular D=Z^.004 captures O(Z^(-.001)), and the good-finite-principal choices D=1 capture O(Z^(-.003)). A fixed positive fraction in this coordinatewise norm-approximation strategy requires D at least a constant multiple of (N/K)^2=Z^.006. These are squared-mass statements about the exact native tensor, not size statements about its signed pairing with the character kernel.

The sample cutoff D=Z^.004 is a concrete frequency threshold only. The .004 H pressure deficit does not by itself impose that conductor budget, and no such identification is used in a return estimate.

The joint product-conductor version is also useful: q_f1_good*q_f2_good<=Y forces q_a2(h)<=sqrt(Y), hence its squared-mass fraction is at most C K Y^(1/4)/N divided by the same eligible bracket. A fixed fraction therefore requires Y at least a constant multiple of (N/K)^4=Z^.012. A pair-product budget Z^.008 still captures only O(Z^(-.001)). Thus the common quadratic conductor cannot be allocated independently between the two cubic marks to evade the count. For Y>C Q^2 the trivial fraction bound is used.

The representative convention is material: the result is for bounded integral lifts, which are exactly what makes a proposed small-conductor reciprocity argument quantitative. Adding arbitrary modulus multiples is not a permitted way to preserve the claimed conductor budget. The original Fourier value itself is independent of that presentation; a route using unbounded alternative lifts would have to charge its new support, conductor and moving weights separately.

## G208: exact pair mass and a fifth actual row class

The reviewer sharpens the uniform block calculation. Write

    s=(1+beta)/2, w_p=log N(p)/log D,
    I=sum_(p in J,p|L)w_p,
    V=sum_(p in J,p not|L)w_p N(p)^(-s).

Then the EXACT positive pair mass is

    A_L=sum_(p,q in J)w_p w_q N(pq/gcd(pq,L))^(-s)
       =(I+V)^2-sum_(p in J,v_p(L)=1)w_p^2[1-N(p)^(-s)]
       <=(I+V)^2.                                  (3)

Distinct pairs factor. On the diagonal, valuation0 contributes p^(-2s),
valuation1 contributes p^(-s), and valuation at least2 contributes1.
Only the middle case differs from the diagonal of `(I+V)^2`. This proves
(3), including all p=q and shared-prime cases, with no extra diagonal loss.
Since `I<=1+O(1/log D)` and `V<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2)`, it also
reproves the uniform block bound above. It is a sharper label-specific
positive mass, not a new global power saving or signed contraction.

Keep all FOUR previously paid classes FIRST. Their remaining actual rows
have `|C_T^[1-theta]|>|M(R)S(D)|/4`. On that complement, define

    Omega_pair={u: |C_T^[omega](u)|>=|M_u(R)S_u(D)|/8}.

before beta is weakened to physical delta, giving

         <<H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).             (4)

Q is never divided out. This fifth class is disjoint by construction;
its preloss reserve above the requested eta is `9eta/25`.
Every remaining row satisfies

    |C_T^[1-theta-omega]|>|M(R)S(D)|/8,
    N(n/rad n)<T NP,
    0<=1-theta(b)-omega(b)<=1-theta(b).               (5)

and were paid explicitly in (1)-(3). The repeat support is a necessary

## 4. Development23: full large-prime complement and sharp diameter

Let sqrt(X)<=y<=X, fix low-prime unit phases and zeros at p|q0, and put a_z(n)=mu(n)z(n). Every squarefree n<=X with a prime factor p>y has exactly one such factor, with n=pm and m<=X/p<p. Thus

    M_z(X)=S_y(X)-sum_(y<p<=X,p not dividing q0)z_p A(X/p),
    S_y(X)=sum_(n<=X,P^+(n)<=y)a_z(n),
    A(t)=sum_(m<=t)a_z(m), t<=X/y<=y.                 (R7)

The cofactor is determined entirely by the low phases. There is no missing gcd(m,p) restriction, because m<p, and repeated-prime contributions vanish by mu. Natural zeros remain in A and in the outer exclusion.

Set R_y(X)=sum_p |A(X/p)|. Choosing each independent z_p to align its whole cofactor gives maximum distance R_y from S_y and diameter2R_y between two compatible sums. These are a radius and a diameter, not a claim that every point of the intervening disk is attainable. If low phases are real signs, A is real; opposite sign choices attain S_y+R_y and S_y-R_y. The preceding CRT proof realizes both by actual real characters, with the same low data and zeros through X.

Grouping by the EXACT integer m=floor(X/p) gives

    R_y(X)=sum_(1<=m<=floor(X/y))|A(m)|
       [pi_q0(X/m)-pi_q0(max(y,X/(m+1)))].            (R8)

The lower endpoint is strict and the upper inclusive; a terminal empty interval contributes zero. When y<=X/2, A(1)=1 gives R_y>=pi_q0(X)-pi_q0(X/2). For fixed q0, ordinary PNT makes this (1/2+o(1))X/log X. I checked the ordinary prime asymptotic in [NIST DLMF 27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12); no progression uniformity or improved zero-free input is used. The exact identities and prime-count inequality require no PNT.

This is a genuine obstruction to a CONDUCTOR-INDEPENDENT, phase-blind small-prime certificate that claims a uniformly sublinear complement. It is not an obstruction for one fixed chi as X tends to infinity.

The reported fixed-modulus escape is proved: characters modulo a fixed q that agree on every unramified prime<=q agree on every unit residue. Factor its least positive representative r<=q into such primes; nonunit values are already zero. Hence y>=q removes the apparent freedom in the tail. For y=sqrt X this holds once X>=q^2. The adversarial pair uses changing, generally different moduli, precisely where that argument is unavailable.

The whole smooth complement, every cofactor and all pairwise interactions in a later energy remain. The geometric radius is no estimate of the actual fixed-character signed sum. The useful next input must exploit the fixed modulus's global linkage, rather than treat its large-prime values as independent phases.

statement:
## 2. Independent reconstruction of the author's deletion and parity claims

Let D_X={n<=X:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, including1, for fixed q and real X>=1. Let k(n)=omega(n), K_X=max_D k(n), 0<rho<=1, lambda=1-rho and R=(2-rho)/rho. Retain zero outside D_X. The channel and inverse, with ROW d and COLUMN n, are

 B(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^k(d) lambda^(k(n)-k(d)),
 C(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^(-k(n))(-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)).                 (1)

For C B, the intermediate e contributes rho^(-k(e))*rho^k(e); the remaining sum over e/d is (lambda-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)). For B C the analogous cancellation has the remaining rho^(k(d)-k(n)), which equals1 on the diagonal. Every intermediate divisor belongs to D_X. Thus BOTH products are the identity, with the endpoint rho=1 interpreted by0^0=1. Column sums give exactly ||B||_1=1 and ||C||_1=R^K_X.

Since the product of k distinct primes is at least(k+1)!, K_X<=(1+o(1))log X/loglog X. Fixed rho therefore costs X^o(1). This is the actual size-downset operator, not a full prime cube of dimension2^pi(X); charging exp(c*pi(X)) would be wrong. Conversely rho_X=(log X)^(-b), b>0, has R^K_X=X^(b+o(1)), using K_X~log X/loglog X from primorials and ordinary PNT. The asymptotic prime facts are verified in [DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), specifically27.12.1 and27.12.4-5. No progression, GRH or growing-q estimate is imported.

The actual input is nu(n)=chi(n) on D_X, not mu(n)chi(n). Its output is

 b_X(d)=rho^k(d)chi(d) sum_(m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1) mu(m)^2 chi(m)lambda^k(m).              (2)

The erased character phase and coprimality are forced, not optional. The observer h(d)=(-R)^k(d) satisfies sum_(d|n)h(d)B(d,n)=(-1)^k(n), since lambda-rho R=-1 at every prime. Hence <h,b_X>=M_chi(X), with ordinary bilinear evaluation, NO conjugation. The complete residual inequality is

 |M_chi(X)| <= |<h,btilde_X>| + R^K_X ||b_X-btilde_X||_1.                          (3)

Every-epsilon bounds on both terms at a common gamma give the full Mertens exponent for all real X and each fixed chi. A selected label set, nonprincipal phase deletion, or omitted approximation error invalidates this return. The construction supplies no such approximation.

Compressing by k(d) gives P_X(z)=Z_X(lambda+rho z), Z_X(z)=sum_D chi(n)z^k(n). This is an EXACT cutoff polynomial; the unrestricted finite Euler product contains products exceeding X and needs its size projection. Evaluation P_X(-R)=M_chi(X) and circle Parseval give |P_X(-R)|<=sqrt(sum_(j<=K)R^(2j)) ||P_X||_circle. At fixed rho the evaluation cost is subpower, but the required whole-circle estimate fails for the actual principal source.

Indeed principal coefficients beta_j are nonnegative and primes contribute lambda+rho z, so beta_0+beta_1>=pi_q(X) for every retention schedule. Thus ||P_X||_circle>=pi_q(X)/sqrt2. Removing all original degrees<=r, fixed integer r>=0, still leaves at least c_(q,r) X/(log X)^(r+1) products of r+1 distinct primes in((X/2)^(1/(r+1)),X^(1/(r+1))]. Each contributes a nonnegative degree-(r+1) coefficient vector of total mass1. Their sum has l2 norm at least its mass/sqrt(r+2). Remaining original layers add nonnegative coefficients. This verifies the author's lower bound uniformly even for X-dependent rho. It is a norm lower bound, NOT a lower bound for its alternating evaluation, not a rejection of growing signed deflation, and not a refutation of G106's exact quotient.

For fixed0<rho<1, cofactor primes give b_X(d)>>X/log X at every fixed label d. This particular lower bound excludes rho=1; the full observer norm is still due there.

statement:
### 1.3 Signed large-core tail, including its lower boundary

Put R=floor(X^delta). For any y>0, integration by parts using (R1.2)
gives

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(r/y))|
      <= C_beta y^beta Q_beta(log(R/y)),
    Q_beta(v)=exp(beta v)g(v)
                 +integral_v^infinity exp(beta w)|g'(w)|dw. (R1.6)

The first term pays the actual boundary -A_f(R)g(log(R/y)). Q_beta
is bounded for v<=0 and decays faster than every exp(-Bv) for v>=0.
For Y>=1, splitting integers k at Y and then into dyadic intervals,
using sum_(k<=V)d(k)<=C V log(2V), yields

    sum_k d(k)k^(-beta)Q_beta(log(k/Y))
       <= C_beta Y^(1-beta)log(2Y).                   (R1.7)

Apply this with y=x/(pq), k=pq and Y=x/R. Summing (R1.6) over every
actual p<q, and only then majorizing by d(k), bounds the entire removed
core by

    C x R^(beta-1)log(2x/R)=O(X^(1-eta)L).            (R1.8)

This is cancellation of the actual unrestricted f(r) core furnished by
(R1.4)--(R1.5). It is not a bound for an arbitrary smooth or masked core.

## 1. Exact sources and input contract

Internal sources:

- [Main manuscript B0.21--B0.25](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md#b03-the-physical-probe-signed-gram-bound-and-compensator): the actual probe, the \(Y^{-3/2}\) additive source, the outside \(Q^{-1/2}\), the original profiles and the exact finite compensator.
- [T06.1--T06.3 and T06.6](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]#t06-the-complete-same-core-sextic-square-function): every embedded branch, the completed coefficient \(q_c^{-1/2}q_n^{-1}\), actual marked weight \(K_D\), and its uniform rapid envelope.
- [PC1--PC5](../[private research revision]-continuation/physical-covariance.md): exact prime-power Gauss support, natural zeros, fixed-place factors and primitive character completion.
- [FR3, FR6--FR10 and FR19](../[private research revision]/physical-forced-rows.md): interpolation with the actual forced divisor, including principal multiples of six. The current FR file records independent review; this record proves its separate linear application.

External provenance is pinned throughout to CrossNox commit
\[
\texttt{f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db}.
\]

- [gram_mixed.tex, lines 17--31](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): raw source and completed-coefficient conventions.
- [Lines 145--240](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): the active/passive split and compact row profile.
- [Lines 287--373](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): the all-source Ramanujan identity and the nonsummable sixth-power tail in the unweighted refined count.
- [GramMixedArithmetic.lean](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/lean/GramMixedArithmetic.lean): the local transform and calibrated complete-mean identities. Its declarations do not assert the analytic block theorem proved below. No Lean rebuild is claimed.

The external identities are used as evidence and are derived in the local calculation below. The new estimate is the combination of that exact single-source reduction with a forced-row weight and its summable squareful-source Euler series.

**I-SEXTIC-XM.** Work over \(\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[\omega]\), with the original fixed excluded prime set \(S\), one primary generator for every good ideal, and the original finite unit/ray sectors. Write \(q_a=Na\). At each good prime the residue character has exact order six. Natural zero extensions, including those for positive exponents divisible by six, are retained. The fixed calibration \(\xi\) has fixed conductor, is nonprincipal, and is coprime to every good moving modulus. The original finite ray split puts source/completed reciprocity phases in row-independent coefficients; the only moving row character is \(\chi_A(m)\). All such coefficients have the inherited unit or fixed bounded size.

The source profiles \(W_0,W_1\) are the original smooth positive-annulus profiles; the completed profile is
\[
V(x)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt\pi}\exp(-(\log x)^2/4).
\]
The fixed slot count, fixed profile supports and fixed arithmetic data do not grow with \(Z\). The prime-slot weights are the actual bounded smooth weights, or their inherited divisor-bounded majorants.

**I-POISSON-XM.** Ordinary Poisson summation on the Eisenstein lattice is available for a primitive character of good conductor \(\mathfrak h\), multiplied by this fixed calibration. Its complete zero frequency is zero and its Gauss transform has modulus \(O_S(\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}})\). Section 3 gives the resulting row estimate, including subunit row scales. No I-HECKE, I-ZETA, Dedekind nonvanishing or higher moment estimate is used.

All scale parameters in the final probe application are in fixed polynomial ranges, with \(Q_D,Y_D\ge1\). Estimates for individual completed dyads are stated with their own small factors \((YCTNH_0Q)^\eta\), before summing the original infinite profile tails. This avoids treating infinite completed labels as polynomially bounded.

statement:
## 6. The already accepted family bound improves the source MP

The dependency is explicit and acyclic:

    original PR9/Gao inputs -> accepted c10 family theorem
      -> original PR9 B3.40 at fixed kappa10
      -> stronger weighted density below -> proposed c11.

PR9 B3.40 assumes 7/10<=kappa<=3/4, beta_*>=51/100 and 2beta_*-1<=kappa. It is uniform over that kappa interval with the original mesh/height/fixed-family order. In the contradiction for c11, accepted c10 gives beta_*<=theta10; hence kappa10=2theta10-1 is allowed. The lower beta_* condition follows whenever a high-bin zero exists. The density coefficient is fixed at kappa10 before any target or witness, not set to the desired unproved c11 value. If one had accepted only an ordinary-character statement without the same Hecke-family supremum bound, this bridge would be unavailable. The accepted frozen review explicitly retains that family return.

Use the original MP with its reduced capacity K=6kappa10 only in the free density proof. Keep inverse amplification, all physical descendant budgets and low/fallback capacity 9/2 unchanged. For general fixed K in [28114053/6250000,9/2], replace the plain line by

    P_K(m)=1-2delta m+delta[v-(1-2m)/K]_+.

Set D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta and

    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)D_K],
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K.

The same inverse and plain crossing argument gives

    G_K(W,z)=min(3k(delta)z, a_K W+b_K z),
    sum_high |Q|^2 << Z^[rho W+delta z-G_K(W,z)+epsilon] H_J. (D6)

The full-mark branch still uses t=(5-6delta v)/(5-2delta), r_b=2t/3. Otherwise

    t=[15K-10-6delta-12delta(K-1)v]/D_K,
    r_b=[(2K-2)t+1-Kv]/(3K-2).

The switch is v=(5-6delta)/[3K(5-2delta)-12delta]. The seven cleared source gates are positive over the FULL box delta in [.68,.70], K in [K_new,4.5], v in [0,.05], certified by 64 rational Bernstein coefficients. In particular t is within [1,3/2], the plain witness is in [0,1/2], the short crossing precedes 1-2v, and a_K<1/500. Four exact polynomial identities check balance, switch and the following gain change. This is not an extrapolation from the endpoint K value.

When both affine branches apply, the gain change is particularly transparent:

    G_K(W,z)-G_(9/2)(W,z)
     =delta(5-6delta)^2 (9/2-K)(W-2z)/(D_K D_(9/2)).     (D7)

It is positive for W>2z and also in the allowed empty-common-support sector W=M-6a. Thus this is a real source improvement there, independent of any conjectural failure of high-bin saturation. Where the min chooses 3kz, there is no gain, and no strict inequality is asserted there. The full nonlinear envelope is always used before deciding its active branch.

The actual threshold, label, anchor, pool, raw-root, height and puncture arguments from Sections 2 and 4 are unchanged; D6 is unconditioned on slot amplitudes. The raw root tail still pays because G_K<=3kz; the main root sum still decays since a_K<1/500. This proves the raw z<=W/21 version required by the actual source.

statement:
## A shorter-factor corollary and the actual limits of the estimates

The order (log X)^(1/3) is a convenient first instance, not a structural boundary. The same proof gives the following stronger source-compression corollary. Put f(L)=sqrt(L)/log L and allow all integers

  (2/5) f(L)<=K<=2 f(L), K>=2,                           (N30)

with the identical definitions Y=floor(exp(L/(K-1/2))), V=L/(2K-1), W=V/2. Then the source theorem(N4) and the sector estimates(N25)--(N29) still hold uniformly. Now every balanced Möbius factor lies between exp(c sqrt(L)log L) and exp(C sqrt(L)log L), which are shorter than the first displayed exp(Theta(L^(2/3))) scale.

To verify every changed asymptotic: V,W are comparable to sqrt(L)log L; the leading negative term in(N9) is of order -L(log L)^2, while K V log V=O(L log L), K^2=O(L/(log L)^2), and all tuple counts cost exp(O(L)). Thus the faces and product tails are still smaller than every inverse power. The same holds for(N10). The diagonal and gcd constants cost exp(O_delta(K^2))=X^o(1), derivative and height constants cost exp(O(Klog L))=X^o(1), log N=(1/2+o(1))L, and W/K is comparable to(log L)^2, validating the balanced positive cone. These checks are uniform over the band(N30).

For the future inverse choose K=2ceil(f(log X)/2). Up to t=4log X, the ratio of f(log X) to f(log Z) tends uniformly to at least1/sqrt5>2/5, and the upper band also has a strict margin. Thus the SAME fixed order remains admissible on every future shell, with(N16) unchanged. All later implications hold with(N30) replacing the first band. This is a genuine uniform source theorem with shorter actual factors, but it still does not prove(N28).

The proof used a comfortable gap between L^2/K^2 and L log L. Its general sufficient asymptotic condition is K going to infinity with K^2 log L=o(L), together with a future-compatible order family. Equality or the failure of this sufficient comparison is NOT an impossibility theorem. No claim is made that this rate is optimal, or that an epsilon-loss moment cannot hold at a vanishing reserve. This is separate from every old local-window coefficient boundary.

statement:
## 2. A shift lemma that pays a genuine Type I operator

Suppose a restoration sequence b has bounded partial sums

    B(y)=sum_(ell<=y)b(ell),  B(y)=0 for y<1,
    sup_(y>=0)|B(y)| <= C_b.

Extend h_b(v)=exp(-av)B(exp(v)) by zero for v<0. Then

    ||h_b||_L1(R) <= C_b/a.                            (H2)

For each integer k>=1 the kernel exp(-a(t+u))B(exp(t+u)/k) equals k^-a h_b(t+u-log k). Reflect and zero-extend one input to R, then apply the ordinary L1--L2 convolution inequality. Translation on R costs no norm. Thus its FULL L2(0,L) Hankel norm is at most C_b k^-a/a, independently of L and k. This argument retains all off-diagonal rectangles and uses no derivative or smoothness norm of the test functions.

For A_Y(a)=sum_(d<=Y)|mu(d)chi(d)|d^-a <= C_a Y^(1-a), H2 gives

    ||Gamma[a0*a0*b]_(a,L)|| <= (C_b/a) A_Y(a)^2
                              <<_(a,b) Y^(2(1-a)).   (H3)

This is an actual restricted arithmetic estimate: cancellation in the complete restoration partial sum B precedes absolute summation over the short factors. It is not obtained by replacing b(ell) with its magnitude.

For nonprincipal chi, finite-period orthogonality gives |sum_(n<=y)chi(n)|<=q. Take b=1_chi in H1. A finite atom z(n) contributes a shifted kernel with L1 norm |z(n)|n^-a/a, so

    | ||Gamma[a]_(a,L)|| - ||Gamma[a1*a1*1_chi]_(a,L)|| |
      <= (2/a)A_Y(a)+(q/a)A_Y(a)^2
      <<_(a,q) Y^(2(1-a)).                            (H4)

This directly concerns G149's ORIGINAL mu(n)chi(n) source for every fixed nonprincipal character. It does not assume cancellation in either long factor.

### The actual principal obstruction

Principal characters cannot simply inherit H4. At Y=1 their removed coefficient sequence is 2delta_1-1_chi, with partial sum 2-C_chi(x). Since C_chi(x)=(phi(q)/q)x+O(q), its Hankel operator contains a nonzero rank-one kernel -(phi(q)/q)exp((1-a)(t+u)), plus a uniformly bounded remainder. Its norm is therefore

    (phi(q)/q)(exp(2(1-a)L)-1)/(2(1-a))+O_(a,q)(1).

This is an ACTUAL source term of H1, not a toy kernel imported from elsewhere. A positive budget for that term misses every gamma<1. The full long-factor term may cancel it, so this is not a lower bound on M_chi or the complete source.

statement:
# [private research revision] direct joint-window lane: current worklog



Objective: an actual arithmetic estimate for the original inverse moment on
same-zero large-plain rows near G137's crossing, or a useful proved subcase with
its complement. Current written c11=.1251459636 and licensed density
K=28114053/6250000 remain unchanged; F0, positive-slot uniformity and external
admission remain open. No formalization, new packet, children or provider work.

Completed source intake: [restricted research revision] density and [restricted research revision] same-character/same-zero contract,
G137 and its full joint-window source, literal PR9 B0.17--20 and B3.39--40,
PR15 PlainUnmarkedDensity, and relevant [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] duplicate boundaries.
The dyadic witnesses have common character, real power and height; slot heights
remain independent. Full cutoff cancellation does not hold on each dyadic pair.
The mixed convolution is outside the original canonical column contract.

Current survivor: a complete large-gcd inverse/plain estimate uses the SAME
buffered plain bound on every shortened scale, then the fully marked original
MI. A second square-divisor removal pays all its intersections with that gcd
part. This proves the desired inverse saving on an actual proper row subclass;
the complementary near-coprime, nearly squarefree plain source remains open.
Completed: complementary source/failed shortcuts, one exact identity check run,
source pins and full artifact readbacks. Remaining: final freeze, own release
and the reserved independent handoff. No c gain is claimed.

## 1. Literal source and statement

Write U=Z^W and use the original Eisenstein ideals, primary/unit convention,
excluded set S and finite natural character dictionary. One whole orientation
is fixed, phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n)^(+/-1), with its actual zeros. The fixed nu
need not have order six. Put R=U^r, D=U^m and

    M_u(R)=R^(-1/2) sum_a mu(a)phi_u(a)W_I(Na/R),
    S_u(D)=D^(-1/2) sum_b phi_u(b)W_P(Nb/D),
    B_u=M_u(R)S_u(D).

The profiles include the original common real power and common witness height.
The original slot product Q_u retains its independent heights, all canonical
pools, every individual coefficient, root/puncture hole and natural zero.
Its total normalized width is v. No pool or profile is changed here.

Fix the physical bin delta in[.68,.70], v in[0,.05], 0<eta<=.001 and the
G137 cutoff t=t_*(delta,v)-eta BEFORE witnesses. After their original
construction, partition by label, internal bin and dyads, and retain the
parts with |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta. The dyads are common within each ensuing norm;
the original moment thresholds are uniform before that partition. G137's certificate
supplies r>1/2, 0<m<=1/2 up to its small allocated tolerances, and

    r+2v <= 1-c_1,       2r+8v <= 3-c_2,                 (1)

with fixed positive reserves (the first exceeds .01017 before fine losses).
We reuse these gates, not another optimization or scalar certificate. The
following estimate in fact holds in any fixed length box satisfying(1).

Omega contains only the original NONPRINCIPAL supported-witness rows. Principal,
artificial and fixed-inducing exceptions are not reclassified into it.
Partition the original rows by their actual internal buffered zero bin and
fixed witness label/dyads. Call one part Omega and its lower squared grade beta.
Here beta>=delta-small, beta<=3/4; the internal maximum can exceed the physical
bin. At the selected common real part/height the literal B0.15/B0.18 bounds give

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E)|^2 <= E^beta U^(epsilon_det) H_J,
          0<E<=C D, u in Omega.                         (2)

The second bound uses the direct (unreflected) line in B0.15, so it is valid
even when a small endpoint tolerance makes m slightly exceed1/2. Every E
below is an ACTUAL shortened scale with the SAME character, real power, height
and plain profile. Bounded nonempty subunit E are comparable to a fixed positive
constant and satisfy(2) with a fixed multiplier; smaller E have empty support.
The source buffer/derivative losses may be chosen arbitrarily small BEFORE U.
They will be absorbed in the displayed final epsilon. We never put beta in
place of delta in a physical slot upper price.

Throughout H_J means a finite polynomial (1+T)^J in all retained heights;
the separate symbol H below denotes a square-divisor threshold, not that height.
For a nonnegative original radial weight (or its paid U^epsilon majorant),
write ||F||_Omega^2=sum_(u in Omega) w_u |F_u|^2. Enlarging this set is allowed
only AFTER a pointwise use of(2), inside a positive original MI norm. No
zero-conditioned Poisson formula is asserted. The literal PR9 B0.4/B3.31 gives

    ||M_u(E) Q_u||_(all original rows)^2
          << H_J U^(1+epsilon),        0<E<=C R,          (3)

uniformly over the shortened scales and the required rowwise witness parameters.
Section5 below pays its profile, mask, height and small-scale interfaces.

For ideals b define the integral ideal

    s_2(b)=prod_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2).

Let G,H>=1 be fixed functions of U, chosen before witnesses. Split the literal
ordered (a,b) coefficient sum of B disjointly into

    B_g:       N(a,b)>=G;
    B_s:       N(a,b)<G and N s_2(b)>=H;
    B_c:       N(a,b)<G and N s_2(b)<H.                   (4)

Thus B=B_g+B_s+B_c exactly, with equality placed on the first two sides as
written. These are signed source polynomials, not positive projections.

**Restricted arithmetic theorem.** For fixed positive g,h and G=U^g,H=U^h,
within all the preceding source hypotheses,

    ||B_g Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m-beta*g+epsilon),
    ||B_s Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*h+epsilon).
                                                               (5)

The common buffer grade is used before weakening to physical delta. Define
the disjoint actual row classes

    Omega_g={u in Omega: |B_g(u)|>=|B(u)|/4},
    Omega_s={u in Omega\Omega_g: |B_s(u)|>=|B(u)|/4},
    Omega_c=Omega\(Omega_g union Omega_s).

Then(2),(5) prove bounds for the ORIGINAL inverse moment, not a substituted
coefficient family:

 sum_(Omega_g) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(1-delta*g+epsilon),
 sum_(Omega_s) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(1-2delta*h+epsilon).
                                                               (6)

On the entire complement,

    |B_c(u)|>|B(u)|/2, u in Omega_c.                     (7)

In particular choose g=4eta,h=2eta. Both proper classes save at least
(68/25)eta before freely chosen losses, hence imply the requested saving eta
there with substantial reserve. This is a genuine source-relative arithmetic
estimate on defined actual rows. It does NOT prove that all rows lie in their
union, or supply J_eta^all on Omega_c. No actual high-zero row or nonempty
dominance class is constructed. Empty common support is allowed, including
v=0. No c increase or complete new physical return is asserted.

## 2. Large common divisor: exact signs, all holes, and the bin saving

For an ideal q define

    A_G(q)=sum_(d|q, Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Ideal divisor inversion gives the exact identity

    1_(Nk>=G)=sum_(q|k) A_G(q),
    A_G(q)=0 if Nq<G,       |A_G(q)|<=tau(q).             (8)

Because a is squarefree, every contributing q|a is squarefree. With a=qc,
mu(qc)=mu(q)mu(c)1_(c,q)=1. There is no coprimality condition on b/q. Thus

 B_g(u)=sum_(q sf,Nq>=G) A_G(q)mu(q)phi_u(q)^2/(Nq)
           M_u^(q)(R/Nq) S_u(D/Nq),                    (9)

where M^(q) has the extra column condition (c,q)=1. Every q up to the literal
profile endpoint remains; q can meet a slot, the row or a fixed hole. Character
zeros are retained in phi_u(q)^2; no phase is divided out or reduced to a unit.

To avoid an illicit moving-mask MI input, restore the inverse exactly:

    M_u^(q)(E)=sum_(k supported on primes of q)
                   phi_u(k)/(Nk)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nk).       (10)

At each p|q the local convolution mu*1 is1 at exponent0 and0 otherwise.
Consequently(10) includes ALL k=p^j and preserves natural zeros even at shared
row primes. It is finite on an actual annulus. Its absolute mass is

    prod_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.
                                                               (11)

Small primes supply a fixed constant and each sufficiently large prime factor
is at most (Np)^epsilon. A fixed polynomial extra inverse puncture, if not
already part of the licensed natural character, is restored by the same formula
over q times that puncture; its complete mass is again U^epsilon. Actual slot
holes remain in their fixed bounded coefficients, as permitted by MI. This is
the existing [restricted research revision] restoration device, here used on ONE inverse and an unchanged
plain factor; it is not claimed as a new general divisor identity.

Apply Hilbert Minkowski to(9),(10), then use the SAME-bin plain bound(2) and
the fully marked moment(3). The outside phases are contractions. This gives

 ||B_g Q||_Omega
   << H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2)
          sum_(Nq>=G) tau(q)^(O(1)) (Nq)^(-1-beta/2)
   << H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2) G^(-beta/2).
                                                               (12)

The last estimate follows from ideal counting on dyadic shells, uniformly for
beta in a fixed positive compact interval. Every q-shell count is present: the
factor(Nq)^(-1) in(9) alone would only yield logarithmic mass; the additional
power comes precisely from the shortened plain sum at the same buffered zero.
Squaring proves the first part of(5). A mere trivial plain bound would give
U D/G instead and need a much larger G. This use of(2) is the substantive
same-zero improvement of the [restricted research revision]-style decomposition.

## 3. Large plain square divisors, including their complete intersection

Define A_H(k) by(8) with H in place of G. Since k|s_2(b) iff k^2|b,

    1_(N s_2(b)>=H)=sum_(k^2|b) A_H(k).                 (13)

Unlike the gcd divisor q, k need NOT be squarefree. Define the actual plain
part S_bad(D) with this indicator. Multiplicativity gives

 S_bad(D)=sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi_u(k^2)/(Nk)
                         S_u(D/(Nk)^2).

Using(2) BEFORE triangle and ideal counting afterwards yields the uniform
pointwise bound on the same buffered rows

    |S_bad(D)| << H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2) H^(-beta).
                                                               (14)

All prime powers, equality at H, terminal nonempty scales and fixed holes remain.
Consequently ||M S_bad Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)H^(-2beta).
This alone does NOT license deleting the intersection with B_g from a signed
source. We pay that intersection next.

Let B_gs restrict to BOTH N(a,b)>=G and N s_2(b)>=H. Expand(8),(13) simultaneously.
For squarefree q, put L=[q,k^2]=q k^2/(q,k). Then a=qc,b=Ld, and EXACTLY

 B_gs(u)=sum_(q sf,k;Nq>=G,Nk>=H)
    A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi_u(qL)/(Nq NL)^(1/2)
                    M_u^(q)(R/Nq) S_u(D/NL).           (15)

This formula includes q/k intersections of every valuation. It is not obtained
by incorrectly replacing lcm(q,k^2) by qk^2. Restore M^(q) by(10). The coefficient
mass left after(2),(3) is

 sum_(q,k) tau(qk)^(O(1)) (Nq)^(-1/2)(NL)^(-(1+beta)/2).

Primewise, put i=v_p(q) in{0,1}, j=v_p(k)>=0. Then
v_p(L)=max(i,2j)=i+2j-min(i,j). Thus its non-divisor weight equals
q^(-1-beta/2) k^(-1-beta) (q,k)^((1+beta)/2) in norm notation.
For i=1,j>=1 its local factor is exactly
(Np)^(-1/2-j(1+beta)); the shared prime is not counted twice.
For i=1,j=0 it is (Np)^(-1-beta/2), and for i=0 it is
(Np)^(-j(1+beta)). These exhaust all valuation cases, including holes.

Writing d=(q,k), k=de, and dropping only positive coprimality restrictions gives

 sum_(Nk>=H) (Nk)^(-1-beta) N(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
       << U^epsilon H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) (Nd)^((beta-1)/2)
       << U^epsilon H^(-beta) tau(q).                  (16)

For Nd<=H, sum the e tail from H/Nd. For Nd>H, its complete sum is bounded;
(Nd)^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)(Nd)^((beta-1)/2). Thus BOTH ranges satisfy(16).
The strict compact upper bound beta<1 is used, and all divisor losses fit the
arbitrarily small U^epsilon. Summing q then proves

    ||B_gs Q||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).
                                                               (17)

Finally B_s=M S_bad-B_gs. Hilbert triangle and G>=1 prove the second part of(5).
No signed subset monotonicity or independent signs have entered. The three
pieces in(4) are exhaustive, and every low/high cross term is paid by the
same Hilbert triangle when a complete norm is needed.

## 4. The original inverse moment and the exact surviving source

On Omega_g, |M S|<=4|B_g|. Divide by the actual lower plain bound in(2),
retaining its error and common beta, then sum with w_u|Q_u|^2. Equation(12)
gives U^(1-beta*g+small). The same argument using(17) and(14) gives
U^(1-2beta*h+small) on Omega_s. Since beta>=delta-small and all ranges are fixed,
the freely allocated losses give(6). At no point is the inverse witness divided
out; the conclusion is the original restricted inverse MOMENT. A subsequent
division by its usual inverse spike is legal, but is not needed to state(6).

On Omega_c the strict inequalities in the two preceding class definitions and
B=B_g+B_s+B_c prove(7) by triangle. The whole original common-zero product lower
bound B0.20 is therefore retained by B_c, up to the fixed factor1/2 and the old
small errors. No witness is chosen afresh and no new cutoff is selected.

The surviving literal coefficient has the two tuple restrictions

    N(a,b)<G,   N s_2(b)<H,
    mu(a)phi_u(ab)W_I(Na/R)W_P(Nb/D)/(RD)^(1/2).        (18)

After including one prime from each original disjoint slot pool, equal ideal
products may be merged WITH their signs. All their original tuple restrictions,
labels, independent slot heights and zeros stay in that merged coefficient.
The following intrinsic fact survives all coincidences. Since a is squarefree,

    (ab)/rad(ab)=(a,b) b/rad(b),
    N((ab)/rad(ab)) < G H^2.                            (19)

Indeed b/rad(b) divides s_2(b)^2 primewise. The original slot product P is
squarefree; multiplying it changes the repeat factor by (P,ab), whose norm
is at most NP. Thus the full merged column n=abP obeys

    N(n/rad(n)) < G H^2 NP.                             (20)

These are support statements, not signed norm bounds. The small repeated-prime
part can be frozen for a later legitimate source analysis; doing so does not
make the squarefree remainder canonical automatically. With g=4eta,h=2eta,
the unmarked repeat factor has width<8eta, and the full one width<8eta+v.

## 5. Admissibility, profiles, every shortening and the physical complement

The input gates are literal PR9 B0.3--4/B3.31 and B0.13--20, together with the
accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] fixed-dictionary and same-zero selection bridges. In particular:

1. The physical delta and cutoff t are fixed first; the actual label and internal
   buffered bin are selected by the original finite procedure. Lemma1W permits
   ANY t in[1,3/2] fixed before its witnesses. Its proof supplies the spike at the
   actual internal beta BEFORE weakening it to physical delta. Using the weaker
   physical spike but the larger internal beta only in the shortened upper bound
   would lose an unwanted factor D^(beta-delta). That invalid shortcut is avoided
   in(2),(6). No upper slot price is replaced by an internal maximum.
2. In(9) the new inverse scale is R/(Nq Nk); in(15) it is the SAME scale after
   restoration. The plain scale is D/Nq or D/NL. These all decrease. If r' is
   the logarithmic inverse scale, then r'<=r; hence BOTH gates(1) improve.
   When r'<0 but the support is nonempty, replace its scale by1 and make a
   bounded dilation of the common profile. This still has r'=0<=r and gives
   2v<=1/10<1 and 8v<=2/5<3. No artificial amplifier, added slot, enlarged
   prime pool, or new derivative index is introduced. The same original Q
   is inside each MI application; there is no unpriced U^v slot factor.
3. The inverse source profile includes the old cutoff
   V_le(R y/U^t). After a=qkc and E=R/(Nq Nk), its argument is still
   V_le(R(c/E)/U^t), so this is exactly the SAME function of its normalized
   variable. It is not a moving arithmetic coefficient or a new cutoff chosen
   after q,k. The plain normalized variable has the identical property.
   Character phases from q,L,k keep their zero values; every exponent, including
   a multiple of six, remains a literal character power with its natural hole.
4. The source's finite Sobolev orders give (3) for rowwise real powers/heights
   and for the finite derivative-profile list. Scale derivatives replace W by
   -W/2-yW', and real/height derivatives add the original logarithmic weights.
   The gcd/square-divisor thresholds are frozen at U BEFORE this operation and
   are not differentiated. Smooth scale suprema use the original logarithmic
   boxes, not a row-dependent coefficient choice. Independent slot heights are
   never equated to the witness height. A fixed global polynomial support bound
   may be used for q,k and restoration variables before these norms; individual
   terms vanish outside their real profile support. This avoids differentiating
   a moving summation endpoint.
5. The plain bound(2) is used only on the retained buffered rows. Its direct
   Mellin shift is uniform for the common shortened profiles and heights by
   B0.14--15. Explicitly the fixed finite conjugation-stable dictionary Theta
   gives X(u)={nu psi_u^(+/-1)}; the good-prime rows have conductor O_S(U).
   With fixed buffer e>0 and I=ceil(1/e)+2, the selected i<I obeys
   a<=B_i<a+e and B_(i+1)<a+2e. Here B_j is the maximum of51/100 and
   real zero parts in that dictionary up to height3^j T. The nonfloor zero
   has a<=Re(rho)<a+e and |Im(rho)|<=3^i T. Put beta=2a-1. On the retained
   height segments the direct line Re(s)=a+6e gives the E^beta bound, with
   its original small U loss, common smooth seminorms and deleted Euler zeros.
   Shortening E changes neither this bin nor its zero-free region, character,
   profile or selected heights. It does not request a new bin at scale E.
   The finitely many independent coordinates use fixed fractions of T;
   discarded tails are U^B T^(-N), with B including polynomial divisor counts
   fixed before N, in the source range U^tau_minus<=T<=U^tau_plus.
   At large heights retain the source's polynomial factor. Choose
   the finite profile orders, bin/mesh and epsilon shares before the internal
   small polynomial height exponent, and the raw tail powers before their decay
   order and final threshold. Above that internal height range, the original
   trivial row count and absolute polynomial bounds on M,Q and the source parts
   are paid by a larger fixed height degree. This final degree may depend on the
   already chosen internal height exponent. The external physical height
   exponent is chosen AFTER that degree, to fit its cost below the eta reserve;
   it is not identified with the internal exponent. No growing-conductor
   uniformity or new growing-height theorem is imported.
6. All sums over q,k in the proof use actual nonempty polynomial support. A
   positive convergent extension was used only AFTER absolute values to bound
   their mass. Every root/puncture hole is retained in the original factor or
   explicitly restored as in(10). Extra slot holes are fixed coefficients
   permitted by MI; MP with arbitrary coefficients is never invoked. Disjoint

The physical meaning of(6) is deliberately limited. It can be applied on an
ACTUAL positive child norm only after the original signed reconstruction has
produced that norm, its complete character and its live slot list. One must
test the defined dominance class with that child's own R,D,Q and actual zero.
It cannot be attached to a parent and pushed through a signed projector.
Keep both projectors, missing radicals, joint-label counting, every original
clipped rectangle, all extraction scalars and masks unchanged. A Cauchy pair

For a raw decomposition w=u b^6 the old root holes remain frozen before free

for K remains its accepted c10 ancestry. The present MI-based proper-sector
lemma does not alter K, physical kappa, the accepted c11 or its open admissions.

## 6. Actual next obstruction and a deliberately coarse complete test

Two potentially attractive shortcuts were tested and fail at identifiable
source steps, not by an abstract nonexistence theorem.

First, applying the complete mu*1 cancellation to an individual selected
inverse/plain dyad is false. On the unmarked, fully coprime squarefree part of
(18), merge n=ab and extract the row factor psi_u(n)^(+/-1).
Then mu(a)=mu(n)mu(b), so the literal coefficient is

 c(n)=mu(n)nu(n)/(RD)^(1/2)
       sum_(b|n) mu(b)W_I(N(n/b)/R)W_P(Nb/D),           (21)

with the original tuple cuts and zeros. At a common height and real power,
the two norm twists DO combine into one function of Nn/(RD). This pays their
normalization exactly, but the divisor-profile sum in(21) remains arithmetic.
It is not a smooth profile of Nn, a fixed ray character or a coprimality mask.
An additional original prime-slot tuple contributes its own literal factors
and product coincidences; it does not change this conclusion.

For a transparent actual coefficient test, take two distinct unramified prime
ideals p,l with Np on the inverse annulus, Nl on the much shorter plain annulus,
and choose nonnegative smooth profiles nonzero at these two points with small
fixed relative supports. At n=pl, only a=p,b=l lies in those two annuli; a=l,
a=1 and a=pl do not. The coefficient is -nu(pl) times their nonzero normalized
weights, before any natural row zero. It lies in N(a,b)=1, s_2(b)=1 and hence
survives every G,H>1. This is a literal coefficient failure of dyadic divisor
cancellation, not an example of a high zero or saturation of a whole norm.
No density, positive lower bound for the complete moment or independence of
such rows is asserted. The completed cutoff identity G115 still holds only
after all its required divisor/dyadic pieces have been reconstructed.

Second, the original canonical energy B3.6 expressly permits NO further
coefficient on its squarefree column. The divisor-profile factor in(21) is
outside that contract. Divisor boundedness, the common height, empty support
and the tiny repeated-prime bound(20) do not license its removal. The usual
unmarked inverse theorem B3.39 also has actual mu(n) coefficients; it cannot
be applied to(21) just by writing a new symbol for this factor. Such an
extension would require a new proof using the displayed signed divisor law.

The complete coarse test makes the remaining deficit explicit. On Omega,
the SAME-bin bound(2), followed by marked MI, gives

    ||B Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon).

Using B_c=B-B_g-B_s and the already proved estimates gives the same upper
power for ||B_c Q||_Omega^2, with every mixed term paid by Hilbert triangle.
On Omega_c the only available comparison back to the original inverse is

    |M_u(R)| <= 2|B_c(u)|/|S_u(D)|.

The plain lower bound therefore yields U^(1+epsilon), precisely the old
inverse moment. It supplies NO positive eta saving. Replacing this triangle
by an unsupported comparison with a signed subset would be the missing proof.

This pinpoints the next arithmetic repair without a scalar re-optimization:
estimate the signed divisor-profile source(18)/(21), with its near-coprime
inverse/plain factors and small repeated-prime part, on the same buffered
large-plain rows. An estimate only for a different canonical coefficient,
for averaged unrelated heights, or for selected q/k terms is insufficient.
The full core with its actual product signal(7) is now the only unpaid source
inside this crossing window. It is not known to be easier merely because it
has been renamed. The substantive new progress is(5)--(6) and the exact,
overlap-paid support reduction(18)--(20), not a claimed solution of that core.

## R4. The prefix is paid over the whole slot interval

Let N0(P) be the complete sum over free rows of squared tensor Sobolev norms on [a,1] times the enlarged height interval, with derivatives partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j, i,j in {0,1}, and the original nonnegative row majorant. The real width is at least 3/20. The previous prefix proof applies with this fixed t>1 and gives

    N0(P)<<H_J U^(J_t+epsilon),
    J_t=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.              (R7)

Here is the exponent reconstruction. R2 restricts the complementary cofactor to Nm<C_H L/R. For fixed m, the inner inverse dyads satisfy R<<D<<L/Nm. The centrally normalized free inverse moment is U^(1/6)D^(5/6+epsilon); d^(-s) supplies D^(-delta) in its square. Apply common-profile separation before fixing the live cofactor, and keep the profile containing the original R unchanged under every shortened inverse scale in B0.7. Hilbert triangle over inverse dyads is dominated by D~L/Nm because 5/6-delta>0. Multiplication by phi_u(m) is a contraction, even with common primes and zeros. The resulting norm is bounded by

    H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon)L^[(5/6-delta)/2]
                   sum_(Nm<C_H L/R)(Nm)^(-11/12).

Indeed a+(5/6-delta)/2=11/12 exactly. The ideal count, with its unit, gives (L/R)^(1/12). Squaring gives U^(1/6)L^(5/6-delta)(L/R)^(1/6), exactly R7. The same argument treats the finite tensor derivatives by logarithmic factors. No cancellation between different cofactors is assumed.

Only after positive evaluation at an actual zero multiply its exceptional-set count by the physical slot price. Thus

    sum_(|P(rho_u)|>=1/4)|Q_u|^2
        <<H_J U^(J_t+delta v+epsilon).                (R8)

No zero selector has been inserted in Poisson or in the inverse moment. This is not the full marked norm estimate with cost 5v/3.

For the current density envelope put

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3hD_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    G=min(3kv,a_K+b_K v), E_K=rho+delta v-G.

On the full rectangle, E_K-J_t-delta v>eta. A sufficient lower bound uses G<=a_K+b_K/20. Multiplying its excess above eta by Den=3hD_K gives a cubic whose four Bernstein coefficients are positive; the least is 31963522910683/488281250000000. The review reconstructed this from the rational functions, not from the author's coefficient array. Consequently the previous t=4/3 failure at v=.05 is not being ignored: this t=33/25 detector pays the complete prefix over v<=.05. statement:
### Fixed-ray squarefree selector estimate

For one of these fixed characters `chi`, squarefree `R`, and a moving deleted set `M1`, define
\[
U_\chi(X;M_1,R)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf},\,(c,M_1)=1,\,R\mid c}
\chi(c)\sqrt{q_c}W_0(q_c/X).
\]
If `R` meets the deletion set or the character conductor, this is zero. Otherwise, for every fixed `sigma>1/2`,
\[
|U_\chi(X;M_1,R)|
\ll(q_{M_1}q_R)^\epsilon q_R^{-\sigma}X^{\sigma+1/2}.
\tag{T05.3}
\]
Indeed `sqrt(q_c)W0(q_c/X)=sqrt(X)W(q_c/X)`. Its squarefree forced-divisor Dirichlet series is
\[
\chi(R)q_R^{-s}{L^S(s,\chi)\over L^S(2s,\chi^2)}
\prod_{p\mid M_1R}(1+\chi(p)Q_p^{-s})^{-1},
\]
with repeated primes counted once and conductor/excluded primes omitted. The denominator reciprocal converges absolutely for `Re s>1/2`; a principal numerator pole at one is canceled by the original root `W-hat(1)=0`. Moving local factors cost a subpower by the same elementary argument as T01. Shift Mellin to `Re s=sigma`; fixed-character height growth is absorbed by rapid Mellin decay. This proves (T05.3), including small `X`. No new zero-free input is used here.

**Profile qualification:** this is the original root-preserving profile, its conjugate, and permitted Euler derivatives retaining that root. An arbitrary multiplicative norm twist moves the root and is not covered by this argument without a corrected residue calculation. Do not advertise T05 for such a family merely because another theorem uses Mellin twists.

## G142. Actual logarithmic improvement and the remaining complete core

Use Green–Tao's [published Theorem1.1, pp.542–543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf):
fixed-degree polynomial nilsequences have every fixed logarithmic Möbius
saving, uniform in the polynomial coefficients, with ineffective constants.
A fixed torus with the degree-k abelian filtration and fixed sine/cosine
functions gives sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)e(P(n))<<_A Y(log(2Y))^-A. A dummy torus
coordinate is available to satisfy the stated dimension convention.
The GRH power-decay remark is unused. The separately inspected
[Gao–Zhao v2 Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09241v2) assumes GRH
and is not an unconditional input.

Expand the actual periodic chi in its finite additive Fourier series,
retaining zeros and coefficient absolute sum<=q. Apply the polynomial
bound to ell n/q-n^k/(2*pi*x^k). Splitting prefix lengths at sqrt M
and Abel summing the decreasing damping proves
|W_<=M(x)|<<_(q,A) M(log M)^-A, uniformly in real x. For k=6,b=3/2,
take M=X(log X)^B, B=(D+2)/4, A=B+(D+2)/2. The core log exponent
is -D-2, the complete off-diagonal log exponent -D-1, so

    E(X)<<_(q,D) X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^-D,
    ||W||_1<<_(q,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^-D

for every fixed D>0. This is actual arithmetic progress for this new
source. It still misses the first-gain energy threshold1.7497080728
by .2502919272 in power; logarithmic strength cannot grow with X.

For 0<c<=1/4 put gamma=1-c and r=1+c/2. Freeze L=X^gamma,M=X^r
before x varies over[X,2X]. The prefix n<=L costs O(X^gamma), while
G141 gives ||W_>M||_2^2<<X^(3/2)+X^(6-4r)<<X^(2gamma).
Both complementary L1 and L2 norms are therefore O(X^gamma). The
SINGLE complete core target is

    integral_X^(2X)|sum_(X^gamma<n<=X^r) mu(n)chi(n)
              exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6)|dx/x
                   <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).  (CORE1)

By the norm triangle inequality in both directions this is equivalent
to the full source L1 input. The same holds for L2, which is sufficient
but stronger. The complements also permit exact big-O equivalence.
No omitted cross is hidden: the full tail function was first bounded
in L2, and only then used in the L1 triangle inequality.

| Conditional c | gamma | Upper cutoff exponent r | L2 target |
|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | .8748 | 1.0626 | 1.7496 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 5/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/2 |

Every row is OPEN. The first would exceed c11 by135091/2500000000.

The review also proves a fixed-parameter larger conditional architecture.
For ANY fixed 1/2<gamma<1 choose 1<b<=2gamma, integer k>2 with
r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b, and integer K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Low prefix
and complete tail still cost O(X^gamma); CORE1 on X^gamma<n<=X^r
is sufficient. Use ALL the shifts in G140. Starting with 1/L holomorphic
on Re s>1, solve for the unshifted reciprocal on
Re s>max(gamma,a-(b-1)) whenever it is known on Re s>a. Each j>=1
term is already holomorphic. A finite number of steps reaches gamma;
the nonzero A0, principal pole and actual Euler holes are paid throughout.

For example gamma=3/5, b=11/10, k=12, K=5 gives r=27/25, remainder
boundary1/2 and tail energy exponents11/10,6/5. It is a fully paid
conditional c=2/5 architecture, with its actual CORE1 still OPEN.
It conveys no greater likelihood of success than the near target.
All parameters are fixed before X. There is no theorem at gamma=1/2
or uniformity as gamma approaches it.

Adding the low source proves (H), with the stated conservative log^4. This norm-triangle completion pays all cross terms between low/high sources, distinct row blocks and distinct output blocks. ## 4. The complete short-arc observation and zero-exclusion return

Here is the weakest full source estimate used by this replacement. Fix 0<c<1/2 and gamma=1-c. For every fixed ordinary chi modulo q, use the fixed parity-compatible r above, put h=1/(qN), and require, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large integers N,

    E_arc(N):=integral_0^h |R_N(x)|^2 dx
       <<_(chi,r,epsilon) N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon).        (10)

The positive epsilon loss is chosen after c; thresholds may depend on the fixed character and epsilon. No average over characters or exceptional scale set is allowed. In fact(10) is equivalent, up to arbitrary epsilon losses, to M_chi(X)=sum_(n<=X)mu(n)chi(n)<<X^(gamma+epsilon). This equivalence is stated explicitly: the new source estimate is not called easier merely because its notation differs.

Proof of the forward direction, including the observation cost: discrete Fourier inversion modulo q writes chi(k)=sum_(a=0)^(q-1) c_a e(ak/q). The Fourier formula for the periodic Bernoulli polynomial gives

    Phi(x)=-(2pi i)^r/r! sum_a c_a B_r({x+a/q}).

Thus on 0<x<1/q, Phi is one fixed polynomial P(x) of degree at most r. It is continuous at0 since r>=2, and its constant term is

    beta=Phi(0)=2L(r,chi)!=0.

The nonvanishing here is the absolutely convergent Euler product on r>1; no zero-free assertion to the left of1 is used. In particular principal and imprimitive characters are covered with their original zeros. Let p_r be the endpoint reproducing polynomial on [0,1]:

    p_r(u)=sum_(j=0)^r (2j+1)(-1)^j P_j(2u-1),

where P_j is the Legendre polynomial. Orthogonality, or integration against monomials, proves

    integral_0^1 p_r(u)u^j du=1_(j=0) (0<=j<=r),
    integral_0^1 |p_r(u)|^2du=(r+1)^2.               (11)

For the first identity it suffices to test the shifted Legendre basis: the integral selects its j-th coefficient with value (-1)^j, exactly the value of that basis polynomial at0. The norm is sum_(j=0)^r(2j+1). The Bernoulli Fourier formula used above follows by repeated integration by parts from B_j'=j B_(j-1), mean zero and B_1(x)=x-1/2; it has no additional analytic input. In particular B_2=x^2-x+1/6 and B_3=x^3-3x^2/2+x/2 cover the two orders needed here.

Define O_N f=integral_0^1 p_r(u)f(hu)du. Every n<=N has nhu<=1/q, so the same local polynomial applies to every original term, without a moving choice of a cell. It follows exactly that

    O_N D_N=beta sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n^r.

Writing eta_N=O_N E-2, Taylor's theorem and(11) give |eta_N|<=C_r h^(r+1). Since sum a(n)/n^r=1/L(r,chi),

    beta sum_(n>N)a(n)/n^r = O_N R_N-eta_N.          (12)

Cauchy-Schwarz pays the full observation cost:

    |O_N R_N| <=(r+1) sqrt(qN) E_arc(N)^(1/2).       (13)

Equations(10)-(13) give T_N:=sum_(n>N)a(n)/n^r<<N^(gamma-r+epsilon). For integer N, ordinary partial summation, with T(t)=T_floor(t), gives the exact inverse formula

    M_chi(N)=1/L(r,chi)-N^r T_N
                 +r integral_1^N t^(r-1)T(t)dt.     (14)

It yields M_chi(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon), and real X follows by taking its integer part. All integer N are required; a sparse scale family is not silently interpolated.

For completeness, the reverse direction is equally paid. Phi is bounded and globally Lipschitz: this follows from its finite Bernoulli representation, including r=2 and the finitely many derivative jumps. Abel summation in(1), using |M_chi(t)|<<t^(gamma+epsilon) with gamma+epsilon<1, gives

    |R_N(x)| << N^(gamma-r+epsilon)
                      +|x|N^(gamma-r+1+epsilon)

for 0<=x<=h. The derivative integral converges since r>=2>gamma+1+epsilon. Integrating its square proves(10), after relabelling epsilon. This uses the actual full tail and not a pointwise Fourier series summation shortcut.

The zero return has no hidden height truncation. The Mertens estimate makes

    A(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma and equal to 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. For nonprincipal chi, bounded period sums give L(s,chi) holomorphic on Re(s)>0. For principal chi modulo q, the floor integral for zeta together with product_(p|q)(1-p^(-s)) gives the usual meromorphic continuation, with its only pole in that half-plane at1. The identity A(s)L(s,chi)=1 then continues throughout the connected half-plane with that pole removed. Hence L has no zero with Re(s)>gamma, at any imaginary height. At the principal pole the excluded point remains a pole, not a zero. Finite imprimitive Euler factors have zeros only on Re(s)=0. This is an ordinary-character conditional theorem. It neither supplies the open estimate(10) nor resolves the separate pinned PR9 source/K-scope issue in the incumbent proof.
