# W60: prime-factor turnover is the missing cost in local coding

No arithmetic power saving or increase in c is proved. The two developed outputs are a source-specific obstruction to **every fixed-radius, short-displacement prime code/flow** (W60-12), and a cut obstruction to **all disjoint divisibility matchings**, including adaptive character-one pivots (W60-23). The first identifies a precise remaining arithmetic sector, beyond the previous fixed-pivot and unsigned homology calculations. The other four selected cards received the concrete first tests below; their proposed shortcuts fail at their stated scopes. No formalization, proof packet, or public claim is supplied.

The current written value stays c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, gamma11=.8748540364. Its inherited analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity, and external definition/import/admission remain open. The accepted baseline is a research premise. Statements called proved below are author derivations submitted for independent review, not automatic project acceptance.

## 1. Frozen selection and evidence

The complete thirty-card seeds.md was written and read before detailed history/current-proof/index intake: SHA-256 **8d7f8088bcfa5b092f3aa457977361467dd57b3be242fd43d475de678a48cc5b**. All six groups and four recipes are retained. Literal p values are subjective generation typicality, not success probabilities. Recipe, frozen problem, stable prefix, and sampler hashes matched the assignment. An administrative search for the prefix exposed only coordination snippets before the seed freeze; that exposure is disclosed in the deck.

After source inspection, selection.json froze W60-28 (strongest bridge), W60-23 (protected high reach), and W60-12 (different mechanism), SHA-256 **8f8bcd2b7f4e9f0cae565fd46b0e0e888fc79d898e797d5bc9398fbb5f0c8fcb**. No complete mechanism was excluded; broad ancestors were not treated as family-wide failures. Three fresh independent OS-entropy stages used all remaining qualifying cards across every group. Each complete ordered pool was written, flushed, read back, and hashed before its own entropy was read. Rejection mapping is unbiased; all three first samples were accepted, so no rejection or redraw occurred.

| Stage | Complete pool size | Zero-based index | Card | Draw SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| p<.10 | 25 | 21 | 26 | bb88a9448eaa327c27a604238622df2224c05f0f15e8662640affda78b7c00f6 |
| p<.01 | 15 | 11 | 25 | f332a9e3627e0122890a69b794e792972540cc46f5a314217c8f36745cfebf61 |
| remaining wildcard | 25 | 24 | 30 | 47176f2c65bcedd2eb3ea4b684386ae4e6034c1aa3d42716765eaf438bbe2609 |

The six actual first tests are therefore 28,23,12,26,25,30. Only 12 and23 receive extended development. The rare/wildcard selections were not replaced by more convenient cards. Their exact failed realizations and viable but unpaid variants are preserved in Sections5-7. The other24 cards are untested, not disproved.

checks.py ran once and wrote checks-result.json, SHA-256 **b7483aa3f10da4532045ed4a6b764437cd33cbf37706478cda390525b46845d2**. It checks finite matching, actual quartic-character phases, 4,211 exact turnover incidences, rational thresholds, torsion determinants, and a Krylov determinant. Infinite and uniform conclusions depend on the written proofs, not those finite checks. The native H source inspection is documentary, not a synthetic native H evaluation.

## 2. A complete direct return, and the proposed code graph

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and retain a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including every squareful/nonunit zero. Let S_q be the squarefree q-units, including1. No ideal/arithmetic-H source is substituted for this rational source. Write M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n).

**Matching return.** Suppose there is a disjoint pairing of some members of S_q, with each pair (u,v) satisfying

    a(u)=-a(v),  |u-v|<=C_chi min(u,v)^theta,  0<=theta<1.       (M1)

Finitely many exceptional pairs may be charged separately. Suppose the unmatched count through x is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0, with delta<1. All pairs are in one global pairing; separate unrelated finite-cutoff matchings are not being silently glued.

Every pair wholly below x cancels exactly. A pair crossing x has its lower endpoint in [x-C_chi x^theta,x], so at most C_chi x^theta+1 distinct pairs cross. Coefficient moduli are1. Consequently

    |M_chi(x)| <= C_chi x^theta + O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))+O_chi(1).
                                                                  (M2)

Thus a common gamma=max(theta,delta)>0 gives the every-epsilon M bound. For Re(s)>gamma the integral

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1) dx              (M3)

converges locally uniformly with all derivatives: choose the epsilon below the compact's distance to gamma, and absorb powers of log x. On Re(s)>1 it is exactly1/L(s,chi). The identity L F=1 continues meromorphically to the whole half-plane. A regular zero of L there is impossible. A principal pole at1 forces the reciprocal zero and causes no zero-exclusion exception. This covers every finite height and every imprimitive character directly, with its actual Euler-factor zeros retained. Constants/onsets may depend on each fixed chi. No growing-conductor estimate is asserted.

For simultaneous characters modulo a fixed q, sufficient edge conditions are mu(u)=-mu(v) and u=v mod q. They imply a(u)=-a(v) for every character; squareful and nonunit states still have zero mass. The matching hypothesis is OPEN at every improved exponent.

A plausible coded realization uses small symmetric differences of prime sets. For distinct unramified primes p,r,s and a squarefree m coprime to prs,

    u=mp, v=mrs, p=rs mod q
    => mu(u)chi(u)=-mu(v)chi(v).                              (M4)

These are three-coordinate exchanges between incomparable integers. For example6 and11 cancel for all characters modulo5. One-prime toggles are divisibility edges; two-coordinate exchanges preserve mu's sign and cannot cancel the principal source. A three-coordinate exchange is the first possible nondivisibility cancellation of this kind. Its geometric bill is m|p-rs|, not merely the Hamming length3. A complete matching must retain the common-cofactor and coprimality conditions, all unmatched states, and every cutoff crossing.

For targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4, M1-M2 with theta,delta<=gamma would give respectively c=.12515,1/6,1/4. The first would exceed c11 by10091/2500000000. These are conditional numerical returns; no matching input is supplied. The point of the next result is that **fixed code radius cannot supply the required absolute unmatched budget**, even if the codewords and flow coefficients are otherwise arbitrary.

## 3. Developed W60-12: exact phase compatibility and arithmetic isolation

### 3.1 A binary checksum does not automatically preserve a complex character

For a finite unramified prime set P and subset S, write w(S)=(-1)^|S| chi(product S). For a fixed nonempty toggle C,

    w(S symmetric_difference C)/w(S)
      =(-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                    product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).       (C1)

Therefore w(S xor C)=-w(S) for EVERY S if and only if

    chi(p)^2=1 for every p in C,
    (-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)=-1.                            (C2)

Necessity follows by comparing S empty with each singleton in C; sufficiency is substitution. The hypothesis product_C chi(p)=1 alone is insufficient for an odd toggle when nonreal phases occur.

Actual counterexample: take the primitive quartic character mod5 with chi(2)=i, chi(3)=-i, chi(11)=1 and C={2,3,11}. The empty subset pairs1 with66 with opposite coefficients. But {2} pairs2 with33, whose actual coefficients are BOTH -i. All four integers are squarefree5-units. The exact script checks all eight states. The restricted edge6<->11 is valid; a code must track the state as well as its syndrome.

For a binary matrix A and principal chi, if the parity vector1 lies in the row space of A, parity is constant on every syndrome class and there is no within-class sign cancellation. If it does not, the full uncut cube has balanced parity in every class: translate by an odd element of ker A. The multiplicative cutoff need not respect that translation. This is elementary code duality, not a new theorem about arithmetic cancellation. C1-C2 identify the extra phase failure for the actual complex coefficients.

### 3.2 Turnover lemma: a short move must replace a large factor

For distinct positive integers n,m, put g=gcd(n,m). Then

    g divides n-m, so g<=|n-m|.                                 (C3)

If C>0, 0<=theta<1, and |n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta, it follows exactly that

    n/g >= C^(-1) n^(1-theta).                                  (C4)

When n is squarefree, n/g is the product of the prime factors deleted from n. If all those primes are <=y and at most d are deleted, then n/g<=y^d. Thus n has NO such neighbor whenever

    n^(1-theta)>C y^d.                                         (C5)

This argument allows m to be squareful or nonunit: adding zero-mass auxiliary integer states does not help when an edge may delete at most d of n's prime factors. In particular it applies to the usual squarefree Boolean Hamming radius<=d, whose number of deleted coordinates is<=d. No coefficient estimate or character-distribution assumption is used.

### 3.3 A large actual isolated set exists on every sufficiently large shell

Fix q, C>0, an integer d>=1, and 0<=theta<1. Precisely, every graph edge {n,m} must satisfy the displayed distance bound and delete at most d prime factors from EACH squarefree endpoint when passing to the other endpoint. This condition is independent of a flow's orientation; an incoming edge cannot bypass the source-side budget. Squarefree Hamming radius<=d satisfies it, and optional zero-mass integer vertices are allowed subject to the same endpoint rule. Choose an integer

    k > d/(1-theta),   y=(2X)^(1/k).                            (C6)

Let V_X contain all products of k DISTINCT primes in

    (X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)].

Each n in V_X is squarefree, X<n<=2X, and for large X is coprime to the fixed q. All its primes are<=y. Since1-theta-d/k>0, inequality C5 holds for every n in V_X once X is sufficiently large. Hence every such vertex is isolated in the entire short-move graph, including possible neighbors outside this shell or cutoff.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives, for this FIXED k,

    t_X=#primes in the displayed interval
       ~ k(2^(1/k)-1) X^(1/k)/log X.

Unique factorization counts distinct vertices exactly as binomial(t_X,k). Therefore

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.                                (C7)

Only fixed-relative-width intervals are used, not a primes-in-short-interval theorem or a growing-k substitution. For the external input, the published PNT was checked in the official [NIST DLMF27.12, equations4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12). All deductions C3-C7 are given here. The constants can be tiny and the onset large; both are permitted and neither changes the power obstruction.

It follows that ANY disjoint matching in this graph leaves at least A_k X/(2(log X)^k) actual unit-modulus source coefficients unmatched on [X,2X], for every sufficiently large X. The absolute unmatched mass cannot be O(X^delta) for ANY delta<1. Thus the fixed-radius candidate cannot meet M2, at a near gain,1/6,1/4, or any other power-saving target.

This extends beyond integral matching. For an arbitrary complex edge flow F supported on the same graph, let div F(n) be its net outgoing mass, whenever defined. In any exact source decomposition a=div F+r, an isolated vertex satisfies r(n)=a(n). Hence

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.                               (C8)

No choice of complex flow weights, linear combinations of codewords, or repeated local steps removes an isolated vertex. Chaining cannot start there. The result still holds for any uniformly bounded family of radii and for subpower inflation of C, by first replacing theta by a fixed slightly larger number below1. It does NOT cover growing radii, genuinely long edges, nonlocal auxiliary states with a different exact transfer, or a bound retaining signed cancellation among the isolated states.

| Intended exponent theta | Fixed radius d | k used | Strict isolation exponent1-theta-d/k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|17497/20000=.87485|3|24|3/20000|
|5/6|3|19|1/114|
|3/4|3|13|1/52|

The first row has about X/(log X)^24 isolated24-prime products, all with principal coefficient+1. The next two rows use19- and13-prime products, with principal coefficient-1. This is a lower bound for the absolute residual and for those particular signed subcollections. It is NOT a lower bound for the complete signed residual or M_chi: different prime-count layers can cancel, and that cancellation remains an eligible arithmetic input.

### 3.4 What survives and what has changed

The remaining high-ceiling target is an exact phase-compatible interaction with enough **prime-factor turnover**, or a signed estimate for the smooth isolated complement coupled to other prime-count layers. At a vertex n with largest allowed deleted prime y, C4 requires at least

    ((1-theta)log n-log C)/log y

deleted prime factors. This is the quantity a growing code or multiscale construction must pay; a small Hamming distance by itself is the wrong budget. The concrete three-prime exchange M4 repairs the large-prime failure of deletion matchings but leaves the proved high-degree smooth obstruction. A future combined construction must estimate both parts and their signed interaction. No favorable coding distance or representation count pays that term.

Functional signature: actual squarefree mu-chi source; additive-near, bounded prime-turnover graph; exact coefficient cancellation/flow; C3 forces isolated high-degree products; complete unmatched-count return M1-M3. The new claimed record delta is C6-C8 for all fixed-radius local flows, plus the source-phase criterion C2 and explicit reopening condition. The general pairing return is existing transport ancestry. No literature priority is claimed.

## 4. Developed W60-23: all divisibility matchings have a prime cut

The exact deletion/contraction identity is retained, not claimed as new. For unramified p, put A_p(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n) and B_p(X)=A_p(X)-A_p(X/p). Splitting according to p|n gives

    M_chi(X)=A_p(X)-chi(p)A_p(X/p)
            =B_p(X)+(1-chi(p))A_p(X/p).                        (D1)

This is the full character defect, including squareful zeros. Choosing chi(p)=1 removes the interior twist but leaves B_p. W57's topology development already proves this identity, the weighted commutator, and the linear absolute bill for its canonical least-prime cone. This round tests whether an ADAPTIVE decision tree or arbitrary comparable-face matching could evade that specific cone.

On the finite squarefree q-unit complex through X, allow a pair of ANY distinct comparable vertices u|v, with opposite actual coefficients. This includes adding/removing any odd number of prime factors with the needed character phase, arbitrary pivots chosen with X and chi, and every ordinary disjoint Morse pairing. Each vertex may be used at most once. Every unramified prime p in (X/2,X] has just one possible comparable distinct vertex:1. It has no other divisor and no proper multiple<=X. Hence at most ONE of these primes can be paired. The unmatched count is at least

    # {X/2<p<=X, p not|q} -1.                                 (D2)

For a fractional matching with vertex capacity1, the same bound holds for residual unmatched mass: the terminal primes' entire common neighbor has capacity1. No acyclicity condition was needed, so imposing Morse acyclicity cannot improve the bound. By PNT, D2 is asymptotic to X/(2log X) and has exponent1. The test thus rejects a power bound on the absolute critical-cell bill for EVERY such disjoint comparable-vertex matching, even with a moving prime list and character-one choices. It does not reject arbitrary linear homotopies with shared vertices and paid coefficients.

For principal chi and X=30,100,300, exact maximum bipartite matching leaves respectively3,19,47 of19,61,183 squarefree vertices unmatched. The terminal-prime counts are4,10,27, with exactly one paired in each computation. These examples check the cut, not its asymptotic proof.

This is weaker in numerical size than W57's linear bill for one particular cone, but strictly broader in the allowed matching architecture. It is also different from G76's all-power f3 involution; its coefficient source here is squarefree mu-chi, not f3, and its pairs are constrained to remain inside the sharp cutoff.

The earliest viable escape is precisely to couple incomparable integers, such as M4. Section3 then supplies a second obstruction that survives that change: fixed-radius SHORT exchanges fail on high-degree smooth products. The protected high-reach attempt therefore received a complete deletion identity, an arbitrary-adaptive matching test, a concrete changed construction, a full zero return, and a further actual-arithmetic obstruction. It was not abandoned solely for lacking a ready-made bridge.

## 5. W60-28 and W60-26: what the native H packet actually permits

Freeze the literal finite packet and both independent heights before forming its matrix. The conventions in G75 give H=w*Tv, T=K^T. T contains the complete short-core sum, all original masks/projectors, both rooted mark factors, natural zeros, ray/CRT phases, and every original coefficient. The raw target remains G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]sqrt(Omega1 Omega2)P_orig; the outside factor N^-1 G^-2 is applied once. Nothing below estimates that target or its complementary branches.

**W60-28 first test: the proposed mark constraint is not source-valid.** In [restricted mathematical source] Section1 the native coefficients are a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n), xi(g)=alpha(g)^3eta(g)^3, and the two mark arrays u_i are independent original arrays. They are not the rational sequence mu(n)chi(n). A relation u(pn)=-chi(p)u(n) is therefore not available. ## New quantitative theorem

For every required fixed finite ray, every nonzero integral h, and
each fixed buffered strip 1/2+epsilon<=sigma<=B, write T=1+|t|.
The full sixth-order family and each norm sector satisfy

\[
|\Psi_{\nu,d}(h,\sigma+it)|+|\Psi_\nu(h,\sigma+it)|
\ll Tq_h^4+T^3q_h^{6-2\sigma}.
\]

All original fixed-prime valuations are allowed. The constants depend
on the fixed level, S, rays and strip, not h or t. Finite squarefree
extraction transfers this with an arbitrarily small q_h^delta loss.
The exact forced-divisor identities give explicit polynomial g,h
growth, with all outside collision zeros retained.

Combined with [private research revision] holomorphy, this justifies pole-free buffered
Mellin shifts for every finite row/divisor truncation. Summing the
coarse row powers over unbounded divisors is not justified. The
incidence mean, original product-kernel transfer and both moment
zero-frequency terms remain open.

The proof is in sixth-forced-divisors.md Sections 16--17, (50)--(59).
The controller derived fixed-argument Whittaker inversion;
review_cubic independently checked it. sixth_order supplied
the elliptic cutoff-resolvent construction. The controller supplied
the spinor spectral lower bound that makes the argument uniform at
all t; sixth_order and independent review_sixth checked that
identification and its constants. review_sixth then reviewed the
integrated theorem, including arithmetic powers and truncation limits.

At y_h=x/(2pi R_h), R_h=2q_h^2/sqrt(3), the exact local vector has
norm comparable to T^(-1)q_h^(2sigma-3). The large-order K expansion
has a dominant Gamma(w) term; its exponential size cancels the
Gamma(w+1) denominator. Compactness and whole-vector nonvanishing
handle bounded t. The x=2 leading constant is an asymptotic, not an
exact finite-height formula.

On the fixed arithmetic quotient the standard SU(2) type gives a
rank-two spinor bundle, with a flat unitary genuine twist. For
D=-(Omega1+Omega2),

\[
D=2\nabla^*\nabla-\tfrac32
=2\mathscr D_{\mathrm{spin}}^2+\tfrac32,\qquad
\lambda(w)=\tfrac32-2(w-\tfrac12)^2.
\]

Essential self-adjointness and compact-support form positivity imply
spec(D) is contained in [3/2,infinity). For v=sigma-1/2,
the distance of lambda(w) to this half-line is 2(v^2+t^2) if
|t|<=v and 4v|t| otherwise. It is at least v(v+|t|), giving
a resolvent bound O_epsilon(T^(-1)) for all t.
An initially suggested extra factor two in that lower bound was
withdrawn: t=v/2 disproves it. The stated weaker inequality suffices.

Subtract ALL incoming cusp terms with fixed cutoffs. The forcing
is compactly supported and O(T); the remaining outgoing and
nonconstant terms are L2 for each fixed parameter. The resolvent
therefore gives an O(1) L2 norm and O(T^2) covariant H2 norm.
Scaled Sobolev evaluation costs H^(3/2) at reduced cusp height H.
Adding the incoming part proves

\[
|E(g,w)|\ll H(g)^{\sigma+1/2}+T^2H(g)^{3/2}.
\]

The elementary bound H(n(z)a_y)<<1+y+y^(-1), uniform over the
finite components of the adelic Fourier integral, then gives the
displayed arithmetic estimate through Whittaker inversion.

Primary inputs:
[DLMF Bessel connection formula](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.27.E4),
[I-series](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.25.E2),
[Gamma asymptotics](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.11),
[Melrose, twisted Lichnerowicz formula, Section 3.2](https://math.mit.edu/~rbm/18.199-S06/18.199-S06.pdf),
and [Braverman--Milatovic--Shubin, Theorem 2.3 and Corollaries 2.9--2.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0201231v3).
The cycle-6 KP realization supplies the actual Eisenstein family.

The earlier alternative Q=(Omega1-Omega2)/i was not used: formal
symmetry and centrality did not establish its proposed self-adjoint
domain and strong commutation. A separate compact-t cusp-propagation
argument also became unnecessary once the spinor lower bound was
proved. Neither alternative remains an active proof dependency.

## 4. Square-core middle estimate: unrestricted cubic outer variable

Factor the integral frequency ideal as ell=kappa*b^2, kappa squarefree, allowing (kappa,b)>1; the fixed Delta/unit factors are understood literally as above. On every unit and nonunit,

    chi_m(ell)^eta=chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(b)^(2eta).     (4.1)

For fixed kappa the second factor is cubic. Absorb the first into the actual inner coefficient. Its squared mass still satisfies (2.3), independent of b. The common (f,ell)=1 restricts outer b and/or kills the fiber; source/slot intersections with b are exactly the natural zeros of the cubic symbol.

The precise unconditional input is [Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Theorem4.1/Corollary4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3): with squarefree primary inner m of length X and an arbitrary inner sequence, the unrestricted outer variable b of length B has energy bounded by

    (BX)^epsilon B^(1/3)(B+X) * inner squared mass.      (4.2)

Cubic reciprocity/conjugation supplies the orientation in (4.1), after the fixed ray handling just stated. This is Section4's large sieve, NOT the paper's cuspidal bilinear theorem. Neither squarefreeness of b nor an arbitrary joint matrix is assumed.

In an a-dyad the outer length is B<~(H_A/Nkappa)^(1/2). For a core cap C>=1, sum kappa by ideal counting. Using sum_(Nkappa<=C)Nkappa^(-2/3)<<C^(1/3) and sum Nkappa^(-1/6)<<C^(5/6), the complete positive fiber price is

    H_J U^epsilon [H_A^(2/3) C^(1/3)
                              +X H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6)].  (4.3)

Sharp middle restrictions and the core selector are allowed by Section3. Empty B<1 fibers contribute nothing; fixed bounded clipping costs are harmless. Both scalar sides satisfy (4.3), so Cauchy pays their product at this same price, not its square.

Restore (2.1), both allocation multiplicities, and O(A) original a labels. The exact dyad/f prices are

    U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^(-1) N0^(1/3) (Nf)^(-1) C^(1/3),
    U^(5/6+tau/6) A^(-4) N0^(1/3) (Nf)^(-2) C^(5/6).

The A sums are geometric and bounded. The f^-1 sum with tau(f)^C is harmonic up to an arbitrarily small power; the f^-2 sum converges after such a loss. Therefore the literal signed selected middle obeys

    |R_sq(C)| << H_J U^epsilon [
        U^(1/3+2tau/3) N0^(1/3) C^(1/3)
       +U^(5/6+tau/6) N0^(1/3) C^(5/6)].              (SQ)

All roots, original slots and both f allocations have been paid. This is an actual joint frequency/source estimate; replacing every frequency by (2.4) would give a larger price.

## G138. Full integral persistence and fixed versus moving readouts

Use the augmented squarefree complex with deg(e_n)=omega(n),
ordered prime-deletion differential and C(x)=0 for x<1. For each odd
squarefree m set b_m=e_(2m), z_m=d b_m=e_m-e_2 wedge d e_m.
Every correction has index 2m/p<m. This gives an integral
unitriangular basis at EVERY real cutoff, with d b_m=z_m and d z_m=0.
Thus the entire persistence module splits into intervals [m,2m) in
augmented degree omega(m), including [1,2) in degree 0 (reduced -1).
Inclusions are identity while an interval survives and zero at death.
This is a direct filtered-basis proof, not an imported barcode theorem.
Classical static topology retains its Björner/W27 attribution.

All logarithmic lifetimes equal log2. The map H(C(x))->H(C(2x)) is
zero, although M(3)=-1. A selection of longer-lived classes deletes
the signal. For fixed alpha in[1/2,1), write

    O_chi(x)=sum_(odd n<=x) mu(n)chi(n),
    R_alpha,chi(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(alpha x),
    M_chi(x)=O_chi(x)-chi(2)O_chi(x/2).

Character weighting is an arithmetic readout, not a commuting chain
map. Include chi(2)=0, every natural zero and the n=1 atom. On Re s>1,

    Mellin R=(1-alpha^s)/[s(1-chi(2)2^-s)L(s,chi)].

Both extra factors are nonzero on Re s>0. A COMPLETE every-epsilon
dyadic L2 bound at exponent 2gamma therefore excludes zeros Re s>gamma
for every fixed ordinary character at every height, with common gamma
and character-dependent constants. The left tail vanishes below 1;
dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz pays holomorphy and its derivatives. The principal
pole is a meromorphic point and actual imprimitive factors remain.
Pointwise reconstruction is the finite-for-each-x sum
O_chi(x)=sum_j R_alpha,chi(alpha^j x), costing (1-alpha^gamma)^-1.
Unsigned rank remains [4(1-alpha)/pi^2]x+O(sqrt x).

For T(x)=x-x^(1-eta), 0<eta<1, the arithmetic difference
R_eta(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(T(x)) is bounded trivially by x^(1-eta)+1.
Its persistence interpretation starts at x>=2^(1/eta); the initial
bounded interval is paid separately. Iteration until x<2 takes at
most 2+2^(k eta) steps in the dyadic band [2^k,2^(k+1)). Thus a
uniform pointwise R_eta=O(x^gamma), gamma>=0, only gives
O_chi=O(x^(gamma+eta)). The odd constant comparison source proves

readout does not supply it. Keep the signed-window target OPEN.

# Signed readouts, paid prime cutoffs and actual positive Gram prices

13 October2026. The controller reconstructed the complete frozen W66
[author](wild66/report.md), [independent review](wild66-review/report.md),
[two pre-outcome audits](wild66-review/audits.md), and the independently
reviewed [positive-hole corollary](positive-hole-review/report.md).
The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves all30 cards,
literal draws, failures and finite diagnostics separately from these proofs.
Untested cards remain untested. Literature priority is not asserted.

The number c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 remains a CONDITIONAL
SOURCE-RELATIVE benchmark. PR15's stronger weighted source and endpoint
are [explicitly unfinished](../imports/qrtracker-20261013/pr15-status-clarification.md).
Nothing below repairs that premise, proves F0 or positive-slot uniformity,
admits PR26, or establishes a larger c. The prior formal packet is complete;
no new kernel, formalization or public-record claim is involved.

## G222. Exact prime-deletion inversion and the full signed readout

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and real X>=1. Let D_X
be the squarefree q-units n<=X, including1. It is a divisor downset.
For each unramified prime choose0<rho_p<=1, lambda_p=1-rho_p,
R_p=(2-rho_p)/rho_p. With row d and column n in D_X, define

    B(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|d)rho_p prod_(p|n/d)lambda_p,
    C(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|n)rho_p^-1 prod_(p|n/d)(-lambda_p).
                                                               (222.1)

Empty products and0^0 are1. Every intermediate divisor e between d,n
remains in D_X. Expanding BC or CB factors over primes of n/d, giving
the cancellation(lambda_p-lambda_p) at each missing prime and diagonal1.
Consequently both products equal the identity. Absolute column sums give

    ||B||_(1->1)=1,
    V(X):=||C||_(1->1)=max_(n in D_X) prod_(p|n)R_p.          (222.2)

For uniform fixed rho, V=R^K_X, K_X=max_D omega(n). The factorial bound
n>=(omega(n)+1)! implies K_X<=(1+o(1))log X/loglog X, so V=X^o(1).
The size downset is essential: a full prime cube would give the wrong
exponential price. Uniform moving rho_X=(log X)^-b instead costs
X^(b+o(1)); the matching lower factor count follows from primorials and
the ordinary [prime number theorem](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).

For a FIXED prime-dependent sequence, the exact criterion is

    V(X)=X^o(1) iff log R_p/log p ->0.                       (222.3)

Necessity uses the column n=p at X=p. For sufficiency, given epsilon>0
choose P with R_p<=p^epsilon for p>P. Then the product is at most
[prod_(p<=P,p not|q)R_p]n^epsilon. The constant is independent of X.
Thus rho_p=min(1,(log p)^-b), b>0, may tend to0 while inversion remains
subpower. This is different from assigning the SAME rho_X to all primes.
For arbitrary X-dependent choices, the maximum in(222.2), not(222.3),
is the bill. No prime theorem is needed for the fixed-sequence criterion.

Apply B to nu(n)=chi(n) on D_X. The actual output and observer are

    b_X(d)=chi(d)prod_(p|d)rho_p
      *sum_(m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1)mu(m)^2 chi(m)prod_(p|m)lambda_p,
    h(d)=prod_(p|d)(-R_p),
    M_chi(X)=sum_(d in D_X)h(d)b_X(d).                       (222.4)

The cofactor phase chi(m), every natural zero, unit and cutoff remain.
Indeed summing over d|n gives prod_(p|n)(lambda_p-rho_p R_p)=mu(n).
The readout is bilinear, without a conjugation. For ANY full approximant
btilde_X, with e_X=b_X-btilde_X, one has

    |M_chi(X)|<=|sum_d h(d)btilde_X(d)|+V(X)||e_X||_1.       (222.5)

Under(222.3), complete every-epsilon bounds at exponent gamma for BOTH
right-hand quantities before the subpower loss give the same exponent
for M. Under a moving inverse cost X^b, the residual must pay b.
A selected label or omitted error does not have this return. No such
arithmetic approximation has been constructed here.

For one common gamma in(0,1) and every fixed ordinary character, this
Mertens estimate continues s int_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi)
normally to Re s>gamma after an epsilon buffer. The continued identity
LF=1 excludes all regular zeros at every finite height. The principal
pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero; imprimitive zeros and modulus
conventions remain those of [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15).
Constants and onsets may depend on the fixed character. No growing-q
uniformity or native Eisenstein-source transfer follows.

The inverse is affordable, but positive readout certificates fail in an
exact broader sense. For principal chi, b_X(d)>0, even when some rho_p=1,
because n=d contributes. For ANY moving retentions and positive diagonal
weights w_d,

    P_abs=sum_d |h(d)|b_X(d)
       =sum_(n in D_X)prod_(p|n)(3-2rho_p),
    #D_X<=P_abs<=3^K_X #D_X=X^(1+o(1)),
    ||w h||_2 ||b_X/w||_2>=P_abs.                          (222.6)

The minimum is attained by w_d^2=b_X(d)/|h(d)|. The same lower bound
holds for any conjugate Holder pair. The fixed-q squarefree count
#D_X=kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not|q)(1-p^-2)>0,
follows by expanding mu^2 and counting q-units; it needs no PNT.
Thus arbitrary adaptive diagonal weights cannot make this principal
separable certificate power-small. This does not bound the signed readout
from below or exclude nonlocal signed norms or growing signed centering.

Uniform rho also gives the exact cutoff polynomial

    P_X(z)=sum_d b_X(d)z^omega(d)=Z_X(lambda+rho z),
    Z_X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)chi(n)z^omega(n), P_X(-R)=M_chi(X).
                                                               (222.7)

Its circle evaluation costs at most sqrt(sum_(j<=K_X)R^(2j)), subpower
for fixed rho. For principal chi all coefficients are nonnegative and
the prime layer has beta_0+beta_1>=pi_q(X), hence ||P_X||_circle>=pi_q(X)/sqrt2.
Deleting every original degree<=r, for fixed r, does not fix that norm:
products of r+1 distinct primes in((X/2)^(1/(r+1)),X^(1/(r+1))] supply
at least const X/log(X)^(r+1) mass in r+2 nonnegative coefficients.
Their l2 norm is at least mass/sqrt(r+2), uniformly in moving retention.
Other original layers only increase coefficients. This is a norm
obstruction, not an alternating-sum lower bound; signed quotient and
growing-layer methods survive. With varying rho_p there is generally no
single scalar z representing h: retain the labeled/multivariate readout.

## G223. Critical small-prime payment with its exact margin debit

Use the complete ordinary-character source of
[G173](../[private research revision]/wild62-integration.md): fixed tau>0,1/2<gamma<1,

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^-1/2 exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=e^(-gamma y)U(y),
    I_R=int_0^R y|z|^2, E_R=int_0^R |z|^2.

The coefficient identity a(n)log n=-sum_(d|n)chi(d)Lambda(d)a(n/d)
retains ALL prime powers, including cancellation at squareful n. It gives

    tau z'+(y+tau gamma)z+K1 z+K2 z=0,
    K1 z(y)=sum_p chi(p)log p p^-gamma z(y-log p),
    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2,
    Qj=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z)Kj z.                         (223.1)

G173 pays |Q2|<=eta I_R+B_eta for every eta>0 by its summable j>=2
coefficient norm, the complete Gaussian past and a fixed initial interval.
No unknown future bound is used. The same-output prime diagonal is
nonnegative and O(1): its coefficient is1 precisely at squarefree
q-units n=pm, the prime log-weights sum to at most log n, and

    int_R e^(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =e^(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi*tau)).

Here is a larger paid small-prime region. Fix a0>0 and set

    b=1/(1-gamma), Y(y)=a0(1+y)^b,
    kappa=a0^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).

Assign equality to p<=Y(y). PNT and partial summation give
S_gamma(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p p^-gamma~t^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).
The row sum is(kappa+o(1))y. Apply2|z(y)z(y-log p)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(y-log p)|^2.
For the column put v=y-log p; the mask gives log p=O(log y), so for
any epsilon>0 and all large y, y<=v/(1-epsilon). Its column sum is at
most S_gamma(a0(1+v/(1-epsilon))^b)<=(kappa/(1-epsilon)+o(1))v.
Both half factors are present. The bounded initial region has finitely
many primes and a fixed bounded source interval. Therefore

    |Q_small(R)|<=(kappa+eta)I_R+B_eta, every R>=0.          (223.2)

The elementary theta(t)<=4(log2)t instead gives4(log2)kappa. This
critical mask is larger than G173's logarithmically reduced mask, but
its nonzero debit must be retained; it does not inherit the old zero
relative price or an unproved hard estimate for another mask.

Let H_a0,R be the ENTIRE p>Y(y), n!=pm expansion with literal summand

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))chi(p)a(m)] log p e^(-2gamma y)
                 *g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),                  (223.3)

integrated over0<=y<=R, all m,n>=1. Gaussian majorants justify the
compact-interval sums; diagonal and every complementary source remain.
If THIS jointly chosen mask has constants delta>kappa,B_chi,R0_chi with

    H_a0,R<=(1-delta)I_R+B_chi, every R>=R0_chi,             (223.4)

then pay eta=(delta-kappa)/4 in(223.2) and the higher powers to obtain

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+((delta-kappa)/2)I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'.  (223.5)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(e^(gamma y)). Its complete bilateral transform equals
e^(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) initially on Re s>1 and continues normally to
Re s>gamma; the numerator never vanishes. This excludes every zero
at every finite height there, preserves the principal pole and all
natural zeros, and assumes no height-uniform numerator lower bound.
Gamma is common across the family; a0,delta and constants may depend
on a fixed character. This is a one-way ordinary-source return.

Choosing a0=[delta(1-gamma)/2]^(1/(1-gamma)) spends kappa=delta/2;
it does NOT manufacture the margin for the resulting mask. The targets
c=.12,.12515,1/6,1/4 require gamma=.88,.87485,5/6,3/4 and critical powers
25/3,20000/2503,6,4. The .12515 target exceeds conditional c11 by.0000040364.
None of the corresponding complete inequalities(223.4) is proved.

The generic leading coefficient is sharp even for a one-sided form.
For principal chi take arbitrary test input
f_T(y)=exp(i*pi*y/log Y_T)1_[T,T+sqrt T], Y_T=a0(1+T)^b.
Delays lose only O(log T/sqrt T) relative overlap, Y(y)/Y_T->1 uniformly,
and prime-weight mass below Y_T^(1-epsilon) is negligible. On the rest
the real phase tends to-1 as T then epsilon tend to their limits. Hence
-Re<f_T,K_small f_T>/int y|f_T|^2->kappa. A supercritical fixed power b'
instead gives asymptotic kappa T^(b'(1-gamma)-1), which diverges.
These are arbitrary inputs, not the actual z, and do not lower-bound its
signed form. Even granting |U(y)|<=C e^(beta y), gamma<beta<1, the
coarse absolute full-prime price has exponent1+beta-2gamma against
2beta-2gamma for I_R: the missing saving remains1-beta.

## G224. Exact chirp and paired-character audits, with reconstruction paid

The two independent unselected audits preserve useful alternatives and
their exact limits. For z=a-i kappa, a>0, the analytic square root gives

    sqrt(z/(2*pi)) exp(t^2/(2z))
       *int_R exp(-z u^2/2+i t u)du=1,
    P_z(t)=(|z|/a)^1/2 exp(a t^2/(2|z|^2)).                 (224.1)

The first identity follows by the Gaussian Fourier integral and normal
continuation on Re z>0. The second is its exact completely absolute
price. On |t|<=T set E=a T^2/(2|z|^2)>0,
C=|kappa|T^2/(2|z|^2). Then P_z(T)=(1+(C/E)^2)^1/4 e^E
>=sqrt(C)e^E/sqrt(E)>=sqrt(2e C). A power-sized exterior chirp C=X^delta
therefore costs at least X^(delta/2) under absolute payment. Finite
insertion is legitimate; infinite insertion must pay its exterior
exponential against the original full tail. Signed/L2 use remains open.

For odd prime Q, A nonzero mod Q, c=(4A)^-1 and
G_A=sum_v e_Q(A v^2), completing the square gives
sum_v e_Q(A v^2+t v)=G_A e_Q(-c t^2), |G_A|^2=Q.
For actual residue sums B_r and F_v=sum_r B_r e_Q(c r^2+v r),

    S=sum_r B_r=G_A^-1 sum_v e_Q(A v^2)F_v,
    sum_v |F_v|^2=Q sum_r |B_r|^2,
    |S|^2=Q^-1 sum_(v,w)e_Q(A(v^2-w^2))F_v conjugate(F_w).
                                                               (224.2)

All crosses and natural zeros remain. The Cauchy bound |S|^2<=sum_v|F_v|^2
is generically sharp: B_r=1 gives equality Q^2. That is an ambient
coherent example, not a claim about the actual arithmetic residue array.
The four-point curvature of one bilinear t=mn channel has phase
c(m^2-m'^2)(n^2-n'^2)+v(m-m')(n-n'); complete channel recombination
restores multiplier1. A selected curved channel is not a full estimate.

The other audit distinguishes conjugate heights and observation loss.
F_barchi(s)=conjugate(F_chi(conjugate(s))) for F=1/L. A pole at rho maps
to conjugate(rho), not necessarily rho. For a Laurent vector with leading
coefficient v and continuous observation A(s), the leading squared signal
is v* A(rho)* A(rho) v. Positive semidefiniteness alone can annihilate v;
one needs coverage of actual residue directions, or a uniform lower
singular-value bound. A complete bank must keep every associated source.

At real x, the actual pair satisfies
||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))||^2=2|M_chi(x)|^2. This also holds with common
REAL weights; complex weights and heights must be conjugated as well.
A full every-epsilon shell-L1 pair estimate has the ordinary all-height
Abel return in G222, but is exactly the scalar estimate up to sqrt2.
The difference observation for a real character is identically zero.
Degenerating coordinate changes must pay their inverse. These adapters
preserve existing detector/curvature ancestry and supply no exponent gain.

The author's other selected tests retain the complete asymmetric
hyperbola identity u_U*u_V*chi=a-m_U-m_V+m_U*m_V*chi. Its principal
absolute long-long tuple price is at least const X when U,V<=sqrt X/2,
by pairs of squarefree q-units in(sqrt X/2,sqrt X]. This is not a signed
corner lower bound. Exterior-boundary and least-prime matching tests
duplicate G164-G165: the outgoing boundary remains, critical coordinates
need not be harmonic, and the matched character bulk a(n)(1-chi(p))
cannot be discarded outside the principal case. Their failures and all
22 untested cards are retained without broad rejection of the mechanisms.

## G225. Actual positive cofactor-hole prices, including after integration

Use the full G218 Gaussian over integers or Eisenstein integral ideals,
q_a=a or Na, with fixed eta,tau,S. Put c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1).
Let S+ add ALL natural-zero primes of the PRESENTED character, including
imprimitive modulus primes. On each entire shell[X,2X], choose arbitrary
nonnegative theta_Q with sum1 on radicals coprime to S, q_Q<=X^A,
fixed A>0. The choices may depend on X and the actual arithmetic source,
but are frozen in x. Define

    p(a)=sum_Q theta_Q 1_((a,Q)=1),
    K_X(a,b)=int_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x,
    A_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(rad(ab)),
    B_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(a)p(b).
                                                               (225.1)

The first is the average absolute-real Gram price of each hole field;
the second is that price for their averaged field. Both include diagonal
and both off-diagonal orientations. They are not the signed energies.

Uniformly over this entire family,

    X^2/log(2X)^2 << A_theta, B_theta << X^2.                (225.2)

Constants/onsets depend on R,S,eta,tau,A, not theta or Q. The lower bound
survives diagonal removal. This is a corollary of the G218 count and
G221 real-rank bound with a useful logarithmic refinement.

For Q*=rad(S+ Q), D(Q*)=prod_(p|Q*)(1+q_p^-1)^-1 satisfies

    D(Q*)^-1=sum_(d|Q*)q_d^-1
       <=sum_(q_d<=q_Q*)q_d^-1 << log(2q_Q*) << log(2X).

Partial summation of the elementary A_R(T)<<T proves this without PNT.
Subtract the uniform G218 squarefree counts at2X and X. The errors
are O(sqrt X log(2X)S_1/2(Q*)) over ideals and O(sqrt X d(Q*)) over
integers. The elementary small/large-prime split gives each factor sum
<<_delta q_Q*^delta; take delta=1/(4A). Thus errors are
O(X^(3/4)log(2X)), smaller than the main X/log(2X). No Q<=X
restriction is needed. Since g has a positive minimum on[-log2,log2],

    W_Q(x)=sum_a |c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g(log(q_a/x))
       >>X/log(2X), every x in[X,2X],                     (225.3)

while the complete Gaussian majorant gives W_Q(x)<<x. No character
zero is replaced by a unit phase.

Regard xi_a=c_a/|c_a| as a unit vector in R^2 on its nonzero support.
With positive weights w_a, let M=sum_a w_a xi_a xi_a^T and W=sum_a w_a.
Then

    sum_(a,b)w_a w_b |xi_a dot xi_b|
      >=trace(M^2)>=W^2/2.                               (225.4)

The first step uses |t|>=t^2 on[-1,1]; the second uses two nonnegative
eigenvalues. All ACTUAL Mobius signs and character phases remain.
Apply it first to w_a=|c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g, average theta and integrate.
Apply it separately to w_a=|c_a|p(a)g, whose mass is sum theta_Q W_Q.
These prove both lower bounds without comparing their kernels. For real
eta the constant1/2 can be1. Truncation, nonnegative convergence and the
Gaussian O(x) majorant justify every infinite sum and the O(X^2) upper bound.

The diagonals are sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a) and the same with p(a)^2.
Both are O(X), since0<=p<=1 and the squared Gaussian is a constant times
a narrower Gaussian. Subtracting them preserves(225.2) for large X.
The covariance kernels are not ordered entrywise: theta_1=theta_lm=1/2
gives joint/product1/2,1/4 at a=l,b=m, whereas theta_l=theta_m=1/2
gives0,1/4, for two distinct good primes and sufficiently large X.

For each pair the phase is independent of x and K_X is positive, so
int |Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|g_a g_b dx/x
=|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))K_X(a,b)| exactly. Hence taking pairwise real
absolute values AFTER integration gives the same scalar Gaussian price.
This identity does not discard cancellation in a collective signed sum,
extend to oscillatory joint-label kernels, or certify an arbitrary theta
as a zero detector. The latter needs its own complete fixed-source return.
G222's principal deletion-channel Holder floor and G127's different
curved-source obstruction retain their distinct priority and scope.

## G226. A dimension-free obstruction after paying a common linear readout

This develops the user's quaternion proposal beyond the G221 bounded
rank-four argument. Root's [discovery and initial proof](linear-readout/root-draft.md)
tested growing dimension and delayed absolute values as possible escapes.
The [independent review](linear-readout/review.md) sharpened the initial
constant4/pi^2 to the sharp1/2 and clarified the complex-kernel and
variable-readout scopes. The earlier argument remains historical evidence.

Let H be ANY real Hilbert space, T:H->R^2 a bounded real-linear map with
norm L, and(v_a) a finite family. Define y_a=T v_a,
M=sum_a|y_a| and B=sum_(a,b)|<v_a,v_b>|, with all ordered pairs. Then

    L^2 B >= M^2/2.                                      (226.1)

No dimension or upper bound on individual vectors appears. To prove it,
let u_a=y_a/|y_a| when y_a!=0 and u_a=0 otherwise. Define A:R^2->H by
A e_j=sum_a u_(a,j)v_a. Its Hilbert-Schmidt norm satisfies

    ||A||_HS^2=sum_(a,b)<v_a,v_b><u_a,u_b><=B,
    TA=sum_a |y_a|u_a u_a^T,
    M^2/2<=trace((TA)^2)=||TA||_HS^2<=L^2||A||_HS^2.

The positive2x2 operator has trace M and squared eigenvalue sum at least
M^2/2. This proves(226.1). Equality occurs for
T=identity on R^2, v_1=e_1,v_2=e_2. If all images lie on one real line,
the constant improves to1. More generally a target R^r gives the sharp
constant1/r, depending on OUTPUT dimension rather than lift dimension.
This is not the false termwise inequality
|<Tv_a,Tv_b>|<=L^2|<v_a,v_b>|.

Separate maps per index do not meet this hypothesis: v_i=e_i in R^n,
T_i(v)=v_i gives B=n, M=n and separate norms1. The COMMON recovery
v->sum_i v_i has norm sqrt(n), restoring the missing bill.

For an infinite family, apply(226.1) to every finite subset and take
nonnegative limits. No convergence of an infinite vector sum is needed
for this extended inequality. Each vector and readout must still exist.
The result includes arbitrary dimension, additional quaternion components,
and X-dependent choices of the common map, once its norm is paid.

Pointwise, if T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x), then

    L_x^2 sum_(a,b)|<v_a(x),v_b(x)>|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a|c_a K(q_a/x)|]^2.                    (226.2)

For the G221 quaternion lift w_a(xi_a+t_a j), first-complex-coordinate
projection has L_x=1. Thus the actual full/middle source has quadratic
pointwise absolute price even WITHOUT a bound on t_a. The old necessary
dimension/readout tradeoff remains valid but is weaker: growing the
dimension does not reduce the price after a common linear recovery is paid.

There is a corresponding after-integration theorem. Put I=[X,2X],
measure dx/x and length ell=log2. Let v_a belong to its direct-integral
real Hilbert space, and let T_x be measurable common recovery maps with
essential supremum norm L_X<infinity on the shell. Assume

    T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x),
    J(t)=int_1^2 K(t/u)du/u.

The common map Tcal(v)=int_I T_x v(x)dx/x has norm at most L_X sqrt(ell)
and sends v_a to c_a J(q_a/X). Apply(226.1) in the direct integral:

    L_X^2 ell sum_(a,b)|int_I <v_a(x),v_b(x)>dx/x|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a |c_a J(q_a/X)|]^2.                  (226.3)

All absolute values on the left are AFTER pair integration. A fixed
common ambient H is sufficient; measurable Hilbert bundles also work
when the stated direct integral and maps are well defined. It suffices
to apply the argument to finite central subsets; infinite absolute prices
then dominate those finite ones. Arbitrary x-dependent lifts are allowed.

The variable bound int_I ||T_x||^2 dx/x also bounds Tcal's squared norm,
but it does NOT automatically pay full shell-L2 reconstruction. For the
actual source-energy certificate the uniform L_X above is sufficient:
||sum_a T_x v_a||_(L2)^2<=L_X^2||sum_a v_a||_(L2(H))^2<=L_X^2 B_after
when the sums/convergence required for that upper estimate are justified.
If no such finite reconstruction bill is available, do not claim a
source upper bound from the averaged-functional inequality alone.

The right side has quadratic order for the exact Jordan source, including
its retained middle. Its fixed kernel is generally COMPLEX for nonreal
chi, and G215 gives K(t)=e^-t+O(e^-2t), so K is continuous, nonzero and
tends to0 at infinity. More generally these three properties imply J is
not identically zero: in logarithmic coordinates J'=K(t)-K(t/2); J=0
would force K(t)=K(2t), hence K=0 by repeated scaling to infinity.
Choose a fixed interval[a,b] in(0,infinity) on which |J|>=k>0. The
fixed-q squarefree count gives

    sum_(d>=1)|mu(d)chi(d)J(d/X)| >>_(q,K) X.              (226.4)

For G215's middle, d in[aX,bX] lies in x^alpha<d<=2x log x for EVERY
x in[X,2X] once X is large, because alpha<1. Thus these central vectors
have exactly the same integrated image c_d J(d/X); they alone prove the
same lower bound in(226.3). No omitted tail, principal main term or
varying-cutoff identity has been discarded. The actual compensated K,
not the uncentered Jordan source, is used.

For the G218 Gaussian, positivity directly gives |J(t)| bounded below
on[1,2]. Fixed holes give mass >>X; polynomial-sized holes, or their
positive normalized field averages, give >>X/log(2X) by G225, with all
presented character zeros retained. Applying(226.3) separately to each
hole also permits a positive average of its complete lifted price.
No arbitrary oscillatory joint-label kernel is identified with that
positive-mask construction.

These are TOTAL-price lower bounds. To conclude the same for the absolute
off-diagonal, also pay the diagonal. In G221's bounded lifts with fixed
C, sum_a int_I ||v_a||^2=O(C^2 X), so the quadratic lower bound survives
its removal. Without such a bound an unbounded lift may move the bill
onto its diagonal; no off-diagonal assertion is then made.

The complete returned shell-L2 target gamma=1-c requires energy exponent
2-2c. The paid source-index absolute-Gram price above has exponent at
least2, leaving deficit2c: .24 at c=.12, .2502919272 at conditional c11,
.25030 at c=.12515,1/3 at c=1/6 and1/2 at c=1/4. G215/G218 supply their
own L2-to-L1 and all-height returns; the price theorem proves none of
the necessary signed estimates and imports no cross-family transfer.

The scope matters: one vector per actual source coefficient, a common
linear recovery, the COMPLETE pairwise absolute Gram, and a paid norm.
Cancellation inside blocks before the absolute value, full signed
companion comparisons, nonlinear reconstruction, or genuinely different
X-dependent profiles with a proved return remain open. The theorem is
not a lower bound on the actual signed source energy. It strengthens
G221's finite-dimensional price and closes its generic after-integration
escape for these fixed Gaussian/Jordan profiles and common recoveries;
it does not reject quaternion or matrix approaches as a whole.

## DQ10--DQ11. The legitimate weighted cubic-sieve estimate

Retain the BC polynomial smoothing

`V(x)=(2 pi i)^(-1) integral exp(w^2)x^(-w) dw/w`,
`N=D^4 T^4`, `T=2+|Im z|`, `z=a+it`.

BC9--BC10 justify
`L(1-z,bar eta)=sum_n bar eta(n) q_n^(z-1)V(q_n/N)+error`.
The original finite-order FE, not an absolutely convergent series at `1-a`,
pays the error. After the outside FE its bound is
`O_J(D^(-2J)T^(-2J))`, harmless after absolute core counting and the original
profile. On dyads `q_n~M`, `q_d~U`, there are
`O_epsilon((M/U)^(1/3+epsilon))` possible cube factors `kappa`.

For each fixed `kappa` and common-core projector divisor `g`, retain
`(c,kappa g)=1` in the coefficients and `(d,g)=1` on the rows. Cubic reciprocity
separates the permitted fixed ray sectors. The normalized core energy is
`O((D/g)^(1+epsilon))`, so M (5.15) gives

`(D/g) [U+D/g+(UD/g)^(2/3)]`

up to arbitrarily small powers. The full common-core projector is inserted
before Cauchy--Schwarz. Its first contribution costs only a logarithm; the
other two `g` sums converge. Original outside cubes have rapid decay in this
balanced sector; their support masks remain in the coefficients before
positive estimates. Using the actual dual weight `M^(a-1)` gives

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal B^{\mathrm{dual}}_{M,U}(a+it)|
\ll T^A D^{2-2a+\epsilon}M^{a-2/3}
\left[U^{2/3}+DU^{-1/3}+D^{2/3}U^{1/3}\right].}
\tag{DQ10}
\]

The factor `D^(1-2a)` is the outside FE, another `D` is core energy, and
`(M/U)^(1/3)` counts cube factors. Thus the cube multiplicity is not omitted.
For a row `d=d1d2^2`, its actual primitive conductor is `rad(d)`, and every
natural zero at `d kappa` stays present. The cube-free sieve is applied on
its stated cube-free ideal index set, without replacing this conductor by
`q_d` in a separate Hecke bound or introducing `(d,kappa)=1`.

Summing `M>=U>=G` and using rapid decay beyond `N` yields, with fixed `a`
chosen inside the final epsilon budget,

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal B^{\mathrm{dual}}_{q_d\ge G}|
\ll T^A D^{2+\epsilon}
\left(1+\frac D G+\frac{D^{2/3}}{G^{1/3}}\right).}
\tag{DQ11}
\]

The harmless factors `N^a` and `K^a` are charged by this fixed choice for
`K<=D^B` with fixed `B`. The bound pays `q_d>=D^2` in this smoothed analytic
decomposition. It is not a physical-row sector theorem or an improvement of
the full original remainder. In particular, the long artificial smoothing
length by itself is not the dominant obstruction; `q_d<D^2` remains.

statement:
## 3. Exact H-orbit geometry: what “both cells” does not specify

Write H elements as (x,y,t), acting in the affine chart by

    (z1,z2,z3) -> (t^2 z1+x, t^2 z2+y, t^2 z3+x+y).

Each infinity coordinate stays infinity. In the fully finite chart,
d=z3-z1-z2 transforms to t^2 d. Consequently the orbit list over an
algebraic closure is:

| Representative | Number of strata | Orbit dimension | Stabilizer |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| (0,0,1), d!=0 | 1 | 3 | t=+/-1, x=y=0 |
| (0,0,0), d=0 | 1 | 2 | T_delta |
| (infinity,0,0) and its other two placements | 3 | 2 | T_delta |
| Two infinities and one zero | 3 | 1 | T_delta with one unipotent dimension |
| (infinity,infinity,infinity) | 1 | 0 | H |

For example, with first coordinate infinity the independent translations
y and x+y set the other two coordinates to zero. With two infinities only
one translation condition remains. This proves completeness and distinguishes
all nine strata without a classification theorem.

Over the actual odd nonarchimedean field, the open finite-chart orbit splits
according to d in F^*/F^{*2}, which has four classes. This is a rational-orbit
distinction; it does not create four more geometric boundary divisors. The
other eight orbits do not split, so there are twelve F-rational orbits in all.
Over the finite residue field there are ten: two open square classes plus
those same eight closed orbits. The
selected Fourier line (nu,nu,-nu), nu=c m^2, fixes a square class on the
Fourier side. Identifying it with a particular d-orbit is still an unfolding
map to be supplied; equality of the two class counts is not that map.

The complement of the geometric open orbit has four irreducible divisors:
the closure of d=0, and z1=infinity, z2=infinity, z3=infinity. At their standard
representatives their stabilizer is T_delta. The normal coordinate of d=0
has weight t^2. Each infinity divisor has normal coordinate 1/zi of weight
t^-2. The tangent measure on each two-dimensional orbit has Jacobian |t|^4.
These normal characters, fiber characters and the chosen density line are
the inputs needed to define boundary distributions. Their multiplicities do
not collapse because two quartic source vectors happen to be equal.

Even the simultaneous ordinary Weyl action does not simply exchange the
affine incidence divisor and itself. Where all coordinates are nonzero,

    d after (z1,z2,z3)->(-1/z1,-1/z2,-1/z3)
      = ((z1+z2)z3-z1 z2)/(z1 z2 z3).

On d=0 its numerator is z1^2+z1 z2+z2^2, generally nonzero. Thus “apply
Fourier and exchange two cells” needs a specified correspondence, not just
this simultaneous group element.
title: 3. Exact H-orbit geometry: what “both cells” does not specify

## 1. Decision

**Accept the component theorems and conditional return, with the observation-norm clarification below.** The literal twisted squarefree Redheffer determinant, prime-cover exponential, all-depth positive-chain exponent, common-filter fixed-color payment, complete Newton remainder and every p-valuation survive independent reconstruction. The author has proved an arithmetic bound for a complete finite collection of chain sectors, including principal characters; the result is more than a change of notation for an unknown norm.

There is no proof of the full signed remainder estimate OPEN-RHCHAIN, no c gain and no improved Mertens exponent. The determinant and conditional return are exact source interfaces. The positive-chain and projected-prime lower prices apply only to their stated positive or projected objects. They do not lower-bound the complete signed determinant or filtered tail. The new source remains an ordinary fixed-character architecture; it does not acquire a native Hecke or Gao-source admission by analogy.

The review adds a modest complete endpoint improvement. For the same common fixed filter, the t=1 color costs O(sqrt x), the t=2 color costs O(sqrt x log^3(2x)), and the entire first J chain sectors cost **O(x^(1-1/J)) for every fixed J>=3**, without an epsilon loss. For J=2 the complete low-chain bound is O(sqrt x log^3(2x)). This follows from the actual Euler correction, not an unproved divisor-problem estimate. The proof is in Section5 and support.md. It changes no target c and does not control the remaining tail.

One sentence needs correction: author line376 calls an unspecified L2 condition stronger than the pointwise sharp-source hypothesis. For the usual multiplicative-shell L2 norm at the same exponent, the implication runs from the pointwise bound to L2. Section7 proves the weaker complete shell-L1 return directly, without changing the sharp source or discarding a complement. The author's actual pointwise implication remains correct; neither version's arithmetic input is proved.

Current source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and gamma11=.8748540364 are unchanged. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain open. Near .1252, 1/6 and 1/4 are conditional targets. Root owns acceptance and integration; this review makes no literature-priority claim.

## 3. Geometry alone cannot improve the supplied upper-budget family

This is a certificate about the combination of S.5 and B0.41,
not an impossibility theorem for the actual arithmetic sums.
Use only geometries for which those estimates and their marked
row counts apply, including their supply and retention conditions.
In particular the endpoint d=h is retained, 0<h<2y, and the
physical restriction ell<=M/2 is satisfied. Losses from buffers
and meshes are nonnegative.

Let b in [.87,b0), kappa=2b-1, h=1+ell-x,
tau=x+y+ell-1, so y=h-2ell+tau. The physical exponent supplied
by S.5, after the square root in the physical bound, is

\[
b_{\rm phys}=\frac{11}{12}-\frac\ell4+\frac\tau{12}
+\max\{0,(1+3\ell-2x-2y)/8,\tau/2\}. \tag{V11}
\]

For kappa in [.74,.75], let delta be the smaller root of

\[
P(\kappa,\delta)=(324\kappa^2-3)\delta^2
+(-756\kappa^2+54\kappa+5)\delta
+300\kappa^2-40\kappa=0. \tag{V12}
\]

It lies in (.46,.48). The identity B0.48 gives
R_kappa(delta,1/2)=5/9+delta/(18kappa).
At this admissible amplitude class, the d=h numerator endpoint
from B0.46 is

\[
F=\frac{1+\delta}{2}-\frac\ell2+\frac{\ell\delta}{2}
+h\left(\frac12+\frac{\delta}{24\kappa}\right)-\frac y2
-\frac{\delta}{24\kappa}\min(h,2y-h).
\]

Since min(h,2y-h)<=2y-h, it follows exactly that

\[
F\ge f(\ell,\kappa)-A_\tau\tau,\quad
f(\ell,\kappa)=\frac{1+\ell}{2}+\frac\delta2
+\frac{\delta\ell}{2}\left(1+\frac1{3\kappa}\right),
\quad A_\tau=\frac12+\frac{\delta}{12\kappa}. \tag{V13}
\]

Equality holds when y<=h<2y. If h<=y, the extra term is
delta(y-h)/(12kappa)>=0. Thus h cannot avoid this necessary
budget. This uses a permitted upper-bound class, not a claim
that actual rows saturate its count.

Put ell_b=4((1-b)-1/12)=(5-6kappa)/3 and
A_ell=(1+delta(1+1/(3kappa)))/2. Dropping only the nonnegative
row branch in (V11), b_phys<=b forces

\[
\ell\ge
\begin{cases}
\ell_b+\tau/3,&\tau\le0,\\
\ell_b+7\tau/3,&\tau\ge0.
\end{cases} \tag{V14}
\]

The coefficients of tau after insertion in (V13) are

\[
\frac{A_\ell}{3}-A_\tau
=-\frac13+\delta\left(\frac16-\frac1{36\kappa}\right)<0,
\quad
\frac{7A_\ell}{3}-A_\tau
=\frac23+\delta\left(\frac76+\frac{11}{36\kappa}\right)>0.
\]

Both signs therefore give F-b>=f(ell_b,kappa)-b.
The best possible necessary budget occurs at tau=0.

Here is an exact rational certificate for the last inequality.
On the displayed kappa/delta rectangle, the functions
P(kappa,.46) and P(kappa,.48) increase with kappa, and

\[
P(.74,.46)=717189/390625>0,\quad
P(.75,.48)=-5577/2500<0.
\]

Elementary interval bounds give

\[
P_\delta\le-245507/1250,\quad
35297/15625\le P_\kappa\le21397/1250.
\]

Thus 0<delta'(kappa)<=21397/245507<1. Differentiating yields

\[
\frac{d}{d\kappa}\left[
f(\ell_b,\kappa)-\frac{1+\kappa}{2}\right]
=-2A_\ell-\frac12
+\frac{\delta'}2\left(1+\ell_b+\frac{\ell_b}{3\kappa}\right)
-\frac{\delta\ell_b}{6\kappa^2}
\le-\frac{25459}{16650}<0. \tag{V15}
\]

For this upper bound use delta>=23/50, kappa<=3/4,
ell_b<=14/75, kappa>=37/50, and delta'<=1.
The accepted baseline equations give f(ell_0,kappa_0)=b0
and ell_b=ell_0 at kappa_0=2b0-1. Hence F>b for every b<b0
in the stated interval. No choice of geometry in this supplied
budget family certifies an improvement, even before restoring
the omitted positive costs.

This closes the wider-geometry loophole left by [private research revision]'s
Gaussian test only when its linear comparator stays in the
domain just specified. It does not exclude new coefficient
estimates, signed cancellation, other detector families, or

### Gram localization is not a vector projection

The three terms in B0.22's nonnegative majorant have square-root exponents
\[
\frac x2,\qquad \frac{y-x}{2},\qquad
\frac x2+\frac{y-x}{12}.
\]
The middle term is smaller than the first for \(y<2x\). This correctly identifies the \(P_a^{1/6}\) term as the sole excess in that majorant.

However the label \(k=r^6\) occurs after expanding pairs of outer columns, with profile argument \(\sqrt Q\,r^6/(ab)\). It is not a fixed additive spectral projection of \(A\). GS §2 states this caveat, but §7 then writes \(A^{(6)}\) without constructing it. Therefore the claimed “sixth-power portion of \(A\) paired with \(B\)” is **not presently a defined mathematical object**. Retain (A14.1), or construct an exact theta-paired bilinear identity/projector and prove its principal calibration before using that language. Positivity of a raw neutral-ray Gram does not refute a theta-specific cancellation estimate; it also does not define such a projection.

The claimed “full deletion permits only a detached window near \(.12937\)” is also too strong. That window is merely the diagnostic obtained by forcing equality \(\sigma=(y-x)/12\) and a particular stationary geometry. A stronger valid estimate may be deliberately weakened; for example the certified \(.1255\) geometry needs only \(\sigma=.0006\), much less than its full excess. The detached saturated-geometry window is not an obstruction to smaller improvements.

statement:
# [private research revision]: the arithmetic content of the optimal f3 spectral core

The [W41 author](wild41/report.md) and [independent review](wild41-review/report.md)
give a source-specific spectral reduction and two exact arithmetic interfaces.
The controller accepts the scopes below after reading both complete arguments.
Written c5=7821/62500=.125136 remains unchanged. Frozen author examples using
c4 or calling .125136 a new target are historical: an improving exponent must
now be strictly below .874864. No new formal-kernel evidence is claimed.

## 1. An optimal finite-rank core still contains the full arithmetic problem

Use the literal source f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))), including all prime powers:
f(p^k)=-1 for p!=3 and f(3^k)=1. For sigma>1/2, the multiplicative Hankel
T(m,n)=f(mn)(mn)^(-sigma) is Hilbert--Schmidt with norm squared zeta(2sigma)^2.
At p!=3 its nonzero local block is

    H_p = [[1,-sqrt(R_p)],[-sqrt(R_p),-R_p]],
    R_p=p^(-2sigma)/(1-p^(-2sigma)).

Write lambda_p^+ for its positive eigenvalue and c_p=1/(lambda_p^++R_p).
Then 0<c_p<1 and 1-c_p=c_p(1+c_p)R_p. The p=3 block is rank one.
Retain p=2,3 exactly and the positive local eigenvector at every p>=5.
The resulting B_sigma is the optimal rank-two truncation in both operator
and Hilbert--Schmidt norm. The proof orders the local singular ratios
r_2>r_5>r_7>... and passes from finite prime-semigroup compressions using
Hilbert--Schmidt convergence. It does not assume a complete infinite tensor
eigenbasis or identify this source with W29's different local blocks.

Its first column is C_sigma b_sigma(n)n^(-sigma), C_sigma>0, where
b_sigma(2^k)=-1, b_sigma(3^k)=1 and b_sigma(p^k)=-c_p for p>=5.
For every fixed rho>1/2 there are exact inverse Dirichlet kernels a,d with

    b_sigma=a*f,  f=d*b_sigma,
    sum_n (|a(n)|+|d(n)|) n^(-rho) < infinity.           ([restricted research revision]-S1)

At p=2,3 both kernels are the identity. At p>=5 their local series are

    A_p(z)=(1-(1+c_p)z)/(1-2z),
    D_p(z)=(1-2z)/(1-(1+c_p)z).

The nonconstant absolute mass is O_(sigma,rho)(p^(-2sigma-rho)); small
prime factors are retained exactly. Consequently the complete Gaussian
fields of b_sigma and f have equivalent all-shell, every-epsilon power
norms for every gamma>1/2. Minkowski pays every shifted shell and both
small-scale tails. This is a transfer for complete fields, not a hereditary
estimate for signed submasks.

For each fixed ordinary character chi, including its ramified zeros,
multiplication of both kernels by chi gives the same equivalence. The
complex twisted operator uses left and right unitary multiplication;
it need not be self-adjoint. If 2 divides the modulus, the optimal retained
core has rank one. The literal Euler numerator W_chi is nonzero in
1/2<Re(s)<1, so the complete Gaussian bound has its own ordinary-character
zero-exclusion return. No ideal, angular or growing-conductor assertion is
inferred from this twist.

The physical readout has norm O(x^(sigma+1/2)). A column approximation
error epsilon_X therefore costs X^(sigma+1/2)epsilon_X. At sigma=3/4,
the current boundary requires epsilon_X=O(X^(-.375136)) before any strict
improvement. A fixed nonzero spectral residual does not decay with X.
The strongest consequence is that treating the optimal leading modes as
an easy main term is unjustified: their actual arithmetic field already
contains the full target exponent through ([restricted research revision]-S1). Signed cancellation
among retained and complementary modes remains a possible research input.

## 2. Exposed prime bits and the remaining full covariance

For a finite prime set P containing 2 and excluding 3, let
Q=product_(p in P)p, a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)), and
r_P(n)=f(n)a_P(n). The actual source is on all integers. Its occupancy
probabilities are 1/p, whereas the squarefree law in W38 uses 1/(p+1).
The zero mean at p=2 is essential.

For every fixed delta>0 and any moving family with Q<=X^(1-delta),
periodic Gaussian Poisson summation gives F_P(x)=O_A(X^-A) on [X,2X]
for every A. It also gives the entire occupancy-pattern law in L1 to
arbitrary power accuracy; summing at most 2^|P|<=Q patterns is paid.
This uses the actual Gaussian measure mu_x(n)=g(log(n/x))/Z(x),
Z(x)=e^(tau/2)x+O_A(x^-A).

The exact remaining identity is

    F(x)=Z(x) Cov_mu_x(a_P,r_P)+F_P(x) E_mu_x[r_P].       ([restricted research revision]-S2)

Thus the complete exponent gamma is equivalent to the all-shell squared
covariance target X^(2gamma-2+epsilon). Every conditional tail mean,
including rare patterns, remains. Exposed-bit independence does not bound
this covariance. Credit [private research revision] S24--29 and Sol D33 for the prior mechanism;
W41 adds the full-pattern L1 statement and explicit normalized covariance
form, not a new finite-prime cancellation discovery.

## 3. Two parked proposals now have precise mathematical contracts

The protected audit20 gives the exact finite-observation criterion:
a functional is bounded by observations E precisely when its representing
vector lies in range(E*); the optimal squared constant is a*G^dagger a.
Regularization must retain its lambda||alpha||^2 cost. An explicit ordinary
Dirichlet polynomial takes value 1 at three sampled points but vanishes at
an unsampled rho in (1/2,1). This is a finite, unrestricted-source diagnostic,
not an actual Möbius counterexample or an obstruction to positive-measure
observation. Source-specific uniform observability and tails remain open.

The uniform audit25 repairs the proposed additive/multiplicative checksum.
Let A be prefix summation and D divisor summation on 1,...,N. Their exact
commutator has entries floor(n/k)-#{d|n:d>=k}. For actual Möbius coefficients,

    q(n)=((AD-DA)mu)(n)=1-sum_(d|n) M(d),
    M(n)=1_(n=1)-sum_(d|n) mu(d) q(n/d).                ([restricted research revision]-S3)

For gamma>0, all-n every-epsilon bounds of exponent gamma for q and M
are equivalent by the divisor bound. Partial summation then supplies the
complete ordinary-zeta zero return. The c5 premise already gives its
baseline; an improvement still needs an actual bound below .874864.
Every column k>N/2 of the finite commutator is zero, so a single finite
checksum cannot recover arbitrary tail coefficients. This makes the
parked seed coherent and identifies its exact limitation; general divisor
inversion and floor-sum identities retain their classical ancestry.

## 4. Preservation and acceptance limits

All [30 initial cards](wild41/initial-cards.md), six first tests, two
development lines and both critic audits are retained. Twenty-two cards
remain untested. The scoped failures concern single-prime-edge transport,
a source-blind two-mode frame and unrenormalized finite Euler reciprocals;
they do not reject their broader families.

The author's complete selection plan/rules were saved before sampling, but
individual exact pool bytes were serialized only after their draws. The
literal all-group memberships and draws check out; this chronology is weaker
than the protocol and is not repaired by rerolling or retrospective claims.
The critic's protected20/uniform25 audit selection was frozen before outcomes.
Independent exact finite checks support bookkeeping. The displayed infinite,
uniform and source-return arguments establish the accepted mathematical scope.

The next substantive input is a complete arithmetic bound for the spectral
field, the full conditional covariance or the actual checksum. Equivalence
can make a representation useful for mix-and-match estimates; it supplies
no exponent gain by itself. The full original29-family/109-child portfolio,
fixed-family endpoint and distinction between analytic and formal evidence
are preserved.

## 3. Exact arithmetic reconstruction of the complete detector

Let h and k be multiplicative sequences given by these local values:

For p=2 or 3:

    h(p^j)=j+1 (j>=0),
    k(1)=1, k(p)=-2, k(p^2)=1, k(p^j)=0 (j>=3).

For p>=5:

    h(1)=1, h(p)=0, h(p^j)=-(j-1) (j>=2),
    k(1)=1, k(p)=0, k(p^j)=2^(j-2) (j>=2).

Here local occurrences of h(1)=k(1)=1 specify the same unit coefficient.
Their Euler products, initially in the common absolute half-plane, are

    H_6(s)=prod_{p|6}(1-p^(-s))^(-2)
           *prod_{p>=5}(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2,
    K_6(s)=prod_{p|6}(1-p^(-s))^2
           *prod_{p>=5}(1-p^(-s))^2/(1-2p^(-s)).       (GC9)

At p>=5 the first nonconstant term has degree two. For every fixed
sigma>1/2, 2p^(-sigma)<1 for all such primes, and the nonconstant
absolute local masses are O_sigma(p^(-2sigma)). Consequently

    H_abs(sigma)=sum_n |h(n)|n^(-sigma)<infinity,
    K_abs(sigma)=sum_n |k(n)|n^(-sigma)<infinity.        (GC10)

More explicitly, their positive local products are

    H_abs(sigma)=prod_{p|6}(1-p^(-sigma))^(-2)
       *prod_{p>=5}[1+p^(-2sigma)/(1-p^(-sigma))^2],
    K_abs(sigma)=prod_{p|6}(1+p^(-sigma))^2
       *prod_{p>=5}[1+p^(-2sigma)/(1-2p^(-sigma))].

These are genuine uniformly-in-height bounds for the two Dirichlet
multipliers, since |H_6(sigma+it)|<=H_abs(sigma) and similarly for K_6.
They require no finite-height exception. Also H_6 K_6=1 throughout
Re s>1/2, by absolute convergence and the local factors.

The exact coefficient identities are

    f_3=h*A,       A=k*f_3.                            (GC11)

They may be checked coefficientwise, without continuation. At p>=5,
the f_3 factor is (1-2z)/(1-z), the A factor is 1-z, and their ratio
is (1-2z)/(1-z)^2. At p=3 the f_3 factor is (1-z)^(-1),
while A has 1-z, giving (1-z)^(-2). At p=2 the f_3 factor is
(1-2z)/(1-z) and A has (1-2z)(1-z), again giving (1-z)^(-2).
Thus the original exceptional prime-two coefficients 1,-3,2,0,...
are recovered exactly; they have not been replaced by ordinary mu.

For any sequence c write (T_c V)(x)=sum_{r>=1}c(r)V(x/r).
Coefficientwise absolute Fubini against the Gaussian gives

    F_tau=T_h G_tau,        G_tau=T_k F_tau.           (GC12)

For example, at a fixed sigma>1, GC10 and sum n^(-sigma)<infinity
bound the absolute double coefficient sum after multiplying by
C_(sigma,tau)x^sigma. This justifies the initial rearrangement for
every x>0. No low-height truncation or product cap is interchanged
with T_h or T_k without an error estimate.

The exclusion of BOTH primes 2 and 3 from the primitive original pair
is deliberate. With only prime 2 excluded, K has a p=3 denominator
1-2*3^(-s), and its absolute series requires sigma>log(2)/log(3).
With neither excluded, p=2 gives the worse threshold sigma>1.
The fixed mask (de,6)=1 removes these finite obstructions and gives
GC10 for the full useful half-plane sigma>1/2. This is an arithmetic
choice of source with its reconstruction paid, not an assumption that
deleting small primes from a signed energy is harmless.

## 5. Uniform sharp-endpoint PNT and the source integral

For retained r and x set y=x/r. The central prime interval is

    y e^(-W)<p<=y e^W.

Its endpoints lie in [X^.98,2X^1.01]. For all sufficiently large X this entire interval is above z throughout F3. Thus the condition p>z is automatic here AFTER the tails were paid. It is not removed in the original source by assertion.

Apply Stieltjes summation to w(v)=g_tau(log(v/y)) on the half-open interval (a,b], with a=ye^(-W),b=ye^W. The exact error is

    R(b)g_tau(W)-R(a)g_tau(-W)
       -integral_a^b R(v)g_tau'(log(v/y))dv/v.

For fixed N, F9 and the positive-power corridor bound this by

    C_(tau,N)y L^(-N)
       [e^Wg_tau(W)+e^(-W)g_tau(-W)
                           +integral_R e^u|g_tau'(u)|du]
                <=C_(tau,N)y L^(-N).                 (F24)

The bracket is uniformly bounded; tau is fixed. Both sharp endpoints remain in the formula, including when an endpoint is prime. Summing1/r over the retained cores with full valuations costs O(t). With N=10 fixed once and for all, F6 has become

    T_z(x)=-x integral_(-W)^W e^u g_tau(u)
           sum_(r<=R_0,r in S(z))
                   [f(r)/r]/(ell+u-log r) du + E_0,   (F25)

where

           +t X^(.7525)+Xt e^(-W^2/(4tau))+Xt L^(-10)]. (F26)
