# [private research revision]: corrected prime pressure and complete arithmetic readouts

Accept the scoped statements below from [W53](wild53/report.md) and its
[independent review](wild53-review/report.md). No arithmetic cancellation
estimate or increase in c is established. Current written c11 is
312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364. The original c10
calibration is preserved in the frozen sources, with the review's c11
addendum. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and
external definition/import/admission remain open. No formalization occurs.

## G119. Anchored one-sided pressure has an exact zero-exclusion return

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q with its natural ramified zeros.
Let delta be1 for principal chi and0 otherwise. For Re s>0 define

    J_y(s)=integral_2^y u^(-s)/log(u) du,
    H_y(s)=delta J_y(s)+sum_(p<=y)log(1-chi(p)p^(-s)),
    Q_y(s)=exp(H_y(s)).

Each logarithm means its fixed local power series, including every prime
power. No unknown prime sum is subtracted in J_y. On Re s>1 the complete
Euler expansion gives Q_y -> exp(delta J_infinity)/L(s,chi). The function

    B(s)=(s-1)exp(J_infinity(s))

extends to an entire nonvanishing function because
B'/B=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1) is entire, including its removable value log2.
Fix the multiplicative constant at one real point>1. The optional series
in the source agrees with [NIST 6.6.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/6.6.E2);
the derivative proof suffices without that formula. The identity to extend is

    (s-1)^delta L(s,chi) Q(s)=B(s)^delta.                 (80.1)

For principal chi the first factor at s=1 is product_(p|q)(1-1/p),
nonzero. Finite imprimitive Euler factors have zeros only at Re s=0.
Thus a holomorphic limit Q satisfying (80.1) excludes all L-zeros in its
domain, while treating the principal pole explicitly.

For0<a<1, suppose for every compact K in Re s>a and every epsilon>0,
eventually for every integer k,

    integral_K (Re H_(2^k)(s))_+ dA <= C_(K,chi,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).
                                                               (LP_a)

This is an area estimate on the complete dyadic sequence. A countable
rectangle exhaustion suffices. The subharmonic area mean inequality
gives local upper bounds on Re H. At one real b>1, the actual logarithms
are uniformly bounded as complex numbers. Borel-Caratheodory in the safe form

    sup_(D(c,R/2))|h| <=3|h(c)|+2 max(0,sup_(D(c,R))Re h)

propagates this anchor through a fixed finite disk chain. Hence H_(2^k)
is locally O(2^(k epsilon)) for every epsilon. Its increments f_k are
O_b(2^(-k(b-1))) on Re s>=b>1 by the integer tail majorant.

Choose overlapping inner/middle/outer disks with radii r,2r,4r inside
Re s>a. Three-circle interpolation propagates a decay exponent d_j by
d_(j+1)=(d_j-epsilon)/2. For N fixed steps, epsilon<d_0/2^(N+1)
makes every resulting exponent positive. Centers at distance<=r let
the previous middle disk cover the next inner disk. Finite covers handle
any compact. Therefore sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly, H_(2^k)
has a holomorphic limit H and Q=exp(H) is nonzero. The identity theorem
extends (80.1). This is an all-height return: every alleged finite-height
zero lies in a suitable compact. Constants may depend on chi and K.

For this exact anchored sequence, LP_a is EQUIVALENT to local uniform
convergence of H_(2^k): the reverse follows from local boundedness. For
a>1/2 the higher-prime-power logarithm converges absolutely, so LP_a is
also equivalent to local convergence of the centered DYADIC prime sum
sum_(p<=2^k)chi(p)p^(-s)-delta J_(2^k)(s). This is not an equivalence
with bare zero exclusion or a claim about every intermediate cutoff.
It refines the one-sided sufficient input without providing cancellation.

A separate global-height hypothesis gives a numerical loss budget. Suppose
a>0,kappa>=0,a+kappa<1, and for every epsilon>0 there are fixed A,C with

    |H_y(a+it)| <= C(1+|t|)^A y^(kappa+epsilon)

for every dyadic y and real t. Apply three-lines to f_k(s)/(s+D)^m,
D>1,m>A, on a<=Re s<=b with b>1. Each finite source is bounded in height;
the denominator pays the horizontal boundary. The resulting exponent is

    E=[(kappa+epsilon)(b-sigma)+(1-b)(sigma-a)]/(b-a).

At epsilon=0 its zero is
r_b=a+kappa+kappa(1-a-kappa)/(kappa+b-1). For each compact to the right
of a+kappa choose finite b large enough, then epsilon small enough.
Geometric convergence and (80.1) return Re s>a+kappa. For kappa=0 the
same argument uses a positive epsilon buffer. A_y growing with cutoff,
or an estimate on finitely many heights, does not meet this contract.

At a=3/4 the current first-gain threshold is
kappa<312135091/2500000000=.1248540364. The conditional choice
kappa=78/625 returns c=.1252, gain135091/2500000000 over c11.
Choices (a,kappa)=(3/4,1/12) and (2/3,1/12) return1/6 and1/4.
All these inputs remain open. The actual direct bound is y^(1-a),
giving a+kappa=1. Synthetic h_k=sum_(j<=k)2^(j(a+kappa-s))/j shows
the strict abstract boundary cannot improve for free: its exponential
limit has a pole at a+kappa. This model is not an arithmetic L-source.

## G120. Complete phase blocks and thermal readout prices

For NONPRINCIPAL chi, partition every unramified prime into disjoint
finite blocks B and an unmatched set U. Suppose fixed m,C satisfy
|B|<=m, r_B=min B, diameter B<=C r_B^(1-eta), exact sum_B chi(p)=0,
eta>0, and U(x)<=C x^delta_U. Every exception belongs to U. For
sigma0>gamma_B=max(1/2,1-eta,delta_U),

    |sum_B chi(p)p^(-s)| <=m C |s| r_B^(-sigma0-eta).

This follows from the derivative of u^(-s) and exact phase balance.
Distinct blocks have distinct integer anchors. Their singleton sum,
all higher powers and the full unmatched logarithm converge normally.
Exponentiation and initial Euler agreement return zero exclusion
Re s>gamma_B. The omitted anchor-Y tails are respectively
O_K(Y^(1-sigma0-eta)), O_K(Y^(1-2sigma0)), O_K(Y^(delta_U-sigma0)).
No selected or unpaired prime is omitted.

For0<eta<=1 an incomplete block crossing x has anchor in
(x-Cx^(1-eta),x]. Counting these anchors gives the actual natural-cutoff
prime discrepancy O_chi(x^(1-eta)+x^delta_U+1). The difference between
anchor and natural Euler cutoffs is O_K(Y^(1-eta-sigma0)+Y^(-sigma0)).
Thus this is a structural sufficient condition for the classical prime
discrepancy route, not a separate obtained saving. Principal unramified
phases are all1, so no nonempty balanced block exists; the entire prime
set as unmatched has exponent1. A separate principal input is mandatory.
Current first gain requires eta>c11 and delta_U<theta11, with common
exponents across the covered characters. Approximate balance incurs an
additional complete block-residual sum. Its price is not zero.

The protected23 audit constructs the precise finite thermal object. On
two-state unramified sites let N_p=diag(0,1), K_y=sum_p(log p)N_p,
Z_y^+(sigma)=product_p(1+p^(-sigma)), rho_y=exp(-sigma K_y)/Z_y^+,
and U_(chi,t)=tensor_p diag(1,-chi(p)p^(-it)). Then

    P_y(s)=Z_y^+(sigma) Tr(rho_y U_(chi,t)),
    Q_y(s)=exp(delta J_y(s))Z_y^+(sigma) Tr(rho_y U_(chi,t)).

rho_y is positive with trace1, U is unitary and distinct-site correlations
factor exactly. Trace cyclicity proves the finite Gibbs/KMS identity.
These facts do not control the extensive parity readout. Positivity only
bounds its magnitude by1 and leaves the full Z_y^+ and principal vacuum.
The exact LP integrand is the positive part of
delta Re J_y+log Z_y^++log|Tr(rho_y U)|. A useful mixing theorem must
bound that complete expression. Analyticity comes from the exact source,
not a separate claim that rho_y depends holomorphically on s.

For the normalized signed functional on the finite supremum-norm algebra,

    ell_y(F)=P_y(s)^(-1) sum_(n|product P)mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s)F(n),
    ||ell_y||=Z_y^+(sigma)/|P_y(s)|.

At principal real0<sigma<=1, log||ell_y||>=2 sum_(p<=y,p not|q)p^(-sigma)
tends to infinity. The occupied one-site expectation is negative.
Compatible ell_y therefore cannot extend boundedly to the supremum-norm
completion of the infinite cylinder algebra. A scalar vacuum multiplier
does not change this normalized functional. This is a specified norm
obstruction; different norms, full parity estimates and signed arithmetic
projections remain eligible. It neither lower-bounds M_chi nor refutes LP.

## G121. Exact threshold rank and the complete signed rectangle return

At integer N partition ALL unramified primes<=N into disjoint L,R.
List squarefree L-products u_i<=N and R-products v_j<=N increasingly,
including1. Put T_ij=1_(u_i v_j<=N), alpha_i=mu(u_i)chi(u_i) and
beta_j=mu(v_j)chi(v_j). Unique factorization gives

    M_chi(N)=alpha^T T beta.                              (80.2)

Ramified sites are zero rows/columns, not inverted factors. All retained
phases have modulus1; diagonal multiplication preserves matrix rank and
singular values while the final scalar may still cancel.

Let t_i be the row's prefix length, and0<h_1<...<h_d its distinct positive
values, h_0=0. The exact decomposition is

    T=sum_(ell=1)^d 1_(t_i>=h_ell) 1_(h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell).

Choosing one row of each length h_i and columns h_j gives the triangular
submatrix L_d=(1_(j<=i)), determinant1. Thus rank T=d. Each length is
a function of floor(N/u_i), giving d<=2 floor(sqrt N). This is an
O(sqrt N) representation, not a polylogarithmic rank or cancellation bound.

L_d^(-1)=I minus a truncated shift has operator norm<=2. Restrict any
rank-r approximation T_r, r<d, to this submatrix and use an orthonormal
basis of its kernel, dimension at least d-r. Every vector has error norm
at least1/2. Hence ||T-T_r||_F^2>=(d-r)/4 and ||T-T_r||_op>=1/2.
Restriction is a contraction for either norm; the same result holds for
the character-weighted tensor. No rank-growth assumption is needed.

If R_N,C_N are the row and column counts, the COMPLETE scalar error is
alpha^T(T-T_r)beta, bounded above by sqrt(R_N C_N)||T-T_r||_op, or
the same factor times the Frobenius norm. Leakage outside uv<=N is part
of this error. The matrix lower bounds are not lower bounds on its signed
scalar contraction. A norm budget tending to zero forces r>=d; no claim
that every prime partition has such a budget or large rank is made.

Contracting the exact decomposition gives

    M_chi(N)=sum_ell [sum_(i:t_i>=h_ell)alpha_i]
                       [sum_(h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell)beta_j].

Every prime restriction and endpoint is explicit. A selection of rectangles
must bound both its full signed contribution and the entire omitted signed
sum by N^(gamma+epsilon), for all large N/every epsilon/every fixed chi
and common gamma<theta11. Moving partitions need uniform bounds in their
actual choice. Then s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx continues
1/L to Re s>gamma, giving ordinary all-height zero exclusion. This uses
the full source, not analytic continuation of the moving tensors.

## Evidence, ancestry and next estimates



Root read both complete reports, both mathematical helpers, sampling code,
all seed cards and relevant source contracts. Independent exact checks
cover three saved draws, four disk chains, three strip budgets, every
finite prime prefix through43, three Gibbs cases and nine complete
cutoff tensors. These are finite algebra evidence, not proofs of LP/P/PB
or any new arithmetic cancellation. No unchanged helper was rerun.

W33/W36 own singleton pressure and the explicit vacuum/prime-discrepancy
ancestry; [restricted research revision] owns the compact nonvanishing Mellin kernel; G105 owns
floor-state compression; G108's cutoff Mobius block source is different
from the Euler logarithm here. The topological first test retains the
weighted commutator and inherited unsigned Betti cost from
[Bjorner's original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704), not a new
topological no-go. Schur rank-one and symmetric finite-outlier tests
are synthetic restricted counterexamples, not L-function examples.

Next decisive work is an actual corrected-pressure, full parity,
prime-block/discrepancy or signed rectangle estimate meeting the complete
current threshold. These are alternative arithmetic targets with exact
returns; none is promoted by favorable finite examples or model agreement.

## 1. Frozen exploration, source contact and six tests

`seeds.md` contains all 30 cards and original p labels, frozen and fully read back before detailed history. SHA256 d336e16f016813388887c843e1a3aaeded8675094b08ddf2b160251edb2c8120. The problem and immutable recipe hashes match the assignment. Six selections, in order: **01,02,04,26,28,16**. The protected bridges were 01/02; the sequential literal-threshold draws were 04 (p<.10), 26 (p<.01), then most-different 28, wildcard 16. Every eligible card from every group entered its literal stratum. Pools were frozen before draws, with no reroll. `selection-results.json` SHA256 dd6b40a8c2e428b5791e825611c5fac2cf16a5b36d71c6ead3da103f7f45d5d8. Root received both freezes before outcomes.

Afterward I used the maintained 29-family/109-child navigation and the early/late/[private research revision]/[private research revision] source pointers, current proof, [private research revision] integration, PR9's actual paper B0.35--36/B0.62, the ordinary ideal dictionary, W35's calibrated Gram identity, W31's free quotient, and W40's actual prime-projection audit. No claim is made to have reread every historical proof. Relevant ancestors are F01/F09/F11/F16, N28, U-FILTRATION, W31 R31.30, W35 T1/T3 and current G28--30. The claimed delta is the literal PR9 Euler correction and its priced prime tail, not general convolution/Gram theory or literature priority.

**T01, two-witness convex duality.** Let Gamma be a positive definite 2x2 Hermitian Gram and v a nonzero required complex signal vector. The least quadratic cost among w with v* w=1 is 1/(v* Gamma^-1 v), by weighted Cauchy--Schwarz; the optimizer is Gamma^-1 v/(v* Gamma^-1 v). For a singular positive semidefinite Gram, a nonzero component of v in ker(Gamma) permits a zero-cost feasible vector. Otherwise v lies in its range and the same formula uses the Moore--Penrose inverse. The case v=0 is infeasible. For two copies of one reciprocal L-function the pole residues are proportional to their multiplier values, so v is not an independent two-zero constraint. This is useful bookkeeping with F09/F11 ancestry, not an estimate. D02 identifies the actual multiplier.

**T02, paid transfer.** The direct source calculation is D02 below. It passes: neither a kernel replacement nor the source's qualitative |H_eta-1|<=1/2 statement is used as a substitute for a coefficient norm. The full physical J_eta-f_eta comparison remains outside this transfer.

**T04, prime-power quotient.** This card's phrase 'prime powers' includes primes. For actual rational f3, the prime-power field equals minus the smoothed prime sum, apart from the prime 3 and a higher-power O(X^(1/2+epsilon)) term. By the prime number theorem and fixed Gaussian integration, the field is asymptotic to -exp(tau/2)x/log x, uniformly for x in [X,2X]. The inherited F3=O(X^beta), beta<1, then forces the complementary field to have the opposite leading term. Erasing that source is not a power-small error; the cross term is essential. This is a scoped actual-source failure, consistent with existing rough/mixed-opposition results. Erasing only powers of degree at least two costs O(X^(1/2+epsilon)) but leaves primes and the hard signed energy. No claim about an arbitrary prime-power orthogonal projection follows from this support calculation.

**T26, prime-factor conditional coupling.** W40's exact four-label Gaussian weights (1,2,2,1) at p=2,q=5 give covariance -1/12 and correlation -1/3: independent prime revelation is not legitimate. Rather than assume that drift vanishes, D26 uses the exact deterministic local factors of the old/new transfer and pays every unrevealed prime. This is a specified constructive repair of the seed's coupling premise, not a stochastic independence theorem.

**T28, free-product shadow.** In degree j the word-to-commutative quotient has norm sqrt(j!), and actual Möbius signs are constant on each j!-word fiber. W31 R31.30 already proves this exact test; at j=2 the two words pq/qp have equal signs and reinforce. No hidden cancellation is created by the free model. This duplicate failure stops the naive transfer; arithmetic estimates for the actual symmetric lift remain open.

**T16, two-detector susceptibility.** For actual shell fields U,V, put E0=||U||^2, E1=||V||^2 and C=<U,V>, with <U,V>=integral U conjugate(V). If E1>0,

    ||U-lambda V||^2 = E0-|C|^2/E1 + E1 |lambda-C/E1|^2.       (T16)

Both terms must be paid. A shellwise optimizer can change with X and does not itself define a fixed zero detector. For the source-normalized D02 pair take U=M_eta,2 and V=C_S^-1 exp(-25/36)P_eta(exp(5/3)x), so V has Mellin transform h(s) times that of U. Their combined multiplier is 1-lambda h(s): choosing lambda=1/h(rho) annihilates a simple pole at the proposed zero rho. An unconstrained energy optimizer can therefore destroy the signal. Fixed coefficients with a nonzero multiplier at rho retain the ordinary Mellin return, but their full signed cross energy is open. This adds a source-specific warning to the inherited W35 identity, not a third substantive development or a no-go theorem for simultaneous use.

## 4. Full row conductor and a general summation lemma

For fixed coprime cores put `eta_(c,e)=vartheta_c bar(vartheta_e)`.
The complete unit sum annihilates the row series unless this character
is trivial on the six units. Otherwise
\[
\sum_{k\ne0}\eta_{c,e}(k)q_k^{-z}
=6L_{\mathbb K}(z,\eta_{c,e}),\qquad \Re z>1.
\tag{DC11}
\]
Its primitive good conductor is `ce`, as established in
[review [private research revision], section 1](../review-cycle-9.md).
Because `(c,e)=1` and both are nonunit, it is nonprincipal. The row
function is the full Hecke function, including all fixed-prime row
Euler factors and natural zeros at the good conductor primes.

Let `R=Phi_hat` be the original radial Schwartz row profile, written
as a function of the norm variable, and
`R_tilde(z)=integral_0^infty R(v)v^(z-1)dv`. The single original
row Mellin inversion is
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\le C,*}=\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(\rho)}
\widetilde R(z)K^z
\sum_{\substack{1<q_c\le C,\ e>1\\
c,e\ {\rm sf},\ (c,e)=1\\
\eta_{c,e}|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}
L_{\mathbb K}(z,\eta_{c,e})T_{c,e}(z)\,dz,
\qquad \rho>1.
\tag{DC12}
\]
Initial exchanges are absolute. Shift only this row line to a fixed
positive `sigma`. There is no principal residue, and the contour does
not cross zero. The two rapid envelopes in (DC10) provide normal
convergence and absorb polynomial conductor growth throughout the
fixed strip. The row Mellin transform absorbs every polynomial height
cost. The original common profile and its Mellin roots are unchanged.

Suppose the available bound on the destination line is
\[
|L_{\mathbb K}(\sigma+it,\eta_{c,e})|
\ll(q_cq_e)^{h+\epsilon}(1+|t|)^A,\qquad h\ge0.
\]
Then the precise summation lemma is
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{\le C,*}|
\ll K^\sigma D^{4/3+h+\epsilon}C^{2/3+h}.
}
\tag{DC13}
\]
Indeed, since `|beta(c)beta(e)|=1`, the core sums in (DC10) cost
\[
\sum_{q_c\le C}q_c^{h-1/3+\epsilon}
\ll C^{h+2/3+\epsilon},\qquad
\sum_e q_e^{h-2/3+\epsilon}E_N(q_e/D)
\ll D^{h+1/3+\epsilon}.
\]
The second sum includes all `q_e>D`: its dyadic tail is a convergent
geometric sum once `N>h+1/3+epsilon`. Swapping the columns handles
the unrestricted `q_c>D` tail in the reverse orientation.

To cover `min(q_c,q_e)<=C`, split it disjointly into `q_c<=C` and
`q_c>C,q_e<=C`. The estimate applies to both, because the extra
core restriction can be dropped after absolute core summation.
This pays both ordered mixed terms without invoking positivity or
replacing them by diagonal squares. No cube-dependent mask is added.

# [private research revision]: the quartic boundary object is partly defined

The frozen [author](quartic-boundary/report.md) and independent
[review](quartic-boundary-review/report.md) establish useful local geometry
and source calculations. Full controller reads accept the stated scopes.
They do not construct the coupled boundary matrix or improve c6=.125139.
Their c5=.125136 numbers remain historical benchmarks.

## [restricted research revision]-Q1: nine strata, their normal spaces and a nonsimple boundary

For H={(n(x)a(t),n(y)a(t),n(x+y)a(t))} acting on (P1)^3 in characteristic
different from2, the finite chart has d=z3-z1-z2 transforming to t^2 d.
There is one geometric open orbit d!=0, one d=0 orbit, three single-infinity
orbits, three double-infinity curves and the all-infinity point. The review
gives every stabilizer. Normal weights are +2 at d=0, -2 at each
single-infinity orbit, (-2,-2) at each curve and (-2,-2,-2) at the point.
Unipotents act trivially on these first-order quotients, not necessarily
on higher jets. The open stabilizer is mu2; source fibers still carry its
central-character condition.

Odd nonarchimedean local fields have four open square classes, hence12
rational orbits; finite fields of odd order have10. Replacing H(F) by the
F-points of its effective algebraic quotient would erase real information.
The eight product Bruhat charts do not form the H-orbit decomposition.

There are four boundary divisors: three coordinate infinities and
D0: Z3 W1 W2-Z1 W2 W3-Z2 W1 W3=0. Three divisors meet at each boundary
curve in a two-dimensional normal space. At the deepest point D0 has
equation w1w2-w1w3-w2w3=0, an ordinary quadratic-cone singularity. The
boundary is not simple normal crossings. Counting strata or divisors
does not supply a basis of equivariant germs or justify a matrix size.

The group is nonunimodular: left Haar measure is dx dy d*t/|t|^4,
with modular function |t|^-4. The open orbit has invariant measure
dz1 dz2 dd/|d|^3; G^3/H does not acquire an invariant measure thereby.
Source fibers, Mellin character, density and specialization must be fixed
before converting normal weights to a spectral exponent.

## [restricted research revision]-Q2: actual source constants and a conditional local functional

Pinned primary zero-frequency formulas give, for the literal pair
f=(V theta_i1,-V theta_i2), constants at infinity,0,eta respectively
(C,0),(2C,0),(0,-2C), multiplied by v^(3/4), where
C=pi Res_(w=1)zeta_lambda(w)/zeta_lambda(2). Each ray uses its own
seed-dependent linear combination in BOTH quartic slots. Cross terms
remain; no nonzero combination in this two-dimensional seed span is
cuspidal at both specified finite cusps.

This is not a proof of an uncancelled final relative boundary: the full
U' average forces nu1=nu2=-nu3, and the odd unary theta has no zero
coefficient. A cusp constant and a relative asymptotic germ are different
functionals. The global24-cusp equation is not a good-prime2x2 matrix.

With the author's explicitly compatible metaplectic sections, its concrete
trilinear integral Lambda_s,chi has covariance

    Lambda(T_delta(b)v)=|b|^(5/2-s) chi(b)^-1 Lambda(v).

The Weil scalar gamma_q(x) is essential. The identity-ray normalization
produces B_(2j)=(chi2(p)Q)^j and B_(2j+1)=-(chi2(p)Q)^j on the stated
good congruence ray. These algebraic calculations are accepted. Binding
the torus lifts, bad places and odd archimedean character to one actual
adelic source remains open; no multiplicity-one assumption supplies it.

## [restricted research revision]-Q3: a finite-to-Hilbert limit exposes the missing uniform bound

Finite radial Schwartz vectors E(a_(u,2J)) are Fourier-fixed and have both
value and integral zero. Their literal identity readout is

    J_s(Ea_(u,2J))=(1-z) sum_(j=0)^(J-1)(Au z^2)^j,
    A=chi2(p)Q, z=Q^-s.

Their Hilbert limits yield (1-z)/(1-Au z^2) for Re(s)>1/2. These functions
have nonzero residues (1-Q^-s0)/(2log Q) on Re(s0)=1/2. At u=1 the limit
vector is1_O even though every finite vector vanishes at the origin:
point evaluation is not L2-continuous. Finite-stage cancellation therefore
does not prove uniform cancellation of the limiting boundary. This is a
statement about the defined Mellin readout, not the still-undefined H germ.

Distinct phases have disjoint pole sets. Finite scalar combinations cannot
retain the constant coefficient1 and remove all phase poles. Positive
continuous scalar averaging does so only with Haar phase measure. This
does not prohibit a retained vector with a moving auxiliary numerator.

The exact Hilbert distance squared at phases +/-1 is
4q(2+q)/(1+q)^2, q=Q^-2; its readout difference divided by the Hilbert norm
of the vector difference has order Q^(2-2sigma). This is a lower cost on this local family only,
not a global impossibility theorem. At the CURRENT sigma=.874861 its
exponent is .250278; the frozen review's .250272 belongs to c5.

## What remains to be constructed

Fix the local modules, torus lifts and density before exceptional
specialization. Construct actual restriction/asymptotic maps on all four
divisors with their intersections or a justified resolution. Transport the
chosen Whittaker functionals through the relevant source intertwiners.
Evaluate on finite E(a_(u,2J)) and its phase derivative with uniform J and
phase bounds. Only a proved quotient may reduce the boundary space.

A first current gain still requires a complete same-source signed vector
norm exponent a<.874861 with every ray correction, cross term, tail and
bad-place complement paid. The physical relative field carries X^-5/2,
so its corresponding exponent is a-5/2. Common phase must survive until
vector zero return. For this Q(i) source the return controls zeta_Q(i),
hence ordinary zeta; the larger Hecke scope needs its own construction.

This removes a vague two-germ starting point and supplies a precise next
definition task. It supplies no new arithmetic bound. Six stream failures
were reconciled with the same reviewer and frozen work; release/handoff
completed without rewriting the saved mathematics or resetting deadlines.

## G219. Actual principal channels and the cheapest generic price

Use the fixed primary representatives and symbol of
[[restricted research revision] G212-G214](../[private research revision]/sieve-layer-integration.md). On all good ideals,
with original zero extension,

    chi_a(f)^4 chi_a(f^2 e^6)=1_((a,fe)=1).                (219.1)

At a shared prime the left side remains zero; on coprime inputs its total
symbol exponent is divisible by6. Global primary multiplicativity keeps
the unit. This is not an arbitrary insertion of labels into an old source.

For X=Z^N,F=Z^V,E=Z^R form the genuinely NEW coefficient family

    T_fk(x)=X^-1/2 sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)
                  chi_a(k)chi_a(f)^4 g(log(q_a/x)).       (219.2)

The non-character coefficients/profile are independent of f,k. They are
not canonical Gauss coefficients, the old physical numerator, or a PR26
source. On k=f^2e^6, T_fk=X^-1/2 U_rad(fe). For fixed f the map e->k is
injective, q_k<=4F^2E^6, and the selected PAIR count is exactly N_F N_E.
Thus, with M=2V+6R,

    B_FE=(N_F N_E)^(-1)sum_(f,e)||U_rad(fe)||_2^2,
    J=F^-1 sum_f sum_(q_k<=4Z^M)||T_fk||_2^2,
    B_FE <= C_S X E^-1 J.                               (219.3)

There is no extra division by F or by the full row count. All row
repetitions remain. Gaussian annuli have polynomial derivative factors
times exp(-c j^2); all length prices grow at most exponentially in|j|.

Conditional on [restricted research revision]'s NAMED sixth-order and squarefree cubic sieve inputs,

    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M){(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)},

PRICE N+Emix-R>=2N+V/6. It cannot certify gamma<1.

    Emix(2V+6R,N,V)-R
      =sup_(0<=t<=2V+6R){(2V-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)}.       (219.5)

Only the domain grows with R, so extra e repetitions cannot improve this
recovered certificate. The f-only detector legitimately uses e=1, M=2V,

    Emix(2v,1,v)=1+v/6           for0<=v<=1/3,
                 5/6+2v/3       for1/3<=v<=1/2,
                 1/3+5v/3       for1/2<=v<=1,
                 2v            forv>=1.                (219.6)

For v<=1/2, L=1-v: the only extra maximum is t=v with value1+v/6;
compare it with the endpoint C(2v,1). Their crossing is v=1/3. For

|1/6|5/3|37/18|7/18|

## 1. Statement and exact sector

Write M for [the merged manuscript](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md).
Use its original common column profile `W0`, smooth with all required
Euler derivatives rapidly decreasing at both endpoints, and its original
smooth radial Schwartz row profile `R = Phi_hat`, viewed as a function
of the norm variable. Indices for columns are good primary ideals, one
generator per ideal, and `q_a = Na`. Rows include all nonzero Eisenstein
elements, their six units, and all fixed-prime valuations. Fixed finite
ray/deletion refinements are discussed in section 5.

Let `Q_{1,*}` be the ordered part of M (2.15) with first squarefree core
one and second squarefree core `e > 1`; let `Q_{*,1}` be the reverse
orientation. For `D,K >= 1`, every fixed `0 < delta < 1`, and every
`epsilon > 0`, the theorem is
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|+|\mathfrak Q_{*,1}|
\ll_{\delta,\epsilon}
K^\delta D^{11/6-\delta/2+\epsilon}.
}
\tag{UC1}
\]
Consequently, for any fixed `B0 > 0`,
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|+|\mathfrak Q_{*,1}|
\ll_{\epsilon,B_0}D^{11/6+\epsilon},
\qquad 1\le K\le D^{B_0}.
}
\tag{UC2}
\]
Constants may depend on the original fixed profiles, the specified
finite number of Euler-derivative seminorms, fixed strip margins, and
the required fixed finite ray/deletion family. No uniformity for
arbitrary moving angular types or additional moving row masks is claimed.

M (2.14) gives
\[
\mathcal C_k(cB^3)=\beta(c)\vartheta_c(k)\xi(B)q_B,
\qquad \xi=\overline\alpha^{\,3},\qquad |\beta(c)|=1.
\]
M (2.8) establishes that there is no additional `1_{(B,k)=1}`.
Therefore the exact sector is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak Q_{1,*}
=\sum_{\substack{e>1\\e\ {\rm sf}}}\overline{\beta(e)}
\sum_{\substack{B,E\\(B,E)=1\\(B,e)=1}}
&\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}q_Bq_E
 \overline{W_0(q_B^3/D)}W_0(q_eq_E^3/D)\\
&\times\sum_{k\ne0}\overline{\vartheta_e(k)}
 R\!\left(\frac{q_k}
 {K(q_B^3/D)(q_eq_E^3/D)}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC3}
\]
The exact total-column coprimality is `(B,E)=(B,e)=1`.
The own-column overlap `(e,E)>1` remains allowed. Natural row zeros at
primes dividing `e` remain inside `vartheta_e`.

statement:
### Test22: parabolic frequency cells have no free curvature return

For a fixed original prime pair and physical indices, the JN7 additive
phase is

    -R h/(pi*pi') - P s/pi + P' s'/pi',                     (26)

inside the original additive character. As a function of real frequency
coordinates h,s,s', its Hessian is ZERO. It is bilinear when physical
and frequency variables move jointly; no assertion of a zero joint
Hessian is made. Curvature in inverse prime locations would be a different
source-dependent problem, retaining all moving weights and sharp masks.

At the largest denominators the exact adjacent row frequencies h and
h+1 differ by1/(pi*pi'), of absolute value Q^(-1/2), asymptotic to1/N.
Adjacent mark frequencies differ by1/pi or1/pi', of size N^(-1/2).
These are the native lattice spacings. A proposed parabolic cell does
not increase them; any useful separation still has to be shown for its
actual coefficient-bearing subset and priced complement.

Thus parabolic cells in just these frequency coordinates do not get a
stationary-phase saving from a nonexistent quadratic term. More decisively,
the accepted JN12 bound applies to the exact recombined native tensor:
for every row-frequency set E of cardinality J, independent of the two
mark coordinates,

    ||1_E(h) W_hat||_2^2 <= C_orig K J/Q ||W_hat||_2^2.       (27)

This follows from original row support O(K), row Cauchy and all three
unitary finite transforms. It preserves both projectors and all signed
short-core terms. A proposed O(N)-frequency curved packet captures at
most O(K/N)=O(Z^(-.003)) of squared norm at the hard box. Capturing a
fixed norm fraction requires J of order at least Q/K, regardless of
the shape of the cell. This is the previously proved JN obstruction,
reused instead of reproved as a new result.

It does not lower-bound H, rule out adaptive sets depending on marks, or
preclude signed cancellation in the omitted pairing. The complete far
complement remains exactly that signed omitted form. The wildcard path
therefore fails in its proposed frequency-curvature/norm-capture form;
no reroll or replacement test was performed.
title: Test22: parabolic frequency cells have no free curvature return

statement:
### 5.1 From large dyadic shells to all positive scales

Suppose alpha>0, H is locally square-integrable, and

    D_H(2^j) <= C 2^(j alpha)

for all sufficiently large integers j. This does not by itself
control the left tail. Assume additionally that for each fixed N>0,

    |H(x)| <= C_N x^N,                  0<x<=1.          (5.3)

Then ||H||_{D_alpha}<infinity. To see this, first absorb the finite
number of intermediate shells by local square integrability. If
2^j<=T<2^(j+1), the shell [T,2T] lies in the union of the two
dyadic shells starting at 2^j and 2^(j+1). Hence, for T>=1,

    D_H(T)^2 <= C^2(2^(2j alpha)+2^(2(j+1)alpha))
             <= C^2(1+2^(2alpha)) T^(2alpha).             (5.4)

For T<=1/2 choose N>=alpha in (5.3) and integrate x^(2N)
over [T,2T]. This gives D_H(T)<<T^N<<T^alpha. Compact scales
1/2<T<1 cause no problem. This proves the claim and accounts for
both non-dyadic shifts and the entire left tail.
title: 5.1 From large dyadic shells to all positive scales

statement:
### Uniform arithmetic supply

For half-bandwidth h≥1, choose distinct primes p_r>h, p_r∤q, for each
0<|r|≤h. Impose

\[
n\equiv1\pmod q,\quad n\equiv-r\pmod{p_r^2},\quad
Q=q\prod_r p_r^2.
\]

The residue a_0 modulo Q is coprime to Q. Every shifted neighbor n+r is
squareful. For any coprime residue modulo any Q, square-divisor expansion
gives the explicit uniform estimate, N≥4,

\[
\#\{n\le N:n\equiv a_0\pmod Q,\ \mu(n)^2=1\}
=\frac NQ\prod_{p\nmid Q}(1-p^{-2})+R,\qquad
|R|\le3\sqrt N.                                       \tag{96.4}
\]

There are at most √N counting errors, each at most1, for d²|n with
(d,Q)=1. The omitted Euler tail contributes at most2√N/Q. The product is
at least1/ζ(2)>1/2. Deleting at most2h endpoint indices produces

\[
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N-2h).                        \tag{96.5}
\]

No prime theorem in progressions is used. The elementary central-binomial
bounds 4^m/(2m+1)≤binom(2m,m)≤(2m)^{π(2m)} supply π(x)≫x/log x:
each prime contributes at most2m to that factorization. Thus the required
2h primes can lie below C_q h log(2h), and

\[
\log Q\le\log q+4h\log(C_qh\log(2h)).                 \tag{96.6}
\]

For h=o(log N/loglog N), (96.3)–(96.6) force root cost N^{1−o(1)}.
For h=⌊κ log N/loglog N⌋ with fixed0<κ<1/8, they give
sqrt(a*Pa)≥N^{1−4κ−o(1)}. The upper restriction ensures the main term in
(96.5) dominates √N. Fixed h gives K≫_{q,h}N.

More generally let D_N be a symmetric set of permitted nonzero offsets,
all of absolute value at most N−1, and let k=|D_N|. Assign each r a
distinct prime not dividing qr. At any assignment at most
k−1+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋ primes are forbidden, so the first
J=k+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋+1 primes suffice. Their sizes are O(J log(2J)). The same
CRT construction gives

\[
\log Q\le\log q+2k\log(CJ\log(2J)),\qquad
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N).                           \tag{96.7}
\]

Neighbors outside the cutoff are irrelevant; no endpoint deletion is
needed. Hence k=o(log N/loglog N) also forces root cost N^{1−o(1)}, and
k∼κ log N/loglog N,0<κ<1/4, gives N^{1−2κ−o(1)}. Offsets may be large,
move with N, or be chosen after seeing the source. Crucially k counts
the **total union of offsets**, including both signs. Bounded row degree
with many distinct offsets is not covered; neither are general prime
dilation graphs merely because their rows are sparse.

For a target root exponent γ, the necessary thresholds are κ≥(1−γ)/4
for half-bandwidth and κ≥(1−γ)/2 for the offset union:

| Target | Half-bandwidth coefficient | Total-offset coefficient |
|---|---:|---:|
| Strict improvement over c11 | >.0312864909 | >.0625729818 |
| c=.1252 | ≥.0313 | ≥.0626 |
| c=1/6 | ≥1/24 | ≥1/12 |
| c=1/4 | ≥1/16 | ≥1/8 |

These are necessary widths, not sufficient savings or claims at an
unresolved equality threshold. q stays fixed.
title: Uniform arithmetic supply

### B. Finitely many original degree layers cannot repair it

Remove all original terms with k(n)<=r, where r is fixed, before the affine substitution. The remaining polynomial is

    P^(>r)(z)=sum_(n in D_X,k(n)>r)(lambda+rho z)^k(n)         (B4)

for principal chi. Fix k=r+1. Products of k distinct unramified primes in ((X/2)^(1/k),X^(1/k)] lie in (X/2,X] and are distinct. PNT gives at least c_k X/(log X)^k such products for all large X. Each contributes the same degree-k polynomial, with nonnegative coefficients summing to1. Its coefficient l2 norm is at least1/sqrt(k+1). Other layers only increase every coefficient. Hence, uniformly over every retention schedule,

    ||P^(>r)(e^(it))||_2 >>_(q,r) X/(log X)^(r+1).            (B5)

This rejects finite original-layer subtraction as a repair of the positive circle norm. It does not cover exact deflation with signed quotient coefficients, growing r, or a full signed combination of the retained and removed layers. In particular it does not refute G106's actual root/quotient return. The selected fixed-k layer is used only to lower-bound a nonnegative coefficient norm, never the signed arithmetic sum.

## 6. Independent checks and reproducibility

The review was divided into cubic/completion/source, sextic/full-field, detector/geometry, and full-portfolio tasks, with cross-checks across those divisions. New T06–T07 algebra, actual prime-mark accounting, moving embeddings and endpoint allocation received an independent second read. T08's new corridor, full-profile summation and T10's continuum criterion also received an independent second read. Root checked the new auxiliary identities and the final cross-track consequences. This is a record of the work performed, not a substitute for the proofs supplied in documents 01–02.

The small checks directory is deliberately limited to reproducible finite evidence:

| File | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
|---|---|---|
| cubic_checks.py and cubic_exact_checks.json | 512 three-prime valuation tuples, 1,000 cube incidences including 784 shared-prime cases; eight exact mask-density identities; rational Type I and transfer budgets | An analytic mean or uniform cancellation |
| grok_transfer_certificate.py and grok_transfer_certificate_result.txt | Corrected outward interval certificate for all five conditional targets, including the global amplitude rectangle and other geometric margins | The full-probe hypothesis |
| inherited_H_geometry.py | Unchanged supplied exact certificate for the saved .12551 H geometry; used to check the new T07 tail exponents | A new [private research revision] result or a proof of H |
| verify_cycle20.py and verification_receipt.json | Exact new rational identities, finite counterexamples, corridor/exponent bookkeeping, all proof/family IDs, source and bundle consistency | Validation of inherited or new infinite analytic theorems by numerical testing |
| input_file_map.tsv, baseline_file_map.tsv, portfolio_source_crosswalk.json, claim_registry.json | Full input disposition, semantic aliases, stable claims and family/child coverage | Independent truth from agreement or metadata |

Run the scripts with Python 3; they use the standard library. The full interval certificate is the longest check. Its recorded output is the independently rerun corrected version. Small exact verification checks the receipt and relevant script hashes; it does not needlessly repeat every interval subdivision.

The original SA missing-script issue above is distinct from the supplied and executed GS certificate. Existing check receipts were read as source evidence; only independently executed or re-derived checks are described as such.

### External theorem checks

The primary source [dispersion.tex in the OpenAI cubic Gauss-sum preprint](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-Gauss-sums-September-25-2026/build/sections/dispersion.tex) was inspected on 2026-10-10. Its coefficient-distribution hypothesis and length range do not authorize SA's desired direct substitution. In the stated \(AB\asymp X\) range, \(X^{.32}\le B\le X^{.5}\); larger \(B\) uses a specified smooth-prime convolution family. Low-height logarithmic error is different from the power-saving averaged-height statement, which also restricts \(B\). The moving coefficient admits a resonant nonprincipal test, and raw substitution \(A=K,B=D\) would require \(D\le K\). A03 gives the exact surviving prime-convolution lemma and failed substitution. No new global saving is imported from this paper.

The [NIST DLMF Laguerre generating function, 18.12.13](https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.12#E13) was checked for A11. The displayed polynomial/generating-series expansions and cancellation are also derived in the auxiliary record. Other named spectral, Kloosterman or trace-function mechanisms remain proposals unless their exact inherited or supplied hypotheses are established here.

statement:
## G154. Actual coupled cancellation, and the surviving obstruction

For a principal character let B_X be the selected ordered source with
distinct primes d,e in (sqrt(X)/2,sqrt(X/2)] and cofactor l=1. For large
X these primes are unramified and satisfy every balanced-core cutoff.
If J is their number, the ordinary prime number theorem gives
J~2(1/sqrt(2)-1/2)sqrt(X)/log X. Uniformly on the full real shell,

    Re B_X(x)>=exp(-X^(1-b)/2)cos(2^(-k))J(J-1).

Thus ||B_X||_1 and ||B_X||_2 are comparable to X/log^2 X. The only
external input is ordinary PNT, e.g. [Selberg's original theorem (1.1),
printed p.305](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf),
used here for fixed-proportion prime counts. This is a lower bound for
the selected arithmetic cell. It is NOT a lower bound for an unselected
dyadic factor box, T, R or C_p. It obstructs a triangle budget that pays
this cell separately at X^(gamma+epsilon), epsilon<1-gamma.

When u>1/2 the asymmetric core has zero coefficient on this cell, while
the balanced core has coefficient two per unordered pair. Put

    D_X=T_(p,chi,X)-A_(p,chi,X), K_X=D_X-B_X.

Equations (91.4) and (91.7) UNCONDITIONALLY give

    ||B_X+K_X||_j<<X^(gamma+epsilon)=o(||B_X||_j), j=1,2.

K_X contains every other exact term in the difference, with its signs
and cutoffs. In L2 this implies

    ||K_X||_2/||B_X||_2 -> 1,
    Re <B_X,K_X>=-||B_X||_2^2

## 6. The full Newton remainder and its literal valuation coupling

For j>=0 define

    W_J(j)=(-1)^j-sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)t^j,
    r_J(n)=mu^2(n)chi(n)W_J(omega(n)),                     (6.1)

using 0^0=1. The exact identity (4.8) gives

    mu chi=L_J+r_J.                                      (6.2)

Thus W_J(j)=0 for j<=J. This is a resummation of the entire finite chain expansion at each n, including every depth greater than J, not a truncation that drops its error.

Summing (6.1) as a formal generating series gives

    sum_(j>=0)W_J(j)z^j
      =(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)! z^(J+1)
                       /[(1+z)prod_(t=1)^J(1-tz)].       (6.3)

For a direct verification, the rational left side is 1/(1+z) minus the finite sum of binomial weights/(1-tz). Its first J+1 coefficients vanish. Its common-denominator numerator has degree at most J+1; the highest coefficient, from the t=0 term, is (-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. This proves (6.3) at every degree. Combining (1+z)(1-z)=1-z^2 yields

    W_J(J+1+h)=(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)![z^h]
                   1/[(1-z^2)prod_(t=2)^J(1-tz)].        (6.4)

For J>=2 all displayed coefficients are strictly positive, since the factor (1-2z)^-1 has positive coefficients at every nonnegative degree. Hence the principal unfiltered residual has one fixed sign on j>=J+1; its first coefficient is (-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. At J=1 the remaining factor 1/(1-z^2) gives the author's parity zeros, though the main statement uses J>=2.

The finite-color formula (6.1), independent of x, gives |W_J(j)|<=C_J J^j. Therefore |r_J(n)|<<_(J,epsilon)n^epsilon: only finitely many primes below J^(1/epsilon) require a fixed constant, and each remaining distinct prime pays J by its p^epsilon factor. This removes the factorial representation cost, but proves no saving in the signed summatory source.

Now define the literal complete sharp sources, for all real x,

    T_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*r_J)(n),
    S_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*mu chi)(n).

Equations (5.4) and (6.2) give the stronger complete transfer

    |S_(p,J)(x)-T_(p,J)(x)| << x^(1-1/J),         J>=3,
    |S_(p,2)(x)-T_(p,2)(x)| << sqrt x log^3(2x).           (6.5)

All constants retain p,q,J. The author's every-epsilon version follows. The finite filter terms whose shifted argument is below one are zero. No lower interval, p-valuation, chain depth or real endpoint is removed.

To verify all p-valuation signs, write n=p^a m, p not dividing m, with m squarefree. Set j=omega(m) and take binomial coefficients outside 0,...,J to be zero. In the convolution, r_J(p^(a-i)m) can be nonzero only for a-i=0 or1. These two terms are exactly

    (v_(p,J)*r_J)(p^a m)
      =chi(p)^a chi(m)[(-p)^a binom(J,a)W_J(j)
              +(-p)^(a-1)binom(J,a-1)W_J(j+1)].          (6.6)

The second term is absent at a=0. The a=J+1 term is retained; only a>J+1 vanishes. Nonsquarefree m or a ramified prime in m gives zero. The two coefficients are linked by the SAME W_J and must not be treated as independent signs. A source restricted to p-free integers is a projection of (6.6), not a valid signed upper bound for the whole source.

For principal chi choose a fixed product A of J distinct primes avoiding pq. On n=A*l with l prime avoiding Apq, the literal a=0 coefficient is the nonzero constant (-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. Ordinary pi(y)>>y/log y, unaffected by finitely many exclusions, gives an absolute projected summatory price >>_(A,J)x/log x. This arithmetic lower bound is valid and source-specific. It rules out paying every such projection separately with a power below one. It does not lower-bound T_(p,J), because all p-divisible cross-valuations and remaining prime counts still participate. The required prime lower bound follows from the unconditional ordinary prime asymptotic in [NIST DLMF 27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12); no RH-conditional or progression estimate is used.

## 7. Variance and the complete coarse arithmetic test

At an unramified prime l the exact g coefficient is
chi(l)^nu(-1)^nu(floor(nu/2)+1). Therefore

    |g(n)|^2=1_{(n,q)=1} sum_{d^2|n}d_2(d^2).

The local identity is sum_{j<=floor(nu/2)}(2j+1)=(floor(nu/2)+1)^2;
multiplicativity and the natural ramified zero prove the full formula.
Coprime integer counting yields

    sum_{n<=Y}|g(n)|^2=C_chi Y+O_q(sqrt(Y)log^2(2Y)),
    C_chi=(phi(q)/q)sum_{(d,q)=1}d_2(d^2)/d^2>0.

The sum of errors and the omitted main tail both have the displayed size:
d_2(d^2)<=d_3(d), and the elementary triple-divisor count is
O(Z log^2(2Z)). The constant series converges absolutely. The finite v
convolution and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz retain all its cross terms and
give sum_{n<=Y}|c(n)|^2<<_{p,q}Y. This is an upper bound for c, not an
unproved exact c-diagonal asymptotic.

For n>=M>=X, the off-diagonal row sum of the squared-decay integer kernel
is O(X^6/n^5). Comparable terms follow from |n^6-m^6|>>n^5|n-m|;
each distant complement costs O(X^12/n^11), no larger for n>=X.
Use 2|c_n c_m|<=|c_n|^2+|c_m|^2, keeping both orientations, and partial
summation of the second moment. Actual damping pays the diagonal, while
the off-diagonal is absolutely summable even after removing damping. Thus

    ||sum_{n>M}c(n)f_x(n)||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^6 M^(-4).          (R12)

Combining M=X with the full low-prefix bound from Cauchy–Schwarz gives
||C||_2<<X. That is a complete failed first power test, not a hidden gain.

The exact identity g=(mu chi)*s*s has coefficient expansion

    g(n)=sum_{r^2m=n}d_2(r)chi(r)^2 mu(m)chi(m),

without a gcd restriction. Apply the primary Green–Tao specialization to
the inner fixed-degree polynomial. Split r at a fixed logarithmic power
of Y. For smaller r, log(Y/r^2) is comparable to log Y; sum the inner
bound against the convergent d_2(r)/r^2 series. The entire larger-r part
costs Y sum_{r>R}d_2(r)/r^2<<Y log(2R)/R. This proves every fixed
logarithmic polynomial-prefix saving for g, hence for the four fixed v
dilations in c. The strength is uniform in polynomial coefficients, with
fixed character and degree. It is neither a growing-degree result nor a
power bound deduced from the conditional remark in Green–Tao.

Abel summation against the actual decreasing damping then bounds the
prefix through M by M(log M)^(-A). Split very small prefix lengths at
sqrt(M); their total O(sqrt(M)) follows from the actual second moment
and is absorbed. Taking M=X(log X)^B in (R12), with fixed A,B chosen
after the desired fixed logarithmic strength D, proves

    ||C||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D),
    ||C||_1 << X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D).                          (R13)

Replacing D by a larger fixed value before taking square roots gives the
stated L1 exponent. (R11) transfers this logarithmic bound to the complete
core. No fixed logarithmic strength supplies X^(gamma+epsilon) at a fixed
gamma<1. This is a paid arithmetic test, with its failure recorded.

    a_i=conjugate(b_i), <u,v>=sum_i conjugate(u_i)v_i.

Every native coefficient, ray/unit factor, zero extension, mask and sharp endpoint occurs once in b_i or phi_i. This is only a factorization of the actual finite summand. It does not normalize nonunit terms away or identify two ordered terms. In particular, an original zero coefficient remains zero. An identically zero packet has no asserted positive mass. Rooted short sums may be expanded here, but may not be individually estimated and then advertised as the accepted complete signed tensor W.

Choose a finite oriented graph on this full vertex list and positive edge weights w_e. Put B for its incidence matrix, W=diag(w_e), L=BWB*, h=projection_(ker L)a. With v=L^dagger a and j=WB*v,

    Bj=a-h,

Every other current with the same divergence differs by a cycle in ker B, orthogonal to j in the W^(-1) metric; this proves minimum energy. Thus

                 sqrt(sum_e w_e |(B*phi)_e|^2)
                    +|<h,phi>|.                    (R43-H2)

For A=.004,T=10 the first-gain threshold relative to c_G is
gamma<.874881596247255573680243744715..., not the author's historical

through x^2.01 exp(sqrt(log x)). T=10 is covered by the cited rigorous

The continuous prime-density model, including the actual q_2 correction,

density defeats a fixed-power gain in both L1 and L2 under baseline-only

The rotated discovery preserved five mechanisms: genuine second quadratic

Canonical sources are linked above and in the [coherent proof](../current-proof.md),
[controller review](../[private research revision]/controller-review.md), and
[Gao integration](../[private research revision]/gao-local-moment-integration.md).
All card inventories and original frozen author/reviewer bytes remain.
Untested, duplicate, scoped-false, repairable, open and proved-relative-to-input

The author tested02/03/04/16/20/22; the critic independently audited27/06 after immutable outcome-free selection. There is no new arithmetic cancellation estimate or change to c6=.125139. ## G87: a fixed-order return from the literal G72 energy Fix tau>0 and arbitrary complex |a(n)|<=1, extended by zero for n<=0. Set g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2*tau)), F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log(n/x)), and retain exactly B_H(k)=sum_(j=0)^(H-1)a(k-j), w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4*tau)), E_a(X,H)=(1/H)sum_(k>=1)|B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k). With h_tau(t)=g(log t) extended smoothly by zero for t<=0, define J_j=integral|h_tau^(j)|, K_tau=sqrt(2*pi*tau)exp(tau/2)+2 and C_(tau,r)=(2^r-1)sqrt(K_tau/(2*pi*tau)) *exp(3(log2)^2/(2*tau)). Previously this consequence required thetagamma; the strict exponent gap is2(beta-gamma). Equality is not decided. A proof using those properties can escape the model. ## G89: precise observation contracts and their unpaid arithmetic The protected H audit freezes the complete native same-scale prime-far packet, with both projectors, signed core sums, independent heights, original JN phase and1/Q normalization. For its literal pairing H_raw=, kappa=conjugate(K), any counting-measure conditional expectation P gives exactly H_raw=

+<(I-P)What,(I-P)kappa>. ## 7. C01: exact rank and the paid analytic approximation

On disjoint finite prime sets U,V outside the conductor, the hard
product-cap matrix is

    T_de=mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e) 1_(de<=x).

Its sign/character factors are diagonal unitaries. They preserve
rank and singular values of the incidence matrix B, while its
signed scalar contraction still retains both boundary phases.
Sorted rows of B are prefix vectors; distinct nonzero prefix
lengths give independent vectors by successive subtraction.
Hence rank(B) is exactly the number of distinct nonzero prefix
lengths. The two-prime matrix has determinant -chi(p)chi(q) when
p<q<=x<pq and rank 1 after the cap disappears. This is a correct
test of the cutoff's rank cost, with the Sol wave01 A34 tensor
network seed explicitly credited.

For the Gaussian matrix K_de=g_tau(log d+log e-y), remove positive
row/column factors to leave exp(-u_i*v_j/tau). A nonzero real
combination of n distinct real exponentials has at most n-1
distinct real zeros: divide by one exponential, differentiate,
and apply Rolle inductively. A singular real n-by-n evaluation
matrix would give a real nullvector and n zeros, a contradiction.
Every square minor with distinct row/column logarithms is therefore
nonzero, proving full rectangular rank. The two-prime determinant
ratio exp(-log p log q/tau)-1 has the stated negative sign.

Full exact rank does not rule out approximation. With centered
logs u_d,v_e, |u_d|<=U, |v_e|<=V, w=a+b-y, the exact factorization
is C(w)A_d(w)B_e(w)exp(-u_d*v_e/tau), with the source's positive
C,A_d,B_e. The degree r-1 Taylor expansion gives rank <=r and
pointwise remainder <=e^Z Z^r/r!, Z=UV/tau. After the actual
signed contraction its absolute error is bounded by

    C(w)e^Z Z^r/r! (sum_d |mu(d)chi(d)| A_d)
                       (sum_e |mu(e)chi(e)| B_e).        (R39.12)

This includes the mass factors often omitted by an abstract
low-rank claim. The operator error is bounded using the analogous
l2 factors, since the Frobenius square is dominated by their
product. If the positive scalar prefactor is <=exp(C_1 L),
Z<=C_2 L and r=ceil(C_3 L), the factorial bound gives exponent
at most C_1+C_2+C_3 log(e C_2/C_3)+o(1), times L.
Choosing a sufficiently large fixed C_3 pays any fixed negative
power. Fixed-constant O(sqrt L) log-bin widths and center mismatch,
with finite coefficient masses exp(O(L)), meet those hypotheses.

This bounded-bin approximation is valid. It is neither a uniform
estimate on all unbinned prime states nor an algorithm that
computes the required signed moments cheaply. Each separated
factor is a signed moving-endpoint arithmetic sum of growing
degree. Reassembly needs all bins, tails, heights and cross-Gram
terms with their own error budgets. The actual cancellation
remains unproved. Existing W35 finite Gaussian/Fourier machinery
is related representation ancestry; no paid sector is added here.

statement:
### A3. Why the ordinary L-function replenishes the complex bound

For Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F(y)e^(-s y)dy=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).     (W39.9)

If F(y)<<_epsilon exp((h+epsilon)y) for every epsilon>0 as y tends to +infinity, its left Gaussian tail makes the integral holomorphic on Re s>h, including every fixed s derivative. Multiply by L and continue from Re s>1. At any zero rho in this domain, the left product would vanish while exp(tau rho^2/2) does not. A principal pole at1 is separately removable in the reciprocal and creates no false zero exclusion. Hence there are no L zeros in Re s>h.

Conversely, if a fixed ordinary L has no zeros in Re s>h, with h>0, then for EVERY fixed b>h and tau>0 the very same F satisfies W39.4 for some C,K. We need only polynomial growth of 1/L on the fixed line, and derive it here to avoid an unproved inverse-bound assumption.

For a nonprincipal ordinary character, its periodic partial sums are O_q(1). Abel summation gives

    L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity A_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt,
    |L(s,chi)| <= q |s|/Re s, Re s>0.                   (W39.10)

For a principal character A_chi(t)=ct+O_q(1); subtract ct in this integral. It gives the simple principal pole and a polynomial upper bound for P(s)=(s-1)L(s,chi) on every closed positive strip. In the nonprincipal case put P=L. The finite imprimitive Euler factors stay literal and are nonzero on Re s>0.

Fix h<b<2; b>=2 is trivial. Around 2+it take an outer disk of radius R_0=2-(h+b)/2 and inner radius r_0=2-b. The outer disk is zero-free for P, lies in Re s>h, and the gap R_0-r_0=(b-h)/2 is fixed. An analytic logarithm log P exists on that disk. Choose its value at the center to have imaginary part in [-pi,pi]. The absolutely convergent Euler product at2 bounds |L(2+it)| above and away from0; the regularizing factor changes its logarithm by O(log(2+|t|)). Thus |log P(2+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)). The polynomial upper bound for P gives Re log P<=C log(2+|t|) throughout the disk. The elementary Borel--Caratheodory inequality now bounds |log P(b+it)| by C_(h,b,q) log(2+|t|), proving

    |1/L(b+it,chi)| <= C(1+|t|)^K.                       (W39.11)

For completeness put f=log P, choose M>sup Re f, and set g=M-f. Then Re g>0 and H(z)=(g(z)-g(0))/(g(z)+conj(g(0))) maps the disk into the unit disk and vanishes at its center. Schwarz gives |H(z)|<=r_0/R_0 on the inner disk. The triangle inequality then bounds |g(z)| by (R_0+r_0)/(R_0-r_0) times |g(0)|. Since M and |f(0)| are O(log(2+|t|)), the stated bound for f follows. A compact low-height region is absorbed into C. Uniform bounds hold across a fixed closed horizontal strip by using the smallest gap; the reciprocal has a zero at the principal pole, not a singularity.

Mellin inversion on a line >1, followed by a contour shift to b, now gives for all complex z

    F(z)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_R
       exp(tau(b+it)^2/2) exp((b+it)z)/L(b+it,chi) dt.    (W39.12)

Horizontal sides vanish by the Gaussian exp(-tau t^2/2), with W39.11; locally uniform convergence also proves the identity for complex z. Completing the square in -tau t^2/2-tv gives

    |F(u+iv)| <= C exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)) (1+|v|)^K,

which is W39.4. Neither a conjectured Möbius Mertens bound nor subpower height growth was required. The polynomial degree K may worsen at each fixed iteration; W39.7 absorbs it, since only finitely many iterations are used for a chosen output epsilon.
