statement:
# [private research revision] discovery pass: arithmetic dilates and the localization deficit

Status: completed bounded mathematical report, 2026-10-12; independent review pending. Sole writer scope is this directory. Accepted source-relative endpoint at assignment was c6=0.125139, gamma6=0.874861; the controller's later acceptance of c7=.125140 is recorded in Section5 and is the final calibration. No formalization, provider consultation, canonical mutation or endpoint promotion is performed.

## Compact worklog and discovery decisions

The objective is a genuinely different upstream source, retaining an honest full return. The accepted G83-G85 growing-order completion, Gaussian moment and its all-real-scale Mertens equivalence are inputs, not discoveries of this pass. In particular the old Q/Core estimate is not advertised as easier than Mertens. The full 29-family/109-child library remains retained.

Six mechanisms were considered before selecting one for detailed calculation:

1. A character-adapted Davenport/Bernoulli dilation source. Exact multiplicative inversion gives a two-frequency target, while the complete-period Gram can be evaluated through gcds. Potential reach is every gamma>1/2 if a sufficiently strong shrinking-arc estimate can be proved. Selected: it actually uses the global law mu*1=delta, unlike the earlier complex countermodel.
2. Prime-color expansion of the accepted growing moment. The uncapped local multiplicities are binomial, but a left-line Euler product does not follow from finite local calculations; G69 mass escape and the now-proved Q equivalence remain. Not duplicated.
3. Replicate a fixed character by inducing it to larger moduli and apply a large sieve. The copies are not independent primitive characters; their repeated direction carries the corresponding large eigenvalue. Removing the extra Euler factors also has a physical complement. No source bridge was found; not used.
4. A pole-normalized fractional reciprocal with fractional convolution. The library already contains W22-A/C and W21; an unnormalized fractional reciprocal creates a principal branch singularity at 1. There is no new contribution from renaming that route.
5. Quantitative almost-periodic repetition of a hypothetical zero. The naive box prescribing many independent prime phases has exponentially small volume, while the available approximation-tail control in that attempted construction is polynomial. No paid quantitative recurrence-to-zero-density bridge was obtained. This is a rejected unproved construction, not a theorem ruling out a better recurrence argument.
6. Renewal/Nyman positive floor kernels and a changed observation space. F08 and the Round25 floor/renewal pilots already retain the positive-cover and boundary-observation costs. The selected dilation calculation tests a different, explicit arithmetic Hilbert-space source rather than treating a finite Nyman fit as closure.

Primary outside source inspected on the web: C. Aistleitner, I. Berkes, K. Seip and M. Weber, *Convergence of series of dilated functions and spectral norms of GCD matrices*, Acta Arithmetica 168.3 (2015), DOI 10.4064/aa168-3-2, arXiv:1407.5403v2. Section3, equations(3.2)-(3.5), records the classical Bernoulli/gcd Gram identity and its Hurwitz extension. The elementary calculation below proves its exact instance and the character factors directly. Classical Davenport series, Fourier inversion and the Franel-Landau identity are not claimed as new literature results. URL: https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82044 ; bibliographic version: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5403v2 . Only these elementary identities, not a stronger spectral theorem, are imported.

The selected route currently has an unconditional global estimate, an exact arithmetic obstruction to fixed finite scale filtering, and an open localized signed estimate. This report will distinguish these from any actual improvement in c.

## 1. Exact ordinary-character source

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q>=1, including imprimitive and principal characters with their usual zeros. Let r>=2 be a fixed integer with chi(-1)=(-1)^r. Thus r=2 for an even character and r=3 for an odd one suffice. Write e(x)=exp(2 pi i x), a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), and

    Phi(x)=sum_(k in Z, k!=0) chi(k) e(kx)/k^r,
    D_N(x)=sum_(n<=N) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx),
    E(x)=e(x)+e(-x)=2cos(2pi x),
    R_N(x)=E(x)-D_N(x).

All sums defining Phi and D_infinity converge absolutely and uniformly because r>1. Complete multiplicativity, including character zeros, gives at every positive or negative frequency k

    Fourier(D_infinity)(k)=chi(k)k^(-r) sum_(d|abs(k))mu(d).

The parity choice makes the two surviving coefficients at k=+1,-1 equal to1. Consequently D_infinity=E pointwise, and

    R_N(x)=sum_(n>N) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx).                 (1)

There is no discarded height, future tail, exceptional zero bin or inducing-conductor shift in this exact periodic identity. q, chi and r are fixed before N tends to infinity. The restriction to ordinary integer characters is explicit; no Eisenstein or Hecke analogue is asserted.

For abs(k)<=N, R_N has zero Fourier coefficient. For N<abs(k)<=2N,

    Fourier(R_N)(k)=chi(k)mu(abs(k))/k^r.              (2)

The latter follows because the only divisor exceeding N is abs(k) itself. These are actual squarefree coefficients, not a random-sign replacement.

For n,m>=1, g=gcd(n,m), Fourier orthogonality gives

    <Phi(nx),Phi(mx)>_[0,1]
      =2 L(2r,chi0) chi(m/g) conjugate(chi(n/g))
         *g^(2r)/(nm)^r,                             (3)

where chi0 is the principal character modulo q. When multiplied by a(n)conjugate(a(m))/(nm)^r, the character phase cancels for (nm,q)=1, and otherwise the term is zero. Thus

    ||R_N||_2^2=2L(2r,chi0)
      sum_(n,m>N; (nm,q)=1) mu(n)mu(m)
         gcd(n,m)^(2r)/(nm)^(2r).                    (4)

Every double series is absolutely convergent; the same calculation applies to finite tails and passes to the limit by dominated convergence. Equation(4) does not discard the off-diagonal signs.

## 2. An actual signed global asymptotic

For d>=1 put

    delta(d)=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|d) p/(p+1).

The elementary squarefree count, uniformly for real T>=1, is

    sum_(g<=T; (g,d)=1) mu(g)^2
       =delta(d)T+O(2^omega(d) sqrt(T)).              (5)

Indeed mu(g)^2=sum_(h^2|g)mu(h); counting the remaining integers coprime to d costs O(2^omega(d)) per h<=sqrt(T), and the absolutely convergent h^(-2) main term has a sqrt(T) truncation error. Partial summation gives

    sum_(g>T; (g,d)=1) mu(g)^2/g^(2r)
       =delta(d)T^(1-2r)/(2r-1)
        +O_r(2^omega(d)T^(1/2-2r)).                  (6)

In(4) write n=ga,m=gb with (a,b)=1. A nonzero term has a,b,g squarefree and g coprime to abq; then mu(ga)mu(gb)=mu(a)mu(b)mu(g)^2. Both n,m>N mean g>N/min(a,b). Applying(6) proves

    ||R_N||_2^2 = C_r(q) N^(1-2r)
                    +O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)),          (7)

where the absolutely convergent, signed arithmetic constant is

    C_r(q)= 2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      *sum_((a,b)=1; (ab,q)=1)
        mu(a)mu(b)delta(abq) min(a,b)^(2r-1)/(ab)^(2r).

Here r and q are fixed. To verify the error without hiding a second large-parameter limit, first restrict min(a,b)<=N. The error sum is bounded by

    N^(1/2-2r) sum_(a,b)
       2^omega(abq) min(a,b)^(2r-1/2)/(ab)^(2r).

This converges for r>=2: after a<=b, use 2^omega(n)<=C n^(1/4) twice and sum b first, obtaining a convergent O(sum_a a^(1-2r)). For min(a,b)>N the actual sum and the corresponding proposed main term are both O_(q,r)(N^(2-4r)), smaller than the displayed error. Thus no growing-divisor uniformity is assumed in(7).

The first exact Fourier band(2), Parseval and(5) show

    C_r(q)>=2 delta(q)(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1)>0.          (8)

For clarity, partial summation evaluates its squared norm as

    2 sum_(N<k<=2N; (k,q)=1)mu(k)^2/k^(2r)
     =2delta(q)(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1) N^(1-2r)
        +O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)).

Consequently the global energy is genuinely of order N^(1-2r) for the actual arithmetic source, even after using all signs. It depends on q and r, but not on which character modulo q is chosen with the required parity. In the complete-period norm the character phases have cancelled exactly. This is a proved source estimate and a substantive limitation of this specific proposed replacement, not an artificial complex-coefficient countermodel.

The tempting remainder in(7) gains a half power. That is exactly the formal energy gain that a c=1/4 return would need below. However subtracting C_r(q)N^(1-2r) from an energy destroys the available positivity comparison with its restriction to an arc. The next result rules out implementing this subtraction by any fixed finite normalized scale filter of the actual source.

## 3. Fixed finite scale filtering cannot remove that leading energy

Fix 0<lambda_1<...<lambda_J and complex coefficients c_j, not all zero. Put

    F_N=sum_(j=1)^J c_j R_floor(lambda_j N).

Take the first nonzero coefficient, relabelled c_1. Choose a fixed B strictly between lambda_1 and min(2lambda_1,lambda_2), interpreting lambda_2=infinity if no later scale exists. On the positive-frequency interval

    floor(lambda_1 N)<k<=BN

for sufficiently large N, only the first source can have a nonzero Fourier coefficient, and its contribution is c_1 mu(k)chi(k)/k^r. Floor errors affect only O(1) endpoints and can alternatively be avoided by choosing a slightly smaller B. Equation(5) therefore gives

    ||F_N||_2^2 >= c(q,r,B,lambda_1)|c_1|^2 N^(1-2r)

for large N, with a strictly positive constant. An upper bound of the same order follows from(7) and the triangle inequality.

There is also a uniform lower constant when sum|c_j|^2=1, allowing the coefficients to depend on N while the finite scales remain fixed. Otherwise take a violating sequence and a convergent subsequence of coefficient vectors. Its limit is nonzero. The difference of the fields has norm o(N^(1/2-r)) by the individual upper bounds, contradicting the just-proved lower bound for the limit vector. Thus

    inf_(sum|c_j|^2=1) ||sum c_j R_floor(lambda_jN)||_2^2
       >=c_(q,r,lambda_1,...,lambda_J) N^(1-2r)       (9)

eventually. No uniform lower constant is asserted as J grows or scales collide. This does not prohibit a growing-order or shrinking-spacing construction; it rules out the actual fixed finite cancellation proposed in this pass, including normalized N-dependent coefficients. It is stronger than observing merely that the scalar coefficient in(7) is positive.

## 4. The complete short-arc observation and zero-exclusion return

Here is the weakest full source estimate used by this replacement. Fix 0<c<1/2 and gamma=1-c. For every fixed ordinary chi modulo q, use the fixed parity-compatible r above, put h=1/(qN), and require, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large integers N,

    E_arc(N):=integral_0^h |R_N(x)|^2 dx
       <<_(chi,r,epsilon) N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon).        (10)

The positive epsilon loss is chosen after c; thresholds may depend on the fixed character and epsilon. No average over characters or exceptional scale set is allowed. In fact(10) is equivalent, up to arbitrary epsilon losses, to M_chi(X)=sum_(n<=X)mu(n)chi(n)<<X^(gamma+epsilon). This equivalence is stated explicitly: the new source estimate is not called easier merely because its notation differs.

Proof of the forward direction, including the observation cost: discrete Fourier inversion modulo q writes chi(k)=sum_(a=0)^(q-1) c_a e(ak/q). The Fourier formula for the periodic Bernoulli polynomial gives

    Phi(x)=-(2pi i)^r/r! sum_a c_a B_r({x+a/q}).

Thus on 0<x<1/q, Phi is one fixed polynomial P(x) of degree at most r. It is continuous at0 since r>=2, and its constant term is

    beta=Phi(0)=2L(r,chi)!=0.

The nonvanishing here is the absolutely convergent Euler product on r>1; no zero-free assertion to the left of1 is used. In particular principal and imprimitive characters are covered with their original zeros. Let p_r be the endpoint reproducing polynomial on [0,1]:

    p_r(u)=sum_(j=0)^r (2j+1)(-1)^j P_j(2u-1),

where P_j is the Legendre polynomial. Orthogonality, or integration against monomials, proves

    integral_0^1 p_r(u)u^j du=1_(j=0) (0<=j<=r),
    integral_0^1 |p_r(u)|^2du=(r+1)^2.               (11)

For the first identity it suffices to test the shifted Legendre basis: the integral selects its j-th coefficient with value (-1)^j, exactly the value of that basis polynomial at0. The norm is sum_(j=0)^r(2j+1). The Bernoulli Fourier formula used above follows by repeated integration by parts from B_j'=j B_(j-1), mean zero and B_1(x)=x-1/2; it has no additional analytic input. In particular B_2=x^2-x+1/6 and B_3=x^3-3x^2/2+x/2 cover the two orders needed here.

Define O_N f=integral_0^1 p_r(u)f(hu)du. Every n<=N has nhu<=1/q, so the same local polynomial applies to every original term, without a moving choice of a cell. It follows exactly that

    O_N D_N=beta sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n^r.

Writing eta_N=O_N E-2, Taylor's theorem and(11) give |eta_N|<=C_r h^(r+1). Since sum a(n)/n^r=1/L(r,chi),

    beta sum_(n>N)a(n)/n^r = O_N R_N-eta_N.          (12)

Cauchy-Schwarz pays the full observation cost:

    |O_N R_N| <=(r+1) sqrt(qN) E_arc(N)^(1/2).       (13)

Equations(10)-(13) give T_N:=sum_(n>N)a(n)/n^r<<N^(gamma-r+epsilon). For integer N, ordinary partial summation, with T(t)=T_floor(t), gives the exact inverse formula

    M_chi(N)=1/L(r,chi)-N^r T_N
                 +r integral_1^N t^(r-1)T(t)dt.     (14)

It yields M_chi(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon), and real X follows by taking its integer part. All integer N are required; a sparse scale family is not silently interpolated.

For completeness, the reverse direction is equally paid. Phi is bounded and globally Lipschitz: this follows from its finite Bernoulli representation, including r=2 and the finitely many derivative jumps. Abel summation in(1), using |M_chi(t)|<<t^(gamma+epsilon) with gamma+epsilon<1, gives

    |R_N(x)| << N^(gamma-r+epsilon)
                      +|x|N^(gamma-r+1+epsilon)

for 0<=x<=h. The derivative integral converges since r>=2>gamma+1+epsilon. Integrating its square proves(10), after relabelling epsilon. This uses the actual full tail and not a pointwise Fourier series summation shortcut.

The zero return has no hidden height truncation. The Mertens estimate makes

    A(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma and equal to 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. For nonprincipal chi, bounded period sums give L(s,chi) holomorphic on Re(s)>0. For principal chi modulo q, the floor integral for zeta together with product_(p|q)(1-p^(-s)) gives the usual meromorphic continuation, with its only pole in that half-plane at1. The identity A(s)L(s,chi)=1 then continues throughout the connected half-plane with that pole removed. Hence L has no zero with Re(s)>gamma, at any imaginary height. At the principal pole the excluded point remains a pole, not a zero. Finite imprimitive Euler factors have zeros only on Re(s)=0. This is an ordinary-character conditional theorem. It neither supplies the open estimate(10) nor resolves the separate pinned PR9 source/K-scope issue in the incumbent proof.

## 5. Finite signed core with every complement paid

The source estimate can be put into an explicitly finite arithmetic form without using the old moment machinery. Choose fixed kappa>0 with 2c+kappa<1 and set

    G=ceil(N^(2c+kappa)),
    T=ceil(N^(1+2c/(2r-1)+kappa)),
    R_N,T=sum_(N<n<=T) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx).

Define the incomplete-period Gram kernel

    K_N(n,m)=integral_0^(1/(qN)) Phi(nx)conjugate(Phi(mx))dx,

and its signed small-gcd core

    C_N,T,G=sum_(N<n,m<=T; gcd(n,m)<G)
        a(n)conjugate(a(m))(nm)^(-r) K_N(n,m).        (15)

The natural zeros of both coefficients remain. The pair set is symmetric, so(15) is real, but it need not be nonnegative. The required bound is the one-sided estimate

    C_N,T,G <= A_(chi,r,epsilon,kappa)
                   N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon).             (16)

Here A is a positive constant independent of N. This is neither an absolute bound on the real core nor an absolute-value estimate on each pair. The parameters are frozen as the displayed functions of N before any summand or cancellation is inspected.

The kernel itself has a finite description: the Bernoulli representation expresses each Phi as a fixed finite sum of periodic polynomials, and on this bounded interval their finitely many breakpoints give an exact piecewise-polynomial integral. No Fourier-height truncation is being called exact.

The large-gcd complement costs

    sum_(n,m>N; gcd(n,m)>=G) |a(n)a(m)|(nm)^(-r)|K_N(n,m)|
       <<_r N^(1-2r)/G+N^(-2r).                     (17)

Indeed |Phi|<=2zeta(r) and the interval has length at most1/N. Write n=ga,m=gb and drop coprimality only for this positive upper bound. For G<=g<=N the resulting summand is at most C_r N^(2-2r)g^(-2); for g>N its sum is O_r(N^(1-2r)). Multiplication by1/N proves(17). The diagonal, squareful gcds, zero terms and all far indices are included, never renamed as cancellation. For the chosen G, both terms lie strictly below the target in(16), because gamma>1/2.

The infinite completion error is exactly R_T, whose squared global norm is O_(q,r)(T^(1-2r)) by(7), or just by its absolute gcd bound. Thus

    E_arc(N)<=2||R_N,T||_(L2[0,h])^2+2||R_T||_(L2[0,1])^2.

The second term is O(N^(1-2r-2c-(2r-1)kappa)). Combining(16), (17) and this inequality proves(10) without estimating a cross term against an unpaid global field. There is no hidden infinity in the proposed core, no derivative of a moving cutoff, and no character deletion or phase normalization.

Conversely, if(10) holds, this same completion inequality in the reverse direction bounds the finite field, and(17) bounds its removed large-gcd sector. Therefore(16), for these choices, is also equivalent to(10) up to epsilon losses. This is another exact encoding of the hard Mertens bound, with a useful finite complement contract; it is not by itself an arithmetic saving.

The exact complete budgets are as follows. The energy improvement needed over the unconditional global norm is N^(-2c), independent of r. Ignoring the freely chosen positive kappa in the completion cutoff:

| Target c | Required energy gain | T exponent, r=2 | T exponent, r=3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .125139 (incumbent at assignment) | .250278 | 1+.250278/3 | 1+.250278/5 |
| .125140 (c7, accepted during this pass) | .250280 | 1+.250280/3 | 1+.250280/5 |
| 1/6 | 1/3 | 10/9 | 16/15 |
| 1/4 | 1/2 | 7/6 | 11/10 |

A strict first improvement over the accepted c therefore needs(16) with c strictly larger than that accepted value; an equality of an auxiliary reserve is not an impossibility theorem. No row in this table asserts(16).

Calibration update received from the controller during this pass: c7=6257/50000=.125140, gamma7=.874860, was independently and controller accepted at07:18 UTC, with the same source-relative PR9/Gao qualifications; [private research revision] integration is pending. The stronger .12514261 supplement is still unaccepted. Thus the first-gain comparison for this completed pass is c>.125140, not merely c>.125139. The initial calibration above is retained as history. This update changes no argument or claimed theorem here.

## 6. Deliberately coarse bounds and two failed repairs

The elementary positive estimate on(15) is

    |C_N,T,G|<=C_r h (sum_(n>N)n^(-r))^2
                <<_r N^(1-2r).                     (18)

It misses the c7 first-gain requirement by a power strictly exceeding .250280. Raising the fixed Bernoulli order r does not reduce that missing exponent: its apparent extra decay is exactly cancelled by the weighted-tail observation and Abel inverse. Formula(7) shows that a complete-period signed estimate cannot repair(18); even the exact signed energy has this same order.

The positivity failure is not just a hypothetical choice of signs. For q=1,r=2, Phi(x)=2pi^2 B_2({x}), where B_2(u)=u^2-u+1/6. The squared period norm of B_2 is integral B_2^2=1/180, and B_2 is globally Lipschitz with constant1 and supremum1/6. Put eta=1/120. If 1<=a,b<=1+eta,

    integral_0^1 B_2({au})B_2({bu})du
       >=1/180-eta/3=1/360.                         (19)

This follows by comparing each factor to B_2(u) using the stated Lipschitz and supremum bounds. Therefore, for every integer pair N<n,m<=(1+eta)N,

    K_N(n,m)>=pi^4/(90N).

There are asymptotically delta(1)eta N squarefree integers in this interval by(5). Pairs with gcd>=G are at most

    sum_(g>=G) floor((1+eta)N/g)^2
       <=(1+eta)^2N^2 sum_(g>=G)g^(-2)=O(N^2/G).

Thus, for any fixed positive power G of N, the actual absolute-pair price even after integrating the oscillatory kernel satisfies

    sum_(N<n,m<=T; gcd(n,m)<G)
       |a(n)a(m)|(nm)^(-2)|K_N(n,m)| >> N^(-3).     (20)

Here T eventually contains the fixed narrow interval, and all coefficients are the actual squarefree Mobius coefficients. Replacing mu(n)mu(m) by its absolute value loses exactly the needed power at the level of this route. Equation(20) does NOT lower-bound the signed core or the actual local energy. It rules out the specified absolute-kernel repair, not a cancellation theorem, and is compatible with RH.

Repair A was to subtract the computable leading term in(7), whose remainder already has the formal half-power needed for c=1/4. This fails as a positive localization argument. A difference of scalar energies has no inherited inequality controlling the energy on a subinterval. Implementing the subtraction as any fixed finite normalized linear combination of the underlying fields fails by(9). A growing-scale family remains outside(9) and would require its own observation and conditioning costs.

Repair B was to remove the first Fourier band, leaving a possibly smaller global source. At x=0 that actual band is

    B_N(0)=2 sum_(N<n<=2N)mu(n)chi(n)/n^r.           (21)

To bound(21) by N^(gamma-r+epsilon) for every integer N at a stronger gamma would already give the needed new Mertens estimate: sum(21) over N,2N,4N,... to obtain T_N with the same exponent, since gamma<r, and apply(14). Conversely a Mertens bound gives that estimate by Abel summation. Thus the removed band cannot be charged an improved bound as though it were an innocuous known error. Paying it only with the incumbent Mertens exponent returns at most the incumbent. The exact spectral gap does not exempt this entire band.

## 7. Trying actual squarefree averaging in the localized Gram

The next attempted repair keeps the signed mu(a)mu(b) and uses only the arithmetic square mu(g)^2. This is the source of the global half-power error in(7); it is natural to test whether the same averaging works after localization. The following restricted theorem identifies the precise loss.

For an integer H>=1, let E_(N,H) be the part of E_arc(N) with reduced quotients a=n/g,b=m/g both <=H. This is a symmetric signed sector, not necessarily a positive energy. For H<=N, define

    J_(a,b)=integral_(1/min(a,b))^infinity v^(-2r)
               integral_0^(1/q) Phi(av u)conjugate(Phi(bv u))du dv,

    D_H=sum_(a,b<=H; (a,b)=1; (ab,q)=1)
        mu(a)mu(b)chi(a)conjugate(chi(b))
            delta(abq) J_(a,b)/(ab)^r.

Then, for every fixed epsilon>0,

    E_(N,H)=N^(-2r)D_H
             +O_(q,r,epsilon)(N^(-2r-1/2)H^(3/2+epsilon)),
    |D_H|<<_(q,r) H.                               (22)

These statements do not use a hypothetical Mobius correlation estimate. To prove them, keep g as the variable carrying mu(g)^2 and substitute x=u/N. For each reduced pair a,b the summand before the outer coefficient is

    N^(-2r-1) sum_(g>N/min(a,b); (g,abq)=1)
                     mu(g)^2 F_(a,b)(g/N),
    F_(a,b)(v)=v^(-2r) integral_0^(1/q)
                          Phi(av u)conjugate(Phi(bv u))du.

Apply(5) by partial summation. Boundedness and the Lipschitz bound for Phi give, almost everywhere,

    |F(v)|<=C_(q,r)v^(-2r),
    |F'(v)|<=C_(q,r)[v^(-2r-1)+(a+b)v^(-2r)].

With m=min(a,b), the error for that pair is at most

    C_(q,r) 2^omega(abq) N^(-2r-1/2)
       [m^(2r-1/2)+(a+b)m^(2r-3/2)]/(ab)^r.

For a<=b, summing the first term gives O(H^(3/2+epsilon)); the part involving b uses sum_(a<=b<=H)b^(1-r), which gives the same bound (an inessential logarithm when r=2 is absorbed by epsilon). The part involving a is no larger than the first term. This proves the error in(22). The main term satisfies |J_(a,b)|<=C min(a,b)^(2r-1); after a<=b, summing a^(r-1)b^(-r) gives O(H), proving the second bound. The derivative jumps of the periodic Bernoulli functions do not contribute hidden atoms: Phi is continuous and Lipschitz, so the displayed first derivative bounds suffice for absolute-continuity partial summation.

This is where the tempting global proof changes. In(7), complete-period Fourier orthogonality supplies an extra factor (ab)^(-r), making the density-error sum convergent over every quotient. In the localized sector that factor is absent, and the accumulated error is H^(3/2+epsilon). At H on the order of N, the error returns to N^(1-2r+epsilon), with no power gain. Moreover H=N still omits a,b>N; those contain the genuinely small-gcd pairs in the finite core and cannot be called a negligible tail. For comparison, choosing H=N^(1-2c-kappa) makes both parts of(22) smaller than the desired energy. This only covers a sector already included in the paid large-gcd region g>N/H; it is not a new endpoint improvement.

Thus there is a proved, uniform arithmetic sector approximation, but using it at the scale needed for the full source requires a new cancellation or density-discrepancy estimate. The failed extension is quantitative: one must improve the H^(3/2) accumulated error, and control the omitted large quotients, rather than simply quote squarefree equidistribution. No assertion that equality in this coarse error is an impossibility theorem is made.

## 8. Result, limits, and next live action

This pass proves an exact all-character periodic source, the signed global asymptotic(7) with strictly positive leading coefficient, the finite-scale obstruction(9), the complete localized observation/zero return(10)-(14), the finite signed core with paid large-gcd and infinite-tail complements(15)-(17), an actual absolute-kernel lower price(20), and the restricted squarefree-density approximation(22). The classical identities underlying the source are credited above; the role claimed here is an independently derived research component and a decisive test of this proposed route, not literature priority.

No improvement in c has been proved. The actual open estimate is(16) with c>.125140 after the controller's calibration update. At c=1/4 the cutoff for the odd-character r=3 source is only N^(1.1+kappa), but its small-gcd kernel still needs a half-power signed saving. Finite length, low rank, smooth profiles, or the exact global remainder do not supply that saving.

The useful redirect is precise. Complete-period gcd spectral improvements and fixed finite scale differences cannot prove the required localization. The next arithmetic attack must retain the signed incomplete-period small-gcd kernel, or develop a genuinely growing filter with a paid observation bound. A density argument must address the accumulated H^(3/2) error and the large-quotient sector explicitly. The all-real-scale old Q/Core route and its equivalence are not relabelled as a result of this pass; the source and the obstruction here are different.

This pass does not modify the accepted PR9/PR15 proof, its original sources, descendants, shortened slots, density bins, or their source-relative qualifications. It replaces none of them without its own open hypothesis. All-height ordinary zero exclusion is a conditional consequence of(16), proved above. No new Hecke/Eisenstein statement, uniform-in-conductor estimate, source-free c7 certificate, or formal proof is claimed.

## 9. Verification and evidence limits

The owned helper check.py was written independently for this source and executed once successfully. checks.json records 1,080 coefficient/spectral-gap/first-band cases for six actual characters, including an imprimitive principal character and a quartic complex character; 21,600 exact character-phase cases including natural zeros; exact endpoint-polynomial moments and norms for r=2,3; and a 72-interval rational integration of a finite Bernoulli source agreeing exactly with its full signed gcd Gram. It also verifies the local original-cell projection, the positive-kernel rational margin and the exact exponent budgets. These finite checks corroborate identities and normalization, not the infinite asymptotic, an all-scale cancellation estimate, or any zero-free theorem. The analytic arguments are in the preceding sections.

The local Python launcher printed its existing real-location diagnostic but returned exit0 and the complete PASS receipt; it was not silently retried. No author helper in another scope was run. Source provenance and exact local source hashes are in sources.json. Public primary-source evidence records the inspected published version, page and formula locations; it does not mislabel a web rendering hash as a hash of the PDF bytes. The c7 controller acceptance receipt was read completely; its remaining PR9/Gao ancestry and admission qualifications are retained above. No underlying c7 author audit was duplicated.

At final freeze all owned output is read back in full and its exact byte sizes and SHA256 values are recorded in freeze.json. The freeze is an evidence record, not independent mathematical acceptance.

Take

\[
b=\frac{8749}{10000},\qquad
K=X^{187/500}=X^{.374},\qquad
P=X^{7489/10000}=X^{.7489}.
\tag{SP25}
\]

These choices satisfy \(K\le Y/2\) for large \(X\). The single-edge
and nearby-product costs both have exponent

\[
b+\frac12+.374=1+.7489
=\frac{17489}{10000}=1.7489,
\qquad
1.74898-1.7489=\frac1{12500}.
\tag{SP26}
\]

The overlap cost has exponent \(1+2(.374)=1.748\), with margin
\(49/50000\). All arbitrary small losses can be chosen below the
displayed fixed margins. For general \(K=X^\kappa\), a fixed margin
is available when

\[
\kappa<\min\{1.24898-b,\ .37449\}.
\tag{SP27}
\]

Optimizing over the accepted \(b>b_0\) therefore permits every
\(\kappa<.374093352960035869\ldots\). No improvement of the accepted
Mertens exponent is used in this optimization.

Define \(Q_{\rm far}\) by retaining all original conditions in the
expanded quartic form and additionally imposing

\[
|rd_i-sd_j|>X^{.374}
\quad(ij\in\{13,14,23,24\},\ 1\le r,s\le J),
\qquad
|\ell de-mfh|>X^{.7489}.
\tag{SP28}
\]

First remove \(A(K)\) by (SP13). Then apply (SP21) to the nearby
product band on its complement. This is the signed identity with
controlled remainder

\[
Q_{\rm good}=Q_{\rm far}
+O_\epsilon(X^{1.7489+\epsilon}).
\tag{SP29}
\]

Both removed sectors are directly bounded signed quartic forms. This
does not change the distinction between squared-energy subtraction and
the \(L^2\) triangle step in MG34. The previous gcd costs retain their
already established exponent \(4897/2800\); the present bounds do not
reprove or weaken them.

## 4. Independent general-phase strengthening and its honest scope

The full proof is in support.md; this is its decisive calculation. For fixed b>1, integer k>=4 and H=X^k/N^(k-1), retain the N/G^2 version of (R5). The comparable block has both bounds

    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)[HN/G^2+N^2/G^3],
    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)(N/G)(1+H).

Their minimum is at most the common factor times

    X^k/(G^2N^(k-2))+N/G
                     +min(N^2/G^3,X^k N^(2-k)/G).      (R7)

Absorb N^(2eta) into the actual damping at the cost X^(2b eta). This is essential at k=4 and for G not bounded by a power of X; using G^eta<=X^epsilon would be false. The last two branches meet at N_*=XG^(2/k). Their complete geometric sum is

    O_k(X^2 G^(4/k-3)) <=O_k(X^2/G^2), k>=4.            (R8)

The first term sums from N>=cX to X^2/G^2, while damping pays the isolated N/G term by X^b/G. Both far orientations sum to X^(2+2eta)/G^2; low/high triangle remains unchanged. This proves (R2).

Consequently the additional large-gcd complement with G=X^(1-gamma) is paid whenever gamma>=b-1, for every k>=4. The author's additional condition gamma>=(k+2)/(3k-2) is a sufficient condition extracted from its weaker displayed general bound, not a necessary restriction of this complement. All old square-source, derivative-gap and full-tail conditions remain required separately. This review does not obtain a new complete architecture merely by lowering k.

Two scoped lower examples clarify the result. The author's mask retaining d=e=r, G<r<=2G and r^2 l<=X/2 has full positive real part and norm at least cX/G for G<=c' sqrt(X). For the damped diagonal, put Y=floor(X^b), retain d=e=r, G<r<=2G and Y/2<r^2 l<=Y. Its output multiplicities A_n have sum A_n^2>=sum A_n>>Y/G for G<=c' sqrt(Y). Assign each output n an independent sign epsilon_n, common to all its tuples. The second and fourth sign moments give

    E|sum epsilon_n z_n| >=(sum |z_n|^2)^(1/2)/sqrt(3).

Since |f_x(n)|>=e^-1 throughout the shell, integrating this finite expectation proves that some ONE frozen sign mask has L1 norm at least cX^(b/2)/sqrt(G), and hence the same L2 lower price. This is a deterministic existence consequence of a finite probability calculation, with no sampled signs or average over actual arithmetic. It says nothing about a lower bound for the real Liouville signs. The broad-class condition gamma>=b-1 cannot generally be dropped for gamma>1/2.

The refinement is useful analytic progress in a paid component. It supplies no power saving in the retained small-gcd sum. Improving the already paid large-gcd component again would not settle the research target.

### 3.3 Character-specific transform and all-height zero return

For Re s>1, exact Euler/Fubini gives Mellin(F_chi)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi). At p!=3,

    H_(chi,p)=(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2;
    H_(chi,3)=(1-chi(3)3^-s)^-2.

At every p|q the factor is1, including2 or3 when ramified. At unramified p>=5, the degree-one term cancels, so the product converges absolutely locally for sigma>1/2. Numerator zero lines are sigma=log_p2<1/2; denominators have possible zero lines sigma=0. At2 the numerator zero line is sigma=1, which must remain exceptional;3 has no numerator. Thus H_chi is holomorphic/nonzero for1/2<sigma<1. Complex characters alter phases, not these real parts.

The fixed field has a Gaussian left tail. Dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz with an epsilon smaller than the compact strip distance makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on sigma>gamma, with every fixed derivative. Multiplying by L and continuing the exact identity gives a contradiction at each L-zero with gamma<Re rho<1, because exp(tau*rho^2/2)H_chi(rho)!=0. The usual independently known right boundary handles sigma>=1; principal pole treatment is meromorphic and not a falsely excluded zero. There is no height cutoff or requirement of a nonvanishing p2 numerator at sigma=1. This is a separate fixed-chi implication: zeta-only OPEN-D04 does not imply the needed field estimate for every chi. No growing-conductor, angular or new Eisenstein transfer is proved.

**Verdict:** ACCEPT D04.7 as an ordinary fixed-character conditional zero return. The exact f3 transform is a changed source relative to matched-Max's mu detector, not a harmless renaming. Its character zeros, p2/p3 factors and conditional c=1-gamma are all retained.

## 3. Simultaneous detectors can cover numerator zeros

The genuinely different simultaneous opportunity is the unprojected quartic
phase family over K=Q(i). For fixed excluded primes and a fixed bounded
positive-length interval I,

    F_t(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1+it) F_K(X/Nd²),
    Mellin(F_t)(s)=M(s)L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2)/zeta_K^S(s).

The squarefree part c and square part d need not be coprime. The denominator
is fixed, while the auxiliary numerator moves with t. Assuming the fixed
profile M is nonzero in the target half-plane, the full estimate

    integral_I ||F_t||_[X,2X]^2 dt <<_epsilon X^(2a+epsilon)

excludes every zero of zeta_K^S in Re(s)>a: at a hypothetical zero, the
L2(I)-valued numerator cannot vanish identically, by the identity theorem for
the fixed L-function. All multiplicities are covered. The original merged
profile was stipulated, not specified; choosing the geometric or reviewed
near-log profile supplies nonvanishing but requires the actual arithmetic
estimate for that profile. This is a Q(i), hence ordinary-zeta, return; it is
not automatically the project's whole fixed ordinary/Eisenstein-Hecke scope.

There is quantitative capture on any fixed compact height window using
m0=min_s max_t|N_s(t)|>0 and a derivative bound. There is no supplied numerical
all-height lower bound. For arithmetic energy, O_A(log X) positive Gauss
quadrature samples of the phase approximate the full fixed-I norm to any
X^-A error, since the phase bandwidth is O(log X). Their nodes move with X;
this is not a finite fixed list known to cover all zeros. The d,e crosses
inside each sampled energy remain fully present.

The overlap cost is decisive. Direct absolute transfer from F_K at exponent
a to F_t costs sum_(Nd<=sqrt X) Nd^(1-2a), losing X^(1-a) and leaving only X.
Attenuating by Nd^(-2tau) makes both the convolution and its Dirichlet inverse
bounded when **a+tau>1**, with constants at most zeta_K^S(2a+2tau-1).
At the current boundary this requires tau>.125136. This safe family is
equivalent to the original norm problem. The unattenuated family may have
better coupled source geometry, but its complete arithmetic estimate is open.

Projection can destroy the reason for using the family. At a good odd local
place, compact averaging with the first two source vectors fixed sends every
unary vector to its one-dimensional spherical projection. The resulting
phase family is A(t) times one vector with the SAME arithmetic L numerator;
A(t)=zeta_K^S(2-it)/zeta_K^S(2) is nonzero. Thus that projected family cannot
cover each other's numerator zeros. The unprojected family must be retained
through the needed estimate.

statement:
# [private research revision]: weighted physical radical mass

**Status: proved relative to the stated physical inputs; independently reviewed by the cubic lane.** HC1–HC18 retain all declared restrictions. The accepted zero-free constant is unchanged. No new I-HECKE assertion is used.

Sources: `[restricted mathematical source]` PC1-PC15, especially the repaired forced-valuation convention in PC4; `[restricted mathematical source]` T06-T07; and the saved geometry in `[restricted mathematical source]`. Preserve the exact definitions
\[
Q=q_{b_*}XY,\qquad P_a=Y^2/Q,\qquad Y_D=Y/q_D.
\]
The fixed factor \(q_{b_*}\) is not set to one.

## Full sector and exact residual

For polynomial \(1\le T\le Z^C\), the full estimate, including arbitrary outer powers, actual marks, unequal embeddings, and bounded row-independent masks, is
\[
\boxed{\sum_{R\le T}|C_{\lambda\mu}-Z_{\lambda\mu}|
 \ll_{\epsilon,C} Z^\epsilon\frac{L^{5/3}T}{QY^{2/3}}.} \tag{HC1}
\]
The sum is the absolute atom-pair sum in the PC convention; for \(R>1\), the complete zero \(Z_{\lambda\mu}\) vanishes. Consequently PC15 becomes
\[
\mathcal C_< =\mathcal C_{<,R>T}
 +O_\epsilon\!\left(Z^\epsilon\left[Y^{-1}
 +\frac{L^{5/3}T}{QY^{2/3}}\right]\right). \tag{HC2}
\]
For the target \(Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon\), the exact affordable threshold is
\[
\boxed{T_* = \frac{QY^{-1/3}P_a^{1/6}}{L^{5/3}}
 =\left(\frac{Q}{L^2}\right)^{5/6}.} \tag{HC3}
\]
At the saved geometry, where \(X=Z^x,Y=Z^y,L=Z^\ell\), write
\[
T_*=q_{b_*}^{5/6}Z^{\tau_*^{\rm rad}},\qquad
\tau_*^{\rm rad}=\frac56(x+y-2\ell)
=\frac{12347}{30000}=0.4115666666666666\ldots.
\]
This decimal is the **scale exponent**, not the exact finite-\(Z\) logarithm:
\(\log_ZT_*=\tau_*^{\rm rad}+\tfrac56\log_Zq_{b_*}\).
The old PC14 affordable threshold has scale exponent
\(0.21799823482243477\ldots\). In particular \(R\le Z^{2/5}\) is paid with a strict scale-exponent margin \(0.0115666\ldots\).

## 1. Keep the actual local Gauss size

For a good prime of norm \(q\), define
\[
B_p(j)=\begin{cases}
1,&j=0,\\
q^{(j-1)/2},&j>0,\ 6\nmid j,\\
q^{j/2},&j>0,\ 6\mid j,
\end{cases}
\qquad B(a)=\prod_p B_p(v_p(a)). \tag{HC4}
\]
PC2 gives the middle value exactly on its forced valuation. PC3 has divisibility-coefficient mass
\[
q^{j/2-1}(q+1)=(1+q^{-1})B_p(j).
\]
Multiplying the two exact local kernels, retaining forced row valuations at every \(p\mid\mathfrak r\), and expanding divisibility masks only outside \(\mathfrak r\), refines PC4 to
\[
K(r)=K_S(r)\sum_k b_k1_{k\mid r}\psi_{\mathfrak r}(r/k),\qquad
\sum_k|b_k|\ll_\epsilon B(a)B(b)(q_aq_bq_Aq_{A'})^\epsilon.
\tag{HC5}
\]
All original zero extensions remain. At conductor primes, the residual primitive character supplies the exact unit support after the forced valuation substitution. Thus
\[
|\text{row sum}|\ll_\epsilon B(a)B(b)\sqrt R
(q_aq_bq_Aq_{A'})^\epsilon\quad(R>1). \tag{HC6}
\]
For \(R=1\), the same bound without \(\sqrt R\) applies to row sum minus complete zero.

The common profile remains exactly
\[
W_0(q_r/(Hx_a))\overline{W_0(q_r/(Hx_b))},\qquad
H=Q/q_{[D,E]}^2.
\]
This uses the same uniform smooth character Poisson estimate as PC5, including \(H/q_k<1\). Fixed-place factors stay in the inherited fixed family. No separate physical row scale is assigned to an embedded branch.

## 2. Weighted coherent mass

Work first on the coherent primes using PC6:
\[
\begin{gathered}
c=gu,\quad c'=gv,\qquad n=hys^2,\quad n'=hxt^2,\\
a=d_0u x^3r_1^6,\qquad b=d_0v y^3r_2^6,\qquad
x\mid e,\ y\mid d.
\end{gathered} \tag{HC7}
\]
Retain every local support restriction before taking a positive majorant. Split \(d_0\) canonically as \(d_0=d_\circ f^6\): at a prime whose positive \(d_0\)-valuation is divisible by six, place its entire power in \(f^6\); place every other positive valuation in \(d_\circ\). In particular \((d_\circ,f)=1\). On the surviving coherent support,
\[
\boxed{B(a)B(b)=
\frac{q_{d_0}}{q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}}
(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3q_xq_y.} \tag{HC8}
\]

The local justification includes the unequal embeddings:

- Away from \(de\), a prime dividing \(AA'\) forces unit \(r\) and outer exponents zero or one. A residual core incidence \(u\) or \(v\) cannot overlap \(d_0\) or a residual sixth power. Its \(B\)-factor is one.
- Away from \(AA'de\), coherence gives \(\alpha\equiv\beta\pmod6\). A common exponent \(j>0\) contributes \(q^{j-1}\) when \(6\nmid j\), and \(q^j\) when \(6\mid j\). Each residual sixth power contributes its cube to \(B(a)B(b)\), exactly as in HC8. Zero common exponent also has the stated factor.
- At \(p\mid e\), natural zeros require \(A\) to be a unit. If \(p\mid A'\), the unit row restricts outer exponents to \(\alpha\in\{0,3\}\), \(\beta\in\{0,1\}\). The coherent exponent-three case is precisely \(p\mid x\), contributing \(q_p\); \(d_0\) and residual sixth powers cannot overlap it. The case \(p\mid d\) is symmetric and contributes \(q_y\).
- At an embedding-only prime, coherent nonprincipal positive outer exponents would require both \(\alpha-\beta=\pm2\) and \(\alpha\equiv\beta\pmod6\); they cannot survive. Principal multiples of six remain covered by HC8.

This preserves the exponent-three embedding exception rather than imposing a squarefree outer restriction.

Temporarily write \(U=Y_D,V=Y_E\). The completed coefficient remains
\[
(q_g\sqrt{q_uq_v}\,q_h^2q_xq_yq_s^2q_t^2)^{-1}.
\]
The outer annuli give the original PC7 count
\[
\sum_{u,v}(q_uq_v)^{-1/2}
\ll\frac{\sqrt{UV}}
{q_{d_0}(q_xq_y)^{3/2}(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3}.
\]
After multiplying HC8, the remaining factors involving \(d_0,x,y,r_i\) are
\[
\frac{\sqrt{UV}}
{q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}(q_xq_y)^{3/2}}. \tag{HC9}
\]
The sixth-power factors have not disappeared: their number must now be counted. Since \(u,v\) are nonzero ideals, the outer supports imply
\[
q_fq_{r_1}\ll\left(\frac{U}{q_{d_\circ}q_x^3}\right)^{1/6},
\qquad
q_fq_{r_2}\ll\left(\frac{V}{q_{d_\circ}q_y^3}\right)^{1/6}.
\]
Ideal counting and the convergent \(f\)-sum give
\[
\sum_{f,r_1,r_2}1
\ll(UV)^{1/6}q_{d_\circ}^{-1/3}(q_xq_y)^{-1/2}
\sum_fq_f^{-2}
\ll(UV)^{1/6}q_{d_\circ}^{-1/3}(q_xq_y)^{-1/2}. \tag{HC10}
\]
Dropping coprimality restrictions is harmless in this positive count. The remaining \(d_\circ\)-sum converges:
\[
\sum_{d_\circ}\frac1{q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}q_{d_\circ}^{1/3}}
\le\prod_{p\notin S}\left(1+\sum_{j\ge1}q_p^{-1-j/3}\right)
<\infty. \tag{HC11}
\]
The \(x,y\) exponents have become two; the \(h,s,t\) exponents remain two.

As in PC8, sum the harmonic common-core variable \(g\) against the two original rapid envelopes before discarding their dependence. Its sum is uniform in both scales. Thus it can precede the displayed positive outer counts. The actual \(K_D,K_E\) marks remain bounded by T06's divisor envelope, with no extra slot count. Small powers of arbitrarily large completed columns are absorbed into the original two-sided rapid envelopes. All infinite cube tails and the unit ideal remain included. Consequently
\[
\boxed{\mathscr M_{\rm coh}^{B}(U,V)
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon(UV)^{2/3}.} \tag{HC12}
\]

## 3. A fixed relative conductor retains its inverse square root

Fix a good radical \(\mathfrak r\). Split all six labels into their \(\mathfrak r\)-parts and coprime parts. The latter obey HC12 at
\[
U=Y_D/q_{a_R},\qquad V=Y_E/q_{b_R}.
\]
If one of these scales is below the nonempty outer-support range, there are no terms; their bounded lower endpoints are harmless. Each conductor prime contributes
\[
M_p^B=\sum_{\substack{\alpha,\beta\ge0,\ i,j\in\{0,1\},\ k,l\ge0\\
i-j+3(k-l)-\alpha+\beta\not\equiv0\ (6)}}
B_p(\alpha)B_p(\beta)
q_p^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/3-(i+j)/2-k-l}. \tag{HC13}
\]
The extra \(1/6\) in each outer exponent comes from counting the coherent sixth powers after the conductor parts consume their outer length.

Put \(F_p=\sum_{j\ge0}B_p(j)q_p^{-2j/3}\). Direct summation gives
\[
F_p=1+\frac{q_p^{-2/3}+q_p^{-5/6}+2q_p^{-1}
+q_p^{-7/6}+q_p^{-4/3}}{1-q_p^{-1}}
=1+O(q_p^{-2/3}). \tag{HC14}
\]
The zero exponent vector is excluded from HC13. Enlarging to every other vector gives
\[
M_p^B\le F_p^2
\frac{(1+q_p^{-1/2})^2}{(1-q_p^{-1})^2}-1
\ll q_p^{-1/2}. \tag{HC15}
\]
The local constants have subpower product, so
\[
\boxed{\mathscr M_{\mathfrak r}^{B}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon(Y_DY_E)^{2/3}R^{-1/2+\epsilon}.} \tag{HC16}
\]
This is an absolute coefficient estimate, not a change of the actual field. The original roots, ray factors, signed marks, collision masks and profiles remain in that field. No prime of \(\mathfrak r\) is moved into the fixed excluded set. Polynomial conductor ranges allow the displayed small powers to be absorbed in the final \(Z^\epsilon\).

## 4. Physical normalization and embedding sum

Multiply HC16 by \(\sqrt R\) from row Poisson and by the raw normalization \((Y_DY_E)^{-1}\). For a fixed radical this gives
\(Z^\epsilon(Y_DY_E)^{-1/3}\). PC9's physical factor is exactly
\[
\frac1{Q\sqrt{q_Dq_E}}.
\]
The fixed-\((D,E,\mathfrak r)\) bound is therefore
\[
Z^\epsilon\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|}
{QY^{2/3}(q_Dq_E)^{1/6}}. \tag{HC17}
\]
For the original fixed slot subsets,
\[
\sum_D\frac{|\omega_D|}{q_D^{1/6}}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon L^{5/6}.
\]
There are \(O(T)\) good radicals of norm at most \(T\); this proves HC1. For \(R=1\), use the discrepancy version of HC5-HC6 and the same mass calculation. In particular PC10 improves to
\[
\sum_{R=1}|C_{\lambda\mu}-Z_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\frac{L^{5/3}}{QY^{2/3}}.
\]
PC11 still supplies the absolute complete-zero bound \(Z^\epsilon/Y\), proving HC2.

The proof sums absolute atom-pair row covariances after each row sum. Hence arbitrary bounded row-independent masks, including true-gcd cutoffs and true gcd one, are permitted. It does not infer positivity for a gcd mask, allow arbitrary row-dependent masks, or define a pair-dependent vector projection.

## 5. Locally nonprincipal outer refinement

In the sector where every positive outer valuation is nonzero modulo six, the surviving coherent coprime parts have \(r_1=r_2=1\), and \(f=1\). Away from the embeddings the exact nonprincipal row valuations force equal outer exponents; the unequal embedding cases are already the exponent-three factors in HC7. This sector includes every squarefree outer column and arbitrarily high nonprincipal exponents.

Rankin's bound gives
\[
\sum_{q_{d_\circ}\ll Y}q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}^{-1}
\ll_\epsilon Y^\epsilon,
\]
because inserting \(q_{d_\circ}^{-\epsilon}\) produces the convergent product
\(\prod_p(1+\sum_{j\ge1}q_p^{-1-j\epsilon})\).
Thus HC9 directly gives weighted coherent mass
\(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Y_DY_E}\), since the \(x,y\) exponents remain \(3/2>1\).

At a conductor prime, the outer exponent weights are now
\(B_p(\alpha)q_p^{-\alpha/2}=q_p^{-1/2}\) for positive allowed \(\alpha\). Regularize the arbitrarily high exponent sums by a factor \(q_p^{-\delta\alpha}\). The compensating global factor \((q_aq_b)^\delta\) is affordable on the original polynomial outer annuli, with \(\delta>0\) fixed sufficiently small for the final epsilon. The resulting local nonzero mass is \(O_\delta(q_p^{-1/2})\); its constants again have subpower product. The same fixed-radical calculation gives
\[
\boxed{|\mathcal C_{\theta,\,1<R\le T}^{\rm locally\ nonprincipal}|
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\frac{L^2T}{QY}.} \tag{HC18}
\]
Its exact threshold is
\[
T_{\rm np}=\frac{QP_a^{1/6}}{L^2}
=\frac{Q^{5/6}Y^{1/3}}{L^2}
=q_{b_*}^{5/6}Z^{\tau_{\rm np}},
\]
where the saved **scale exponent** is
\[
\tau_{\rm np}=x+y+(y-x)/6-2\ell
=0.5083508825887826\ldots.
\]
The exact finite-\(Z\) logarithm additionally contains
\(\tfrac56\log_Zq_{b_*}\). Positive multiples of six are excluded only from HC18, not from HC1.

## Objection, sanity check, and remaining gap

The strongest objection to a careless argument is real: principal sixth powers cannot be assigned subpower total mass. Their Gauss amplitudes cancel the apparent \(r_i^{-3}\) decay. HC10 explicitly pays their count, producing the \((Y_DY_E)^{1/6}\) loss. Treating all \(d_0\)-powers as though they had the nonprincipal \(1/\operatorname{rad}(d_0)\) weight would give an unsupported stronger theorem.

A deterministic finite sanity check covered 157 surviving local configurations with unequal embedding valuations, core exponents zero or one, cube exponents through four, and outer exponents through eighteen. HC8 had no failures. This is only a finite arithmetic check; the local case argument above supplies the proof.

This does not improve the accepted \(c_0\). Generic coprime \(A,A',a,b\) can have \(R\asymp Y^2(ZL)^2\), far above both thresholds. The true-gcd conductor in T07 remains a separate object. The full physical residual is reduced to \(R>(Q/L^2)^{5/6}\), and its locally nonprincipal outer portion further to \(R>T_{\rm np}\). The same-core theorem, T07 tail, original numerator/contour transfer and all-height requirements are neither replaced nor strengthened here.

## 6. Size of the new payment and the primitive-row obstruction

At `gamma=1/4`, `K=D^.87653`, and the fixed choice `delta=.02`,

\[
 \Lambda=D^{.03449},\qquad
 \min(C_*,E_*)\ge D^{.89653}.
\tag{SR17}
\]

This is a part of the double-large-core C--C range well beyond BC's
small-core band. It includes both ordered columns, moving outside
cubes and their opposite deletions, the full common-gcd projector,
and every row in each chosen quadratic class. Even the bare cube
pair `B=E=1` illustrates a power improvement: separate I-HECKE
Möbius bounds, with `b>b0`, and the `O(H^(1/2))` class count give
only `D^(2b+epsilon) sqrt(K)`. Its limiting exponent at the displayed
K is `2.188038294079928...`; SR2 gives `2+epsilon`. This comparison
is solely an upper-bound comparison, not a lower bound for that
class's actual sum.

The result does **not** extend by declaring d to be a moving datum.
For a squarefree dual row n, its quadratic square class has
representative `d=n`. At a good prime p dividing n, the quotient
needed to replace `bar chi_c(n^2)` by `chi_c(n)` is the ramified
quadratic character `chi_c(p)^3`. A fixed finite family of twists
unramified at p cannot provide it. On local units such twists are
trivial on inertia, while this quotient has order two. Deletion
masks are also identically one on these units. Thus the exact inverse
deletion identity does not turn a moving ramified quadratic twist
into a fixed datum. This is a local obstruction to the proposed
**freeze-the-conductor and use the short-row moment** shortcut.

There is a second, quantitative obstruction even if one grants
uniform constants for every `nu rho_d`. Separate estimates

\[
 \sum_{u\asymp H}|M_{\nu\rho_d,u}(D)|^2\ll H
 \quad\hbox{for each }d
\]

alone bound the moving diagonal `u=d`, `q_d~H`, only by `H^2`.
An array `M_{d,u}=sqrt(H) 1_(u=d)` satisfies every such separate
estimate and saturates that diagonal bound. This logical example
is not asserted to be a Möbius counterexample; it proves that the
separate moment inequalities, even uniformly stated, do not imply
the desired diagonal estimate. At the balanced physical
normalization `D^2/H`, this shortcut costs `D^2 H`.

The exact remaining primitive-row target is still a joint diagonal
moment, with the normalized columns, original masks and projector
described above:

\[
\boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{q_n\asymp H\\n\ {\rm squarefree}}}
 \left|D^{-1/2}\sum_{(c,R)=1}\mu(c)\nu(c)
       \rho_n(c)\chi_c(n)F(q_c/D)\right|^2
 \ll T^A H(DHq_R)^\epsilon,\qquad H=D^2/K.}
\tag{SR18}
\]

One must keep the full projector when using this as a covariance
input. A quadratic large sieve cannot simply be applied to
`rho_n(c)`: its accompanying factor `chi_c(n)` also depends on n,
and their product is exactly the original cubic character. Guo's
fixed-datum short-row assertion is unproved in any event; the new
theorem above does not use it. At the present physical balanced
length H>D, ordinary inherited UM already suffices for the fixed
classes, whereas the moving diagonal is a different estimate.

The projection in SR2 is made in the **actual C--C Poisson formula**.
It is not an identification with a piece of II. In particular, no
frequency in the whole II subtraction is removed, no fixed-class
residue is identified with II, and no positivity of the signed
kernel is assumed. Subtracting the paid SR2 contribution leaves
the remaining double-large-core C--C Poisson rows and outside
cubes, **minus the original whole II**. The large primitive class
of DQ12 remains in that remainder.

## 8. Actual row split, complete residual and the unclosed sector

Retain ALL previously paid classes, in their existing order, first.
Only on their remaining class Omega_out use the exact old signal
|C_T^[1-theta]|>|B|/4. Define the new actual class

    Omega_pair={u in Omega_out: |C_T^[omega](u)|>=|B(u)|/8}.

Its predicate refers to the original same-zero, same-height values.
On this class |M Q|<=8|C_T^[omega]Q|/|S(D)|. Dividing(2) by the
ORIGINAL plain spike in(4) cancels D^beta, giving

    sum_(Omega_pair)w_u|M_u(R)Q_u|^2
       << H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).              (19)

Every remaining row has |C_T^[omega]|<|B|/8 and therefore(3).
No signal is divided by a shifted shortened factor, and Q is never divided
out. The full remaining coefficient is exactly the original signed tuple
coefficient times 1-theta-omega. By(9) this preserves all previous vanishing
coefficients. Multiplying by it cannot create a merged coefficient outside
the necessary support N(n/rad n)<T NP. Original band prime squares remain
absent because p^2|b with Np>=A forces F>=A^2=T. The new lower band's
prime squares are allowed and were explicitly paid in(13),(15).

There is a quantitative coefficient effect in a previously untouched
case. If all prime factors of b lie in J and its tuple survives F<T, then

    log N(b/rad b) <= 2log Ns2(b) <4eta log U,
    ell_rad,J(b)>log Nb-4eta log U,
    d_1,J(b)<=2eta(log U)(log Nb).

Writing e_b=eta log U/log Nb, which is small in the actual positive m
range, equations(8) and theta=0 imply

    0<=1-omega(b)<=[1-(1-4e_b)^2]+2e_b<=10e_b.       (20)

This is a genuine damping of those actual tuple coefficients, not a bound
for their signed sum. It gives a constant small factor at fixed eta, not
a U-power saving, and does not itself permit deleting this sector.

If b is a good prime ideal at its original plain scale D, then for large U
it lies above Y and outside J. On any coprime squarefree inverse tuple,
F=1 and theta=omega=0. Such a source coefficient is unchanged. Likewise
many tuples with only one distinct J prime have omega=0 unless that prime

The full coarse norm is still explicitly paid by

    C_T^[1-theta-omega]=C_T-C_T^[theta]-C_T^[omega].

The complete old norm of C_T is H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon); the other two
norms have the proved saving. Hilbert triangle gives that same coarse

OPEN-OUT-PAIR is the actual remaining estimate

    ||C_T^[1-theta-omega] Q||_Omega_rem^2
         << H_J U^(1+beta*m-eta+epsilon),             (21)

or another complete arithmetic estimate giving the same original inverse
moment saving on those actual rows. With it, the disjoint paid classes
would complete G137's J_eta^all; G137 then gives its stated complete free
and raw-row envelope saving. No new physical endpoint is assigned here.
Every positive child would need its own actual witness, source and live

All physical roots, counts, missing radicals, extraction scalars, BOTH

### 2.2 Separate line budget and its strict endpoint

The stronger height-sensitive input P_(a,kappa) is not derived from LP. It says, for every epsilon>0, some fixed A,C independent of y,t satisfy

    |H_y(a+it)|<=C(1+|t|)^A y^(kappa+epsilon)

for all dyadic y and every real t. Fix b>1, D>1, integer m>A, and apply three-lines to f_k(s)/(s+D)^m on a<=Re s<=b. The denominator has no pole in the strip. For each fixed y, the finite prime power-series sums and finite integral in(C1) are uniformly bounded in t on this closed strip. Division by the polynomial therefore supplies the required horizontal boundary control; no unproved uniform meromorphic reciprocal bound enters.

The exact exponent is

    E=[(kappa+epsilon)(b-sigma)+(1-b)(sigma-a)]/(b-a).

Without epsilon its zero is

    r_b=(b kappa+(b-1)a)/(kappa+b-1)
       =a+kappa+kappa(1-a-kappa)/(kappa+b-1).             (C6)

For a+kappa<1 and kappa>0, r_b decreases to a+kappa as b grows. For any fixed compact strictly to its right, choose finite b first, then a sufficiently small epsilon. E is strictly negative, so the increments sum. For kappa=0 the same buffered argument works with r_b=a. The ensuing limit uses(C3), proving exactly Re s>a+kappa. Bounds on a finite height interval or uncontrolled A=A_y do not meet this hypothesis.

The synthetic h_k^*(s)=sum_(j=1)^k2^(j(a+kappa-s))/j is a valid sharpness check at kappa>0: its left-line size is O(2^(k kappa)); its right increments satisfy the needed y^(1-b) budget since a+kappa<1. The limit exponential is1/(1-2^(a+kappa-s)), with a pole at the claimed strict boundary. It is not an arithmetic prime source. It prevents a free improvement of the abstract exponent, not an arithmetic theorem stronger than the input.

For a=3/4, kappa=78/625, the conditional c is313/2500=.1252. Its gain over root-accepted c10 is1351/25000000=.00005404. The corresponding first-gain test is kappa<.12485404. The1/6 and1/4 rows are also exact. The actual crude bound |H_y(a+it)|<=C_a y^(1-a) has a+kappa=1 and yields no useful strip. The author correctly does not replace this with a claimed estimate.

## 9. Fixed-power late flow and the square-root critical profile

The [[private research revision] threshold integration]([private research revision]/f3-threshold-integration.md)
and [independent proof]([private research revision]/f3-review/report.md) extend the literal
source in two separate ranges. Keep F, T_z and R_z=F-T_z as above and
L=log X. For fixed 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2 and a fixed buffered
mu-Mertens exponent 1/2<beta<1, set eta=(1-2rho_1)(1-beta)/4. Then

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f e^(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                        +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),
    C_f=9log2 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2),
    B(rho)=2log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.     (G37)

B is negative and strictly decreasing. Thus the actual band from
X^(3/8) to X^(2/5) is positive, with coefficient
C_f e^(tau/2)[79/225+2log(10/9)]. This sign differs from G35's
subpower bands. The complete tail above any fixed rho_plus>1/2 is
O_A(X^-A), so the band from a fixed rho<1/2 to rho_plus is negative.
No uniformity through rho=1/2 or moving transition has been proved.

The proof uses the actual f=h*mu convolution and the double zero of
its reciprocal series at1: signed reciprocal core moments are0,0,2C_f.
The two-rough-prime source identity is exact only below z^3; its
outside discrepancy, all repeated powers and the artificial p=q
diagonal are paid. Signed Abel summation removes large cores before
both sharp PNT substitutions. A signed Taylor remainder and its
derivative, not an unsigned harmonic estimate, pay O(X/L^4).

There is a separate theorem needing no Mertens or complete-F input.
For fixed tau>0 and kappa>=1, define the absolutely convergent profile

    J(v)=integral_v^infinity e^u(u-v)g_tau(u)du,
    Phi(q)=sum_(r>=1)f3(r)/r J(log(rq)).

Then uniformly on the full shell,

    R_(kappa sqrt(X))(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)
                                      +O(X/L^3).      (G38)

For kappa^2>=2e^(3tau), Phi(q)>=(3/4)J(log q)>0 throughout
q in [kappa^2/2,kappa^2]. Consequently, for fixed rho_plus>1/2,

    T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X))
       =2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)+O(X/L^3)>0.            (G39)

All continuous-core extension tails and both Stieltjes errors are
absolute here. The global prime-density expansion, after scaling
p,q by sqrt(X), has integrable error O(L^-3); its unordered factor
1/2 times density4/L^2 gives2. The r=1 term dominates the entire
r>=2 profile by a factor at least4/3. This is fixed-kappa positivity,
not a uniform assertion for moving kappa or every threshold jump.

Both source theorems retain all Gram entries, the true original O(X)
diagonal and both independent heights. For the exact split in G36,
b=||R|| is comparable to X/L^d, with d=3 in G37 and d=2 for the
positive G38 profile. A full new 1/2<gamma<.874867 requires BOTH

    |a-b| << X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+rho << X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^(2d).               (G40)

The baseline near cancellation normalized by actual b^2 is distinct
from the additional O(1/L) error introduced by a leading profile.
Neither a logarithmic asymptotic nor its rank-one leading Gram closes
G40 at new power precision. The fixed full-field convolution return
applies after reconstructing F; arbitrary moving masks inherit none.

### A. New paid interface

For fixed a>0 take

    b=1/(1-gamma), Y_a(y)=a(1+y)^b, y>=0,
    kappa(a,gamma)=a^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).                     (C3)

Equality belongs to the small-prime sector. Let Q_small use precisely p<=Y_a(y). Then for every eta>0,

    |Q_small(R)| <= [kappa(a,gamma)+eta] I_R+B_eta,a,chi,tau,  (C4)

for every R, with B using only a fixed bounded interval of the actual source and its left tail. It does not require any unknown future bound.

Proof: PNT and partial summation give

    S_gamma(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p p^(-gamma)
                 ~t^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).

Thus the row sum at y is (kappa+o(1))y. Apply 2|z(y)z(y-log p)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(y-log p)|^2. For the column put v=y-log p. The mask implies log p<=log a+b log(1+y)=o(y); hence v/y->1 uniformly over all admitted primes as y->infinity. More explicitly, for any fixed small epsilon>0, eventually y<=v/(1-epsilon), so the column is bounded by

    S_gamma(a(1+v/(1-epsilon))^b)
       <=[kappa/(1-epsilon)+o(1)]v.

Choose epsilon and the tail onset to absorb both errors into eta. The remaining y are bounded and have only finitely many permitted primes and a bounded past interval. Their contribution is B. No second factor2 survives in the asymptotic coefficient; both rows and columns were counted. PNT is used only in this classical scalar prime-weight sum. Replacing it by G173's theta(t)<=4(log2)t gives the entirely elementary, weaker coefficient 4(log2)kappa and the same cutoff power.

This is larger eventually than the G173 cutoff ((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^b, by a growing logarithmic factor. The price is a nonzero, explicitly budgeted kappa; the old cutoff had relative bound0. It is not legitimate to enlarge that mask while retaining its old arbitrarily small price.
