# Independent review of the actual R4 middle power-core sectors



**Verdict:** the proposed SQ and CU restricted estimates survive independent review relative to the retained G185-G187 and PR9 source contracts. The whole merged coefficient is permitted by the two actual large-sieve theorems. Its normalized squared mass, the sixth-power natural hole, both independent allocations, both restored roots, and all label powers are accounted for. I found no missing arithmetic estimate in these restricted payments. This is evidence for controller review, not automatic theorem admission or a larger zero-free constant.

The strongest possible defect would have been an inner coefficient depending on its live sieve row, especially through a sixth-power deletion or a row-specific Fourier measure. The argument avoids this: the common measure precedes live labels; the cube argument fixes z before averaging squarefree t. The hole at z must remain. I give that check explicitly below, together with an independent refinement: the core caps may grow with the original a-dyad as A^(24/5), preserving the same paid error. The complete signed large-core/nonunique residual remains open.

## 1. Frozen evidence and inherited scope

Review source-pins.json was frozen before substantive analysis at 2026-10-13T02:17:35Z, SHA256 6444c4a558e35f35a07e2d03a87678c83559a5ca00db8f330a9e56d0dfc242fe. It binds 23 local inputs. Author report SHA256 is 17bb3e93eff1c23d4a9c1283d9453beb3e59113ad87f34e22471373d2cce9c49; author manifest SHA256 is af087d6b803ae0620191f0d07943af8d1b08e8423a7050815859201ffd1cfc55. The original mathematical pins match; only attempt-index had acquired controller additions for Cycles103-106. The diff was inspected: they do not alter G185-G187 or either imported sieve. Initial pins are not rewritten.

The final source recheck found only a further [private research revision] index append, whose diff was inspected; all other 22 pinned inputs remain unchanged. The primary-source read dates recorded in source-recheck.json, 13 October, correct the prospective 12 October dates in the immutable initial pin metadata. After a model-capacity interruption, all six saved review files and the exact claim were reconciled with the controller recovery record before closeout resumed at03:08 UTC. Mathematics was already complete; the recovery bound03:30 UTC does not replace the original missed00:50 UTC deadline.

Inputs read include the complete author report, helper, receipt and worklog; accepted [private research revision] primitive-low-dual-integration; the matching prior author/reviewer reports retained from their earlier full read; PR9 B1.1-B1.11, B2.24-B2.25 and B3.1-B3.5; G156-G157's original relative-conductor scope; the root budget, as unaccepted corroboration only; and exact [restricted research revision]-MQ ancestry. The two new external permissions were independently checked in their primary sources. No unchanged author diagnostics were rerun.

Use q_x=N(x), D1=U^r, D2=U^s, P0=U^v, N0=D1 D2 P0, L=r+s. The source is the literal product of TWO original inverse polynomials and the original ordered slot polynomial Q. Their heights are independent, their real parameter is common, and the entire right copy is conjugated. All natural zeros, original slot pool membership, slot coefficients, root profiles, fixed rays and unit conventions remain. Both full sextic orientations e=1,-1 are present. The row enclosure is the inherited nonzero sixth-power-free free-row source, after its licensed divisor-weight domination; this review inserts no physical projector.

The retained parameter box is

    17/25<=delta<=7/10, 17/20<r<47/50,
    33/25<s<141/100, s-r>3/8, 0<=v<=1/20.

Retain exactly T=delta L+E_K, K=28114053/6250000 with its existing license, E_K>=rho, rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)]. In particular L>217/100, L<47/20 and T>=123353/67500. This physical-bin comparison does not replace the stronger signal extraction at an internal buffered witness.

G186 already gives, with tau=1/1000 fixed here,

    ||F_<||_U^2=R_nonunique+R_middle
                         +O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).       (V1)

On a fixed original sixth-divisor dyad q_a~A, its literal middle is

    U^(39/25)<q_ell<=H_A,  H_A=U^tau A^6 N0^2/U.

The entire far tail was paid on the genuine source before coprime extension or absolute Fourier integration. The full kernel remains inside this finite middle. R_nonunique is the complete signed complement of the squarefree/coprime merged-column source; none of it is paid by this review.

Fix once the S-supported denominator-clearing element Delta. Every power core is the core of the INTEGRAL IDEAL (Delta*ell), with the author's prescribed unit/fixed-place representatives. Fixed scaling constants stay in their exact conventions. Clearing Delta multiplies each source coefficient by a unit chi_m(Delta)^(-eta), since m is S-good. No vanishing moving character value is inverted.

## 2. Whole coefficient, prior common profile, and exact roots

The inherited primitive pair has good conductor nn', local exponents 1 and 5, and no zero-frequency contribution. Primes shared by ell and a source factor give primitive Fourier zeros, including slot primes. Fixed row ray restrictions modulo a disjoint fixed modulus preserve this good-prime zero by CRT. Original principal inducing rows have not been deleted.

G185's finite identities give, apart from nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')),

    e=-1: R(n,n')chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n))G(n')
           a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell)),
    e=+1: R(n,n')G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
           conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell).

The CRT ratio R is the fixed ray sign; the finite dictionary separates these factors. Both signs are retained. In particular the common-source extraction law is a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m)chi_m(f)^4, or its full conjugate. A second cross-copy cubic phase is not being suppressed.

Extend the displayed formal product expression to individually squarefree columns, and insert the FULL identity sum_(f|n,f|n')mu(f). Artificial noncoprime pairs cancel pointwise, including inverse-slot and slot-slot coincidences. A frequency selector independent of f survives this identity unchanged. There is no assertion of imprimitive Poisson on the added pairs.

For fixed f, write n=fm,n'=fm'. Each column is squarefree, so m,m' avoid f. Each prime of f is assigned to one of its actual original inverse colors or named slots, independently on the two sides. Write f=f1 f2 fP=g1 g2 gP. Both residual product scales equal

    X=(D1/q_f1)(D2/q_f2)(P0/q_fP)=N0/q_f
     =(D1/q_g1)(D2/q_g2)(P0/q_gP).

All assigned slot tests and coefficients are retained. At fixed slot depth, both allocation counts together are bounded by tau(f)^C. No equality between the two shortened inverse pairs is assumed.

For one fixed allocation, finite dictionary entry and common Fourier component, the entire residual column is

    B_f(ell)=X^(-1/2) sum_(m sf) c_f(m) chi_m(ell)^eta,
    eta in {1,-1}.                                      (V2)

Here c_f is the ACTUAL sum over all residual original factorizations m=xyP, with their separate profiles and slot labels. It includes a0(m) or its conjugate, fixed ray factors, the appropriate f twist, and the a/f holes. For fixed squarefree m, each prime has at most j+2 places. Slot restrictions only reduce this count, even though a named slot may contain at most one prime. Thus |c_f(m)|<=H_J tau(m)^C and

    X^(-1) sum_(q_m~X)|c_f(m)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon.        (V3)

Indeed tau(m)^C<<_eta q_m^eta, and the ideal count is O(X). Choose eta after the fixed polynomial cap on X. Assigned f-slot choices have already been paid outside; they are not paid again as a new P0 mass. This is uniform in each separate allocation, fixed punctures and modulus-one twists. Empty windows stay empty. A nonempty nominal subunit scale differs from one by only a fixed support factor, so clipping gives a bounded dilation, including X near one.

The whole coefficient being divisor bounded is sufficient for these TWO arbitrary-sequence sieves. It remains insufficient for PR9 B3.6, whose canonical merged coefficient forbids such an extra weight. No canonical reflected-energy extension is used.

PR9 B3.3 separates the profile on the original ambient normalized inverse/individual-slot box on both copies, with nominal a,ell dyads A,H. Its kernel argument is C*y_ell/(y_a^6 product(y_source)), C=UH/(A^6N0^2). Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded in C by fixed Schwartz seminorms. The measure is fixed BEFORE a,f,kappa,b,t,z and slot choices. Only then substitute the factorizations. Extracted imaginary powers have modulus one; original real roots occur in the profile once. The resulting c_f may depend on nominal A,H and the fixed Fourier component, but not on the live sieve row. Enlarging a positive frequency energy uses this one separated extension, not a newly chosen row-dependent profile.

Both unnormalized residual columns are sqrt(X) times (V2). Hence the original U/(q_a^6 N0^2) becomes EXACTLY

    [U/(q_a^6 N0^2)]sqrt(X)sqrt(X)
        =U/(q_a^6 N0 q_f).                             (V4)

The real ratio N0/sqrt(q_n q_n') becomes X/sqrt(q_m q_m'), still a bounded profile factor. It supplies neither an extra q_f nor a second inverse q_f. The common frequency twist is |chi_f(ell)|^2=1_((f,ell)=1), an outer restriction; no division by this zero is made.

For a selector w on frequencies, scalar Cauchy bounds sum w B_left conjugate(B_right) by the product of the square roots of two POSITIVE energies with weight |w|. Only then is the frequency set enlarged. The two columns keep distinct coefficients and independent allocations, but have the same upper X and common S0 below. Their energy prices are not multiplied a second time.

## 3. SQ: the permitted unrestricted cubic row

The primary [Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Section4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3), dated 23 June 2025, states Theorem4.1 with squarefree primary inner c, arbitrary complex inner sequence, and unrestricted outer d. Its price is M^(1/3)(M+N) times the inner squared mass, up to (MN)^epsilon. Corollary4.2 and its displayed proof give the transposed residue-symbol orientation by reciprocity, including units and lambda powers. By l2 duality that bilinear bound also yields the required energy orientation. Conjugating the entire inner sum permits the conjugate cubic symbol. These are Section4 character estimates; the cuspidal Fourier-coefficient theorems elsewhere in that paper are not imported.

Write (Delta*ell)=kappa*b^2, kappa squarefree. At each prime, v(kappa)=v(Delta*ell) mod2 and v(b)=floor(v(Delta*ell)/2). No condition (kappa,b)=1 is allowed or needed. For fixed kappa,

    chi_m(ell)^eta = fixed_Delta_unit_factor
                      *chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(b)^(2eta).  (V5)

This is valid at nonunits as well as units. The kappa factor is a fixed multiplier of c_f; its zero values simply remove columns. It is independent of b. The remaining symbol is cubic, with b unrestricted and m squarefree; it satisfies the precise theorem above. The common f-hole is an outer b restriction, or kills the entire fiber, and the internal b/m hole is the cubic symbol's natural zero.

Finite ray classes are resolved before the sieve. Strip any fixed S-supported part of a live outer variable, shorten its length, and retain its coefficient twist. There are O((log U)^|S|) such parts under the polynomial frequency cap; powers modulo6 give only fixed character data. Units have bounded multiplicity. For the quadratic live row later, its squarefree S-part has only finitely many possibilities. Fixed outer periodic factors have bounded modulus in the positive energy. No growing prime is added to S and no high fixed-prime valuation is dropped.

By (V3), the NORMALIZED b-energy with q_b<=B is

    << H_J U^epsilon B^(1/3)(B+X).

Dyadic annuli yield the ball form at a subpower cost. Empty small balls are omitted, with bounded support clipping where needed. Here B<< (H_A/q_kappa)^(1/2). Ideal counting gives

    sum_(q_kappa<=C) energy
      << H_J U^epsilon [H_A^(2/3) C^(1/3)
                              +X H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6)].   (V6)

The exponents come from sums of q_kappa^(-2/3) and q_kappa^(-1/6). Squarefreeness of kappa only reduces those counts. All middle/core/priority selectors are outside the inner source and survive Cauchy as positive outer restrictions.

## 4. CU: exact sixth-power holes and the clipped repetition sum

Write uniquely (Delta*ell)=kappa*t^3*z^6 with kappa cubefree and t squarefree. Primewise the exponents are

    v_kappa=v_ell mod3,
    v_t=floor(v_ell/3) mod2,
    v_z=floor(v_ell/6),

where v_ell here means v(Delta*ell). They need NOT have disjoint support. A prime of valuation4 occurs in both kappa and t; valuation10 occurs in all three. The exact identity is

    chi_m(ell)^eta = fixed_Delta_unit_factor
       *chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1).        (V7)

The quadratic factor is real, so its exponent is unchanged for eta=-1. The last factor cannot be replaced by one: at a good source prime p with valuation6 in (Delta*ell), the local kappa and t valuations are zero and the z valuation is one. The original local factor is zero, while dropping the z-hole would give one. Fixed-place factors do not change this local counterexample. This is the first decisive obstruction to an incautious repeated-row argument.

Fix kappa AND z before averaging t. The inner coefficient is c_f(m)chi_m(kappa)^eta 1_((m,z)=1), with any fixed Delta/unit factor. It remains squarefree, satisfies (V3), and is independent of live t. An overlap with t remains the quadratic symbol's own zero; overlaps among kappa,t,z impose no additional mask. The outer common f-hole is retained independently.

The primary [Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642), dated 31 May 2012, allows arbitrary inner coefficients for a quadratic Hecke family, with BOTH ideal variables squarefree, and price M+N up to a subpower. Its family hypotheses include primitivity, trivial infinite type, finite-group reciprocity, and the primitive product conductor for coprime equal-class indices. PR9 B2.24 supplies the actual family check: the lambda sign correction, its primitive inducing convention, fixed primary square classes modulo4, and ray reciprocity. These are retained source assumptions, not replaced by a generic power-symbol analogy. Finite class splitting and transpose duality identify the present m,t orientation.

More explicitly, PR9's character on an ideal (x) is vartheta_m((x))=epsilon_lambda(x)^(e(m)) (x/m)_2, with e(m)=(q_m-1)/2 modulo2 and primitive conductor m*lambda^(e(m)). After fixed S-parts are removed, the difference from chi_m(t)^3 is precisely this lambda unit factor. Splitting e(m) and the fixed ray classes makes it an outer t factor of modulus one. Equal-class products cancel that lambda correction and have primitive good conductor equal to the product, as required. Neither an extra moving conductor cost nor a live-t coefficient is introduced.

The t-energy for q_t<=T0 is therefore <<H_J U^epsilon(T0+X). The independent pointwise input is G185 on the two original colors of ONE copy:

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon S0,
    S0=P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].                        (V8)

The new z-hole splits between x,y and the ORIGINAL remaining slots; it does not create an arbitrary joint coefficient. Fixed kappa and other holes do the same. Thus (V8) applies after the exact conditioning in (V7), using the actual shortened colors on each side and their common S0 upper bound. Those two colors are not cross-copy products.

Set B=(H_A/q_kappa)^(1/3). For fixed z, T0=B/q_z^2; q_z<=sqrt(B) on every nonempty fiber, up to fixed support constants. Two available bounds are T0+X and T0*S0. For 1<=Z<=sqrt(B), ideal counting gives

    sum_(q_z<=Z)(B/q_z^2+X) << B+XZ,
    sum_(q_z>Z) B*S0/q_z^2 << B*S0/Z.                 (V9)

In particular XZ, the repeated-row price, has NOT disappeared. Put Z0=sqrt(B*S0/X). If 1<=Z0<=sqrt(B), balancing proves B+O(sqrt(B*S0*X)). If Z0<1, the all-pointwise price B*S0 is at most sqrt(B*S0*X). If Z0>sqrt(B), then S0>X, and the all-quadratic price B+Xsqrt(B) is at most B+sqrt(B*S0*X). This proves in every regime

    sum_(t,z) |B_f(kappa*t^3*z^6)|^2
       << H_J U^epsilon [B+sqrt(B*S0*X)].              (V10)

Thus no unproved S0<=X restriction is hidden in the choice of split. Coefficients are different for different z, which is permitted because each quadratic application fixes z; they are not different for live t. Any core priority selector remains an outer t restriction after kappa,z are fixed.

Sum cubefree kappa up to C. The powers q_kappa^(-1/3), q_kappa^(-1/6) give

    H_J U^epsilon [H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3)

    S0 << P0(D1D2)^(2/3),

### Reconstructing the baseline, including the end ranks

Assume the accepted **buffered** fixed-source summatory input `S(t)=O(t^beta)`, `1/2<beta<1`. For c6 any fixed beta>.874861 is permitted by the retained premise; beta=.874861 itself is not supplied. The G28 inverse coefficients transfer the buffered Möbius/A input to f3. Then counts of ± signs are `t/2+O(t^beta)`. Equal rank pairing satisfies `p_k,m_k asymp k` and `|p_k-m_k|=O(k^beta)`, uniformly up to N. The excess O(N^beta) ranks lie in `[N-O(N^beta),N]`, so the ghost does not arbitrarily collect interior mass.

Writing w=log(n/X), differentiate the exact product expression:

    ||d phi_w/dw||_2² = b(w)² g_(2nu)(0)
             [w²/sigma²+alpha²/(2nu)].                 (R10)

The mixed integral vanishes since `integral g_nu g_nu'=0`. The paired log distance is `O(n^(beta-1))`; integrating the derivative gives a cost bounded by

    C n^(2beta-2)(1+w²)exp(-c w²)

for a fixed c>0 after a harmless variance enlargement. To justify it uniformly even when X and n are widely separated, absorb `|w|n^(beta-1)` into `epsilon*w²+C_epsilon` above a fixed initial threshold. The finitely many smaller n have superpower Gaussian decay. Summing over n about X yields `O(X^(2beta-1))`: the logarithmic variable leaves an integrable `exp((2beta-1)w-cw²)(1+w²)`.

The excess ghost pair costs are `O(X^(beta-C²/sigma+o(1))+X^(beta-D²/sigma+o(1)))`, below that bound after choosing the already free fixed tail constants. Thus

    C_r(X)<<X^(2beta-1), uniformly for all r>=0.         (R11)

R9 returns beta for d=0; positive d gives the weaker beta+d/2. R11 is an upper bound on one plan, not an optimal-cost lower bound. It leaves open a better source-specific plan. Matched-Max MM-D2 already owns monotone log transport with a paid ghost; this adaptation earns the exact new metric and full f3 Gaussian-tail accounting, not a second discovery of the transport method. W41's single-prime-edge obstruction is not contradicted: these pairs may have arbitrary near-one ratios.

**Verdict B:** accept B1–9 with these quantifiers. The required new cost is strictly `q+d<.749722`; none is proved. Large-r attenuation alone does not deliver that estimate. ## Stronger exact calculation: the full-strength boundary eigenspace

Let p_* be the SMALLEST prime with w_(p_*)!=0; weights at smaller primes may be zero. The multiplicity of the eigenvalue W of E=B^*B is EXACTLY

    h_N=#{n:squarefree,(n,q)=1,p_* not|n,N/p_*<n<=N}.
    Therefore ||E||=W whenever h_N>0.                 (F10)

This is uniform in arbitrary weights on the other primes and in a moving active prime set. It strengthens F9 for this ambient spectral certificate: at least (kappa_q/8)N eigenvectors have full boundary loss for every sufficiently large N. It still says nothing below about the signed arithmetic readout.

Proof without a spectral approximation. Let U be the span of the states counted in h_N. Every active prime is >=p_*, so D kills U. In the quotient by U, each p_*-free state with n<=N/p_* is paired with its p_*-multiple. The p_* part of D gives an invertible coefficient w_(p_*) between each pair; all other active creation operators anticommute with p_* annihilation. Thus the quotient complex is contractible, with homotopy w_(p_*)^-1 c_(p_*)^*, taken modulo U. Equivalently it is the mapping cone of w_(p_*) times the identity on the lower p_*-free complex. No creation from U can return under the cutoff. The short exact sequence of these finite complexes gives H(D)=U as graded vector spaces. Finite-dimensional orthogonal decomposition gives dim(ker D intersect ker D^*)=dim H(D)=h_N. By F4 this is exactly ker(W Pi-E) inside Pi's range, proving F10. If p_*>N, the quotient is empty and D=0, which gives the same formula.

For q=1 and p_*=2 this is the familiar squarefree-complex critical-cell count in Bjorner's Theorem3.1. [restricted research revision]/G144 already includes the q-unit least-prime critical rank and its filtration price. The present statement keeps arbitrary zero/nonzero moving weights, their least ACTIVE prime, and the exact boundary-Gram eigenvalue. This is a useful explicit specialization/extension in this record, not a claim of a new topological theorem in the literature. A proposed spectral-gap shortcut below W fails on these actual cutoff states. Source-sensitive graded cancellation among those states remains entirely eligible.

### A1. Fixed detector and the seed's unnecessary desmoothing loss

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including q=1, put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with chi zero on nonunits. Define

    M_chi(t)=sum_(n<=t) a(n),
    E_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) exp(-n/x),       x>0,
    R_r(N)=sum_(n<=N) a(n)(1-n/N)^r,         r>0.

The endpoint n=N has weight0. These are the full coefficients, without a favourable sector or hidden coprimality change. Absolute Fubini for Re(s)>1 gives

    int_0^infty E_chi(x)x^(-s) dx/x = Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    int_0^infty R_r(N)N^(-s) dN/N
        = Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/[Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)].       (A1)

For fixed r the multiplier in the second line is nonzero when Re(s)>0. Thus an every-dyadic L2(dx/x) exponent gamma>0 for either fixed field directly excludes zeros in Re(s)>gamma. Sharp recovery of M_chi is unnecessary. This is standard Mellin/Riesz ancestry, including [restricted research revision]-C1 and Sol04-D12, not new detector credit. The Beta integral and nonvanishing of Gamma are recorded in [DLMF5.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12) and [DLMF5.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2); the coefficient identities above are derived here by n/x substitution.

For completeness, if ||E_chi||_[X,2X] <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon) on every sufficiently large dyadic X, Cauchy-Schwarz and dyadic summation make its Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma, with all logarithmic derivatives. Near0 the absolute geometric sum is O(exp(-1/x)). Identity continuation gives L(s,chi)H(s)=Gamma(s). At an L-zero in that half-plane the left side vanishes and the right side does not. The pole of a principal L at1 is treated meromorphically; it is not a zero. This proof treats every fixed character separately, with constants allowed to depend on q and chi, and makes no growing-conductor assertion.

The open issue becomes quantitative when r grows: (A1) is not the Mellin transform of a field whose r varies with the physical shell. The following comparison restores a single fixed field first.

### A2. Uniform first- and second-order comparison

Suppose, as an explicit input, |M_chi(t)|<=C_chi t^beta for all t>0, where beta>0. Taking beta=1,C_chi=1 is unconditional. A stronger buffered summatory bound may be substituted only if its own source contract is available; it is not inferred here merely from the number c11.

For real r>=2 define

    k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r,
    B_r(x)=R_r(rx)=sum_n a(n) k_r(n/x),
    V_r(x)=2B_(2r)(x)-B_r(x),
    A(u)=u-u^2/2,
    K1(beta)=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3),
    K2(beta)=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
             +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

Then, uniformly in all x>0 and r>=2,

    |B_r(x)-E_chi(x)| <= C_chi K1(beta) x^beta/r,
    |V_r(x)-E_chi(x)| <= (3/2)C_chi K2(beta) x^beta/r^2.  (A2)

No coefficient tail, moving-order constant, last integer or second branch has been suppressed. V_r includes the support out to2rx and both ordered cross terms in any squared norm. Its literal coefficient weight is2(1-n/(2rx))_+^(2r)-(1-n/(rx))_+^r.

Proof. For0<u<r, k_r'(u)=-(1-u/r)^(r-1); for u>r it is0. The function is continuous and absolutely continuous, and for r>=2 its derivative also matches0 at r. On0<=u<=r/2 let

    z_r(u)=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u.

The log series gives z_r<=u/r,

    |z_r| <= (u+u^2)/r,
    |z_r-A(u)/r| <= (u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.                (A3)

Indeed the terms of order>=3 have absolute sum at most
(r-1)(u/r)^3/[3(1-u/r)] <=2u^3/(3r^2). Using
|exp(z)-1-z|<=(z^2/2)exp(max(z,0)) proves

    |k_r'(u)+exp(-u)| <=(5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k_r'(u)+exp(-u)[1+A(u)/r]|
                       <=P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,             (A4)
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.

Here the first inequality on the short range even holds with u+u^2. For u>=r/2 use |k_r'|<=exp(-u/2) on its support and0 outside, and r<=2u. After multiplying the proposed second inequality by r^2, the two constant terms cost at most8u^2, the u/r term at most2u^2 and the u^2/(2r) term at mostu^3. This is bounded by P(u). The first inequality follows there from2<=4u/r. Thus (A4) holds on the entire positive half-line, including the part beyond the finite support.

Abel/Stieltjes integration, with vanishing endpoint terms, gives

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M_chi(xu)h'(u)du.       (A5)

Apply (A4) to h=k_r-exp(-u), then integrate u^beta times its bound. For the second line write k_r'=-exp(-u)[1+A(u)/r]+e_r; the A/r terms cancel exactly in2k_(2r)'-k_r'+exp(-u). The complete remainder is at most(2/4+1)P exp(-u/2)/r^2. Its integral is(3/2)K2(beta)/r^2. This proves (A2), including the infinite exponential tail. Constants are deliberately coarse and explicit; their finiteness and uniformity matter more than their size.

### A3. Complete return and the actual scale budget

Fix delta>0. On each dyadic shell[X,2X], freeze one common

    r_X=max(2,ceil(X^delta)),   V_X(x)=V_(r_X)(x).

The complete approximation error is O_(chi,beta)(X^(beta-2delta)) pointwise and in shell L2. Consequently, for any gamma>0 with beta-2delta<=gamma, the every-epsilon shell bounds of exponent gamma for V_X and E_chi are equivalent. Use a strict inequality when a fixed power margin is desired. Only after this comparison is the fixed E Mellin transform used. With beta=1 this return needs no inherited cancellation at all.

| Prospective gamma | Prospective c | delta using only |a|<=1 | Complete error exponent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .87485 | .12515 | .063 | .874 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .084 | .832 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .126 | .748 |

These are conditional targets, not proved improvements. All signed V_X moments remain open. For an independently supplied beta=.874855, delta=.000003,.021,.063 would instead give error exponents .874849,.832855,.748855. That optional buffer is explicitly an extra input to this version of A2.

The largest raw cutoff on[X,2X] is4r_X X, of orderX^(1+delta). A raw-cutoff power bound R_r(N)=O(N^eta) corresponds to effective-scale exponent(1+delta)eta, not eta. In particular the unconditional positive bound

    |B_r(x)| <= sum_(n<=rx)(1-n/(rx))^r <=rx/(r+1)<=x

uses the decreasing integral test. It remains exponent1 at the effective scale. V_r costs at most3x by this method. The apparent saving from enlarging r is entirely a change of observed scale. This is a complete coarse estimate on the actual coefficients; it fails to beat the target and rules out the intended free smoothing gain.

The fixed signed extrapolation order2 is essential to the proved constant. No growing extrapolation order, asymptotic Gamma-ratio uniformity in moving height, Gaussian inverse or implicit convergence of changing Mellin transforms is claimed. The complete moment of V_X contains all interactions between both Riesz branches; bounding one favourable piece is insufficient. A is a source-exact refinement of smoothing/restoration ancestry, not literature priority or arithmetic-gap credit.

In particular no nonvanishing claim is made for the Mellin multiplier of a fixed V_r: a difference of two Gamma quotients need not inherit their separate nonvanishing. The moving V_X estimate reaches the fixed E by the explicit error before any zero argument. This resolves that numerator objection without assuming a new Euler identity.

### 3.1 Actual prime law and orthogonal coefficients

Let P be any finite set containing2 and excluding3. Put Q=product_(p in P)p,

    a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)),
    r_P(n)=f3(n)a_P(n), R_(P,chi)(u)=sum_n r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u).

Thus f3=a_P r_P pointwise, |r_P chi|<=1 and r_P(pn)=r_P(n) for p in P, including all powers. Let pi be the product law of B_p with q_p=1/p. Define

    Z_p=(B_p-q_p)/sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)),
    m_p=1-2q_p, v_p=2sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)), Z_S=product_(p in S)Z_p.

Then the exact Boolean identity is

    a_P(B)=sum_(S subset P) A_S Z_S,
    A_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)v_p product_(p notin S)m_p. (C1)

The Z_S are an orthonormal basis under pi, and sum A_S^2=1. Since m_2=0 and v_2=1, A_S=0 unless2 is in S. Positive-prime-power occupancy is used; the squarefree law1/(p+1) is not used.

For an integer D>=0 set q_D(B)=sum_(|S|<=D)A_S Z_S. The exact discarded squared norm is

    rho_D^2=E_pi |a_P-q_D|^2=Pr(K>D),
    K=sum_(p in P) Y_p, Pr(Y_p=1)=nu_p=4(p-1)/p^2.     (C2)

The Y_p are independent auxiliary Bernoulli variables encoding coefficient ENERGY, not a claim that the arithmetic tail is random. In particular Y_2=1 deterministically. If lambda=sum nu_p and D+1>=lambda, its elementary exponential-moment bound is

    rho_D^2 <= (e lambda/(D+1))^(D+1).                (C3)

Indeed E exp(tK)=product(1+nu_p(e^t-1))<=exp(lambda(e^t-1)); use t=log((D+1)/lambda), then drop the extra exp(-lambda). The exact finite Poisson-binomial tail is available and often sharper.

### Singleton proof and all-depth count

If distinct u<v lie in the SAME integer interval(C1), then

    m v<=N/p<(m+1)u,  so m(v-u)<u.

Since v-u>=1, u>m. Consequently any fiber containing a cofactor<=m is a singleton even before smoothness, squarefreeness or character masks. This applies whichever member is smallest. No short/long mixture can occur. A ramified value may make the singleton coefficient zero, but never creates an additional nonzero path.

For a short active path d=pu with u<=m=floor(N/d) and m>p^r,

    p u^2<=N,       p^(r+1)u<N.

Thus, dropping arithmetic restrictions only in this positive count,

    S_r(N)<=sum_(j>=2)min((N/j)^(1/2),N/j^(r+1))
          <=(4+1/r)N^alpha_r,  alpha_r=(r+1)/(2r+1).           (C3)

Split at J=ceil(N^(1/(2r+1))). The initial part is at most2sqrt(NJ)<=2sqrt(2)N^alpha_r; the tail is at most N/(rJ^r)<=N^alpha_r/r. The stated larger constant works for every N>=1. Integer counts may be rounded down; the real upper envelopes remain valid. For q-units every singleton has absolute coefficient1, so S_r is its exact coefficient mass. The whole short contribution is at most D_N S_r when D_N bounds ALL active prime-state defects.

This is an ALL-depth price. It is not the old fixed-depth x^(k/(k+r)) estimate, and no unmerged exponent-one lower bound survives this grouping. It also does not estimate cancellation among the remaining merged coefficients.

## D02 and the seven other selected first tests

D02 is mathematically decisive in its stated scope. For the finite actual Gaussian Gram M>0 and source c, E=c*Mc. The determinant lemma gives

    det(M+lambda cc*)/det M = 1+lambda c*M^-1 c.

This is the dual energy, not E. Setting v=Mc repairs it:

    det(M+lambda vv*)/det M = 1+lambda E.

The repaired determinant therefore encodes exactly the original hard energy. Gaussian translate independence proves M>0 at distinct physical sample points. Near-singular conditioning prices approximate Mc and any inversion; the exact identity does not require numerically stable inversion. The rank-one Fredholm determinant of I+lambda|F><F| has the same energy identity and inherits its complete tail requirement. Actual Gaussian absolute tails or the existing G13 return must be paid; finite matrices alone prove no infinite detector. Validity: accept failure and repair. Novelty/potential: duplicate energy-encoding mechanism, no weaker sufficient input obtained.

S08's 2x2 example proves only that deleting a negative cross term can increase a general quadratic energy; it is not a native H lower bound. It blocks an inference from isolated mask/taper size to full source contraction. S06's log2/log3 argument validly excludes representing a generic literal Dirichlet polynomial as a single polynomial in a common exponential variable with integer exponents. It does not exclude quantitative multivariable resultants. S18 correctly identifies missing algebraicity at arbitrary complex s and unpaid heights; it proves no universal impossibility theorem.

S46 uniqueness is stated for the unit-coefficient zeta convolution. For general chi the exact recurrence includes chi(n/r), giving mu(n)chi(n). The author does not claim otherwise, but future summaries must preserve this qualification. A nonlinear/different scalar detector is not refuted. S41's commutator formula and -1 quadratic witness check exactly; trace zero is inadequate. This duplicates prime migration/masked-boundary warnings. S37 and S49 validly show unitary coordinate gauges preserve norm, while natural character/projector zeros are not unit phases. A nontrivial actual transport defect or cocycle remains unbridged. These scoped failures must not become blanket rejection of their full seeds.

statement:
## 2. D1/S01: complete conditional prime-flux return

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, principal or imprimitive allowed, and tau>0 independent of scale. Throughout this section a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including n=1, prime 2, all squareful zeros and all character zeros. Put

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) g(log n-y),  z(y)=exp(-gamma*y)U(y),
    1/2<gamma<1.

Gaussian coefficient majorants prove local absolute convergence of every fixed derivative, and polynomial-times-Gaussian decay as y tends to minus infinity. These preliminary facts use no cancellation hypothesis.

### Exact identity and signs

The convolution identity a*chi=delta gives, including every prime power,

    a(n) log n = -sum_(d|n) a(n/d) chi(d) Lambda(d).

For a squareful local exponent the last two surviving prime-power terms cancel. Omitting prime powers would change the actual source. Since tau U'(y)+yU(y)=sum a(n)log n g(log n-y),

    tau U'+yU+K1 U+K2 U=0,
    K1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K2 U=sum_p sum_(j>=2) chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

After weighting, delays d carry chi(d)Lambda(d)d^(-gamma). Define

    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Qj(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(Kj,gamma z)(y)dy.

The exact energy equation is

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau*gamma*E_R=Q1+Q2.       (R1)

In particular the derivative boundary and drift have the signs required for absorption. This identity is inherited Gaussian renewal/logarithmic-source algebra, not a new family.

### Full prime powers and the moving row AND column

For gamma>1/2,

    C_gamma=sum_(p,j>=2) log p*p^(-j*gamma)
      <=(1-2^(-gamma))^(-1) sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2*gamma)<infinity.

Truncate z only above R, retain its whole past, and use translation contraction and Cauchy. Then |Q2|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z|^2. The past is unconditionally finite. Split the positive integral at a fixed sufficiently large Y, using y>=Y on the tail. For every eta>0,

    |Q2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                      (R2)

B_eta is finite from fixed bounded intervals and the Gaussian left tail; no assumed future norm is hidden in it. This relative form bound does not assert cancellation in K2 itself.

For the author's small-prime cutoff p<=(2+y)^A, A(1-gamma)<1, eventually log p<=y/2. Thus v=y-log p is in [y/2,y]. The row sum is at most C(2+y)^(A(1-gamma))log(2+y)=o(y), by summing over integers. In the second half of 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, change variables separately for each p. Since y<=2v, the column is bounded by the same sum with p<=(2+2v)^A, hence o(v). Its upper endpoint satisfies v<=R. The initial bounded y interval uses finitely many primes and a fixed bounded v interval. Therefore, uniformly in every R,

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                (R3)

The column payment is necessary; a row estimate alone would not prove this quadratic-form statement. The written proof does pay both. There is no assumption about z at future points beyond R.

### The exact same-output diagonal and the remaining form

Expand Q_hard before absolute values. Its summand is

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))*chi(p)*a(m)] log p
      *exp(-2*gamma*y)g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),

over p>(2+y)^A, all m,n>=1, and 0<=y<=R. The equality n=pm contributes only when pm is a squarefree q-unit; then -conjugate(a(pm))*chi(p)*a(m)=1. The total retained log-prime weight at fixed n is at most log n. Exactly,

    int_(-infinity)^infinity exp(-2*gamma*y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =exp(tau*gamma^2)n^(-2*gamma)/(2*sqrt(pi*tau)).

Thus the actual hard same-output diagonal D_R obeys

    0<=D_R<=exp(tau*gamma^2)/(2*sqrt(pi*tau))
                 *sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2*gamma)<infinity.          (R4)

This bound includes all cutoff changes and both infinite source sums. It gives no positive domination for arbitrary signed subcollections. Set H_R=Q_hard-D_R, literally the complete n!=pm form with its signs and moving mask.

The proposed arithmetic premise OPEN-PF is: for every fixed chi there exist delta_chi>0, B_chi and R0_chi such that

    H_R<=(1-delta_chi) I_R+B_chi for every R>=R0_chi.             (PF)

Take eta=delta_chi/4 in each of (R2),(R3), use (R4), and absorb the finite initial interval. Equation (R1) implies

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R+tau*gamma E_R<=B'_chi.       (R5)

Hence U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma*y)) at all large real y, with the unchanged fixed Gaussian. No interpolation across missing scales is needed. PF has not been proved; a finite-R fit, a positive selected sector, or a formal identity is not this uniform strict-coercivity premise. This is a sufficient criterion, with no automatic equivalence at the boundary exponent gamma asserted.

### Full zero return and scope

The bilateral transform F(s)=int_(-infinity)^infinity U(y)e^(-s*y)dy is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly with all derivatives, by (R5) and the Gaussian left tail. On Re(s)>1, absolute summation gives

    F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Thus L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) as a meromorphic identity on Re(s)>gamma. The right side never vanishes. A zero of L at any finite height is impossible there. The principal pole at 1 is allowed and forces the corresponding zero of F; it is not an L-zero. Natural zeros and imprimitive factors were present in a from the start. No uniform lower bound for the Gaussian multiplier as height tends to infinity is needed for this pointwise nonvanishing argument, and no reciprocal-growth or unsmoothing theorem is silently imported. The standard character Euler product and principal-pole distinction agree with [DLMF 25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15).

The exponent gamma is common to the family, while delta, constants and onset may depend on fixed chi. This proves an all-height ordinary-character return if PF holds for every such chi. It says nothing about a moving modulus, an Eisenstein Hecke family, or the physical H branches. The endpoint gamma=1/2 is not supplied because both positive payments diverge there. Conditional targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4,.5001 in the author are in range; none has its arithmetic premise established.

The inherited bound U(y)=O(e^(beta*y)) and absolute prime summation give a generic flux envelope with exponent 1+beta-2gamma, whereas I has exponent 2beta-2gamma. The gap 1-beta explains why that absolute route cannot prove PF. An upper envelope is not a signed lower bound or proof that PF fails.

### F07.C / F13.T — Changed Jacobi phase and a quadratic-row triple source

The inverse-cubic-character Jacobi transform
\[
\sum_x\vartheta_p(x)\overline{\vartheta_p(1-x)}e_p(tx)
=\sum_{v\ne-1}\vartheta_p(v)e_p(tv/(1+v))
\]
has zero-frequency value -1; CRT encodes ideal Möbius for squarefree moduli without an angular Gauss-square factor at that stage. A rational additive pushforward may produce a different trace kernel, but must first be inserted into an exact zeta-sensitive detector. Contracting it immediately adds nothing. Raw multiplicative rank-one kernels admit compensating coefficients; a rational phase is useful only after its diagonal strata and full modulus are classified.

A different hybrid preserves **quadratic rows** while realizing the column Möbius sign by \(\bar\alpha(c)\mathfrak G(c)^3\). Twisting one triple source by \(\psi_u\) suggests the ratio
\[
J_r(s)L^{(S)}(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang}\psi_u)/L^{(S)}(s,\psi_u).
\]
The equal-element projector survives formally and the total-index twist acts on both c and B. Exact local/ray normalization, a quadratic number-field transfer and the ramified trilinear restriction remain open. AB12 does not cover arbitrary quadratic twists; termwise translation can cost the entire conductor. Test one ramified prime, one square row and one core/cube shared prime before a global realization. Multiplying the **row** by a cubic character destroys the principal-square advantage.

## 7. W60-30: full cyclic compression has zero Feshbach self-energy

Use the exact Hermitian dilation A_theta of the unchanged native packet. For a fixed source x let C=span{x,Ax,...,A^(D-1)x}, where D is the full finite dimension. Cayley-Hamilton makes C invariant; Hermitian symmetry makes C-perp invariant too. If P projects onto C and Q=I-P, then QAP=PAQ=0. Therefore the proposed Feshbach term

    PAQ(z-QAQ)^(-1)QAP

vanishes identically whenever the inverse is defined. The compressed operator preserves exactly the original source spectral measure, but the suggested nonlocal self-energy has disappeared because the chosen subspace is already reducing. The cyclic subspace can be full: for T=diag(1,2), x=(0,0,1,1), the four Krylov columns have determinant-18. This is explicitly a synthetic example; it is not an evaluation of native H. The reducing-subspace identity itself applies to the actual matrix.

For the different projection onto a unit source LINE, the genuine Schur formula is

    <x,(z-A)^(-1)x> = [z-a-b*(z-D0)^(-1)b]^(-1),
    a=<x,Ax>, b=QAx, D0=QAQ.                                  (F1)

Its large-z coefficients are1/z+a/z^2+(a^2+||b||^2)/z^3+... . For the original nonzero source x0=(w,v), use x=x0/||x0||, giving a=2 Re(e^(i theta)H)/(||w||^2+||v||^2); the recorded source norm restores H. With x=(0,v)/||v||, a=0 but the second moment is ||Tv||^2/||v||^2, whose improved bound is still needed. Thus the coherent rescue is a source-line spectral-measure estimate with its entire resolvent cost; neither cyclicity nor the formula supplies it. No native norm lower bound or all-architecture impossibility is inferred.

statement:
# Quaternion norm applied to the complete Jordan source

**A source-exact bridge and two scoped obstructions; no new arithmetic bound or endpoint.** The user's quaternion identity really does encode the Jordan compensator in one channel. Its other channel is an explicit arithmetic companion, and a sufficiently sharp *lower* estimate for that companion would upper-bound the desired source. The complete deficit and recovery costs below identify exactly what must be proved. A separate dimension-four argument shows that bounded quaternion lifts cannot obtain a power saving by taking pointwise absolute values of their expanded Gram entries, even on the actual already-localized Jordan middle. This is stronger than saying that a constant embedding is isometric; it does not rule out a signed companion comparison.

c11=.1251459636 remains CONDITIONAL SOURCE-RELATIVE. Nothing here repairs PR15's unfinished weighted Hecke source. This lane concerns the literal ordinary-character Jordan source G215-G216. All new identities, failures and reopening conditions are retained irrespective of record utility.

## 1. Literal source and quaternion conventions

Use the complete G215 data: a fixed ordinary character chi modulo its PRESENTED q, with natural nonunit zeros; r>=2 of the same parity as chi; fixed m>=0. Put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), lambda=2^(r+1), D H(X)=H(X/2), and

    P_m(D)=product_(j<m)(I-2^(-(2j+1))D),
    F(X)=sum_n chi(n)J_r(n)e^(-n/X),
    J_r(n)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)(n/d)^r,
    E(X)=F(X)-A X^(r+1), E_m=P_m(D)E,
    g(t)=sum_n chi(n)n^r e^(-nt)-m_q r!t^(-r-1),
    H(t)=P_m(T)g(t), T g(t)=g(2t),
    E_m(X)=sum_n a_n H(n/X),
    Phi(X)=E_m(X)-lambda E_m(X/2)
          =sum_n a_n K(n/X), K(t)=H(t)-lambda H(2t).    (1)

Here A=m_q r!/L(r+1,chi), with m_q=phi(q)/q for principal chi and 0 otherwise. These are the original complete sums, not a finite or squarefree substitute for F: J_r has deliberate prime-power coefficients, while the outer divisor source in (1) has mu's squareful zeros. The original g and its principal algebraic tail remain in H. The source K vanishes to order 2m+1 at 0, decays exponentially at infinity, and has leading exponential e^(-t). It is nonzero. G215 proves E_m=O(X), Phi=O(X) at infinity and the stated small-scale behavior. All these constants may depend on fixed chi,r,m.

For q=z+w j use j z=conj(z)j. Then

    (z+w j)(u+v j)
      =(zu-w conj(v))+(zv+w conj(u))j,
    N(q)=|z|^2+|w|^2,
    M(q)=[[z,w],[-conj(w),conj(z)]].                   (2)

Thus M is the user's algebra homomorphism and det M=N. Throughout sections 2-3 quaternionization is pointwise at a positive REAL scale X. No holomorphic positivity claim is made.

## 2. The compensator is one quaternion product channel

Set A_X=E_m(X), B_X=E_m(X/2), and q_X=A_X+B_X j. Right multiplication by the fixed real-coefficient quaternion 1+lambda j gives

    q_X(1+lambda j)=Phi(X)+Psi(X)j,
    Psi(X)=lambda E_m(X)+E_m(X/2)
           =sum_n a_n K_+(n/X),
    K_+(t)=lambda H(t)+H(2t).                         (3)

There is no conjugation error in (3): both coefficients of the right multiplier are real. In particular no chi(2) is factored from a scale dilation, including when 2 divides q. The complete sum-of-squares identity is

    |Phi(X)|^2+|Psi(X)|^2
       =(1+lambda^2)(|E_m(X)|^2+|E_m(X/2)|^2).         (4)

Both the positive companion and its actual source are now explicit. The inverse product recovers

    E_m(X)=(Phi(X)+lambda Psi(X))/(1+lambda^2),
    E_m(X/2)=(Psi(X)-lambda Phi(X))/(1+lambda^2).       (5)

These are exact for complex characters. They are not estimates for either channel.

For the full shell measure dx/x write ||.||_X for L2([X,2X]). Define the complete deficit

    Delta_Q(X)=(1+lambda^2)(||E_m||_X^2+||D E_m||_X^2)
                                      -||Psi||_X^2.

Then

    Delta_Q(X)=||Phi||_X^2>=0.                        (6)

Consequently a LOWER companion estimate

    ||Psi||_X^2 >= (1+lambda^2)(||E_m||_X^2+||D E_m||_X^2)
                                           -C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon) (7)

would prove the desired full Phi energy bound. It is not invalid to seek (7): the positive companion can furnish an upper bound through a proved deficit. But positivity alone supplies only Delta_Q>=0, the wrong direction for a saving. Bound (7) is currently OPEN and is exactly equivalent to the Phi L2 premise. It is not asserted equivalent to the weaker G215 L1 premise or to bare zero exclusion.

For a common family region, gamma must be fixed before chi and (7) must hold for every fixed ordinary character, with character-dependent constants and onsets. A bound for one character supplies only that character's return.

The exact arithmetic quantity hidden by a name such as “alignment” is

    <E_m,D E_m>_X
      =sum_(d,e>=1) a_d conj(a_e)
          integral_X^(2X) H(d/x)conj(H(2e/x)) dx/x.     (8)

Every pair, both orientations, shared prime, squareful zero, nonunit zero and principal tail remains. Absolute convergence on a fixed shell justifies this expansion. No signed-subset domination or diagonal lower bound is used.

More precisely set alpha=||E_m||_X, beta=lambda||D E_m||_X. If alpha beta>0, let rho=Re<E_m,D E_m>_X/(||E_m||_X||D E_m||_X). Cauchy gives -1<=rho<=1, and (6) is

    Delta_Q=(alpha-beta)^2+2alpha beta(1-rho).           (9)

The zero-norm cases are given directly by (6). Thus (7) requires BOTH the amplitude mismatch and the full phase-correlation defect to be paid. If alpha beta has order X^2, the correlation defect needs order X^(2gamma-2+epsilon); norm multiplication supplies none of it. This identifies a legitimate coupled arithmetic target without separating its projections.

### Complete recovery and the raw-main cost

There is no free one-channel inverse. G216's actual O(Y) bound and lambda=2^(r+1)>2 give

    E_m(X)=-sum_(j>=1)lambda^(-j)Phi(2^j X).           (10)

The finite remainder is lambda^(-J)E_m(2^J X)=O(X2^(-Jr)), so every future scale is included and the homogeneous X^(r+1) solution is excluded by a proved source bound. For any beta<r+1, a complete bound ||Phi||_{Lp([Y,2Y])}<=C Y^beta at all sufficiently large dyadic Y implies, for p=1 or 2,

    ||E_m||_{Lp([X,2X])}
       <= C X^beta/[2^(r+1-beta)-1].                  (11)

Minkowski and the geometric series prove (11). Conversely finite shifts give Phi from E_m, and (3) gives Psi. Hence the COMPLETE every-epsilon exponent classes of Phi and the two-channel bank are equivalent. This is a cost calculation for the actual field, not a theorem that every new estimate for (7) is circular or useless.

Using raw F instead of E would hide a much larger problem. For principal chi put U=P_m(D)F, V=U(X/2). Their main coefficient is

    A_m=A product_(j<m)(1-2^(-(r+2j+2)))>0,
    U=A_m X^(r+1)+E_m(X), V=A_m X^(r+1)/lambda+E_m(X/2).

The first quaternion channel U-lambda V is still Phi. Its companion lambda U+V has main term A_m(lambda+lambda^(-1))X^(r+1). Both positive terms on the right side of the raw version of (6) have size X^(2r+2), with identical leading constant. A target X^(2gamma+epsilon) therefore requires relative deficit precision X^(2gamma-2r-2+epsilon) on that raw scale, not just removal of the leading coefficient. For r=2 this is X^(2gamma-6+epsilon). Cross terms involving the O(X) error still cost up to X^(r+2) before exact centering. Formula (1) performs the centering legitimately; the remaining arithmetic deficit in (9) is unpaid.

Under (7), G215's already paid outside-divisor terms and full Mellin identity supply ordinary all-height zero exclusion for Re s>gamma. The numerator Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi) has its established nonvanishing in the target strip, including Re s=1; the allowed principal pole is preserved. This uses the scalar Phi bound, not analytic continuation of N(q_X). The possible gain remains conditional on (7). No Hecke, varying-conductor or new independent-height transfer follows.

## 3. A dimension-four obstruction on the ACTUAL Jordan middle

This theorem permits arbitrary X-dependent quaternion directions, not merely one constant embedding. Fix the source above and gamma in (0,1). Let either I_X be all positive integers, or precisely the G215 retained set

    I_X={n: X^alpha<n<=2X log X},
    alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2).

For n in I_X put w_n=|a_n K(n/X)|. When w_n>0 put
xi_n=a_n K(n/X)/w_n, so |xi_n|=1. All original coefficient zeros stay zero. Choose ANY quaternions

    v_n=z_n+t_n j, z_n=xi_n, N(v_n)<=C^2, C>=1,       (12)

with C fixed independently of X; set v_n=0 when w_n=0. No arithmetic independence is assumed. The encoded field Q_X=sum_n w_n v_n has first complex channel exactly the complete Phi(X), or the exact retained Cmid(X), respectively. Hence the scalar square is at most N(Q_X).

Consider the particular positive certificate obtained by taking absolute values of the POINTWISE expanded quaternion Gram:

    B_+(X)=sum_(d,e in I_X) w_d w_e
                       |Re(v_d conjugate(v_e))|.      (13)

It includes both orientations and the diagonal. Then the unconditional bound is

    B_+(X) >= [sum_(n in I_X) w_n]^2/(4C^2).           (14)

Proof. Regard H as R^4 and form the positive matrix S=sum_n w_n v_n v_n^T. Its trace is at least sum w_n because (12) implies N(v_n)>=|z_n|^2=1. Its rank is at most 4, so tr(S^2)>=(tr S)^2/4. On the other hand tr(S^2)=sum w_d w_e (v_d dot v_e)^2, and |v_d dot v_e|<=C^2. Thus (13)>=tr(S^2)/C^2, proving (14). Finite truncation followed by monotone convergence proves the statement for the full infinite source; all sums converge since sum |a_n K(n/X)| is finite.

G216 supplies the ACTUAL, character-specific weighted squarefree asymptotic

    sum_n w_n=kappa_q X I_K+O(sqrt X),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1),
    I_K=integral_0^infinity |K(t)|dt>0.                (15)

For I_X equal to the retained middle, the removed absolute mass is O(X^gamma)+O(X^-1), so its sum is still kappa_q I_K X+o(X). Therefore for BOTH actual source choices,

    B_+(X)>=(kappa_q^2 I_K^2/(4C^2)+o(1))X^2.         (16)

Integrating the pointwise majorant over the complete real shell retains exponent 2. It cannot establish an energy exponent 2gamma<2 for any fixed gamma<1. This applies even though the diagonal alone has exponent 1 and is already affordable at gamma>1/2.

For the explicit principal q=1,r=2,m=0 source,

    K_0(t)=e^(-t)(1-e^(-t))/(1+e^(-t))^3>0,
    I_K=1/4, integral K_0^2=1/60,
    B_+(X)>=(1/(64C^2 zeta(2)^2)+o(1))X^2.            (17)

The diagonal of (13) is at most C^2[X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X)]. Thus a quadratic cost persists in the absolute OFF-diagonal price too. This is not a lower bound on N(Q_X), |Phi|^2, the actual signed cross form, or (7). Negative Gram entries can still cancel.

The reconstruction condition in (12) matters. If C=1, |z_n|=1 forces t_n=0: there is no second-channel freedom at all. For C>1 bounded, the rank proof shows why finite extra directions do not change this certificate's exponent. More generally, in real dimension d with a scalar/complex readout ell of norm L and ||v_n||<=C, exact ell(v_n)=xi_n gives

    L^2 B_+(X) >= [sum w_n]^2/[d(CL)^2].              (18)

Indeed ||v_n||>=1/L and the same trace proof applies. Rescaling the lift cannot hide a cost: CL is invariant under reciprocal rescaling of lift and readout. A necessary condition for this particular positive certificate to reach X^(2gamma+epsilon) is d(CL)^2 at least X^(2-2gamma-epsilon), up to constants. This is not sufficient. It leaves growing dimension, unbounded conditioning with a fully paid return, and source-specific signed comparisons eligible.

The scope is pointwise absolute Gram payment. Taking an absolute value only AFTER integrating a signed pair over x, or retaining a collective companion deficit such as (7), is a different certificate and is not excluded by (14). Nor is the full automorphic spinor space four-dimensional: four real quaternion coordinates at one point must not be confused with a function-space rank bound.

## 4. Multiplicative arithmetic and complex-height costs

The quaternion homomorphism M respects quaternion multiplication; it does not turn commutative integer multiplication into a noncommuting representation. A true multiplicative map u from positive integers (or from the squarefree coprime prime products used by mu) must satisfy

    u(p)u(l)=u(pl)=u(l)u(p), p!=l.                    (19)

Nonzero commuting quaternions all lie in one complex slice unless they are all real: writing a quaternion as a real scalar plus an imaginary vector, its commutator is twice the cross product of the imaginary vectors. One nonreal image fixes their common axis. Ramified zero images do not alter this statement for the remaining primes.

For the outer mu source, multiplicativity is only required on COPRIME inputs. One must still set the squareful coefficients to zero; asserting u(p^2)=u(p)^2 for the FULL mu coefficient would already be false. On its actual squarefree support, however, (19) forces the prime images into the same commuting slice. Thus a genuinely coprime-multiplicative quaternion lift cannot obtain arbitrary noncommuting prime rotations while keeping that source contract.

An ordered-prime word is an admissible DIFFERENT construction, but needs a new return. Already u(2)=i,u(3)=j gives i j=k and j i=-k; their difference has Euclidean magnitude 2 and N=4 at the actual squarefree output 6. Norms of the two products agree; their recoverable signed coefficients do not. Taking a norm erases exactly the order defect that scalar reconstruction needs. Repeated primes and the mu zero extension cannot be restored by that norm equality.

There is a further all-height issue even when coefficient quaternions commute in a different slice. If n^(-s) is represented in the user's chosen complex plane C_i, it need not be central in H. For example

    (j 2^(-s))(j 3^(-s))
       =-2^(-conj(s))3^(-s),                         (20)

whereas ordinary Dirichlet convolution would demand -6^(-s). They differ unless the indicated 2-height phase happens to be real. This is an exact obstruction to importing a real-sigma quaternion Euler product unchanged to complex heights.

The constructive alternative is the genuinely holomorphic matrix series sum_n M(v_n)n^(-s), with CENTRAL complex scalar matrices. Its entries are

    [[Z(s),W(s)],[-W#(s),Z#(s)]],
    Z#(s)=conjugate(Z(conjugate(s))),
    det=Z(s)Z#(s)+W(s)W#(s).                          (21)

Here multiplication correctly uses ordered matrix Dirichlet convolution in its absolute half-plane. But (21) is a positive quaternion norm only for real s; at general height it is an algebraic holomorphic determinant. The exact reflected companion and all prime-order defects still require estimates. This is a lawful alternative to explore, not a proof that all quaternion methods fail. It preserves the distinction root is recording between a holomorphic matrix construction and pointwise quaternionization.

## 5. Prior SU(2) use and useful next action

The existing section9 matrix k(g) is literally M(q_g), with

    q_g=t(g)(conj(d)-conj(c)j),
    N(q_g)=t(g)^2(|c|^2+|d|^2)=1.

Thus the user’s representation already matches the actual minimal angular SU(2) type. Sections9/17 and review-cycle-7 use the FULL two-component spinor, fixed flat twist, complete incoming cusp subtraction and self-adjoint resolvent. They prove the stated polynomial row/height bounds, while the sparse prime-fourth mean and original source transfer remain open. Replacing that full vector by its quaternion norm does not license summation over unbounded forced divisors. The Iwasawa compact factor k(g) is not automatically a group homomorphism g->k(g); its other factors/cocycles cannot be discarded in an arithmetic lift.

Earlier S44 was genuinely untested beyond an isometry caution. This report does not relabel it as disproved. The new source application is (3)-(11), the sharpened actual-source positive-certificate obstruction is (14)-(18), and the arithmetic/height escape conditions are (19)-(21).

The useful next calculation is an estimate for the full one-sided Jordan companion deficit (7), or a structured quaternion/matrix lift whose recovery controls a genuinely different signed readout before absolute values are taken. Any proposal must state its actual coefficient map, allowed masks, both channels, noncommuting-order correction, reflected complex-height series and scalar recovery norm. The dimension-four theorem does not exclude such a comparison; it tells us exactly which positive proof shortcut would fail.

No new c, complete moment theorem, unconditional Hecke transfer or formal acceptance is claimed. One exact diagnostic checks 192 literal Jordan/filter coefficients across principal, nonprincipal, imprimitive and quartic characters; four finite complex channel products; one eight-term actual weighted squarefree Gram; and the two failed order/noncentral-variable examples. These are finite algebra checks, not infinite-source or exponent evidence. The source references, read extents, hashes and final owned-file allowlist accompany this report. Root owns review and integration.

statement:
# [restricted research revision] independent review: exact depth of the W67 absolute residual bill

Decision: accept ROOT's proposed lower bound, with the fixed-modulus, fixed-fraction cutoff and sequence quantifiers stated below. A matching elementary upper bound is also available. For this specified family, completing depth k asymptotic to kappa log N/loglog N makes BOTH complete absolute residual bills have exponent 1-kappa, for 0<kappa<1. Thus equality at kappa=1-gamma suffices for the residual payment alone. It does not suffice for the complete certificate, because the retained coordinate z_1 still contains the Mertens problem.

This is a scoped certificate calculation, not a new Mertens estimate, signed residual lower bound, general-approximant barrier, zero-free constant or PR15 repair. Conditional source-relative c11=.1251459636 and the unfinished PR15 weighted theorem/endpoint, F0, positive-slot and external-admission obligations remain unchanged.

## 1. Scope and evidence



Read sources: W67 author report section 2; W67 independent report sections 1-2; W43 report section 3; [restricted research revision]-W2 integration; G78 in [private research revision]; the ancestry discussion for G83-G85 in [private research revision]; G222's fixed-layer circle obstruction; and narrow related passages in the current proof and attempt index. The latter explicitly preserve the corrected conditional status of c11. `source-inputs.json` records exact local file hashes and read scope. No unchanged W67 diagnostic was rerun. All new assertions below are algebraic or asymptotic proofs, not finite numerical acceptance.

## 2. Independent inverse and complete residual reconstruction

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a FIXED positive integer q, and an integer N>=1. Let

    S_N = {a<=N : a is squarefree and gcd(a,q)=1},
    E_(a,d) = 1_(d divides a),
    M = diag(mu(a)),
    D = diag(mu(d) conjugate(chi(d))),
    A = E D E^T.

All indices lie in S_N, ordered increasingly; 1 is included. This set is divisor closed. Mobius inversion gives E^(-1)=M E M. Every entry of D is nonzero, since |chi(d)|=1 on S_N, and D^(-1)=diag(mu(d)chi(d)). Consequently

    (A^(-1))_(a,b)
      = mu(a)mu(b) sum_(d in S_N, lcm(a,b)|d) mu(d)chi(d).       (1)

The transpose is the ordinary transpose, not the conjugate transpose. For nonreal characters A is complex symmetric, generally not Hermitian. The gauge diag(chi) K diag(chi) of the untwisted K would keep its inverse (1,1) entry untwisted and is not an alternative derivation of (1).

Write g=gcd(a,b), l=lcm(a,b), and d=lm. The requirement d squarefree is equivalent here to m squarefree and gcd(m,l)=1; natural character zeros add gcd(m,q)=1. Since mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g), (1) becomes

    (A^(-1))_(a,b)
      = mu(g)chi(l) sum_(m<=N/l, gcd(m,lq)=1) mu(m)chi(m).       (2)

It is zero for l>N. In particular

    R(a) = (A^(-1))_(1,a)
         = chi(a) sum_(m<=N/a, gcd(m,aq)=1) mu(m)chi(m),
    |R(a)| <= floor(N/a) <= N/a,
    (A^(-1))_(1,1) = M_chi(N) = sum_(n<=N) mu(n)chi(n).         (3)

For ANY column z on the actual S_N set r=e_1-Az. Multiplication by A^(-1), followed by its first coordinate, gives the COMPLETE identity

    M_chi(N) = z_1 + sum_(a in S_N) R(a)r(a).                  (4)

Define two distinct complete absolute bills

    B(z) = sum_(a in S_N) |R(a)r(a)|,
    W(z) = N sum_(a in S_N) |r(a)|/a.

Then |M_chi(N)-z_1|<=B(z)<=W(z). A sufficient pointwise certificate is |z_1|+B(z), or the stronger explicit |z_1|+W(z), bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large N. With the fixed-character quantifiers this gives the usual Mellin continuation of 1/L and zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. The principal pole at 1 is permitted. Nothing below supplies the required estimate of z_1.

## 3. Exact proposed column and prime witness

Fix 0<beta<1. Let k>=0 be an integer and 1<=T<=beta N; T may be real because only integer comparisons occur. Put

    F_(T,k)(d) = 1_(d<=T OR omega(d)<=k),
    z = E^(-T) (chi(d)F_(T,k)(d))_d.

Here E^(-T) means (E^T)^(-1). Its first row has entries mu(d), and D(chi F)=mu F. Therefore, with no missing or conjugated phase,

    z_1 = sum_(d in S_N) mu(d)chi(d)F_(T,k)(d),
    r(a) = sum_(d|a) mu(d)(1-F_(T,k)(d))
         = sum_(d|a, d>T, omega(d)>k) mu(d).                   (5)

The identity e_1(a)=sum_(d|a)mu(d) supplies the residual sign. Every coordinate with a<=T or omega(a)<=k vanishes. If omega(a)=k+1 and a>T, every proper divisor has omega<=k and is retained, so r(a)=mu(a).

Let p'_1<p'_2<... be the primes not dividing q, b_k=product_(j=1)^k p'_j, and b_0=1; use P^+(1)=1 when referring to a largest prime. Set c=max(beta,1/2), x=N/b_k, and

    P_(N,k) = {prime p : cx<p<=x and p does not divide b_k q}.

Every p in P_(N,k) gives a DISTINCT actual coordinate a=b_k p in S_N, with omega(a)=k+1, a>beta N>=T, and a>N/2. Since N/a<2, the cofactor sum in (3) has only m=1. Thus R(a)=chi(a), r(a)=mu(a), and |R(a)r(a)|=1. It follows, at EVERY finite N, that

    W(z) >= B(z) >= #P_(N,k).                                (6)

The count can of course be zero at small N or excessive k. No finite positivity or effective threshold is asserted.

The ordinary prime number theorem pi(x)~x/log x, and the equivalent p_j~j log j, are the only external asymptotic inputs. They are recorded in the authoritative [NIST DLMF 27.2.3-4](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2#E3), checked on 2026-10-13. All uses are fixed-ratio intervals, not short intervals or progressions. The following consequences are derived here.

For fixed k, excluded primes divide the fixed integer b_k q, and

    #P_(N,k) ~ (1-c)N/(b_k log N).                           (7)

For growing k, removing the finitely many prime divisors of fixed q shifts prime indices by a bounded amount. Hence p'_k~k log k, and summing logarithms gives

    log b_k = (1+o(1)) k log k                              (k->infinity).

If k=o(log N/loglog N), then log b_k=o(log N), x=N^(1-o(1)), and the prime count in (6) is N^(1-o(1)). This also covers bounded subsequences of k by (7).

If k~kappa log N/loglog N with FIXED 0<kappa<1, then

    b_k=N^(kappa+o(1)),
    x=N^(1-kappa+o(1)),
    p'_k=O(log N).

Thus cx eventually exceeds both p'_k and every prime divisor of q: the collision and ramification exclusions disappear from the interval. Ordinary PNT along this moving x gives

    #P_(N,k) ~ (1-c)x/log x = N^(1-kappa+o(1)).               (8)

Uniformity in a varying modulus is neither used nor available. A fixed fraction beta<1 is essential; T=N would have zero residual at every depth.

## 4. Sharpening: an upper bound matches the lower exponent

ROOT's lower bound is valid but does not exhaust the readily provable result. Put h=k+1, H_N=sum_(m<=N)1/m, and A_N=sum_(p<=N)1/p. The latter sum may include conductor primes, which only enlarges the following upper bound.

Taking the triangle inequality in (5), exchanging finite sums, and dropping squarefree/coprimality restrictions only from the nonnegative inner sum gives

    W(z)
      <= N sum_(d in S_N, d>T, omega(d)>=h) (1/d)
                    sum_(m<=N/d, dm in S_N) 1/m
      <= N H_N sum_(d<=N, d squarefree, omega(d)>=h) 1/d
      <= N H_N sum_(j>=h) A_N^j/j!
      <= N H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!.                            (9)

The elementary-symmetric-sum bound in the third line is valid because each unordered set of j distinct primes occurs j! times in A_N^j; allowing repeated primes and products above N enlarges the sum. For the final line use (h+r)!>=h!r! and sum over r>=0. This bound includes ALL residual coordinates and is uniform in every cutoff T>=1.

Partial summation from pi(t)=O(t/log t) gives A_N=O(loglog N), while H_N<=1+log N. If h~kappa log N/loglog N for fixed kappa>0, the elementary factorial estimate log(h!)=h log h-h+O(log h) yields

    log(H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!) = -kappa log N+o(log N).

Combining (6), (8) and (9), for 0<kappa<1, proves

    B(z) = N^(1-kappa+o(1)),
    W(z) = N^(1-kappa+o(1)),                                (10)

uniformly for 1<=T<=beta N. The notation means that both logarithms divided by log N converge to 1-kappa. For k=o(log N/loglog N), (6) and the bound W<=N H_N exp(A_N) give exponent 1. No claim of a precise fixed-k logarithmic asymptotic for B or W is made.

A sharp sequence formulation is useful. Fix 0<gamma<1, fixed q and beta, and one integer sequence k_N>=0 and one cutoff sequence satisfying 1<=T_N<=beta N for all sufficiently large N. Neither sequence varies with the epsilon in the following statement. Then

    B(z_N) <<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0
    iff W(z_N) <<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0
    iff liminf_(N->infinity) k_N loglog N/log N >= 1-gamma.    (11)

Constants may also depend on the fixed q, beta and sequences. For sufficiency, fix 0<a<1-gamma; the liminf condition eventually puts k_N above a log N/loglog N. The nonnegative tail in (9) decreases with h, so its bound at that smaller depth is N^(1-a+o(1)). Let a approach 1-gamma according to epsilon. For necessity, if the liminf is smaller, choose 0<a<1-gamma above it and use infinitely many k_N<=a log N/loglog N. On that subsequence b_(k_N)<=N^(a+o(1)), its largest prime is O(log N), and the same fixed-ratio PNT count is at least N^(1-a-o(1)). This contradicts the claimed bound for any sufficiently small fixed epsilon.

Thus the original phrase 'equality is no sufficiency assertion' is correct as a description of what the LOWER-BOUND proof alone establishes, and remains essential for the COMPLETE |z_1|+bill certificate. With (9), equality IS sufficient for the residual bill alone. This distinction should be preserved if ROOT integrates the sharpening.

## 5. Why paying the residual has not repaired the source

The retained coordinate is explicitly

    z_1 = M_chi(N)
          - sum_(d in S_N, d>T, omega(d)>=h) mu(d)chi(d).     (12)

Let D be the number of terms in that omitted sum. A separate elementary count gives

    D <= sum_(n<=N) binom(omega(n),h)
      = sum_(d<=N, d squarefree, omega(d)=h) floor(N/d)
      <= N A_N^h/h!.                                       (13)

For k~kappa log N/loglog N this is N^(1-kappa+o(1)). Hence after depth reaches the desired threshold, z_1 already approximates the full hard Mertens sum within the desired exponent. Under the condition in (11), the every-epsilon |z_1| bound at exponent gamma is equivalent, by (4) and (9), to the same M_chi(N) bound. The residual estimate is proved, but the new arithmetic input remains exactly at z_1.

Neither (6) nor (10) lower-bounds the complete SIGNED sum in (4). Characters can produce different phases, and even for the principal character different residual coordinates can cancel. For higher layers the individual residual sign can already vanish: at N>=30, k=1, T=11, r(30)=mu(15)+mu(30)=0. The first-unpaid-layer calculation must not be extended to all omega(a)>k.

## 6. Ancestry and live repair condition

W43.2-4 / [restricted research revision]-W2 already establish the fixed-depth lesson for literal Newton/geometric reciprocal completion. With d_Y=delta-1*m_Y and Q_(Y,j)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(j-1))), its residual is d_Y^(*j). On a Y-rough squarefree integer with exactly j prime factors it equals (-1)^j j!. Counting such products yields a full absolute Gaussian obstruction of exponent 1 at fixed j. Its complete signed complement and reciprocal feedback cannot be omitted.

The present family is not literally that Newton column. It uses the coefficient w(d)=mu(d)F_(T,k)(d) and residual delta-1*w restricted to the actual squarefree divisor downset. For example, with T=1, k=1 and a product of two distinct primes, (5) is +1, whereas the order-2 Newton residual d_1*d_1 is +2. More generally the present first unpaid layer is (-1)^(k+1), while the Newton order-(k+1) rough layer has the extra (k+1)! factor. W43 also includes nonsquarefree integers and a Gaussian readout; here mixed small-prime/large-prime labels are legitimate, the field is finite, and R(a)=chi(a) exactly on a>N/2. These differences require the reconstruction above; W43 cannot simply be cited as the proof of this B(z) bound.

Nevertheless, the fixed-k conclusion is an adaptation of the known first-unpaid-layer obstruction, not an independent arithmetic saving. G222 in [private research revision] separately already rejects deleting finitely many omega layers in its positive circle norm. G78 in [private research revision] has already paid a DIFFERENT growing-depth Newton restoration and full Gaussian tail; it would be stale to describe W43's old uniform-depth/tail obligation as still globally open. G83-G85 likewise preserve paid growing-order completion and the remaining complete signed source.

The useful delta here is narrower and explicit: (6) identifies a literal, cofactor-priced unpaid coordinate after any fixed number of low-omega repairs; (9)-(11) locate the exact growing-depth threshold for BOTH complete absolute bills in this specified family; (12)-(13) expose where the original signed arithmetic difficulty then resides. This is a consequential admission condition for a proposed W67 repair: paying primes or any fixed number of layers does not close OPEN-RES, and paying sufficiently many layers does not by itself pay z_1. An independently proved z_1 estimate or a different complete signed mechanism is still required.

There is no new c. No all-approximant impossibility statement, growing-conductor result, literature-priority claim, formalization, kernel or new expert packet is asserted. No finite computational check was needed for these elementary identities and asymptotic estimates; the exact proof, source readback and frozen hashes are the evidence.

## 7. Handoff

ROOT may accept the proposed bound as stated with the explicit quantifiers, and may integrate the matching upper bound and sharp criterion (11). The report is complete within the assigned scope. Root owns canonical integration, tracker/Git work and any further research. The final freeze is a separate local record; the tool's normal exact-own claim-release receipt completes the handoff. These records do not establish mathematical acceptance beyond this report.

## 8. Attempted escape: a zero-sum compensator bank really deflates cells

Section7 is not a theorem against every compensator bank. In particular
normalization sum lambda=1 is essential when using cutoffs of the SAME
source. A zero-sum combination of DIFFERENT compensators need not have
zero Mellin signal. I tested the simplest such escape explicitly rather
than silently extending the obstruction to it.

For any fixed integer K>=0 put

    v_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*q_p,
    b_K=v_K*h,
    c_K=v_K*a,
    h_K=v_K-b_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*h_p.    (8.1)

For K>=1, v_K=q_(p^(K+1))-q_(p^K), where
q_m=delta1-m chi(m)delta_m. In particular its coefficient at1 is
zero. Explicitly

    b_K(j)=chi(j)[p^K 1_(p^K|j)-p^(K+1)1_(p^(K+1)|j)]. (8.2)

This is periodic of period Q_K=p^(K+1)q and has mean zero. The principal
mean cancels because p^K/p^K=p^(K+1)/p^(K+1); nonprincipal complete
character sums vanish. The unramified hypothesis remains essential.
All squareful support in this changed detector is retained.

The adaptive theorem applies verbatim with q_p replaced by v_K,
b_p by b_K, and eta_K=1/(100k Q_K). Its constants now depend on the
FIXED K,p,q. The short sources have absolute price at most
(p^K+p^(K+1)) times their cutoff lengths. The cofactor sum has a
nonzero-frequency gap1/Q_K, and the full residual has the uniform-in-X
divisor bound p^(K+1)d_3(n). Thus every complement in (4.3) is still
paid for each fixed K; none is erased by support notation.

At tau=1 the remaining h_K cofactor is zero at every prime j for K>=1.
For j prime this also follows directly from
(v-v*h)(j)=-v(1)chi(j)=0. On the region B_X(n)>=1 this also excludes
the long-variable label d=1, while h_K(1)=0 excludes d=n. Hence its
WHOLE semiprime projection, including squares of large primes, is
exactly zero. If u=2gamma-r>0 (as in all three target rows), B_X(n)>=1
throughout the finite core for sufficiently large X, so the whole-core
claim applies. Without that hypothesis it is a statement only on the
specified region; the possible d=1 upper complement must be retained.
This is a real escape from the semiprime profile in Section7.

It also preserves the zero return: the numerator of c_K is

    chi(p)^K p^(K(1-z)) P_p(z),                   (8.3)

and the extra factor never vanishes. The same fixed two-prime bank,
all-height local uniformity, finite-shift descent and ordinary-character
scope therefore apply for fixed K. This is no claim about K growing
with X. In fact (8.1) is precisely a fixed multiplicative dilation of
the original compensated source, so deflation alone gives no new
arithmetic exponent. It is credited as an attempted repair, not as an
independent new detector or an additional conditional c gain.

The next actual arithmetic cell is explicit. For principal chi take
n=p^(K+1)d, with d prime in

    X/(4p^(K+1))<d<=X/(2p^(K+1)).                (8.4)

For fixed K and large X, d>B_X(n)=X^gamma. The term with long variable
d has coefficient mu(d)h_K(p^(K+1))=(-1)(-p^K)=p^K. The possible
long variable pd has h_K(p^K)=0, and any higher p-adic power in that
variable has Mobius coefficient0. Every other long-variable label is
excluded or zero. Hence the ENTIRE merged coefficient is+p^K.
Its selected full-shell norm is comparable to

    p^K X/[p^(K+1) log X] = X/[p log X].         (8.5)

Thus eliminating all semiprimes has shifted the positive cell to a
fixed valuation; it has not reduced its power price. This pays the
exceptional p-adic terms rather than discarding them after deflation.

There is also a precise limited growing-K diagnostic. Fix delta>0
with delta<1-gamma and allow p^(K+1)<=X^(1-gamma-delta).
Then the primes d in (8.4) still exceed X^gamma by a power. Ordinary
PNT is uniform because d is at least a fixed positive power of X.
With eta_K as above, B_X(n)=X^gamma throughout (8.4) for large X:
eta_K X is at least a constant times X^(gamma+delta).
The same exact merged-cell calculation therefore gives a uniform
lower bound of constant times X/log X. This concerns that selected
arithmetic cell only. It does NOT import (4.3) uniformly in growing K.
Indeed the elementary row constant is at most a fixed multiple of
p^(K+1)Q_K^2, and the short-term absolute budget contains p^K X^gamma.
Those costs grow as powers when K is proportional to log X. Beyond
this diagnostic range the cell can leave the long-variable support,
but the growing source, short terms and all-height return must then be
proved afresh. These are limitations of the proved upper budgets, not
lower bounds for the full short source or an impossibility theorem for
growing banks. The fixed-K theorem provides no permission to omit them.
