# Independent review: curved additive Laplace source



## Decision and material qualifications

**Recommend accepting the curved-source Mellin expansion, the complete
conditional ordinary-character zero return, the unconditional pointwise
x^(5/4+epsilon) bound, the exact rational-frequency formula, and the actual
diagonal/absolute-price results. No increased c is proved.** All parameters
and ordinary characters are fixed unless a formula explicitly introduces
an auxiliary modulus. Natural zeros, both short Vaughan terms, all physical
cutoffs and the infinite damping tail survive the reconstruction below.

Two distinctions should accompany integration. First, the unconditional
energy exponent 5/2 does not itself measure arithmetic progress: Section 8
proves the stronger E_b(X)<<_b X^(b+1), without epsilon, for EVERY bounded
coefficient sequence. The author's pointwise 5/4 estimate remains a genuine
arithmetic power saving over x^(3/2). Second, the rational identity is exact
at specific real x, but a shell L1/L2 hypothesis does not bound those points
at the same exponent. Section 9 supplies a paid point-observation bound;
isolated rational points alone are not an energy obstruction.

The independent additions include a paid reduction on each whole shell to
the coherent nonprincipal Gauss bank: for a frozen prime P comparable to X,
the principal Gauss term AND ramified correction cost only X^(b-1).
They also include the generic complete energy bound with a
sharp bounded-coefficient example, an upper absolute-price estimate matching
the author's lower exponent, and the explicit observation cost for this
actual curved source. A simple non-Mobius model also shows why the first
absolute Mellin remainder naturally stops at Re s=1/2. These statements
clarify the remaining arithmetic requirement; none supplies it.

Current comparison: c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and
theta11=.8748540364. This controller-accepted comparison remains relative
to F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external definition,
import and admission obligations. This review does not discharge them.
Its replacement return addresses fixed ordinary Dirichlet characters at
every finite height, with the principal pole exception; it makes no Hecke
or growing-conductor enlargement.

## 1. Source and ancestry audit

The complete frozen author report (26,153 bytes) and manifest were read in
tool chunk 718933. Report SHA256:
55d114a933cf619a68c9f0eaf34e118814ff2ec5cd71d99d56bd01a01eae42d0.
Manifest SHA256:
62f55d99df2ac46ca99e4128353b63c4efaffb8b8968a58d1a049201fe0cafeb.
The helper and output were read, not run. The independent helper verifies
these four complete frozen files against the supplied byte counts/hashes.

The current [restricted mathematical source] was read completely, recovering its
short wrapper-truncated tail separately; [restricted mathematical source] was
read in three complete bounded slices from the saved tool output. The
current proof's assumptions, detector return and latest relevant additions
were inspected, along with relevant entries in both older collective
indices. This is not a claim to have reread every linked historical proof.
W24 C5 proposed angular Mellin contours but supplied no paid curved-source
bound. W21's excursion argument supplies the general peak-width ancestry
for Section 9; only the curved source's derivative and resulting exponents
are added here. The prior renewal/BV pass is complete and not reopened.

The primary Green--Tao PDF was opened independently. Its Lemma 4.1 uses
positive integers U,V,N with UV<=N and a dyadic interval N<n<=2N. Its short
terms vanish there; that omission cannot be inherited by arbitrary prefixes.
The author's displayed all-integer convolution identity correctly restores
them, and is proved again below. [Green--Tao, Lemma 4.1, pp.1876-1877](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.2401.pdf).

The primary Bourgain--Sarnak--Ziegler Theorem 2 was also checked: a fixed
small correlation parameter gives a sufficiently-large-cutoff conclusion;
no power rate uniform under a shrinking parameter is provided by that
statement. It is discovery ancestry only. [Original source, Theorem 2](https://publications.ias.edu/sites/default/files/disjointness%20b-s-z%20oct.pdf).
No external theorem is imported to bound the new source. These primary
web reads do not establish locally retained original PDF binary hashes.

## 2. Contour rotation and absolute remainder

Fix b>1, delta=b-1, a_n=mu(n)chi(n), and

    F(z)=sum_(n>=1)a_n exp(-nz), Re z>0,
    V_b(x)=F(x^(-b)+i/x).

The series is normally convergent there, with |a_n|<=1 and the original
character zeros. For Re s>0 put

    I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-int)t^(s-1)dt.

With v=nt and e=n^(-delta), this is n^(-s) times the integral of
exp(-iv-e v^b)v^(s-1). Choose a FIXED angle 0<alpha<pi/(2b) and use
principal powers on -alpha<=arg v<=0. For each e>0 the large joining arc
is dominated by exp(-e R^b cos(b alpha)), because the modulus of exp(-iv)
is at most one throughout that sector. The small arc tends to zero for
Re s>0. Thus rotation to v=r exp(-i alpha) is valid. On that ray
Re(v^b)>0 and |exp(-iv)|=exp(-r sin alpha).

The integral Taylor remainder for exp(-z), Re z>=0, has modulus at most
|z|^K/K!. Consequently, for every fixed positive integer K,

    I_n(s)=sum_(k=0)^(K-1) A_k(s)n^(-s-delta k)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_k(s)=(-1)^k Gamma(s+bk)exp(-i*pi*(s+bk)/2)/k!,       (R1)
    |R_(n,K)(s)|<=C_(b,K,C)n^(-Re s-delta K).

The last estimate is uniform on each compact C in Re s>0. A valid
ray-integral majorant before taking its compact maximum is

    exp(alpha Im s) Gamma(Re s+bK)
      /[K! (sin alpha)^(Re s+bK)].

The coefficient integral can be evaluated by w=iv and rotation within
Re w>0. This gives precisely the phase in A_k; changing the sign of i/x
would conjugate the phase, so its sign is substantive. Every remainder
is holomorphic on Re s>0 by local integral domination. The n sum then
converges normally on Re s>max(0,1-delta K), including every finite
height. There is no claim of a bound uniform as |Im s| tends to infinity,
K grows, or b tends to 1.

Absolute Fubini initially holds on Re s>b, since the integral with the
oscillation removed is Gamma(sigma/b)n^(-sigma/b)/b. It gives

    H(s):=integral_0^infinity F(t^b+it)t^(s-1)dt
       =sum_(k=0)^(K-1) A_k(s)/L(s+delta k,chi)+R_K(s).   (R2)

This uses exactly the ordinary reciprocal L-series, with no artificial
Euler-factor deletion. Both sides have their usual meromorphic
continuations into the domain of the displayed remainder. In particular
at b=3/2, K=1,

    H(s)=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2)/L(s,chi)+R_1(s),
    R_1 holomorphic on Re s>1/2.                         (R3)

The rotation was justified for each n first; the uniform remainder bound
then justifies the infinite summation. No interchange at e=0 on the
unrotated oscillatory ray, no Mertens estimate and no assumed zero-free
strip entered this argument.

The half-plane of this K=1 ABSOLUTE remainder is sharp as a generic
bounded-coefficient statement. For the diagnostic sequence a_n=1,
F(z)=1/(exp z-1). At b=3/2, as t decreases to zero,

    F(t^(3/2)+it)=-i/t+t^(-1/2)+O(1).

The first Mellin term is A_0(s)zeta(s); it removes the pole at 1 but has
no pole at 1/2. The difference therefore has a nonzero pole at 1/2.
This model does NOT assert a pole for the actual Mobius remainder or
obstruct use of K>=2. It checks the necessity of the author's domain
qualification without importing unproved arithmetic cancellation.

## 3. Complete return and its exact quantifiers

Suppose for each fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0, on all large
dyadic shells,

    integral_X^(2X)|V_b(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (R4)

The fixed b and fixed gamma are common to the intended family; the
constant and onset may depend on chi and epsilon. Weighted absolute
integrability for every sigma>gamma is equivalent to (R4): one direction
is dyadic summation, and the reverse bounds one shell by its weight.
The L2 hypothesis with exponent 2gamma+epsilon implies (R4) by shell
Cauchy--Schwarz. No pointwise estimate or uniform conductor constant is
deduced in this step.

Under t=1/x, the small-t Mellin integral is holomorphic on Re s>gamma.
On each compact sub-half-plane choose epsilon strictly smaller than its
distance to the boundary; powers of log x needed for s derivatives are
absorbed by that fixed margin. For t>=1,

    |F(t^b+it)|<=exp(-t^b)/(1-exp(-t^b))

pays the full complementary tail. Hence H is holomorphic there.

For b=3/2 and gamma>1/2, (R3) directly makes 1/L holomorphic on
Re s>gamma. Its numerator Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2) has no zero or pole
there. Multiplication by L, first away from its principal pole, excludes
every L zero in that half-plane. At s=1 a principal L has its usual pole
and the reciprocal has a zero; this is retained, not called a zero of L.
Natural imprimitive Euler factors are part of L from the beginning;
their zeros on Re s=0 have not been removed from the source.

For a general fixed b>1 and 0<gamma<1 choose FINITE K such that
1-delta K<gamma. Start with the Euler-product zero-free domain Re s>1.
If 1/L is already holomorphic on Re s>alpha, all k>=1 shifted terms
in (R2) are holomorphic on Re s>max(gamma,alpha-delta). Solving (R2)
for 1/L, with the nonvanishing A_0, extends it to that half-plane.
Finitely many repetitions reach Re s>gamma. Strict inequalities at strip
edges cause no gap, because each extension is to an open half-plane.
The SAME H and fixed source occur throughout. Higher shifted reciprocals
are not silently placed in the error where they could have poles.

This is a proved conditional return, not an estimate for (R4). No reverse
equivalence to an ordinary Mertens bound has been shown. At b=3/2 the
conditional energy targets remain 1.7497 for gamma=.87485, 5/3 for
gamma=5/6, and 3/2 for gamma=3/4, each with every epsilon. Any first
gain must use gamma<.8748540364. The boundary gamma in the input is
allowed because the conclusion is the OPEN half-plane sigma>gamma.

## 4. The arithmetic pointwise bound survives the full prefix audit

For a given sufficiently large REAL x, put N=x^(3/2), T=N(log x)^2,
and U=V=floor(sqrt x). These integers are fixed throughout every
auxiliary prefix and the subsequent partial summation. The exact identity

    mu=mu_<=U+mu_<=V-mu_<=U*mu_<=V*1+mu_>U*mu_>V*1      (R5)

follows by expanding the last term and using mu*1=delta_1. It includes
n=1, squareful n, and BOTH short sums. The latter cost O(U+V).

Finite additive Fourier inversion of the original chi(n) reduces to
finitely many phases beta=ell/q-1/(2*pi*x), with total coefficient mass
bounded in terms of the fixed modulus q. This identity is applied before
the triangle inequality, so its exact natural zeros remain represented.

The following two elementary bounds are valid uniformly for real x large:

    sum_(d<=x)min(Y/d,1/(2||beta d||))
                      <<_q x log(2x)+Y/x,               (R6)
    sum_(h<=H)min(M,1/(2||beta h||))
                      <<_q (H/x+1)(M+x log(2x)).         (R7)

Here an exact resonance uses the finite first argument of min. To prove
(R7), split integers into intervals of length at most x and then into
their q residue classes. The fractional phase, with the rational part
frozen, advances monotonically by q/(2*pi*x); the total advance is less
than 1/(2*pi), up to harmless endpoint rounding. Remove at most two
nearest points to an integer, costing O(M). The other inverse distances
sum to O_q(x log(2x)) by their spacing. There are O(H/x+1) intervals
and only q classes. This proof also covers an integer lying just outside
the phase interval, and makes no Diophantine approximation assumption.

For (R6), the classes with ell d=0 mod q have exact distance d/(2*pi*x)
on d<=x and cost O(x log(2x)). On another class the initial fractional
part is j/q, 1<=j<q. A crossing of zero occurs at d*=2*pi*x*j/q.
Every nearest point in a fixed small neighborhood of that crossing has
d>=c_q x, so its finite cost is O_q(Y/x). The other points obey the same
harmonic-spacing bound. Distance to the integer 1 is at least 1/q on
these classes. If the crossing lies outside the interval, use its nearest
endpoint or the same spacing estimate. There is no discarded resonant d.
For example q=17, ell=1, d=103, x=1751/(2*pi) gives beta=6/103 and
beta d=6 EXACTLY, at a real x>d. It is handled by Y/d<<_q Y/x.

Type I has c_d=sum_(ab=d,a<=U,b<=V)mu(a)mu(b), supported on d<=UV<=x.
Using |c_d|<=tau(d)<<_eta d^eta and (R6), uniformly for Y<=T, gives
O_(q,epsilon)(x^(1+epsilon)). In particular Y/x<=x^(1/2)(log x)^2.
This is an upper bound, not a claim of an unavoidable actual Type I size.

For Type II write b_d=sum_(c|d,c>V)mu(c). The complete summation domain
is m>U, d>V, md<=Y. Dyadic boxes (M,2M]x(L,2L] which meet it have
ML<=Y and M,L<<Y/U; endpoint-truncated boxes are retained. Cauchy in m
gives an upper bound by M times the COMPLETE nonnegative Gram sum

    sum_(d,e)b_d conjugate(b_e)
       sum_(m in (M,2M], m<=Y/max(d,e)) e(beta m(d-e)).   (R8)

The inner set is one interval; its geometric sum is bounded by
min(CM,1/(2||beta(d-e)||)). Taking absolute values only at this stated
stage, and retaining the diagonal, gives

    |B|^2 << T^eta [M^2 L+ML(L/x+1)(M+x log(2x))]
          << T^eta (Y^2/U+Y^2/x+Yx)log(2x).              (R9)

Indeed M^2 L and ML^2 are <=C Y^2/U, (ML)^2/x<=Y^2/x,
and MLx<=Yx. The source's conjugation, difference sign and hyperbolic
intersection in (R8) are correct. No rectangular replacement of that
intersection is used. With Y<=T, (R9) is O(x^(5/2+epsilon)); the finite
Fourier expansion and O(log^2 x) boxes are absorbed. Thus

    sup_(Y<=T)|sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)chi(n)exp(-in/x)|
                        <<_(chi,epsilon)x^(5/4+epsilon). (R10)

Partial summation against exp(-n/N) costs at most a fixed multiple of
that supremum. The omitted infinite tail is bounded by
C N exp(-T/N)=O_A(x^(-A)) for every fixed A. This proves the literal
infinite-source estimate for every sufficiently large real x. No
character-free approximation, changing cutoff derivative, omitted short
term, integer-x restriction or unpriced tail remains.

## 5. Rational frequency decomposition, including its ramified branch

For P prime, P not dividing q, and (a,P)=1, finite orthogonality gives
on P-units

    e(an/P)=1/(P-1) sum_(psi mod P)psi(a)tau(conjugate psi)psi(n).

For Re s>1 this yields the unit part of the additive Dirichlet series.
For n=Pm use mu(Pm)=-mu(m)1_(P not dividing m), multiplicativity of
chi, and e(am)=1. The complete result is therefore

    sum_n mu(n)chi(n)e(an/P)n^(-s)
     =1/(P-1)sum_psi psi(a)tau(conjugate psi)/L(s,chi psi)
        -chi(P)P^(-s)/L(s,chi psi0).                    (R11)

The coefficient psi(a), not its conjugate, follows from the condition
u=an in the orthogonality sum. The negative ramified correction includes
the absence of P^2 multiples and every chi zero. Since tau(psi0)=-1,
the principal numerator is -1/(P-1)-chi(P)P^(-s), and

    L(s,chi psi0)=(1-chi(P)P^(-s))L(s,chi).

Both signs and that Euler factor are correct. The independent exact check
uses P=3 and a complex mod-5 character, so the ramified factor chi(P) is
nonreal; it does not merely repeat the author's real-character example.

At x=P/(2*pi) the source's phase is e(-n/P). Hence an attempted proof
using rational-frequency expansions must retain the growing-modulus twists
and the correction above. Bounds with uncontrolled character-dependent
constants cannot simply be summed uniformly over that moving family.
Absolute Gauss-sum summation may lose sqrt(P); this is a property of
that certificate, not a lower bound for the signed source. Moreover,
(R11) at isolated x does not turn (R4) into a pointwise hypothesis.
Section 9 quantifies a valid observation consequence instead.

### A paid whole-shell nonprincipal-bank reduction

There is a useful stronger conclusion from the literal identity. Freeze
an unramified prime P comparable to X before varying x over [X,2X], and
put w_P(x)=x^(-b)+i(1/x-2*pi/P). For any ordinary eta let
F_eta(w)=sum_n mu(n)eta(n)exp(-nw), Re w>0. Apply finite character
orthogonality to e(-n/P), leaving exp(-nw_P(x)) as the COMMON profile.
Absolute convergence proves for EVERY real x in the shell

    V_b,chi(x)=G_(P,chi)(x)+B_(P,chi)(x),                (R20)
    G_(P,chi)(x)=1/(P-1) sum_(psi mod P,psi!=psi0)
           psi(-1)tau(conjugate psi)F_(chi psi)(w_P(x)),
    B_(P,chi)(x)=-F_(chi psi0)(w_P(x))/(P-1)
                    -chi(P)F_(chi psi0)(P w_P(x)).

In the second branch n=Pm, the phase exp(-i m(P/x-2*pi)) is exactly
the original exp(-i Pm/x). Thus this is not merely an identity at the
isolated rational point x=P/(2*pi). The P^2 deletion remains in psi0;
the character product and all other natural zeros are unchanged.

The elementary bound |F_eta(w)|<=1/(exp(Re w)-1)<=1/Re w gives

    |B_(P,chi)(x)|<=x^b/(P-1)+x^b/P<=3x^b/P
                                      <<_b X^(b-1).   (R21)

Both branches are therefore paid over the ENTIRE physical shell, even
where the residual imaginary part vanishes. No estimate uniform in a
growing character is needed for (R21). For fixed q, all sufficiently
large such P are unramified. This statement is for any chosen P comparable
to X; selecting one per dyadic shell changes only the exact auxiliary
representation, not the global source used in the Mellin return.

For gamma>=b-1, the every-epsilon complete L1 hypothesis for V_b is
equivalent to that for the coherent G_(P,chi); the same is true of the
L2-energy hypotheses by the triangle inequality for their square-root
norms. Constants require a fixed lower bound for P/X. Equality at
gamma=b-1 is allowed in the every-epsilon formulation. At b=3/2 all
three targets in Section 3 have gamma>1/2, so the principal and ramified
sectors are fully paid. The remaining bank has only nonprincipal psi,
and for (P,q)=1 its products chi psi are also nonprincipal.

This is a restricted payment and an exact remaining target, not a bound
for that bank. A further triangle inequality over its P-2 terms generally
loses the coherent signs and may cost sqrt(P) in Gauss weights. The
source-relative fixed-character endpoint alone supplies no uniform
growing-family substitute. The useful task is the WHOLE signed bank norm
with the common w_P(x), retaining every x in the shell.

## 6. Actual diagonal and absolute price

Let a_n=mu(n)chi(n), with chi of fixed modulus q. From
mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counting q-units in each progression gives

    sum_(n<=Y)|a_n|^2=d_q Y+O_q(sqrt Y),
    d_q=(1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.        (R12)

The factor is (phi(q)/q)sum_((d,q)=1)mu(d)/d^2, which simplifies to
the displayed expression. The d tail and the O_q(1) counting errors both
cost O_q(sqrt Y). Damping and partial summation then give
sum_n |a_n|^2 exp(-2n/x^b)=d_q x^b/2+O_q(x^(b/2)).

With the author's exact kernel

    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(X^b u^b))
                         exp(-i(n-m)/(Xu))du/u,

absolute Fubini is valid on each fixed shell. The diagonal of the complete
energy is exactly

    d_q(2^b-1)X^b/(2b)+O_q(X^(b/2)).                    (R13)

This is not a lower bound for the whole signed energy.

For the absolute off-diagonal price put N=X^b and partition [N,2N]
into O(N/H+1) bins of length at most H=floor(X/4). There are
A=d_q N+O_q(sqrt N+1) squarefree units. If A_j counts them in the
bins, sum A_j^2>=A^2/(number of bins)>>_q NH. Removing A diagonal
pairs still leaves >>_q NH distinct ordered pairs. On each such pair
|n-m|<=X/4 and n+m<=4X^b; hence

    Re K_X(n,m)>=exp(-4)cos(1/4)log 2>0.

Their coefficient modulus is one. This proves the author's genuine
actual-coefficient lower price

    sum_(n!=m)|a_n conjugate(a_m)K_X(n,m)|>>_(q,b)X^(b+1). (R14)

No signed Mobius correlation, principal-character restriction or total
energy lower bound was inserted. The same conclusion holds for every
fixed ordinary character because d_q>0.

An independent upper estimate identifies the exponent of that price.
For h=|n-m|>=1, substitute v=1/u and integrate the phase once by parts.
The amplitude v^(-1)exp(-(n+m)v^b/N), its endpoint values and total
variation are bounded by C_b(1+(n+m)/N)exp(-c_b(n+m)/N). Absorb the
polynomial into a slightly weaker exponential to obtain

    |K_X(n,m)|<=C_b exp(-c'_b(n+m)/N)min(1,X/h).         (R15)

Summing first over min(n,m), and then h, costs
O_b(N[X+X log(2N/X)])=O_b(X^(b+1)log(2X)) for fixed b>1.
Together with (R14), the logarithmic power exponent of the actual
absolute off-diagonal price is b+1. This does not constrain a proof
which retains aggregate signs before pricing the pairs.

## 7. What remains unpaid in the author's arithmetic proof

At b=3/2 the short terms have exponent 1/2, Type I has only the proved
upper exponent 1, Type II has only 5/4, and the tail is rapidly paid.
The Yx and Y^2/U entries of (R9) both reach x^(5/2) at the longest
prefix. Neither is removed by changing an epsilon reserve. A better
Type II estimate alone would leave Type I above every proposed target.

A sufficient modular input is an every-shell L1 bound with exponent
gamma<theta11 for BOTH full smoothed Type I and Type II, retaining the
same frozen U,V, exact chi coefficients and every branch. A weaker and
potentially more useful input bounds their complete SIGNED combination;
the already-paid short terms and tail then give (R4). No individual
box, selected rational denominator, diagonal or generic square sum proves
either input. These remain exact open arithmetic problems.

The pointwise exponent 5/4 is a saving against the damping length x^(3/2),
not against the observation scale x. It therefore supplies no new c.
It is neither a lower bound nor a claim that changing b can solve the
problem through the same absolute Type II inequality.

## 8. Independent complete energy bound and its generic sharpness

For ANY fixed sequence |a_n|<=1 and fixed b>1, let V_b have the same
literal damping and phase. Then

    integral_X^(2X)|V_b(x)|^2 dx/x <<_b X^(b+1).         (R16)

This requires no Mobius identity, conductor information or epsilon.
Here is a direct proof retaining the infinite source and variable damping.
Set d=1/[2(2X)^b] and

    G(z)=sum_(n>=1)a_n exp(-dn)z^n.

It is analytic past the closed unit disk. For x in [X,2X], write
theta=1/x and Delta=x^(-b)-d. Then d<=Delta<=(2^(b+1)-1)d and
V_b(x)=G(exp(-Delta-i theta)). The subharmonic Poisson inequality,
which also follows from Cauchy--Schwarz in the Poisson representation,
gives

    |G(exp(-Delta-i theta))|^2
      <=(1/(2*pi)) integral_0^(2*pi) P_Delta(theta-phi)
                                         |G(exp(-i phi))|^2 dphi,
    P_Delta(t)=sinh(Delta)/(cosh(Delta)-cos t).

Since Delta is between d and C_b d, P_Delta(t)<=C'_b P_d(t)
uniformly in t for X large: increase the numerator to sinh(C_b d)
and decrease the denominator to cosh d-cos t. The ratio
sinh(C_b d)/sinh d is bounded by a b-dependent constant.

Now dx/x=dtheta/theta<=2X dtheta in absolute value. Integrate theta
over [1/(2X),1/X], enlarge that interval to one full period only in
the positive Poisson integral, and use its mass 2*pi. Parseval gives

    E_b(X)<=C_b X sum_n |a_n|^2 exp(-2dn)
            <=C_b X/d <<_b X^(b+1).

The Poisson domination, rather than an unproved substitution of fixed
damping, is what licenses this complete varying-profile estimate.

The exponent is sharp for uniform bounds over arbitrary bounded arrays
at a single scale. Take N=floor(X^b), x0=3X/2, and a_n=exp(in/x0)
for 1<=n<=N, zero otherwise. Where |1/x-1/x0|<=1/(4N), the real part
of every rotated term is positive and bounded below by a fixed constant;
the sum has size >>_b N. This interval lies in [X,2X] for large X and
has logarithmic measure comparable to X/N. Its energy is >>_b NX.
These coefficients depend on X and are not mu(n)chi(n). The example
only proves sharpness of the generic certificate, not of the arithmetic
source or of a theorem for a single preselected coefficient sequence.

At b=3/2, (R16) improves the author's unconditional energy statement by
removing epsilon, but carries NO arithmetic exponent gain. Its exponent
is 5/2, still far above 1.7497080728. The pointwise theorem (R10)
is not subsumed by (R16); converting the latter back to pointwise
control by the next section recovers only the trivial x^b exponent.

## 9. Paid observation at rational points

Differentiation of the actual absolutely convergent source gives, on a
fixed enlarged shell [X/2,4X],

    |V_b'(x)|<=C_b sum_n n exp(-n/x^b)
                                 (x^(-b-1)+x^(-2))
               <<_b X^(b-1)+X^(2b-2)<<_b X^(2b-2).     (R17)

If |V_b(x0)|=A at x0 in [X,2X], it remains >=A/2 on an interval of
length >>_b A/X^(2b-2). The trivial A<<X^b ensures this interval
fits inside the enlarged shell for large X because b>1. Thus its L2
mass is >>_b A^3/X^(2b-1), and its L1 mass is
>>_b A^2/X^(2b-1). Applying all-shell hypotheses to the finitely many
dyadic shells covering that interval yields

    E_b(X)<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)
       => |V_b(x0)|<<X^((2gamma+2b-1)/3+epsilon),        (R18)
    L1_b(X)<<X^(gamma+epsilon)
       => |V_b(x0)|<<X^((gamma+2b-1)/2+epsilon).         (R19)

The every-epsilon convention absorbs fixed factors and the rescaling of
epsilon. At b=3/2, the quarter-energy target implies pointwise exponent
7/6, not 3/4. At the current first-gain energy boundary, (R18)'s limiting
point exponent is (2theta11+2)/3=1.249902690933... . The L1 hypothesis
has a still weaker point consequence. No lower bound for values at
rational points is provided by (R11), and no isolated values are silently
used as lower bounds for shell integrals. This is the precise scope
qualification needed for the author's growing-twist discussion.

The peak-width principle is old in this project's W21 review. The new
content here is its direct derivative price for this curved additive
source and its use to delimit the rational-frequency interpretation.

## 10. Verification, research value and next action

The finite independent helper verifies all four author pins, the exact
rational-frequency formula for P=3, a=+/-1 and the complex mod-5 character
through n=243, including its ramified and natural-zero cases. It separately
checks the ordered-pair Gram against the original varying hyperbolic
row sums at beta=1/3: both give the nonzero value 3. It records an exact
real-x resonance and rational target/observation exponents. The run
returned PASS, exit0, chunk 8ba707; the Python launcher also emitted its
existing path diagnostic. No author helper or unchanged check was rerun.
These finite checks are evidence for signs, endpoints and arithmetic
consistency. They are not proofs of contour rotation, asymptotics, power
bounds or zero exclusion; the arguments above carry those claims.

The report establishes a genuine replacement detector and a useful actual
pointwise arithmetic theorem. It does not prove the much stronger
complete shell arithmetic input. Its novel-to-record content should be
credited separately from W24's angular-contour seed, classical Vaughan
factorization, ordinary Poisson/Parseval estimates and W21 observation
ancestry. No literature-priority assertion is made.

The next mathematical action is a signed estimate for the COMPLETE
smoothed Type I/II recombination, the coherent nonprincipal bank (R20),
or a direct bound for (R4), on every large physical shell. For P comparable
to X the principal and ramified sectors are now paid by (R21); the moving
nonprincipal family and common shell measurement remain. Any pairwise
energy method must avoid the X^(b+1)
absolute price. Both near gains and the 1/6 and 1/4 targets remain live
conditional goals. None follows from the present representation or
generic energy bound.

No current endpoint, original source obligation, other writer's claim,
or frozen author file is changed. Final whole-file readback, hashes and
normal release of this review's exact fresh claim precede the root STOP
handoff.

## 6. Joint high count and exact label costs

**Classification: proved written reconstruction/density application relative to the fixed-family inputs above.**

For one first-side orientation let `L_c=log_Z NF_c`, `T_c=(c-d)_+`, and let `R0` be the active radical width whose signed row residue cancels. The actual support of the complete row gives

`log_Z Nw <= W+O(eta)`, `W=M-R-T_c+L_c-6a`, `L_c<=5(R-R0)`.

The extra `-omega` is favorable and may be dropped. Every genuine second common prime and the first projector divides `w`. The first radical absent from `w` has width at most `p-R-E+R0`: this includes the inactive net-zero primes and the canceled active ones. Count that missing radical explicitly. Once it and `w` are fixed, all remaining first and second common labels, first projector, valuations and bounded allocation choices are divisor-many.

This last statement does not rely on bounded valuations. Uniformly for `NQ<=Z^B`, `NI<=Z^T`, Rankin gives

`#{I: rad(I)|Q, NI<=Z^T} <= Z^(sT) product_(p|Q) (1-(Np)^(-s))^(-1)`.

Choose `sT` small. For any `b>0`, all sufficiently large prime factors in the product are at most `(Np)^b`; the finitely many smaller factors give a constant. Choosing `bB` small gives `O(Z^epsilon)`. Counting the missing radical itself costs exactly its norm exponent, since the fixed field has `O(X)` ideals of norm at most `X`. Fixed finite slot assignments can increase the eventual constants but not this exponent. This proves the arbitrary-valuation reconstruction needed by the source family.

Density therefore bounds the **joint** rows and first/common labels by

`Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+eta) (1+T_h)^J`.

If the supported bound is negative the row set is empty. A nonempty slightly negative nominal `W` is at least `-O(eta)`; fill the bounded row ball and charge that same tolerance. No population below one is asserted for a nonempty integral window.

The second projector label is deliberately outside this reconstruction. In each dyadic sector PR9 B3.67–B3.69 pays its count together with **both** exact extraction scalars. After that cancellation the remaining pointwise clipping reductions are nonpositive: paired cost is `delta(alpha1+alpha2-rclip1-rclip2)/2+O(thetaN)`. One may consequently use the pre-reduction paired size `Z^(delta(A-c-b2)+eta)` without incorrectly claiming `t|w`. Signs lost by a triangle inequality cost only the scalar masses that were paid; no unrestricted new arithmetic coefficient is substituted into a moment theorem.

The outside second-transform exponent at the actual main radius is

`A-min(c,d)+R+E-M+5a+g2-t2-b2+O(eta)`.

Subtracting the joint target `p+A-c+R+E+B_c` gives exactly PLA LA.13:

`M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)`

`+(1-rho)T_c-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c+rho L_c+R0`

`+g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+O(eta)`.

I independently expanded this expression, retaining the missing-radical and first-radical terms; the controller independently reported the same result. To bound its second line use `c=min(c,d)+T_c`, `min(c,d)>=p>=R`, `L_c<=5(R-R0)`, `rho+delta>1`, `5rho>1`, and `4rho-1>0`. It is at most

`(4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c <= -79p/270-E-B_c`.

The third line is at most `-delta b2-t2` since `g2<=b2`. On `delta in [0.7,0.75]` the weaker `A/M<=113/125` gives

`1-rho-delta A/M >= 259/16875`, `5-6rho<=23/7`.

With `a=M/2000`, even adding total high losses `M/1000` leaves excess below `-M/100`. Every genuinely high bin has lower `delta>=0.7`, hence zero-real-part threshold at least `17/20`, precisely the density range. The low side handles bins crossing the threshold. The joint proof already paid the first labels; no additional label factor is charged afterward.

### Exact source and replacement

Use current-proof G11--G20, with tau=1,kappa=C=D=2,a=3/4 and Y=floor(X^.495). Keep each original bin I_i, its actual intersection with Y<d<=Dmax, all ordered pairs i+j=-2,-1,0,1, mu(d), the complete alternating ell source and eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s). Native interval endpoints/cap inclusions are not redefined. There are O(sqrt(log X)) ordered components. On every nonempty bin the endpoint sizes D_i obey

    X^(.495+o(1))<=D_i<=X^(.505+o(1)),
    D_i D_j=X^(1+o(1)) on every retained ordered pair.       (D04.1)

Here D_i is its actual upper endpoint; clipping changes these only by subpower factors. This follows from Y, Dmax=B_X/(Y+1) and each of the four bin diagonals. None is an SP smooth-state bin.

Fix0<delta<.495. For each exact interval choose a C-infinity function psi_i(v) with0<=psi_i<=1, supported within its real interval, equal to1 away from collars of lengths endpoint*X^-delta at both endpoints. For a very short clipped interval the collars may cover it completely; setting psi_i=0 is allowed. Then on the integers the difference from the original indicator is supported in the two collars, including every integer endpoint whose convention differs. There is no missing endpoint atom. The collar contains O(D_i X^-delta+1) integers; its n-values are D_i X^o(1). Such functions exist from a fixed C-infinity step with derivatives vanishing at its endpoints. Their k-th log derivatives cost O_k(X^(k delta)); derivative constants are NOT free subpower costs.

Define finite literal polynomials

    U_i(s)=sum_(d in I_i)mu(d)d^-s,
    V_i(s)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d)psi_i(d)d^-s,
    Delta_i=U_i-V_i.

The new source is a deliberately changed mask. Its differences remain explicit. For the accepted buffered rational Mertens bound M(t)=O(t^beta), take the conservative beta=8749/10000. At a=3/4, Abel summation at both original endpoints gives

    |U_i(a+it)| << (1+|t|)D_i^(beta-a),
    |Delta_i(a+it)| << X^(-delta+o(1))D_i^(1-a).           (D04.2)

The second inequality uses only |mu|<=1 and the full collar count. Because delta<.495, D_iX^-delta tends to infinity and absorbs the+1 endpoints. It makes no assumption of Möbius short-interval cancellation. The empty/clipped-bin case is included.

Put

    Zpsi_X(x)=(2pi)^-1 integral_[-T,T]
      exp((a+it)^2/2)eta(a+it)
         sum_(i+j=-2,...,1)V_i(a+it)V_j(a+it)x^(a+it)dt,
    T=2sqrt(log X).

This retains all ordered interactions and both independent height variables when its square is expanded. It does not introduce H projectors or claim anything about the distinct H form. No ell-dependent source mask has been smuggled into G8/G9.

## 3. Exact strengthened local theorem

**Theorem L44, relative to the accepted PR9 analytic inputs and Gao's signed-row/dictionary/density/transport lemmas.** Assume 51/100<=beta_*<=7/8. Fix the same admissible natural parent family as LA: a fixed finite ray factor times the literal extended sextic row, with no positive-width moving parent support. For d<1/2, ell/d>2ell>1/3 while old capacity is <=1/(6kappa)<=5/21; elsewhere y<4ell proves old supply. No lower-row supply condition is omitted.

## 2. Independent inverse and complete residual reconstruction

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a FIXED positive integer q, and an integer N>=1. Let

    S_N = {a<=N : a is squarefree and gcd(a,q)=1},
    E_(a,d) = 1_(d divides a),
    M = diag(mu(a)),
    D = diag(mu(d) conjugate(chi(d))),
    A = E D E^T.

All indices lie in S_N, ordered increasingly; 1 is included. This set is divisor closed. Mobius inversion gives E^(-1)=M E M. Every entry of D is nonzero, since |chi(d)|=1 on S_N, and D^(-1)=diag(mu(d)chi(d)). Consequently

    (A^(-1))_(a,b)
      = mu(a)mu(b) sum_(d in S_N, lcm(a,b)|d) mu(d)chi(d).       (1)

The transpose is the ordinary transpose, not the conjugate transpose. For nonreal characters A is complex symmetric, generally not Hermitian. The gauge diag(chi) K diag(chi) of the untwisted K would keep its inverse (1,1) entry untwisted and is not an alternative derivation of (1).

Write g=gcd(a,b), l=lcm(a,b), and d=lm. The requirement d squarefree is equivalent here to m squarefree and gcd(m,l)=1; natural character zeros add gcd(m,q)=1. Since mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g), (1) becomes

    (A^(-1))_(a,b)
      = mu(g)chi(l) sum_(m<=N/l, gcd(m,lq)=1) mu(m)chi(m).       (2)

It is zero for l>N. In particular

    R(a) = (A^(-1))_(1,a)
         = chi(a) sum_(m<=N/a, gcd(m,aq)=1) mu(m)chi(m),
    |R(a)| <= floor(N/a) <= N/a,
    (A^(-1))_(1,1) = M_chi(N) = sum_(n<=N) mu(n)chi(n).         (3)

For ANY column z on the actual S_N set r=e_1-Az. Multiplication by A^(-1), followed by its first coordinate, gives the COMPLETE identity

    M_chi(N) = z_1 + sum_(a in S_N) R(a)r(a).                  (4)

Define two distinct complete absolute bills

    B(z) = sum_(a in S_N) |R(a)r(a)|,
    W(z) = N sum_(a in S_N) |r(a)|/a.

Then |M_chi(N)-z_1|<=B(z)<=W(z). A sufficient pointwise certificate is |z_1|+B(z), or the stronger explicit |z_1|+W(z), bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large N. With the fixed-character quantifiers this gives the usual Mellin continuation of 1/L and zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. The principal pole at 1 is permitted. Nothing below supplies the required estimate of z_1.

statement:
# Uniform stationary expansion used in the independent H proof

This is supplementary proof detail for report.md Sections3-4. It concerns only the fixed physical phase exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6), fixed period Q, all real x in[X,2X], and smooth common output blocks. It does not grant arbitrary sharp row cutoffs, live-x coefficients or varying periods.

Write x=Xz, n=Nt, T=(N/X)^6, rho=N/X^(3/2), a_z(t)=w(t)exp(-rho t/z^(3/2)), and R=rN/T. The oscillatory integral is

    N integral a_z(t)exp(i T phi_(R,z)(t))dt,
    phi_(R,z)(t)=2pi R t/Q-t^6/z^6.

For c_Q<=R<=C_Q and1<=z<=2, the critical point

    t0=(pi R/(3Q))^(1/5)z^(6/5)

belongs to a fixed positive compact interval J_Q. Moreover phi''(t0)=-30 t0^4/z^6 is negative and bounded away from zero; every fixed derivative is bounded on an enlarged fixed positive interval. These bounds include t0 outside the support[1,4] of w. Every fixed derivative of a_z, in t and z, is bounded by C_j e^(-c rho), because a polynomial in rho times e^(-rho/2^(3/2)) has that bound after weakening c. The constants do not depend on N,X,r,m or live z.

Choose a small fixed radius eta_Q so that the phi'' bound holds within distance2eta_Q of every such t0. Let chi0 be a smooth bump equal to1 at distance<=eta_Q and0 at distance>=2eta_Q. Split a_z into chi0(t-t0)a_z and its complement. The phase has a uniformly nonzero first derivative on the support of that complement, and two integrations by parts give O(T^-2 e^(-c rho)) before multiplying by N. All cutoff derivatives are uniform, including the t0-dependence. This is a pointwise estimate in z; no derivative of the remainder is required for the later error sum.

On the near part set

    y=sgn(t-t0)sqrt(phi(t0)-phi(t)).

The ratio (phi(t0)-phi(t))/(t-t0)^2 is uniformly positive with bounded derivatives. Thus y(t) is a smooth increasing local coordinate with a uniformly smooth inverse, and y'(t0)=sqrt(|phi''(t0)|/2). The transformed amplitude B_(R,z,rho)(y), including the cutoff and Jacobian, is supported in one fixed compact interval and has every fixed derivative bounded by C_j e^(-c rho). Smooth extension by zero is valid because the cutoff is flat at its support boundary. The transformed phase is exactly phi(t0)-y^2.

The Fresnel leading term is

    integral B(y)e^(-iT y^2)dy
      =e^(-i pi/4)sqrt(pi/T)B(0)+O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)).

One can obtain the quoted weak error directly with a fixed even bump kappa equal to1 near0. Write B(y)=B(0)kappa(y)+y C(y). The quotient C extends smoothly through0, has compact support and bounded first derivative controlled by finitely many derivatives of B. For its contribution use y e^(-iTy^2)=-(2iT)^(-1)(d/dy)e^(-iTy^2), then integrate by parts; its absolute value is O(T^-1 ||C'||_1). The kappa integral differs from the full regularized Fresnel integral by O(T^-2) through integration by parts away from0. This last assertion follows first with a decaying regulator and then by convergence, or with finite symmetric endpoints followed by their oscillatory limit. All constants are uniform on the compact parameter family. This proves the needed weak expansion without assuming uniformity from an unspecified asymptotic O-constant.

Since B(0)=a_z(t0)sqrt(2/|phi''(t0)|), restoring N gives exactly

    sqrt(pi/15)x^3 n_r(x)^(-2)w(n_r(x)/N)
           exp(-n_r(x)/x^(3/2))
           exp(i5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5)r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4),

with error O((N/T)e^(-c rho)). If t0 lies outside the support of w, B(0)=0. When it crosses an endpoint of that support, the whole construction remains uniform; no endpoint transition was dropped. A sharp, row-dependent indicator would invalidate this smooth-amplitude argument and is deliberately absent.

For nonstationary aliases the rescaled derivative is 2pi hN/(Qm)-6Tt^5/z^6. Outside the fixed near-positive window it has the lower bounds used in the report. Twice applying the operator (i phi_full')^-1 d/dt differentiates the amplitude twice and the phase at most three times. In the moderate-alias regime all phase derivatives are O(T) and the first is >=cT, giving T^-2. In the far-alias regime L=|h|N/m dominates T and all higher derivatives are O(T)<=O(L), giving L^-2. The original prefactor N/m therefore gives respectively (N/m)T^-2 and (m/N)h^-2. This includes both signs of h; h=0 and other multiples of Q vanish exactly through beta_h. Every amplitude derivative retains e^(-c rho).

The final Gram integration uses no derivative of this remainder: the complete transformed-row remainder is first summed absolutely and paid by norm triangle. Only the explicit main amplitude Z_r is differentiated. For its derivative, n_r(Xz) has derivative(6/5)n_r/z; on the support of w or w', n_r~N. The prefactor x^3 n_r^-2 is O(N/sqrt T), and differentiating it changes only a bounded factor. Differentiating damping introduces O(rho), absorbed in e^(-c rho). Hence both |Z_r| and |dZ_r/dz| are O((N/sqrt T)e^(-c rho)).

The product Z_r conjugate(Z_s)/z has the same type of first-variation bound at squared scale. The difference phase derivative is comparable to N|r-s| and its logarithmic derivative is1/(5z). Ordinary integration by parts on[1,2] therefore retains the two finite endpoint terms and proves the complete Gram estimate. No shell smoothing or endpoint cancellation is required at this stage.

Primary reference checked: https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/247b.1.07w/notes8.pdf, printed pages6-8. Only the standard Fresnel/nonstationary normalization is borrowed; the family-uniform estimates, explicit scales, all alias sums, denominator floor and source transfer are established in the report and this supplement. No outside arithmetic result is used.

## 6. What changed, what survived, and the next useful mathematical test

Proved here (pending independent review):

- The literal squarefree divisor source has exp(B)=Z with its complete arithmetic
  cutoff and character, and its entire positive chain mass has sharp power1. This
  repairs the uncontrolled factorial/full-integer permanent price in the initial
  Redheffer prospect. It also identifies the exact norm-only semigroup failure.
- The same fixed prime compensator pays the COMPLETE first J chain sectors at
  beta_J=max(1/2,1-1/J) for all fixed ordinary characters. This is an actual source
  estimate, including principal characters, all shifts and all overlaps.
- The unbounded remaining chain sum is exactly a bounded-color Newton remainder,
  with explicit positive principal coefficients before compensation and every
  p-valuation after it. Its complete coarse bound and the precise missing power
  are retained. No total signed saving has been proved.

The new arithmetic target is cancellation across the entire valuation-linked tail
(27), equivalently its complete summatory source(23). A useful next test must keep
those links, or improve a genuinely growing-depth complete estimate; another
individual-color estimate or a singular-vector alignment theorem alone is not
sufficient. The route's high ceiling is conditional and not evidence that it is
currently easier than OPEN-RECT or the original reciprocal source. The recent
constant-cut/Hecke work remains available with its own source contracts.

Credit: finite-poset Redheffer identity and ordered-factorization interpretation
are due to Wilf/Redheffer; Vaughan supplies characteristic-polynomial ancestry.
The optional controller prospect proposed this squarefree downset and flagged the
factorial danger. Prime-cover exponentials, Stirling/Newton identities, periodic
hyperbola inclusion-exclusion and Euler products are standard ingredients. The
bounded source-specific combination and the full estimates/limitations above are
new in this record, without any literature-priority claim.

## Independent parked audit B: uniform S52, literal post-projector Fourier visibility

The protected S29 was reserved. Excluding the10 author-tested cards and S29 leaves49 cards from ALL groups. The entire ordered pool was frozen before a single uniform draw: pool SHA256 1723f4d7dbc8d023f5d199509c46c08165c845ce1956b320bb8806fef57e9c42; seed144058667576375153821187610876778501730; index40; chosenS52; timestamp01:28:03.404407UTC. No reroll. This is a selection audit distinct from the following mathematical argument.

Use the actual JN1-JN16 long-prime packet, with both physical coprimality projectors, sharp masks, complete signed core w=sum_d W_d, and original character zeros. q,q' are distinct degree-one long-prime norms about N, Q=qq' about N^2. The row support has O(K) elements; each mark support has O(L). These inject into their finite quotient rings because Q>>K and q,q'>>L. The group is (O/(pi pi')) times (O/pi) times (O/pi'), of size Q^2; joint Fourier normalization is1/Q. All actual coefficients and projectors stay inside w.

JN12 proves for any J row frequencies E, retaining all mark frequencies,

    sum_(h in E,s,s')|w_hat(h,s,s')|^2 <= C KJ/Q ||w_hat||_2^2.

The actual JN9 characters subsequently delete h nonunit mod pi pi', s=0 mod pi and s'=0 mod pi'. On the surviving set their powers are unit phases. To make the denominator after these deletions explicit, apply the same support/partial-Plancherel argument to each marginal. There are q+q'-1 nonunit h frequencies by CRT; each singleton s or s' captures at most C L/q or C L/q' of the full energy. The union bound gives

    ||P_visible w_hat||_2^2 >= (1-kappa)||w_hat||_2^2,
    kappa=C_orig[K(q+q'-1)/Q+L/q+L/q'].

No independence of the three losses is assumed. The constant is fixed for the specified original packet/common profile, not uniform over arbitrary changing input families. In its hard box K=Z^.835507578307735986, L=Z^.170813789153867993, N=K Z^.003, one has kappa=O(Z^-.003)+O(L/N), tending to zero. Thus, for large Z,

    captured visible fraction <= C KJ/[Q(1-kappa)].

A single literal row-Fourier-channel mode captures at most O(K/N^2). A norm-faithful dictionary needs J comparable to at least Q/K=N Z^.003. Even O(N) channels capture only O(Z^-.003). This statement uses the ACTUAL signed source after both physical projectors and remains valid after the natural zero-extended Fourier character factors. It fills the visible-denominator detail in the already known JN11-JN14 obstruction.

Scope: this is not a native resolvent-pole certificate. No actual evolution operator or nearly undamped eigenvalue was supplied by S52. It excludes only the specified small coordinate dictionary as a faithful full norm representation. A single DENSE rank-one direction adapted to the entire w is not excluded. The full signed H scalar can cancel even when Fourier norm is large; no scalar lower bound or H exponent follows. Exceptional packets outside this explicitly chosen JN box and full original-family summation are not discarded by this local calculation. Validity: accepted source-specific Fourier visibility bound. Novelty: mostly duplicate JN dictionary obstruction with a narrow actual-character extension. Potential: guards source-resolvent proposals against claiming that both projectors or natural zeros cheaply remove the missing frequency mass. General S52 remains promising-unbridged.

Restoring the previously paid pure-cube and one-unit-core sectors gives
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak Q_{\rm rem}
={}&\mathfrak Q_{q_c>C,\ q_e>C}-\mathfrak Q_{II}\\
&+O_\epsilon\!\left(
DK^{1+\epsilon}+D^{11/6+\epsilon}
+D^{7/6+2b/3+\epsilon}C^{4b/3-1/6}\right).
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{BC18}
\]
The whole signed II subtraction is retained. T05 pays its stated
physical cube-row piece only; this packet makes no new claim about
the rest of II and does not identify it with a transformed zero term.

For balanced largest cores `C=E=D`, the proved moment budget is only
\[
|\mathcal B_{D,D}(a+it)|\ll T^A D^{1+2b+\epsilon},
\]
whose limiting exponent is
`1+2b0=2.749773294079928...`. Thus the argument does not pay the
remaining double-large sector, and this budget should not replace a
better existing global sieve bound where that applies.

A concrete sufficient next estimate is (BC5), with its exact
`T_c,e`, bounded by
\[
|\mathcal B_{C,E}(a+it)|
\ll T^A D^{2+\epsilon}E_N(C/D)E_N(E/D)
\]
uniformly for the remaining core dyads, with `a` chosen as above.
At `C=E=D`, its dual formulation has the actual twists (BC12),
effective dual length `D^4 T^4`, primitive conductors at most
`q_mathfrak_n`, and weight
`q_mathfrak_n^(a-1) V(q_mathfrak_n/(D^4 T^4))`.
The present separate Möbius bounds leave a further required saving
`D^(2b0-1)=D^.749773294079928...`. That weighted average is open;
no uniform Hecke moment is asserted.

statement:
# Outside-band arithmetic: a two-prime source and its complete complement



## 1. Result and boundary

There is a further source-relative moment saving for an explicit quadratic
prime-divisor weight supported BELOW the accepted prime band. It uses TWO
new prime slots, their full repeated-prime diagonal, and the exact quotient
of a prime pair by its gcd with every extracted plain ideal. Its complete
joint-cut subtraction is paid. The original signs, natural zeros and all
original slots remain.

Put Z=U^eta, A=Z^2 and Y=T=Z^4. Let J be the good prime IDEALS with
Z<=Np<A. For Nb>1 define

    omega(b) = (log Nb)^(-2)
       sum_(p,q in J, pq|b) (log Np)(log Nq),             (1)

where the pair is ordered and p=q requires p^2|b. Set omega(1)=0.
This is not the square of the old additive band weight. The result is

    ||C_T^[omega] Q||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon).             (2)

Here C_T is the COMPLETE literal tuple cut from the accepted coupled-cut
proof, beta is the SAME internal buffered grade in both the original plain
spike and every shortened upper bound, and all notation is fixed in Section2.
The estimate concerns the actual signed source, not a positive subseries.

Keep every previously paid row class first. A new disjoint class saves
2delta eta in the original inverse moment. Every remaining row retains

    |C_T^[1-theta-omega]| > |M(R)S(D)|/8,               (3)
    0 <= 1-theta(b)-omega(b) <= 1-theta(b),
    N(n/rad n) < U^(4eta) NP.

The middle inequality is a COEFFICIENT statement; no signed norm ordering
is inferred from it. Pure large-prime plain columns remain unchanged. The
complete coarse inverse moment is still U^(1+epsilon). Thus J_eta^all and
a larger c remain OPEN. The accepted written c11=.1251459636, c10-licensed
K, F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external
admission obligations are unchanged.

The serious large-prime attack in Section3 fails at its actual extraction
price. Equation(2) is instead a proved candidate further restriction on
outside-band coefficients that the previous one-slot convolution did not
detect. No theorem quota, high-zero existence or literature priority claim
is being used.

## 2. Literal source and fixed quantifiers

Use the original Eisenstein ideal/primary convention, excluded set S,
fixed finite dictionary and phi_u=nu psi_u^(+/-1) with one common orientation.
The fixed phase nu need not have order six. Natural character zeros and
fixed holes remain in every sum. Licensed anchoring or whole conjugation
is performed on the WHOLE system before this argument.
Every displayed prime pool retains the fixed plain prime omissions; moving
holes remain the original character zeros, not row-dependent pool choices.

    M_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_a mu(a)phi_u(a)W_I(Na/E),
    S_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_b phi_u(b)W_P(Nb/E).

Write R=U^r, D=U^m and B=M(R)S(D). Q is the complete original product of
disjoint prime slots of total width v. Their coefficients, pools, profiles,
holes and independent heights remain literal. The fixed slot count is
increased by TWO before the source's final threshold and height choices.
All enlarged slot data and required finite orders precede these witnesses.
No slot is divided out, and no new moving character is hidden in a coefficient.

Fix delta in[17/25,7/10], 0<eta<=1/1000 and 0<=v<=1/20. G137's common
cutoff t=t_*(delta,v)-eta is selected BEFORE witnesses. Work in its entire
crossing window |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta with the inherited fine endpoint padding.
Its actual saturated pair has r+m>=t-small, m<=1/2+small and m bounded
away from zero. Only the original licensed nonprincipal supported rows
are in Omega; all other branches retain their old estimates.
Norms use the original nonnegative row measure and its already paid divisor
envelopes, not an arbitrary new row weight.

Fix the internal bin, presentation and dyads. The SAME character, witness
real power and original height occur in M and S. With beta=2a-1,
beta>=delta-small and beta<=3/4, literal PR9 B0.13--20 gives

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E;V)|^2 <= H_J U^epsilon_det E^beta,
                         0<E<=C D.                    (4)

The upper bound uses the direct retained line a+6e, including the slight
tolerance beyond m=1/2. Nonempty subunit scales are bounded dilations;
smaller scales are empty. V belongs to the common smooth derivative family.
H_J denotes a fixed polynomial height envelope whose degree can increase
between displays. Beta cancels BEFORE weakening to physical delta.

The fully marked MI, PR9 B0.4/B3.31, permits arbitrary bounded fixed prime
coefficients and arbitrary disjoint prime supports. It gives U^(1+epsilon)
when r'+2z<=1-c1 and 2r'+8z<=3-c2. The whole crossing window has
r+2v<=1-.01017 before fine losses. Shortening an inverse improves both gates.
PR9 B3.6 does NOT allow an arbitrary merged-column coefficient.

The accepted coupled source split is B=B_T+C_T, on original ordered tuples,

    F(a,b)=N(a,b)*(N s2(b))^2,
    B_T: F>=T,          C_T: F<T,
    s2(b)=product_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2).

Equality belongs to the removed side. Its full divisor expansion uses
squarefree q0, arbitrary k, L=lcm(q0,k^2), the exact coefficient

    A_T(q0,k)=sum_(d|q0,e|k)mu(q0/d)mu(k/e)
                                      1_(Nd*(Ne)^2>=T),

and blocks M^(q0)(R/Nq0) S(D/NL). Their scalar includes
mu(q0)phi_u(q0 L)/sqrt(Nq0 NL). The accepted absolute MI coefficient mass,
after the shortened plain upper bound, is U^epsilon T^(-beta/2).
Every q0-smooth restoring power is included; no shared prime is declared
independent. This is the exact G198 input used below.

The accepted prime band is [A,Y], with
theta(b)=sum_(p in that band)v_p(b)log Np/log Nb. Its full weighted core
satisfies the analogue of(2). After all its earlier paid classes, the
remaining actual rows have |C_T^[1-theta]|>|B|/4. Superscripts always mean
tuple coefficient multiplication BEFORE the original signed summation.

## 3. Direct large-prime extraction: the actual unpaid price

For fixed squarefree h the exact inverse divisibility component is

    M_(h|a)(R)=mu(h)phi_u(h)(Nh)^(-1/2) M^(h)(R/Nh). (5)

The moving mask is restored by ALL h-smooth powers, with absolute mass
product_(p|h)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1)<<_epsilon (Nh)^epsilon.
This uses the original inverse, rather than a new coefficient theorem.

Suppose an outer shell Nh~U^kappa is summed absolutely with divisor-bounded
coefficients, before putting a plain prime of norm U^lambda into MI.
The shell coefficient price furnished by ideal counting is U^(kappa/2+epsilon).
The squared price is U^kappa. The first new gate requires

    r-kappa+2v+2lambda<1,
    kappa>2lambda-g,       g=1-r-2v,                  (6)

and the second additionally requires
kappa>r+4v+4lambda-3/2. The shortened plain upper bound saves beta lambda
in the squared norm. Thus this method's paid squared saving is at most

    beta lambda-max(0,2lambda-g),                    (7)

even before its second gate, fine losses and a full divisor cover. It
ceases to give a power saving once lambda>=g/(2-beta). This is a bound
on what this stated absolute extraction proves, NOT a lower bound for the
actual signed source. A thinner or coherently summed extraction could behave
differently, but needs its own complete cover and arithmetic estimate.

Keeping an extracted inverse prime as another live prime slot is no repair:
its first-power term has r'=r-kappa and z=v+kappa+lambda, so the first
gate becomes r+2v+kappa+2lambda<1, worse than the original large-prime gate.
The full coprimality restoration does not remove this first-power term.

A complete inverse decomposition cannot simply assume a divisor in the
desired intermediate shell. A prime inverse ideal has no such divisor.
Together with a coprime large-prime plain ideal it has F=1, theta=0 and
survives the actual source. This is a coefficient example, not an actual
high-zero row or a norm lower bound. The full complement has not been paid.

The already accepted amplified marked estimate G90 also remains available:

    E_MI=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2(v+lambda),
                                      (2r+8(v+lambda))/3).

The prime extraction and(4) yield inverse exponent E_MI-beta lambda.
For example take physical/internal grade7/10, v=0, eta=1/1000, the
full-fit G137 crossing t=25/18-1/1000, r=2t/3, m=t/3, and lambda=m.
Even with margins omitted this available exponent is
1121789/810000>1. This only shows that this licensed estimate does not
settle the large-prime sector; it is not evidence that signed cancellation
is impossible. The next arithmetic action there is a coherent estimate
across the h-sum, or a native estimate for the full large-prime marked
divisor profile, with the inverse-prime complement included.

## 4. The new weight is a genuine part of the outside mass

For a plain ideal b write

    ell_rad,J(b)=sum_(p in J,p|b)log Np,
    d_1,J(b)=sum_(p in J,v_p(b)=1)(log Np)^2.

Exact ordered-pair expansion gives

    omega(b)=[ell_rad,J(b)^2-d_1,J(b)]/(log Nb)^2.     (8)

The diagonal is included exactly once when p^2|b, even if v_p(b)>2.
Thus no higher valuation is silently omitted: every such b appears in the
remaining cofactor sum. The weight is defined by divisibility of a pair,
not by choosing two independently labelled occurrences in b.

Let ell_J(b)=sum_(p in J)v_p(b)log Np. Since J=[Z,A) is disjoint from
the previous CLOSED band[A,Y],

    0<=omega(b)<=ell_J(b)^2/(log Nb)^2
                  <=(1-theta(b))^2<=1-theta(b).       (9)

Consequently B^[1-theta-omega]=B^[1-theta]-B^[omega]
is an exact subtraction from the old remaining coefficient. There is no
product theta*omega to estimate and no reintroduction of the old band.
In particular a plain ideal entirely supported on the old band still has
zero remaining coefficient.

This avoids an invalid shortcut: bounding M S^[omega] Q alone would not
bound the tuple-cut core by a signed-subset inequality. Section7 pays the
whole weighted removed source explicitly.

## 5. Full product moment: two added slots and every diagonal

Let

    V_D,2(x)=W_P(x) (log D/log(Dx))^2.

Its required Euler, real and scale derivatives are uniformly bounded on
the original annulus because m has a fixed positive lower bound. The exact
convolution identity is

    S^[omega](D)=1/(log D)^2 sum_(p,q in J)
       (log Np)(log Nq) phi_u(pq)/sqrt(Np Nq)
                         S(D/(Np Nq);V_D,2).         (10)

No primality multiplicity, fixed hole or natural zero is changed. Both
p=q and p!=q occur, and each cofactor is unrestricted except for its
original plain support and character zeros.

First take p!=q and dyads P1<=Np<2P1, P2<=Nq<2P2, with the exact J
endpoints kept in the arithmetic supports. Their log_U lengths satisfy
eta-small<=lambda_i<=2eta, so the total new slot width is at most4eta.
Put E=D/(P1 P2) and separate the common profile V_D,2(y1 y2 z), where
y1=Np/P1, y2=Nq/P2 and z=Nc/E. The normalization is EXACT:

    P1^(-1/2) P2^(-1/2) E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2).

Use fixed coefficients log Np/log U and log Nq/log U, extracting the
common scalar(log U/log D)^2=1/m^2. They are bounded, row independent
and are not differentiated when D varies. The sharp band endpoints stay
frozen when scales or heights are differentiated.

Apply(4) to the shortened plain first. Once the disjoint-support/collision
steps below are paid, MI on M(R), Q and the two new slots gives

    ||M Q * this complete off-diagonal dyad||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta(P1 P2)^(-beta).     (11)

Indeed the first gate is at most
1-.01017+8eta<=1-.00217 before fine losses. The second is at most
2-.02034+4v+32eta<=3-.78834. Both have fixed slack on the WHOLE window.
No new hypothesis about MP or arbitrary merged column weights is used.

Here is the complete collision payment. The original pools are disjoint,
so each of the two distinct new primes can equal at most one old slot
prime; if both do, those old slots are distinct. Split into these finitely
many equality patterns before taking norms. For each new/old equality,
remove that old slot and extract its common prime. Its exact normalizers
are (P_i0 Np)^(-1/2); nonempty annuli force P_i0 comparable to the new
prime dyad. The absolute mass sum_p(P_i0 Np)^(-1/2)<<1 by ideal counting.
The shortened plain factor still contributes the full(P1 P2)^(-beta/2).
The phase phi_u(p)^2 is a contraction with its natural zero, and its
original coefficient and height are retained. Removing slots only eases
MI. With two equalities the two absolute masses are each paid once.
Any remaining prime is required to differ from the extracted fixed primes
by deleting those primes from its row-independent support for that outer
term. This is within MI's arbitrary prime-support contract.

For the remaining distinct active prime variables use a single finite
coloring on the UNION of their full prime-IDEAL pools. If there are h
active indices, assign each prime independently one of h colors. Then

    1_(p_1,...,p_h all distinct)
       =h^h E_color product_i 1_(color(p_i)=i).        (12)

For distinct primes the event has probability h^(-h); if two indices
coincide it is impossible. Under each coloring the active supports are
disjoint and all coefficients remain bounded and row independent. Hilbert
Minkowski under the NORMALIZED measure costs h^h, a fixed constant, not
the number of colorings. If no active prime variables remain, the empty
product is1 and the unmarked MI is applied without coloring; h=1 is trivial.
The original slot count K0 and h<=K0+2 are fixed
before U. Different ideals of the same norm have different color labels.
This covers two new primes lying in the same old pool, in overlapping
new dyads, or in different old pools. No equality pattern is omitted.
The inverse may contain any of these primes: that interaction remains
inside literal MI and is never declared coprime.

For p=q retain the COMPLETE old Q inside its original MI norm. Apply the
plain upper bound and take absolute values only over p. In a dyad P,

    sum_p (log Np/log D)^2 (Np)^(-1-beta)
       << U^epsilon P^(-beta).                       (13)

Thus the squared diagonal norm is at most
H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta Z^(-2beta). A coincidence of this p with an old
slot or the inverse needs no extra omission: the extracted phi_u(p)^2
is only removed as a row contraction, while the full Q and inverse stay
in the norm. This also pays the possible triple equality p=q=p_i.

Summing all dyads and finite patterns by Hilbert triangle gives

    ||M S^[omega] Q||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta Z^(-2beta).        (14)

This estimate is independent of the old joint cut. The only elementary
count used here is O(x) ideals of norm<=x, obtained from the original
primary Eisenstein lattice; no prime density theorem is used.

## 6. Full Fourier-height implementation

Use the accepted reviewer implementation, now with three new norm
coordinates. Write the original witness twist as
W_P(x)=W_0(x)x^(sigma+i gamma). Factor

    (y1 y2 z)^(sigma+i gamma)
       =y1^(sigma+i gamma)y2^(sigma+i gamma)z^(sigma+i gamma)

BEFORE applying B3.3 to the remaining smooth kernel
W_0(y1 y2 z)(log D/log(D y1 y2 z))^2. Larger individual cutoffs are fixed
on its full ambient compact support. The Fourier measure is chosen before
a live row, prime, equality pattern or coloring. Its high derivatives do
not acquire |gamma|^N. The independent frequencies tau_1,tau_2,tau_3
remain in their respective tests; the plain factor has height gamma+tau_3.
Original slot heights remain independent, and no shifted factor is asked
to supply a new zero witness.

On a fixed reserved fraction of the retained height padding, apply(4)
at gamma+tau_3. On its ENTIRE complement use absolute ideal counting
|S(E)|<=C E^(1/2). At the inherited internal floor T_ht>=U^kappa,
the polynomial bound E<=C D implies, for a fixed J1>C0/kappa,

    E^(1/2)<=C E^(beta/2)(1+|tau_3|)^J1.

The unconditioned MI has polynomial cost in tau_1,tau_2 and the original
heights. B3.3 integrates the resulting finite polynomial weight against
the same height-free kernel. All Fourier frequencies are paid, not simply
discarded because T_ht is called large. Nonempty subunit E satisfies the
same inequality up to a constant; empty E remains zero.

Fix the enlarged MI/Sobolev degree and real/bin losses first, then the
internal small height exponent so its cost fits those losses. The larger
decay order above belongs to the height-free kernel and does not enlarge
that already fixed MI degree. Below the internal floor use its dictionary;
above the original small polynomial range use a larger final external
height degree to pay the absolute source. Fix the physical height exponent
after that degree. The original detector tails retain their B-before-N
ordering and are not reopened here.

Tensor Sobolev covers log scales and independently varying real/height
parameters through these same profiles. Only the positive upper majorant
is differentiated; the dominance signal is not asserted for derivatives.
The arithmetic J, old band, tuple cutoff and equality conditions stay fixed.

## 7. Exact weighted extracted blocks, including all shared powers

Fix an extracted ideal L from the G198 expansion, let E=D/NL and define

    S_(omega,L)(E)=E^(-1/2)sum_c phi_u(c)W_P(Nc/E)omega(Lc).

For an ordered pair p,q in J put d=pq and h=d/(d,L). Primewise valuation
arithmetic gives d|Lc if and only if h|c. Consequently the EXACT formula is

    S_(omega,L)(E)=1/(log D)^2 sum_(p,q in J)
       (log Np)(log Nq) phi_u(h)(Nh)^(-1/2)
                                  S(E/Nh;V_D,2).    (15)

There is no division by a character value. If p=q, h is respectively
p^2,p or1 according as v_p(L) is0,1 or at least2. If p!=q, h contains
exactly the primes not already dividing L. The case L containing only one
power of p is therefore retained, rather than incorrectly treating p^2
as already extracted. The denominator is exact because
log(NL Nc)=log(D(Nc/E)). All remaining c valuations are still present.

Set s=(1+beta)/2 and

    I_L=sum_(p in J,p|L)log Np/log D,
    V_L=sum_(p in J,p not|L)(log Np/log D)(Np)^(-s).

The support of L in a nonempty original block has NL<=C D, so
I_L<=1+O(1/log D). Ideal counting and beta<1 give
V_L<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2). For p!=q the absolute coefficient mass
after(4) is at most (I_L+V_L)^2. For the diagonal, p|L terms are bounded
by I_L^2 even when h=p; p not|L terms cost at most
U^epsilon sum_(p in J)(Np)^(-1-beta)<<U^epsilon Z^(-beta).
Thus uniformly in every extracted L,

### 3.2 Fixed b>1 pays every growing-depth coefficient constant

Let `||a||_b=sum_n |a(n)|n^-b`. Dirichlet convolution is a Banach algebra
in this norm by absolutely convergent rearrangement. Fix ANY b>1. Choose
one fixed integer Y>=2 large enough that

    eta := zeta(b) Y^(1-b)/(b-1) < 1.                          (6)

This choice is independent of X, the depth, and chi. Define

    m_Y(n)=mu(n)chi(n)1_(n<=Y),
    d_Y=delta-l_chi*m_Y,
    Q_k=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))), k>=1.                (7)

Because l_chi*(mu chi)=delta and the tail of mu chi starts above Y,

    d_Y=l_chi*((mu chi)1_(n>Y)),
    ||d_Y||_b <= zeta(b) sum_(n>Y)n^-b <= eta,
    ||Q_k||_b <= zeta(b)/(1-eta),                             (8)

uniformly in k. Every character zero, every multiplicity and every signed
Dirichlet convolution in (7) is literal. The estimate uses b>1 only;
it does not assert contraction at the prospective zero-free boundary.

Exact telescoping in the arithmetic-function ring gives

    delta-l_chi*Q_k=d_Y^(*k),
    mu chi-Q_k=(mu chi)*d_Y^(*k),
    d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y,
    (mu chi-Q_k)(n)=0 for n<(Y+1)^k.                          (9)

All coefficient operations at a fixed integer are finite. In particular

    ||mu chi-Q_k||_b <= zeta(b)(1+1/(1-eta)) =: B_b.          (10)

The stronger bound zeta(b)eta^k is also valid but is not needed. Keeping
the deliberately coarse constant (10) makes the tail argument independent
of how far a Newton depth overshoots its requested threshold.

## 7. Literal threshold bands and their signs

Let A_z(n)=1_(omega_z(n)<=1). If z_2>z_1 then A_z2>=A_z1, so

    T_z2-T_z1=sum_n f(n)[A_z2(n)-A_z1(n)]g_tau(log(n/x)) (F34)

is EXACTLY the field of the newly admitted coefficient set. No coefficient mask changes during x integration. At a prime threshold p,

    A_p(n)-A_(p^-)(n)=1_(p divides n, omega_p(n)=1),    (F35)

which retains every positive power of p. There is only one integer n here, so the two-original-factor shared-prime subtraction of RN is not this jump law. F35 gives no sign for an individual prime jump.

For fixed lambda>1 with t,lambda t in F3, and t tending to infinity, F5 and F11 give, for every fixed N,

    T_(z^lambda)(x)-T_z(x)
      =h_z exp(tau/2) x/ell^2
          *[lambda^(-1)-1+O_(tau,lambda,N)(t/L+t^(-N))]. (F36)

For lambda=2, explicitly require 4<=t<=L/(2000 log L), so BOTH t and2t lie in F3, and t tends to infinity. Then

    T_(z^2)=(1/2+o(1))T_z,
    T_(z^2)-T_z=(-1/2+o(1))T_z,                       (F37)

uniformly on the full shell. T_z is eventually positive, and the complete added band is eventually negative there. This is an actual signed arithmetic estimate for the full coefficient band, despite its selector being nonnegative. It is not a pointwise-in-prime-jump assertion. If lambda tends to1, the subtractive error still applies at any proved uniform parameter range but need not give a relative asymptotic for that small band; no such uniform moving-lambda assertion is claimed here.

There is no exact finite terminal threshold for the UNCAPPED Gaussian source: n is unbounded. For any increasing z_j tending to infinity, dominated convergence and the disjoint coefficient partition give the exact locally uniformly convergent identity

    F_6-T_z0=sum_(j>=1)(T_zj-T_z(j-1)).                (F38)

Indeed the sum of the absolute band fields is at most sum_n g_tau(log(n/x))<=C_tau x. F38 is an exact decomposition, not an asymptotic extrapolation of F36 outside F3. The remaining late flow cannot be evaluated by extending the factor lambda^(-1) to fixed-power thresholds or infinity.

# [private research revision]: moving negative norms, full transport and cutoff failures

Accepted after full author, independent and controller review. The frozen
[author](wild44/report.md), [critic](wild44-review/report.md), seeds, immutable
draws and all30 dispositions are retained. This cycle adds useful conditional
interfaces and actual-source counterexamples; it does not improve c6=.125139.

## [restricted research revision]-W1: a moving negative norm with its complete return

For the fixed complete Gaussian field F(x), with coefficients a(n) satisfying
sum |a(n)|n^-B<infinity, take fixed tau,kappa>0 and define sigma=tau+kappa,
nu=tau*kappa/sigma, alpha=kappa/sigma. The localized field
W_X(v)=g_kappa(v)F(Xe^v) has exact expansion

    W_X(v)=sum_n a(n)g_sigma(log(n/X))g_nu(v-alpha log(n/X)).

Consequently its Fourier transform has Gaussian envelope
C X^B exp(-nu t^2/2). For the full inhomogeneous negative norm N_r=||W_X||H^-r,
the exact signed double sum uses

    J_r,X(n,m)=b_n b_m E_r,nu(alpha log(n/m)),
    b_n=g_sigma(log(n/X)),

where E is the positive Gaussian-mixture kernel from the report. Positivity
of that kernel does not permit removal of the signed coefficient products.
All n,m, prime powers and natural character zeros remain. Its diagonal is
O(X) for bounded coefficients and O(X^(1+epsilon)) for divisor bounds.

For every T>0,

    ||W_X||2 <= (1+T^2)^(r/2) N_r + C X^B exp(-nu T^2/2).

The high-frequency tail is NOT multiplied by the negative-norm inverse
weight. If d=limsup r_X loglog X/log X is finite and every sufficiently
large dyadic shell has N_rX<=X^(eta+epsilon), choosing T^2=M log X with
fixed sufficiently large M gives the complete shell exponent eta+d/2.
The d=0 version is an exponent equivalence with the complete field; for
d>0 only this sufficient return and the unshifted converse are claimed.

For actual mu*chi and f3*chi the existing Mellin pole bridge then gives
ordinary-character zero exclusion when eta+d/2<.874861. The f3 numerator
has no zero in .5<Re(s)<1; its prime-2 boundary zeros at Re(s)=1 require
the separately retained classical right-boundary theorem. This does not
automatically transfer to ideal coefficients or growing conductors.

Examples of sufficient, still OPEN inputs:

| eta | allowed d for a first gain | sample conditional conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| .75 | d<.249722 | d=.24 gives exponent .87 and c=.13 |
| 5/6 | d<.083055333333... | d=.08 gives exponent131/150 and c=19/150 |
| .87449 | d<.000742 | d=.0007 gives exponent .87484 and c=.12516 |

These are paid target conversions, not arithmetic-gap credit. The underlying
full signed kernel still needs a new all-scale estimate.

## [restricted research revision]-W2: exact feature transport and the existing baseline

For the actual untwisted f3 signs, use the Gaussian Hilbert features phi_n
from W1 with their full radial weights. The distance squared is
J(n,n)+J(m,m)-2J(n,m), not a translation-invariant substitute. Cut at
N=floor(X exp(C sqrt(log X))) and put a ghost at X exp(D sqrt(log X)), D>C.
Taking C^2,D^2>2sigma(1+A) pays all tails and the ghost by X^-A+o(1).
The ghost carries exactly the signed mass imbalance. For any nonnegative
transport plan of mass M<=N between the augmented charges and cost C_r,

    N_r <= sqrt(M C_r) + full tail and ghost errors.

Thus C_r<=X^(q+epsilon) gives exponent (1+q+d)/2, and first improvement
requires q+d<.749722. Complex characters require separate complete real
and imaginary plans, keeping their zeros; there is no automatic ideal lift.

The known buffered summatory exponent beta>.874861 already gives monotone
rank matching with cost O(X^(2beta-1)). The proof pays the small-n range,
all tails, end ranks and unmatched mass; the exact feature derivative is

    ||partial_w phi||^2=b(w)^2 g_(2nu)(0)[w^2/sigma^2+alpha^2/(2nu)].

This recovers the incumbent. It is an upper bound, not an optimal-cost
theorem. Prior MM-D2 matching is credited; the new contribution is the
complete source metric and its moving-order adapter. A better cost remains
open, and artificial loss from d may overwhelm a claimed improvement.

## [restricted research revision]-W3: a literal rough cutoff loses nonvanishing

The precise rough source, including its unit, is

    H_N(s)=sum_(n<=N,Pminus(n)>sqrt N) mu(n)n^-s
          =1-sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^-s.

Strict endpoints remove all composites. For large N these retained signs
also equal the actual f3 signs. Ordinary PNT and uniform partial summation
on compact lambda ranges give

    sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^(-1+lambda/log N)
      -> integral_(1/2)^1 exp(lambda v)dv/v.

The latter is strictly increasing from log2, hence equals1 at a unique
lambda*>0. The cutoff has a real zero
sigma_N=1-lambda*/log N+o(1/log N). This refutes inheritance of nonvanishing
for this particular cutoff source; it is not a zeta counterexample, a
lower bound for the whole field, or an impossibility theorem for every
compensated stability/tropical construction.

## [restricted research revision]-W4: independent inverse and code-fibre audits

For S={p<=Y}, inclusion-exclusion gives the FULL omitted-prime error
e=delta1-1*m_S=-1_(n>1,Pminus(n)>Y), or -chi(n) times that indicator.
Its absolute Dirichlet convolution norm diverges for sigma<=1. Even a
growing Y<=N/2 leaves a prefix lower bound >>N^(1-sigma)/log N for fixed
sigma<1. Finite geometric inversion has

    mu=v_K+mu*e^(*K),   V_K=(1-E^K)/L,   E=1-L M_S.

At a hypothetical L-zero, E=1: the finite approximation cancels its own
reciprocal pole and the remainder retains it. Other quantitatively proved
norms are still eligible. The Newton/geometric ancestry is already W43;
the added result identifies this seed's actual rough residual and norm.

The independent coding audit uses actual prime-presence bits for2,5,7
and syndrome 2|n. Residues modulo70 have conditional partial-parity mean
(-1)^s3/7, whereas fictitious uniform-bit fibres would give zero. The best
decoder has residual mean square40/49. Fixed-period Gaussian Poisson
summation transfers these values with superpower-small errors. For the
full f3*chi source, exact conditional decomposition retains BOTH the
predictable term and the complete conditional covariance; no code
orthogonality deletes the latter. All mixed square terms and tails remain.

## Sampling, novelty and preserved limits

Author six tests:08/07/24/18/17/11. Pools were formed from all30 candidates
using their literal numerical typicalities: every unreserved card under
the relevant threshold was eligible, regardless of group. Saved pools and
indices are retained. The author used OS draws without a replayable entropy seed.
The critic's protected30/uniform12 order was frozen before its outcome
intake, but after an author report prefix already existed. Do not call
this globally before-outcomes sampling. The24 author-untested cards stay
author-untested; only12/30 received additional independent tests.

Prime counterterm regularization is the existing W36/A12/W21 result.
Generic decoder loss is scoped to arbitrary uniform-cube inputs, not a
full f3 lower bound. G54/W38/W41 already retain parity covariance. All
original29-family/109-child entries and their reopening conditions survive.
