# [private research revision]: a complete stationary-cofactor estimate and constant inverse cuts

Status: completed analytic candidate; independent review pending. No new c. Current written c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364. Root owns canonical research, tracker and Git. No formalization, new packet, children or model-provider contact.

## 0. Current worklog and disposition

The frozen problem and assignment matched their supplied hashes. Relevant [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] arguments, current index and recorded Poisson/Type-II failures were checked before selecting this mechanism. The initial direct stationary expansion of the sharply cut retained rows had unpriced endpoint transitions. The successful repair completes the entire small-double source BEFORE subtraction, applies Poisson on common smooth output blocks and groups every rational alias exactly. This proves a new complete source estimate, rather than a sampled calculation or a bound for a selected signed subset.

Surviving claims: Theorem H below pays a whole bounded-periodic cofactor source with arbitrary frozen short coefficients. Its application pays the entire stationary small-double source, so BOTH inverse cutoffs can stay constant across the full finite core. Every old short-root source, high tail, large-gcd source and full return is retained. For the balanced choice, the new restriction also pays the diagonal in a subsequent bilinear Cauchy test for gamma>=6/7. The actual signed off-diagonal power bound is OPEN. The deliberately coarse full first-gain test still gives exponent1. Final readback, hashes and ownership release are recorded separately; no helper proves an asymptotic theorem.

Credit: [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] supply the compensated periodic source and original completion; [restricted research revision] supplies the Liouville square source, every square-short collision bound and its all-height return; [restricted research revision] supplies the complete large-gcd theorem. W24's local count and the older alias/kernel arguments keep their existing credit. The new ingredient here is the complete linear-cofactor stationary estimate H and its constant-cut application. Earlier smooth-master Poisson results in W29-W36 remove nonstationary frequencies; they do not already pay this source's entire stationary alias bank. [restricted research revision] equation(91.3) explicitly stops at UV<=eta X^(2gamma-r) and says that UV=X^gamma needs a new argument; H supplies that missing whole-alias estimate for this source. [restricted research revision]'s warning that fixed phase is slow near n~X remains valid. No broad literature novelty is asserted.

## 1. Exact source and original obstruction

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, including its natural zeros, and a prime p not dividing q. Write a=lambda chi, h=chi, s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 and s=0 off squares. Set q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p, q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2 and b0=v*h. Then a*h=s and

 c=a*a*b0=v*a*s,
 b0(l)=chi(l)[1-p1_(p|l)-p1_(p^2|l)+p^2 1_(p^3|l)].                 (1)

The p^2 coefficient is -p chi(p)^2, not -p^2 chi(p)^2. The actual b0 has period Q=p^3q, zero mean, and |b0|<=(p+1)^2. Both compensations, every valuation and the natural character zeros remain literal. Put

 f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6),
 ||F||_j=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j), j=1,2,
 C(x)=sum_(n>=1)c(n)f_x(n).                                      (2)

All parameters except X are fixed before the real shell x in[X,2X]. Original adaptive cuts make each cofactor row end at a d,e-dependent sharp endpoint. A naive stationary formula with that endpoint erased is false: a critical point crossing it has a transition contribution of the same order as a main stationary term. We neither assert that its variation is bounded nor discard it. The repair below changes the proof object to the complete small-double sum. No sharp-row stationary theorem is assumed.

## 2. Theorem H: whole short-coefficient / periodic-cofactor source

Fix a bounded Q-periodic sequence b of mean zero, a fixed0<=alpha0<1, X>=2 and real1<=D<=X^alpha0. Let A_m be arbitrary complex coefficients fixed before x. If |A_m|<=A, define the absolutely convergent complete source

 H_D(x)=sum_(1<=m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)b(l)f_x(ml).

Then, with a fixed power of the logarithm (power4 is more than sufficient),

 ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2
   <<_(Q,alpha0,||b||inf) A [D+X^(3/4)] log^4(2X).                (H)

For any divisor-bounded family |A_m|<<_eta m^eta for every eta>0, this gives

 ||H_D||_(1,2) <<_epsilon X^epsilon[D+X^(3/4)].                   (H')

Constants include the family constants and fixed data. Choose eta after epsilon. There is no growing-period, live-x coefficient or arbitrary cofactor/output-mask license. All integer endpoints in m<=D are exact. A may depend on X; it is explicitly charged.

### 2.1 An exact smooth partition, not a replacement cutoff

Choose a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi on[0,infinity), phi=1 on[0,1], phi=0 on[2,infinity). For every positive n,

 1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0) w(n/(2^j X)), w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t).        (3)

Here w is smooth, supported in[1,4], and nonnegative. Every overlap/transition is retained with its exact weight. The identity telescopes; for each n only boundedly many high terms are nonzero. Damping permits interchanging the complete sums. No original sharp cutoff is approximated by (3).

For the low part, expand b(l)=sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j exp(2pi i jl/Q). Its zero coefficient vanishes. On ml<=2X (and the extra last integer increment, lying below3X) the nonlinear phase increment in l is O(m/X), uniformly for x in[X,2X]. Since m<=X^alpha0, this is <1/(4Q) for all sufficiently large X. Each nonzero Fourier mode has monotone derivative separated from every integer by at least1/(2Q). Discrete first-derivative summation gives O_Q(1) for every prefix; Abel summation with phi(ml/X)exp(-ml/x^(3/2)), of bounded total variation, preserves that bound. Summing |A_m| gives O(AD). The finitely bounded initial-X range enters the fixed constant.

### 2.2 Complete Poisson expansion and every nonstationary frequency

Fix a high output scale N=2^j X and a row block I_M=[M,2M) intersect[1,D], with dyadic M. Put T=(N/X)^6>=1 and define

 beta_h=Q^(-1)sum_(r mod Q)b(r)exp(-2pi i hr/Q), h in Z.

It is periodic, |beta_h|<=||b||inf and beta_h=0 for h divisible by Q. Poisson on the smooth compactly supported positive-variable function, extended by zero, gives exactly

 sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)
   =(1/m)sum_(h in Z) beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
 I_r(x)=integral_0^infinity w(n/N)exp(-n/x^(3/2))
              exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.                       (4)

This includes both signs and every integer alias, not just one period. The h=0 term is exactly zero. For r>0 there is one positive critical point,

 n_r(x)=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
 Phi_r(n_r)=kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
 kappa_Q=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5), Phi_r''(n_r)=-30n_r^4/x^6.            (5)

Choose fixed positive c_Q,C_Q so that r in R_N=[c_Q T/N,C_Q T/N] includes every critical point that can meet[1,4]N for every x in[X,2X], and leaves a fixed derivative gap outside it. One explicit choice is c_Q=3Q/(128pi), C_Q=6Q*4^5/pi. This frequency range is chosen BEFORE x and BEFORE individual live labels. In rescaled variable n=Nt, the positive near phases form a compact smooth family with one nondegenerate stationary point in a fixed positive compact interval. The derivative of order2 at that point is bounded away from zero. All derivatives of the damped amplitude of any fixed needed order are O(exp(-cN/X^(3/2))), after absorbing fixed polynomial factors.

The uniform first stationary term is therefore

 I_r(x)=Z_r(x)exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4)
            +O_Q((N/T)exp(-cN/X^(3/2))), r in R_N,              (6)
 Z_r(x)=sqrt(pi/15) x^3 n_r(x)^(-2)
                     w(n_r(x)/N)exp(-n_r(x)/x^(3/2)).

The deliberately weak O(T^-1) remainder is sufficient. To justify its uniformity, localize near the unique critical point with one fixed-width smooth partition; the Morse change y=sgn(t-t0)sqrt(|Phi(t)-Phi(t0)|/T) has uniformly bounded inverse derivatives on this compact family. The Gaussian/Fresnel leading integral gives (6); subtract its value at zero and integrate the residual, or use one further Taylor term, to get O(T^-1). Away from that neighborhood two integrations by parts suffice. When t0 is outside the support of w the main coefficient is zero; its approach to the smooth support edge is covered by the same uniform estimate. No sharp edge is present. This is the standard one-dimensional nondegenerate stationary-phase calculation, with all varying parameters restricted as stated.

For completeness, let H_m=mT/N. The number of positive near aliases is O(1+H_m). If any such integer h exists, H_m>=c>0, so their combined remainder after the prefactor1/m is

 O((N/(mT))(1+H_m)exp(-cN/X^(3/2)))=O(exp(-cN/X^(3/2))).         (7)

Outside R_N, negative and small positive aliases with |h|=O(H_m) have derivative of size T after n-scaling. Two integrations by parts give O((N/m)T^-2) per alias, with damping. There are O(H_m) such nonzero integers when present, hence total O(T^-1). For |h|>C H_m the derivative has size |h|N/m; two integrations by parts give O((m/N)h^-2). Its entire two-sided tail is O(T^-1) if H_m>=c, and O(m/N) if H_m<c. Since m<=X^alpha0 and N>=X, all these costs are O(1), with damping retained. Enlarging fixed constants covers intermediate finitely sized ranges. Thus the whole transformed row equals the stationary bank in (6) plus a uniform damped O(1) error. After summing the block, the error is O(AM exp(-cN/X^(3/2))). There is no unpaid frequency tail or endpoint.

### 2.3 Exact coincident aliases and their coefficient energy

For a near alias write h/m=u/v in lowest terms, u,v positive and coprime. Then m=vj,h=uj. Crucially the ENTIRE function Z_(h/m)(x), including its support and damping, depends only on u/v,N,x. The ONLY separate original-m factor is1/m in (4). Thus define the x-independent grouped coefficient

 C_(u/v)=sum_(j>=1: vj in I_M) A_(vj) beta_(uj)/(vj).             (8)

The complete stationary bank is exactly

 sum_(r=u/v in R_N, v<=2M) C_r Z_r(x)
                       exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4).   (9)

Truncation m<=D, skipped aliases beta_h=0, all coincidences and arbitrary coefficient phases stay in (8). There is no averaging or assumption that beta_(uj) is constant. Since j lies in a factor2 interval, |C_(u/v)|<<A||b||inf/v. Also u>=1 and r<=C_Q T/N force v>=N/(C_Q T). Counting possible positive numerators and then dropping coprimality only in an upper bound gives

 sum_r |C_r|^2
  << A^2||b||inf^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_Q T))<=v<=2M)
                     [vT/N+1]/v^2
  << A^2||b||inf^2 (T/N)log(2M).                              (10)

The lower denominator cutoff is essential. Without it the +1 term would falsely leave N^2/T in the final energy. The sum v^-2 from that cutoff is O(min(1,T/N)), which is <=O(T/N) in both regimes. If the denominator range is empty there is no main bank.

### 2.4 Full real-shell energy, moving amplitude and all cross terms

Write x=Xz,1<=z<=2. For j=0,1,

 |d^j/dz^j Z_r(Xz)| << (N/sqrt(T))exp(-cN/X^(3/2)), r in R_N.    (11)

Indeed n_r(Xz)~N where w or its derivative is nonzero, dn_r/dz=(6/5)n_r/z, and all damping derivatives are fixed polynomials in N/X^(3/2), absorbed by a weaker exponential. This proves the required variation bound after the exact separation (8); no m-dependent amplitude has been pulled through a sum.

For two distinct r,s in R_N, the derivative in z of their phase difference has magnitude comparable to N|r-s|, because

 X^(6/5)(T/N)^(1/5)=N.

Its second derivative is a bounded multiple of its first. One integration by parts, including BOTH actual shell endpoints z=1,2, yields

 |integral_X^(2X) Z_r(x)conjugate(Z_s(x))
       exp(i kappa_Q(r^(6/5)-s^(6/5))x^(6/5)) dx/x|
 << (N^2/T)exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) min(1,1/[N|r-s|]).                  (12)

On the exact diagonal use the same scale with the minimum1. The spacing of distinct reduced fractions with v<=2M is at least1/(4M^2). If J is their number, ordering them therefore gives a complete absolute kernel row sum

 <<1+(M^2/N)log(2+J), J<<_Q M+M^2 T/N.                         (13)

Use 2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 on the COMPLETE pair sum, with both orientations and the diagonal. Combining (10)-(13), and log(2+J)<<_Q log(2N) for N>=X>=2,M<=X, proves

 ||stationary bank||_2^2
   << A^2 exp(-cN/X^(3/2))[N+M^2]log^2(2N).                   (14)

Adding the full error (7) by the norm triangle gives the same bound for the entire (M,N) block, with constants enlarged. No signed-subset norm comparison is used.

### 2.5 Summing all blocks and proving H

Sum (14) in norm over dyadic M<=D and N=2^j X, retaining every block in (3). The M contributions sum geometrically to O(D) for each N; their damping sum contributes O(log(2X)). The sqrt(N) contributions sum with actual damping to O(X^(3/4)log(2X)), multiplied by at most O(log(2D)) row blocks. The far infinite N tail converges exponentially; no polynomial truncation is imposed. The low part costs O(AD). Fixed logarithmic powers are bounded by log^4(2X). Finite-measure Cauchy gives L1 from L2. This proves H and H'. All low/high, inter-row and inter-block interactions are paid by norm inequalities after each whole source estimate.

## 3. A complete constant-cut core

Fix3/4<=gamma<1 and choose tau before x in the CLOSED interval

 max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= (11gamma-3)/8.

Set

 L=X^gamma, M=X^r, r=(6-2gamma)/4,
 U=X^(gamma tau), V=X^(gamma(1-tau)), G=X^(1-gamma).              (15)

These inverse cuts are CONSTANT throughout the shell, independent of n. In particular UV=L. Define full coefficient sequences

 Q_U=a_(<=U)*(v*s), Q_V=a_(<=V)*(v*s),
 S=a_(<=U)*a_(<=V)*b0,
 R=a_(>U)*a_(>V)*b0.

The exact identity is

 c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R.                                                (16)

All ordered terms and strict complements are retained. The small-double source has coefficients

 A_m=sum_(de=m,d<=U,e<=V)a(d)a(e), m<=UV=L, |A_m|<=d_2(m).

They are frozen, so H' with D=L gives ||sum_n S(n)f_x(n)||_(1,2)<<X^(gamma+epsilon), since gamma>=3/4. This pays its ENTIRE infinite cofactor tail and every stationary alias. No original mask is attached after this mean-zero estimate.

For Q_U and Q_V use the accepted [restricted research revision] complete square-short theorem with infinite root endpoints and the two literal physical labels1,p with weights1,-p chi(p). At D=X^alpha its norm exponents are

 alpha, (3+8alpha)/11, 3/8+alpha/4,
             min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4).

Each is <=gamma under (15): alpha<=gamma, the second is the stated corridor, and the last two follow already from gamma>=3/4. Fixed p only changes constants. Natural root zeros beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)), both physical multipliers and all cross-row collisions remain paid by the source theorem. Its hypotheses include arbitrary frozen prefixes, so infinity is allowed.

Every tuple in R has de>UV=L. Hence R(n)=0 for n<=L; there is NO missing low-output prefix. Also |R(n)|<=(p+1)^2 d_3(n). The accepted complete coefficientwise high-tail theorem gives

 ||sum_(n>M)R(n)f_x(n)||_2^2
      << X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon)
      << X^(2gamma+epsilon).                                 (17)

The whole infinite tail, its diagonal and both cross orientations are included. Next apply [restricted research revision] G182, b=3/2,k=6, to the exact mask

 1_(L<del<=M)1_(d>U)1_(e>V),

with actual colors a(d),a(e),b0(l), and strict gcd(d,e)>G. It pays that full removed source by X^epsilon[X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)]<<X^(gamma+epsilon). No condition involving gcd(d,l) or gcd(e,l) is inserted.

Define the new finite core

 T_rect(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) f_x(n)
       sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l).             (18)

Combining (16), H', both complete short sources, (17) and G182 proves

 ||C-T_rect||_(1,2) <<_(chi,p,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon),  (19)

uniformly in allowed frozen tau. For fixed gamma the corridor is a compact subset of(0,1); its largest exponent (11gamma-3)/8 is <1. All thresholds/constants can consequently be chosen uniformly in tau. H' uses alpha0=gamma<1. The endpoints gamma=3/4 and corridor equality are INCLUDED with the usual every-epsilon losses. No equality-impossibility assertion is made.

The old [restricted research revision] core T_ad uses the same n window and gcd cutoff but U(n)=B(n)^tau,V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau), with B(n)<=L. Thus (18) is literally a further restriction of its tuple set. Its signed removed wedge is paid as

 ||T_ad-T_rect||_(1,2) <=||T_ad-C||_(1,2)+||C-T_rect||_(1,2)
                         <<X^(gamma+epsilon).                (20)

This is a comparison of two independently proved COMPLETE source transfers, not monotonicity under signed deletion. It does not reapply the periodic mean after a gcd mask.

## 4. Quantitative effect and remaining arithmetic

Every retained tuple now has

 de>L, l<n/L<=M/L=X^((3/2)(1-gamma)).                           (21)

At the old high endpoint B(M)=eta X^((5gamma-3)/2), so its old cofactor cap was eta^(-1)X^(3(1-gamma)). The new exponent is half that value. In the balanced case tau=1/2 the inverse floor is X^(gamma/2) throughout, improving the old high-end exponent (5gamma-3)/4 by3(1-gamma)/4. These are proved source restrictions, not new zero-free constants.

For gamma11 the new cofactor exponent is .1877189454; at the illustrative nearer gamma=.8748 it is .1878; at gamma=5/6 it is1/4; at gamma=3/4 it is3/8. The corresponding balanced inverse floors have exponents gamma/2. All targets are retained; none of their core estimates is proved here.

The exact merged coefficient in (18) is

 sum_(ml=n)a(m)b0(l)
   #{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G}.                    (22)

It follows from complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de), including shared primes and natural zeros. There is no squarefree deletion or Hecke transfer. Full norm cancellation is still needed in this coefficient.

### 4.1 The deliberately coarse complete first-gain test

Take the balanced cuts and gamma>6/7, covering gamma11 and .8748. To test a bounded-coefficient bilinear estimate, first remove the gcd cutoff from the WHOLE finite core using G182, paying X^(gamma+epsilon). Decompose its finite original d,e,l,n ranges dyadically; O(log^4 X) labels suffice. There is no continuum sampling. On a cell n~N>=X, d~D,e~E, DE l~N, relabel the two original colors if needed so D>=E. Both are at least a fixed multiple of X^(gamma/2). Keep the sharp product cutoff N<del<=2N (intersected with the actual M endpoint) and both lower inverse cuts.

For fixed l and x, Cauchy in d leaves the exact signed e-correlation with an inner d sum. For e'=e+h, the difference-phase derivative in d has size

 T h/(DE), T=(N/X)^6,

and is monotone. Its maximum is O(T/D). Since N<=M and gamma>6/7,

 T<=X^(3(1-gamma))=o(X^(gamma/2))<=o(D).

The discrete first-derivative bound therefore gives

 |K_(e,e+h)| <<min(D,DE/(T h)).                               (23)

The d interval is the intersection of the two original product intervals and the fixed dyadic/lower-cut interval, hence one interval or empty. Its endpoints are kept. Summing all h and both orders, and retaining the diagonal, yields

 |sum_(d,e in cell) a(d)a(e)f_x(del)|
  <<DE [E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))],                       (24)

up to harmless bounded-variation partial summation for the actual damping. On these cells n<=M<X^(3/2), the damping and its first needed variations are uniformly bounded. More explicitly it may be kept inside K and the original Cauchy amplitudes; the same Abel bound holds. No estimate for signed Liouville correlations was used in obtaining (24).

Summing |b0(l)| with DE~N/l and all dyadic labels gives the full n~N contribution bounded by

 X^epsilon [N X^(-gamma/4)+X^3/N^2].                          (25)

The first exponent over N<=M is r-gamma/4=3/2-3gamma/4, <=gamma exactly when gamma>=6/7. The second is <=X^gamma only when N>=X^((3-gamma)/2)=M. Thus the coarse test pays the diagonal throughout but fails on the interior transition, returning O(X^(1+epsilon)) when all N>=X are summed. Outputs L<n<X also cost at most X^(1+epsilon) by the actual coefficient bound. The paid gcd complement adds X^(gamma+epsilon). This is a complete failed first-gain calculation, not a claim that an unproved bilinear bound succeeds.

### 4.2 Actual arithmetic repair attempted; precise surviving inequality

Before taking absolute values in (23), Cauchy gives D times a Gram expression with diagonal <=DE and off-diagonal

 B_(l,x)=2 Re sum_(e<e' in cell) a(e)conjugate(a(e'))
          sum_(d in I_e intersect I_e') exp(-i[(del/x)^6-(de'l/x)^6])
                times the actual two damping factors.                      (26)

The natural zeros are retained. Its actual coefficient is lambda(ee')chi(e)conjugate(chi(e')), not an independent sign. The outer eliminated a(d) was bounded only by Cauchy, with no coprimality hypothesis.

A SUFFICIENT stronger arithmetic repair, for EVERY finite-core cell L<n<=M (including the cells with N<X), fixed l and every real x, would be the one-sided bound

 B_(l,x) <= C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^gamma/N)^2.             (27)

The diagonal already fits: E is at least a fixed positive multiple of X^(gamma/2), while (N/X^gamma)^2<=X^(3(1-gamma)) up to a fixed cell factor. The inequality gamma/2>=3(1-gamma), equivalent to gamma>=6/7, pays those fixed factors in the estimate constant. A negative B is helpful; neither |B| nor separate pairwise absolute bounds are required. Then (24) improves to DE X^(gamma+epsilon)/N, and summing the full original labels/cofactors would prove the target X^(gamma+epsilon). Uniformity in those labels, every epsilon and all large shells is essential. This is a concrete sufficient correlation estimate, not asserted to be the weakest one.

For N>=X the actual coarse test of (26), retaining its signs until the final estimate, only proves B<<D E^2 T^(-1)log(2E). It misses (27) by the power

 X^(6-2gamma)/N^4=(M/N)^4,                                    (28)

up to logarithms. For L<=N<X, the coarse bound B<<DE^2 misses by (N/L)^2; this low transition is INCLUDED in the open requirement(27), not silently paid by its high-frequency version. At N~X the missing power in the SQUARE is X^(2(1-gamma)). Applying complete multiplicativity to the e pairs turns it into the explicit shifted product lambda(e(e+h)); it supplies no quantitative cancellation for (26). No theorem here estimates that full weighted shifted correlation. This is the first unpaid arithmetic step of this repair. The already known slow phase near X is not being claimed as an impossibility result for the actual signs. The new result is the removal of the stationary small-double and bilinear diagonal costs, leaving this stated actual correlation problem.

## 5. Weakest complete target and full conditional return

The weakest complete input developed here is the FULL norm of (18): choose ONE common3/4<=gamma<gamma11 before chi or a putative zero. For each fixed ordinary chi and each member p of a fixed covering pair of unramified primes, require, for EVERY epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

 integral_X^(2X)|T_rect,tau_X(x)| dx/x <<_(fixed data,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                                    (OPEN-RECT)

Tau_X may depend on the fixed data, epsilon and shell within (15), but must be frozen before x. There is no independent moving height, conductor, selected residue class, sampled x, finite range or single epsilon substitute. L2 at that exponent suffices. By (19), this hypothesis is equivalent to the corresponding full fixed-source C L1 bound, and to the old core norm hypothesis by (20). It is not claimed equivalent to zero exclusion. The nontrivial new content is the source estimate H and the proved smaller core, not the equivalence alone.

For the nearer choice gamma=2187/2500=.8748, the conditional c=.1252 exceeds c11 by135091/2500000000=.0000540364. The1/6 and1/4 targets correspond to gamma=5/6 and3/4. The latter two retain (19), although the uniform small-derivative calculation in Section4.1 was only claimed for gamma>6/7. No c increase has been proved.

For completeness retain the entire inherited Mellin return. The fixed source has

 D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
 P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).

The [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] clockwise-contour identity, initially where it is absolutely valid, is

 H_p(z)=integral_0^infinity C(1/t)t^(z-1)dt
       =A0(z)D_c(z)+E_p(z),
 A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6,
 E_p holomorphic on Re z>1/2.                                (29)

The full source norm supplies H_p holomorphy on Re z>gamma; epsilon is chosen below the distance of a compact set to that line. Actual damping pays x near zero. The remainder has the inherited locally uniform coefficient/derivative bound O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)); it is not discarded or replaced by a finite endpoint. A0 has no zero there, J_p has zeros only on Re z=1/2, and L(2z,chi^2) is finite and nonzero above1/2. P_p zeros are on Re z=1. Two distinct fixed unramified primes cannot share a nonzero-height zero of P_p, since chi(p) has finite order and log p1/log p2 is irrational. For nonprincipal chi choose one covering prime with chi(p)!=1 to cover height zero. For principal chi the pole at z=1 is retained as the allowed exception. Thus OPEN-RECT gives the same conditional fixed ordinary-character zero-exclusion return at every finite height. There is no growing-q uniform estimate or Hecke claim.

The prescribed b=3/2,k=6 needs only the one-term identity (29). No general varying-b/k claim or omitted positive Mellin shift is introduced. If a later general detector is used, EVERY fixed shifted term and its strip descent from [restricted research revision] remain required. Existing F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity, exact external root-definition/import/admission and record scope stay OPEN. Nothing here performs formalization or grants record admission.

## 6. Source evidence, checks and limits

The source manifest records hashes and exact read extents of the stable prefix, frozen problem/assignment, accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] integrations and relevant earlier proof files. The initial broad duplicate search output was truncated; no complete-read claim is made for that result. Its relevant passages were subsequently read in bounded slices. Earlier index/history is retained rather than replaced.

The only outside primary analytic reference used is Terence Tao, *Lecture Notes8 for247B*, Winter2007, Lemmas2.6-2.8, printed pp.6-8 (PDF pp.6-8). It supplies the standard smooth stationary-phase normalization and Morse proof. Here the compact parameter family, damping derivative bounds, entire alias count and its source sum are checked explicitly in Section2. The note's constants are not assumed uniform in arbitrary parameters. The public PDF text was read through the relevant lemmas and proof; no pixel inspection is claimed. Source: [Tao's primary lecture notes](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/247b.1.07w/notes8.pdf). No outside arithmetic cancellation theorem is imported.

The direct PDF download failed with a DNS resolution error; no local PDF binary or binary hash is claimed, and no download retry was made. The successful primary web read is the stated reference evidence.

The small exact helper checks convolution signs including a ramified character, constant-cut partition and strict gcd endpoints, rational alias coincidences with nonconstant periodic coefficients, and exact exponent implications at the incumbent and nearer/1/6/1/4 targets. It does not numerically simulate an asymptotic bound or certify the proof. A further theorem check is conceptual: setting the mean of b nonzero would restore h=0 and its low-frequency main source, so H is deliberately NOT stated for arbitrary bounded cofactors. A source with live-x coefficients, a cofactor-dependent cutoff, or a separately varying stationary amplitude cannot use (8)-(14) without a new proof.

Final disposition: a complete strengthened analytic source input and a strictly smaller constant-cut retained core are proposed for independent acceptance. The full signed power estimate remains open, c11 is unchanged, and the exact remaining arithmetic obligation is OPEN-RECT (with (27) one sufficient repair). Every original source sign, zero, repeated factor, covering prime, shell endpoint and complementary norm cost remains present.

## 5. Retaining the quadratic Jacobi variables

For coprime odd squarefree integer columns n,m, set q=nm,
chi=chi_n chi_m, and K_n(x)=chi_n(x(1-x)). The exact retained
auxiliary-variable transform is

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{r\bmod q}\sum_{x\bmod n,y\bmod m}
\chi_n(-r x(1-x))\chi_m(-r y(1-y))e_q(kr)\\
&\qquad=\mu(n)\mu(m)\tau_\chi\overline{\chi(k)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Indeed the r sum is the primitive Gauss transform, and
J_n(0)=chi_n(-1)mu(n) contracts the two constant-weight auxiliary
sums. No nonzero auxiliary Fourier frequency has been created.
For shared core g, n=ga,m=gb, the row character is instead
chi_ab(u) 1_((u,g)=1); expanding its mask gives every r|g branch
with row scale H/r and primitive conductor ab. The principal case
a=b=1 remains.

The [Blomer--Pascadi fixed-modulus theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24311v1#S1.SS1)
requires two interval arguments. Our exact Jacobi transform fixes
the first argument and puts squares in the second, so its balanced
saving is unavailable. At H=D^1.498 and q comparable to D^2 the
row-dual length would be q/H=q^0.251; this does not create two
independent interval arguments of length comparable to sqrt(q).

Decomposing every positive integer row u=v a^2, with v squarefree,
retains chi_n(u)=chi_n(v)1_((a,n)=1). Applying the
[quadratic large sieve](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3A[private operational identifier omitted])
to each v family therefore gives

\[
\frac1D\sum_{u\le H}
\left|\sum_{n\ {\rm odd}}\mu(n)\chi_n(u)W(n/D)\right|^2
\ll(HD)^\delta[H+D\sqrt H].
\]

This preserves the principal-square repetitions. At H=D^1.498 its
excess over H is D^0.251. The exact detector has not supplied a paid
transfer to two independent Kloosterman arguments or an improved CM2.

## 5. Uniform audit W58-08: genuine lift, principal branch obstruction, exact repair

The original seed leaves its two-variable source unspecified. Here is one explicit source satisfying its divisor/cofactor requirement. Fix an ordinary character chi with its natural zeros. For Re(s),Re(t)>1 define

    F_chi(s,t)=sum_(m,n>=1) c(m,n)m^(-s)n^(-t),
    c(m,n)=mu(mn)chi(mn) 2^(-omega(mn))
           (zero if mn is not squarefree).

The prime two is present unless ramified, and c(1,1)=1. Unique allocation of each squarefree prime to m or n gives

    F_chi(s,t)=product_p [1-chi(p)(p^(-s)+p^(-t))/2],
    F_chi(s,s)=1/L(s,chi).

More strongly, on every finite hard product cutoff mn<=X, summing the complete diagonal coefficient of k gives mu(k)chi(k), because a squarefree k has 2^omega(k) divisor allocations. This is an exact source identity, not a decoupled random model. The absolute convergence cone of this series is exactly Re(s)>1 and Re(t)>1: sufficiency follows from the prime sum; the single-prime terms on either coordinate axis force the two respective prime series. Removing finitely many ramified primes does not alter this obstruction at exponent one. Merely introducing a second variable has not enlarged the absolute domain.

There is a useful exact analytic factorization. Write x=chi(p)p^(-s),y=chi(p)p^(-t), and define on D={Re(s)>1/2,Re(t)>1/2}

    log G(s,t)=sum_p [log(1-(x+y)/2)
                     -(1/2)log(1-x)-(1/2)log(1-y)].

Each logarithm is defined by its power series, since |x|,|y|<1. The linear terms cancel. The quadratic term is (x-y)^2/8, and the remainder is bounded uniformly on each compact subset of D by a constant times |x|^2+|y|^2. The prime sum therefore converges normally. Hence G is holomorphic and nowhere zero on D, with G(s,s)=1. On the initial absolute domain,

    F_chi(s,t)^2 L(s,chi)L(t,chi)=G(s,t)^2.                 (A08.1)

For a **principal** character modulo any fixed q, fix a real t0>1. Its L(s,chi) has a simple pole at s=1. If this F had a holomorphic extension to a neighbourhood of (1,t0), equation(A08.1) would give

    F_chi(s,t0)^2=G(s,t0)^2/[L(s,chi)L(t0,chi)],

whose right side has a zero of order one at s=1. The square of a holomorphic function has even vanishing order. This is impossible. Thus this concrete normalized squarefree lift cannot be holomorphic on a whole product half-plane Re(s),Re(t)>gamma for any 1/2<gamma<1, **even if ordinary zero exclusion were available**. On the diagonal the two reciprocal factors coincide and the order becomes two; the original diagonal 1/L is perfectly consistent. A one-variable principal correction cannot be silently omitted in the two-variable construction.

This is an actual source-specific failure of this lift's uncorrected product-domain promise. It does not rule out a sloping tube avoiding (1,t0), a different lift, or a correctly pole-normalized mechanism with its own diagonal return.

A clean repair is to use B=F^2, retaining its actual two-variable convolution coefficients

    b(m,n)=sum_(d|m,e|n) c(d,e)c(m/d,n/e).

They are not the original c coefficients. The meromorphic continuation is explicit:

    B(s,t)=G(s,t)^2/[L(s,chi)L(t,chi)],
    B(s,s)=1/L(s,chi)^2.

For each fixed 1/2<gamma<1, holomorphy of B on the product half-plane is **equivalent** to zero exclusion of L on Re(s)>gamma. In the forward direction fix any safe real t0>1; nonvanishing G prevents cancellation of an L zero in s. In the reverse direction, 1/L is holomorphic on the zero-free half-plane, with a removable zero at the principal pole; multiplication by the holomorphic G gives B. This equivalence claims no growth bound, contour shift, or coefficient cancellation from holomorphy alone. It is a fully paid return, not a new estimate.

Independent exact checks cover 1,024 complete hard-product diagonal coefficients for principal, real and genuinely complex ordinary characters, including ramified zeros and n=1. The infinite factorization and principal branch contradiction are proved above, rather than inferred from those checks. Multiple-Dirichlet, diagonal-return and fractional-branch ideas have broad prior ancestry; no literature priority is asserted. Relative to this seed, the useful increment is an exact source, its unconditional branch obstruction, and a repaired target explicitly equivalent to the old arithmetic problem.

statement:
## 2. W40-20: the Poisson budget and complete conditional return

Let h be holomorphic beyond the closed unit disk, h(0)=1, and
u(theta)=Re h(e^(i theta)). With dm=dtheta/(2pi), define
B=integral(-u)_+ dm. Mean value gives integral u_+=1+B and integral
u_-=B. For |z|=rho, the Poisson kernel ranges between
k=(1-rho)/(1+rho) and k^-1. Therefore

    Re h(z) >= k(1+B)-B/k.                          (R40.1)

The right side is nonnegative exactly when B<=b(rho), where
b(r)=(1-r)^2/(4r). Since b is strictly decreasing on (0,1),

    B<=b(r) implies Re h(z)>0 for every |z|<r.      (R40.2)

The non-strict budget is sufficient for the OPEN disk. On the target
circle equality only assures nonnegativity. The signed representation
by (e^(i theta)+z)/(e^(i theta)-z) follows directly from Fourier
coefficients of Re h and h(0)=1; no positive measure or logarithm of h
has been assumed.

Sharpness is correctly qualified. The two-atom signed Herglotz function
(1+B)(1+z)/(1-z)-B(1-z)/(1+z) vanishes at-r_B, with
B=b(r_B), and has boundary poles. Replacing z by tz, t<1, and choosing
r_B=tr gives a function analytic past the circle with its zero at-r.
As t tends to1, the positive and negative Poisson kernels concentrate at
opposite points, so the negative mass tends to b(r). For any larger
proposed budget choose r'<r with b(r') still below that budget, then
approximate at r'. Its zero lies inside the target disk. This proves
sharpness of the uniform budget even in the smooth-boundary class;
it does not claim attainment there at a boundary pole.

For a fixed ordinary or fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Eisenstein
character, take P=L for a nonprincipal member and P=(s-1)L for a
principal member, including the removable value at1. The fixed lattice
argument and periodic character sums give the respective counting errors
O_f(sqrt x+1) and O_q(1). Abel summation makes P holomorphic on Re s>1/2,
with nonzero regularized principal value at1. The Euler product is
nonzero on Re s>1. This package was independently reconstructed in W39
and is now explicitly accepted in [private research revision]; no small-set hypothesis is
being imported here. Fixed ray modulus and all deleted Euler factors
remain. Moving conductors or nontrivial infinite type are outside scope.

With R=7/5, h_t(z)=P(2+it+Rz)/P(2+it) is analytic beyond the unit disk,
whose left edge is .6>.5. For .6<gamma<1 set r=(2-gamma)/R. A zero
beta+it with gamma<beta<=1 gives a zero of h_t inside |z|<r; the Euler
product covers beta>1. Hence the all-real-height B(h_t)<=b(r) hypothesis
does imply the stated fixed-member zero-free half-plane. Each family
member needs that hypothesis separately. This is a complete local-disk
return, not a mean-height or finite-height assertion.

The target budgets check exactly: c=.125136 gives r=70321/87500 and
B<=295118041/24612350000; c=1/6 gives1/120; c=1/4 gives9/2800.
The first numerical difference from c4 is only a CONDITIONAL .000001.
No such all-height budget has been proved.

A finite Euler product E_t(s) preserves zeros on this disk because each
1-chi(p)N(p)^(-s) is nonzero for Re s>0, with trivial factor1 at natural
zeros. It is legitimate to choose a different finite product at each t
for this local theorem. Its existence with the required budget is an
additional arithmetic condition. The theorem does not silently assert a
single fixed Mellin transform for those varying products.

The constructive finite-height certificate is also valid. A negative-part
map is1-Lipschitz; integrating distance from each left grid endpoint gives
angle error pi M_theta/N. A height net with nearest distance delta/2 adds
M_t delta/2. Quotient differentiation yields exactly the author's
R sup|Q'|/m and sup|Q'|/m+sup|Q|sup_anchor|Q'|/m^2 bounds. An interval
certificate pays value errors as well and covers only its stated heights.
The packet performed no such L-function numerical certificate.

## 8. The proposed Deligne saving has no derived trace family and misreads a local case

**Local error and unsupported global implication.** BM §6 assigns \(-q^{-1}\) to AB16 at \(\alpha=\beta=0\), which actually gives the constant kernel and only zero Fourier frequency. The \(-q^{-1}\) unit-frequency value requires equal positive valuations not divisible by six; equal positive multiples of six give \(1-2/q\). A universal local square-root saving is false. Nor does an incidence equation identify a nondegenerate hyper-Kloosterman family. Even a valid complete-sum bound must pay incomplete ranges, composite moduli, exceptional strata, marks and profiles. Derive the actual two-column additive/rational kernel and its conductor/degenerations before claiming \(N/K\). [BM R3.1, §§3,5–6; [restricted research revision] AB16; portfolio F17.T.]

The full-fit inverse gate, r>1/2, plain0<m<1/2 and1<t<3/2 hold throughout the whole4eta window. The critic's independent20-by25 rational interval partition covers the continuous delta/v/eta box, using eta itself as the interval[0,.001]. Conservative reserves include inverse full-fit>.0101796, r-1/2>.371939, m>.443360,1/2-m>.0323015 and t-1>.327148. These are interval inequalities, not floating-grid extrapolations. The full-fit gate r+2v<1, with r>1/2, also pays the original stricter slot compatibility2r+8v<3. Original tiny grade/mesh margins can be preallocated. A bounded/zero plain witness cannot occur in the short regime because m>=t-r>t-1>0. The other populations keep their original treatment.

For raw rows w=u_core*b^6 put s=log_Z Nb and V=W-6s. In V>=20W/21, z/W<=1/21 gives z/V<=.05, including z=0. The old E0 is the maximum of two affine forms with W-slopes rho and rho-a_K, where

    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)D],
    k=rho+delta-1.

Hence E0(V,z)<=E0(W,z)-6(rho-a_K)s. After paying root count Z^s and the free saving h*eta*V, the exponent is at most

    E0(W,z)-h*eta*W-[6(rho-a_K-h*eta)-1]s.

The bracket is>1.10376 in the critic enclosure. This prices all roots; replacing V by W without this calculation would be wrong. In V<20W/21, s>W/126 and the old unmarked tail provides a reserve at least

    [(rho-1/6-3k)/21-h*eta]W >.00109398 W.

The fixed-inducing raw populations also fit this reserve; they are not declared finite. The analogous J2 scalar root/tail reserves are positive, as independently checked; its affine-piece gates were also read in the author's complete400-box rational certificate. No author program was rerun.

This proves the source-relative CONDITIONAL raw bound

    Z^[E0(W,z)-(2/15)eta W+epsilon] H_J,   0<=z/W<=1/21,

assuming J_eta^all on every required actual live list. The argument retains all zero/clipped widths, root holes and old tails. It does not construct the missing moment estimate. G115's rank-one common-zero signal supplies neither that estimate nor its uniformity.

## 7. Amplifier errors, zeros, exceptions and recovery

An extracted error has nominal defect <=g+sigma+w-w_o+eta and allowance >=w. Remove slots at the GLOBAL old squared pointwise rate (3/4)/(9/2)=1/6, using the same exact-width correction and old unrestricted zero-slot input when exhausted. Since lambda>=sigma/4=3a/4:

| Original valuation | Exact lower reserve | New value |
|---|---|---|
| 1: w=w_o=lambda | a/4-g/6 | 93M/80000 |
| 6: w=6lambda,w_o=0 | 13a/4-g/6 | 1593M/80000 |
| 7: w=7lambda,w_o=lambda | 4a-g/6 | 123M/5000 |

Keep the zero-power hole, valuation-one/seven moving factors and normalized prime average. No second prime count, low-bin heredity, fresh density or improved descendant is used.

The first zero frequency uses the original powerful-product count. The added zero Gauss row is unamplified with its -s0 allowance. The main second zero has excess <=A-M+5a+O(eta), giving reserve 1439M/20000.

For fixed-inducing children retain the paired exceptional predicate, masks, forced congruence residues, raw scalars and whole-product norm power. At the ACTUAL main radius the exact B3.75 term is

\[
 F_1=\begin{cases}
 (c+5d+R+E)/6+B_c-4a-5\omega/6,&c\ge d,\\
 c+(R+E)/6+B_c-4a-5\omega/6,&c\le d.
 \end{cases}
\]

Thus F1>=2c/3-4a-O(eta), F2>=2b2/3. For v=c+min(c2,d2), L=M/4, the centered-lattice cancellation gives exactly

\[
 \max_{v\ge0}\{A-5M/6-2v/3-(L-v)_+\}=A-M
\]

at v=L. The MAIN exceptional reserve is 1-A0-4a0=391/5000; the unchanged error-radius estimate gives 1-A0-9a0=939/20000. The exact main term is -4a, not -5a. Leading terms cancel because the rectangles retain the same product, profiles, holes, whole character and norm power, including independent heights. No fixed a cost is hidden in epsilon.

All positive reserves, in units of M, are

\[
 7/100,\ 13/300000,\ 3149/1350000,\ 93/80000,
 \ 1593/80000,\ 123/5000,\ 1439/20000,\ 391/5000,\ 939/20000.
\]

Choose an aggregate error budget below a strict fraction of their minimum and epsilon. Choose physical mesh and support/frequency reserves before the target dictionary. Fixed conductor constants use small padding at the final threshold. Once the finite slot list is fixed, aggregate annular tolerance tends to zero with Z; it is not a permanent per-slot loss.

For a target dictionary obtain the final density height degree, then choose the DISTINCT tau_out so polynomial height factors fit the allocated budget. Separate common Fourier frequencies inside a still smaller buffer. FM supplies one integrable density majorant even for label-dependent scale parameters, with a diagonal multiplier of norm <=1; no label count repeats. Arbitrarily large input heights use a fixed sufficiently large polynomial height allowance to absorb the bounded-geometry raw Z-power. Choose derivative/height orders backwards through the finite graph, then Fourier orders, then one threshold before live parameters.

Both Cauchy steps average exponents instead of doubling losses. Minkowski sums already paid coefficient masses. Repeat for the four derivative pairs and use two-variable scale-supremum recovery. This proves L44 with the stated uniformity.

statement:
# [private research revision] common extracted divisor: independent review of H branches B and A



## Disposition and current checkpoint

ACCEPT the restricted auxiliary estimate BGC1, with its complete
ordered cross-cell scope, relative to the explicitly accepted native
quadratic/cubic sieve and original profile-return inputs. Independent
reconstruction finds no missing common-divisor multiplicity and no
row-dependent cubic coefficient in the order actually used. The
full-allocation identities BGC12--16 are correct.

Branch A, read only after its authorized recovery/freeze, independently
gives the same mechanism in HA11/HA16 and the same full-allocation
identity in HA19/HA20. Count this as ONE mathematical result. HA28
correctly states the different identity for fixed label subsets. Its
correction is necessary for the proposed pressure-cell continuation;
it does not invalidate either proof of the restricted estimate.

The paid part is an auxiliary pair form. After full allocation
completion it consists of composite common-core counterterms with
prime cofactors. For threshold U>1 it contains no original prime
pair. The literal complement contains the original prime scalar
with coefficient one, minus the paid counterterm. Thus there is no
proved improvement of the complete hard prime packet, all H, or c.
This is an actual restricted estimate and exact mechanism diagnosis,
not a physical-H subfamily theorem.

Completed: bindings; exact algebra; coefficient independence at both
sieves; common-divisor and mark/core multiplicities; full sharp-gap,
root/profile/height return; unit/complement audit; A/B reconciliation.
Remaining outside this review: a genuinely new bound on the small-gcd
allocation interaction or another argument for the complete prime
scalar. No further analytic assumption is supplied here.

## 1. Exact source and quantified accepted statement

JPS is [restricted mathematical source] HPR is its
canonical independent review. M is zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md.
This review uses their accepted inputs; it does not reprove either
imported large sieve or extend its family.

Retain JPS1--4 and the SECOND, perpendicular extension in JPS Section 4:

    N > C_orig (K+L+G^2), C_orig G < A_0,
    1 <= L <= sqrt(N), G >= 1,
    S(N,L) = N+L+(NL)^(2/3),
    Omega_i = sum_(P original) |u_i(P)|^2/q_P.             (R1)

All squarefree conditions are on good primary IDEALS. They are not
conditions of squarefree integer norm. All original finite/ray/unit
components, rationally primitive short sources, endpoint constants,
opposite-prime conditions and zero extensions remain as in JPS.

The native factors and linear collision expression are

    a(n)=alpha(n) eta(n) chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3,
    a(ve)=a(v)a(e)chi_v(e)^4,
    chi_R(ng)^3 chi_P(n)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1, n=ve.             (R2)

The source has the original masks (ve,g)=(ve,bar(g))=1. The two
mark arrays are arbitrary original arrays independent of live n,g,R.
Their roots are q_P^(-1/2). The physical squared scalar is still
N^(-1)G^(-2). The sharp far selector is

    |q_n-q_n'| > H0, H0=floor(Z^.05),                   (R3)

excluding both equal-rational-norm orientations. The original complex
short-core weight is h((g,g')); it is not recomputed as a new true
core of an auxiliary composite. The original global corrections and
prime-only selectors were evaluated BEFORE auxiliary extension, in
the exact order established by JPS/HPR.

Let V_1,V_2 be fixed subsets of the original extracted-v labels
(a cell, a union, or all labels, including the unit). They cannot
depend on the live row, mark, e or g. Let C[V_1,V_2;w;h] be the
literal ordered auxiliary JPS covariance with extra pair weight
w((v,v')). Define

    r_w(t)=sum_(s|t) mu(t/s)w(s).                       (R4)

The proved statement is

    |C[V_1,V_2;w;h]|
      <<_(epsilon,orig) Z^epsilon
         G(K+NG/U) S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig, (R5)

provided r_w(t)=0 for q_t<U and |r_w(t)|<=tau(t), with U>=1.
The same proof allows a FIXED divisor power in this last condition
after adjusting the internal epsilon allocations. In B, |w|<=1 and
w(s)=0 for q_s<U imply both required conditions. In particular
w_U(s)=1_(q_s>=U) is admissible, with its exact >= endpoint.

For every fixed epsilon>0 the bound is uniform on all retained
polynomial dyads in R1, in both original mark arrays, in all fixed
V_i, original profiles/heights with their stated seminorm dependence,
and real thresholds U. An empty quotient or high-gcd support remains
empty; bounded nonempty quotient ranges use original comparison
constants. If U is larger than every possible extracted gcd, the
selected form is zero. The explicit JPS12 completion gates govern
the later degree-one return; they are not replaced by one numerical
pressure-point calculation.

P_orig means exactly the paired original root envelopes, finite
component masses and required profile seminorms in JPS Section 8.
It is not a new norm-one profile hypothesis or a lower bound.
Neither R5 nor its proof estimates dyads outside the original domain.

I use t for B's common extracted inversion ideal d, to distinguish
it from divisor-cell names D,D'. This t is not the original rational-
content decomposition index.

## 2. Exact common-divisor extraction

Mobius inversion gives, before any inequality,

    w((v,v')) = sum_(t|v,t|v') r_w(t).                 (R6)

The signs of r_w are essential. For the high selector and U>1 a
prime t above U has r_w(t)=1; a product of two prime factors each
above U has r_w(t)=-1. No positivity of this pair mask is used.

At fixed t write v=t z, n=v e=t m, m=z e. On the surviving
squarefree support, (t,m)=1 and mu(tz)=mu(t)mu(z). Put

    b_(i,t)(m)
       = sum_(z|m, tz in V_i)
             mu(z) log(q_m/q_z)/log(q_t q_m),
    b_(i,t)(1)=0.                                    (R7)

Each displayed logarithmic ratio lies in [0,1] on its actual
support, so |b_(i,t)(m)|<=tau(m). The only formal zero denominator,
t=m=1, is outside the original long window and is assigned zero.
The e=1 contribution has numerator zero and is never restored.

Using the original cocycle, each allocation has the SAME recombined
factor a(tm). Consequently its complete fixed-t linear side equals

    mu(t)a(t)chi_R(t)^3
      sum_P u_i(P)chi_P(t)^4/sqrt(q_P) 1_(P,R)=1
      sum_(m,g) a(m)b_(i,t)(m)xi(g)chi_t(m)^4
          chi_R(mg)^3 chi_P(m)^4 1_(P,g)=1
          C_i(tm) A_i(g),                            (R8)

with every original source-only mask, sharp window, height and row
factor retained. Formula R8 is BGC5--6/HA7--8 independently derived.
The characters at t retain their natural row, mark and long-source
zeros. Nothing has been transferred into g, and the physical index
is tm g^3, not m(tg)^3.

The scalar mu(t)a(t) is kept in the exact paired expression. If
the two native components differ their paired scalar need not be
one; its modulus can be bounded in the ensuing positive estimate.
The proof requires no false cross-component phase cancellation.


## 3. Positive norm reconstruction: where every label is paid

### 3.1 Complete core and mark projectors

Expand the entire original short-core function:

    h((g,g'))=sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f), |r_h(f)|<=tau(f),
    g=f b, g'=f b'.                                  (R9)

Fix t,f. Product perpendicularity implies that m,b are coprime
squarefree ideals, with all original restrictions on tm and fb.
In particular j=m b is a genuine squarefree quadratic column.
For a dyad T<=q_t<2T its containing norm range is

    q_j << N G/(T q_f).                              (R10)

Resolve the WHOLE original 1_(P,R)=1 projector by Delta|(P,R),
including its Mobius sign, and write P=Delta Q,R=Delta k. Retain
(Delta,Q)=(Delta,k)=1. The root becomes
q_Delta^(-1/2)q_Q^(-1/2). Rowwise divisor Cauchy over Delta costs
only a divisor power in the original polynomial range.

There is NO residual (Q,k)=1 projector in an individual inversion
term. Reinstating it would change the exact expansion and obstruct
the argument's asserted coefficient independence.

The fixed row multiplier is chi_k(tf)^3, including its zero.
Its modulus is at most one and its row restriction can be enlarged
only after entering the positive fixed-t,f,Delta norm. The combined
Delta factor is, explicitly,

    chi_Delta(tf)^3 chi_Delta(mb)^3 chi_Delta(tm)^4
       = chi_Delta(tm) chi_Delta(fb)^3.               (R11)

The equality uses exponents 3+4=7=1 modulo six and holds with the
original zero extension. This factor and 1_(Delta,fb)=1 are source-
only factors, independent of k,Q. Forbidden Delta intersections
remain zero until a legitimate positive enlargement.

For fixed Delta,f,b define the actual mark polynomial

    M_(i,Delta,f,b)(n)
       = sum_Q u_i(Delta Q)/sqrt(q_Q)
               1_(Delta Q,fb)=1 chi_Q(n)^4,          (R12)

with all original P=Delta Q supports and (Delta,Q)=1 in its
coefficient. Its coefficient square mass is at most

    q_Delta Omega_(i,Delta),
    Omega_(i,Delta)=sum_(Delta|P)|u_i(P)|^2/q_P.       (R13)

This is the crucial mark bookkeeping: chi_Q(t)^4 is combined
with chi_Q(m)^4 into chi_Q(tm)^4, including zeros. It is not
discarded or left as a t-dependent coefficient when t is summed.

### 3.2 Quadratic sieve with t fixed

After the specified common profile separation, the fixed-t,f,Delta
row sum has the form, up to its fixed row multiplier,

    sum_(j sf) chi_k(j)^3
       sum_(mb=j) c_(i,t,f,Delta)(m,b) M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm).
                                                               (R14)

The coefficient c contains the native a(m), xi(fb), exact b_(i,t),
chi_t(m)^4, R11, original product windows/masks, normalized profiles
and the norm-gap phase when present. It does NOT depend on k or Q.
Its bounded normalized modulus has only fixed divisor growth.
Thus the inner coefficient of the actual j is independent of the
quadratic row. M B2.24 applies with factor

    K/q_Delta + NG/(T q_f).                           (R15)

Only after that sieve, Cauchy over mb=j costs tau(j). It is not a
triangle over all m, t, or extracted divisors. The resulting positive
sum permits the bounded source factors in c to be discarded.
This is the first place chi_t(m)^4, C_i(tm), the native coefficients
and a unit far phase are replaced by their moduli.

For nonnegative weights w_t<=tau(t), the fixed-Delta bound for the
sum of fixed-t norms is consequently at most

    Z^epsilon q_Delta^(-1)
       (K/q_Delta+NG/(T q_f))
       sum_(t~T,m,b original) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm)|^2. (R16)

The weights w_t, |b_(i,t)(m)|^2 and tau(j) have separate small-power
allowances. They are each bounded by fixed divisor powers in the
retained polynomial ranges. This suppression costs no T power.

### 3.3 Sum t only now; cubic sieve in the original n

At fixed f,b,Delta, the polynomial R12 depends on t,m only through
the original product n=tm. All its COEFFICIENTS are independent
of n,t,k. Since t is a divisor of the same squarefree n,

    sum_(t~T,m original) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm)|^2
       <= Z^epsilon sum_(n sf,q_n<<N) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(n)|^2
       << Z^epsilon S(N,L/q_Delta) q_Delta Omega_(i,Delta).
                                                               (R17)

The second inequality is precisely the accepted cubic sieve M
B2.25 with one coefficient vector for the live n. Any remaining
source-only constraints are enlarged only in the first positive
inequality. The same reasoning retains fixed arbitrary V_i because
their exact contribution was R7 and was bounded only after R14.

There is no O(T) multiplicity: for a fixed n, t|n yields only
tau(n) possibilities. There is no moving quadratic-row coefficient:
k has already been removed before R17. A separate cubic bound of
length N/T for each t would generally waste a T-label or mark
factor, but it is not the argument in either frozen source.

There are O_orig(G/q_f) possible b, with empty and bounded quotient
ranges interpreted as in JPS. Multiplying R17 into R16 cancels
q_Delta against the squared original mark root. Finally

    sum_Delta Omega_(i,Delta)
       <= sum_P tau(P)|u_i(P)|^2/q_P
       << Z^epsilon Omega_i.                         (R18)

Replacing K/q_Delta by K and S(N,L/q_Delta) by S(N,L) increases
the positive bound. We have therefore proved

    sum_(t~T) |r_w(t)| sum_(R original) |V_(i,t,f)(R)|^2
       << Z^epsilon (G/q_f)
          (K+NG/(T q_f)) S(N,L) Omega_i,              (R19)

where V is the literal fixed-t,f vector R8, including its independent
norm phase. This is BGC10/HA11, with the profile envelopes temporarily
normalized as in the accepted JPS proof.

### 3.4 Return to the complex paired scalar

Cauchy is applied between the two original arrays in the positive
joint measure (t,R) weighted by |r_w(t)|. The exact signed/complex
r_w and r_h were present before this upper bound; no PSD assertion
about their original pair masks is needed.

Summing the complete f inversion in R9 uses

    sum_(q_f<<G) tau(f)/q_f << (log(2G))^O(1),
    sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2 < infinity.                   (R20)

The resulting one-T-dyad bound is

    Z^epsilon G(K+NG/T) S(N,L)
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                (R21)

All contributing t have q_t>=U. Use a first dyad [U,2U), then
successive doubled ranges. The K terms cost only the number of
nonempty dyads, O(log Z), while sum_T 1/T=O(1/U). This proves R5.

No equality of the two divisor cells was used. One may either sum
their O(log^2 Z) ordered pairs or use V_1=V_2=all directly in R7.
The latter shows explicitly that the complete selected cross-cell
covariance has the same bound. Cross terms have not been inferred
from an estimate on a diagonal cell.

## 4. Original sharp gap, profiles, heights and physical return

The proof first works with finite original cutoffs and one component
of the accepted common separation. The literal norm difference in
R3 has a finite cyclic Fourier expansion with modulus larger than
twice its original range. Its coefficient L1 mass is O(log(2N)).
Each term inserts a factor exp(2 pi i ell q_t q_m/M0) on a linear
side. At fixed t this is a SOURCE-only unit factor in R14. Its
modulus is discarded only after actual-j Cauchy, making R17 uniform
in ell. There is no differentiation of this possibly rapid product
phase and no asserted independent separation in t and m.

The full finite Fourier sum restores the strict >H0 gap and both
equal-norm exclusions. Positivity of the pair selector is not
assumed. All original complex side-two conjugations are retained.

For the original whole profile, apply M B2.22 ONCE before row
enlargement, with its original common separating density. Its two
paired norm-height variables stay independent. The physical long
and short roots remain at N,G and the profiles remain literally
C_i(tm), A_i(fb). Norm twists are bounded phases, so neither sieve
introduces a new height-conductor power. Each original linear
root envelope min(Y^(1/4),(1+Y)^(-A)) occurs once per side,
not once per divisor or projector term.

Every added arithmetic multiplicity is a fixed divisor power of
retained original indices. The original full absolute lattice
tail M B2.23 and source/root ends B2.37--40 therefore acquire only
an arbitrarily small norm power, or a fixed polynomial majorant
before choosing the available Schwartz order. For a paired tail,
multiply first by a polynomial majorant on the other side, then
choose the decay order. This pays BOTH ordered mixed tails and the
squared tail. The two independent rapid height densities absorb
their original finite seminorm powers in the same way. This uses
the original arbitrary-order decay contract, not an invented
uniformity over profiles with only one weak bounded seminorm.

All fixed-place/six-unit components return with their original
weights. Original sharp annuli are never differentiated. No
other-cusp coefficient identity is inferred. Allocate the requested
epsilon among the finitely many divisor, sieve and logarithmic
costs; polynomial scale caps then give the advertised Z^epsilon
uniformity. No number of t labels is charged to P_orig.

Most importantly, the high and low auxiliary forms must FIRST
recombine to the all-prime row scalar. Only then use JPS11's
all-prime-minus-inert identity, including the inert square and
BOTH ordered inert cross terms. Its already accepted total raw
budget is

    Z^epsilon G^2(K+N)
       [sqrt(N)L + {S(N,L)sqrt(N)L}^(1/2)]
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                (R22)

JPS12's explicit general gates remain applicable. The accepted
transport and complete-unit Jacobi subtraction JPS32 then return
once, with their original budgets

    Z^epsilon G^2(K+N)S(N,L)sqrt(L/K),
    Z^epsilon G^2 K L/N,                           (R23)

times the original array/profile mass. They do not bound the
unpaid small-gcd fluctuation.

Auxiliary composites are NOT separately subjected to a redefined
native matching-core, total-index, rational-content, or old paid-
source-complement selector. Such a change would generally destroy
the exact allocation cancellation. The extension retains the
evaluated JPS contract; only complete recombination has the
accepted original physical return. This restriction is essential
to the affirmative review.


## 5. Full versus truncated allocation contraction

For a squarefree nonunit n and t|n,

    sum_(v|n,t|v) mu(v) log(q_n/q_v)
       = mu(t) sum_(z|n/t) mu(z) log(q_(n/t)/q_z)
       = mu(t) Lambda_K(n/t).                     (R24)

The unit cofactor contributes zero. The second side has the same
real Mobius/log coefficient; the two mu(t) factors multiply to
one. Hence completing ALL allowed allocations on both sides gives

    B_w(n,n')
       := sum_(v|n,v'|n') mu(v)mu(v') w((v,v'))
          log(q_n/q_v)log(q_n'/q_v')/(log q_n log q_n')

       = sum_(t|(n,n')) r_w(t)
          Lambda_K(n/t)Lambda_K(n'/t)
             /(log q_n log q_n').                 (R25)

This is BGC13=HA19. No sign, factorial, conjugate orientation or
root factor is missing. Ideals are ordered exactly as the original
two sides; there is no passage to unordered prime pairs.

On the actual far support q_n!=q_n', each nonzero cofactor is a
prime ideal because n,n' are squarefree. If n/t=p and n'/t=p'
then q_p!=q_p', so p and p' are distinct and coprime. It follows
that t=(n,n') is the unique possible surviving divisor. Thus R25
equals

    r_w(s) log(q_p)log(q_p')/(log(q_sp)log(q_sp')),
    n=s p, n'=s p', s=(n,n'), (s,pp')=1, q_p!=q_p'. (R26)

It is zero if the cofactors are not prime. Equal-norm conjugate
primes cannot create a second surviving orientation; the original
gap excludes them. Without that gap R25 is still correct, but the
unique-gcd simplification R26 is not the general diagonal formula.

The far selector in R26 is exactly
q_s |q_p-q_p'|>H0, equivalently
|q_p-q_p'|>floor(H0/q_s). This is equality of integer endpoint
conditions, not a smoothed replacement.

The native a(n), a(n'), row/mark factors, both short-source
coefficients, product profiles and original extension masks depend
on the full products after R2, not their allocation labels.
Therefore R25--26 multiply the actual decorated scalar unchanged.
This is original arithmetic, not an unweighted coefficient model.
It remains the EVALUATED auxiliary extension, not a theorem about
a redefined true core of sp and sp'.

For FIXED label sets V_1,V_2, the correct formula instead is

    B_w^(V_1,V_2)(n,n')
       = sum_(t|(n,n')) r_w(t)
          b_(1,t)(n/t)b_(2,t)(n'/t),                (R27)

with b as in R7, including the original log denominators. This is
HA28 and follows from the same exact substitution v=t z. The
second b is real for the stipulated indicator label sets; no
conjugation ambiguity occurs. If one were to introduce complex
label weights, the appropriate second-side conjugation would be
required, but neither reviewed theorem needs that extension.

Only for the FULL allowed label sets does

    b_(all,t)(m)=Lambda_K(m)/log(q_t q_m)            (R28)

reduce R27 to R25. One may not use BGC13/HA19 to identify a fixed
pressure-cell covariance with prime cofactors.

A decisive original-allocation check makes this distinction visible.
Take V_1=V_2={1}, w=1, and eligible squarefree composites
n=r p, n'=r p' with distinct-norm prime cofactors. Their unit-cell
allocation coefficient is exactly one: v=v'=1, each original
logarithmic ratio is one. The FULL coefficient R25 is zero,
since Lambda_K(rp)=Lambda_K(rp')=0. The missing nonunit allocation
terms provide that cancellation. For a nonunit cell containing
only r among the divisors, its paired coefficient is

    w(r) log(q_p)log(q_p')/(log(q_rp)log(q_rp')).     (R29)

It is nonzero when w(r)!=0. These are exact coefficient statements
on eligible support, not
energy lower bounds or assertions that every original array/window
is populated. They prove why the truncation correction matters.

Branch A's HA28 is therefore accepted as the required correction
to an otherwise overbroad pressure-cell use of HA19/HA20. Branch B
already states its contraction for the complete allocation sum;
no change to BGC13 itself is required. Its use as a falsification
test for any proposed cellwise estimate must respect R27.

## 6. What is actually paid; the unit and low-gcd complement

For w=1, r_w(t)=1_(t=1), so R25 returns exactly the ordered
all-prime pair scalar. For w_U(s)=1_(q_s>=U), r_w(t)=0 below U.
If U>1, R26 has only composite long products with a common core
of norm at least U and two distinct-norm prime cofactors. The core
itself can be prime or composite. There is no original prime-pair
coefficient.

This restricted form is not vacuous as an arithmetic expression:
if s is a good prime with q_s>=U and the other original factors
are eligible, r_w(s)=1 and R26 is nonzero. The review uses no
prime-counting asymptotic or covariance lower bound to establish
its analytic estimate.

For w_coprime(s)=1_(s=1), r_w(t)=mu(t). In particular the full
coefficient at n=r p, n'=r p' with r prime is the NEGATIVE of
R29 with w(r)=1. Coprime EXTRACTED labels therefore still create
shared composite long cores after full allocation summation.
The signs cannot be replaced by an independence heuristic.

The exact low complement w_<U=1-w_U has transform

    r_<U(t)=1_(t=1)-r_U(t).                         (R30)

For U>1 this is one at the unit, zero at 1<q_t<U and -r_U(t)
at q_t>=U. Consequently, after summing all label cells,

    C_all-prime = C_<U + C_>=U,
    C_<U = C_all-prime - C_>=U.                     (R31)

These are partitions of ordered AUXILIARY PAIRS, not a high/low
decomposition of a linear source. There is no invented additional
Cauchy cross term between the two pair masks. Every ordered
D,D' interaction already belongs to one of them.

Every pair with v=1 or v'=1 belongs to C_<U for U>1, including
unit/nonunit interactions. The unit self cell is not itself a pure
prime source: it contains the original long composite extensions
as well, as R29's preceding example shows. Actual primes have only
the v=1 nonzero allocation, so their full coefficient stays one
in the low complement. Both facts are needed for an honest return.

At the frozen pressure point

    K=Z^k, k=.835507578307735986...,
    N=K Z^.003, G=Z^.001,
    L=Z^.170813789153867993..., S(N,L) comparable to N,

the bound R5 divided by the original raw target G K S(N,L) is

    Z^epsilon [1 + Z^(.004-u)], U=Z^u.             (R32)

Thus U0=NG/K=Z^.004 pays the WHOLE high-gcd auxiliary pair
form at target size. The outside N^(-1)G^(-2) is unchanged
and cancels from this comparison. Away from this pressure point
one can use U0=max(1,NG/K); if NG/K<=1 the incumbent bound is
already target-sized. This convention introduces no new H scope.

However, R31 shows that at U0 an estimate for the full low form
at any proposed budget at least target size is equivalent, up to
an already target-sized additive error, to the same estimate for
the original all-prime form. In particular B's NEXT or A's HA27
is not yet an independently easier global theorem. This is the
strongest relevance limitation on the otherwise valid bound.

At present the low form has only the incumbent budget
Z^epsilon G(K+NG)S(N,L) times the original masses, obtained by
the EXACT identity R31, JPS24 and R5, not by signed-submask
inheritance. Its pressure exponent deficit remains .004.
No target-sized high-sector estimate justifies reducing that
incumbent bound or a unit/nonunit cross budget.

A cellwise continuation such as A's HA26 can still be a useful
research question. It must estimate the actual coupled truncated
coefficient R27, and return every other small-gcd cell, the unit
self term and all ordered unit/nonunit interactions. Even completing
the retained prime packet would leave the other original H branches
and quantitative zero-exclusion return. The accepted c0 remains
0.125113352960035869... without promotion.

## 7. Branch A's additional bound and comparison

A's HA17 is a valid further formulation at its stated scope.
With divisor-cell sizes D,D', E=N/D,E'=N/D', freeze t first and
rerun the positive JPS17 proof on v=t z. The remaining extracted
label z has size D/q_t; the actual quadratic column z e b has
length NG/(q_t q_f). The cubic coefficients at fixed z,b contain
the retained chi_Q(tz)^4 and are independent of live e and row k.
The fixed-t diagonal estimate is therefore

    Z^epsilon (D/q_t) G(K+NG/q_t) S(E,L) Omega_i,    (R33)

after the same complete f,Delta costs. One need not assert a
new JPS3 prime theorem at N/q_t: this is only a rerun of its
positive sieve proof, with all original product supports retained.

Cauchy between the two sides, then the signed t-transform with
absolute divisor weights, uses harmonic sum 1/q_t in the K term
and tail sum 1/q_t^2 in the NG term. It gives

    Z^epsilon sqrt(D D') G(K+NG/U)
       sqrt(S(N/D,L)S(N/D',L))
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                (R34)

This validates HA17, including the shortened label count.
Its main restricted application is already covered by R5.

Indeed, for every D>=1,

    D S(N/D,L)
       = N+D L+(NL)^(2/3)D^(1/3)
       >= N+L+(NL)^(2/3) = S(N,L).                 (R35)

Hence with the SAME original N on both sides,
sqrt(D D')sqrt(S(N/D,L)S(N/D',L)) >= S(N,L).
Up to the fixed dyadic comparison constants, R34 is dominated
by R5. It is a correct comparison to the proposed JPS30 scale,
not a second quantitative improvement over HA16/BGC1.
At the pressure cells with N/D,N/D'>=L^2 the two long factors
are comparable, explaining the matching scale there.

A's fixed-set formulation and B's union-of-cells argument use
the same bound |b_(i,t)|<=tau(m); no extra row-dependent selection
is permitted by either. A's r_W-support formulation is a convenient
generalization of the hypothesis, but it uses the same analytic
mechanism. HA28 is a useful scope correction and exact interface,
not a second sieve gain.


## 8. Functional novelty, objections and next mathematical action

Within the inspected JPS/HPR record, the new functional step is
to resolve a divisor common to the TWO extracted labels at the
paired level, freeze it while taking the quadratic norm, and only
then regroup its positive output by the original n before the
cubic mark sieve. JPS18--24 grouped a live v into the actual
quadratic column v e b, retaining length NG; JPS21's early freezing
paid a full independent label triangle. The present pairing permits
length NG/q_t while paying only divisor multiplicity at the later
n stage. The short-core inversion f in JPS7/JPS20 is a different
already established operation.

The paired allocation identity R25 extends the one-source
JPS23 and the actual semiprime cancellation JPS26 to an arbitrary
extracted-label gcd weight. Standard Mobius inversion, the native
Gauss cocycle and the large sieves themselves are not new. The
review makes no literature-priority claim and imports no external
prime-distribution, Hecke, cuspidality or metaplectic hypothesis.
A and B count once for both this mechanism and the common
prime-cofactor contraction.

The strongest analytic objections were checked directly:

1. A hidden T count would arise from estimating each completed
   t norm separately. R16--17 instead sum by t|n while the original
   n remains live for the cubic sieve. The coefficients in R12
   are explicitly independent of n,t,k.
2. A moving row factor would invalidate a premature cubic sieve.
   R14 uses chi_k(tf)^3 only as a FIXED row factor at fixed t,f,
   removes the quadratic row first, and then invokes R17.
3. A missing mark root or incomplete collision projector would
   change the bound. The full Delta inversion supplies
   q_Delta^-1 in energy and q_Delta Omega_Delta in the cubic
   coefficient mass; the cancellation is explicit. No child
   reinstates a (Q,k) projector.
4. A false native source change would replace tm g^3 by m(tg)^3
   or reinterpret its core/corrections. Neither operation occurs.
   The original N,G roots and evaluated extension remain literal.
5. A signed-submask inference would not be justified. The new
   pair mask is expanded exactly and estimated afresh; the sharp
   far mask uses its whole finite Fourier expansion.
6. Prime-cofactor contraction in a single cell would be false.
   R27, not R25, is its coefficient. The unit/composite example
   supplies an exact failure witness.
7. Paying composite counterterms alone does not pay primes.
   R31 shows the original prime scalar remains in the low
   complement with coefficient one.

There is no analytic correction required to BGC1 at this scope.
For integration, attach the following explicit qualifications:

- Use the full-allocation qualification whenever citing BGC13--16
  or HA19--20, and cite HA28/R27 for a fixed label subset.
- Do not describe the paid high-gcd form as a physical H source
  subfamily or as new prime cancellation.
- Count the two branches once. HA17 is valid but dominated by
  the global grouped bound for the same original N.
- The remaining global low-gcd target is equivalent, modulo the
  already paid correction, to the retained original prime target;
  it is not automatically a simpler theorem.

The next genuinely informative mathematical action is narrower
than restating the global target. On the original pressure cells,
retain the literal coprime/small-gcd two-label coefficient R27
with its truncated b factors, original row character and both
marks through a proposed dispersion step. Derive and price a
new covariance identity that uses cancellation unavailable to
the two positive sieves above. Test that identity on the exact
unit/composite and common-prime-core coefficients before spending
time on its tails. If it supplies no bound beyond JPS17/JPS24,
this common-divisor mechanism has exhausted its present gain.
Any successful continuation must separately return the unit
self cell, all unit/nonunit cross cells and every remaining
small-gcd cell, plus the untouched original H obligations.

## 9. Evidence, source bindings and handoff

The stable subagent prefix and frozen [private research revision] problem snapshot
were read first. The bound B artifact was inspected in full and
reconstructed against JPS/HPR and the actual M coefficient/sieve/
profile slices. Branch A was read in full only after the controller
reported successful recovery, freeze and STOP, then checked for
its independent convergence, HA28 correction and HA17 comparison.

The mathematical evidence in this review is the displayed exact
algebra and legal sequence of two positive sieve applications,
not favorable agreement between agents. Author finite arithmetic
checks were not counted as proof or needlessly replayed. No new
test, numerical c optimization or unrelated source audit was run.

Bindings to the exact source bytes read:



The canonical JPS/HPR bindings above include their current wrapper
headers and differ from the historical draft hashes quoted inside
those sources. This review does not silently substitute a
historical source binding.

Only the assigned review path was written. The first attempted
replacement patch was rejected before any file operation because
it named the same target twice; the successful writes then replaced
the partial checkpoint and appended this review exactly once.
No other artifact, provider, process, claim, tracker or Git state
was mutated. The direct-ALT author file stayed frozen.

The complete review will be read back and its exact byte count
and SHA-256 reported in the handoff. After that receipt the reviewer
stops writing this artifact. This is evidence for the controller's
independent integration decision, not automatic theorem acceptance
or a larger zero-free constant.
