## R5. Marginal payment and the residual box

Dividing B0.9 by one inverse witness in R6 gives the unweighted count exponent

    I(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r.

Taking the two MP0 plain profiles equal and dividing its fourth moment by a plain witness gives P(m)=1-2delta m. The literal zero-slot source allows independent heights and every bounded length, so the marginal plain application is licensed. Fixed masks remain fixed for the row sum; B3.41 gives the required signed removal and its coefficient mass before Minkowski. No positive-slot MP, arbitrary prime subset, or extra inverse coefficient is invoked in these marginal bounds. The slot cost is added afterward as delta v.

Set

    e=rho-G-eta, q=5/6-delta,
    A=(1-e)/delta, C=(e-1/6)/q.                       (R9)

Then I(r)<=e on A<=r<=C and P(m)<=e on m>=A/2. This uses the actual decreasing inverse branch r<=1 and increasing branch r>=1; the point r=1 is not omitted. The exact whole-interval certificates give

    A<47/50<1<t<C,
    C-A>3/8, 3A/2-C<3/40.                            (R10)

Pay the union of every row admitting an easy witness in either presentation and in either of the two profile families used in R6 below. There are only fixed finite presentation choices and logarithmically many dyads/annuli; continuous parameters use the prescribed source Sobolev bounds. The union costs H_J U^(E_K-eta+small). Allowing a small padded interval [A-p,C+p] and threshold m>=A/2-p changes its exponent by at most 2p before the witness/source losses. The helper additionally certifies strict coarse gaps after 8p, with p=10^-6. One may choose the remaining aggregate loss below eta/2. Boundaries and equality therefore enter the paid set; they are not discarded.

Outside that union, the original inverse has r_-<A+small, and the complementary inverse has r_+>C-small. Both plain lengths are below A/2+small. Product compatibility then gives

    C-small<ell<3A/2+small,
    ell-A-small<m_-<A/2+small,
    0<=m_+<ell-C+small,
    r_+-r_->C-A-small.                               (R11)

After the fixed padding and endpoint errors, the strict coarse residual is

    17/20<r_-<47/50, 3/8<m_-<47/100,
    33/25<r_+<141/100, 0<=m_+<3/40,
    r_+-r_->3/8,
    r_-+m_-=r_++m_++o(1).                            (R12)

There are two independent Fourier heights, one common real part, one common character and one actual product annulus. The lower endpoint r_->17/20 follows from C-A/2>17/20 with room; the helper certifies it directly. All inequalities are uniform in delta and v, not merely endpoint calculations.

To verify the algebra, let e_min=rho-a_K-b_K/20-eta=N/Den. Then e>=e_min. Increasing e decreases A, increases C and decreases 3A/2-C. The cleared polynomials for R10 are

    Den*delta*(47/50-A_min),
    Den*q*(C_min-t),
    Den*delta*q*(C_min-A_min-3/8),
    Den*delta*q*(3/40-3A_min/2+C_min),

where A_min and C_min mean A,C evaluated at e_min. The review constructs these directly as rational functions at delta=17/25+x/50 and interpolates the exact cleared polynomials. Bernstein positivity over 0<=x<=1 proves the interval statements. Positive denominator and k numerators are separately checked. This proof uses an upper envelope of G, so no switch of its min branches or unverified monotonicity in v is concealed.

## C. Centered Mayer feedback: exact return and a new next-return formula

Mayer's primary source defines L_s on A_infinity(|z-1|<3/2), gives its nuclear meromorphic continuation and Z_mod(s)=det(1-L_s)det(1+L_s). A nontrivial Riemann zero rho yields a zero at s=rho/2 and hence a +1 OR -1 eigenvalue. The source's sign-specific correspondence is explicitly conjectural there; retaining both signs is essential. [Mayer, pp.3–5,8–9](https://archive.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/id/eprint/346/1/preprint_1990_86.pdf).

For Re(s)>0 the centered operator

    Q_s f(z)=sum_(n>=1)[(n+z)^(-2s)f(1/(n+z))-n^(-2s)f(0)]

converges locally normally. Its rank-one completion is L_s=Q_s+zeta(2s)Pi. At s=rho/2, L_s=Q_s exactly. Relative to f=c+g, g(0)=0,

    Q_s = [[0,ell_s],[h_s,Ktilde_s]],
    h_s(z)=sum_n[(n+z)^(-2s)-n^(-2s)],

      <= |2s(2s+1)| zeta(2sigma+1)^2 zeta(2sigma+2).

statement:
### M3. Fixed affine correlations, including conjugation

Take fixed positive-slope affine forms L_i(n)=A_i n+B_i, integer coefficients, A_i>0, with A1 B2-A2 B1!=0. Finitely many n for which a form is nonpositive may be discarded. First change only a fixed finite set F of prime values; include primes of q. Write Q=product_{p in F}p and D=2^{|F|}. On a nonzero term write L1(n)=d r, L2(n)=e s, with d,e|Q and r,s squarefree and coprime to Q. Any ramified or squareful zero is simply omitted.

After conditioning on all random values at primes in F, the remaining conjugated monomial is epsilon(r/s); the unconjugated monomial is epsilon(rs). Distinct positive rational ratios, respectively distinct positive integer products, are orthogonal under the remaining Steinhaus variables. For a fixed ratio r/s and fixed d,e, the equation L1(n)/L2(n)=(d/e)(r/s) has at most one n, because the determinant is nonzero. A monomial class therefore contains at most D^2 terms. For a fixed product rs and fixed d,e, the quadratic equation L1(n)L2(n)=de*rs has at most two n, giving at most2D^2 terms. Coefficients arising from finite prime values or fixed character weights have modulus at most1. Consequently, for either correlation sum C_N,

  E |C_N|^2 <= 2D^2 N+O_F(1).

Markov and Borel--Cantelli along N=j^2 show C_{j^2}/j^2 tends to zero almost surely; bounded summands fill the gaps, since(j+1)^2-j^2=O(j). Take the countable intersection over finite F, integer affine pairs, and fixed ordinary character weights. The estimate is uniform over conditioned finite prime phases, since only their moduli entered.

Now transfer to the infinite random set P. Truncate it at Y, along with the fixed prescriptions and primes of q. The infinite and truncated sequences can differ at a positive integer only if some p in P above Y divides it. For a fixed form A n+B, put the finitely many p|A into the truncation. Each remaining p has at most N/p+1 roots with n<=N and p<=C N. The density of exceptional n is therefore at most

  sum_{p in P,p>Y}1/p + O(#P(CN)/N).

The second term tends to zero by the bound O(N^b), b<1; the first tends to zero as Y tends to infinity. Products of two bounded terms change by at most2 on the union of their exceptional sets. First take N to infinity, then Y to infinity. Both asserted Cesaro correlations vanish. This argument is compatible with the probability-one events of M1 and M2 because the whole list is countable. It produces one fixed outcome, not a new sequence at each scale.

In particular, for every FIXED integer H>=1,

  (1/N) sum_{m<=N}|sum_{j=1}^H a(m+j)|^2 -> H d_q,

where d_q=product_{p|q}(1-1/p) product_{p not dividing q}(1-1/p^2)>0 is the squarefree coprime density. Off-diagonal terms vanish by M3; the diagonal follows by the elementary squarefree density computation. There is no uniformity for growing H. Ordinary Cesaro cancellation also implies the qualitative logarithmic fixed-form conclusions by partial summation, including long logarithmic intervals with length parameter tending to infinity. It does not establish every nonpretentiousness hypothesis of an outside theorem, nor its quantitative uniformities.
title: M3. Fixed affine correlations, including conjugation

<=Z*exp(3H_Z). Thus |t|>D*sqrt(log Z) costs a field
O(Z^(-A_0+o(1))). For the fully capped coefficient form one can

polynomial; the same proof uses its d_3 majorant. Both presentations

## 5. Low bins and the canonical actual-width correction

**Classification: proved source transfer; this disposes of the strongest possible low-bin objection.**

The low-bin indicator is introduced only **after both transforms**, on a positive child energy. The exact pinned `Energy.AllocatedChildren.commonChild_energy`, `AllocatedNaturalRadial.allocated_radial_bound`, and `AllocatedRayDictionary.common_clipped_energy` permit an arbitrary extra `keep` predicate. They retain the canonical row, masks, relative characters and normalizers. Thus the bin need not be hereditary through a subsequent transform: no subsequent Poisson transform of that bin is used.

On such rows, first bound and remove a greedy prefix of surviving prime slots of total width `dz`. Their actual nonprincipal natural characters lie in the common buffered bin, so their squared pointwise cost is `Z^((0.7+O(e))dz+eta)`, including restoration of polynomial-size holes. Each removed slot releases old capacity `4.5 dz`. Stop when the old capacity holds, or when all slots are exhausted. After this **pointwise** removal, drop the row restriction by positivity and apply the old canonical moment to the whole remaining eligible family. If empty, use the separate unrestricted zero-slot theorem, which does not demand plain total length below the width. This is not a bootstrap of the improved moment.

Actual canonical width can be below the nominal `M'`, because moving support may cancel. Write `d_* = M_actual-M'`, with upper bound `delta2` but no lower bound. If `F` is the nominal affine defect then actual defect is at most `(F-d_*)_+`. For `0<=r<=1`, the elementary inequality

`d_* + r(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2 + r F_+`

holds: `x -> x+r(F-x)_+` is nondecreasing and at `x=delta2` is at most `delta2+rF_+` when `delta2>=0`. Equivalently, split at `x=F`. This covers negative `d_*` instead of assuming it is nonnegative. PR9 extraction gives `F<=g+6a+eta`. With `r=(0.7+O(e))/4.5`, the combined width/removal exponent is at most

`M' +(7/45)(g+6a)+eta`.

It is strictly inside the available `M'+a` because

`a-(7/45)(g+6a) >= M/2000 -(7/45)(M/10000+3M/1000) = 4M/225000 > 0`.

The one greedy mesh overshoot, `omega`, bin upper-edge error and support padding are selected within a smaller budget. A bin straddling `0.7` is assigned low and uses its upper edge `0.7+O(e)`. Thus neither the cutoff endpoint nor the possibly negative actual-width correction is hidden.

## R7. Fourier compression and the sharp endpoint

Let C_Y(n) denote precisely the remaining masked coefficient in Section R6, including its gcd mask, and S_Y its partial sum. The observed causal kernel is

    k(v)=e^(-av)S_Y(e^v)1_(0<=v<=log X).

It gives the exact remaining operator on (0,L)^2. For s=a+i tau, integrate each cumulative atom, which is a finite operation:

    int_(log n)^(log X) e^(-sv)dv
       =(n^(-s)-X^(-s))/s, n<=X.

Thus

    hat k(tau)=[sum_(n<=X)C_Y(n)n^(-s)-X^(-s)S_Y(X)]/s. (R11)

No half-weight convention at integers changes this Lebesgue integral. The atom at n=X has zero contribution; the corresponding t=u=L corner is a null set. Noninteger X uses its exact floor in both sums. The endpoint term is essential, and the author has retained it.

Use |b(ell)|<=1+r and discard masks only for the positive upper bound. Summing ell first gives

    sum_(n<=X)|C_Y(n)|n^(-a)
       <<_(a,r)X^(1-a)sum_(de<=X)1/(de)
       <<X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2.                        (R12)

The actual partial sum is smaller than the corresponding absolute restoration count: `|S_Y(X)|<=C_b X(1+log X)`. Both numerator terms of (R11) are consequently bounded. Since a is fixed and positive,

    |hat k(tau)|<<_(a,q,r)X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/(1+|tau|).

Split this whole symbol by the two indicators |tau|<=Omega and >Omega, on the full real line. Plancherel says that each is a bounded full-line multiplier with norm at most its supremum. Reflection, zero extension and compression all have norm one. Therefore

    ||T^hi||<<X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.             (R13)

The low-frequency kernel is no longer causal or compactly supported. That is harmless because it is defined as the full-line multiplier followed by the stated compression, not as a guessed local kernel. The two compressed pieces sum exactly to the original observed operator. Every coupled time rectangle remains. No square-root gain is inferred from a scalar average.

In particular OPEN-LOW concerns the complete symbol (R11) before compression, or more weakly its complete compressed operator. A sup-norm bound for that symbol is sufficient but is not an equivalent necessary condition on the compressed operator. The author states this distinction correctly. Omitting the endpoint, dropping the mixed hyperbolic cap, or asserting norm monotonicity under a signed arithmetic restriction would invalidate the proof; none occurs.

Combining the genuine operator differences from R4, R6 and (R13) yields (R1). It is valid also on the original nonprincipal source with b=chi and C_b=q. There are no unpriced principal, unit, short-factor, diagonal, high-gcd or high-frequency pieces within this stated source decomposition.

## R42.3. Both inverse coefficient costs, including the 2/3 edge

For sigma>2/3 let d=Q^-sigma and r=Q^(3-6sigma). Weighted local coefficient norms, including every valuation, satisfy

    ||h_p-1||_sigma <= [r+t(d+r)/(1-d)]/(1-r),
    ||h_p^-1-1||_sigma
      <= [td+(1-t)r+dr]/[1-(1-t)d-tr].                 (R42.3)

To check the second bound, the exact numerator after subtracting1 is -tD-(1-t)R+DR. Expand the actual denominator N, not a conjectured nonzero value: (1-t)d+tr<=Q^-2/3+Q^-2<=2^-2/3+1/4<1. Both quantities in R42.3 are O_sigma(Q^-1-sigma+Q^(3-6sigma)). Ideal counting # {Na<=T}=O(T) and partial summation make their sums finite. The convergent products of (1+local norm) therefore give multiplicative h,j with

    h*j=delta_1, A_sigma=sum |h(a)|Na^-sigma<infinity,
    B_sigma=sum |j(a)|Na^-sigma<infinity.               (R42.4)

These identities prove local and global holomorphy and nonvanishing of H and its reciprocal on Re s>2/3. The original source's convenient .87 nonvanishing region was not an absolute limit of this correction. This extension concerns the correction alone; it does not extend any contour box or arithmetic moment in PR9.

The claimed boundary of this particular absolute method is also real. Exact expansion gives h(p^6)=t a^6+(1-t)bQ^3, of magnitude at least (1-Q^-1)Q^3-Q^-1. Consequently its weighted mass contains a positive multiple of sum_p Q^(3-6sigma), divergent for sigma<=2/3. One may use the source's stated prime ideal theorem; alternatively the pole of the positive ideal zeta series and its absolutely convergent higher-prime-power logarithm imply sum_p1/Q=infinity. This is not a lower bound for a signed Gaussian norm and does not forbid a different method beyond c=1/3.

Write

    U_eta,tau(x)=sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a) g_tau(log(Na/x)),
    g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)).

The Gaussian and ideal counting justify locally uniform absolute convergence and Mellin inversion on Re s>1, where the transform is exp(tau s^2/2)/L_K^S(s,eta). Since exp((s-5/6)^2)=exp(25/36)exp(-5s/3)exp(s^2), the **two** exact field identities are

    P_eta(x)=C_S exp(25/36) sum_a h(a)U_eta,2(exp(-5/3)x/Na),
    U_eta,2(x)=C_S^-1 exp(-25/36)
                         sum_a j(a)P_eta(exp(5/3)x/Na). (R42.5)

A single absolute coefficient line majorizes all series and their composition; Gaussian tails then justify inversion and direct field equality. In particular no contour passage through an unknown zero was needed to establish these identities.

For ||F||_[X,2X]^2=integral_X^(2X)|F|^2 dx/x and ||F||_sigma=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma||F||_[X,2X], Minkowski applied at the actual dilated shell gives

    ||P||_sigma <= C_S exp(25/36-5sigma/3) A_sigma ||U||_sigma,
    ||U||_sigma <= C_S^-1 exp(-25/36+5sigma/3) B_sigma ||P||_sigma. (R42.6)

The factors exp(plus/minus5sigma/3) have the stated signs. A real shell is covered by at most two adjacent dyadic shells; Gaussian left tails pay X<=1. Thus every-positive-epsilon all-dyad bounds are equivalent at each gamma>=2/3, using sigma=gamma+epsilon and slightly smaller input losses when necessary. At gamma=2/3 this does not assert a finite exact-power norm.

Any such full bound at gamma makes Mellin(U) holomorphic on Re s>gamma: dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz gives absolute summability and every logarithmic derivative on compact subsets, while the Gaussian left tail pays zero. The identity exp(s^2)/L then rules out every L-zero there; a principal pole produces a reciprocal zero and causes no difficulty. For a common family boundary the same gamma and the every-epsilon hypothesis must hold **separately for each fixed target**. Constants, S and thresholds may depend on that target. A zeta-only or single-eta estimate does not supply the family conclusion.

Original far masking retains |q_pi-q_pi'|>floor(Z^.05), the distinct-rational-norm condition and the remaining front selectors. The full signed d sum, centered Jacobi subtraction and source complements remain. A divisor child has no inherited estimate merely because its parent has one.

With inner product linear in its second argument, k is the CONJUGATE kernel vector. For an isometry V and orthogonal P, exactly

    <k,W>=<PVk,PVW>+<(I-P)Vk,(I-P)VW>.                 (R9)

The author's convention is correct. The complement vanishes if P preserves Vk; known kernel-invariant orbit projections are legitimate examples. Otherwise it must be estimated after all outer phases, d and heights are recombined. Unitary norm conservation supplies no signed improvement.

The historical fixed-u,v raw target remains GKS sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), against G(K+N)S, with N/K=Z^.003 and outside squared factor N^(-1)G^(-2) paid once. The all-g .004 deficit is separate. No generic dilation theorem pays either. The simple two-dimensional norm example is only a warning against discarding the complement, not a lower bound for actual H. This matches JN, FG and [private research revision] source contracts; no new native H result is admitted.

**27, hidden pole.** For A=diag(7/8,-1), B=(1,1)^T and C=(0,1), the observable transfer is1/(s+1). The mode at7/8 is reachable but unobservable. This correctly refutes the GENERIC inference from stable output to stable full state. It does not place such a mode in H or an L-function. The actual numerator/observability and all complementary source modes remain unproved.

**30, causal delays.** Define K_chi=sum_n chi(n)delta_(log n), and F(u)=M(e^u) for u>=0, zero otherwise. Locally finite convolution and (R1) give

    (K_chi*F)(u)=sum_(n<=e^u)chi(n)M(e^u/n)=1_(u>=0).
                                                               (R10)

For Re(s)>1, Laplace(K)=L(s,chi) and Laplace(F)=1/[sL(s,chi)]. For real sigma<=1, sum_n |chi(n)|n^(-sigma) diverges, since the unit residue classes have positive density. A CAUSAL exponential input has output

    e^(su) sum_(n<=e^u)chi(n)n^(-s),

not the untruncated L(s,chi)e^(su) below absolute convergence. Its moving endpoint and the signed residual must be paid. The principal character exhibits the growing partial-sum main term when Re(s)<1. No stability estimate follows. This is existing inverse/renewal/control ancestry with a correct boundary warning, not a new obstruction to every signed delay method.

statement:
# W62 independent review: paid prime flux and two retained audits

Verdict: retain D1 as a correct conditional ordinary-character zero-exclusion criterion, with its full prime-power, moving-column and diagonal payments. Retain D2 and D3 as explicit actual-source identities and obstructions at their stated scopes. None proves the missing signed estimate or improves c. The critic's additional S22 and S10 calculations below preserve their original source returns; they expose costs rather than supply cancellation. A modest strengthening of D1's paid cutoff is proved in Section 3.

Current accepted written calibration is c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, gamma11=.8748540364. First gain requires gamma<gamma11, complete raw squared exponent<1.7497080728, or corresponding saving>.2502919272. All inherited analytic/F0, positive-slot uniformity and external binding/admission obligations remain open. Ordinary fixed-character arguments below are not an adapter to native Eisenstein H or growing conductor. No formalization, proof packet or literature-priority claim is made. Controller acceptance remains separate from this review.



## 1. Inputs, independent selection and sampling

The immutable author report is 25,664 bytes, SHA256 `51cc3b99cd924e60965fce4db7c8a5f371ece20bf7e6b480f8fe9e3e2a74ee72`; author freeze SHA256 `623bfc380e5315942b1da30fe6e3deabca95d041a231c35337d70e57f7143949` binds 15 files. All were read completely at the byte level, decoded/parsed as applicable and matched. The full report, seeds, helpers and receipts were semantically inspected; no author helper was run or author file changed. `source-receipt.json` binds the initial intake, and `review-sources.json` distinguishes fresh full reads, bounded slices and retained prior context.

Blind critic preparation froze at 19:27:49.647652 UTC, SHA256 `d53ef3c3c4a96af157fc4bc428d9b3c82e6180a6f94891ee9e69bbe8d3ba572c`. It preserved all 30 seed IDs, deterministic mechanism priority and one independent uniform permutation. The all-card pool was saved/read before fresh 16-bit rejection entropy; the 29-step Fisher-Yates receipt is exact and had no rejected words. No author selection or outcome had been read by the critic at that freeze. Author selections already existed on disk: this is an outcome-blind, selection-blind critic preparation, not a claim that it preceded the author's selection event. The author's limited prior pilot-excerpt exposure is disclosed; perfect author history blindness is not claimed.

The frozen rule gives protected **S22** and uniform **S10**, excluding exactly author six S01/S13/S16/S21/S25/S07 and removing the protected ID before the uniform choice. `audit-selection.json` was saved before opening the main outcome report; original pool, priority, permutation and entropy remain unchanged. Both choices were author-untested. The immutable preparation's S07 label G134 was already corrected append-only to W55's G135; no priority changed.

Independent exact replay checked literal probabilities using rationals, every group, saved prior selections, pool hashes, pool-before-entropy timestamps, rejection limits and zero-based indices. There were 25 cards with p<.10 and 16 with p<.01 in the original 30. Deliberate reservations were S01/S13/S16. The three subsequent complete conditional pools were:

| Stage | Pool size | Saved index | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p<.10, all groups | 23 | 13 | S21 |
| p<.01, all remaining groups | 14 | 8 | S25 |
| Uniform all remaining | 25 | 5 | S07 |

There were no duplicate exclusions, rerolls or missing random slots. Subjective p measures generation typicality, not mathematical success. S13 received a real protected test before being parked; S21 received substantial development. The other 24 author cards remain author-untested, with exactly two separately identified critic audits.

## 2. D1/S01: complete conditional prime-flux return

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, principal or imprimitive allowed, and tau>0 independent of scale. Throughout this section a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including n=1, prime 2, all squareful zeros and all character zeros. Put

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) g(log n-y),  z(y)=exp(-gamma*y)U(y),
    1/2<gamma<1.

Gaussian coefficient majorants prove local absolute convergence of every fixed derivative, and polynomial-times-Gaussian decay as y tends to minus infinity. These preliminary facts use no cancellation hypothesis.

### Exact identity and signs

The convolution identity a*chi=delta gives, including every prime power,

    a(n) log n = -sum_(d|n) a(n/d) chi(d) Lambda(d).

For a squareful local exponent the last two surviving prime-power terms cancel. Omitting prime powers would change the actual source. Since tau U'(y)+yU(y)=sum a(n)log n g(log n-y),

    tau U'+yU+K1 U+K2 U=0,
    K1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K2 U=sum_p sum_(j>=2) chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

After weighting, delays d carry chi(d)Lambda(d)d^(-gamma). Define

    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Qj(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(Kj,gamma z)(y)dy.

The exact energy equation is

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau*gamma*E_R=Q1+Q2.       (R1)

In particular the derivative boundary and drift have the signs required for absorption. This identity is inherited Gaussian renewal/logarithmic-source algebra, not a new family.

### Full prime powers and the moving row AND column

For gamma>1/2,

    C_gamma=sum_(p,j>=2) log p*p^(-j*gamma)
      <=(1-2^(-gamma))^(-1) sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2*gamma)<infinity.

Truncate z only above R, retain its whole past, and use translation contraction and Cauchy. Then |Q2|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z|^2. The past is unconditionally finite. Split the positive integral at a fixed sufficiently large Y, using y>=Y on the tail. For every eta>0,

    |Q2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                      (R2)

B_eta is finite from fixed bounded intervals and the Gaussian left tail; no assumed future norm is hidden in it. This relative form bound does not assert cancellation in K2 itself.

For the author's small-prime cutoff p<=(2+y)^A, A(1-gamma)<1, eventually log p<=y/2. Thus v=y-log p is in [y/2,y]. The row sum is at most C(2+y)^(A(1-gamma))log(2+y)=o(y), by summing over integers. In the second half of 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, change variables separately for each p. Since y<=2v, the column is bounded by the same sum with p<=(2+2v)^A, hence o(v). Its upper endpoint satisfies v<=R. The initial bounded y interval uses finitely many primes and a fixed bounded v interval. Therefore, uniformly in every R,

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                (R3)

The column payment is necessary; a row estimate alone would not prove this quadratic-form statement. The written proof does pay both. There is no assumption about z at future points beyond R.

### The exact same-output diagonal and the remaining form

Expand Q_hard before absolute values. Its summand is

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))*chi(p)*a(m)] log p
      *exp(-2*gamma*y)g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),

over p>(2+y)^A, all m,n>=1, and 0<=y<=R. The equality n=pm contributes only when pm is a squarefree q-unit; then -conjugate(a(pm))*chi(p)*a(m)=1. The total retained log-prime weight at fixed n is at most log n. Exactly,

    int_(-infinity)^infinity exp(-2*gamma*y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =exp(tau*gamma^2)n^(-2*gamma)/(2*sqrt(pi*tau)).

Thus the actual hard same-output diagonal D_R obeys

    0<=D_R<=exp(tau*gamma^2)/(2*sqrt(pi*tau))
                 *sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2*gamma)<infinity.          (R4)

This bound includes all cutoff changes and both infinite source sums. It gives no positive domination for arbitrary signed subcollections. Set H_R=Q_hard-D_R, literally the complete n!=pm form with its signs and moving mask.

The proposed arithmetic premise OPEN-PF is: for every fixed chi there exist delta_chi>0, B_chi and R0_chi such that

    H_R<=(1-delta_chi) I_R+B_chi for every R>=R0_chi.             (PF)

Take eta=delta_chi/4 in each of (R2),(R3), use (R4), and absorb the finite initial interval. Equation (R1) implies

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R+tau*gamma E_R<=B'_chi.       (R5)

Hence U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma*y)) at all large real y, with the unchanged fixed Gaussian. No interpolation across missing scales is needed. PF has not been proved; a finite-R fit, a positive selected sector, or a formal identity is not this uniform strict-coercivity premise. This is a sufficient criterion, with no automatic equivalence at the boundary exponent gamma asserted.

### Full zero return and scope

The bilateral transform F(s)=int_(-infinity)^infinity U(y)e^(-s*y)dy is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly with all derivatives, by (R5) and the Gaussian left tail. On Re(s)>1, absolute summation gives

    F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Thus L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) as a meromorphic identity on Re(s)>gamma. The right side never vanishes. A zero of L at any finite height is impossible there. The principal pole at 1 is allowed and forces the corresponding zero of F; it is not an L-zero. Natural zeros and imprimitive factors were present in a from the start. No uniform lower bound for the Gaussian multiplier as height tends to infinity is needed for this pointwise nonvanishing argument, and no reciprocal-growth or unsmoothing theorem is silently imported. The standard character Euler product and principal-pole distinction agree with [DLMF 25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15).

The exponent gamma is common to the family, while delta, constants and onset may depend on fixed chi. This proves an all-height ordinary-character return if PF holds for every such chi. It says nothing about a moving modulus, an Eisenstein Hecke family, or the physical H branches. The endpoint gamma=1/2 is not supplied because both positive payments diverge there. Conditional targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4,.5001 in the author are in range; none has its arithmetic premise established.

The inherited bound U(y)=O(e^(beta*y)) and absolute prime summation give a generic flux envelope with exponent 1+beta-2gamma, whereas I has exponent 2beta-2gamma. The gap 1-beta explains why that absolute route cannot prove PF. An upper envelope is not a signed lower bound or proof that PF fails.

## 3. Independent useful refinement: a larger paid prime cutoff

D1 can pay more small primes without using PNT or arithmetic cancellation. For integer n, the product of primes in (n,2n] divides binomial(2n,n)<=4^n. Dyadic summation and monotonicity give

    theta(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p<=4(log 2)t  (t>=2).

Partial summation therefore gives, for 0<gamma<1 and Y>=2,

    sum_(p<=Y)log p*p^(-gamma)
      <=[4 log 2/(1-gamma)]Y^(1-gamma).                         (R6)

Use the exact monotone cutoff

    Y_gamma(y)=((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^(1/(1-gamma)), y>=0,           (R7)

with equality assigned to the small sector. Its logarithm is O_gamma(log(2+y)), so eventually every small delay still satisfies y/2<=v<=y. By (R6) the row is O_gamma((2+y)/log(e^2+y))=o(y); the column is bounded with p<=Y_gamma(2v) and is likewise o(v). The same change of variables and bounded-initial-region argument proves (R3) for this cutoff. The prime-power payment and diagonal bound are unchanged. Define H_R with the new exact complementary mask. Then PF with this H_R implies the identical (R5) and complete return.

Asymptotically (R7) is (y/log y)^(1/(1-gamma)), larger than every fixed (2+y)^A with A<1/(1-gamma). This is an enlargement of the unconditionally paid region, not a proof of the remaining signed coercivity or a transfer of PF from one mask to another. The latter is a separate arithmetic hypothesis. At gamma11 the critical power is about 7.99, but the formula, not a rounded cutoff, defines the result. No endpoint gamma=1/2 or uniformity as gamma tends to 1 is claimed.

Ancestry and usefulness: W35 already gives the Gaussian renewal/heat commutator; G118 has the full logarithmic source, and G79 records the one-sided energy drift. W62's combined paid prime-power sector, moving column, exact finite diagonal and explicit residual coercivity form give a useful source-specific reduction. The refinement (R6)-(R7) modestly strengthens that interface. It does not create a new general renewal method or remove the full arithmetic problem.

## 4. D2/S21: unordered insertions and a precise weighted escape

Let S_N be all squarefree q-units n<=N, and B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) if p does not divide n and pn<=N, zero otherwise. Distinct unramified insertions commute: if the product fits, either order fits, and if not, both products vanish. These unordered commuting operators are not the ordered CAR boundary from W59 or G145's sorted creation.

For p!=r, the mixed commutator C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^* acts only as

    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))*chi(r)e_(rm),
    m squarefree, (m,qpr)=1,
    N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r).                                    (R8)

The lower endpoint is strict: at equality the two compositions cancel. The upper endpoints are inclusive. This is a phased partial isometry with norm 1 when its domain is nonempty and 0 otherwise. With a_N=sum_(n in S_N)mu(n)chi(n)e_n,

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#domain(R8).                               (R9)

Every character phase cancels, including complex and imprimitive cases. For a profile f it is exactly -sum_m conjugate(f(rm))f(pm); arbitrary complex profiles cannot be replaced by a positive count.

For the k unramified primes in (N/2,N], the sum of all ordered C_pr on their span is -D_chi(J_k-I_k)D_chi^*. The actual source -D_chi 1 is an eigenvector with eigenvalue -(k-1), giving quadratic value -k(k-1) and norm k-1 for k>=2. Transporting a gauge together with the source preserves this value. This refutes the specific unweighted independence/orthogonality shortcut, not signed cancellation across every sector.

The strongest escape deserves an explicit formula. If external prime weights are allowed, define C(lambda)=sum_(p!=r)conjugate(lambda_p)lambda_r C_pr on that terminal span. Then

    <a_N,C(lambda)a_N>=sum_p|lambda_p|^2-|sum_p lambda_p|^2.    (R10)

For two primes, weights (1,1),(1,-1),(1,i) give -2,+2,0. Thus the unweighted commutator's coherence does not exclude all weighted compensation. This qualification does not contradict G164's different positive E=B^*B obstruction for arbitrary moving weights. The operators and the scalar being bounded differ.

The complete source remains a_N=product_(p<=N,p not|q)(I-B_p)e_1, with every prime inserted once and exact cutoff; M_chi(N)=<1,a_N>. No estimate for this full readout follows from (R8)-(R10). If the readout has a common all-scale N^(gamma+epsilon) bound for every fixed ordinary chi, Abel continuation gives the usual all-height reciprocal return. That hypothesis is still open.

Record value is the explicit unordered mixed-adjoint boundary, full character contraction and profile formula. G145's sorted operators, G160's phase obstruction, G162's terminal cut and [restricted research revision] G164-G166's ordered complex/harmonic results retain their own credit. In particular a critical basis need not be harmonic, the natural covariant incidence kernel is span(mu chi), and the character heat/supertrace bulk cannot be erased. None of those accepted statements licenses a lower bound for M or a blanket rejection of source-sensitive compensation.

## 5. D3/S16: the conditional-square certificate really is too costly

The finite coding example is correct: if a linear syndrome over F2 does not contain parity in its row span, uniform measures conditioned on even and odd parity have the same uniform syndrome law, with opposite parity biases. A kernel vector with odd parity pairs the two extensions in every syndrome fiber. This is a model obstruction to inferring a missing character from syndrome entropy; it is not a theorem about all arithmetic observations.

For the actual principal character modulo fixed q, partition S_N by the entire set of prime divisors <=sqrt(N). Its empty cell is exactly

    C0={1} union {p:sqrt(N)<p<=N, p not dividing q}.

Write L for the number of these primes and Q=#S_N. For any partition P set

    E(P)=sum_(C in P)|sum_(n in C)a(n)|^2/|C|.

Cauchy gives |M(N)|<=sqrt(Q E(P)); the cell C0 alone contributes

    (L-1)^2/(L+1)=L-3+4/(L+1).                                (R11)

Refinement cannot reduce E, by applying Cauchy inside each old cell. Every refinement of this complete small-prime observation has the same lower certificate price.

Square-divisor expansion gives Q=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N), with kappa_q=(6/pi^2)product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0. Also binomial(2m,m)>=4^m/(2m+1), and each prime contributes at most 2m to its prime factorization: its valuation is at most the number of powers <=2m. Hence binomial(2m,m)<=(2m)^(pi(2m)), proving pi(N)>>N/log N. Subtracting sqrt N and the fixed ramified set gives L>>_q N/log N. Consequently

    sqrt(Q E(P))>>_q N/sqrt(log N).                           (R12)

This is a lower bound for the numeric right side of an upper certificate, not for |M|. In particular E(P)<<N^(2gamma-1+epsilon) for every epsilon fails for this partition and its refinements whenever gamma<1. The current strict first-gain energy threshold is 2gamma11-1=.7497080728; the author's .74970 was the illustrative gamma=.87485.

Coarsening across small-prime patterns, retaining signed cross-cell terms, unrelated syndromes and nonprincipal phase cancellations are not excluded. One principal character already blocks a proposed theorem applying this same positive certificate to every character. G103/G117's full energy and fiber costs, G145/G162's coherent terminal structure and G165's positive critical floor are related ancestry, not identical assumptions. Newly accepted [restricted research revision] G167 concerns GLOBAL P>=ell ell^* with constrained integer-offset support. Here Q times the cell-constant orthogonal projection is indeed a global majorant, but its cell blocks need not have that support: the empty cell joins widely separated primes. Conversely G167 does not exclude arbitrary bounded row degree, general prime dilations or proved source-only inequalities. No broader positive-method impossibility is inferred by label alone.

## 6. Other actual author tests

S13 uses the RESTRICTED two-prime exterior complex with basis (1,2,3) at cutoff 5, d e_2=d e_3=e_1, and missing e_6. There is one degree-one class; adding e_6 at cutoff 6 kills it through d e_6=e_3-e_2. This is not the full all-prime cutoff-5 complex, which also contains 5. The author's wording preserves the two-prime scope. W27 and [restricted research revision]'s stronger cutoff results already cover the proposed unsigned-gap shortcut. It is a legitimate tested duplicate, not a new homology theorem or a dismissal of every signed construction.

S25 keeps H=w^*Tv, with T the transpose, not adjoint, of the scalar kernel matrix and the entire original source included. tr((T^*T)^2)<=B0^4 is sufficient for ||T||<=B0. It includes all four-cycles and diagonals. Fixed rank cannot upper-bound the largest singular value; diag(M,1,...) is a synthetic algebra example only. This is G80/G163 reuse with no native-H evaluation. No favorable submatrix, mark-independent toy, dropped height or substituted Mobius vector pays the actual target.

S07's average over ALL characters of fixed q is precisely the full same-residue signed covariance from G103. Each individual energy is at most phi(q) times the average, a permitted fixed-q factor. Its q=1 component remains the entire signed Mobius energy. A tensor or character-basis relabeling supplies no saving. W55/G135's character/AP/rank matching remains separately credited.

## 7. Protected critic audit S22: complete scattering return on native H

This audit was selected before outcomes for its potential to pay the entire far-gap operator and its complementary channels. Here is an exact realization and its inverse cost, without replacing H by the ordinary-character source.

### Literal source contract

Use the Eisenstein field's original primary, fixed-ray, six-unit and fixed bad-place conventions. Long prime ideals pi,pi' occupy the original windows, have distinct rational norms, and exclude both equal-norm orientations. Retain both ordered good squarefree rationally primitive short ideals g,g', including g=g', the actual bounded complex core h((g,g')), and the rational gcd screen on their norms. The native coefficient is

    a_H(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3.

Every term keeps the original phases/profiles/masks, both projectors 1_(P,Rg)=1 and 1_(P',Rg')=1, and both independent separating heights. Put v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'); each root occurs once, ||v||^2=Omega1 and ||w||^2=Omega2. With the entire signed short-source sum folded into the scalar matrix K, set T=K^transpose so that the literal finite packet is H=w^*Tv. No positive divisor child replaces the common core. No extra opposite-coprimality screen is inserted.

The raw target is B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), where

    B0=G K0 [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] P_orig.

K0 denotes the original K scale, and P_orig retains the original kernel coefficients and weighted profile seminorms. The physical outside N^(-1)G^(-2) is applied exactly once afterward. The original range/collision restrictions and every other physical branch remain obligations. The following finite identities are uniform in the entries, so apply at each pair of heights; an arithmetic bound must still have the required uniform constants.

### Cayley realization, reflected state and residual

For any r>0, even without r>=||T||, set A=[[0,T^*],[T,0]]. Its Cayley transform C_r=(A-irI)(A+irI)^(-1) is unitary because A is self-adjoint. Writing G0=T^*T, D=(G0+r^2I)^(-1), its input-reflection and input-to-output blocks are

    R=(G0-r^2I)D,  J=-2ir T D,
    R=R^*, R^2+J^*J=I, I-R=2r^2D.

The exact returned input is x=(I-R)^(-1)v. Direct substitution gives

    Tv=ir Jx,
    ||Tv||^2=r^2(||x||^2-||Rx||^2)
             =r^2(2Re<x,v>-||v||^2).                          (R13)

The inner product is conjugate-first. Thus global ||T||<=r is equivalent to R<=0. At the actual v, ||Tv||<=r||v|| is equivalent to Re<x,v><=||v||^2. The latter is a sufficient condition for the raw bilinear bound against every w of its allowed mass; it is stronger than controlling one particular scalar pairing. At r=B0>0 it returns the desired raw target exactly. The degenerate B0=0 requires the zero pairing directly.

This is a finite source-preserving identity, not an arithmetic estimate for x. On a singular mode of T with singular value sigma,

    R=(sigma^2-r^2)/(sigma^2+r^2),
    |J|=2r*sigma/(sigma^2+r^2),
    (I-R)^(-1)=(sigma^2+r^2)/(2r^2).

For sigma much larger than r, transmission is small while the inverse grows quadratically. Hence unitary scattering or small J alone cannot imply a small original T. The scalar T=[M] illustrates this algebra; it is not an evaluated arithmetic H counterexample. If only a known ||T||<=B is available, Cauchy and ||J||<=1 give

    |H|<=[r/2+B^2/(2r)] ||v|| ||w||,
    r/2+B^2/(2r)>=B.

Optimizing r merely recovers the known B bound. It creates no improvement.

For an approximate returned state xhat define d=v-(I-R)xhat. The COMPLETE scalar is

    H=ir w^*J xhat+w^*T d.                                    (R14)

No favorable truncated scattering term controls the original form without its residual channel. This explicit formula also governs a proposed iterative or blockwise implementation; the source-sensitive error must be paid in the actual native T.

[restricted research revision]'s Julia realization assumes a known contraction normalization r>=||T||. Cayley realization removes that prerequisite but replaces it by the explicit reflected-state inverse; G163's Schur/source complements remain the governing ancestry. These are classical operator constructions applied to the exact packet, not a claim of a new general scattering theory. The audit preserves S22 as a possible route only if one proves the arithmetic estimate in (R13), a full scalar variant of (R14), or another complete returned-source estimate. It supplies no H saving, no ordinary-character replacement and no c increase.

## 8. Uniform critic audit S10: one compact sensor, all heights, paid stability

S10 proposed complementary compact Mellin sensors. A single explicit box already gives a one-way nonvanishing bridge on any positive half-plane; stable reconstruction is a different question. For fixed h>0, extend M_chi(x)=0 for x<1 and define

    S_h(x)=int_0^h M_chi(x exp(-u))du
          =sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n) min(h,log(x/n)).                (R15)

At n=x the weight is zero; at n=x exp(-h) it is h. The unit, all natural zeros and complete moving cofactor region are included. Absolute integration for Re(s)>1 gives

    int_1^infinity S_h(x)x^(-s)dx/x
       =(1-exp(-h*s))/(s^2 L(s,chi)).                          (R16)

Fix 0<gamma<1. If for each fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0 the COMPLETE S_h(x) is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) at all sufficiently large x, the left side is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. Multiplying by L gives the nonzero factor (1-exp(-h*s))/s^2 there. Its nontrivial numerator zeros have Re(s)=0, and s=0 is outside this domain. Therefore no L-zero can occur anywhere in Re(s)>gamma. Principal poles are treated meromorphically as in Section 2; imprimitive factors and natural zeros were never removed. This is an all-finite-height argument, not a finite-height screen, and it uses no lower multiplier bound uniform in height. The complete arithmetic sensor bound remains open.

For stability, on a weighted log L2 line with fixed sigma>0 the convolution multiplier is

    K_h(s)=(1-exp(-h*s))/s,
    (1-exp(-h*sigma))/|sigma+it|<=|K_h(sigma+it)|
       <=(1+exp(-h*sigma))/|sigma+it|.                         (R17)

Consequently a bounded global inverse on unrestricted weighted L2 is impossible without a derivative cost. Precisely, with S(y)=S_h(e^y),

    S'(y)=M_chi(e^y)-M_chi(e^(y-h)) almost everywhere.

The causal inverse for this DIFFERENCE has weighted L2 norm at most (1-exp(-h*sigma))^(-1), by the geometric sum of backward translations. Its input is e^(-sigma*y)S'(y), not merely e^(-sigma*y)S(y); equivalently the weighted derivative is f'+sigma f. The derivative factor in (R17) has not disappeared. The unweighted pointwise telescoping ends when y-jh<0 and is exact away from the jump endpoints. All sums can instead be interpreted distributionally at endpoints.

More generally a finite bank of compact L1 kernels has multipliers tending to zero as |t| tends to infinity on each such line. To see this without any number-theoretic hypothesis, approximate each weighted kernel in L1 by finite interval step functions: each step's Fourier integral tends to zero, and the approximation error uniformly bounds the multiplier error. Thus a fixed finite weighted sum of squared multiplier magnitudes also tends to zero. Fourier packets concentrated near large heights show there is no positive global lower frame bound on unrestricted weighted L2. This says nothing against the one-way pole bridge, the actual arithmetic source, a bank with derivatives/atoms, or a scale-dependent bank with separately paid costs.

The main lesson is exact: complementary zeros are not necessary for this positive half-plane box sensor, but a cheap stable reconstruction has not been obtained. ## UR4. The averaged all-height zero-exclusion bridge is valid

For fixed tau>0 let

    H_delta(x)=sum_n h_chi,delta(n) g_tau(log(n/x)).

The d3 bound gives local uniform convergence. For x<=1, writing u=-log x>=0, `(log n+u)^2 >=(log n)^2+u^2` gives a uniform Gaussian left tail. Polynomial factors from differentiation are harmless. Thus integration over x near zero gives an entire Mellin contribution.

For `Re s>1`, absolute Fubini and the substitution v=log(n/x) give exactly

    integral_0^infinity H_delta(x)x^(-s) dx/x
                           =exp(tau*s^2/2)D_delta(s).

In particular the Gaussian multiplier is `exp(+tau*s^2/2)`, never zero. No determinant of physical Gaussian fields has been used.

Suppose D11 holds for one fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0 on all sufficiently large dyadic X, at a fixed `4/5<gamma<1`. For any fixed sigma0>gamma, choose epsilon<2(sigma0-gamma). Summing the weighted dyadic bounds gives

    integral_I integral_1^infinity
                   |H_delta(x)|^2 x^(-2sigma0) dx/x ddelta < infinity.

The finitely many initial shells are finite by local convergence. Tonelli supplies finite weighted L2 norm for almost every delta. Cauchy--Schwarz, with the remaining factor `x^(-(Re s-sigma0))`, gives absolute Mellin convergence and holomorphy for `Re s>sigma0`; logarithmic factors needed for all complex derivatives are integrable on compact sub-half-planes. Intersecting over one countable sequence sigma0 decreasing to gamma gives one full-measure set of fixed delta with a holomorphic transform on `Re s>gamma`.

Independently, the zeros of the nonzero meromorphic function L form a countable set. For each zero rho in `Re rho>gamma`, UR3 excludes only a null set of shifts. The union of these sets is null. Choose delta outside that union and the previous L2 exceptional set. This single delta, selected after the all-scale summation, is valid for every zero and every height.

Because `gamma+1/5>1`, all shifted entries occurring in C and E are holomorphic throughout `Re s>gamma`. D is meromorphic there through the identity `D=CF+E`. Its Mellin identity continues meromorphically from `Re s>1`; the left side is holomorphic and the exponential is nonvanishing. A zero of L of any multiplicity would give the uncancelled leading pole from UR3, a contradiction.

For principal characters, the pole of L at one is a zero, not a pole, of F. It creates no missing residue or obstruction. For imprimitive characters, the natural coefficients and the specified modulus have been retained throughout. Finite Euler-factor zeros at Re s=0 lie outside the asserted region in any case. A theorem for each ordinary chi at the same gamma proves a common constant without conductor-uniform implicit constants. If desired, the full-measure shift sets can be intersected over the countable family of ordinary characters; this is not needed for the individual conclusion.

Thus the bridge is valid at all heights, with an open boundary `Re s>gamma`. A finite-height sample, a bound on a subsequence of X, or a bound for only one selected delta would not be the stated hypothesis. None is being substituted here.

## 7. A stronger exact floor and the literal interpolating coefficients

The whole resonance lattice gives a useful sharper bound. Put a=1-sigma, h=log q, and

  I_q(u)=(q^u-1)/u for u!=0,   I_q(0)=log q.

Then every W in W_q obeys

 ||1-W||_sigma^2 >= J_(q,sigma),
 J_(q,sigma)=(1-q^(-2a))/(1-q^(-1))^2
       *[ I_q(-2sigma)-I_q(1-2sigma)^2/I_q(2a) ] >0.         (B10)

Proof. The isometry U F(y)=exp(-sigma*y)F(exp(-y)) sends H_sigma to L2(0,infinity). The evaluation vectors for the nonreal lattice are exp(-a*y)exp(2pi i k y/h), k!=0. Their closed span consists exactly of exp(-a*y)phi(y mod h), where phi has zero unweighted mean on [0,h]. This follows because the induced weight

  W(r)=exp(-2a*r)/(1-exp(-2a*h))

is bounded above and below by positive constants on that compact interval. The target U1=exp(-sigma*y) pairs with phi through

  H(r)=exp(-r)/(1-exp(-h)).

Its projected squared norm onto this annihilating subspace is

  integral H^2/W -(integral H/W)^2/(integral 1/W),            (B11)

all integrals over [0,h]. The orthogonal complement of the zero-mean phi space in L2(W dr) is span{1/W}; this proves B11. Evaluating the three elementary integrals gives B10. Strict Cauchy-Schwarz gives positivity because H(r) is not constant. Every q-wavelet is orthogonal to every vector in this closed span by B3. No unproved characterization of the full annihilator is needed: B10 is a lower bound, not an assertion of the exact distance to W_q.

For the first-gain example sigma=.874864, the displayed all-mode value is approximately .0098719719458. This decimal is illustrative; B10's formula and strict positivity are proved, and the deliberately coarser exact certificate remains

   ||1-W||^2 > 383229/137656250.                            (B12)

The current c4 floor is 1226323/440500000; the corresponding floors at 1/6 and 1/4 are 49/13215 and 49/8810. These positive constants are complete norm obstructions, not error exponents to be added to the separate Gaussian or H budgets.

There is also an exact arithmetic explanation for the tail escaping every fitted prefix. Define

  a_q(n)=sum_(j>=0:q^j divides n) q^j mu(n/q^j),
  b_q(n)=1-q 1_(q divides n).

Their finite Dirichlet convolution is a_q*b_q=delta_1. Consequently

  H_(q,N)(k)=sum_(n<=N)a_q(n) w_(q,n)(k)=1 for k<=N.         (B13)

These coefficients are uniquely forced if only w_(q,1),...,w_(q,N) are used to fit all first N cells, by the triangular diagonal w_(q,n)(n)=1. For q=2 and odd m,

  a_2(m)=mu(m),
  a_2(2^r m)=2^(r-1)mu(m), r>=1.                           (B14)

Thus original squarefree zeros in mu(m) are retained literally. Despite pointwise prefix convergence, B10 gives ||1-H_(q,N)||^2>=J_(q,sigma) for every N. Since its error is supported on reciprocal cells k>N, whose H_sigma measure is (N+1)^(-2sigma)/(2sigma), the conditional RMS of that complete future error is at least

  sqrt(2sigma J_(q,sigma)) (N+1)^sigma.                     (B15)

This is an actual-source tail growth statement. It does not presume a conjecture about Mertens sums. It shows why finite prefix agreement and an attractive first leakage shell cannot certify the proposed infinite signed scheme.

# [private research revision]: a sharper exceptional branch from the literal transforms



## Verdict and intended use

There is a concrete loss to remove in the existing exceptional-child calculation. Keeping all forced valuation residues, rather than only the common-multiplicity-one residue, gives

    F2_sharp >= b2.

Keeping the correctly oriented first-transform character also gives

    F1_sharp + S >= c                 (unamplified nominal case),
    S = c+d-2p-R-Bc-Bd >= 0.

With the original centered rectangle cancellation, these inequalities give a proposed extra M/24 reserve in the original first-Cauchy bookkeeping for every term containing an exceptional child. This is a written source-relative refinement, with a proof below and exact closure boundaries. It is not a stronger estimate for the entire moment: its nonexceptional terms and zero frequencies remain present.

This does not increase c6 through the unchanged assembly. Its low and high nonexceptional bins already have much smaller reserves than its exceptional branches. Their inequalities do not contain this exceptional count, so replacing the count leaves the current binding inequalities unchanged. No value exceeding c6 is claimed. The accepted c0 premise, source-relative c6 = 125139/1000000, and outstanding F0/applicability, positive-slot uniformity and root-definition obligations retain their prior status.

One phase discrepancy is material to this refinement: old D.10 has the orientation obtained directly by CRT; the printed PR9 B3.52 discussion uses an inverse common-character factor. Section 2 records the exact difference. This is a candidate finding for the controller, not a unilateral change to the pinned source or its accepted status.

## 1. Sources, ancestry and scope

The primary mathematical sources used here are:

* Hailey Collet, PR9 paper.md, pinned head 58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b: B1.12–B1.19, B3.50–B3.80. Local path and SHA-256 are in source-receipts.json.
* The preserved 10 October 2026 input, zeta_zero_free_4_33_self_contained.md, Appendix D, especially D.9–D.27. Its exact D.10 orientation supplies the consistent first-transform convention. The directory date is provenance, not a newly inferred authorship date.
* Gaozhongpai PR15, pinned ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef, PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex, explicitly dated 11 October 2026, paragraphs 3 and 7.
* The 12 October forward manuscript, sections 2.13–2.24, supplies the actual c6 costs and bottlenecks; its source-map.original.json was created 03:08:26 UTC. It is not an independent primary proof of the imported estimates.

The attempt index and [private research revision] expert-endpoint review, especially lines 181–191, already preserve the old F2 >= 2b2/3 and exact main F1 = base - 4a. [private research revision] noticed that the source proves a stronger multiplicity-one count than it spends. The present work develops the full residues and the first-common-support contribution. I did not find this refinement in those inspected records; this is no claim of literature novelty or a complete search of the repository.

The argument is narrow: finite CRT and correlation, exact normalizations, necessary exceptional-row congruences, and the existing masked lattice cancellation. It does not reopen the general analytic-base audit.

## 2. Literal first transform and the phase that matters

Use the source's centrally normalized product and its full equal-product rectangle difference. For full column products Ca and Db, C and D contain their complete common prime support; hence (a,b) = (ab,CD) = 1. All original twists and masks remain zero at their original nonunits. Any allocation meeting an old moving support is already zero and is discarded while still zero.

Write c,d,p for log_Z N(C), log_Z N(D), log_Z N(rad(CD)). At a common good prime P with multiplicities i,j, the actual row character is chi_P(k)^(i-j). Let r be the radical of those with i-j nonzero modulo 6 and let

    xi_r = product_(P|r) chi_P^(i-j),  R = log_Z N(r).

The complementary common row mask expands over e | rad(CD)/r. Put E = log_Z N(e). Thus R+E <= p. Substituting k=e k' leaves the frozen scalar

    mu(e) tau(C) conjugate(tau(D)) xi_r(e),

besides frozen norm powers/profile factors, and the separate factors chi_a(e) conjugate(chi_b(e)). A zero frozen scalar remains zero.

For G_chi(m,h) = N(m)^(-1/2) sum_(x mod m) chi(x) e(hx/m), CRT gives exactly

    G_(xi_r chi_a conjugate(chi_b))(rab,h)
      = xi_r(ab) chi_a(rb) conjugate(chi_b(ra))
        G_xi(r,h) G(a,h) conjugate(G(b,-h)).

The reason for xi_r(ab), rather than its inverse, is the inverse of ab in the additive CRT coordinate: G_xi(r,h/(ab)) = xi_r(ab) G_xi(r,h). This holds for every h, including its zero cases. Reciprocity changes chi_a(b) conjugate(chi_b(a)) into the fixed ray sign R(a,b). Thus the consistent individual twists are exactly those printed in old D.10:

    tau_C(a) = tau(a) chi_a(er) xi_r(a),
    tau_D(b) = tau(b) chi_b(er) conjugate(xi_r(b)).

The first expression is consequently

    H/[X N(e) sqrt(N(r))] sum_(h!=0) G_xi(r,h)
      sum_((a,b)=1) A_C(a) conjugate(A_D(b))/sqrt(N(a)N(b))
        tau_C(a) conjugate(tau_D(b)) R(a,b)
        G(a,h) conjugate(G(b,-h))
        K1(H N(h)/[N(e)N(r)N(a)N(b)]).

The scalar H/[X N(e) sqrt(N(r))] follows from Poisson's H/[N(e)N(r)N(a)N(b)], the three unnormalized Gauss roots, and the original X^(-1), X=Z^A. No normalization is suppressed in the exponents below.

PR9 lines 2314 and 2323 instead display conjugate(xi_r(a)) on the C side and claim the CRT contribution conjugate(xi_r(ab)), while still labeling the Gauss coefficient G_xi. Under its declared common-row-character convention this is not the identity above. Merely changing h to -h cannot invert a column-dependent xi_r(ab). If an inverse definition of xi was intended, the Gauss label and both column factors must be changed consistently. The supporting finite CRT calculation detects the difference. Existing bounds that use only the full moving support may be insensitive to this correction; the sharper residue argument is not. This report derives its orientation from the actual initial row character, not from that printed inverse phase.

Keep the signed coefficient

    D_b(l1,l2) =
      W1(N(b1 l1)/X1) W2(N(b2 l2)/X2)
      - W1(N(b1 l1)/Y1) W2(N(b2 l2)/Y2),
    X1 X2 = Y1 Y2,

with the same extracted b1,b2 in both rectangles, including an empty rectangle. Every live slot, the whole-product character tau_1(u), one whole-product norm power N(u)^(it), the original common mask and 1_(s|u) remain inside it.

Before positivity, extend the separated Gauss expression artificially off (a,b)=1, then insert the complete sum sum_(s|a,b) mu(s). It is only the complete sum that agrees with the original expression. Fourier separation uses the row norm and the two whole-product norms; it does not assign unrelated powers to the two plains. Only then use Cauchy and |G_xi| <= 1.

The resulting literal C-side norm is

    N_C = sum_(h!=0) omega_K(N(h)/Z^K)
      |Z^[-(A-c)/2] sum_(s|a)
        A_C(a) tau'_C(a) N(a)^(it) G(a,h)|^2.

Here tau'_C differs from tau_C only by the finite ray characters introduced in separating R(a,b); it has the same good-prime exponents. All original and extracted masks remain inside the coefficients. The D norm has the same form after the radial change h to -h, with its own whole-product power and the displayed tau_D. No good-prime conjugation is introduced by that change.

The source's sufficient C-side Gauss allowance and frequency scale are

    qtilde = q+R+E,  K0 = 2A-c-d+R+E-m,
    N_C <= Z^[A-c+qtilde+Bc-s0+epsilon],
    Bc = (3c-5d-R)_+/6,  s0 = log_Z N(s).

The outside exponent is m-A-R/2-E; common-support and first-projector labels cost p+s0. With the exchanged D allowance, their total is M-S/2, where M=m+q and S is defined above. PR9 B3.56 proves S>=0 primewise; it is retained, not silently discarded.

## 3. Literal second transform, projector and actual width

After an extracted amplifier alternative, put a0=A-c-w. Its unweighted Gauss allowance is

    Lambda_c = a0+qtilde+wo+w+Bc-s0,

where the extracted squared scalar is Z^(-wo). With row-ball length K+g and density Z^(-ell), additive orthogonality gives

    Z^(-ell-a0) sum_h Phi2(N(h)/Z^(K+g))
       |sum_u B(u) tau_1(u) N(u)^(it) G(u,h)|^2
    = Z^(K+g-ell-a0) sum_(u,v)
       B(u) conjugate(B(v)) tau_1(u) conjugate(tau_1(v))
       N(u)^(it) N(v)^(-it) / sqrt(N(u)N(v))
       sum_j F(u,v;j) K2(Z^(K+g)N(j)/[N(u)N(v)]).

Here F is the literal finite correlation in B1.14, with Fourier identity B1.15. In particular F(u,v;0)=1_(u=v) phi(u). The second zero is not part of the gain proposed here.

For nonzero j extract u=D2 a, v=E2 b, with complete common support and (a,b)=(ab,D2E2)=1. The exact identity is

    F(D2 a,E2 b;j) =
      F(D2,E2;j) R(a,E2) R(b,D2) R(a,b)

Thus the two residual whole characters are tau_1(n) chi_n(j), up to fixed ray factors (including the -1 on the second side). There is no inversion of j on one child. Whole conjugation, when used to identify a family, must conjugate the entire character and its heights.

Use c2,d2,b2=(c2+d2)/2,p2,g2 from B3.62–B3.63. Put Gc=(D2,E2). At equal common multiplicity i not divisible by 6, split j/Gc into unit and nonunit cases, of radical widths t2,V, and write j=Gc V_id h'. The source scalar

    1_part F(D2,E2;Gc V_id h') / Z^(g2-t2)

has modulus at most one and is zero off the original partition. Every extracted prime punctures every remaining factor. A cancelled exponent remains a hole.

The nominal and actual widths are exactly

    m' = 2a0-K-g-g2-V,
    q' = qtilde+wo+t2+V,
    M' = M+J-g-g2+t2,  J=d-c+(K0-K)-2w+wo,
    m'_act=m'+delta2, M'_act=M'+delta2, 0<=delta2<xi.

The pulled-back weight and partition scalar are extended by zero on the rest of the actual enclosing ball. A negative supported upper length means an empty range; it is not replaced by a fictitious row of norm one. The source choices give M'<=M-sigma and actual decrease at least sigma/2 after the reserved padding.

The exponent ledger is

    -a0 + (K+g-a0) - ell + (p2-s0)
      + (g2-t2) + (a0-b2).

The p2-s0 uses the genuine first-projector divisor s in both second common parts. Subtracting this ledger from Lambda_c leaves the original allowance

    M'+Delta,  Delta=b2-p2+w+Bc+ell >= w+ell.

Before separating residual columns, retain every factor and insert the full residual projector sum_(t|a,b) mu(t). Extra primes in an individual artificial t term are not added to the genuine common parts. Use the source priority allocation, both extraction scalars and divisor count; selected plain quotients do not gain an invented puncture. The subsequent exceptional count below is valid even if a partition restriction is bounded by one, so artificial projector terms cause no extra congruence assumption.

## 4. The full forced exceptional count

An exceptional child has primitive inducing character in the fixed dictionary, unramified at the source's good primes. Use the original fixed bad set at this stage, containing the fixed dictionary conductors as in its exceptional-row argument. No additional Euler deletion is performed here. At every good prime, the total sextic exponent must be zero modulo 6.

First common support, second common support and the original moving support are pairwise disjoint on every nonzero genuine allocation. This follows from the retained natural zeros, not from a squarefree approximation. Amplifier primes are chosen outside the frozen supports; an extracted amplifier prime becomes a new puncture, so it cannot subsequently become a genuine second common prime.

For the C-side first common prime of multiplicities i,j, write r_P=1_(6 does not divide i-j), and e_P=1_(P|e). The new fixed row exponent is

    alpha_C(P) = 1+i-j mod 6, if r_P=1;
                 1,          if e_P=1;
                 0,          otherwise.

It follows from tau_C and reciprocity; the ray sign introduces no good-prime conductor. Let rho_C(P) be the least nonnegative residue of -alpha_C(P), and set

    T1_C = sum_(first common P) rho_C(P) log_Z N(P).

For the D side interchange i,j. In particular (i,j)=(2,1) forces rho_C=4, a saving missed by a support-only estimate.

On second common primes put rho_2 equal to the least nonnegative residue of minus the valuation of Gc V_id:

* equal i not divisible by 6, unit: rho_2=(-i) mod 6;
* equal i not divisible by 6, nonunit: rho_2=(-i-1) mod 6;
* equal i divisible by 6: rho_2=0;
* unequal i>j, necessarily 6|j and unit: rho_2=0.

Write T2=sum rho_2(P) log_Z N(P). In the genuine unit case in the first bullet, h' is a unit and exceptionality is actually impossible. We do not need this stronger exclusion: allowing its forced valuation is still a valid upper bound after dropping a partition.

At first common primes the second row factor Gc V_id has valuation zero; at second common primes the old twist is unramified. Hence these two lists of necessary residues are independent and multiply in the sixth-power-free part h0 of h'. All remaining prescribed residues can only increase its norm. For each fixed ray/unit sector,

    (h') = h0 v^6,  N(h0) >= Z^(T1_C+T2),
    #exceptional h' <= Z^[(m'+delta2-T1_C-T2)/6+o(1)].

If the forced initial norm exceeds the actual ball, the range is empty. The proof is ordinary ideal counting for v, with finitely many fixed sectors. It adds no count of live slots, common radicals, projectors or amplifier primes. Those counts are already in the original ledger.

The source B3.73 spends only f/6 in this calculation, where f=2 times the nonunit multiplicity-one radical width. It explicitly mentions the stronger 2f/6 count. The present T2 contains that full 2f, all other second-support residues, and T1_C from the literal first phase.

## 5. Sharp local inequalities

Replace B3.75 by

    F1_sharp = F1 + T1_C/6,
    F2_sharp = 2b2-5g2/6-p2+t2+V/6+T2/6,
    F1 = c/6+5[d+(K0-K)]/6+w/3+qtilde/6+wo+Bc-5g/6+ell.

Then the exceptional volume excess is still exactly

    (m'-T1_C-T2)/6 + a0-b2 -(M'+Delta)
      = A-5M/6-F1_sharp-F2_sharp.

The actual ball adds delta2/6 and the original paired-volume/profile errors; it does not alter this nominal identity.

The primewise F2_sharp table, in units log_Z N(P), is:

| Case | F2_sharp | b2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| equal i, 6 does not divide i, unit | i+ceil(i/6) | i |
| equal i, 6 does not divide i, nonunit | i+floor(i/6) | i |
| equal i=6k | 7k-1 | 6k |
| unequal i>j=6k, unit | i+k-1 | (i+j)/2 |

Each first entry is at least the second. In the last row the difference is (i-j)/2+k-1 >= 1/2. Thus F2_sharp>=b2, sharply for nonunit i=1,...,5 and equal i=6.

For the first inequality begin with w=wo=ell=0, K=K0, g=(d-c)_+. Then

    F1_base = min(c,(c+5d)/6)+qtilde/6+Bc.

If c<=d, F1_base+T1_C/6+S>=c immediately. If c>=d, Bd=0 and the difference from c, multiplied by six, is

    c+11d-12p-5R+E+q+T1_C.

Its local non-q contribution is

    i+11j-12-5r_P+e_P+rho_C(P) >= 0.

For j>=2 it is at least i+5. For j=1, i=1 gives 6e_P; i congruent to 1 mod 6 gives i-1+6e_P; all other i give 6 ceil(i/6)-6. This proves, without a finite multiplicity cutoff,

    F1_base + T1_C/6 + S >= c.

The first dyad permits K0-K>=-delta1. The base expression is increasing with this difference with slope between 0 and 5/6, so at most 5delta1/6 is lost.

For the source zero-slot choice g=J_++sigma the additional loss is 5sigma/6. For the positive main, g=J_++2sigma, ell=sigma/3, w=wo=0, the loss is 4sigma/3. For errors, g=J_++sigma, ell=0 and 0<=wo<=w<=7sigma/3. Since -2w+wo<=0, the perturbation is at least w/3+wo-5sigma/6. Relative to c+w this loses at most 43sigma/18<3sigma. Uniformly over all original alternatives,

    F1_sharp + S >= c+w-3sigma-5delta1/6.

No amplitude or density credit has been counted twice.

## 6. Rectangle cancellation and the parent return

Use the original lower plain length L=M/4. The mask-uniform lattice expansion in B3.77–B3.78 has the same leading coefficient on both rectangles. The profiles may include their independent input heights; the newly separated norm power remains common to the whole product. Equality X1 X2=Y1 Y2 cancels the leading terms. Empty formal rectangles and the raw scales are retained until this cancellation.

With x=min(c2,d2), the source saving is

    r=(L-c-w-x)_+.

Under the full second projector its exact paired reduction is B3.79:

    t_- - r1-r2 -(r-r1)_+
      = (t_- - r2)-max(r,r1) <= omega2-r.

Thus paired volume is at most Z^(a0-b2-r+2theta_N+o(1)). This uses both extraction scalars and the full divisor dyad. Live slot labels enter here by their original absolute volume; there is no further prime count.

Since b2>=x,

    F1_sharp+F2_sharp+r+S
      >= c+w+x+(L-c-w-x)_+ -3sigma-5delta1/6

The C-side exceptional excess over its Gauss allowance is consequently

    E_C <= A-13M/12+S+3sigma
           +O(delta1+delta2+theta_N)+epsilon_share.       (1)

The unchanged weaker source bound also remains available:

    E_C <= A-M+3sigma+O(delta1+delta2+theta_N)+epsilon_share. (2)

Keep the outside first-transform saving S/2. In a Cauchy term with one exceptional bound and an opposite-side Gauss bound at its original allowance, (1) and (2) imply the parent exponent

    M-S/2 + (A-M+3sigma+small)/2
             + min(0,S-M/12)/2
      <= M-M/24 +(A-M+3sigma+small)/2.

If both sides select an exceptional bound, one may use the original opposite-side Gauss target, so the same conclusion applies. This is a bound on terms of the source's positive Cauchy/triangle bookkeeping, not an assertion that the original row norm has an orthogonal exceptional subspace. In the padded source core A<=M+delta, it gives M-M/24+O(sigma+delta+xi+theta_N)+epsilon. Uniform finite profile/height factors are exactly those of the existing transform and masked lattice lemmas.

The opposite-side target and all nonexceptional targets are explicit imports in this return. The calculation cannot replace them by itself. In particular it does not establish a better full moment, an increased affine slot capacity or a new zero-free endpoint.

## 7. Actual physical amplifier costs and the c6 obstruction

For the actual Gao main radius,

    K_main=K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega, ell=a,

alongside the old E_C<=A-M+4a+small. Whenever the other side is controlled at its original target, its parent Cauchy term has reserve at least

    M/24 + (M-A-4a)/2 - small.

Use the source's fixed amplifier pool and omit primes dividing h,s or any frozen support. The literal amplification identity is G(u,hP^6)=G(u,h) for P not dividing u, and an extracted column valuation i has

    G(P^i u,h)=R(P,u)^i chi_P(u)^(2i) G(P^i,h) G(u,h).

The original extracted error alternatives remain (w,wo)=(lambda,lambda),(6lambda,0),(7lambda,lambda), with squared scalars N(P)^(-1),(1-N(P)^(-1))^2,N(P)^(-1), and normalized prime averaging. The remaining whole twist includes chi_P(u)^(2i) and the fixed ray factor. At i=6 its exponent 12 is the retained puncture, not the constant one. The pool avoids the frozen first common support, and the extracted prime punctures all remaining factors, so these phases do not change T1_C or interfere with genuine second common primes.

Their actual unamplified radii have increment 3a+padding. The same argument gives F1_sharp+S>=c+w-9a-small (in fact the direct perturbation above gives a smaller loss using lambda<=a). Thus the existing 9a error cost may be retained, giving reserve M/24+(M-A-9a)/2-small where its source partner target is available.

At c6 the manuscript records normalized reserves:

    low:          7/30000000,
    high:         720486667/30493190000000,

    error fixed:  988504553/40210800000.

The first two are about 2.33e-7 and 2.36e-5; the latter two are about .08446 and .02457. The low identity comes from slot deletion against the old 9/2 moment; the high identity comes from the signed-row density and its amplifier slope. Neither uses F1/F2's exceptional saving. Increasing the exceptional reserve therefore leaves both active comparisons exactly as before. It also does not improve the first zero-frequency estimate or the genuine second diagonal.

A first attempted shortcut, spending only the stronger multiplicity-one count, gives merely F2>=3b2/4. It is exactly the point at which the printed first-transform phase matters.

## R3. Exact convolution identities, including the exclusions

Take the literal smooth V with V=1 on[0,1] and V=0 on[2,infinity), R=U^(4/3), and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).

For every ideal n other than the unit, sum_(d|n)mu(d)=0. Subtraction and the bijection m=n/d give

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n)mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)]
          =-sum_(m|n)mu(n/m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].             (R2)

This proof is valid at all valuations. The unit exception is essential: A_R(1)=1 for R>=1, while the displayed complementary sum is zero. In the completed tail n has norm>R, so that exception is absent. A summand in R2 is nonzero only if Nd>R; equality contributes zero. Under Nn<=C L the cofactor therefore satisfies Nm<C L/R, with C retained. No coprimality between d and m has been inserted.

For the actual complete multiplicative natural character phi_u=nu*psi_u in one whole orientation, phi_u(dm)=phi_u(d)phi_u(m) also at shared primes and nonunits. Thus multiplication by phi_u preserves R2 exactly. Every natural zero remains; it is not a coprime-only identity. Original slots can meet either factor.

If all proper divisors of n have norm at most R, their cutoff values are one, giving A_R(n)=mu(n)[V(Nn/R)-1]. This verifies S6 without assuming a least prime norm or an arithmetic density for such n. None of these formulas changes the existing inverse detector or its zero signal.

## 4. Literal arithmetic returns and the first-gain contract

For fixed ordinary chi, set a_n=mu(n)chi(n), with all Möbius/conductor zeros. A1 holds at b=2. Explicitly |F(u)|<=A_b*g_tau(u) for u<=-max(tau*b,0): in each term the factor exp(b*v)g_tau(v-u), v=log(n)>=0, is then decreasing in v. Thus the entire left Gaussian tail is integrable against e^(-su) for every complex s. On Re s>1 the complete Mellin identity is

    integral_R F(u)e^(-su)du = exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).  (A13)

A5 makes the left side holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Multiply by L and continue; its principal pole at1 is separately removable in the reciprocal. The exponential multiplier never vanishes. Thus A4 (or A12) at0<gamma<1 excludes L zeros in Re s>gamma, with the known principal pole excluded.

For each fixed finite-order, trivial-infinity Eisenstein Hecke character psi, use the literal ideal sum mu_K(a)psi(a)g_tau(log N(a)-u), with the presented-modulus zero extension. The absolute ideal count is O(X), so A1 holds at2; W39's fixed lattice proof supplies the needed meromorphic continuation on Re s>1/2 and its principal pole convention. For gamma>1/2, the identical transform proof gives the same result. Constants depend on the fixed member; no moving-conductor or angular uniformity is asserted.

For the literal multiplicative f3 field, f3(1)=1, f3(p^k)=-1 for p!=3,k>=1 and f3(3^k)=1. Retain its exact multiplier

    sum_n f3(n)n^(-s)=B(s)/zeta(s),
    B(s)=(1-2^(1-s)) H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^(-s))^(-2)(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
           *product_(p>=5)(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.      (A14)

H and1/H are holomorphic and bounded on every closed half-plane strictly to the right of1/2; the p>=5 factors start at degree2 and2/sqrt(5)<1. Thus B has no zero in1/2<Re s<1. A4/A12 for F3 at gamma>1/2 supplies the ordinary-zeta return, retaining the zeros of1-2^(1-s) on Re s=1 and using the established right edge. It also gives its full signed square moment immediately; no hereditary signed-submask comparison is used.

**OPEN-A(gamma):** prove the actual complete field satisfies A4, or the weaker local geometry A12, for every epsilon>0. A concrete single choice is

    |E_k| >= exp(-sqrt(k)/log(k+2)),
    ess sup_Ek |F| <<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)k)       (A15)

in every large integer interval. A15 for any gamma<.874865 gives a further gain. At gamma=.874864 it would give c=.125136; gamma=5/6 gives1/6 and gamma=3/4 gives1/4. These are conditional returns, not achieved constants. The coarse analytic estimates above clear all transfer costs. The coarse arithmetic bound, including the accepted buffered calibration |F|<<exp((gamma4+epsilon)u), does not establish A15 at any smaller gamma.

## HC1. Source bindings and bounded candidate comparison

The adjacent frequency-receipt.json binds the actual bytes of nine read sources, including all four required intake files. The mathematical dependencies are:

| Source | Actual dependency and limit |
|---|---|
| [restricted mathematical source] [restricted mathematical source] [restricted mathematical source] | Incumbent and route status; no candidate arithmetic estimate imported as proved. |
