The current-proof snapshot is a4a739c9563585771c68567b165331d25219b8720d8172f676f7763b60aa8d53 (25,155 bytes). All remaining byte bindings are in the receipt.

Three distinct mechanisms were screened:

1. **Fractional future-filter attenuation.** A candidate exponential readout with growth map s -> s-A(1-s)^alpha, A>0 and 0<alpha<1, would attenuate a baseline even at large heights. But at a hypothetical zero rho=sigma+i t, Re(1-rho)^alpha is asymptotic to |t|^alpha cos(pi alpha/2). Its proposed real growth therefore tends to minus infinity with |t|. A decay assertion for this moving output would no longer see every high zero at a desired fixed boundary. This rejects this particular growth map before assuming an implementable filter or new arithmetic estimate; it is not a theorem about every future filter.
2. **Imaginary dispersion of the actual determinant.** Replacing delta by z=delta+i theta makes the two Vandermondes generate integer log frequencies, suggesting an extra mean square could cheaply diagonalize a three-factor sum. This has a high prospective ceiling, is distinct from the separately assigned generic Fock lane, and permits an exact low-frequency calculation. It is selected below.
3. **Fixed-alpha fractional renewal bootstrap.** The normalized-source and return components are available, but their missing signed renewal stability is already explicit in W22/W35. No new coarse contraction was found here. Repackaging that hypothesis would not meet the assignment, so this branch was not developed.

The strongest objection to candidate 2 is that one twist frequency may leave an entire unweighted factor free. HC2--HC4 prove that this happens for the actual signed coefficients. HC5 supplies a paid remainder; HC6--HC8 test the complete finite estimate against c=1/6,1/4 and the formal half-strip target. No literature-priority claim is made.

## HC2. Actual complex-shift source, every sign and a uniform coarse bound

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi with its specified modulus and natural zero extension, including imprimitive and principal characters. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), F(s)=1/L(s,chi),
    g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2*tau)), g=g_1,
    M(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n)g(log(n/x)),
    z=delta+i theta, delta>0.

Initially Re s>1. Define

    D_z(s)=det[F(s+(i+j)z)]_(0<=i,j<=2),
    V_z(a,b,c)=(a^(-z)-b^(-z))(a^(-z)-c^(-z))(b^(-z)-c^(-z)).

Finite Cauchy--Binet and absolute convergence give

    D_z(s)=sum_(a<b<c) a(a)a(b)a(c)V_z(a,b,c)^2(abc)^(-s),       (HC2.1)
    H_(delta,theta)(x)=sum_(a<b<c) a(a)a(b)a(c)
                                V_z(a,b,c)^2 g(log(abc/x)).    (HC2.2)

The square is analytic, not a modulus square. On live tuples, a(a)a(b)a(c)=chi(abc)lambda(abc), including squareful outputs and common primes among factors. No coprimality restriction or output representation is deleted. The coalesced complex-shift weight can be complex; its positivity is not assumed.

Let alpha,beta independently range over the six permutations of (0,1,2), with their signs. Expanding the square gives all 36 signed monomials

    V_z(n_1,n_2,n_3)^2
      =sum_(alpha,beta) sgn(alpha)sgn(beta)
                    product_(j=1)^3 n_j^(-z(alpha_j+beta_j)).   (HC2.3)

The orientation sign of one Vandermonde disappears in the square. For a<b<c, each single permutation product has modulus at most a^(-2delta)b^(-delta), by rearrangement. Every monomial in HC2.3 is therefore at most a^(-4delta)b^(-2delta) in modulus.

There is a finite absolute K such that, for every y>0,

    sum_(n>=1) g(log(n/y)) <= K y.                             (HC2.4)

On log(n/y) in [j,j+1), the number of possible n is at most exp(j+1)y. Sum this times the Gaussian supremum on that interval; the resulting bilateral series converges. The argument includes y<1 without an extra constant.

Sum first over c in HC2.2 to obtain the joint absolute bound

    sum_(a<b<c; alpha,beta) |a(a)a(b)a(c)|
       product n_j^(-delta(alpha_j+beta_j))g(log(abc/x))
       <=36K zeta(1+4delta)zeta(1+2delta)x = C_delta x.          (HC2.5)

It holds for all x>0, uniformly in theta and chi, and justifies frequency grouping and every theta integral below. The corresponding positive counting measure with the same 36-term majorant is at most 36 zeta(1+4delta)zeta(1+2delta)t on abc<=t. These absolute bounds remain valid for subsets of tuple terms. No signed-subset norm bound is inferred from a full signed norm bound.

## HC3. Exact signed reciprocal atoms at prime-square frequency

For a term of HC2.3, its integer frequency label is

    r=product_(j=1)^3 n_j^(alpha_j+beta_j).

Absolute grouping gives

    H_(delta,theta)(x)=sum_(r>=1) r^(-delta)B_r(x)exp(-i theta log r).

B_r retains every permutation sign, character phase and Gaussian output weight. The five possible sorted exponent patterns are

    (0,2,4), (0,3,3), (1,1,4), (1,2,3), (2,2,2).                (HC3.1)

Let p be the least prime not dividing the specified modulus. It is also the least integer n>1 with a(n) nonzero. The smallest live integer frequency is p^2. It occurs only for the tuple (1,p,c), c>p, with exponent 4 on 1, 2 on p and 0 on c. The permutations are identical, hence their product sign is +1. All-positive patterns use two distinct nonunit live labels at least p and q>p, so give r>=pq>p^2. The (0,3,3) pattern gives r>=p^3. The (0,2,4) pattern attains p^2 only in the stated assignment.

Consequently the coefficient is the COMPLETE signed reciprocal field with precisely two labels removed:

    B_(p^2)(x)=a(p)[M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))],       (HC3.2)
    B_(p^2)(s)=a(p)p^(-s)[F(s)-1-a(p)p^(-s)].                  (HC3.3)

No prime number theorem, zero-free premise, random signs or common-divisor payment enters. The free c runs over every live integer, including squarefree composites divisible by p. This is not a positive semiprime subseries.

In fact HC3.2--HC3.3 hold for EVERY unramified prime p, not only the least. If r=p^2, every positive-exponent label must be a power of p. A live label is squarefree, so can only be 1 or p. Three distinct labels require one zero exponent. HC3.1 then forces exactly the same (4,2,0) assignment with free c distinct from 1,p. Now c can be smaller than p, but the M formula already includes it. In all cases the median of (1,p,c) is at most p.

Finitely many deleted theta-frequency channels therefore cannot remove all these reciprocal copies: select another unramified prime whose square was not deleted. This statement concerns specified frequency deletion, not a prohibition on genuinely new arithmetic cancellation.

## HC4. A positive bounded projector and complete median removal

Use the least unramified p for the simplest finite source. Define

    h=1/(4p^2), omega_p=2 log p,
    K_h(theta)=3h/(8*pi)[sin(h theta/4)/(h theta/4)]^4,           (HC4.1)

with its continuous value at zero. K_h is nonnegative, has mass 1, and its Fourier transform is supported on [-h,h]. For normalization, the sum of four uniforms on [-1,1] has density at zero

    [4^3-4*2^3]/(2^4*3!)=1/3.

Its characteristic function is sinc(t)^4, so the integral of sinc(t)^4 is 2*pi/3. Scaling t=h theta/4 gives HC4.1. Fourier support follows from the convolution support [-4,4]. This is also the elementary cubic B-spline Fourier calculation.

For any other integer r, |log(r/p^2)|>h: already log(1+1/p^2)>1/(p^2+1)>h, and the lower neighbor has larger logarithmic distance. Therefore

    P_p U(x)=integral_R K_h(theta)exp(i omega_p theta)U(theta,x)dtheta

is bounded by Cauchy--Schwarz and satisfies exactly

    P_p H(x)=p^(-2delta)B_(p^2)(x),                            (HC4.2)
    M(x)=a(p)^(-1)p^(2delta)P_p H(px)
                          +g(log(1/x))+a(p)g(log(p/x)).        (HC4.3)

The inverse is a fixed scalar, with |a(p)|=1. No cofactor exception, good-real-shift selection, atom repair, conductor-uniform lower bound or large-shift Neumann inverse is needed. The Dirichlet-side return follows from HC3.3 on Re s>1. No unrelated operator readout is substituted.

At every fixed x there is the exact weighted Pythagorean identity

    integral_R K_h|H|^2 dtheta
      =p^(-4delta)|B_(p^2)(x)|^2
       +integral_R K_h|H-p^(-2delta)B_(p^2)(x)exp(-i omega_p theta)|^2 dtheta.
                                                                    (HC4.4)

The cross term is zero by HC4.2. A proposed theta-energy bound must therefore control the complete signed square of HC3.2. It retains every ordered c,d pair with a(c)conjugate(a(d)). All those pairs are theta-diagonal because c,d have zero theta exponent. Frequency diagonalization is not output diagonalization.

At fixed x the Bohr mean also equals sum_r r^(-2delta)|B_r(x)|^2, by absolute convergence and averaging. This is not asserted as an estimate for a finite uniform theta window; its other frequency gaps can be small. The positive projector gives finite-window control without such an assertion.

Every contributing p^2-frequency tuple has median <=p. Thus

    P_p(H-H_(b<=p))=0.                                        (HC4.5)

For least unramified p, the only live tuples with b<=p have a=1,b=p,c>p. Put

    J_(delta,theta)(x)=a(p)sum_(c>p) a(c)
                      V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,c)^2g(log(pc/x)).  (HC4.6)

Then P_p J=P_p H. The ENTIRE b>p complement vanishes under the full-line readout, including its unbounded c range and common-divisor cases. This removes the moving median cutoff prerequisite for this recovery formula. It does not claim a hereditary norm bound for J from a full signed norm bound for H.

## HC5. Twenty-four monomials and both ordered mixed terms are paid

Exactly 12 ordered permutation pairs in HC2.3 have a zero exponent: choose its coordinate in 3 ways and the other two entries of each permutation in 2 ways each. The remaining 24 have every exponent >=1. Let H_free denote the 12 terms with an untwisted factor and H_pos the other 24, retaining their ORIGINAL signs. Then H=H_free+H_pos.

For the latter Dirichlet coefficients,

    |b_pos,z(n)|<=24 d_3(n)n^(-delta).                         (HC5.1)

The generous ordered-factor count includes squareful outputs and repeated representations. It is an upper bound, not a coefficient identity. It gives absolute convergence of D_pos on Re s>1-delta. Also, for x>=1 and every epsilon>0,

    |H_pos(x)|<<_(delta,epsilon) x^(1-delta+epsilon),           (HC5.2)

uniformly in theta and chi. Indeed, write each Gaussian summand as n^(-1-epsilon)x^(1-delta+epsilon) times exp((1-delta+epsilon)v)g(v), v=log(n/x). This last factor has finite supremum, and sum d_3(n)n^(-1-epsilon)=zeta(1+epsilon)^3.

Fix delta=3/5. For ANY nonnegative theta weight w_X of mass at most 1, use dx/x on [X,2X]. HC2.5 and HC5.2 imply

    ||H||_(w_X,x)<<X,   ||H_free||_(w_X,x)<<X,
    ||H_pos||_(w_X,x)<<_epsilon X^(2/5+epsilon),
    | ||H||^2-||H_free||^2 |<<_epsilon X^(7/5+epsilon).          (HC5.3)

The exact energy difference is 2 Re <H_free,H_pos>+||H_pos||^2. Both ordered mixed terms are retained. Their coarse exponent is 1+2/5=7/5 and the square exponent is 4/5. No Mertens premise is used. This applies to K_h and its truncated windows; it also applies with the SAME tuple/product masks on every monomial, since the absolute bounds survive restrictions.

The exponent 7/5 is below the quarter-strip energy target 3/2 and sixth-strip target 5/3. It is NOT below the half-strip energy target 1. Conditional norm transfer for the latter is possible: a retained norm O(X^(1/2+epsilon)) instead gives mixed exponent 9/10+epsilon.

D_pos is holomorphic on Re s>2/5 by HC5.1. All zero-detecting poles of D in the quarter-strip region therefore reside in D_free. Its exact free-factor formula is

    D_free(s,z)=sum_(m<n) a(m)a(n)(mn)^(-s-2z)(m^(-z)-n^(-z))^2
                              [F(s)-a(m)m^(-s)-a(n)n^(-s)].    (HC5.4)

Fix the zero-exponent label and square the two by two Vandermonde of the other labels. The free label ranges over every integer except m,n, yielding both displayed collision corrections. Each unordered triple has three possible free labels, each with four monomials, reproducing all 12 terms. HC5.4 is first justified on Re s>1; further analyticity is asserted only where established.

Deleting all 12 free-factor terms leaves a function already holomorphic in the target half-plane. It removes the determinant pole detector along with the difficult arithmetic. HC5 is a paid signed-source remainder, not payment for HC3.2.

## HC6. Finite source, sharp masks and every tail

Keep delta=3/5 and fixed p,h. For sufficiently large dyadic X put

    A_X=X exp(-2 sqrt(log X)),
    B_X=2X exp(2 sqrt(log X)),
    T_X=X^(1/5).

Define the finite source and coherent projector

    J_X(theta,x)=a(p)sum_(c>p; A_X<=pc<=B_X)
                      a(c)V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,c)^2g(log(pc/x)),
    P_X(x)=integral_(-T_X)^(T_X)
                   K_h(theta)exp(i omega_p theta)J_X(theta,x)dtheta. (HC6.1)

Both product boundaries are included, and c>p is exact. All ramified zeros and composite c remain. The theta endpoints are included, though immaterial to measure. Delta,p,h are fixed before X; only the caps and T_X grow. This is a new complex-shift family at delta=3/5, not an assertion that the old real interval [1/5,1/4] or its open D20 bound transfers automatically.

The complete product complement of J is O(X^(-1+o(1))), uniformly in theta and x in [X,2X]. Apply the positive O(t) counting bound from HC2 to this face. Below A_X the Gaussian is at most a constant times X^(-2), giving O(A_X X^(-2)). Above B_X, Stieltjes integration gives an endpoint term and a constant times

    x integral_(2 sqrt(log X))^infinity exp(v)(1+v)g(v)dv
                                                    = O(X^(-1+o(1))).

Complete the square in -v^2/2+v. This includes every c above the cap; no masked complement or overlapping sector was omitted.

Next,

    K_h(theta)<=96/(pi h^3 theta^4),
    integral_(|theta|>T) K_h(theta)dtheta<=64/(pi h^3 T^3).       (HC6.2)

The uniform O(x) bound for J pays the entire omitted theta range by O_(chi)(X T_X^(-3))=O_(chi)(X^(2/5)). The constant may depend on the specified character modulus through p; no conductor-uniform constant is claimed.

Combining the FULL-LINE identity P_p J=P_p H with these two tails gives uniformly on [X,2X]

    P_X(x)=p^(-2delta)a(p)
      [M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))]
           +O_(chi)(X^(2/5))+O_(chi)(X^(-1+o(1))).             (HC6.3)

The median complement is absent because its full-line projection is exactly zero. Its truncated-theta projection is NOT asserted to vanish. Starting instead from a truncated full H pays its possible leakage by the same O(X T_X^(-3)) tail, using HC2.5. Thus finite-window cancellation has not been falsely inferred from infinite-window cancellation.

The sufficient positive energy is

    Q_X=integral_(-T_X)^(T_X) K_h(theta)
                     integral_X^(2X)|J_X(theta,x)|^2 dx/x dtheta.   (HC6.4)

On expansion this keeps every ordered pair c,d satisfying the two exact masks, a(c)conjugate(a(d)), the factor |a(p)|^2=1, the Gaussian overlap and

    integral_(-T_X)^(T_X) K_h(theta)
       V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,c)^2
             conjugate(V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,d)^2)dtheta.

No c!=d pair is deleted, analytic squares are not replaced by positive weights, and no independent phase is attached to the free factors. Every internal permutation sign survives. The Gaussian overlap can remain as its exact integral or use

    g(log(pc/x))g(log(pd/x))
        =g_2(log(c/d))g_(1/2)(log(p sqrt(cd)/x)).

Q_X averages energies at the same theta. The energy of the COHERENT source P_X has two independent variables theta,eta and retains the entire factor

    K_h(theta)K_h(eta)exp(i omega_p(theta-eta))
       V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,c)^2
             conjugate(V_(delta+i eta)(1,p,d)^2).

All mixed theta,eta terms belong there. The inequality ||P_X||_L2(dx/x)^2<=Q_X follows from Cauchy--Schwarz and the truncated kernel mass <=1, not from dropping those terms.

## HC7. Weak sufficient estimate, all-height return and prospective ceilings

Among direct physical growth assumptions, an L1 bound for the actual coherent readout suffices and is weaker than the positive energy condition. Fix gamma>2/5. Suppose for the chosen ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_X^(2X)|P_X(x)|dx/x
                     <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).      (HC7.1)

The stronger finite estimate

    Q_X<<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)                     (HC7.2)

implies HC7.1 by Cauchy--Schwarz and adjustment of epsilon. Neither estimate is proved here. HC7.1 is not claimed logically necessary among every conceivable return criterion.

HC6.3 transfers HC7.1 to M on [X/p,2X/p], since gamma>2/5 and the two atom corrections decay faster than every power for large X. These shifted dyadic shells cover all sufficiently large x. For sigma>gamma choose epsilon<sigma-gamma and sum weighted L1 shell bounds. The Mellin integral from 1 to infinity is then absolutely convergent and holomorphic on Re s>gamma, locally uniformly with logarithmic derivatives. For x<=1,

    (log n-log x)^2 >= (log n)^2+(log x)^2

gives a Gaussian left tail, so the integral from 0 to 1 is entire. Initially on Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    integral_0^infinity M(x)x^(-s)dx/x
                          =exp(s^2/2)/L(s,chi).               (HC7.3)

The exponential never vanishes. Holomorphy of the left side on Re s>gamma excludes every zero of L there, of every multiplicity and at every height. The principal pole at one gives a zero of 1/L and no exception. Natural finite Euler factors of imprimitive characters were retained; no even-modulus atom repair is needed. There is no cofactor-exception set or height-uniform lower-bound assumption. No Mellin transform is taken of a source whose definition changes with X: HC6.3 first returns to one fixed M.

If HC7.1 or HC7.2 holds for EVERY ordinary chi at the same gamma, the common constant is c=1-gamma, with constants allowed to depend on chi. A zeta-only estimate gives only the zeta conclusion. A finite-height sample, finite list of X or subsequence estimate is insufficient. The region is open Re s>gamma; equality at the boundary is not excluded.

The SAME parameters delta=3/5 and T_X=X^(1/5) give these prospective targets:

| gamma | Prospective c | Energy power 2gamma | Complete projection error q | gamma-q | Target/error cross power gamma+q |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5/6 | 1/6 | 5/3 | 2/5 | 13/30 | 37/30 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | 3/2 | 2/5 | 7/20 | 23/20 |
| 1/2 | 1/2 | 1 | 2/5 | 1/10 | 9/10 |

The error square has power 4/5; product tails have power -1+o(1). Fixed scalar recovery leaves these powers unchanged. All listed target/error crosses and error squares lie strictly below their target energies; both ordered crosses have the same bound. Comparing energies with only the unconditional ||M||=O(X) instead costs cross power 7/5, useful for the first two rows but not the last. Under the target assumption, norm transfer gives the smaller table exponents.

The last row is only a formal half-strip target, not an RH proof. No row is an achieved c. Analytic prerequisites allow substantial headroom beyond c1 while the exact arithmetic obstruction remains.

## HC8. Decisive test: the finite face estimate is equivalent to the original signed field

The return map does not show the proposed moment is easier. Test the selected mechanism further. Write u=p^(-z), v=c^(-z). Multiplication gives exactly

    V_z(1,p,c)^2=(1-u)^2[
      u^2-2u(u+1)v+(u^2+4u+1)v^2-2(u+1)v^3+v^4].              (HC8.1)

The full face J thus has leading term

    a(p)u^2(1-u)^2
         [M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))],

plus four terms with free coefficients a(c)c^(-jz), j=1,2,3,4, and the displayed polynomial coefficients. These four terms are uniformly O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(1-delta+epsilon)) for x>=1, by the weighted Gaussian bound in HC5.2 and |c^(-jz)|<=c^(-delta). Every sign is retained in the identity; an absolute bound is sufficient for this remainder.

The leading scalar is bounded above and away from zero uniformly in theta:

    p^(-2delta)(1-p^(-delta))^2
       <=|u^2(1-u)^2|<=p^(-2delta)(1+p^(-delta))^2.             (HC8.2)

At delta=3/5 the remainder has power 2/5+epsilon. The product cap changes the field by O(X^(-1+o(1))). The truncated K_h mass tends to 1 and is >=1/2 for sufficiently large X by HC6.2. Thus for each fixed gamma>2/5, the following ALL-SCALE statements are equivalent, with character-dependent constants and every epsilon>0:

    Q_X<<X^(2gamma+epsilon) for every sufficiently large dyadic X;
    integral_(X/p)^(2X/p)|M(y)|^2dy/y<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)
                                  for every sufficiently large dyadic X. (HC8.3)

Forwards, apply HC8.1--HC8.2 in the joint positive-weight Hilbert norm, divide by the fixed lower bound and absorb the complete 2/5 error. Backwards, use the fixed upper bound and triangle inequality. Both directions preserve mixed terms by norm inequalities. HC7.1 likewise has the same all-scale exponent as the corresponding M L1 estimate, directly from HC6.3. Moving to a determinant has not manufactured arithmetic cancellation.

This is stronger than the earlier positive absolute semiprime obstruction: it is exact signed bounded recovery from the ACTUAL determinant and its finite physical source, valid for complex ordinary characters, with a reverse finite-face estimate. It also identifies more than the statement "D20 is open": an entire theta-frequency diagonal retains every original pair correlation; a fixed median suffices for its readout; finitely many prime-square deletions do not cure it. This is a statement about the location and strength of the required arithmetic input, not a lower bound on the true size of M or H.

The next bottleneck is cancellation in this free-factor signed channel, or a new source/readout retaining all-height zero information after eliminating it. Theta orthogonality, prime-power annihilation, finite-frequency deletion and the now-paid 24 shifted terms do not supply that estimate. Removing the entire free-factor sector loses the relevant determinant poles by HC5. A new coupling that actually pays the free factor would be substantive; it is absent from this bounded pass.

## HC9. Evidence, limits and handoff

check_frequency.py enumerates all 36 signed permutation pairs and actual squarefree triples of product <=160 using exact Gaussian-integer character values. Cases are zeta, an order-four character modulo 5, the nonprincipal character modulo 4, and principal characters modulo 6 and 30. It checks every output coefficient <=160 in the isolated channel, the least frequency p^2, the two forbidden labels, equality with the fixed-median atom, the zero atom in the full median complement, and the stronger prime-square identity for every unramified prime up to 13. Least unramified primes are respectively 2,2,3,5,7.

The helper also checks the five exponent patterns, 12/24 count, exact rational evaluations of HC8.1, the sinc-fourth normalizer and tail constant, and rational target/mixed exponents. Finite checks are regression evidence; HC2--HC8 supply infinite and all-character proofs. The polynomial evaluations do not replace elementary multiplication. No open moment, zero distribution or statistical cancellation is numerically inferred.

The current receipt reports PASS for five cases and all listed checks. It stores compact coefficient-table hashes plus source-byte bindings. Its initial moving-median table is explicitly superseded by the fixed-median p table; the parent recovery copy retains the historical checkpoint. Only the report, helper and receipt in this owned directory are active artifacts. No frozen source receipt was regenerated.

Limits: no new c, no proof of D20/B17/H, no conductor-uniform moment, no finite-height replacement for an all-height theorem, and no unsigned subfamily estimate presented as signed cancellation. HC5.3 and HC4.2--HC4.5 are proved. HC7.1--HC7.2 are open, and HC8 identifies their arithmetic strength. Independent review must precede promotion.

**STOP: the bounded discovery and mathematical output are complete.** Remaining handoff operations are full readback, byte counts and SHA256 hashes, then release of only the exact [private research revision]-high-ceiling claim. The original 21:20 UTC deadline remains binding; no extension or new lane is requested.

## 3. Development07: actual finite character realization, with its quantifier boundary

For squarefree n<=X coprime to a fixed q0, the prime monomials z(n)=product_(p|n)z_p are orthonormal on the product unit torus. Consequently

    P_X(z)=sum_(n<=X,(n,q0)=1)mu(n)z(n),
    ||P_X||_2^2=Q_q0(X).

Point evaluation on the entire squarefree coefficient space has norm sqrt(Q_q0(X)): Cauchy gives the bound, and the conjugate evaluation vector attains it. For these PARTICULAR coefficients, z_p=-1 gives mu(n)z(n)=mu(n)^2, so P_X=Q_q0(X). The evaluation loss is exactly sqrt(Q_q0(X))=X^(1/2+o(1)).

The CRT realization is correct. For each odd prime p<=X not dividing q0 choose a nonzero residue r_p of the prescribed Legendre sign and impose D==r_p mod p. At ramified primes and additional prime divisors of q0 impose D==1 mod p. Make D positive and D==1 mod4. If2 is prescribed, use D==1 or5 mod8 for its positive or negative sign. These conditions are compatible; when2 is ramified an odd D==1 mod8 is a harmless choice.

The facts needed are that the Jacobi symbol (n/D) is a character for any positive odd D, and reciprocity plus the supplementary2-law apply to composite D as well. I independently checked those statements in [NIST DLMF 27.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.9). They do not require D squarefree or prime.

Using them, chi_D(n)=1_((n,q0)=1)(n/D) is an ordinary character modulo q0D with the desired signs at every unramified p<=X. CRT makes D coprime to q0 and every prime<=X, so all its prime factors exceed X. On n<=X its zeros are exactly the q0 zeros; GLOBALLY the additional D zeros remain. D=1 in a possible trivial prescription is permitted. No prime-in-progression theorem or factorization of D is needed. Complete multiplicativity gives (mu chi_D)*chi_D=delta globally, not just on the prescribed prefix.

This validates the finite trace obstruction even among actual Dirichlet characters. The torus norm computed using q0 equals that using the actual modulus q0D at this cutoff, because their zero masks agree through X.

However, the constructed character depends on X. A bound with a single constant for all conductors is refuted; a bound C_(chi,epsilon)X^(1/2+eta+epsilon) valid after X0_(chi,epsilon) is not. Nothing bounds those character-dependent constants or onsets in this construction. It therefore supplies NO fixed-character asymptotic obstruction, no actual Mertens-energy lower exponent for a fixed chi, and no contradiction to c8.

The fixed-q repair is exact:

    (1/phi(q))sum_chi |M_chi(X)|^2
      =sum_(r mod q,(r,q)=1)|sum_(n<=X,n==r mod q)mu(n)|^2,
    |M_chi(X)|<=sqrt(phi(q)) ||M_.(X)||_(average L2).     (R6)

The trace constant is now allowed to depend on q, but its ambient norm contains complete signed same-residue correlations. It is not the independent-prime squarefree count. Integrating (R6) gives (R4)--(R5), still open.

The additional partial-inverse statement is also correctly scoped. Unit-triangular equations (b*chi)(n)=delta for n<=Y fix b(n) only through Y; higher coordinates are free under those LINEAR constraints. Full multiplicativity is an additional nonlinear constraint. The CRT example supplies actual multiplicative finite bad prefixes, but does not turn the free-coordinate statement into a fixed-character theorem.

Prior random-phase/trace and code warnings, G68's complete response, G71's DIFFERENT fixed-sequence asymptotic countermodel, and the early prime-toggle program remain credited. T3 is a useful actual-character finite refinement relative to that record. It must not replace G71's different quantifiers or be promoted to a new universal obstruction.

## G72. A complete quantitative short-window return

For any |a(n)|<=1, extended by zero to n<=0, define

    B_H(k)=sum_(j=0)^(H-1) a(k-j),
    w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4tau)),
    E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

Every endpoint and both tails are included. Put ell=log2 and

    K_tau=exp(ell^2/(3tau))
          [exp(tau/3+4ell/3)/sqrt(3pi tau)+1/(pi tau)].

For X>=1 and integer H>=1,

    sup_(X<=x<=2X)|F_a(x)|
       <=sqrt(K_tau (X/H+1) E_a(X,H))+2H g_tau(0).

Partition the positive integers in each of the H possible block offsets.
Replacing each Gaussian by its value at the right endpoint costs at most
H times its total variation, namely2H g_tau(0). Weighted Cauchy, the exact
Gaussian square completion and a unimodal lattice sum bound give the
displayed factor. Averaging the H offsets pays precisely the normalization
1/H; no extra H is hidden.

The exact signed lag expression is

    E_a=(1/H) sum_(|h|<H) sum_(n>=max(1,1-h))
       a(n) conjugate(a(n+h))
       sum_(j=max(0,h))^(min(H-1,H-1+h)) w_X(n+j).

The weight moves with n,j. It is not replaced by a triangular constant,
and no off-diagonal term is removed by positivity.

For H=floor(X^theta),0<theta<1, the OPEN hypothesis

    E_(mu chi)(X,H) <<_(epsilon,chi,tau) X^(e+epsilon)

for every epsilon, each fixed ordinary character, and all sufficiently
large dyadic X returns the complete fixed Gaussian exponent

    gamma=max(theta,(1-theta+e)/2).

The O(H) replacement error is included in gamma. Both Gaussian tails and
the nonvanishing Mellin factor exp(tau s^2/2) then return ordinary
Dirichlet zero exclusion on Re(s)>gamma. This is a fixed detector; growing
H changes an estimate of it. Principal s=1 is its usual reciprocal zero,
with the external explicit exclusion retained. No Hecke or root-definition
identification is inferred.

The first-gain conditions are theta<.874861 and e<.749722+theta.
At theta=.26, e=1.00898 would give c=.12551; its first-gain boundary is
1.009722. Further conditional examples are:

| 1/3 | 1 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 1/2 | 1 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

### A3. Sharp power at each path depth

For fixed positive integer k and fixed r>=1, let N_(k,r,q)(x) count the integers in A5 with omega(d)=k. Then

    C_(k,r,q) x^(k/(k+r))/(log x)^k
        <= N_(k,r,q)(x) <= x^(k/(k+r))                    (A6)

for all sufficiently large x, with a positive constant C. Thus its exact power exponent is k/(k+r).

Upper bound: every prime factor of d is <=P^+(d), so P^+(d)>=d^(1/k). The condition d P^+(d)^r<x implies d<x^(k/(k+r)); counting all integers in that interval gives the stated bound, without a sieve assumption.

Lower bound: set Y=x^(1/(k+r))/4 and choose k distinct unramified primes in (Y,2Y]. Their product satisfies d P^+(d)^r <=(2Y)^(k+r)<x. Unique factorization makes these products distinct. Ordinary PNT gives asymptotically Y/log Y primes in the interval; deleting the fixed prime divisors of q costs only finitely many. Choosing k of them proves A6. Only ordinary PNT is imported, not a new fixed zero-free strip. The primary source inspected is Johnston–Yang, arXiv2204.01980v2 (20 April 2022), Corollary1.3 on PDF page2, which supplies more than the asymptotic needed here: [source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980). Its explicit onset and sharper constants are not used.

Since N_(r,q)(x)<=x while A6 holds for every fixed k, it follows that

    lim_(x->infinity) log N_(r,q)(x)/log x =1.              (A7)

For any proposed gamma<1, choose k with k/(k+r)>gamma. Uniform O(1) local defect enclosures, even with exact A4, therefore do not imply an O(x^gamma) output error by this UNMERGED unsigned certificate. The statement allows every fixed r; it says nothing about a suitably growing r with its own exact-collar cost, or about structured correlated defects. ## 4. C: exact renewal and a stronger elementary check on absolute small gain

With a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), Dirichlet convolution gives

    a log=-a*(Lambda chi),
    R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n.

Every prime power and natural zero is retained. Finite Abel summation gives

    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x),
    M(x)=1-R(x)/log x-int_2^x R(t)dt/[t(log t)^2], x>=2.

The constant1 is forced by a(1)=1 and R(2-)=0. This can also be checked by Stieltjes integrating dM=-dR/log t; it is not a guessed integration constant. For gamma>0, R=O(x^gamma log x) implies M=O(x^gamma), and the first identity proves the converse. The statements carry every-epsilon losses. This is an equivalent complete target, not a weaker arithmetic hypothesis.

The positive kernel sum S_gamma(X)=sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)|chi(d)|d^-gamma has infinite limiting mass for 0<gamma<=1. Indeed sum Lambda(d)floor(X/d)=log(floor X!), so S_1(X)>=log X-O_q(1). Removing each ramified prime-power ray costs only a finite constant. This is a positive-operator norm obstruction, never a lower bound for the signed R.

One can strengthen the author's normalized claim without a prime-number theorem. Put Y=exp(sqrt(log X)). Since Lambda(d)<=log d,

    S_1(Y)<=sum_(d<=Y)log(d)/d
            <=(1/2)(log Y)^2+O(log Y)
            =(1/2)log X+O(sqrt(log X)).

Hence S_1(X)-S_1(Y)>=(1/2+o(1))log X. For each fixed 0<gamma<1,

    S_gamma(X)/log X
      >=(1/2+o(1))*exp((1-gamma)sqrt(log X)) -> infinity.

Thus even division of this finite positive renewal kernel by log X gives no fixed subunit norm below1. At gamma=1 its lower limiting ratio is at least1. This excludes the specified absolute small-gain estimate. It does not exclude signed cancellation, compatible-source norms, or a different probabilistic representation with its complete correction paid. The coarse identity |R(x)|<=sum log n<=x log x returns only exponent1.

S09's equation a*(chi log)=-(a log) was false in the initial seed. The correct left side is Lambda chi. At n=4, chi=1, it equals log2 while -(mu(4)log4)=0.       =O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(2gamma+epsilon)),

choose epsilon<2(sigma-gamma). Dyadic covering, finite initial shells
and the preceding all-y bound give its finite N_sigma norm, where
N_sigma(V)=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||V||_[X,2X]. Since sigma>beta, its causal
inverse converges geometrically, with cost

    w_j^(-1/2)/(1-lambda_j^(beta-sigma)).

The K-th telescoping remainder is lambda_j^((K+1)beta)
U(x/lambda_j^(K+1)), bounded by C_A x^A
lambda_j^(-(K+1)(A-beta)); it tends to zero. Thus (75.4) returns the

asserted. This corrects the shared review's unnecessarily strict beta<gamma.

theorem follows.

nonsummable banks, different critical lines, signed cross-channel forms,

Between adjacent reciprocal knots, spacing is at least H/(4d^2), while peak difference is at most2(H/d)^sigma; the slope is at most8H^(sigma-1)d^(2-sigma)<=1/2. The outer segments have slope<=1. Thus |b(n)|<=1, with finite support. Both endpoint half-coefficients of a are retained.

At the single physical endpoint H the divisor identity gives

    sum_(n<=H)(a*b)(n)=sum_d a(d) B(floor(H/d))
                        =sum_d |a(d)| t_d^sigma.

Since t_d>=H/(2d), the normalized output is at least2^(-sigma)sum_(d=2)^N d^(-sigma), which tends to infinity. The domain norms are bounded uniformly. No uniform convolution-algebra constant exists on this finite-sequence class. For H comparable to N^((2-sigma)/(1-sigma)), the constructed partial sum has order at least H^(1/(2-sigma)); the exponent calculation is sigma+(1-sigma)^2/(2-sigma)=1/(2-sigma).

The claim is valid as a sequence of finite examples. It is not a single fixed infinite arithmetic sequence violating an exponent, and not an actual Mobius counterexample. In particular, using a source-specific norm, additional correlations, or a more structured renewal operator remains logically possible. Integer rounding of the peaks loses at most the number of knots; it does not affect the divergence. The author's rational7/8 examples are supporting certificates, not the uniform proof. This is a sharper obstruction than simply saying that an absolute l1 norm loses signs, but it does not rule out every signed feedback scheme.

## 3. W43-15: exact Newton feedback and the missing detector

Write m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y), d_Y=delta-1*m_Y, M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)n^(-s), D_Y(s)=1-zeta(s)M_Y(s). For fixed integer k>=1,

    q_(Y,k)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^{*(k-1)}),
    delta-1*q_(Y,k)=d_Y^{*k}.                         (R43-N1)

This is the geometric identity in Dirichlet convolution. Because d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y, its kth power vanishes for n<(Y+1)^k, and convolution by mu gives q_(Y,k)(n)=mu(n) on that strict prefix. There is no free improved coefficient list there: truncating below the cap returns the ordinary longer Mobius prefix. The equality endpoint need not vanish.

For the Dirichlet series Q=M_Y sum_(j<k)D_Y^j, at every zeta zero rho in the critical strip, D_Y(rho)=1 and Q(rho)=kM_Y(rho). These values are finite; Q is a polynomial in zeta and M_Y locally at rho. If Q^tr is the prefix polynomial and T=Q-Q^tr, then

    1-zeta Q^tr=D_Y^k+zeta T.                        (R43-N2)

Both sides equal1 at rho. The apparent quotient(1-D_Y^k)/zeta has a removable singularity, not the required nonzero reciprocal pole. A small Gaussian norm of the defect alone does not have the old detector's zero return. This is an analytic issue independent of finite coefficient agreement or a formal squaring gain. T here means the exact continued difference; absolute convergence of its coefficient series in the critical strip is not asserted.

For Y-rough n>1, only divisor1 contributes to1*m_Y, so d_Y(n)=-1. Consequently d_Y^{*k}(n)=(-1)^k F_k(n), where F_k counts ordered factorizations into k factors>1. It vanishes for Omega(n)<k and equals k!/product_p v_p(n)! for Omega(n)=k. Prime powers and collisions are included. This gives a one-sign complete rough Gaussian subfield, not a one-sign full defect.

Put Y=floor(X^theta), k fixed. If0<theta<=1/k, take k distinct primes from(X^(1/k),2X^(1/k)]. They all exceed Y, including at equality. Their products lie in[X,2^kX]. For x in[X,2X] the fixed Gaussian has a positive minimum on the resulting compact logarithmic range. Prime counting gives at least a constant times X/(log X)^k such weighted products after ordered/unordered multiplicities are paid. Thus the rough field has magnitude at least that amount. This rules out a fixed power saving from its absolute majorant; it is not a lower bound for the full signed defect, whose complementary terms can cancel it. The complete rough field is well defined by the divisor bound and Gaussian decay.

If theta>1/k, the exact support starts beyond X^(k theta). Since |d_Y|<=d_2 and |d_Y^{*k}|<=d_(2k), divisor summation bounds the entire absolute Gaussian field by O_A(X^(-A)) for every fixed A. The logarithmic gap is(k theta-1)log X+O(1), so its Gaussian square decay beats the positive counting factor and fixed logarithmic powers. This small physical defect still has D_Y(rho)^k=1: moving Y with X and moving its support beyond the observed scale do not create a fixed reciprocal-pole detector.

The dichotomy includes theta=1/k in the obstruction branch and excludes growing k from both fixed-constant arguments. Growing-order signed analysis remains a distinct reopening, owing every k-dependent constant, exact truncation correction and zero return. For fixed ordinary chi, twisting commutes with convolution even at ramified primes because chi is completely multiplicative with its natural zero extension. The corresponding defect identity and prefix result hold for L(s,chi); rough absolute lower bounds can omit finitely many conductor primes, but no signed lower bound after complex twisting follows. No Eisenstein, moving-conductor or H transfer is implicit.

The independent finite check uses divisor sums through800, Y=3,7 and k=1,2,3. It verifies all coefficient identities, strict prefixes and rough signs; the uniform proofs above establish what finite checking cannot.

## 4. W43-06: source projection, complete Gram and calibration

Fix tau>0 and |a(n)|<=1. Write g_tau(u)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-u^2/(2tau)), F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), L=log X. For a prescribed A>0 take

    C=sqrt(2tau(A+2)),
    j_-=-ceil(C sqrt L), j_+=ceil(log2+C sqrt L)-1,
    m=ceil(2(A+2)L/log L).

Use every complete unit logarithmic bin I_j={n: j<=log(n/X)<j+1}, j_-<=j<=j_+, with the stated half-open endpoints. On each counting-measure sample set let P_j be orthogonal projection onto values of polynomials of degree<m in t=log(n/X)-j; if there are fewer points than m this means the whole value space. Set P_X to their direct sum. It acts on the actual coefficient list, not a continuum surrogate or random signs.

**Gaussian error.** Outside the retained interval, |log(n/x)| is at least C sqrt L for x in[X,2X]. Counting/summation bounds both tails by X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1))=X^(-A-1+o(1)). The lower tail uses at most X exp(-C sqrt L) integers and the upper tail includes the e^v counting density. Rounding adds only bounded logarithmic shifts and does not consume the fixed power buffer.

For any real center c and complex |z|=R,

    |g_tau(c+z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(R^2/(2tau)).

Indeed the negative square of the real part can be discarded and |Im z|<=R. Cauchy's coefficient bound and summation of the Taylor tail on0<=t<=1, with R=sqrt(tau m)>=2, give

    eps_m <= 2(2pi tau)^(-1/2) (e/(tau m))^(m/2).    (R43-P1)

There is no unpriced center-dependent exponential. The sampled Gaussian vector on each bin lies within sqrt(#I_j)eps_m of the polynomial space. Self-adjointness and ||a||_2<=sqrt(#N_X) therefore bound the complete pairing error by #N_X eps_m. Since #N_X<=2eX exp(C sqrt L), log eps_m=-(A+2)L+o(L), this is O(X^(-A)) for sufficiently large X. Finite-X diagnostics that miss the asymptotic target are not a contradiction and do not certify an explicit threshold.

Thus uniformly for x in[X,2X],

    F_a(x)=sum_(n in N_X)(P_Xa)(n)g_tau(log(n/x))
              +O_(A,tau)(X^(-A)),
    rank P_X=O_(A,tau)(L^(3/2)/log L).               (R43-P2)

The coefficient bound is on a, not on P_Xa pointwise. No such latter bound is needed. All discarded coefficients and both physical tails have been paid before using the projection.

Choose a real orthonormal basis q_alpha for the finite polynomial value space, c_alpha=sum_n a(n)q_alpha(n), V_alpha(x)=sum_n q_alpha(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), and K_(alpha,beta)=integral_X^(2X)V_alpha(x)V_beta(x)dx/x. Then exactly

    ||F_X^proj||_2^2=c* K c.                        (R43-P3)

Complex source coefficients are allowed; the real symmetric Gram and conjugation in c* retain every cross term. For fixed gamma>0, the full all-dyadic every-epsilon Gaussian exponent gamma is equivalent to the same exponent for(R43-P3), by the arbitrary-power error and the norm triangle inequality. Replacing K by its diagonal is not justified. A projection independently recomputed at each dyadic X is permitted for this approximation; it does not define one fixed Dirichlet series in X.

The readout operator has squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm at most(log2)/(2pi tau)#N_X=X^(1+o(1)). Hence

    E_X=||P_Xa||_2^2=sum_alpha |c_alpha|^2
          <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-1+epsilon)           (R43-P4)

is a sufficient input. It can be strictly stronger than the complete Gram condition because it discards favorable interference. E_X<=#N_X is the available generic bound and only returns gamma=1. At the present limiting gamma=.874864 the proposed energy exponent is .749728; a first gain needs a strict buffered reduction. At5/6 and3/4 these exponents are2/3 and1/2. They do not denote H's physical pressure deficit.

**Growing degree is paid.** For a polynomial of degree<m, equispaced Lagrange interpolation yields ||p'||_infinity<=D_m||p||_infinity with D_m=m(2e)^m. For d=m-1, the sum of reciprocal node-product denominators is d^d2^d/d!, and differentiating contributes at most d; d!>=(d/e)^d gives the displayed bound. The constant-polynomial case has derivative0. This proof applies to complex coefficients too.

A one-sided interval of length1/(2D_m) near a maximum has modulus at least half the maximum, proving sup|p|^2<=8D_m integral_0^1|p|^2. On a COMPLETE bin R<=n<eR, integration against floor(t)-t gives

    sum |p(log(n/R))|^2
     =R integral_0^1|p(t)|^2 e^t dt
         +O(sup|p|^2+Var(|p|^2)).                   (R43-P5)

The error is O(D_m^2) times the continuous squared norm. All bins have R>=X exp(-C sqrt L-1), whereas D_m^2=exp(O(m))=X^o(1). Therefore the discrete norm dominates half the R-weighted continuous norm uniformly for large X. A discrete unit basis vector satisfies sup|q|+Var(q)<=R^(-1/2)exp(O(m)). No uniform orthogonal-polynomial estimate was assumed without proof.

If A_a(t)=sum_(n<=t)a(n)=O(t^beta), beta>1/2 fixed, Abel summation with A_a(R-) and A_a(eR-) explicitly retained gives

    |sum_(R<=n<eR)a(n)q(log(n/R))|
        << R^(beta-1/2) exp(O(m)).

Summing squares over polylogarithmically many basis vectors yields E_X<<X^(2beta-1+o(1)). Both the lowest and highest R equal X^(1+o(1)), so this is uniform across the growing range. Arbitrarily short terminal bins would need another argument; the author's full-bin alignment avoids them. This establishes W43.6, not a better beta.

For actual f3, the inherited buffered Mobius bound implies the same summatory exponent for the filtered coefficient A from G2; G28 then gives f3=h*A with the paid weighted absolute h norm. It is important to preserve the prime2 filter rather than claim that the full f3 Euler product has a reciprocal absolutely convergent beyond1/2 without qualifications. The accepted G28/G29/G31 return applies to the full Gaussian field: its Mellin numerator contains1-2^(1-s), which has no zeros in gamma<Re(s)<1. Its zeros on Re(s)=1 must not be erased. The known right half-plane boundary and all-height fixed-field Mellin argument complete the relevant zero exclusion. For gamma>1/2 the conditional projected complete moment supplies this same return and no new one. W43 does not prove a Hecke-family or moving-conductor adapter.

The broad analytic-rank mechanism, optimized Taylor reasoning and need for complete contractions are inherited from W39-C01 and the Gaussian observation work. **19, completed functional-equation flux.** For a primitive character let f(s)=Lambda(s,chi) and g(s)=Lambda(1-s,bar chi). The functional equation says f=epsilon_chi g with constant epsilon_chi. ## 7. Uniform parked audit18: continuation of a state does not continue zero exclusion

The seed proposes a cross-ratio continuation chain for analytic value/derivative pairs. A simple exact example isolates the issue: f(z)=1-z, D0={|z|<3/4}, D1={|z-1/2|<3/4}. The disks overlap; f is entire, nonzero on D0 and bounded on both closed disks, yet its zero z=1 lies inside D1. The state(f,f') never vanishes because f'=-1, including state(0,-1) at the zero. Thus an invertible transfer of a nonzero two-component state does not ensure a nonzero first coordinate. For an analytic scalar equation, no determinant or state norm removes this distinction.

The logarithmic derivative f'/f=-1/(1-z) has the expected pole. Changing projective charts hides that pole in one coordinate but does not eliminate the zero divisor of f. A cross-ratio is invariant under an appropriate projective coordinate change; scalar zero location is a distinguished-coordinate condition, not the assertion that the projective state is defined. Mere overlapping charts, bounded Taylor transport and a nonzero start therefore cannot give the proposed unconditional propagation.

A correct local replacement is explicit: if P_j is holomorphic and zero-free on a disk and its boundary, and a rigorous source enclosure satisfies sup_boundary|F-P_j|<inf_boundary|P_j|, then Rouche gives zero count0 for F there. More generally it preserves the known count of P_j. The positive boundary margin is the missing arithmetic quantity; knowing only that F was nonzero on the previous overlap does not supply it. To cover a whole target strip, every disk, every unbounded height, all tails and every relevant character must have the enclosure and margin with the required scope. A finite mesh or a finite collection of checked disks cannot be represented as such an all-height proof.

For the actual ordinary source one may take F=(s-1)zeta(s), with its removable nonzero value at1 restored, or the correctly pole-cleared fixed L-function. If a locally finite disk cover of Re(s)>gamma has the stated enclosures and zero-free comparison polynomials, every point is covered and the actual source is zero-free there. This is a direct conditional return, not a new estimate or a transfer from a generic analytic counterexample. A pole-clearing factor must not introduce or conceal a zero in the region, and primitive/imprimitive factors remain literal. For the Gaussian reciprocal detector the alternative is its existing complete Mellin return; cross-ratios do not improve that input for free.

The finite example refutes only propagation based on overlap and nonzero state. It does not refute a paid Rouche cover, a source-specific lower modulus estimate, or a different coupled system with a proved scalar-output observability bound. This preserves the candidate's rare continuation mechanism while identifying its first unpaid hypothesis. It is related to the original Hardy/covering, W35 local reciprocal and W40 boundary-budget records, not a fresh reason to discard all analytic patching.

## 4. Quantitative return, headroom and the still-open estimate

Let0<theta<1 be fixed, H=floor(X^theta), and r be fixed. For all sufficiently large X, 2rH<=X. The last term of (2) is O_A(X^-A) for each fixed A>0, because its logarithm has the negative quadratic leading term

    -(1-theta)^2 (log X)^2/(2tau).

The complete residual in (10) is O_(tau,r)(X^(1-r(1-theta))). Suppose, for every epsilon>0 and all large dyadic X,

    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) <<_epsilon X^(e+epsilon).          (OPEN-W)

Then Theorem W48.1 gives the complete fixed-source exponent

    gamma_r=max((1-theta+e)/2, 1-r(1-theta)).               (11)

The exponent epsilon is harmless because the hypothesis supplies every epsilon. This is a sufficient implication, not an asserted converse or an equivalence of all high-frequency information. For any fixed target gamma>(1-theta+e)/2 one can choose a fixed r with1-r(1-theta)<gamma. Endpoint equality also gives the usual every-epsilon exponent.

For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), where chi is any fixed ordinary Dirichlet character, the zero extension and all ramified zeros remain exactly those in (1). No primitive-character replacement or growing-conductor bound is used. Initially on Re(s)>1,

    integral_0^infinity F_a(x)x^(-s)dx/x
                         =exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).        (12)

The x<=1 tail is Gaussian, by |a(n)|<=1 and log n>=0. A dyadic L2 bound at the exponent in (11), obtained from (2), makes the complete Mellin integral holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma_r. Multiplying (12) by L continues the identity. At any zero of L that is not its principal pole, the left product would vanish while exp(tau s^2/2) does not. This excludes every such zero in that half-plane, at every finite height and every multiplicity. The principal pole at1 is explicitly excepted; 1/L has a removable zero there. Constants may depend on fixed chi and tau; the exponent must be common to all fixed chi. Natural imprimitive Euler-factor zeros are never divided away.

The accepted RN theorem gives a concrete multiscale block hierarchy.

Bj=P_exp(tj)-P_exp(t_(j-1)) for j>=1. These are disjoint original-label
blocks; their sum is the exact final prefix. Their number is
1+floor(log2(tmax/t0)), asymptotic to loglogX/log2 when t0=(loglogX)^2.

research program and not a fraction of the full arithmetic difficulty.

For the prefix vector set a_j=C_theta*p_exp(tj)^2*X/L and h(x)=x/X.
Uniform RN gives P_j=a_j*h+e_j with ||e_j||2<=C*a_j*tj/L. Since

matrix of operator norm at most2 and retains the corresponding bound.

## 3. A double compensated completely multiplicative source

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including its actual zero values, and one prime p not dividing q. All parameters and this character are fixed before X, epsilon and any target zero. Let * denote Dirichlet convolution and let delta_m be the unit mass at m. Define

    a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n),
    s(n)=1_(n=r^2 for an integer r>=1) chi(r)^2,
    q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g.

Prime powers give a*h=s, and hence a*a*b=v*a*s=c. Complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de) is literal, including nonunits; lambda has no artificial squarefree zeros. We do not identify this a with the original Mobius coefficient.

In Re(z)>1 the absolute Euler identities are

    D_a(z)=L(2z,chi^2)/L(z,chi),
    D_c(z)=P_p(z) J_p(z) L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z),
    J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2 p^(1-2z).                         (3.1)

J_p has all zeros on Re(z)=1/2. L(2z,chi^2) is holomorphic and nonzero for Re(z)>1/2 by its absolutely convergent Euler product; its possible principal pole at z=1/2 is on the excluded boundary. Thus this replacement has its own zero-detection numerator. It has no new zero above1/2 except P_p's familiar line Re(z)=1.

The ordinary cofactor b is periodic of period Q=p^3 q and has mean zero. Indeed b=q2*b1 with b1(n)=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)); b1 has period pq and zero mean, and its p^2-dilate does too. Explicitly

    b(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    |b(n)| <= (p+1)^2.                                (3.2)

For the square-supported short source put w=q2*s. It is supported at r^2 and

    w(r^2)=beta(r):=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)).              (3.3)

beta is periodic of period Q0=pq, bounded by p, and has mean zero. If chi^2 is nonprincipal both period sums vanish. If chi^2 is principal, chi(p)^2=1 and the unrestricted and p-divisible root counts cancel. Finally v*s=q1*w, so only the two root rows with physical multipliers d and pd occur. Their coefficients 1 and -p chi(p) and their distinct masks are retained.

statement:
## A. The actual JN row-frequency translation defect

### A1. Source and finite arithmetic calculation

Freeze one original same-scale long-prime pair pi,pi' of distinct degree-one rational norms p,r. The actual field is Eisenstein, with the original primary, ray, unit, bad-place and angular conventions. Source: [restricted research revision] h-joint/report.md Section2, JN4-JN9 interface; its hash is in exact-receipt.json. The exact finite group is

    G=(O/(pi*pi')) x (O/pi) x (O/pi'), |G|=(pr)^2.

Its unitary Fourier normalization is1/(pr). The complete signed short sum, both mark projectors, all sharp supports, profiles and independent heights are folded into W before any norm. The kernel is

    K(h,s,s')=b0 chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3
                    chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4.                  (A1)

Here b0 retains b(pi)conj(b(pi')) and the exact fixed CRT phase. It is never set to1 in a native estimate. If b0=0 the following multiplier is zero; otherwise all singular values below are multiplied by|b0|. The factors vanish at their original nonunits. In the two degree-one fields, the cube of either primitive sextic character is the quadratic character. Thus the row factor is exactly

    m(h)=ell_p(h_p)ell_r(h_r), ell_p(0)=ell_r(0)=0,
    Q=pr, phi=(p-1)(r-1).

No ordinary Mobius coefficient is substituted into this H source.

Let S_t f(h)=f(h+t), with t nonzero modulo both primes, and M_m be diagonal multiplication by m on the complete row space. Then

    D_t=M_m S_t-S_t M_m
       =diag(m(h)-m(h+t)) S_t.                               (A2)

This is a specified row-FREQUENCY translation test, not an assertion about the displacement rank of the folded physical mark matrix.

For any odd prime p and a!=0,

    sum_x ell_p(x)ell_p(x+a)=-1.                              (A3)

Proof without an imported character-sum estimate: scaling reduces to a=1. Count z^2=y(y+1). The change to u=2y+1-2z, v=2y+1+2z is a bijection with uv=1, which has p-1 solutions. The same count is p+sum_y ell_p(y(y+1)). This proves(A3), including the zero sites.

CRT therefore gives sum_h m(h)m(h+t)=1. Both entries are nonzero at B=(p-2)(r-2) sites. Both are zero at exactly two sites; exactly one is zero at2(p+r-3) sites. The numbers with opposite and equal nonzero signs are(B-1)/2 and(B+1)/2. Consequently D_t has singular spectrum

    2, multiplicity n2=(Q-2p-2r+3)/2;
    1, multiplicity n1=2(p+r-3);
    0, on every remaining coordinate.                       (A4)

In particular

    rank D_t=(Q+2p+2r-9)/2,
    ||D_t||_HS^2=2(Q-p-r)=2(phi-1), ||D_t||=2.                (A5)

The admissible primes have p,r>=7, so the displayed norm2 occurs. For a shift nonzero only at p, the multiplicities are n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2 and n1=2(r-1), with correlation -(r-1); the symmetric case is analogous. These one-prime shifts also have a bulk defect.

On the full group G, the commutator of M_K with a row-only shift has(A4) replicated exactly phi times, since there are phi nonzero mark pairs and every nonzero mark factor has modulus1. All other mark coordinates contribute zero. Thus

    rank = phi(n1+n2),
    HS squared =2|b0|^2 phi(phi-1).                           (A6)

Fourier conjugation with the native1/Q normalization preserves these quantities; there is no extra1/Q factor to claim afterward. For p=7,r=13, the row rank is61 and row HS squared142. After factoring out|b0|, the full-carrier singular multiplicities are2448 at1 and1944 at2, with3889 zeros. This is an exact finite coefficient evaluation, not an evaluated full H packet.

### A2. Approximation, signed stencils and coordinate changes

If R has rank k<n2, then ||D_t-R||>=2: the kernel of R meets the n2-dimensional right singular subspace. More precisely, for k<=n2 its squared Hilbert-Schmidt approximation error is at least

    4(n2-k)+n1.                                              (A7)

One sees this by projecting onto the largest singular directions, or directly from the min-max dimension argument applied successively. For the full kernel, replace n2,n1 by phi*n2,phi*n1 and multiply errors by|b0| or|b0|^2. A rank o(Q) row boundary cannot approximate this defect with a power-small ambient error.

The same obstruction is not limited to one translate. Let J be any k distinct positive integers below min(p,r), let c_j be arbitrary complex coefficients, and P=sum_(j in J)c_j S_j. Different shifts occupy disjoint cyclic matrix diagonals. Their signs therefore do not cancel in the complete Hilbert-Schmidt norm:

    ||[M_m,P]||_HS^2=2(phi-1)sum_j|c_j|^2,
    ||[M_m,P]||<=2sum_j|c_j|<=2sqrt(k)(sum_j|c_j|^2)^1/2,
    rank[M_m,P]>=(phi-1)/(2k)                                (A8)

when some c_j!=0. The full mark carrier multiplies the HS square by|b0|^2 phi and the operator norm by|b0|; for b0!=0 its rank lower bound is multiplied by phi. The coefficients may move with the parameters. Thus a fixed nonzero stencil has no ambient Hilbert-Schmidt power saving relative to|b0|, even after signed combination. This is not a theorem about arbitrary growing stencils, source-restricted norms or approximate recurrences with a separately bounded residual.

A simultaneous unitary change of coordinates, including a chirp together with the transported shifts, preserves this test. Gauging only a coefficient while freezing the old source/observer changes the pairing and is not licensed. Conversely, unit multiplication h->u h gives m(uh)=m(u)m(h), hence an exactly zero appropriately twisted multiplicative defect. That zero-defect relation is satisfied by every scalar multiple of m and supplies no amplitude bound. Low displacement rank by itself is therefore neither necessary nor sufficient for the desired small H pairing; the useful question is the complete source/observer estimate for a particular recurrence.

### A3. What this pays, and what it does not

This calculation rejects the proposed boundary-only approximation for this additive row-frequency carrier in an unrestricted norm. It does NOT show that the native W is an extremizer, that its pairing is large, that a signed subset is monotone, or that every low-rank representation fails. In particular M_K is not identified with the physical mark matrix T. The actual W can have special arithmetic correlations, small physical support, projector structure and cancellations not seen by(A4). Those remain possible escape routes.

The complete native return remains the [restricted research revision]/G75/G89 contract. With rooted marks v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P') placed once, the physical convention is H=w*Tv, T=K_physical^T. For row parameter K0 and S=N+L+(NL)^(2/3), its raw target is

    Z^epsilon G0 K0 S sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig,
    Omega_i=sum_P |u_i(P)|^2/q_P.                            (A9)

The outside factor N^(-1)G0^(-2) is applied once, giving K0 S/(N G0) times the same masses/profiles. G0 here is the original short-core scale, not the finite group G. Every ordered short pair including equality, bounded complex core, rational gcd screen, both projectors, natural zeros, orientations, all component coefficients, independent heights, tails and other prime/composite/exceptional branches remain due. No actual estimate at(A9) has been proved in W64. In particular the carrier calculation earns no part of the current full-H deficit and no new c. Its record-relative increment is the exact native local singular spectrum and stencil price, beyond W28's untested displacement-rank suggestion; literature novelty is not asserted.

## Exact moving Bessel filter

Fix tau>0. Put f(u)=G_tau(e^u) with the exact G1 coefficients

    A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)*mu(n/2),
    f(u)=sum_(n>=1) A(n)g_tau(log n-u).

The accepted baseline implies f(u)<<_epsilon exp((b0+epsilon)u) for u>=0.
Each b>b0 is fixed before its constant; there is no b=b0 bound or buffer
shrinking with u. This uses the ordinary Mertens consequence in the
canonical PR9 interface and [private research revision]'s accepted ordinary baseline use
([restricted mathematical source] opening and section OS).
Partial summation gives the f bound with the exact even correction A(n).
The left tail is Gaussian. Its bilateral Laplace transform in Re s>b0 is

    Phi(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)*(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s).

Here the continuation below 1 uses the accepted baseline, not absolute
Dirichlet convergence. Let F(s)=integral_0^infinity f(t)exp(-st)dt. Then
Phi(s)=F(s)+E(s), where E(s)=integral_(-infinity)^0 f(t)exp(-st)dt is entire.
In particular F is meromorphic with exactly the same zeta poles in 0<Re s<1.

For a fixed strength h>0, the distribution

    k_h(v)=delta_0(v)-1_(v>0) exp(-v)*sqrt(h/v)*J_1(2sqrt(hv))

has multiplier integral k_h(v)exp(sv)dv=exp[-h/(1-s)] for Re s<1.
For p=1-s,

    sqrt(h/v)J_1(2sqrt(hv))
      =sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k h^(k+1)v^k/(k!(k+1)!),
    integral_0^infinity exp(-pv)sqrt(h/v)J_1(2sqrt(hv))dv
      =sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k h^(k+1)/((k+1)!p^(k+1))
      =1-exp(-h/p).                                       (B0)

Absolute termwise integrals sum to exp(h/Re p)-1, so the interchange is
valid throughout Re p>0. The multiplier has no zeros there; its essential
singularity at 1 is not discarded or called entire.

For A>0 and u>=0 define the actual moving detector

    D_A(u)=f(u)-integral_0^infinity exp(-v)*sqrt(Au/v)
                    *J_1(2sqrt(Auv))*f(u+v)dv.                 (B1)

At u=0 the integral is zero. There are no omitted masks or coefficient
subfamilies: B1 acts on the full fixed Gaussian field. The real-argument
bound |sqrt(Au/v)J_1(2sqrt(Auv))|<=Au gives

    |D_A(u)|<=C_b exp(bu)*(1+Au/(1-b)), b0<b<1.             (B1a)

This proves absolute convergence and the initial half-plane for H. The parameter
A log x is intrinsic to this new detector; G2 cannot simply be asserted for
it. The following separate return calculation is therefore essential.

Let H(w)=integral_0^infinity D_A(u)exp(-wu)du. Swapping the triangular region
0<=u<=t in B1 gives H(w)=integral_0^infinity f(t)K_w(t)dt, where

    K_w(t)=exp(-wt)-exp(-t)*integral_0^t exp((1-w)u)
                     *sqrt(Au/(t-u))*J_1(2sqrt(Au(t-u)))du.

Expand J_1 in K and write p=q+1. For Re q sufficiently large, the integral
part before multiplication by exp(-t) has transform

    sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k A^(k+1)/((p+w-1)^(k+2)*p^(k+1))
       =A/((p+w-1)*(p*(p+w-1)+A)).

Subtracting this from 1/(q+w) gives

    integral_0^infinity K_w(t)exp(-qt)dt
       =(q+1)/((q+1)(q+w)+A).                              (B2)

If s1,s2 solve

    s1+s2=1+w,  s1*s2=w+A,
    w=phi_A(sj),  phi_A(s)=s-A/(1-s),
    sj=(1+w +- sqrt((1-w)^2-4A))/2,

then partial fractions and uniqueness of the ordinary Laplace transform
give K_w(t) as the corresponding combination of exp(-s1*t),exp(-s2*t).
For real w sufficiently large both roots lie to the right of b, yielding

    H(w)=[(1-s1)F(s1)+(s2-1)F(s2)]/(s2-s1).                (B3)

The identity holds on an open neighborhood of that real w and continues
meromorphically. The expression is symmetric
under exchanging roots. When F is holomorphic at their collision, the
apparent branch singularity cancels; its limit is F(s)-(1-s)F'(s).
This removes the initially suspected automatic branch-floor obstruction
for the full signed field. It does not remove genuine singularities of F.

If a zero rho maps to w=phi_A(rho), the other preimage is

    rho*=1-A/(1-rho).                                      (B4)

For any previously possible zero with Re rho<=b0 and 0<Re rho<1, choosing
0<A<c0^2 implies Re rho*>b0: write delta=1-Re rho>=c0 and use
A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)<=A/delta<c0. Thus the second root lies in the
accepted zero-free half-plane. It cannot cancel the pole associated with
rho. Also phi_A'(rho)=1-A/(1-rho)^2 is nonzero there. This is one convenient
sufficient parameter condition, not a ceiling: finite-height information
allows larger A in the complete return below.

## Complete return theorem for the moving detector

Fix A>0, tau>0, and 1/2<a<b0. Suppose off-line zeta zeros have |Im rho|>T,
where T>=1-a is a fixed certified height. Define

    d(a,A,T)=A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2),
    gamma_crit(a,A,T)=a-d(a,A,T).                           (B5)

Assume d(a,A,T)<c0, gamma<=gamma_crit(a,A,T), and prove the actual norm

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |D_A(u)|^2 du
         <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon)                    (B6)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X. A,tau,a,T,gamma
are fixed before epsilon and X; constants may depend on those fixed
parameters. Then zeta has no zeros with Re s>a. This is a proved conditional
return, with B6 OPEN. Its conclusion gives c=1-a only when B6 is proved.

In fact the proof only needs the weaker first-moment hypothesis

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |D_A(u)|du
                    <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).         (B6-L1)

This is the weakest norm hypothesis used in this file; B6 is a convenient
stronger certificate that exposes the complete Gram. Neither is proved at
an improved exponent. No assertion of an optimal criterion among all
possible zero-detection methods is intended.

Proof of the analytic and zero accounting:

(i) Cauchy--Schwarz on logarithmic shells makes H(w) holomorphic for
Re w>gamma under B6, with every fixed w-derivative justified on compact
subsets by the same geometric summation. The finite initial u interval contributes an entire
function. No moving-X Mellin formula is being assumed.

(ii) F=Phi-E is meromorphic on the whole complex plane. Exchanging the two
algebraic roots leaves B3 unchanged, so it is single valued. At a collision
it is a symmetric divided difference, meromorphic in w, and holomorphic
when F is holomorphic at the collision. In the numerical cases below the
collisions occur at s=1+-sqrt(A), real positive points where zeta is
nonzero; the reciprocal is regular at 1 as well. Thus B3 defines a
meromorphic function R(w) throughout the plane. Image poles are locally
finite: the map is rational, zero preimages are discrete, and they cannot
accumulate at s=1. The identity theorem identifies H with R in the initial
right half-plane and then on Re w>gamma. R has no pole there. For a larger
A that puts a collision at a real trivial zero, symmetry still gives a
meromorphic expression; no example in this file needs that complication.
In particular, applying the symmetric expression to the entire left-tail
correction E gives an entire function of w; it contributes no hidden pole
or branch term.

(iii) Suppose a<Re rho<=b0. Put delta=1-Re rho, so c0<=delta<1-a. Its
paired root has

    Re rho*=1-A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)
             >=1-d(a,A,T)>b0.                             (B7)

Here T>=1-a makes delta/(delta^2+T^2) increasing on the required interval.
F is therefore holomorphic at rho*: no second pole can cancel the pole
at rho. Also rho is nonreal, so phi_A'(rho) cannot vanish. The coefficient
of F(rho) in B3 equals

    (1-rho)/(rho*-rho)=1/phi_A'(rho),

which is nonzero. A simple pole of F with residue R_rho produces a pole
of H at phi_A(rho) with the SAME residue. For a pole of order m, the leading
coefficient is multiplied by phi_A'(rho)^(m-1), also nonzero. Simplicity of
zeta zeros is not assumed.

(iv) On this delta interval and at height at least T,

    Re phi_A(rho)=1-delta-A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)
       > a-A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2) >= gamma.                 (B8)

The strict inequality follows from Re rho>a; for T>=delta the displayed
expression decreases strictly with delta. This contradicts (i)--(iii).
Zeros to the right of b0 were excluded by the accepted baseline, and
zeros of height at most T by the finite-height theorem. The Gaussian never
vanishes, and 1-2^(1-rho) is nonzero for 0<Re rho<1. Neither numerator
cancels a pole. No even correction, height range, reflected contribution,
or residual branch term has been dropped.

As an independent algebra check, for f(t)=exp(rho*t) on t>=0 one has

                  =1/(w-phi_A(rho)).                     (B9)

Thus there is neither an extra Jacobian nor an unpriced second exponential

There is also an explicit inverse identity, useful for auditing the

s*=1-A/(1-s), rearranging B3 gives

      =2sqrt(A)*exp(u)*K_1(2sqrt(A)*u)
      ~sqrt(pi)*A^(1/4)*u^(-1/2)*exp((1-2sqrt(A))*u).       (B11)

Absolute Fubini in the preceding double integral follows from the same
v^(-3/2) bound; no exchange of a merely formal asymptotic series occurs.
For fixed h instead of Au the corresponding leading expression is
sqrt(pi)*h^(1/4)*u^(-3/4)*exp(u-2sqrt(h*u)), only subpower suppression.

A fixed Gaussian does not invalidate the model, but one cannot simply
apply a fixed number of terms in its 1/u expansion when the filter order
grows. Here is the complete Gaussian density calculation. Set l=log 2,

    P_cont(u)=integral_l^infinity exp(y)/y*g_tau(y-u)dy.

Choose a fixed R>2sqrt(A). Splitting the representation 1/y=int_0^infinity

Let delta=1-b and fix 0<tau'<tau. The elementary inequality

    tau'*t^2/2+A*delta*u/(delta^2+t^2)
       >=sqrt(2*A*delta*tau'*u)-tau'*delta^2/2

leaves an integrable Gaussian exp(-(tau-tau')t^2/2). Hence the rigorous
easy full-field estimate is

    |D_A(u)| <<_(A,b,tau,tau')
              exp(bu-sqrt(2*A*(1-b)*tau'*u)).              (B20)

This is a real analytic saving, but not a fixed-power improvement. Every
b>b0 remains fixed; no bound at b0 or uniform limit b down to b0 is asserted.
It does not improve the full collection of buffered baseline bounds; its
use here is to locate the height cost in this proposed filter.
The first failed inequality required for a fixed exponent gamma<b is

    A*(1-b)/((1-b)^2+t^2) >= b-gamma for all t.             (B21)

Its left side tends to zero as |t| tends to infinity. Gaussian damping
does not repair it: optimizing against the Gaussian selects |t| of order
u^(1/4), producing the square-root-u correction in B20. Bounding a fixed
height interval is therefore not an all-height estimate. Cutting at height
of order sqrt(u) and paying a Gaussian tail also leaves B21 unpaid on the
remaining heights.

This is not merely an artifact of a loose absolute contour bound. Take an
arbitrarily large fixed real t and s=b0+it, and construct the test density

    f_s(u)=integral_0^infinity exp(s*y)g_tau(y-u)dy.

It has a Gaussian left tail and obeys the baseline bound exp(b0*u) on the
right. Completion of the square gives

    f_s(u)=exp(tau*s^2/2)*exp(s*u)+O_s(exp(-c_tau*u^2)),
    D_A f_s(u)=exp(tau*s^2/2)*exp(phi_A(s)*u)
                                      +O_s(poly(u)exp(-c_tau*u^2)).

For any gamma<b0, choose t with

    t^2 > A*c0/(b0-gamma)-c0^2.

Then Re phi_A(s)>gamma, defeating a gamma bound in this baseline-controlled,
Gaussian-smoothed class. Taking a real part provides a real example; at a
fixed sufficiently large t its L2 norm on each fixed-length u interval has
the same exponential order. The small constant exp(-tau*t^2/2) is nonzero
and cannot change the asymptotic exponent. This is a test density, NOT a
counterexample using actual Mobius coefficients. It proves that those
coefficients must enter an additional arithmetic estimate.

For the listed V values, B20 and B16 bound B17 at gamma=b0 in the usual
every-epsilon sense. They give none of the smaller
gamma values in the table. This is the exact weakest-paid-versus-easy gap.

## New versus subsumed, and the next mathematical action

The recorded contribution is the moving detector B1, its two-root return
B3--B10, the Gaussian density asymptotic B12a including the exact q_2
factor, the finite source B14--B18 with paid complements, and the sharp
baseline-only obstruction B21. These are proposed new project derivations
for independent review. They do not establish B17-L1 or increase c0.

Specific prior-work credit and limits:

* [private research revision] V1--V5 and [private research revision] RB13--RB15 already handle the fixed profile
  with multiplier 2(1-s)K_s(2), including its inverse height cost. W02-A's
  nonvanishing theorem is subsumed there. B1 uses J_1 at a moving argument
  and the quadratic composition phi_A; it is not a reproof of that fixed
  K-in-the-order theorem. W02-A's pure-power witness motivates the stress
  test, while B21 gives this new transform's exact failure inequality.
* [private research revision] DA28--36 / DR9--11 prove the actual fixed-r prime-cell obstruction
  and its own return with the q=.872754297... floor. This file does not
  alter their masks, replace their profile, or claim to refute them. It
  changes the detector, derives its own return, and openly pays its much
  longer arithmetic range. No old q-floor or payment transfers for free.
* W29's trace-class prime tensor has the wrong logarithmic readout; the
  Helson papers do not fix that. Those proposals are rejected duplicates
  here. The F07 all-row CM2 and F12 correlated-prime witnesses remain
  meaningful separate open programs, without a new saving from this pass.
* The N29 density-subtracted Cayley/Laguerre criteria and F22 potential
  criteria already have exact analytic returns. B1 is not claimed as a
  new philosophical equivalence between arithmetic growth and zero
  exclusion. Its candidate contribution is the explicit moving kernel,
  noncancellation check, and concrete finite arithmetic source.
* Current G1--G3 and the four-diagonal completion are credited without
  duplication. No attempt to estimate the other lane's exact Gaussian
  moment occurs here. If that lane proves G3 at an improved exponent,
  its original return is already stronger than passing through B5.

A bounded search of the maintained attempt index and the relevant recent
creative/cycle sources found no existing Joukowski/essential-singularity
moving-Bessel derivation. This is a limited project-record comparison,
not an exhaustive literature search or a priority claim. The Bessel
identities, divided differences, Laplace method and finite-height theorem
are credited external mathematics; their new arrangement is evidence
for review, not accepted theorem status by authorship.

The next mathematical action is narrow: take A=.004, V=.004, tau=1 and
the exact B14 kernel. Seek a bound for B17-L1 at any fixed exponent below
B10, initially with the buffered gamma=.874484. A useful next experiment
or lemma must exploit the actual A(n), keep the moving cap, and act on the
entire signed n sum before taking its absolute value. The first source
diagnostic should be a proved asymptotic or cancellation estimate for the
q_2 prime component AND its interacting signed complement under this
moving kernel. A PNT density main term alone fails, as B12 and B20 show.
For a second-moment approach, the exact object is B18, including its cross
terms; separate positive classes will not do.

Reopening conditions are explicit. Either supply a genuine arithmetic
improvement for B17-L1/B18, or find a new exact source decomposition in

## Verification and handoff ledger
