## 7. Actual relative conductors and complete natural holes

For n!=n', put `e_p=v_p(n)-v_p(n')`. Up to the whole orientation, nonzero values are ±1, ±2, ±3. Let qj contain primes with |e_p|=j, and

    Qj=Nqj, Q=Q1Q2Q3, V=Q1Q2^2Q3^3.                 (7.1)

All qj are pairwise coprime radicals. The full oriented local vector, not just (Q1,Q2,Q3), specifies the relative character. At every nonzero good prime its local conductor is that prime. The fixed ray data can only alter the fixed S factor. Thus n!=n' supplies a nonprincipal relative character; principal relative rows have already been included in (6.4). The two signs of 3 specify the same sextic local phase but different integer ratios, a divisor-many multiplicity retained in the coefficient count.

Write n=g a, n'=g b with (a,b)=1. For a fixed oriented integer valuation vector, `Na Nb=V`. Their common annular support implies

    Ng<<N0/sqrt(V).

Every such g contributes a coefficient product of size at most `H_J N0^(-1)U^epsilon`; ideal counting therefore gives

    sum_(n,n' with that vector)|c(n)c(n')|
       <<H_J U^epsilon V^(-1/2).                    (7.2)

If the upper bound for Ng is below 1 there are no pairs; fixed annulus constants give the same estimate when it is bounded. Allowing all g overcounts but never removes natural restrictions. Divisor-many choices of signs and local allocations have subpower cost. Summing vectors in dyadic conductor ranges yields

    sum |c(n)c(n')|<<H_J U^epsilon (Q1/Q3)^(1/2).    (7.3)

This is the finite-product counterpart of the accepted [restricted research revision] weighted-gcd calculation. It is not a new claim of cancellation.

The actual row kernel is

    K(n,n';U)=sum_(free u) Phi(Nu/U)
              xi_e(u) 1_((u,E_(n,n'))=1),            (7.4)

with its licensed fixed ray/unit restrictions. E includes ALL primes in nn' at which the phase has canceled, and every retained frozen hole not already supplied by the primitive conductor. In particular equal powers at a common prime leave a zero at that prime. Fixed nu phases stay in c. The norm of E is polynomial in U on this finite product source.

Literal B3.5, with the original deleted zeros, and the [restricted research revision] derivation R16--R18 give uniformly

    |K(n,n';U)|<<H_J U^epsilon min(U,U^(1/6)Q^(5/12)). (7.5)

For completeness, primitive nonprincipal Poisson at scale X has prefactor X/sqrt(Q), normalized Gauss amplitude 1, dual argument X Nh/Q, and zero dual term zero. Decay and lattice counting bound it by sqrt(Q); ordinary counting bounds it by X. Expanding the sixth-free row indicator as `sum_(b^6|u)mu(b)` and the complete hole as `sum_(d|rad E)mu(d)` leaves scale U/[(Nb)^6 Nd]. Splitting the b sum at `[U/(Nd sqrt(Q))]^(1/6)` gives

    U^(1/6) Q^(5/12) prod_(p|E)(1+(Np)^(-1/6))
      <<U^(1/6+epsilon) Q^(5/12).

A split below 1 uses the whole convergent sixth-power tail and the same bound. Nonempty bounded/subunit windows have the fixed support interpretation of B0.8. Polynomial E pays the displayed product by a subpower. This is the existing full-mask argument, not a second clean-coprime-only transform. Every shared-prime zero remains present.

The fixed finite inducing free exclusions cost O_fixed(1) in each kernel and can be deleted since the right side of (7.5) is at least a constant. Alternatively retain them in the ambient norm, for which (5.2) and the same relative expansion hold. No unrestricted moving high-bin exclusion or varying physical projector is licensed. For a requested fixed finite list of raw core restorations, the inherited G147 absolute row payment remains available; arbitrary raw/positive-child transfer is NOT established by (7.5).

## R5. Independent reconstruction of the clean first Poisson formula

Let l,l' be coprime good squarefree nonunit ideals, with no slots or extra row selector in this statement. Define xi(k)=chi_l(k)*conjugate(chi_l'(k)) with its zeros and take compact radial Phi. The finite transform modulo ll' has CRT factor

    chi_l(l')*conjugate(chi_l'(l))=R(l,l'),

by the source's sign-valued reciprocity. Its other factors are the unnormalized Gauss sums of chi_l and conjugate(chi_l'). The latter equals the conjugate of the chi_l' Gauss sum at -h. This explains the sign -h without an absolute-value substitution. With source-normalized Gcal, ordinary row Poisson gives

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') * R(l,l')
      *sum_h Gcal(l,h)conjugate(Gcal(l',-h))
                  F Phi(U Nh/(Nl Nl')).                 (R5)

This is also exactly the clean C=D=1 specialization of B3.52 before column central factors are added. Its U/sqrt(Nl Nl') prefactor includes the two unnormalized Gauss factors; U/(Nl Nl') would be wrong. The source Fourier pairing and lattice measure are retained.

Insert the exact sixth-free row projector sum_(b^6|(u))mu(b), where ideal b uses its primary generator and the residual element retains all six units. Writing u=b^6k gives chi_l(b^6)conjugate(chi_l'(b^6))=1_((b,ll')=1), including the natural zeros. Hence R5 becomes

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') *sum_b mu(b)/(Nb)^6 *1_((b,ll')=1)
      *R(l,l')*sum_h Gcal(l,h)conjugate(Gcal(l',-h))
             F Phi(U Nh/((Nb)^6 Nl Nl')).                (R6)

Keep the original finite range Nb<=(C_Phi U)^(1/6). There is no multiplicity six for b; the units belong to k. Adding k=0 in Poisson is harmless here because the nonprincipal natural character is zero there. For squarefree l, Gcal(l,h)=gamma_1(l)conjugate(chi_l(h)), including zero at conductor nonunits; the frequency h=0 therefore vanishes. This verifies S10.

Fixed row ray restrictions require their finite character expansion, including the value at b^6. A fixed hole mask requires the full sum over d|rad(E), the factor mu(d)xi(d)/Nd and scale U/((Nb)^6 Nd). A density family omitting fixed-inducing free rows subtracts its actual finite row kernel. None is implicit in R6, and none licenses a zero-bin/amplitude selector as a Poisson weight. General shared support, slots, unequal roots and arbitrary valuations require the full source reconstruction, which R6 alone does not supply.

At l,l' of norm about L, the first dual scale is L^2/U. At L=U^(4/3) it is U^(5/3), larger than L. This is an exact scale obstruction to claiming a short frequency merely from high conductor. It does not preclude a more substantial signed transform.

## 2. Exact source and the complete critical two-prime estimate

Write

    g(u)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)),  tau>0 fixed,
    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X) g(log(m/x))g(log(n/x)) dx/x.

Throughout, ||W||^2 means integral_X^(2X)|W(x)|^2 dx/x; every
displayed shell norm uses this same logarithmic Gaussian normalization.

All powers of a prime other than 3 have local sign -1; all powers of 3
have sign +1. Fix kappa with kappa^2>=2 exp(3 tau), put z=kappa sqrt(X),
L=log X, and freeze this original threshold on the whole closed shell.
Let A_R(n)=1_(omega_z(n)>=2), A_T=1-A_R and let R,T,F be the Gaussian
fields with coefficients f A_R,f A_T,f. Thus F=T+R exactly. There is no
moving-tau or moving-kappa uniformity claim.

For bounded real coefficient sequences u,v define

    C_1(u,v)=sum_((m,n)=1) u(m)v(n)K_X(m,n).

The coprime mask is not positive semidefinite. Every use of positivity below
is an explicitly positive majorant, not a masked Cauchy--Schwarz step.
The only coprime diagonal is m=n=1. The rough coefficient vanishes there,
so RR,TR,RT and FR have no coprime diagonal.

Set

    V(x)=sum_(z<p<q) g(log(pq/x)),
    U(x)=sum_(r>=2) sum_(z<p<q) g(log(rpq/x)),
    J(v)=integral_v^infinity exp(u)(u-v)g(u)du.

I independently obtain the bounded-core-coefficient version of A6:

    S_c(x):=sum_(r>=1)c(r)sum_(z<p<q)g(log(rpq/x))
       = (2x/L^2) sum_(r>=1)c(r)/r J(log(rz^2/x)) + O(X/L^3),       (R1)

uniformly in x in [X,2X] and all |c(r)|<=1. Such coefficients may be
chosen anew with X and need not be multiplicative. This is a linear PNT
approximation with an absolute error, not a theorem giving cancellation
for an arbitrary arithmetic mask.

Here are the complete tail and density payments used to obtain R1.

First, the all-scale lattice estimate is

    sum_(n>=1) g(log(n/y)) <= C_tau y,                       all y>0. (R2)

For y>=1, compare on multiplicative intervals or use the integrable
Gaussian majorant and its variation. For 0<y<1, g(log(n/y))<=C(y/n)^2,
so the sum is O(y^2), which is O(y). More generally, splitting the
Gaussian into two factors gives, for fixed epsilon>=0,

    sum_(|log(n/y)|>=W) n^epsilon g(log(n/y))
       <= C_(tau,epsilon) y^(1+epsilon) exp(-W^2/(4 tau)). (R3)

The remaining Gaussian has variance 2 tau, and its weighted all-scale
lattice bound follows in the same way. This includes y<1; no small-scale
exception is hidden in a later divisor sum.

In the completed two-prime sum, multiplicity at a product n is at most
d_3(n). The parts r>X^.01 or max(p,q)>X^.52 force
log(rpq/x)>=.01 L-O(1). Applying R3 with d_3(n)<<_epsilon n^epsilon
therefore gives O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A. This pays all prime powers,
all core valuations and all overcounted representations in these tails.

On r<=X^.01 and z<p,q<=X^.52, replace p<q by half the ordered pair,
subtracting the actual p=q completion diagonal. Its full positive cost is

    sum_(p>z)sum_(r>=1)g(log(rp^2/x))
       <= C x sum_(p>z)p^-2 <= C sqrt(X).                       (R4)

This is a diagonal of the two-prime representation, not the true m=n
diagonal of an energy scalar.

Use fixed-order PNT pi(t)-li(t)=O_N(t/log^N t), with N=10 fixed before
X varies. If q,r are fixed, the two Stieltjes endpoint terms at z and
X^.52, and the derivative term, each have bound Cx/(rq L^N):

    sup_p p g(log(rpq/x)) <= C x/(rq),
    integral p |d[g(log(rpq/x))]| <=
                       (x/(rq)) integral exp(u)|g'(u)|du.

The lower endpoint is correctly excluded even if z itself is prime.
Summing the first error over r,q costs at most two harmonic factors.
Apply the second Stieltjes replacement inside the positive first-prime
integral, with both of its endpoints retained. Its derivative estimate
has the same form, and the sum/integral of reciprocals again costs at
most O(L^2). Total PNT error is O(X/L^8). There is no unaccounted
product of two PNT errors.

The extension of the continuous rectangle to all r,p,q is absolute.
For a=z^2/x in the compact interval [kappa^2/2,kappa^2], its unweighted
positive integral can be written

    x integral_(log a)^infinity exp(u)g(u) W_a(u)du,
    W_a(u)=sum_(r<=exp(u)/a) (u-log(ar))/r
           <<_(kappa) (1+u_+)^2.

Every omitted part has u>=.01 L-O(1), giving a superpower tail after
the entire core sum. The prime-density denominators are bounded on
p,q>=z and do not spoil this estimate.

For the leading density put p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w. Since kappa>=1,
v,w>=kappa, and the global inequality

    |1/[(L/2+log v)(L/2+log w)] - 4/L^2|
       <= 8(log v+log w)/L^3                                   (R5)

holds, rather than only a compact Taylor expansion. The integral of
(1+log v+log w)g(log(rvw/s)), s=x/X in [1,2], summed over all r,
is uniformly finite. Indeed h=log(vw/kappa^2)>=0 turns it into an
integral bounded by a constant times

    kappa^2 integral_0^infinity exp(h)(1+2log kappa+h)h
                     g(h+log(rkappa^2/s))dh,

which is O_B(r^-B) for any fixed B. Thus R5 costs O(X/L^3) globally.
The leading double integral is (s/r)J(log(rkappa^2/s)). Its prefactor
is (1/2)X(4/L^2), giving exactly 2x/(rL^2), with the positive sign
in R1. This verifies the factor 2, both PNT replacements, and the
completed-core extension independently.

The choice of kappa gives the uniform small-core-complement bound.
Completing the square gives

    J(v)=exp(tau/2) integral_0^infinity h g(h+v-tau)dh.

For v>=3 tau and r>=1,

    J(v+log r) <= r^-2 J(v),

because the Gaussian quotient is at most
exp(-(v-tau)log r/tau-(log r)^2/(2 tau)). Now
z^2/x>=kappa^2/2>=exp(3 tau), and

    sum_(r>=2)r^-3 <= 1/8 + integral_2^infinity t^-3 dt = 1/4.

Consequently, if V_0=(2x/L^2)J(log(z^2/x)), R1 yields

    V=V_0+O(X/L^3),   U<=V_0/4+O(X/L^3),
    V asymp X/L^2,    0<=U<=V/3                             (R6)

eventually, uniformly on the shell. The gap from 1/4 to 1/3 absorbs
the absolute errors. All constants can depend on the fixed tau,kappa;
J is strictly positive on their compact range. No Mertens estimate
has entered R1--R6.

# [private research revision] next headroom pass — actual Möbius inversion



Accepted incumbent remains source-relative c6=.125139, boundary b6=.874861. G71/G72 from the previous pass are accepted in [private research revision]. This pass must use actual arithmetic excluded by G71, not add another general countermodel. All29 families/109 children, nearer targets,1/6,1/4 and existing source obligations remain.

## Discovery checkpoint

1. Exact higher-order Möbius inverse completion, with multiple alternating restoration factors. This is selected for development: the global inverse law is available, and every low face has a potentially rapidly decreasing completed kernel. Need derive full faces and test whether a genuinely cheaper arithmetic norm follows.
2. Additive minor-arc estimates for the complete short-window energy. A preliminary Vaughan-style scale screen against G72 gave no usable complete estimate. The near-zero arc still contains the detector signal and has no newly proved quantitative bound. No minor-arc theorem or large-denominator saving is being asserted from this screen.
3. Signed prime Volterra evolution of the actual Möbius source. The exact derivative/convolution law retains every prime power. W22/W35 already supply the normalized renewal equation and show that absolute row variation diverges. This is a duplicate unless a new signed estimate is proved; not selected.
4. Actual first-eligible-prime f3 matching. The W46 independent audit's full critical Q² residual and uniform Omega(X) positive-price obstruction were read. This remains available for signed estimates; repeating its positive argument would be a duplicate.
5. Higher simultaneous pole/derivative detectors using generalized von Mangoldt coefficients. The primary Vaughan/Heath-Brown derivation suggests a systematic global-inversion construction, but all-height signed arithmetic estimates are still needed. Retained as a distinct potential route, not assumed to inherit original moments.
6. Liouville/primitive-pair and quadratic-residue sources. The square-divisor return and nonzero L(2s,chi²) numerator are retained. A new arithmetic estimate on primitive pairs would be needed; no completely multiplicative substitution for actual squarefree coefficients is made.

Outside primary mathematics was screened through Tao's author exposition of multiplicative/derived identities and the Green--Tao primary quadratic-uniformity paper. Exact source URLs, used claims and read limits will be bound before finalization. No published logarithmic cancellation is being converted into a fixed power gain.

Current mathematical milestone: W01 RA4--RA11 already proves the fixed-order completion and fixed-order future inverse, explicitly excluding growing order. Its profile is built from exp(-t-t^(-1)) with one pre-existing Euler derivative. The argument below uses the fixed logarithmic Gaussian and explicitly pays all K-1 derivatives and growing-order constants, rather than importing that profile's fixed-order bounds. No arithmetic exponent gain is claimed. The coarse original-data estimate has been reconstructed and still gives b6+epsilon; the exact missing high-moment inequality is identified below. Every original source and frozen claim remains untouched.

## Proposed growing-order source theorem: statement and exact algebra

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q, and tau>0. In this report convolution is Dirichlet convolution, while a(n)=mu(n)chi(n) is a pointwise product. Set

  F(x)=sum_n a(n) g_tau(log(n/x)),
  g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
  D=d/d(log x), r=K-1, phi_r(v)=(1+d/dv)^r g_tau(v).

Then F_r=(1-D)^r F is exactly sum a(n)phi_r(log(n/x)). For large X, write L=log X and allow EVERY integer

  (1/2)L^(1/3)<=K<=2L^(1/3), K>=2.

Let Y=floor(exp(L/(K-1/2))), V=L/(2K-1), W=V/2. Thus the unrounded cutoff is exp(2V). Put m(n)=a(n)1_(n<=Y) and u=a-m. The global arithmetic law is a*chi=delta_1, including ramified zeros. Its exact K-fold expansion is

  u^{*K}*chi^{*(K-1)}
    =a+sum_(j=1)^K (-1)^j binom(K,j)m^{*j}*chi^{*(j-1)}.       (N1)

The j=1 term has chi^{*0}=delta_1. There is no pairwise-coprime assumption, and repeated primes shared between factors remain. Formula(N1) is a classical higher inverse identity, not a claimed invention. It is precisely where the G71 surrogate's missing prescribed inverse matters.

Define the complete short-factor source

  C_(X,K)(x)=(-1)^(K+1)
     sum_(d_1,...,d_K<=Y) product_i a(d_i)
     sum_(ell_1,...,ell_(K-1)>=1) product_j chi(ell_j)
       phi_(K-1)(log(d_1...d_K ell_1...ell_(K-1)/x)).          (N2)

Every ordered tuple and every plain factor is retained. The source is absolutely convergent for each fixed X,K,x; the absolute coefficients are bounded by d_(2K-1)(n). Introduce C^bal by imposing just the additional PRODUCT restriction

  X exp(-W)<=d_1...d_K<=2X exp(W).                          (N3)

No plain factor is capped, and all its character zeros remain. Each surviving d_i satisfies exp(V/2)<=d_i<=Y: divide the lower product bound by Y^(K-1)<=X exp(-V). Hence all its Möbius data lie between exp(c L^(2/3)) and exp(C L^(2/3)), uniformly over the K-band. These are genuine subpower factor lengths, not X^constant/k with fixed k.

The claimed uniform conclusion, proved in the following sections, is that for every fixed A>0,

  sup_(X<=x<=2X)|F_(K-1)(x)-C^bal_(X,K)(x)|
       =O_(A,q,tau)(X^(-A)),                              (N4)

uniformly for every allowed K. This pays all lower faces, the full all-large source, and both removed product tails. It does not estimate the surviving complete signed source.

## Uniform estimates paying all growing faces

For r>=0 and real v, Cauchy's formula on the complex unit circle about v gives

  |g_tau^(j)(v)|<=j! C_tau exp(-v^2/(2tau)+|v|/tau).

Summing binom(r,j)j! and weakening the Gaussian exponent yields

  |phi_r(v)|<=exp(C_tau(r+1)log(r+2)) exp(-v^2/(4tau)).       (N5)

This estimate holds for all r,v; constants depend on fixed tau only. It explicitly replaces any fixed-derivative O_r notation. The same argument with weighted Gaussian integrals pays fixed additional derivatives when needed; none are required in(N4).

For 1<=j<=K define the completed face kernel

  T_(j,K)(y)=sum_(ell>=1) chi^{*(j-1)}(ell)
                                      phi_(K-1)(log(ell/y)).

Initially on Re(s)=2 its Mellin representation is

  T_(j,K)(y)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral e^(tau*s^2/2)
                       (1-s)^(K-1)L(s,chi)^(j-1)y^s ds.   (N6)

The integrand apart from y^s is entire: the only possible pole of L is its principal pole at1, of order j-1, and K-1>=j-1 cancels it. Imprimitive finite Euler factors are not deleted. Natural zeros cause no division and no pole. On any finite vertical strip, standard polynomial bounds for L and Gaussian decay justify shifting the line completely to Re(s)=-B, for every real B>=1. For each finite X,K,B the horizontal limits are taken before the uniform estimates below.

Here is a uniform negative-line estimate sufficient for this growing order. For fixed q and every B>=1,t real,

  |L(-B+it,chi)|<=C_q^(B+1) Gamma(B+1) exp(pi*|t|/2).      (N7)

For a primitive character this follows from its functional equation, the integral bound |Gamma(B+1-it)|<=Gamma(B+1), and the absolutely convergent bound |L(1+B-it,bar chi)|<=zeta(2). The trigonometric factor costs at most2exp(pi|t|/2). For imprimitive chi, its finitely many factors1-chi_0(p)p^(B-it) contribute at most2^omega(q)q^B, absorbed into C_q^(B+1). The ordinary zeta functional equation gives the q=1 case. Thus q stays fixed; no growing-conductor claim is hidden.

On the shifted line, |1+B-it|^(K-1)<=(B+1)^(K-1)exp(K|t|/(B+1)). Combine(N7) and the Gaussian, and complete the square in |t|. Stirling's elementary upper bound for Gamma(B+1) gives

  log |T_(j,K)(y)|
   <=-B log y+tau B^2/2
       +C_(q,tau)[K(B+1)log(B+2)+K^2+K log(K+2)]           (N8)

after increasing the constant, uniformly in1<=j<=K. At a zero value of the kernel the inequality is interpreted as an upper bound, not a finite logarithm assertion. Equivalently exponentiate the right side to avoid that notation entirely.

For every y>=exp(Z), with Z>=1, choose B=Z/tau once for the entire range (or B=max(1,Z/tau)). Then for sufficiently large Z,

  |T_(j,K)(y)|
    <=exp(-Z^2/(2tau)+C_(q,tau)[K(Z+1)log(Z+2)+K^2+Klog(K+2)]). (N9)

When Z is V or W and K lies in the specified band, Z is comparable to L^(2/3), Z^2 is comparable to L^(4/3), while K Z log Z=O(L log L). Hence(N9) is at most exp(-c_(q,tau)L^(4/3)) for all large L, uniformly in j,K, with some positive c. No unspecified factorial depending on a growing order has been discarded.

For a lower face j<K, d_1...d_j<=Y^(K-1)<=X exp(-V), so x/(d_1...d_j)>=exp(V). Its at most Y^j tuples, all binomial coefficients, and the K-1 faces together cost at most exp(O(L+K)); this is absorbed by the negative L^(4/3) exponent. Therefore the sum of every lower face is smaller than any prescribed inverse power of X.

For the all-large term in(N1), n>=product_i d_i>=(Y+1)^K>X exp(V), so n/x>exp(V-log2). Apply(N5), split its Gaussian decay into two halves, and use exp(-v^2/(8tau))<=C_tau exp(-2v). Since

  sum_n d_(2K-1)(n)n^-2=zeta(2)^(2K-1),

the entire absolute tail is at most

  X^2 exp(-c_tau V^2+O_tau(Klog(K+2)+K))=O_(A,q,tau)(X^-A). (N10)

This includes every plain factor, both character and Möbius zeros, all mixed prime powers, and the Gaussian tail beyond any finite cap. No fixed-K divisor estimate is borrowed uniformly without its dependence.

Finally remove the two product tails from(N2). Below Xexp(-W), use(N9) with Z=W and the bound Y^K<=exp(L+V) for the number of ordered d-tuples. Above2Xexp(W), all log(ell/y)>=W, where y=x/(d_1...d_K). Apply(N5) and the same n^-2 argument just to the K-1 plain factors; sum over at mostY^K short tuples. Both errors are exp(-c L^(4/3)+O(L log L)) and thus arbitrarily small powers. Together with(N1), the sign(-1)^(K+1) in(N2), and the lower faces this proves(N4).

This is an actual arithmetic source estimate: the discarded complete fields are uniformly negligible as K grows. It is not an estimate of a mask borrowed from the old Type I theorem, and it does not turn the surviving source into a proved arithmetic gain.

## Return to the same fixed detector, with the full future integral

This return uses the retained source-relative summatory input for the chosen fixed ordinary character:

  M_chi(z)=sum_(n<=z) mu(n)chi(n) <<_(chi) z^b, b=7/8.       (N11)

The accepted boundary b6 is smaller than7/8. Where the original PR9 character/K scope has not been independently discharged, (N11) is an explicit hypothesis; this report neither resolves that issue nor widens it to Hecke characters. The algebra and estimates(N1)--(N10) themselves do not need(N11).

Abel summation and the derivative version of(N5) imply, for every integer r>=0 and x>=1,

  |F_r(x)|<=exp(C_(chi,tau,b)(r+1)log(r+2)) x^b.             (N12)

Indeed the relevant integral is bounded by x^b times the weighted integral of |phi_r'|; its e^(bv) factor is integrable against the weakened Gaussian. This pays the dependence on the derivative order.

Repeated integration by parts, with all future boundaries killed by b<1, gives the EXACT identity for each fixed integer r>=1:

  F(e^u)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity e^(-t)t^(r-1)
                                            F_r(e^(u+t)) dt. (N13)

At base scale X choose the even integer K=2ceil((log X)^(1/3)/2), and then keep r=K-1 FIXED throughout this integral. Do not replace r by a scale-dependent derivative inside the integration. For0<=t<=4log X, every dyadic Z meeting [Xe^t,2Xe^t] has log Z between log X-O(1) and5log X+O(1). Hence this fixed K lies in the band specified above for all those Z, for sufficiently large X; the lower margin is5^(-1/3)>1/2. At most two dyadic shells cover each shifted interval.

Suppose for some1/2<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0 the complete sources satisfy, uniformly over all sufficiently large dyadic Z and every EVEN K in the band,

  ||C^bal_(Z,K)||_(L2([Z,2Z],dx/x)) <<_(epsilon,chi,tau)
                                                     Z^(gamma+epsilon). (N14)

Use(N4) on those future shells and Minkowski in(N13). The portion t<=4log X is bounded by

  O(X^(gamma+epsilon))(1-gamma-epsilon)^(-r)
       =X^(gamma+epsilon+o(1)),                            (N15)

for epsilon<1-gamma. The remaining t>4log X is, by(N12), at most

  X^b exp(-4(1-b)log X+O_(chi,tau)(K log log X))
       =X^(5b-4+o(1))=X^(3/8+o(1)).                       (N16)

For the incomplete gamma tail used here, t^(r-1)e^(-(1-b)t) is decreasing once t>(r-1)/(1-b); bounding its logarithm at4log X and integrating a remaining exponential gives the displayed bound. The factorial and the prefactor in(N12) are also exp(O(K log log X)). Thus (N14) implies the SAME complete-shell bound for the original fixed F at exponent gamma+epsilon, after renaming epsilon. Every future scale and derivative-order constant has been paid.

The fixed field has a rapidly decreasing left tail. Its Mellin integral initially equals exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) for Re(s)>1. The complete-shell L2 bound and Cauchy--Schwarz make this Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma. Multiplying the continued identity by L(s,chi) excludes every zero there: the Gaussian factor never vanishes. The principal pole at1 is a zero of the reciprocal, not an excluded zero; it is handled by multiplying once by s-1 if using holomorphic products. This is a fixed ordinary-character, every-fixed-complex-s conclusion under its stated source hypotheses, not a fixed-height truncation. Constants may depend on q and chi. There is no uniform growing-conductor theorem, proof-assistant claim, or new identification with an unverified project root definition.

## The explicit arithmetic estimate sufficient for a gain

Let sigma be fixed with1/2<sigma<1 and write

  M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y) mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s).

The uncapped source(N2) has the exact Mellin representation

  C_(X,K)(x)=(-1)^(K+1)/(2pi i) integral_(sigma)
    e^(tau s^2/2)(1-s)^(K-1)L(s,chi)^(K-1)M_Y(s)^K x^s ds. (N17)

The contour can be moved from2 to sigma without residue: the pole at1 has been canceled, and M_Y is a finite polynomial. Define the nonnegative quantity

  H_(X,K)(sigma)=integral_R e^(-tau t^2/2)
    |1-sigma-it|^(K-1)|L(sigma+it,chi)|^(K-1)
                             |M_Y(sigma+it)|^K dt.         (N18)

Then ||C_(X,K)||_shell <=C_(sigma,tau) X^sigma H_(X,K). The difference from C^bal is already paid by(N4). Therefore the uniform estimate H<=X^(eta+epsilon) supplies(N14) with gamma=sigma+eta, and hence a zero-exclusion return, whenever1/2<gamma<1. We require all large scales and the specified orders, not numerical samples. The exponential threshold within this explicit sufficient estimate is

  eta<b6-sigma.                                             (N19)

At sigma=3/4 the first-gain threshold is eta<.124861. A concrete c=.125140 would require eta=.124860; c=1/6 requires eta=1/12; c=1/4 requires eta=0, always allowing every positive epsilon. These are OPEN sufficient estimates, not candidates certified by this report. The uniform K-band is a convenient sufficient family; no assertion is made that it is logically the weakest possible hypothesis over all architectures.

To obtain a common ordinary-character constant, the hypothesis must hold for EVERY fixed positive integer q and every complex ordinary character chi modulo q with the SAME gamma; its constants and onset may depend on that fixed character. A bound for one character supplies only that L-function's conclusion. No finite list of conductors or extension to Hecke data is inferred. Fix gamma and the finite source choices before taking large-scale thresholds; then choose the epsilon buffers needed for each target s with Re(s)>gamma.

The all-height obligation in(N18) is inexpensive but real. On this fixed line one-step summation of the periodic character, or the Hurwitz representation for the principal case, gives |L(sigma+it,chi)|<=C_(q,sigma)(1+|t|). Also |M_Y|<=C_sigma Y^(1-sigma). Put T_X=3sqrt(log X/tau). Since Klog(K+T_X)=o(log X), the entire |t|>T_X contribution is at most

  Y^(K(1-sigma)) exp(-tau T_X^2/2+o(log X))
    =X^(1-sigma-9/2+o(1))=O(X^-3).                         (N20)

For example absorb the polynomial into a Gaussian tail by maximizing its logarithm; beyond T_X its derivative is dominated by -tau t. This is not permission to discard the height band |t|<=T_X. The same estimate pays any larger height cap.

First coarse arithmetic attempt: retain any b>b6 with b<1 for which M_chi(z)<<z^b is supplied. For sigma<b, partial summation gives

  |M_Y(sigma+it)|<=C_(b,chi,sigma)(1+|t|)Y^(b-sigma).

Inserting this in(N18) and integrating the Gaussian times its polynomial yields

  H<=Y^(K(b-sigma)) exp(O_(b,chi,sigma,tau)(Klog(K+2)))
    =X^(b-sigma+o(1)).                                    (N21)

Thus the actual available summatory estimate gives back b, not b/K. At sigma=3/4 it approaches eta=.124861 from above and supplies no first gain. This failed coarse bound is retained because it is the strongest cheap original-data comparison, not a numerical parameter scan.

## A growing high moment with an explicitly paid arithmetic sector

Take K=2m. The polynomial L bound just used and a Gaussian square completion imply

  H_(X,K)(sigma)<=exp(O_(q,sigma,tau)(Klog(K+2))) Q_(m,Y)(sigma),
  Q_(m,Y)(sigma)=integral_R e^(-tau t^2/4)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^(2m)dt. (N22)

Here the constant may be fixed before X and m. Expand M_Y^m exactly. If N_(m,Y)(n) denotes the number of ORDERED factorizations n=d_1...d_m with each d_i<=Y squarefree, then

  [n^(-s)]M_Y(s)^m=lambda(n)chi(n)N_(m,Y)(n),               (N23)

where lambda(n)=(-1)^Omega(n). This follows since every surviving product of Möbius signs equals lambda(n). All factorizations at a fixed n have the SAME phase; their multiplicities do not cancel internally. Repeated primes between different factors and squareful output integers remain. Ramified outputs have chi(n)=0 exactly. Also N_(m,Y)(n)<=d_m(n), with support n<=N:=Y^m=X^(1/2+o(1)).

Gaussian integration, with no frequency selection, gives

  Q=sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_(n,k<=N)
    lambda(n)lambda(k)chi(n)conj(chi(k)) N_(m,Y)(n)N_(m,Y)(k)
      (nk)^(-sigma) exp(-(log(n/k))^2/tau).                (N24)

All ordered pairs and both conjugate terms are present. The full sum is real and nonnegative because it is the integral defining Q; individual sectors need not be nonnegative.

The diagonal is bounded by

  sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_n d_m(n)^2 n^(-2sigma)
      <=sqrt(4pi/tau) zeta(2sigma)^(m^2)=X^o(1).           (N25)

For completeness d_m(p^j)^2<=d_(m^2)(p^j): a pair of weak compositions of j into m parts can be realized as the row and column margins of a nonnegative integer m-by-m matrix. Choose one such matrix deterministically for each pair. Different margins give different matrices, so this is an injection into the m^2-part weak compositions. Multiply over primes. The exponent m^2=O((log X)^(2/3)) is why this growing order still has a subpower diagonal. A bound stated only for fixed m would not suffice.

Write n=ga,k=gb with (a,b)=1. The exact phase is lambda(a)lambda(b)chi(a)conj(chi(b))|chi(g)|^2. The absolute price of the sector g>=G, including any diagonal it contains, is bounded uniformly for1<=G<=N by

  P_(g>=G) <<_(sigma,tau,epsilon) X^(1-sigma+epsilon)/G.    (N26)

Proof: d_m(uv)<=d_m(u)d_m(v), as follows prime by prime by deterministically splitting each composition of j+k into compositions of j and k. For any fixed delta>0, drop coprimality and the Gaussian, use N_(m,Y)<=d_m, and bound each residual sum by

  sum_(a<=N/g) d_m(a)a^(-sigma)
    <=(N/g)^(1-sigma+delta) zeta(1+delta)^m.

Consequently its price is at most

  C_tau N^(2-2sigma+2delta) zeta(1+delta)^(2m)
          sum_(g>=G) d_m(g)^2 g^(-2-2delta)
   <=C_tau N^(2-2sigma+2delta) G^(-1-delta)
                              zeta(1+delta)^(m^2+2m).

Because log N=(1/2+o(1))log X and m^2=o(log X), choose delta sufficiently small for the requested epsilon, then take X large. This proves(N26), with constants uniform in the K-band. No fixed-conductor dependence is needed for this upper bound beyond |chi|<=1.

The absolute price with |log(n/k)|>=(log X)^(2/3) is O_A(X^-A) for every A. Its Gaussian contributes exp(-(log X)^(4/3)/tau), whereas the unrestricted positive mass is at most N^(2-2sigma+2delta)zeta(1+delta)^(2m)=exp(O(log X)). This pays the full ratio tail, including all pairs outside a nominal comparable-product box.

Let gamma=sigma+eta<1, eta>=0, c=1-gamma, and fix0<kappa<gamma-1/2. Choose G=X^(c+kappa), which stays below N for large X. Define Core to be exactly the sum in(N24), including its sqrt(4pi/tau), restricted to

  n!=k, gcd(n,k)<G, |log(n/k)|<(log X)^(2/3).               (N27)

It is real, because the domain is closed under exchanging n and k. Then a ONE-SIDED signed upper bound

  Core <=O_(epsilon,chi,sigma,tau,kappa)(X^(eta+epsilon))    (N28)

uniformly in the specified scales and orders is sufficient. The diagonal is X^o(1), the removed common-divisor sector is at most X^(eta-kappa+epsilon), and the ratio tail is arbitrarily small. Thus(N28) implies Q<=X^(eta+epsilon), then(N22),(N18),(N14)--(N16), and finally the fixed Gaussian zero-exclusion return. An absolute bound on Core is stronger than needed. This is the remaining arithmetic inequality, with every other sector paid. No old fixed-order correlation or original Type I/II/III moment is assumed to apply to these growing-order weights.

## Second coarse attempt: the actual positive price survives

The positive price of Core cannot be reduced to X^(eta+epsilon) just by discarding signs: actual Möbius coefficients themselves provide a large positive subcollection. This is a limitation of coefficientwise or separately positive estimates, not a lower bound for the full signed Q.

Put B=floor(X^(1/K)), so B<=Y for large X. For fixed q, squarefree integers coprime to q in[B/2,B] number at least c_q B for large B. An elementary proof expands mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counts coprime multiples with error O_q(1), and obtains density (phi(q)/q)product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0 with O_q(sqrt B) error. Their values mu(d)chi(d) lie in a fixed finite set of unit phases. Pigeonhole one phase zeta_X and a set D of at least c'_qB such integers with this phase.

Every ordered m-tuple from D contributes phase zeta_X^m and an output in[(B/2)^m,B^m]. By(N23), every other factorization of any one of these outputs has the identical phase. The total weighted mass of these outputs, with multiplicity, is therefore at least

  |D|^m B^(-m sigma) >=(c'_q)^m B^(m(1-sigma)).

Partition their logarithms into O(m+1) intervals of length at most1. One interval carries at least this mass divided by O(m+1). All ordered pairs of these outputs in that interval have positive phase product1 and Gaussian at least exp(-1/tau). Their contribution to the POSITIVE selected price is at least

  C_tau (c'_q)^(2m) B^(2m(1-sigma))/(m+1)^2
      =X^(1-sigma-o(1)).                                 (N29)

Removing the diagonal(N25) and the large-gcd positive price(N26) leaves the same exponent, since c+kappa>0. These pairs already obey the ratio condition in(N27). Moreover their total short-factor product nk lies between(B/2)^K and B^K, hence between Xexp(-Klog2-o(1)) and X. Since W/K tends to infinity, this entire positive subcollection lies INSIDE the balanced product window(N3), rather than solely in a product tail already discarded. This observation concerns the selected moment pairs; it does not identify Q with the physical norm of C^bal. Thus the coefficientwise absolute price of the actual small-gcd core is at least X^(1-sigma-o(1)). Since the needed eta=gamma-sigma is strictly below1-sigma, triangle inequalities cannot supply(N28).

This refines the location of the necessary cancellation: it must occur between different actual phases in the small-gcd, comparable-product sector. It does not preclude that cancellation, prove a zero, or exclude an epsilon-loss estimate at an equality boundary. The general positive-cone/prime-box obstruction has earlier ancestry; the added statement here is its uniform persistence for these actual growing-order squarefree-factor multiplicities, after a quantitatively paid large-gcd deletion. It is not advertised as a new general parity principle.

## A shorter-factor corollary and the actual limits of the estimates

The order (log X)^(1/3) is a convenient first instance, not a structural boundary. The same proof gives the following stronger source-compression corollary. Put f(L)=sqrt(L)/log L and allow all integers

  (2/5) f(L)<=K<=2 f(L), K>=2,                           (N30)

with the identical definitions Y=floor(exp(L/(K-1/2))), V=L/(2K-1), W=V/2. Then the source theorem(N4) and the sector estimates(N25)--(N29) still hold uniformly. Now every balanced Möbius factor lies between exp(c sqrt(L)log L) and exp(C sqrt(L)log L), which are shorter than the first displayed exp(Theta(L^(2/3))) scale.

To verify every changed asymptotic: V,W are comparable to sqrt(L)log L; the leading negative term in(N9) is of order -L(log L)^2, while K V log V=O(L log L), K^2=O(L/(log L)^2), and all tuple counts cost exp(O(L)). Thus the faces and product tails are still smaller than every inverse power. The same holds for(N10). The diagonal and gcd constants cost exp(O_delta(K^2))=X^o(1), derivative and height constants cost exp(O(Klog L))=X^o(1), log N=(1/2+o(1))L, and W/K is comparable to(log L)^2, validating the balanced positive cone. These checks are uniform over the band(N30).

For the future inverse choose K=2ceil(f(log X)/2). Up to t=4log X, the ratio of f(log X) to f(log Z) tends uniformly to at least1/sqrt5>2/5, and the upper band also has a strict margin. Thus the SAME fixed order remains admissible on every future shell, with(N16) unchanged. All later implications hold with(N30) replacing the first band. This is a genuine uniform source theorem with shorter actual factors, but it still does not prove(N28).

The proof used a comfortable gap between L^2/K^2 and L log L. Its general sufficient asymptotic condition is K going to infinity with K^2 log L=o(L), together with a future-compatible order family. Equality or the failure of this sufficient comparison is NOT an impossibility theorem. No claim is made that this rate is optimal, or that an epsilon-loss moment cannot hold at a vanishing reserve. This is separate from every old local-window coefficient boundary.

## Comparison with the frozen W47 mechanism

The W47 author report received during this pass was read in full for sections3.1--3.3 only, and its frozen report and manifest hashes were checked. Its independent review was still pending at intake; none of its claims is used as a premise above.

W47 develops Q_k=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^{*(k-1)}), d_Y=delta-chi*m_Y. At fixed b>1, it proves a uniform weighted absolute coefficient bound and exact agreement with mu chi below(Y+1)^k. Its concrete b=2,Y=4 construction, with k of order log X, then pays the entire physical Gaussian remainder at exponent1/2+o(1). Thus a growing inverse restoring the fixed Gaussian field, and even fixed-prefix arithmetic generation, are already present in W47. This report claims neither of those as a new independent discovery. W47's physical restoration does not need the subunit Mertens hypothesis(N11), whereas the future inverse used here does.

The distinct result here is a balanced all-short-factor family with explicit lower faces uniformly killed by a K-1 derivative, while K grows slowly enough that its exact high-moment diagonal and large-gcd sector remain subpower-controlled. The moment coefficients(N23), the paid bound(N26), and persistence of a positive cone after that deletion are additional arithmetic information about this particular family. W47's b>1 coefficient envelope alone supplies none of the left-line moment bound(N28), and our source completion supplies none of the signed bound for its entire Newton output. Neither is declared the universally stronger architecture.

There is an exact but non-saving composition: if the W47 agreement identity is used at a depth satisfying5^k>Y, its four-term-generated coefficients equal mu(n)chi(n) for every n<=Y. They can therefore replace each short coefficient in(N2) or M_Y without changing any value. This is an algebraic generation of the SAME source, not a bound on it. Expanding every inverse iterate before estimating creates many more plain factors; one cannot keep the small K^2 diagonal constant after that expansion without a new argument. The present proof keeps the exact simplified coefficients and never imports an unproved contraction below Re(s)=1.

Primary outside mathematics consulted during discovery and derivation:

- Green and Tao, *Quadratic uniformity of the Mobius function*, Annales de l'Institut Fourier58(2008), [primary PDF](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.2401.pdf), Lemma4.1 and its discussion, printed pages1876--1877. Used to inspect the exact Vaughan decomposition and its loss of coefficient structure after Cauchy; no unpublished power estimate or logarithmic-to-power conversion is used.

statement:
## 0. Exact source, accepted inputs, and common Gaussian bounds

Throughout tau>0 is fixed, and

    g(u)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)),
    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))),
    F(x)=sum_n f(n) g(log(n/x)).

Every positive power of a prime other than 3 contributes exactly one
minus sign; powers of 3 contribute +1. Thus |f(n)|=1, f is
multiplicative, and f is not completely multiplicative. Let omega_z
count DISTINCT prime divisors greater than z, retaining all valuations,
and define the original fields

    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1) f(n)g(log(n/x)),
    R_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)>=2) f(n)g(log(n/x)).

Then F=T_z+R_z exactly, on the uncapped positive integers. All shell
norms and inner products below use dx/x on the CLOSED shell X<=x<=2X.
No endpoint convention for integration changes the pointwise uniformity.

The fixed-order PNT input is, for each chosen fixed N,

    pi(v)=li(v)+O_N(v/(log v)^N),  v>=2.

N is selected before X tends to infinity. Neither argument needs an
order depending on X. The fixed-power theorem additionally uses the
accepted buffered assertion M(u)=sum_(n<=u)mu(n)=O_beta(u^beta),
where 1/2<beta<1 is fixed. In the current application beta is a fixed
number ABOVE .874872; beta=.8749 is still a permissible concrete choice
already supported by the earlier accepted input used in this review.
There is no assertion at the unbuffered boundary, nor uniformity as
beta approaches that boundary. The critical-window theorem needs no
Mertens or complete-field estimate at all.

The elementary Gaussian lattice bound is

    sum_(n>=1) g(log(n/y)) <= C_tau y,  y>0.             (R0.1)

For example, comparison with the integral plus the maximum of the
unimodal function of n proves it for y>=1; the same comparison and
g(log(1/y))=O_tau(y) prove it for y<1. The maximum issue when the peak
lies below 1 is thus paid. Completing the square gives the identical
bound after a fixed exponential weight in log(n/y).

If |log(n/x)|>=W, split half the Gaussian decay off as
exp(-W^2/(4 tau)), leaving a Gaussian of variance 2 tau. Consequently,
for fixed epsilon>=0,

    sum_(|log(n/x)|>=W) n^epsilon g(log(n/x))
      <= C_(tau,epsilon) x^(1+epsilon) exp(-W^2/(4 tau)). (R0.2)

For W=c log X-O(1), c>0 fixed, this is O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A,
uniformly on the full shell. Any fixed divisor multiplicity is covered
by d_k(n)<=C_(k,epsilon)n^epsilon. These are bounds for the complete
tails, not declarations that a numerical truncation equals the field.

### A. The prime layer survives every retention schedule

For principal chi write P(z)=sum_j beta_j z^j. All beta_j>=0. Every unramified prime contributes lambda+rho z; therefore, for EVERY 0<rho<=1, even X-dependent,

    beta_0+beta_1 >= pi_q(X),
    ||P(e^(it))||_2^2=sum_j beta_j^2 >= pi_q(X)^2/2.           (B3)

Since pi_q(X)~X/log X, this circle norm cannot be O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for gamma<1 and every epsilon. This is stronger than just noting R_rho>1: even a small inverse cost and adaptive retention do not remove the coherent positive prime mass. It obstructs an uncentered scalar/cardinality circle certificate, not the value P(-R_rho), which retains cancellations between all coefficients.

### 4.1 The exact coefficient mass is retained

PR9 B0.42–B0.44 and B4.10–B4.17 are the unchanged physical coefficient inputs. At a row prime \(p^j\Vert u\), \(1\le j\le5\), a monomial shift \(Q^k\) allocates \(\min(k,j-1)\) powers to \(h_r\), dividing the repeated-prime deficit
\(\Lambda_u=q_u/q_{\operatorname{rad}(u)}\); the rest belongs to \(h_0\). The physical local table retains all shared-prime cases, with natural zeros at row primes.

Its bounds are
\[
 X_u\ll_S (U/Y)h_0,\qquad
 \sum_{h_0,h_r}|c_u(h_0,h_r)|h_0^{\delta/2}\ll U^\epsilon. \tag{E2}
\]

The scale inequality and coefficient damping use the same conductor allocation. At \(j\ge2\), the potentially large linear error is of size Q; its central factor \(Q^{-1}\) cancels that size, and its shift is already assigned to the repeated-prime part. It is not available for a second conductor saving. I find no second charge in Gao's endpoint use.

The original annular support imposes \(h=h_0h_r\ll Y\), hence \(h_0\ll Y\). Deleting and restoring fixed Euler factors contributes the original bounded absolute mass and only shortens the reflected scales. The low reflected annuli have summable central coefficients; upper annuli are removed by the source rapid-decay estimate before the moment is invoked. Row-dependent coefficients are bounded by (E2), then the remaining row-dependent scales are replaced by a common-profile scale supremum. They are not inserted as new arithmetic coefficients into the moment.

## 4. W56-01: exact finite bank and its limits

Let U be the SAME complete ordinary-character Möbius Gaussian, S U(x)=U(x/2), a=15/8, b=31/16. Then D_a=(1-aS)U and D_b=(1-bS)U retain coefficients mu(n)chi(n)-a*1_(2|n)mu(n/2)chi(n/2), with natural zeros at their own arguments. Replacing the second chi by chi(n), or dropping its ramified distinction, would change the source.

The exact identities are

    U=31D_a-30D_b,
    |u-av|^2+|u-bv|^2
      =|u|^2/1861+(1861/256)|v-(976/1861)u|^2.

Thus the full positive bank dominates |U|^2/1861 for all complex u,v, with a sharp ambient constant. No arithmetic sharpness is claimed. Independent exact complex rational checks confirm both coefficients and conjugations.

The finite Bezout identity removes the common numerator-zero problem:31(1-a2^(-s))-30(1-b2^(-s))=1. Individual real numerator lines log_2(a),log_2(b) lie above theta11 but are disjoint. No infinite causal inverse or unpaid tail is used. Full all-dyad bank energy at gamma yields U energy at gamma. Mellin U has the fixed nonzero Gaussian factor times1/L(s,chi); the Gaussian left tail is integrable at every fixed s, and the right energy gives the entire required half-plane. The principal and imprimitive qualifications are as above.

Conversely complete U energy at gamma controls both filters using the adjacent x/2 shell. Therefore the bank condition is exponent-equivalent to the complete source problem. It is not a weaker arithmetic theorem. A moving separation |a_X-b_X|~X^(-eta), with bounded coefficients, prices amplitude X^eta and energy X^(2eta); the author's u=x,v=x/2 example demonstrates the generic loss without proving any arithmetic lower bound.

Retain this as a small explicit paid detector module, with G47/G52/G109 and analytic-ideal ancestry. It is not a new general inverse family. Every-epsilon complete energies below1.7497080728 would give a first gain;5/3 and3/2 would conditionally correspond to1/6 and1/4. No such estimate is provided.

statement:
## 4. The full forced exceptional count

An exceptional child has primitive inducing character in the fixed dictionary, unramified at the source's good primes. Use the original fixed bad set at this stage, containing the fixed dictionary conductors as in its exceptional-row argument. No additional Euler deletion is performed here. At every good prime, the total sextic exponent must be zero modulo 6.

First common support, second common support and the original moving support are pairwise disjoint on every nonzero genuine allocation. This follows from the retained natural zeros, not from a squarefree approximation. Amplifier primes are chosen outside the frozen supports; an extracted amplifier prime becomes a new puncture, so it cannot subsequently become a genuine second common prime.

For the C-side first common prime of multiplicities i,j, write r_P=1_(6 does not divide i-j), and e_P=1_(P|e). The new fixed row exponent is

    alpha_C(P) = 1+i-j mod 6, if r_P=1;
                 1,          if e_P=1;
                 0,          otherwise.

It follows from tau_C and reciprocity; the ray sign introduces no good-prime conductor. Let rho_C(P) be the least nonnegative residue of -alpha_C(P), and set

    T1_C = sum_(first common P) rho_C(P) log_Z N(P).

For the D side interchange i,j. In particular (i,j)=(2,1) forces rho_C=4, a saving missed by a support-only estimate.

On second common primes put rho_2 equal to the least nonnegative residue of minus the valuation of Gc V_id:

* equal i not divisible by 6, unit: rho_2=(-i) mod 6;
* equal i not divisible by 6, nonunit: rho_2=(-i-1) mod 6;
* equal i divisible by 6: rho_2=0;
* unequal i>j, necessarily 6|j and unit: rho_2=0.

Write T2=sum rho_2(P) log_Z N(P). In the genuine unit case in the first bullet, h' is a unit and exceptionality is actually impossible. We do not need this stronger exclusion: allowing its forced valuation is still a valid upper bound after dropping a partition.

At first common primes the second row factor Gc V_id has valuation zero; at second common primes the old twist is unramified. Hence these two lists of necessary residues are independent and multiply in the sixth-power-free part h0 of h'. All remaining prescribed residues can only increase its norm. For each fixed ray/unit sector,

    (h') = h0 v^6,  N(h0) >= Z^(T1_C+T2),
    #exceptional h' <= Z^[(m'+delta2-T1_C-T2)/6+o(1)].

If the forced initial norm exceeds the actual ball, the range is empty. The proof is ordinary ideal counting for v, with finitely many fixed sectors. It adds no count of live slots, common radicals, projectors or amplifier primes. Those counts are already in the original ledger.

The source B3.73 spends only f/6 in this calculation, where f=2 times the nonunit multiplicity-one radical width. It explicitly mentions the stronger 2f/6 count. The present T2 contains that full 2f, all other second-support residues, and T1_C from the literal first phase.

statement:
## 3. Fixed-ratio prime intervals from the inherited input

This short lemma supplies the block's count without an additional
arithmetic premise. For any fixed \(0<b<1\), the bound
\(M(t)\ll t^b\) implies

\[
\psi(t)=\sum_{n\le t}\Lambda(n)
=t+O_b\!\left(t^{1/(2-b)}\log(2t)\right).
\tag{SF15}
\]

To prove it, Abel summation gives locally uniform convergence near
\(s=1\) of the Möbius Dirichlet series and its first derivative.
For \(s>1\) the series is \(1/\zeta(s)\); the simple pole of
\(\zeta\) at \(1\), of residue \(1\), therefore gives

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{\mu(d)}d=0,\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{\mu(d)\log d}d=-1,
\quad
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{d>U}\mu(d)/d=O_b(U^{b-1}),\\
\displaystyle\sum_{d>U}\mu(d)\log d/d=O_b(U^{b-1}\log(2U)).
\end{cases}
\tag{SF16}
\]

For an integer \(1\le U\le t\), apply the exact convolution
\(\Lambda=\mu*\log\), splitting at \(d=U\):

\[
\psi(t)=
\sum_{d\le U}\mu(d)\sum_{m\le t/d}\log m
+\sum_{m\le t/U}\log m\,[M(t/m)-M(U)].
\tag{SF17}
\]

The formula includes real \(t\) and all floor endpoints. Uniformly
for \(z\ge1\),
\(\sum_{m\le z}\log m=z\log z-z+O(\log(2z))\).
Thus (SF16) makes the first sum

\[
t+O_b(tU^{b-1}\log(2t)+U\log(2t)).
\tag{SF18}
\]

The absolute bound on the second sum is

\[
\ll_b t^b\sum_{m\le t/U}m^{-b}\log(2m)
       +U^b\sum_{m\le t/U}\log(2m)
\ll_b tU^{b-1}\log(2t).
\tag{SF19}
\]

Take \(U=\lfloor t^{1/(2-b)}\rfloor\). This proves (SF15).
Prime powers of exponent at least two contribute
\(O(\sqrt t\log^2(2t))\), by direct counting. Hence, for every
fixed \(0<A<B\),

\[
\#\{p\text{ prime}:AN\le p\le BN\}
\gg_{A,B,b}\frac{N}{\log N}.
\tag{SF20}
\]

Indeed the corresponding difference of prime log sums is
\((B-A)N+o(N)\), and each prime has logarithm at most
\(\log(BN)\). With (SF2), the error exponent in (SF15) is exactly
\(10000/11251<1\). Only the inherited rational input and the
actual Möbius convolution have been used.
title: 3. Fixed-ratio prime intervals from the inherited input

statement:
## Own protected audit S31: an actual finite certificate and its infinite obligation

S31 needs finite patches for the actual complete field and a uniform infinite return. The following is a source interface; no interval solver was run.

Fix a computable positive tau, for example tau=1, and a(n)=f3(n)chi(n) for one fixed ordinary chi, including natural zeros. Let ell=log2. For X>=1 the logarithmic derivative obeys

    |d/dy F_a(e^y)| <= 2K_tau X, log X<=y<=log(2X),
    K_tau=exp(tau)/sqrt(tau)+2/tau.                  (AS2-4)

Proof: for H(t)=|g_tau'(log t)|, its L1 norm is at most exp(tau)/sqrt(tau) by Gaussian Cauchy--Schwarz, and its variation is at most integral|g_tau''(u)|du<=2/tau. The unit-mesh sum bound gives sum_n H(n/x)<=x||H||_1+Var(H)<=K_tau x for x>=1. This bounds the derivative termwise by |a|<=1. The same estimate holds for any truncation of the actual coefficient list.

For a positive integer N, y_l=log X+l ell/N,0<=l<N, replace a finite field F_R on each grid cell by its left endpoint value. The L2 error on the WHOLE shell is at most

    2K_tau ell^(3/2) X/N.                           (AS2-5)

All signs stay inside each sample; this is a source-value interpolation error, not independent random samples. To truncate, take R=ceil(2X exp(Csqrt(log X))). For Csqrt(log X)>tau, decreasing-tail integration gives the explicit uniform bound

    |F_a-F_R| <= T_X,
    T_X=2X exp(tau/2) * tau/(Csqrt(log X)-tau)
                    *g_tau(Csqrt(log X)-tau).       (AS2-6)

Indeed integral_R^infinity g_tau(log(t/x))dt is x exp(tau/2) times a Gaussian tail starting at log(R/x)-tau. The displayed Gaussian tail bound follows by one integration comparison. Since R is an integer, the sum beyond R is bounded by that integral. T_X=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)); every low integer remains in F_R, and the full upper tail is paid. Small X outside the displayed range is handled separately.

Suppose rigorous finite evaluations enclose F_R(e^y_l) in disks centered at z_l with radii rho_l. Then the actual certificate is

    ||F_a||_[X,2X] <=
      sqrt[(ell/N) sum_l (|z_l|+rho_l)^2]
        +2K_tau ell^(3/2) X/N+sqrt(ell) T_X.          (AS2-7)

Proof is the piecewise-constant norm, pointwise enclosure, and two norm triangles. Every n,m interaction survives inside |sum_(n<=R)a(n)g_tau(...)|^2 before the finite enclosure. No unsigned surrogate is substituted. Choose N>=X^(1-gamma+eta), eta>0 fixed, C with1-C^2/(2tau)<gamma-eta, and sufficiently precise enclosures. Then the representation error is subordinate to X^gamma. This gives a legitimate all-scale finite-certificate interface for gamma>1/2, with the existing fixed-character Mellin return. The N power is the cost of THIS Lipschitz scheme, not a lower bound on every analytic interpolation scheme: W43 already supplies a different polylogarithmic analytic projection.

The first unpaid input is the finite signed sample energy for ALL sufficiently large dyadics, with one uniform C_epsilon for each epsilon. Proving that an algorithm halts with a valid such certificate at every index would supply the required argument; observing any finite prefix of its outputs would not. Summable numerical rounding or patch-overlap errors alone do not bound the arithmetic center values z_l. No current certificate stream, universal inductive invariant or all-scale arithmetic estimate is supplied here.

There is a precise generic obstruction to inferring infinity from finitely many bounded-source patches. For any fixed N0 let a(n)=1_(n>N0). On every fixed compact x range its Gaussian field tends uniformly to0 as N0 tends to infinity, while for each fixed N0 and x tending to infinity it equals exp(tau/2)x+O_tau(N0+1). The latter follows by the same sum-versus-integral variation bound. Hence finite patch agreement and arbitrarily small finite errors do not imply a global exponent gamma<1 in the bounded-source class. This is not an actual-f3 counterexample. It identifies the missing uniform invariant in a compactness-only argument while retaining a source-specific conditional return(AS2-7). No claim of a new automatic verification algorithm is made.
title: Own protected audit S31: an actual finite certificate and its infinite obligation

statement:
### 2.3 Every alias remainder is paid

Put H_m=mT/N. The near integer bank has O(1+H_m) aliases, and if nonempty then H_m is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. Thus the sum of (2.2)'s remainders after the original factor 1/m is O(e^(-cN/X^b)). This includes the case of an empty near bank.

For nonstationary positive aliases below the near range, at most O(H_m) terms occur, each bounded by O(N T^-2 e^(-cN/X^b)). Negative aliases have the stronger bound O(N(T+N|h|/m)^-2 e^(-cN/X^b)); summing them after 1/m costs O(T^-1 e^(-cN/X^b)). The full positive tail above the near range costs

    e^(-cN/X^b) (m/N) sum_(h>cH_m,h>=1) h^-2
       << e^(-cN/X^b)(T^-1+m/N).

Because m/N<=4, every complete row remainder is O(e^(-cN/X^b)), uniformly in the original finite D. Summing the entire row-block error costs O(AM e^(-cN/X^b)) in either norm. Its interaction with the stationary bank is paid by the norm triangle, before any Gram estimate.

statement:
## 1. The actual source family, signs, zeros and fixed ideal

**Classification: compatible after a proved source transfer; no change to the accepted family.**

The ideal convention is important: `Q subseteq m` means that `m` divides `Q`, not a numerical norm inequality. For the source family `F` and slot anchor `eta0`, the fixed ideal is literally

`Q_* = internalQ(F.modulus intersect (72), eta0)
      = F.modulus intersect (72) intersect q_eta0`.

This remains fixed after extraction; the moving child whole-product character `tau` is not substituted for the anchor in `internalQ`. The source theorem `NaturalFixedRaySourceCharacters.relativeCharacter_fixedQ` gives the required containment for `nu_theta = chi_theta eta0^(-1)`. `AllocatedRayDictionary.originalImage_fixedQ` preserves it for surviving original slots. Its `both_common_rectangles` keeps their original relative characters, profiles, and heights. No arbitrary new slot coefficient or ray twist is substituted.

At an active common prime of net exponent `1 <= t <= 5`, using the source's zero-extended coefficients and reciprocity phase `q(pi,n)`, the two exact identities are

`c_n(pi) c_pi(n)^t = q(pi,n)^t c_n(pi)^(1+t)`,

`c_n(pi) conjugate(c_pi(n)^t) = q(pi,n)^(6-t) c_n(pi)^(7-t)`.

They hold off units as well, since both products are then zero. Thus the formal left residue is `1+t mod 6`, and the formal right residue is `1-t mod 6`. Side names may be exchanged only consistently. A resulting exponent six is the coprimality indicator `1_(n,pi)=1`; it is not the constant one. Canceled active primes therefore remain genuine holes. These signs agree with `FirstColumns.leftCoefficient/rightCoefficient`, not merely with a proposed valuation table.

The generator of an ideal can differ by a sixth-root unit from the product of the chosen primary prime generators. Retain this unit `u0` in the row or in the fixed six-unit dictionary. No equality between these generator conventions is needed.

On the second transform the genuine correlation vanishes unless its frequency has the form `j = G V h'`: `G` is the common gcd generator and `V` the forced nonunit radical. The normalized partition scalar has modulus at most one, including its zero extension. Multiplicativity gives the complete nonzero integer row

`w = u0 e F G V h'`.

The full residual coefficient on every ideal is

`c_eta_lambda(I) s_(m0^6 w)(I) 1_(I,R)=1`, with `m0=2(1-omega)`.

On unsupported ideals the `m0` factor supplies zero; on supported ideals the signed identity supplies the coefficient; canceled-prime holes are in `R`. The reflected rectangle has row `-w`. If a whole rectangle is conjugated, its entire character is conjugated and its height reflected. Replacing `conjugate(eta s_w)` by `conjugate(eta) s_w` is not justified and is not used here.

The first projector `s` really divides both genuine second common parts, hence `G` and `w`; `SecondSourceMask.source_pair_divisor_common/divisor_dvd_common` verify this. The second projector `t` is different: terms in the artificially separated off-coprime extension need not have `t|w`. The proof retains its original signs and pays that label through allocation/scalars, never through this divisibility claim. For an assigned plain divisor `d`, `psi_w(dv)=psi_w(d)psi_w(v)` is the exact identity; the possibly zero outside scalar remains. There is no invented restriction `(d,v)=1` on the quotient plain sum.

The exceptional/nonexceptional bridge is literal. `FixedRowMask.fixedInducingRow_mul_mask_iff` removes a nonzero extra mask from the *predicate*, not from the coefficient sum. `FixedRayInducingTransport.fixedInducingRow_product_iff` proves invariance under a permitted `Q_*`-character twist; its reverse implication uses the inverse twist and a restored modulus mask, so does not divide by a possibly zero coefficient. `SecondExceptionalFamily.Family.inducing_iff` identifies the actual reduced row; `paired_inducing_iff` identifies the reflected row with the **same** fixed ideal. Their hypotheses include the genuine nonzero row and the good-lambda and 2 divisibility of the bad mask, satisfied by `m0` and its retained products.

statement:
## 2. Complete Poisson cancellation before truncating the third factor

Let D=t d/dt. Cauchy estimates for z exp(-z-1/z), with radius
u/2 when 0<u<=1 and radius 1/2 when u>=1, give

\[
\|\phi^{(j)}\|_1\le CA^j(j!)^2.
\]

On the first range the integral of u^(-j) exp(-c/u) supplies a
second factorial; the exponential tail handles the second range.
The same conclusion holds for each fixed polynomial weight in u
and each fixed Euler derivative, with its own constants.
Optimizing integration by parts at j comparable to sqrt(|xi|)
therefore gives |hat phi(xi)|<<exp(-c sqrt(|xi|)).

With the Fourier convention exp(-2 pi i u xi), Poisson summation
and integral phi=0 yield the exact identity

\[
K(t):=\sum_{\ell\ge1}\phi(\ell t)
 =t^{-1}\sum_{m\ne0}\widehat\phi(m/t),\qquad
|D^rK(t)|\ll_r
\begin{cases}
e^{-c_r/\sqrt t},&0<t\le1,\\
e^{-t/2},&t\ge1.
\end{cases} \tag{V6}
\]

For the second estimate use the original sum; fixed polynomial
factors are absorbed by the exponential. The same argument with
weighted Fourier transforms proves the first estimate for every
fixed r.

For large N, write L=log N and set

\[
Y=\lfloor\sqrt N/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=N/L^4,\quad T_u=NL^2,\quad J=\lceil2L^6\rceil.
\]

Choose fixed smooth 0<=rho,chi<=1 with rho=0 on (0,1], rho=1
on [2,infinity), chi=1 on (0,1], and chi=0 on [2,infinity).
The exact identity mu=2m-m*m*1+r*r*1, where
m=mu 1_(n<=Y) and r=mu-m, gives

\[
S_\phi(N)=
2\sum_{n\le Y}\mu(n)\phi(n/N)
-\sum_{d,e\le Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)K(de/N)
+\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)K(de/N). \tag{V7}
\]

All rearrangements are absolute. For every fixed A>0:

- The first term is O(Y exp(-N/(2Y)))=O_A(N^(-A)).
- In the second term de/N<=L^(-4); (V6) bounds its absolute
  value by N exp(-c L^2)=O_A(N^(-A)).
- Removing Type II products de<=2T_l costs at most
  O(N log N exp(-c L^2/sqrt(2))) by summing the divisor count.
- The omitted upper-product tail is INFINITE. Its bound is
  sum_(q>=T_u) tau(q)|K(q/N)|
  <<exp(-L^2/4) sum_q tau(q)exp(-q/(4N))
  <<N log N exp(-L^2/4).
- Only after these steps truncate the ell sum. On the retained
  support t=de/N>L^(-4), so Jt>=2L^2. Every fixed Euler derivative
  of K-sum_(ell<=J)phi(ell t) is bounded by
  C_r(1+t^(-1))poly_r(Jt)exp(-Jt/4). There are
  O(N log^3 N) retained pairs, so the total tail is O_A(N^(-A)).

It follows that

\[
\boxed{S_\phi(N)=\mathcal B_\phi(N)+O_A(N^{-A}),}
\quad
\mathcal B_\phi(N)=
\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
\rho(de/T_l)\chi(de/T_u)
\sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell de/N). \tag{V8}
\]

Every nonempty pair in this FINITE sum satisfies

\[
\frac{\sqrt N}{\log^2N}<d,e<2\sqrt N\log^4N,
\qquad \ell\le\lceil2\log^6N\rceil. \tag{V9}
\]

The original signs, shared primes, and Mobius zeros are unchanged.
No coprimality surrogate has been inserted.

The N-dependent cutoff profile

\[
F_N(t)=\rho(tL^4)\chi(t/L^2)\sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell t)
\]

has uniformly bounded fixed Euler seminorms. Lower-cutoff
derivatives occur where (V6) and the ell-tail are exponentially
small in L^2; upper-cutoff derivatives occur at t comparable to
L^2. This uniformity need NOT hold for the truncated ell sum
alone near t comparable to 1/J. That range is excluded here.

Two-dimensional Stieltjes summation, retaining every edge and
corner and the cut at Y, bounds an actual dyadic pair rectangle
by O_delta((DE)^(b0+delta)) times its controlled profile seminorm.
Both variables have only O(log log N) possible dyadic sizes,
and DE<<N log^2 N. The accepted Mertens bound therefore gives

\[
\mathcal B_\phi(N)\ll_\epsilon N^{b_0+\epsilon}. \tag{V10}
\]

This recovers the baseline only. Improving this ONE fixed
kernel to N^(.87449+epsilon) at every integer scale would give
c=.12551 by (V4)--(V8). The missing amplitude saving is
b0-.87449=.000396647039964... . Neither Poisson cancellation
nor the logarithmic balance supplies that saving.

## 6. Strongest objection and the arithmetic development still missing

The main objection is that higher frequency gaps could merely move the
old hard cancellation into n around X. That objection survives, in an
exact and useful form. Near n~X the phase exp(-i(n/x)^6) varies on the
scale X, not on a much shorter scale. Neither (5) nor an ordinary absolute
Gram estimate gives a power saving there. Polynomial Mobius orthogonality
does give the actual estimate (14), but its fixed logarithmic saving is
not enough.

For clarity, the GENERIC power exponent 2 is sharp for bounded arrays;
this is not a lower bound for Mobius. Given a shell X, set a_n=1 for
1<=n<=floor(X/2) and zero otherwise. On every x in [X,2X] all phases have
argument in [-1/64,0] and the damping is >=exp(-X/(2X^(3/2))). The real
part of W is bounded below by a positive constant times X, so E>>X^2.
The array depends on X and does not satisfy the global Mobius prime law.
Thus the generic argument alone cannot reach CORE_c. Equation (14), in
contrast, uses the actual Mobius function through a primary arithmetic
theorem and is genuinely stronger than that generic bound.

A precise remaining development target is CORE1 at .8748; the stronger
signed core energy bound X^(1.7496+epsilon) would also suffice.
The available estimate has only fixed logarithmic savings. All n<=X^.8748 and all
n>X^1.0626 have now been paid. Alternatively, one may prove a strong
enough signed cancellation in the explicit finite Gram sum for that
middle interval; its kernel is K_X(n,m), with coefficients
mu(n)mu(m)chi(n)overline(chi(m)). Any proposed treatment by residue
classes, nilsequence factorization or Vaughan decomposition must retain
the joint cross terms of the whole interval. The slow transition near
n~X is the first place to attack; a further treatment of very long
frequencies would repeat an already paid component.

# Reviewed observation, source-filter and positivity components

These are written analytic results, accepted after independent review and
controller reconstruction. They do not prove an improved arithmetic moment
or a new value of c. The [private research revision] incumbent is c4=.125135 at intake; historical
examples in the frozen reports retain their original numerical meanings.
Original OpenAI, Hailey Collet, Akash Levy and Gao credits remain unchanged.

## 1. A stronger complete-field observation theorem

The [headroom A proof](headroom-a/report.md) and
[independent review](headroom-a-review/report.md) replace W39's particular
kappa<1/2 interpolation restriction. For a fixed Gaussian of width tau and
coefficients with sum |a_n|n^-b finite at some b>gamma, suppose EVERY sufficiently
large unit logarithmic interval [j,j+1] contains E_j with

    log(1/|E_j|)=o(sqrt(j)),
    ess sup_Ej |F(u)| <= C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j).

Then F has full pointwise exponent gamma, with every positive epsilon.
Every fixed polynomial density j^-kappa is allowed, with no upper restriction
on fixed kappa. Missing uncontrolled intervals and density-one information do
not satisfy this hypothesis. The full signed field is essential.

The proof multiplies e^-bu F(u) by a Gaussian window of squared radius sqrt(j),
cuts angular Fourier frequency at T sqrt(j), and applies the explicit infinity
norm form of Kovrijkine's theorem. Its cost is
(200/delta_j)^(132 T sqrt(j)+1)=exp(o(j)). Both the complete frequency remainder
and the artificially observed exterior are multiplied by this cost before
discarding them. The spatial exterior is exp(-c j^(3/2)), so it remains paid.
This is a different composition from W39, whose proof and scope remain valid.

At critical density log(1/|E_j|)<=(D+o(1))sqrt(j), the proved sufficient output
exponent is

    gamma_src + 132 D sqrt(2(b-gamma_src)/tau),

with fixed positive buffers. For the actual f3 Gaussian, accepted buffered
summatory control permits any fixed b>gamma4=.874865, rather than b>1.
Thus a first gain follows conditionally if

    D < sqrt(tau*(gamma4-gamma_src)/2)/132,
    1/2 < gamma_src < gamma4.

All parameters and buffers are chosen before the scale. This is a finite-loss
criterion; positive D does not return gamma_src without loss. The actual
every-interval sublevel estimate is OPEN. The theorem has literal separate
returns for each fixed ordinary character and each fixed finite-order,
trivial-infinity Eisenstein ideal source; f3 alone gives the zeta conclusion.
No growing-conductor or angular family is imported.

The accompanying counterexample realizes an exact squarefree/coprime support
with coefficients in {0,+1,-1}, a_1=1, and even a prescribed buffered summatory
calibration. It has critical-density valleys in EVERY unit interval while
retaining a strictly larger growth exponent. For ANY D>0 the parameters can
be chosen to exhibit this failure of a universal lossless theorem. A finite
three-coefficient modification explicitly violates multiplicativity without
changing the asymptotics. This is not a counterexample for actual mu or f3.

The signed kernel K=FourierInverse(exp(-t^4)) has bilateral Mellin multiplier
exp(-s^4), never zero, and decay exp(-c|u|^(4/3)). Its own observation theorem
allows log(1/|E_j|)=o(j^(3/4)). A quartic window and bandwidth O(j^(1/4)) pay
both amplified tails. Its arithmetic zero return is proved separately, but
Gaussian positivity, rough self-correlations and Gaussian observations do not
automatically transfer. This remains an alternative detector with an OPEN
arithmetic input, not evidence that this input is easier.

## 2. Literal rough f3 and periodic comparison

The smaller Sol High batch is retained with its
[author](sol-post52-01/report.md), [Sol High review](sol-post52-01-sol-review/report.md)
and [independent Astra Max validation](sol-post52-01-astra-review/report.md).
All sixty cards, ten tests, two developments and frozen critic audits survive.

D04 keeps all powers of every deleted unramified prime p>=5. For
P_X={5<=p<=log(X)^A:p does not divide q}, held fixed during every dilation,
the exact reconstruction is F_chi(x)=sum_r a_P(r)V_P(x/r), over all smooth r,
where a_P(p^j)=-chi(p)^j. Its positive cost is product(1-p^-u)^-1.
Under A(1-sigma)<1 and sigma+delta(1-sigma)<gamma, a complete rough moment on
EVERY real shell X^delta<=U<=X gives the full gamma moment: the long-cofactor
head costs X^(sigma+delta(1-sigma)+o(1)). The inverse coefficients
2^(j-1)chi(p)^j also have subpower weighted mass for u>log_5(2).
Consequently the rough and original full moments are EQUIVALENT at the
every-epsilon exponent level. This pays a range obligation and supplies
usable organization; it does not weaken the arithmetic exponent required.

D33 gives actual periodic small-prime signs e_P(n), mean zero when 2 is
included and 3 excluded, and exact correlation product of 1 or 1-4/p.
For Q=product P, Gaussian Poisson summation gives
|W_P(x)|<=C_m x^(1-m)Q^m. With primes up to a log X/loglog X, a<1,
this is smaller than every prescribed power. Its transform has zeta in the
NUMERATOR. The full field is W_P plus the exact unexposed-prime correction;
bounding that correction remains equivalent to the original full moment.
[private research revision]'s periodic ray/prime2 results retain ancestry credit. Marginals alone
cannot control the correction: an admissible hidden-sign relaxation makes
the entire coefficient positive.

## 3. A concrete simultaneous two-filter detector

The protected S42 audit derives, for the SAME actual f3*chi field,

    G_lambda(x)=F_chi(x)-lambda^beta F_chi(x/lambda),
    Mellin(G_lambda)(s)=(1-lambda^(beta-s)) Mellin(F_chi)(s).

Both complete filtered gamma moments, for lambda=2 and 3, exclude zeros in
gamma<Re(s)<1 except possibly one simple real zero at s=beta. Their only
common symbol zero is beta: a nonreal one would make log2/log3 rational.
Higher multiplicity at beta would still leave a pole. For zeta the real
exception is absent by positivity of its alternating series. For a general
fixed character it must be retained unless separately excluded, or beta<=gamma.
This proves a useful conditional joint return. The two arithmetic moment
hypotheses are OPEN; neither follows from filtering an incumbent bound.

Simultaneous Diophantine approximation also makes both symbols arbitrarily
small along unbounded heights. There is no fixed positive uniform gain.
This does not invalidate qualitative zero detection at each fixed zero.
Changing a counterterm with scale introduces an additional exact error:
to cancel a nonzero beta-mode down to gamma<beta requires coefficient
accuracy of order X^(-(beta-gamma)). A mere o(1) error is insufficient.

The uniform S22 audit supplies the sharp positive-range/readout price for
a signed realization. For v=(u,Ku), ||K||=kappa<1,

    ||v||^2 <= (1+kappa^2)/(1-kappa^2) * v*diag(I,-I)v.

For the actual readout d*u, the best constant is d*(I-K*K)^-1 d.
A signature count or small indefinite energy alone gives no positive bound.
The native Gaussian matrix remains its actual positive Gram; no arithmetic
graph-range condition or near-null alignment is proved by this finite audit.

## 4. W40: exact limits of positivity and phase routes

The [W40 author](wild40/report.md) and [independent critic](wild40-review/report.md)
retain thirty seeds, six tests and protected12/uniform22 audits. The disk
negative-boundary-mass condition B<=(1-r)^2/(4r) implies positive real part
inside radius r, with a sharp limiting bound. Applied to normalized
pole-corrected L-values it is a conditional zero-free budget, not a bound
on that budget. Andersson universality makes the bare zeta budget unbounded.

The critic proves more: for EVERY fixed finite prime universe S, the minimum
budget over ALL Euler-deletion subsets A of S is still unbounded along common
heights. One phase-winding target beats all finitely many subset multipliers
simultaneously, with lower modulus, upper modulus and angular derivative paid.
Choosing the subset adaptively with height inside S cannot repair this route.
Growing or unbounded prime universes remain OPEN, as do different budgets.

For literal f3, the minimum positivity correction on the full finite
prime-presence algebra is (Z_B-F_B)/2, of leading order exp(tau/2)x/2.
The rapidly truncated integer tail is paid. This is a correction-mass cost,
not a lower bound for the final signed energy. A smaller algebra needs its
own zero readout. Rank-one projector cycles obey the stated phase-loss bound,
but length-N cycles can carry phase pi with only O(1/N) loss; a fixed triangle
obstruction does not prove a macroscopic power loss.

The protected audit exhibits noncommuting prime conditional projections for
the actual four-label Gaussian weights: covariance -1/12 and normalized
correlation -1/3. A Doob variance identity still contains the unknown full
mean. The uniform audit pays both unmatched mass and angular mismatch in
antiphase transport. Neither supplies the native H cancellation estimate.

## Evidence and next use

Frozen source manifests, original draws, helper programs and independent
finite receipts are retained alongside these reports. Host-local claim and
release files are excluded. Full controller argument reads and 53 exact copy
bindings are recorded in the local [private research revision] receipt. Finite checks protect
identities and bookkeeping; the written arguments establish the stated
analytic results. One post-[private research revision] Sol batch has now completed both review
stages. Keep the existing smaller lane; reassess after three comparable
batches or a material proof-object change, without inventing cache/cost data.

The next useful steps are actual complete small-value, rough-correction or
paired-filter moment estimates. Repeating these valid adapters without a
new arithmetic input would not constitute another mathematical cycle.
