statement:
## G109. Fixed countable banks, exact buffering and the complete source

Let lambda_j>1, w_j>0 and 0<W=sum_j w_j<infinity be fixed. Write
ell_j=log(lambda_j), r_j=exp(-delta ell_j), for delta>=0, and

    F_delta(t)=sum_j w_j |1-r_j exp(-it ell_j)|^2,
    A(delta)=sum_j w_j (1-r_j)^2.

Both sums converge uniformly in real t by domination with 4w_j. Exactly

    F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      =2 sum_j w_j r_j (1-cos(t ell_j)) >=0.             (75.1)

For any finite head of length r and integers H,L>=1, divide the unit
r-torus into H^r boxes. Two of the H^r+1 points nL(ell_1,...,ell_r)/(2pi)
modulo1 lie in the same box. Their difference gives t=Lq with
L<=t<=L H^r and distance(t ell_j/(2pi),Z)<=1/H for every j<=r.
Consequently, uniformly for delta>=0,

    0<=F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      <=4pi^2 W_head/H^2+4W_tail.                      (75.2)

Given any fixed T>=0, first take L>=max(1,ceil(T)), then a sufficiently
small full tail and sufficiently large H. Equations75.1-2 prove

    inf_(t>=T) F_delta(t)=A(delta).                    (75.3)

This uses no independence assumption on the logarithms. It keeps every
channel and never changes character to manufacture adverse phases. The
principal character modulo1 already defeats a shortcut required for all
ordinary characters. Arbitrarily prescribed complex target phases on
related scales are outside this identity-target recurrence proof. The
large bound L H^r gives no useful arithmetic power estimate in height.

At delta=0 the infimum is zero. At delta>0 it is positive and also equals
F_delta(0). Dominated convergence gives A(delta)->0 as delta decreases
to zero. Furthermore,

    A(delta)/delta^2 -> sum_j w_j (log lambda_j)^2,

where the limit may be +infinity. For a finite second log moment use
dominated convergence; otherwise arbitrarily large finite partial moments
force the liminf to infinity. Summability alone does not supply a finite
quadratic coefficient or a universal decay rate. For lambda_j=2^j,
w_j=2^-j, j>=1, the exact checks are A(1)=10/21 and second log moment
6(log2)^2.

On the global space L2(R_+,x^(-2sigma) dx/x), put sigma=beta+delta and
D_j V(x)=V(x)-lambda_j^beta V(x/lambda_j). The unitary logarithmic change
f(u)=exp(-sigma u)V(exp u), Tonelli and Plancherel give

    sum_j w_j ||D_j V||_global^2 >= A(delta)||V||_global^2.

Continuity of the uniformly convergent symbol and localized Fourier
packets show sharpness, also near arbitrarily high near-minimizers.
These are unrestricted test functions, not arithmetic sources. A single
point frequency is not a nonzero L2 extremizer. The theorem is not an
exact constant for a joint physical-shell norm, nor for a sum of separate
shell suprema. Those distinctions from G52/Sol03 remain essential.

### Formation is paid for the actual Gaussian source

Fix tau>0 and the normalized Gaussian g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)
exp(-v^2/(2tau)). Let

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), U(y)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/y)).

For any A>max(1,beta), the elementary bound |a(n)|<=1 proves for all y>0

    |U(y)|<=C_A y^A,
    C_A=zeta(A)(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(tau A^2/2).

Indeed n^A g_tau(log(n/y)) is at most y^A times the supremum of
exp(Av)g_tau(v), and sum_n n^-A=zeta(A). Hence |D_j U(x)|<=2C_A x^A
uniformly in j, since lambda_j^(beta-A)<=1. In particular

    sum_(j>r) w_j |D_j U(x)|^2 <=4C_A^2 x^(2A) W_tail.

The entire bank is therefore well defined locally and on every finite
shell, with its complete tail paid. This closes the source-formation
qualification in the shared review. It supplies only an exponent A>1;
the desired subtrivial arithmetic moment remains OPEN.

### Endpoint correction: gamma=beta is admissible

Suppose the COMPLETE bank obeys, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently
large dyadic X,

    sum_j w_j integral_X^(2X) |D_j U(x)|^2 dx/x
      =O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(2gamma+epsilon)),
    0<gamma<1, beta<=gamma.                            (75.4)

Choose one fixed channel with positive weight. For every sigma>gamma,
choose epsilon<2(sigma-gamma). Dyadic covering, finite initial shells
and the preceding all-y bound give its finite N_sigma norm, where
N_sigma(V)=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||V||_[X,2X]. Since sigma>beta, its causal
inverse converges geometrically, with cost

    w_j^(-1/2)/(1-lambda_j^(beta-sigma)).

The K-th telescoping remainder is lambda_j^((K+1)beta)
U(x/lambda_j^(K+1)), bounded by C_A x^A
lambda_j^(-(K+1)(A-beta)); it tends to zero. Thus (75.4) returns the
same every-epsilon exponent gamma for U, INCLUDING gamma=beta.
The inverse constant may diverge as sigma approaches beta; that is
permitted in an every-epsilon conclusion. No inverse at sigma=beta is
asserted. This corrects the shared review's unnecessarily strict beta<gamma.

The direct Mellin check gives the same result: the numerator of this
channel is (1-lambda_j^(beta-s)) exp(tau s^2/2), which has no zero in
Re(s)>gamma when gamma>=beta. Its transform is holomorphic there under
the complete shell hypothesis and the paid left tail, so the reciprocal-L
identity excludes every zero in that half-plane. For gamma<beta one
channel leaves numerator zeros on Re(s)=beta. Two multiplicatively

## Fixed powers below one half

Fix 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2, tau>0, and a buffered Mertens
exponent 1/2<beta<1 with sum_(n<=u)mu(n)=O_beta(u^beta). The retained
baseline permits beta=.8749; the new accepted endpoint permits any
fixed beta>.874872. Put L=log X, delta=(1-2rho_1)/4 and
eta=delta(1-beta)>0. Then

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f e^(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                       +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),
    C_f=9log2 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)>0,
    B(rho)=2log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.

B is strictly negative and decreasing on (1/3,1/2). Hence the band
T_(X^b)-T_(X^a), for fixed 1/3<a<b<1/2, is positive with leading
coefficient C_f e^(tau/2)[B(a)-B(b)]. For a=3/8,b=2/5 this difference
is exactly 79/225+2log(10/9)>0. The complete terminal complement at
any fixed rho_plus>1/2 is O_A(X^-A), so the band from such a fixed a
to rho_plus is negative of order X/L^3. Signs of individual threshold
jumps have not been proved.

The mechanism is source-specific. Its Euler series is H(s)/zeta(s),
where H has absolutely summable coefficients for Re(s)>1/2 and a
simple zero from p=2 at s=1. Transferring the buffered mu-Mertens
bound through its actual convolution proves the f partial-sum bound.
The reciprocal series consequently has a double zero at1, giving
ordinary-order signed core moments 0,0,2C_f. It is not legitimate to
derive these partial sums merely by inverting a Gaussian norm bound.

Below a fixed power U<z^3 the original source has exactly n=rpq,
p<q both greater than z, each of valuation one, r<z, coefficient f(r).
Outside U the completed formula can fail; its full divisor-weighted
Gaussian tail is paid. Signed Abel summation removes r>X^delta before
prime-density substitution. The p=q correction and both sharp PNT
endpoints are paid. Two sequential fixed-order Stieltjes replacements
give the exact unordered density phi_t(A)=A^-1 log((A-t)/t), A>2t.
The Taylor remainder and its derivative are summed by signed Abel,
not an unsigned harmonic bound. The resulting C_f phi_t'' gives B.
The complete proofs price every source-completion and reciprocal-core
tail before reading off its sign.

The compact rho interval is fixed. No uniformity at rho=1/3, at
rho=1/2, or through a moving transition is asserted. In particular
[private research revision]'s negative subpower bands cannot be extrapolated into this
positive fixed-power band range.

## 5. Independent protected audit X23: an exact divisor Bellman contract

This audit was selected from the original seed before outcomes. It is separate from the author's six tests. Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), c(n)=chi(n), so a*c=delta on all integers, including ramified zeros and all prime powers. The exact sequential recurrence is

    a(1)=1; a(n)=-sum_(d|n,d<n)a(d)chi(n/d).

Let x_n=(a(1),...,a(n)) and let T_n append that divisor row to x_(n-1). Its entries are literally -chi(n/d)1_(d|n), not unsigned incidence weights. With ell_N=(1,...,1), M_chi(N)=ell_N x_N.

For Hermitian matrices P_n>=0, possibly depending on N, a complete Bellman certificate consists of

    P_N>=ell_N*ell_N,
    T_n*P_nT_n<=P_(n-1)+E_n.                         (R17)

The E_n may be Hermitian signed debts. Evaluating on the actual source and telescoping gives

    |M_chi(N)|^2<=x_1*P_1x_1
                      +sum_(n=2)^N x_(n-1)*E_n x_(n-1).     (R18)

The whole actual right side must be bounded. Replacing every debt by a positive bound is a sufficient but possibly wasteful choice, not part of the identity. A bound O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(2gamma+epsilon)) for every epsilon and all N returns M=O(N^(gamma+epsilon)) after relabeling epsilon. Abel/Mellin continuation of sum mu(n)chi(n)n^-s then excludes L-zeros in Re s>gamma at every height; the principal pole is matched by a zero of the reciprocal. The same gamma is required for every fixed ordinary chi. No cancellation is proved merely by writing(R17).

The seed specifically proposes testing only reachable states. For that formulation, it is enough to require each inequality in(R17) after evaluation on the actual x_(n-1), and the terminal inequality only on x_N; the identical telescoping proof gives(R18). Global matrix inequalities are a stronger sufficient certificate, not an inferred property of the reachable set. Even a diagonal terminal form can then escape the quadratic global price below: at N=2,chi=1, x=(1,-1) has output0, so the zero form is sufficient on that state. The uninformative choice D=|M_chi(N)|^2 I/K also has the exact reachable energy but already requires the unknown output. A finite usable description of reachability and a noncircular signed bound remain the live high-ceiling part of X23.

The exact no-debt backward metric is instructive. Define a row, for d<=n,

    w_(N,n)(d)=sum_(j<=n/d)chi(j) M_chi(floor(N/(dj))).       (R19)

To verify it without missing a tail, start from an arbitrary prefix x_1,...,x_n. Set b(k)=sum_(d|k)x_d chi(k/d) for k<=n and b(k)=0 for k>n. The continuation is b*(mu chi), and its sum through N is sum_(k<=n)b(k)M_chi(floor(N/k)). Reordering gives(R19). Hence w_(N,N)=ell_N, w_(N,n-1)=w_(N,n)T_n, and w_(N,1)=M_chi(N). The matrices P_n=w_(N,n)*w_(N,n) satisfy(R17) with E_n=0, but P_1=|M_chi(N)|^2. This exact certificate is circular unless constructed/bounded by new arithmetic information. It shows precisely where the full signed response resides.

A concrete restricted class already has exponent-two cost. Even remove every forced-zero coordinate at the terminal time: I={n<=N:mu(n)chi(n)!=0}, K=|I|. Every remaining actual source coordinate has modulus1. A positive diagonal D dominating ell_I*ell_I must satisfy sum_(i in I)1/d_i<=1. Consequently its actual terminal energy is sum_i d_i>=K^2; equality is attained by d_i=K. Natural zeros do not erase this cost. Direct squarefree counting gives

    K=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=1/zeta(2) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^-1>0.      (R20)

Indeed sum_(d<=sqrt N,(d,q)=1)mu(d) times the number of q-units m<=N/d^2 gives the formula; the coprime-prefix error and the convergent d^-2 tail each cost O_q(sqrt N). Thus a diagonal terminal majorant on this active subspace costs Theta_q(N^2). This is NOT a lower bound on |M_chi(N)|^2 or on every reachable/source-specific Bellman certificate. Signed off-diagonal geometry remains live. It is the actual divisor-source specialization of the known U-VARIATIONAL/W38 magnitude-only SDP obstruction, with the exact adjoint response and conditional return now stated.

statement:
## 4. CU: exact sixth-power holes and the clipped repetition sum

Write uniquely (Delta*ell)=kappa*t^3*z^6 with kappa cubefree and t squarefree. Primewise the exponents are

    v_kappa=v_ell mod3,
    v_t=floor(v_ell/3) mod2,
    v_z=floor(v_ell/6),

where v_ell here means v(Delta*ell). They need NOT have disjoint support. A prime of valuation4 occurs in both kappa and t; valuation10 occurs in all three. The exact identity is

    chi_m(ell)^eta = fixed_Delta_unit_factor
       *chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1).        (V7)

The quadratic factor is real, so its exponent is unchanged for eta=-1. The last factor cannot be replaced by one: at a good source prime p with valuation6 in (Delta*ell), the local kappa and t valuations are zero and the z valuation is one. The original local factor is zero, while dropping the z-hole would give one. Fixed-place factors do not change this local counterexample. This is the first decisive obstruction to an incautious repeated-row argument.

Fix kappa AND z before averaging t. The inner coefficient is c_f(m)chi_m(kappa)^eta 1_((m,z)=1), with any fixed Delta/unit factor. It remains squarefree, satisfies (V3), and is independent of live t. An overlap with t remains the quadratic symbol's own zero; overlaps among kappa,t,z impose no additional mask. The outer common f-hole is retained independently.

The primary [Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642), dated 31 May 2012, allows arbitrary inner coefficients for a quadratic Hecke family, with BOTH ideal variables squarefree, and price M+N up to a subpower. Its family hypotheses include primitivity, trivial infinite type, finite-group reciprocity, and the primitive product conductor for coprime equal-class indices. PR9 B2.24 supplies the actual family check: the lambda sign correction, its primitive inducing convention, fixed primary square classes modulo4, and ray reciprocity. These are retained source assumptions, not replaced by a generic power-symbol analogy. Finite class splitting and transpose duality identify the present m,t orientation.

More explicitly, PR9's character on an ideal (x) is vartheta_m((x))=epsilon_lambda(x)^(e(m)) (x/m)_2, with e(m)=(q_m-1)/2 modulo2 and primitive conductor m*lambda^(e(m)). After fixed S-parts are removed, the difference from chi_m(t)^3 is precisely this lambda unit factor. Splitting e(m) and the fixed ray classes makes it an outer t factor of modulus one. Equal-class products cancel that lambda correction and have primitive good conductor equal to the product, as required. Neither an extra moving conductor cost nor a live-t coefficient is introduced.

The t-energy for q_t<=T0 is therefore <<H_J U^epsilon(T0+X). The independent pointwise input is G185 on the two original colors of ONE copy:

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon S0,
    S0=P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].                        (V8)

The new z-hole splits between x,y and the ORIGINAL remaining slots; it does not create an arbitrary joint coefficient. Fixed kappa and other holes do the same. Thus (V8) applies after the exact conditioning in (V7), using the actual shortened colors on each side and their common S0 upper bound. Those two colors are not cross-copy products.

Set B=(H_A/q_kappa)^(1/3). For fixed z, T0=B/q_z^2; q_z<=sqrt(B) on every nonempty fiber, up to fixed support constants. Two available bounds are T0+X and T0*S0. For 1<=Z<=sqrt(B), ideal counting gives

    sum_(q_z<=Z)(B/q_z^2+X) << B+XZ,
    sum_(q_z>Z) B*S0/q_z^2 << B*S0/Z.                 (V9)

In particular XZ, the repeated-row price, has NOT disappeared. Put Z0=sqrt(B*S0/X). If 1<=Z0<=sqrt(B), balancing proves B+O(sqrt(B*S0*X)). If Z0<1, the all-pointwise price B*S0 is at most sqrt(B*S0*X). If Z0>sqrt(B), then S0>X, and the all-quadratic price B+Xsqrt(B) is at most B+sqrt(B*S0*X). This proves in every regime

    sum_(t,z) |B_f(kappa*t^3*z^6)|^2
       << H_J U^epsilon [B+sqrt(B*S0*X)].              (V10)

Thus no unproved S0<=X restriction is hidden in the choice of split. Coefficients are different for different z, which is permitted because each quadratic application fixes z; they are not different for live t. Any core priority selector remains an outer t restriction after kappa,z are fixed.

Sum cubefree kappa up to C. The powers q_kappa^(-1/3), q_kappa^(-1/6) give

    H_J U^epsilon [H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3)
                       +sqrt(S0*X)H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6)]. (V11)

A general divisor-bounded merged coefficient would give (V3) but would not necessarily give (V8). The cube proof genuinely uses both the arbitrary-sequence quadratic contract and the original-color pointwise structure.

## 1. The complete arithmetic average

Let R be the positive integers or the nonzero integral ideals of
K=Q(omega). Write q_a=a or Na, respectively. Fix tau>0, a finite prime set S,
and one ordinary Dirichlet character eta, or one finite-order,
trivial-infinity Hecke character. Retain the original zero extension.
For the sextic construction S includes the primes above6. Define

    U_Q(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,SQ)=1) g_tau(log(q_a/x)),
    U=U_1,  g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)).       (R1)

Q denotes a finite radical outside S. All sums in this review are COMPLETE
Gaussian sums. Fix the label sets

    Fset={f squarefree: F<q_f<=2F, (f,S)=1},
    Eset={e: q_e<=E, (e,S)=1},
    P_FE(x)=(N_F N_E)^(-1) sum_(f,e) U_rad(fe)(x),              (R2)

with their exact positive cardinalities. Shared primes between f and e
are allowed, and e=1 is present. For large F,E, N_F~_S F,N_E~_S E.
The ideal count counts one ideal, not six associates.

For Q squarefree, put h(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-1),
D(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1+q_p^-1)^(-1), and S_a(Q)=sum_(d|Q)q_d^-a.
The elementary ideal lattice count is

    A_K(T)=kappa T+O(sqrt(T)), kappa=pi/(3sqrt(3));
    A_Z(T)=T+O(1).

Inclusion-exclusion, then mu^2(a)=sum_(r^2|a)mu(r), gives uniformly in Q,
for T>=1,

    A_Q(T)=kappa T h(Q)+O(sqrt(T) S_1/2(Q))                  [K],
    A_Q^sf(T)=kappa T D(Q)/zeta_K(2)
                     +O(sqrt(T) log(2T) S_1/2(Q))          [K],
    A_Q(T)=T h(Q)+O(d(Q)),
    A_Q^sf(T)=T D(Q)/zeta(2)+O(sqrt(T) d(Q))                [Z]. (R3)

There is no Q<=T restriction. In the squarefree main term the factors
h(Q) prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-2)^(-1) are exactly D(Q).

Consequently the two avoidance probabilities for a fixed a have main terms

    A(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S) q_p/(q_p+1),
    B(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S) (q_p-1)/q_p.

Their product is w(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)(q_p-1)/(q_p+1).
The errors after division by the EXACT sample counts are, respectively,
F^-1/2 log(2F) S_1/2(rad a), E^-1/2 S_1/2(rad a) over K;
F^-1/2 d(rad a), E^-1 d(rad a) over Z. Since all probabilities and
main terms lie in[0,1], the product error is bounded by the sum of the
two errors. No additional mixed error or independence of prime events is
assumed; independence here is simply the Cartesian choice of f and e.

With the ONE fixed field

    W(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)w(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x)),

the full comparison is

    |P_FE(x)-W(x)| << x log(2F)(F^-1/2+E^-1/2)              [K],
    |P_FE(x)-W(x)| << x(1+log(2+x))(F^-1/2+E^-1)           [Z]. (R4)

These bounds include both infinite source ends and hold uniformly for x>0
when the label counts have reached their fixed-S asymptotic range. Indeed
sum_(q_a<=T) S_1/2(rad a)<<T and sum_(n<=T)d(rad n)<<T log(2T).
Gaussian integration gives the stated whole-source bounds; at x<1 the
left tail is smaller than every fixed power of x. The complete sources
also satisfy |U_Q(x)|<<x uniformly in Q by the absolute coefficient count.

Minor clarification1: the author's(A2) should explicitly say T>=1 or replace
log(2T) by log(2+T). No use in the report requires a logarithm of negative
sign at tiny T. The underlying A1 remains valid at T<1.

statement:
## G140. The actual source and its nonvanishing Mellin return

Fix an ordinary complex character chi modulo q, retain
a_n=mu(n)chi(n) with every squareful/nonunit zero, and choose fixed b>1
and integer k>2. Define for every real x>0

    W_(b,k),chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a_n exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

The sum converges absolutely and locally uniformly. The selected source
has b=3/2, k=6. The phase uses n^k but the damping uses n; neither may
be substituted for the other in the Mellin calculation.

For Re s>0 let I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-i(nt)^k)t^(s-1)dt.
After v=nt, rotate clockwise by fixed
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)), with principal power branches. The large
arc is killed, for each n, by exp(-n^(1-b)R^b cos(b alpha)); the other
exponential has modulus at most1 throughout the sector. The small arc
vanishes for Re s>0. On the rotated ray exp(-iv^k) has modulus
exp(-|v|^k sin(k alpha)). Taylor's integral remainder for Re z>=0 gives
|exp(-z)-sum_(j<K)(-z)^j/j!|<=|z|^K/K!. Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-(b-1)j)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s)=(-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)
                  exp(-i*pi*(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),
    |R_(n,K)(s)| <= n^(-sigma-(b-1)K) exp(alpha Im s)
       Gamma((sigma+bK)/k)
       /[k K! sin(k alpha)^((sigma+bK)/k)].

The coefficient follows by a decaying gamma-ray rotation. Local
domination, including each fixed logarithmic derivative, proves remainder
holomorphy. Its series with a_n is normally convergent on
sigma>max(0,1-(b-1)K). Initial Fubini is used only for sigma>b, where
the absolute sum of integrals equals Gamma(sigma/b)zeta(sigma/b)/b.
Thus, for H(s)=integral_0^infinity W(1/t)t^(s-1)dt,

    H(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi)+R_chi,K(s).

For b=3/2,k=6,K=1 this is

    H(s)=Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/(6L(s,chi))+R_chi,1(s),

with R holomorphic on Re s>1/2 and nonzero leading multiplier on Re s>0.
The complete every-epsilon shell L1 bound

    integral_X^(2X)|W(x)|dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)

for one fixed gamma>1/2 makes H holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Choose
epsilon below the compact real-part margin; shell summation also pays
all fixed derivatives. At x tending to zero the bound
1/(exp(x^(-b))-1) pays every Mellin power. Continuation of the displayed
identity excludes every zero of the actual L in that half-plane. The
principal pole produces a reciprocal zero and is retained; imprimitive
Euler factors remain in L. Arbitrary compact height ranges suffice for
all finite heights. For all characters, gamma is common, while constants
and onsets may depend on the fixed character. L2 at exponent2gamma is a
stronger sufficient premise; equivalence with zero exclusion is not claimed.

### A5. The stated Eisenstein Hecke family, with fixed-conductor quantifiers

Let K=Q(sqrt(-3)), O_K its Eisenstein lattice, and psi a fixed finite-order Hecke character of trivial infinite type, extended by zero on ideals not coprime to its fixed PRESENTED ray modulus f. Include any specified finite deleted primes in f; it need not be the minimal conductor. Define

    F_psi(z)=sum_(nonzero integral ideals a)
                 mu_K(a)psi(a)g_tau(log N(a)-z).          (W39.14)

Use the literal ideal Möbius coefficient: squareful ideals give zero. This is not the ordinary integer coefficient transplanted by notation.

All needed analytic facts in Re s>1/2 follow from an elementary fixed-lattice argument. The triangular Eisenstein lattice has covering radius <1 after norm normalization, giving the Euclidean division algorithm and hence every ideal is principal. There are six units. The weight psi((alpha)), with its conductor zeros, is a bounded periodic function of alpha modulo f, invariant under units. A nonprincipal character has mean zero over the finite residue group; the principal character has its actual positive coprimality mean. Decompose the norm disk N(alpha)<=X into fixed f-lattice cells. Complete cells contribute the appropriate mean; only O_f(sqrt X+1) boundary cells remain. Dividing by6 gives

    sum_(N(a)<=X) psi(a) = c_psi X+O_f(sqrt X+1),         (W39.15)

where c_psi=0 for nonprincipal psi. The zero lattice vector is excluded and changes only O(1). In particular the total ideal count is O(X). Abel summation of W39.15 gives L(s,psi) meromorphic for Re s>1/2, with only the principal simple pole at1, and a polynomial upper bound on every closed strip inside that domain after regularizing the pole. The Euler product on Re s>1 is nonzero. All constants here depend on the fixed conductor; no uniform moving-conductor estimate follows.

Thus the proof A1--A4 applies word for word for any fixed gamma>1/2, choosing every replenishment disk inside Re s>1/2. The disk radius in A3 can be shortened if necessary, or use h>gamma>1/2 directly. Ideal counting supplies W39.2; ideal Euler inversion supplies W39.9; the natural conductor zeros and finite omitted factors remain in every identity.

**Theorem W39-H.** For EACH fixed member of exactly the finite-order, trivial-infinite-type Eisenstein Hecke family, W39.13 with W39.14 in place of F and gamma>1/2 implies zero exclusion Re s>gamma and the full all-scale Gaussian bound. Constants and thresholds may depend on that member. An assertion for every member requires W39.13 separately for every member, or an independently proved family-uniform hypothesis. Angular/infinite-order characters are outside this theorem. This covers the proposed near,1/6 and1/4 targets at the level of a quantitative conditional return.

The family identification agrees with [restricted mathematical source] opening statement. The older I-HECKE package in [restricted mathematical source] is not used to assume a better reciprocal bound: W39.15 and the disk argument establish the particular analytic prerequisites used here.

## 2. The first phase: an exact repair, and its impact

Write the full products as \(Ca,Db\), with complete common support in \(C,D\). Then \((a,b)=(ab,CD)=1\). At a common prime with multiplicities \(i,j\), the original row factor is \(\chi_P(k)^{i-j}\). On its active radical r the primitive character is therefore

\[
 \xi=\prod_{P\mid r}\chi_P^{i-j}.
\]

For any character extended by zero and any unit t modulo m, the substitution \(y=tx\) gives
\(\mathcal G_\chi(m,th)=\overline{\chi(t)}\mathcal G_\chi(m,h)\), including nonunit h. The CRT coordinate at r is multiplied by \((ab)^{-1}\); hence its contribution is **\(\xi(ab)\)**. The full exact identity is

\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal G_{\xi\chi_a\bar\chi_b}(rab,h)
={}&\xi(ab)\chi_a(rb)\overline{\chi_b(ra)}\,
\mathcal G_\xi(r,h)\mathcal G(a,h)
\overline{\mathcal G(b,-h)}.
\end{split}
\]

The substitution \(k=ek'\) supplies the frozen common scalar \(\mu(e)\xi(e)\tau(C)\overline{\tau(D)}\) and the separate e factors. Reciprocity then yields

\[
 \tau_C(a)=\tau(a)\chi_a(er)\xi(a),\qquad
 \tau_D(b)=\tau(b)\chi_b(er)\overline{\xi(b)}.
\]

These are exactly old D.10's two displayed twists. They give first-prime exponents \(1+i-j\) and \(1-i+j\), respectively, modulo six, together with fixed ray factors.

PR9 lines 2314 and 2323 instead put an inverse xi factor on the C coefficient and in the CRT product while retaining \(\mathcal G_\xi\). With the above declared row and Gauss character this is not the same identity. Replacing h by -h changes a fixed unit factor and does not invert \(\xi(ab)\). Defining xi to mean the inverse common character would also require replacing the Gauss label by the inverse character. Exchanging C and D is possible only if the entire ordered transform, common character and conjugations are exchanged consistently. A scalar frozen independently of a,b cannot absorb this discrepancy.

This is best classified as a **repairable written phase inconsistency**, rather than a demonstrated intentional model change. Gao's `SignedReconstruction.tex` explicitly derives left residue \(1+t\), right residue \(1-t\), and says that assigning the conjugate coefficient to the C side requires a consistent exchange of side names. It therefore provides independent primary-source corroboration of the repair.

The effect on c6 is limited and precise. PR9's old exceptional count uses only newly forced second-support residues and disjointness from old support; its first F1 inequality uses \(\widetilde q\ge R\), not the sign of xi. The first target and balance use only c,d,p,R,E. Gao's high estimate permits either signed residue and uses the bound \(L_c\le5(R-R_0)\); its finite dictionary treats the two first-side orientations separately. Low-bin deletion also uses the actual natural family and width, not a preferred residue sign. Therefore the repaired coefficient is within the exact classes used in the accepted source-relative assembly, with unchanged costs. The correction does matter for the **new** T1 gain, which cannot be derived by keeping the incorrect inverse C phase with the original c,d labeling.

No assertion about the implementation or validity of any proof-assistant artifact is made here. The finite CRT derivation is sufficient for this written repair.

### B2. Isolated prime-power cells survive centering

Let

    D=floor(min(sqrt(N)/4, N/[4(Y+1)])).

For every unramified prime power2<=d<=D put m=floor(N/d). It lies strictly above Y; also m>=N/(2d). Its quotient cell contains d and has length

    L_m<=d^2/(N-d)<=1/8.                                   (B6)

There is therefore exactly one integer in the cell. Different d give different m. The FULL merged coefficient at that state is

    c_m=Lambda(d)chi(d)-delta_chi L_m,
    |c_m|>=Lambda(d)/2.                                    (B7)

Here |chi(d)|=1; ramified prime powers are omitted precisely because their original coefficient is zero. The elementary inequality log2>1/2 makes(B7) immediate from(B6). Consequently

    C_(beta,Y)(N)>=2^(-beta-1)
                   sum_(2<=d<=D,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta).
                                                                    (B8)

This lower bound is for the actual merged, centered kernel. It does not rely on independent unmerged copies of a quotient state.

An elementary Chebyshev lower bound suffices to price(B8). For n>=1, the p-adic exponent of binomial(2n,n) is at most floor(log_p(2n)); hence

    psi(2n)>=log binomial(2n,n)>=2n log2-log(2n+1).

Taking2n<=D within1 of D gives psi(D)>=cD for large D. Removing the finitely many prime-power rays dividing fixed q changes this by O_q(log D), so psi_chi0(D)>=c_q D. Therefore

    C_(beta,Y)(N) >= c_(q,beta) D^(1-beta).                   (B9)

For fixed0<=theta<1 and Y=floor(N^theta), this gives

    C_(beta,Y)(N)/log N
      >>_(q,beta,theta) N^((1-beta)min(1/2,1-theta))/log N.  (B10)

The centered operator remains unbounded even after a power-size known prefix and the log N normalization of(B1). With theta<=1/2, the powers are .0625729818 at beta=.8748540364,1/12 at beta=5/6, and1/8 at beta=3/4. These are obstruction exponents for this norm, not zero-free gains or lower bounds for actual M. Any bounded-density smooth drift in place of delta_chi du has the same argument after reducing the fixed constant in D.

 B_(l,x) <= C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^gamma/N)^2.             (27)

statement:
## G85. Full-scale moment return without the baseline

For fixed 1/2<sigma<=gamma<1 and eta=gamma-sigma>=0, the Q hypothesis
for every sufficiently large **real** X and every admissible even K in
either band is equivalent to M_chi(Y)<<_delta Y^(gamma+delta), for every
delta>0. The full-X one-sided Core hypothesis is equivalent too.

For every large integer Y, put u=log Y and choose

    band I:  K=2ceil(sqrt(u)/2),
    band II: K=2ceil(u/(8(log u)^2)),
    X=Y^(K-1/2).

Each choice is admissible in its respective band, tends to infinity and
hits the integer cutoff exactly. Write A=|M_Y(sigma)| and choose
D_Y=C_sigma Y^(1-sigma)log Y>=1. The elementary derivative bound
|d M_Y(sigma+it)/dt|<=D_Y shows, when A>=1,

    Q >= c_tau (A/2)^K / D_Y.

Indeed an interval inside [-1,1] of length at least 1/D_Y has amplitude
at least A/2. Thus the assumed Q bound gives

    A <= 2(C_epsilon D_Y/c_tau)^(1/K)
          Y^((1-1/(2K))(eta+epsilon)).

Fix epsilon before sending Y to infinity. The derivative-width cost is
Y^o(1), so the weighted partial sums are O_delta(Y^(eta+delta)), also
at eta=0. Abel inversion recovers Mertens with exponent gamma. The
converse follows by Abel summation, giving
|M_Y(sigma+it)|<<_delta(1+|t|)Y^(eta+delta), and the Gaussian integral
cost exp(O_delta(Klog(K+2))). No initial subunit Mertens bound is used.

The recovered Dirichlet series sum a(n)n^(-s) is holomorphic on
Re(s)>gamma and agrees with 1/L(s,chi) for Re(s)>1. Analytic continuation
therefore excludes zeros throughout Re(s)>gamma, retaining the principal
pole exception and including nonprincipal s=1. A common exponent must
hold for every fixed ordinary character before its own threshold; no
uniform growing-conductor or automatic Hecke statement follows.

**Do not substitute dyadic X for full real X in this equivalence.**
Dyadic cutoff gaps can have size Y/K and cannot be filled by a trivial
power-saving interpolation. The weaker dyadic balanced-source route
above retains its future-growth premise. This distinction is essential.

At sigma=3/4, the open eta targets are .124861 for the incumbent
boundary, .124860 for c=.125140, 1/12 for c=1/6, and0 for c=1/4.
Existing Mertens exponent b yields only Q<=X^(b-sigma+o(1)); raising
the order does not divide this exponent by K. No target bound is proved.

## 5. What the author's bank obstruction actually proves

For a principal character, take a normalized signed bank with cuts tau_j,
weights lambda_j, sum lambda_j=1 and sum |lambda_j|<=Lambda, and initially
fixed cardinality J. Cutoffs and weights may depend on X but not on x.
The paid complement remains uniform with an extra factor Lambda.

For distinct unramified primes n=rs comparable to X, B(n)=L for all large X.
The only long-long factorizations are (r,s,1) and (s,r,1), including the
endpoint cuts because their long inequalities are strict. Put c=1-gamma,
t_j=gamma tau_j and alpha=log r/log X. The ideal coefficient profile is

    F(alpha)=sum_j lambda_j [1_{t_j<alpha<t_j+c}
                       +1_{gamma-t_j<alpha<1-t_j}].

It is symmetric under alpha -> 1-alpha, bounded by 2Lambda, and its
signed integral on [0,1] is exactly 2c. This integral cannot be replaced by
an integral of absolute weights. With delta=c/(4Lambda), the central left
half has integral of Re F at least c/2. The set where Re F>=c/2 in
[delta,1/2] has measure at least m=c/(8Lambda).

With fixed J the at most 4J breakpoints supply an interval of fixed positive
length where F is constant and its real part is positive. Trim its ends
before inserting the O(1/log X) displacement in log s/log X. Ordinary PNT
then supplies >> X/log X actual distinct prime products in that interval,
uniformly for exponents in a fixed compact subset of (0,1/2). Their phase
on the whole shell lies in a fixed short arc and damping is positive. Rotate
the fixed complex coefficient if necessary. The selected projection has
both L1 and L2 norm >> X/log X.

This is a lower bound for a specifically selected positive semiprime
projection. It is not a lower bound for the full signed core, a larger box,
or the sum of all projected pieces. Cross-piece cancellation is exactly the
unpaid possibility. The same distinction applies to all lower bounds below.

statement:
## 5. D3/S16: the conditional-square certificate really is too costly

The finite coding example is correct: if a linear syndrome over F2 does not contain parity in its row span, uniform measures conditioned on even and odd parity have the same uniform syndrome law, with opposite parity biases. A kernel vector with odd parity pairs the two extensions in every syndrome fiber. This is a model obstruction to inferring a missing character from syndrome entropy; it is not a theorem about all arithmetic observations.

For the actual principal character modulo fixed q, partition S_N by the entire set of prime divisors <=sqrt(N). Its empty cell is exactly

    C0={1} union {p:sqrt(N)<p<=N, p not dividing q}.

Write L for the number of these primes and Q=#S_N. For any partition P set

    E(P)=sum_(C in P)|sum_(n in C)a(n)|^2/|C|.

Cauchy gives |M(N)|<=sqrt(Q E(P)); the cell C0 alone contributes

    (L-1)^2/(L+1)=L-3+4/(L+1).                                (R11)

Refinement cannot reduce E, by applying Cauchy inside each old cell. Every refinement of this complete small-prime observation has the same lower certificate price.

Square-divisor expansion gives Q=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N), with kappa_q=(6/pi^2)product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0. Also binomial(2m,m)>=4^m/(2m+1), and each prime contributes at most 2m to its prime factorization: its valuation is at most the number of powers <=2m. Hence binomial(2m,m)<=(2m)^(pi(2m)), proving pi(N)>>N/log N. Subtracting sqrt N and the fixed ramified set gives L>>_q N/log N. Consequently

    sqrt(Q E(P))>>_q N/sqrt(log N).                           (R12)

This is a lower bound for the numeric right side of an upper certificate, not for |M|. In particular E(P)<<N^(2gamma-1+epsilon) for every epsilon fails for this partition and its refinements whenever gamma<1. The current strict first-gain energy threshold is 2gamma11-1=.7497080728; the author's .74970 was the illustrative gamma=.87485.

Coarsening across small-prime patterns, retaining signed cross-cell terms, unrelated syndromes and nonprincipal phase cancellations are not excluded. One principal character already blocks a proposed theorem applying this same positive certificate to every character. G103/G117's full energy and fiber costs, G145/G162's coherent terminal structure and G165's positive critical floor are related ancestry, not identical assumptions. Newly accepted [restricted research revision] G167 concerns GLOBAL P>=ell ell^* with constrained integer-offset support. Here Q times the cell-constant orthogonal projection is indeed a global majorant, but its cell blocks need not have that support: the empty cell joins widely separated primes. Conversely G167 does not exclude arbitrary bounded row degree, general prime dilations or proved source-only inequalities. No broader positive-method impossibility is inferred by label alone.
title: 5. D3/S16: the conditional-square certificate really is too costly

statement:
## A. Higher arity: a paid bridge already exists, and the positive hard cell remains

This section credits W48/R6 and W01/W35; its identity is not new. Put a=mu chi, h=chi, a*h=delta_1, m=a 1_(n<=U), u=a-m. For fixed k>=2 and an unramified prime p, let q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p and b_p=q_p*h. The exact identity is

    q_p^{*(k-1)}*a
      =u^{*k}*b_p^{*(k-1)}
       +sum_(j=1)^k (-1)^(j+1) binom(k,j)
          m^{*j}*q_p^{*(k-j)}*b_p^{*(j-1)}.             (A1)

All stars are Dirichlet convolution; the j=1 term has b_p^0=delta_1. Without the repeated q_p factor, principal cofactor powers h^{*(j-1)} have remaining poles for j>=3, so the old single mean-zero row estimate cannot simply be reused.

For fixed k and U=X^((1-delta)/k), delta>0 fixed, every restoration product is <=U^k=X^(1-delta). The Dirichlet series B_p(s)=P_p(s)L(s,chi), P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-s), is entire. For each fixed j, the Gaussian convolution of b_p^{*j} has Mellin integrand exp(tau s^2/2)B_p(s)^j. Moving to any fixed negative line gives arbitrary power decay in its scale; the standard polynomial growth on fixed vertical strips is dominated by the Gaussian. Coefficient counts and finitely many p-shifts are polynomial. Thus all restoration fields in (A1) are smaller than any chosen power of X on the full real shell. This is precisely the existing fixed-order restoration, with constants depending on k, delta, p, q and the requested power. No growing-k version is inferred.

Let R_k=u^{*k}*b_p^{*(k-1)}. For principal chi, take n equal to a product of k distinct unramified primes, each in [X^(1/k),2^(1/k)X^(1/k)]. For large X each exceeds U. Every nonzero factorization into k long factors must put one prime in each factor and leave cofactor 1. Therefore

    R_k(n)=(-1)^k k!.                                  (A2)

There are order X/log^k X such unordered products, by fixed-proportion prime counts; all lie in [X,2X]. The fixed Gaussian is bounded below on their full shell, so this selected actual signed sector has norm at least a positive constant times X/log^k X. At the same time, Omega(n)<k makes R_k(n)=0. Increasing fixed arity really removes the lower-degree cells, including the old semiprimes when k>=3, but moves a linear-exponent same-sign cell to degree k. This only blocks paying that selected sector separately. It does not lower-bound the whole R_k, its Gaussian field, or M. It is a source test of the coarse estimate, not a new return theorem or a universal higher-order obstruction.

Prime-counting input: [Selberg, 1949, theorem (1.1), printed p.305](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf). The passage from theta(x)~x to fixed-proportion prime counts is partial summation. No growing-k uniformity is claimed.

statement:
### The exact obstruction to a free overlap transfer

Using the same physical weighted shell norm as current-proof G28, absolute Minkowski on F_t costs

    sum_d Nd^(1-2a),

which diverges for every a<=1. Truncating at Nd<=sqrt(X) costs X^(1-a), cancelling the gain X^a and yielding only X (logarithms at the boundary). Uniform local Hilbert norms do not remove this arithmetic restriction cost. A scalar phase has correlations int_I exp(it log(Nd/Ne))dt, a sinc kernel, not independent-prime orthogonality. Equal norms are fully coherent, and nearby log norms have large overlap.

There is a stable attenuated equivalence, which identifies precisely the easy case. Put

    F_(tau,t)(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1-2tau+it) F_K(X/Nd²).

For fixed a+tau>1, both this convolution and its Dirichlet inverse are bounded on the global weighted shell norm. Their absolute constants are at most

    sum_d Nd^(-(2a+2tau-1))=zeta_K^S(2a+2tau-1),

with the inverse using mu_K(d)chi2(d)Nd^(1-2tau+it). These bounds are uniform for real t. They also hold for a Hilbert-valued t-family. Their Mellin numerator lies in Re(2s-1+2tau)>1 for Re(s)>a. Thus the attenuated family has a safe numerator but the same arithmetic exponent problem as F_K. Strictly crossing the threshold costs tau>c; equality is not covered. This is an exact counterpart of the older W26 shifted-reciprocal safe-region equivalence, with a different square-dilation exponent.

For the unattenuated phase family the denominator-only return is a real addition to F25.E/N28's noncommon-multiplier idea: it moves an auxiliary arithmetic L-function without moving the zeta denominator. The sufficient moment is not weaker in its required power. It may permit a better coupled period estimate; it does not inherit one.

statement:
### R39-C. The fixed-line reciprocal bound is proved after that step

For nonprincipal ordinary chi, periodic partial sums A_chi(x) are
O_q(1), so Abel summation continues L=s integral_1^infinity
A_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt to Re s>0 and gives a polynomial upper bound.
For principal chi, write A_chi(t)=ct+E(t), E=O_q(1). Then

    L(s)=c*s/(s-1)+s integral_1^infinity E(t)t^(-s-1)dt.

Consequently P=L in the nonprincipal case and P=(s-1)L in the
principal case are holomorphic with polynomial upper growth on
every closed positive real-part strip. In the principal case
P(1)=c>0. All imprimitive factors remain; their zeros have real
part 0 and do not intrude on this domain.

Assume the zero-free conclusion already obtained above: Re s>h,
h>0. Fix h<b<2. At center 2+it choose outer radius
R_0=2-(h+b)/2 and inner radius r_0=2-b. The outer disk stays in
Re s>h; its positive gap is (b-h)/2. The regularized P is
holomorphic and nonzero there. Choose a local log f=log P whose
center imaginary part is in [-pi,pi]. The Euler product on Re s=2
bounds L above and away from zero. Together with the regularizing
factor this gives |f(2+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)). The polynomial upper
bound for P gives sup Re f=O(log(2+|t|)) on the disk.

Here is the quantitative log estimate. Choose positive
M>max(0,sup Re f), of size O(log(2+|t|)), and set g=M-f. Then Re g>0.
The map (g-g(center))/(g+conj(g(center))) takes the disk to the unit
disk and vanishes at its center. Schwarz's inequality bounds its
modulus by r_0/R_0 on the inner disk. Hence

    |g| <= (R_0+r_0)/(R_0-r_0) |g(center)|,
    |f| <= C_(h,b,q) log(2+|t|).

This proves |1/P(b+it)|<=C(2+|t|)^K. For principal chi multiply
by |b+it-1| to recover 1/L. Compact low heights are harmless.
The same fixed disks bound every point b<=Re s<=2, uniformly in
height. No Phragmen--Lindelof premise, conjectural reciprocal bound,
or conductor-uniform estimate has entered this argument. The
author's strip here must be understood as a fixed real-part strip
with all heights; the disk proof supplies exactly that bound.

Mellin inversion starts on Re s=2, where the Dirichlet series is
absolutely convergent. Shift to b. The integrand is holomorphic,
including at the principal pole's reciprocal zero. Horizontal sides
vanish because exp(-tau*t^2/2) beats the just-proved polynomial,
uniformly across b<=Re s<=2. Thus

    F(z)=(1/(2pi)) integral_R exp(tau*(b+it)^2/2)
                         exp((b+it)z)/L(b+it,chi)dt.     (R39.7)

For z=u+iv, completing the square gives
-tau*t^2/2-tv=-(tau/2)(t+v/tau)^2+v^2/(2tau).
The shifted Gaussian integral of (1+|t|)^K is bounded by
C_(tau,K)(1+|v|)^K. This proves R39.3 **for all v**, not just on
a fixed complex strip. It therefore supports the growing Cauchy
disks used in R39.4. All fixed derivatives follow by polynomial
factors of b+it under this same integral.

The possible circularity is resolved in the correct order:
interpolation first proves an improved real exponent; R39.6 first
proves the corresponding zero-free domain; only then does this disk
argument improve the complex bound for the next step.
title: R39-C. The fixed-line reciprocal bound is proved after that step

statement:
## T01. Quantitative fixed-factor division — PROVED

**Provenance:** SA Part I §§3–6, (S5)–(S10); SB §2, (N1); BA R1; BB R02. The merged proof is the dimension-free disk argument; SA's longer circle/Blaschke argument is compatible and superseded here.

### Disk lemma

Let `g` be holomorphic near the closed disk `Omega=D(c,R)`, with `m=|g(c)|>0` and `M>=sup_Omega |g|`. Suppose `D(z,r)` lies in `Omega`, and `U` is a holomorphic map near the smaller closed disk into a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Then
\[
\|U(z)\|^2\le
M^{-2}(M/m)^{2R^2/r^2}
\frac1{\pi r^2}\int_{D(z,r)}\|g(w)U(w)\|^2\,dA(w).
\tag{T01.1}
\]
The constant is independent of the vector dimension.

**Proof.** Put `u=log(M/|g|)`. It is nonnegative and locally integrable, including at zeros of `g`. The submean inequality for `log|g|`, integrated over radii about `c`, gives
\[
\int_\Omega u\,dA\le\pi R^2\log(M/m).
\]
If `U(z)=0` the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise choose a unit linear functional `ell` with `|ell(U(z))|=||U(z)||`. The logarithmic submean inequality for `ell(U)` gives
\[
\log\|U(z)\|^2
\le \operatorname{Avg}_{D(z,r)}\log\|gU\|^2
-2\log M+2\operatorname{Avg}_{D(z,r)}u.
\]
Use the preceding integral bound and concavity of logarithm, then exponentiate. Discrete zeros are harmless for the area integrals; the scalar identically-zero case cannot occur under the choice of `ell`. This proves the assertion without division at a zero. ∎

### Polynomial-height consequence

Suppose `F` is fixed and entire, has polynomial growth on every fixed vertical strip, and has a positive uniform lower bound on one fixed right-hand vertical line. For `s0=sigma+it` in a buffered strip, take a fixed small disk about `s0` and a larger fixed-radius disk anchored on that right-hand line. In (T01.1), `m` is bounded below and `M<<T^B`, `T=2+|t|`. Consequently
\[
\|U(s_0)\|^2\ll T^C\sup_{|s-s_0|\le r}\|F(s)U(s)\|^2.
\tag{T01.2}
\]
A completed vector estimate with arithmetic exponent `X^rho` therefore retains that exponent after extraction. The larger disk need only be a domain for `F`; only the smaller disk requires holomorphy and bounds for `U`.

Take `F(s)=L^S(3s-1,xi)`, where `xi` is the fixed nontrivial angular Hecke character. Entire continuation, fixed-strip polynomial growth, and the fixed-conductor functional equation are among the source inputs. The absolutely convergent Euler product gives the required lower bound on a right-hand line. For moving finite deletions,
\[
L^{(Sh)}(3s-1,\xi)=F(s)E_h(s),\qquad
E_h(s)=\prod_{p\mid h,\,p\notin S}(1-\xi(p)Q_p^{1-3s}).
\]
On `Re s>=a>1/2`, for every `delta>0`,
\[
|E_h(s)|+|E_h(s)|^{-1}\ll_{a,S,\delta}q_h^\delta.
\tag{T01.3}
\]
Indeed `|xi(p)Q_p^{1-3s}|<=Q_p^{-(3a-1)}<1`. For sufficiently large prime norms each local factor or inverse is at most `Q_p^delta`; the finitely many smaller primes contribute a fixed constant. Multiply over distinct primes only. This costs a subpower of the physical row norm as well because the conductor radical divides the row.

If the completed estimate is given on every fixed vertical line, obtain the local strip bound by choosing two fixed neighboring lines, scalarizing the finite row vector against an arbitrary unit functional, and applying three-lines after division by a sufficiently high power of `C+s`. FD (59) permits the strip maximum principle with no uncontrolled height growth. Recover the vector norm by taking the supremum over unit functionals. This does not introduce a dimension factor or replace a sum by a sum of rowwise suprema. Cauchy estimates give any fixed number of spectral derivatives on a smaller strip.

Thus completed and uncompleted means, with arbitrary positive exponent losses and every fixed buffer, have the same arithmetic exponent. A Lipschitz dependence of that exponent on `Re s` is handled by choosing the local radius inside the allocated loss.

**Limits:** separate holomorphy is essential; the lemma cannot prove holomorphy of `1/zeta` from a holomorphic product. It does not create a missing period realization, extend a primitive-current estimate to a missing ray component, handle a moving angular character without uniform hypotheses, or remove a gamma factor with exponential height behavior. [restricted research revision]'s gamma removal remains a necessary inherited step.
title: T01. Quantitative fixed-factor division — PROVED

## 2. An actual signed global asymptotic

For d>=1 put

    delta(d)=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|d) p/(p+1).

The elementary squarefree count, uniformly for real T>=1, is

    sum_(g<=T; (g,d)=1) mu(g)^2
       =delta(d)T+O(2^omega(d) sqrt(T)).              (5)

Indeed mu(g)^2=sum_(h^2|g)mu(h); counting the remaining integers coprime to d costs O(2^omega(d)) per h<=sqrt(T), and the absolutely convergent h^(-2) main term has a sqrt(T) truncation error. Partial summation gives

    sum_(g>T; (g,d)=1) mu(g)^2/g^(2r)
       =delta(d)T^(1-2r)/(2r-1)
        +O_r(2^omega(d)T^(1/2-2r)).                  (6)

In(4) write n=ga,m=gb with (a,b)=1. A nonzero term has a,b,g squarefree and g coprime to abq; then mu(ga)mu(gb)=mu(a)mu(b)mu(g)^2. Both n,m>N mean g>N/min(a,b). Applying(6) proves

    ||R_N||_2^2 = C_r(q) N^(1-2r)
                    +O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)),          (7)

where the absolutely convergent, signed arithmetic constant is

    C_r(q)= 2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      *sum_((a,b)=1; (ab,q)=1)
        mu(a)mu(b)delta(abq) min(a,b)^(2r-1)/(ab)^(2r).

Here r and q are fixed. To verify the error without hiding a second large-parameter limit, first restrict min(a,b)<=N. The error sum is bounded by

    N^(1/2-2r) sum_(a,b)
       2^omega(abq) min(a,b)^(2r-1/2)/(ab)^(2r).

This converges for r>=2: after a<=b, use 2^omega(n)<=C n^(1/4) twice and sum b first, obtaining a convergent O(sum_a a^(1-2r)). For min(a,b)>N the actual sum and the corresponding proposed main term are both O_(q,r)(N^(2-4r)), smaller than the displayed error. Thus no growing-divisor uniformity is assumed in(7).

The first exact Fourier band(2), Parseval and(5) show

    C_r(q)>=2 delta(q)(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1)>0.          (8)

For clarity, partial summation evaluates its squared norm as

    2 sum_(N<k<=2N; (k,q)=1)mu(k)^2/k^(2r)
     =2delta(q)(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1) N^(1-2r)
        +O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)).

Consequently the global energy is genuinely of order N^(1-2r) for the actual arithmetic source, even after using all signs. It depends on q and r, but not on which character modulo q is chosen with the required parity. In the complete-period norm the character phases have cancelled exactly. This is a proved source estimate and a substantive limitation of this specific proposed replacement, not an artificial complex-coefficient countermodel.

The tempting remainder in(7) gains a half power. That is exactly the formal energy gain that a c=1/4 return would need below. However subtracting C_r(q)N^(1-2r) from an energy destroys the available positivity comparison with its restriction to an arc. The next result rules out implementing this subtraction by any fixed finite normalized scale filter of the actual source.

statement:
### D1a. Explicit isolated-root lemma

Let Z(z)=1+A z+R(z), with R(z)=sum_(k>=2)c_k z^k a polynomial, sum|c_k|<=B, |A|>=8, and lambda=B/|A|^2<=1/8. Then Z has exactly one zero, counted with multiplicity, in |z|<2/|A|. This zero alpha is simple and satisfies

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A| <= |alpha| <= (1+2lambda)/|A|.      (D1.2)

If B=0 this is immediate from alpha=-1/A. Otherwise, on |z|=2/|A|,

    |1+Az|>=1,    |R(z)|<=B|z|^2<=4lambda<=1/2.

Rouche's theorem gives exactly one zero in the disk. On the circle centered at -1/A with radius 2lambda/|A|, the linear part has modulus 2lambda, whereas

    |R(z)| <= lambda(1+2lambda)^2 <=25lambda/16 <2lambda.

The smaller disk therefore contains that same unique simple zero. Both estimates use |z|<1, justified by |A|>=8. This proves D1.2. In particular alpha is the unique nearest zero to the origin; all remaining zeros have modulus at least 2/|A|.

Define the exact polynomial

    Q(z)=Z(z)/(1-z/alpha),    Q(0)=1.

The factorization is exact, not a truncated series division. Reverse triangle inequalities and D1.2 give

    |A|/2 <= |1+1/alpha| <= 2|A|,
    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)| <= |Z(-1)| <= 2|A||Q(-1)|.         (D1.3)

For example the lower bound follows from |1/alpha|-1>=(4/5)|A|-1>=|A|/2. The upper bound follows from 1+(4/3)|A|<=2|A|.

For real A>0 and real coefficients, the unique zero is real by conjugation. D1.2 then makes it negative. This applies to all principal characters. Complex characters require no positivity for the isolated-root lemma, but their root need not lie on the negative real axis.
title: D1a. Explicit isolated-root lemma

## 5. Strongest objections and decisive limitations

**Does adaptive mark dependence defeat ([restricted research revision].4)?** It defeats the older argument if one merely asserts that a selected set commutes with mark Fourier transform. Here the selector need not commute: its support is contained in the proven row-only set E_D by ([restricted research revision].1). Positive squared Fourier masses can first be enlarged to that set. Only then are the two mark Plancherel identities used. This is precisely the previously unproved conductor-count adapter mentioned at JN immediately before its second-mean discussion and excluded from JNR6's mark-independent scope.

**Do primitive-conductor cancellations, squares or natural zeros defeat it?** Squares are the reason for the sqrt(QD) count: they are all included, not discarded. Odd row valuations force exponent 1,3 or5 modulo6, so neither cubic mark exponent can cancel them. Canceled factors keep their original natural zero. The zero representative and h divisible by either long prime are absent from U; JNR5 proves that those zero-kernel frequencies cannot hold the missing tensor mass in this box. A good finite principal character is included at D=1. Its small NATIVE TENSOR NORM FRACTION does not mean that its signed contribution to H is paid.

**Does this prohibit a signed orbit reduction?** No. JN22--24/JNR9 already provide an exact kernel-invariant orbit projection which can discard tensor norm while preserving its kernel pairing. ([restricted research revision].4) is a restriction on coordinatewise low-conductor NORM approximation of the actual unprojected tensor, even with mark-adaptive coordinates. It does not apply to a new orbit-weighted tensor, an unbounded-lift reparameterization, or an argument that directly controls a small signed pairing without approximating the tensor. These are the legitimate directions to pursue; their moving weights and return costs must still be proved. The live residual after the first approach is signed averaging allowing conductor at least on the Z^(.006-o(1)) scale, or a controlled orbit recombination, not a missing bound on a few principal frequencies.

To test the tempting but invalid inference that a small low-conductor norm fraction already buys the .004 physical saving, a coarse complete Cauchy calculation can be made. For the fully recombined all-g tensor, |W(R,P,P')| is bounded by O(G^2) times the original two rooted mark coefficients and original profile norms, so ||W||_2<=C G^2 sqrt(K) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2). The set in ([restricted research revision].4) has at most O(N^3 sqrt(D)) eligible coordinates by ([restricted research revision].3). Kernel Cauchy and ([restricted research revision].4) give the following deliberately coarse certificate

    |C_low| <= C G^2 K N^3 sqrt(D)
                       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig,  ([restricted research revision].13)

after summing O(N^2) original prime pairs. Its ratio to GKN is G N^2 sqrt(D). Even D=1 is not paid by this crude procedure. This is solely an UPPER-BOUND METHOD calculation; no lower bound for C_low or H follows. A smaller set from the cubic conductor restrictions might improve it, but ([restricted research revision].13) is enough to reject the claimed automatic .004 return. We do not substitute this certificate for a new analytic result.

**Can sparse-graph coverage finish the far set?** The new adapter supplies no saving in B beyond JSR20. For a complete bipartite prime set with m,m' vertices, any cover by graphs of maximum degree B requires at least max(m,m')/B layers, simply by counting all neighbours of one vertex. Summing ([restricted research revision].8) in absolute value across such a cover reproduces the full degree price; it does not recover the cancellations between layers. This exact combinatorial obstruction is not an H lower bound. The remaining original-prime form is C_far-C_E on every frozen short pair, with the same heights, roots, projectors and core; it has not been estimated by the present work.
title: 5. Strongest objections and decisive limitations

statement:
## 5. A quantitative failed-inequality counterexample

This section tests the stronger, false proposed assertion that the
unit-core sector is always \(O(Z^\epsilon K B S(N,L))\) for **every**
coefficient allowed by B2.29. Its coefficient choice below is not
the physical beta. It proves a limitation on that uniform method,
not a lower bound for the physical H sum.

Choose a fixed nonzero nonnegative smooth row profile supported in
\([A_-,1]\), with upper support endpoint 1. Its SQ zero-frequency
coefficient is nonzero. Indeed one-dimensional Fourier inversion
on a line, with M's additive pairing and self-dual measure, gives

\[
\int_0^\infty\Omega(u^2)\,du
=\int_0^\infty\Phi(r^2)\,dr,
\qquad
c_\Omega=\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt3}
\int_0^\infty\Phi(r^2)\,dr>0.                    \tag{SC11}
\]

For example, integrate the radial two-dimensional transform along
the real frequency line. The inverse transform in the perpendicular
coordinate evaluates the original radial function on its real line;
the factor \(2/\sqrt3\) in the measure cancels the corresponding
factor in the additive pairing. Schwartz decay justifies that
one-dimensional inversion. This proves SC11 without assigning a
sign to the full oscillatory transform.

Take any fixed nonvanishing unit-trivial principal-square sector;
the primitive principal fixed-S factor is already a permitted
example. Then \(|C_{\Phi,S}|>0\). Let \(\ell\) be a rational prime
\(\ell\equiv1\pmod3\), avoiding D. There are exactly two prime
ideals of norm \(\ell\), each with Möbius value -1. Since ideal
norms are integers,

\[
\mathfrak M(\ell;D)-\mathfrak M(\ell-\tfrac12;D)
=-\frac2\ell.
\quad\text{Hence}
\quad
\max\{|\mathfrak M(\ell;D)|,
|\mathfrak M(\ell-\tfrac12;D)|\}\ge\frac1\ell.
                                                               \tag{SC12}
\]

For each arbitrarily large such \(\ell\), choose the endpoint
\(S_0\in\{\ell-1/2,\ell\}\) attaining this lower bound, and set
\(K=S_0^2\). Thus
\(\sqrt K|\mathfrak M(S_0;D)|\ge1/2\), for large \(\ell\).
This exact jump is not a conjectural lower bound for Mertens sums
and uses no zero near the boundary of I-HECKE.

Let \(W\ge0\) be fixed, smooth, bounded by one, supported in a fixed
prime-column annulus and positive on a subannulus. Choose
\(a(1)=1\) and
\(\beta(n,1)=1\) on good primes in the fixed ray class of SC9,
zero otherwise. This satisfies every B2.29 independence condition;
the smooth factor is \(W(q_n/A)\). In particular \(v_p=W(q_p/A)\)
is nonnegative. No coefficient depends on the row or mark.

For clarity, the prime-count input follows from the fixed finite
ray-character part of the supplied I-HECKE hypothesis. Finite ray
orthogonality and Mellin inversion of \(-L'/L\), shifted to any
fixed line between \(b_0\) and 1, give
\(\sum_{p\ {\rm in\ class}}W(q_p/A)\log q_p=c_W A+o(A)\),
with \(c_W>0\); B0.14 prices the logarithmic derivatives and smooth
height tails. Prime powers contribute \(O(A^{1/2+\epsilon})\).
Consequently \(\sum_p W(q_p/A)\asymp A/\log A\), and the same
argument applied to a positive subannulus gives the needed lower
bound. This uses only finitely many fixed Hecke characters, but is
explicitly placed under I-HECKE here; it is not inferred from the
principal zeta reciprocal alone.

The bracket in SC10 is therefore
\(\gg A^2/(\log A)^2\), since its subtracted diagonal is only
\(O(A/\log A)\). Combining with SC12 yields

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal M_{\{1\}}^{\rm prime}(S_0)|
\gg_{\Phi,S,W}\frac{A^2}{(\log A)^2}.}
                                                               \tag{SC13}
\]

This lies in the narrow short-divisor corridor. For any fixed
\(\kappa_0>0\) and \(0<\delta<0.006322\), define Z along this
sequence by \(K=Z^{\kappa_0}\) and set
\(A=Z^{\kappa_0+\delta}\). Then \(K<NB=A<KZ^{0.006322}\),
\(B=L=1\), and \(S(A,1)\asymp A\). Put \(Y=A/K\). For large Z,
\(1\le A_0Y<c_*A\), with the original fixed endpoint constants.
All selected primes exceed \(S_0\), and \(J=1\) satisfies SQ1 and
lies below \(A^2/K^{2-b}\) for every fixed \(0<b<1\).

For any \(\epsilon<\delta\), SC13 divided by
\(Z^\epsilon K S(A,1)\) tends to infinity as
\(Z^{\delta-\epsilon}/(\log Z)^2\). SQ's error is
\(O(Z^\epsilon KA)\); choosing a smaller epsilon shows that the
exact unit-square-class fragment with these auxiliary coefficients
also has the SC13 scale. This does not give a lower bound for the
sum of all dual classes.

Likewise SC7 shows that its added complementary tail has this
scale, since the transfer error is only
\(O(Z^\epsilon\sqrt K A)\). Thus an argument that declares the
added tail negligible merely because each **complete** dual sum
vanishes is quantitatively false. The example includes the full
finite s cutoff, every z, every square power, and both preprojections.
title: 5. A quantitative failed-inequality counterexample

## R5. Wildcard S23: actual compact certificate, with the all-scale premise visible

The source is exactly G128's, rather than a free finite prefix. With delta indicating principal chi, r=delta phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), b(t)=A(e^t)-r e^t, periodicity gives |b|<=q. The function

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s

is holomorphic for Re s>0 and has exactly the L-zeros there with their multiplicities. At the principal pole its removable value is r/2, nonzero. The nonprincipal case must not receive an s-1 factor. The literal causal source is

    f(t)=b(t)                              nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r e^-t+b(t)-2 integral_0^t e^(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                          principal.

Thus F=Laplace(f), |f|<=C_q=1+3q. This follows by multiplying the exact identity L/s=r/(s-1)+Laplace(b). Imprimitive factors and natural zeros are retained. For Re s>=sigma0>0,

    |F-F_T|<=C_q e^(-sigma0 T)/sigma0,
    |F'|<=C_q/sigma0^2.                              (R5.1)

Integrating |f| and t|f| proves both estimates, uniformly at all heights on that half-plane. For a convex compact cell with center z and radius d, a certified value v of F_T(z), error epsilon, and the strict inequality

    |v|>epsilon+C_q e^(-sigma0 T)/sigma0
                       +(C_q/sigma0^2)d             (R5.2)

give a nonzero lower bound throughout the cell. This pays the whole source tail, point error and interpolation; a successful finite grid by itself would not do so. Finite integrals use the actual finite character table and its jumps at log n. Computable rectangles and parameters, including every displayed rational target gamma, admit certified interval evaluations; no efficiency estimate is asserted.

If F has no zero on a given compact K, its minimum modulus m_K>0. Taking each of the three errors <=m_K/8 forces eventual success, with |v|>=3m_K/4. Conversely the sound test cannot succeed on a compact containing a zero. The procedure is therefore a semidecision algorithm for zero-free compacts. The increasing K_m={gamma+1/m<=Re s<=m+2, |Im s|<=m} exhaust Re s>gamma. Success for **every m**, for each fixed ordinary chi at a single common gamma, is equivalent to zero exclusion there. ## G163. Exact native Schur and four-cycle bills

These independent audits clarify complete costs, rather than provide
an arithmetic saving. Freeze an actual finite native-H packet and its two
independent heights. Keep the Eisenstein primary/fixed-ray/six-unit/bad-place
data, distinct-rational-norm long primes, both orientations, every ordered
short pair including equality, bounded complex h, rational gcd screen,
both projectors, natural zeros, all profiles and CRT phases.
The source contract is [[restricted research revision] §1](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), with the
corrected matrix convention in [G75 review R10–R11](../[private research revision]/wild46-review/report.md).

Specifically, `v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P)`, `w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P')`,
and the scalar sum `sum v_P K_PP' conjugate(w_P')` is `H=w* T v`
with `T=K^T`. The rooted marks are in v,w **once**. Every other original
factor is in T. This explicit reviewer convention controls the author's
compressed Section5 wording that could double-count the roots.
The raw target is `B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2)`, where
`B0=G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig`, K0 is the original row parameter and
P_orig the actual profile/component costs. Apply `N^(-1)G^(-2)` once
afterward. Full heights, tails, components and other branches remain due.

For a partition `T=[T_R,T_E]`, `v=(u,z)`, let Pi be the output projection
onto ran T_E. Then, exactly,

    ||Tv||^2 = ||(I-Pi)T_R u||^2 + ||Pi T_R u+T_E z||^2,
    S=T_R*(I-Pi)T_R=A-B D^dagger B*,
    A=T_R*T_R, B=T_R*T_E, D=T_E*T_E.

The singular case follows from ker D=ker T_E, B annihilating this kernel,
and `T_E D^dagger T_E*=Pi`. Thus S>=0 and the fill-in is bounded by A.
For `D_lambda=D+lambda I`, lambda>0, there is also the exact completion

    v*(T*T)v = u*(A-B D_lambda^(-1)B*)u
      +(z+D_lambda^(-1)B*u)*D_lambda(z+D_lambda^(-1)B*u)
      -lambda ||z||^2.

A small Schur term alone does not bound the full source: z is fixed,
not freely minimized. The projection has norm 1, while an inverse
representation must pay its own spectral distance. For the synthetic
matrix `[[1,1,1],[0,e,-e]]`, e!=0, eliminating columns 2,3 makes S=0,
yet the source u=1,z=0 has energy 1 in the completion. This is an algebra
diagnostic, not an evaluated native packet. A sufficient OPEN-SC is the
sum of both displayed squared norms <=`B0^2(||u||^2+||z||^2)` with all
original uniformities. It is the full source bill after elimination.
Prior [G107](../[private research revision]/wild51-integration.md) and U-VARIATIONAL retain credit.

For two distinct input columns j,k, put
`b_i=conjugate(T_ij)T_ik`, `s_jk=sum_i|b_i|`,
`eta_i=b_i/|b_i|` only on nonzero entries, and
`psi_jk=sum_(i<l)|b_i||b_l||eta_i-eta_l|^2` over active pairs.
Expansion gives

    |(T*T)_jk|^2 = s_jk^2-psi_jk,
    ||T||^2 <= max_j [sum_i|T_ij|^2
                         +sum_(k!=j)sqrt(s_jk^2-psi_jk)],
    ||T||^4 <= sum_j (sum_i|T_ij|^2)^2
                         +sum_(j!=k)(s_jk^2-psi_jk).

The phase is the four-edge product
`conjugate(T_ij)T_ik T_lj conjugate(T_lk)` divided by its modulus.
Natural-zero entries contribute zero without division. The Hermitian
dilation is bipartite on two separate mark spaces, so it has no triangular
cycle even if the numerical labels coincide. Transported unitary gauges
preserve this four-cycle invariant; fixing source vectors while gauging
the matrix changes H. Short-core interference must remain inside each T entry.

An arithmetic bound on the complete Gram-row expression by B0 squared,
or on the complete fourth-moment expression by B0 to the fourth power,
would suffice. The diagonal and every significant coherent component
remain. A few frustrated cycles or a constant local deficit do not supply
a power saving. The 2-by-2 unit-entry formula `2+2|cos(Phi/2)|` is already
G75, and [W40's retained phase-length scope](../[private research revision]/reviewed-library-integration.md)
remains relevant. No native phase values were numerically evaluated here.

## 4. Literal arithmetic returns and their exact limits

For a fixed ordinary character chi with its presented-modulus zeros, set
a_n=mu(n)chi(n). On Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F(u)exp(-su)du=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).     (R14)

The left tail is fully paid. For a general A_b sequence, if
u<=-max(tau b,0), then for v>=0 the function
exp(bv)g_tau(v-u) is decreasing in v. Thus
|F(u)|<=A_b g_tau(u) there. The right tail supplied by Theorem A is
integrable on every compact subset of Re s>gamma after selecting a smaller
fixed epsilon. The same domination handles all s derivatives. The transform
is consequently holomorphic on that half-plane.

Multiply R14 by L and continue from Re s>1. An L zero in the claimed domain
would force the product to vanish whereas exp(tau s^2/2) never vanishes.
The principal pole at one is treated meromorphically and is removable in
the reciprocal; it is not a prohibited zero. This proves the ordinary
return for 0<gamma<1. It uses the complete coefficient, not a selected
arithmetic submask or a probability law with different zeros.

For a fixed finite-order, trivial-infinity Eisenstein Hecke character psi,
the literal coefficients are mu_K(a)psi(a) over nonzero integral ideals.
The presented ray modulus, including any fixed deleted primes, remains.
The retained W39 lattice argument has the required scope: the Eisenstein
lattice is Euclidean, so ideals are principal with six generators; the
character weight is periodic modulo the fixed modulus and invariant under
units. Complete residue cells have mean zero for nonprincipal psi and the
actual positive coprimality mean in the principal case. Boundary cells
give O_f(sqrt(X)+1). Hence

    sum_(N(a)<=X)psi(a)=c_psi X+O_f(sqrt(X)+1),             (R15)

and the absolute ideal count is O(X). Abel summation provides the needed
meromorphic continuation in Re s>1/2, with only the principal pole at one.
The identical transform argument therefore works for gamma>1/2. It proves
a conclusion for each fixed member whose observation hypothesis is supplied.
It does not supply angular, infinite-order or growing-conductor uniformity,
nor a family conclusion from the zeta field alone.

For literal f3, retain all prime powers and its special prime 3:

    D3(s)=sum_n f3(n)n^-s=B(s)/zeta(s),
    B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^-s)^(-2)(1-3^-s)^(-2)
          product_(p>=5)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)^2.            (R16)

The p>=5 factors start in degree two. Since 2/sqrt(5)<1, H and 1/H are
analytic, bounded and nonzero on every fixed closed half-plane strictly
right of 1/2. The multiplier B has no zeros in 1/2<Re s<1; its zeros on
Re s=1 are retained. The Mellin transform is exp(tau s^2/2)B(s)/zeta(s).
For gamma>1/2, holomorphy excludes zeta zeros between gamma and one; the
already established zero-free right edge completes the return. This is the
ordinary-zeta consequence, not an automatic character or Hecke-family result.

The full pointwise Gaussian bound immediately gives its full signed square
moment on any dyadic x shell under dx/x. Every mixed piece, prime power and
true diagonal stays in that field. The accepted f3 hard-region obstruction
still prohibits replacing the complete sum by a favorable threshold piece.
It does not obstruct a small-value theorem for the complete field.

All first-gain examples in the author report are conditional. In particular
gamma=.874864 would yield c=.125136 only if the actual observation input
were proved. The arithmetic premises are not consequences of the analytic
sampling theorem, of sign changes alone, or of the already available
buffered bound. No endpoint formalization or kernel replay is supplied here.

### 4.2 Exact squarefree Euler correction and all p shifts

On Re s>1 the literal f_t has Euler product

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.       (4.4)

The product is over primes. Each local polynomial has constant one and zero linear term. Its coefficients g_t therefore satisfy

    Gabs_t(sigma):=sum_n|g_t(n)|n^-sigma<infinity
                                      for every sigma>1/2, (4.5)

for each fixed t. This follows from the absolutely convergent product of the finite local absolute polynomials; ramified local factors are one. No nonvanishing claim about G_t is needed or implied.

For 1<=t<=J the exact coefficient identity is

    v_(p,J)*f_t=b_p^(*t)*v_(p,J-t)*g_t.                   (4.6)

This retains a COMMON filter on the left. It follows from Q_p^t*chi^(*t)=b_p^(*t); it is not a subtraction of estimates obtained with different filters. For t=0 the source is the finite sequence v_(p,J).

Take sigma>1/2 with sigma>=beta_t:=1-1/t. On every real x, (4.2), (4.5) and (4.6) give

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*f_t)(n)|
      <= C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma.    (4.7)

To justify every endpoint, sum only over p^a d<=x, use the bound at y=x/(p^a d)>=1, and replace y^beta_t by y^sigma. The finite shifts have weights binom(J-t,a)p^a and arguments x/p^a, giving exactly the displayed factor. Terms whose argument is below one are empty, not approximated. At t>=3 choose sigma=beta_t>1/2; at t=1,2 choose sigma=1/2+epsilon. This proves the author's individual-color bound and preserves all dependence on fixed J,p,q.

Define a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu^2(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k), k>=1. Finite differences give

    a_k=sum_(t=0)^k(-1)^(k-t)binom(k,t)f_t.

Summing (-1)^k for k<=J gives the exact low-chain combination

    L_J:=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.              (4.8)

Equations (4.7)-(4.8) prove the author's complete common-filter estimate

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*L_J)(n)|
         <<_(p,q,J,epsilon)x^(max(1/2,1-1/J)+epsilon).     (4.9)

It includes every first-J chain sector and every compensator term for all real x. It is a genuine arithmetic estimate, including principal characters; it is not an estimate of an arbitrarily selected signed subsource.

## 4. D3 / S24: a lossless ambient system must pay scale and defect return

For any finite operator A, an exact representation A=alpha P U Q with U unitary and P,Q contractions necessarily has alpha>=||A||. Conversely, alpha=||A|| is achievable by the standard Halmos dilation of C=A/alpha (the zero operator is trivial):

    U_C=[[C,(I-CC*)^(1/2)],[(I-C*C)^(1/2),-C*]],
    P U_C Q=C.                                         (6)

The intertwining C(I-C*C)^(1/2)=(I-CC*)^(1/2)C makes block multiplication prove unitarity. This is standard, not a new dilation theorem; Robinson's primary manuscript gives the construction: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.09329 , Theorems1-2. The application is that the least possible contractive projection normalization is exactly the original operator norm, not an omitted constant. For the actual k-prime coprimality cube it is phi^k. Character diagonal unitary gauges preserve that singular-value cost; ramified zero sites must be removed, not inverted.

A second, different loss arises if one recycles the same finite ambient system. If C is selfadjoint, D=(I-C^2)^(1/2), then U_C=[[C,D],[D,-C]] satisfies U_C^2=I. Therefore

    P U_C^2 Q=I,             C^2=I-D^2.                 (7)

The returned defect channel D^2 is exactly the missing difference. The one-step dilation does NOT preserve powers. In a multiscale interpretation, either keep the full returning defect, insert intermediate physical projections, or construct a genuine power dilation. A fresh-ancilla realization of a product retains the product of all original normalizations; saying that each enlarged step is unitary does not remove it. These statements concern the proposed architecture, not a claim that every larger-system method fails.

For an approximate reconstruction A_tilde with ||A-A_tilde||<=delta, the complete scalar boundary error obeys

    |u* (A-A_tilde)v|<=delta||u||_2||v||_2.              (8)

For a general coefficient/mask matrix W the alternative complete bound is |tr((A-A_tilde)W)|<=||A-A_tilde||_F||W||_F. In either case the ACTUAL W contains all source masks and phases; a low-rank factorization of one gate alone does not estimate W. A source-restricted estimate could be much cheaper and remains eligible. Equations(6)-(8) give a constructive finite representation with its full error budget, but no new detector power.

This rare draw is retained as a useful repair condition. The next substantive step would be an actual source-specific boundary alignment or a cancellation estimate for the entire returning defect channel. Merely refining a one-step unitary realization has no arithmetic benefit. G175's native Cayley work and the earlier indefinite-observer contracts retain their separate source ancestry.
