This discovery-first headroom pass accepts G194-G196 after the frozen
[author development](headroom/report.md), independent
[review](headroom-review/report.md) and [endpoint proof](headroom-review/support.md).
The actual squarefree matrix, all-depth positive price, common-filter
low-chain estimate and full linked-valuation remainder are reconstructed
below. These are ordinary fixed-character results. The complete signed
remainder estimate is OPEN. Current source-relative
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 is unchanged, including its preceding-c10
K license and open F0/ancestry, positive-slot and external-admission duties.

## G194. The literal matrix and its complete positive price

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q with its natural zero extension.
For every real x>=1 use the finite divisor downset

    D_x={n<=x: mu²(n)=1,(n,q)=1}, N=|D_x|.

Order its indices increasingly. Let e be the coordinate of1, v=1-e, and

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(n/d prime), P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.

Every prime-cover path stays in the original downset. Its product is
chi(n/d), and each ordering of the k distinct factors gives one path:

    B^k(d,n)=k!chi(n/d)1_(d|n,omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z, exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).

These are finite polynomial exponentials. The determinant lemma, detZ=1,
gives exactly detR=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n). No zero character value is inverted.
If K=max_(n in D_x)omega(n)>=1, define

    A_k=e^T P^k v=sum_(n in D_x,n>1)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k).

Strict chains correspond to ordered partitions into k nonempty blocks.
For y=lambda-1, the finite resolvent identity and polynomial continuation
through y=0 yield

    det(lambda I-R)
      =y^(N-K-1)[y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k y^(K-k)].

The multiplicity at1 can exceed N-K-1 when a twisted top coefficient
cancels. K=0 means R=(1). The product of j distinct primes is at least
(j+1)!, so K=O(log(2x)/loglog(3x)); this alone bounds no determinant.
The classical ancestry is [Wilf's finite-poset construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408263v1)
and [Vaughan's characteristic calculation](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf).
No full-integer spectral conclusion is imported to this altered support.

Put F_0=1 and F_j=sum_(k=1)^j k!S(j,k). Ordering each block internally,
then concatenating with marked cuts, proves F_j<=2^(j-1)j! for j>=1.
For any sigma>1, split primes at a fixed Y with
R_sigma=sum_(p>Y)p^-sigma<1/4. The tail elementary symmetric function
of degree b is at most R_sigma^b/b!. If a is the number of chosen small
primes, its entire remaining contribution is bounded by a fixed multiple
of sum_b(2R_sigma)^b(a+b)!/b!, which converges. The finitely many small
prime choices therefore prove

    sum_(n squarefree)F_(omega(n)) n^-sigma<infinity,
    P_q(x):=sum_(n in D_x)F_(omega(n)) <<_(q,epsilon)x^(1+epsilon).

This pays ALL depths, including growing depths. For principal chi it is
the permanent of R: each nonidentity permutation cycle is a strict chain
through1. It is also1+sum_k|A_k| in that case. Moreover

    P_q(x)>=|D_x|=delta_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    delta_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.

The density follows directly from mu²(n)=sum_(d²|n)mu(d), paying floors
and the tail of sum d^-2. Hence the full positive price has exact exponent1.
This is not a lower bound for the signed determinant.

Two tempting operator shortcuts also fail in their stated norms.
The unitary diagonal diag(chi(n)) gauges B to the principal matrix, but
changes the closing vector v. Parity diag((-1)^omega(n)) conjugates B to
-B, so ||exp(-B_chi)||_2=||exp(B_1)||_2. The Hermitian part of -B_1 has
a two-dimensional compression with positive eigenvalue sqrt(pi_q(x))/2.
There is no contraction in this Euclidean norm. This says nothing about
a different signed observable or a lower bound for M_chi.

## G195. Every fixed low-chain sector under one common filter

Fix p not dividing q and integer J>=2, independent of x. Define

    Q=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p, v_J=Q^(*J),
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b=Q*chi=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)),
    f_t(n)=mu²(n)t^omega(n)chi(n), f_0=delta1.

b has period pq and mean zero, including principal/imprimitive characters.
Choose D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|); D=p²q suffices.

For any fixed bounded mean-zero periodic b, the full ordered hyperbola
identity proves

    |sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t),
    C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)².

Indeed each t-tuple of product<=x has a coordinate<=Y=x^(1/t).
In inclusion-exclusion with j<t short coordinates and m=t-j, induction
costs C_m x^(1-1/m)[sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^(-1+1/m)]^j,
at most C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t). For j=t the product cutoff is automatic:
the term is the bounded quantity(sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t. All overlaps and real
floors are retained. The recurrence and m!m^(t-m)<=t! prove the stated
constant bound.

The exact Euler correction is

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.

The local linear term vanishes. The absolute coefficient series
Gabs_t(sigma)=sum|g_t(n)|n^-sigma converges for every fixed t and sigma>1/2.
Consequently, for1<=t<=J,

    v_J*f_t=b^(*t)*v_(J-t)*g_t,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_t)(n)|
      <=C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma,
          sigma>1/2, sigma>=1-1/t.

Each finite p^a coefficient is evaluated at x/p^a; arguments below1
contribute zero. All colors on the left use the SAME filter v_J.

The independent review sharpens the two low endpoints without assuming
Euler convergence at1/2. For t=1, g_1 is supported on r² with coefficient
mu(r)chi(r)². For t=2, the local polynomial1-3z²+2z³ has absolute
coefficients dominated by(1-z²)^-3(1-z³)^-2. Thus

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_1)(n)|<=D(1+sqrt p)^(J-1)sqrt x,
    sum_(n<=x)|g_2(n)|/sqrt n
      <=zeta(3/2)²(1+0.5log x)³,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_2)(n)|
      <=3D²zeta(3/2)²(1+sqrt p)^(J-2)sqrt x(1+0.5log x)³.

The second inequality follows by writing the majorant as
sum_(a²c³=n)d_3(a)d_2(c): the c-series converges, and the a-series is
bounded by the cube of a harmonic sum. The periodic two-variable
hyperbola bound is3D²sqrt x. All p shifts remain in these bounds.

Set a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu²(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k). Finite differences
give the complete first-J chain combination

    L_J=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.

Combining ALL colors and their common filter proves, for every real x>=1,

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*L_J)(n)| <<_(p,q,J) x^(1-1/J), J>=3;
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_2*L_2)(n)| <<_(p,q) sqrt x log³(2x).

The exponent for J>=3 has no epsilon loss. This is a complete arithmetic
estimate of the low source, including principal characters.

Growing depth is not free. Splitting primes at t^(1/sigma) proves
logGabs_t(sigma)<<_sigma t^(1/sigma)log(2t) for fixed1/2<sigma<1.
The factorial hyperbola constant, finite p-shift factors and binomial
combination must all be paid, and sigma>=1-1/t still applies. These upper
prices establish no impossibility theorem for a better growing-depth proof.

## G196. The complete linked remainder and its weaker sufficient norm

With0^0=1 define

    W_J(j)=(-1)^j-sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)t^j,
    r_J(n)=mu²(n)chi(n)W_J(omega(n)),
    mu chi=L_J+r_J.

The exact generating function is

    sum_(j>=0)W_J(j)z^j
      =(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!z^(J+1)/[(1+z)prod_(t=1)^J(1-tz)].

In particular W_J(j)=0 for j<=J; for J>=2 its remaining coefficients
have fixed sign(-1)^(J+1), since the denominator reduces to
(1-z²)prod_(t=2)^J(1-tz). Nevertheless |W_J(j)|<=C_J J^j, hence
|r_J(n)|<<_(J,epsilon)n^epsilon. The full factorial representation cost
has disappeared, without removing any chain depth.

Let T_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_J*r_J)(n) and
S_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_J*mu chi)(n). Then

    |S_(p,J)(x)-T_(p,J)(x)| << x^(1-1/J), J>=3,
    |S_(p,2)(x)-T_(p,2)(x)| << sqrt x log³(2x).

For n=p^a m, p not dividing m, m squarefree, j=omega(m), the literal
coefficient is

    chi(p)^a chi(m)[(-p)^a binom(J,a)W_J(j)
                  +(-p)^(a-1)binom(J,a-1)W_J(j+1)].

At a=0 the second term is absent. a=J+1 is retained; only a>J+1
vanishes. Out-of-range binomial coefficients are zero; nonsquarefree m
or ramified factors give zero. These linked valuations cannot be bounded
as arbitrary independent signed subsets.

Fix ONE gamma with1/2<gamma<gamma11 and choose fixed J with
max(1/2,1-1/J)<=gamma. For every fixed chi and a fixed covering pair of
distinct unramified primes, the following complete hypothesis suffices:

    OPEN-L1-CHAIN:
    integral_X^(2X)|T_(p,J)(x)|dx/x
      <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X.

G195 pays the entire difference from S in the same norm. Initially for
Re s>1, ordinary partial summation gives

    P_p(s)^J/L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity S_(p,J)(x)x^(-s-1)dx.

On a compact set Re s>=gamma+delta, choose epsilon<delta/2. Each dyadic
shell, including any fixed s derivative, costs
O((log(2X))^m X^(-delta+epsilon)); the sum converges normally. The finite
initial interval is entire. Therefore the quotient is holomorphic in
Re s>gamma, with every sharp endpoint and filter term retained.

P_p zeros lie on Re s=1. A common nonzero-height zero for two distinct
primes would make logp1/logp2 rational, since character values are roots
of unity. For a nonprincipal character choose one prime with chi(p)!=1
to cover height0. Such a prime exists by factoring a unit integer on
which chi is nontrivial. For principal chi, the pole of L at1 is the
allowed exception. This fixed pair exposes every hypothetical ordinary
zero in Re s>gamma. No growing conductor or uniform height bound is used.

A pointwise T bound implies shell L2, and shell L2 implies shell L1.
This corrects the reversed norm wording at author line376; its original
bytes are retained. No reverse implication or attained norm estimate is
claimed. Both pointwise and complete shell hypotheses remain OPEN.

| Prospective gamma | Fixed J | Paid low exponent | Conditional c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 |7|6/7|.1252|
|5/6|6|5/6|1/6|
|3/4|4|3/4|1/4|

The nearer prospective gain is135091/2500000000=.0000540364. Equality
with the paid low exponent is allowed. The full coarse bound is still
|T_(p,J)(x)|<<x log^(J-1)(2x), since J^omega=d_J on squarefree integers
and every p^a coefficient meets x/p^a. It supplies no first power gain.
Color8's available exponent7/8 misses gamma11 by.0001459636; improving
only that color would leave all higher depths.

For principal chi, the p-free subfamily n=A*l, with A a fixed product of
J primes avoiding pq and l another prime, has nonzero constant residual
coefficient. Its absolute price is at least a constant times x/log x,
using the [ordinary prime bound](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
This obstructs separately paying that projection below exponent1. It
does not lower-bound the full filtered sum, whose linked p valuations
can cancel. Setting J>=K(x) kills the residual below x but changes the
filter with x and makes the paid exponent tend to1; it has no fixed-source
Mellin return under the present estimates.

## Evidence, usefulness and next action

The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves13 original
files,10 source bindings and the preceding raw scorecard. The author and
reviewer stopped and normally released their own scopes. Root read the
full author and review mathematics, helper, receipt and metadata and
reconstructed the consequential arguments. No unchanged helper was rerun;
finite matrix/valuation checks establish only their stated finite identities.

The useful new contract pays every fixed low chain sector under ONE
filter, with a complete all-depth residual and a complete shell-L1 return.
Its determinant, compensation and prime-insertion ancestry are credited
to the prior index and primary sources. Potential1/4 is a conditional
target, with the full signed estimate explicitly unpaid. This pass is
not evidence of a larger c, formalization or external admission.
The next decisive attack must control the entire linked valuation source
or prove a uniform growing-depth estimate together with its moving-filter
return. The direct incumbent same-zero lane remains separately active.

## 6. Actual marks, every completed dyad and both infinite tails

For the embedded subset \(D\), retain exactly
\[
K_D(A)=
\sum_{\substack{U'\mid A\ {\rm in\ complementary\ slots}\\(U',D)=1}}
\omega_{U'}\overline{\eta(U')}V(q_A/(Zq_{U'})).
\tag{XM27}
\]
The symbols \(U'\) and \(u\) are unrelated: the former is a marked product and the latter is the squareful source part. The number of marked tuples dividing \(A\) is divisor-bounded. Also \(q_{U'}/L_D\) lies in a fixed compact multiplicative interval. Hence, for any prescribed small \(\eta>0\),
\[
|K_D(A)|\ll_\eta q_A^\eta E(q_A/N_D),
\tag{XM28}
\]
where \(E\) is nonnegative and decays faster than every power at both endpoints. This follows directly from the original Gaussian and bounded marked weights. In particular there is no separate count by the total complementary slot lengths and no factor \(q_{U'}^{-1/2}\).

On each \(q_A\asymp T\) dyad, (XM8) permits (XM25) with a bounded compact completed window, multiplied by \(T^\eta E_*(T/N_D)\), where \(E_*\) is another two-sided rapid envelope. For fixed \(T\), the number of nonempty pairs of core/cube dyads \(C,N\ge1\), \(CN^3\asymp T\), is \(O(1+\log(2T))\). Their bounded overlap and all unit choices cost only fixed constants or logarithms.

For every fixed \(\alpha>0\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{T=2^j\\j\ge0}}
(1+\log(2T))^B T^\alpha E_*(T/N_D)
\ll_{\alpha,B} N_D^\alpha(1+\log(2N_D))^B
\tag{XM29}
\]
when \(N_D\ge1\). To verify it, write \(T/N_D\) on geometric intervals. Above one use rapid upper-tail decay stronger than \(\alpha+B+2\); below one use rapid lower-tail decay stronger than \(B+2\). The resulting geometric sums converge, uniformly in the fractional position of \(N_D\) between dyads. A power of \(\log(2T)\) is bounded by a power of \(\log(2N_D)\) plus a fixed power of \(|\log(T/N_D)|\), which is absorbed by the same endpoint decay.

The finitely many bounded lower dyads include the unit ideal. The upper dyads are not truncated. Small powers of arbitrarily large \(A\) are absorbed using (XM29), with \(N_D\) polynomial in \(Z\). Source divisor losses contribute only \(Y_D^\eta\). Choose all these losses sufficiently small before fixing the final \(\epsilon\). This proves the full original-profile statement (XM26).

The passage from finite completed truncations agrees with the original field. Indeed, ideal counting and the same rapid envelope give, for every fixed small \(\eta>0\),
\[
\sum_{I,J}\frac{q_{IJ^3}^{\eta}}{\sqrt{q_I}\,q_J}
E(q_Iq_J^3/N_D)
\ll_\eta N_D^{1/2+\eta}\sum_Jq_J^{-5/2}<\infty.
\]
For the inner \(I\)-sum this uses the bound at scale \(N_D/q_J^3\); its subunit scales follow from rapid upper-tail decay. Source labels and physical rows are finite on their original annuli, and the Mellin density is integrable. Thus the original sum is absolutely defined before the sharper row estimates; taking its completed truncations and passing to the limit is legitimate.

All bounds were taken after the exact row calculation. The signed phases and the exact masks remain in the defining field; only their actual coefficient magnitudes were majorized. Thus the argument applies to a restricted linear probe without replacing its defining marks by an unrelated coefficient sequence.

The Mellin integral in (XM9) is now absolutely controlled by
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat W_0(iv)|(1+|v|)^{J_0}\,dv<\infty.
\tag{XM30}
\]
This proves the all-height passage with the original window. Any real inverse completed height appears only as a modulus-one label phase and never needs differentiation. If it is integrated in the original inverse representation, its original rapidly decreasing density remains available. The proof does not create a moving profile depending on the chosen labels.

## 4. A concrete alternating chain and another stage

One allowed chain is

    F_o → S_no F_o=F_n → A_beta F_n
        → (S_gn direct-sum S_gn) A_beta F_n
        = A_beta F_g → R_a A_beta F_g=F_g → A_beta F_g.

It uses a bank, forward smoothing of the whole bank, a paid left inverse, and a further bank. S_h,D_lambda,E_lambda commute on the just established domains because they are scalar convolutions in log scale. The causal sums and convolution interchange by their positive-weight absolute bounds. No stage inverts M_g/M_n. Recombination is useful for retaining a simple source for another argument, though the displayed final bank equals the preceding Gaussian bank and is not an independent gain.

A less redundant explicit two-level bank, with smoothing between levels, is

    G_ij = D_i S_gn D_j S_no F_o = D_iD_j F_g,
                     i,j in {2,3}.                      (H11)

Its four channels retain H=L²(I). Applying R_a to either index and then the other reconstructs F_g, with global norm <=A^(−1) and all-shell norm <=2/A. Its global frame bounds are A² and B²: the symbol is d tensor d. This supplies a fully specified alternating construction and a paid route to another stage. Depth m costs A^(−m/2) globally and at most (sqrt(2/A))^m in the stated shell bound; it is not free if depth grows with X.

For a fixed finite composition the product of all C_h(a), frame, shift and reconstruction constants is a fixed constant. If depth depends on X, the whole product must be X^o(1) to preserve an every-epsilon exponent, or its explicit power must be subtracted from a strict gain. For a uniform stage bound C>1, depth o(log X) suffices for subpower cost, while depth proportional to log X generally costs a power. The source/profile choices must also be consistent: the direct chain has only the allowed forward arrows, and growing-depth identities must still reconstruct one fixed source before its Mellin return. Moving profiles cannot simply be assigned the fixed Mellin identity. At beta=a the causal series no longer contracts and A=0; the easy inverse and frame lower bound fail.

For H11 the actual profile, with z=log(Nm/x), is

    kappa_ij(z)=g_tau(z)−i^beta g_tau(z+log i)
       −j^beta g_tau(z+log j)+(ij)^beta g_tau(z+log(ij)).   (H12)

This formula includes repeated indices, whose equal middle terms add. Each kernel has left/right Gaussian decay and Mellin multiplier M_g(s)d_i(s)d_j(s), nonzero at Re s>beta. One can instead stop at the compact bank if that source admits a cheaper arithmetic estimate; H6 carries such an estimate forward. One cannot obtain an old-compact bank estimate back from a Gaussian one by these operators.

For reference, even the one-stage square has the complete expression

    ||D_lambda F(x)||_H²=||F(x)||_H²
      +lambda^(2beta)||F(x/lambda)||_H²
      −2lambda^beta Re<F(x),F(x/lambda)>_H.               (H13)

The last term, all original signed ideal pairs within it, and the integral in t are part of the task. For two stages there are the full sixteen ordered profile cross terms per channel before equal terms are collected. Taking absolute values before a proposed cancellation pays only an upper bound; it cannot be credited with a negative cross term. A weighted signed recombination of different detectors also creates all its cross terms and needs a nonvanishing combined multiplier. H9 avoids that uncertainty by proving its exact left-inverse identity.

## 7. What remains unpaid in the author's arithmetic proof

At b=3/2 the short terms have exponent 1/2, Type I has only the proved
upper exponent 1, Type II has only 5/4, and the tail is rapidly paid.
The Yx and Y^2/U entries of (R9) both reach x^(5/2) at the longest
prefix. Neither is removed by changing an epsilon reserve. A better
Type II estimate alone would leave Type I above every proposed target.

A sufficient modular input is an every-shell L1 bound with exponent
gamma<theta11 for BOTH full smoothed Type I and Type II, retaining the
same frozen U,V, exact chi coefficients and every branch. A weaker and
potentially more useful input bounds their complete SIGNED combination;
the already-paid short terms and tail then give (R4). No individual
box, selected rational denominator, diagonal or generic square sum proves
either input. These remain exact open arithmetic problems.

The pointwise exponent 5/4 is a saving against the damping length x^(3/2),
not against the observation scale x. It therefore supplies no new c.
It is neither a lower bound nor a claim that changing b can solve the
problem through the same absolute Type II inequality.

## 10. The complete hard correlation cannot be bounded piece by piece

The [[private research revision] actual-source proof]([private research revision]/f3-hard-correlation-integration.md)
and its independent review preserve the complete critical rough field R
at z=kappa sqrt X, kappa^2>=2exp(3tau), with F=T+R. Writing L=log X,
the gcd-one Gaussian bilinear form satisfies

    C1(R,R) asymp X^2/L^4,
    C1^H(T,R)=C1^H(R,T)=-C1^H(R,R)
                          +O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C1^H(T,T)=C1^H(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4).        (G41)

Here H=X/L^6 removes small shifts while preserving the leading term;
the frozen proof uses a fixed historical buffer beta>.874872. The
general C1(F,fA)=O(X^(1+beta)) holds for one original mask0<=A<=1,
with the other factor complete, not for two masks or arbitrary pair masks.
C1 is not positive semidefinite. No lower bound for the full F norm follows.

Retain the exact low-gcd hard sum of G34 with h>H, g<D, both ordered
mixed pieces and the original scales, masks and two Mellin heights. Then

    Q_off=Q_hard+O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)
                          +XH log(2D)+X^-4),
    Q_hard(R,R)=||R||^2+O(X^2/D+XH log(2D)+X+X^-4)
                  asymp X^2/L^4.                       (G42)

The second line uses a separate positive high-gcd count, not a signed
submask transfer. It holds for fixed D=X^theta with theta>0 and H=X^alpha
with alpha<1; its error is small relative to X^2/L^4, not automatically
to the desired power. A power-small complete Q_hard would prove OPEN-F3
when theta>(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1),0<=alpha<2gamma-1 and gamma>.5.
Both mixed terms have the opposing leading size. This eliminates a
separate R,R power-saving route even after gcd and shift truncation;
it leaves the joint cancellation entirely open. The historical near
example gamma=.874871 no longer improves the current .8748540364 boundary.

## 5. Reconstructing the inherited raw graph contract

The transport claim must start with the radial graph theorem, not assume that a positive sieve is hereditary under every signed mask. JSR10 supplies the required sharp row bound. Its central conductor exponent is `a=103/512`; balancing the all-height smooth estimate `X^(1/2) [C(3+|tau|)^2]^a H^(2a)` against the full sharp boundary error `X/H+1` gives

`beta=(1/2+2a)/(1+2a)=231/359`, `delta=a/(1+2a)=103/718`.

The row bound is

`(2 C X q_T)^epsilon X^beta C^delta (3+|tau|)^(2delta+epsilon)`.

The +1 pays literal endpoints; subunit intervals are empty, and the bounded regime uses the absolute estimate. The original row set remains the full good squarefree norm interval with its fixed ray and punctures. No arbitrary row subset or additive row phase is licensed by this input. The smooth radial factor is paid by its supremum and total variation. JSR's natural-zero Euler quotient keeps every ramified prime removed even when the character is squared, and the primitive numerator stays nonprincipal at the long good primes. These are part of the accepted source contract; the present review does not import or strengthen its external subconvex input.

To check both mark projectors, expand them completely. With P=DP1 the first coefficient retains `mu(D)/sqrt(q_D)` and residual rooted array `u(DP1)/sqrt(q_P1)`. At a shared D prime the exponent is `3+4=1 mod 6`, with its natural zero. There is no extra `(P1,R/D)=1` condition after the full expansion, and the original prime length remains N. For the pair D,D', put J=[D,D'] and R=Jr. The row length is K/q_J, with all actual phases and the puncture `(r,Jd)=1`.

The cubic sieve in M B2.25 applies to the squarefree ideal mark coefficients common across live primes. It yields `||b_D||_2^2 <= Z^epsilon S(N,L/q_D) Omega_D`, where `Omega_D=sum |u(DP1)|^2/q_P1`. Both roots produce the vectors `x_D=(Omega_D/q_D)^(1/2)`. The remaining kernel is `q_[D,D']^(-beta)`. With Schur weight `q_D^(-beta)`, its row sums are bounded by

`zeta_K(2beta) sum_(f|D) q_f^(-beta) <= C_epsilon q_D^epsilon`.

Here `2beta>1`. Moreover `sum_D x_D^2<=Z^epsilon Omega`. This is the full D,D' estimate, including cross terms, and no ambient mark-count factor is omitted. It is different from the later absolute transport bound, where both mark counts are explicitly paid.

For fixed original g,g', write d=(g,g'), u=g/d, v=g'/d. The exact natural-zero row identity is

`chi_R(pi g)^3 conjugate(chi_R(pi' g')^3)=chi_R(pi*pi'*u*v)^3 1_(R,d)=1`.

The good primitive conductor is exactly pi*pi'*u*v and has norm at most `C_orig N^2 G^2/q_d^2`. Opposite ideal orientations do not cancel as CRT characters; a square rational norm is not a square ideal character. Distinct long primes remain nonprincipal even for g=g'. Original core and rational-gcd screens reduce to h(d) and the actual short screen under the stated endpoint inequalities, without a new opposite row/mark exclusion.

For a graph independent of live marks and rows, with both degrees at most B, edge Cauchy is

`sum_E |b_D(pi) b_D'(pi')|<=B ||b_D||_2 ||b_D'||_2`.

It also follows from absolute Schur row sums. The graph may be frozen with each short pair. Summing the at most O(G^2) ordered original short pairs and using conductor exponent delta gives

`|C_E| <= Z^epsilon G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359) N^(103/359) S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig`.

This is exactly JSR19, already accepted. The new report does not count it as a second proof of a newly paid raw-H sector. The inherited proof requires neither a separable graph mask nor an additive row-character estimate.

## A16. Unequal Type I cutoffs

**PROVED bounded extension of the inherited Type I theorem.** Sources: BB R04b; M (3.15), (M.4)–(M.7), (M.35).

Let \(m_i=\mu1_{q\le Y_i}\), \(u_i=\delta-m_i*\mathbf1\), and \(R=Y_1Y_2\). Convolution algebra gives
\[
 \mu=m_1+m_2-m_1*m_2*\mathbf1+\mu*u_1*u_2.
\]
For the completed product Type I array \(a=-m_1*m_2\), one has support \(q_r\le R\), divisor-bounded coefficients, and prime valuations at most two. The unchanged central estimate M (3.15) costs
\(DK\|a\|_2^2\ll(DKR)^\epsilon DKR\).
The mixed estimate M (M.35) has outer weight
\(q_{\operatorname{rad}(rs)}^{1/2+\epsilon}/q_r\); the two divisor-weighted sums have sizes \(R^{1/2+\epsilon}\) and \(R^{3/2+\epsilon}\). Their product is \(R^{2+\epsilon}\). The double-residue factors \(q_r^{-1},q_s^{-1}\) have only subpower summed cost, exactly as in M (M.4)–(M.7). Therefore
\[
 |\mathfrak Q[I,I]|\ll(DKR)^\epsilon
 \{D^{5/3}K^{1/3}+D^{4/3}K^{7/12}R^2+DKR\}. \tag{A16.1}
\]
Both original Mellin roots and whole profiles remain in force. At \(K=D^k\), the two cutoff-dependent terms are affordable when
\[
 \log_D R<\min\{1-k,(8-7k)/24\}. \tag{A16.2}
\]
This enlarges the choice of decomposition geometry; it proves no improved remainder estimate.

## G79. Exact drift and normalized Ward defects

For h>0, a_h=exp(gamma h), E_j=int_(jh)^((j+1)h)|U(e^y)|^2dy and
D(y)=U(e^(y+h))-a_h U(e^y),

    E_(j+1)-a_h^2 E_j=int (|D|^2+2a_h Re(D conjugate(U)))dy.

An every-j one-sided drift estimate at exponent2gamma is equivalent to
the energy bound. The actual squarefree diagonal has density
kappa_q=prod_(p|q)(1-1/p)prod_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2) and pointwise main term
kappa_q exp(tau/4)e^y/(2sqrt(pi tau)), with O_(q,tau)(e^(y/2)) error.
Its drift is negative for gamma>1/2; the signed off-diagonal is unbounded
by this calculation. This is an adaptation of the existing scale family.

For a finite prime exterior space, Q=sum w_p a_p^*, W=sum|w_p|^2>0,
and even diagonal Z, the CAR identity yields

    Str(Q^*[Q,Z])=W Str(Z).

For actual Gaussian entries, Str(Z)=U_P. Every individual prime term is
|w_p|^2 U_P, so no prime-count cancellation occurs. Primes through N_X
give full omitted error X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). Exponent equivalence is
for the normalized defect divided by W, or W=1; arbitrary moving W is
charged. This corrects the unqualified raw-defect wording in the author.

statement:
## 3. The remaining signed problem and a paid prime-switch error

Two exact forms of the complete low-gcd complement are useful.
First, without any positive squares or auxiliary divisor insertion,

    Q_<D(X)=2 sum_{1<=g<D} sum_{h>=1}
       sum_{a>=1;(a,h)=1}
          f_g(a(a+h)) K_{X/g}(a,a+h).                  (S15)

The equality uses b=a+h and coprimality (a,b)=(a,h)=1, so
f_g(a)f_g(a+h)=f_g(a(a+h)). The factor 2 restores both orders.
There are no diagonal terms in S15. Every h and all prime powers in
a(a+h) remain. This is an actual signed shifted-correlation target,
not the absolute sum of the shifted correlations.

Second, including its precisely specified small diagonal,

    T_<D(X)=sum_{r>=1} a_D(r)E_r(X/r),
    a_D(r)=sum_{g|r,g<D}mu(r/g),
    Q_<D=T_<D-Delta_<D.                                (S16)

For D>1, a_D(1)=1; for 1<r<D, a_D(r)=0; for r>=D,
a_D(r)=-A_D(r). If D=2, then a_D(r)=mu(r). The actual open scalar
therefore already has a signed outer sum of whole nonnegative
energies. Bounding every E_r and summing its absolute coefficient
gives the old exponent, including the r=1 copy of the unknown E_1.
This is the precise point where an apparent positive-square reduction
fails to create a gain. It is not an impossibility theorem about S15.

The following coefficient-aware estimate strengthens this reduction
without pretending to control that r=1 term.

For p not dividing 3r, define

    U_{r,p}(y)=sum_{n>=1;p not |n} f_r(n)g(log(n/y)),
    V_{r,p}(y)=sum_{j>=1}U_{r,p}(y/p^j).

The local p coefficients give EXACTLY

    F_r=U_{r,p}-V_{r,p},
    F_{rp}=U_{r,p}+V_{r,p},
    E_{rp}(Y)-E_r(Y)
       =4 integral_Y^(2Y)U_{r,p}(y)V_{r,p}(y)dy/y.     (S17)

Every prime power p^j is in V, and the V^2 terms cancel before any
absolute value is taken. In particular S17 is a signed covariance;
there is no general sign assertion or deletion of its negative part.

The coefficient series for U_{r,p} divided by the mu series has the
same factors as S4 except that its p factor is (1-z)^(-1).
Since (1-p^(-beta))^(-1) is uniformly bounded for p>=2, S4--S6 give

    |U_{r,p}(y)| <= C_(beta,tau,delta)r^delta y^beta,
    |V_{r,p}(y)| <= C r^delta y^beta
                            p^(-beta)/(1-p^(-beta)).

Thus, uniformly in r,p,Y,

    |E_{rp}(Y)-E_r(Y)|
          <= C_delta r^delta Y^(2beta)p^(-beta).       (S18)

Delta in S18 is arbitrary after renaming the exponent in the squared
S4 bound. The full prime-power tail j>J is bounded in exactly the
same way with p^(-beta) replaced by p^(-(J+1)beta).

Let P>=3 and let s_P(r)=product_{p<=P}p^v_p(r), the COMPLETE small-
prime part. Telescoping the switches at the distinct primes >P gives

    |E_r(Y)-E_{s_P(r)}(Y)|
        <= C_delta r^delta Y^(2beta)
                          sum_{p|r;p>P}p^(-beta).     (S19)

This is a direct estimate on the literal arithmetic family. It is not
an unrestricted operator norm or a comparison with an invented
independent-sign sequence.

**Theorem S-STATE.** For any fixed delta>0 sufficiently small, uniformly
in D>=1, P>=3 and X>=2,

    | T_<D(X)
       -sum_{r>=1}a_D(r)E_{s_P(r)}(X/r) |
          <= C_delta X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+delta).        (S20)

Proof: |a_D(r)|<=d(r). Insert S19, absorb its r-loss and d(r) into
r^delta (choosing the earlier losses smaller), and sum absolutely:

    X^(2beta) sum_{r>=1}r^(-2beta+delta)
                          sum_{p|r;p>P}p^(-beta)
      = X^(2beta) zeta(2beta-delta)
                          sum_{p>P}p^(-3beta+delta)
      <= C_delta X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+delta).

Choose delta<min(2beta-1,3beta-1). Using all integers to bound the
last prime sum is sufficient; no prime theorem is used. This is also
the complete error in the off-diagonal version after subtracting the
UNCHANGED Delta_<D. It includes every switch covariance in S17 and
all prime-power tails.

For P=X^kappa, this error lies below X^(2gamma) if

    kappa > (2beta-2gamma)/(3beta-1),                   (S21)

with a strict margin for delta. For beta=.87489, gamma=.87449,
kappa=.0005 gives exponent 1.748967665 before the selectable loss.
The inherited beta=.8749 can instead use kappa=.00051, yielding
1.748971403. The limiting thresholds as beta down to theta_G are
.000488225288765... for gamma=.87449, .051153191168596... for 5/6,
and .153738770418274... for 3/4. These are ERROR thresholds, not
proved bounds for the remaining scalar.

Putting S12 and S20 together gives a fully paid equivalent target at
any theta,kappa satisfying their strict inequalities:

    L_{D,P}(X):=sum_r a_D(r)E_{s_P(r)}(X/r),
    Q_off(X)=L_{D,P}(X)-Delta_all(X)
               +T_>=D(X)+O(X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+delta)). (S22)

Consequently a one-sided X^(2gamma+epsilon) estimate for L_{D,P}, with
D=X^theta and P=X^kappa, would suffice and is equivalent within these
paid errors. The fixed original f3 detector is what enters the zero
return: the moving P is never inserted into a claimed fixed Mellin
transform.

**Important limit of S22.** It is not a lower-complexity theorem for
the unknown detector merely because its auxiliary labels use small
primes. The r=1 summand is still E_1(X), and absolute estimation of all
other r yields only the already paid tail. An independent argument
must exploit the complete scalar S15 or a genuinely new joint
covariance estimate. S20 quantitatively pays high-prime CHANGES in the
auxiliary fields; it does not pay their common unsolved component.
Large primes remain in every base f3 coefficient; only the locations
where that base prime sign has been switched to +1 are simplified.

When P>=D, there is a further exact bookkeeping factorization. Write
r=st with s P-smooth and all prime factors of t>P. Then

    a_D(st)=a_D(s)mu(t),
    L_{D,P}(X)=sum_{s P-smooth}a_D(s)
                  sum_{t P-rough}mu(t)E_s(X/(st)).     (S23)

If t has a square factor its right side and left side are both zero,
because every g<D dividing r lies wholly in s. The identity retains
all smooth prime powers and the exact g<D edge. Removing the rough
Möbius filter, changing its scale while freezing the wrong P, or
declaring it contractive would add an unpaid assertion. S23 does not
improve the preceding limit.
title: 3. The remaining signed problem and a paid prime-switch error

statement:
## 6. Quartic kernel: contour, signedness and transform

Define, with the same angular-frequency convention,

    K(x)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_R exp(-t^4+itx)dt.

It is real and even. For real x shift the contour to t+iy, where y has
the sign of x. On the horizontal line,

    -Re(t+iy)^4-yx <= -t^4/2+17y^4-yx.                   (R32)

The difference between the right and left sides is exactly
(t^2-6y^2)^2/2. For each fixed x,y, the vertical closing sides vanish:
their real quartic term is -T^4+O_y(T^2), which dominates the remaining
terms as T tends to infinity. There is no contour pole.

Choose |y|=(|x|/68)^(1/3). Then 17y^4-yx=-51y^4, yielding

    |K(x)|<=C exp(-c|x|^(4/3)),
    c=51/68^(4/3)>0.                                    (R33)

Each fixed derivative inserts a polynomial in t+iy. Its bound has at most
a fixed polynomial factor in |x|, which preserves integrability under every
fixed exponential weight. This is sufficient for the stated Abel and
Mellin arguments; no uniformity in derivative order is claimed.

The bilateral Laplace integral of K is entire in s by R33, uniformly on
compact s sets. On the imaginary axis, Fourier inversion identifies it
with exp(-s^4); the identity theorem extends this to all complex s:

    integral_R K(x)exp(-sx)dx=exp(-s^4).                 (R34)

Evenness gives the same value for the opposite sign in the exponential.
There is no sign mistake from log n-u in the field. This entire multiplier
never vanishes. Also K(0)>0, whereas integral x^2K(x)dx=-hat K''(0)=0.
Since K is continuous and positive near zero, it cannot be nonnegative
everywhere. Thus the signed-kernel description is correct, and positive
Gaussian mass comparisons cannot be carried over on that basis.

For F4(u)=sum_n a_n K(log n-u), absolute weighted Fubini gives
h4=exp(-bu)F4 in L1 intersect L-infinity and

    hat h4(t)=exp(-(b+it)^4) sum_n a_n n^(-b-it),
    |hat h4(t)|<=A_b exp(17b^4)exp(-t^4/2).               (R35)

The exponent bound follows from the same exact square as R32 with y=b.
These statements need only A_b<infinity; positivity of K is never used.
title: 6. Quartic kernel: contour, signedness and transform

### 5.2 A strictly larger all-row canonical sufficient region

For M>0 and the literal target exponent N+V, R10-R11 give exactly the following boundary for THIS upper envelope:

    E_mix<=N+V  iff  V>=g(M,N),
    g(M,N)= M-N                    (0<=N<=M/2),
             5M/6-2N/3             (M/2<=N<=M),
             (2M-N)/6              (M<=N<=8M/7),
             M/7                   (N>=8M/7).         (R12)

The word "exactly" concerns this proved upper-envelope criterion, not a lower bound for the true energy. Equality is valid with the usual Z^epsilon loss; an induction needing a strict reserve must impose a strict padded inequality.

For N<=M, sufficiency follows from E_mix<=E_all. Necessity for the envelope comes from its t=M endpoint: C(M,N) reaches N+V only at the old boundary, while M+L<=N+V requires V>=max{M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4}, which is no weaker in these ranges.

For N>=M the proposed threshold is at most M/6. Check first 0<=V<=M/6; then L=N-V, t=N-L=V is present, and R11's crossing costs N+(M-V)/6. Paying it requires V>=M/7. The t=M endpoint has label branch M+N-V>N+V in this interval; its sieve branch requires V>=(2M-N)_+/6. Together these give max{M/7,(2M-N)/6}, with the switch at N=8M/7. At that threshold both branches are paid. Larger V only decreases E_mix and increases the target, proving sufficiency for every V. Smaller V fails one displayed envelope branch. This proves R12.

For example M=1,N=8/7,V=1/7 gives

    E_mix=9/7=N+V,
    E_all=55/42,
    E_label=2.

The gain over the previous sixth-order price is1/42, and the global label minimum alone gives no such gain. At N=2,V=1/7 the corresponding prices are15/7,13/6 and20/7. Common punctures of any fixed polynomial size are still allowed; this is genuinely outside the old V>=M/6 sufficient region, even when a large Q also defeats B3.7. No favorable puncture is selected after the row.

The mechanism is a valid complement payment: few repetitions are paid with the sixth-order sieve, many repetitions with the genuine label average, and EVERY intervening dyad is included by R10. It retains the original weights, characters, marks and natural zeros. It is not a theorem about freely conditioning coefficients on f. At V=0, L=N and R10 evaluates to E_all exactly. The repeated principal layers remain charged. In particular E_mix>N for every M>0: the unlabeled canonical target is still unpaid by this new family of estimates.

statement:
# [private research revision] discovery-first headroom pass: mean-zero completion of the nonlinear source



## Current compact worklog

Objective: develop a genuinely source-specific way through the nonlinear
transition near n~X, retaining first gains beyond c11=.1251459636 and the
1/6,1/4 guideposts. Current theta11=.8748540364; the inherited F0,
positive-slot and external admission obligations remain OPEN.

Completed: full independent [private research revision] review and relevant old completion
read; four mechanisms compared; exact unramified completion, a
divisor-bounded tail lemma, full small-divisor estimate and two-prime
all-height return proved below. The remaining finite arithmetic input
and all complements are explicit. A real principal prime-pair component
defeats the attempted separated positive budget. No c is increased.

Exact coefficient/budget checks passed once (native f9db12), and all four
local source pins were read back. Final full report readback and frozen
handoff follow. The mathematical next action is to couple
the positive prime-pair component to other signed factorization/cofactor
cells before taking a norm. This report does not supply that estimate.

## 1. Discovery comparison before selection

1. **Logarithmic prime convolution.** The literal identity
   mu(n)log n=-(mu*Lambda)(n) couples actual prime powers and Möbius signs.
   Subtracting the continuous principal prime law suggests a signed Volterra
   equation. However, its prime discrepancy convolved with mu has not been
   estimated, and the absolute weighted kernel grows for every gamma<1.
   A baseline prime-number error cannot be silently substituted for the
   required bilinear error. Retained as a possible distinct upstream attack;
   this pass does not advertise the convolution identity as a saving.

2. **Growing phase bank.** Averaging exp(-it(n/x)^k) over a long t-window
   improves frequency separation, but the Mellin signal scales as
   t^(-s/k). Removing the slow t~1 sector changes the physical scale to
   x/t^(1/k); reconstruction/normalization remains a real cost. A generic
   second-moment bound alone does not pay that sector. Not selected.

3. **Actual multiplicative extraction.** Ramaré/Kátai-type prime extraction
   could use mu(pm)=-mu(m) for p not dividing m. In the transition the
   cofactor interval shrinks as p grows, keeping (pm/x)^k of order one.
   Close prime rows retain coherent correlations. A complete extraction
   must keep prime divisibility exceptions and the numbers without a
   selected prime. This remains a distinct route, not disproved here.

4. **Mean-zero completion plus the nonlinear phase — selected.** The old
   q2=delta1-2delta2 completion turns the long free cofactor into the
   genuinely alternating sequence b(l)=1-2*1_(2|l). Its literal row
   retains an additive frequency pi while the polynomial phase is slow.
   The new nonlinear tail bound can pay the entire region where that
   frequency separation fails. This may remove an actual small-divisor
   sector at a power threshold for every fixed character, including the
   principal one. It is an arithmetic identity plus an estimate, rather
   than a new name for the full norm. The surviving signed large-divisor
   term will still need a new estimate.

Outside-primary discovery inspected Matomäki–Teräväinen's published
short-interval Möbius theorem and extraction lemma, as detailed in
Section7. The row estimate below is proved directly. No external
power-saving theorem has been imported.

## 2. Literal completion, including characters at ramified primes

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Write
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), and write h(n)=chi(n), so a*h=delta1. Choose a prime
p not dividing q, FIXED before any shell parameter. Put

    q_p=delta1-p*chi(p)*delta_p,
    b_p=q_p*h,
    b_p(l)=chi(l)(1-p*1_(p|l)),
    c_p=q_p*a.

In particular |b_p(l)|<=p and b_p is periodic modulo Q=pq. Its mean is
zero: the sum over a period is p(1-chi(p))*sum_(a mod q)chi(a), which
vanishes for nonprincipal chi by orthogonality, and for principal chi
because chi(p)=1. Choosing p ramified would destroy this argument for a
principal character and is explicitly forbidden. No primitive-character
replacement or conductor-uniform bound is used.

The new global source is

    C_p(x)=sum_(n>=1)c_p(n)f_x(n),
    f_x(t)=exp(-t/x^b-i(t/x)^k).

It is literal: c_p(n)=a(n)-p*chi(p)*1_(p|n)*a(n/p). Every underlying mu
and chi value, including zero values, is retained. Compensation can create
nonzero coefficients at some squareful n; these are part of c_p and may
not be discarded. The coefficients satisfy |c_p(n)|<=p+1. Absolute local
convergence follows from the damping. The second term is f_x(pn), not
f_(x/p)(n): those damping factors differ when b>1.

For real U,V>=1 define m_U(n)=a(n)*1_(n<=U), u_U=a-m_U, and similarly
at V; the displayed indicator multiplication is pointwise. Direct
convolution expansion using a*h=delta1 gives, at EVERY positive integer,

    c_p=q_p*m_U+q_p*m_V-m_U*m_V*b_p+u_U*u_V*b_p.          (2.1)

This is the old alternating completion in a new kernel and with its exact
unramified-character factor. It is not claimed as a new algebraic identity.
The new question is whether its full small-divisor term can be bounded
at a useful power for this nonlinear source. Shared prime factors, both
ordered d,e roles, all l, and strict versus closed cutoffs remain literal.

Write S_p,U,V(x) for the source with coefficients m_U*m_V*b_p and
R_p,U,V(x) for the source with coefficients u_U*u_V*b_p. The short two
terms in (2.1) have absolute value at most (p+1)(U+V). Both S and R have
coefficient modulus at most p*d_3(n), uniformly in U,V. In particular
they converge absolutely with f_x, and for each fixed eta>0 their
coefficients are O_(p,eta)(n^eta). The familiar divisor bound follows
elementarily by absorbing each prime-power factor (e+1)(e+2)/2 in
p^(eta e), with only finitely many small-prime constants.

## 3. A complete divisor-bounded tail lemma

The accepted independent review Section7 proves a smooth positive
majorant for the ORIGINAL sharp shell [X,2X]. The following extension
keeps the divisor-bounded coefficients needed in (2.1). It is proved
here rather than silently applying its bounded-coefficient statement.

For fixed b>1,k>2 and |v_n|<=A_eta*n^eta, with 2eta<k-2, define

    B_M(x)=sum_(n>M)v_n f_x(n).

Then, for every real shell-fixed M>=2,

    ||B_M||_2^2 <<_(b,k,eta) A_eta^2
          [X^(b(1+2eta))+X^k M^(2-k+2eta)],              (3.1)

where every norm in this report uses dx/x on the FULL real shell.

Proof. Use the accepted C^2 function phi>=1 on [1,2], supported on
[1/2,4], and majorize the full |B_M|^2 before expansion. Two integrations
by parts give the weighted kernel bound

    |K_phi(n,m)| <<_(b,k) min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2).

The moving damping is differentiated: on the fixed transformed support
every A-polynomial times exp(-cA), A=(n+m)/X^b, is uniformly bounded.
For n>m, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m); also n^eta*m^eta<=n^(2eta).
With delta_n=X^k/n^(k-1), summing the complete lower row gives

    sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta_n/h)^2)<<delta_n.

Thus BOTH off-diagonal orientations cost at most
O(A_eta^2 X^k sum_(n>M)n^(1-k+2eta)), which is the second term in (3.1).
The diagonal retains its exponential damping and costs
O(A_eta^2 sum n^(2eta) exp(-c n/X^b))=O(A_eta^2 X^(b(1+2eta))).
Absolute convergence first justifies finite-square expansion; the displayed
summable bounds justify the infinite limit. This proves the full tail
norm, including all interactions within that tail. In a subsequent
triangle inequality with the core, this complete norm pays its cross
effect; no individual signed cross is asserted positive.

Consequently if b<=2gamma and r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), then M=X^r has

    ||B_M||_2+||B_M||_1 <<_(p,q,b,k,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon) (3.2)

for divisor-bounded coefficients, with eta chosen sufficiently small
AFTER epsilon and before X. This choice works even when b=2gamma;
no strict reserve is being asserted at equality. Constants are uniform
in U,V and their cutoff-dependent coefficients.

## 4. Power-paid small-divisor theorem for the actual completed source

Fix gamma,k,b satisfying

    1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, 1<b<=2gamma,
    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2),
    u=k-(k-1)r=2gamma-r>0.                              (4.1)

For the main near/1/6/1/4 examples use b=3/2,k=6. Set

    eta0=1/(100*k*p*q),
    U=V=floor(sqrt(eta0)*X^(u/2)),  M=X^r.              (4.2)

All quantities are chosen from the ORIGINAL shell X, before x varies.
For sufficiently large X, U,V>=1. The floor only decreases UV and
never changes its upper bound eta0*X^u. Then for every epsilon>0,

    ||S_p,U,V||_1+||S_p,U,V||_2
          <<_(chi,p,b,k,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (4.3)

This is an unconditional estimate of the ACTUAL small-divisor source,
uniform on the entire shell in its finite part. It uses no Möbius
cancellation in d,e and no unproved character moment.

To prove it, first restrict the physical integer n=de*l to n<=M.
For D=de<=UV, expand the zero-mean periodic b_p in its finite Fourier
series modulo Q=pq:

    b_p(l)=sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j e(j*l/Q),
    sum |beta_j|<=p*Q.

Every row has phase

    F_j(t)=j*t/Q-(D*t/x)^k/(2pi).

On 1<=t<=M/D its derivative is decreasing and satisfies

    0<=k*D^k*t^(k-1)/(2pi*x^k)
       <=k*UV*M^(k-1)/(2pi*X^k)
       <=k*eta0/(2pi)<1/(2Q).

The equality of powers here is EXACTLY u+(k-1)r=k. Hence F_j' stays
between 1/(2Q) and 1-1/(2Q); it never crosses an integer.

For completeness the needed first-derivative estimate is elementary.
For integer t, Delta_t=F_j(t+1)-F_j(t) is monotone and stays in that
same interval whenever both endpoints lie in the row. Put z_t=e(F_j(t))
and g(v)=1/(e(v)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v). Then
z_t=g(Delta_t)(z_(t+1)-z_t). Summation by parts bounds every row prefix
by the endpoint terms plus the total variation of g along a monotone
interval. Both are O(Q), since |sin(pi v)| is bounded below at its
endpoints and cot is monotone. A final unpaired atom costs1. This proves
the bound for every real upper cutoff, not only integer or sampled x.

Abel summation with the actual decreasing exp(-D*l/x^b) multiplies
that bound by at most2. The Fourier expansion therefore gives O_p,q(1)
for each row, uniformly for all real x in the shell and all d,e<=U,V.
Summing |mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e)|<=1 proves

    |S_(n<=M)(x)| <<_(p,q) U*V <<_(p,q,k) X^u.          (4.4)

Since r>1>gamma, u=2gamma-r<gamma. The remaining n>M portion of S
has coefficients bounded by p*d_3(n) and is paid by (3.2). This proves
(4.3), INCLUDING the region in which the row's discrete frequency can
approach an integer. It is not dropped, estimated by the row lemma
outside its range, or assigned a fictitious zero value.

The complete short terms in (2.1) cost O_p(U+V)=O(X^(u/2)), hence are
also paid. This is the substantive combination with the accepted tail
theorem: its generic bound is used only on a genuine, completely retained
complement; the new small-divisor cancellation occurs before that split.

The argument does not authorize U=V=X^.495, nor UV=X^gamma. At fixed
k,gamma its demonstrated nonstationary condition is UV<<X^u. Beyond it
the current proof has a discrete alias/stationary range. Vanishing of
this reserve is not an impossibility theorem for other estimates.

## 5. The remaining finite arithmetic input and its complete return

In addition to (4.1), first take b=3/2,k=6 and gamma>=3/4 for the
three explicit targets below. Define L=X^gamma and M=X^r. For each fixed
unramified compensator prime p use (4.2), and define the literal finite sum

    T_p,chi,X(x)=sum_(d>U,e>V,L<de*l<=M)
        mu(d)mu(e)chi(de*l)(1-p*1_(p|l))
        exp(-de*l/x^(3/2)-i(de*l/x)^6).                  (5.1)

The sum includes ALL positive integer l, both ordered d,e variables,
noncoprime pairs and both sharp physical cuts. Each original mu factor
and character zero is left in place. No arithmetic projector or residue
class has been deleted. The internal period is the actual pq, not the
primitive conductor.

The n<=L portion of R costs O_(p,eta)(L^(1+eta)) by its divisor bound.
The n>M portion costs O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) in both L1 and L2 by (3.2).
Equation (2.1), (4.3) and the complete short-term bound then give

    ||C_p-T_p,chi,X||_j <<_(chi,p,gamma,epsilon)
                                  X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2. (5.2)

All constants are uniform over the entire real shell and every dyadic X
above a fixed onset. In particular an every-epsilon bound at exponent
gamma for T is equivalent to that bound for C_p, separately in L1 and
L2. L2 implies L1; the converse is not asserted. The price of each full
complement is an actual norm, so the triangle inequality pays every
interaction with T and between the removed terms. No independent height
has been identified with another, and no square expansion drops a cross.

The weakest complete developed premise is the L1 bound for a fixed
TWO-PRIME bank, for every fixed ordinary chi:

    for each p in {p1,p2}, for every epsilon>0,
    integral_X^(2X)|T_p,chi,X(x)|dx/x
                   <<_(chi,p,gamma,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon). (OPEN-T)

The primes are fixed once for chi BEFORE epsilon,X or a target zero.
They are distinct and unramified. If chi is nonprincipal choose p1 with
chi(p1)!=1; such a prime exists, since a unit integer with nontrivial
chi-value factors into unramified primes. For a principal character any
two distinct unramified primes suffice. No theorem uniform in growing q
or primes is claimed. A sum of the two L1 norms is equivalent to these
two premises with constants changed; there is no unpriced bank readout.

Here is the complete detector return, including the line Re s=1. The
accepted contour calculation applies termwise to c_p, whose coefficients
are bounded. At K=1,b=3/2,k=6 it gives on the initial absolute half-plane
sigma>3/2, and then by continuation,

    H_p(s)=integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(s-1)dt
          =A_0(s) P_p(s)/L(s,chi)+E_p(s),
    A_0(s)=Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/6,
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)*p^(1-s).                            (5.3)

E_p is normally holomorphic for sigma>1/2, by the accepted remainder
bound multiplied by p+1. A_0 is holomorphic and nonzero for sigma>0.
From (OPEN-T) and (5.2), shell summation with epsilon smaller than a
compact real-part margin makes H_p holomorphic on sigma>gamma. The
x tending to zero complement is bounded by (p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1).
It pays every fixed Mellin derivative. All finite heights are covered by
arbitrary compacts; no uniform bound as |Im s| tends to infinity is used.

Every zero of P_p has sigma=1. The two polynomials P_p1,P_p2 have no
common zero with nonzero imaginary part: because chi-values are roots
of unity, a common zero 1+it would make both t*log(p_j)/(2pi) rational.
For t!=0 this makes log(p1)/log(p2) rational, contradicting unique prime
factorization. At t=0 a common zero requires chi(p1)=chi(p2)=1. The
choice of p1 excludes this for nonprincipal chi. For principal chi it
leaves only s=1, the allowed pole, not a zero. Thus (5.3) for the TWO
fixed sources excludes every zero of the actual meromorphic L throughout
sigma>gamma, with the principal pole exception retained. This argument
does not silently import nonvanishing on the entire line sigma=1.

The actual imprimitive L and its finite Euler holes occur throughout.
Their Re s=0 zeros do not enter this half-plane, but no factor has been
removed in obtaining (5.3). The common gamma is selected before chi;
primes, constants and onsets may depend on that fixed character. This
is ordinary-character scope only, with no new Hecke or conductor-uniform
claim and no resolution of the external root-definition/admission issue.

The exact useful rows are:

| Conditional c | gamma | r | u=UV exponent | each divisor exponent u/2 | cofactor bound exponent r-u |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|313/2500=.1252|2187/2500|5313/5000|687/1000|687/2000|939/2500|
|1/6|5/6|13/12|7/12|7/24|1/2|
|1/4|3/4|9/8|3/8|3/16|3/4|

The first row improves the current c11 only CONDITIONALLY, by
135091/2500000000. No row's OPEN-T is proved. Constants in the upper
cofactor bound account for the floors in U,V: for large X they give
l<=O_(p,q,k)(X^(r-u)), not a unit-constant bound.

For example the first row completely pays n<=X^.8748, n>X^1.0626,
the original two short sources and the full small-small divisor source.
The open sum has d,e>floor(sqrt(eta0)*X^.3435) and
l<=O_(p,q)(X^.3756). It retains all shell points. There is no claim that
these cutoffs constitute a stronger zero-free theorem by themselves.

For completeness the same architecture has conditional headroom for
every fixed gamma>1/2. Choose k large enough that u>0, choose
1<b<=2gamma, and a fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. The full Mellin formula
now contains ALL shifts A_j(s)P_p(s+(b-1)j)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi).
Put F_p(s)=P_p(s)/L(s,chi). The identical finite-strip descent from the
accepted review extends F_p holomorphically from sigma>1 to sigma>gamma:
at each step every j>=1 shift is already known and nonzero A_0 solves
for the unshifted F_p. The two-prime noncommon-zero argument then returns
L itself. All parameters are fixed before X, and the proof makes no
claim at gamma=1/2 or about a growing degree or growing K.

This headroom statement requires no r<b: when r>=b the actual damping
only helps the tail bound. Requiring r<b as in the earlier review is
also permissible and can always be arranged with sufficiently large k.

## 6. Coarse attempts on the actual hard remainder

The first deliberately coarse estimate uses only |coeff R|<=p*d_3.
Split its physical integer at X, use the divisor bound on the prefix
and (3.1) on the tail. It proves

    ||R||_1+||R||_2 <<_(chi,p,epsilon) X^(1+epsilon)

when b<=2. The same bound for T follows from the paid complements.
It misses the first-gain L1 threshold gamma<.8748540364 by at least
.1251459636 in power. It is a complete estimate, not a dropped-tail
or point-sampling estimate, and it fails to give a new c.

The previously imported fixed-degree Green--Tao polynomial theorem also
applies to C_p. Indeed C_p is the sum of the two literal mu*chi series
with weights f_x(n) and -p*chi(p)*f_x(pn). A constant dilation changes
only fixed phase/damping constants; the accepted truncated-polynomial
bound and full bounded-coefficient tail proof work with those constants.
For every FIXED D>0 this gives, for b=3/2,k=6,

    ||C_p||_1 <<_(chi,p,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D),
    ||T_p,chi,X||_1 << X^(gamma+epsilon)+X(log X)^(-D).  (6.1)

The latter is actual arithmetic control of the remaining sum, but only
with a logarithmic improvement on exponent1. D may not grow with X.
No uniform constant for growing degree, conductor, compensator or
logarithmic strength is imported. This is reuse of G142, not a second
novel arithmetic saving credited to this pass.

The stronger claim that every dyadic factor block is already affordable
fails for an ACTUAL principal-character block. Let chi be principal
modulo fixed q and select in (5.1) l=1 and distinct prime d,e in

    sqrt(X)/2 < d,e <= sqrt(X/2).

For large X these primes are unramified, exceed U,V and have
X/4<de<=X/2, inside (L,M]. Their coefficient is exactly +1 in EACH
compensated source: mu(d)mu(e)=1, chi(de)=1, b_p(1)=1. The ordered
prime-pair count is J(X)(J(X)-1), where the prime number theorem gives
J(X)~2(1/sqrt(2)-1/2)sqrt(X)/log X. The exclusion d=e ensures no
squareful original product is smuggled into this selected component.

For every x in [X,2X], the phase satisfies (de/x)^k<=2^(-k), and the
damping is at least exp(-X^(1-b)/2). The REAL PART of this selected
component B_p(x) is consequently at least

    exp(-X^(1-b)/2) cos(2^(-k)) J(X)(J(X)-1)
                       >>_q X/(log X)^2.               (6.2)

Thus both its L1 and L2 norm have exponent1. This is an actual signed
arithmetic component, with its sign proved, rather than a shell-dependent
arbitrary-array countermodel. Any estimate that partitions the exact sum
into cells and pays this cell's norm separately by a positive triangle
budget cannot achieve X^(gamma+epsilon) for ANY fixed gamma<1. The
same obstruction survives the two-prime detector bank, whose l=1 cells
are identical. It is only an obstruction to this separated budget.
It is NOT a lower bound for the full R,T,C_p, nor a no-gain theorem for
signed cross-cancellation or nonprincipal characters.

Accordingly the next surviving route has to couple this prime-prime
cell with other exact factorization/cofactor cells before taking an
absolute value or squared norm. The mean-zero free cofactor helps on
small products de; it cannot cancel the l=1 cell by itself when de~X.
This is the strongest source-specific failed coarse test in this pass.

## 7. Primary sources, novelty boundaries and dispositions

The new outside source inspected is Kaisa Matomäki and Joni Teräväinen,
*On the Möbius function in all short intervals*, JEMS25(2023),1207–1225,
DOI10.4171/JEMS/1205, [published primary PDF](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32826?nt=1).
Theorem1.1 (printed1208) has fixed theta>.55 and only a logarithmic
relative error H/(log x)^(1/3-epsilon). Theorem1.5 (printed1209) is
uniform in linear twist alpha for fixed theta>3/5, with the same type
of error. Lemma3.1 (printed1212) extracts a small prime with an explicit
H*log(P)/log(Q) error and size/support conditions; its square-divisibility
correction is paid in the proof. These exact statements were inspected
in primary web text, with the v2 arXiv text used to disambiguate OCR.
They motivate the separate extraction candidate but do not supply a
power bound for our two-long-variable sum. Summing their logarithmic
errors across an X-length transition still leaves exponent1. No claim
of a general character-twisted extension from those statements is used.

For (6.2) the only prime-distribution input is the ordinary prime number
theorem, with fixed-proportion intervals obtained by partial summation.
Its primary proof is Atle Selberg, *An Elementary Proof of the Prime-Number
Theorem*, Annals50(1949),305–313, [original article scan](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf),
equation(1.1), printed305. No prime-in-short-interval or progression
uniformity is needed: deleting primes dividing one fixed q is finite.
The source is used for an obstruction to a separated budget, not for
an unproved Möbius cancellation estimate.

Local sources and exact SHA256 pins are in checks.json. The FULL accepted
nonlinear author/review and integration underpin the new source; this
pass independently rederived the character completion and new estimates.
The old Gaussian identity is R35.2 in
[restricted mathematical source] whose first108 lines were read here.
Its growing-derivative Gaussian argument R35.3–R35.7 already pays a
much larger small-divisor square for a DIFFERENT kernel. It cannot be
transferred to exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k) merely by matching exponents: the
new kernel has actual discrete stationary frequencies in its long tail.
Conversely, this report does not improve that old Gaussian lemma or
claim priority for mean-zero completion itself.

What is newly established for the live nonlinear source is the combination:

* a full divisor-bounded tail estimate uniform in the changing original
  truncations, including every paired label;
* an unconditional completed small-divisor source estimate with product
  cutoff exponent u=2gamma-r and full norm O(X^(gamma+epsilon)), with
  the failing discrete-frequency region paid;
* a finite two-prime numerator bank and a complete signed two-long-factor
  input, including the principal boundary and all finite heights;
* an actual positive prime-pair component of that exact remaining source,
  identifying a specific coupling that the next estimate must preserve.

The first two points are useful source restrictions, not a solved full
moment. The finite return is conditional on OPEN-T; its equivalence to
the complete compensated norm does not make the arithmetic premise free.
The prime-pair obstruction retires only estimates that pay its norm
separately. It neither retires the architecture nor establishes a lower
bound for the actual full signed source.

Disposition of the four discovery candidates: logarithmic prime
convolution remains open at its signed prime-discrepancy input; the
growing phase bank has unpaid restoration/normalization and was not
developed into a theorem; multiplicative extraction remains eligible
but the inspected published log estimates miss the power budget; the
selected completion earns the restricted theorem above and a concrete
failed coarse test, with no numerical gain. All29 original families,
109 children and other valid components are retained, not silently
replaced or classified as disproved.

The strongest remaining objection is substantive: near n~X the phase
does not force power cancellation of the actual Möbius factors, and the
prime-pair cell proves that some truly signed cross-cell estimate is
necessary. The next credible development is a coupled evaluation of
that cell and its cofactor/composite compensators using exact convolution
or a source-specific bilinear input. A further tail refinement alone
would not address the remaining term and is not proposed as a new pass.

## 8. Evidence limits and final state

The mathematical assertions are the written analytic arguments, not the
finite helper. check.py checks exact Gaussian-integer character identities,
periodic means (including a deliberately ramified failure), sharp cutoff
convolution identities, coefficient majorants and rational exponent
budgets. It does not numerically sample a whole rectangle or certify
OPEN-T. No original/frozen helper is executed or changed.

Primary PDFs were read through primary web text; no local PDF binary,
screenshot-byte inspection or binary hash is claimed. The source-evidence
file records the exact URLs, theorem locations and readback limits.
F0/positive-slot/external-binding obligations remain at their prior open
scope. The new ordinary-character return is its own analytic theorem;
it does not cure those upstream admissions or authorize a Hecke extension.

 The
first report prefix and all successful later edits were preserved; an
atomic patch-context mismatch changed no bytes and was corrected against
the saved last line. No mathematical work is claimed during the failed
requests. The lean check ran once, exit0 (f9db12), and wrote checks.json
4778bytes, SHA25698235aeaef30fb512b768dfefe7ac1e32b3830ed314c71c3c381dd057c01e9aa.
It was not rerun. The complete helper was read back in583efb; the complete
receipt and source-evidence file were read back in fc865a. Freeze and
normal exact own-release/absence receipts will accompany handoff.
