statement:
# [restricted research revision]: genuine cofactor-labelled detectors and their recovery price

Status: author development for independent review. No improved zero-free constant is proved. The results below construct an actual labelled source with a complete return, prove its uniform cofactor-averaging error, and locate a coefficient-blind obstruction. They do not use PR15's unfinished weighted source theorem or PR26's active high-row/fiber bridge.



## 1. Outcome and ancestry

A full label average cannot simply be inserted in the current physical source. We instead construct a new Gaussian Möbius source and manufacture its labels exactly. Along the actual sextic character channels k=f²e⁶ the labels turn into the natural coprimality hole (n,fe)=1. Averaging these holes over squarefree f and unrestricted e produces a FIXED multiplicative weight. Its Euler product differs from the original reciprocal L-function by a zero-free factor absolutely convergent on Re(s)>0.

The resulting signed scalar average is a legitimate source-independent zero detector. It needs only a complete shell L1 estimate, including the label average before the absolute value. Its approximation error is explicitly paid, even for labels growing with the observation scale. This repairs the missing signal definition for this particular label-producing architecture.

The natural positive-bank bound remains too weak. Recovering its principal channels divides by their actual repetition count, not by the entire row count. The [restricted research revision] envelope then cannot certify any gamma<1; a single fixed positive squarefree coefficient array shows that a coefficient-blind power improvement below the trivial source exponent is impossible. This obstruction does not lower-bound the actual Möbius source.

Ancestry: [restricted research revision] G212–G214 supplies the fixed-family binding, natural zeros, all-repetition envelope and labelled M/7 gate. [restricted research revision] G109 and [restricted research revision] G125–G127 supply existing Gaussian/Mellin and bank-return methodology. PR30's imported radical/mod6 feature prevents forgetting holes. Historical PR1/2/4 and [restricted research revision] distinguish scalar obstructions from arithmetic lower bounds. The new parts here are the actual k=f²e⁶ diagonal with counted multiplicity, the uniform cofactor-average-to-fixed-Euler-source transfer, and its complete quantitative signal/price comparison. Neither a generic bank idea nor Mellin continuation alone is claimed new.

## 2. Ordinary and Eisenstein sources

Work first over R=Z, or over the ideals of O_K for K=Q(omega), using q_a=a or q_a=N(a). For the ideal version use the source's fixed primary/ray convention. Let S be a fixed finite set of primes, including any ramified character primes; for the sextic application it also contains the primes above6. Let eta be one fixed ordinary Dirichlet character or one fixed finite-order, trivial-infinity Hecke character. All its natural zeros remain.

Fix tau>0 and
    g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v²/(2tau)).
For a finite radical Q outside S define
    U_Q(x)=sum_a mu_R(a) eta(a) 1_((a,SQ)=1)
                      g_tau(log(q_a/x)),                 (2.1)
    U(x)=U_1(x).
These are the COMPLETE infinite sums. Ideal/integer counting gives
    sum_(q_a<=T)1=κ_R T+O_R(T^theta_R),
    theta_Z=0, theta_K=1/2,                              (2.2)
with the O(1) interpretation for Z and an all-T>0 version. For K, (2.2) follows by counting Eisenstein lattice points and dividing by the six units. It implies absolute local convergence and |U_Q(x)|<=C_(R,tau)x for every x>0, uniformly in Q. Gaussian left tails are smaller than every fixed power of x as x decreases to0. No Mertens estimate is used.

Fix F,E>=1, frozen over each physical shell. Let
    Fset={squarefree f: F<q_f<=2F, (f,S)=1},
    Eset={e:0<q_e<=E, (e,S)=1};
denote their exact cardinalities by N_F,N_E. For sufficiently large F,E they are positive and comparable to F,E with S-dependent constants. Small fixed cases can be defined using f=1 or e=1 separately. Set
    P_(F,E)(x)=(N_F N_E)^(-1) sum_(f inFset,e inEset)
                                      U_rad(fe)(x).      (2.3)
Shared primes of f,e are allowed. We do not require e squarefree. Every sign mu_R(a), character value, profile and natural hole in (2.1) survives (2.3).

## 3. A fixed source emerges, with a complete error bound

Put
    w(p)=(q_p-1)/(q_p+1),  w(a)=product_(p|a,p notinS)w(p),
    W_eta(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)
                              w(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x)).     (3.1)
The weights are fixed; they do not depend on F,E,X or a chosen zero.

Uniformly for all x>0 and all sufficiently large F,E,
    |P_(F,E)(x)-W_eta(x)|
       <= C_(S,R,tau) x L_R(x,F)
             [F^(-1/2)+E^(-(1-theta_R))],               (3.2)
where one may take
    L_Z(x,F)=1+log(2+x),
    L_K(x,F)=1+log(2+F).
The Z bound can harmlessly use 1+log(2+x)+log(2+F). Character constants need not be uniform over moving conductors; the displayed bound itself uses only |eta|<=1 and fixed S.

Proof: the squarefree f probability of avoiding a has main term
    A(a)=product_(p|a,p notinS)(1+q_p^(-1))^(-1),
and the unrestricted e probability has main term
    B(a)=product_(p|a,p notinS)(1-q_p^(-1)).
Their product is exactly w(a). Inclusion–exclusion and mu²=sum_(r²|a)mu(r) give
    error_f <= C_S F^(-1/2) log(2F) S_(1/2)(rad a)       [K],
    error_e <= C_S E^(-1/2) S_(1/2)(rad a)               [K],
    error_f <= C_S F^(-1/2) d(rad a),                   [Z],
    error_e <= C_S E^(-1) d(rad a),                     [Z],
where S_h(Q)=sum_(d|Q)q_d^(-h). Both probabilities and both main terms lie in[0,1], so their product error is bounded by the SUM of these errors, without multiplying them.

For ideals, sum_(q_a<=x)S_(1/2)(rad a)<=C x sum_d q_d^(-3/2)<=C' x. For integers, sum_(a<=x)d(rad a)<=C x log(2x). Partial summation against the full Gaussian pays both infinite ends and proves (3.2). The details and small-x qualification are in support.md. No favourable subset of the signed source has been deleted.

For Re(s)>1 absolute Mellin Fubini gives
    integral_0^infinity W_eta(x)x^(-s)dx/x
        =exp(tau s²/2) H_eta(s)/L^S(s,eta),             (3.3)
    H_eta(s)=product_(p notinS)
          [1-w(p)eta(p)q_p^(-s)]/[1-eta(p)q_p^(-s)].
Both H_eta and its inverse have absolutely convergent Dirichlet series for every Re(s)>0. Indeed the local deviations have coefficient mass bounded by
    2/(q_p+1) * q_p^(-sigma)/(1-q_p^(-sigma)),
summable over primes for every fixed sigma>0. Every numerator and denominator is nonzero there. Thus H_eta is holomorphic and zero-free on Re(s)>0. This is an explicit signal multiplier, not an assumed average over the old physical source.

The same local expansions give two-way Gaussian field convolution between W_eta and U with absolutely sigma-summable coefficients for every sigma>0. This is an exponent-preserving change of source, not an arithmetic power saving.

## 4. Complete zero-exclusion return and protected targets

Let 0<gamma<1. For every dyadic X choose F_X=X^v,E_X=X^r, with fixed v,r>0, and keep these choices fixed as x ranges over[X,2X]. Suppose for each fixed eta and every epsilon>0 that
    integral_X^(2X) |P_(F_X,E_X)(x)| dx/x
        <= C_(eta,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)           (OPEN-COF-L1)
on every sufficiently large shell. The absolute value is OUTSIDE the complete signed f,e average.

If
    min(v/2,r)>=1-gamma                   [Z],
    min(v/2,r/2)>=1-gamma                 [K],          (4.1)
then (3.2) supplies the same every-epsilon L1 bound for the fixed W_eta. Equality in (4.1) is allowed with the every-epsilon formulation; logarithms are absorbed. Padding gives a literal power reserve.

Dyadic summation and the Gaussian left tail make the left side of(3.3) holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, including every fixed derivative and every finite height. Multiplication by the ORIGINAL L^S extends the identity. Its right numerator never vanishes there, so L(s,eta) has no zero in that strict half-plane, with its principal pole at1 excluded. No moving cutoff is assigned a fixed Mellin transform.

This gives the following explicit padded label choices:

| target c=1-gamma | gamma | ordinary(v,r) | Eisenstein(v,r) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| repair target below c11: .12 | .88 | (.241,.121) | (.241,.241) |
| conditional c11: .1251459636 | .8748540364 | (.251,.126) | (.251,.251) |
| near target .12515 | .87485 | (.251,.126) | (.251,.251) |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | (.334,.167) | (.334,.334) |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | (.51,.26) | (.51,.51) |

These are target conversions, not proved estimates. The ordinary version directly treats every positive-modulus Dirichlet character, including imprimitive ones and their zeros. Its exponent gamma must be common across the family; constants and thresholds may depend on the fixed character. The K version concerns precisely the finite-order trivial-infinity family; no angular character scope is inferred.

A sufficient, stronger input is the positive principal bank
    B_(F,E)(X)=(N_F N_E)^(-1)
               sum_(f,e) integral_X^(2X)|U_rad(fe)(x)|² dx/x
           << X^(2gamma+epsilon).                    (OPEN-COF-L2)
Jensen and shell Cauchy imply OPEN-COF-L1. Signed cancellation between f,e can make the L1 target weaker; it must not be discarded as a positive subfamily estimate. The actual coarse bound |U_Q(x)|<=Cx proves only B<<X² and |P|<<X. Every complementary source and label is included in that statement.

## 5. Genuine embedding in the [restricted research revision] joint bank

For K, use the exact source-bound sextic symbol psi_k(a)=chi_a(k), with its zero extension and [restricted research revision] G212's global primary representatives. These representatives multiply on good ideals, so f0²e0⁶ represents f²e⁶ without an untracked unit. For good squarefree f and arbitrary good e,
    chi_a(f)^4 chi_a(f²e⁶)
           =1_((a,fe)=1).                            (5.1)
This holds even when f and e share primes, and when a shares one of those primes: both sides are then zero. No cancelled character power is replaced by1 at a nonunit.

For Z tending to infinity and x on a shell X=Z^N with fixed N>0, form the normalized joint source
    T_(f,k)(x)=X^(-1/2) sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)
       1_((a,S)=1) chi_a(k)chi_a(f)^4
                         g_tau(log(q_a/x)).            (5.2)
These are new coefficients, not the canonical Gauss coefficients or the old physical numerator. They are independent of live f,k and have the normalized squarefree column mass used by the generic sieves. (5.1) gives
    T_(f,f²e⁶)(x)=X^(-1/2)U_rad(fe)(x).                (5.3)
For each f, e->f²e⁶ is injective in ideals. Fix
    F=Z^V, E=Z^R, M=2V+6R, Urow=Z^M,
with fixed V,R>0 for the two-sided approximation; the V=0 one-sided
variant is defined below.
All selected k satisfy q_k<=4Urow. The exact selected pair count is N_F N_E, not N_F Urow. The full positive joint norm dominates its selected principal part, so
    B_(F,E)(X)
       <= C_S X Z^(-R) [ F^(-1) sum_(f) sum_(q_k<=4Urow)
                           integral_X^(2X)|T_(f,k)(x)|² dx/x ].
                                                               (5.4)
Constants account only for the exact F/E counts. This is lawful positive-norm restriction, not signed subset domination. Full Gaussian tails can be treated by annular decomposition and Gaussian summability; there is no sharp source cutoff or unpaid small scale.

[restricted research revision]'s generic proof uses arbitrary f,k-independent column coefficients. Conditional on its NAMED sextic and squarefree cubic sieve inputs, it therefore supplies the same normalized upper-envelope exponent
    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M)
        {(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L(N,V))},
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6),
    L(N,V)=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).                         (5.5)
It does not supply a new Möbius-specific cancellation estimate.

When V=0, take Fset={1}. The corresponding fixed detector has local weight
1-q_p^(-1), not(q_p-1)/(q_p+1); its sole cofactor error and the same
zero-free multiplier proof are given in support SectionB. Thus the V=0
price comparison below also belongs to a legitimate detector variant.

## 6. Recovery price defeats that generic upper envelope

Since V<=M and L(N,V)>=N-V, choose t=V in(5.5). Both C(V,N) and V+L are at least N. Hence
    Emix >= N+(M-V)/6 = N+R+V/6.                       (6.1)
The upper bound obtained by combining(5.4) with that envelope costs
    X Z^(Emix-R) >= Z^(2N+V/6)                         (6.2)
as a CERTIFICATE PRICE. To certify the target X^(2(1-c)), the actual joint bound must improve on this displayed envelope branch by at least
    2cN+V/6.                                          (6.3)
There is no improvement at V=0 either: its minimum price is X². This is not the earlier V=0 substitution into an unlabelled source; it is the cost of recovering a genuinely labelled, independently defined detector.

At [restricted research revision]'s example(M,N,V)=(1,8/7,1/7), R=5/42 and Emix=9/7. The field energy price is97/42 in baseZ, giving only gamma=97/96 in the observation scaleX. At(1,2,1/7) it gives gamma=169/168. The labelled gain1/42 does not become zero exclusion after its actual signal price. For the approximation choices in Section4 the cofactor errors are also paid; ignoring them would be a separate failure.

This statement is about what the two generic inequalities certify. It is NOT a lower bound for the true Möbius bank or a universal barrier to the labelled architecture.

## 7. A fixed coefficient counterexample strengthens the diagnosis

There is a real obstruction to any coefficient-blind power improvement, beyond the particular form of(5.5). Replace mu_K(a) in(5.2) by the FIXED sequence
    b(a)=mu_K(a)² conjugate(eta(a))
on the S-coprime ideals, so b(a)eta(a)=mu_K(a)². It is still squarefree-supported, bounded, and independent of f,k,X. Along every principal channel, the sum is positive.

For any fixed A>0, uniformly over q_Q<=X^A,
    sum_(X<q_a<=2X,(a,SQ)=1) mu_K(a)²
          >>_(S,A,epsilon) X^(1-epsilon).              (7.1)
The proof in support.md uses elementary ideal counting, inclusion–exclusion and the positive density product product_(p|SQ)(1+q_p^-1)^-1. The errors are O_S(sqrt X logX S_(1/2)(Q)); divisor products are subpower when q_Q is polynomial inX.

The Gaussian has a positive lower bound on this annulus. Therefore every corresponding positive U_Q(x) is X^(1-o(1)) on the full shell, and its principal bank has energy X^(2-o(1)). In the full normalized joint bank the principal pairs alone contribute
    Z^(N+R-o(1)).                                     (7.2)
Thus a bound strong enough to force c>0 cannot hold uniformly for all such column coefficients. A useful improvement must use the actual Möbius signs (or a genuinely different signal-carrying observation). A new orthogonality argument that only improves the coefficient-blind operator envelope cannot remove this obstruction.

## 8. Retained alternatives and next action

The frozen slate survives. Routes1/7 led to the complete signed scalar L1 target, rather than the full joint positive norm. Routes2/10 produced Sections2–7. Route4 (signed cutoff averaging) is represented by the exact cofactor averaging transfer but no arithmetic power bound; arbitrary signed kernels remain outside the positive-bank obstruction. Routes3/6 overlap the existing nonlinear/Euler-source work;5 overlaps complete commutator/cofactor accounting;8/9 overlap the retained renewal/future-law constructions. They are not relabelled disproved.

The strongest live escape is OPEN-COF-L1 with genuine signed correlation between the coprime cofactor fields, or a Möbius-specific estimate for the principal diagonal after retaining the divisor/prime signs. All coefficients and holes are explicit. The resulting fixed weighted source has the same exponent class as U, so the change of representation alone does not reduce the arithmetic difficulty. It supplies a fully paid place to seek that cancellation.

No source-independent c gain, PR15 repair, F0 proof, positive-slot uniformity proof or external admission follows. The current c11 remains conditional. This pass constructs and audits an alternative upstream source and proves the precise failure of a natural coarse sieve route, rather than altering the pending PR26 proof.

### Sum of the original coefficients

The modulus of a paired completed coefficient is
\[
\frac1{q_g\sqrt{q_uq_v}\,q_h^2q_s^2q_t^2}.
\]
For fixed \(d_0,r_1,r_2\), the outer annuli imply
\[
\sum_{u,v}(q_uq_v)^{-1/2}
\ll \frac{Y}{q_{d_0}(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3}.
\]
The original log-Gaussian profiles satisfy
\[
\sum_gq_g^{-1}|V(T_1q_g)V(T_2q_g)|\ll1
\]
uniformly in \(T_1,T_2>0\), by dyadic ideal counting and Cauchy. The \(h,s,t\) sums converge at norm exponent two, the \(r_i\) sums at exponent three, and \(\sum_{q_{d_0}\ll Y}q_{d_0}^{-1}\ll\log(2Y)\). Thus total absolute coefficient/profile mass is \(O(Y\log(2Y))\). Small powers of completed column lengths are absorbed in the original two-sided log-Gaussian envelope.

Multiplying by the raw prefactor \(Y^{-2}\) and the \(O(Y)\) per-pair discrepancy proves (A01.2). In the squarefree outer subcase that discrepancy is \(O(1)\), proving the stronger bound.

For a fixed number of all-marked slots at **unembedded \(D=1\)**, replace \(V\) by the exact AA18 kernel. Permitted divisors of \(A\) are divisor-bounded, and AA20 supplies a common envelope at scale \(ZP\). No extra tuple count or \(q_U^{-1/2}\) is inserted. The same proof applies.

**Unpaid:** nonprincipal good-character pairs, including their values at sixth-power additive frequencies; mixed embedded arguments \(e^2r,d^2r\); arbitrary \(A\)-dependent weights; growing slot counts; the full physical saving.

**Precise follow-up:** derive the actual embedded coherent row kernel first, with \(\operatorname{lcm}(D^2,E^2)\) and all character zeros. Once such a kernel is a fixed-sector divisibility combination, dilation introduces no difficulty for (A01.4), because \(1_{p^j\mid\lambda r}=1_{p^{(j-v_p(\lambda))_+}\mid r}\) and cannot increase coefficient \(\ell^1\) mass. The remaining problem is the correct character/coefficient incidence and total marked mass, not a blanket “long period” obstruction.

**Sources:** BB R08; [restricted research revision] AA14–AA20; [restricted research revision] AB16.

# [private research revision] moving Bessel detector: independent mathematical review

Status: independent review of the frozen discovery source, 11 October 2026.
The analytic return and finite-source reduction below pass review. The
actual arithmetic estimate B17-L1 is OPEN. This review proves no increase
in the zero-free constant and supplies no new kernel certification.



Frozen source examined in full:
`[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, 35,857 bytes,
SHA-256 `3721156c7614472f3db8552c28bae1eb010123c1ad32a790a6ffff30d570f060`.
The source's B labels are retained for comparison. The independent
extensions here are the explicit Gaussian coefficient-tail bound in HCR8,
the first-moment version of the baseline-class counterexample in HCR12,
and the updated first-gain calculation. These do not close B17-L1.

## HCR1. Disposition and actual input

I accept B0--B9a as an independently checked analytic construction and
conditional return, with exactly the all-dyad hypotheses stated below.
B9b's bounded partner correction is valid with a fixed positive baseline
buffer. B11--B12a are valid continuous-density calculations, including
the even correction, and establish no estimate for the actual Mobius
field. B13--B18 retain the literal coefficients and pay the two indicated
infinite complements. B19--B21 identify a genuine failure of the proposed
baseline-only proof, without proving that the arithmetic target is false.

To avoid confusing the filter parameter A with its coefficients, write

    a_n = mu(n) - 2*1_(2|n)*mu(n/2),
    g_tau(v) = (2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),
    f(u) = sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-u),   tau>0 fixed.

If n=2^j m, m odd and squarefree, the actual coefficient is mu(m) for j=0,
-3 mu(m) for j=1, 2 mu(m) for j=2, and 0 for j>=3. It is 0 if m is not
squarefree. In particular a_1=1, a_2=-3, a_4=2; replacing a_n by mu(n), or
deleting all squareful n, changes the field. The uniform bound |a_n|<=3
is used only for an absolute source tail, not for the main signed norm.

The ordinary buffered Mertens consequence of the accepted baseline is
used in its actual form: for EACH FIXED beta>b_* one has
M(y)=O_beta(y^beta). There is no estimate at beta=b_* or one uniform as
beta decreases to b_*. This is the ordinary interface already used by the
author; the external endpoint itself is a stipulated controller input,
not re-proved here. Every quantitative finite-source calculation uses the
old-safe exponent b=.8749, so the tiny baseline update changes none of its
tail estimates.

The summatory function of a_n is M(y)-2M(y/2). Partial summation against
g_tau therefore gives |f(u)|<=C_b exp(bu), u>=0, for each fixed b>b_*.
For u<=0, the direct absolutely convergent series gives

    |f(u)| <= C_tau exp(-u^2/(2*tau)).

Indeed (log n-u)^2 >= u^2+(log n)^2 there, and the remaining n-series
converges. Thus the left-tail transform

    E(s)=integral_(-infinity)^0 f(u) exp(-su) du

is entire. Initially by absolute Dirichlet convergence in Re s>1, and
then by continuation in Re s>b_*,

    Phi(s)=integral_R f(u) exp(-su) du
          =exp(tau*s^2/2)*(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s),
    F(s)=integral_0^infinity f(u) exp(-su) du=Phi(s)-E(s).

The last identity continues F meromorphically to C. Every nontrivial
zeta zero in 0<Re s<1 gives a pole of F of the same order: the Gaussian
factor never vanishes, and the zeros of 1-2^(1-s) all have Re s=1.
Subtracting the entire E cannot remove a pole.

## HCR2. Fixed-strength identity and moving-strength definition

For h>=0 and v>0 set

    B_h(v)=sqrt(h/v)*J_1(2*sqrt(hv)).

Its continuous endpoint value is B_h(0)=h. The Bessel power series gives

    B_h(v)=sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k h^(k+1)v^k/(k!*(k+1)!).

For Re p>0 the sum of the absolute term integrals is
exp(h/Re p)-1. Hence

    integral_0^infinity exp(-pv) B_h(v) dv = 1-exp(-h/p).

This checks B0, including its sign. The atom delta_0 has full unit mass
on the half-line, so the multiplier of delta_0-exp(-v)B_h(v)dv is
exp(-h/(1-s)), Re s<1. It is nonvanishing on that half-plane and has an
essential singularity at s=1; it is not an entire multiplier.

The source's real-argument estimates |J_1(z)|<=1 and |J_1(z)|<=|z|/2 follow
from the integral representations for J_n and J_1. I checked the power
series and the relevant integral identities against [NIST DLMF 10.2.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.2#E2)
and [DLMF 10.9.2, 10.9.4](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.9). In particular
|B_h(v)|<=h for all v>=0, as used in the actual-field bounds.

Now fix A>0, independent of u, and define for u>=0

    D_A f(u)=f(u)-integral_0^infinity exp(-v) B_(Au)(v) f(u+v) dv.

At u=0 the integral is zero. If b_*<b<1 is fixed, then

    |D_A f(u)| <= C_b exp(bu)*(1+Au/(1-b)).                 (HCR2.1)

Thus the signed full field defines an absolutely convergent v-integral.
The later arithmetic expansion over n must respect how this definition
was obtained; it does not authorize absolute double summation over the
entire future v-range.

Putting h=Au into the fixed-h identity is legitimate at a FIXED u when
acting on an exponential. It does not turn D_A into a fixed convolution
operator or give its one-sided Laplace transform by multiplication. For
example, applying D_A to f(u-c) uses strength Au, whereas shifting
D_A f by c uses A(u-c). Those operators do not generally commute. This
also prevents automatic import of the previous fixed-Gaussian coprime
convolution equivalence. The author's separate return calculation below
is necessary and supplies the missing bridge.

## HCR3. Independent reconstruction of the two-root transform

Let H(w)=integral_0^infinity D_A f(u) exp(-wu) du. For Re w>b, HCR2.1
and |B_(Au)(v)|<=Au make the triangular Fubini step absolutely valid:
the double absolute majorant is a constant times

    integral_0^infinity u exp(-(Re w-b)u)du
    * integral_0^infinity exp(-(1-b)v)dv < infinity.

Writing t=u+v gives H(w)=integral_0^infinity f(t)K_w(t)dt with

    K_w(t)=exp(-wt)-exp(-t)*integral_0^t exp((1-w)u)
                   *sqrt(Au/(t-u))*J_1(2sqrt(Au(t-u)))du.

In a far right q-half-plane, integrate the Bessel series term by term.
The k-th term in the transform of the second summand equals

    (-1)^k A^(k+1)/((q+w)^(k+2)*(q+1)^(k+1)).

Here the integrals of u^(k+1) and v^k cancel both factorials. The resulting
geometric series, initially where it converges absolutely, yields

    integral_0^infinity K_w(t)exp(-qt)dt
       = 1/(q+w)-A/((q+w)*((q+w)*(q+1)+A))
       = (q+1)/((q+1)*(q+w)+A).                           (HCR3.1)

Let s_1+s_2=1+w and s_1*s_2=w+A. Then the denominator is
(q+s_1)(q+s_2), and

    K_w(t)=[(1-s_1)exp(-s_1*t)+(s_2-1)exp(-s_2*t)]/(s_2-s_1).

For real w sufficiently large both roots have real part greater than b;
the smaller root tends to 1 from the right. In an open neighborhood of
such w we may integrate against f and obtain exactly

    H(w)=[(1-s_1)F(s_1)+(s_2-1)F(s_2)]/(s_2-s_1).         (HCR3.2)

The relation between each root and w is

    w=phi_A(s)=s-A/(1-s),
    s_(1,2)=(1+w +/- sqrt((1-w)^2-4A))/2.

The plus/minus ordering is immaterial. HCR3.2 is symmetric in the roots.
At a collision s_1=s_2=s with F regular, it tends to
F(s)-(1-s)F'(s). There is no forced branch singularity of the full field.
More generally a symmetric meromorphic divided difference descends
meromorphically through the quadratic cover. On compact w-sets its roots
remain bounded, so only finitely many poles of F occur. This gives a
single-valued meromorphic function R(w) on the whole plane. Applying the
same expression to the entire E gives an entire function of w, including
at collisions. The Gaussian left tail contributes no hidden branch pole.

For the displayed A values the collision roots 1+/-sqrt(A) are positive
real numbers where F is regular. Real zeta has no zero in (0,1), as also
follows from its alternating eta representation; it is nonzero for real
s>1. The reciprocal zeta factor is regular at 1. Larger A need not share
this collision simplification, but meromorphic descent still holds.

A useful independent sign/residue check is f(u)=exp(rho*u), Re rho<1.
Directly, D_A f(u)=exp(phi_A(rho)*u). Substitution of F(s)=1/(s-rho) in
HCR3.2 simplifies to 1/(w-phi_A(rho)), exactly. There is no extra Jacobian
or an additional unpriced exponential in this single-pole signal.

## HCR4. All-dyad norm return and complete pole accounting

The following is the exact sufficient theorem, expressed relative to the
updated accepted premise. Fix tau,A>0, 1/2<a<b_*, and a certified fixed
T>=1-a such that every nontrivial off-critical-line zero has |Im rho|>T.
Trivial zeros are outside the candidate region. Put

    d=A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2),      gamma_crit=a-d.

Assume d<c_* and gamma<=gamma_crit. If, for every epsilon>0 and every
sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |D_A f(u)|du
          <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),                 (HCR4.1)

then zeta has no zero with Re s>a. All of tau,A,a,T,gamma are fixed before
epsilon and X. The bound is required on every sufficiently large dyad,
not on a selected sequence of favorable shells. Its threshold X_0 and
constant may depend on epsilon and the fixed parameters. The stronger
bound with |D_A f|^2 and exponent 2gamma+epsilon suffices by
Cauchy--Schwarz on the constant-length logarithmic shell.

Proof: shells [k log 2,(k+1)log 2] tile the tail. On any compact subset
Re w>=gamma+eta, choose epsilon<eta. Summing HCR4.1 with exp(-Re w*u)
gives a convergent geometric series. Inserting any fixed power u^j does
not affect convergence. Therefore H and all its fixed w-derivatives are
holomorphic in Re w>gamma. The initial bounded u interval gives an entire
function. By HCR3.2 and the meromorphic identity theorem, H agrees there
with R and R has no pole in this half-plane.

Suppose a<Re rho<=b_* and set delta=1-Re rho. Then
c_*<=delta<1-a and |Im rho|>T. The other preimage of phi_A(rho) is

    rho^*=1-A/(1-rho).

Because delta/(delta^2+T^2) is increasing for 0<=delta<=T,

    Re rho^* = 1-A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)
              >= 1-d > b_*.

F is regular at rho^*. Moreover

    phi_A'(rho)=1-A/(1-rho)^2 != 0,
    (1-rho)/(rho^*-rho)=1/phi_A'(rho).

Nonvanishing follows already from delta>0 and Im rho!=0: (delta-i Im rho)^2
cannot be the positive real number A. Near w_0=phi_A(rho), a pole of F of
order m with leading coefficient C gives a pole of R of the same order
with leading coefficient C*phi_A'(rho)^(m-1). Thus simple-zero assumptions
are unnecessary; the simple-pole residue is unchanged. There cannot be
cancellation from another nontrivial or trivial zero, because the only
other root is in the accepted zero-free half-plane.

Finally, for |t|>=T>=1-a the function
1-delta-A*delta/(delta^2+t^2) decreases strictly in delta on this interval.
Since delta<1-a,

    Re phi_A(rho) > a-A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2) >= gamma.

This contradicts holomorphy of H. Zeros to the right of b_* were already
excluded by the baseline; zeros at height <=T are handled by the stated
finite-height input. The conclusion concerns the open region Re s>a;
gamma=gamma_crit is allowed because the candidate zero has Re rho>a.
This proves the conditional return, not its hypothesis.

## HCR5. The second root is quantitatively paid; T=10 is legitimate

Solving HCR3.2 for F(s), with s^*=1-A/(1-s), gives

    F(s)=phi_A'(s)*H(phi_A(s)) + A/(1-s)^2*F(s^*).         (HCR5.1)

For a<=Re s<=b_* and |Im s|>=T,

    Re s^*>=1-d,   |Im s^*|<=A/T,   |A/(1-s)^2|<=A/T^2.

Take the FIXED beta=(b_*+1-d)/2. From |f(u)|<=C_beta exp(beta*u),

    |F(s^*)| <= 2*C_beta/(c_*-d),

with a harmless fixed adjustment if the f bound was first stated only
for large u. Thus the second term is uniformly bounded by
2A C_beta/[T^2(c_*-d)]. This quantifies the complement over the entire
unbounded candidate-height range. No unknown norm of a reflected source
is being used. The identity is meromorphic, so it is also valid as an
identity near a possible candidate pole.

The low-height input has a primary-source justification: Platt and
Trudgian's Theorem 1 in [arXiv:2004.09765v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.09765v1)
certifies that the nontrivial zeros through height 3,000,175,332,800 lie
on Re s=1/2; its stated weaker 3*10^12 consequence is ample here. Negative
heights follow by conjugation, and the real interval (0,1) has no zeta zero.
Thus T=10 is a deliberately weaker permissible input, not an unverified
low-height assumption. This review checked the exact primary theorem;
it did not reproduce that computation.

This finite-height theorem only locates possible zeros. It neither
truncates the contour in B19 nor supplies HCR4.1/B17-L1. Those are still
all-large-dyad estimates for the complete field. T, A and the baseline
buffer cannot silently depend on X. One may instead fix the larger
certified T and use its better return constant, but the arithmetic input
must still be proved at an exponent below the accepted baseline.

## HCR6. First-gain boundary and exact target replay

For fixed A,T with T>c_* and the partner condition valid for a<b_* near
b_*, all HCR4 parameter conditions persist in a left neighborhood of b_*.
Continuity of gamma_crit(a,A,T) gives the sufficient strict condition

    gamma < b_*-A*c_*/(T^2+c_*^2).                         (HCR6.1)

Equality is not a claimed improvement. At A=.004, T=10, the updated
boundary is

    0.87488159624725557368024374471503149711926937645611...

and the deduction from b_* is

    0.000005003752744426319756255284968502880730623543890...

The source's .8748816432891003... is correct for its OLD b0; it is not the
first-gain threshold relative to the newly accepted c_*. No table row is
threatened by this correction. For T=3*10^12 the exact deduction remains
.004*c_*/(9*10^24+c_*^2), approximately 5.56059556*10^(-29), rather than
zero. Even that tiny loss does not turn a baseline bound into a gain.

The following entries use T=10. All finite decimals are exact rationals.

| a | Conditional c=1-a | A | gamma_crit | Chosen gamma | Exact gamma_crit-gamma |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .87449 | .12551 | .004 | .8744849803907270067... | .874484 | 490272582803/500078763800500000 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .007 | .8333216699065074516... | .83332 | 451/270075000 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .016 | .7499600249843847595... | .74995 | 321/32020000 |

The exact margins are positive. The respective d values are approximately
.000005019609273, .000011663426826, .000039975015615, all strictly less
than c_*. The .016 choice is valid even though A>c_*^2; the certified
height pays its partner. A<c_*^2 is only an optional sufficient shortcut
when no useful height bound is invoked, not a universal ceiling.

The corresponding density exponents 1-2sqrt(A) are approximately
.873508893593265, .832667994693185, and .747017787186530. They lie below
the chosen gammas. This is a checked comparison of the model exponents,
not an arithmetic estimate. The full second-moment target exponents
would be 1.748968, 1.66664 and 1.4999 respectively.

## HCR7. Density suppression survives the fixed Gaussian, with limits

For the continuous unsmoothed model f_0(u)=exp(u)/u, u>0, the future
integral converges absolutely even at growth exponent 1: the bound
|J_1|<=1 leaves v^(-3/2) at large v. Using
1/(u+v)=integral_0^infinity exp(-r(u+v))dr and B0 gives exactly

    D_A f_0(u)=exp(u)*integral_0^infinity exp(-u*(r+A/r))dr
             =2sqrt(A)*exp(u)*K_1(2sqrt(A)*u).

The last identity follows from [DLMF 10.32.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.32#E9),
or directly from r=sqrt(A) exp(t) and symmetry in t. The unique positive
saddle r=sqrt(A) yields

    D_A f_0(u) ~ sqrt(pi)*A^(1/4)*u^(-1/2)
                         *exp((1-2sqrt(A))*u).

In contrast, a fixed h gives exp(u-2sqrt(hu)) times u^(-3/4) and a fixed
constant. Substituting a moving strength into a fixed-order asymptotic
would not justify the result; the displayed exact integral does.

For the actual fixed smoothing of the density, put l=log 2 and

    P(u)=integral_l^infinity exp(y)/y*g_tau(y-u)dy.

For any fixed R>2sqrt(A), the identity 1/y=integral_0^infinity exp(-ry)dr
and completion of the Gaussian square give

    P(u)=integral_0^R c_tau(r)exp((1-r)u)dr + E_R(u),
    c_tau(r)=exp(tau*(1-r)^2/2),
    |E_R(u)| <= C*(exp((1-R)u)+exp(-c*u^2)),  u>=1.

The r>=R contribution is bounded by replacing 1/y by 1/l and integrating
the resulting full Gaussian. The missing y<l range for 0<=r<=R is
Gaussian-small, uniformly in that compact r interval. Filtering this
error costs at most O((1+u)exp((1-R)u))+O(poly(u)exp(-c'*u^2)).

For completeness, interchange of r and v in the main term needs a bound
near r=0. Compactness bounds c_tau(r), and
integral_0^R exp(-r(u+v))dr<=1/(u+v). Together with
|B_(Au)(v)|<=sqrt(Au/v) this is integrable at infinity; near zero use
|B_(Au)(v)|<=Au. Thus absolute Fubini holds, and the main term becomes

    integral_0^R c_tau(r)exp(u*(1-r-A/r))dr.

At its interior saddle r=sqrt(A), (r+A/r)''=2/sqrt(A). Laplace's method
therefore proves the precise constant

    D_A P(u) ~ exp(tau*(1-sqrt(A))^2/2)*sqrt(pi)*A^(1/4)
                   *u^(-1/2)*exp((1-2sqrt(A))*u).           (HCR7.1)

The model of the q_2 image of the prime portion of mu is
-P(u)+2P(u-log 2). Applying the SAME strength Au to this whole function
replaces c_tau(r) by (2^r-1)c_tau(r), so HCR7.1's constant is multiplied
by 2^sqrt(A)-1>0. This is correct despite the noncommutation in HCR2:
it does not shift the already filtered P, which would use the wrong
strength. The q_2 numerator has not been dropped.

None of this is a prime-sum asymptotic or a norm bound for a_n. Even a
granted pointwise prime remainder O(exp(bu)), b>b_* fixed, is sent by the
available estimate to O((1+u)exp(bu)), above all target exponents. A
continuous model cannot remove the rest of mu's signed coefficients or
their interactions. Nor is its saddle exponent a forced branch floor for
the full detector: HCR3's meromorphic full F is regular at the numerical
collision roots, and its symmetric branches cancel there. The density
model has a different singularity structure. No positivity inference
from a prime component to the full signed field is used or permitted.

## HCR8. Finite arithmetic reduction and both infinite complements

Fix tau=1, b=.8749 and A,V>0. For u>=1 define

    N(u)=floor(exp((1+V)u+sqrt(u))),
    W_u(n)=g_1(log n-u)
       -integral_0^(Vu) exp(-v)B_(Au)(v)g_1(log n-u-v)dv,
    Q_(A,V)(u)=sum_(1<=n<=N(u)) a_n W_u(n).                (HCR8.1)

The cap is inclusive, all mu zeros are literal, and B_(Au)(0)=Au.
The continuous upper integration endpoint is Vu; changing a single
endpoint has no effect. These definitions are exact for the actual field.

First, before any arithmetic expansion, the signed-field future obeys

    |integral_(Vu)^infinity exp(-v)B_(Au)(v)f(u+v)dv|
       <= C_b Au/(1-b)*exp((b-(1-b)V)u).                  (HCR8.2)

This uses only the fixed baseline bound for the COMPLETE f. The sign
cancellations already present in f must not be replaced by an absolute
sum of coefficients in this infinite-v estimate.

Second, on 0<=v<=Vu the n-series may be interchanged absolutely. Here is
a direct uniform verification of its cap error, slightly sharpening B15.
Put y=u+v, h=(1+V)u+sqrt(u). Since n>N(u) implies n>exp(h),

    log n-y > sqrt(u)+(Vu-v) >= sqrt(u).

Thus even the integer floor causes no loss in the lower bound for an
included omitted term. The decreasing positive function
t -> g_1(log t-y) can be bounded by its first omitted term plus its
integral from that term to infinity. Changing variable z=log t-y gives

    integral_(t_0)^infinity g_1(log t-y)dt
       =exp(y+1/2)*GaussianTail(log t_0-y-1).

The lower endpoint is at least sqrt(u)-1. The usual Gaussian tail bound,
with a larger constant for bounded u, and |a_n|<=3 consequently give

    sum_(n>N(u)) |a_n|g_1(log n-u-v)
       <= C exp(u/2+v+sqrt(u)),   0<=v<=Vu, u>=1.          (HCR8.3)

One can equally use the source's weaker O(sqrt(u)) notation. The first
omitted term is smaller than this bound. Multiplication by exp(-v)
cancels its exp(v), and |B_(Au)(v)|<=Au makes the integrated coefficient
tail at most C A V u^2 exp(u/2+sqrt(u)). The direct g_1 tail obeys the
same bound without that polynomial. It follows that

    D_A f(u)=Q_(A,V)(u)
       +O_(A,b,V)(u exp(q_v*u))
       +O_(A,V)((1+u^2)exp(u/2+sqrt(u))),
    q_v=b-(1-b)V.                                        (HCR8.4)

This proves B13--B16 without a full-future arithmetic Fubini step. The
constants are independent of u. The coefficient tail is
O_epsilon(exp((1/2+epsilon)u)) for each fixed epsilon>0, not a bare
uniform O(exp(u/2)). The choice tau=1 matters: for general fixed tau and
cap exp((1+V)u+B sqrt(u)), the same calculation has coefficient-tail
power 1-B^2/(2tau), up to exp(O(sqrt(u))). It is not legitimate to vary
tau or the cap silently while borrowing the stated 1/2 exponent.

## HCR9. Norm transfer, cap cost and every signed interaction

If gamma>1/2 and q_v<gamma, HCR8.4 gives an error smaller than exp(gamma*u)
for all sufficiently large u after its fixed polynomial and square-root
factors are absorbed. Therefore the all-dyad, every-epsilon L1 bound

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |Q_(A,V)(u)|du
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)                    (HCR9.1)

implies HCR4.1. In fact the two L1 hypotheses are equivalent at that
exponent because the same additive error works in the reverse direction.
The analogous L2 hypotheses are equivalent by the norm triangle
inequality. No Cauchy--Schwarz loss in the field exponent occurs in
transferring between D_A f and Q. L2 implies L1; L1 need not imply L2.

The exact source choices are:

| A | gamma | V | q_v | gamma-q_v | Cap scale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .004 | .874484 | .004 | .8743996 | .0000844 | x^1.004 exp(sqrt(log x)) |
| .007 | .83332 | .34 | .832366 | .000954 | x^1.34 exp(sqrt(log x)) |
| .016 | .74995 | 1.01 | .748549 | .001401 | x^2.01 exp(sqrt(log x)) |

All q_v are strictly below gamma, and all gamma exceed 1/2. With the
author's V=1.01, the quarter target's source extending beyond x^2 is a real
cost, not a logarithmic tail. This table does not assert that 1.01 is the
smallest permissible V. The floor and bounded initial u interval do not
change it.

For the optional second moment set U=log X, L=log 2, and
N_max=N(U+L). Since N is increasing, its exact Gram is

    sum_(m,n<=N_max) a_m a_n
       *integral_U^(U+L) 1_(m<=N(u))*1_(n<=N(u))*W_u(m)*W_u(n)du.

This is B18. Kernels and coefficients are real. Both moving cap masks
must remain inside the integral. Expanding W_u(m)W_u(n) gives direct,
both direct/future cross terms, and the double future integral. Expanding
each a_n gives all four q_2 terms with multipliers 1,-2,-2,4 and their
correspondingly shifted integer caps. No diagonal, rough-prime mask,
projector, coprimality gate or positive subfamily can replace this Gram.
If a decomposition is introduced, every interaction or a proved
whole-field norm inequality must return it to HCR9.1/B18.

The author has not asserted a false signed-subfamily inference here.
The previous fixed-Gaussian four-diagonal/coprime results also do not
by themselves bound this new moment over a future range as long as
[x,x^(1+V)]. HCR8.1 and HCR3 are this replacement detector's own source
and return, which is why the reconstruction is meaningful despite that
remaining arithmetic difficulty.

## HCR10. Exact remaining first-gain target

For tau=1, A=.004, V=.004, and gamma=.874484, use the literal a_n, N(u)
and W_u(n) of HCR8.1. The unresolved claim is

    for every epsilon>0, for all sufficiently large dyadic X,
    integral_(log X)^(log(2X))
       |sum_(1<=n<=floor(exp(1.004u+sqrt(u)))) a_n
          [g_1(log n-u)-integral_0^(.004u) exp(-v)
             *sqrt(.004u/v)*J_1(2sqrt(.004uv))
             *g_1(log n-u-v)dv]| du
       <<_epsilon X^(.874484+epsilon).                   (HCR10.1)

All parameters are frozen before epsilon and X. This is B17-L1 with all
coefficients and endpoints restored. If proved, HCR8--HCR9 would give
HCR4.1 and HCR4 would exclude Re s>.87449, yielding c=.12551. It has not
been proved. A first gain smaller than that target could instead use any
fixed gamma below HCR6.1, with V and a chosen to pay the same explicit
conditions. The externally accepted .1251134 endpoint cannot replace
the missing estimate.

## HCR11. Exact easy bound and its failed inequality

Choose FIXED b_*<beta<b<1. Partial summation gives

    1/zeta(b+it)=(b+it)*integral_1^infinity M(y)y^(-b-it-1)dy,
    |Phi(b+it)| <= C_(b,beta,tau)(1+|t|)exp(-tau*t^2/2).

The weighted f is integrable on the whole real line, and Phi is
integrable in t, so Fourier inversion is legitimate. Substituting it into
D_A is an absolute Fubini step: |B_(Au)(v)|<=Au and b<1 dominate the
future integral, uniformly in t before the integrable Phi factor. B0
then gives the actual all-height contour

    D_A f(u)=(2*pi)^(-1)*integral_R Phi(b+it)
                              *exp(u*phi_A(b+it))dt.      (HCR11.1)

Let delta=1-b>0 and 0<tau'<tau. For y=delta^2+t^2, the arithmetic-geometric
mean inequality gives

    tau'*t^2/2 + A*delta*u/(delta^2+t^2)
       =tau'*y/2+A*delta*u/y-tau'*delta^2/2
       >=sqrt(2*A*delta*tau'*u)-tau'*delta^2/2.

The remaining exp(-(tau-tau')t^2/2) absorbs (1+|t|). Hence

    |D_A f(u)| <= C exp(bu-sqrt(2*A*(1-b)*tau'*u)).         (HCR11.2)

This is B20. The contour uses all real t, not only |t|<=T or a fixed
window. For an absolute pointwise contour argument to force exponent
gamma<b, the missing uniform attenuation would be

    A*(1-b)/((1-b)^2+t^2) >= b-gamma   for every real t.

Its left side tends to zero. Optimizing it against the Gaussian puts
|t| at order u^(1/4), producing only the square-root-u loss in HCR11.2.
A Gaussian cutoff at order sqrt(u) leaves these smaller but growing
heights inside the contour. A fixed-height estimate does not cover them.

This failed inequality is a failure of the easy absolute method, not a
necessary condition for all possible estimates exploiting the phase and
the actual arithmetic coefficients. Nor may b decrease with u using an
uncontrolled C_b. The family of buffered estimates gives the usual
every-epsilon exponent b_* and none of the proposed improved exponents.
Combined with HCR8.4 it also pays the finite Q at exponent b_*, which is
strictly above the first-gain boundary.

## HCR12. Baseline-class obstruction, including the first moment

The author's stress test shows why growth and Gaussian smoothing alone
cannot close the gap. It can be strengthened to the actual L1 norm used
in B17-L1, while retaining the important scope limitation.

Fix a large real t and s=b_*+it. Define the test density

    f_s(u)=integral_0^infinity exp(sy)g_tau(y-u)dy.

It has a Gaussian left tail and satisfies |f_s(u)|<=C_s exp(b_*u) on the
right. Completing the full Gaussian and subtracting y<0 gives, as u
increases,

    f_s(u)=exp(tau*s^2/2)*exp(su)+O_s(exp(-c*u^2)).

The subtracted half-line is bounded by a Gaussian directly; filtering
that error with |B_(Au)(v)|<=Au preserves Gaussian decay up to a fixed
polynomial. Therefore

    D_A f_s(u)=exp(tau*s^2/2)*exp(phi_A(s)u)
                              +O_s(poly(u)exp(-c'*u^2)).

For any gamma<b_*, choose the FIXED t so large that

    t^2 > A*c_*/(b_*-gamma)-c_*^2.

Then lambda=Re phi_A(s)>gamma. We can also ensure
omega=Im phi_A(s)=t*(1-A/(c_*^2+t^2)) is nonzero. Taking the real part
gives a real test function. On a fixed interval of length L=log 2, the
integral of exp(lambda*v)|cos(omega*v+theta)| has a positive minimum as
theta varies over a compact period: continuity and omega!=0 exclude an
identically zero cosine. The integral with weight exp(2lambda*v) and
cosine squared has the same property. Consequently,
uniformly over all sufficiently large shell starting points U,

    integral_U^(U+L) |D_A Re(f_s)(u)|du >= c_s exp(lambda*U),
    integral_U^(U+L) |D_A Re(f_s)(u)|^2du >= c_s' exp(2lambda*U).

The Gaussian errors are negligible. Choosing epsilon<lambda-gamma
disproves the every-epsilon L1 target at gamma in this baseline-controlled
Gaussian-smoothed class; the L2 assertion fails too. The small factor
|exp(tau*s^2/2)| is a nonzero fixed constant and cannot alter an exponent.

This is NOT a counterexample with the actual a_n, nor with the exact
zeta transform Phi. It proves only that the baseline growth hypothesis
and the chosen smoothing do not force the desired saving. A successful
proof must use additional structure of the actual signed arithmetic
field. The source makes the correct distinction; this review does not
promote the class obstruction to impossibility of B17-L1.

## HCR13. Research disposition and next mathematical action

The useful contribution survives independent review: a moving detector
with an exact, globally consistent two-root return; a uniformly paid
second root; and a finite actual-coefficient source with both infinite
complements controlled. The continuous model has a genuine power saving,
but the first inexpensive actual-field argument stops at the accepted
buffered baseline. The first unpaid quantity is precisely HCR10.1.

The next mathematical action should retain its signed coefficients and
moving kernel and seek a bound for that L1 integral, or an eligible bound
for its complete Gram. Any proposed source decomposition must price its
cross terms and the future range before comparison with the conditional
c targets. Another finite-height verification or a stronger density-model
asymptotic alone does not address the failed all-height arithmetic step.

This report supports controller acceptance of the conditional adapters
and the scoped failures. It does not establish c=.12551, 1/6 or 1/4, and
does not certify any new formal kernel. Novelty is confined to what was
derived and compared in this project record; no literature-priority
claim is made. Final readback, byte count and SHA-256 are supplied in the
handoff after the last write; this file contains no self-referential hash.

statement:
# [private research revision]: a paid initial segment of the completed detector

The [partial author](high-core/report.md) and
[independent recovery review](high-core-review/report.md) establish G131–G133
below. The review completes the author's unfinished estimate. These are
useful bounds on the actual arithmetic source, not a larger zero-free
constant. The accepted source-relative value remains
`c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`, with
`theta11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364`. Inherited F0/analytic ancestry,
positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain
OPEN. No formalization or public record claim is made.

The source is pinned PR9 `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`, especially
B0.7–B0.16 and B3.1–B3.6, B3.31–B3.39 and B3.52. The retained [restricted research revision] marked
amplification and PR15 natural-row conventions supply the marked extension
and ideal count. Exact input hashes and fourteen byte-preserved artifacts
are in the [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json). Source-relative
use does not re-prove that entire analytic ancestry.

## G131. Complementary divisors and the actual Poisson boundary

Use ideal norms and the literal cutoff V, equal to one on [0,1] and zero
on [2,infinity). Let `R=U^(4/3)` and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).

For every nonunit n, the complete divisor sum of mu is zero, so exactly

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n) mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)]
          =-sum_(m|n) mu(n/m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].             (1)

The unit is excluded: its left side is one and complementary sum zero.
Nonzero summands have `Nd>R`; under `Nn<=C L`, therefore `Nm<C L/R`.
There is no coprimality restriction. Complete multiplicativity of the
natural character `phi_u` preserves (1), including shared primes and
all natural zeros. If every proper divisor has norm at most R, the
original sum gives `A_R(n)=mu(n)[V(Nn/R)-1]`.

On good squarefree n only, the source Gauss identities give

    gamma_1 gamma_2=mu alpha G,  a0=conj(alpha)gamma_2,
    |gamma_2|=1,
    A_R(n)gamma_1(n)=G(n)conj(a0(n))mu(n)A_R(n),
    mu(n)A_R(n)=-sum_(m|n)mu(m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].         (2)

Here G is the fixed ray function. The last formula fails at prime squares:
the formal n=4,R=2 example has left side zero and right side minus one.
Equation (1) still holds. Even on squarefree n, the new amplitude can
equal two when n has three distinct prime factors individually at most R
and pair products at least 2R. Thus it is not the literal coefficient
allowed by B3.6, which permits no further arithmetic coefficient on n.
A divisor bound does not repair that source contract. This obstruction
does not prove a lower bound for the actual signed sum.

For coprime good squarefree nonunit l,l', without slots or a moving row
selector, the clean sixth-free row Poisson specialization is

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') sum_b mu(b)/(Nb)^6 1_((b,ll')=1) R(l,l')
      *sum_h Gcal(l,h)conj(Gcal(l',-h))
        F(Phi)(U Nh/((Nb)^6 Nl Nl')).                    (3)

The b range is finite, `Nb<=(C_Phi U)^(1/6)`. The CRT factor is the actual
reciprocity sign R(l,l'). The conjugate Fourier factor explains `-h`;
the two Gauss normalizers explain `U/sqrt(Nl Nl')`. The identity
`u=b^6 k` retains all six units in k, without multiplying b by six.
The scalar from b is the displayed natural-zero indicator. Frequency
zero vanishes for these nonprincipal natural characters.

A fixed ray restriction still needs its finite character expansion; a
fixed hole mask needs every `d|rad(E)` with its coefficient, scalar and
rescaled kernel; omitted fixed-inducing rows need their actual subtraction.
Shared support, arbitrary valuations and original slots require the full
source reconstruction. A zero-bin selector cannot be inserted into (3).
At `Nl,Nl'~L=U^(4/3)`, the first dual length is `L^2/U=U^(5/3)`, so this
first transform alone does not produce a short dual sum.

## G132. A complete positive prefix estimate

Fix a finite natural dictionary and one whole orientation. Let H be smooth,
equal to one on [0,1], between zero and one, supported in [0,C] for fixed
C. For fixed `B`, bounded `lambda>=0`, and `t=4/3`, put

    L=U^(t+lambda), Y=U^B,
    P_u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n) A_R(n) (Nn)^(-s)
                         exp(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L).             (4)

All nonunit terms below R vanish anyway. For
`17/25<=delta<=7/10`, set `a=(1+delta)/2`. Let N0(P) be the sum over
nonzero sixth-free element rows, with a nonnegative smooth ball majorant,
of squared tensor Sobolev norms on `[a,1] x [-T-1,T+1]`, using derivatives
`partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j`, `i,j in {0,1}`. The real interval has
width at least 3/20. For every epsilon>0,

    N0(P) << H_J U^(J(delta,lambda)+epsilon),
    J(delta,lambda)=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.     (5)

H_J retains finite smooth seminorms and polynomial height costs. Constants
may depend on the fixed dictionary and profiles; no moving conductor
uniformity is inferred.

To prove (5), insert (1) before expanding a square:

    P_u(s)=-sum_(Nm<C L/R) phi_u(m)(Nm)^(-s)
       *sum_d mu(d)phi_u(d)(Nd)^(-s)[1-V(Nd/R)]
                      H(Nd Nm/L)exp(-Nd Nm/Y).           (6)

On a d dyad of size D, `D` is at least a fixed multiple of R and
`D<<L/Nm`. The inner inverse coefficient remains exactly `mu(d)phi_u(d)`.
The coupled cutoffs are common smooth profiles: on fixed positive annuli,
all Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded in their positive dilation
parameters. Apply the full-box B3.3 common-profile representation before
choosing a live m or row. Freeze the entire profile during restoration;
in particular, do not reset R when the inverse scale is shortened.

The old centrally normalized inverse moment and its Sobolev consequence
give `H_J U^(1/6)D^(5/6+epsilon)` in this range, including the row ball's
smaller dyads and unit window. The weight `Nd^(-s)` changes its squared
bound by `D^(1-2a)=D^(-delta)`. All mixed derivatives pay logarithms and
the retained finite height factors. Hilbert triangle over D is dominated
by `D<<L/Nm`, since `5/6-delta>0`. The outside character is a contraction
even at shared primes and natural zeros. The resulting norm is at most

    H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon)L^((5/6-delta)/2)
       *sum_(Nm<C L/R)(Nm)^(-a-(5/6-delta)/2).

The exponent on Nm is exactly `-11/12`. The ideal count O(X), with its
unit included, bounds this sum by `O((L/R)^(1/12))`. Squaring gives
`U^(1/6+epsilon)L^(5/6-delta)(L/R)^(1/6)`, exactly (5). No signed
cancellation between cofactors was assumed or hidden in a divisor loss.

For the actual original slot product Q_u of total width v, keep the
slots inside the same positive norm. The retained marked inverse estimate
has exponent

    E_MI(1,r,v)=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2v,(2r+8v)/3).

With active `r>=4/3+o(1)` and `v<=1/20`, its maximum is `r+2v`. Thus the
same proof yields

    Nv(P Q) << H_J U^(J(delta,lambda)+5v/3+epsilon).     (7)

This uses the [restricted research revision] fine slot mesh, chosen from the loss and bounded ranges
before the eventual dictionary, slots, profiles and heights. Original
independent heights and the complete orientation remain. Shared cofactor
and slot primes are handled by the natural contraction, not deleted.
Equation (7) bounds the complete positive norm, not a signed pair slice.

## G133. Two restricted returns with rational interval certificates

For actual nonprincipal buffered zero rows, the licensed completed detector
has `D_R,u(rho_u)=-1+O(U^(-A))`. Its original contour, smoothing and height
order must be retained. On the subset E_pre where `|P_u(rho_u)|>=1/4`,
positive Sobolev evaluation bounds the cardinality by (5). Only then use
the physical bin slot estimate `|Q_u|^2<<H_J U^(delta v+epsilon)`:

    sum_(u in E_pre)|Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(J+delta v+epsilon). (8)

This is a positive counting argument, with no E_pre selector in Poisson.
It is not a principal detector theorem or an arbitrary coefficient moment.

Keep the independently accepted preceding-family constant
`K=28114053/6250000`; do not feed c11 back into it. Write

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,a_K+b_K v).

All denominators, k and b_K are positive on the closed delta interval.
For `0<=lambda<=1/2500` and `0<=v<=1/25`,

    E_K-(J+delta v)>=1/5000.                             (9)

Indeed, set `J0=23/18-4delta/3`. A sufficient lower bound after subtracting
1/5000 is `rho-J0-a_K-b_K/25-(1-delta)/2500-1/5000`.
Multiply by `3h D_K` and substitute `delta=17/25+x/50`. Its cubic
Bernstein coefficients on `0<=x<=1` are

    17291065395149/1464843750000000,
    35476907047777/109863281250000,
    25900645202087/43945312500000,
    24797299722/30517578125,

all positive. This is a whole-interval certificate. For the full marked
norm, `0<=v<=1/200` suffices for

    E_K-(J+5v/3)>=1/5000.                                (10)

Use `min(3kv,a_K+b_K v)<=3kv`. Multiply the sufficient lower bound
`rho-J0-(1-delta)/2500-(5/3-delta+3k)/200-1/5000` by `3h`.
Its quadratic Bernstein coefficients after the same substitution are
`737/1171875,37031/3750000,1993/125000`, all positive.
After choosing all epsilon, buffer, endpoint, logarithm and height-power
shares to spend less than 1/10000, at least 1/10000 remains. The unspent
algebraic 1/5000 must not be advertised as the final paid margin.

The proposed whole range `v<=1/20` fails already for (8): at
`delta=17/25,v=1/20,lambda=0`, its exact comparison is
`-228190682/298987653375`. Larger lambda worsens that value. No global
optimality follows, but this failed extension must be retained.

## The remaining mathematical task

Define `D_far=D_R-P` with exactly the same H, before merging slots or
expanding pairs. The completed terminal exponential tail is paid under
its existing contract. Hilbert triangle pays prefix/far crosses only
after both complete norms are bounded. Alternatively the zero signal
splits the rows into `|P|>=1/4` or `|D_far|>=1/4`; (8) pays only the former.
The latter still requires its complete weighted bound with original
slots, valuations, natural zeros, common factors and tails.

The initial segment is not a high-conductor sector of the expanded
merged polynomial. No R22 signed sector has been removed. In particular
this positive exponent bound does not resolve the unit-row obstruction
in an unrelated negative-exponent target. A complete far-source estimate
and physical return are OPEN. That exact residual, rather than another
clean coprime Poisson calculation, is the next useful attack.

The independent helper verifies 4364 finite formal divisor examples and
the seven rational interval coefficients; infinite claims use the written
proofs above. Root read the complete author, review and helper plus exact
primary source slices and marked-amplifier proof. Original missed
13:15/13:45 deadlines, the partial author freeze, and the separately
completed 15:15 recovery review remain immutable provenance. All original
29 families/109 children and nearer targets,1/6,1/4 remain preserved.

statement:
## T07. Common-divisor cancellation with the actual prime marks

**Status: PROVED RELATIVE TO the inherited physical inputs; the sharper versions also use the explicitly imported all-finite-order Hecke strip I-HECKE.** They do not follow from a Riemann-zeta-only premise. Sources: SA Parts IV–V, CC1–CC40 and PM1–PM19. The original common-core mechanism occurs in inherited SG §8; the new scope here is the full physical compensator.

For \(G\ge1\) and a fixed smooth annular \(w\), localize the *true squarefree-core gcd*:
\[
 \mathcal C(G)=\sum_{c\ne c'}w(q_{(c,c')}/G)\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle.
 \tag{T07.1}
\]
For every \(\epsilon>0\), the following upper bounds hold, with \(Y^{-1}\mathcal F_AZ^\epsilon\) suppressed:

| Assumptions on the marks and analytic input | Bound for \(|\mathcal C(G)|/(Y^{-1}\mathcal F_AZ^\epsilon)\) |
|---|---:|
| Absolute core counting, original mark envelope | \(ZL/G\) |
| Bounded marks in the original slots; ordinary smooth character Poisson | \(Z^{3/2}L^{5/2}/G^2\) |
| Bounded marks in those slots; I-HECKE | \(Z^{1+b_0/2}L^{3-b_0/2}/G^2\) |
| **Actual smooth product prime weights**; I-HECKE | \(Z^{1+b_0/2}L^{1+3b_0/2}/G^2\) |

The limiting exponents in the last two rows mean arbitrary-loss estimates obtained on fixed buffered lines. No contour passes along \(\Re s=b_0/2\).

### 1. The coupled character survives all mixed embeddings

For two branches write
\[
 D=G_*d,\quad E=G_*e,\quad(d,e)=1,
 \quad m'=[D,E]^2r,
 \quad c=gu,\quad c'=gv,
\]
where \(g,u,v\) are pairwise coprime squarefree cores and \(u\ne v\). The original rows are \(e^2r,d^2r\). The cubic Gauss cocycle and row characters give, respectively,
\[
 \gamma_2(gu)\overline{\gamma_2(gv)}
 =\gamma_2(u)\overline{\gamma_2(v)}\vartheta_g(v)\overline{\vartheta_g(u)},
\]
\[
 \chi_g(e^2r)\overline{\chi_g(d^2r)}
 =\vartheta_g(e)\overline{\vartheta_g(d)}.
\]
The angular and multiplicative core phases cancel, and the remaining quadratic-refinement phase is a fixed-ray factor by M B1.4. Consequently the moving character in \(g\) is exactly
\[
 \psi(g)=\vartheta_g(ve)\overline{\vartheta_g(ud)}, \tag{T07.2}
\]
times one of finitely many characters supported on the original fixed set. Natural zeros impose
\[
 (g,ruvde)=1,\qquad(u,e)=(v,d)=1. \tag{T07.3}
\]
These conditions imply \((ve,ud)=1\). Every good prime exponent in either product is one or two. Hence the good conductor is \(\operatorname{rad}(uvde)\), with norm \(R\ll q_uq_vq_dq_e\). Its character is nonprincipal unless all four labels are units, which would give the excluded equality \(c=c'\). A fixed-place twist cannot cancel a nontrivial good conductor. This argument is performed before row Poisson or outer-column Cauchy; the outer fields are independent of \(g\) after the finite ray split.

### 2. Squarefree sums and the two weaker cancellation bounds

The inherited smooth Poisson estimate, obtained by opening \(\mu^2(k)=\sum_{a^2\mid k}\mu(a)\), is
\[
 \sum_{k\ {\rm sf},(k,M)=1}\psi(k)W(q_k/K)
 \ll(KRq_M)^\epsilon\min(K,K^{1/2}R^{1/4}).
\]
Indeed an ordinary smooth character sum of length \(U\) is \(O(\min(U,\sqrt R))\); split the \(a\)-sum at \(q_a=\sqrt K R^{-1/4}\). Finite coprimality masks are kept during the opening and cost a subpower. For a forced squarefree divisor \(F\), substitution \(g=Fk\) therefore gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}
 \frac{\psi(g)}{q_g}W(q_g/G)
 \ll(GRq_Mq_F)^\epsilon G^{-1/2}q_F^{-1/2}R^{1/4}. \tag{T07.4}
\]
Incompatible forced divisors give zero.

For the Hecke improvement fix \(b_0<b<1\), put \(\sigma=b/2\), and keep this choice fixed before varying scales. The inherited buffered bounds and the primitive functional equation give by three lines
\[
 |L(s,\psi)|\ll R^{(b-\Re s)/2+\epsilon}T^A,
 \qquad1-b\le\Re s\le b.
\]
Here \(\sigma\ge1-b\), since \(b>2/3\). The exact series is
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}\psi(g)q_g^{-s}
 =\psi(F)q_F^{-s}\frac{L^S(s,\psi)}{L^S(2s,\psi^2)}
 \prod_{p\mid FM,\,p\notin S}(1+\psi(p)q_p^{-s})^{-1}. \tag{T07.5}
\]
Ramified factors retain value zero. The good part of \(\psi^2\) is nonprincipal; its reciprocal is bounded on \(2\sigma=b>b_0\). Finite factors are nonzero for \(\Re s>0\) and cost \((q_Fq_M)^\epsilon\). Moving the Mellin line gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}
 \frac{\psi(g)}{q_g}W(q_g/G)
 \ll(GRq_Mq_F)^\epsilon G^{\sigma-1}q_F^{-\sigma}R^{\sigma/2}T^A.
 \tag{T07.6}
\]
This has the same form as (T07.4), with \(\sigma=1/2\) in the Poisson case.

For bounded marks, assign each marked prime first to \(g\), then to its residual core, then to its cube label. This is a disjoint assignment even when cores and cubes share primes. Forced assignments give divisibility in \(g,u,v,n,n'\); priority exclusions stay inside \(M\). After applying (T07.4) or (T07.6), ideal counting gives
\[
 \sum_{A\mid u}q_u^{-1/2+\sigma/2}E(q_u/H)
 \ll H^{(1+\sigma)/2}q_A^{-1},
\]
and the cube exponents become \(1+3(1+\sigma)/2>1\). Every distinct marked prime pays at least \(q_p^{-\sigma}\). A slot marked once therefore costs at most \(P^{1-\sigma+\epsilon}\); a slot marked on both sides costs at most \(P^{2(1-\sigma)+\epsilon}\), including its equal-prime diagonal. The completed core/cube sums have bound
\[
 G^{-2}Z^{1+\sigma}(L_DL_E)^{(3-\sigma)/2}(q_dq_e)^{\sigma/2}Z^\epsilon.
 \tag{T07.7}
\]
This proves the two weaker cancellation rows after the outer/embedding accounting in §4 below. The actual profiles used in the \(g\)-sum are the annular gcd weight times the two original \(V\)-factors. Their derivatives on \(q_g\asymp G\) have the envelope factors \(E(Gq_uq_n^3/N_D)E(Gq_vq_{n'}^3/N_E)\). Divisor losses involving arbitrarily large columns are absorbed into these envelopes, so no compact truncation of the log-Gaussian is assumed.

### 3. The extra saving from the actual prime slots

For the original smooth/fixed-character prime weights, keep the assigned-to-\(g\) primes inside the transform. Set
\[
 \mathscr S_M(s)=\frac{L^S(s,\psi)}{L^S(2s,\psi^2)}
       \prod_{p\mid M,\,p\notin S}(1+\psi(p)q_p^{-s})^{-1},
 \qquad f_s(p)=\frac{\psi(p)q_p^{-s}}{1+\psi(p)q_p^{-s}}.
\]
For \((F,M\mathfrak f_\psi)=1\), the exact forced series equals
\(\mathscr S_M(s)\prod_{p\mid F}f_s(p)\). At \(\Re s=\sigma=b/2\),
\[
 f_s(p)=\psi(p)q_p^{-s}-\psi(p)^2q_p^{-2s}+O(q_p^{-3\sigma}).
 \tag{T07.8}
\]
Both leading good characters remain nonprincipal after every fixed-place factor. The inherited prime estimate therefore gives, for a fixed smooth annular \(w\), fixed real \(\Re a\), and a deleted radical \(B\),
\[
 \sum_{p\nmid B}\eta_0(p)w(q_p/P)q_p^a f_s(p)
 \ll P^{\Re a+b-\sigma+\epsilon}(Rq_B)^\epsilon T^A.
 \tag{T07.9}
\]
To see every term: the first two powers cost \(P^{\Re a+b-j\sigma+\epsilon}\), \(j=1,2\). The remaining powers cost \(P^{\Re a+1-3\sigma+\epsilon}\), which is smaller because \(1\le2b\). Removing specified primes costs their divisor count. Thus the first potentially principal third power is paid, not suppressed.

If both sides mark the same slot, independent prime sums count a common prime twice. The *exact* correction is the single-prime sum with multiplier
\[
 f_s(p)-f_s(p)^2
 =\psi(p)q_p^{-s}-2\psi(p)^2q_p^{-2s}+O(q_p^{-3\sigma}).
 \tag{T07.10}
\]
It obeys (T07.9) with the combined norm power; since \(b-\sigma>0\), its bound fits that of the product of the two slot sums. Different slots have disjoint supports.

Fix \(u,v,n,n',r,D,E\) and a priority pattern. Marks assigned outside \(g\) have divisor-many choices, because they divide those fixed cores or cube labels. Freeze them first. Their priority exclusions enter \(M\). Marks assigned to \(g\) avoid those choices and the embedded products, and are summed with (T07.9)–(T07.10). A common prime of \(D,E\) is excluded as a *mark*, but is not deleted from \(g\) unless an original character zero requires it. A prime assigned to \(g\) on one side and outside it on the other is correctly excluded. A prime in both \(g\) and a cube label remains allowed.

For completeness, the original coupled profiles survive this step as follows. Let \(a,a'\) be their independent Mellin variables and \(z\) the variable of \(w(q_g/G)\). Replace \(z\) by the squarefree-series variable \(s=1+a+a'+z\). The transformed factor is
\[
 \widehat w(s-1-a-a')G^{s-1-a-a'}\widehat V(a)\widehat{\bar V}(a')
 (Z/(q_uq_n^3))^a(Z/(q_vq_{n'}^3))^{a'}\mathscr S_M(s),
\]
times the finite prime expressions, with \(q_U^a,q_{U'}^{a'}\) still present. Fix the real parts of \(a,a'\) first and shift only \(s\) to \(\sigma\). The two Gaussian transforms and the annular transform control all three independent heights. Choosing either sign for the fixed real parts recovers rapid envelopes in both scale ratios. It follows that the complete marked \(g\)-sum is at most
\[
 Z^\epsilon G^{\sigma-1}R^{\sigma/2}(L_DL_E)^\sigma
 E\!\left(\frac{Gq_uq_n^3}{ZL_D}\right)
 E\!\left(\frac{Gq_vq_{n'}^3}{ZL_E}\right). \tag{T07.11}
\]
No arbitrary bounded prime coefficients are covered by this argument.

Put \(\nu_*=(1+\sigma)/2\). The outside coefficients are \(q_u^{-1/2}q_v^{-1/2}/(q_nq_{n'})\), and \(R^{\sigma/2}\ll(q_uq_vq_dq_e)^{\sigma/2}\). Counting \(u,v\) and summing the cube tails gives
\[
 \frac{Z^{1+\sigma}(L_DL_E)^{1/2+3\sigma/2}(q_dq_e)^{\sigma/2}}{G^2}Z^\epsilon.
 \tag{T07.12}
\]
The power of \(G\) is exactly \((\sigma-1)-2\nu_*=-2\).

### 4. Outer fields, branch summation, and endpoint allocation

The common row Cauchy inequality, after the character transform, is
\[
 \sum_r|\xi(e^2r)\xi(d^2r)\mathcal A_{D,t}(e^2r)\mathcal A_{E,t'}(d^2r)|
 \ll Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q_DQ_E/(Y_DY_E)}\sqrt{\mathcal F_D\mathcal F_E},
\]
where \(\mathcal F_D=1+P_a^{1/6}+q_DP_a^2/Y\). It follows by injectivity of the two row maps and (T06.7). The physical normalizations multiply this by exactly
\[
 q_D^{-3/2}q_E^{-3/2}(Q_DQ_E)^{-1/2}
 \sqrt{Q_DQ_E/(Y_DY_E)}=1/(Yq_Dq_E).
\]
Use \(L_DL_E=L^2/(P_JP_{J'})\), \(q_dq_e\le q_Dq_E\asymp P_JP_{J'}\), and \(\sqrt{\mathcal F_D\mathcal F_E}\ll\mathcal F_A\). In (T07.12) the remaining embedded-slot factor is
\((P_JP_{J'})^{-(1+2\sigma)/2}\); in (T07.7) it is \((P_JP_{J'})^{-(3-2\sigma)/2}\). Both are bounded by one. Summing \(|\omega_D|/q_D\) and \(|\omega_E|/q_E\) proves the three cancellation rows of the theorem. Absolute counting instead uses harmonic \(g\)-mass and two \(u^{-1/2}\)-counts, giving \(ZL/G\).

For the strongest Hecke estimate \(\sigma=b/2\), the ratio between the numerator at \(b>b_0\) and its displayed limit is \((ZL^3)^{(b-b_0)/2}\). If \(L\le Z^\Lambda\), choose a fixed positive \(b-b_0\) small enough in terms of the final \(\epsilon\), then allocate the remaining losses, and only then vary \(Z\). The weaker Hecke row uses the ratio \((Z/L)^{(b-b_0)/2}\), also harmless. This proves the endpoint-looking arbitrary-loss statements. ∎

### 5. The remaining small-gcd problem

The strongest bound pays a smooth dyadic tail above
\[
 \boxed{G_0=Z^{1/2+b_0/4}L^{1/2+3b_0/4}.} \tag{T07.13}
\]
At the inherited \(.12551\) geometry, \(\log_ZG_0=0.916210583782689249\ldots\). A rational buffered choice \(b=7/8\) gives \(G_0=Z^{23/32}L^{37/32}\), with exponent \(0.916253443709159867\ldots\). The earlier physical-tail thresholds were \(0.9635172364\ldots\) from ordinary Poisson and \(0.9375816697\ldots\) from the Hecke strip with absolute mark counting. These compare bounds for the same physical gcd; they do not improve or identify the different reflected quadratic-core threshold in inherited SG §10.

Choose a complementary smooth partition \(w_<+w_{\ge}=1\). The exact sufficient residual is
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{c\ne c'}w_<(q_{(c,c')})\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle
 \ll Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon.} \tag{OPEN-SMALL-GCD}
\]
The bound is one-sided and concerns the actual fields. It is **UNPROVED**. The tail theorem bounds full gcd-localized covariance, not its zero and nonzero pieces separately. The global complete zero may be removed using (T06.9); a gcd truncation does not preserve positivity of that form (A15 gives a two-by-two counterexample). At \(g=1\) there is no common-divisor length in which (T07.2) can cancel. Controlling that case requires a new estimate in the remaining columns, marks, or rows. Together with T06, an estimate of this strength would complete the inherited \(.12551\) physical transfer with its original numerator, contour, fixed-family, and all-height requirements. Neither T06 nor T07 establishes it.

statement:
### Conditional return and an explicit weaker defect requirement

W16 assumes D_N<<N^epsilon and bounds |F(N,1)|+|Delta(N,1)|+|H_F(N)| by N^(gamma+epsilon), with gamma>max(alpha_r,1-1/A). Equations(C4)-(C6) prove the stated full Mertens estimate. Root-dependent F is allowed: each root must use one F on its complete reachable system, its actual Delta, and the same quantitative bounds. No consistency between different roots is required for the resulting bound on the fixed M_chi. All roots and every fixed chi, with common gamma but chi-dependent constants, are required.

A useful review consequence is that the subpower premise can be weakened. For a fixed delta>=0, it suffices that

    D_N<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(delta+epsilon),
    delta+max(alpha_r,1-1/A)<gamma,
    |F(N,1)|+|Delta(N,1)|+|H_F(N)|<<N^(gamma+epsilon).          (C7)

Choose smaller internal epsilon allowances for each product and the Rankin bound. This proves the same conclusion; no unpriced source term is added. For the author's unchanged example choices, allowable strict defect exponents are

| Target gamma | r,A | Allowed delta |
|---|---|---|
| .87 | 1,7 | delta<9/700 |
| 5/6 | 1,5 | delta<1/30 |
| 3/4 | 1,3 | delta<1/12 |

For a prospective first gain at c10, r=1,A=3 would permit delta below theta10-2/3=15614053/75000000=.208187373333..., after choosing gamma strictly between delta+2/3 and theta10. This uses a SMALLER paid small-prime sector than A=7 and therefore a LARGER hard remainder; it is a tradeoff, not an automatic improvement of the same H_F estimate. No candidate F meeting(C7) is supplied. The terminal-only F still has a large defect; F=R has zero defect but leaves F(N,1)=M_chi(N), a circular root estimate.

The final bridge is complete. If M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon and all large real x, then s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx is holomorphic on Re s>gamma: on each compact set choose epsilon with room for all logarithmic derivatives. It equals1/L(s,chi) on Re s>1 by a*chi=delta. Meromorphic continuation of L times this function=1 excludes all zeros in the half-plane. The principal pole at1 gives a reciprocal zero; it is not an excluded L-zero. Floor extension covers real x; every finite height is present, and all imprimitive zeros remain. There is no Hecke or growing-conductor transfer.

## Diagonal, covariance and integration checks

The two exact diagonal prices are

    D_A=sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a),
    D_B=sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a)^2.

Since0<=p<=1, both are at most integral sum_a g(log(q_a/x))^2 dx/x=O(X).
This follows from the same lattice/integer count; the Gaussian squared
is a constant multiple of a narrower Gaussian. Thus removing D_A or
D_B from(1) leaves at least a fixed positive multiple of X^2/log(2X)^2
for sufficiently large X. Both orientations remain; no factor2 is lost.
This proves the requested off-diagonal claim for every epsilon>0 as well.

The kernels p(rad(ab)) and p(a)p(b) are neither generally equal nor
entrywise ordered. Choose two distinct fixed good primes l,m outside S+.
With theta_1=theta_lm=1/2, at a=l,b=m they are1/2 and1/4. With
theta_l=theta_m=1/2, they are0 and1/4. All these holes obey q_Q<=X^A
for sufficiently large X. These examples concern kernel entries; no
