## 3. Actual coefficient and positive source contract

Fix the original finite natural character dictionary, its bad-prime set S, one complete orientation, and its fixed admissible slot system. Ideal columns use primary generators; element rows retain all six units. Each column avoids S. The presentation is

    phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n),  psi_u(n)=chi_n(u)^(+/-1).

The fixed nu remains in the coefficient even when its order does not divide six. The symbol includes all natural zeros. A whole conjugation changes every corresponding factor; conjugating only nu is not permitted. The natural representative and its ordinary L-function, not an unspecified row-character existence choice, supply the completed zero identity.

Use the exact original disjoint prime pools, common profiles, individual ray factors, normalized bounded real powers, independent heights, and frozen coprimality holes. Their product is

    Q_u=U^(-v/2) sum_P alpha(P)psi_u(P),
    0<=v=sum_i z_i<=1/20.                              (R1)

P contains one prime from each original pool. With no slots P=1 and v=0. Shared primes between n and P are allowed; complete multiplicativity with zero extension still holds. Fixed slot count, annuli and profile controls give NP comparable to U^v and divisor-many tuple representations. Slot coefficients are independent of the live row. This does not introduce a new permission to apply UM, MI or MP to a merged coefficient.

Let R=U^t, Y=U^B and let V be the actual cutoff, one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity). Put

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y).

The reviewed completion gives D_R,u(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)) at an actual zero of the same natural nonprincipal character in the retained rectangle. Nonprincipal here refers to the primitive inducing character. Extra natural Euler holes do not turn a primitive principal character into a nonprincipal one. The contour argument and its choice of B are inherited exactly; no assertion that derivatives vanish at a zero is made.

For the norm analysis first terminate at Nn<=U^(B+1), using a fixed bounded terminal cutoff if desired. The discarded genuine exponential tail is smaller than any fixed U-power after all required fixed derivatives. First fix the raw row, slot and height powers, then choose its error order. A crude polynomial bound on the retained expression pays any cross term with the discarded tail. Thus the original completed norm and its finite version differ by an arbitrarily small absolute power error. All subsequent classifications concern that finite version; extending its positive bounds to infinite ideal sums is safe.

After merging equal nP=l with their signs, write

    F_u(s)=D_R,u(s)Q_u=sum_l b_l(s)psi_u(l),
    b_l(s)=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l,Nn>R)
       A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y)alpha(P).           (R2)

The terminal cutoff is understood in R2 during expansion. It only contracts the bounds used here. Every natural zero and frozen hole remains in the actual expression. For a required fixed derivative, compact sigma interval in (1/2,infinity), and polynomial terminal support,

    |partial b_l(s)| << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
                              (Nl)^(-sigma),
    Nl>=L0=c0 U^(t+v) when b_l!=0.                    (R3)

This is a divisor bound on the actual coefficient. Norm differentiation supplies logarithms; normalized profile and height differentiation supplies the fixed seminorms and a polynomial H_J. Polynomial support allows their small powers to be allocated to epsilon with constants fixed before the actual height. One can alternatively lower sigma slightly in convergent majorants. No live arithmetic coefficient or growing slot count is hidden inside H_J; constants may depend on the fixed slot system.

Choose a smooth nonnegative radial Phi at least one on the requested row ball, fixed before expansion. The main row family consists of all nonzero sixth-power-free elements, with precisely the fixed-dictionary exclusions, or with that finite exceptional set retained. PR15 proves the excluded free set is finite because its prime support is fixed and each valuation is at most five. Removing it is not the same as removing all small rows.

For a fixed positive-width real interval I, with lower edge at least (1+delta)/2-h0 and 0<=h0<=10^(-5), use

    N(F)=sum_(u free,eligible) Phi(Nu/U)
      sum_(i,j in {0,1}) integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
         |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j F_u(s)|^2
           d tau d sigma.                            (R4)

Finite extra derivatives, labels and orientations mean the corresponding finite sum. An original nonnegative row weight bounded by U^epsilon and row subset may be dominated by R4 before expansion. Their signed residual is not asserted to be dominated pair by pair. The majorant's fixed width and Sobolev constants are retained. Row-dependent profile selection, moving ray dictionaries, or arbitrary amplitude masks are not new licensed inputs.

## 5. The complete arithmetic target and zero signal

For the four-channel phase family a sufficient new target is

    [sum_(i,j) integral_I integral_X^(2X)
       |sum_(c,d)mu_K(c)chi2(d)Nd^(1+it)
          kappa_ij(log(Nc Nd²/x))|² dx/x dt]^(1/2)
      <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),

where 1/2<gamma<.874864, beta<gamma, and

    kappa_ij(z)=g_tau(z)-i^beta g_tau(z+log i)
               -j^beta g_tau(z+log j)
               +(ij)^beta g_tau(z+log(ij)).

All repeated-square towers, Gaussian tails, signs and ordered profile/source
cross terms remain. If using the quartic relative period, require uniform
finite-source approximation bounds and both actual orbit cells; local
Fourier symmetry or an ambient Hilbert norm is insufficient.

The Mellin numerator is the tensor product of the nonzero smoothing factor,
the filter-symbol bank and t->L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2). The last vector is nonzero
at every fixed s by the identity theorem. Hence the complete bound gives a
zero contradiction in Re(s)>gamma without dividing by one possibly vanishing
scalar numerator. This proves a conditional ordinary-zeta conclusion via
zeta_K=zeta L(s,chi_-4); other fixed families need their own constructions.

The phase interval must survive the proof. A scalar phase average or the
specific rank-one compact projection can erase the signal. A small fixed
interval is sufficient qualitatively, but if it shrinks around a numerator
zero of order r its squared signal is of order h^(2r+1), with derivative
constants. Shrinking intervals and growing height windows require new
quantitative capture estimates.

For fixed operators the complete bank bound is equivalent, up to the paid
constants and epsilon buffers, to the complete Gaussian phase-family bound.
There is no weaker exponent merely because more channels are present. The
bank can still be useful as a proof tool if its signed cross terms, or the
harvesting decomposition above, admit a better arithmetic argument.

## 5. All collision sums and the nine original-color components

For one collision type put h=a+b>=2 and k0=1_(a!=b). A reciprocal norm exponent w>1 is summable over its squarefree ideal, after a small divisor loss. At w=1 the sum is harmonic up to its fixed polynomial support and must be paid. Norm exponents<1 need a genuine support bound.

The SQ0 and SQ2 exponents are 2h/3-k0/6 and2h/3+k0/3, with minima7/6 and4/3. Both complete thirteen-label sums converge. The left SQ cross exponent is5h/12+k0/12+a/2. Its only deficient type is(0,2), exponent11/12, giving(GP0)^(1/12); the right orientation transposes it.

CU0 has exponent h/3+k0/6. Its deficient types are(1,1) at2/3 and(2,0),(0,2) at5/6. Equation(3) gives N0^(1/3)(GP0)^(1/3). For the left CU cross, use Si<=C P0(D1D2)^(2/3), valid on the retained box. Its exponent is(h+a+k0)/4: (1,1),(0,2) cost3/4, while(0,3) is harmonic. The total extra cost is N0^(1/4)(GP0)^(1/4), with the transpose on the right.

For CU2 before Si, w=5h/12+k0/3. Only type(1,1), with w=5/6, can fail summability. Expand each quarter power of the THREE positive terms in(9). For a type(1,1) prime:

* A linear D1 component contributes an extra1/4 when its site is inverse1 or a slot, and zero at inverse2; D2 swaps the roles.
* A geometric component contributes1/6 at either inverse and1/4 at a slot.

Thus any geometric component leaves at worst a harmonic exponent. A pair of linear components is deficient ONLY if the shared prime occupies both omitted inverse sites. There are exactly four such configurations, with complete product norm bounded by the corresponding original Hij. Each has weight exponent5/6 and costs Hij^(1/6). Other collision patterns remain summable. Dropping their mutual coprimality enlarges only a positive majorant after all exact identities and support bounds. No independent-edge assumption is made.

The complete nine-component certificate is particularly transparent. Remove the common factor P0^(1/3); after N0^(-1/6) and collision summation, the remaining factors are

| Left/right component | Deficient edge, if any | Remaining factor |
|---|---|---|
| D1,D1 |22| D1^(1/3) U^(-1/8) |
| D2,D2 |11| D2^(1/3) U^(-1/12) |
| D1,D2 or D2,D1 |21 or12| (D1D2)^(1/12) U^(1/10) |
| D1,geometric or geometric,D1 |none; harmonic allowed| D1^(1/4) |
| D2,geometric or geometric,D2 |none; harmonic allowed| D2^(1/4) |
| geometric,geometric |none| (D1D2)^(1/6) |

Every entry except D2,D2 is bounded by(D1D2)^(1/6) on the full closed outer r,s rectangle. The remaining ratio is exactly U^((s-r-1/2)/6). This proves(S) and confirms that dropping the D2,D2 term would be unjustified where s-r>1/2. The exact helper checks these affine inequalities on all rectangle vertices; the table and local powers supply their proof. Reading the author's box partition is permissible certificate verification; trusting its coefficient evaluation would not be.

The three receipts retain all 948 coefficients, power polynomials, full covers, exact scalar margins and failed trials. There are 43,43,45 positive scalar checks for the old, linear and nonlinear routes, respectively, plus five separate nonlinear checks. The unbounded valuation proof below explains why a six-residue computation is complete; the finite checks alone are not offered as that proof.

## 3. Literal valuations, both signs and the unbounded certificate

At a first common prime let i,j>=1 be its complete multiplicities in the two full columns. B3.50--52 includes both plain powers and every slot occurrence. With l_p=log_Z Np, the C orientation has t=(i-j) mod 6. The source's active radical r, exponent e in F, and active canceled indicator r0 are:

| t | r | e | r0 | f_t=(1+rho)r-rho e-r0 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

The inactive t=0 case is not assigned an exponent one. It is already in the common puncture and its optional divisor expansion contributes through E separately. The t=5 sixth power is exactly the coprimality mask; exponent zero in F does not erase that zero. For the other side exchange i and j, so its active exponent is 1-t rather than 1+t. The same table applied to its own ordered pair proves the same bound. Generator units remain in the finite unit dictionary. Consequently c=sum i l_p, d=sum j l_p, R=sum r l_p, L=sum e l_p and R0=sum r0 l_p are the actual source quantities. The first mask divisor has E>=0. The target is LA.4,

    Bc=(3c-5d-R)_+/6.

It is a joint target. First-label Cauchy and B3.56 retain

    M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(Bc+Bd)/2 <= M.

Retaining Bc in the relative excess improves a bound inside this same target and does not spend its outside balance twice. LA.13 gives

    E1=(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-Bc+rho L+R0,
    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)], .68<=delta<=.70.       (V1)

If c<=d, the positive parts vanish. Since 1-4rho<0 on the interval, i>=1 and f_t>=1-4rho imply f_t>=(1-4rho)i. Summation yields

The minimum i+2j in residue t=0,...,5 is 3,4,5,6,7,5. Every positive pair reduces by multiples of six in each coordinate to a pair in [1,6]^2 with the same residue. Increasing i by six adds 6(19rho-4)>0 to (V3); increasing j by six adds 12(19rho-4)>0. This proves reduction to the least representatives for all unbounded multiplicities. At their minima, the six expressions are

    57rho-12, 12+54rho, 8+36rho, 4+18rho, 0, 147rho-29.

All are nonnegative for 19/54<=rho<=103/273. Thus

    E1<=-Hval(delta)c-E,
    Hval=min(delta+1-4rho, delta-(6+27rho)/37).        (V4)

Both constituents strictly increase with delta because rho'<0. They cross at rho=43/121, delta=585/839. Their minimum is increasing, with Hval(.68)=1166/6825. The helper verifies the entire affine dual identities using their two coefficients, as well as the least-residue table. It does not extrapolate a sampled finite valuation search.

The old relaxed equality R=min(c,d), c=2d, L=5R is impossible for nonempty actual support: R=d forces all common primes active with j=1, whereas L=5R forces t=4 and hence every i>=5. Thus c>=5d contradicts c=2d.

## 4. Paired linear and nonlinear transfers

The literal row is w=u0 e F G V_id h'. Freeze its missing first radical before the weighted sum; other first labels and the first projector reconstruct divisor-many. ## 3. Density on the new range from literal source hypotheses

**Lemma D+.** Fix the same finite natural-character dictionary as PR15, with ideal coefficients c_eta(I)s_(m0^6u)(I) and natural modulus norm<=K_eta Nu. Let N(Y,a,T) count free rows Nu<=Y having a zero of some member with real part>=a and |Im|<=T. For every epsilon>0 there are C,J,Y0, fixed before a,T, such that

    N(Y,a,T)<=C(1+T)^J Y^(rho(2a-1)+epsilon),
    rho(delta)=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],
    33/40<=a<=7/8, T>=0, Y>=Y0.                           (5)

The global incumbent beta<=7/8 remains an input. If the relevant nonexceptional set is nonempty, beta>=a>.51, so proposition P's beta>=.51 assumption holds. No improved zero-free conclusion is assumed in this proof.

Set U=KY, K=max(1,max K_eta), so row norms and natural moduli are<=U with no power loss. Use the natural representative; the abstract RowData choice has no conductor bound. Remove the fixed finite union E of free fixed-inducing rows: every prime factor lies in the fixed anchor, valuations are<=5 and units cost a factor6. Remaining members of the SAME parent translate are nonprincipal. E contributes O(1), including principal characters, without a detector witness. It is not the entire interval of small rows.

PR9 B0.9 gives inverse exponent

    e_I(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6), 0<=r<=2.                     (6)

It retains natural coefficients, the common truncated inverse profile and its derivatives. B0.8 and rowwise Sobolev retain bounded real powers and all frequencies |v|<=H at a fixed polynomial height cost. The actual no_slot_inverse_count threshold precedes a,tstar,T,allowance, live rows/characters, labels, dyads and height. It requires a>=1/2,0<=r<=R and the exact RowData coefficient identity; use R=2. Its premises include RawMoment W and RawMoment scaleProfile(W) for logarithmic orders<=2. These are the old actual inverse inputs, unchanged by the new range.

PR15 proposition P supplies the no-slot plain pair moment for m<=3/4,j+k<=2,sigma in[0,1],|v|<=H, with threshold before H. Its proof uses only the completed old zero-slot bound and a direct estimate on E. The auxiliary zero-profile legacy slot imposes no positive prime supply on the original rows. We use no_slot_plain_count, whose requirements are a>=0, witnesses, common label/dyads, bounded frequency and those derivative-pair moments. We do NOT call a marked-fiber theorem with missing marked premises. Its factor192(1+H) pays rowwise real part/frequency through Sobolev; the inverse factor is12(1+H). One C(1+H)^J0 dominates both moment families, uniformly in detector bins and dyads. J0 precedes the internal detector height exponent.

Fix 0<eps_det<=1/1000 and eps_m>0 first and obtain the moment degree J0 above. Next choose e>0 and positive k_aux,eta_aux satisfying

    e<1/1000,
    12e(22+2)+8k_aux+2eta_aux<=eps_det/2,
    0<k_aux<=1, 0<=eta_aux.                              (7)

Choose tau_det>0 afterward with tau_det<1/2,4tau_det<eta_aux and tau_det(J0+1) inside the assigned loss. These are the supported-witness hypotheses at dmin=dmax=1. There is no .7 gate. Its threshold is before every character and real a,tstar, not chosen separately for each bin.

If T<=U^tau_det, the finite buffered-bin construction gives1<=i<=I=ceil(49/(100e)) and b on the grid .51+e*integer such that

    b<=M(3i U^tau_det)<b+e,
    M(3(i+1)U^tau_det)<b+2e,
    b>a-e, b<=7/8.                                      (8)

M is the actual maximum in the finite nonprincipal dictionary of this parent translate, with floor .51. Here b>.825-e>.51 and delta_b=2b-1>.65-2e>.648, so the bins are uniformly nonfloor. Set

    tstar=5/(5-2delta_b)                                 (9)

before choosing witnesses for the entire bin. Since0<delta_b<=3/4<5/6,1<=tstar<=3/2. It does not change from row to row inside a moment fiber.

actual_supported_witness_family requires .51<b<=1, nonprincipal residues, modulus<=U, both maxima(8), the cutoff interval and(7). All now hold literally. It yields one label, an actual zero with real part sigma in[0,1], one common frequency for its two factors, and dyads r,m satisfying

    r<=tstar+eps_det, r+m>=tstar-eps_det,
    0<=m<=1/2+75eps_det<=23/40,
    r>=tstar-1/2-76eps_det>=0,
    |M(U^r)|^2>=U^(delta_b r-2eps_det),
    |P(U^m)|^2>=U^(delta_b m-2eps_det).                  (10)

The frequency is2pi*nu-Im zero, |nu|<=U^(tau_det/2), hence |frequency|<=H_i=2pi U^(tau_det/2)+3i U^tau_det<<_e U^tau_det. The original proof of the m bound needs only delta_b>=1/50, satisfied here. The inverse profile is the original dyadic test times V_le(U^r y/U^tstar); derivatives of V_le are supported on a fixed annulus, giving uniform seminorms. No arithmetic cutoff is replaced. The actual lengths obey0<=r<2, exactly inside(6).

Partition by the fixed finite label and two dyads, costing O((log U)^2) times a constant. The literal no-slot counts give, with the common polynomial height factor,

    count <= U^[e_I(r)-delta_b r+2eps_det+eps_m],
    count <= U^[max(1,2m)-2delta_b m+4eps_det+eps_m].       (11)

For r<=1, max(1,2m)<=1+150eps_det and max(r,2m)>=2(r+m)/3>=2(tstar-eps_det)/3. Taking the better bound in(11) gives exponent at most

    1-(2/3)delta_b tstar+156eps_det+eps_m
      =rho(delta_b)+156eps_det+eps_m.                    (12)

For r>1, the first exponent has positive r-slope5/6-delta_b; its endpoint is at most

    1/6+(5/6-delta_b)tstar+3eps_det+eps_m
      =rho(delta_b)+3eps_det+eps_m.                      (13)

Both equalities are direct substitution of(9). Thus the balanced count is proved on the new range without appealing to a theorem stated only above .7. The original compiled count algebra also allows0<=delta<=5/6, but no new compilation claim is needed.

Since rho decreases and |rho'|<=200/147 on this compact interval, b>a-e implies rho(2b-1)<=rho(2a-1)+3e. Allocate eps_det,eps_m,dyadic losses and tau_det(J0+1) below epsilon. Enlarge C to cover bounded Y uniformly in a,T. This proves all-height(5).

Finally rho(delta)>=2/7>1/6 for delta<=.75. The original uniform bounded-window completion and sixth-power convolution in HeightUniformDensity give the raw-row version. Sixth powers introduce Euler holes without moving any zero in Re>0 or changing the fixed dictionary. Choose the EXTERNAL physical tau_out only after the returned J. It is distinct from tau_det. Lemma D+ is now proved with all its quantifiers.

## 1. Imported statements and the exact finite form

\[

\[

\]

Here \(0\le\rho,\chi\le1\), \(\rho=0\) on \((0,1]\),
\(\rho=1\) on \([2,\infty)\), \(\chi=1\) on \((0,1]\),
and \(\chi=0\) on \([2,\infty)\). The exact detector approximation,
including arbitrary power errors and each fixed Euler derivative, is
[T09.2](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]#frozen-dyad-balanced-finite-form).
Support and elementary derivative bounds are

\[
T_l<de<2T_u,\qquad
Y<d,e<U_{\max}:=2T_u/Y\ll\sqrt X L^4,\qquad
\sup_{q,x}|(q\partial_q)^r\Xi_X(q;x)|\ll_r L^6.
\tag{PO5}
\]

The complete profile has the much stronger endpoint bounds

\[
\mathcal K(t)=\sum_{j\ge1}\phi(jt),\qquad
|(t\partial_t)^r\mathcal K(t)|\ll_r
\begin{cases}
e^{-c_r/\sqrt t},&0<t\le1,\\
e^{-t/2},&t\ge1.
\end{cases}
\tag{PO6}
\]

This is exactly [[private research revision], V6](../review-cycle-12.md#2-complete-poisson-cancellation-before-truncating-the-third-factor).
It uses the actual profile's zero integral and quantitative Gevrey
Fourier decay. A generic smooth profile with zero integral is not
substitutable in this proof.

Write \((d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4)=(d,e,f,h)\),
\(\mathcal E=\{13,14,23,24\}\), \(n=\ell de\), and
\(n'=mfh\). For any bounded tuple mask \(F\), define the *raw*
finite quartic form

\[
\begin{split}
\mathscr Q_X[F]=\int_X^{2X}
\sum_{d,e,f,h>Y}\ \sum_{1\le\ell,m\le J}
&\mu(d)\mu(e)\mu(f)\mu(h)F(d,e,f,h,\ell,m)\\
&\cdot w_X(de)w_X(fh)
\phi(n/x)\overline{\phi(n'/x)}\,\frac{dx}{x}.
\end{split}
\tag{PO7}
\]

In particular \(\mathscr Q_X[1]=\|B_X\|_2^2\), where the norm is
in \(L^2([X,2X],dx/x)\). No positivity is assumed for masked forms.
The original masks retained by the separated-products remainder are

\[
\begin{split}
G&=1_{(d,e)<H}1_{(f,h)<H}
\prod_{ij\in\mathcal E}1_{(d_i,d_j)<R},\\
C&=\prod_{ij\in\mathcal E}
1_{\{|rd_i-sd_j|>\Delta\ \text{for every }1\le r,s\le J\}},\\
Q_{\rm far}[F]&=\mathscr Q_X[GCF1_{|n-n'|>P_{\rm gap}}].
\end{split}
\tag{PO8}
\]

These are precisely [SP5, SP25--SP29](../[private research revision]/mobius-separated-products.md#5-exact-exponents-and-the-residual-signed-form).
All six gcds are gcds of the original four variables. In particular,
an auxiliary divisor from a coprimality expansion never replaces an
original gcd.

## 2. The full allocation mask and the new sector theorem

Let \(W\) be any squarefree integer with

\[
2\le W\le\sqrt L.
\tag{PO9}
\]

The choice may depend on \(X\), but is frozen on the dyad. Only
squarefree \(d_i\) contribute, so there is a unique decomposition

\[
u_i=(d_i,W)\mid W,\qquad d_i=u_iD_i,\qquad (D_i,W)=1.
\tag{PO10}
\]

Define \(\Omega_W(D_1,D_2,D_3,D_4)\) to be the product of the following
indicators:

\[
\begin{gathered}
(D_1,D_2)<H/W,\qquad (D_3,D_4)<H/W,\\
(D_i,D_j)<R/W\quad(ij\in\mathcal E),\\
|raD_i-sbD_j|>\Delta
\quad\left(ij\in\mathcal E,\ a,b\mid W,\ 1\le r,s\le J\right).
\end{gathered}
\tag{PO11}
\]

Thus \(\Omega_W\) is independent of the allocations \(u_1,\ldots,u_4\).
It is the exact intersection of the original six gcd and four
short-cofactor masks over every choice of those allocations. Indeed,

\[
\max_{u_i,u_j\mid W}(u_iD_i,u_jD_j)=W(D_i,D_j).
\tag{PO12}
\]

The individual restrictions \(d_i>Y\), the smooth product cutoffs,
and the finite third-factor endpoints are not included in the orbit
mask. They stay in (PO7) and are handled explicitly below. Since the
actual allocations are among the choices in (PO11), \(\Omega_W\le GC\).

Finally put

\[
\sigma_W(n)=\prod_{p\mid W}(1-1_{p^2\mid n})
=\sum_{\substack{k\mid W\\k^2\mid n}}\mu(k).
\tag{PO13}
\]

This is the indicator that the completed product \(n\) is squarefree
at every prime dividing \(W\), not the indicator that its individual
factors are pairwise coprime.

**Theorem PO-A (the local-prime square sector).** Uniformly for (PO9),
and for every \(A>0\),

\[
\mathscr Q_X[\Omega_W(1-\sigma_W(n)\sigma_W(n'))]
=O_A(X^{-A}).
\tag{PO14}
\]

Consequently

\[
\left|Q_{\rm far}
[\Omega_W(1-\sigma_W(n)\sigma_W(n'))]\right|
\ll_\epsilon X^{1.7489+\epsilon}.
\tag{PO15}
\]

The constants are uniform in the moving integer \(W\). This statement
uses actual Möbius allocation identities, not just prefix-sum bounds.
The passage from (PO14) to (PO15) has a power cost; a sharp completed
product gap is not silently carried through the cancellation.

## 3. Exact coefficients, the finite third factors, and both endpoints

Expand the square-divisibility union exactly:

\[
1-\sigma_W(n)\sigma_W(n')
=-\!\sum_{\substack{k,l\mid W\\(k,l)\ne(1,1)}}
\mu(k)\mu(l)1_{k^2\mid n}1_{l^2\mid n'}.
\tag{PO16}
\]

Here \((k,l)\ne(1,1)\) denotes exclusion of that ordered pair, not a
coprimality condition. For a summand with \(k>1\), cancel the left pair;
when \(k=1,l>1\), interchange the two pairs. This treats all
intersections of square-divisibility events with their exact signs.

For \(k>1\), write the exact \(k\)-parts of \(d,e\) as

\[
d=aU,\quad e=bV,\quad a,b\mid k,\quad(UV,k)=1,
\quad \mu(d)\mu(e)=\mu(a)\mu(b)\mu(U)\mu(V).
\tag{PO17}
\]

Natural squarefree zeros are retained. Because \(k\mid W\), changing
\(a,b\) leaves the four \(W\)-free variables in (PO11) unchanged.
The event \(l^2\mid n'\) also remains fixed. Moreover,

\[
k^2\mid\ell abUV\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\ell=\frac{k^2}{ab}j\quad(j\ge1).
\tag{PO18}
\]

For each prime of \(k\), the denominator \(ab\) has exponent zero,
one or two; hence \(k^2/(ab)\) is an integer. After freezing
\(U,V,f,h,m\), the exact finite left allocation sum is

\[
\mu(U)\mu(V)
\sum_{a,b\mid k}\mu(a)\mu(b)
1_{aU>Y}1_{bV>Y}w_X(abUV)
\sum_{1\le j\le Jab/k^2}\phi(k^2jUV/x).
\tag{PO19}
\]

The last upper endpoint means its integer floor. In particular it is
not replaced by \(J\), and an empty inner sum remains empty.

If an outside coefficient in (PO19) is nonzero, then
\(T_l<abUV<2T_u\). Put \(t=k^2UV/x\). For every omitted term when
the \(j\)-sum is completed to infinity,

\[
jt>JabUV/x\ge JT_l/(2X)\ge4L^2,
\qquad t\ge\frac1{2L^4}.
\tag{PO20}
\]

For each fixed Euler derivative of \(\phi\), its large-argument
bound is \(O_r(e^{-u/2})\). A geometric sum therefore bounds the
omitted terms by

\[
O_r\bigl((1+t^{-1})e^{-2L^2}\bigr)
=O_r(L^4e^{-2L^2}).
\tag{PO21}
\]

This also covers an empty finite sum: every added term then satisfies
(PO20). Thus completion is quantitative and uniform, including when
\(k\) grows with \(X\).

After completion, the common profile is
\(\mathcal K(k^2UV/x)\), multiplied by the exact coefficient

\[
C_k(U,V)=\sum_{a,b\mid k}\mu(a)\mu(b)
1_{aU>Y}1_{bV>Y}w_X(abUV).
\tag{PO22}
\]

Let \(q=UV\). On the entire middle interval

\[
2T_l\le q\le T_u/k^2,
\tag{PO23}
\]

all product weights in (PO22) equal one, since
\(2T_l\le abq\le k^2q\le T_u\). Hence

\[
C_k(U,V)=
\left(\sum_{a\mid k}\mu(a)1_{aU>Y}\right)
\left(\sum_{b\mid k}\mu(b)1_{bV>Y}\right)=0.
\tag{PO24}
\]

To justify the last equality at both sharp lower endpoints: if
\(U>Y\), the first factor is \(\sum_{a\mid k}\mu(a)=0\); the same
holds for \(V>Y\). If neither inequality holds, then
\(q\le Y^2\le T_l\), contradicting (PO23). No smoothing of the
conditions \(aU>Y,bV>Y\) has been used.

The two remaining product ranges have independently affordable
profile bounds. If \(q<2T_l\), then

\[
0<t=k^2q/x\le2W^2/L^4\le2L^{-3},\qquad
|(t\partial_t)^r\mathcal K(t)|\ll_r e^{-c'_rL^{3/2}}.
\tag{PO25}
\]

If \(q>T_u/k^2\), then

\[
t> T_u/(2X)=L^2/2,\qquad
|(t\partial_t)^r\mathcal K(t)|\ll_r e^{-L^2/4}.
\tag{PO26}
\]

For large \(X\), (PO23) is nonempty because \(k^2\le L\).
Also \(|C_k|\le\tau(k)^2\le W^2\le L\). Whenever a term of
\(C_k\) is nonzero, (PO5) implies \(U,V\le U_{\max}\). The two
right factors also lie below \(U_{\max}\). Thus there are
\(O(X^2L^{16})\) possible four-factor choices. The right third
factor has at most \(J=O(L^6)\) choices; the ordered pairs
\(k,l\mid W\) number at most \(\tau(W)^2\le W^2\le L\).
Combining these counts, (PO21), and (PO25)--(PO26), gives, for a
fixed Euler derivative in \(x\) if requested, a bound of the shape

\[
O_r\!\left(X^2L^{30}
\left(e^{-c'_rL^{3/2}}+e^{-L^2/4}+e^{-2L^2}\right)\right)
=O_{A,r}(X^{-A}).
\tag{PO27}
\]

The logarithmic exponent is a harmless upper bound. No number of
unbounded third-factor terms is counted trivially: their entire tail
was summed in (PO21). The integration interval has logarithmic length
\(\log2\). This proves (PO14).

Finally [SP20--SP22](../[private research revision]/mobius-separated-products.md#4-nearby-expanded-products-with-arbitrary-further-masks)
give, after any further bounded tuple mask, the absolute bound

\[
\mathscr Q_X^{\rm abs}[1_{|n-n'|\le P}]
\ll_\epsilon X^{1+\epsilon}(P+1),\qquad 0\le P\le X.
\tag{PO28}
\]

Here the superscript means that all coefficients and summands have
been replaced by their absolute values. Its elementary proof counts
representations of \(n\le2JT_u\) by \(d_3(n)\), applies Cauchy--Schwarz
for each difference, and uses \(d_3(n)^2\le d_9(n)\).
Subtract the nearby band with \(P=P_{\rm gap}\) from (PO14).
Since \(\Omega_W\le GC\), this proves exactly (PO15).

## 4. An actual signed block with absolute mass of order X squared

Take \(W=2\). Choose odd squarefree, pairwise-coprime base variables

\[
D,E\in[\sqrt X,1.1\sqrt X],\qquad
f,h\in[3\sqrt X,3.1\sqrt X].
\tag{PO29}
\]

Retain the bases satisfying the orbital cofactor exclusions in
(PO11). For each such base quadruple, the following four terms all
belong to the new sector, with the right third factor \(m=1\):

| \(d\) | \(e\) | \(\ell\) | Relative Möbius sign |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(D\) | \(E\) | \(4\) | \(+1\) |
| \(2D\) | \(E\) | \(2\) | \(-1\) |
| \(D\) | \(2E\) | \(2\) | \(-1\) |
| \(2D\) | \(2E\) | \(1\) | \(+1\) |

Their common completed product is \(n=4DE\); all four product
cutoffs equal one for sufficiently large \(X\). Their individual
lower endpoints hold, and \(1,2,4\le J\). Also

\[
n\le4.84X,\quad n'\ge9X,\quad
\frac{n}{x}\in[2,4.84],\quad
\frac{n'}x\in[4.5,9.61].
\tag{PO30}
\]

Both profile values are negative and bounded away from zero on these
compact intervals, because the positive zero of \(1-t+t^{-1}\)
is \((1+\sqrt5)/2<2\). Thus each of the four integrated absolute
weights is bounded below by a positive constant. The gap condition
holds since \(|n-n'|\ge4.16X>P_{\rm gap}\), and
\(1-\sigma_2(n)\sigma_2(n')=1\).

There are \(\gg X^2\) base quadruples before the cofactor exclusion.
For completeness, this positive density can be proved by imposing
the desired divisibility patterns modulo finitely many prime squares.
The local density for an odd prime is
\((1-1/p)^4(1+4/p)=1+O(p^{-2})\): at most one variable has
valuation one, and all others valuation zero. The factor at two is
\(1/16\). The infinite product is positive. For primes above a
fixed cutoff, the excluded square divisors and shared prime divisors
have total upper bound
\(O(N^4\sum_{p>P}p^{-2}+N^{7/2}+N^3\log N)\), where
\(N=\sqrt X\). The first term is made arbitrarily small by choosing
the fixed cutoff, and the other terms are \(o(N^4)\). Finite Chinese
remainder counting then gives the asserted density in the four
fixed-ratio intervals.

For a fixed edge, a fixed \(a,b\mid2\), and fixed \(r,s\le J\),
the excluded relation \(|raD_i-sbD_j|\le\Delta\) leaves at most
\(O(\Delta+1)\) choices for the second variable after the first is
fixed. The two free remaining variables give an overall excluded
count

\[
O\bigl(J^2X^{3/2}(\Delta+1)\bigr)
=O(X^{1.874}L^{12})=o(X^2).
\tag{PO31}
\]

All gcd conditions in (PO11) hold for these base quadruples, since
their base gcds are one. Hence this is a block of absolute mass
\(\asymp X^2\) canceled exactly, quadruple by quadruple, by

\[
1-1-1+1=0.
\tag{PO32}
\]

This cancellation explains the distinction from the positive model
in SP30--SP34, which satisfies certain prefix and divisor-mask bounds
but does not preserve these Möbius convolution identities.

It also gives a sharp obstruction to a stronger claim. Restricting
the *actual* four factors to the fully pairwise-coprime stratum
removes the last row, because \((2D,2E)=2\). The other three rows
remain, and their relative signed coefficient is \(1-1-1=-1\).
Thus this cancellation crosses permitted internal-gcd strata; it
does not prove cancellation on the fully pairwise-coprime stratum
alone. Likewise, a base internal gcd in \([H/2,H)\) can cause the
original cutoff to remove the last allocation. This is the reason
for the exact orbital preparation below.

## 5. Internal-gcd preparation is a norm comparison

For a positive integer \(g\), write \(g^{\langle W\rangle}=g/(g,W)\).
Define

\[
B_X^{(W)}(x)=\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
1_{(d,e)^{\langle W\rangle}<H/W}\,\Xi_X(de;x).
\tag{PO33}
\]

On nonzero terms, \((d,e)^{\langle W\rangle}=(D_1,D_2)\).
Also \((d,e)\le W(d,e)^{\langle W\rangle}<H\). Thus this is
exactly the internal orbital restriction on each bilinear factor.

The proof of [MG12--MG16](../[private research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#3-the-strengthened-internal-gcd-tail)
gives the following slightly more explicit form: for arbitrary
coefficients \(|\alpha_g|\le1\) supported on \(g\ge Z\),

\[
\left\|\sum_g\alpha_g B_{X,g}\right\|_2
\ll_{b,\epsilon}X^{b+\epsilon}Z^{1-2b},
\tag{PO34}
\]

where \(B_{X,g}\) retains the exact original gcd \(g\). Indeed its
exact expansion is
\(B_{X,g}=\mu(g)^2\sum_{(q,g)=1}\mu(q)F_{gq}\), with
\(F_c\ll X^bL^C c^{-2b+2\eta}\). The proof takes absolute values
only after the two Möbius sums in \(F_c\) have been estimated, then
sums the absolutely convergent \(q\)-series and the \(g\)-tail.
Inserting \(\alpha_g\) cannot increase this majorant. The index
\(q\) remains auxiliary and never changes the location of the
coefficient \(\alpha_g\).

The coefficient of \(B_X-B_X^{(W)}\) is
\(1_{g^{\langle W\rangle}\ge H/W}\), whose support has
\(g\ge H/W\). Thus

\[
\|B_X-B_X^{(W)}\|_2
\ll_\epsilon X^{b+\epsilon}(H/W)^{1-2b}
\ll_\epsilon X^{\gamma+\epsilon},\qquad
\gamma=b+\frac{1-2b}{1400}
=\frac{6120551}{7000000}=.874364428571\ldots .
\tag{PO35}
\]

The power of \(W\) is logarithmic and has been absorbed. Precisely,

\[
a-\gamma=\frac{879}{7000000}>0.
\tag{PO36}
\]

Therefore \(\|B_X\|_2\ll_\epsilon X^{a+\epsilon}\) is equivalent
to the same bound for \(B_X^{(W)}\), by the two triangle
inequalities. Squaring the error in (PO35) is affordable, with
exponent \(2\gamma=1.748728857142\ldots\), but this is not an
additive estimate for the difference of the two energies.

In fact using only the baseline norm bound for the mixed term would
produce exponent

\[
2b+\frac{1-2b}{1400}
=\frac{12244851}{7000000}=1.749264428571\ldots,
\qquad
\left(2b+\frac{1-2b}{1400}\right)-2a
=\frac{1991}{7000000}>0.
\tag{PO37}
\]

This obstruction is retained. The proof never asserts an affordable
additive error between \(\|B_X\|_2^2\) and
\(\|B_X^{(W)}\|_2^2\).

## 6. Cross-gcd and short-cofactor preparation at the energy level

Start from \(\|B_X^{(W)}\|_2^2\). In its quartic expansion retain

\[
(d_i,d_j)^{\langle W\rangle}<R/W
\quad(ij\in\mathcal E).
\tag{PO38}
\]

The complementary union implies \((d_i,d_j)\ge R/W\) for some
cross edge. Every condition here, including the two internal
conditions in (PO33), is a bounded function of the original six
gcds. Hence it stays fixed on the original prime-incidence variables
through the cancellation in
[MG21--MG30](../[private research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#5-original-prime-incidence-and-masks-for-all-gcds).
Apply the positive shared-incidence majorant only after that
cancellation. It bounds the entire signed complementary union by

\[
O_\epsilon\bigl(X^{2b+\epsilon}(R/W)^{1-2b}\bigr)
=O_\epsilon(X^{\beta+\epsilon}),\qquad
\beta=2b+\frac{1-2b}{700}
=\frac{6120551}{3500000}=1.748728857142\ldots .
\tag{PO39}
\]

The fixed incidence mask can be dropped in the final positive
majorant; it is not differentiated or recomputed in auxiliary
coprimality variables. Thus this use is uniform in \(W\).

Now impose all cofactor conditions in (PO11). For one edge let
\(A^W_{ij}\) be the event that some \(a,b\mid W\) and
\(r,s\le J\) violate that condition. This event depends only on
the original pair \((d_i,d_j)\). Write
\(d_i=u_iD_i,d_j=u_jD_j\) as in (PO10). A violation implies

\[
|r'd_i-s'd_j|\le W\Delta,\qquad
r'=raW/u_i,\quad s'=sbW/u_j,\qquad
1\le r',s'\le JW^2.
\tag{PO40}
\]

The displayed multipliers are integers. Thus the actual bad-pair
set is contained in an ordinary rational-strip union with
multiplier limit \(JW^2\) and tolerance \(W\Delta\). These are
only logarithmic enlargements, and \(W\Delta\le Y/2\) for large
\(X\).

The proof of [SP9 and SP15--SP17](../[private research revision]/mobius-separated-products.md#2-uniform-divisor-masks-in-one-and-two-möbius-sums)
applies with all six prepared gcd masks. To spell out why: after
freezing a squarefree cross pair, say \(d,f\), set
\(D=\operatorname{rad}(df)\). The four conditions relating \(e\)
or \(h\) to \(d,f\) are bounded functions of \((e,D)\) and
\((h,D)\). The remaining condition is a bounded coefficient
\(a_{(e,h)}\). SP9 estimates the two unfrozen Möbius sums uniformly
in all those functions. The fixed pair's mask is then retained
while bounding its count by the larger union in (PO40). This is
not a restriction of a signed estimate to an arbitrary subset.

The single-edge bound is consequently
\(O_\epsilon(X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(\Delta+1))\).
For the union of four edges, use the exact inclusion error bound
\(|1_{k\ge1}-k|\le\binom{k}{2}\), where \(k\) counts the bad
edge events. Two distinct cross edges form a forest, so the
absolute intersection count, with (PO40), is
\(O(XL^C(\Delta+1)^2)\). This proves for the full signed union

\[
O_\epsilon\left(
X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(\Delta+1)
+X^{1+\epsilon}(\Delta+1)^2\right)
=O_\epsilon(X^{1.7489+\epsilon}+X^{1.748+\epsilon}).
\tag{PO41}
\]

Sharp individual endpoints remain those of (PO7), and all weights
in the two-variable Abel estimate are the original \(\Xi\) factors
with their \(O(L^{12})\) mixed Euler seminorms. The cofactor mask is
independent of \(\ell,m\), so those finite sums can be kept inside
\(\Xi\) during this step. After both preparations, the retained
four-variable mask is exactly \(\Omega_W\).

## 7. Exact residual form and the power budget

Define the remaining signed form

\[
Q_W^{\rm sf}:=
\mathscr Q_X\!\left[
\Omega_W\,\sigma_W(n)\sigma_W(n')
1_{|n-n'|>P_{\rm gap}}
\right].
\tag{PO42}
\]

First perform the two energy-level preparations (PO39), (PO41).
Then apply the cancellation (PO14), before any completed-product
gap is imposed. Finally remove the nearby completed-product band
by (PO28). The exact resulting estimate is

\[
\|B_X^{(W)}\|_2^2
=Q_W^{\rm sf}+O_\epsilon(X^{1.7489+\epsilon}),
\tag{PO43}
\]

uniformly for squarefree \(2\le W\le\sqrt{\log X}\). All
constants implicit in this statement come from fixed profiles,
the accepted exponent \(b\), and the arbitrary epsilon loss;
there is no unbounded moving-prime constant.

The exact exponents and gaps are:

| Step | Exponent | Gap below its target |
|---|---:|---:|
| Internal preparation, norm | \(6120551/7000000=.874364428571\ldots\) | \(879/7000000\) below \(a\) |
| Cross-gcd preparation, energy | \(6120551/3500000=1.748728857142\ldots\) | \(879/3500000\) below \(2a\) |
| One cofactor edge | \(b+1/2+.374=1.7489\) | \(1/12500\) below \(2a\) |
| Two cofactor edges | \(1+2(.374)=1.748\) | \(49/50000\) below \(2a\) |
| Nearby completed products | \(1+.7489=1.7489\) | \(1/12500\) below \(2a\) |
| Prime-square sector before the gap | Arbitrary negative power | From (PO27) |

As usual, the displayed strict gaps allow a sufficiently small
positive epsilon to be spent inside the proof. The arbitrary-epsilon
formulations follow by renaming that loss.

Combining (PO35) and (PO43), the full target is equivalent to

\[
|Q_W^{\rm sf}|\ll_\epsilon X^{1.74898+\epsilon}.
\tag{OPEN-PO}
\]

For the reverse direction, (PO43) controls the nonnegative energy;
for the forward direction it controls the modulus of the signed
remainder by that energy plus the absolute error. The norm
comparison (PO35) is applied separately in both directions.

The remainder still contains all original six gcd masks, the
original short-cofactor exclusions, the original finite
\(\ell,m\le J\), the original factor endpoints \(d_i>Y\), and
the broad far completed-product range. It has the additional
allocation-invariant restrictions and is squarefree at the selected
primes in both completed products. One may choose a growing
primorial subject to \(W\le\sqrt{\log X}\); no prime-distribution
asymptotic is needed for this choice or for the proof.

No estimate for (OPEN-PO) is proved here. In particular, local
prime-square cancellation does not estimate the remaining locally
squarefree coefficients, does not provide cancellation in the
fully pairwise-coprime stratum by itself, and does not supply a
new zero-free constant or a finite-height-to-infinite-height
inference. The imported T09 detector and its height and
calibration qualifications remain exactly as stated in the source.

statement:
## 7. Closure boundary and next action

The proposed new analytic statement is (11), and its raw z<=W/21 version, with exact common profiles, same ray pool, fixed parent translate, original natural holes, both orientations, all inverse-length regimes and uniform heights. The decisive new move is partial use of the actual marked PLAIN theorem, not importing the marked INVERSE permission. The support estimate (12) is independent of that lemma and yields a simpler route to the displayed endpoint via accepted [restricted research revision] density.

This report does not audit the full transitive analytic base anew. The source-relative imported F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and root-definition binding keep their prior status. It does not claim a public record. Independent review should prioritize Sections 5--6: Bc in the actual joint target, accepted-density transfer and the complete endpoint. ## 4. Licensed energies and unequal-length price reconstruction

[Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Theorem4.1 and Corollary4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3) allow an arbitrary squarefree primary inner sequence and an unrestricted cubic outer variable. The normalized energy price is B^(1/3)(B+Xi), up to the stated small powers. The outer variable need not be squarefree. Reciprocity and fixed units/rays permit the needed orientation; this uses Section4, not the paper's cuspidal coefficient results.

[Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2) give price B+Xi for the squarefree quadratic family with arbitrary inner coefficients. PR9 B2.24 identifies the ACTUAL family: the lambda correction, primitive inducing convention, trivial infinite type, finite reciprocity group and equal-class coprime product conductor are essential. Fixed k,d and hole twists go into arbitrary sequences or positive outer restrictions, not into a new conductor-dependent sieve family.

For square cores write(Delta ell)=kappa2 b^2, with kappa2 squarefree and arbitrary b; overlap is allowed. For each fixed kappa2, the b symbol is cubic. Summing through core cap C gives each normalized column energy

    As+Xi Bs,
    As=Hc^(2/3)C^(1/3), Bs=Hc^(1/6)C^(5/6).                (8)

Fixed N(Delta) factors are retained in the comparison constant. Only nonempty ranges kappa2<=N(Delta)Hc use the sieve; extending the positive bound to C does not assert a theorem at an empty subunit B.

For cube cores write(Delta ell)=kappa3 t^3 z^6, with kappa3 cubefree and t squarefree, keeping all overlaps. The exact symbol includes chi_m(kappa3)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1). The z-hole must be kept even at a sixth power. For fixed kappa3,z, apply the quadratic theorem over t with that fixed puncture in the inner sequence.

Let l_i1,l_i2,l_iP be the collision norms extracted from the two original inverse colors and slots on side i. Their product is L or R. Ignoring additional f shortenings only for an upper bound, the pointwise color estimate is

    Si=(P0/l_iP)[D1/l_i1+D2/l_i2
                            +(D1D2/(l_i1 l_i2))^(2/3)].     (9)

To justify it, expand the fixed remaining slots and apply B1.11 to each actual color pair. The only live coupling is the cubic symbol between those two colors. All collision/a0/f/z and fixed-frequency punctures separate into zero coefficients or restrictions of the positive outer norm. PR9 B2.25 permits these arbitrary one-color sequences. Triangle over normalized slots costs the remaining slot length after squaring. This remains true with independent heights and either complete conjugation orientation. It supplies no permission for arbitrary two-color matrix coefficients.

For B=(Hc/N(kappa3))^(1/3), split z at Z. Short repetitions cost B+Xi Z; long repetitions cost B Si/Z. If sqrt(B Si/Xi) lies in[1,sqrt(B)], balance the two. Below1 use the pointwise bound throughout; above sqrt(B) use the sieve throughout, noting Si>Xi. Each regime is bounded by B+sqrt(B Si Xi). Summing cubefree kappa3 gives

    Ac=Hc^(1/3)C^(2/3), Bc=Hc^(1/6)C^(5/6),

For unequal positive x,y, scalar Cauchy gives

    sqrt((A+xB)(A+yB))
       <=A+B sqrt(xy)+sqrt(AB)(sqrt(x)+sqrt(y)).              (11)

Apply(11) with x=XL,y=XR in SQ and x=ZL,y=ZR in CU. Both mixed terms in EACH sector are necessary in this chosen upper bound. No equality of the shortened lengths is imposed.

Multiplying by(7), summing O(A) a0 labels, and substituting(5) produces the following complete monomials. D=LR; each cross row occurs for i=L and i=R. Only fixed constants,H_J and allocated small powers are omitted.

| Term | Restored price |
|---|---|
| SQ0 | U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^-1 N0^(1/3) Kc^(1/6) D^(-2/3) F^-1 qd^(-1/3) C^(1/3) |

The empty face has degree0, so this is the usual augmented complex with all degrees shifted by1. It has d^2=0. Put D_chi e_S=chi(n(S))e_S. Then, literally,

    Str(D_chi)=sum_S (-1)^|S| chi(n(S))=M_chi(X).       (T1)

## A09. Optimal shell correction and a genuine higher-moment escape

**PROVED identities; convergence OPEN.** Source: BB R11. For the inherited prefix interpolants set \(r_N=1-h_N\), \(c_N=h_{2N}-h_N\). On \(N\le k<2N\), \(c_N=r_N\); both vanish earlier. Let
\[
 F=\|r_N1_{[N,2N)}\|^2,\quad T=\|c_N1_{[2N,\infty)}\|^2,\quad
 J=\langle r_N1_{[2N,\infty)},c_N1_{[2N,\infty)}\rangle.
\]
Expansion gives
\[
 \|r_N\|^2-\|r_N-\lambda c_N\|^2
 =2\lambda(F+\Re J)-\lambda^2(F+T).
\]
For \(F+T>0\), the best real scalar is
\(\lambda_*=(F+\Re J)/(F+T)\), with gain \((F+\Re J)^2/(F+T)\).
Clamp \(\lambda_*\) to \([0,1]\) if underrelaxation is required. This can improve on full refitting, but leaves \((1-\lambda)r_N\) on the first shell; moving only forward freezes that error.

An arbitrary specified shell residual can still be matched by the actual arithmetic span. Put
\[
 b_n=nf_n-2Nf_{2N},\qquad
 a_n=-[r(n)-r(n-1)]/n,\quad r(N-1)=0,\quad N\le n<2N.
\]
On that shell \(b_n(k)=-n1_{k\ge n}\), so \(\sum a_nb_n(k)=r(k)\), and the correction is zero earlier. Future repetitions persist. The special formula \(h_{2N}-h_N\) must not be reused after arbitrary damping.

Under \(\Pr(K=k)=k^{-2\sigma}-(k+1)^{-2\sigma}\), Hölder for a residual supported on \(K\ge N\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E|r_N|^2\le
 N^{-2\sigma(1-1/p)}(\mathbb E|r_N|^{2p})^{1/p},\quad p>1.
\]
Hence the genuinely new target \(\mathbb E|r_N|^{2p}\ll N^\kappa\) with
\(\kappa<2\sigma(p-1)\) would force convergence. The inherited tail upper bound only decays for \(\sigma>1/(2-b_0)\approx.8887993351\), which is weaker than the premise. Its failure to decay is not proof of divergence.
title: A09. Optimal shell correction and a genuine higher-moment escape

### 3.1 Exact output partition and low source

Choose smooth nonincreasing phi, equal to1 on[0,1], zero on[2,infinity), and w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t). Then

    1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0)w(n/(2^j X)), n>0.                  (R4)

This is an exact telescoping identity, with w supported on[1,4]. No original sharp mask is replaced. For the low term ml<=2X, the nonlinear phase derivative in l, after division by2pi, is -3m(ml)^5/(pi x^6). Its magnitude is O(m/X), including the final discrete increment. For m<=X^alpha0 this is eventually less than1/(4Q). Each nonzero Fourier mode j/Q therefore stays a fixed distance from every integer, and has monotone derivative. Discrete first-derivative summation bounds every prefix by O_Q(1). The product phi(ml/X)exp(-ml/x^(3/2)) has bounded total variation. Abel summation gives O_Q(1) per row, hence O(AD) for the full low source. Bounded initial X values are covered by the fixed constant.

The last-increment issue is real: it suffices to use ml<=3X for that increment since m=o(X). Section4 gives a version with an explicit small multiple of X, which also avoids this asymptotic qualification.

## 5. Completed cube-free means, finite incidence and spectral alternatives

### F03.OM — Physical orientations first

Use a single common fixed completion
\[
\mathbf S_h(s)=F(s)\mathbf D_h(s),\qquad
F(s)=L^{(S)}(3s-1,\xi_{\rm ang}),
\quad D_h(s)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf}}\beta(c)\vartheta_c(h)q_c^{-s}.
\]
The finite vector is the actual ray orbit closed under the required arithmetic switches. Do not manufacture a geometric period for a component merely because its analytic D-series is defined. T01 transfers completed/uncompleted means without a dimension penalty, using separate holomorphy and buffered-strip means. T02 also transfers directly in the completed selector without division.

T03 reduces \(h=ab^2d^3\) to cube-free physical rows \(ab^2\), preserving all extra cube-prime deletions and overlaps. The sharp universal positive lift works for weight exponent \(v>1/3\); this is different from the [restricted research revision] scalar-shell obstruction. The target is
\[
\sum_{q_aq_b^2\le X}\|\mathbf S_{ab^2}(s)\|^2
\ll X^{35/32+\epsilon}T^A.
\]
The physical norm is \(q_aq_b^2\), primitive conductor essentially \(q_aq_b\), and reduced sixth Fourier index \(a^4b^2\). These are three different quantities.

A sufficient rectangular bound is \(A^{1+\eta}B^{2+2\eta}\), or the stronger useful fixed-\(b\) form \(A^{35/32}B^{1+\epsilon}\). Combine genuinely different box estimates \(A^{r_j}B^{s_j}\) by the exact frontier
\[
R=\max_{0\le z\le1/2}\min_j\{r_j(1-2z)+s_jz\};
\]
A02 records its proof. An optimistic pointwise mixed bound \(q_aq_b^{1/2}\) only pays a narrow inverse edge for the \(35/32\) target. The actual prime-square inverse sector is already \(\ll X^{3/2-\sigma+\epsilon}\), but cube descendants can delete new primes and create ordinary orientations. It is not an isolated closed family.

**First method:** average the actual translated current covariance before separate tests:
\[
q_h^{-1}\sum_{x,y\bmod h}^{*}\overline{\psi_h(x)}\psi_h(y)
P_{h,x}\overline{P_{h,y}}.
\]
At a prime, adding the two nontrivial cubic orientations gives \(3\,1_{y/x\ {\rm cube}}-1\), not a Kronecker delta. Keep that sign with the physical orientation weights. Compute the ordinary face \(b=1\), its diagonal and one off-diagonal orbit, after the actual incoming calibration.

**Second method:** project the test onto an independently defined finite current/spectral image before estimating its Riesz norm. A prescribed deck character and controlled spectral window is a legitimate definition; “the unknown useful part” is not. The two unprojected cusp channels already cost \(Q(Q-1)\) centrally. A new restriction may do better, but another minimization of the same seed does not.

**Bounded auxiliary child:** tensor an ordinary cusp at \(a\)-primes with a broad inverse cusp at \(b\)-primes. Test \(pq^2\) first, including CRT multipliers, incoming tails, nonunit Fourier indices and a shared cube prime. Prime formulas cannot simply be multiplied. Promote an inverse-composite extension only if it opens a new box beyond the already-paid edge. A18 screens the simple diagonal oldforms: r=0,1 vanish, and the first unit-compatible r=2 still costs Q at the central edge before any new current-norm cost. General combinations and actual projected tests remain open.

### N27 — Finite incidence, including its completed version

The exact finite trace is
\[
\mathcal T(K,G;s)=\sum_{q_k\le KG}\|\mathbf D_k(s)\|^2
\sum_{\substack{g\mid\operatorname{rad}_{=1}(k)\\q_k/K\le q_g\le G}}q_g^{-2\sigma}.
\tag{FIN-weight}
\]
The radical contains primes of valuation **exactly one**. For \(k>K\) this demands a real intermediate divisor; large prime rows are absent when \(G\le K\). For \(k\le K\), \(g=1\) remains. Formal divisor counting does not prove the sought \(K^{1+u}G^v\) bound. T08 proves the transfer throughout \(u,v\ge0,3u+v<1\), not only the narrower B domain \(v\le u<1/4\).

T01 applied to the finite \((g,h)\)-vector gives the same exponents for the common-F-completed incidence norm. This is a new merger consequence: no separate completion-removal prerequisite remains for N27 either. It does not supply a period realization or the incidence saving.

**New proved corridor reduction (T08).** It is enough to prove FIN for every \(K\) and \(1\le G\le C K^\gamma\), for a fixed dyadic constant \(C\), where \(\gamma=(1-u)/(2+v)>1/3\), with the full family/strip/profile hypotheses. The detector only uses \(G=\max(K^{1/3},KD^{-1/2})\) at a strictly interior row exponent; whole-profile tails close by the blockwise enlargement proved in T08. Thus the formerly provisional \(K^{.431}\) target is now the exact sufficient corridor exponent \(28/65\) for \((u,v)=(1/8,1/32)\). This is a real reduction of the needed uniform range, not an energy saving. Partition the first-admissible-divisor attack inside this corridor before asking for a larger G range.

**N27.P:** sum one forced-prime dyad \(g\sim E\) before row expansion; retain the common-core masks and aim to save divisor exponent \(v\), not merely estimate every index through \(KE\). **N27.D:** partition by the first admissible divisor in \([q_k/K,G]\), controlling overlapping divisor-rich classes exactly. **N27.X:** handle exceptions by their actual FIN-weight and amplitude, not cardinality alone. The prototype \((u,v)=(1/8,1/32)\) needs a substantial \(g=1\) mean but tolerates a weaker row exponent than OM's \(3/32\).

**N27.N1 — New pass 1, signed selector before divisor Cauchy.** Reconstruct the finite h-by-divisor bilinear kernel at the precise place FD's transfer takes a divisor norm. Keep the completed selector coefficients
\(x_{g/d}\prod_{p\mid d}(1-x_p)\beta(d)\vartheta_d(h)q_d^{-s}\), with all outside zeros, and test whether an actual signed selector energy is cheaper than FIN-weight. The first missing lemma is an exact sufficient transfer for that smaller energy; cancellation between divisors cannot be assumed merely because coefficients alternate. This is a genuine escape from demanding the positive trace only if the full detector and tails close. It is not a second name for N27.P.

### F14/F17/F15 — Expensive mechanisms for the mean, with scope retained

A coefficient-sensitive relative trace formula must unfold to the actual current covariance or H-col, with correct cover, multiplier, angular type, level, cusp pair, residual spectrum, sparse index and nonunit values. First match local coefficients and two-/three-prime cocycles; then price the geometric diagonal and dual length. The identity and saving are separate milestones.

A03 pays fixed smooth nonprincipal prime convolutions relative to I-HECKE. Moving residual coefficients can principalize a permitted test, so that gain does not automatically establish a dispersion hypothesis for the actual mean. A changed coupled estimate must retain the resonance addback.

The corrected torus tensor reproduces \(\beta\), but direct Parseval costs \(C^{2-2\sigma}\). Ordinary cubic A3 identification, a fixed twist and a scalar Euler quotient fail exact cocycle tests. A matrix/twisted-convolution series or coupled-root-number transform remains possible. A useful new functional relation must enlarge the actual continuation cone, not just exhibit a formal symmetry. For the positive row series, real-axis holomorphy past the needed abscissa with quantitative growth would suffice; proving the whole multi-variable functional equation may be unnecessarily strong.

The reduced index \(h^4=a^4b^8\mapsto a^4b^2\) preserves sixth-power phases and nonunit zeros on squarefree columns. A nominal AFE length \(A^2BT^5\) is still conditional on the intertwining matrix, reflected coefficients and their energies. Even granting ideal dual energies, a generic sieve only pays an inverse-dominant wedge; balanced ordinary boxes remain too expensive. The older infinite sparse \(p^4\) trace survives as a different, higher-distance branch; replacing it by ambient full Fourier energy fails.

Changed sources remain legitimate within their exact hypotheses. Cube damping \(q_B^{-\nu}\) shifts the formal completion and has explicit local source/period factors (A07). Since fixed-factor removal is now paid, shifting its argument alone no longer addresses the critical gap. A one-squarefree-vector **current** norm, a current graph norm or a changed reference tensor could escape the scalar whole-shell theorem. Simple diagonal shell Sobolev weights do not. The new finite-shell Cauchy calibration in A07 supplies a sharper test of arbitrary diagonal renorming; it does not rule out all graph norms or justify a claim about divergent angular Euler products without checking phases.

 S_z^+\!\left(\frac{Y_e}{q_\ell q_s}\right)\right].

## B. Uniform S17: the full feedback denominator and the missing native map

The seed proposes neighboring native H packets as a feedback state. Accepted G136 already retains the exact two-block recursion, and G151 says no compatible inter-scale map between changing prime-pair groups has been constructed. Its fixed native packet is an Eisenstein source, NOT an ordinary mu or positive-divisor surrogate: retain original coefficients a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma2(n), xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3, distinct rational long-prime norms, both short-core orders including equality, natural zeros, both projectors, rooted marks, masks, independent heights, CRT/angular data and1/Q Fourier normalization. Its full finite ambient group has dimension Q^2. Raw readout is <F W,kappa>, with the exact complex character kernel and kappa=conj(K).

Already at the fixed-packet level, translation does not commute with a sharp mask:

    [P_A,V_delta]W(R,...)
      =(1_A(R)-1_A(R-delta))W(R-delta,...).                 (B1)

The translated rooted-projector arguments also change. A smooth-profile adapter that leaves these arguments fixed is a different operation. If neighboring prime pairs have different Q, their complete finite state dimensions differ. A bijective ambient state transfer cannot simply be assumed; an embedding/projection needs its full discarded or forced complement. This is an ambient dimension observation, not a lower bound on a source-only state reduction.

Here is a completely priced conditional feedback lemma, to state what an actual scale construction would need. For a fixed finite compatible map, let

    T=[[a,b],[c,D]], z_(j+1)=T z_j+f_j, z_j=(alpha_j,eta_j).

Take r>||D||, K=(r-||D||)^(-1), and define the Schur denominator

    s(w)=w-a-b(wI-D)^(-1)c.                                (B2)

The exact resolvent is

    (wI-T)^(-1)=diag(0,R_D)
                  +[1;R_D c] s(w)^(-1) [1,b R_D],
    R_D=(wI-D)^(-1).                                      (B3)

Thus a signed bound on D alone is insufficient. One needs the full feedback denominator and its numerator/forcing. A simple sufficient ambient condition is

    Delta=r-|a|-||b||||c||/(r-||D||)>0.                     (B4)

For |w|>=r the reverse triangle inequality gives |s(w)|>=Delta. Hence T has no eigenvalue there, and on |w|=r its resolvent norm is at most

    C_r=K+(1+K||c||)(1+K||b||)/Delta.                       (B5)

Cauchy's matrix integral and the COMPLETE Duhamel sum then give

    ||T^j||<=C_r r^(j+1),
    ||z_j||<=C_r r^(j+1)||z_0||
                 +C_r sum_(k<j)r^(j-k)||f_k||.             (B6)

Every forcing and initial mode is retained. More favorable signed feedback may replace(B4), but must ensure no Schur zero throughout |w|>=r and pay its contour minimum. A contour bound without controlling exterior poles does not suffice. A varying family T_j needs product/Volterra control; applying this stationary lemma separately to each step is invalid without a proved common metric or compatible product estimate.

The first decisive diagnostic reproduces the known G136 obstruction:

    T=[[1,e],[e,0]], e>0, D=0,
    s(w)=w-1-e^2/w,
    lambda_plus=(1+sqrt(1+4e^2))/2>1.

The innovation block vanishes, yet the scalar observable grows. The exact recurrence is alpha_(j+1)=alpha_j+e^2 alpha_(j-1). Reversing one feedback sign changes the polynomial to w^2-w+e^2; for0<e<1/2 both roots lie inside the unit circle. Signs therefore matter. Neither matrix is claimed to be a realized native arithmetic source.

To use(B6) in actual H, construct the exact compatible state maps, price every projector/mask translation defect and both boundary forcing channels, bind r^j to the physical scales, and sum all packet readouts with their true norms. The full raw target remains G Kphys [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, followed by physical N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. The symbol Kphys here is the physical parameter, distinct from the resolvent constant K above. No .004 gain follows from the generic lemma.

Disposition before author outcomes: **the coarse innovation-only route fails in its stated abstract class; native feedback remains open because its compatible map and complete return are unconstructed.** The resolvent/forcing formula is a precise conditional budget, not an arithmetic estimate. G136/G151 retain priority for the underlying countermodel and native-complement warning. No new c or claim that all signed feedback is impossible.

## 5. Author Section D: smoothing and fixed-layer deletion

Let w be fixed continuous nonnegative, compactly supported, w(0)>0, and positive on some [a,b] with 0<a<b. For fixed q define C_j(X) by summing w(n/X) over squarefree q-units with omega(n)=j. Then C_0(X)=w(1/X) tends to w(0), and sum_j C_j(X)=O(X). After deleting precisely layers 1 through ell-1, ell fixed, the complete polynomial is

    Z_X^[ell](z)=C_0+C_ell z^ell+sum_(j>ell) C_j z^j.

Distinct primes in [a^(1/ell)X^(1/ell),b^(1/ell)X^(1/ell)] yield C_ell>=c X/log^ell X. Unique factorization pays multiplicity ell! as a fixed constant, and finitely many ramified primes do not alter the lower bound. For R=(2C_0/C_ell)^(1/ell), eventually R<1 and

    |C_0+C_ell z^ell|>=C_0 on |z|=R,
    |sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j|<=C X R^(ell+1)
       =O(X^(-1/ell)log^(ell+1)X)=o(1).

The comparison polynomial has all ell roots strictly inside that circle. Rouche's theorem therefore gives exactly ell roots of the full polynomial inside it, with multiplicity. All higher degrees have been paid together; no truncation is treated as the original polynomial. Consequently the logarithm at zero cannot have a scale-independent positive convergence radius. If w vanishes on a neighborhood of zero, C_0=0 eventually and that logarithm is already unavailable. This last sentence does not cover every merely w(0)=0 weight.

Any removed fixed positive-degree layer has linear-exponent absolute size by the same prime construction. Restoring the endpoint requires its signed contribution, which could cancel; the argument does not lower-bound the full restored signed source. These activity roots are not L-function zeros. Signed or moving weights, growing ell, exact deflation and differently normalized objects remain outside this theorem, with their recovery obligations intact. This is a valid extension of G106/G108/G120/G145 in a specified direction, not a claim of literature novelty.

## 6. Merging the small-gcd coefficient: all sixth-power coincidences

Retain exactly `B_{<G}Q`, including both inverse profiles, all slot coefficients, signs and the condition `N(d1,d2)<G`. For fixed parameters merge a tuple into

    n=d1 d2 prod_i p_i,   N0=D1D2 prod_i P_i.

Its actual coefficient c(n) includes the normalization N0^(-1/2), `mu(d1)mu(d2)`, all fixed nu/relative phases and profile values, summed over the allowed tuple factorizations. The resulting row polynomial is

    B_{<G,u}Q_u=sum_n c(n) psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1).      (6.1)

This is an identity, not a claim that c is an allowed B3.6 coefficient. A common puncture remains in the tuple; it is never replaced by an unrelated coefficient family. Each column n has norm in a fixed annulus about N0. At a good prime,

    v_p(n) in {0,1,2,3}: two squarefree inverse
    appearances plus at most one original slot appearance.              (6.2)

Valuation 3 really is allowed: the same prime can occur in d1,d2 and one slot. None of those collisions is dropped. For two such n,n', their valuation difference lies in [-3,3]. It is a multiple of 6 exactly when it is zero. Hence the COMPLETE same-sixth-power ideal class is simply n=n'. There are no unequal ideal sixth-power roots in this finite paired source. Fixed units/primary generators contribute their original finite phases and can be separated into the licensed finite sectors; they do not create a growing root sum. This simplification is specific to (6.2), not applicable to the older completed A_R coefficient with unbounded powers.

The number of tuple factorizations of n is divisor bounded, even with named fixed slots. The normalized coefficient and its fixed derivatives therefore satisfy

    |c(n)|<<H_J N0^(-1/2) U^epsilon,
    sum_n |c(n)|^2<<H_J U^epsilon.                  (6.3)

For the second estimate one may use Cauchy inside the tuple factorization sum and the linear ideal count in every original annulus. Dropping the small-gcd restriction after absolute values only enlarges this majorant. Both heights remain inside c; no assertion of their equality or statistical independence is made.

After expansion the full diagonal is

    sum_n |c(n)|^2 sum_(free u) Phi(Nu/U)1_(u,n)=1
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon).                         (6.4)

Retained fixed holes can only decrease this positive diagonal. This is the whole diagonal, including every inverse/slot overlap. It is an upper bound on the diagonal contribution, NOT a lower bound for the entire norm; its off-diagonal can be negative.

statement:
## 2. A marked product-interval square function

The exact source is `[restricted mathematical source]`,
D1--6; M is `zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md`, B1.9--11 and
B2.21--30. JPS is `[restricted mathematical source]`.
The native coefficients remain

    a(n)=alpha(n) eta(n) chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3,
    a(de)=a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4 on coprime d,e.

All ideal labels retain their original good primary squarefree and
finite-ray conventions; no squarefree integer-norm hypothesis is used.
The source has its original zero extension at shared d,e. The mark
array u(P) is the original one, independent of live n,g,R.

Notation and domain are exactly [private research revision] D1. Fix the original R,g and
one original separated profile component. The original n is de, with
q_d in a D dyad and q_e in an E dyad, DE comparable to N. The source
coefficients c(d),b(e) are source-only and divisor-bounded, with all
their actual cutoff and prime supports. The masks (de,g)=(de,bar(g))=1,
the squarefree product, all fixed finite-ray conditions and the
projector 1_(P,Rg)=1 remain. Let

    V_I(R,g) = sum_(d,e,P; q_de in I)
       c(d)b(e)a(d)a(e) chi_d(e)^4 chi_R(de)^3
       [u(P)/sqrt(q_P)] chi_P(de)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1
       C(de) 1_(de,g bar(g))=1.                       (SF1)

Intervals I are intervals of REAL NORM VALUES with arbitrary strict
or non-strict endpoints. Their evaluation is on the original integer
norm q_de. The original long-source support is intersected with I;
it is never replaced by an interval on a quotient. The physical short
factor xi(g)A(g)chi_R(g)^3 is still on the outside, including its zero.

**Claim SF (proved below, relative to M B2.25).** For every finite
family of pairwise disjoint norm intervals I_j,

    sum_j |V_(I_j)(R,g)|^2
       <<_(epsilon,orig) Z^epsilon
          N T(D,E;L) Omega P_lin^2,
    T(D,E;L)=min{S(E,LD), S(D,LE)},
    S(X,Y)=X+Y+(XY)^(2/3),
    Omega=sum_P |u(P)|^2/q_P.                        (SF2)

There is NO factor for the number of intervals. The bound is uniform
in their endpoints, R,g and the original independent norm height.
P_lin denotes the original linear profile mass; in a normalized
single separated component it is one. This is a simultaneous estimate,
not an inference from separate applications of D2. The allowed masks
are the ones displayed in SF1 and the inherited fixed supports. No
arbitrary extra bounded function of de is asserted.

### 2.1 Proof before profile integration

First take a product profile C(de)=C_d(d)C_e(e); its factors have the
original bounded envelopes. Include C_d in c and C_e in b. The exact
characters on d and the mark are put in

    A_(R,g,J)(t)
      = sum_(P d=t; q_d in J)
          [u(P)/sqrt(q_P)] c(d)a(d) chi_R(d)^3
          chi_P(d)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1 1_(d,g bar(g))=1.  (SF3)

Here J is a norm interval on the ORIGINAL d dyad. All P and d
supports, their finite phases, and squarefree conditions are retained.
The zero chi_P(d)^4 forces (P,d)=1, so t=Pd is squarefree.
All e-dependent characters then have exactly the product
chi_t(e)^4. In particular the zero at (e,t)>1 supplies BOTH the
original (e,P)>1 and (e,d)>1 zeros. The remaining coefficient is

    B_(R,g)(e)=b(e)a(e)chi_R(e)^3 1_(e,g bar(g))=1.   (SF4)

Its squared mass is O(Z^epsilon E). No inverse character is used at
a collision. P has NOT been replaced by t in the physical mark root.

Build a fixed binary interval tree on the attainable integer norm
values in the D dyad (zero coefficients may fill missing values).
Pad to the next power of two if necessary. Let J range over all its
nodes, and let ell_D=O(log(2D)) be its depth plus one. Any interval of
d norms is a disjoint union of at most 2 ell_D tree nodes. For fixed
e, the intervals I_j/q_e are disjoint. Their canonical tree covers
are therefore disjoint as sets of d norms, so any fixed node J occurs
at most once among all these covers at that e.

Apply Cauchy in e to each SF1, then sum j. Apply the just-described
tree cover and Cauchy over its at most 2 ell_D nodes. This gives

    sum_j |V_(I_j)|^2
      << Z^epsilon E ell_D
         sum_J sum_(e original)
             |sum_t A_(R,g,J)(t) chi_t(e)^4|^2.     (SF5)

This step retains the actual product endpoint. There is no claim that
e(a q_d q_e) separates. The set of d norms selected at fixed e is an
interval simply because q_e>0 and q_(de)=q_d q_e.

For each J the coefficients SF3 are independent of live e. The cubic
sieve M B2.25, with the original zero extension, gives

    sum_e |sum_t A_(R,g,J)(t) chi_t(e)^4|^2
      << Z^epsilon S(E,LD) sum_t |A_(R,g,J)(t)|^2.  (SF6)

The orientation uses the even reciprocity already admitted in D2.
The t length is LD, not a new source length or a new physical mark.
For each t there are at most tau(t) factorizations t=Pd. Therefore

    sum_J sum_t |A_(R,g,J)(t)|^2
      <= Z^epsilon sum_J sum_(P,d; q_d in J)
                    |u(P)|^2/q_P |c(d)|^2
      << Z^epsilon ell_D D Omega.                  (SF7)

Each d occurs in exactly one node at each tree level. That is why
the total cost is ell_D, not the total number of nodes or intervals.
The full root q_P^(-1/2) is essential: changing it to q_t^(-1/2)
without q_d^(1/2) would incorrectly remove the D in SF7.

Equations SF5--7 give N S(E,LD) Omega times logarithms. Reversing d
and e, keeping their actual source coefficients and both original
supports, gives N S(D,LE) Omega. Taking the smaller proves SF2.
The unit dyad is included by using a one-node tree; no factorization
of a prime into two nonunits has been introduced.

### 2.2 Actual profile and endpoint return

For the actual smooth C(de), use its common Mellin/logarithmic Fourier
separation ONCE and apply Minkowski in the Hilbert space of all interval
outputs j. A norm height factors exactly as q_d^(it)q_e^(it), with
unchanged modulus; the coefficients SF3 remain independent of e.
The original two sides later have their own independent heights.
All original sharp product endpoints can be intersected with the
I_j and kept in the tree; they need no new smooth approximation.
Fixed finite-ray restrictions on de are separated by the original
finite character resolution, with its fixed coefficient mass.

Thus the common profile seminorm and root envelope are exactly the
ones already permitted in JPS/[private research revision]. If a particular profile factor
has already been separated into d,e factors, it is not separated a
second time. Source-only angular and Gauss factors stay in a(d),a(e).
The proof does not extend arbitrary row-dependent or n-dependent
selectors beyond the stated original contract.

The D/D' in this lemma are factor lengths, not the mark/row collision
divisor Delta. That projector stays literal in SF3. If it is instead
expanded before this lemma, EVERY Delta term and intersection must be
restored: its root is q_Delta^(-1/2), its mark squared mass is at most
q_Delta Omega_Delta, and their cancellation is the original one. This
lemma provides no extra division of N or D by q_Delta.

    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau))<=(11gamma-3)/8.              (R18)

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_(<=U)*(v*s), Q_V=a_(<=V)*(v*s),
    S=a_(<=U)*a_(<=V)*b0, R=a_(>U)*a_(>V)*b0.               (R19)

This follows by expanding the two a colors, not by assigning signs after a mask. Every ordered tuple survives in exactly the required inclusion-exclusion combination.

For each epsilon choose a small divisor exponent after epsilon. Applying H to the WHOLE cofactor sum gives ||S||_(1,2)<<X^(gamma+epsilon), because gamma>=3/4. This is the new arithmetic-source payment. No cofactor/output/gcd mask is inserted into H afterward.

           min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4).

For a fixed gamma the whole closed tau corridor has alpha bounded strictly below1, so its constants are uniform. Infinite root endpoints are explicitly in that theorem's scope.

Every tuple in R has de>UV=L. Consequently R(n)=0 for n<=L EXACTLY, and |R(n)|<=(p+1)^2d_3(n). The full coefficientwise tail estimate gives

The generic divisor-bounded tail theorem applies to R, whereas the sharper actual-c variance theorem alone would not suffice for an arbitrary R.

                 sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l),

### 3.2 The corrected main term uses the same energy

First restrict the main sum to k>=rH. Every shift j occurring in psi obeys0<=j<rH<=k. Write v=log(k/X). For X<=x<=2X,

    log((k+j)/x)=v+b,   |b|<=ell.

Consequently

    f_x(k+j)^2/w_X(k)
      =(2 pi tau)^(-1)
         exp([-3v^2/4-2bv-b^2]/tau)
      <=(2 pi tau)^(-1) exp(3ell^2/tau) exp(-v^2/(2tau)). (5)

The last inequality follows from 2|bv|<=v^2/4+4b^2. Using the absolute coefficient sum of Q_r, (5) applies to |psi_x(k)|^2 with the extra factor (2^r-1)^2.

For any positive unimodal function with maximum1, its positive-integer sum is at most its integral plus2. Substituting k=X exp(v) therefore gives

    sum_(k>=1) exp(-log(k/X)^2/(2tau))
       <=X sqrt(2 pi tau) exp(tau/2)+2 <=K_tau X.           (6)

Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, using the ENTIRE sum defining E and restricting only the test-function norm, now yields

    |(1/H) sum_(k>=rH) B_H(k) psi_x(k)|
          <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H)).               (7)

For the remaining indices1<=k<rH use |B_H(k)|<=H. Every positive argument of f_x in psi is <2rH<=X<=x, where f_x increases toward its maximum. Thus this whole part is at most

    rH (2^r-1) g(0) exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2tau)).           (8)

## 3. Reconstructing the complete integer-state coefficient

For the rough source

    R_chi(t,y)=sum_(n<=t;P-(n)>y)mu(n)chi(n), P-(1)=infinity,

least-prime factorization gives R=1-sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)R(t/p,p). Let F be floor-invariant and define its actual defect by the same recurrence. Every increasing-prime path is a distinct squarefree product d, with sign mu(d)chi(d). Grouping by p=P+(d) and m=floor(N/d), rather than by path depth, gives exactly

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m)C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_(N,chi)(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<v<=N/(pm);P+(v)<p)mu(v)chi(v).     (V4)

The lower endpoint is strict and the upper endpoint inclusive. The v=1 term is included. Strict prime ordering removes repeated primes; zero character values remain zero. This is G92's actual complete coefficient, not its unmerged norm.

Fix an integer r>=1 and an exact integer collar m<=p^r. The norm on independently bounded remaining defects is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.

For a principal chi0 and unramified p, the intervals for all m>p^r form a disjoint cover of

    (0,U_p], U_p=N/[p(p^r+1)].

Therefore

    sum_(m>p^r)C_(N,chi0)(m,p)=-W_q(U_p,p-).            (V5)

The plus one is mandatory in this exact identity. It comes from the first allowed integer m=p^r+1; replacing it by p^r before telescoping would change the source. The later asymptotic replacement U_p=(N/p^(r+1))(1+O(p^(-r))) is legitimate and explicitly paid.
