## 1. Inputs and the new results

Use the notation of [M](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md), [CP](../cubic-packets.md), [BC](../[private research revision]/cubic-mobius-core-moment.md), and [the independently accepted SR packet](../[private research revision]/cubic-square-row-moment.md). The independent SR review, recorded in [[private research revision]](../review-cycle-23.md), checks the original CP normalization and fixed-class statement. Write \(q_a=Na\), and put \(\vartheta_c=\chi_c^2\) for the cubic character. Every power retains its nonunit zeros.

The exact inputs used here are:

* **I-C3CF:** M (5.15), the cubic sieve with cube-free ideal rows and columns, arbitrary column coefficients, and its stated finite ray/reciprocity variants:
  \[
  \sum_{q_a\le A}^{\mathrm{cube\!-\!free}}
  \left|\sum_{q_c\le X}^{\mathrm{cube\!-\!free}}
       z_c\vartheta_c(a)\right|^2
  \ll_\epsilon(AX)^\epsilon
       \{A+X+(AX)^{2/3}\}\sum_c|z_c|^2.
  \tag{MQ1}
  \]
  The actual columns below are squarefree. This is the cube-free theorem already stated in M, not an unmentioned extension of the squarefree-only version B2.25. Fixed column exclusions can be imposed through zero coefficients. Its constants do not depend on the arbitrary coefficients.

* **I-HECKE, used only for the all-repetition result:** the inherited all-primitive-finite-order zero-free strip with boundary \(b_0=.874886647039964131\ldots\), together with buffered conductor/height bounds for reciprocal Hecke functions, exact deleted factors, and finite profile orders. Relevant anchors are M Theorem B0 and (B0.14), and BC (BC13), including its interval-endpoint version. This is stronger than ordinary-zeta nonvanishing. It is explicitly required wherever the parameter \(b>b_0\) occurs.

* **I-CP:** M (2.8), (2.14)--(2.15) and CP (21)--(25), with the original coefficient, all total-column masks, fixed components, zero terms and single product kernel. Original column profiles and their fixed derivatives are rapid at both endpoints; the row Fourier profile is Schwartz. The fixed core twists have the finite-order scope of BC section 8. Angular outside-cube factors remain outside the core moment.

No assertion from the enlarged plain family M (B3.40) is silently applied to a Möbius polynomial. In particular, its moving-support contract does not identify a row-varying twist with fixed datum.

Write each nonzero element row in its quadratic class as

\[
n=d a^2,\qquad q_n=q_dq_a^2,
\tag{MQ2}
\]

where \(d\) is squarefree at every prime, with a prescribed unit representative modulo squares. The choice of generator for \(a\), modulo its bounded unit ambiguity, indexes every row with bounded multiplicity. There is no condition \((d,a)=1\). Separate the finitely many fixed-prime parity and unit choices; no moving prime is added to \(S\). Let \(d(n)\) denote this representative and use \(q_{d(n)}\) for its norm, rather than a character conductor.

For a frozen ideal \(R\), an interval \(\mathcal I\) of core norms, a fixed permitted finite-order twist \(\nu\), and an original common profile \(F\), set

\[
\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)
=X^{-1/2}\!
 \sum_{\substack{c\ {\rm squarefree},\ (c,R)=1\\q_c\in\mathcal I}}
 \mu(c)\nu(c)\overline{\vartheta_c(n)}F(q_c/X).
\tag{MQ3}
\]

The original exclusion \(S\) is understood. The interval may have an infinite endpoint. Its endpoints are frozen independently of the row. For a fixed nonnegative Schwartz radial majorant \(\Omega\), let \(\mathcal E_6(H,X,\Delta)\) be the sum of \(|\mathcal M_n^R|^2\Omega(q_n/H)\) over \(q_{d(n)}\le\Delta\) and rows sixth-power-free **away from \(S\)**. Let \(\mathcal E_{\rm all}\) have the same class cutoff and every row valuation. All fixed-prime valuations and element units are retained in both definitions.

Uniformly for \(H,X,\Delta\ge1\), \(1\le\Delta\le H\), and frozen polynomial-norm deletion ideals, the new bounds are

\[
\boxed{\mathcal E_6(H,X,\Delta)
\ll_\epsilon (HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon\mathscr S(F,\Omega)^2
\left\{(H\Delta)^{1/2}+X\Delta+
       H^{1/3}X^{2/3}\Delta^{2/3}\right\}.}
\tag{MQ4}
\]

For every fixed \(b_0<b<1\), I-HECKE additionally gives

\[
\boxed{\begin{split}
\mathcal E_{\rm all}(H,X,\Delta)
\ll_{b,\epsilon}(HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon\mathscr S_b(F,\Omega)^2
\bigl\{&(H\Delta)^{1/2}+X\Delta+
       H^{1/3}X^{2/3}\Delta^{2/3}\\
       &+H^{1/6}X^{(2b+1)/3}\Delta^{5/6}\bigr\}.
\end{split}}
\tag{MQ5}
\]

These are estimates for the actual joint row family. The class representative is allowed to grow in the entire range being summed, and the constants are uniform in it. The first bound in particular gives

\[
\Delta\le H/X\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal E_6\ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon.
\tag{MQ6}
\]

Put

\[
\kappa_b=\frac{4b+2}{5}>1.
\]

Then the all-repetition bound gives

\[
\Delta\le H/X^{\kappa_b}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal E_{\rm all}\ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon.
\tag{MQ7}
\]

Fixed profile and height factors are suppressed in MQ6--MQ7. Their finite orders are uniform in every moving label. All preliminary losses are chosen below the final loss. No uniformity is asserted as \(b\) approaches \(b_0\).

statement:
## 5. Protected audit23: actual thermal state, parity and the missing infinite norm

The seed proposes a KMS mixing converse. It does not supply an algebra, dynamics, positive state, observable or limiting norm. Instead of treating that missing object as a theorem, here are two exact realizations for the actual finite Euler source. They distinguish a positive thermal model with a costly readout from a signed model whose norm cannot stay bounded. Neither is a universal rejection of source-specific dynamics.

Fix s=sigma+it with sigma>0 and let P(y,q) contain all unramified primes<=y. Ramified sites may equivalently be kept frozen empty: their occupied coefficient is zero. On the finite tensor product of two-dimensional site spaces, set N_p=diag(0,1),

    K_y=sum_(p in P(y,q)) (log p)N_p,
    Z_y^+(sigma)=Tr exp(-sigma K_y)=product_p(1+p^(-sigma)),
    rho_y=exp(-sigma K_y)/Z_y^+(sigma),
    U_(chi,t)=tensor_p diag(1,-chi(p)p^(-it)).             ([restricted research revision])

rho_y is a genuine positive state of trace1, and U is unitary on the active sites. It is the finite Gibbs state for K_y. Its usual KMS identity follows directly from trace cyclicity for the dynamics A->exp(iuK_y)Aexp(-iuK_y); no infinite-volume uniqueness theorem is invoked. Every distinct-site connected correlation vanishes because rho_y is a product state, and disjoint tensor observables factor exactly.

The full extensive observable, however, obeys

    P_y(s):=product_(p<=y)(1-chi(p)p^(-s))
                 =Z_y^+(sigma) Tr(rho_y U_(chi,t)),
    Q_y(s)=exp(delta J_y(s))Z_y^+(sigma)
                                      Tr(rho_y U_(chi,t)). ([restricted research revision])

This is the actual finite Dirichlet polynomial sum_(n|product P)mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s), including every squarefree product, not a hard-cutoff Mertens polynomial. There is no missing factor from ramified primes, nor a replacement of all-integer f3 by squarefree parity. Those other sources require separate adapters.

Positivity gives only |Tr(rho_y U)|<=1. It therefore leaves the complete partition function Z_y^+ and the explicit principal vacuum in([restricted research revision]). Local mixing is already perfect for every y and every sigma>0; it does not itself give the cancellation of the extensive parity observable. In fact the raw products in the principal case satisfy T21's actual non-normality obstruction, despite this finite positive thermal realization. The corrected Q_y is a different limiting problem, and this audit does not claim its pressure hypothesis is false.

Because every finite P_y is nonzero in Re s>0, its finite parity expectation is nonzero. The exact LP target in this representation is

    integral_K [delta Re J_y(s)+log Z_y^+(Re s)
                    +log|Tr(rho_y U_(chi,Im s))|]_+ dA
                                   <=C_(K,epsilon)y^epsilon. ([restricted research revision])

Thus a successful mixing theorem must price the complete extensive observable strongly enough to offset the two explicitly written volume terms on every compact and dyadic y. Connected correlations for fixed proper subcollections, an operator norm of1, or finite-volume uniqueness do not supply([restricted research revision]). The dependence of rho_y on Re s is harmless for the algebraic equality([restricted research revision]); analyticity is supplied by its exact P_y source, not asserted for rho_y separately. If an actual estimate proves([restricted research revision]), D1 supplies the complete common-character return. No converse from unnamed KMS uniqueness is available.

There is also an exact norm obstruction to a more direct signed-state proposal. On the finite commutative site algebra with supremum norm, define

    ell_y(F)=P_y(s)^(-1) sum_(n|product P(y,q))
                                  mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s)F(n).

It is a normalized product functional: ell_y(1)=1, and mixed connected correlations between distinct sites vanish algebraically. Its operator norm is its total variation,

    ||ell_y||=sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s)|/|P_y(s)|
             =Z_y^+(sigma)/|P_y(s)|.                    ([restricted research revision])

For the principal character at real0<sigma<=1,

    ||ell_y||=product_(p<=y,p not dividing q)
                        (1+p^(-sigma))/(1-p^(-sigma)),
    log||ell_y||>=2 sum_(p<=y,p not dividing q)p^(-sigma)
                                                     ->infinity. ([restricted research revision])

Prime harmonic divergence suffices, since p^(-sigma)>=1/p and only finitely many primes are ramified. An elementary proof of that divergence is the harmonic-sum domination by finite Euler products, already retained in W41. Positivity fails even before taking a limit: at a principal site the occupied indicator has expectation -p^(-sigma)/(1-p^(-sigma))<0. With a nonreal character phase its expectation need not even be real.

The compatible ell_y cannot extend to a bounded linear functional on the supremum-norm completion of the infinite cylinder algebra in this principal range: such an extension would bound all the restriction norms([restricted research revision]), contradicting([restricted research revision]). This is a precisely specified infinite norm obstruction, not just a finite negative-probability metaphor. Multiplying all finite weights by exp(delta J_y) leaves the normalized ell_y unchanged, so the continuous vacuum does not make this signed functional positive or bounded. It repairs the analytic partition source for D1, which is a different operation.

Useful escapes remain. A genuinely different source-specific norm, a controlled extensive-observable estimate in the positive state, or a proved bounded projection with its entire complement could support a bridge. The principal obstruction does not establish a lower bound for actual signed Mobius sums, nor refute every nonprincipal restricted sector. W33 singleton pressure, W36's real source divergence and W38/W41 complete occupation/covariance distinctions are the close ancestry. The added evidence here is the literal Gibbs/parity return and exact normalized-functional cost; no new arithmetic estimate is asserted.

## Development14: exact cover, weighted defect and reconstruction

Let chi be any fixed ordinary Dirichlet character modulo q, with its natural zeros. Work on the augmented squarefree q-unit cutoff complex: a face S has product n<=X and degree |S|=omega(n), including the empty face in degree0. Its oriented deletion differential is d. Let D_chi e_n=chi(n)e_n. Then Str(D_chi)=M_chi(X), where M_chi(X)=sum_(n<=X) mu(n)chi(n). This convention fixes the reduced-chain sign shift.

The exact commutator is

    [D_chi,d] e_n
      = sum_(p|n) orientation(p,n) chi(n/p)(1-chi(p)) e_(n/p).

For distinct deletions the target faces are distinct. A local deletion coefficient that commutes with the character insertion must therefore vanish whenever chi(p)!=1. Ordinary weighted deletion cannot silently become a chain map for this insertion.

The author's proposed full residue cover does not solve that issue. Its basis is (S,g), g in G=(Z/qZ)^*, and deletion of p sends (S,g) to (S\{p},gp), with the usual orientation. The conserved coordinate h=g*product(S) conjugates this differential to d tensor I_G. Thus the cover is a trivial direct sum after a relabeling. In the Fourier sector sum_g chi(g)^(-1)e_(S,g), the differential has coefficient chi(p); it is D_chi^(-1)dD_chi. Every such sector has one vector per face and the same Euler index M_chi0(X), not M_chi(X).

This is an actual source discrepancy, not a dimensional slogan: for q=3, the nonprincipal chi and X=5, the allowed faces are1,2,5. The Euler index is1-1-1=-1, whereas M_chi(5)=1+1+1=3. Inserting chi(h) on the complete conserved register commutes but has trace0 for nonprincipal chi. Anchoring the register to g=1 recovers chi(n) but breaks the chain condition. The statement is restricted to this full regular-residue cover and this readout; it excludes no different nonlocal construction.

The paid repair is correct. Let ell be the least prime not dividing q. The subcomplex formed by ell-free faces of product<=X/ell and their ell-cones is contractible. Every boundary face of a critical ell-free face in (X/ell,X] lies in that cone: all its prime factors exceed ell. Let h insert ell on eligible ell-free faces, with positive insertion sign, and vanish otherwise. On the cone, dh+hd=I. On a critical face set P e_S=e_S-hd e_S; set P=0 on the cone. Directly, P^2=P, dP=Pd=0 and dh+hd=I-P. The author's projection is not merely the diagonal indicator of critical faces; the correction is necessary.

Graded cyclicity now gives the complete identity

    Str(D_chi) = Str(D_chi P) + Str([D_chi,d]h).

Writing A(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,ell∤n) mu(n)chi(n), B(X)=A(X)-A(X/ell), and c=chi(ell), its two terms are exactly B(X) and (1-c)A(X/ell). Hence

    M_chi(X) = B(X) + (1-c) sum_(j>=1) B(X/ell^j).

All sums terminate below1. A uniform all-scale bound B(X)=O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)), gamma>0, therefore returns M with the explicit geometric cost 1+|1-c|/(ell^(gamma+epsilon)-1), after paying a finite head. Conversely A(X)=sum_(j>=0)c^j M_chi(X/ell^j), so a full M bound gives the same B exponent. This is an exponent-equivalent source target, not a weaker arithmetic input. It includes principal, complex and imprimitive ordinary characters, with fixed-chi constants allowed.

Unsigned ranks remain too large. For r fixed,

    Q_r(X)=#{n<=X: n squarefree, (n,r)=1}
          = kappa_r X + O_r(sqrt X),
    kappa_r=(phi(r)/r) product_(p∤r)(1-p^(-2)) > 0.

The elementary proof uses mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counts integers coprime to r, and pays the convergent square-divisor tail. Thus the critical rank is kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X), including the principal q=1 value2X/pi^2. Bounding the scalar by this complete unsigned rank cannot establish M cancellation.

The sampled13 annular extension follows from the long exact sequence: total relative reduced Betti mass is at least b(K_X)-b(K_(X/Y)). It is linear for fixed Y>1. For any finite filtration, including a different finite filtration at each X, the sum of its relative masses telescopes to at least final mass minus initial mass. If initial mass=o(X), refining annuli cannot lower the complete unsigned price below order X. This does not reject signed pairings across annuli or pretend that D_chi commutes in a twisted index.

## 4. New component [restricted research revision]-C1: paid transfer among the three fixed detectors

Let k_o be the existing geometric-width compact kernel (widths 2^-j), k_n the new D2 kernel, and g_tau the fixed Gaussian. Their bilateral transforms are M_o,M_n and M_g(s)=exp(tau s²/2). Keep exactly A(n)=mu(n)-2 1_(2|n)mu(n/2). This is a full-field result, not a transfer of arbitrary moving masks or separate components.

For each fixed strip 0<a<=Re s<=b and T=|Im s|, direct product estimates give

    |M_o(s)| >= exp[-C_(a,b)(log(2+T))²],
    |M_n(s)| >= exp[-C_(a,b)(1+T)log(2+T)].                  ([restricted research revision].1)

Proof: |sinh(c s)/(c s)|>=Re(s)/|s| for c>0. Split the old product at J~log(2+T) and the new product at J~1+T. Beyond J, |c s|<=1/2 and log|sinh(c s)/(c s)|>=-C|c s|². The old tail costs O(1), the new one O(T), because a_j<<1/j and sum_(j>J)a_j²<<1/J. Multiply the first J lower bounds. This coarse estimate is sufficient; it asserts nothing on Re s=0, where compact transforms have zeros.

D5 and [restricted research revision].1 show that **M_n/M_o** and **M_g/M_n** are holomorphic on Re s>0 and decrease faster than every inverse power on each closed positive strip. Their inverse bilateral transforms h_no,h_gn satisfy, for every gamma>0,

    integral_R |h(v)| exp(gamma v) dv < infinity.             ([restricted research revision].2)

Invert on a positive vertical line. For v>=0 move to a_+>gamma; for v<0 move to 0<a_-<gamma. Rapid vertical decay pays the horizontal contours; the bounds are e^-a_+v and e^-a_-v. This includes the left tail, where h itself need not decrease. Fourier inversion gives k_n=h_no*k_o and g_tau=h_gn*k_n, hence

    F_n(x)=integral h_no(v) F_o(xe^v) dv,
    F_g(x)=integral h_gn(v) F_n(xe^v) dv.                     ([restricted research revision].3)

The safe coefficient scope includes actual A and arbitrary fixed sequences with polynomial coefficient mass: first choose an inversion line beyond that exponent to justify absolute rearrangement. For shell bounds at every sufficiently large scale, Minkowski, [restricted research revision].2 and a fixed covering by dyadic shells give

    ||F_o||_shell << X^(gamma+epsilon)
       => ||F_n||_shell << X^(gamma+epsilon)
       => ||F_g||_shell << X^(gamma+epsilon), gamma>0.        ([restricted research revision].4)

Every large shift v and every small shifted scale is included. Compact source fields vanish sufficiently far left; the bounded small-scale part is integrable since a_-<gamma. Gaussian fields, when separately used, have superpolynomial left decay. Constants depend on fixed kernels and margins, never on X. Correct direct direction: **old compact -> new compact -> Gaussian**.

There is no bounded reverse translation-invariant transfer on a positive weighted L2 line. The lower bound for M_o and upper bound for M_n force |M_o/M_n| to infinity; [restricted research revision].1 and Gaussian decay force |M_n/M_g| to infinity. On a finite band the reverse costs at least the supremum of the quotient. On the new near-log height window the old/new quotient already has a superpolynomial lower bound, so this inverse cannot be treated as free. Pointwise nonzero multipliers do not give a uniformly conditioned inverse.

A distinct **actual-source every-epsilon exponent equivalence** does hold. If one full detector has all-shell growth at gamma in(0,1), its fixed Mellin identity excludes zeros strictly right of gamma. On any narrower positive strip there, polynomial vertical growth of1/zeta follows by Borel–Caratheodory applied to a holomorphic logarithm of (s-1)zeta(s), starting at Re s>1 and using the standard polynomial bound for zeta on fixed strips. The exponent depends on the strip margin. Each M decreases faster than every power there, so the full inverse Mellin contour shifts to gamma+epsilon, giving all other detectors O(x^(gamma+epsilon)). Thus these fixed complete arithmetic targets are equivalent up to every epsilon. This uses the complete return and the specific zeta source; it is neither bounded deconvolution nor component/mask equivalence. Separately fixed Hecke families need their own growth/numerator statement; no conductor-uniform extension is asserted.

Signal bounds remain explicit. Each M is nonzero at any possible zero0<sigma<1. On a fixed positive strip and finite height interval [restricted research revision].1 gives a positive lower bound, while |1-2^(1-s)|>=2^(1-sigma)-1. Uniform signal bounds deteriorate with height: Gaussian attenuation is exp(-tau t²/2), old compact has lower bound exp(-C log²|t|), and new compact has the coarse exp(-C|t|log|t|) lower bound. Old compact has better inverse conditioning; new compact has better direct auxiliary decay. Neither proves a better arithmetic exponent.

For joint use, fixed coefficients c_j give multiplier sum c_j M_j(s), which detects only where that sum is nonzero. Complete energy is sum c_i bar(c_j)<F_i,F_j>, with both ordered cross terms. Scale-dependent least-squares coefficients may minimize a norm but do not automatically define a fixed detecting source. A positive vector energy is at least each weighted component and has no new blind-spot advantage here: all three M's are already nonzero in the target strip. A useful joint theorem needs easier bounds on complementary source ranges or a paid negative cross term, plus quantitative nonvanishing/covering. None is proved. Representation transfers are paid; the new signed arithmetic estimate is not.

## 7. Fixed-depth deflation and its qualifications

For a fixed integer K>=1 define

    v_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_{p^K}*q_p,
    b_K=v_K*h, c_K=v_K*a, h_K=v_K-b_K.

Equivalently v_K=q_{p^(K+1)}-q_{p^K}. Its coefficient at 1 is zero, and

    b_K(j)=chi(j)[p^K 1_{p^K|j}-p^(K+1)1_{p^(K+1)|j}].

This is zero-mean periodic with period Q_K=p^(K+1)q. The moving-row proof
works with eta_K=1/(100kQ_K), keeping all K-dependent constants. One has
h_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_{p^K}*h_p, so h_K(1)=0 and h_K(l)=0 for every
prime l. At tau=1, provided B(n)>=1, the possible d=1 contribution is
excluded and the entire semiprime projection, including prime squares,
vanishes. If B(n)<1, d=1 may remain. This exception is essential. If
u=2gamma-r>0, B(n)>=1 throughout the finite core for large X, as in all
three target rows above.

The Mellin numerator gains the factor chi(p)^K p^{K(1-s)}, which never
vanishes, and keeps P_p(s). The same two-prime return survives for fixed K.
This operation is a fixed multiplicative dilation and does not itself save
an exponent.

For a principal character the positive obstruction moves to
n=p^(K+1)d with d prime in (X/(4p^(K+1)),X/(2p^(K+1))]. The complete
merged long coefficient is +p^K: h_K(p^(K+1))=-p^K and mu(d)=-1;
the potential pd row has h_K(p^K)=0; rows with higher p-valuation have
zero Mobius coefficient; fixed small powers of p do not pass the long cut.
PNT supplies asymptotically X/(4p^(K+1)log X) such d for fixed K, hence
a projected norm of order X/(p log X).

There is also a valid selected-cell diagnostic for growing K satisfying
p^(K+1)<=X^(1-gamma-delta), with fixed 0<delta<1-gamma. Then d exceeds
X^(gamma+delta), B(n)=L on this cell for large X, and pure p powers are
below L because gamma>1/2. PNT is uniform for the resulting polynomially
large prime arguments, so the projected lower bound remains >> X/log X.
This does not prove a growing-K full complement theorem. Row and short-term
upper budgets grow with K; failure of those upper budgets is not an
impossibility theorem for a better method.

## 3. Full shrinking-arc observation and all-height return

Discrete Fourier inversion writes chi(k)=sum_(a mod q)c_a e(ak/q). The periodic Bernoulli identity, with its actual sign, is

    Phi(x)=-(2pi i)^r/r! sum_a c_a B_r({x+a/q}).

On 0<x<1/q this is one polynomial of degree at most r. The endpoints agree by continuity for r>=2; no measure or endpoint term is lost. Its constant is beta=2L(r,chi), nonzero by the absolutely convergent Euler product at r>1. This does not assume a zero-free half-plane to the left of 1.

Let h=1/(qN). The endpoint reproducing polynomial p_r satisfies

    integral_0^1 p_r(u)u^j du=1_(j=0), 0<=j<=r,
    integral_0^1 |p_r(u)|^2du=(r+1)^2.

The shifted Legendre construction proves both identities. Independent rational inversion of the moment matrix gives p_2=9-36u+30u^2 and p_3=16-120u+240u^2-140u^3, with squared norms 9 and 16. Since nhu<=1/q for every ORIGINAL n<=N, the observation O_Nf=integral p_r(u)f(hu)du gives exactly

    beta T_N=O_NR_N-eta_N,
    T_N=sum_(n>N)a(n)n^(-r),
    eta_N=O_N(2cos(2pi x))-2=O_r(h^(r+1)).                (R5)

The full observation price is (r+1)sqrt(qN) times the arc L2 norm. Therefore for fixed 0<c<1/2, gamma=1-c, the every-integer-N estimate

    integral_0^(1/qN)|R_N(x)|^2dx
      <<_(chi,r,epsilon)N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon)               (R6)

gives T_N<<N^(gamma-r+epsilon). The exact inverse

    M_chi(N)=1/L(r,chi)-N^rT_N
                  +r integral_1^N t^(r-1)T_floor(t)dt

then gives M_chi(X)<<X^(gamma+epsilon) for every real X. Conversely Phi is globally Lipschitz, including its r=2 derivative jumps, and Abel summation gives

    |R_N(x)|<<N^(gamma-r+epsilon)+|x|N^(gamma-r+1+epsilon)

on this arc. The derivative integral converges after choosing epsilon so gamma+epsilon<1. Squaring and integrating recovers (R6), with epsilon relabelled. This is a two-way equivalence, not merely an implication from an easier known estimate.

The Mellin integral s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma and initially equals 1/L(s,chi). For nonprincipal characters the bounded periodic sums continue L to Re(s)>0; for principal characters the floor integral for zeta and the original finite Euler factors give a meromorphic function with its simple pole at 1. The reciprocal identity extends on the connected half-plane with that pole removed and excludes every zero there, with no height restriction or multiplicity exception. The principal point 1 remains a pole. Natural imprimitive factor zeros at Re(s)=0 were never divided away. No growing-conductor, Hecke or Eisenstein conclusion follows.

# [private research revision]: the actual merged renewal norm and signed profile corrections

Accept G112-G113 after full reads of the [author](headroom/report.md),
[independent review](headroom-review/report.md), both helpers and G92's
original integer-state construction. Root visually inspected original
Tenenbaum theorem pages224-226. The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json)
binds14 frozen artifacts, including the primary PDF, page images and
the complete independent regularity/BV extension. No unchanged helper was
rerun. Finite identity evidence and asymptotic proof remain distinct.

The highest accepted written source-relative endpoint stays
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636. This cycle resolves the particular
merged-norm question left open in [G92](../[private research revision]/wild49-integration.md)
and tests a fully constructed signed repair. It gives no Mertens lower
bound, new zero-free constant, universal renewal impossibility, or
nonprincipal-character obstruction. F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot
uniformity and external root-definition/import/admission stay OPEN.
No formalization, kernel work or new proof packet occurred.

## G112. Coalescence does not lower the independent-defect power cost

For each fixed ordinary character chi preserve all natural zeros and put
R(t,y)=sum_(n<=t,P^-(n)>y)mu(n)chi(n), with P^-(1)=infinity.
Its least-prime recurrence is R=1-sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)R(t/p,p).
For a floor-invariant approximation F let Delta be its full recurrence
defect. G92 gives the exact root identity

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_(N,chi)(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<v<=N/(pm),P^+(v)<p)mu(v)chi(v).    (77.1)

All coefficients are merged by the actual integer state BEFORE absolute
values. The strict lower/inclusive upper endpoints, v=1 and strict prime
ordering matter. For the exact integer collar m<=p^r, fixed integer r>=1,
the independent bounded-defect norm is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.        (77.2)

The earlier real-state exponent-one lower bound did not prove anything
comparable after signed coalescence. The actual cancellation at
(N,p,m)=(20196,17,18), v=65,66 remains valid. Here a new arithmetic
argument proves, for EVERY fixed principal character chi0 modulo q,

    lim_(N->infinity) log B_(r,chi0)(N)/log N=1.        (77.3)

The external input is Tenenbaum's fixed-order friable Mobius expansion,
combining Theorems2-3 in the [original source](headroom/Erdos-Alladi.pdf).
Write omega for the Buchstab function. For fixed K>=1 and a fixed compact
I contained in(K+1,infinity), uniformly for u=log x/log y in I,

    W(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P^+(n)<=y)mu(n)
      =x sum_(j=1)^K a_j omega^(j)(u)/(log y)^(j+1)
        +O_(I,K)(x/(log y)^(K+2)),
    sum_(j>=1)a_j z^j=1/[(1+z)zeta(1+z)], a1=1.        (77.4)

The primary images confirm the sign, derivative index and logarithm power.
The source domain exp((log x)^(2/3+epsilon))<=y<=x holds for a fixed
epsilon in(0,1/3) and large y at each fixed compact u-range. That compact
is away from the first K+1 exceptional integers. Its extra error
Psi(x,y)/L_epsilon(y) is smaller than every needed fixed logarithmic
order. No uniform growing K or u estimate is imported. The published
theorem and ordinary PNT are mathematical premises, not consequences of
the local finite helper or a complete reproof of the twenty-page source.

The strict cutoff is exactly y=p-1. Its replacement by log p changes the
main expression by O(x/[p(log p)^2]), within the fixed-order remainder.
For principal q define A_q(s)=product_(ell|q)(1-ell^-s)^-1. Once p exceeds
every prime divisor of q, the complete convolution is

    W_q(x,p-)=sum_(d q-smooth) W(x/d,p-),
    sum_(j>=1)b_(j,q)z^j=A_q(1+z)/[(1+z)zeta(1+z)].    (77.5)

All powers of the primes dividing q occur. Truncating at D=(log p)^B
costs at most x D^-eta A_q(1-eta), for fixed0<eta<1. Fixed logarithmic
moments of d then justify the Taylor product on a slightly larger compact.
Thus (77.4) holds with b_(j,q) and b_(1,q)=q/phi(q). This retains the
principal character's natural zeros; it is not a nonprincipal extension.

For fixed p the intervals in(77.1), summed over m>p^r, cover exactly
(0,U_p], U_p=N/[p(p^r+1)]. Hence

    sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)=-W_q(U_p,p-).          (77.6)

Choose a FIXED u>2 with omega'(u)!=0 and P=N^(1/(u+r+1)). Uniformly for
P<p<=2P, log U_p/log p=u+O(1/log P), and the K=1 expansion has a fixed
nonzero sign. PNT with partial summation gives

    sum_(P<p<=2P)sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)
      ~ -(q/phi(q))omega'(u) kappa_r N P^-r/(log P)^3,
    kappa_r=(1-2^-r)/r>0.                              (77.7)

The plus one in U_p is exact; its later relative O(p^-r) replacement is
paid. Triangle inequality gives a lower bound for the actual merged norm,
with power theta(u,r)=(u+1)/(u+r+1). Expanding the merged coefficients
before the upper bound counts each squarefree q-unit d at most once,
so B<=N. There are admissible u arbitrarily large: an eventually zero
omega' would make omega constant on a tail, and
u omega'(u)=omega(u-1)-omega(u) propagates that constant backward to
(1,2), contradicting omega(u)=1/u. Taking successively larger FIXED u
in the liminf bound proves(77.3), without a growing-u asymptotic.

## G113. Actual signed profiles buy logarithms, with exact limits

An explicit attempted repair cancels the leading mean. Set
g(v)=(v-1)^3(2-v)^3 on[1,2], zero elsewhere, and h(v)=v^2 g'(v).
Then h is C1, vanishes at the two endpoints, |h|<=3/4, and

    m0=integral h(v)v^-2 dv=0,
    m1=integral h(v)v^-2 log v dv
      =-integral_1^2 g(v)/v dv=8log2-111/20<0.           (77.8)

Prescribe Delta_N(m,p)=1_(P<p<=2P)h(m/p^r), root defect zero, and all
other defects zero. Finite triangular back substitution constructs F_N
with exactly these defects; the collar is descendant-closed and receives
its exact rough-sum values, which need not be1 when r>1. No unknown
Mertens value is used in the construction. Its root value and computation
cost are not thereby bounded. The complete root error is the signed
scalar(77.1), with no discarded complementary residual.

Put L=log p, A=N/p^(r+1), u_p=log A/log p, v_m=m/p^r and
S_m=W_q(N/(pm),p-). Exact discrete summation gives

    sum_m C_m h(v_m)=-sum_m S_m[h(v_m)-h(v_(m-1))].     (77.9)

Zero extension pays both support boundaries, including the last
difference. The K=2 expansion yields the full response

    F_N(N,1)-M_chi0(N)
      ~ (q/phi(q))m1 omega''(u) kappa_r
                           N P^-r/(log P)^4,           (77.10)

for fixed u>3 with omega''(u)!=0. The second source coefficient cancels
with m0; its sign is not needed. There is a real logarithmic gain but
no uniform sublinear power over all admissible prime-band placements.

More generally take a fixed nonzero complex C1 profile compactly
supported inside(1,V), and let J be the first nonzero logarithmic moment
m_J=integral h(v)v^-2(log v)^J dv. Such a finite J exists by polynomial
density after the change of variable log v. Then for fixed u>J+2 with
omega^(J+1)(u)!=0 the full response is

    [(q/phi(q))(-1)^(J+1)m_J/J!] omega^(J+1)(u)
                       kappa_r N P^-r/(log P)^(J+3).   (77.11)

Here and above the ratio to the displayed nonzero main term tends to1.
The identity integral h'(v)v^-1(log v)^k dv=m_k-km_(k-1) shows that
only source index1 and Taylor index J survive at the first order.
Total variation, rather than the number of states, pays the uniform
source remainder. For the smooth main approximation s, writing profile
increments as exact integrals proves the quadrature bound

    |sum_m s(v_m)Delta h_m-integral s(v)h'(v)dv|
      <=p^-r sup|s'| integral|h'|=O(A/[p^r L^2]).       (77.12)

This completes the author's C1 argument without assuming h' is Lipschitz.
For each fixed derivative order, omega^(k) is nonzero arbitrarily far
out: otherwise a tail polynomial would satisfy the delay equation, whose
degrees force it to be constant, giving the preceding contradiction.

The independent review extends(77.11) to any fixed nonzero RIGHT-CONTINUOUS
complex profile of bounded variation, compactly supported inside(1,V).
With nu=dh, exact sampling assigns each increment to nu((v_(m-1),v_m]);
the bound(77.12) becomes p^-r sup|s'| |nu|(R). Stieltjes integration by
parts, with the zero extension retaining endpoint atoms, gives the same
moments. Right continuity rules out isolated values invisible to them.

For example h=(5/9)1_[5/4,7/4)-1_[7/4,9/4) has m0=0,m1<0, and the
complete one-prime response is

    -(5/9)S_ceil(5p^r/4)+(14/9)S_ceil(7p^r/4)
                                     -S_ceil(9p^r/4). (77.13)

The half-open endpoints and ceilings are mandatory. An independent exact
case(N,p,q,r)=(441,7,6,1) gives5/9 by three representations. Four earlier
zero cases remain in the receipt. These finite examples do not prove the
asymptotic; that uses(77.4),(77.12) and PNT.

## What remains usable for a new zero-free estimate

For every fixed h,q,r and proposed gamma<1, choose a sufficiently large
FIXED admissible u with theta(u,r)>gamma, then let N grow. This gives
an obstruction uniform over admissible band placements. It does not say
one prescribed fixed-u family's exponent equals1, or that every natural
residual fails. Bands with theta<=gamma, cross-prime correlations,
changing profiles and growing collars remain outside that conclusion.

Subtracting a truncated deterministic Buchstab mean W_q=H+E preserves
the complete E response on a finite quotient block[a,b]:

    -E(N/(pa))Delta_a+E(N/[p(b+1)])Delta_b
       -sum_(m=a+1)^b E(N/(pm))(Delta_m-Delta_(m-1)).    (77.14)

The identical H expression must be restored. Arbitrary bounded defects
can have variation of order the state count. Fixed K gives only the stated
logarithmic accuracy; growing K requires new uniform estimates, transition
and collar payments, plus the restored H contribution.

A sufficient complete return still needs, for EACH fixed ordinary
character, every epsilon>0 and ALL large N, both |F(N,1)| and the entire
signed defect in(77.1) bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon). Then the actual
Mertens bound follows, with noninteger x handled by flooring. Abel/Mellin
continuation of 1/L pays all finite heights and derivatives, ramified and
imprimitive zeros, and the principal pole. No Hecke or moving-conductor
extension is inferred. The current first-gain requirement is

    gamma<.8748540364; theta(u,r)>1-c iff u>r/c-r-1.

Nearer gains,1/6 and1/4 use this same complete budget. The old frozen
.125143/.125145 conditional examples no longer improve the incumbent.
No new arithmetic input for that return is proved here.

This pass discovered six mechanisms before developing the actual renewal
source and a signed repair. It resolves a live missing prerequisite and
redirects a concrete approach. Next use a proved relation across prime
bands or a fully controlled varying profile/collar; another fixed profile
alone cannot supply the hoped-for power. The full29-family/109-child
portfolio and the discarded mechanisms remain. Tenenbaum/Alladi retain
the friable-asymptotic credit, G92/W49 the source and coalescence credit,
and the independent review its C1 completion and BV extension. Literature
priority is not asserted. Original09:20/09:50 deadlines remain missed;
same-owner recovery preserved the completed source, evidence and handoff.

statement:
### 3.2 Turnover lemma: a short move must replace a large factor

For distinct positive integers n,m, put g=gcd(n,m). Then

    g divides n-m, so g<=|n-m|.                                 (C3)

If C>0, 0<=theta<1, and |n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta, it follows exactly that

    n/g >= C^(-1) n^(1-theta).                                  (C4)

When n is squarefree, n/g is the product of the prime factors deleted from n. If all those primes are <=y and at most d are deleted, then n/g<=y^d. Thus n has NO such neighbor whenever

    n^(1-theta)>C y^d.                                         (C5)

This argument allows m to be squareful or nonunit: adding zero-mass auxiliary integer states does not help when an edge may delete at most d of n's prime factors. In particular it applies to the usual squarefree Boolean Hamming radius<=d, whose number of deleted coordinates is<=d. No coefficient estimate or character-distribution assumption is used.

statement:
## 3. Independent proof of W48.1

Fix tau>0 and an arbitrary complex sequence |a(n)|<=1 for n>=1, with a(n)=0 for n<=0. Define

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),
    f_x(t)=g(log(t/x)) (t>0), and f_x(t)=0 (t<=0),
    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) f_x(n).

The SAME G72 energy is

    B_H(k)=sum_(j=0)^(H-1) a(k-j),
    w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4*tau)),
    E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

It includes the first partial window, the complete positive line, every coefficient zero and both tails. Its exact signed lag expansion is

    E=(1/H) sum_(|h|<H) sum_(n>=max(1,1-h)) a(n) conjugate(a(n+h))
              *sum_(j=max(0,h))^min(H-1,H-1+h) w_X(n+j).

Thus neither deleting off-diagonal terms nor replacing the inner weight by a constant triangular count is allowed.

Put h_tau(t)=g(log t), extended by zero at t<=0, and

    J_j = integral_0^infinity |h_tau^(j)(t)| dt,
    ell=log 2, K_tau=sqrt(2*pi*tau) exp(tau/2)+2,
    C_(tau,r)=(2^r-1) sqrt(K_tau/(2*pi*tau)) exp(3*ell^2/(2*tau)).

Every derivative is a fixed polynomial in log t times t^(-j)g(log t); h_tau is smooth and flat at zero and rapidly decreasing at infinity. In particular every J_j is finite and ||f_x^(j)||_1=x^(1-j)J_j.

**Accepted exact inequality.** For fixed integer r>=1, X>=1 and integer H>=1 with 2rH<=X,

    sup_(X<=x<=2X) |F_a(x)|
      <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H))
       + ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r X^(1-r)+J_(r+1) X^(-r)]
       + rH (2^r-1) g(0) exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2*tau)).       (R1)

Constants depend only on tau,r. This is not a claim of controlled constants for growing r.

### 3.1 Orientation and exact adjoint

Use the FORWARD average T f(n)=H^(-1) sum_(j=0)^(H-1) f(n+j). Set

    Q_r(T)=sum_(j=0)^(r-1)(I-T)^j
          =sum_(k=0)^(r-1)(-1)^k binom(r,k+1) T^k.

The exact identity T Q_r(T)+(I-T)^r=I and its coefficient l1 norm 2^r-1 give, with psi=Q_r(T)f_x and R=(I-T)^r f_x,

    F_a(x)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) B_H(k) psi(k) + sum_(n>=1) a(n)R(n).   (R2)

Indeed k=n+j in the first sum yields sum_n a(n)T psi(n); indices n<=0 vanish by the stipulated extension. Each T^k is a probability average of shifts from 0 to k(H-1). No backward adjoint, missing boundary term or altered coefficient sequence occurs.

### 3.2 The weighted norm and small-index objection

For k>=rH, every shift j in Q_r lies below rH<=k. Write v=log(k/X), b=log((k+j)/k)+log(X/x), so |b|<=ell. Then

    f_x(k+j)^2 / w_X(k)
      =(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp((-3v^2/4-2bv-b^2)/tau)
      <=(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp(3ell^2/tau) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)).

The underlying difference after replacing ell^2 by b^2 is (v/2+2b)^2>=0. This directly verifies the exponent and constant, rather than invoking an unpriced change of Gaussian width. The unimodal sum satisfies

    sum_(k>=1) exp(-log(k/X)^2/(2*tau)) <= K_tau X.

Its integral is X sqrt(2*pi*tau)exp(tau/2), and comparison to the integral costs at most 2. The absolute coefficient sum of Q_r and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz now give the first term of (R1):

    (1/H) sqrt(sum |B_H|^2 w_X) sqrt(sum |psi|^2/w_X)
       <= C_(tau,r) sqrt(X E/H).

For 1<=k<rH, the preceding ratio estimate is not available uniformly. Instead |B_H(k)|<=H, every test argument is <2rH<=X<=x, and the Gaussian is monotone there. Summing at most rH indices gives exactly the last term of (R1). This pays the strongest inverse-weight objection; applying the large-index ratio everywhere would be invalid.

### 3.3 The complete repeated-difference remainder

For nonnegative integer j,

    f(n)-f(n+j)=-integral_0^j f'(n+u)du.

Iterating gives the signed r-fold derivative integral for (I-T)^r, averaged over j_1,...,j_r in {0,...,H-1}. If f and f' are integrable and f is absolutely continuous, then for all v>=0,

    sum_(n>=1)|f(n+v)| <= ||f||_1+||f'||_1.

Compare f(n+v) to f(t) on [n+v-1,n+v], integrate, and sum disjoint intervals in the positive half-line. Applying this to f_x^(r), integrating the r shift lengths, and using their mean (H-1)/2 proves

    sum_(n>=1)|R(n)|
       <=((H-1)/2)^r [J_r x^(1-r)+J_(r+1)x^(-r)].

For r>=1 and x>=X the displayed powers are bounded by the corresponding X powers. This proves (R1), including the whole right tail and the flat left extension. H=1 has exactly zero remainder, consistent with the formula.

## 4. At the unit dual core the exact Euler operator can be rank one

The next calculation is an exact compression of the source matrix.
It identifies what remains of the actual phase; it is not a
replacement of the complete physical column family by primes.

Take the admitted unit-mark endpoint \(P=1,L=1\), original \(b=1\),
\(N=A\), and the sharp selector \(\mathfrak h(g)=1_{g=1}\).
Choose \(1\le A_0Y<c_*A\). Restrict both column indices to good prime
ideals p of norm comparable to A, in one sufficiently fine **fixed**
identity ray class. All these primes have norm exceeding \(S_0\).

The ray modulus can simultaneously include 3, 4, the fixed conductor,
and the conductors of the finitely many quadratic characters obtained
by evaluating at fixed deleted primes. It ensures, for distinct
retained p,q,

\[
\gamma_3(pq)=1,\quad
\kappa_S(pq)=1,\quad
\chi_{pq}(\mathfrak f_S)^3=1,\quad
\chi_{pq}(z)^3=1\quad(z\mid T_S),
                                                               \tag{SC9}
\]

where \(T_S=\operatorname{rad}(D_0)/
(\operatorname{rad}(D_0),\mathfrak f_S)\), and
\(D=\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak f_ST_S)\) is exactly the original
fixed deletion/conductor radical. For the first identity, M B1's
quadratic Gauss phase is \(\Gamma_q(pq)\), which equals one when
the primary generator \(pq\equiv1\pmod4\). The other conditions
are finitely many fixed ray conditions; no moving conductor or
pair-dependent ray class has been introduced.

On this compression, \(j=p,w=1\), the true gcd is one for distinct
primes, \(T=T_S\), and \(\mathfrak f=\mathfrak f_Spq\).
Every prime in pq exceeds \(S_0\), so exactly
\(\mathfrak M(S_0;\mathfrak fT)=\mathfrak M(S_0;D)\).
The complete z-sum is the fixed nonzero product
\(Z_S=\prod_{r\mid T_S}(1-\kappa_S(r)/\sqrt{q_r})\).
In this principal-square sector \(\kappa_S\) is quadratic on units.
Any radial component nontrivial on units vanishes; otherwise
\(U_\kappa=6\). Each factor in \(Z_S\) is positive. CRT retains
the fixed factor \(\gamma_{\kappa_S}\), rather than setting the
full Gauss sum to one.

Let \(v_p\) be the original normalized column coefficient on these
primes, including its unchanged smooth column profile and original
finite/height twists. Put \(\rho_p=1-q_p^{-1}\). SQ9 with the
singleton selector \(\sigma=1_{h_0=1}\) gives exactly

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal M_{\{1\}}^{\rm prime}(S_0)
=C_{\Phi,S}\sqrt K\,\mathfrak M(S_0;D)
\left(
\left|\sum_p\rho_p v_p\right|^2
-\sum_p\rho_p^2|v_p|^2\right),
\quad
C_{\Phi,S}=6c_\Omega\rho(\mathfrak f_S)
\gamma_{\kappa_S}Z_S.}
                                                               \tag{SC10}
\]

The original finite-sector expansion coefficient and any original
outside scalar multiply both sides. For two different separated
column profiles, replace the square by the product of their two
sums, and the diagonal by the corresponding inner product.

Both original removed diagonals are present in this calculation:
with \(P=1,b=1\), they both mean p=q. That case also has true gcd
p and is outside the sharp support. The subtraction in SC10 is an
algebraic way to express the distinct-prime sum, not a restoration
of a physical diagonal. The complete d-projector is one on each
remaining pair. Every z is a fixed z0 divisor and z1=1; there is no
missing ambient z count. All original s, all square powers t, and
all fixed-place zeros have already been included in SQ9.

For the actual unextracted infinity source, \(v_p=f(p)W(q_p/A)\),
with its **actual**
\(f(p)=\overline{\alpha(p)}\gamma_2(p)\nu(p)\) from SH12.
Thus SC10 exposes a cubic-Gauss first moment. The sign
\(\overline{\kappa(h_0)}\) is exactly one at this core, and the
Euler/Möbius operator is a common scalar. Neither sign supplies
additional column cancellation. SC10 does not assert that the
actual first moment is large.

## 7. Source Euler data and quantitative costs

Factoring the primary zero-frequency quotient gives

    C_p(xi)=(1-Q^(3-4xi))/(1-Q^(4-4xi)).

Direct evaluation and differentiation give C_p(5/4)=1+Q^-1, C_p(3/4)=0, and C_p'(3/4)=-4 log(Q)/(Q-1). These match the author. Two raw source constant factors contribute C_p(xi1)C_p(xi2), before the actual cusp/ray linear combinations. At the forward residual point their scalar product is (1+Q^-1)². It cannot by itself erase the nonconstant identity phase direction. At the reflected point there are zeros, but substituting zero into an unspecified intertwiner is not a boundary theorem: transported Whittaker functionals, normalization and specialization order can have compensating poles. The principal-series intertwining integral is also different from right multiplication by the compact Weyl element.

The scalar factors are source constant-term Euler data, not verified entries in a relative matrix. Their unrestricted prime product is not absolutely convergent; it cannot be absorbed into the O(Q^-2) selected-vector convergence budget. Likewise the explicit cusp constants in section 4 do not replace an actual opposite-cell calculation.

For sigma=Re(s)>1/2 and r=Q^(1-2sigma), the difference formula gives

    (1-Q^-sigma)r|u-v|/(1+r)²
      <= |J_s(Ea_u)-J_s(Ea_v)|
      <= (1+Q^-sigma)r|u-v|/(1-r)².

Put q=Q^-2. Annulus integration for b=a_-1-a_1 gives ||b||²=4q/(1+q) and integral b=-2q/(1+q). The completion norm identity ||Eb||²=2||b||²-|integral b|² therefore gives

    ||Ea_-1-Ea_1||²=4q(2+q)/(1+q)².

The ratio of the readout difference to this Hilbert distance has size Q^(2-2sigma) for fixed sigma as Q grows. At sigma=.874864 the exponent is .250272. This is a genuine lower cost on the displayed local family, not an operator bound on all inputs, and not a license to multiply local lower bounds into a global impossibility claim.

The author's first phase derivative norm also checks: the annulus mass at floor(v/2)=j is (1-q)q^j, giving (log Q)² q(1+q)/(1-q)². Completion costs at most a factor 2 in squared norm. Fixed higher derivatives have q times a fixed logarithmic power, and their vacuum overlaps have the same summable order. Thus smooth selected Hilbert tensor families are plausible with these explicit estimates; moving restriction and relative distribution norms remain unpaid. No ambient-L2-to-moving-trace inference is made.

## B. Pole subtraction after actual integer-quotient merging

### B1. Exact centered source

Now use the distinct ORDINARY source a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), for a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character modulo q. Retain a(1)=1, prime2, squareful zeros and every character zero. Set M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), psi_chi(y)=sum_(d<=y)Lambda(d)chi(d), and delta_chi=1 for principal chi and0 otherwise. [restricted research revision]/W55 C1-C3 already proves

    R_chi(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d),
    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R_chi(x).                     (B1)

The inverse formula with unit/head terms and its complete zero return are prior credit. W64 does not relabel that identity or the old divergent absolute kernel as new.

For integer N>=2 and any floor-invariant input f(t)=f_floor(t), define the pole-centered functional

    J_N(f)=sum_(d<=N)Lambda(d)chi(d)f_(floor(N/d))
                    -delta_chi int_1^N f_(floor(N/u))du.     (B2)

The continuous measure du has Mellin transform1/(s-1), so it is exactly the principal logarithmic-derivative pole subtraction. At finite N its endpoints are literal. The complete return is

    R_chi(N)=J_N(M)+delta_chi int_1^N M(N/u)du.               (B3)

In particular the restored principal term cannot be dropped. It equals N sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n-M(N), including the endpoint n=N correctly.

Merge equal integer quotients BEFORE absolute values. For1<=m<N let

    L_m=N/[m(m+1)],
    c_m=psi_chi(N/m)-psi_chi(N/(m+1))-delta_chi L_m.

Then exactly

    J_N(f)=sum_(m=1)^(N-1)c_m f_m.                           (B4)

The lower interval endpoint is strict and the upper inclusive. The state m=N contributes zero, since its only possible atom is d=1 with Lambda(1)=0 and its continuous interval has length0 after clipping at1. Thus neither an independent-error norm before merging nor a lost unit term is being used here.

For0<beta<1 and a prefix Y<N define the scaled norm on remaining independent states by

    C_(beta,Y)(N)=N^(-beta)sum_(m>Y,m<N)|c_m|m^beta.           (B5)

This is the exact operator norm under |f_m|<=m^beta and f_m=0 for m<=Y: choose f_m=m^beta conj(c_m)/|c_m| at nonzero c_m. A fixed known prefix is a separately known affine contribution; differences of admissible continuations have this zero-prefix form.

### B2. Isolated prime-power cells survive centering

Let

    D=floor(min(sqrt(N)/4, N/[4(Y+1)])).

For every unramified prime power2<=d<=D put m=floor(N/d). It lies strictly above Y; also m>=N/(2d). Its quotient cell contains d and has length

    L_m<=d^2/(N-d)<=1/8.                                   (B6)

There is therefore exactly one integer in the cell. Different d give different m. The FULL merged coefficient at that state is

    c_m=Lambda(d)chi(d)-delta_chi L_m,
    |c_m|>=Lambda(d)/2.                                    (B7)

Here |chi(d)|=1; ramified prime powers are omitted precisely because their original coefficient is zero. The elementary inequality log2>1/2 makes(B7) immediate from(B6). Consequently

    C_(beta,Y)(N)>=2^(-beta-1)
                   sum_(2<=d<=D,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta).
                                                                    (B8)

This lower bound is for the actual merged, centered kernel. It does not rely on independent unmerged copies of a quotient state.

An elementary Chebyshev lower bound suffices to price(B8). For n>=1, the p-adic exponent of binomial(2n,n) is at most floor(log_p(2n)); hence

    psi(2n)>=log binomial(2n,n)>=2n log2-log(2n+1).

Taking2n<=D within1 of D gives psi(D)>=cD for large D. Removing the finitely many prime-power rays dividing fixed q changes this by O_q(log D), so psi_chi0(D)>=c_q D. Therefore

    C_(beta,Y)(N) >= c_(q,beta) D^(1-beta).                   (B9)

For fixed0<=theta<1 and Y=floor(N^theta), this gives

    C_(beta,Y)(N)/log N
      >>_(q,beta,theta) N^((1-beta)min(1/2,1-theta))/log N.  (B10)

The centered operator remains unbounded even after a power-size known prefix and the log N normalization of(B1). With theta<=1/2, the powers are .0625729818 at beta=.8748540364,1/12 at beta=5/6, and1/8 at beta=3/4. These are obstruction exponents for this norm, not zero-free gains or lower bounds for actual M. Any bounded-density smooth drift in place of delta_chi du has the same argument after reducing the fixed constant in D.

### B3. Strongest objection: actual cumulative inputs have bounded increments

The independent-state norm permits unrealistic adjacent oscillations. A source-specific proof could exploit them being cumulative sums. The following free-exploration test shows that adding only bounded increments and natural zeros still does not repair this centered contraction certificate.

Fix1/2<beta<1 and

    0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta).                              (B11)

For every sufficiently large integer N there exists a SYNTHETIC coefficient sequence b_N(n), depending on N, with

    |b_N(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),
    F_m=sum_(n<=m)b_N(n), |F_m|<=m^beta,
    |J_N(F)| >= c_(q,beta,alpha) N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).     (B12)

It is essential that b_N is not claimed to have the fixed Mobius signs or the Mobius convolution law. This is a kinematic counterexample to a particular enlarged norm certificate, not a counterexample to the desired arithmetic estimate.

Here is a complete construction. Let

    Q_q(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1)product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.              (B13)

This elementary count follows by inserting mu(n)^2=sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-unit multiples with error O_q(1), and paying the sum of at mostsqrt x errors and the convergent e^-2 tail. No prime distribution theorem is used.

For each unramified prime power2<=d<=floor(N^alpha), set m_d=floor(N/d), H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8), and

    B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|).

Each B_d is a triangular bump in the actual squarefree q-unit count. Its integer increment has modulus at most mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1), exactly0 at every natural-zero site. Since beta>1/2, (B13) puts its support within m_d+O_q(H_d). Since beta<1, every supported n is comparable to m_d and B_d(n)<=n^beta for large N.

The nearest possible distinct centers are separated by a constant multiple of N/d^2. Their support-width-to-separation ratio is at most a constant times

    N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta)
      <=N^(beta-1+alpha(2-beta)) ->0                       (B14)

by(B11). Thus the supports, including their increment boundaries, are disjoint. Under u->floor(N/u), the support of each bump lies in an interval around the corresponding integer d of width O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta)+d^2/N)=o(1), uniformly in d. Hence its only integer contact is d itself. It does not couple to another prime power or hide an omitted integer atom.

Put

    F_n=sum_d conj(chi(d)) B_d(n), b_N(n)=F_n-F_(n-1), F_0=0.

The preceding disjointness proves every natural-zero, increment and growth condition in(B12), including extension by0 before and after the finite supports. Each discrete atom in(B2) contributes exactly Lambda(d)H_d, a positive real number. For nonprincipal chi the drift is absent. For principal chi all selected phases equal1; each continuous contribution is at most H_d times its o(1) u-width, hence at most Lambda(d)H_d/2 eventually. Therefore

    |J_N(F)|>= (1/2)sum_d Lambda(d)H_d
       >> N^beta sum_(d<=N^alpha,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta)
       >> N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).                          (B15)

The same elementary Chebyshev estimate proves the last step. All bumps lie at states at least a constant multiple of N^(1-alpha). Thus any prescribed zero-error prefix m<=N^theta with theta<1-alpha is also preserved. One may choose alpha smaller to accommodate any fixed theta<1.

After dividing by log N, this norm still grows by N^(alpha(1-beta))/log N. At a near-current beta the admissible alpha is small but positive. The construction explicitly answers the bounded-jump/natural-zero objection; fixed signs, multiplicativity, the exact convolution inverse, and correlations tied to the actual single arithmetic source are the indispensable remaining escapes. No conclusion is drawn against those escapes.

### B4. Complete arithmetic return and limitation

For the actual source, the required signed input remains the COMPLETE R_chi(x), including the restored term in(B3), with a bound O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)log x) at all large real x, for every fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0. [restricted research revision]'s exact inverse then gives M_chi(x)=O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)). Neither the isolated-cell lower bound nor the synthetic b_N construction supplies or contradicts that signed bound.

For completeness, the resulting fixed-source function

    F_chi(s)=s int_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

would converge holomorphically on Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives. It equals1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. For nonprincipal chi, periodic partial sums continue L to Re(s)>0; for principal chi retain its ordinary pole at1. The identity L F=1 excludes regular zeros in Re(s)>gamma at every finite height, while a principal pole gives a reciprocal zero. All imprimitive Euler factors stay literal; their additional zeros lie on Re(s)=0. Constants and onsets may depend on fixed chi; no moving-modulus result is inferred. Gamma<2187135091/2500000000 would improve current c11, with5/6 and3/4 the1/6 and1/4 targets. No such gamma estimate has been obtained.

The record-relative increment beyond [restricted research revision] is the pole-centered, already-coalesced exact finite norm, its growing-prefix lower bound, and the natural-zero bounded-increment counterexample. [restricted research revision]'s separate merged rough-renewal norm and [restricted research revision]'s divisor-erasure prices retain their exact scopes and credit. No literature-priority claim is made.

\tag{DC1}

\ll_{b,\epsilon}
K^{1-b}D^{5/6+b+\epsilon}C^{1/6+b}.
}
\tag{DC2}
\]

\[
\boxed{

### F25.E — Triple-theta compact-profile energy

The true double-torus Fourier equations enforce equality of **elements**. Its Mellin identity is
\[
\int_0^\infty P_r(y)y^{2s-3}{dy\over y}
=J_r(s){L^{(S)}(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang})\over\zeta_K^{(S)}(s)}.
\]
T09 treats \(r\in[1,2]\) as a Hilbert-valued profile. Analyticity in r and the nonzero small-r limit ensure that \(J_r(s)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere on this compact interval. This avoids an individually zero-free \(J_1\), uniformity as \(r\to0\), or height-uniform inverse factors. The remaining theorem is TRI's signed small-y decay.

Keep the actual three-source correlation through a spectral or horospherical restriction and compute residual, continuous and cusp-boundary pieces. A fixed r-profile family may help annihilate a genuinely identified nuisance channel, but its remaining multipliers must have no common zero. Finite r-quadrature is useful only with explicit profile-derivative error bounds. A proof for a finite spectral packet is partial until the complement is summed.

A finite cube-deleted **trilinear** functional is an admissible structural child: it changes the functional tested in [restricted research revision] and could escape that particular linear-period obstruction. It introduces projection/level costs. Absolute inversion of the common angular cube factor stalls at \(a=5/6\) (A05); varying r does not remove this numerator. Moving below that threshold requires a changed completion or separately proved angular cancellation, not extrapolation of TRI.

## G169. Complete occupation and compact-source interfaces

For uniform n∈{1,…,N}, every prime p≤N, including ramified primes, set

\[
U_p(n)=-(1+\chi(p))1_{p\mid n}+\chi(p)1_{p^2\mid n},
\quad Z_N(z)=\mathbb E\prod_p(1+z_pU_p).
\]

The factors equal1 at valuation zero,−χ(p) at valuation one and0 at
larger valuations. Thus Z_N(1)=Mχ(N)/N. First and distinct-prime moments
retain their literal floors:

\[
m_p=\frac{-(1+c_p)\lfloor N/p\rfloor+c_p\lfloor N/p^2\rfloor}{N},
\]
\[
m_{pr}=\frac{(1+c_p)(1+c_r)\lfloor N/(pr)\rfloor
 -(1+c_p)c_r\lfloor N/(pr^2)\rfloor
 -c_p(1+c_r)\lfloor N/(p^2r)\rfloor
 +c_pc_r\lfloor N/(p^2r^2)\rfloor}{N}.                  \tag{96.11}
\]

The formal log includes overlapping and repeated clusters; even though
Z_N is multiaffine, the z_p² coefficient of log Z_N is−m_p²/2.
Convergence at the physical activity requires a separate theorem.

For independent n,m define V_p=U_p(n)+conjugate(U_p(m))+
U_p(n)conjugate(U_p(m)). Then E∏(1+V_p)=|Mχ(N)/N|², including the
complete diagonal and off-diagonal. Its distinct two-prime connected
coefficient is |1+m_p+m_r+m_pr|²−|1+m_p|²|1+m_r|². A bound for a
selected cluster or a different Gaussian kernel is not a bound for this
complete contraction.

For q=1, keep only primes √N<p≤N and give them common activity t.
No integer up to N contains two of them, so

\[
Z_H(t)=1-B_Nt,\qquad
B_N=\frac2N\sum_{\sqrt N<p\le N}\lfloor N/p\rfloor
\longrightarrow2\log2>1.                              \tag{96.12}
\]

The limit follows from the [ordinary PNT](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3),
partial summation and floor error at mostπ(N)/N=o(1). Thus this actual
partial marginal has a zero t_N=1/B_N inside(0,1) for all large N.
At N=100, B_N=27/25. Its logarithm at zero has radius less than1 and
the absolute series ∑B_N^j/j diverges at1. This blocks an absolutely
convergent log expansion on the full unit activity polydisc. It does
not turn a marginal zero into an L-zero or refute resummed, conditioned,
signed or differently parametrized replica expansions. The full
cross-sector return remains necessary. G145's high-prime clique, W51
fugacity and W38/[restricted research revision] occupation laws retain their ancestry.

The author also provides an explicit compact verification interface for
[G128's literal normalized source](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md).
Let δ indicate principal χ, r=δφ(q)/q, b(t)=∑_{n≤e^t}χ(n)−re^t, and

\[
F_\chi(s)=\left(\frac{s-1}{s+1}\right)^\delta\frac{L(s,\chi)}s
 =\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f(t)\,dt,\qquad |f(t)|\le C_q=1+3q.
\]

Here f=b for nonprincipal χ and
f(t)=re^−t+b(t)−2∫₀ᵗe^{−(t−u)}b(u)du for principal χ. F has exactly
the ordinary L-zeros on Re(s)>0; its value at the removed principal pole
is r/2, nonzero. If F_T truncates the integral at T, then on Re(s)≥σ₀>0,
|F−F_T|≤C_qe^−σ₀T/σ₀ and |F′|≤C_q/σ₀².

For a convex compact cell of radius d around z, a certified value v of
F_T(z) with error ε proves nonvanishing throughout that cell if

\[
|v|>\varepsilon+C_qe^{-\sigma_0T}/\sigma_0
                  +(C_q/\sigma_0^2)d.                 \tag{96.13}
\]

This pays truncation, evaluation and interpolation. If F is nonzero on
a given compact K, its positive minimum modulus lets all three errors
shrink below one eighth of that minimum, forcing eventual success.
Conversely soundness forbids success on a compact containing a zero.
Thus it is a semidecision procedure, with no efficiency claim and no
numerical execution in this cycle. Success on every
K_m={γ+1/m≤Re(s)≤m+2, |Im(s)|≤m} is equivalent to zero exclusion on
Re(s)>γ. The all-m premise remains unproved. Finite successes cannot
replace it, and G130's raw principal global-polynomial obstruction does
not reject this normalized compact construction.

## 3. Gap-versus-density extension

The same proof needs only the following local geometry around each large center j. For fixed epsilon, let a_j>=1,0<d_j<=1 and let E^(j) be a measurable subset of [j/2,3j/2] on which |F(u)|<=C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)u). Require that every interval of length a_j contained in this range meets E^(j) in measure at least d_j*a_j, and require

    (a_j+1) log(C/d_j) = o(sqrt(j)).                    (A12)

Add the whole exterior. For j large, a_j=o(sqrt(j)) and the central range is longer than4a_j. Every interval of length2a_j either contains an a_j interval inside the central range, or has at least a_j length in the exterior. The augmented set is (d_j/2,2a_j)-thick. A3 costs exp[O((a_j*sqrt(j)+1)log(C/d_j))]=exp(o(j)). The same two tails and the same completed-square source bound prove A5.

Examples: a_j=j^alpha and d_j=exp(-j^theta) are sufficient whenever alpha+theta<1/2 (alpha>=0,theta>0). With d_j bounded below, gaps o(sqrt(j)) are allowed; with polynomial density, it suffices that a_j log(j)=o(sqrt(j)). The sets must satisfy the stated local geometric contract at every large center. A density-one list of globally good shells alone does not imply it.

There is also an explicit finite-loss version at the critical density. Suppose the sets in A4 instead obey log(1/delta_k)<=(D+o(1))*sqrt(k), for a fixed D>=0, at source exponent gamma_src<b. In the proof replace I_j by the integer-ended interval with endpoints j+/-j^(7/8)+O(1), and use T_j=t*sqrt(j), t>0. The exterior tail is now exp(-j^(5/4)/2+o(j^(5/4))); sigma_j=tau+O(j^(-1/2)); and log(delta_j^*)^(-1)<=(D+o(1))*sqrt(j). Thus the complete output exponent is at most

    max{gamma_src+132*D*t, b-tau*t^2/2+132*D*t}.        (A16)

All displayed exponents allow an arbitrarily small positive buffer. In particular t=sqrt(2*(b-gamma_src)/tau) gives

    gamma_out=gamma_src+132*D*sqrt(2*(b-gamma_src)/tau). (A17)

This follows from the same source, localization and frequency tails, and does not assume a fixed-thickness theorem for a varying set. For the bounded ordinary/f3 coefficients and the fixed ideal count one may take any fixed b>1. Hence the strict condition

    gamma_src+132*D*sqrt(2*(1-gamma_src)/tau)<gamma4     (A18)

already gives a first-gain contract, by then choosing b>1 sufficiently close to1. This is a sufficient cost, not an optimal constant. The width tau is the SAME fixed Gaussian in the observation hypothesis; increasing it would change the arithmetic input. Subcritical A4 has D=0 and avoids this finite penalty entirely.

The decisive source is literal B3.40, not the prose sentence describing PR9's original contradiction. For positive slots its hypotheses are

## 4. Canonical coefficients, witnesses and the conditioned theorem

The fixed-character witnessing presentation need not be the slot's original parent. The accepted [restricted research revision] re-anchoring uses the same original modulus M0, ray subgroup, quotient characters, genuine prime pool and common profile. Set Q*=M0 intersect (72) intersect q_eta0 and express the witnessing label as tau_lambda=tau0*kappa0 with kappa0 a fixed Q*-ray character. Present the new anchor eta0*kappa0 modulo Q* and replace the relative character accordingly. The whole fixed factor tau_lambda need not have conductor dividing Q*; its separately fixed conductor is paid by the original small width padding. On Q*-units the two whole slot coefficients agree algebraically. At primes dividing Q*, equality is equality of zeros: old pool exclusion, bad-mask zeros or the original relative-character zero supplies it. No zero is canceled by division. FE1/FE2 preserve the literal fixed-inducing predicate. Whole-product conjugation also reflects every height; conjugation of the fixed factor alone is not allowed.

Fixed additional slot holes are removed with B3.41's **signed** subtraction before Minkowski. The actual complementary slot product is priced before that expansion. Remaining slots are subsets of the original canonical family; exhaustion uses the old zero-slot theorem. A varying arbitrary coefficient family, arbitrary pool or unequal-mask moment is not imported. Frozen raw sixth-power roots and missing radicals can supply polynomial-size fixed holes within this exact bridge.

Lemma1W permits a cutoff t in [1,3/2] fixed before the class's witnesses. With row scale normalized to W=1 it gives r<=t, r+m>=t and 0<=m<=1/2, up to a preallocated small loss, with squared inverse/plain witnesses at least Z^(delta r) and Z^(delta m). Both witnesses have the same presentation, real part and height. The physical bin alone supplies the upper price for original slot subproducts; a larger internal witness height maximum may supply a lower witness bound but is not substituted as an upper slot price.

For the conditioned statement, positive squared-amplitude grades q_i in [0,delta] obey sum q_i z_i<=qv, where v=z/W and delta-.01<=q<=delta. This is a positive-grade condition; a small factor cannot offset an unbounded one. Sorting by grade and discarding one fractional slot makes a fixed subset per amplitude class/dyad. ## A01. The coherent unembedded nonzero sextic aggregate

**Status:** proved restricted-sector estimate relative to the exact inherited raw field. It is not a bound for every nonzero frequency, the full compensated energy, or mixed embedded covariances.

Use the raw [restricted research revision] §5 field
\[
H(m)=Y^{-1}\sum_{a,A}c_{a,A}G_a(m)\chi_A(m)
W_0(q_m/(Qx_a)),
\quad
G_a(m)=q_a^{-1/2}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m),\quad x_a=q_a/Y,
\]
with exactly its original coefficients and all fixed sectors. Here \(A=cn^3\), \(c\) squarefree. Expand \(\sum_m|\xi(m)|^2|H(m)|^2\). Select pairs satisfying
\[
\frac{aA'}{bA}\in I_{\rm good}^{\,6}. \tag{A01.1}
\]
For every selected pair subtract its complete additive zero covariance in the AA19 sense, retaining the full continuous product profile. Denote the signed sum of differences by \(\mathcal E_{\ne,\rm coh}^{\rm raw}\). Then
\[
|\mathcal E_{\ne,\rm coh}^{\rm raw}|\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon. \tag{A01.2}
\]
If both good outer indices \(a,b\) are squarefree, the bound improves to \(Z^\epsilon/Y\). Physical energy includes the additional factor \(Q^{-1}\).

### Local masks and exact coherent incidence

At \(p\mid AA'\), write \(\alpha_p=v_p(a)\), \(\beta_p=v_p(b)\), \(d_p=v_p(A)-v_p(A')\pmod6\). AA14 forces \(\alpha_p,\beta_p\le1\) because the column character requires a unit row. The local row character exponent is \(d_p-\alpha_p+\beta_p\). Under (A01.1) it is zero and the factor is a unit scalar times \(1_{p\nmid m}\).

Since \(A=cn^3,A'=c'n'^3\), the difference between the two squarefree incidence differences lies in \([-2,2]\). It cannot cancel an odd multiple of three. Therefore, at those primes,
\[
\alpha_p-\beta_p=v_p(c)-v_p(c'),\qquad
v_p(n)-v_p(n')\equiv0\pmod2.
\]
Outside \(AA'\), the coherent condition is \(\alpha_p-\beta_p\equiv0\pmod6\), with the additional support restrictions below.

Consequently all surviving pairs admit the exact good-ideal parametrization
\[
c=gu,\ c'=gv,\quad
a=d_0ur_1^6,\ b=d_0vr_2^6,\quad
n=hs^2,\ n'=ht^2.
\]
Here \(g,u,v\) are pairwise coprime squarefree; \(h\) is squarefree; \((r_1,r_2)=1\); \((r_1r_2,AA')=1\); \((d_0,uv)=1\); and \(v_p(d_0)\le1\) at \(p\mid AA'\). Core/cube overlaps among \(g,u,v,h,s,t\) otherwise remain. In particular, \(r_i\) may share primes with \(d_0\) outside \(AA'\).

At a good prime outside \(AA'\), let \(E_j=1_{p^j\mid m}\), \(E_0=1\). Lifting a normalized local Gauss sum gives, for \(j\ge1\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}1_{p^{j-1}\mid m}
\sum_{x\bmod p}^{*}\chi_p(x)^j
\psi_p(-mx/p^{j-1}).
\]
If \(6\nmid j\),
\[
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-1}(E_{j-1}-E_j).
\]
If \(6\mid j\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}(qE_j-E_{j-1}),\quad
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-2}\{(q^2-2q)E_j+E_{j-1}\}.
\]
These explicitly retain principal-on-units spikes.

For unequal coherent valuations \(\alpha>\beta\), positive \(\beta\not\equiv0\pmod6\) gives disjoint supports. If \(\beta=0\), the principal formula for \(G_\alpha\) applies; if \(6\mid\beta>0\), \(G_\beta\) is constant on \(G_\alpha\)'s support. Every surviving local product is a linear combination of divisibility masks with coefficient \(\ell^1\) norm at most \(2q^{(\alpha+\beta)/2}\). CRT therefore writes the full good kernel as
\[
K_S(m)\sum_e b_e1_{e\mid m},\qquad
\sum_e|b_e|
\ll_\epsilon(q_aq_b)^{1/2}
(q_aq_bq_Aq_{A'})^\epsilon. \tag{A01.3}
\]
Here \(K_S\) belongs to the original fixed finite periodic family; no moving prime is placed in \(S\). If \(a,b\) are squarefree, the factor \((q_aq_b)^{1/2}\) is unnecessary.

### Uniform discrepancy, including periods beyond the row range

For every bounded smooth annular profile family on the Eisenstein lattice,
\[
\sum_{e\mid m}\Psi(m/\sqrt Q)
-\frac{Q}{q_e}\int_{\mathbb C}\Psi
=O_\Psi(1), \tag{A01.4}
\]
with the fixed lattice covolume included and uniformly in \(Q,e\).

To prove it, rotate and scale the ideal lattice by a generator of \(e\), and put \(L=(Q/q_e)^{1/2}\). For \(L\ge1\), Poisson bounds the nonzero dual sum by
\[
O_N\!\left(L^2\sum_{\xi\ne0}(1+L|\xi|)^{-N}\right)=O(1)
\]
for fixed \(N>2\). For \(L<1\), the compact annulus meets only \(O(1)\) lattice points and its continuous mass is \(O(L^2)\). Fixed residue classes satisfy the same argument. This proves (A01.4) with \(K_S\) and its actual zero average.

Applying this to (A01.3), each pair's row sum minus its complete zero mode is \(O(YZ^\epsilon)\) times fixed profile seminorms.

### Sum of the original coefficients

The modulus of a paired completed coefficient is
\[
\frac1{q_g\sqrt{q_uq_v}\,q_h^2q_s^2q_t^2}.
\]
For fixed \(d_0,r_1,r_2\), the outer annuli imply
\[
\sum_{u,v}(q_uq_v)^{-1/2}
\ll \frac{Y}{q_{d_0}(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3}.
\]
The original log-Gaussian profiles satisfy
\[
\sum_gq_g^{-1}|V(T_1q_g)V(T_2q_g)|\ll1
\]
uniformly in \(T_1,T_2>0\), by dyadic ideal counting and Cauchy. The \(h,s,t\) sums converge at norm exponent two, the \(r_i\) sums at exponent three, and \(\sum_{q_{d_0}\ll Y}q_{d_0}^{-1}\ll\log(2Y)\). Thus total absolute coefficient/profile mass is \(O(Y\log(2Y))\). Small powers of completed column lengths are absorbed in the original two-sided log-Gaussian envelope.

Multiplying by the raw prefactor \(Y^{-2}\) and the \(O(Y)\) per-pair discrepancy proves (A01.2). In the squarefree outer subcase that discrepancy is \(O(1)\), proving the stronger bound.

For a fixed number of all-marked slots at **unembedded \(D=1\)**, replace \(V\) by the exact AA18 kernel. Permitted divisors of \(A\) are divisor-bounded, and AA20 supplies a common envelope at scale \(ZP\). No extra tuple count or \(q_U^{-1/2}\) is inserted. The same proof applies.

**Unpaid:** nonprincipal good-character pairs, including their values at sixth-power additive frequencies; mixed embedded arguments \(e^2r,d^2r\); arbitrary \(A\)-dependent weights; growing slot counts; the full physical saving.

**Precise follow-up:** derive the actual embedded coherent row kernel first, with \(\operatorname{lcm}(D^2,E^2)\) and all character zeros. Once such a kernel is a fixed-sector divisibility combination, dilation introduces no difficulty for (A01.4), because \(1_{p^j\mid\lambda r}=1_{p^{(j-v_p(\lambda))_+}\mid r}\) and cannot increase coefficient \(\ell^1\) mass. The remaining problem is the correct character/coefficient incidence and total marked mass, not a blanket “long period” obstruction.

**Sources:** BB R08; [restricted research revision] AA14–AA20; [restricted research revision] AB16.

       <= D_F(X)+O(X^(.495+delta))
       << X^(gamma+epsilon/2),                           (6.2)

The fixed field F has the left tail (5.5), so it belongs to
D_alpha. Apply the lemma with k_6, whose norm is finite by
(2.5), and the other identity in (2.9). This proves the G
estimate at exponent 2gamma+epsilon.

equivalent. No constant is asserted to be uniform as epsilon
tends to zero. Thresholds for sufficiently large dyads may depend

This proof never applies K_6 or J_6 to the family

statement:
## 2. Moving deletion ideals can be removed without moving the datum

Fix the full zero-extended presentation of a finite-order character
`omega`, and write

\[
\begin{split}
A_u^R(X;F)
 =\sum_{(m,R)=1}\mu(m)\omega(m)\chi_m(u)F(q_m/X),\\
M_u^R(X;F)=X^{-1/2}A_u^R(X;F).
\end{split}
\]

The underlying fixed S restriction is understood. For every finite
ideal R, the exact inverse deletion identity is

\[
\boxed{
\begin{split}
A_u^R(X;F)
 &=\sum_{\operatorname{rad}(a)\mid R}
       \omega(a)\chi_a(u)A_u(X/q_a;F),\\
M_u^R(X;F)
 &=\sum_{\operatorname{rad}(a)\mid R}
       \frac{\omega(a)\chi_a(u)}{\sqrt{q_a}}
           M_u(X/q_a;F).
\end{split}}
\tag{SR3}
\]

Here `a` ranges over all powers supported on R, not just its squarefree
divisors. For a prime dividing R the coefficient identity is
`sum_{j=0}^v mu(p^(v-j))=0` for `v>=1`; outside R it is the original
Möbius coefficient. Multiplicativity, including zeros, proves SR3.
In particular no `(a,u)=1` hypothesis is added. For compact annular F
only finitely many `a` occur; for the original rapid profile the double
sum converges absolutely, by its large-argument bounds.

For every fixed `epsilon>0`,

\[
\sum_{\operatorname{rad}(a)\mid R}q_a^{-1/2}
 =\prod_{p\mid R}(1-q_p^{-1/2})^{-1}
 \ll_\epsilon q_R^\epsilon.
\tag{SR4}
\]

Indeed each sufficiently large-prime factor has logarithm at most
`epsilon log q_p`; the finitely many smaller primes contribute a
constant. No conductor-dependent reciprocal L-function is invoked.

Apply Minkowski in the positive row Hilbert space to SR3. The phases
have modulus at most one. M (B0.8), or the same Sobolev argument for
the fixed common profile, then gives

\[
\sum_{u\ne0}\Omega(q_u/H)|M_u^R(X;F)|^2
 \ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon\mathcal S(F)^2,
 \qquad H\ge X^{1+\vartheta},
\tag{SR5}
\]

for fixed `vartheta>0` and a fixed nonnegative rapid row majorant
`Omega`. The statement is uniform in R. The fixed datum remains
`omega,S`; R has not been absorbed into it. Dyadic row majorization
uses UM inside a fixed larger polynomial range. Above that range,
absolute row and column counting, with an arbitrarily high Schwartz
power, pays the rest of the infinite row tail. Subunit column
scales are bounded directly. Smooth height twists cost a fixed power
of the height, as in M (B0.3), rather than a conductor-dependent order.

We shall use SR5 with the stronger slack `H>=X D^delta`, `X<=D`.
This also allows the original noncompact two-endpoint profiles. For
detail, split them into fixed-annulus profiles. Column annuli up to
`D^(delta/4) X` still satisfy UM with a smaller fixed positive margin
(one can use `vartheta<delta/8`). Higher annuli have arbitrarily small
mass by the original rapid endpoint bounds: absolute column counting
and the `O(H)` row-majorant mass suffice. The same argument applies to
each required Euler derivative. There is no change of the original
Mellin root. All profile constants used here are finite seminorm and
endpoint constants of the prescribed original family.
title: 2. Moving deletion ideals can be removed without moving the datum
