statement:
### A paid whole-shell nonprincipal-bank reduction

There is a useful stronger conclusion from the literal identity. Freeze
an unramified prime P comparable to X before varying x over [X,2X], and
put w_P(x)=x^(-b)+i(1/x-2*pi/P). For any ordinary eta let
F_eta(w)=sum_n mu(n)eta(n)exp(-nw), Re w>0. Apply finite character
orthogonality to e(-n/P), leaving exp(-nw_P(x)) as the COMMON profile.
Absolute convergence proves for EVERY real x in the shell

    V_b,chi(x)=G_(P,chi)(x)+B_(P,chi)(x),                (R20)
    G_(P,chi)(x)=1/(P-1) sum_(psi mod P,psi!=psi0)
           psi(-1)tau(conjugate psi)F_(chi psi)(w_P(x)),
    B_(P,chi)(x)=-F_(chi psi0)(w_P(x))/(P-1)
                    -chi(P)F_(chi psi0)(P w_P(x)).

In the second branch n=Pm, the phase exp(-i m(P/x-2*pi)) is exactly
the original exp(-i Pm/x). Thus this is not merely an identity at the
isolated rational point x=P/(2*pi). The P^2 deletion remains in psi0;
the character product and all other natural zeros are unchanged.

The elementary bound |F_eta(w)|<=1/(exp(Re w)-1)<=1/Re w gives

    |B_(P,chi)(x)|<=x^b/(P-1)+x^b/P<=3x^b/P
                                      <<_b X^(b-1).   (R21)

Both branches are therefore paid over the ENTIRE physical shell, even
where the residual imaginary part vanishes. No estimate uniform in a
growing character is needed for (R21). For fixed q, all sufficiently
large such P are unramified. This statement is for any chosen P comparable
to X; selecting one per dyadic shell changes only the exact auxiliary
representation, not the global source used in the Mellin return.

For gamma>=b-1, the every-epsilon complete L1 hypothesis for V_b is
equivalent to that for the coherent G_(P,chi); the same is true of the
L2-energy hypotheses by the triangle inequality for their square-root
norms. Constants require a fixed lower bound for P/X. Equality at
gamma=b-1 is allowed in the every-epsilon formulation. At b=3/2 all
three targets in Section 3 have gamma>1/2, so the principal and ramified
sectors are fully paid. The remaining bank has only nonprincipal psi,
and for (P,q)=1 its products chi psi are also nonprincipal.

This is a restricted payment and an exact remaining target, not a bound
for that bank. A further triangle inequality over its P-2 terms generally
loses the coherent signs and may cost sqrt(P) in Gauss weights. The
source-relative fixed-character endpoint alone supplies no uniform
growing-family substitute. The useful task is the WHOLE signed bank norm
with the common w_P(x), retaining every x in the shell.
title: A paid whole-shell nonprincipal-bank reduction

## Other first tests and scope boundaries

Card26 correctly prices the unordered integer fiber in the full free-word lift. An integer with k distinct prime factors has k! word representatives, all with the same arithmetic phase. The evaluation norm sqrt(k!) cancels the minimum lift norm1/sqrt(k!). The complete weighted version is the existing G117 fiber Cauchy floor, not a new cancellation theorem. It does not prohibit beneficial correlations between different integers.

Card16 correctly applies inertia only under invertible congruence of the principal signed form. Cancelling positive/negative planes leaves the unproved imbalance |M|. A complex-character matrix cannot be treated as that same Hermitian signature. Its standard Hermitian dilation has signature0 regardless of the original trace: the actual q=3,N=5 example has coefficient matrix I_3, trace3, but balanced dilation signature. A separate weighted readout would need its full cost.

Card20's formal second-order cutoff polymer calculation is correct:

    log Z_X(z)=sum_p z_p - (1/2)sum_p z_p^2
               -sum_(p<r,pr>X) z_p z_r + terms of degree>=3.

Repeated powers here are cumulants, not new squareful Mobius coefficients. The restricted high-prime clique has Z=1+sum z_p. At principal activity z_p=-t it is1-rt, whose logarithmic expansion has radius1/r. Already X=5 with primes3,5 gives a zero at t=1/2. The number of primes in (sqrt X,X] is unbounded along a sequence: a uniform bound would imply pi(X)=O(loglog X) and convergence of the reciprocal-prime sum. This defeats the naive absolute cluster expansion at t=1, not every resummation or the complete field.

The exact large-prime repair is

    M_chi(X)=sum_(n<=X,P+(n)<=sqrt X) mu(n)chi(n)
             -sum_(sqrt X<p<=X) chi(p)M_chi(X/p).

Every n<=X has at most one such prime; its cofactor is below sqrt X and automatically coprime to p. Both complete signed sectors remain. This is the retained largest-prime/renewal mechanism, not an unpaid new bridge.

statement:
## 6. Exact gain and a proved obstruction to a tempting iteration

For \(H_G=D^{1-\delta}\), \(0\le\delta\le1/100\), NP1 gives
\[
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{np}}(D,H_G;W)
\ll D^{\,1-\delta/6+\epsilon}\|W\|_{C^J}^2
=H_G D^{\,5\delta/6+\epsilon}\|W\|_{C^J}^2 .
\tag{NP18}
\]
Positive enlargement using UM gives \(D^{1+\epsilon}\) in this interval. Thus the gain is \(D^{-\delta/6}\), exactly \(D^{-1/600}\) at the short endpoint; the unpaid factor is \(D^{5\delta/6}\), exactly \(D^{1/120}\) there. At \(H_G\ge D\), NP1 already has the requested size \(H_GD^\epsilon\).

To justify the following iteration with actual rowwise scales, repeat NP10–NP16 with column scale \(E\le D\), retaining D as the ambient parameter in NP4. All row radii remain \(R\le D^B\). Apply log-scale Sobolev to this uniform bound, using W and \(\Lambda W=-W/2-xW'\) and treating bounded scales directly. The extra logarithms are absorbed into the arbitrary loss. Hence, for every fixed B and \(\eta>0\), one finite \(J'\) gives
\[
\sum_{0<q_u\le R}\sup_{0<F\le D}|M_u(F;W)|^2
\ll (2DR)^\eta
\bigl(R+R^{1/6}D^{5/6}\bigr)\|W\|_{C^{J'}(I)}^2,
\qquad 1\le R\le D^B.
\tag{R2}
\]
The same holds on the nonprincipal family. Apply R2 with \(R=UP^6\), for \(P\ge1\) in a fixed polynomial range, to the forward reconstruction. After division by the amplifier count, the two terms are \(UP^5\) and \(U^{1/6}D^{5/6}\), up to arbitrary small losses. Every finite repetition of this particular positive comparison preserves the latter exponent. In particular, the following calculation does not exchange a rowwise supremum and a row sum without an estimate.

The new bound does not improve the inherited sixth-power-free exponent \(e(r)=\max\{1,(1+5r)/6\}\) used in the existing zero-free certificate. This is not merely because no reoptimization was attempted. Iterating the same sixth-power amplification with the new all-row bound provably leaves its second term unchanged. Indeed, if a core ball has radius U and the amplifier radius is P, its image lies in radius \(UP^6\). Division by the amplifier count converts the new two-term bound into
\[
\frac1P\left(UP^6+(UP^6)^{1/6}D^{5/6}\right)
=UP^5+U^{1/6}D^{5/6}.
\tag{NP19}
\]
The second term is independent of P, and the first cannot decrease for \(P\ge1\). Logarithms and the allowed small losses do not change this exponent calculation. Every finite repetition of this exact positive comparison within fixed polynomial ranges stalls at the same \(1/6\) row exponent. This falsifies the proposed shortcut “bootstrap the improved all-row estimate through the same amplification to obtain GS22.” It is not a lower bound for the actual energy.

Two related shortcuts also fail at the actual coefficient level:

- Primitive induction alone does not permit \(M_{v\alpha^6}=M_v\). At a good prime \(p\mid\mathfrak a\), \(p\nmid v\), the original column coefficient \(-\psi_v(p)\) is deleted on the left. NP9 keeps this difference.
- The inverse deletion is not a sum only over \(d\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak a\). At a single prime, replacing the full geometric inverse by \(1+\psi_v(p)x\) leaves
  \[
  (1-\psi_v(p)x)(1+\psi_v(p)x)=1-\psi_v(p)^2x^2,
  \tag{NP20}
  \]
  with an erroneous nonzero \(p^2\)-coefficient when \(\psi_v(p)\ne0\). The full prime-power sum in NP10 is essential even though the original Möbius columns are squarefree.

To close GS22 at its short endpoint, further work must save \(D^{1/120}\) beyond NP18 while retaining the exact Möbius/deletion structure. The proof identifies the missing information: UM bounds the complete amplified row ball, whereas the image of the injective sixth-power map occupies only its specified core/root families. The present positive comparison supplies no additional energy saving for that image. A new estimate there, or signed cancellation before the amplifier Cauchy step, is needed. No such estimate is claimed in this packet.
title: 6. Exact gain and a proved obstruction to a tempting iteration

## D02. Rank-one determinant detector: an exact attempted bridge that fails to weaken the input

Take a finite actual Gaussian coefficient list, either capped G13
with its prescribed error G20 or the full f3 coefficients truncated
only AFTER paying the absolute Gaussian tail. Let M be its native
physical Gram, c the COMPLETE signed coefficient column (complex
twists use conjugate transpose). The original energy is E=c*Mc.
M is positive definite for distinct n: a finite linear combination
of Gaussian translates vanishing on a real interval is an entire
combination vanishing identically, and its distinct exponential
frequencies are linearly independent by the Vandermonde derivative
matrix. Thus its determinant is positive; it may be ill conditioned.

The naive rank-one detector has, for lambda>=0,

    det(M+lambda cc*)/det(M)=1+lambda c*M^-1c.          (D02.1)

It measures the DUAL source norm, not E. D48.1's actual consecutive
columns show an inverse-Gram cost of order X^2 on the cheap innovation
direction; its primal-to-dual ratio is order X^4. In general M=diag(epsilon,1),
c=(1,0) gives E=epsilon but c*M^-1c=1/epsilon.
This is an exact normalization failure, not an H counterexample.

To preserve the original scalar one must instead take v=Mc:

    det(M+lambda vv*)/det(M)=1+lambda c*Mc.             (D02.2)

Proof: det(M+lambda vv*)=det(M)det(I+lambda M^-1v v*),
and the last determinant is1+lambda v*M^-1v. With v=Mc
this is E. Every signed coefficient and every cross term is now
inside v, so no local determinant algebra pays the arithmetic.

For an infinite field the same construction is the finite-rank
operator I+lambda |F><F| on its shell Hilbert space, whose only
nontrivial eigenvalue is1+lambda||F||^2. Its determinant is therefore
the SAME complete moment. It is not an independently cheap detector.

Complete conditional return, with all finite leakage, fixing lambda=1:
choose physical truncation n<=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)) after exact f3
coefficients, C large fixed, so the Gaussian absolute tail is
X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). For finite G13 use its existing G20 bound
instead, not the f3 coefficient list. Choose C so tail exponent is
strictly below desired gamma; norm triangle returns to the respective
fixed source. A bound for the corrected determinant ratio minus1
by X^(2gamma+epsilon) is then equivalent to that complete finite
source energy. For f3 the fixed convolution and D48.5 give ordinary-
character zero exclusion at gamma>.5. The prospective near gamma
.8748,5/6,3/4 each has room for C, but the determinant estimate is
literally OPEN-F3 in new notation. No weaker necessary input found.

Strongest objection resolved: M may become nearly singular. D02.2
is algebraically correct without a condition-number hypothesis but
requires the exact Mc. Approximating Mc incurs inverse amplification
and must be source-readout priced. A small det(M) is not a certificate
of a small source energy; arbitrary matrix rank compression loses
the vector that matters.

Ancestry: U-DETERMINANT, F08/F26 resolvents, W38 actual-law determinant
failure, [restricted research revision] reciprocal Hankel face-energy equivalence, and [restricted research revision] native
spectral core. This is a useful scoped failure/test, not an asserted
new determinant architecture or independent research gain. Next action
would need an actual signed determinant estimate that exploits Mc
more effectively than the Gram; none is supplied. Stop the naive
cc* proposal rather than launch another generic determinant calculation.

### 3.2 An exact prime-graph storage identity, including the harmonic part

Here is a concrete alternative that uses the long multiplicative edges rather than a short additive metric. Let S={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}. Use all edges n--np with p not dividing nq and np<=N, with arbitrary positive weights w_e. This graph is connected through divisors to 1. Let L be its ordinary weighted graph Laplacian and U=diag(a_n) on S. Then |a_n|=1, and

    L_a=U L U*,
    x*L_a x=sum_(n--np) w_e |x_(np)+chi(p)x_n|^2,
    L_a a=0.                                                (12)

Every edge relation is the literal arithmetic one. Squareful and nonunit vertices contribute zero to the original output and are not assigned artificial inverse equations here. The complete graph and all its retained endpoints are specified.

For lambda>0 and eta>0 define the anchored storage

    H=lambda L_a+eta e_1 e_1*.

It is positive definite, and its actual source energy is exactly a*Ha=eta. A successful global majorant H>=ell ell* would therefore prove |M_chi(N)|^2<=eta. Its full criterion, however, is

    H>=ell ell*  iff  |M_chi(N)|^2/eta+E_N/lambda <=1,
    E_N=f_R* (L_RR)^-1 f_R,  f=U*ell, R=S minus {1}.        (13)

E_N>=0 includes the entire signed Green contraction. For N=1 it is zero. To prove (13), use the rank-one criterion ell*H^-1ell<=1 and conjugate by U. Solve (lambda L+eta e_1e_1*)x=f. Summing all coordinates gives x_1=(sum f)/eta. Writing x=x_1 ell+y with y_1=0 gives y_R=(L_RR)^-1 f_R/lambda. Consequently

    f*x=|sum f|^2/eta+f_R*(L_RR)^-1 f_R/lambda,

and sum f=conjugate(M_chi(N)). No off-diagonal Green terms or zero mode have been removed.

If M!=0, feasibility requires lambda>E_N and

    eta >= |M_chi(N)|^2/(1-E_N/lambda).                      (14)

If M=0, lambda>=E_N suffices for any eta>0, with equality allowed. If lambda<E_N no eta works. These edge cases prevent treating the complementary Green cost as a free or strictly contractive term.

A graph gap may help bound E_N. It cannot remove the first term of (13): the actual arithmetic vector is exactly the harmonic state. This supplies a sharp finite version of the older G74 harmonic-mode warning, now with the literal squarefree ordinary-character graph, an explicit positive complement and arbitrary edge weights. It is a legitimate high-ceiling architecture only if a noncircular method proves the complete majorant at eta<<N^(2gamma+epsilon). The formula does not provide that method. It is not a claim that all prime graphs, indefinite storage or source-restricted observers fail.

For gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 the necessary complete storage exponents are respectively 1.7496,5/3,3/2 (allow every epsilon). Mere boundedness of (I+T)^-1, a graph gap, vanishing edge defects or finite numerical feasibility does not establish any of these targets. The next mathematical action is to estimate nonlocal signed observation structure, or a proved reachable-state class that avoids the global majorant, while retaining the full Green/harmonic reconstruction.

statement:
## 4. An explicit cofactor and its nontriviality

Expanding D1 at its upper-left entry gives exactly

    D_delta(s)=C_delta(s)F(s)+E_delta(s),
    C_delta(s)=F(s+2delta)F(s+4delta)-F(s+3delta)^2,
    E_delta(s)=-F(s+delta)^2F(s+4delta)
                +2F(s+delta)F(s+2delta)F(s+3delta)
                -F(s+2delta)^3.                           (D7)

The chi subscript is understood throughout D7. Every sign and all three complementary terms are retained. This is a determinant of Mellin-side reciprocal entries, not the determinant of three physical Gaussian fields.

For a point rho with Re rho>4/5 and delta in I, all shifted entries in C_delta and E_delta lie in Re s>1. They are therefore holomorphic at rho. The coefficient of any pole of F at rho is exactly C_delta(rho), with the same pole order whenever that coefficient is nonzero.

There is a second Cauchy--Binet formula:

    C_delta(s)=sum_(m<n) mu(m)mu(n)chi(mn)
       (mn)^(-s-2delta)(m^(-delta)-n^(-delta))^2.           (D8)

Let p be the least prime not dividing the specified modulus of the ordinary character (equivalently the least integer n>1 with a_chi(n) nonzero). Along real delta tending to infinity, the unique first term is

    -chi(p)p^(-rho-2delta)(1-p^(-delta))^2.

The ratio of the remaining absolute sum to its magnitude tends to zero. For the m=1 terms use the tail sum over n>=p+1, whose ratio is bounded by a constant times

    (p/(p+1))^(2delta) [1+(p+1)/(Re rho+2delta-1)].

For m>=p, use (m^(-delta)-n^(-delta))^2<=m^(-2delta) and sum

    sum_(m>=p) m^(-Re rho-4delta)
               sum_(n>m) n^(-Re rho-2delta).

After division by p^(-Re rho-2delta), this also tends to zero by an integral comparison. Constants here may depend on the fixed p and rho; no quantitative height assertion is extracted from this asymptotic.

Thus delta -> C_delta(rho) is a nonzero analytic function on the connected half-plane in delta where all its displayed reciprocal arguments have real part >1. It has only isolated real zeros in I. This proves the exact nonvanishing property needed below. We do not assume a uniform lower bound for |C_delta(rho)| on I.

For an imprimitive character, p means the least prime not dividing the specified modulus, so its natural Euler zeros are respected. The distinction from a primitive conductor does not change the argument; the coefficient definition a_chi is authoritative.

statement:
## 1. Exact replacement source: squarefree divisor incidence

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a positive integer q, with its natural zero extension.
For real X>=1 use the literal finite downset

    D_X={n<=X: n squarefree, (n,q)=1}.

It is closed under positive divisors. Order it increasingly, put N=|D_X|, and let e
be the coordinate of1 and v=1-e. Define upper triangular matrices

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d) 1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d) 1_(n/d is prime), d,n in D_X,
    P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.                                      (1)

No zero character value is divided: excluded nonunits and nonsquarefree integers
already have mu(n)chi(n)=0. Matrix products preserve the original product-size
cutoff because every intermediate divisor of n belongs to D_X.

If j=omega(n/d), every path of j prime covers from d to n is a permutation of the
j distinct prime factors, and its character weight telescopes to chi(n/d).
Consequently

    B^k(d,n)=k! chi(n/d) 1_(d|n, omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z, exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).            (2)

All exponentials are finite polynomials. This removes the factorial path cost
EXACTLY through1/k!, before any estimate; it does not create a contractive norm.
The determinant lemma, det Z=1 and(2) give

    det R=1+e^T Z^(-1)v=sum_(n<=X)mu(n)chi(n)=M_chi(X).       (3)

This is the character-twisted squarefree version of Wilf's finite-poset identity.
The downset restriction changes the ambient matrix, but not this scalar arithmetic
source. No old nonlinear/Hecke source is silently substituted into a prior theorem.

Let K=max_(n in D_X)omega(n). For X with K>=1, P^(K+1)=0, and

    A_k(X)=e^T P^k v
          =sum_(n in D_X,n>1)chi(n) k! S(omega(n),k),
    det(lambda I-R)=y^(N-K-1)
         [y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k(X)y^(K-k)], y=lambda-1.    (4)

Here S(j,k) is the Stirling number of the second kind. Indeed a strict divisor
chain is an ordered partition into k nonempty blocks of the distinct prime
factors. The resolvent determinant identity gives(4) first at y!=0 and then as a
polynomial identity. At least N-K-1 eigenvalues are1; it is not asserted that this
multiplicity is exact when a twisted leading coefficient cancels. At y=-1, all
chain depths together give the original mu sign. X below the first unramified
prime is the trivial one-dimensional case R=(1).

Since an integer with j distinct prime factors is at least(j+1)!, elementary
Stirling estimates give K=O(log(2X)/loglog(3X)). Small degree alone does not bound
the polynomial at y=-1 or the product of its nontrivial roots.
title: 1. Exact replacement source: squarefree divisor incidence

statement:
## G5 — p<.01, far-gap H phase/projectors, geometry/discrete optimization

### W40-21 — Minimum-frustration forest certificate; p=.009
O: Build the exact ordered H incidence graph, choose a maximum-weight forest, gauge its phases away and pay every non-tree edge by its cycle holonomy.
B: An explicit graph energy identity could bound H by a flat part plus a computable frustration term while both arithmetic projectors remain attached.
T: Compare a triangle, a long cycle and a tree; determine whether large total curvature can yield a spectral saving without graph expansion.
X: Flat tree pieces can carry all mass, and large-girth graphs can have negligible normalized gap.
R: Constructive hard H attack with exact obstruction separating phase information from expansion requirements.

### W40-22 — Complex cone-cover certificate for ordered interactions; p=.007
O: Cover actual H edge phases by narrow cones chosen through a discrete partition; pair cones through exact projector-preserving involutions.
B: Opposed cones with nearly equal weighted masses could cancel before absolute estimates, leaving a provably small unmatched flow.
T: Solve the optimal transport balance for four phase atoms with unequal multiplicities and derive a total-variation residual.
X: Phase coverage does not imply matching masses; involutions may not preserve primes, shifts, gcd or height constraints.
R: Algorithmic certificate whose sole hard input is a full arithmetic imbalance bound.

### W40-23 — Discrete complex Laplacian domination; p=.005
O: Embed H in a magnetic connection Laplacian and seek a signed factorization H = D*D minus an explicitly bounded diagonal, with exact edge projectors.
B: A coercive lower bound for D*D could create the missing cancellation in H without termwise prime estimates.
T: Factor the three-cycle matrix and check the sign of the diagonal correction and both projection orders.
X: Positive Laplacian control often bounds the wrong side of H, or the correction restores the full trivial bound.
R: High-reach structural reformulation; exact sign failure would be a useful stop result.

### W40-24 — Integer cycle-flow cancellation; p=.008
O: Treat signed H incidences as a circulation and decompose balanced integer flows into cycles; attach the actual complex product to each cycle.
B: A bounded residual imbalance plus cancellation around short arithmetic cycles could control the whole signed packet.
T: Exact min-cost circulation on a small ordered multigraph, keeping repeated edges and zero coefficients, then derive the residual identity.
X: Additive complex edge sums do not telescope from multiplicative cycle holonomy; phase/coefficient compatibility is extra.
R: New exact full-return identity if compatibility holds; otherwise a sharp obstruction to graph-only reasoning.

### W40-25 — Determinant-line compatibility of two projectors; p=.003
O: Track the determinant line of the two arithmetic projector images along parameter shifts; use their relative phase as an invariant of otherwise incompatible local representations.
B: A nonzero winding or determinant separation could force an orthogonality defect across all bad profiles.
T: Two rank-one projections moved around a triangle: compute overlap products and show what is gauge-invariant versus norm-informative.
X: Berry phase may be nontrivial while all pairwise overlaps approach one; topological information alone has no power scale.
R: Very high ceiling only with quantitative metric control; likely useful conceptual obstruction.
title: G5 — p<.01, far-gap H phase/projectors, geometry/discrete optimization

## 5. The fixed-order future return and its necessary distinction

For this route retain the author's explicit source-relative input

    M_chi(z)=sum_{n<=z} a(n) <<_chi z^b,  b=7/8<1.       (9)

Abel summation and the derivative version of (3) give

    |F_r(x)| <= exp(C_{chi,tau,b}(r+1)log(r+2))x^b,
    x>=1.                                               (10)

For instance its absolute integral is at most Cx^b integral e^(bv)|phi_r'(v)|dv. Gaussian decay pays both tails and the displayed derivative dependence. Repeated integration by parts now gives, for each fixed positive integer r,

    F(e^u)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity
              e^(-t)t^(r-1)F_r(e^(u+t))dt.                (11)

The boundaries vanish by b<1. This also excludes the homogeneous e^u times polynomial modes annihilated by (1-D)^r; the derivative filter alone does not give an unconditional inverse.

At base scale X choose K=2ceil(L^(1/3)/2) in band I, or K=2ceil(sqrt(L)/(2log L)) in band II. Keep that integer and r=K-1 fixed throughout (11). For 0<=t<=4L, the dyadic shells needed to cover [Xe^t,2Xe^t] have log Z in [L-O(1),5L+O(1)]. In band I the limiting minimum ratio K/(log Z)^(1/3) is 5^(-1/3)>1/2. In band II it is 1/sqrt(5)>2/5. The upper-band margins are also strict. Therefore this one fixed derivative order is admissible on every required future shell.

Assume the complete balanced-source L2(dx/x) bound of exponent gamma+epsilon, uniformly over the specified even orders and sufficiently large dyadic shells, where 1/2<gamma<1. Cover each shifted interval by at most two such shells and use (8) and Minkowski. The portion t<=4L costs at most

    C X^(gamma+epsilon) (1-gamma-epsilon)^(-r)
        =X^(gamma+epsilon+o(1)),                          (12)

for epsilon<1-gamma. The negligible completion errors integrate to a negligible term as well. The tail from (10) is bounded by

    X^b exp(-4(1-b)L+O(Klog L))
        =X^(5b-4+o(1))=X^(3/8+o(1)).                     (13)

To see the stated exponent rather than a weakened tail rate, use the logarithmic derivative (r-1)/t-(1-b) on t>=4L. It is bounded above by -(1-b)+o(1); integrating from the endpoint costs a fixed reciprocal rate, and t^(r-1), Gamma(r) and (10)'s prefactor contribute only exp(O(Klog L)). In both bands Klog L=o(L).

After allocating epsilon buffers, (12)--(13) return the same complete-shell exponent gamma for the original fixed Gaussian. Its small-x tail is O_A(x^A) for every A by bounded coefficients. Cauchy--Schwarz on the complete logarithmic shells makes

    integral_0^infinity F(x)x^(-s)dx/x

holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly on compact subsets. Initially, for Re(s)>1, this is exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi). The Gaussian multiplier is nonzero. Meromorphic continuation therefore excludes all zeros in Re(s)>gamma. The principal pole at 1 is handled by multiplying by s-1 if an everywhere-holomorphic product is desired; nonprincipal s=1 is included. This is an all-height conclusion, not a bounded-height test.

The convenient baseline 7/8 is stronger than needed for this particular four-L tail. With the same proof, any fixed available b<1 satisfying 5b-4<=gamma suffices for an every-epsilon return; the largest such b is (gamma+4)/5. The equality here is harmless because the target already allows every positive epsilon. This is a weaker sufficient growth input within this proof, not an assertion that an arbitrary o(x) bound gives a power tail. One only needs source estimates for the chosen fixed orders on their actual future corridors; the full uniform K-band is a convenient sufficient contract, not a globally minimal hypothesis.

The direct full-X moment route in Section 7 is different: it obtains the desired Mertens bound from the open estimate and therefore removes (9) there. It does not retroactively remove (9) from the dyadic balanced-source argument just proved.
title: 5. The fixed-order future return and its necessary distinction

summation, gives pointwise `F(x)=O_(beta,tau)(X^beta)` and hence the
same bound for its shell norm. It follows from the EXACT identity
T_z=F-R_z and (C3) that

    T_(X^rho)(x)
      =-C_f exp(tau/2)B(rho)x/L^3
             +O(X/L^4+X^(1-kappa)L+X^beta).          ([restricted research revision])

This is not an independent improvement of F. Unlike (C3), (C4) and
([restricted research revision]), this prefix assertion uses that accepted full-field bound.

To expose every ordered interaction, choose the literal disjoint
partition at a=3/8, b=2/5, c=3/5:

    C_0=T_(X^a),
    C_1=T_(X^b)-T_(X^a),
    C_2=T_(X^c)-T_(X^b),
    C_3=R_(X^c).

These are original f(n) coefficients times disjoint 0/1 masks, with
all prime powers. Their sum is EXACTLY F. Define the common field

    V_X(x)=C_f exp(tau/2)x/L^3,
    N_X^2=||V_X||_[X,2X]^2
         =(3/2)C_f^2 exp(tau)X^2/L^6,
    (b_0,b_1,b_2,b_3)
      =(-B(a), B(a)-B(b), B(b), 0).                 ([restricted research revision])

The first two coefficients are positive; the third is negative;
their sum is zero. The new direct arithmetic estimates give C_1,C_2
and the negligible C_3 at these signs, without full F. C_0 uses ([restricted research revision]).
For this fixed partition,

    ||C_i-b_i V_X|| <= C epsilon_X N_X,
    <C_i,C_j>=[b_i b_j+O(epsilon_X)]N_X^2,           ([restricted research revision])
    epsilon_X=L^(-1)+X^(-kappa)L^4+X^(beta-1)L^3.

Every i,j pair, including both ordered mixed directions, is included.
In particular the C_0,C_1 leading cross term is POSITIVE, whereas both
have negative leading cross terms with C_2. There is no positivity
claim about arbitrary depth submasks. The complete covariance is the

For any of the actual coefficient pieces c_i(n), absolute convergence
gives exactly

    <C_i,C_j>=sum_(m,n) c_i(m)c_j(n)K_X(m,n),         ([restricted research revision])

with current-proof G22's ORIGINAL Gaussian kernel. Each own true
diagonal is O_tau(X); cross diagonals between the disjoint pieces
vanish because their coefficient supports are disjoint. In particular,
with the ORIGINAL full true diagonal Delta_all,

    Q_off(X)=sum_(0<=i,j<=3)<C_i,C_j>-Delta_all(X).

No negative off-diagonal term is deleted. For an explicit two-height
readout, fix sigma>1 and put `D_i(s)=sum_n c_i(n)n^(-s)`, with X and
all masks frozen. Absolute convergence gives

    <C_i,C_j>=(2pi)^(-2) integral_R integral_R
      exp(tau(sigma-it_1)^2/2) exp(tau(sigma+it_2)^2/2)
      conjugate(D_i(sigma+it_1)) D_j(sigma+it_2)
      [integral_X^(2X) x^(2sigma+i(t_2-t_1))dx/x]
      dt_1 dt_2.

The two original Gaussian height densities and both heights are
retained over the full real lines. At sigma>1, |D_i|<=zeta(sigma),
so both Gaussian integrals converge absolutely without an unpriced
height truncation. No diagonal-height substitution is used. These
moving masked series are not substituted for the fixed full detector
in the zero-exclusion argument.

For the actual two-part split T_z,R_z, put

    a_X=||T_z||, b_X=||R_z||,
    rho_X=Re<T_z,R_z>/(a_X b_X).

The new source theorem supplies `a_X,b_X` comparable to X/L^3 after

    ||F||^2=(a_X-b_X)^2+2a_X b_X(1+rho_X).           ([restricted research revision])

Therefore a proposed full target `||F||<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)`,
with 1/2<gamma<.87488, is equivalent to BOTH requirements

    |a_X-b_X| <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+rho_X <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^6,       ([restricted research revision])

after renaming epsilon. Necessity follows from the nonnegative terms

identity. If proving sufficiency independently of the baseline, the

statement:
## 4. A full-coefficient prime block in the retained far form

Put \(N=\sqrt{X/W}\). Choose four primes in disjoint intervals:

\[
\begin{array}{ll}
2N\le p_1\le(21/10)N,&(11/5)N\le p_2\le(23/10)N,\\
3N\le p_3\le(31/10)N,&(16/5)N\le p_4\le(33/10)N.
\end{array}
\tag{SF21}
\]

For large \(X\), uniformly in the permitted \(W\), all four
primes exceed \(J\) and are coprime to \(W\). They are distinct.
Require precisely the cofactor conditions in (SF6) with
\(D_i=p_i\). The gcd conditions hold automatically because these
bases have gcd \(1\) and \(H/W,R/W>1\). Let \(\mathcal P_{X,W}\)
denote this set of prime quadruples.

There are

\[
\#\mathcal P_{X,W}\gg \frac{N^4}{L^4}
=\frac{X^2}{W^2L^4}.
\tag{SF22}
\]

For completeness, (SF20) counts \(\gg N^4/(\log N)^4\)
quadruples before exclusions. Fix one cross edge \(ij\), divisors
\(\alpha,\beta\mid W\), and \(r,s\le J\). After fixing
\(D_i\) and the two other variables, the condition
\(|r\alpha D_i-s\beta D_j|\le\Delta\) permits at most
\(2\Delta+1\) integer choices for \(D_j\), since \(s\beta\ge1\).
Counting *all integers*, not only primes, bounds the excluded union by

\[
O\!\left(J^2\tau(W)^2N^3(\Delta+1)\right).
\tag{SF23}
\]

Its ratio to the prime main term is

\[
\ll \frac{J^2\tau(W)^2L^4(\Delta+1)}N
\ll X^{-63/500}L^{69/4}=o(1),
\tag{SF24}
\]

uniformly in \(W\), using \(\tau(W)\le W\le\sqrt L\) and
\(N\ge\sqrt X/L^{1/4}\). This proves (SF22) with every original
short rational-cofactor exclusion retained, including the expanded
selected-prime allocation multipliers.

For a quadruple in \(\mathcal P_{X,W}\), set

\[
n=Wp_1p_2,\qquad n'=Wp_3p_4.
\tag{SF25}
\]

These integers are globally squarefree. Their ranges are

\[
\frac{22}5X\le n\le\frac{483}{100}X,
\qquad
\frac{48}5X\le n'\le\frac{1023}{100}X,
\qquad n'-n\ge\frac{477}{100}X>P_{\rm gap}.
\tag{SF26}
\]

**Complete coefficient claim.** Every factorization contributing to
\(C_{X,W}(n,n')\) is accounted for by the selected-prime allocations
below, and

\[
C_{X,W}(Wp_1p_2,Wp_3p_4)=4.
\tag{SF27}
\]

To prove this, consider any \(\ell de=Wp_1p_2\) in (SF11).
Since \(\ell\le J<\min(p_1,p_2)\), neither large prime can divide
\(\ell\). Since \(d,e>Y>W\), neither long factor can consist
only of primes dividing \(W\). Thus each long factor contains
exactly one of \(p_1,p_2\). The *only* possibilities are

\[
(d,e,\ell)=\left(up_1,vp_2,\frac{W}{uv}\right)
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
\left(up_2,vp_1,\frac{W}{uv}\right),
\qquad uv\mid W.
\tag{SF28}
\]

Here \(u,v\) are positive integers; \(uv\mid W\) entails
\((u,v)=1\). Conversely every displayed allocation occurs.
Indeed
\(\min(d,e)\ge2N>Y\) and \(\ell\le W\le J\).
Furthermore

\[
de\ge p_1p_2\ge\frac{22X}{5W}>2T_l,
\qquad de\le Wp_1p_2\le\frac{483}{100}X<T_u.
\tag{SF29}
\]

So \(w_X(de)=1\), with neither cutoff transition involved.
The same statements hold on the right, where the upper bound is
\((1023/100)X<T_u\). They hold uniformly because
\(W\le\sqrt L\) and \(L\longrightarrow\infty\).

Changing an allocation leaves the \(W\)-free bases unchanged.
Interchanging \(p_1,p_2\), or \(p_3,p_4\), also leaves the value

set of four cross conditions in (SF6) are preserved. Hence

For each orientation, the exact sum of the left Möbius signs is

\[
\sum_{uv\mid W}\mu(up_1)\mu(vp_2)
=\mu(p_1)\mu(p_2)\prod_{p\mid W}(1-1-1)
=\mu(W).
\tag{SF30}
\]

There are two distinct orientations. The full coefficient on each
side is therefore \(2\mu(W)\), proving (SF27). In particular,
this is the coefficient of the *entire* completed-product pair,
not the contribution of a subset of its factorizations. Selected

The lower long-factor endpoints and the upper third-factor endpoint

statement:
## 2. Integrated logarithmic Hankel criterion: accept the full conditional bridge

For a fixed ordinary character set M(x)=sum_(n<=x) mu(n)chi(n), with M(x)=0 below one. For 0<a<1 put h_a(v)=exp(-av)M(exp(v)) for v>=0. The full truncated Hankel operator on L2(0,L) has kernel h_a(t+u). No positive diagonal replacement or omission of off-diagonal rectangles is allowed. For complex chi use the bilinear form B(f,g)=integral h_a(t+u)f(t)g(u)dtdu; its norm is the same as the usual sesquilinear operator norm by conjugating one test input. The arithmetic chi is not conjugated or doubled.

If K_a(L)=||Gamma_(a,L)|| is bounded uniformly in L, the forms extend by density to a bounded bilinear form on L2(0,infinity). For Re(z)>0, E_z(t)=exp(-zt) is a holomorphic L2 vector with squared norm 1/(2Re(z)). Hence Q(z)=B(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic and |Q(z)|<=K/(2Re(z)). Initially s=a+z with Re(s)>1 permits Fubini and differentiation:

    Q(z) = integral_0^infinity v M(exp(v)) exp(-sv) dv
         = -d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))].

A zero of L at rho with Re(rho)>a creates a pole of this derivative; rho is nonzero since a>0. The holomorphic Q cannot have it. The principal pole instead makes 1/L vanish, so creates no false obstruction. The identity theorem for meromorphic functions supplies every finite height. A countable a-sequence decreasing to a common gamma is sufficient for a complete gamma return; uniform constants in a or in growing q are not asserted.

The pole-mode test is correct: for a single kernel R exp(lambda(t+u)), the singular value is |R| integral_0^L exp(2Re(lambda)t)dt. A critical mode Re(lambda)=0 grows linearly; an unstable mode grows exponentially. This identifies a model obstruction, not a license to split an infinite arithmetic spectrum or discard selected modes without paying their complete complement.

The exact Hilbert-Schmidt square is

    integral_0^(2L) w_L(v) exp(-2av) |M(exp(v))|^2 dv,
    w_L(v)=v (v<=L), and 2L-v (L<=v<=2L).

This positive estimate would recover the familiar full logarithmic energy difficulty. The function h(v)=exp(iv^2) provides a legitimate **nonarithmetic** separation: its truncated operator norm is at most sqrt(pi) by extension, Fourier transform at frequency 2t and Plancherel, whereas its Hilbert-Schmidt norm is L. Thus operator and HS targets need not agree as functional bounds. This does not construct arithmetic cancellation for mu(n)chi(n).

The strongest potentially missing step, rectangular blocks away from the diagonal, is paid. For I_j=[j,j+1), the I_i by I_j block is unitarily transported by opposite translations of its two coordinates to the square on [(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1). Those translations preserve t+u. Therefore its norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1). At a heavier weight sigma>a, the two multipliers cost at most exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)). If

    K_a(L) <= C exp(2 eta L),       eta>=0,

then the complete sum of block norms is at most

    C exp(2 eta) [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2)

whenever sigma>a+eta. This includes every off-diagonal rectangle and proves boundedness of the heavier-weight infinite Hankel form. Thus the all-L/every-epsilon hypothesis

    K_a(L) <<_(chi,epsilon) exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L),
    0<a<=gamma<1,

returns all ordinary-character zero exclusion Re(s)>gamma. Given sigma>gamma, take epsilon<sigma-gamma before summation. The baseline |M(x)|<=x gives only exponent 2(1-a), so supplies no improvement. At a=1/2, a first c11 gain needs K growth exponent strictly below .7497080728; the 1/6 and 1/4 targets would be 2/3 and 1/2. None is proved here.

The partial-work distribution identity also survives: extending h by zero to v<0 gives (partial_v+a)h_a=sum_n mu(n)chi(n)n^(-a) delta_(log n), including the atom n=1. For compactly supported smooth f,g in (0,infinity), pairing with f*g gives a B(f,g)-B(f',g); the convolution derivative identity has no f(0) endpoint. This produces an H1 by L2 test bound from the accepted Hankel bound, not an unproved converse or a transfer to native H.

Retain the integrated kernel and balanced-block adapter as a useful source-specific interface. General Hankel/observability, old W29 source dictionaries, W50 energy, W54 complete prediction and the existing reciprocal-return library remain substantial ancestry. The claim is not a new general Hankel method or an achieved arithmetic bound.

Fix tau>0. Write

    g_tau(u)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)),
    f(n)=f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))),
    omega_z(n)=#{p>z:p divides n},
    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1) f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).       (F1)

The count is of DISTINCT primes. All their powers remain. Put

    L=log X, ell=log x, t=log z,
    P(z)=product_(5<=p<=z) (p-2)/(p-1),
    h_z=3 log(2)P(z)>0,
    D_z=-3 log(2)-log(3)
           +2 sum_(5<=p<=z) p log(p)/((p-1)(p-2)).       (F2)

The following assertions hold uniformly for the CLOSED shell X<=x<=2X and

    4 <= t <= L/(1000 log L).                           (F3)

All constants are independent of z,x,X. They can depend on the fixed tau and on fixed classical PNT constants. For all sufficiently large X,

    T_z(x)=h_z exp(tau/2) x/ell^2
            *[1-(2 tau+D_z)/ell+O_tau(t^2/L^2)].        (F4)

In particular,

    T_z(x)=3 log(2) exp(tau/2) P(z) x/(log x)^2
                      *[1+O_tau(t/L)].                (F5)

Here D_z=2t+O(1). For z=(log X)^B, with fixed B>0, one has t=B log L, eventually inside F3. Thus the candidate's POSITIVE main term is correct, with relative error O_(tau,B)(loglog X/log X). Its proposed coarser remainder also suffices at this fixed-B scope. The second term and F3 are separately proved reviewer extensions, not claims in the frozen candidate.

The upper range is z=exp(L/(1000 log L)), still subpower in X. At that endpoint the leading field has size comparable to X loglog X/(log X)^3. It still has exponent one. Nothing in this proof reaches a fixed power z=X^rho, rho>0.

Split integers into p-adic valuations before estimating. Their exact
local signs give F_r=U-V and F_(rp)=U+V, hence the energy difference is
4 integral U V. The V-square cancels. The p-deleted U has convolution
factor (1-z)^(-1) at p, with a uniformly bounded absolute beta norm.
Summing all positive p powers therefore gives p^(-beta), including the
complete power tail. Telescoping switches proves S19.

The decisive remaining sum is

    sum_r r^(-2beta+delta) sum_(p|r,p>P)p^(-beta)
      = zeta(2beta-delta) sum_(p>P)p^(-3beta+delta).

It converges for sufficiently small fixed delta and pays exactly the
P^(1-3beta+delta) error. S22 has the correct diagonal subtraction and
retains the signed high-gcd scalar. In S23, P>=D forces every g<D
dividing st to divide its P-smooth part s. This proves the factorization

## 4. Actual squarefree-unit diagonal and floor

For the literal coefficients, |a_n|^2=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1). Using
mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) gives

    A_q(y):=sum_(n<=y)|a_n|^2=d_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.               (R6)

For each d<=sqrt y with (d,q)=1 the remaining count is
(phi(q)/q)y/d^2+O_q(1); the total counting error and the omitted absolutely
convergent Euler-product tail are O_q(sqrt y). This proves (R6) equally
for principal, nonprincipal and imprimitive fixed characters.

Stieltjes partial summation against exp(-2t/(Nu^b)), uniformly in 1<=u<=2,
therefore yields

    D_all(X)=C_(q,b)N+O_(q,b)(sqrt N),
    C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b).

Deleting n<=M costs O(M), so (R5) proves exactly the author's

    E(X)=E_<=X^(19/16)(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)
                                  +O_q(X^(5/4)log X).   (R7)

The tail alone has that main term and error as well. Positivity of the
remaining core in (R7) NOW proves
E(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2). Thus a full every-epsilon L2 premise with
gamma<3/4 is impossible for this fixed source: choose epsilon strictly
below 3/2-2gamma. Gamma=3/4 is not ruled out. There is no corresponding
L1 impossibility proved here, and no assertion about other sources.

**Independent refinement: retain the diagonal cutoff explicitly.** For
any real M>=2, define the positive quantity

    Q_(q,b)(X,M)=(d_q N/2) integral_1^2
                    u^(b-1) exp(-2M/(Nu^b))du.           (R8)

Then, uniformly in M,

    D_>M(X)=Q_(q,b)(X,M)+O_(q,b)(sqrt N).                 (R9)

To prove this, integrate (R6) on the open interval (M,infinity). The
boundary error is O_q(sqrt M exp(-lambda M)) and the integral error is
O_q(lambda integral_M^infinity sqrt t exp(-lambda t)dt), where
lambda=2/(Nu^b). Each is O_q(lambda^(-1/2))=O_(q,b)(sqrt N).
The continuous main term is d_q exp(-lambda M)/lambda. This also handles
integral M, because A_q(M) includes that atom and the tail excludes it.

Combining with (R5) gives the sharper, explicit complete identity

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+Q_(q,b)(X,M)
                   +O_(q,b,k)(X^(b/2)+X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)). (R10)

The same formula without E_<=M holds for the tail's own squared norm.
For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(4/3), the cross exponent is2/3, below3/4, hence

    E(X)=E_<=X^(4/3)(X)+Q_(q,3/2)(X,X^(4/3))+O_q(X^(3/4)),
    E_>X^(4/3)(X)=Q_(q,3/2)(X,X^(4/3))+O_q(X^(3/4)).     (R11)

No logarithm remains in this particular error because X^(2/3)log X is
O(X^(3/4)). Q/N tends to C_(q,3/2), but replacing Q by C N prematurely
would lose its explicit cutoff correction of order X^(4/3). This is an
actual arithmetic tail theorem, not an estimate of the hard transition
core or a better zero-free constant.

    T_(chi,c,X)(x)=sum_(X^gamma<n<=X^r) mu(n)chi(n)
                                exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6).

Both cutoffs are fixed from the original shell X, BEFORE x varies over
[X,2X]. The lower complement has squared norm at most (log2)X^(2gamma).
Equation (6) pays every term involving n>M by
O(X^(2gamma)log X), and the diagonal X^(3/2) is within budget because
gamma>=3/4. Consequently the SINGLE estimate

    for every epsilon>0, every sufficiently large dyadic X,
    integral_X^(2X)|T_(chi,c,X)(x)|^2 dx/x
                       <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(2-2c+epsilon) (CORE_c)

is sufficient for zero exclusion Re(s)>1-c, including the full
complement, physical damping, sharp cutoffs, natural zeros, principal
pole, imprimitive Euler factors and every finite height. A common c must
be fixed for all ordinary chi before the character-dependent constants
and onsets. This is a finite-band version of THIS detector input, not a
conductor-family average or a claim about an easier Mertens problem.

More precisely, for these fixed c the whole energy bound (4) and CORE_c
are equivalent at the every-epsilon level. In the forward direction use
(7), the lower complement and the norm triangle inequality. In the
reverse direction (6) and D_>M>=0 give E_<=M<=E+O(X^(2gamma)log X),
then subtract the already paid lower complement. No tail diagonal is
discarded on the reverse implication. This equivalence is useful because
(6) is a proved, nontrivial complement estimate; it supplies no saving
inside CORE_c.

| conditional c | gamma | upper core exponent r | complete energy target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 313/2500=.1252 | 2187/2500=.8748 | 5313/5000=1.0626 | 2187/1250=1.7496 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 5/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/2 |

The near target would exceed c11 by exactly 135091/2500000000.
These are CONDITIONAL implications only. The known estimate (14) has
power exponent 2 and does not meet any row. A deliberately coarse bound
already established here therefore FAILS the first-gain test by a power
gap 2* c11=.2502919272, before even asking for a positive improvement.

**Weaker complete target.** The minimum norm premise developed here is
actually L1, not L2. Applying the proof of (6) only to n,m>M gives

    integral_X^(2X)|W_>M(x)|^2 dx/x
                  << X^(3/2)+X^(2gamma)log X.

Thus its whole-shell L1 norm is O(X^gamma sqrt(log X)) for the targets
above. Together with the absolute lower-cutoff cost, this proves that

    integral_X^(2X)|T_(chi,c,X)(x)| dx/x
                         <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(1-c+epsilon) (CORE1_c)

is itself a COMPLETE sufficient input, and is equivalent, at every-epsilon
level, to the whole W shell L1 input. Both directions use only the triangle
inequality and the already proved complement estimates. CORE_c implies
CORE1_c, but the converse is neither assumed nor asserted. For the near
target CORE1 requires exponent .8748; the 1/6 and 1/4 targets require 5/6
and 3/4. From (14) we do obtain the actual arithmetic bound

    integral_X^(2X)|W_chi(x)|dx/x
                          <<_(q,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D)

for every fixed D, after replacing D in (14) by 2D. This still fails the
first-gain power threshold by c11=.1251459636. No pointwise estimate or
energy floor is being substituted for the weaker L1 target.

There is no claim that this source is the only possible detector or that
its CORE target is necessary for zero exclusion itself. The old linear
Gauss-bank identity cannot simply be transplanted: its Fourier weights
and paid principal branch belong to exp(-i n/x), not to exp(-i(n/x)^6).
The new proof instead starts from the literal coefficients and constructs
its own Mellin bridge. No old Type I/II, Gao local-moment descendant,
joint-label estimate or high-conductor bound is invoked beyond scope.

statement:
## 6. Tests 17 and 22: native coefficients, signs and scoped failures

The exact JN7 transform has unitary factor (1/Q), (Q=q_\pi q_{\pi'}), on a group of size Q²:
\[
 \widehat W(h,s,s')={1\over Q}\sum_{R,P,P'}W(R,P,P')
 e(-Rh/(\pi\pi')-Ps/\pi+P's'/\pi'). \tag{R14}
\]
The plus sign in the second mark is conjugation. JN9's kernel is
\[
 K(h,s,s')=\chi_\pi(h)^3\chi_{\pi'}(h)^3
                 \chi_\pi(s)^2\chi_{\pi'}(s')^4. \tag{R15}
\]
The reciprocity phase ζπ,π′, both long-prime coefficients and the entire short-core sum remain attached. There is no additional Q factor. Both complete projectors precede or are fully recombined after this transform; equal-rational-norm pairs remain deleted. The common-unit Jacobi mean is subtracted with its existing paid cost, not asserted zero.

For the **particular unit/nonunit syndrome** in test17, its unit fiber has size ((q_\pi-1)^2(q_{\pi'}-1)^2). On it |K|=1 and K has mean zero, because the nontrivial cubic mark character averages to zero. Its conditional variance is therefore exactly 1. Already in the norm7 field, s=1 and s=3 have the same unit code but different cubic phase. Ramified zeros occur outside the proper unit fiber, not as omitted side conditions. The norm7/norm13 author count has all six exponents equally frequent (864 each); the mathematical mean-zero proof, not that finite count, establishes the stated scope.

The remaining pairing with the actual \(\widehat W\) is a full covariance. Cauchy's cost is \(\sqrt{|\mathcal U|}\,\|1_{\mathcal U}(\widehat W-\overline W_{\mathcal U})\|_2\). A richer code that includes K itself transfers the difficulty to the predictable mean. A synthetic \(\widehat W=\overline K\) can saturate Cauchy but need not belong to the native source. Thus there is no original-H lower bound or general coding impossibility.

For test22, the phase in R14 is affine **as a function of the frequency coordinates**, so its frequency Hessian is zero. Its joint dependence on physical and frequency variables is bilinear; no zero joint Hessian is claimed. Adjacent row frequencies are spaced $1/(\pi\pi')$, of modulus $Q^{-1/2}\asymp N^{-1}$; mark frequencies have scale $N^{-1/2}$. An artificial Hamming distance does not force separation of this native phase.

The exact complete source has row support at most (C_{\rm orig}K) modulo ππ′, because its original disk embeds without collisions when Q≫K. After summing every core child and applying both mark transforms, JN12 gives for every row-frequency set E of size J **independent of the mark coordinates**
\[
 \|1_E\widehat{\mathcal W}\|_2^2
 \le {C_{\rm orig}KJ\over Q}\|\widehat{\mathcal W}\|_2^2. \tag{R16}
\]
J≈N captures at most (O(K/N)) of the norm; at the cited box this is (O(Z^{-.003})). Capturing a fixed fraction needs J≳Q/K. This does not apply to an arbitrary adaptive mark-dependent set. It also does not estimate the signed pairing with the omitted frequencies, so it is neither an H bound nor an H lower bound. Both tests are useful native-source obstructions to the proposed shortcuts.

statement:
### Cayley realization, reflected state and residual

For any r>0, even without r>=||T||, set A=[[0,T^*],[T,0]]. Its Cayley transform C_r=(A-irI)(A+irI)^(-1) is unitary because A is self-adjoint. Writing G0=T^*T, D=(G0+r^2I)^(-1), its input-reflection and input-to-output blocks are

    R=(G0-r^2I)D,  J=-2ir T D,
    R=R^*, R^2+J^*J=I, I-R=2r^2D.

The exact returned input is x=(I-R)^(-1)v. Direct substitution gives

    Tv=ir Jx,
    ||Tv||^2=r^2(||x||^2-||Rx||^2)
             =r^2(2Re<x,v>-||v||^2).                          (R13)

The inner product is conjugate-first. Thus global ||T||<=r is equivalent to R<=0. At the actual v, ||Tv||<=r||v|| is equivalent to Re<x,v><=||v||^2. The latter is a sufficient condition for the raw bilinear bound against every w of its allowed mass; it is stronger than controlling one particular scalar pairing. At r=B0>0 it returns the desired raw target exactly. The degenerate B0=0 requires the zero pairing directly.

This is a finite source-preserving identity, not an arithmetic estimate for x. On a singular mode of T with singular value sigma,

    R=(sigma^2-r^2)/(sigma^2+r^2),
    |J|=2r*sigma/(sigma^2+r^2),
    (I-R)^(-1)=(sigma^2+r^2)/(2r^2).

For sigma much larger than r, transmission is small while the inverse grows quadratically. Hence unitary scattering or small J alone cannot imply a small original T. The scalar T=[M] illustrates this algebra; it is not an evaluated arithmetic H counterexample. If only a known ||T||<=B is available, Cauchy and ||J||<=1 give

    |H|<=[r/2+B^2/(2r)] ||v|| ||w||,
    r/2+B^2/(2r)>=B.

Optimizing r merely recovers the known B bound. It creates no improvement.

For an approximate returned state xhat define d=v-(I-R)xhat. The COMPLETE scalar is

    H=ir w^*J xhat+w^*T d.                                    (R14)

No favorable truncated scattering term controls the original form without its residual channel. This explicit formula also governs a proposed iterative or blockwise implementation; the source-sensitive error must be paid in the actual native T.

[restricted research revision]'s Julia realization assumes a known contraction normalization r>=||T||. Cayley realization removes that prerequisite but replaces it by the explicit reflected-state inverse; G163's Schur/source complements remain the governing ancestry. These are classical operator constructions applied to the exact packet, not a claim of a new general scattering theory. The audit preserves S22 as a possible route only if one proves the arithmetic estimate in (R13), a full scalar variant of (R14), or another complete returned-source estimate. It supplies no H saving, no ordinary-character replacement and no c increase.

## Exact signed source and coefficient

Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), F(s)=1/L(s,chi), z=delta+i theta. Cauchy–Binet gives

    det[F(s+(i+j)z)]_(0<=i,j<=2)
      =sum_(u<v<w) a(u)a(v)a(w)V_z(u,v,w)^2(uvw)^(-s).

The square is analytic, not a squared modulus. Its36 signed permutation
occurrences have exponent patterns024,033,114,123,222. Replacing (uvw)^(-s)
by the fixed Gaussian g(log(uvw/x)) defines H(theta,x), with a uniform
absolute bound O_delta(x). For EVERY unramified prime p, its frequency p^2
has the exact coefficient

    B_(p^2)(x)=a(p)[M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))],
    M(y)=sum_n a(n)g(log(n/y)).                         (HC-I1)

There is one contributing monomial per distinct set {1,p,c}. Squareful
outputs, free composites divisible by p, complex phases and both excluded
atoms remain. Choose the least unramified p. The entire coefficient then
lies on the face (1,p,c), c>p.

With h=1/(4p^2), the nonnegative probability kernel

has Fourier support [-h,h]. Thus P_p U=integral_R K_h exp(2i theta log p)U
extracts p^(-2delta)B_(p^2). The associated rank-one orthogonal projection
obeys Pythagoras and retains the entire signed c,d correlation. Its full-line
median-complement projection vanishes. This is a statement about a linear
functional; it supplies no pointwise arithmetic positivity, zero complement
energy or hereditary signed-submask estimate.

## 2. Complete kernel and every pair

Choose fixed smooth nonnegative w supported in [1/2,3], w>=1 on [1,2]. Put f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k). For n!=m, two integrations by parts after x=Xu give

    |int w(x/X) f_x(n) conjugate(f_x(m)) dx/x|
      << exp(-c(n+m)/X^b) min(1,[X^k/|n^k-m^k|]^2),    (S5)

with the minimum equal to one when n=m. The phase derivative is a nonzero constant multiple of (n^k-m^k)u^(-k-1)/X^k. Every derivative of the real damping is a fixed polynomial in (n+m)/X^b times that damping; its polynomial is absorbed by decreasing c. Compact support eliminates boundary terms. Constants depend on fixed b,k,w. This is a continuous full-shell estimate.

Split at n<=X. By (S4), the full low source has pointwise magnitude O(X^(1+eta)/G), hence the same norm bound. Its entire interaction with the high source will be paid by norm triangle. All high-source expansions may first be finite; exponential damping and divisor bounds justify the limiting expansion and positive majorants.

Cover every comparable ordered high pair by a bounded-overlap collection [N/2,4N]^2, N>=c0 X dyadic. On a block put H=X^k/N^(k-1). The kernel factor is at most min(1,(H/|n-m|)^2). Let P_N be the positive absolute pair sum on this full block, including the diagonal. Equations (S3), (S4), and annuli about any integer center give

    P_N << exp(-cN/X^b) N^(2eta)
            [HN/G^2 + N^2/G^3].                         (S6)

For H>=1, the ball and doubling annuli have mass O(H/G+N/G^2), after summing their geometrically decaying weights. For H<1, the possible diagonal is paid by O(N/G^2); off-diagonal distances start at one and their weights give O(H^2/G+H^2 N/G^2), bounded by the same claimed quantity. Endpoint and empty intervals were included in (S3). Multiply the row bound by the full r_G mass O(N/G).

Independently, the integer-kernel row sum is O(1+H). Applying 2|v_n v_m|<=|v_n|^2+|v_m|^2 and (S2),(S4) to the SAME full positive pair sum gives

    P_N << exp(-cN/X^b) N^(2eta) (N/G)(1+H).            (S7)

Make constants and exponential rates common, then take the minimum. The inequality min(A+B,C+D)<=A+C+min(B,D) gives

    P_N << exp(-cN/X^b) N^(2eta)
       [ X^k/(G^2 N^(k-2)) + N/G
                 + min(N^2/G^3, X^k N^(2-k)/G) ].      (S8)

All distinct root representations and both ordered orientations were counted before this minimum. It does not compare two different signed sources.

One may also separate the exact diagonal first: it is at most the common factor times N/G. The off-diagonal integer row sum is O(H) even when H<1. Taking the minimum of (S6) and the off-diagonal bound HN/G then bounds all off-diagonal pairs by the first and last terms of (S8). Thus the X^b/G term below can be reserved solely for the diagonal.

## 3. Independent useful survivor: prime-dependent retention and optimal positive price

Fix for each unramified prime p a number0<rho_p<=1. Write lambda_p=1-rho_p and R_p=(2-rho_p)/rho_p. These choices are fixed as X varies for the subpower equivalence below; no common positive lower bound is required. For d,n in D_X define

 B(d,n)=1_(d|n) product_(p|d)rho_p product_(p|n/d)lambda_p,
 C(d,n)=1_(d|n) product_(p|n)rho_p^(-1) product_(p|n/d)(-lambda_p),
 h(d)=product_(p|d)(-R_p).                                                        (4)

All products over1 are1. Prime-by-prime binomial cancellation proves B C=C B=I, exactly as in(1), because D_X contains the entire divisor interval. The exact column sums and observer give

 ||B||_1=1,
 V(X):=||C||_1=max_(n in D_X) product_(p|n)R_p=max_D|h(n)|,
 M_chi(X)=sum_D h(d)b_chi,X(d),                                                   (5)

where b_chi,X(d)=chi(d)product_(p|d)rho_p times the ENTIRE sum over m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1 of mu(m)^2 chi(m)product_(p|m)lambda_p. This retains every natural zero, cofactor and sharp endpoint. It is an exact positive deletion channel acting on a complex source, not a randomness assumption on its factors.

**Exact fixed-prime criterion.** V(X)=X^o(1) if and only if log R_p/log p ->0 along unramified primes. Necessity: take X=p and the column n=p, obtaining R_p<=V(p). For sufficiency, fix epsilon>0 and choose P with R_p<=p^epsilon for p>P. Then every squarefree n<=X satisfies

 product_(p|n)R_p <= [product_(p<=P,p not|q)R_p] n^epsilon <= C_epsilon X^epsilon.  (6)

The finite product is independent of X. Since R_p>=1, this proves the equivalence with no prime theorem. It also proves the exact quantitative statement needed to absorb inversion into every-epsilon estimates. A fresh choice rho_p depending on X is NOT covered by this if-and-only-if criterion; then the maximum in(5) itself is the correct bill.

For example rho_p=min(1,(log p)^(-b)), fixed b>0, tends to0 yet has log R_p=O(1+loglog p)=o(log p), so inversion is subpower. This differs materially from setting the SAME rho_X=(log X)^(-b) at every prime, whose cost in the author's example is X^(b+o(1)). The former keeps small-prime information more faithfully. It is a permissible new source design with the same complete return, not an exponent saving by itself. Under(6), if BOTH |<h,btilde_X>| and ||b_X-btilde_X||_1 are O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)) at every scale, (3) with V(X) proves M_chi(X)=O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)). This arithmetic hypothesis is OPEN.

**Exact positive price, including arbitrary moving weights.** Now permit rho_p=rho_(p,X) to be arbitrary in(0,1] at each X; this next identity does not need the fixed-prime condition. For the PRINCIPAL source b_X(d)>0. Then

 P_abs(X):=sum_D |h(d)|b_X(d)
   =sum_(n in D_X) product_(p|n)(lambda_p+rho_p R_p)
   =sum_(n in D_X) product_(p|n)(3-2rho_p).                                        (7)

Every local factor is in[1,3), so

 #D_X <= P_abs(X) <= 3^K_X #D_X, hence P_abs(X)=X^(1+o(1)),                        (8)

uniformly over all these retention choices at the level of powers, for fixed q. The lower count #D_X=kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q)product_(p not|q)(1-p^(-2))>0, follows by mu^2(n)=sum_(r^2|n)mu(r), counting q-units in the inner interval, and bounding the r>sqrt X tail by sum r^-2. It needs no PNT. The upper uses only the factorial bound for K_X.

For EVERY positive diagonal weight w_d, even X-dependent and chosen using the source, Cauchy gives

 ||(w_d h_d)||_2 ||(b_d/w_d)||_2 >= sum_D |h_d|b_d=P_abs(X).                       (9)

This minimum is EXACTLY attained by w_d^2=b_d/|h_d|: b_d>0 because the original column n=d contributes product rho_p, and |h_d|>=1. The same lower bound follows for any conjugate Holder pair. Thus optimizing diagonal weights cannot make this raw principal readout power-small, even where inversion is affordable. This is stronger than the author's particular unweighted output/circle certificates, but only concerns those positive separable certificates. It does not exclude nonlocal signed norms, growing signed centering, cancellation between an approximant and its residual, or the original Mertens sum.

There is also a scalar-compression limit for varying rho_p: P_X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)product_(p|n)(lambda_p+rho_p z), so the author's positive prime-layer and fixed-original-layer obstructions still hold by coefficient mass. In general there is NO single z giving the full observer h(d); one must keep the multivariate or labeled readout(5). I do not import the uniform-rho affine formula into this extension.

Finite independent exact checks at X=40, q=1,3,6 and unequal rational retentions (including rho_2=1) confirm both matrix products, norm(5), the complete principal/quadratic readouts and equality(7). Script run once8894af, complete readbackb7022b; independent-checks.json is evidence for those finite cases only. Proofs(4)-(9), not that diagnostic, establish the general statements.

statement:
## 2. Marked inverse amplification with the actual slots

Let free mean sixth-power-free with all six source units retained. Fix natural rows u with 0<Nu<=Z^W, a finite fixed ray dictionary, and a product Q_u of the source's centrally normalized prime slots of total logarithmic width z. A polynomial-size row-independent puncture is permitted. For this section only, their prime coefficients may be arbitrary bounded row-independent coefficients, exactly as in B3.31. Let M_u(Z^r) be the actual inverse detector polynomial, including its common smooth cutoff and bounded real power. All lengths are in fixed bounded ranges, with W bounded away from zero.

For every epsilon>0 there is a sufficiently fine mesh, chosen before the eventual character family, slot list, profiles and heights, for which

    sum_free u |M_u(Z^r) Q_u|^2
      << Z^[E_MI(W,r,z)+epsilon] H_J,
    E_MI(W,r,z)=W/6+(5/6)max(W,r+2z,(2r+8z)/3).          (2)

Here H_J denotes the same kind of finite seminorm and polynomial-height cost as the sources. The bound is uniform in fixed polynomial-size punctures in the slot coefficients. The witness inverse has its natural row character; no arbitrary moving coefficient is inserted into it.

Proof. Put H0=max(W,r+2z,(2r+8z)/3), choose a small fixed xi>0, and set H=H0+xi W, alpha=(H-W)/6. Take a fixed prime-ideal pool Z^alpha/2<Np<=Z^alpha, prime to the fixed bad set, with the source's chosen primary generators. It has Z^[alpha+o(1)] primes by the same fixed-field prime ideal theorem used in B3.7. Choose every slot length below xi W/12. Since alpha>=xi W/6, the pool is disjoint from every slot support once Z exceeds the fixed endpoint threshold. This is why the new lemma retains a fine-mesh hypothesis.

For every pool prime, the literal zero-extended identity B0.7 reads

    M_u(D)=M_(up^6)(D)-mu_unit(u,p) (Np)^(-1/2) M_(up^6)(D/Np),
    mu_unit(u,p)=varphi_u(p),                            (3)

where the minus sign is mu(p)=-1. The displayed scalar has modulus at most one and is zero when the natural character requires it. There is no coprimality requirement between u and p. Because the pool misses all slots,

    Q_u=Q_(up^6)

exactly, including their original zeros, fixed masks, signs and relative characters. Apply the two-term squared triangle bound to (3), multiply by |Q_u|^2, and average with the literal normalized prime measure. The map (u,p)->up^6 is injective on free u: valuations modulo six recover u, and the quotient recovers p; the chosen prime generator preserves the unit of u. Thus the positive enlarged sum is at most

    Z^[-alpha+o(1)] sum_(Nv<=Z^H)
        sup_(0<E<=D) |M_v(E) Q_v|^2.                   (4)

Both exact restoration terms have been retained; the second's factor (Np)^(-1) can be bounded by one. Its p-dependent scale is handled by the common logarithmic-scale supremum, not by turning p into an inverse arithmetic coefficient. Differentiate the inverse profile using -W/2-yW', as in B0.8, and integrate over unit logarithmic boxes. Subunit scales are empty below a fixed scale and otherwise contribute only boundedly many boxes. B3.31 applies at row width H to every E<=D, since H-r-2z>=xi W and 3H-2r-8z>=3xi W. Its exponent is H; (4) has exponent H-alpha=W/6+5H/6. Taking xi and the source power losses small proves (2).

The same argument handles the actual cutoff W(y)V_le(Z^r y/Z^t), its scale derivatives, rowwise bounded real powers and frequencies by the source's Sobolev argument. In (3)--(4) all inverse polynomials keep this same frozen profile: at the shortened scale D/Np one must not reset the original truncation parameter from D to D/Np. Its dilation, real-power and frequency seminorms are uniform, and the scale supremum differentiates that fixed profile. The slot heights remain independent. A detector label differing from a slot's parent fixed character is absorbed into that slot's fixed relative coefficient; B3.31 explicitly allows such bounded coefficients. Whole orientation is kept throughout, or wholly conjugated using its allowed second orientation.

## 4. Raw sixth-power lifting with the original zeros

For raw width W require z<=W/21. Write w=u b^6 with free u and its original unit, fix b, and retain the added natural holes at every prime dividing b. Put s=log_Z Nb and V=W-6s. Positive-real primitive zeros are unchanged; Q_w is literally Q_u with these fixed additional holes. Section 1 and (2), not a loss of these holes, license the free estimate.

If V>=20W/21, z/V<=1/20. The linear theorem's root sum has exponent

    rho W+(delta-eta_plus)z-(6rho-1)s.

It converges since rho>=19/54. For the stronger (8), its loss under width reduction is at most a_delta(W-V); hence the root sum instead decays by [6(rho-a_delta)-1]s. Uniformly a_delta<1/500, for example by bounding its positive numerator at delta=.70 and 5-6delta at .68 and its denominator at .70. Thus this decay is also strict.

If V<20W/21, use the old unmarked free density plus the ORIGINAL physical slot bound for the natural character. The available root-tail saving is (rho-1/6)W/21. It pays even the stronger gain because

    G<=3kz, z<=W/21,
    rho-1/6>=5/27 > 3k(.68)=391/2275,
    5/27-391/2275=818/61425>0.

Bounded free-core windows and fixed-inducing free cores are bounded by the raw population Z^(W/6+delta z+small), when not already excluded by the original FI predicate; they are not called a finite raw population. The same strict gap pays them. This proves the raw version of (11) and (8), with z<=W/21, uniformly for the fixed translate, fixed polynomial punctures, both whole orientations and all heights. No arbitrary mask varying with the free live row was admitted.

statement:
## G164. Least-active-prime boundary multiplicity

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character χ modulo q. The source is
a(n)=μ(n)χ(n), including a(1)=1 and all squareful/nonunit zeros. Let P be a
finite set of primes coprime to q containing all such primes at most N;
additional primes larger than N are allowed. Use the ordered exterior basis
indexed by squarefree products of P, with creation operators c_p and their
usual fermionic signs. Let Π project onto products at most N, Q=I−Π, and

\[
d=\sum_{p\in P}w_pc_p,\quad W=\sum_p|w_p|^2>0,\quad
D=\Pi d\Pi,\quad B=Qd\Pi,\quad E=B^*B.
\]

All weights may be complex, N-dependent, and zero. Divisor closure gives
Qd*Π=0 and ΠdQ=0. The canonical anticommutation relations therefore imply

\[
D^2=0,\qquad D^*D+DD^*=W\Pi-E,\qquad 0\le E\le W\Pi.       \tag{95.1}
\]

Let p* be the least **active** prime, meaning w_p*≠0. Define U to be the
span of p*-free basis states with N/p*<n≤N. Every active creation kills U
after truncation, so D|U=0. On V_N/U, the operator
(1/w_p*)c_p*^* is a contracting homotopy: the full anticommutator is the
identity, and every term that fails to cancel after truncation lies in U.
The long exact sequence of the quotient complex identifies H(D) with U
as graded vector spaces. Finite-dimensional Hodge theory and (95.1) give

\[
\dim\ker(E-WI)=\dim H(D)=C_{p_*}(N),\qquad
C_p(N)=\#\{N/p<n\le N:\mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1,p\nmid n\}.       \tag{95.2}
\]

This is an eigenspace **dimension**, not a statement that the critical
basis vectors themselves are harmonic. For example, at q=1,N=12 the
critical states7 and11 need not be killed by D*. The quotient contraction
need not have a uniform norm when w_p* tends to zero. If p*>N then D=0,
U=V_N, and the same formula still holds.

Set κ_q=ζ(2)^−1∏_{p|q}p/(p+1). Square-divisor inclusion-exclusion gives
Q_q(x)=κ_q x+O_q(√x). For fixed p∤q,

\[
C_p(N)=\kappa_q\frac{p-1}{p+1}N+O_{q,p}(\sqrt N).
\]

For a bound uniform in p, handle the finitely many p<4/κ_q with this
formula. For the other primes, count q-unit squarefree states in (N/2,N]
and subtract at most N/p multiples of p. Thus, for all N sufficiently
large depending only on q, every unramified p satisfies
C_p(N)≥κ_qN/8. The trace counts outgoing creation edges exactly, so

\[
\frac{\kappa_q}{8}WN\le\operatorname{Tr}E
=\sum_p|w_p|^2C_p(N)\le WN,
\quad \|E\|=W,\quad
\dim\ker(E-WI)\ge\frac{\kappa_q}{8}N.                    \tag{95.3}
\]

Consequently no choice of these moving weights produces an ambient
positive spectral gap or a power-saving positive trace certificate.
This does **not** give a lower bound for the complete signed arithmetic
source or for another detector. Signed cancellation within the large
boundary space is still an eligible mechanism.

Let Tχ be diagonal multiplication by χ(n), and Str the parity-weighted
trace. Supertrace of the full identity gives the exact source return

\[
W M_\chi(N)=\operatorname{Str}(T_\chi E)
 +\operatorname{Str}([T_\chi,D^*]D).                     \tag{95.4}
\]

For each p, its normalized contribution is

\[
\sum_{N/p<n\le N\atop p\nmid n}a(n)
 +(1-\chi(p))\sum_{n\le N/p\atop p\nmid n}a(n)=M_\chi(N).
\]

Both endpoints, the unit, and nonunit zeros are included. Dropping the
commutator bulk is invalid for general characters. Restricting active
primes to χ(p)=1 does kill that bulk, but retains (95.3). Moving χ phases
into the differential is a unitary gauge change: it preserves the
spectrum and moves the arithmetic dependence into the observer/bulk.

An estimate for the **complete** right side of (95.4), at most
C_{χ,ε} W N^{γ+ε} for every N and ε>0, with a common 0<γ<2187135091/2500000000
over the required fixed-character family, would give Mχ(N)≪N^{γ+ε}.
The actual reciprocal-L Dirichlet series then continues through Abel
summation to Re(s)>γ, and excludes zeros there, with the allowed principal
pole treated normally. No such estimate is supplied here; no uniformity
for growing conductors or native-H transfer is inferred.

The ordered product ∏_{p increasing}(I−χ(p)c_p), acting with its largest
factor first, generates the literal μχ source. Averaging over all orders
kills degrees at least2, hence changes the source. Restoring the missing
parity/signs restores the original source. This rejects that averaging
shortcut, not all fermionic representations.

Classical ancestry is [Björner2011, Theorems2.1/3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704)
for the squarefree complex and [Bravyi–Kitaev2000v2, Eqs1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0003137)
for creation signs. The weighted truncated identities and uniform bound
above are proved in the frozen development; no literature novelty claim
is made.
