statement:
## 3. Exact far-mask return without an additive product phase

Let A_i(m;R,g) denote the complete coefficient of the ORIGINAL norm
q_n=m in one SF1 block on side i, including all ideals of that norm.
This is notation for regrouping, not a replacement of ideals by integer
factorization. The intervals used below select m, so both distinct ideal
orientations with equal rational norm always stay together.

Fix an integer H>=0. Choose a power-of-two integer interval containing
all possible values of x=m and y=m'+H. Its width is O(N) when H is below
the original norm range; if H exceeds that range the far mask is empty.
For each binary-tree node J let J_L,J_R be its left and right children.
The exact integer identity is

    1_(m>m'+H)
      = sum_(all internal J)
          1_(m in J_R) 1_(m' in J_L-H).             (SF8)

Every strict ordered pair is separated at its unique lowest common
ancestor. Equality m=m'+H contributes zero. At EACH fixed tree level,
the J_R intervals are disjoint, as are all translated J_L-H intervals.
All endpoints in SF8 are integer membership conventions, so there is
no smoothing or missing boundary strip. The reverse strict orientation
has the same identity with m,m' interchanged. Adding them gives exactly
1_(|m-m'|>H), without either equality orientation.

For any original bounded complex true-core weight h,

    h((g,g')) = sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f),
    r_h(f)=sum_(a|f) mu(f/a)h(a), |r_h(f)|<=tau(f). (SF9)

This is the entire original core inversion, with g=f b,g'=f b'.
It is not a recomputed core of de,d'e'. All source and short masks,
the original squarefree/primitive conditions, and both original g
windows remain in the summands. In particular chi_R(f)^3 keeps its
zero until a positive bound permits dropping its modulus.

Apply SF8 before any inequality. At one fixed level and f the ordered
covariance is a sum over disjoint interval pairs. Cauchy in the JOINT
coordinates (tree node,R), followed on each side by triangle over the
actual O(G/q_f) short sources, and then SF2, gives

    << Z^epsilon K (G/q_f)^2 N
           sqrt(T(D,E;L) T(D',E';L))
           sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.            (SF10)

For different source coefficients the two SF2 estimates are applied
to their own arrays, profiles and independent heights. The bounded
paired row factor is retained until its absolute value enters this
Cauchy measure. The O(K) row count is displayed; no new row theorem
is hidden here. All signs of r_h and every ordered bilinear interaction
were present in the exact expression before this bound.

There are O(log(2N)) levels. Sum the entire f inversion using
sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2<infinity, or the admitted subpower allowance. This
proves the following replacement for [private research revision] D6:

**SF-far theorem (restricted, proved).** Under the original D1/JPS
contract, with DE,D'E' comparable to the same original N,

    |C_(D,E;D',E')^far[h]|
      <<_(epsilon,orig) Z^epsilon K G^2 N
             sqrt(T(D,E;L) T(D',E';L))
             sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.          (SF11)

The sharp threshold may be the actual H0=floor(Z^.05), including its
strict endpoint. The estimate also holds uniformly for any integer H
at this same scope. There is no +(H0+1)L term. The same proof works for
the near mask by subtracting the two strict far orientations from the
complete product; that is an EXACT identity, not signed-submask
inheritance. The sharper preexisting near-prime theorem remains a
different input and is not invoked for auxiliary composites.

SF11 does not require and does not assert that exp(i a q_d q_e)
factors into d and e phases. It uses interval selection and a proven
simultaneous square function instead. It also does not infer SF11 by
taking a difference of two independently unproved norms. Each tree
rectangle is bounded in a common positive (node,R) measure.

The proof gives a useful abstract interface: a simultaneous bound for
all disjoint original norm intervals controls any single threshold
staircase m>m'+H at logarithmic cost. The sign of H and reversed order
are handled by the same exact finite identity. Arbitrary pair masks
are not covered merely because their values are bounded.

statement:
## 3. Independent reconstruction of the large-gcd identity

Let `B=M(D1;W1)M(D2;W2)`. The projection `B_{>=G}` imposes `N gcd(d1,d2)>=G` on its two inverse indices before merging. It does not constrain the slot indices or select rows. Define

    a_G(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Interchanging `d|q|g` gives

    sum_(q|g)a_G(q)=1_(Ng>=G),
    a_G(q)=0 for Nq<G, |a_G(q)|<=d(q).                            (R5)

All q actually dividing both nonzero Mobius terms are squarefree. For `d1=qx,d2=qy`, squarefreeness yields

    mu(qx)mu(qy)=mu(x)mu(y)1_((x,q)=1)1_((y,q)=1).

There is no condition `(x,y)=1` here. The two q factors in the natural character give `phi_u(q)^2`; they are zero, not invertible phases, when a natural zero applies. If `M^(q)` includes the displayed extra column coprimality, central normalization gives exactly

    B_{>=G,u}=sum_(q sf,Nq>=G)
       a_G(q)phi_u(q)^2/(Nq)
       M_u^(q)(D1/Nq;W1)M_u^(q)(D2/Nq;W2).                       (R6)

The sum ends at a fixed multiple of D1. Indeed `(Nq)^(-1)(D1/Nq)^(-1/2)(D2/Nq)^(-1/2)=(D1D2)^(-1/2)`. Omitting the `1/Nq` would lose the entire q-label count and invalidate the claimed result.

B0.9 cannot be applied directly to the new moving q-mask. The exact repair is

    M_u^(q)(E;W)=sum_(h q-smooth)
             phi_u(h)/(Nh)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nh;W).                    (R7)

For `p|q`, convolution of the local Mobius sequence `(1,-1,0,...)` with `(1,1,1,...)` is `(1,0,0,...)`. At other primes it stays Mobius. This proves the coefficient identity on ideals; complete multiplicativity carries it through natural zero values. The normalization is exact because `h^(-1/2)(E/h)^(-1/2)=E^(-1/2)`. At every actual profile support the h sum is finite. It can safely be absolutely bounded by

    sum_(h q-smooth)(Nh)^(-1/2)
       =prod_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1)
       <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.                                (R8)

Separate finitely many small primes; each remaining factor is at most `(Np)^epsilon`. For an already retained polynomial-size puncture R0, use primes dividing qR0. This extension is explicit and has the same subpower cost; it does not license an arbitrary growing source dictionary. Neither a q-mask nor a `mu*mu` coefficient is hidden in a smooth test.

## G134. Uniform second-order moving Riesz comparison

For each fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi, including principal,
imprimitive and complex characters with their presented-modulus zeros,
put `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, `M(t)=sum_(n<=t)a(n)` and

    E(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)exp(-n/x),
    R_r(N)=sum_(n<=N)a(n)(1-n/N)^r,
    B_r(x)=R_r(rx), V_r(x)=2B_(2r)(x)-B_r(x).

Endpoint n=N has weight zero. For real r>=2 and an explicit summatory
input `|M(t)|<=C t^beta`, beta>0, the complete bounds are

    |B_r(x)-E(x)| <= C K1(beta)x^beta/r,
    |V_r(x)-E(x)| <= (3/2)C K2(beta)x^beta/r^2,           (1)
    K1=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3),
    K2=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
       +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

These hold for every x>0 and real r>=2, uniformly in both. The unconditional
input beta=C=1 gives K1=176 and K2=11904, hence second-order constant17856.
A stronger summatory beta is an extra hypothesis, not a consequence of
writing down the accepted c alone.

Here is a global remainder proof. Set `k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r` and
`A(u)=u-u^2/2`. On `0<=u<=r/2`, write
`z=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u`. The complete logarithmic series gives

    z<=u/r, |z|<=(u+u^2)/r,
    |z-A(u)/r|<=(u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.

Apply `|exp(z)-1-z|<=(z^2/2)exp(max(z,0))` and
`exp(-u+max(z,0))<=exp(-u/2)`. Then

    |k'_r+exp(-u)| <= (5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k'_r+exp(-u)(1+A/r)| <= P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.                                (2)

For `u>=r/2`, the derivative is zero beyond r and at most exp(-u/2)
in modulus on its support. Since `r<=2u`, multiplying the proposed
second inequality by r^2 costs at most `2r^2+r|A|<=10u^2+u^3<=P`.
The first inequality follows from `2<=4u/r`. Thus (2) covers the full
positive half-line, not just the expanding finite interval.

Abel integration with vanishing endpoints gives

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M(xu)h'(u)du.

Integrating (2) against C x^beta u^beta proves the first part of (1).
Writing `k'_r=-exp(-u)(1+A/r)+e_r`, the first-order term cancels
exactly in `2k'_(2r)-k'_r+exp(-u)`. The remaining multiplier is
`2/4+1=3/2`; integration proves the second part. This pays the branch
`rx<n<=2rx`, endpoint integers and the entire exponential tail. Any
squared V norm retains `4|B_(2r)|^2+|B_r|^2-4Re(B_(2r)conj(B_r))`.

On each shell [X,2X], freeze one `r_X=max(2,ceil(X^delta))`. Equation (1)
gives a uniform pointwise and L2(dx/x) comparison error
`O(X^(beta-2delta))`. Therefore the every-positive-epsilon shell exponent
gamma for the moving V is equivalent to that of the fixed E whenever
`beta-2delta<=gamma`. Strict inequality supplies a fixed margin.

Only after this comparison use the fixed Mellin transform. Absolute
Fubini for Re(s)>1 and substitution n/x give

    Mellin(E)(s)=Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    Mellin(R_r)(s)=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)).

The beta identity and nonvanishing Gamma are classical
[DLMF facts](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12.E1), with
[Gamma's analytic properties](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2).
A fixed-field dyadic exponent gamma>0 makes its Mellin integral
holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma: choose epsilon below the compact set's
distance to gamma and sum by Cauchy–Schwarz, including every logarithmic
derivative. E decays exponentially at zero; fixed R_r vanishes below1.
Multiply by L and continue the identity. Every hypothetical L-zero at
any fixed height contradicts the nonzero numerator. The principal pole
is treated meromorphically, not mistaken for a zero. Constants may depend
on each fixed character; no growing-conductor uniformity is asserted.

A moving-r field has no direct fixed-r Mellin formula. Nor is a difference
of two Gamma quotients automatically nonzero. The comparison to E avoids
both issues. With beta=1, the following are sufficient conditional targets:

|gamma|c|delta|Complete comparison error exponent|
|---|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|.063|.874|
|5/6|1/6|.084|.832|
|3/4|1/4|.126|.748|

The largest raw cutoff is `4r_X X`, of order `X^(1+delta)`. A raw-cutoff
bound with exponent eta yields `(1+delta)eta` only with constants uniform
in the moving order. The decreasing integral bound `|B_r(x)|<=x` gives
`|V_r(x)|<=3x`, still exponent one. Increasing r alone gains nothing.
The new useful component is the uniform actual-source comparison, not
a new Mellin principle or arithmetic saving. Only fixed extrapolation
order two is proved; growing extrapolation order has no paid bound here.
title: G134. Uniform second-order moving Riesz comparison

statement:
## 3. Finite reconstruction and complete scalar error: GC15--GC16

Fix X_0>=2 and let

    R_X(x)=sum_{r<=X/X_0} k(r)
              P_{floor((X/r)^.495)}(x/r),     X<=x<=2X.

The local scale is Z=X/r, whereas the argument is y=x/r in [Z,2Z].
Each cutoff floor(Z^.495) is therefore frozen throughout its local
shell, exactly as needed by (C1).

For any epsilon>0 take sigma=1/2+epsilon and choose
0<delta<sigma-.495. Exact reconstruction and subtraction give

    G_tau(x)-R_X(x)
      = sum_{r<=X/X_0} k(r)
           [F_tau(x/r)-P_{floor((X/r)^.495)}(x/r)]
        + sum_{r>X/X_0} k(r)F_tau(x/r).                  (C3)

For the first sum, Z>=X_0>=1 and (C1) imply

    |F_tau(x/r)-P_{floor(Z^.495)}(x/r)|
       << Z^(.495+delta) <= Z^sigma.

Thus its absolute value is at most a fixed multiple of
X^sigma K_abs(sigma). No subpower count of r labels is asserted.

For the second sum, 0<x/r<2X_0. The Gaussian left tail and boundedness
on every compact positive interval give

    sup_{0<t<=2X_0} t^(-sigma)|F_tau(t)|<infinity.        (C4)

This is the required compact-plus-left-tail statement; boundedness
alone would not imply (C4) at zero. Hence the second sum is bounded
by C x^sigma sum_{r>X/X_0}|k(r)|r^(-sigma), which is O(X^sigma).
Both sums are genuinely absolutely convergent. This proves GC15
pointwise, uniformly on the complete shell, with all small scales
included. It does not require an arithmetic moment assumption.

For GC16, the inherited Mertens premise gives
M(t)=O(t^beta), beta=.8749. Consequently

    sum_{n<=t}A(n)=M(t)-2M(t/2)=O(t^beta).

Abel summation against the fixed Gaussian yields

    |G_tau(x)| <= C x^beta
                    integral_R e^(beta v)|g_tau'(v)|dv
                << x^beta.                              (C5)

Thus ||G_tau||_2<<X^beta. This is also the precise inherited input
in R35.20; it is not inferred from a finite numerical zero search.

Write E_X=G_tau-R_X and use GC15 with epsilon/2. The exact Hilbert
space expansion gives

    | ||G_tau||_2^2-||R_X||_2^2 |
       <=2||G_tau||_2||E_X||_2+||E_X||_2^2
       << X^(beta+1/2+epsilon/2)+X^(1+epsilon)
       << X^(1.3749+epsilon).                           (C6)

Both ordered mixed terms and the error square are covered. The
last inequality uses beta>1/2. This allocation works for every
epsilon>0, without silently treating the error as a squared error
alone. The exponent 1.3749 is below the stated target 1.74898.

If Q_X is one of the complete original W35 finite-band or
four-diagonal scalars, R35.17 and (C5) give an additional comparison
error X^(beta-A_0+o(1)). Adding it to (C6) preserves the displayed
1.3749+epsilon comparison. This says nothing about a new exponent
for ||R_X||_2 itself. For a lower target, the two-way norm theorem
remains the valid return even if this baseline scalar estimate is
too crude.
title: 3. Finite reconstruction and complete scalar error: GC15--GC16

### Why two attractive shortcuts fail

SF's witness uses \(n=Wp q\), \(n'=Wr s\), with the four primes in
separated admissible boxes. Coalescing **all** allocations gives
coefficient 4, not cancellation, while the profile product is positive.
The prior PO local prime-square cancellations are retained. What remains
must exploit signs between different completed products; another local
absolute-value estimate cannot supply the exponent 1.74898.

SC proves that sending the Möbius removal cutoff to infinity moves the
selected main rather than disposing of it. Its auxiliary B2.29 prime
packet gives an explicit obstruction to a uniform coefficient-only
small-core estimate in the original short-divisor corridor. Those
auxiliary coefficients are not the physical infinity coefficient.
For the actual source, SC14 instead retains the full
\(\overline{\alpha(p)}\gamma_2(p)\nu(p)\) Gauss phase. Bounding that
first moment with its marks and deletions, or proving cancellation with
other dual cores, is a substantive remaining step.

## Exact source and norm

Fix the original finite natural dictionary, excluded primes S, complete
orientation and admissible slot system. For ideal columns and element rows,
write phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n), psi_u(n)=chi_n(u)^(+/-1), including all natural
zeros. A fixed nu of order other than six stays in the coefficient. Whole
conjugation acts on every factor. All six units remain in the row family.

For the original row-independent prime pools and profiles,

    Q_u=U^(-v/2) sum_P alpha(P)psi_u(P), 0<=v<=1/20,

with NP comparable to U^v. The no-slot term is P=1,v=0. Common primes
between n and P remain allowed with their zero extensions. No arbitrary
coefficient version of UM/MI/MP is asserted.

Let R=U^t,Y=U^B, and use the actual V, equal to1 on[0,1] and0 on[2,infinity).
Set

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y).

The [accepted completion](../[private research revision]/joint-density-integration.md) gives
D_R,u(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)) at a zero of the same natural nonprincipal character.
The primitive inducing character must be nonprincipal; adding Euler holes
to a principal character does not suffice. The identity is a value
identity, not a claim that derivatives vanish at a zero.

First pay the genuine exponential tail Nn>U^(B+1), with all needed fixed
derivatives and cross terms. A crude polynomial bound on the retained
expression and arbitrarily small absolute tail error suffice. Fix raw
row/slot/height powers before the tail order, B and final threshold. Pair
classification then concerns a finite polynomially supported expression;
it never assigns a uniform subpower loss to unbounded conductors.

Merge equal nP=l with signs:

    F_u=D_R,u Q_u=sum_l b_l(s)psi_u(l),
    b_l=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l,Nn>R)
        A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y)alpha(P).

The finite terminal cutoff is understood. For each required derivative,
on a fixed compact real interval sigma>1/2,

    |partial b_l| << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)(Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l!=0 implies Nl>=L0=c0 U^(t+v).                 (1)

H_J contains fixed seminorms and a fixed height polynomial, not a live
arithmetic coefficient. Divisor multiplicities, logarithms and fixed
derivatives are absorbed into the requested loss before the threshold.

Choose a smooth positive radial Phi>=1 on the required row ball BEFORE
expansion. Use every nonzero sixth-power-free row, with the original
fixed-dictionary exclusions (or retain that finite set). PR15 proves those
exclusions finite from fixed prime support and valuations at most5.
For a fixed positive-width interval I whose lower edge is at least
(1+delta)/2-h0, 0<=h0<=10^(-5), put

    N(F)=sum_(u free,eligible) Phi(Nu/U)
        sum_(i,j in {0,1}) integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
        |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j F_u|^2 d tau d sigma.       (2)

Finite extra derivatives and orientations mean their finite sum. An
original positive row weight bounded by U^epsilon and its selected subset
are dominated on the FULL norm before expansion. This does not dominate
individual signed sectors or license amplitude-selected Poisson kernels.

## 3. B: mixed-direction bank, homotopy and the correct norm constants

With2,3 unramified and a3<sigma<1, b2=2*2^-sigma-1>0, b3=1-2*3^-sigma>0, A=b2^2+b3^2 and w_i=b_i^2/A. The bank R=w2E2^-Y2+w3E3^+Y3 satisfies

    N_sigma(RY)<=A^-1/2 [N_sigma(Y2)^2+N_sigma(Y3)^2]^1/2.

This follows by triangle then Cauchy--Schwarz, exactly as stated in B2. On the global weighted L2 line its multiplier is the row(w2/m2,w3/m3), m_p=1-2chi(p)p^(-sigma-it); its norm is at mostA^-1/2. Near simultaneous phase alignment it approaches that value, so the unrestricted global constant is sharp. Irrational log2/log3 gives a dense continuous two-phase orbit. For trivial phases t=0 suffices, using long smooth packets. This is not a favorable-height arithmetic estimate. The pointwise pseudoinverse is another valid left inverse, not generally identical to R away from aligned phases.

The homotopy signs check algebraically: d0=(D2,D3), d1=(-D3,D2), h1=R, h2=(-w3E3^+,w2E2^-). Commutation gives d1d0=0, h1d0=I, d0h1+h2d1=I and d1h2=I. For actual F, future telescoping uses its pre-existing beta<1 boundary and past telescoping uses the Gaussian left tail. For arbitrary vectors in N_sigma the stable series directly pay both boundaries. If a prime is ramified its D isI and that channel alone reconstructs at cost1; no unit phase is inverted at zero.

The actual channels are correct: for n=2^k m, m odd, D2F has coefficient chi(n)f3(m)[1,-3,1,1,...]_k; D3F has chi(n)mu(rad(n)), including EVERY prime power. D2's Mellin numerator is N2^2J; D3's is N2N3J. In a3<Re(s)<1 each is nonzero. All repeated powers, natural zeros, channel cross terms within each square and the Gaussian tails remain. Both channels independently detect in that strip, and D3 alone has a causal return there. The two-channel topology does not create arithmetic cancellation.

If the complete joint large-dyad channel energy has exponent2gamma+epsilon with a3<gamma<.874861, individual buffered N_sigma norms are finite; the bank returns F's every-epsilon exponent gamma. Conversely finite dilations return the joint energy from F. Global weighted integrability requires a strictly buffered sigma above an actual growth exponent, not the limiting line itself. B4 is therefore an equivalent full arithmetic target. No source masks or cross energies are erased.

**Quantitative acceptance limit:** B2 uses the Euclidean norm of TWO SEPARATE shell suprema. It is not the single joint-shell norm

    J_sigma(Y)=sup_T T^-sigma [||Y2||_[T,2T]^2+||Y3||_[T,2T]^2]^1/2.

The author’s4.44/4.27/3.97 are correct for the displayed B2 norm/global L2 norm. They must not be advertised as the cost from B4's single same-shell energy bound without a further coherent-source estimate. A safe generic bound there is sqrt(2/A), exactly the distinction retained by G52. This changes fixed-constant interpretation, not the exponent theorem.

### Critic-added exact joint-shell cost for this R

In fact the specified R has unrestricted J_sigma->N_sigma norm

    C_R=(b2+b3)/A.

Upper bound: each component N_sigma<=J_sigma, hence the triangle sum is w2/b2+w3/b3. Sharpness for trivial phases: fix T>0, put Y2(x)=-x^sigma for x>=2T and0 otherwise, and Y3(x)=x^sigma for0<x<2T and0 otherwise. Their supports are disjoint and |Y2|^2+|Y3|^2=x^(2sigma), so J_sigma=C_sigma=[(2^(2sigma)-1)/(2sigma)]^1/2. On[T,2T], every future prime2 argument lies in Y2's support and every past prime3 argument lies in Y3's support. The two geometric sums yield RY=C_R x^sigma exactly; hence its norm on that shell is C_R C_sigma. A small-scale cutoff followed by smoothing approximates the same lower bound if a Gaussian/zero left tail is desired. General fixed unit phases use x^(sigma+it) and simultaneous phase alignment to approach it. This is an unrestricted-function-space counterexample, not a lower bound for the actual arithmetic channels. It need not satisfy d1Y=0; a smaller bound on compatible pairs remains a separate possible theorem.

| Limiting weight | prime2 future | global/B2 cost | actual R joint-shell cost | safe sqrt2 bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .874861 |11.03597|3.96919|5.13115|5.61329|
| 5/6 |8.16580|4.27384|5.87858|6.04412|
| 3/4 |5.28521|4.43528|6.13413|6.27244|

Consequently the stated bank's joint-shell constant need not beat the prime2-only reconstruction constant at3/4, even though its global inverse constant does. At5/6 the displayed fixed bank can still improve the constant in the corresponding norm. No numerical constant alters c=1-gamma. Gamma=.8748 would conditionally give c=.1252, a further gain61/1000000=.000061;5/6 and3/4 conditionally give1/6 and1/4. These inputs remain unpaid, and every proof uses positive buffers before the scale.

**B verdict:** ACCEPT exact mixed-direction homotopy, literal channels and equivalent complete moment return, with the norm distinction above. G52 already supplies quantitative weighted banks and the global/joint-shell distinction; G70 already supplies the exact D2F channel. The scoped combination with different critical real parts1/a3 and the all-prime radical D3 channel is a valid source adaptation. Abstract Koszul exactness, stable geometric series and frame inversion receive no new mechanism credit. No full moment, c gain or native formal evidence.

## 6. Actual new rows and the exhaustive residual

Retain the old disjoint paid classes Omega_g,Omega_s first. On their complement Omega_c, the SAME chosen functions obey |B_c|>|B|/2. Define

    Omega_band={u in Omega_c: |B_c^[theta]|>=|B_c|/2}.

On this actual class, |M Q|<=4|B_c^[theta]Q|/|S(D)|. Divide only by the ORIGINAL unshifted lower bound in R1. The D^beta factor cancels before beta is weakened to physical delta. Thus

    sum_(Omega_band) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2
       <=H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).               (R15)

The entire slot product stays in the inverse moment; Q is never divided out. This class is disjoint from the two prior paid classes by definition. The class predicate is about the original values, not derivative signals or reselected witnesses.

Every remaining row has the exact strict signal

    |B_c^[1-theta]|>|B_c|/2>|M S|/4,                 (R16)
    1-theta(b)=log N(b_outside_band)/log Nb.           (R17)

All old tuple cuts, masks, signs, real powers, heights and prime-slot tuples survive. It vanishes when b is supported entirely in the band. A band prime cannot occur twice in b within this original core: Np>=A=H and p^2|b would imply N s2(b)>=H. This fact does not remove the higher powers from R2 or R10; those complete source/intersection expansions were paid before subtraction.

The old repeat-factor bound remains N(n/rad n)<G H^2 NP. More importantly, a good prime plain ideal b at scale D has Nb>Y for sufficiently large U, since m>4eta. For a coprime squarefree inverse tuple it survives the core and has theta(b)=0. This is a surviving coefficient example, not a constructed high-zero row or lower bound for the signed norm.

The full coarse estimate is still paid: B_c^[1-theta]=B_c-B_c^[theta], the previous complete norm for B_c is H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon), and R14 is smaller. statement:
## 3. Second route: arbitrary-graph transport and centering

JSR19 proves for an arbitrary original row/mark-independent directed graph E with both degrees <=B (possibly frozen separately with each short pair) that

    |C_E| <= Z^epsilon G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359)
             N^(103/359) S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.

It is already an all-short-pair bound and keeps both mark projectors via their complete signed divisor expansion and lcm Schur sum. At the pressure point its sufficient degree exponent is .056035346678811698... with a fixed small power buffer. The accepted transported/centered theorem, however, was proved only for the specified norm-gap graph; it cannot be inherited for arbitrary masks.

A new elementary adapter suffices. The row transport moves only its smooth profile rho(R/sqrt K) to rho((R+P+P')/sqrt K), keeping the original sharp R support. The smooth compact-annulus extension is the actual one in RH/JS; its global mean-value bound is C sqrt(L/K)||grad rho||_infinity. Since |P|,|P'|<=C sqrt(L), this applies even when the segment between the two arguments crosses the edge of the original smooth support. No sharp indicator is differentiated.

For each frozen ordered short pair there are O(NB) long-prime edges. There are O(G^2) such short pairs and O(K) actual rows. Native a(pi), xi(g), all characters and their natural zeros have modulus at most one, and the complete original core has modulus at most one. The two absolute mark sums satisfy, with their roots intact,

    (sum_P |u_1(P)|/sqrt(q_P))
    (sum_P' |u_2(P')|/sqrt(q_P'))
       <= C L sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2).

This charges BOTH mark counts explicitly, rather than importing an unproved submask version of a signed sieve norm. The source and short profiles are charged to their original seminorms. Thus the full transport error is bounded by

    |C_E^tr-C_E|
       <= C_orig G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K)
             sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.             ([restricted research revision].6)

At S>=N the ratio to the target is <=C G B L sqrt(L/K); its pressure exponent is gamma+b+3ell/2-k/2, negative for the entire accepted degree gate. This does not appeal to signed-mask monotonicity or to a row character estimate after an additive twist. All projector deletions occur only inside this explicit absolute error bound, after the exact full difference has been written.

For completeness, the genuine common-unit Jacobi correction is also paid on every such graph. Its local numerator and denominator are exactly JSR28:

    C1(T)=J_+(pi) J_-(pi') chi_pi(T) chi_pi'(T)^(-1),
    h1(T)=product_(p|pi*pi') (q_p^2-3q_p+3-1_(p|T)).

The two local convolution minus signs cancel. Both Jacobi sums have square-root modulus, giving |C1(T)/h1(T)|<=C N^-3, uniformly even at an exceptional total T divisible by one of the primes. An absent third local character is initially the unrestricted constant; replacing it by a unit indicator is justified only because the actual marks lie below both primes. Its induced subtraction is exactly the displayed Jacobi term, not a zero or a supposed principal-character average.

The remaining folded weight retains chi_R(uv)^3, the common-short-divisor puncture, all projectors and all profiles. Absolute summation over the actual graph as above gives

    |M_E^(J,tr)|
       <= C_orig G^2 K B L/N^2
               sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.          ([restricted research revision].7)

This is the full mean including all mark off-diagonals. The N^-2 comes from O(NB) prime pairs times N^-3, not from an additional Fourier normalization. The sharp row support remains on R=T-P-P', and supported totals inject modulo pi*pi' because Q>C_orig(K+L). Thus the smooth transported factor is genuinely constant on each supported residue-total fibre. All original unit/ray components are folded with their own coefficients; there is no division by six.

Writing R_E^(J,tr)=C_E^tr-M_E^(J,tr), the elementary triangle inequality, ([restricted research revision].6)--([restricted research revision].7) and the inherited JSR19 prove the explicit all-short-pair return

    |R_E^(J,tr)| <= Z^epsilon sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig *
       [ G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359) N^(103/359) S(N,L)
         + G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K)
         + G^2 K B L/N^2 ].                           ([restricted research revision].8)

The same formula without the last term controls the uncentered transported covariance. It holds for every graph with both degrees <=B, independent of live marks and rows; the graph and its bounded complex edge weight may be frozen with each original short pair. Empty graphs, bounded B and bounded source windows cause no exception. One may replace the degree condition by the corresponding two absolute Schur row-sum bounds if the edge count in ([restricted research revision].6)--([restricted research revision].7) is interpreted with absolute edge weights.

Three sufficient conditions for payment by the ORIGINAL target, with a fixed small power buffer, are

    B <= K^(128/359) N^(-103/359) G^(-462/359),
    G B L sqrt(L/K) <= 1,
    G B L/N^3 <= 1.                                  ([restricted research revision].9)

The first is exactly the old raw-graph gate. The second and third are new explicit adapter gates, obtained using S>=N and therefore sufficient without an unproved S asymptotic. At the physical pressure point set B=floor(Z^(11/200)). The three relative exponents are respectively

    -.001035346678811698...,
    -.105533105423066003...,
    -2.288708945769339965....                         ([restricted research revision].10)

Choose the total epsilon allowance smaller than one quarter of the first displayed margin, and distribute it through the finitely many inherited divisor and conductor losses. Heights are treated by the actual profile integrals, not by this epsilon budget. Multiplying ([restricted research revision].8) by N^-1 G^-2 yields the complete physical bound

    N^-1 G^-2 |R_E^(J,tr)|
       <= Z^epsilon K S(N,L)/(NG)
               sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig,          ([restricted research revision].11)

for this graph range. Every term of the triangle is paid separately before that conclusion.

### A4. Fixed ordinary characters, with their actual zero extensions

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with chi(n)=0 when (n,q)>1. Put f_chi(n)=chi(n)f(n), b_sigma,chi(n)=chi(n)b_sigma(n). Complete multiplicativity, including the zeros, turns A7 into

    b_sigma,chi=(chi*a_sigma pointwise) * f_chi,
    f_chi=(chi*d_sigma pointwise) * b_sigma,chi.             (A12)

Both weighted absolute kernel norms are at most those in A7. Thus A9 holds for these complete complex Gaussian fields, separately for every fixed chi. This is a newly derived twist of the actual coefficient identities, not an unproved signed-submask transfer.

On l2{n:(n,q)=1}, the twisted Hankel is D_chi T^(q) D_chi, where D_chi(n,n)=chi(n) is unitary and T^(q) omits the ramified prime factors. Left and right unitary multiplication preserve singular values; no self-adjointness of the complex twist is asserted. The optimal core retains2,3 exactly when unramified and the positive eigenvector for every unramified p>=5. It has rank2 when2 does not divide q, rank1 when2 divides q. Its first column is C_(sigma,q)b_sigma,chi(n)n^-sigma; ramified rows and columns remain zero in the full l2(N) extension. If2 is ramified, the all-positive local choice is the largest singular mode, so the same finite-compression proof gives optimal rank1. This prices every bad-prime change.

Here is the complete zero return for the fixed twist, rather than an assumed analogy. On Re s>1, the literal Dirichlet series of f_chi is W_chi(s)/L(s,chi), where

    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)
       /[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
       * product_(p>=5) (1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2.   (A13)

The infinite product and its inverse converge normally on every Re s>=rho>.5: nonconstant local errors are O_rho(p^-2rho), and2p^-rho<1 for p>=5. All denominator factors are nonzero for Re s>0. The prime-two numerator, when nontrivial, has zeros only on Re s=1. Consequently W_chi is holomorphic and nonzero in .5<Re s<1; omitted ramified factors equal1 exactly.

Absolute Mellin transformation initially gives exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi(s)/L(s,chi). Multiplication by the continued L-function and the identity theorem give L(s,chi)M(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi(s) in gamma<Re s<1. The right side never vanishes, so there is no L-zero there. The principal pole at1 is outside this open strip. The original known right-edge facts complete the usual half-plane conclusion. Every height is covered; constants may depend on the fixed character.       << A_delta^2 [X^(b(1+2delta))+X^k M^(2-k+2delta)],

when 2delta<k-2. Norms use dx/x on [X,2X]. This is the whole-tail statement
with a smooth positive shell majorant and two integrations by parts; both
off-diagonal orientations are included. It is not an estimate of only a
separated tail cell. Since b<=2gamma and k+(2-k)r=2gamma, choose delta after
epsilon to pay this tail at X^(gamma+epsilon). The triangle inequality for
the complete sums also pays their interactions with the retained core.

Thus, with the literal finite core

# Independent controller review of the actual f3 gcd sector

11 October 2026. Source: [frozen author report](gaussian-signed/report.md),
SHA-256 `60d5da9a989bf598f6757c17d88f2bb0761237e891693f0b54f52090e7c2a97c`.

summability arguments below. **Accept S10–S23 as written, conditional only
on the explicitly buffered accepted Mertens input.** S24–S31 are valid
additional identities and a useful limitation. None proves a larger c.
The report's numerical choices retain its [private research revision] baseline; formulas with
an arbitrary fixed beta remain the reusable statements.

## Coefficients, sectors and uniform tails

For p not dividing 3r, the local series of f_r is (1-2z)/(1-z).
Dividing by the Möbius factor 1-z gives
1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)z^j. For p dividing 3r the quotient is
(1-z)^(-2). Thus the exact all-power convolution in S4 has finite absolute
beta norm for beta>1/2, bounded by C_(beta,delta)r^delta. This pays prime
2 and prime 3 without introducing a reciprocal factor 1-2*2^(-s).
Its constants are not uniform as beta approaches the accepted boundary.

For m=ga,n=gb and (a,b)=1, the two factors f(g) square to one.
After inserting sum_(q|a,b)mu(q), the next two f_g(q) factors also
square to one. The remaining whole field is exactly f_(gq), so the
signed coefficient of E_r(X/r) is sum_(g|r,g>=D)mu(r/g).
This proves S9 without assigning positivity to a correlation sector.
The Gaussian majorant makes the complete rearrangement absolute.

For r<=X the convolution estimate and the convergent sums in g and q
give X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta). For r>X use the bound independent of
r, |F_r(y)|<=C_A y^A for y<=2. When D>X the ratio of the resulting
tail to the advertised bound is

    X^(delta-epsilon)(X/D)^(2A-2beta-delta) <= 1

after choosing delta<=epsilon and 2A-2beta>delta. When D<=X the same
tail is O(X^(1+delta)) and is absorbed at the worst endpoint D=X.
This independently closes the report's all-real-D quantifier.

The diagonal is the literal sum_(n>=D)K_X(n,n), since f(n)^2=1.
Subtracting it proves the off-diagonal statement. The complementary
sector retains all ordered pairs; writing b=a+h gives f_g(a(a+h))
only because (a,h)=1. The factor two and both Gaussian heights remain.
For gamma>1/2, the strict threshold
(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1) in S13 pays the large-gcd error and the
O(X) diagonal. The remaining one-sided signed estimate is still open.

## Prime switches and the self-containing reduction

Split integers into p-adic valuations before estimating. Their exact
local signs give F_r=U-V and F_(rp)=U+V, hence the energy difference is
4 integral U V. The V-square cancels. The p-deleted U has convolution
factor (1-z)^(-1) at p, with a uniformly bounded absolute beta norm.
Summing all positive p powers therefore gives p^(-beta), including the
complete power tail. Telescoping switches proves S19.

The decisive remaining sum is

    sum_r r^(-2beta+delta) sum_(p|r,p>P)p^(-beta)
      = zeta(2beta-delta) sum_(p>P)p^(-3beta+delta).

It converges for sufficiently small fixed delta and pays exactly the
P^(1-3beta+delta) error. S22 has the correct diagonal subtraction and
retains the signed high-gcd scalar. In S23, P>=D forces every g<D
dividing st to divide its P-smooth part s. This proves the factorization
with mu(t), including nonsquarefree t.

This estimate simplifies auxiliary prime switches. It does not simplify
away the r=1 summand E_1(X), which is the unknown whole energy itself.
Absolute estimation of the remaining summands supplies no bootstrap.

## Rational rays and their actual reach

For coprime a,b, a prime dividing ab but not 3 contributes
2*1_(p|d)-1 to f(ad)f(bd), independently of every valuation. Expansion
gives the finite radical divisor formula and period mean in S24–S26.
When 2 divides ab the odd/even signs have mean zero. Ordinary Poisson
summation of the flat-at-zero logarithmic Gaussian gives S28; its
normalization is consistent with
g_tau(v)g_tau(w)=g_(2tau)(v-w)g_(tau/2)((v+w)/2).
Consequently the main coefficient and the diagonal constant in S29/S31
are correct. The error is uniform only in the displayed low-radical
region; no sharp common-multiplier truncation has been introduced.

Independently counting coprime factorizations of n gives 2^omega(n).
The Rankin product in S30 converges for s>1/3, with the prime-3 factor
handled separately. Thus the region with arbitrary-power cancellation
already has absolute cost X^(4/3-delta/3+epsilon). It is already below
the stated near, 1/6 and 1/4 scalar targets. This is a valid useful
failure of that proposed attack on the hard region, not a general
impossibility result.

## Disposition

The large common factor sector is now paid for the actual two-integer
f3 correlation. W36 concerned a different four-factor overlap and was
not used as an unproved restriction principle. Retain the exact shifted
correlation S15 as the principal remaining obligation, plus the switch
bound as a reusable comparison. Finite arithmetic receipts check

ideals, including squareful and nonunit zeros.

The Eisenstein lattice with basis 1,omega has covolume sqrt(3)/2
and covering radius 1/sqrt(3)<1 in the norm N(alpha)=|alpha|^2.
Nearest-lattice division gives Euclidean division, hence class
number 1. Every nonzero ideal has exactly six generators. The
function psi((alpha)), extended by zero away from elements coprime
to f, is periodic modulo f and invariant under those six units.
A nonprincipal such Hecke character is a nontrivial character of
the residue-unit quotient, so its mean over O_K/f is zero. The
principal mean is |(O_K/f)^*|/N(f)>0.

Tile the disk |alpha|<=sqrt X by cells of the fixed f-lattice.
Complete cells contribute that residue mean. The O_f(sqrt X+1)
boundary cells have bounded total weight per cell. Exclude alpha=0
and divide by six. This proves

    sum_(N(a)<=X) psi(a)=c_psi X+O_f(sqrt X+1),
    c_psi=0 for nonprincipal psi,
    c_principal=(pi/(3sqrt(3))) |(O_K/f)^*|/N(f).         (R39.9)

The displayed constant follows from the unit disk's area and the
covolume; the exact value is not needed for the theorem, but its
positivity proves that the regularized principal pole is nonzero.
This is a fixed-lattice estimate, with no assertion that its error
is uniform in moving f. Nontrivial angular weights are not periodic
in these residue cells and are outside this proof.

In particular the positive ideal count is O(X). Integration by
parts against the real Gaussian, or summation in unit log bins,
then proves the same C_tau exp(u) positive majorant for u>=0 and
the same Gaussian left tail. The ideal sum is therefore entire
with the required complex bound. Euler inversion on Re s>1 gives
its exact Mellin transform exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,psi).

Abel summation of R39.9 gives a meromorphic continuation for
Re s>1/2 and a polynomial upper bound there after multiplying a
principal L by s-1. The residue is c_psi in the principal case.
Every replenishment disk may be kept strictly in Re s>1/2 when
gamma>1/2. The Euler product at 2 supplies the same center bounds.
Thus R39-A--D apply, proving W39-H without importing an improved
I-HECKE reciprocal estimate as a hidden premise.

The family agrees with root's stated finite-order, trivial-infinity
scope. This does not give a moving-conductor, angular or general
number-field theorem. A common zero-free conclusion for every
member requires the small-set hypothesis separately for every
member (or a separately proved uniform hypothesis). A zeta-only
small-set bound does not supply the family hypothesis.

### R39-F. f3 keeps its actual Euler factors and full signed return

The source f3 is multiplicative with f3(p^k)=-1 for every k>=1
and p!=3, and f3(3^k)=1. Thus its local Dirichlet factors are
(1-2z)/(1-z) for p!=3 and (1-z)^(-1) at 3. Dividing by the local
factor of 1/zeta gives exactly

    D3(s)=B(s)/zeta(s), B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^-s)^(-2)(1-3^-s)^(-2)
             product_(p>=5) (1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)^2.        (R39.10)

For p>=5 the linear term cancels. On Re s>=b>1/2, both local
logarithmic series have summable O_b(p^-2b) tails; 2*5^-b<1
excludes every numerator zero. H and its inverse are consequently
analytic, bounded and nonzero on that half-plane. The separate
factors at 2 and 3 are essential. B has its retained zeros on
Re s=1 and no zeros in 1/2<Re s<1.

For the complete F3(z)=sum_n f3(n)g_tau(log n-z), the actual Mellin
identity is exp(tau*s^2/2)B(s)/zeta(s). Holomorphy of this transform
above h excludes zeta zeros in h<Re s<1. The known zero-free right
edge, already available in the project, completes the conclusion;
one must not pretend B is nonvanishing on that edge. Replenishment
uses the independently established reciprocal bound for zeta and
the bounded actual B. R39-A--D therefore prove the f3 criterion for
every fixed gamma>1/2 and kappa<1/2.

This criterion is equivalent, with epsilon buffers, to the full
pointwise Gaussian exponent. The reverse direction simply takes
E_j to be the whole interval. It is also equivalent to the complete
Gaussian square-moment target in the stated range: pointwise bounds
give that moment; conversely, dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz gives holomorphy
of the Mellin transform, then zero exclusion and R39.7 give the
pointwise bound again. Thus equivalence is proved through the
actual meromorphic multiplier, not a generic L2-to-supremum claim.

Current-proof G28 separately gives A=k*f3, f3=h*A, with the
weighted absolute convolution norms finite for each sigma>1/2.
Their fixed-field identities transfer the complete moment; G27
and G29--31 price the moving cutoffs only in their stated order.
The original A(1),A(2),A(4)=1,-3,2 remain. The f3 moment expands
with its true O(X) diagonal and every signed ordered off-diagonal
term. No absolute value may be moved inside that scalar, no negative
term deleted, and no arbitrary submask inherits the valley theorem.

The resulting **OPEN-F3-VALLEY(gamma,kappa)** is an arithmetic
estimate on a measurable subset of **every** fixed log interval,
for the complete f3 sum and gamma<.874867, kappa<1/2. It is not
established by the accepted leading signed-band asymptotics,
independent-prime models, finite sampling, or density-one good
intervals. The f3 corollary supplies zeta's return; ordinary chi and

We now pay application of theta to the complete old core, rather than infer
a bound for a signed subset of(2.6). For any fixed nonempty extracted ideal L,
put E=D/NL and define

 S_(theta,L)(E)=E^(-1/2)sum_c phi(c)W_P(Nc/E)theta(Lc).

The additive logarithm in(1.3) gives the EXACT formula

 S_(theta,L)(E)=L(L)/log D S(E;V_D)
   +1/log D sum_(p in P_band,j>=1)log Np phi(p^j)
                  (Np)^(-j/2) S(E/(Np)^j;V_D).        (3.1)

Here the function L(L) means the band logarithm of the ideal L, not its norm.
In particular (3.1) holds when p divides L: all additional valuations of c
are counted, and no shared prime is omitted. Its denominator is correct
because log(NL Nc)=log(D(Nc/E)). The exact nonempty support gives
0<=L(L)/log D<=1+O(1/log D).

Use the SAME buffered pointwise bound, without inserting a new marked slot
in this step. For j=1 the absolute dyadic mass is
P^((1-beta)/2); for j>=2 it is bounded by(2.5). Thus uniformly in every L,

 |S_(theta,L)(D/NL)|
  << H_J U^epsilon (D/NL)^(beta/2) Y^((1-beta)/2).    (3.2)

This holds also at every bounded nonempty subunit scale; empty sums are zero.
The range beta<1 is essential to the displayed positive Y cost. Divisor,
ray and dyadic losses are allocated within epsilon before U. The exponent
cost in the SQUARED norm is Y^(1-beta), not twice that exponent again.

Recall the literal previous source split B=B_g+B_s+B_c, where B_g has
N(a,b)>=G, B_s has N(a,b)<G and N s_2(b)>=H. Apply theta to each tuple BEFORE
summing. The old exact divisor formulas still hold, with S(D/NL) replaced
by S_(theta,L)(D/NL). Their L are respectively q, k^2 and lcm(q,k^2).
The inverse coprimality masks are restored by ALL q-smooth powers as before;
theta depends only on b and does not change that identity. The common-prime
valuation calculation for L=lcm(q,k^2), including all d=(q,k) above H, is
unchanged. Formula(3.2) has a uniform factor independent of q,k,L, so it can
be extracted once from the already proved absolute coefficient convolution.
No independence of q,k or p is needed.

Consequently, relative to that pending old proof, with F_j=B_j Q,

 ||F_g^[theta]||^2 << H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                                      G^(-beta)Y^(1-beta),
 ||F_s^[theta]||^2 << H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                                    H^(-2beta)Y^(1-beta),
 ||F_gs^[theta]||^2 << H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                           G^(-beta)H^(-2beta)Y^(1-beta). (3.3)

The second bound includes the entire weighted intersection subtraction,
F_s^[theta]=(M S_bad Q)^[theta]-F_gs^[theta]. Thus it is not a signed-subset
comparison. All mixed terms are paid by Hilbert triangle. Inserting the
pointwise loss before the absolute convolution is precisely why the old
G,H powers survive, including arbitrary shared-prime valuations.

Finally C=F^[theta]-F_g^[theta]-F_s^[theta] EXACTLY. Equations(2.6),(3.3) give

 ||C||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
   [ A^(-beta)+(G^(-beta)+H^(-2beta))Y^(1-beta) ].     (3.4)

At A=U^(2eta),Y=G=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), the three savings are

   2beta eta, (8beta-4)eta, (8beta-4)eta.

Since beta>=.68-small>2/3, all are at least2beta eta, with fixed reserve over
eta. At the limiting beta=.68 these are1.36eta and1.44eta. Thus

 ||B_c^[theta] Q||_Omega^2
          << H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon).       (3.5)

This is an actual estimate for the COMPLETE band-weighted residual, preserving
every ordered tuple and sign. It is not a new canonical-column assumption.

For comparison with a possible sharper upstream repeat-product cut, the proof
has the following precisely conditional interface. Suppose a removed source
has an exact divisor-block decomposition with the SAME shortened plain factors
and absolute MI coefficient mass O(U^epsilon T^(-beta/2)). Then(3.2) changes
its squared norm by at most Y^(1-beta). The corresponding core bound becomes
U^(1+epsilon)D^beta[A^(-beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]. If T=U^(4eta), the same
budget applies. This does not prove that product-cut premise, duplicate its
independent proof, or assume its acceptance. Our actual statement(3.5) uses
only the explicitly stated G,H core and retains its pending dependency.

## 4. Actual new rows and the entire surviving source

Use the old disjoint actual classes Omega_g,Omega_s and their full complement
Omega_c, on which |B_c|>|M S|/2 at the SAME zero/profile/height. Within Omega_c,
define the new actual row class

 Omega_band={u: |B_c^[theta](u)|>=|B_c(u)|/2}.

On this class |M Q|<=4|B_c^[theta]Q|/|S(D)|. Divide only by the original plain
spike(1.1), using the SAME beta before weakening to physical delta, to obtain

 sum_(Omega_band) w_u|M_u(R)Q_u|^2
             << H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).         (4.1)

Hence the requested eta saving holds after the freely chosen losses, with
reserve at least.36eta. The large-gcd and large-square dominance classes retain
their earlier stronger savings; their union with Omega_band is disjoint by
definition. No inverse spike is divided out in(4.1).

On EVERY remaining row, without selecting a fresh witness,

 |B_c^[1-theta]| > |B_c|/2 > |M S|/4.                 (4.2)

The new residual coefficient is exactly the old signed coefficient times

 1-theta(b)=log N(b_outside_band)/log Nb.              (4.3)

It keeps N(a,b)<G, N s_2(b)<H, all prime-slot tuples, common height, real power,
natural zeros and fixed holes. It vanishes if b is entirely supported on band
primes. Moreover no band prime can appear twice in this original core:
p>=A=H and p^2|b would imply N s_2(b)>=H. This last observation does not permit
discarding the higher powers from the full-source/intersection calculations
above; those were explicitly paid before subtraction.

The surviving repeat-factor bound is still N(n/rad n)<G H^2 N(P) from the
previous proof. No stronger repeat-product claim is imported. Both orientations
use the identical argument. All exclusions are exact at A,Y,G,H as written.

This is a real further restriction, not a complete row cover. For a good prime
ideal b with Nb on the original plain annulus, m>4eta implies theta(b)=0;
such a column survives unchanged. Thus neither a prime-density heuristic nor
pointwise0<=theta<=1 can remove the remaining signed core. No actual high-zero
row, nonempty dominance class or lower bound for the whole moment is constructed.

The complete coarse test is also paid: use B_c^[1-theta]=B_c-B_c^[theta],
the previous complete U D^beta bound for B_c, and(3.5), with Hilbert triangle.
The result remains U^(1+beta*m+epsilon); dividing by the plain spike on(4.2)
gives only U^(1+epsilon). Thus the full J_eta^all and the endpoint gain are
still OPEN. The new progress is(2.6),(3.5),(4.1), with the exact complement
(4.2)--(4.3), not this unchanged coarse exponent.

## 5. Uniformity and complete physical scope

The source buffer is unchanged: fixed finite conjugation-stable Theta, good
nonprincipal rows of conductor O_S(U), a selected i<ceil(1/e)+2 with
a<=B_i<a+e and B_(i+1)<a+2e, and beta=2a-1. B_j includes all dictionary zeros

Only the ORIGINAL unshifted plain spike is ever divided out. A separated

The new coupled profile in Section2 is separated on a full ambient compact
box BEFORE live p, c, slot labels or colors. Original scale/real/height
derivatives increase only finitely many common seminorm orders. The band

Independent original slot heights remain independent; the separation frequency

Finite orders and real/bin losses are chosen before the internal small height

Nonempty subunit scales are bounded profile dilations; the empty ones remain

Plain deleted Euler zeros are retained, not divided out; every displayed phase
is a contraction even at shared primes. Any logarithmic derivative of V_D has

The O_eta(1) prime-power ranges and fixed count of coloring applications do not

All claims concern actual positive child norms AFTER the old signed projector
reconstruction, with the actual full character and slot list. The row predicate

not doubled. All physical roots, missing radicals, extraction scalars, joint
labels, 6a/9a shortening radii, fixed-inducing K_phys^(5/6), old-only descendants,
short/empty slots and plain alternatives, principal residues, weighted Euler

The logical hierarchy is explicit: original MI and buffered plain estimates

The check does not establish the source moments, high-zero existence, analytic

statement:
## 2. The literal matrix source, including its characteristic polynomial

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, with its natural zero extension. For every real x>=1 take the actual finite divisor downset

    D_x={n<=x: mu^2(n)=1, (n,q)=1}.

Every divisor of an element remains in this set. Nonunits and nonsquarefree integers already contribute zero to mu(n)chi(n); excluding them changes neither M_chi(x) nor an endpoint convention. All matrix indices below are the increasing ordering of D_x. Let N=|D_x|, e be the coordinate of 1 and v=1-e. Define

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(n/d prime),
    P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.

No character value zero is inverted. The matrices B,P are strictly upper triangular. If d|n, the ratio n/d has distinct prime factors. A path of exactly k prime-cover edges exists precisely when omega(n/d)=k, and then all k! permutations of those factors lie inside the original downset. Their weights telescope to chi(n/d). Thus for k>=0,

    B^k(d,n)=k! chi(n/d)1_(d|n,omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z,
    exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).                  (2.1)

All exponentials are finite polynomials, so no limiting operator norm or analytic semigroup assertion is hidden here. Since det Z=1, the determinant lemma gives

    det R=1+e^T Z^(-1)v=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n).             (2.2)

The identity retains the closed cutoff n<=x and all ordinary natural zeros. It is the independently derived twisted squarefree specialization of the finite-poset construction. Wilf's Theorem2 supplies its classical ancestry, not the new arithmetic bounds below. [Wilf, pp.1-4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408263v1).

Let K=max_(n in D_x)omega(n). If K>=1, strict divisor chains give

    A_k=e^T P^k v=sum_(n in D_x,n>1)chi(n) k! S(omega(n),k),
    P^(K+1)=0.

Indeed a strict chain from 1 to n is an ordered partition of its distinct prime factors into k nonempty blocks. For y=lambda-1 and y!=0, the rank-one resolvent formula is

    det(lambda I-R)=y^N[1-e^T(yI-P)^(-1)v].

The k=0 resolvent coefficient vanishes because e^T v=0. Expanding the finite inverse, then using polynomial identity at y=0, proves

    det(lambda I-R)
      =y^(N-K-1)[y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k y^(K-k)].        (2.3)

At least N-K-1 eigenvalues are 1. The multiplicity may be larger if the twisted top coefficient A_K cancels. No full-integer exact-multiplicity theorem is imported. If K=0, D_x={1} and R=(1); this is handled separately. At y=-1, (2.3) agrees with det(-R)=(-1)^N det R, so the alternating chain sign is correct.

The product of j distinct primes is at least (j+1)!, giving K=O(log(2x)/loglog(3x)). This degree estimate does not bound the value at y=-1 or the product of the nontrivial roots. Vaughan's characteristic calculation is classical ancestry only; its full-integer spectral conclusions are not transferred to this altered support. [Vaughan, printed pp.283-286](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf).

# S04 development: overlapping prime removals and the complete correction

Status: source-exact overlap identities and quantitative return costs; no new signed estimate. This develops the strongest deliberate card after the protected Fock calculation. Existing [restricted research revision]/G81, [restricted research revision]/G92, [restricted research revision]/G108 and [restricted research revision]/G135 renewal ancestry is retained.

Fix a presented ordinary character chi modulo q and a finite set B of primes not dividing q. Write P_B=product_(p in B)p and

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    a_B(n)=a(n)1_((n,P_B)=1),
    e_B(d)=mu(d)chi(d)1_(d|P_B),
    r_B(m)=chi(m)1_(every prime factor of m lies in B).

The unit belongs to both e_B and r_B. r_B includes EVERY prime power, whereas e_B is squarefree. Coefficientwise, including all natural zero coefficients,

    e_B*r_B=delta_1,  a=e_B*a_B,  a_B=r_B*a.          (R1)

At a prime in B the first product is (1-z)(1-z)^(-1)=1; at other primes it is one. The factor of a_B at a prime in B is one, otherwise 1-chi(p)p^-s. Thus R1 is not a heuristic independence statement or an equation only on squarefree n.

For finite sets A,B the exact overlap invariant is

    e_A*e_B=e_(A union B)*e_(A intersection B),
    a_A*a_B=a_(A union B)*a_(A intersection B).        (R2)

Every common prime is counted twice. For Re(s)>1 let F=1/L(s,chi) and E_B=product_(p in B)(1-chi(p)p^-s). Then F_B=F/E_B and R2 is F_A F_B=F_(A union B)F_(A intersection B). All four channels share the same unknown scalar F. Therefore the exact rank-one overlap relation cannot by itself exclude a pole: multiplying every channel by any common meromorphic scalar preserves it. This is a SCOPED obstruction to using only the overlap invariant, not to a source-specific joint estimate.

## Complete fixed-block return

For any gamma>0, finite B gives

    sum_d |e_B(d)|d^-gamma=product_(p in B)(1+p^-gamma),
    sum_m |r_B(m)|m^-gamma=product_(p in B)(1-p^-gamma)^(-1). (R3)

Both are finite. If U is the fixed Gaussian or exponential field formed from a, and U_B the same fixed kernel with a_B, R1 yields

    U(x)=sum_d e_B(d) U_B(x/d),
    U_B(x)=sum_m r_B(m) U(x/m).                        (R4)

Absolute Fubini follows on a sufficiently right half-plane from the bounded original coefficients and the finite-prime geometric series; it also follows directly for these rapidly decaying kernels. Minkowski on the all-real-shell norm sup_(T>0) T^-gamma ||U||_[T,2T] gives exactly the two constants R3. Small scales have their genuine decaying tails. Thus fixed-block exponents agree, with the usual positive epsilon buffers; a finite block has no automatic exponent saving.

Every E_B is nonzero in Re(s)>0 because |chi(p)p^-s|<1. For a precise field return, take U_B(x)=sum_n a_B(n) exp(-n/x), or use exp(-(n/x)^2). Use shell norm L^2([T,2T],dx/x). If that norm is O_(chi,epsilon)(T^(gamma+epsilon)) for all large T and every epsilon>0, then the small-x exponential tail and Cauchy--Schwarz on dyadic shells make its Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma. For Re(s)>1 that integral is respectively Gamma(s)/(L(s,chi)E_B(s)) or Gamma(s/2)/(2L(s,chi)E_B(s)). The gamma factors never vanish in Re(s)>gamma>0. Multiplication by the literal meromorphic L and nonzero E_B gives zero exclusion there at every finite height. Principal poles and imprimitive factors remain in that identity. This supplies a complete return but no field estimate. If B varies with X, all R3 constants and all shifted-shell U_B hypotheses must remain uniform and be paid; one cannot take a different fixed-B Mellin transform on each shell. A same-shell statement at X alone is insufficient for R4.

## Exact two-scale localization and the coarse budget

For sharp sums M_B(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_B(n), suppose a single set B=B_N has min B>sqrt N. In R1 every divisor d involving two primes of B exceeds N. Therefore, exactly at every real 1<=x<=N,

    M(x)=M_B(x)-sum_(p in B,p<=x)chi(p)M(x/p).        (R5)

The inner source is the ORIGINAL M: x/p<min B, so no B-prime can divide its index. This is a useful exact localization of the correction, not a replacement by an independently favorable rough source. If B contains no prime <=x the sum is empty. At x=p the inner unit M(1)=1 remains.

Take fixed 1/2<alpha<b<1 and B_N subset (N^alpha,N^b], and assume a bound |M(t)|<=C t^beta for 1<=t<=N^(1-alpha). Absolute treatment of the correction gives the deliberately coarse but rigorous estimate

    sum_(p in B_N)|M(N/p)|
      <= C N^beta sum_(n<=N^b)n^-beta
      <= C[1+1/(1-beta)] N^[beta+b(1-beta)],          (R6)

for 0<beta<1. No PNT is needed. At fixed beta, the best limiting b>1/2 gives exponent (1+beta)/2, which is LARGER than beta. Consequently even an improved estimate for M_B(N) does not improve the current exponent using this absolute correction. Even GRANTING a prior beta just above the current source-relative .8748540364 leaves a correction exponent above .9374270182; that prior estimate is not claimed proved here. This is a bound produced by a method, not a lower bound for the actual signed correction.

If an independently proved small-scale beta were available, reaching gamma through R6 would require beta<(gamma-b)/(1-b). As b decreases to1/2 the conditions approach:

|returned gamma|c|necessary beta for this sufficient absolute method in the b->1/2 limit|
|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|beta<.74970|
|5/6|1/6|beta<2/3|
|3/4|1/4|beta<1/2|

These are deliberately coarse budgets for a source estimate that is NOT supplied. A purported 3/4 small-scale input would miss even the current near target after this correction. Assuming the final improved exponent at all smaller scales merely to pay R5 would be circular unless a genuine induction with strict contraction and initial data is proved; R6 gives no such contraction.

The signed opportunity is the FULL joint difference in R5 or R4. For the same shell, U=U_B-C_B exactly, where C_B is the whole restoration field. Therefore

    ||U||^2=||U_B||^2+||C_B||^2-2Re<U_B,C_B>.         (R7)

No component may be erased because one bound is favorable. R2 offers compatibility of overlapping prime removals, but its vanishing determinant does not force the relative phase or magnitude in R7 at the required power precision. For bivariate or multi-block formulations every overlap cofactor and ordered cross term stays in this identity.

## New content and next action

The R1/R3/R4 core is classical finite Euler-factor removal, already represented in the project. R2 gives the exact overlap invariant proposed by this seed but has no independent pole information. R5–R6 are the first decisive calculation for the proposed coarse two-scale small-gain route. Their role is to prevent a false improvement from dropping the short original-source correction. No broad rejection of cross-prime coupling follows.

The next useful estimate would control the complete signed prime restoration in R5 jointly with M_B, or derive a real contraction on a source-specific space whose norm already includes their relative phase. Existing independent-error and positive-norm failures do not close that possibility. The all-character/all-height return is available only AFTER an actual common gamma bound on the reconstructed original source.
