## 4. Development C: the signed tensor boundary can be retained, but rank is not saving

C01 overlaps the parked tensor-network seed Sol wave01 A34. The following exact test and priced approximation specify its unresolved step rather than recasting it as a new arithmetic theorem.

Split a finite set of primes into disjoint U,V. Let d range over squarefree products from U and e over squarefree products from V, using primes coprime to the fixed character conductor. The actual signed product-state matrix under a hard cap is

    T_(d,e)=mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e) 1_(de<=x).             (W39.22)

All signs are diagonal unitary factors. Therefore its singular values and exact rank equal those of the unsigned incidence matrix B_(d,e)=1_(de<=x). This observation does not identify any signed scalar contraction with an unsigned norm; the boundary vectors retain their phases.

For sorted d_i and e_j, put k_i=#{j:e_j<=x/d_i}. Every row of B is a prefix vector v_(k_i). Distinct nonzero prefix vectors are linearly independent: subtract successive prefixes to obtain disjoint nonempty supports. Hence

    rank B = #{distinct k_i>0}.                          (W39.23)

For the two-prime test d in{1,p}, e in{1,q}, p<q<=x<pq, B=[[1,1],[1,0]] and det T=-chi(p)chi(q), nonzero. If x>=pq the cap disappears and the rank drops to1. The arithmetic cutoff, rather than the local product signs, creates the boundary rank.

For the fixed Gaussian, the unsigned matrix K_(d,e)=g_tau(log d+log e-y) instead has full rank min(#d,#e) whenever its row and column logarithms are distinct. Strip out its nonzero row/column Gaussian factors; the remaining matrix is exp(-u_i v_j/tau). A nontrivial REAL linear combination of n distinct real exponentials has at most n-1 distinct real zeros: divide by the first exponential and use Rolle and induction on the derivative. A singular real evaluation matrix would have a nonzero real nullvector, so its n-by-n determinant cannot vanish over either R or C. The two-prime determinant is explicitly

    K_(1,q)K_(p,1) [exp(-log p log q/tau)-1] <0.         (W39.24)

Signs multiply this determinant by chi(p)chi(q), never make it zero. Again exact full rank is NOT a lower bound on approximate rank or a failure of every compression scheme.

Here is a constructive approximation retaining all signed contractions. Choose centers a,b for the two log intervals, write log d=a+u_d, log e=b+v_e, |u_d|<=U, |v_e|<=V, and w=a+b-y. The exact factorization is

    K_(d,e)=C(w) A_d(w) B_e(w) exp(-u_d v_e/tau),
    C(w)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-w^2/(2tau)),
    A_d=exp(-u_d^2/(2tau)-w u_d/tau),
    B_e=exp(-v_e^2/(2tau)-w v_e/tau).                    (W39.25)

Put Z=UV/tau. Truncating the final exponential after r terms gives rank at most r and the uniform pointwise remainder

    |exp(-u v/tau)-sum_(k=0)^(r-1)(-u v/tau)^k/k!|
       <= e^Z Z^r/r!.                                  (W39.26)

The signed scalar sum is therefore approximated by

    C(w) sum_(k=0)^(r-1) (-1/tau)^k/k!
       [sum_d mu(d)chi(d) A_d u_d^k]
       [sum_e mu(e)chi(e) B_e v_e^k],                    (W39.27)

with absolute error at most

    C(w) e^Z Z^r/r!
       [sum_d |mu(d)chi(d)| A_d]
       [sum_e |mu(e)chi(e)| B_e].                        (W39.28)

For the matrix operator norm, the same factor uses the l2 norms of the positive weighted row and column vectors by the Frobenius bound. Formula W39.28, rather than an unweighted Taylor tail, is the physical scalar budget. If that positive prefactor is at most exp(C_1 L), Z<=C_2 L and r=ceil(C_3 L), then Stirling's elementary bound r!>=(r/e)^r gives exponent at most

    [C_1+C_2+C_3 log(e C_2/C_3)+o(1)]L.

A sufficiently large fixed C_3 makes it less than -A L for any prescribed fixed A. These conditions hold for fixed-width O(sqrt L) log bins whose product center and physical y differ by O(sqrt L), with the actual finite coefficient masses bounded by exp(O(L)). Thus a polylogarithmic-size signed expansion can pay any fixed analytic power error in that bounded setting. This is a finite analytic compression, not a fast algorithm for its arithmetic inputs.

Every term of W39.27 is still a signed, moving-endpoint arithmetic moment of growing degree. When multiple bins or heights are recombined, their full cross Gram is required; bounding one moment or dropping off-block terms does not estimate the whole detector. The current W35 Gaussian/Fourier machinery already provides other finite analytic representations. No independent saving or additional paid sector is claimed for this representation. Its useful conclusion is that exact-rank growth alone is not the decisive obstruction; the exact signed contractions and their joint norm are.

# Combined support gain and the complete c8 endpoint

The [author](high-gain/report.md), [independent reconstruction](high-gain-review/report.md)
and [independent exact certificate](high-gain-review/receipt.json) are
frozen unchanged. Complete author and independent reports were read by

pinned PR9/Gao analytic contracts. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot
uniformity, exact external root-L-function definition binding and external

## G91: combine support and actual slot savings before optimizing

    k=rho+delta-1=delta(5-6delta)/[3(5-2delta)].

    E1 <= -(delta-4rho+1)m-kT-E-Bc <= -k c_s.

## 4. Removing the principal-root loss on its exact exceptional complement

If \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\), then
\[
\mathscr M_{\mathfrak r}^{(0)}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Y_DY_E}\,R^{-1/2+\epsilon}.
\tag{PH14}
\]
This statement is more precise than requiring all outer powers to be locally nonprincipal. Here is its proof from I-HC, retaining principal exponents at conductor primes.

Away from \(\mathfrak r\), use the original PC6/HC7 parametrization. The absence of a positive principal outer valuation there forces the residual sixth roots and the principal part of \(d_0\) to be trivial. A common nonprincipal exponent cannot differ by a nonzero multiple of six on the other side: equal forced valuations require equality in an unembedded pair, and require a difference of two at an unequal embedding. The latter is incompatible with coherence. The column/embedding exception three remains the original \(x^3,y^3\) factor; it is not discarded.

Consequently HC9 has \(f=r_1=r_2=1\). Its \(d_\circ\) sum has the actual nonprincipal weight \(q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}^{-1}\). Insert \(q_{d_\circ}^{-\eta}\), use the convergent Euler product, and pay the compensating power with the polynomial outer annuli. The \(x,y\) exponents remain \(3/2>1\), and the other square-root labels retain exponent two. The common-core harmonic sum is taken against both original rapid envelopes, uniformly in their two scales. This proves coherent mass \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{UV}\).

At a conductor prime principal outer exponents are still allowed. Regularize the outer sums by \(q^{-\eta(\alpha+\beta)}\). With HC4's exact Gauss size, the principal sum is
\(P_p=(1-q^{-6\eta})^{-1}\), the positive nonprincipal sum is \(N_p\ll_\eta q^{-1/2}\), and the completed-column mass is \(D_p=1+O(q^{-1/2})\). The condition \(\ell_p\ne0\) gives the bound
\[
((P_p+N_p)^2-P_p^2)D_p+P_p^2(D_p-1)
\ll_\eta q^{-1/2}.
\tag{PH15}
\]
The principal-only, zero-column vectors are excluded by the actual conductor condition. Thus the same fixed-radical product gives (PH14). Its finite local constants have subpower product; the compensating source powers are polynomial, and completed powers are absorbed into the original envelopes.

Apply (PH10) with \(\sigma=0\) to this restricted mass. The argument through (PH13) now works for every \(0\le\rho\le1\), with the factor \(K^{-\rho}\). The two choices \(\rho=1/2,1\) prove (PH7).

## 4. Multiplicative arithmetic and complex-height costs

The quaternion homomorphism M respects quaternion multiplication; it does not turn commutative integer multiplication into a noncommuting representation. A true multiplicative map u from positive integers (or from the squarefree coprime prime products used by mu) must satisfy

    u(p)u(l)=u(pl)=u(l)u(p), p!=l.                    (19)

Nonzero commuting quaternions all lie in one complex slice unless they are all real: writing a quaternion as a real scalar plus an imaginary vector, its commutator is twice the cross product of the imaginary vectors. One nonreal image fixes their common axis. Ramified zero images do not alter this statement for the remaining primes.

For the outer mu source, multiplicativity is only required on COPRIME inputs. One must still set the squareful coefficients to zero; asserting u(p^2)=u(p)^2 for the FULL mu coefficient would already be false. On its actual squarefree support, however, (19) forces the prime images into the same commuting slice. Thus a genuinely coprime-multiplicative quaternion lift cannot obtain arbitrary noncommuting prime rotations while keeping that source contract.

An ordered-prime word is an admissible DIFFERENT construction, but needs a new return. Already u(2)=i,u(3)=j gives i j=k and j i=-k; their difference has Euclidean magnitude 2 and N=4 at the actual squarefree output 6. Norms of the two products agree; their recoverable signed coefficients do not. Taking a norm erases exactly the order defect that scalar reconstruction needs. Repeated primes and the mu zero extension cannot be restored by that norm equality.

There is a further all-height issue even when coefficient quaternions commute in a different slice. If n^(-s) is represented in the user's chosen complex plane C_i, it need not be central in H. For example

    (j 2^(-s))(j 3^(-s))
       =-2^(-conj(s))3^(-s),                         (20)

whereas ordinary Dirichlet convolution would demand -6^(-s). They differ unless the indicated 2-height phase happens to be real. This is an exact obstruction to importing a real-sigma quaternion Euler product unchanged to complex heights.

The constructive alternative is the genuinely holomorphic matrix series sum_n M(v_n)n^(-s), with CENTRAL complex scalar matrices. Its entries are

    [[Z(s),W(s)],[-W#(s),Z#(s)]],
    Z#(s)=conjugate(Z(conjugate(s))),
    det=Z(s)Z#(s)+W(s)W#(s).                          (21)

Here multiplication correctly uses ordered matrix Dirichlet convolution in its absolute half-plane. But (21) is a positive quaternion norm only for real s; at general height it is an algebraic holomorphic determinant. The exact reflected companion and all prime-order defects still require estimates. This is a lawful alternative to explore, not a proof that all quaternion methods fail. It preserves the distinction root is recording between a holomorphic matrix construction and pointwise quaternionization.

## 5. Scalar return, certificate domains and all retained d

Let
\[
 \kappa_*=2\theta-1,\quad
 V=5/6-\delta,\quad
 D_\kappa=3-p-2p/(3\kappa),\quad
 B_\kappa=2(1-p)(1-p/(3\kappa)),
\]
\[
 c_\kappa=B_\kappa/D_\kappa,\qquad
 R_\kappa=1-\delta+\frac{\delta c_\kappa V}
                         {2(V+\delta c_\kappa)}.
\]
The required rectangle is the *whole closed rectangle*
\[
 0\le\delta\le3/4,\qquad0\le p\le1/2.             \tag{E4}
\]
For \(\kappa\in[7/10,3/4]\),
\(D_\kappa\ge85/42\), \(B_\kappa\ge16/21\),
and \(V\ge1/12\). Thus
\[
 J=VD_\kappa+\delta B_\kappa\ge85/504>1/10.
\]
This elementary lower bound independently justifies clearing the positive denominator.

The old general exponent is exactly the pinned B0.46/B0.55 ledger:
\[
 G_o(d)=\frac{1+\delta}{2}+\frac{13h}{75}
 -\frac y2-\frac\ell2+\ell q
 +d\left(\frac14+\frac{3R_\kappa}{4}-\frac{17}{50}\right)
 -\frac q{12\kappa}\min(d,2y-d).                  \tag{E5}
\]
On the near-endpoint local interval the final term is replaced by
\(-q(2y-d)/(2C)\). At \(d=h\) this reduces algebraically to
\[
 F_{C,\kappa}=\frac{1+\ell}{2}+\frac\delta2+
 h\left(\frac{3R_\kappa}{4}-\frac5{12}\right)
 +\delta p\left(\ell-\frac{h-4\ell}{2C}\right).    \tag{E6}
\]
The reciprocal is estimated only after the complete original w-inversion. No reciprocal estimate was inserted inside a partially reflected numerator.

I inspected local_moment_endpoint_audit.py and the polynomial helper source; I did not execute them. The script constructs \(R_\kappa J\), then precisely
\(J(\theta-\text{margin}-G)\), with the replacement capacity coefficient as above. It uses \(d\ge1/2>y\) only on the three certified endpoints, where \(\min(d,2y-d)=2y-d\) is correct. Its supplied records are:

| d | Physical coefficient | Claimed saving below \(\theta\) at \(\kappa_*\) | Supplied leaves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| h | C | \(10^{-7}\) | 18 |
| \(h-10^{-3}\) | \(6\kappa_*\) | \(10^{-5}\) | 6 |
| \(1/2\) | \(6\kappa_*\) | \(10^{-3}\) | 1 |

Each certificate domain is (E4), of area 3/8. The helper maps each rational subrectangle to the unit square, converts the polynomial to Bernstein coefficients, and verifies the recovered polynomial coefficient by coefficient. Nonnegative Bernstein coefficients prove nonnegativity on the closed subrectangle. Its coverage check requires containment, pairwise disjoint interiors and total area equal to the parent area; because a finite union of closed rectangles is closed, this also covers the boundary. These are the correct symbolic certificate domains and proof obligations. The controller's receipt identified in section 1 now confirms a successful exact replay. This lane checked the symbolic match and relies on that receipt for execution; a floating grid or these tables alone is not the certificate.

The continuation in d then works as follows:

- On \([1/2,h-10^{-3}]\), (E5) is affine in d; its two endpoint certificates suffice.
- At \(d=h-10^{-3}\), the local exponent is no larger than the old exponent because \(C<6\kappa_*\), \(q\ge0\), and \(2y-d>0\). The local exponent is also affine in d, so the junction and h certificate cover the entire local interval.
- The derivative of the local exponent in d is
  \(1/4+3R_\kappa/4-17/50+q/(2C)\). With \(R_\kappa\le1\) and \(q\le3/8\), it is less than 2. Extending to \(h+10^{-10}\) costs at most \(2\cdot10^{-10}\), leaving \(499/5000000000>9\cdot10^{-8}\).
- Below \(1/2\), \(-q\min(d,2y-d)/(12\kappa)\) is convex, so (E5) is convex. The d=1/2 certificate and the direct \(d_0=1/200\) bound cover its interior, including the kink at d=y.
- The direct bound uses \(a\le7/8\), \(R_\kappa\le1\), \(q\le3/8\), and drops the nonpositive capacity term:
\[
 G_o(d_0)\le\frac78-\frac{49h}{150}
   +\frac{7\ell}{8}+\frac{33d_0}{50}
 =\frac{573880513637}{750000000000}<\theta-\frac1{10}.
\]
- The floor classes use \(a=.51,\ R=1,\ q\le.01\), giving at most
  \(.51+h/3+.51\ell=.8598805351\ldots<\theta-.01\), before the tiny extension. They do not require a positive detector zero above the sentinel.

The feedback in \(\kappa\) is separately valid for old and local capacities. Under the contradiction hypothesis \(\mu=\beta_*-\theta>0\), take
\(\kappa=2\beta_*-1\in(\kappa_*,3/4]\). The old hypothesis \(2\beta_*-1\le\kappa\) holds by equality. The local proposition uses only the incumbent initialization, and no desired new zero-free conclusion is assumed.

Direct differentiation gives
\[
 \partial_\kappa c_\kappa
 =\frac{6p(1-p)^2}{[3\kappa(3-p)-2p]^2}<1/18,\qquad
 \partial_cR=\frac{\delta V^2}{2(V+\delta c)^2}\le5/12.
\]
Only R varies on the local branch, so
\(\partial_\kappa G_C\le5d/288<1/50\) on its range. Since \(\kappa-\kappa_*=2\mu\), the saving relative to \(\beta_*\) gains at least \(24\mu/25\).

On the old branch the reciprocal capacity varies as well:
\[
 \partial_\kappa G_o
 \le\frac5{288}
    +\frac{(3/8)(1/2)}{12(7/10)^2}
 =\frac{695}{14112}<\frac18.
\]
Here \(\min(d,2y-d)\le1/2\) and \(d\le1\) are valid throughout the old range. Thus its feedback saving is at least \(3\mu/4\) in addition to its certificate reserve. Applying only the local derivative bound to the old reciprocal-capacity branch would have been wrong; Gao explicitly avoids that.

## 5. Every error, zero and fixed-inducing contribution

Their nominal defect is at most `g+3a_j+w-w_o+eta`, allowance at least w. Use only the old global deletion price `1/6`, with the same actual-width correction. The three reserves are

## 1. Exact source and its quantitative return

Use the literal F08 arithmetic source

  H_sigma=L2((0,1),x^(2sigma-1) dx),   0<sigma<1,
  f_n(x)={1/(n x)}-(1/n){1/x},   n>=1,   f_1=0.

On 1/(k+1)<x<=1/k its value is (k mod n)/n. All cell endpoints are measure-zero and every later reciprocal cell is retained. The exact norm of a cell-constant F is

  ||F||_sigma^2=(1/(2sigma)) sum_(k>=1)
                  [k^(-2sigma)-(k+1)^(-2sigma)] |F(k)|^2.       (B1)

The Mellin functional E_s(F)=integral_0^1 F(x)x^(s-1)dx is continuous for Re(s)>sigma, with norm [2(Re(s)-sigma)]^(-1/2). Direct integration, initially Re(s)>1 and then continuation, gives

  E_s(f_n)=zeta(s)(n^(-1)-n^(-s))/s.                           (B2)

At s=1 the removable value is log(n)/n. No pole is discarded. If 1 is approximable by finite original f_n combinations in H_sigma, then a zero rho with Re(rho)>sigma and rho!=1 would give E_rho(F)=0 for every approximant but E_rho(1)=1/rho, a contradiction. This is the sufficient zero-exclusion return used here; no stronger converse or ordinary-character transfer is claimed.

The actual dormant dyadic extension SW34 in [restricted mathematical source] uses

  w_(2,n)=2 f_(2n)-f_n.

More generally for an integer q>=2 set

  w_(q,n)=q f_(qn)-f_n = floor(k/n) mod q on reciprocal cell k.

It vanishes on all k<n. Directly from B2,

  E_s(w_(q,n))=eta_q(s)n^(-s)/s,
  eta_q(s)=(1-q^(1-s))zeta(s).                               (B3)

For k!=0 let s_(q,k)=1+2 pi i k/log q. These are artificial common zeros: eta_q(s_(q,k))=0, because zeta is holomorphic at those nonreal points. In contrast eta_q(1)=log q. Thus the pole cancellation at the real point does not cancel the nonreal lattice.

### Finite optimization and interpolation do not pay that residual

Every finite constrained minimizer has all roots outside the closed
disk, for any nonzero F with F0!=0. If p=(z-z0)q, variation by zq
preserves p(0)=1. Orthogonality and strict Cauchy-Schwarz for qF,zqF
give |z0|>1. This is classical optimal-polynomial ancestry; see
[Beneteau et al., Theorem3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807), with the
present constrained version proved directly in the retained report.

For F=1-z/r the size-m Gram determinant is sum_(k=0)^m r^(-2k),
so d_N is the ratio of the size N+1 and N determinants. Its limit is
r^-2 for r<1 and1 for r>=1. Grams for r and1/r differ by a scalar,
and hence give identical constrained minimizers despite different
interior zero geometry. For the inner source (z-r)/(1-rz), the Gram is
I while Delta_N=1-r^2. Stable roots and conditioning are insufficient.

If the full error e vanishes at finitely many safe nodes, including0,
form their finite Blaschke product B, including multiplicity. Then
e/B is in H2 with exactly the same norm, and at a hypothetical source
zero w away from those nodes,

    ||e||^2>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.             (14)

There is no extra norm charge for dividing an error already in BH2.
For F=1-z/r, its finite Taylor inverse gives e=-(z/r)^(N+1), so exact
finite matching can coexist with growing full error. Fixed-anchor
amplification at height T costs degree of order T^2/(beta-gamma).
Other node geometries remain eligible only with a paid full residual.

## 7. Independent scale detectors and a new dilation construction

### F01.M — The fixed rational Möbius energy

Keep
\[
V(u)=e^{-u-1/u},\quad \phi(u)=(uV(u))',\quad
\Phi(s)=2(1-s)K_s(2),\quad
S_\phi(x)=\sum_n\mu(n)\phi(n/x).
\]
The fixed Mellin factor has no unwanted zeros in \(\Re s>0\). T09 proves that its dyadic L² energy suffices; no height-uniform reciprocal of \(\Phi\) is needed. Freeze the balanced decomposition throughout \(x\in[X,2X]\): \(Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/\log^2X\rfloor\), product windows \(X/\log^4X\) and \(X\log^2X\), and \(J=\lceil8\log^6X\rceil\). Complete Poisson cancellation precedes multiplicity truncation. The approximation is uniform with each fixed Euler derivative; changing floors during the average would require a separate error theorem.

**F01.N1 — New pass 1, separate the now-cheap diagonal from the actual energy kernel.** The exact target is
\[
E_\phi(X)=\sum_{m,n}\mu(m)\mu(n)K(m/X,n/X),
\qquad K(u,v)=\int_1^2\phi(u/t)\overline{\phi(v/t)}\,{dt\over t}.
\]
Rapid decay gives the elementary diagonal bound \(\sum_n\mu(n)^2K(n/X,n/X)\ll X\), comfortably below \(X^{1.74898}\). The unpaid object is the signed weighted aggregate
\[
2\Re\sum_{h\ge1}\sum_m\mu(m)\mu(m+h)K(m/X,(m+h)/X).
\]
Inserting the frozen balanced identity expresses it as four Möbius signs with coincidences \(\ell de=mfg\); preserve shared primes. Averaging on one log-scale octave does **not** confine \(h\) to a short interval: the kernel correlates a range of comparable ratios. Prove a gain for the complete weighted shift aggregate, or an exact partition whose complementary ranges are all affordable. A theorem for a few fixed shifts, or cancellation of only distinct spectral labels, cannot suffice.

Useful mechanisms are a product-difference dispersion keeping the short \(\ell,m\) variables, a low Mellin-frequency bound after smooth high-frequency tails are paid, and a rigorous comparison to the affine Green form. The latter comparison is presently open. Antisymmetrizing the two long factors kills the symmetric detector; removing an equal Mellin mode can remove the zeta pole being tested. Relative o(1) or logarithmic savings do not reach a fixed half-plane.

### F25.E — Triple-theta compact-profile energy

The true double-torus Fourier equations enforce equality of **elements**. Its Mellin identity is
\[
\int_0^\infty P_r(y)y^{2s-3}{dy\over y}
=J_r(s){L^{(S)}(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang})\over\zeta_K^{(S)}(s)}.
\]
T09 treats \(r\in[1,2]\) as a Hilbert-valued profile. Analyticity in r and the nonzero small-r limit ensure that \(J_r(s)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere on this compact interval. This avoids an individually zero-free \(J_1\), uniformity as \(r\to0\), or height-uniform inverse factors. The remaining theorem is TRI's signed small-y decay.

Keep the actual three-source correlation through a spectral or horospherical restriction and compute residual, continuous and cusp-boundary pieces. A fixed r-profile family may help annihilate a genuinely identified nuisance channel, but its remaining multipliers must have no common zero. Finite r-quadrature is useful only with explicit profile-derivative error bounds. A proof for a finite spectral packet is partial until the complement is summed.

A finite cube-deleted **trilinear** functional is an admissible structural child: it changes the functional tested in [restricted research revision] and could escape that particular linear-period obstruction. It introduces projection/level costs. Absolute inversion of the common angular cube factor stalls at \(a=5/6\) (A05); varying r does not remove this numerator. Moving below that threshold requires a changed completion or separately proved angular cancellation, not extrapolation of TRI.

### F08.V / F19.P — Affine variance and fixed-degree detrending

The paid criterion is \(\min_{A,B}\sum_{N\le k<2N}|M(k)-A-Bk|^2\ll N^{2a+1+\epsilon}\) for every integer shell. The exact decomposition removes the Type I density and leaves a signed hyperbolic four-factor Green form. At \(a=.87449\), the two long factors exceed \(N^{.437245}\), while the third is at most \(N^{.12551}\). High centered sine frequencies are affordable; the unpaid target is
\[
\sum_{j\le N^{1-a}}{|S_j|^2\over j^2}\ll N^{2a+\epsilon},
\qquad S_j=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mu(N+i)\sin(\pi ji/N).
\]
The lowest mode, including j=1, is essential. A06 allows every fixed polynomial detrending degree; growing degree needs new calibration and norm estimates. Remove only an actually identified trend. Compare its Green kernel with MOB or the modular-residue Schur complement before sharing bounds.

### N28.C — New pass 2: continuum dilations and overlap rigidity

A's discrete detector uses \(\Delta_bM(x)=M(bx)-b^\alpha M(x)\), \(b=2,3\), fixed \(0<\alpha<1\); its two multipliers have only the common real zero \(s=\alpha\), where zeta is nonzero. Their simultaneous near-zeros at large heights are irrelevant to the qualitative pole contradiction, but complicate quantitative estimates.

A new variation averages **b continuously**:
\[
\mathcal E_\alpha(X)=\int_X^{2X}\int_2^3
|M(bx)-b^\alpha M(x)|^2\,db\,{dx\over x}.
\tag{CD}
\]
T10 gives the conditional transfer \(\mathcal E_\alpha(X)\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}\Rightarrow c=1-a\). Its multiplier calibration is explicit:
\[
G_\alpha(s)=\int_2^3|b^s-b^\alpha|^2db
=\int_2^3 b^{2\sigma}db+\int_2^3 b^{2\alpha}db
-2\Re{3^{\sigma+\alpha+1+it}-2^{\sigma+\alpha+1+it}\over\sigma+\alpha+1+it}.
\]
On each compact real strip it is bounded below away from zero for \(|t|\ge1\); its only zero is \(s=\alpha\), where it vanishes quadratically. Under the same energy hypothesis this also gives \(|1/\zeta(s)|\ll1+|t|\) on every fixed compact real strip strictly to the right of a: the absolutely convergent Hilbert-valued Mellin transform is uniformly bounded, while its norm equals \(\sqrt{G_\alpha(s)}/|s\zeta(s)|\). The continuum therefore supplies uniform multiplier calibration. It does **not** prove a better Möbius energy.

The new analytic construction is to set \(f(t)=e^{-\alpha t}M(e^t)\). Then CD is an explicit positive weighted integral of \(|f(t+h)-f(t)|^2\) over overlapping finite log-intervals. Seek a source-specific overlap/Poincaré comparison with a power-law-detrended shell variance, charging endpoint intervals and weights. A general graph spectral gap merely bounds residual from the given difference energy; the arithmetic theorem is a bound on that energy. The cheapest useful test is an exact finite-window comparison, followed by one genuine signed cross-scale covariance estimate. A fallback uses finitely many dilation intervals with uniform width, still avoiding discrete small divisors. This is a changed quantitative formulation of N28, not an independent second proof of its cancellation hypothesis.

## 7. Uniform parked audit18: continuation of a state does not continue zero exclusion

The seed proposes a cross-ratio continuation chain for analytic value/derivative pairs. A simple exact example isolates the issue: f(z)=1-z, D0={|z|<3/4}, D1={|z-1/2|<3/4}. The disks overlap; f is entire, nonzero on D0 and bounded on both closed disks, yet its zero z=1 lies inside D1. The state(f,f') never vanishes because f'=-1, including state(0,-1) at the zero. Thus an invertible transfer of a nonzero two-component state does not ensure a nonzero first coordinate. For an analytic scalar equation, no determinant or state norm removes this distinction.

The logarithmic derivative f'/f=-1/(1-z) has the expected pole. Changing projective charts hides that pole in one coordinate but does not eliminate the zero divisor of f. A cross-ratio is invariant under an appropriate projective coordinate change; scalar zero location is a distinguished-coordinate condition, not the assertion that the projective state is defined. Mere overlapping charts, bounded Taylor transport and a nonzero start therefore cannot give the proposed unconditional propagation.

A correct local replacement is explicit: if P_j is holomorphic and zero-free on a disk and its boundary, and a rigorous source enclosure satisfies sup_boundary|F-P_j|<inf_boundary|P_j|, then Rouche gives zero count0 for F there. More generally it preserves the known count of P_j. The positive boundary margin is the missing arithmetic quantity; knowing only that F was nonzero on the previous overlap does not supply it. To cover a whole target strip, every disk, every unbounded height, all tails and every relevant character must have the enclosure and margin with the required scope. A finite mesh or a finite collection of checked disks cannot be represented as such an all-height proof.

For the actual ordinary source one may take F=(s-1)zeta(s), with its removable nonzero value at1 restored, or the correctly pole-cleared fixed L-function. If a locally finite disk cover of Re(s)>gamma has the stated enclosures and zero-free comparison polynomials, every point is covered and the actual source is zero-free there. This is a direct conditional return, not a new estimate or a transfer from a generic analytic counterexample. A pole-clearing factor must not introduce or conceal a zero in the region, and primitive/imprimitive factors remain literal. For the Gaussian reciprocal detector the alternative is its existing complete Mellin return; cross-ratios do not improve that input for free.

The finite example refutes only propagation based on overlap and nonzero state. It does not refute a paid Rouche cover, a source-specific lower modulus estimate, or a different coupled system with a proved scalar-output observability bound. statement:
## 8. Exact residual signed correlation and zero-exclusion return

There is now a particularly explicit equivalent arithmetic target.
For m,n>=1 and dyadic X>=1 put

    W_{tau,X}(m,n)
      = integral_X^(2X)
          g_tau(log(m/x))g_tau(log(n/x)) dx/x
      = (2 pi tau)^(-1) exp(-(log(m/n))^2/(4 tau))
          * integral_{log X}^{log(2X)}
               exp(-(t-(log m+log n)/2)^2/tau) dt.        (8.1)

This weight is real, strictly positive and retains the exact
finite shell endpoints. Absolute summability permits expansion:

    integral_X^(2X)|F_6(x)|^2 dx/x
      = sum_{m,n>=1} f_3(m)f_3(n) W_{tau,X}(m,n).         (8.2)

For clarity, that sign is

    f_3(m)f_3(n)
       = (-1)^[omega(m/3^{v_3(m)})+omega(n/3^{v_3(n)})],

where omega counts distinct prime factors and omega(1)=0.
Every positive prime power other than a power of 3 contributes
one minus sign, irrespective of its exponent. There is no
random-sign assumption and no averaging over tau.

The diagonal is O_tau(X). One direct proof uses unimodality to
bound, for x>=1,

    sum_n exp(-(log(n/x))^2/tau)
       <= 2 + integral_0^infinity exp(-(log(t/x))^2/tau)dt
       = 2 + x sqrt(pi tau) exp(tau/4).

Multiplying by (2 pi tau)^(-1) and integrating dx/x gives
sum_n W_{tau,X}(n,n)<<_tau X.

Consequently, for gamma>=1/2, the exact remaining demand can
equivalently be written as the one-sided signed estimate

    sum_{m != n} f_3(m)f_3(n) W_{tau,X}(m,n)
       <= C_{epsilon,tau,gamma} X^(2 gamma+epsilon)       (8.3)

on every sufficiently large dyadic X, for every epsilon>0.
The off-diagonal is real and bounded below by minus the diagonal,
since the complete moment is nonnegative. No absolute value
inside the sum, sign deletion, or restriction to a favorable
subfamily is permissible. The absolute double sum is in general
only O_tau(X^2), which does not supply a new exponent.

Combining a future proof of (8.3) at 1/2<=gamma<1 with the fixed
G_tau Mellin return in G1--G3 of `[restricted mathematical source]` would
exclude zeta zeros in gamma<Re(s)<1. A first improvement needs
gamma<1-c0. The present transfer supplies no such moment estimate,
so it does not increase the accepted constant or verify a theorem
whose main arithmetic input remains open.

The benefit proved here is structural: the full signed detector
is equivalent, above the stated threshold, to one original
coprime cell and then to the explicit bounded-coefficient field
f_3. The arithmetic difficulty is retained in (8.3). No novelty
relative to the external literature is claimed.

### B3. Zero-exclusion return and family scope

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q, take literally a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including its natural zeros. Its Dirichlet series on Re(s)>1 is1/L(s,chi), so direct absolute Mellin interchange gives

  integral_0^infinity F_a(x)x^(-s) dx/x
    = e^(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

The x->0 estimate in M2 used only |a(n)|<=1 and applies here. If(A) holds, the dyadic-shell estimate gives F_a(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for all x>=1. For every fixed s with Re(s)>gamma, choose epsilon strictly below Re(s)-gamma. The Mellin integral therefore continues holomorphically to that half-plane, locally uniformly on compact subsets. The Gaussian transform is entire and nonzero. By identity with the usual meromorphic continuation, L(s,chi) has no zeros there. The principal-character pole at s=1 is compatible with a zero of1/L and is not a zero-exclusion violation; zero multiplicity causes no cancellation because the numerator never vanishes.

All heights are included by the Mellin transform and absolute x-integrability on compact subsets; no height cutoffs or finite numerical height data are substituted. The H parameter grows only inside the estimate; the returned F is the original fixed Gaussian, so no moving transform is analytically continued. Choose tau,theta,e and the intended strict target before character, scale, epsilon bookkeeping, or data-dependent selection. Constants may depend on the fixed ordinary character and tau. To assert the result for every q and character, hypothesis(A) is needed separately for each such character with the same theta,e. No uniform conductor constant is claimed. This is ordinary Dirichlet scope; no Hecke, arbitrary number-field, or nonordinary Eisenstein extension is inferred. statement:
### 4.1 Periodic hyperbola induction with every overlap

For any fixed bounded periodic mean-zero b, set B_t(x)=sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n). For every fixed integer t>=1,

    |B_t(x)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t), x>=1.                       (4.2)

For t=1 this is bounded periodic partial sums. For t>1 let Y=x^(1/t). Every admissible ordered t-tuple has at least one coordinate <=Y. Inclusion-exclusion over these t events is exact. In a term with j<t designated short coordinates, put m=t-j and beta=1-1/m. Their product is at most Y^j<=x, so the remaining summation threshold is >=1 and the induction hypothesis applies. Bounding ONLY the designated short coefficients costs

    C_m x^beta [sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^-beta]^j
       <=C_m(Dm)^j x^beta Y^(j/m)
       =C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t),                             (4.3)

where D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|). The exponent equality follows from m=t-j. For j=t the product cutoff is automatic and the term is exactly (sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t, bounded by D^t. This last cancellation must not be replaced by Y^t. Every sign and overlap remains; real floors and empty initial intervals cause no error.

The resulting recurrence is

    C_1<=D,
    C_t<=D^t+sum_(m=1)^(t-1)binom(t,m)C_m(Dm)^(t-m).

Induction gives C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2: after division by this proposed bound and j=t-m, each summand is <=2^-j/j!, since m!m^j<=t!. Their sum is <e^(1/2)-1, and the remaining D^t ratio leaves a strict margin for t>=2. This is a valid explicit upper bound, not an optimality claim.

## 3A. Two actual large-factor sectors are also paid

Decompose the exact H9 form into the diagonal d=e, the off-diagonal sector gcd(d,e)>R, and the remaining d!=e, gcd(d,e)<=R, for a fixed shell threshold R>=1. Every sector retains the WHOLE b-restoration before an absolute bound. There is no inference from a signed-subset norm inequality.

For the diagonal the cumulative coefficient is

    sum_(d>Y,d^2<=x) mu(d)^2 chi(d)^2 B(x/d^2),

of modulus at most C_b sqrt(x). Thus its full Hankel norm is bounded by

    C_b integral_0^L exp(2(1/2-a)t)dt.               (H9a)

At a=1/2 this is C_b L; below1/2 it is O(X^(1/2-a)), and above1/2 it is O(1). Shared-prime squareful contributions were retained and bounded, not silently declared zero.

For the high-gcd sector, writing d=gu,e=gv and dropping restrictions only inside a positive count gives

    #{d,e:de<=x,gcd(d,e)>R}
      <=sum_(g>R) #{u,v:uv<=x/g^2}
      <=x(1+log x)sum_(g>R)g^-2
      << x(1+log x)/R.

H6 and the rank-one exponential envelope therefore prove the FULL operator estimate

    ||T_(d!=e,gcd>R)||
      <<_(a,q,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R.                 (H9b)

This includes every ordered high-gcd pair and every restoration index. It is a restricted actual-source theorem for the integrated ordinary-character detector; it is not payment of a native H gcd sector.

Let T^0_(Y,R,L) retain exactly d,e>Y, d!=e and gcd(d,e)<=R in H9. The complete norm difference from T is at most the sum of H9a and H9b. The remaining genuine low-gcd signed interaction has not been estimated.

### F09/F11/F16 — Adaptive probes and mixed compensators

The retained object is the full positive **physical-field** Gram \(G_Z\), principal map \(P\), and growing nuisance map \(E\). Minimize physical energy under \(PW=p\), or use A04's calibrated separation in the true coefficient metric. Singular ranges and nullspaces must be checked before pseudoinversion. A-dependent weights remain open; the rejected A-independent componentwise construction kills both physical principal aliases. A frozen single-column toy can cancel its own signal and is not a viable test.

Try a small family of genuinely distinct A-dependent weights on two unfrozen completed classes; alternatively penalize expensive modes rather than annihilating them; or pair two different embedded slot patterns. In each case keep the mixed numerator covariance and subpower coefficient/profile costs. For embeddings \(D,E\), common rows are \([D,E]^2r\), while original rows are \(e^2r,d^2r\); quotient squares create moving cubic marks. Same-tuple subset supports are disjoint, but cross-tuples can overlap. Regrouping all marks was already allowed and still has completed length \(ZL\).

A derivative or additional Euler jet is admissible only after its principal residue is nonzero and its six valuation classes, nonunit zeros, repeated-prime levels and worst numerator witness are computed. Changing constants inside the old exponent certificate cannot raise \(c\). This cluster is medium-term: finite feasibility screens are cheap, but growing-family conditioning is the missing theorem.

statement:
## 4. Exact rational rays: successful cancellation, bounded reach

This was tested as an alternative to the self-containing square sum
S16. It removes the f_r fields entirely from its inner arithmetic sum.
Let (a,b)=1, R=rad(ab/3^v_3(ab)), and define the WHOLE ray scalar

    Ray_{a,b}(X)=sum_{d>=1} f(ad)f(bd)K_X(ad,bd).

At every p|R, exactly one of a,b contains p. The two coefficients
therefore give the exact local factor 2*1_{p|d}-1. Thus

    f(ad)f(bd)=product_{p|R}(2*1_{p|d}-1)
       =mu(R)sum_{k|R;k|d}(-2)^omega(k).               (S24)

This is true for every prime exponent of a,b,d; prime 3 contributes
nothing. Set nu=tau/2 and

    T_nu(y)=sum_{l>=1}g_nu(log(l/y)).

The original Gaussian product identity now gives the exact finite
divisor readout

    Ray_{a,b}(X)=mu(R)g_{2tau}(log(a/b))
       sum_{k|R}(-2)^omega(k)
          integral_0^log2 T_nu(Xe^u/(k sqrt(ab)))du.    (S25)

No positivity was used in obtaining S24--25. Its average coefficient
over one period R is the signed rational number

    c(a,b)=product_{p|R}(2/p-1).                        (S26)

In particular c(a,b)=0 whenever 2 divides ab. If R=2Q with Q odd,
the inner expansion can instead retain the prime-two sign exactly:

    Ray_{a,b}(X)=mu(R)g_{2tau}(log(a/b))
       sum_{k|Q}(-2)^omega(k)
          integral_0^log2 S_nu(Xe^u/(k sqrt(ab)))du,    (S27)

where S_nu(y)=sum_{l>=1}(-1)^(l+1)g_nu(log(l/y)).
Every k is odd, so the alternating sign survives d=kl unchanged.

For each fixed N, Poisson summation of the Schwartz function
t -> g_nu(log t), extended by zero for t<=0, gives

    T_nu(y)=e^(nu/2)y+O_(N,nu)(y^(-N)),
    S_nu(y)=O_(N,nu)(y^(-N)),                    y>=1. (S28)

The zero extension is smooth and flat at zero; each ordinary
derivative is a polynomial in log t times a power of t^-1 and the
Gaussian, hence rapidly decreasing at both ends. The Fourier tails
in ordinary Poisson and in its half-integer translate prove S28.
This is the same fixed-order Poisson mechanism already validated for
the W35 profile, applied to nu=tau/2, not a new analytic-tail principle.

It follows, uniformly when R sqrt(ab)<=X^(1-delta), delta>0 fixed,
that

    Ray_{a,b}(X)
      =e^(tau/4) X/sqrt(ab) g_{2tau}(log(a/b))c(a,b)
       +O_(N,tau)(3^omega(R) X^(-delta N)).             (S29)

The main constant uses integral_0^log2 e^u du=1. Summing S29 over
ANY subset of these coprime rays still gives an arbitrarily negative
power error after choosing N: there are at most O(X^2 log X) pairs,
R<=X, and 3^omega(R)<=R^2. In particular the COMPLETE sector

    (a,b)=1, a!=b, 2|ab,
    rad(ab/3^v_3(ab))*sqrt(ab)<=X^(1-delta),
    m=ad,n=bd, d>=1

has signed scalar O_(A,delta,tau)(X^(-A)) for every A>0. Both signs
and ALL common-multiplier values d are essential. A sharp truncation
in d would create endpoint terms; none is silently discarded here.

### 4.1 The first decisive size test

This exact cancellation does NOT reach the central primitive-pair
region. In fact its entire low-radical ray sector is already cheap
by a positive count, making it unsuitable as the main new saving.
For T>=1 and every s>1/3,

    sum_{(a,b)=1;R(ab)sqrt(ab)<=T}sum_{d>=1}K_X(ad,bd)
                  <= C_(s,tau) X T^s.                (S30)

To prove this, sum the common multiplier using T_nu(y)<=C_nu y,
valid for all y>0, and bound g_{2tau} by its maximum. There are
2^omega(n) ordered coprime factorizations ab=n, including every
prime power. Rankin's inequality reduces the desired weighted count
to T^s times

    sum_n 2^omega(n) R(n)^(-s)n^(-(1+s)/2),
    R(n)=rad(n/3^v_3(n)).

Its local factor at 3 is
1+2*3^(-(1+s)/2)/(1-3^(-(1+s)/2)). At p!=3 it is

    1+2*p^(-(1+3s)/2)/(1-p^(-(1+s)/2)).

The product converges precisely in the sufficient region s>1/3.
Hence with T=X^(1-delta), S30 costs only
X^(4/3-delta/3+epsilon), already below all three advertised near,
5/6 and 3/4 scalar targets. The stronger alternating-ray theorem is
real arithmetic cancellation, but does not enlarge the currently
unpaid region at those targets.

For the genuinely hard rays a,b comparable to X and essentially
squarefree, R sqrt(ab) is of size X^3 while the common-multiplier
scale X/sqrt(ab) is of size 1. S28 cannot be used there. Estimating
each divisor term in S25 separately loses the original signs and
returns an error of order one per ray, potentially X^(2+epsilon)
in total. Thus the promising next calculation is a JOINT signed sum
of S25 over those a,b (or equivalently S15 over balanced shifts),
not another one-ray periodic average. No such joint bound is proved
in this report.

The special ray a=b=1 is the actual diagonal; S29 gives its sharper
check

    Delta_all(X)=e^(tau/4)g_{2tau}(0)X+O_A(X^(-A)).     (S31)

It is excluded from the off-diagonal sector above. S31 is a constant
check, not an improved moment estimate.
title: 4. Exact rational rays: successful cancellation, bounded reach

## 2. Accepted inputs and the actual double zero

Use the already accepted input

    sum_(n<=u) mu(n)=O_beta(u^beta), u>=1,            (C6)

with beta=.8749 as the inherited calibration, or
`beta=.87488+eta<1` with eta>0 FIXED under the current written endpoint.
The source of (C6) is the accepted buffered Mertens consequence of the
written zero-free baseline, recorded in [private research revision] Gaussian S3 and used
with the current `beta>1-c1` in current-proof G33. Thus the current
choice depends on the accepted c1 analytic input; the old fixed .8749
already suffices for this entire report. Neither choice is deduced
from a bound for F, from E1, or from this late-complement calculation.
No boundary-line Mertens bound is assumed. [private research revision] Gaussian S3--S5
directly prove from (C6), with all valuations retained,

    A_f(u):=sum_(n<=u) f(n)=O_beta(u^beta).           (C7)

This is used for the actual unmasked CORE coefficient f(r). It is never
asserted for a roughness-masked source. Its proof uses the absolutely
convergent h*mu convolution at beta>1/2, not an inverse of the prime-two
zero: explicitly, `|A_f(u)|<=C_beta u^beta sum_a |h(a)|a^(-beta)`.
Every cancellation estimate for cores in this report uses that same
accepted input (C6). All constants below may depend on the fixed beta
and its Mertens constant.

For Re s>1 the exact Dirichlet series is

    D(s)=sum_n f(n)n^(-s)=H(s)/zeta(s),
    H(s)=(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
           product_(p!=3)(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.  (C8)

The h-series for H converges absolutely on Re s>1/2; the finitely many
small-prime factors are kept literally. Equation (C7), by Abel
summation, continues D holomorphically to Re s>beta, with its fixed
derivatives on compact subsets. Near 1, the source identity (C8) and
the simple pole of zeta therefore give an exact DOUBLE zero:

    D(1)=D'(1)=0,       D''(1)=2C_f.                 (C9)

Here is the constant calculation. At p=2 the local H factor is
`(1-2z)/(1-z)^2`, z=2^(-s), whose derivative at s=1 is `4log2`.
The p=3 factor at 1 is 9/4. Each p>=5 contributes
`p(p-2)/(p-1)^2=1-1/(p-1)^2`. Thus H'(1)=C_f. The coefficient of s-1
in 1/zeta(s) is one, so D(s)=C_f(s-1)^2+O((s-1)^3), proving (C9).
Prime 3 and every power of 2 are essential to this calculation.

The reciprocal moments consequently converge in their ACTUAL signed
order and satisfy

    sum_r f(r)/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)log r/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)(log r)^2/r=2C_f.                      ([restricted research revision])

They are not absolutely convergent moments. Their convergence and all
tail estimates below follow from (C7). Replacing f by absolute values
before completing them would destroy the two cancellations.

The prime-distribution input is the already accepted fixed-order PNT
used in [private research revision] renewal F9, itself pinned to [private research revision]'s primary source:

    pi(v)-li(v)=O_N(v/(log v)^N), v>=2,              ([restricted research revision])

for every FIXED N. The proof below uses N=8, fixed before X varies.
There is no short-interval relative PNT, moving-order PNT, unproved
Hecke input or new provider contact.

statement:
### 2.1 Fixed field and all-height return

For Re s>1, absolute Fubini and t=n/x give exactly

    Mellin(E)(s)=Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    Mellin(R_r)(s)=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)).

For fixed r>0 the latter multiplier is holomorphic and nonzero on Re s>0. The beta integral and Gamma's absence of zeros are independently supported by [DLMF 5.12.1](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12) and [DLMF 5.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2). These sources support the special-function facts; the arithmetic identities follow from the displayed coefficient calculation.

If, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X, the L2(dx/x) norm of the fixed field on [X,2X] is O_chi,epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)), then on any compact subset of Re s>gamma choose epsilon smaller than the distance to gamma. Cauchy-Schwarz makes its Mellin integral and every log-weighted derivative converge uniformly on that compact set. E is O(exp(-1/x)) near zero, while a fixed R_r vanishes for N<1. Thus the transform is holomorphic throughout Re s>gamma. Multiplication by L and meromorphic continuation from Re s>1 gives the nonzero numerator identity. At every L-zero in that half-plane it is contradictory. The principal pole at1 is a pole of L, not a zero; the transformed reciprocal cancels it. No bounded-height limitation, assertion of reciprocal growth on an unproved zero-free line, or unjustified contour shift is needed.

This is the established detector/Mellin route, also explicit in Sol04-D12 and earlier Riesz work. It is not a new hard-desmoothing theorem. Constants may depend on the individual fixed chi and modulus. No growing-conductor or Eisenstein/Hecke claim follows.

statement:
## 2. Exact finite prediction and every-height return

Let

    d_N=min_(p0=1,deg p<=N)||pF||_H2^2,
    Delta_N=d_N-|F0|^2=min||pF-F0||_H2^2.              (R6)

The constant coefficient makes the second equality exact. With
G_jk=integral conjugate(z^j F) z^k F dm, the norm is p*Gp; this fixes the complex conjugation convention. G is strictly positive definite and Toeplitz. The constrained minimum is 1/(G^-1)_00. Delta_N is nonnegative and decreases with N; positive definiteness alone gives no useful limiting gap.

If rho=beta+iT is any L-zero with beta>gamma, then w=(rho-gamma-a)/(rho-gamma+a) is a disk zero distinct from0. The residual has constant coefficient0 and takes value -F0 at w. The reproducing-kernel bound on zH2 yields

    Delta_N>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|w|^2
       =|F0|^2*4a(beta-gamma)/[(beta-gamma-a)^2+T^2].  (R7)

Therefore Delta_N->0 for EACH fixed ordinary chi at one common gamma excludes every zero at every finite height in Re s>gamma. There is no exchange of N-limit and a height supremum, and no uniform-in-q claim. The positive floor decays as T^-2, so a finite nonzero residual cannot alone certify an unbounded-height half-plane. No Hecke, angular or growing-conductor transfer is supplied.

### Independent completion: the criterion is exactly equivalent for this source

The classical inputs used here are canonical inner/outer factorization and cyclicity of outer functions. Their statements, including the singular-inner measure representation, are given in Garcia and Ross, *Model spaces: a survey*, Theorems2.12,2.16,2.20 and formula2.10. The following constrained minimization and source-specific boundary argument are proved here. [Primary source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5018).

For any nonzero F in H-infinity with F0!=0, write F=I O, I inner and O outer. The closure of polynomial multiples of F is I H2. Any limit g=Iu of admissible pF still has g(0)=F0, hence u(0)=F0/I(0)=O(0); I(0)!=0. Thus ||g||^2>=|O(0)|^2. Conversely, outer cyclicity gives polynomials q_k with Fq_k->I O(0). Continuity of evaluation at0 gives q_k(0)->1; rescaling q_k/q_k(0) provides admissible polynomials with the same limit. Monotonicity over all degrees therefore proves

    d_infinity=|O(0)|^2=|F0|^2/|I(0)|^2,
    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2(|I(0)|^-2-1).              (R8)

For an arbitrary bounded analytic source, absence of disk zeros is insufficient: a nonconstant singular inner factor still causes a gap. We now remove that possibility for (R1), rather than silently assuming it.

F extends holomorphically across every circle point zeta other than1: its finite Cayley image has real part gamma>0, where (R1) is holomorphic. The boundary zeros away from1 are isolated and form a countable set. In the factorization F=B S_nu O the outer factor is bounded by ||F||_infinity. The singular factor has nontangential limit0 at nu-almost every point, so boundedness of B and O implies F also has limit0 there. Analytic continuation consequently forces nu to be supported on those countably many boundary zeros together with1. It is thus purely atomic.

An atom of mass c>0 at zeta gives along z=r zeta

    |F(r zeta)|<=||F||_infinity exp[-c(1+r)/(1-r)].    (R9)

At zeta!=1 this contradicts the finite order of a zero of the continued nonzero analytic function. At zeta=1, put sigma=s(r). The literal Dirichlet series gives L(sigma,chi)->1 and therefore F_chi(sigma)~1/sigma. Since (1+r)/(1-r)=(sigma-gamma)/a, this too contradicts (R9). All atoms vanish, and nu=0. This proof uses the actual coefficient chi(1)=1 and the pole-corrected source, not a generic zero-free Hardy assumption.

Accordingly I is, up to a unimodular constant, exactly the Blaschke product over the L-zeros rho_j with Re rho_j>gamma, counted with multiplicity. Let w_j=z(rho_j). The bounded-source Blaschke condition and F0!=0 make the product below positive. Equations(R8)-(R9) give the exact census

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2[product_j |w_j|^-2-1].       (R10)

The empty product is1. Each nonempty factor is>1. Thus Delta_N->0 if and only if this fixed L_chi has no zero in Re s>gamma. Zeros on the boundary are allowed and create no atom. This adds the converse missing from the cautious author formulation. It proves no convergence rate or arithmetic estimate: the complete prediction target has precisely the original zero-exclusion difficulty at this source. Applying it to every fixed chi at a common gamma gives exactly the corresponding ordinary-character family statement, with no growing-q uniformity inferred.

## First cheap tests and their limitations

For a fixed h, the continuum prime density x/log x is transformed into

    x*integral_0^infinity exp(-L t-h/t)dt
      =2x*sqrt(h/L)*K_1(2sqrt(hL)),   L=log x.

This has only exp(-2sqrt(hL)) suppression, not a power gain. Taking h=A L
changes the model to exp((1-2sqrt A)L) times a power of L. This is an exact
continuum calculation. It is not yet a prime-sum asymptotic: a PNT remainder
must be propagated through B1, and a classical subpower PNT error can dwarf
this model main term. This distinction is an essential stress test.

The other inexpensive test uses a fixed baseline line b0<b<1:

    D_A(u)=(2pi i)^(-1) integral_(Re s=b) Phi(s)exp(u phi_A(s))ds.

Since Re phi_A(b+it)=b-A(1-b)/((1-b)^2+t^2), the high-height portion has no
uniform fixed-power saving. Gaussian damping makes the optimal coarse
improvement subpower, of the form exp(-C sqrt u), rather than exp(-delta u).
All heights remain in this test. The unresolved task is an arithmetic power
bound for the actual B1 field. The following sections give the complete
return, the finite arithmetic source with its tails, and the decisive
failure of this baseline-only estimate.

statement:
## 3. Positive norm reconstruction: where every label is paid

### 3.1 Complete core and mark projectors

Expand the entire original short-core function:

    h((g,g'))=sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f), |r_h(f)|<=tau(f),
    g=f b, g'=f b'.                                  (R9)

Fix t,f. Product perpendicularity implies that m,b are coprime
squarefree ideals, with all original restrictions on tm and fb.
In particular j=m b is a genuine squarefree quadratic column.
For a dyad T<=q_t<2T its containing norm range is

    q_j << N G/(T q_f).                              (R10)

Resolve the WHOLE original 1_(P,R)=1 projector by Delta|(P,R),
including its Mobius sign, and write P=Delta Q,R=Delta k. Retain
(Delta,Q)=(Delta,k)=1. The root becomes
q_Delta^(-1/2)q_Q^(-1/2). Rowwise divisor Cauchy over Delta costs
only a divisor power in the original polynomial range.

There is NO residual (Q,k)=1 projector in an individual inversion
term. Reinstating it would change the exact expansion and obstruct
the argument's asserted coefficient independence.

The fixed row multiplier is chi_k(tf)^3, including its zero.
Its modulus is at most one and its row restriction can be enlarged
only after entering the positive fixed-t,f,Delta norm. The combined
Delta factor is, explicitly,

    chi_Delta(tf)^3 chi_Delta(mb)^3 chi_Delta(tm)^4
       = chi_Delta(tm) chi_Delta(fb)^3.               (R11)

The equality uses exponents 3+4=7=1 modulo six and holds with the
original zero extension. This factor and 1_(Delta,fb)=1 are source-
only factors, independent of k,Q. Forbidden Delta intersections
remain zero until a legitimate positive enlargement.

For fixed Delta,f,b define the actual mark polynomial

    M_(i,Delta,f,b)(n)
       = sum_Q u_i(Delta Q)/sqrt(q_Q)
               1_(Delta Q,fb)=1 chi_Q(n)^4,          (R12)

with all original P=Delta Q supports and (Delta,Q)=1 in its
coefficient. Its coefficient square mass is at most

    q_Delta Omega_(i,Delta),
    Omega_(i,Delta)=sum_(Delta|P)|u_i(P)|^2/q_P.       (R13)

This is the crucial mark bookkeeping: chi_Q(t)^4 is combined
with chi_Q(m)^4 into chi_Q(tm)^4, including zeros. It is not
discarded or left as a t-dependent coefficient when t is summed.

### 3.2 Quadratic sieve with t fixed

After the specified common profile separation, the fixed-t,f,Delta
row sum has the form, up to its fixed row multiplier,

    sum_(j sf) chi_k(j)^3
       sum_(mb=j) c_(i,t,f,Delta)(m,b) M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm).
                                                               (R14)

The coefficient c contains the native a(m), xi(fb), exact b_(i,t),
chi_t(m)^4, R11, original product windows/masks, normalized profiles
and the norm-gap phase when present. It does NOT depend on k or Q.
Its bounded normalized modulus has only fixed divisor growth.
Thus the inner coefficient of the actual j is independent of the
quadratic row. M B2.24 applies with factor

    K/q_Delta + NG/(T q_f).                           (R15)

Only after that sieve, Cauchy over mb=j costs tau(j). It is not a
triangle over all m, t, or extracted divisors. The resulting positive
sum permits the bounded source factors in c to be discarded.
This is the first place chi_t(m)^4, C_i(tm), the native coefficients
and a unit far phase are replaced by their moduli.

For nonnegative weights w_t<=tau(t), the fixed-Delta bound for the
sum of fixed-t norms is consequently at most

    Z^epsilon q_Delta^(-1)
       (K/q_Delta+NG/(T q_f))
       sum_(t~T,m,b original) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm)|^2. (R16)

The weights w_t, |b_(i,t)(m)|^2 and tau(j) have separate small-power
allowances. They are each bounded by fixed divisor powers in the
retained polynomial ranges. This suppression costs no T power.

### 3.3 Sum t only now; cubic sieve in the original n

At fixed f,b,Delta, the polynomial R12 depends on t,m only through
the original product n=tm. All its COEFFICIENTS are independent
of n,t,k. Since t is a divisor of the same squarefree n,

    sum_(t~T,m original) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm)|^2
       <= Z^epsilon sum_(n sf,q_n<<N) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(n)|^2
       << Z^epsilon S(N,L/q_Delta) q_Delta Omega_(i,Delta).
                                                               (R17)

The second inequality is precisely the accepted cubic sieve M
B2.25 with one coefficient vector for the live n. Any remaining
source-only constraints are enlarged only in the first positive
inequality. The same reasoning retains fixed arbitrary V_i because
their exact contribution was R7 and was bounded only after R14.

There is no O(T) multiplicity: for a fixed n, t|n yields only
tau(n) possibilities. There is no moving quadratic-row coefficient:
k has already been removed before R17. A separate cubic bound of
length N/T for each t would generally waste a T-label or mark
factor, but it is not the argument in either frozen source.

There are O_orig(G/q_f) possible b, with empty and bounded quotient
ranges interpreted as in JPS. Multiplying R17 into R16 cancels
q_Delta against the squared original mark root. Finally

    sum_Delta Omega_(i,Delta)
       <= sum_P tau(P)|u_i(P)|^2/q_P
       << Z^epsilon Omega_i.                         (R18)

Replacing K/q_Delta by K and S(N,L/q_Delta) by S(N,L) increases
the positive bound. We have therefore proved

    sum_(t~T) |r_w(t)| sum_(R original) |V_(i,t,f)(R)|^2
       << Z^epsilon (G/q_f)
          (K+NG/(T q_f)) S(N,L) Omega_i,              (R19)

where V is the literal fixed-t,f vector R8, including its independent
norm phase. This is BGC10/HA11, with the profile envelopes temporarily
normalized as in the accepted JPS proof.

### 3.4 Return to the complex paired scalar

Cauchy is applied between the two original arrays in the positive
joint measure (t,R) weighted by |r_w(t)|. The exact signed/complex
r_w and r_h were present before this upper bound; no PSD assertion
about their original pair masks is needed.

Summing the complete f inversion in R9 uses

    sum_(q_f<<G) tau(f)/q_f << (log(2G))^O(1),
    sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2 < infinity.                   (R20)

The resulting one-T-dyad bound is

    Z^epsilon G(K+NG/T) S(N,L)
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                (R21)

All contributing t have q_t>=U. Use a first dyad [U,2U), then
successive doubled ranges. The K terms cost only the number of
nonempty dyads, O(log Z), while sum_T 1/T=O(1/U). This proves R5.

No equality of the two divisor cells was used. One may either sum
their O(log^2 Z) ordered pairs or use V_1=V_2=all directly in R7.
The latter shows explicitly that the complete selected cross-cell
covariance has the same bound. Cross terms have not been inferred
from an estimate on a diagonal cell.

statement:
### Disk lemma

Let `g` be holomorphic near the closed disk `Omega=D(c,R)`, with `m=|g(c)|>0` and `M>=sup_Omega |g|`. Suppose `D(z,r)` lies in `Omega`, and `U` is a holomorphic map near the smaller closed disk into a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Then
\[
\|U(z)\|^2\le
M^{-2}(M/m)^{2R^2/r^2}
\frac1{\pi r^2}\int_{D(z,r)}\|g(w)U(w)\|^2\,dA(w).
\tag{T01.1}
\]
The constant is independent of the vector dimension.

**Proof.** Put `u=log(M/|g|)`. It is nonnegative and locally integrable, including at zeros of `g`. The submean inequality for `log|g|`, integrated over radii about `c`, gives
\[
\int_\Omega u\,dA\le\pi R^2\log(M/m).
\]
If `U(z)=0` the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise choose a unit linear functional `ell` with `|ell(U(z))|=||U(z)||`. The logarithmic submean inequality for `ell(U)` gives
\[
\log\|U(z)\|^2
\le \operatorname{Avg}_{D(z,r)}\log\|gU\|^2
-2\log M+2\operatorname{Avg}_{D(z,r)}u.
\]
Use the preceding integral bound and concavity of logarithm, then exponentiate. Discrete zeros are harmless for the area integrals; the scalar identically-zero case cannot occur under the choice of `ell`. This proves the assertion without division at a zero. ∎
