# [private research revision]: a short-row gain for the actual nonprincipal Möbius energy

10 October 2026 UTC. Independent mathematical reviewer: c22_formal_interfaces.
Reviewed source SHA-256: 5a5f779431ac083fe1be4dd84b55ee21e0ebf60152fda82178f39c9c96d2d80b.
Review/confirmation SHA-256: 7cd0e155f7725ec3661b4d401967583aec3d49a2d616028417afaa22aff75fb0.
Canonical changes are metadata and repository-link relocation only; the
accepted formulas and their input scopes are preserved. No increase in c
is claimed.

10 October 2026 UTC. Proof by c21_forced_rows, **independently accepted after the fixed-cutoff and maximal-scale repairs**. The new bound is relative to the inherited UM estimate and its finite-seminorm uniformity. It uses the original Möbius coefficients, fixed character presentation, all natural zeros, every unit and prime power, and the full Schwartz row weight. No new I-HECKE input is needed for this bound. The earlier removal of the principal sector remains relative to its explicitly stated fixed principal Dedekind input.

The conclusion is a power improvement for the all-row short moment:
\[
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{np}}(D,H_G;W)
\ll_{\nu,S,I,\Phi,\epsilon}
D^\epsilon\left(H_G+H_G^{1/6}D^{5/6}\right)
\|W\|_{C^J(I)}^2 .
\tag{NP1}
\]
At \(H_G=D^{99/100}\) this is \(D^{599/600+\epsilon}\), a \(D^{-1/600}\) gain over positive enlargement to a D-sized row ball. It still exceeds the requested \(H_GD^\epsilon\) by \(D^{1/120}\). It does not prove GS22, the full covariance estimate, the hybrid hypothesis (H), or any increase beyond \(c_0\). In particular, Guo's \(c=47/375\) remains conditional.

Repair provenance: the original candidate remains unchanged in [restricted provenance path] mathematical source] at SHA256 E43DE3D95D13466A711E06C98F8FB3969320CCF56B9656FF1C6872DF541DDD5A. The independent review by c22_formal_interfaces, guo-nonprincipal-review.md at SHA256 A08CC232D81D68F0AA18C9FECF401EB83DF1F553E9058034F47CCCAA27A433DC, requested exactly the fixed-cutoff restoration R1 and the scale-maximal iteration justification R2 recorded below. The estimate and its remaining deficit are unchanged.

The original candidate, independent review and repaired source are retained separately as immutable evidence. This canonical record includes the accepted R1/R2 repairs.

## 1. Sources, exact family and scope

Write M for zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md, reviewed here at SHA256 5F36C63D15A8EC9BD677D534E3F3CBC65D10053BCB33253BF46DEAE3009CCC6C. The exact inputs are M B0.7 (finite forward reconstruction), B0.8 (the scale-maximal consequence of UM), B0.9 (its sixth-power-free application), and B3.39 (UM with original coefficients and finite profile orders). The marked analogue is M S.8–S.10; it is not needed below.

The target family and the principal-sector reduction are [restricted mathematical source] GS5–GS6 and GS10–GS22, reviewed here at SHA256 A9FF02E405968885343CFC621E7AACCBA200761C21BFD1276ED7477F99BD2EF0. Its external primary-source version is pinned there. This packet does not revalidate the external paper's full theorem.

Let \(K=\mathbb Q(\omega)\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[\omega]\), and \(q_{\mathfrak a}=N\mathfrak a\). Fix exactly the datum of GS5: a finite-order ray character \(\nu\) with its entire zero-extended presentation; a finite S containing its defining-modulus support and the primes above 6; \(I=[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)\); and the fixed nonnegative radial Schwartz majorant \(\Phi\). Define the multiplicative ideal function
\[
\psi_v(n)=\mathbf1_{(n,S)=1}\nu(n)\chi_n(v),\qquad
M_v(E;W)=E^{-1/2}\sum_n\mu_K(n)\psi_v(n)W(q_n/E).
\tag{NP2}
\]
The fixed S-deletion is part of this presentation. Ideal columns occur once. Element rows retain all six units, all fixed-prime powers and all good-prime powers. Integer character powers retain nonunit zeros. Set
\[
\mathcal R_\nu=\{v\ne0:\psi_v^*\ne1\},\qquad
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{np}}(D,H_G;W)
=\sum_{v\in\mathcal R_\nu}\Phi(q_v/H_G)|M_v(D;W)|^2 .
\tag{NP3}
\]
The assertion NP1 holds uniformly for all \(D\ge2\), \(D^{99/100}\le H_G\le D^{101/100}\), and all \(W\in C_c^\infty(I)\), with one finite \(J=J(\nu,S,I,\Phi,\epsilon)\) and a datum-dependent constant. The proof also bounds the full nonzero row family with the same right side.

Every use of UM has fixed data. The preliminary finite restoration R1 below transfers M's optional larger fixed cutoff back to the original \(\nu,S\); the original Guo S is never changed. No moving primitive character or row-dependent mask is supplied as fixed datum. The subsequent new arithmetic operation is an exact inverse deletion, followed by contractions in a row Hilbert space.

## 2. A uniform sixth-power-free estimate down to bounded core scale

### Fixed-cutoff restoration before applying UM

GS5 allows every fixed finite S containing the character's entire defining-modulus support and the primes above 6. M B0.1 additionally describes a sufficiently large fixed small-prime cutoff. One must not silently enlarge S in the defining GS5 polynomial.

Choose a fixed enlargement \(S'\) sufficient for the inherited UM proof, and let \(\mathfrak t\) be the squarefree product of the primes in \(S'\setminus S\). Freeze \(S'\) after the requested loss has been chosen, independently of all scales, rows and roots. Write \(M^S\) and \(M^{S'}\) for the two presentations. Unique splitting of a squarefree column gives exactly
\[
M^S_v(E;W)=\sum_{d\mid\mathfrak t}
 \mu_K(d)\nu(d)\chi_d(v)q_d^{-1/2}
 M^{S'}_v(E/q_d;W).
\tag{R1}
\]
The original columns and their zeros are restored by this identity. The multipliers depending on v have modulus at most one; their finite total absolute mass is fixed. Cauchy or the Hilbert triangle inequality therefore transfers UM and its scale-maximal version from \(S'\) to the exact original S. For positive scales below 2 use the finite-column bound. The same argument applies to the log-scale derivative profile. No moving prime enters the fixed datum, and all extra constants and derivative orders have permitted dependence on the original fixed datum and the requested loss.

If the intended inherited UM is already explicitly stipulated for every such S, R1 merely records its compatibility with the printed M convention. Either way it removes the ambiguity without weakening GS5's quantifier.

The needed formulation of the inherited amplification is slightly more uniform than writing \(D=U^r\): the core scale U may be bounded, so r need not be bounded. For every fixed \(B\ge1\) and every \(\eta>0\), UM implies
\[
\sum_{\substack{0<q_v\le U\\v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free}}}
|M_v(E;W)|^2
\ll_{\nu,S,I,B,\eta}
(2DU)^\eta
\left(U+U^{1/6}E^{5/6}\right)\|W\|_{C^J(I)}^2
\tag{NP4}
\]
for \(D\ge2\), \(1\le U\le D^B\), and \(0<E\le D\). The same estimate holds after restricting to \(\mathcal R_\nu\).

Here sixth-power-free means every prime-ideal valuation lies in \(\{0,1,\ldots,5\}\), including primes in S. All units are retained. There are only finitely many possible S-supported parts of such a core; they cause no varying conductor in the fixed datum.

For completeness, first take \(E\ge2\). Fix a small \(\vartheta>0\) in terms of the requested loss and put
\[
V=\max(2U,E^{1+\vartheta}),\qquad
P=(V/U)^{1/6}.
\tag{NP5}
\]
There are \(\gg_S P\) good ideals \(\mathfrak a\), prime to S, with \(q_{\mathfrak a}\le P\). Choose one generator \(\alpha\); \(\alpha^6\) does not depend on the choice, since every Eisenstein unit has sixth power one. The exact M B0.7 identity is
\[
M_v(E;W)=
\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak a}
\frac{\mu_K(d)\psi_v(d)}{\sqrt{q_d}}
M_{v\alpha^6}(E/q_d;W).
\tag{NP6}
\]
No condition \((v,\mathfrak a)=1\) is imposed. The original natural zeros prove NP6 also at shared primes. The squared absolute divisor mass is \(O_\delta(q_{\mathfrak a}^{\delta})\) for every \(\delta>0\).

The map \((v,\mathfrak a)\mapsto v\alpha^6\) is injective for sixth-power-free v. Valuations modulo six recover v's ideal and the quotient recovers \(\mathfrak a\); \(\alpha^6\) being fixed then recovers v's unit. The S-part of v is unchanged because the amplifier is good.

The scale-maximal UM statement used here is
\[
\sum_{0<q_w\le V}\sup_{0<F\le E}|M_w(F;W)|^2
\ll (2EV)^\delta V\|W\|_{C^{J_1}(I)}^2,
\qquad V\ge E^{1+\vartheta}.
\tag{NP7}
\]
It is M B0.8. It can also be checked directly: logarithmic differentiation replaces W by \(-W/2-xW'\), Sobolev on unit log-scale intervals uses UM for those two common profiles, and the \(O(\log(2E))\) intervals cost a small power. The subunit scales are empty below \(1/b\), and the remaining bounded scales contain finitely many ideals. All orders are fixed before E, U or any amplifier varies.

Averaging NP6 over the amplifiers, applying divisor Cauchy, and then using injectivity and NP7 gives
\[
\sum_{v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free}}^{q_v\le U}|M_v(E;W)|^2
\ll (2EV)^{O(\delta)}\frac VP\|W\|_{C^{J_1}}^2
=(2EV)^{O(\delta)}U^{1/6}V^{5/6}\|W\|_{C^{J_1}}^2.
\tag{NP8}
\]
Since \(U\le D^B\), E and V lie in fixed polynomial ranges relative to D. Choose \(\vartheta,\delta\) sufficiently small in terms of \(B,\eta\); NP5–NP8 then give NP4 with \(E^{5/6}\), absorbing \(E^{5\vartheta/6}\) into the displayed loss. For \(E<2\), either the annulus is empty or \(E\ge1/b\) and only \(O_I(1)\) columns occur, giving \(O_I(U\|W\|_\infty^2)\). This proves NP4 uniformly, including \(U\asymp1\).

The argument uses all rows on the right side of NP7. If one starts with nonprincipal cores, multiplication by a sixth power changes only deletions, so \(\psi_{v\alpha^6}^*=\psi_v^*\). Positive enlargement to all rows is therefore legitimate and does not replace a nonprincipal family by a different coefficient family.

## 3. Exact inverse deletion and its Hilbert-space norm

For any integral ideal \(\mathfrak a\), good or not, the defining zeros give
\[
\psi_{v\alpha^6}(n)=\psi_v(n)\mathbf1_{(n,\mathfrak a)=1}.
\tag{NP9}
\]
The exact inverse to NP6 is an infinite prime-power convolution:
\[
\boxed{
M_{v\alpha^6}(D;W)=
\sum_{\operatorname{rad}d\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak a}
\frac{\psi_v(d)}{\sqrt{q_d}}M_v(D/q_d;W).
}
\tag{NP10}
\]
Only \(q_d\le bD\) can contribute, so the displayed sum is finite for this W and D. Terms containing primes of S vanish through \(\psi_v(d)\).

To prove NP10 coefficientwise, multiply the original Möbius Euler factor \(1-\psi_v(p)x\) by \(\sum_{j\ge0}\psi_v(p)^j x^j\) at every prime \(p\mid\mathfrak a\). Their product is 1, which removes precisely the columns containing p. If \(\psi_v(p)=0\), both sides already have the same deletion and the inverse factor is 1. The constant term denotes absence of p, not an everywhere-one replacement for a displayed zero-extended character. Equivalently, the finite coefficient convolution is
\[
\sum_{\substack{d n=k\\\operatorname{rad}d\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak a}}
\psi_v(d)\mu_K(n)\psi_v(n)
=\mu_K(k)\psi_v(k)\mathbf1_{(k,\mathfrak a)=1}.
\tag{NP11}
\]
This identity allows shared primes between d and n. Adding \((d,n)=1\) would be incorrect.

For \(\sigma>0\), define
\[
\mathcal P_\sigma(\mathfrak a)
=\prod_{\substack{p\mid\mathfrak a\\p\notin S}}(1-q_p^{-\sigma})^{-1}.
\]
At fixed \(\mathfrak a\), apply Minkowski to NP10 in the Hilbert space of sixth-power-free cores \(q_v\le U\), retaining the nonprincipal restriction if desired. Multiplication by \(\psi_v(d)\) is a diagonal contraction because \(|\psi_v(d)|\le1\). NP4, with \(E=D/q_d\), then gives
\[
\begin{split}
\left(\sum_{v}^{q_v\le U}|M_{v\alpha^6}(D;W)|^2\right)^{1/2}
\ll &(2DU)^{\eta/2}\|W\|_{C^J}\\
&\times\left(
 U^{1/2}\mathcal P_{1/2}(\mathfrak a)
 +U^{1/12}D^{5/12}\mathcal P_{11/12}(\mathfrak a)
\right).
\end{split}
\tag{NP12}
\]
The first Euler exponent is \(1/2\). The second is exactly \(1/2+5/12=11/12\), because the shorter column scale remains inside NP4. Both products can be enlarged to all smooth d after taking this positive norm bound. The constants and derivative order do not depend on \(\mathfrak a\).

No theorem allowing only row-independent masks has been invoked with a row-dependent mask: NP10 is an exact identity, and the row-dependent scalar \(\psi_v(d)\) is removed only as a contraction after that identity. Every occurrence of \(M_v\) in NP4 has precisely the original fixed presentation and common W.

## 4. The sixth-root sum has only harmonic mass

Each nonzero Eisenstein element has a unique representation
\[
u=v\alpha^6,
\qquad v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free},\quad
\mathfrak a=(\alpha)\ {\rm an\ integral\ ideal}.
\tag{NP13}
\]
Here \(\alpha^6\) is again independent of generator choice, and v contains the actual unit. Division of every valuation by six proves existence and uniqueness. Arbitrarily high S-valuations are included in \(\mathfrak a\). Moreover \(\psi_u^*=\psi_v^*\), so the nonprincipal restriction is constant along each sixth-power family.

For a row ball \(0<q_u\le R\), its cores satisfy \(q_v\le U_{\mathfrak a}=R/q_{\mathfrak a}^6\), and \(q_{\mathfrak a}\le R^{1/6}\). Squaring NP12 and summing these disjoint families gives
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{\substack{0<q_u\le R\\u\in\mathcal R_\nu}}|M_u(D;W)|^2
\ll &(2DR)^\eta\|W\|_{C^J}^2\\
&\times\left[
R\sum_{\mathfrak a}\frac{\mathcal P_{1/2}(\mathfrak a)^2}{q_{\mathfrak a}^6}
+R^{1/6}D^{5/6}
 \sum_{q_{\mathfrak a}\le R^{1/6}}
 \frac{\mathcal P_{11/12}(\mathfrak a)^2}{q_{\mathfrak a}}
\right].
\end{split}
\tag{NP14}
\]
This holds for \(1\le R\le D^B\), for any fixed B. The first series converges: its local factor is
\(1+(1-q_p^{-1/2})^{-2}q_p^{-6}/(1-q_p^{-6})=1+O(q_p^{-6})\), with fixed small-prime constants.

The second sum costs only \(\log(2R)\), not a small power per root. For any fixed \(\sigma>0\), put
\[
b_\sigma(p)=(1-q_p^{-\sigma})^{-2}-1,\qquad
b_\sigma(p^j)=0\quad(j\ge2),
\]
extend multiplicatively on good ideals, and put \(b_\sigma(p)=0\) at primes in S. Then \(b_\sigma\ge0\),
\(\mathcal P_\sigma(\mathfrak a)^2=\sum_{d\mid\mathfrak a}b_\sigma(d)\), and
\[
\sum_d\frac{b_\sigma(d)}{q_d}
=\prod_{p\notin S}\left(1+\frac{b_\sigma(p)}{q_p}\right)<\infty
\]
because \(b_\sigma(p)=O_\sigma(q_p^{-\sigma})\). Using the ideal harmonic bound therefore proves
\[
\sum_{q_{\mathfrak a}\le A}\frac{\mathcal P_\sigma(\mathfrak a)^2}{q_{\mathfrak a}}
=\sum_{q_d\le A}\frac{b_\sigma(d)}{q_d}
  \sum_{q_m\le A/q_d}\frac1{q_m}
\ll_{\sigma,K,S}\log(2A).
\tag{NP15}
\]
This prices the root sum without moving any prime into the fixed datum. Combining NP14–NP15 yields
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{\substack{0<q_u\le R\\u\in\mathcal R_\nu}}|M_u(D;W)|^2
\ll (2DR)^\eta
\left[R+R^{1/6}D^{5/6}\log(2R)\right]\|W\|_{C^J}^2,
\quad 1\le R\le D^B .
}
\tag{NP16}
\]
The identical proof without the nonprincipal restriction gives NP16 for all nonzero rows. The first term has summable root mass; the second has harmonic root mass. Replacing the latter by an ambient root count would lose the claimed gain.

## 5. Original Schwartz weight, all tails and fixed-datum uniformity

Apply NP16 to the ball \(q_u\le H_G\) and to dyadic balls containing the shells \(2^jH_G<q_u\le2^{j+1}H_G\), as long as their radii are at most \(D^2\). Bound a final partial shell ending at \(D^2\) by NP16 at radius \(D^2\). The bound
\(\Phi(t)\ll_{\Phi,N}(1+t)^{-N}\), with a fixed sufficiently large N, makes both shell series converge. Choose the intermediate loss \(\eta\) sufficiently small in terms of the final \(\epsilon\); since these radii are at most \(D^2\), all losses and logarithms are absorbed in \(D^\epsilon\).

For the remaining infinite tail \(q_u>D^2\), use the actual coefficient bound
\[
|M_u(D;W)|^2\ll_I D\|W\|_\infty^2.
\]
Ideal counting proves this uniformly in u, since the column annulus has \(O_I(D)\) ideals and every coefficient has modulus at most one. Two-dimensional lattice counting on a shell of radius R gives \(O(R)\) element rows. Its weighted contribution is at most
\[
C_{\Phi,N,I}D\,R(R/H_G)^{-N}\|W\|_\infty^2 .
\]
Summing shells beyond \(D^2\), and using \(H_G\le D^{101/100}\), bounds this by
\[
O_{\Phi,N,I}\!\left(D^{\,3-(99/100)N}\|W\|_\infty^2\right).
\tag{NP17}
\]
For example \(N=6\) gives \(D^{-147/50}\), which is negligible against NP1. Thus no UM estimate is used outside its fixed polynomial range, and no Schwartz tail is discarded without a bound.

This proves NP1. The compact Fourier support included in Guo's datum is not needed for this deduction. Only finitely many fixed Schwartz seminorms of \(\Phi\) enter. The original W varies over all \(C_c^\infty(I)\) with one finite seminorm on the right. The finite order is chosen using the requested loss, then fixed before any D, H, core, sixth root or deletion divisor varies.

The zero row is absent from NP3. If the full GS5 family including zero is wanted, GS21 gives \(M_0(D)=D^{-1/2}W(1/D)\) under the unit-ideal convention. Its contribution is \(O_\Phi(D^{-1}\|W\|_\infty^2)\) and is absorbed in NP1. The unit ideal is counted once as a column; the six element units remain distinct rows.

## 6. Exact gain and a proved obstruction to a tempting iteration

For \(H_G=D^{1-\delta}\), \(0\le\delta\le1/100\), NP1 gives
\[
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{np}}(D,H_G;W)
\ll D^{\,1-\delta/6+\epsilon}\|W\|_{C^J}^2
=H_G D^{\,5\delta/6+\epsilon}\|W\|_{C^J}^2 .
\tag{NP18}
\]
Positive enlargement using UM gives \(D^{1+\epsilon}\) in this interval. Thus the gain is \(D^{-\delta/6}\), exactly \(D^{-1/600}\) at the short endpoint; the unpaid factor is \(D^{5\delta/6}\), exactly \(D^{1/120}\) there. At \(H_G\ge D\), NP1 already has the requested size \(H_GD^\epsilon\).

To justify the following iteration with actual rowwise scales, repeat NP10–NP16 with column scale \(E\le D\), retaining D as the ambient parameter in NP4. All row radii remain \(R\le D^B\). Apply log-scale Sobolev to this uniform bound, using W and \(\Lambda W=-W/2-xW'\) and treating bounded scales directly. The extra logarithms are absorbed into the arbitrary loss. Hence, for every fixed B and \(\eta>0\), one finite \(J'\) gives
\[
\sum_{0<q_u\le R}\sup_{0<F\le D}|M_u(F;W)|^2
\ll (2DR)^\eta
\bigl(R+R^{1/6}D^{5/6}\bigr)\|W\|_{C^{J'}(I)}^2,
\qquad 1\le R\le D^B.
\tag{R2}
\]
The same holds on the nonprincipal family. Apply R2 with \(R=UP^6\), for \(P\ge1\) in a fixed polynomial range, to the forward reconstruction. After division by the amplifier count, the two terms are \(UP^5\) and \(U^{1/6}D^{5/6}\), up to arbitrary small losses. Every finite repetition of this particular positive comparison preserves the latter exponent. In particular, the following calculation does not exchange a rowwise supremum and a row sum without an estimate.

The new bound does not improve the inherited sixth-power-free exponent \(e(r)=\max\{1,(1+5r)/6\}\) used in the existing zero-free certificate. This is not merely because no reoptimization was attempted. Iterating the same sixth-power amplification with the new all-row bound provably leaves its second term unchanged. Indeed, if a core ball has radius U and the amplifier radius is P, its image lies in radius \(UP^6\). Division by the amplifier count converts the new two-term bound into
\[
\frac1P\left(UP^6+(UP^6)^{1/6}D^{5/6}\right)
=UP^5+U^{1/6}D^{5/6}.
\tag{NP19}
\]
The second term is independent of P, and the first cannot decrease for \(P\ge1\). Logarithms and the allowed small losses do not change this exponent calculation. Every finite repetition of this exact positive comparison within fixed polynomial ranges stalls at the same \(1/6\) row exponent. This falsifies the proposed shortcut “bootstrap the improved all-row estimate through the same amplification to obtain GS22.” It is not a lower bound for the actual energy.

Two related shortcuts also fail at the actual coefficient level:

- Primitive induction alone does not permit \(M_{v\alpha^6}=M_v\). At a good prime \(p\mid\mathfrak a\), \(p\nmid v\), the original column coefficient \(-\psi_v(p)\) is deleted on the left. NP9 keeps this difference.
- The inverse deletion is not a sum only over \(d\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak a\). At a single prime, replacing the full geometric inverse by \(1+\psi_v(p)x\) leaves
  \[
  (1-\psi_v(p)x)(1+\psi_v(p)x)=1-\psi_v(p)^2x^2,
  \tag{NP20}
  \]
  with an erroneous nonzero \(p^2\)-coefficient when \(\psi_v(p)\ne0\). The full prime-power sum in NP10 is essential even though the original Möbius columns are squarefree.

To close GS22 at its short endpoint, further work must save \(D^{1/120}\) beyond NP18 while retaining the exact Möbius/deletion structure. The proof identifies the missing information: UM bounds the complete amplified row ball, whereas the image of the injective sixth-power map occupies only its specified core/root families. The present positive comparison supplies no additional energy saving for that image. A new estimate there, or signed cancellation before the amplifier Cauchy step, is needed. No such estimate is claimed in this packet.

## 7. Review contract

The substantive checks are: the finite fixed-cutoff restoration R1 to the exact original S; the fixed-datum maximal UM use down to bounded core scale; the exact inverse prime-power convolution NP10–NP11 including shared and S-primes; treating its row-dependent scalars only as Hilbert-space contractions; the distinct \(1/2\) and \(11/12\) Euler exponents in NP12; the unique all-unit/S-power decomposition and harmonic root sum NP13–NP16; the separation of the polynomial row range from the infinite Schwartz tail NP17; and the scale-maximal all-row estimate R2 in the fixed polynomial range required for NP19.

The new conclusion is NP1/NP18, with the exact remaining deficit and the limited iteration obstruction NP19. Source and document checks establish provenance and integrity. The independent review accepted the arithmetic and exponents subject to R1 and R2; the narrow confirmation accepted both insertions without further repair.

statement:
## G159. All arithmetic and frequency complements are accounted for

Split the actual d,e sum disjointly into d=e, d!=e with gcd(d,e)>R,
and d!=e with gcd(d,e)<=R. The last class includes equality at R.
The first has partial sum at most `Cb sqrt(x)` in modulus, so its norm
is at most `Cb D_a(X)`, where

    D_a(X) = integral_0^L exp(2(1/2-a)t) dt.

It is O(X^(1/2-a)) for a<1/2, equals L for a=1/2, and is O(1) for
a>1/2. This estimate does not treat chi(d)^2 as positive.
For the second class, write d=gu,e=gv and discard coprimality only in
the positive counting bound. The count is at most
`x(1+log x) sum_(g>R)g^(-2) << x(1+log x)/R`.
Restoring the complete B before taking absolute values gives norm
`O_(a,q,r)(X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R)`.

For the third class define its exact coefficient

    C_Y,R(n) = sum_(de ell=n; d,e>Y; d!=e; gcd(d,e)<=R)
                   alpha(d)alpha(e)b(ell),
    S(x) = sum_(n<=x) C_Y,R(n).

The observed kernel is `k(v)=exp(-av)S(exp(v))1_(0<=v<=log X)`.
With Fourier convention `hat k(tau)=integral k(v)exp(-i tau v)dv`
and `s=a+i tau`, direct integration of each atom gives

    hat k(tau) = [F_Y,X(s) - X^(-s) S(X)]/s,
    F_Y,X(s) = sum_(n<=X) C_Y,R(n)n^(-s).

Both the complete hyperbolic cap and the sharp endpoint term are essential.
An atom at n=X cancels in this expression, consistent with a corner of
measure zero. Nonintegral X uses its literal summation cap.
The estimates
`sum_(n<=X)|C_Y,R(n)|n^(-a) << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2` and
`|S(X)| << Cb X(1+log X)` yield
`|hat k(tau)| << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/(1+|tau|)`.

Split the entire full-line multiplier at `|tau|<=Omega` and its complement,
then reflect, extend and compress to L2(0,L). This defines Tlo and Thi,
with exact `Tlo+Thi` equal to the third arithmetic class and

    ||Thi|| <<_(a,q,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The low-pass kernel need not be causal; the full-line multiplier definition
makes the compression legitimate. A uniform full-symbol bound is sufficient
for the compressed norm, but is not necessary or equivalent to it.
A finite frequency sample or a rectangularized Dirichlet polynomial does
not supply the missing estimate.

Combining these disjoint contributions gives the complete comparison

    | ||Gamma[c]|| - ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)|| | <<_(a,q,r)
       Y^(2(1-a)) + D_a(X)
       + X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R + X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The original nonprincipal source obeys the same formula with b=chi,c=alpha.
No comparison with a different detector's native norm is asserted.

Choose `0<a<gamma<1`, `gamma>1/2`, and
`0<nu<min(gamma-a,gamma-1/2)`. Put
`delta=(gamma-a-nu)/(2(1-a))`, `omega=1-gamma+2nu`,
`Y=floor(X^delta)`, `R=floor(X^omega)`, `Omega=X^omega`.
Then 0<delta<1/2. The Type I exponent is gamma-a-nu, the high-gcd and
high-frequency exponents are gamma-a-2nu before logarithms, and the
diagonal is strictly smaller. All these errors fit below the target.
What remains is exactly

    OPEN-LOW: ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)||
                 <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma-a+epsilon)
              for every epsilon>0 and all L.

Parameters are fixed before X. The exponent gamma must be common to all
fixed characters; constants and onset may depend on chi and the fixed
repair prime. For these same cutoffs, the complete comparison makes
OPEN-LOW equivalent to the corresponding full-source growth bound up to
the displayed smaller error. Naming it does not create an arithmetic gain.

The following exact corridors use a=1/2:

| conditional c | gamma | nu | delta | omega | d,e exponent cap | ell exponent cap | paid exponent | open X exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .12515 | 17497/20000 | 1/20000 | 937/2500 | 501/4000 | 1563/2500 | 313/1250 | 937/2500 | 7497/20000 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1/600 | 199/600 | 17/100 | 401/600 | 101/300 | 199/600 | 1/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1/1000 | 249/1000 | 63/250 | 751/1000 | 251/500 | 249/1000 | 1/4 |

The first would improve current c11 by `10091/2500000000=.0000040364`
if OPEN-LOW and its complete return were supplied. Its required L-growth
exponent is .7497, below current .7497080728. All three remain conditional;
changing a alone does not save a power.

## 6. Complete adaptive core with the improved corridor

Fix gamma in[3/4,1), L=X^gamma, r_gamma=(6-2gamma)/4, M=X^r_gamma,
Q=p^3q, eta=1/(1000*6*Q), and B(n)=min(L,eta X^6/n^5). Choose tau before
x, with alpha=max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) satisfying (R2). It lies strictly
between0 and1, with alpha bounded away from1 for each fixed gamma<1.
Freeze U(n)=B(n)^tau and V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau) separately at each physical n.
The identity is exactly

    c(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n),
    Q_U(n)=sum_{de=n,d<=U(n)} a(d)(v*s)(e),
    S_tau(n)=sum_{de l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n)} a(d)a(e)b(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_{de l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n)} a(d)a(e)b(l).

This uses a*b=v*s; replacing the short source by the old Mobius short
source would be wrong. If B<1 both short factors vanish and the literal
long-long identity is still retained. There is no cutoff endpoint at
tau=0 or1 in this corridor.

Each Q_U row is an exact shell-fixed root prefix because B(edr^2) decreases
in r. Apply (R1) to D=X^(gamma tau), keeping the two e labels separately
until their actual coefficients merge. Apply it again to Q_V. The norm
exponents are alpha,(3+8alpha)/11,3/8+alpha/4 and
min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4). All are <=gamma under (R2): for
alpha<=3/8 the last is <=9/16, and otherwise it is at most
(11gamma+12)/32<=gamma. Thus both complete short sources cost O(X^gamma).

The small-double source is pointwise O(X^gamma), using the actual zero-mean
b of period Q. For every ordered (d,e), the allowed l form the one prefix
l<=(eta X^6/W)^(1/5)/(de), with W=max(d^(1/tau),e^(1/(1-tau))) and
de<=W<=L. The nonzero Fourier derivative gap pays each row; there are at
most L rows. No alias portion has been erased: its complement lies in R.

The pointwise divisor bound |R_tau(n)|<=(p+1)^2 d_3(n) pays n<=L with
O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)). The complete inherited divisor-bounded tail
at n>M has squared norm

    << A_delta^2[X^((3/2)(1+2delta))+X^6 M^(-4+2delta)].

Choose delta after epsilon. Since 3/2<=2gamma and 6-4r_gamma=2gamma,
the tail costs X^(gamma+epsilon). Both orientations, the full real shell,
and its interaction with the retained core are paid by complete norm
inequalities, with no assertion of a small unconditional additive mixed
energy. Therefore the literal finite core T=sum_{L<n<=M}R_tau(n)f_x(n)
satisfies

    ||C_p,chi-T||_j << X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2,                (R11)

uniformly in the enlarged corridor and shell-fixed tau. This is an actual
restricted source theorem. It is not an arithmetic estimate for T.

The exact merged coefficient remains

    R_tau(n)=sum_{m l=n}a(m)D_{U(n),V(n)}(m)b(l),
    D_{U,V}(m)=#{(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V}.

Its ordered-divisor count, repeated primes, all character zeros and complete
cofactor sum are essential. Near n comparable to X the condition implies
m>X^gamma and l<n/X^gamma. The complete interval through M and every
far cofactor remain present. Complete multiplicativity simplifies a sign;
it does not estimate cancellation against this positive divisor count.

The resulting exact target rows are:

| Conditional c | gamma | r_gamma | improved alpha cap | allowed tau |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | 2187/2500 | 5313/5000 | 16557/20000 | [313/5832,5519/5832] |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 37/48 | [3/40,37/40] |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 21/32 | [1/8,7/8] |

The source theorem at these parameters is proved; the arithmetic premise
at each row is not. The first row would improve c11 by
135091/2500000000 only if its full signed premise were proved.

## 3. Primary imports and local proof review

Primary statements were inspected rather than inferred from the bibliography.

* [Katz, G2 and hypergeometric sheaves, §2, printed pp.3–5](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nmk/g2hyper62finalcorr.pdf): the disjoint-character convention, rank, irreducibility, weight and inertia apply to (1,1;chi), chi nonprincipal. Rank2 and Tate twist1 give weight0. At0 the tame matrix is J2(1); infinity has a tame line of order ord(chi) and a wild line of Swan1.
* [Katz–Tiep, §1B, pp.567–568](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nmk/ktcondSpublished.pdf): finite geometric determinant applies. No constant arithmetic determinant is needed.
* [Katz, Mellin transforms, Lemma22.3 proof, p.107](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nmk/mellin214.pdf): power-map descent and Swan divisibility eliminate a nontrivial finite dilation stabilizer for the determinant line of Swan1.
* [FKMS, §§2–3 and6](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.09459v1): Definition1.2, Theorems2.2/2.4, Lemma3.1 and Propositions3.6/3.11–3.13 were checked. Proposition6.2 is prime-field only; preceding geometric inputs permit the all-extension reconstruction. Section2 justifies middle-extension dual/conjugate traces. Proposition3.13's zero-pullback convention needs the adjustment below. Constants require fixed complexity and sufficiently large characteristic, not merely large cardinality.

The Gauss substitution independently gives q^-1 H_chi(-t)=c_q K(t), c_q=chi(-1)g(bar chi)/sqrt(q), |c_q|=1. Holes remain at y=0,-1 and K(0)=-q^-1/2. Over extensions the scalar need not be a fixed power; balanced trace/conjugate products cancel its absolute phase.

For homotheties, infinity inertia is theta plus theta^-1 D_d. D extends across 0, has finite p-power geometric order and Swan1. A projective equivalence either preserves the two summands, forcing D_d=D_e and d=e, or swaps them. Swapping forces D_e D_d=theta^4; wild and prime-to-p parts separate, so chi^4=1 and D_e=D_d^-1. Squaring the dilation gives e=+-d. Order6 therefore has no nontrivial projective homothety. Finite determinant, irreducibility and the zero unipotent force connected group SL2. Tensor independence removes Hc² if some dilation occurs oddly. Rank16/Swan<=16 give the complete square-root bound; union bounds for the even patterns give the fourth-moment constants. The t=0 term is explicit.

**Part III repair:** literal K has nonzero stalk at 0. In the second-stratum argument declare r=-v_i, at most 2ell values, exceptional. Use the generic cohomological argument only for other r; each exceptional r costs O(q²) in the squared s sum, so the bound stays O_ell(q²). This avoids a source proof line assuming zero stalk. High-parameter complete v sums can likewise be compared away from finitely many singular points, adding O(1). Write the repair explicitly in integration. The dual convention is otherwise supported.

For inert p² use all-extension parameter moments, stratification, the degree/grid lemma and the separate Eisenstein lattice estimate. That estimate counts u1 n2=u2 n1+pi k with bounded k using N²/V<=q and a divisor bound for a nonzero Eisenstein integer. It never substitutes a length-p² integer interval. At ell divisible by3 the strata give V^ell q³+V^(ell+2ell/3)q²+V^(2ell)q^(3/2); V=q^(3/(2ell)) gives L24. The exact1/2400 and 1/40 savings apply to different support regimes.

### 2.4 The exact hard-prime same-output diagonal costs only a constant

Expand the full hard-prime integrand BEFORE taking absolute values:

    Q_hard(R)=-Re int_0^R exp(-2gamma y)
      sum_(p>(2+y)^A)sum_(m,n>=1)
       conjugate(a(n))*chi(p)*a(m)*log p
       g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y)dy.                       (8)

There is no cutoff of m or n. The n=pm terms are nonzero only for squarefree q-units pm, so p does not divide m and

    -conjugate(a(pm))*chi(p)*a(m)=|a(m)|^2=1.

The exact diagonal D_R is therefore nonnegative. At a fixed squarefree n, its retained prime log-weights sum to at most log n. The whole-line Gaussian integral is exact:

    int_(-infinity)^infinity exp(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
       =exp(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi tau)).

Consequently, for gamma>1/2,

    0<=D_R<=B_diag
      =exp(tau gamma^2)/(2sqrt(pi tau))
         *sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2gamma)<infinity.         (9)

Natural zeros only lower this positive majorant. Define H_R=Q_hard(R)-D_R: it is precisely (8) restricted to n!=pm. All p,m,n signs and phases remain inside H_R. This same-output diagonal is different from deleting a signed subset of a completed physical form.

statement:
## 4. Finite optimizer and interpolation obstructions

Every constrained minimizer is zero-free on the closed disk for every nonzero source F with F0!=0. If p=(z-lambda)q, variation by zq is admissible. Orthogonality and the strict Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for qF,zqF imply |lambda|>1. Thus root stability is automatic. This is classical optimal-polynomial approximation; the report's p0=1 version is directly proved, and no literature novelty is assigned. [Beneteau et al., arXiv:1509.04807v2, Theorem3.2 and cyclicity discussion](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807).

For F=1-z/r, r>0, the Gram is tridiagonal with diagonal1+r^-2 and off-diagonal-r^-1. The size-m determinant is D_m=sum_(k=0)^m r^-2k, with D_0=1 for the empty matrix; hence d_N=D_(N+1)/D_N. Its limit is r^-2 for r<1 and1 for r>=1. At r=1, Delta_N=1/(N+1). Because G(r)=r^-2G(1/r), the entire constrained minimizer sequences coincide for r and1/r despite their different interior zero geometry. Coefficient or root geometry alone cannot recover the normalized gap. For the finite-inner toy F=(z-r)/(1-rz), the Gram is I, d_N=1 and Delta_N=1-r^2. Good conditioning has the same limitation.

For X28 take the complete residual e=pF-F0 and a finite Blaschke product B for all exactly fitted safe nodes, including0 and multiplicities. Then e belongs to BH2 and ||e/B||=||e||. At a hypothetical source zero w distinct from those nodes,

    ||e||^2>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.              (R16)

This is evaluation of the divided residual, not an extra norm charge for inner division. For B=z^m it recovers the stated floor. The Taylor inverse to1-z/r gives e=-(z/r)^(N+1), with norm squared r^-2N-2: perfect finite Taylor matching can coexist with a growing complete complement. A fixed-anchor amplification at height T needs degree of order T^2/(beta-gamma); no all-height estimate is extracted. This preserves the exact W22 correction and N29 source geometry. A different paid node geometry or actual full-residual upper bound remains live.

statement:
## G150. Complete matching displacement, with the old rank equivalence retained

Let V have basis the squarefree q-units n<=X, parity mu(n), and all diagonal
character actions W_chi(n)=chi(n). An odd differential d with d squared
zero commuting with every character must preserve each reduced residue
class: the characters separate that finite group. Write E_a,O_a for the
two parity counts and I_a=E_a-O_a. Hodge decomposition then gives

    dim ker(dd*+d*d) >= R_q(X) := sum_a |I_a(X)|.

Matching min(E_a,O_a) opposite signs within each residue attains equality;
unit arrows give nonzero spectral gap one. The gap alone says nothing
about the residual rank. Orthogonality gives the exact comparisons

    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X) <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)|
                                      <= phi(q) max_chi |M_chi(X)|.

These are already [[private research revision] G135](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md).
Do not count this reformulation as a new weaker arithmetic prerequisite.
For example q=5,X=80 has residue indices (0,-3,-4,1), hence minimum rank
eight; a fourteen-state rank of a particular construction is not universal.

For one neutral prime r=1 mod q, the exact pairing m with rm, r not
dividing m, has residual rank

    d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X + O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)),
    d_q = zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1).

The square-divisor expansion proves the squarefree q-unit count
d_q X+O_q(sqrt(X)). If only one chi is being preserved, chi(r)=1 suffices;
otherwise the multiplier 1-chi(r) must remain. This linear-rank obstruction
belongs to the named neutral-prime rule, not to every differential.

### A full future-partner return

In each reduced residue class there are infinitely many negative squarefree
integers (primes) and positive ones (a fixed r=1 mod q times different
primes in that class). Only infinitude of primes in each reduced progression
is imported here; see [NIST DLMF 27.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11.E9).
No prime-distribution error estimate is used. Thus a fixed global
same-residue pairing of the two signs exists. Orient each pair (u,v) by
mu(u)=1, mu(v)=-1 and set a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v). Define

    D_q(X) = sum_(X<=a<2X) (b-a),       X=1,2,4,... .

Every future partner is included, even when b is much larger than 2X.
For a common 0<gamma<1, the full hypothesis

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and every fixed q                 (OPEN-D)

implies ordinary zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. Indeed, initially Re(s)>1,
absolute regrouping gives

    1/L(s,chi) = sum_pairs chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).

For sigma=Re(s)>0 the difference is bounded by
|s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1). Summing dyadic shells with epsilon below a compact
set's horizontal margin gives normal convergence on Re(s)>gamma. The
identity L F=1 continues meromorphically, excluding zeros and permitting
the reciprocal zero at a principal pole. All fixed finite heights and the
literal imprimitive factors are covered; no uniform growth assertion follows.

Monotone same-residue pairing has crossing count R_q(t). Tonelli identifies
the total *clipped* interval length in [A,B] with integral_A^B R_q(t)dt.
That is not the complete D_q(A): omitted future portions and intervals
entering from earlier shells matter. Under G135's existing summatory/rank
bound with gamma>1/2, endpoints grow proportionally to their rank k and
pair displacement is O(k^(gamma+epsilon)); the complete D bound follows.
This adapter has not evaded the original arithmetic difficulty.

The global neutral-prime rule has the unconditional full cost

    D_q(X) = (r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           = (3/2)(r-1)d_(qr) X^2 + O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).

Partial summation of the squarefree count proves it, with the positive main
coefficient intact. Thus this rule cannot meet the positive-cost target for
any gamma<1. Other matchings or signed displacement estimates remain open.
Near/1/6/1/4 cost exponents are respectively below1.8748540364,11/6,7/4.
The new useful bill is complete future-partner cost and this actual rule's
failure; G135, W01 signed transport and [private research revision] priced coupling retain credit.

## 5. Phase signal, interval width and zero return

Assume the fixed chi2 Hecke numerator has its usual holomorphic continuation (it is a nonprincipal fixed angular character), as required by the underlying source contract. Then N_I(s) is an H-valued holomorphic function and is a nonzero vector at every fixed s: if its norm were zero, continuity in t and the identity theorem would make L_K^S(w,chi2) identically zero. Its far-right Dirichlet series excludes that possibility. Individual numerator zeros, of any finite multiplicity, are allowed.

For a filter word of length m with a common terminal kernel k, the vector signal norm on Re s=a is at least

    |M_k(s)| A(a,beta)^(m/2) ||N_I(s)||_H                (H14)

for the full 2^m bank. The bank supplies a quantitative scale-filter factor; it does not supply a uniform lower bound for the L numerator or for the decaying M_k. On a fixed compact set of s, ||N_I(s)|| has a positive minimum by continuity; this gives a finite constant, not a known explicit numerical bound and not a uniform all-height claim. The fixed compact transforms are nonzero at positive real part and the Gaussian is everywhere nonzero; their high-frequency attenuation remains the conditioning in frozen [restricted research revision].1.

A small fixed phase interval suffices qualitatively. Its quantitative width cost is real. If the center t0 gives a numerator zero of order r, with local leading coefficient C in t, then for centered interval width h,

    integral_I |N(s)(t)|² dt
      = |C|² h^(2r+1)/[(2r+1)2^(2r)] (1+O(h)).          (H15)

The inverse signal cost is of order h^(−r−1/2), or h^(−r) with normalized interval measure. C depends on the relevant derivative. A shrinking interval or an increasing height range needs quantitative derivative/multiplicity and remainder bounds; the identity theorem alone does not pay that loss. Keeping I fixed avoids an X-dependent width cost without asserting numerical stability at every height.

Retain the vector until return. Integrating against one fixed weight in t can annihilate the numerator at a possible denominator zero. Finite samples have no proved common-zero exclusion here. An s-dependent projection onto N_I(s), or division by its norm, is not a fixed bounded arithmetic detector without its own conditioning proof. In particular the compact local projection considered in frozen Part VIII collapses the phase family to a scalar multiple of the old numerator; bounded reconstruction from that rank-one projection is not provided by H9. Scale-filter reconstruction and lost phase information are different issues. Ordinary simultaneous stacking of smoothing kernels or dilation filters at one fixed t has the same common scalar numerator: all channels can still vanish where that numerator does. The retained interval vector supplies the new numerator coverage, independently of the scale-bank frame. Every split and recombination above is the identity on that H fiber.

Suppose, for some fixed gamma>max(beta,1/2), one complete bank has all-shell size O_(epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0, with its established small-scale tails. Dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz makes its H^q-valued Mellin transform holomorphic for Re s>gamma. Continue the exact identity

    zeta_K^S(s) Ghat(s)
       = M_k(s) [filter-symbol vector] tensor N_I(s).    (H16)

At a zero rho of zeta_K^S in that half-plane the left side vanishes and the right side is nonzero by H14. The pole of zeta_K at 1 is irrelevant to this zero contradiction; continuation can first be made off that point. Every finite zero multiplicity is excluded. Fixed removed Euler factors are nonzero at positive real part. Thus zeta_K, and by zeta_K=zeta·L(s,chi_(−4)) also zeta, has no zeros at Re s>gamma. This proves the return conditional on the new arithmetic bound; no uniform-height inverse numerator is used.

### M4. Finite masks and what the obstruction actually excludes

Every feasible fixed valuation pattern on a finite set of unramified primes has Dirichlet series D_a(s) multiplied by a product of factors1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) for valuation0 and v_p p^(-s)/(1+v_p p^(-s)) for valuation1. These factors are nonzero at beta. Every such individual masked complete Gaussian retains a nonzero beta mode. An arbitrary signed combination of masks can cancel that mode only by making its combined multiplier vanish at beta; a return to the original source must then repay the missing signal. The full exact recombination retains it. Patterns at ramified primes that require positive valuation are identically zero and are not called feasible.

This strengthens the relevant [private research revision] coarse calibrated countermodel by imposing genuine multiplicativity, exact natural zero support, arbitrary finite prime prescriptions, all fixed character-twist summatory bounds, and vanishing fixed affine correlations. W27 already constructed a multiplicative real-sign source with a prescribed finite prefix and poles inside the baseline strip; multiplicativity itself is therefore not new here. W27 explicitly left quantitative partial-sum/height calibration unproved. The addition here is the simultaneous proven calibration, fixed affine correlation cancellation, and forced growing-window energy lower bound, at the cost of allowing complex unit phases. This is not a strengthening in real-valuedness. It retains W24/W27's warning about global inversion. It is not a counterexample within the actual mu*chi family: at infinitely many unramified primes its unit value differs from -chi(p), and its Dirichlet convolution inverse is not the prescribed character source. Real-valuedness is also not asserted. Thus a proof using the global Möbius prime law, exact convolution inverse, or sufficiently uniform quantitative correlations can escape the obstruction. ## 8. Finite caps and the exact signed scalar

Fix tau=1 for a concrete target and let L=log X,

    B_X=2X exp(2sqrt L),
    A_X=X exp(-2sqrt L).

Uniformly in delta in I, the complete absolute product tails abc>B_X and abc<A_X are X^(-1+o(1)). Use D15a and Gaussian tail integration; the weaker majorant |h_delta(n)|<=d_3(n), with sum_(n<=t)d_3(n)<=t(1+log t)^2, also suffices. For the lower tail, n<=A_X gives log(x/n)>=2sqrt L on the whole shell; integration against the same counting function gives the same exponent. The constants, floors and sufficiently-large thresholds are fixed; the coefficient majorant is independent of chi and delta.

Define the finite field using the literal conventions

    Z_chi,delta,X(x)=sum_(a<b<c; b<=Y_X;
                           A_X<=abc<=B_X)
      mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)chi(abc) V_delta(a,b,c)^2
                                      g_1(log(abc/x)).   (D18)

Equality at either real product cap is included. At the median cap b<=floor(X^.315) is included. The complete complement is the union already paid in D16 and the two product tails; overlap only makes the triangle bound easier. Thus

    (integral_I ||H_chi,delta-Z_chi,delta,X||_[X,2X]^2 ddelta)^(1/2)
                         << X^.874+X^(-1+o(1)).         (D19)

Within D18, c>=A_X/Y_X^2>=X^.37 exp(-2sqrt L). Neither a nor b receives an invented lower cut: the short-factor faces, especially (1,2,c), remain in full.

For n in [A_X,B_X], let w_delta,X(n) be the sum of V_delta^2 over the exact tuples in D18 with abc=n and individually squarefree factors. Then the coefficient is chi(n)lambda(n)w_delta,X(n). The exact target is

    Q_D3,chi(X)=sum_(A_X<=n,m<=B_X)
       chi(n)conjugate(chi(m))lambda(nm) K_X(n,m)
                     integral_I w_delta,X(n)w_delta,X(m) ddelta
                  <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(1.74898+epsilon). (D20)

The family hypothesis is for every ordinary chi, every epsilon>0, and all sufficiently large dyadic X; constants and thresholds may depend on chi and epsilon. A bound only for zeta is only a zeta conclusion.

Here K_X(n,m)=integral_X^(2X) g_1(log(n/x))g_1(log(m/x)) dx/x, equivalently

    K_X(n,m)=g_2(log(n/m))
          *integral_0^(log2)g_(1/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X))du.

Both independent output indices and every tuple-pair interaction remain. The real-shift average is part of the new norm, so there are no omitted cross-delta terms: D20 is exactly integral_I ||Z_delta||^2. For a complex character the conjugation above is essential. No subset of its signed scalar is presumed positive. The Gaussian kernel and the integrated weight are nonnegative, but the coefficient product is signed/complex.

The parameter weight is also elementary and finite. Expand each Vandermonde square as

    sum_(alpha,beta permutations of (0,1,2))
       sign(alpha)sign(beta) product_(j=1)^3 n_j^(-delta*(alpha_j+beta_j)).

For a tuple pair, every resulting term is r^(-delta), with the exact positive integer r obtained from the six labels and their displayed integer exponents. Its integral is

    J(r)=(r^(-1/5)-r^(-1/4))/log r, r>1;
    J(1)=1/20.                                          (D20a)

Thus the finite signed scalar can be written without numerical quadrature or an unspecified profile, using at most 36 squared-Vandermonde terms per triple and all 1296 ordered products per tuple pair. This expansion is an identity, not permission to replace the signed sum by the absolute sum of its terms.

By D19, D20 implies D11 with gamma=.87449, hence the conditional zero-free constant c=.12551, which would exceed c_G. The complete moment remains open; the tail estimate alone supplies no increased constant.

For comparison under the inherited beta=.8749 zeta calibration, the difference between the full and finite averaged squared energies is at most

    X^(beta+.874+epsilon)+X^(2*.874+epsilon)
       << X^(1.7489+epsilon).                            (D21)

This includes both mixed terms and the error square. Its exponent is below 1.74898. The norm argument D19 is sufficient without invoking that calibration; D21 simply records the complete scalar accounting. No percentage of the old source is claimed paid.

The diagonal of D20 is at most X^(1+o(1)): |h|<=d_3 and d_3(n)^2<=d_9(n) suffice with the fixed Gaussian shell weight. Thus the remaining obstruction is a signed off-diagonal correlation of the explicit weighted Liouville outputs, including the 2p channels and their complements.

First take a product profile C(de)=C_d(d)C_e(e); its factors have the
original bounded envelopes. Include C_d in c and C_e in b. The exact
characters on d and the mark are put in

    A_(R,g,J)(t)
      = sum_(P d=t; q_d in J)
          [u(P)/sqrt(q_P)] c(d)a(d) chi_R(d)^3
          chi_P(d)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1 1_(d,g bar(g))=1.  (SF3)

Here J is a norm interval on the ORIGINAL d dyad. All P and d
supports, their finite phases, and squarefree conditions are retained.
The zero chi_P(d)^4 forces (P,d)=1, so t=Pd is squarefree.
All e-dependent characters then have exactly the product
chi_t(e)^4. In particular the zero at (e,t)>1 supplies BOTH the
original (e,P)>1 and (e,d)>1 zeros. The remaining coefficient is

    B_(R,g)(e)=b(e)a(e)chi_R(e)^3 1_(e,g bar(g))=1.   (SF4)

Its squared mass is O(Z^epsilon E). No inverse character is used at
a collision. P has NOT been replaced by t in the physical mark root.

Build a fixed binary interval tree on the attainable integer norm
values in the D dyad (zero coefficients may fill missing values).
Pad to the next power of two if necessary. Let J range over all its
nodes, and let ell_D=O(log(2D)) be its depth plus one. Any interval of
d norms is a disjoint union of at most 2 ell_D tree nodes. For fixed
e, the intervals I_j/q_e are disjoint. Their canonical tree covers
are therefore disjoint as sets of d norms, so any fixed node J occurs
at most once among all these covers at that e.

Apply Cauchy in e to each SF1, then sum j. Apply the just-described
tree cover and Cauchy over its at most 2 ell_D nodes. This gives

    sum_j |V_(I_j)|^2
      << Z^epsilon E ell_D
         sum_J sum_(e original)
             |sum_t A_(R,g,J)(t) chi_t(e)^4|^2.     (SF5)

This step retains the actual product endpoint. There is no claim that
e(a q_d q_e) separates. The set of d norms selected at fixed e is an
interval simply because q_e>0 and q_(de)=q_d q_e.

For each J the coefficients SF3 are independent of live e. The cubic

      << Z^epsilon S(E,LD) sum_t |A_(R,g,J)(t)|^2.  (SF6)

      <= Z^epsilon sum_J sum_(P,d; q_d in J)
                    |u(P)|^2/q_P |c(d)|^2
      << Z^epsilon ell_D D Omega.                  (SF7)

Each d occurs in exactly one node at each tree level. That is why

## 5. Independent protected audit G4-05: exact signed supply, no free coercivity

The seed proposes indefinite storage with the original signed compensation as supply. A useful exact source contract can be written without inventing a state model. Let D=x*d/dx and define the actual complete derivative field

    V_gamma(x)=(D-gamma)M(x)
      =sum_n mu(n)chi(n)[log(n/x)/tau-gamma]g(log(n/x)).

All coefficients, character zeros and the extra Gaussian factor remain. Compact-x differentiation and all integrations below are justified by absolute Gaussian tails. In particular M(x)=O_A(x^A) and V_gamma(x)=O_A(x^A) as x tends to0 for every A>0. For gamma>0,

    d/dlog x [x^-2gamma |M(x)|^2]
       =2x^-2gamma Re(conj(M(x))V_gamma(x)),
    |M(x)|^2=2x^2gamma integral_0^x
       t^-2gamma Re(conj(M(t))V_gamma(t)) dt/t.       (P1)

There is no unsigned replacement of the supply. Integrating P1 over the WHOLE shell yields the exact complete-energy identity

    ||M||_[X,2X]^2=2 integral_0^(2X) t^-2gamma
        W_gamma,X(t) Re(conj(M(t))V_gamma(t)) dt/t,   (P2)
    W_gamma,X(t)=((2X)^2gamma-max(X,t)^2gamma)/(2gamma)
                 for0<t<=2X, and0 otherwise.

Finite-X absolute convergence permits Fubini. The supply itself is the full Hermitian arithmetic pair sum

    sum_(m,n) mu(m)chi(m) mu(n)conj(chi(n))
      [log(mn/t^2)/(2tau)-gamma]
       g(log(m/t))g(log(n/t)).                       (P3)

Symmetrization of Re(conj(M)V_gamma) gives precisely the bracket in P3; no diagonal or cross term is dropped. It is real because exchanging m,n conjugates the coefficient. The bracket changes sign, so bounding its absolute mass would be a different and generally stronger input.

Consequently an upper bound O_epsilon(X^(2gamma+epsilon)) for the COMPLETE signed integral P2 is exactly the original M moment condition, and by A has the full fixed-character zero return. This supplies an unambiguous object for the storage proposal but no weaker arithmetic hypothesis. The Mellin symbol of V_gamma is (s-gamma)exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi), initially in the absolutely convergent half-plane by integration by parts. Its introduced zero is only at the real boundary gamma; it must not be confused with an estimate for V_gamma or for the bilinear supply.

The main obstruction to a shortcut is coercivity. For the two-component state (M,DM), an indefinite candidate storage |M|^2-kappa|DM|^2 with kappa>0 has no uniform positive lower bound for |M|^2. On a test mode x^rho it equals (1-kappa|rho|^2)x^(2Re rho). For Re rho>gamma and sufficiently large |Im rho|, even the upper bound x^-2gamma storage<=C is satisfied while the mode grows faster than gamma. This is an unrestricted mode diagnostic, not an assertion that L has such a zero or that an actual arithmetic field attains the mode. It demonstrates why an indefinite upper storage estimate alone cannot imply the claimed all-height scalar bound. A positive readout/observability inequality or a priced negative-storage correction is necessary.

**Audit verdict:** KEEP P1--P3 as the exact changed signed-supply contract; OPEN its arithmetic estimate. PARK an unspecified indefinite-storage proof until coercivity and all-height readout are paid. The differential energy identity is classical; F26, W39 observation criteria, W44 transport and the source-relative detector returns retain ancestry. This is a source clarification, not a new cancellation theorem.

## G147. Two presentations confine the unpaid rows to a strict residual box

Outside the prefix exception, |F_R,u(rho_u)|>=1/2. A fixed product-annulus
partition therefore supplies X=U^ell with signal at least U^(-small).
On the same nonunit annulus and with the same common weight W_X,

    T_X,u=sum_(d,m) mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                                      V(Nd/R)W_X(Ndm)
         =-sum_(d,m) mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                                  [1-V(Nd/R)]W_X(Ndm). (4)

Complete multiplicativity includes zero values. The inverse arithmetic
coefficient in either presentation remains mu(d)phi_u(d). Split d,m into
fixed dyads. Common-profile separation yields one Fourier coordinate
within each inverse/plain pair; the two presentations may select different
coordinates and dyads. Both use the same actual character, zero and real
part, and their lengths obey r_-+m_-=r_++m_+=ell+o(1), with
r_-<=t+o(1) and r_+>=t-o(1).

The internal/physical-bin distinction is essential. Use [restricted research revision]'s internal
buffered construction and select its attaining zero before either
extraction. Its exponent delta_b can exceed .70 but is at least
delta-O(buffer). It is never substituted into the physical slot price
or E_K. The source product lower bound and actual-bin pointwise bounds are

    |M(U^r)S(U^m)|^2 >= U^(delta_b ell-small),
    |M(U^r)|^2 <= U^(delta_b r+small),
    |S(U^m)|^2 <= U^(delta_b min(m,1-m)+small).

They first force m<=1/2+small, including initially long product annuli.
Then divide by the other factor and weaken delta_b to delta to obtain

    |M_±|^2 >= U^(delta r_±-small),
    |S_±|^2 >= U^(delta m_±-small).                    (5)

The zero may differ from the initially selected physical-bin zero. Both
pairs still use the same internal attaining zero. Its real part is at
least a-O(buffer), so the prefix norm remains applicable with an arbitrarily
small loss. The incumbent zero-free bound keeps its real part in a compact
subset of (1/2,1). No upper assumption delta_b<=.70 is introduced.

Choose finite moment/profile/Sobolev degrees before the internal height
power. Inflate a small supplied witness height to the prescribed internal
power box, putting both Fourier coordinates within its buffered extension;
the fixed polynomial cost fits the allocated small loss. Completion B and
raw tail powers are fixed before the final small buffers and threshold.
Rapid Fourier decay pays the genuine tails under B3.3. Large heights use
the absolute row/slot count and a larger fixed H_J. Original slot heights
and their physical-bin bound are unchanged. These conventions preserve
the source's threshold before live height rather than claiming arbitrary
conductor/profile uniformity.

The licensed marginal count exponents from (5) are

    I(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r,
    P(m)=1-2delta m.

I uses the free inverse moment; P uses the zero-slot fourth plain moment,
not an unproved positive-slot variant. Fixed masks, relative characters
and whole orientations retain B3.40-41/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]'s actual contracts.
After these positive counts, add the physical price delta v.

Put e=rho-G-eta, q=5/6-delta and

    A=(1-e)/delta, C=(e-1/6)/q.

Then I(r)<=e on [A,C], including its change at r=1, and P(m)<=e for
m>=A/2. Exact interval certificates give

    A<47/50<1<t<C, C-A>3/8, 3A/2-C<3/40,

Pay the union of every easy inverse/plain witness in both presentations.
Crucially, freeze BOTH the original product-profile family and the family
with its exponential replaced by one before making this union or any
rowwise selection. Fixed finite choices, dyads and continuous parameters
are paid by the retained partitions and Sobolev estimates. A padding
p=10^(-6) and the independent certificates with eight pads include the
boundaries; the remaining aggregate losses can be chosen below eta/2.

Every row outside this union has, up to the paid small endpoint losses,

    C<ell<3A/2,
    ell-A<m_-<A/2, 0<=m_+<ell-C,

In particular the strict coarse box is

    .85<r_-<.94, .375<m_-<.47,
    1.32<r_+<1.41, 0<=m_+<.075,
    r_+-r_->.375,
    r_-+m_-=r_++m_++o(1).                             (6)

This follows continuously across the rectangle: replace e by
e_min=rho-a_K-b_K/20-eta. Increasing e decreases A and increases C.
Clearing the positive denominators gives polynomials of degree at most
four. The retained independent rational receipt supplies all Bernstein
coefficients, including the five direct/padded endpoint checks.

The prefix inequality also gives

    C-(t+lambda)>lambda/(6q)>=1/2300.                  (7)

Hence H is exactly zero on the selected residual annulus for large U.
V is one on the short inverse dyad, and 1-V is one on the long dyad.
Remove the exponential only AFTER locating ell<1.41. Per row, including

H_J U^((2-a)1.41-B+epsilon), by the divisor bound and ideal count.
Squaring and paying O(U) rows and absolute slot price U^v gives exponent
`10803/2500-2B`. Choose B>A_tail+10 and any larger contour requirement.

Now re-extract both presentations with the exponential-free family on

Let B_hi be the original physical high-row set. Let B_sep be the residual

      << H_J U^(E_K-1/2000+epsilon)

The first term pays the complete prefix, all easy witnesses in BOTH

## 3. A fixed source emerges, with a complete error bound

Put
    w(p)=(q_p-1)/(q_p+1),  w(a)=product_(p|a,p notinS)w(p),
    W_eta(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)
                              w(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x)).     (3.1)
The weights are fixed; they do not depend on F,E,X or a chosen zero.

Uniformly for all x>0 and all sufficiently large F,E,
    |P_(F,E)(x)-W_eta(x)|
       <= C_(S,R,tau) x L_R(x,F)
             [F^(-1/2)+E^(-(1-theta_R))],               (3.2)
where one may take
    L_Z(x,F)=1+log(2+x),
    L_K(x,F)=1+log(2+F).
The Z bound can harmlessly use 1+log(2+x)+log(2+F). Character constants need not be uniform over moving conductors; the displayed bound itself uses only |eta|<=1 and fixed S.

Proof: the squarefree f probability of avoiding a has main term
    A(a)=product_(p|a,p notinS)(1+q_p^(-1))^(-1),
and the unrestricted e probability has main term
    B(a)=product_(p|a,p notinS)(1-q_p^(-1)).
Their product is exactly w(a). Inclusion–exclusion and mu²=sum_(r²|a)mu(r) give
    error_f <= C_S F^(-1/2) log(2F) S_(1/2)(rad a)       [K],
    error_e <= C_S E^(-1/2) S_(1/2)(rad a)               [K],
    error_f <= C_S F^(-1/2) d(rad a),                   [Z],
    error_e <= C_S E^(-1) d(rad a),                     [Z],
where S_h(Q)=sum_(d|Q)q_d^(-h). Both probabilities and both main terms lie in[0,1], so their product error is bounded by the SUM of these errors, without multiplying them.

For ideals, sum_(q_a<=x)S_(1/2)(rad a)<=C x sum_d q_d^(-3/2)<=C' x. For integers, sum_(a<=x)d(rad a)<=C x log(2x). Partial summation against the full Gaussian pays both infinite ends and proves (3.2). The details and small-x qualification are in support.md. No favourable subset of the signed source has been deleted.

For Re(s)>1 absolute Mellin Fubini gives
    integral_0^infinity W_eta(x)x^(-s)dx/x
        =exp(tau s²/2) H_eta(s)/L^S(s,eta),             (3.3)
    H_eta(s)=product_(p notinS)
          [1-w(p)eta(p)q_p^(-s)]/[1-eta(p)q_p^(-s)].
Both H_eta and its inverse have absolutely convergent Dirichlet series for every Re(s)>0. Indeed the local deviations have coefficient mass bounded by
    2/(q_p+1) * q_p^(-sigma)/(1-q_p^(-sigma)),
summable over primes for every fixed sigma>0. Every numerator and denominator is nonzero there. Thus H_eta is holomorphic and zero-free on Re(s)>0. This is an explicit signal multiplier, not an assumed average over the old physical source.

The same local expansions give two-way Gaussian field convolution between W_eta and U with absolutely sigma-summable coefficients for every sigma>0. This is an exponent-preserving change of source, not an arithmetic power saving.

statement:
## T06. The complete same-core sextic square function

**Status: PROVED RELATIVE TO the inherited physical probe, outer Gram, and complete-zero form.** This theorem groups every cube descendant of a squarefree core and every original compensator branch before taking its norm. It does not bound covariance between different cores. Sources: SA, Part III (P1)–(P20); inherited M (B0.21)–(B0.25), [restricted research revision] (Y1)–(Y9c), [restricted research revision] (AA18)–(AA20).

Write
\[
 Q=q_{b_*}XY,\quad P_a=Y^2/Q,\quad L=\prod_iP_i=Z^\ell,
 \quad \mathcal F_A=1+P_a^{1/6}+LP_a^2/Y.
\]
The slot count, fixed arithmetic data, and profiles are fixed before the scales vary. Assume polynomial scale ranges, \(P_a\ge1\), and \(Y/q_D\ge1\) for every embedded product. The prime supports are the original disjoint smooth annuli. For an embedded subset \(J\), its prime product \(D\), and complementary marked product \(U\), put
\[
 X_D=X/q_D,\quad Y_D=Y/q_D,\quad Q_D=Q/q_D^2,
 \quad L_D=P_{J^c},\quad N_D=ZL_D,
\]
\[
 K_D(A)=\sum_{\substack{U\mid A\text{ in the complementary slots}\\(U,D)=1}}
 \omega_U\overline{\eta(U)}V(q_A/(Zq_U)). \tag{T06.1}
\]
There is no additional power of \(q_U\). Retain the original log-Gaussian \(V\), the common row profile \(W_0\), all element units, and all natural character zeros.

Here is an explicit definition of the packets. The finite reciprocity-ray split is indexed by \(t\). Define
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathcal A_{D,t}(m)=Y_D^{-1}\sum_a
 &\frac{\chi_a(b_*)}{\tau\xi(a)}W_1(q_a/Y_D)(q_a/Y_D)^{-1/2}
 q_a^{-1/2}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m)R(t,a)\\[-2pt]
 &\qquad\qquad\cdot W_0\!\left(\frac{q_m}{Q_D(q_a/Y_D)}\right),
\end{split} \tag{T06.2}
\]
over the original good primary outer columns. For \(A=cn^3\), \(c\) squarefree, set
\[
 \lambda(c,n)=\gamma_2(c)\overline{\alpha(cn^3)G(cn^3)}
               \eta(cn^3)\Xi(cn^3)^{-1},\qquad |\lambda(c,n)|=1,
\]
\[
\begin{split}
 H_{D,c}(m)&=q_c^{-1/2}\sum_t\mathcal A_{D,t}(m)
 \sum_{\operatorname{ray}(cn^3)=t}
 \frac{\lambda(c,n)}{q_n}K_D(cn^3)\chi_{cn^3}(m),\\
 F_{D,c}(m)&=(-1)^{|J|}\omega_Dq_D^{-3/2}Q_D^{-1/2}\xi(m)H_{D,c}(m),\\
 S_c(m')&=\sum_{J,D}\mathbf1_{D^2\mid m'}F_{D,c}(m'/D^2).
\end{split} \tag{T06.3}
\]
These are the actual inherited fields: \(c,n\) may share primes, and zero extensions are retained even at exponents divisible by six. Their common physical support has \(q_{m'}\asymp Q\). Exact reassembly gives
\[
 I_\eta^{\rm comp}=\sum_{m',c}S_c(m'),\qquad
 \Big\|\sum_cS_c\Big\|_2^2=\mathcal D_{\rm core}+\mathcal C_{\ne},
\]
\[
 \mathcal D_{\rm core}=\sum_c\|S_c\|_2^2,
 \qquad\mathcal C_{\ne}=\sum_{c\ne c'}\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle.
 \tag{T06.4}
\]
The latter is real, because both orientations occur, but need not be positive.

**Theorem.** For every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal D_{\rm core}\ll_\epsilon Y^{-1}\mathcal F_AZ^\epsilon.}
 \tag{T06.5}
\]
If \(X=Z^x,Y=Z^y\), \(x\le y\), and \(y-2x+\ell<0\), the right side is \(Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon\).

**Proof.** The number of marked tuples dividing an index is a divisor bound. The ratios \(q_U/L_D\) lie in a fixed logarithmic box. Consequently, for a nonnegative envelope \(E\), decreasing faster than every power at both endpoints,
\[
 |K_D(A)|\ll Z^\epsilon E(q_A/N_D).
\]
This bounds the actual profiles; it does not change the defining signed field. Define
\[
 B(t)=\sum_nq_n^{-1}E(tq_n^3).
\]
Ideal counting on \(q_n\asymp2^j\) bounds each annulus by a constant times \(\sup_{u\asymp t2^{3j}}E(u)\). The arguments advance geometrically, hence
\[
 B(t)\ll1\ (t\le1),\qquad B(t)\ll_A t^{-A}\ (t\ge1),
 \qquad \sum_{c\ {\rm sf}}q_c^{-1}B(q_c/N)^2\ll\log(2N).
 \tag{T06.6}
\]
The unit ideal and both infinite tails are included. The inner \(n\)-sum in (T06.3) is bounded by \(Z^\epsilon B(q_c/N_D)\), uniformly in its masks and row.

The supplied signed outer Gram (M B0.22), finite ray splitting, and Mellin separation of the *original* \(W_0\) give
\[
 \sum_m|\xi(m)\mathcal A_{D,t}(m)|^2
 \ll Z^\epsilon\frac{Q_D}{Y_D}
 \left(1+P_a^{1/6}+\frac{q_DP_a^2}{Y}\right). \tag{T06.7}
\]
The equality \(Y_D^2/Q_D=P_a\) is exact. The polynomial height factor in the Gram is integrated against the rapidly decreasing Mellin transform. Cauchy over the fixed ray set and (T06.6) therefore bound the sum of \(\|\xi H_{D,c}\|_2^2\) over \(c\) by (T06.7). Restoring the physical factors gives
\[
 \left(\sum_c\|F_{D,c}\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 \ll \frac{Z^\epsilon|\omega_D|}{\sqrt Y\,q_D}
 \left(1+P_a^{1/6}+\frac{q_DP_a^2}{Y}\right)^{1/2}. \tag{T06.8}
\]
The embedding \(m\mapsto D^2m\) is an isometry in the direct sum over \((c,m)\). Apply its Hilbert-space triangle inequality, use \(q_D\asymp P_J\le L\), and use \(\sum_D|\omega_D|/q_D\ll Z^\epsilon\) in each fixed subset. This proves (T06.5). Finally \(LP_a^2/Y\ll Z^{\ell+y-2x}\), while \(P_a\ge1\), proving the stated geometry specialization. ∎

### The complete-zero form and the precise unpaid covariance

Let \(\mathcal E_0\) be the inherited positive complete-zero form. Its *whole* compensated value is \(O(Y^{-1}Z^\epsilon)\). The same estimate holds for the direct sum of its same-core values:
\[
 \sum_c\mathcal E_0(S_c,S_c)\ll Y^{-1}Z^\epsilon,
 \qquad |\mathcal C_{\ne,0}|\ll Y^{-1}Z^\epsilon. \tag{T06.9}
\]
To justify the first assertion despite moving masks, truncate completed columns, choose one common residue period, and at each residue and continuous row point apply
\[
 \left|\sum_t\mathcal A_{D,t}B_{D,c,t}\right|^2
 \le |\{t\}|Z^\epsilon B(q_c/N_D)^2\sum_t|\mathcal A_{D,t}|^2.
\]
Only then average residues and integrate rows. The unmarked outer zero form has only its equal-column term, of size \(Q_D/Y_D\), by M B1.16. Equation (T06.6) and the residue-density/Jacobian isometry from [restricted research revision] AA19 give the first assertion. Rapid tails control differences of truncations in this positive completion. Polarize after that limit; subtracting the same-core value from the paid whole value proves the second assertion. This argument assumes no common finite period for an infinite family.

Thus the sufficient new estimate is the one-sided bound
\[
 \mathcal C_{\ne,\rm nz}:=
 \sum_{c\ne c'}\{\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle-\mathcal E_0(S_c,S_{c'})\}
 \ll Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon. \tag{OPEN-COV}
\]
It remains unproved. Cauchy over the \(O(Q)\) physical rows would then give
\[
 |I_\eta^{\rm comp}|\ll Z^{x/2+(y-x)/12+\epsilon},
\]
the physical estimate used by the inherited \(c=.12551\) conditional certificate. The available same-core theorem supplies only one summand of this implication.

## 2. The full signed one-grid span has a positive error floor

Let W_q be the H_sigma-closed span of all w_(q,n), n>=1. For any finite or norm-limit W in W_q, B3 and continuity give E_(s_(q,k))(W)=0. Cauchy-Schwarz therefore proves

  ||1-W||_sigma^2 >= 2(1-sigma)/(1+(2 pi k/log q)^2),  k!=0.    (B4)

This is a lower bound on the complete signed source norm, including every future repetition and cross term. It is not a failure of termwise absolute summation. It allows arbitrary complex coefficients, arbitrary choice/order of indices, refitting, and arbitrary finite linear combinations of the exact source wavelets.

In particular the exact operators SW34-SW35 cannot alone form a compatible capture chain converging to 1 in H_sigma at any sigma<1. Their valid second-shell leakage identity SW38 remains valid. What is ruled out is promoting these fixed-dyadic extensions, even with perfectly signed tail estimates, to full closure of the target.

For q=2, log2>2/3 and pi<22/7 give the deliberately coarse rigorous floor

  ||1-W||_sigma^2 > (98/4405)(1-sigma).                       (B5)

Thus even the target sigma=.874864 (c=.125136, only .000001 beyond c4) has a fixed positive floor. Exact rational values are recorded by check_exact.py. The same obstruction persists at sigma=5/6 and sigma=3/4. It already fails at the present endpoint; no rebudgeting of a finite tail can make it a first gain.

## 5. Exact SW34 extension, all repetitions, and actual escaping tails

For B9, the contract inherited from SW34 must remain literal: N>=2;
R is supported on N<=k<2N and is zero elsewhere; and

    d_n=R(n)-R(n-1),   N<=n<=2N.

In particular d_(2N)=-R(2N-1) is included. The candidate's notation references
this contract; omitting its terminal jump would invalidate the identity.
For every k,

    w_(q,n)(k)=sum_(j>=1) [1-q 1_(q|j)] 1_(jn<=k).

All terms relevant to this k are finite. Summing d_n over
N<=n<=min(2N,floor(k/j)) telescopes to R(floor(k/j)), including when floor(k/j)
is beyond 2N because the total jump sum is zero. Consequently

    sum_(n=N)^(2N) d_n w_(q,n)(k)
      =sum_(j>=1) b_q(j) R(floor(k/j)),
    b_q(j)=1-q 1_(q|j).                                  (R11)

This is zero on k<N and equals R(k) on N<=k<2N. It also retains every later
shell. For q=2, b_q(j)=(-1)^(j-1), exactly SW35. SW38's second-shell identity
is preserved, but it never paid the whole norm. For a combined two-grid
extension, R1 applied to |F_2+F_3|^2 contains all four ordered terms
F_2 conjugate(F_2), F_2 conjugate(F_3), F_3 conjugate(F_2), F_3 conjugate(F_3).
No cross-grid tail identity or saving is inherited from the separate formulas.

The independent helper includes a negative control: N=3, R(5)=1, R zero
elsewhere. At k=6 the correct q=2 extension is 0, whereas dropping d_6 gives 1.
Thus this is a real convention, not cosmetic notation. It is a clarification of
the candidate's imported definition, not a counterexample to its stated source.

For the unique prefix fit let

    a_q(n)=sum_(j>=0:q^j|n) q^j mu(n/q^j).

The finite convolution a_q*b_q=delta_1 follows by multiplying the inverse
geometric series sum_j q^j delta_(q^j) with delta_1-q delta_q, and then using
mu*1=delta_1. This works for composite q too; no multiplicativity of a_q is
assumed. Therefore, for k<=N,

    H_(q,N)(k)=sum_(n<=N)a_q(n)w_(q,n)(k)
             =sum_(ell<=k)(a_q*b_q)(ell)=1.               (R12)

The matrix indexed by k,n<=N is triangular with diagonal 1, so these coefficients
are uniquely forced in that finite dictionary. For q=2 and odd m, only the top
two powers can contribute when r>=1:

    a_2(m)=mu(m),
    a_2(2^r m)=2^r mu(m)+2^(r-1)mu(2m)
              =2^(r-1)mu(m).

In particular squareful m still give the actual zero coefficients. The error
1-H_(q,N) is supported on k>N, a set of H_sigma measure
(N+1)^(-2sigma)/(2sigma), while its complete squared norm is at least R10. Its
conditional RMS there is therefore at least

    sqrt(2sigma J) (N+1)^sigma.                           (R13)

This proves the stated source-specific tail growth, without a Mertens premise.
Pointwise prefix convergence does not control the infinite weighted norm.

## 1. Literal source and quaternion conventions

Use the complete G215 data: a fixed ordinary character chi modulo its PRESENTED q, with natural nonunit zeros; r>=2 of the same parity as chi; fixed m>=0. Put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), lambda=2^(r+1), D H(X)=H(X/2), and

    P_m(D)=product_(j<m)(I-2^(-(2j+1))D),
    F(X)=sum_n chi(n)J_r(n)e^(-n/X),
    J_r(n)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)(n/d)^r,
    E(X)=F(X)-A X^(r+1), E_m=P_m(D)E,
    g(t)=sum_n chi(n)n^r e^(-nt)-m_q r!t^(-r-1),
    H(t)=P_m(T)g(t), T g(t)=g(2t),
    E_m(X)=sum_n a_n H(n/X),
    Phi(X)=E_m(X)-lambda E_m(X/2)
          =sum_n a_n K(n/X), K(t)=H(t)-lambda H(2t).    (1)

Here A=m_q r!/L(r+1,chi), with m_q=phi(q)/q for principal chi and 0 otherwise. These are the original complete sums, not a finite or squarefree substitute for F: J_r has deliberate prime-power coefficients, while the outer divisor source in (1) has mu's squareful zeros. The original g and its principal algebraic tail remain in H. The source K vanishes to order 2m+1 at 0, decays exponentially at infinity, and has leading exponential e^(-t). It is nonzero. G215 proves E_m=O(X), Phi=O(X) at infinity and the stated small-scale behavior. All these constants may depend on fixed chi,r,m.

For q=z+w j use j z=conj(z)j. Then

    (z+w j)(u+v j)
      =(zu-w conj(v))+(zv+w conj(u))j,
    N(q)=|z|^2+|w|^2,
    M(q)=[[z,w],[-conj(w),conj(z)]].                   (2)

Thus M is the user's algebra homomorphism and det M=N. Throughout sections 2-3 quaternionization is pointwise at a positive REAL scale X. No holomorphic positivity claim is made.

### T-D02: translated-field Gram determinants miss a dangerous rank-one mode

Let v_j(t)=F(t+h_j), and G_jk=integral_I v_j(t)conj(v_k(t))w(t)dt with w>=0. For F(t)=A exp(rho t),

    G_jk=|A|^2 exp(rho h_j+conj(rho)h_k)
                    integral_I exp(2 Re(rho)t)w(t)dt.    (W39.31)

It has rank1, so every determinant of size>=2 is zero despite arbitrary positive Re(rho). For F=Ae^(rho1 t)+Be^(rho2 t), rank is at most2. With two shifts, its determinant is exactly

    |AB|^2 |e^(rho1 h1+rho2 h2)-e^(rho2 h1+rho1 h2)|^2
      *[J11 J22-|J12|^2],
    Jkl=integral_I e^((rho_k+conj(rho_l))t)w(t)dt.       (W39.32)

As rho2 approaches rho1, both factors vanish quadratically for a nondegenerate interval and distinct shifts; the determinant is fourth order in the frequency/exponent separation. Thus determinant-only SMALL upper bounds cannot exclude a single growing mode. A trace or coercive observable retaining that mode is necessary and needs its own arithmetic estimate. This is a diagnostic of the stated translated-field Gram detector, NOT a counterexample to the distinct reciprocal Hankel D3 construction or an actual-Möbius lower bound.

### 3.1 Exact Euler algebra and the source correction

Put z_p=chi(p)p^-s. For Re(s)>1,

    D_b(s)=sum_n b(n)chi(n)n^-s = H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    H_p=(1-z_p)^-2,                            p=2,3,
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2,                    p>=5.    (2)

The inverse K=1/H has

    K_p=(1-z_p)^2,                             p=2,3,
    K_p=(1-z_p)^2/(1-2z_p)
       =1+sum_(j>=2)2^(j-2)z_p^j,             p>=5.    (3)

Thus K(s)=sum k(n)chi(n)n^-s, with k(2)=k(3)=-2, k(2^2)=k(3^2)=1, k(p)=0 for p>=5, and k(p^j)=2^(j-2) for p>=5,j>=2; all higher2,3 powers vanish. Both weighted absolute coefficient norms are finite for every fixed sigma>1/2. For example, writing r=p^-sigma,

    ||H_p||_sigma <=1+r^2/(1-r)^2,     p>=5,
    ||K_p||_sigma <=1+r^2/(1-2r),      p>=5.              (4)

Since2*5^-sigma<1 and sum_p p^-2sigma converges, the products converge. The finite prime2/3 factors have their exact displayed expansions. These estimates are uniform under deleting ramified factors because z_p=0 there. They also prove H is nonzero above1/2: every displayed factor is nonzero there and the product of its deviation from1 converges normally. This is the G28 compensation mechanism with the alternate source and target correctly identified; it is not a new cancellation theorem.

Absolute convolution and Minkowski on the actual dilated shell give

    U(x)=sum_r k(r)chi(r)B(x/r),
    B(x)=sum_r h(r)chi(r)U(x/r),
    ||U||_sigma<=K_sigma||B||_sigma,
    ||B||_sigma<=H_sigma||U||_sigma.                     (5)

The Gaussian left tail makes the norms finite at small X whenever the large-scale estimate is available. General real shells can be covered by two dyadic ones. No cutoff is held fixed at an incorrect dilated scale.

Literal prime2 coefficient subtraction gives, at EVERY integer and for every character including chi(2)=0,

    f3(n)chi(n)=b(n)chi(n)
                 -2chi(2)1_(2|n)b(n/2)chi(n/2),
    F(x)=B(x)-2chi(2)B(x/2).                            (6)

Consequently the canonical Mellin multiplier is

    Mellin(F)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)
                       (1-2chi(2)2^-s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi). (7)

If chi(2)!=0, the prime2 numerator has zeros on Re(s)=1, not in1/2<Re(s)<1. If chi(2)=0 it equals1. The classical right-boundary complement remains necessary for the canonical detector. The full inverse at prime2 is not an absolutely convergent *past-scale* Dirichlet convolution below1.
