It is smooth, supported on \([-1,1]\), flat at the endpoints and has mass one. Its transform is nonzero in \(\Re s>0\). The arithmetic coefficients remain
\[

\]
\[

\quad

 T_X=\frac{L}{\ell_0m^2},\qquad Q_X=\frac Lm,\qquad U_X=e^{Q_X},

                  \{1+O(t/L)\},\qquad

# [private research revision] controller reconstruction — fixed Gaussian replacement

At the initial W35 integration the accepted c was0.125113352960035869... .
The later [Gao integration](gao-local-moment-integration.md) accepts the
written analytic bound c_G=.1251134 separately; its full endpoint kernel
replay remains pending. The controller accepts W35's Gaussian reduction
and R35.16–20's separately proved extension.
This is analytic progress that removes a prerequisite, not a new bound
for the central arithmetic moment. The [coherent proof](../current-proof.md)
now leads with this architecture. No catalogue or website publication is
part of this integration.

## Independent reconstruction

The author and independent Astra reviewer stopped before integration.
The frozen review is40,420 bytes, SHA256
ccdb8ce3a52cf1cc793b09e20239b1f7bc9beba0718b16c13309e986b88ce7bf.
All three W35 source files are copied without editing; source hashes and
the previous proof/scorecard snapshots are recorded separately.

1. **Detector and zero bridge.** Direct Gaussian integration gives
   exp(tau*s^2/2)(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s). The negative log-time tail is
   Gaussian, while an all-shell logarithmic L2 bound makes the positive
   transform holomorphic to the claimed open half-plane. Multiplying
   by zeta exposes a zero there because the other factors have no
   zeros in the open critical strip. Fixed tau, all dyads and arbitrary
   epsilon are required. Zeros of the numerator on Re s=1 are treated
   by the inherited right-boundary theorem, not ignored.
2. **Convolution signs.** Since mu*b=q_2, expansion of
   (mu-m_Y)^2*b gives A-2m_Y*q_2+m_Y^2*b. Hence G=R+2L-I.
   The genuine Gaussian short term is nonzero, with a paid negative
   quadratic log exponent. The Type-I term uses a complete ell sum.
3. **Growing derivative constants.** In Cauchy's formula the complex
   log disk gives exp(pi^2/(8tau)); the two completed Gaussian
   integrals give 2*2^m*2^(m-1)=4^m. The half-integer Poisson sum is
   2(2^m-1)zeta(m), which gives the stated upper coefficient
   2K_tau zeta(m)(4/pi)^m. This checks the normalization and the
   m-dependent exponential needed for m of order sqrt(log X) or log X.
4. **Original-label rectangle payment.** i+j<-2 implies
   de<X exp(-kappa sqrt L), even at half-open endpoints. Conversely,
   i+j>floor((log B-L)/H) implies de>B. If d>B/(Y+1), the strict
   lower cut on e also implies de>B. These are the exact discarded
   sources. A surviving rectangle can include lower products than
   the literal de cut; its complete ell field is retained. The later
   n-cap therefore has restoration2 exp(3kappa sqrt L), versus
   2 exp(2kappa sqrt L) for the literal product cut.
5. **Mellin and local energy.** The ell transform is first established
   on Re s>1 and continued from its paid tails, so eta(a+it) is not
   obtained by interchanging an absolutely divergent series.
   Local integration gives ((2X)^(2a+i(t-t'))-X^(2a+i(t-t')))/
   (2a+i(t-t')). Both heights and every ordered component cross term
   survive. Global Plancherel yields only a stronger sufficient
   component target. No converse is asserted.
6. **Fixed-A extension.** Setting kappa=C=sqrt(2tau(1+A)) and
   D=sqrt(2(1+A)/tau) gives exponent-A in the product, total-label
   and height tails. Growing derivative/factorial losses are o(log X)
   for fixed parameters. J=floor(1+log2/(kappa sqrt L))=1 eventually;
   increasing fixed cutoffs leaves four diagonals and subpower
   auxiliary costs. For tau=1, kappa=C=D=2 gives-A=-1.
   No parameter is allowed to grow with X in this conclusion.
7. **Scalar mixed terms.** The Mertens calibration gives ||G||<=X^beta.
   Thus the exact polarization comparison is at most
   2||G||||G-R||+||G-R||^2, with exponent beta+q for q<beta.
   Norm equivalence, not an unnecessarily coarse scalar estimate,
   is the correct return for much lower conditional exponents.
8. **Physical Gram.** Multiplying the two Gaussian densities gives
   g_(2tau)(log(n/m))g_(tau/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X)) with the stated
   constants. The d_3^2<=d_9 inequality follows by encoding each
   pair of three-part compositions as margins of a canonical
   nonnegative3-by-3 matrix; different margins remain distinct.
   The far-pair cost2-r^2/(4tau) uses the complete absolute coefficient
   mass. It never supplies an absolute bound for the near scalar.

These checks reconstruct the argument. They are not numerical evidence
for a zeta zero-free endpoint, and no baseline proof or formal kernel
was rerun.

## Choice of forward proof and evidence limits

The old SP source had a fixed positive error exponent, a smooth-part
state partition and a logarithmic restoration span. The new detector
has four ordinary-bin diagonals, O(sqrt(log X)) intervals/heights,
subpower restoration and arbitrarily small fixed-power analytic errors.
Its count is not claimed asymptotically smaller than SP's different
loglog X count times60^55. The removal of arithmetic state filters and
the error floor is the useful change. This meets the admission rule by
removing a real prerequisite upstream of the remaining moment.

Both architectures retain a complete signed moment with no newly proved
power saving. Their component energies are not identified. SP's actual
RN/RNE bands, W34's support reductions, and the stronger [private research revision]
transfer stay available in their own scopes; no new Gaussian analogue
of RN is asserted. The strongest objection is that the simpler factors
still encode the full hard Möbius cancellation and may give no new
estimate. The decisive test is a complete signed four-diagonal estimate,
or a genuinely useful sector that transfers with all complementary
terms paid. The independent direct lane is assigned precisely this test.

For the near-pair alternative the controller chooses tau=1,r=2.
The true diagonal and full absolute far sector then each cost
X^(1+o(1)), affordable for any fixed gamma>1/2. The remaining signed
off-diagonal near scalar is the actual target. This specialization is
a deduction from R35.14–19, not a separately discovered arithmetic theorem.

The coarse baseline at a=.75 is.2498 and the named target.24898.
The accepted c0 endpoint with a positive buffer gives the better
limiting baseline.24977329407992826... . Neither is improved here.
Keep raw benchmark and best limiting baseline distinct in the scorecard.
No fraction of the full problem solved is assigned.

## Other W35 corrections and preserved ideas

R35.21–23's fractional source, transform, semigroup and zero bridge are
exact W22 R22.14–19 reuse; W22 even permits every fixed real alpha>0.
The new useful analysis is the explicit continuous-minus-prime Gaussian
renewal equation, its positive tau*V' commutator sign, and the failure
of a particular absolute contraction. Continuous and atomic variations
add, so alpha(e^(delta u)-1)/(delta u) already diverges. This refutes
that absolute operator majorant, not the signed arithmetic solution or
all possible weights. The raw, unnormalized fractional source has the
separate local branch-at-one obstruction.

All30 cards, six first tests and two independent audits remain. C03's
finite inverse proposal must now beat the already proved subpower
finite-section bound with an actual infinite readout/tail; [restricted research revision]'s chain
argument needs the retained weighted boundary commutator. Neither is
declared impossible in every form.

The review found a real selection-protocol limitation: T3 drew uniformly
from a saved nine-card subgroup, omitting12 other threshold-eligible
cards without a recorded exclusion. Preserve its draw and useful math;
do not reroll or retrospectively certify it as full-pool sampling. The
next generator must form pools from numerical labels across all groups.
This correction changes exploration evidence, not theorem validity.

## Coprime reconstruction and independent comparison

The author, independent derivation and subsequent frozen-source comparison
are accepted at GC1--27, with their exact hashes in the integration receipt.
The independent derivation preceded reading the author; the comparison then
checked the additional quantitative returns. The controller independently
recomputed the local Euler factors and supplied the convergent positive
series sum n^(-delta)/rad(n_(6)), which pays the one-short field by
Y*x^delta. This includes all unbounded prime powers and the true <=Y edge.

The substantive removal is an unproved complement comparison: the single
original cell (d,e)=1,(de,6)=1 has a fixed coalesced field F_6 and two
absolutely summable inverse multipliers for Re s>1/2. Weighted shell
Minkowski acts on the fixed fields, with their Gaussian left tails; only
afterward is the local frozen cutoff inserted. This proves exact-power
equivalence above1/2 and all-epsilon equivalence at1/2. It does not assert
exact endpoint summability or positivity of signed subfamilies.

For the finite reconstruction, the local error exponent.495+delta is
smaller than a chosen sigma>1/2. Its k-weighted sum is O(X^sigma).
The outer r>X/X_0 tail uses bounded t^(-sigma)F_6(t) on0<t<=2X_0,
not a bound on F_6 alone. All local source caps and height tails are
paid before the r sum; the global error is X^(1/2+epsilon), not a
negative power. Polarization with beta=.8749 gives scalar1.3749+epsilon.
Every r,r' cross term and independent local height window remains.

The simpler equivalent signed f_3 correlation has diagonal O(X) and
an open off-diagonal. No random-sign model is used. The finite-matrix
obstruction is also accepted: high columns m in[2e^(4tau)X,4e^(4tau)X]
have zero original capped source, while the actual A readout is positive.
The Gaussian ratio at q>=2 is <=q^-4 and3 sum q^-4<=5/16; a positive
unit vector on these columns gives norm at least c X^(sigma+1/2).
This refutes only promotion of a tiny e_1 error to an unrestricted
operator bound. The arithmetic input itself is not lower-bounded.

## W36: a paid aggregate-overlap sector and scoped failures

The [W36 review](../creative/round36-review.md) is accepted after independent
controller reconstruction of its incidence and Rankin calculation. For four
original squarefree factors, retain D=product(n_i)/lcm(n_i). Fixing the
eleven original shared incidence labels leaves four signed private sums.
The auxiliary coprimality expansion has coefficients6,8,3, whereas the
later original-incidence Euler product has6,4,1. These are different
objects. Auxiliary q12 primes must remain allowed in private variables3,4.

After the four coprime-Mertens cancellations, Rankin with
t=2beta-1-delta gives prime exponents1+delta,2-beta+2delta,
3-2beta+3delta, all>1. Thus the actual signed scalar sector has
absolute size at most X^(2beta+epsilon)T^(-(2beta-1)). The Gaussian
adapter is derived directly using its bounded Euler derivatives and
actual four-diagonal product bounds; it inherits no SP subset theorem.
At beta=.8749,T=X^.0011 the exponent1.74897522 has positive margin
239/50000000 below1.74898. The whole low-D scalar remains open, including
four distinct rough primes. No fraction of the full difficulty is inferred.

The fixed-small-shift detector's zero propagation is valid: a hypothetical
zero moves right by a fixed delta<c0 repeatedly until contradicting the
accepted boundary, before reaching1 or the periodic numerator's zero line.
Its complete norm remains open. The fixed-master finite-prime divergence
uses heights near pi/log z and a block of primes z^(3/4)<p<=z, where
cos(t log p)<=-1/2. The resulting exponential growth is in the approximant's
global energy, not the limiting Mobius field; it escapes to large x.
Centering removes the prime term and reuses A12/W21, with an unpaid inverse.
The determinant audit correctly preserves the adjugate pole residue; a
rank-one pole does not force every nonlinear determinant to cancel it.

W36's numerical-threshold pools include every eligible group. Its wildcard14
was deliberately fixed, so that selection is not random. Preserve this
qualification and the frozen draws; no reroll or retrospective relabeling.

## H: a useful failed bilinear replacement

The [late H source](h-original-prime-covariance.md) is accepted in its stated
restricted scope after controller reconstruction of B1--4 and D1--7. Its
two-cutoff von Mangoldt identity is classical. On actual primes only the

are1 and-1. Their four covariance entries1,-1,-1,1 must remain. An external
common-factor amplifier changes the long length, characters, zeros and

In the derived bilinear bound, the mark root stays q_P^(-1/2) after
t=P d. Its squared coefficient mass is D*Omega, not Omega. The cubic
sieve gives N min{S(E,LD),S(D,LE)}*Omega. Sharp product endpoints cost
only logarithms via an integer-exact smooth Fourier cut. The additive

Paying the whole near band separately gives the additional(H0+1)L term.
Original n,g,g', independent heights and the physical N^-1 G^-2 stay fixed.

Even the optimal factor split leaves the mixed cubic term(NL)^(2/3).
Its target-relative exponent.6738809116 is much worse than.004. Removing
that mixed term would still leave the separate positive proof cost

lower bounds on the true covariance. The next useful H estimate must

## 3. Why the common-divisor expansion really separates the copies

After (R5), extend its displayed product expression, profile and formal product conductor to all individually squarefree n,n' in their original tuple supports. This is only an algebraic extension. No imprimitive Poisson identity is asserted on the added noncoprime pairs. Then insert

    1_((n,n')=1)=sum_(f|n, f|n') mu(f).                (R7)

For a pair with nontrivial common divisor the FULL sum is zero. Thus it removes every forbidden cross-copy coincidence, including inverse-inverse, inverse-slot and slot-slot coincidences. It is stronger than merely reinstating the four inverse gcd cuts. No cross-copy coprimality may be separately dropped in an individual summand; all of it has already been represented by (R7).

Write n=fm,n'=fm'. Individual squarefreeness forces (f,m)=(f,m')=1. The exact extraction law is

    a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m)chi_m(f)^4.                       (R8)

Both columns have the SAME f but not necessarily the same assignment of its primes. Their frequency factors give

    chi_f(ell)conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((f,ell)=1),      (R9)

and no division by chi_f occurs. Residual f-punctures and the a-puncture remain in each column. Every common-prime label carries its original sign mu(f).

For each column, allocate each prime of f to its actual inverse color or actual original slot. Because that column is squarefree the assignment is unique for a specified original tuple. Summing over possible assignments is a reindexing with at most (j+2)^omega(f) choices on each side; their PRODUCT is bounded by tau(f)^C for fixed j. An assigned slot prime keeps its coefficient and its pool membership; an unassigned slot retains its original pool.

The precise two independent maps are

| Copy | Original inverse 1 | Original inverse 2 | Assigned slots | Residual product scale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| left | d1=f1 x, length D1/q_f1 | d2=f2 y, length D2/q_f2 | fP | X_f=N0/q_f |
| right | d1'=g1 x', length D1/q_g1 | d2'=g2 y', length D2/q_g2 | gP | X_f=N0/q_f |

Here f=f1 f2 fP=g1 g2 gP, with pairwise coprime factors within each allocation. The first HB application uses only x,y. The second uses only x',y'. None of xx',xy',yx',yy' is an HB variable. Nonempty nominal subunit windows are clipped by bounded original annular factors; genuinely empty windows remain empty.

The last two factors carry the P-punctures and separate. The x,y coprimality is supplied by the zero of chi_y(x)^4, even though the exponent is not one. statement:
### A1. Elementary measurable-set interpolation, including complex values

Let P be a complex polynomial of degree at most N>=1 on an interval I of length1. If a measurable E subset I has measure delta>0 and |P|<=m almost everywhere on E, then

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N m.                           (W39.3)

Here is a proof rather than an external Remez citation. Replace E by the closed set {|P|<=m} intersect I, whose actual measure Delta is at least delta. Choose N+1 quantile points x_0<...<x_N at cumulative-measure levels (j+1/2)Delta/(N+1). The cumulative distribution is1-Lipschitz, so

    x_j-x_i >= (j-i)delta/(N+1).

The quantile points lie in the closed set. Lagrange interpolation and |x-x_i|<=1 give

    sum_j |ell_j(x)|
      <= ((N+1)/delta)^N sum_j 1/[j!(N-j)!]
      = ((N+1)/delta)^N 2^N/N! <= (4e/delta)^N.

The inequality N!>=(N/e)^N follows by integrating log t. If m is only an essential supremum, enlarge it arbitrarily and pass to the limit. Thus no real-polynomial sign assumption is used.

    N_r(X)^2=sum_(n,m>=1) a(n)conj(a(m)) J_(r,X)(n,m),
    J_(r,X)(n,m)=b_X(n)b_X(m)
                    E_(r,nu)(alpha log(n/m)).           (A13)

Absolute convergence follows from (sum |a|b_X)^2<infinity and E(0)<=g_(2nu)(0). Every coefficient, prime power, character zero and ordered interaction is retained. For actual f3, the products remain signed. Entrywise positivity of J does not permit dropping negative terms. If |a(n)|<=C0, the true diagonal is O(X), uniformly for every r>=0, since sum_n g_sigma(log(n/X))^2=O_sigma(X). One proof groups n into dyads about X and sums the resulting Gaussian bound; both log tails converge. Divisor-bounded coefficient families give the corresponding X^(1+epsilon), not a silently identical diagonal constant.

For fixed tau,kappa, the new arithmetic target is the COMPLETE A13 at exponent2eta, optionally subtracting the explicitly paid diagonal when eta>1/2. There is no subset positivity claim. The Gaussian localizer includes both left and right physical tails with their exact weights.

## G157. Repeated-prime support and the exact remaining estimate

The independent reviewer strengthens the actual small-gcd support.
For a surviving original tuple write \(d_1=gx,d_2=gy\), with g,x,y
pairwise coprime squarefree, and let \(p=\prod_ip_i\), squarefree by
disjoint original pools. Set

\[
A=(g,p),\quad b=(xy,p),\quad g=Ag_0,\quad xy=bz,
\quad p=Abp_0,\quad B=g_0b,\quad C=zp_0.
\]

Then A,B,C are pairwise coprime squarefree and

\[
n=A^3B^2C,\qquad n/\operatorname{rad}n=A^2B=gAb,
\qquad Ab\mid p.
\]

These radicals are intrinsic to the merged n, even when many tuples
contribute to c(n). Thus \(N(n/\operatorname{rad}n)<CGP_0\). Comparing
two such columns, the local valuation table gives
\(q_2q_3^2\mid(n/\operatorname{rad}n)(n'/\operatorname{rad}n')\) and
\(q_3\mid A(n)A(n')\). Consequently

\[
Q_2Q_3^2<CU^{2/5+2v},\qquad Q_3\le CU^{2v}.           \tag{G157.1}
\]

At maximal v the exponents are 1/2 and1/10. Fixed profile constants
require arbitrarily small geometric pads, rather than literal unpadded
finite-U cutoffs. Profile derivatives, independent heights and the
fixed positive common-profile integrals preserve this support. This is
an exact new support fact, not a signed norm saving by itself.

Let \(\mathcal R_{\rm mix}\) be the real ordered off-diagonal paired sum
remaining after G156, with the actual coefficients c(n)\(\overline{c(n')}\)
and full kernels. It has

\[
n\ne n',\quad Q>U^{9/5},\quad Q_1/Q_3>U^{8/5},\quad
Q_2Q_3^2<CU^{2/5+2v},\quad Q_3\le CU^{2v}.
\]

The same definition includes the fixed finite derivative sum and positive
common-profile measure needed for the Sobolev envelope. The necessary
open hypothesis is the **one-sided** estimate

\[
\mathcal R_{\rm mix}\le H_JU^{T-\xi+\epsilon}
\quad\text{for some fixed }\xi>0,                    \tag{OPEN-MIX-RES}
\]

uniformly over the licensed fixed data and both independent heights.
Absolute value would be a stronger optional target, not a proved or
necessary replacement. The residual need not be positive.

This estimate would complete G148 OPEN-MIX with a margin below
\(\min(\xi,1/200)\). Combining the actual separated witness and G147
counted prefix then requires a margin below
\(\min(\xi,1/200,1/2000)\), with every witness, height and buffer loss
chosen from that strict slack. It still does not pay the full raw or
positive-child physical return: both signed coprimality projectors,
family reconstruction, root/slot holes, fixed inducing and exceptional
rows, physical radii/amplifier, clipped rectangles, shifted/shortened
Euler families, principal terms and the actual supremum/common mesh

statement:
## 4. What more moment cancellation buys, and what it does not

The preceding repair has a complete generalization. Let h be a nonzero
fixed C^1 function compactly supported in (1,V), with possibly complex
values, and define m_j=integral h(v)*v^(-2)*(log v)^j dv. There is a finite
least J with m_J!=0: otherwise the continuous finite measure h(v)v^(-2)dv
annihilates every polynomial in log v, hence every continuous function on
its compact support, and is zero. This contradicts h!=0.

THEOREM C. For fixed u>J+2 with omega^(J+1)(u)!=0, the root residual
Delta_N(m,p)=1_(P<p<=2P)*h(m/p^r) has complete signed response

    sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)*Delta_N(m,p)
       ~ [(q/phi(q))*(-1)^(J+1)*m_J/J!]
          *omega^(J+1)(u)*kappa_r
                   *N*P^(-r)/(log P)^(J+3).              (11)

Proof: in (9), use (2) through order J+1 and expand each derivative in
log v/log p. The exact identity

    integral h'(v)*v^(-1)*(log v)^l dv=m_l-l*m_(l-1)

(m_(-1)=0) makes every l<J term vanish. The first remaining contribution
has source index1 and Taylor index J, giving (11); all higher source
indices contribute only later logarithmic orders. Total variation pays
the complete uniform source remainder, and the Riemann error is
O(N*p^(-r-1)*p^(-r)/(log p)^2), negligible against every fixed logarithmic
order. The prime-band calculation is exactly the one already proved.

For every fixed k>=1, omega^(k) is nonzero at arbitrarily large points.
If it vanished on a tail, omega would be a polynomial there. A polynomial
of positive degree cannot satisfy u*omega'(u)=omega(u-1)-omega(u), by
comparison of the highest powers. The remaining constant case propagates
backwards and contradicts 1/u on (1,2). Thus suitable u exist beyond any
target threshold, avoiding the finitely many differentiability boundaries.

TheoremC gives an actual signed estimate with a logarithmic improvement
for every specified finite moment cancellation. It also says that NO
nonzero fixed compact quotient profile annihilates enough of the arithmetic
mean to force a fixed sublinear power uniformly in the root. Increasing a
fixed finite cancellation order changes a logarithm, not the exponent.
This does not cover N-dependent profiles of growing order, additional
cancellation across distinct prime bands, or residuals constrained by a
different arithmetic construction. Those are genuine reopening conditions.

A second version of the repair is to subtract the known Buchstab prefix
directly. For a fixed K, define a deterministic H_(K,p)(v) to agree with

    v sum_(j=1)^K b_(j,q)*omega^(j)(log v/log p)/(log p)^(j+1)

on the fixed compact u-range in question, and to vanish for sufficiently
small v. Retain any transition exactly. Write W_q=H_(K,p)+E_(K,p), and
replace each coefficient difference by the sum of its H and E differences.
For any finite quotient block [a,b], the E contribution is EXACTLY

    -E(N/(pa))*Delta_a+E(N/[p(b+1)])*Delta_b
    -sum_(m=a+1)^b E(N/(pm))*(Delta_m-Delta_(m-1)).        (12)

The identical H expression must still be added. Therefore subtraction
does not erase a deterministic boundary source or the variation cost.
With a fixed-variation residual, (2) only bounds (12) by a fixed logarithmic
improvement to its previous size. With an arbitrary bounded residual,
its variation can be the number of cells, so even that improvement is not
automatic. The explicit profile in (6) actually pays this variation and
boundary, and its surviving term is (8).

Letting K grow with N is NOT licensed by Tenenbaum's fixed-K theorem.
At a minimum, a growing-order version would need uniform constants,
uniform control near all derivative jumps, exact treatment of the growing
transition and collar, and a bound for the complete restored H contribution.
These are analytic prerequisites, not consequences of a finite certificate.
title: 4. What more moment cancellation buys, and what it does not

## 6. A paid off-class region and the exact remaining signed sum

Multiplying ([restricted research revision]) by ([restricted research revision]) gives, on each dyadic relative-conductor triple,

    contribution in absolute value
      << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon]
          min{ U (Q1/Q3)^(1/2),
               U^(1/6) Q1^(11/12) Q2^(5/12) Q3^(-1/12) }.
                                                               ([restricted research revision])

The absolute value here is an absolute bound on the entire sector, obtained by paying its pair coefficient mass and row-kernel bounds. No cancellation between its pairs is assumed. There are only O((log U)^3) conductor triples: terminal l,l' have norm at most a fixed constant times `U^(B+1+v)`. Their finite cost is absorbed before the final epsilon threshold. The same proof holds after the small-core projection because that projection only contracts each absolute coefficient sum.

There is a useful simpler total-conductor consequence. Since H>=Q, sum ([restricted research revision]) and ([restricted research revision]) over all nontrivial residue vectors with Q<=V. Ideal counting and partial summation give

    total absolute contribution for Q<=V
       << H_J U^[1/6-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] V^(11/12). ([restricted research revision])

The ideal sum is the weighted count of `Q^(-1/2+5/12)=Q^(-1/12)` with only divisor-many choices per radical; its growth is V^(11/12), not V^(17/12). Both signs/orientations and all unequal roots are included.

Take t=4/3. In the CURRENT density comparison of Section7, all pairs in the union

    Q <= U^(6/5)  OR  Q1/Q3 <= U^(1/2)                ([restricted research revision])

are paid with a saving greater than 1/100. Use an ordered disjoint union (first the Q cut, then the ratio cut) so nothing is counted as two savings. The remaining sufficient arithmetic input is the ONE-SIDED estimate

    R_hi(U) <= H_J U^[E_K(delta,v)-xi+epsilon],
    0<xi<=1/100,                                     (OPEN-[restricted research revision])

for every required fixed family, smooth majorant and height rectangle. It contains no absolute value on individual remaining pairs. It is unproved. If supplied, ([restricted research revision]), ([restricted research revision])-([restricted research revision]), and the zero/Sobolev identity imply

    weighted high-row mass << H_J U^[E_K(delta,v)-xi+epsilon].

Every low/high cross term has been paid through ([restricted research revision]), and every same-class term through ([restricted research revision]); no part of the full completed norm is silently omitted. ## 5. Admissibility, profiles, every shortening and the physical complement

The input gates are literal PR9 B0.3--4/B3.31 and B0.13--20, together with the
accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] fixed-dictionary and same-zero selection bridges. In particular:

1. The physical delta and cutoff t are fixed first; the actual label and internal
   buffered bin are selected by the original finite procedure. Lemma1W permits
   ANY t in[1,3/2] fixed before its witnesses. Its proof supplies the spike at the
   actual internal beta BEFORE weakening it to physical delta. Using the weaker
   physical spike but the larger internal beta only in the shortened upper bound
   would lose an unwanted factor D^(beta-delta). That invalid shortcut is avoided
   in(2),(6). No upper slot price is replaced by an internal maximum.
2. In(9) the new inverse scale is R/(Nq Nk); in(15) it is the SAME scale after
   restoration. The plain scale is D/Nq or D/NL. These all decrease. If r' is
   the logarithmic inverse scale, then r'<=r; hence BOTH gates(1) improve.
   When r'<0 but the support is nonempty, replace its scale by1 and make a
   bounded dilation of the common profile. This still has r'=0<=r and gives
   2v<=1/10<1 and 8v<=2/5<3. No artificial amplifier, added slot, enlarged
   prime pool, or new derivative index is introduced. The same original Q
   is inside each MI application; there is no unpriced U^v slot factor.
3. The inverse source profile includes the old cutoff
   V_le(R y/U^t). After a=qkc and E=R/(Nq Nk), its argument is still
   V_le(R(c/E)/U^t), so this is exactly the SAME function of its normalized
   variable. It is not a moving arithmetic coefficient or a new cutoff chosen
   after q,k. The plain normalized variable has the identical property.
   Character phases from q,L,k keep their zero values; every exponent, including
   a multiple of six, remains a literal character power with its natural hole.
4. The source's finite Sobolev orders give (3) for rowwise real powers/heights
   and for the finite derivative-profile list. Scale derivatives replace W by
   -W/2-yW', and real/height derivatives add the original logarithmic weights.
   The gcd/square-divisor thresholds are frozen at U BEFORE this operation and
   are not differentiated. Smooth scale suprema use the original logarithmic
   boxes, not a row-dependent coefficient choice. Independent slot heights are
   never equated to the witness height. A fixed global polynomial support bound
   may be used for q,k and restoration variables before these norms; individual
   terms vanish outside their real profile support. This avoids differentiating
   a moving summation endpoint.
5. The plain bound(2) is used only on the retained buffered rows. Its direct
   Mellin shift is uniform for the common shortened profiles and heights by
   B0.14--15. Explicitly the fixed finite conjugation-stable dictionary Theta
   gives X(u)={nu psi_u^(+/-1)}; the good-prime rows have conductor O_S(U).
   With fixed buffer e>0 and I=ceil(1/e)+2, the selected i<I obeys
   a<=B_i<a+e and B_(i+1)<a+2e. Here B_j is the maximum of51/100 and
   real zero parts in that dictionary up to height3^j T. The nonfloor zero
   has a<=Re(rho)<a+e and |Im(rho)|<=3^i T. Put beta=2a-1. On the retained
   height segments the direct line Re(s)=a+6e gives the E^beta bound, with
   its original small U loss, common smooth seminorms and deleted Euler zeros.
   Shortening E changes neither this bin nor its zero-free region, character,
   profile or selected heights. It does not request a new bin at scale E.
   The finitely many independent coordinates use fixed fractions of T;
   discarded tails are U^B T^(-N), with B including polynomial divisor counts
   fixed before N, in the source range U^tau_minus<=T<=U^tau_plus.
   At large heights retain the source's polynomial factor. Choose
   the finite profile orders, bin/mesh and epsilon shares before the internal
   small polynomial height exponent, and the raw tail powers before their decay
   order and final threshold. Above that internal height range, the original
   trivial row count and absolute polynomial bounds on M,Q and the source parts
   are paid by a larger fixed height degree. This final degree may depend on the
   already chosen internal height exponent. The external physical height
   exponent is chosen AFTER that degree, to fit its cost below the eta reserve;
   it is not identified with the internal exponent. No growing-conductor
   uniformity or new growing-height theorem is imported.
6. All sums over q,k in the proof use actual nonempty polynomial support. A
   positive convergent extension was used only AFTER absolute values to bound
   their mass. Every root/puncture hole is retained in the original factor or
   explicitly restored as in(10). Extra slot holes are fixed coefficients
   permitted by MI; MP with arbitrary coefficients is never invoked. Disjoint
   original slot pools can meet inverse/plain factors or q/k freely. None of
   these intersections is replaced by an independence assumption.

The physical meaning of(6) is deliberately limited. It can be applied on an
ACTUAL positive child norm only after the original signed reconstruction has
produced that norm, its complete character and its live slot list. One must
test the defined dominance class with that child's own R,D,Q and actual zero.
It cannot be attached to a parent and pushed through a signed projector.
Keep both projectors, missing radicals, joint-label counting, every original
clipped rectangle, all extraction scalars and masks unchanged. A Cauchy pair
averages its two actual child savings; a gain on one side is not doubled.

For a raw decomposition w=u b^6 the old root holes remain frozen before free
summation. This report proves the local free-row lemma and its exact source
complement, not a uniformly improved raw envelope: Omega_c still has the old
bound. All other raw roots, low/high and fixed-inducing branches, bounded free
windows, first/second/artificial zero, old-only descendants, actual6a/9a radii,

Delta-before-target supremum return therefore retain their OLD paid estimates.
No new physical comparison is performed and the centered M/24 reserve is unspent.

## 3. A fixed relative conductor retains its inverse square root

Fix a good radical \(\mathfrak r\). Split all six labels into their \(\mathfrak r\)-parts and coprime parts. The latter obey HC12 at
\[
U=Y_D/q_{a_R},\qquad V=Y_E/q_{b_R}.
\]
If one of these scales is below the nonempty outer-support range, there are no terms; their bounded lower endpoints are harmless. Each conductor prime contributes
\[
M_p^B=\sum_{\substack{\alpha,\beta\ge0,\ i,j\in\{0,1\},\ k,l\ge0\\
i-j+3(k-l)-\alpha+\beta\not\equiv0\ (6)}}
B_p(\alpha)B_p(\beta)
q_p^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/3-(i+j)/2-k-l}. \tag{HC13}
\]
The extra \(1/6\) in each outer exponent comes from counting the coherent sixth powers after the conductor parts consume their outer length.

Put \(F_p=\sum_{j\ge0}B_p(j)q_p^{-2j/3}\). Direct summation gives
\[
F_p=1+\frac{q_p^{-2/3}+q_p^{-5/6}+2q_p^{-1}
+q_p^{-7/6}+q_p^{-4/3}}{1-q_p^{-1}}
=1+O(q_p^{-2/3}). \tag{HC14}
\]
The zero exponent vector is excluded from HC13. Enlarging to every other vector gives
\[
M_p^B\le F_p^2
\frac{(1+q_p^{-1/2})^2}{(1-q_p^{-1})^2}-1
\ll q_p^{-1/2}. \tag{HC15}
\]
The local constants have subpower product, so
\[
\boxed{\mathscr M_{\mathfrak r}^{B}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon(Y_DY_E)^{2/3}R^{-1/2+\epsilon}.} \tag{HC16}
\]
This is an absolute coefficient estimate, not a change of the actual field. The original roots, ray factors, signed marks, collision masks and profiles remain in that field. No prime of \(\mathfrak r\) is moved into the fixed excluded set. Polynomial conductor ranges allow the displayed small powers to be absorbed in the final \(Z^\epsilon\).

## R5. The 24 positive-exponent terms and both mixed terms

Write H=H_free+H_pos using the exact 12/24 signed-occurrence division. Every exponent in H_pos is at least 1, so its product-n coefficient obeys

    |b_pos,z(n)| <=24 d_3(n)n^(-delta).                      (R5.1)

The ordered divisor count is a valid enlargement of the distinct unordered source and includes all squareful outputs and repeated representations. Hence D_pos is absolutely convergent, locally uniformly holomorphic, for Re s>1-delta. With sigma=1-delta+epsilon and v=log(n/x),

    n^(-delta)g(v)=n^(-1-epsilon)x^sigma e^(sigma v)g(v).

The last Gaussian factor has finite supremum and sum_n d_3(n)n^(-1-epsilon)=zeta(1+epsilon)^3. Thus

    |H_pos(theta,x)| <<_(delta,epsilon) x^(1-delta+epsilon), x>=1,   (R5.2)

uniformly in theta and chi. Every mask applied identically to the monomials preserves this absolute estimate.

Set delta=3/5. For any nonnegative theta weight of mass at most 1 and the shell measure dx/x on [X,2X], R2.3 and R5.2 imply

    ||H||, ||H_free|| << X,
    ||H_pos|| <<_epsilon X^(2/5+epsilon).

The full energy difference is

    ||H||^2-||H_free||^2
       =<H_free,H_pos>+<H_pos,H_free>+||H_pos||^2.           (R5.3)

Both ordered mixed terms cost at most X^(7/5+epsilon), after renaming the arbitrary epsilon, and the square costs X^(4/5+epsilon). This proves the author's unconditional comparison, including for K_h, truncated K_h, and common tuple/product masks. The comparison lies below target energy 3/2 and 5/3, but not below energy 1. If a retained norm at exponent gamma>2/5 is assumed, norm transfer instead prices the two mixed terms at gamma+2/5+epsilon and the square at 4/5+epsilon. At gamma=1/2 these are 9/10+epsilon and 4/5+epsilon. One must not use the unconditional 7/5 estimate to claim the half-strip target.

The full zero-exponent source also reconstructs exactly. Fix the free label and collect the other pair m<n. Their polynomial is (mn)^(-2z)(m^(-z)-n^(-z))^2, and the free label must avoid BOTH m and n. Therefore, initially for Re s>1,

    D_free(s,z)=sum_(m<n) a(m)a(n)(mn)^(-s-2z)
       (m^(-z)-n^(-z))^2 [F(s)-a(m)m^(-s)-a(n)n^(-s)].      (R5.4)

Each triple is counted once for each of its three possible free labels, each contributing four raw permutation terms. This reproduces all 12 occurrences. The two collision corrections are necessary; neither can be dropped. In particular the polynomial identity is not an assertion of independent labels after collisions.

For delta=3/5, D_pos is holomorphic on Re s>2/5. Every pole that the determinant actually detects in that half-plane must therefore lie in D_free. A fixed determinant can still have a zero cofactor at a particular L-zero; this statement does not prove that each individual theta detects every zero. Recovery R4.3 removes that issue for the new readout. Deleting the complete free sector leaves a holomorphic fixed-source transform in the region and loses this determinant pole mechanism.

=(floor(nu/2)+1)^2. Counting coprime integers and d_2(d^2)<=d_3(d)
pays the errors and the convergent constant. The finite v convolution
retains all its cross terms under Cauchy-Schwarz and gives
sum_(n<=Y)|c(n)|^2<<_(p,q)Y. It does not assert an exact c asymptotic.

Consequently, for M>=X the full actual source tail satisfies

    ||sum_(n>M)c(n)f_x(n)||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^6 M^(-4).   (9)

The exact expansion g(n)=sum_(r^2m=n)d_2(r)chi(r)^2 mu(m)chi(m)
transfers the fixed-degree logarithmic input from

Use the fixed torus/filtration, finite character expansion and a fixed

No GRH power remark or growing complexity is imported. Abel summation
of the actual damping and M=X(log X)^B in(9) then give, for each fixed D,

    ||C||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D),
    ||C||_1 << X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D).                     (10)

The constants may be ineffective. Every fixed D still falls short of a
power X^(gamma+epsilon), gamma<1. Equation(6) transfers the logarithmic
bound to the complete core. This is a complete arithmetic test with a
recorded failure, not an inferred power improvement. Standard Liouville
Euler ancestry is also noted in
[Humphries, arXiv v2, pp1-2](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1569441/1/Humphries_the_distribution_of_weighted_sums_of_the_liouville.pdf);
his RH/LI/moment distribution hypotheses are not used.

For fixed k>2,b>1, the same single-square argument gives high cost
X^(b/2)A^(-1/2)+(X/A)^(k/(2k-1)). If b>=2k/(2k-1), the first term
dominates. Even the weaker Minkowski short-source corridor
alpha<=(4gamma-b)/3 is nonempty for every fixed gamma>1/2, by choosing
fixed1<b<=2gamma and sufficiently large fixed k. The complete return
retains all K shifts D_c(z+(b-1)j), with1-(b-1)K<gamma. Finite strip
descent makes every positive shift holomorphic before solving the

The independent finite run checked56 exact collision identities, three

The asymptotic proofs are(1)-(10) and the full retained arguments.

## 6. Tests17 and22: the rare code and wildcard curvature paths

### Test17: an exact original-H coding calculation

Use JN7-JN10 with the whole d sum already recombined. For one distinct-norm
prime pair, Q=q_pi q_pi', the finite group has size Q^2, and its literal
phase-character kernel is

    K(h,s,s')=chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3
                         chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4.          (24)

The full native term pairs this with W_hat, its fixed CRT/ray factor and
both outside prime coefficients. The Fourier transform has normalization
1/Q, is unitary, and retains the plus sign on the conjugate mark in JN7.
The exact support U consists of h unit modulo pi*pi', s unit modulo pi,
s' unit modulo pi', so

    |U|=(q_pi-1)^2(q_pi'-1)^2, ||K||_2=sqrt(|U|).           (25)

A syndrome that records only these unit/nonunit bits is constant on U.
The mean of K on U is ZERO because the s character chi_pi^2 is nontrivial.
Its full conditional variance is therefore1, not0. The entire pairing
survives in the conditional covariance with W_hat. Cauchy gives
`|sum_U K W_hat|<=sqrt(|U|)||1_U(W_hat-mean_U W_hat)||_2`,
with no new norm saving. If a richer syndrome records K itself, covariance
can vanish but the complete original sum moves into its predictable term.
It is not eliminated. The law of total expectation keeps both pieces.

For the affordable actual residue-field test, take a degree-one prime of
norm7. Choose the order-six character orientation chi(3)=exp(2pi i/6),
where3 is a primitive root in F7; conjugating the character conjugates
the following phases and preserves their distinction.
The unit residues s=1 and3 have identical unit syndrome but cubic phases
1 and exp(2pi i/3). Complete summation of chi(s)^2 over all six units is0.
Using norm13 for the second prime and h=s'=1 leaves that exact difference.
This is a local kernel fact, not a claim about the full global Hecke weight.

The metric part of the first test is equally literal: for every good
prime pi of norm>3, s=1 and2 are both units and have the SAME unit
syndrome, while their native mark frequencies differ by1/pi, of complex
absolute value q_pi^(-1/2). Taking larger pi makes distinct frequencies
arbitrarily close inside that one fiber. On the nonzero kernel support
the unit syndrome is constant, so it cannot itself separate frequency
packets. This rejects that concrete coding choice; a richer arithmetic
code would need a proved metric relation and its full covariance return.

An arbitrary test vector W_hat=conj(K) on U would saturate Cauchy, showing
why no coefficient-free code theorem can improve it. That vector is NOT
asserted to satisfy native row/mark supports. The existing JN and [private research revision]
uncertainty bounds supply stronger actual-support restrictions; their
remaining signed pairing is precisely what would have to be estimated.
This is a source-specific version of the existing W44 conditional-covariance
warning, not a new coding family or an actual H lower bound.

### Test22: parabolic frequency cells have no free curvature return

For a fixed original prime pair and physical indices, the JN7 additive
phase is

    -R h/(pi*pi') - P s/pi + P' s'/pi',                     (26)

inside the original additive character. As a function of real frequency
coordinates h,s,s', its Hessian is ZERO. It is bilinear when physical
and frequency variables move jointly; no assertion of a zero joint
Hessian is made. Curvature in inverse prime locations would be a different
source-dependent problem, retaining all moving weights and sharp masks.

At the largest denominators the exact adjacent row frequencies h and
h+1 differ by1/(pi*pi'), of absolute value Q^(-1/2), asymptotic to1/N.
Adjacent mark frequencies differ by1/pi or1/pi', of size N^(-1/2).
These are the native lattice spacings. A proposed parabolic cell does
not increase them; any useful separation still has to be shown for its
actual coefficient-bearing subset and priced complement.

Thus parabolic cells in just these frequency coordinates do not get a
stationary-phase saving from a nonexistent quadratic term. More decisively,
the accepted JN12 bound applies to the exact recombined native tensor:
for every row-frequency set E of cardinality J, independent of the two
mark coordinates,

    ||1_E(h) W_hat||_2^2 <= C_orig K J/Q ||W_hat||_2^2.       (27)

This follows from original row support O(K), row Cauchy and all three
unitary finite transforms. It preserves both projectors and all signed
short-core terms. A proposed O(N)-frequency curved packet captures at
most O(K/N)=O(Z^(-.003)) of squared norm at the hard box. Capturing a
fixed norm fraction requires J of order at least Q/K, regardless of
the shape of the cell. This is the previously proved JN obstruction,
reused instead of reproved as a new result.

It does not lower-bound H, rule out adaptive sets depending on marks, or
preclude signed cancellation in the omitted pairing. The complete far
complement remains exactly that signed omitted form. The wildcard path
therefore fails in its proposed frequency-curvature/norm-capture form;
no reroll or replacement test was performed.

# [private research revision] discovery-first source pass — quantitative short windows and a calibrated multiplicative obstruction



Current checkpoint: policies, relevant current proof/index, [private research revision] headroom/source integrations and both [private research revision] integrations consulted. Seven mechanisms were screened. The result is a complete conditional short-window energy return and a calibrated multiplicative countermodel to deriving its needed power saving from coarse qualitative source data. No actual arithmetic energy improvement and no endpoint gain is claimed. Original04:15 deadline and subsequent recovery failures remain recorded; source evidence, exact checks and the freeze manifest accompany this report.

## Discovery and selection

1. Power-uniform short-window square energy of the literal mu*chi source. Its square-root target at H=X^theta would give c=theta/2, so theta> .250278 beats the incumbent and theta=1/3,1/2 retains1/6,1/4. The complete Gaussian/offset-averaged bridge is developed below. Unlike a finite projection, this estimates an actual arithmetic correlation aggregate.
2. Logarithmically averaged two-point multiplicative correlations, combined with quantitative window growth. Tao's primary arXiv1509.05422v4,29July2016, Theorem1.2 and Corollary1.5 were opened on the web. Its fixed-linear-form, qualitative logarithmic conclusion is not a power-uniform growing-lag theorem. The new obstruction below remains even after strengthening those conclusions to ordinary Cesaro correlations and adding the accepted summatory calibration.
3. Liouville primitive-pair/gcd source. The dormant headroom-B seed and old W24 square-divisor return remain valid. For each ordinary character the exact numerator L(2s,chi^2) is nonzero on Re(s)>1/2; complete lambda*chi Gaussian control would return the same zero strip. Its actual primitive-pair/short-window energy is still needed. No squarefree source is replaced by a completely multiplicative surrogate.
4. Growing two-grid arithmetic-wavelet capture (F08/F19). [private research revision] removes the fixed-grid repair and proves a common-signal comparison. A full signed capture on sigma=.75 would reach1/4, but common-grid absence of resonances does not prove capture. No new tail/cross-grid estimate was found in this pass; keep it open.
5. Fractional reciprocal and signed renewal (W22/W35). Fixed positive fractional order retains the zero signal and potentially all gamma>1/2. Existing renewal and absolute-contraction obstructions already block a profile-only gain. The new biased multiplicative model gives an additional source-level test: a coherent exponent is compatible with all the coarse multiplicative data, so the actual prime signs or a power-uniform correlation have to enter.
6. Higher-order simultaneous logarithmic-derivative/Turan detectors. These use different prime-power coefficients and amplify a possible zero. A complete return would require quantitative signed prime-polynomial bounds with derivative order, height and pole subtraction controlled together. Known qualitative correlations do not supply this bridge; no transfer from original moments is asserted. Protected as a higher-ceiling mechanism, not developed into a theorem here.
7. [private research revision] complete polynomial projection and block source, combined with growing-scale arithmetic correlations. Their errors are already paid, but rank reduction and the summatory baseline reproduce only the incumbent. The selected averaged-window estimate keeps the full signed cross terms and makes the additional power requirement explicit. It is not claimed as a replacement arithmetic estimate merely because blocks are available.

These selections rotate away from the .68 split/600-cell atlas. All29 original families/109 child IDs and unused valid components remain intact. Ancestry is retained; no claim of literature priority is made.

## Theorem M: a calibrated multiplicative obstruction

For every fixed tau>0, fixed q>=1, numbers 1/2<gamma<beta<b6, and any finite prescribed prime values of modulus one away from q, there exists one multiplicative complex sequence a with a(1)=1 and |a(n)|=mu(n)^2*1_((n,q)=1), matching those prime values, such that:

- its summatory function is O_epsilon(x^(beta+epsilon)), with the same bound for every fixed ordinary-character twist;
- every fixed nondegenerate pair of positive affine forms has vanishing normalized Cesaro two-point correlation, both with and without conjugation;
- its complete fixed Gaussian is C_tau*x^beta+O(x^sigma) for every fixed sigma in(1/2,beta), with C_tau nonzero.

Consequently the accepted summatory calibration, exact multiplicativity, natural squareful/ramified zeros, arbitrary finite prime checks and even these stronger qualitative pair correlations do not imply a first-gain complete Gaussian estimate. The sequence is not mu*chi and does not preserve its global prime-sign law. The theorem is a precise restriction on a proposed use of coarse data, not an obstruction to the actual arithmetic problem.

Construction: independent Steinhaus epsilon_p and independent Bernoulli I_p with mean p^(beta-1); put v_p=1 when I_p=1, otherwise epsilon_p, then impose the finite prescriptions. The centered prime series gives an exact meromorphic factorization D_a(s)=zeta(s+1-beta)H(s), with H analytic and nonvanishing on Re(s)>1/2. The rare changed-prime set has summable reciprocal mass and summable sigma-mass for every sigma>beta. The complete proof follows.

### M1. Probability space, support, and summatory calibration

A Steinhaus variable is uniform on the complex unit circle. All epsilon_p and I_p are mutually independent. Initially set a(n)=mu(n)^2 product_{p|n}v_p; delete every prime dividing q and replace finitely many other prime values by their prescribed unit values. This is ordinary multiplicativity, not complete multiplicativity. It gives exactly the asserted squareful and ramified zeros, a(1)=1, and modulus one on every remaining squarefree integer. Prescribing all primes up to any fixed bound matches the full finite prefix of any particular mu*chi source with that conductor support.

Put P={p:I_p=1}. For b>beta,

  E sum_{p in P}p^(-b)=sum_p p^(-(b+1-beta))<infinity.

Consequently, almost surely, sum_{p in P}p^(-b)<infinity for every rational b>beta, hence every real b>beta. In particular sum_{p in P}1/p<infinity. For any b in(beta,1), # {p in P:p<=x} <= x^b sum_{p in P}p^(-b)=O_b(x^b). Neither statement uses a prime-number theorem.

Let a0(n)=mu(n)^2 product_{p|n}epsilon_p. For n!=m, E[a0(n) conjugate(a0(m))]=0, and E|a0(n)|^2<=1. The same holds after multiplying by any fixed ordinary character psi. A useful elementary maximal estimate for such orthogonal variables is

  E max_{m<=2^k}|sum_{n<=m}a0(n)psi(n)|^2 <= (k+1)^2 2^k.

Indeed, decompose each initial segment into at most k+1 disjoint dyadic blocks, apply Cauchy, then bound its sum of block squares by the sum over every block on every dyadic level. The expectation of the total on each level is at most2^k. Markov's inequality at threshold2^{k(1/2+eta)} and Borel--Cantelli give, for every eta>0,

  M0,psi(x)=O_{eta,psi}(x^(1/2+eta))

almost surely. Intersect the probability-one events for rational eta>0 and the countable set of ordinary characters. We retain one outcome on this intersection throughout the argument.

At a changed prime, the exact local quotient is

  (1+v z)/(1+epsilon z)
    =1+sum_{j>=1}(v-epsilon)(-epsilon)^(j-1)z^j.

Its nonconstant coefficient moduli are at most2. Therefore a=a0*d as a Dirichlet convolution, with

  sum_n |d(n)|n^(-b)
   <= finite_factor * product_{p in P}(1+2p^(-b)/(1-p^(-b)))<infinity

for every b>beta. Deleting the finitely many primes of q or imposing finitely many values adds quotients analytic and absolutely convergent for b>0. Complete multiplicativity of psi gives a psi=(a0 psi)*(d psi), where juxtaposition is pointwise multiplication and the star here is Dirichlet convolution. All occurrences of the literal mu*chi source elsewhere in this report mean the pointwise coefficients mu(n)chi(n). Choosing eta with1/2+eta<b now gives

  |sum_{n<=x}a(n)psi(n)|
   <= C x^b sum_{d<=x}|d(d)|d^(-b) =O_b(x^b).

In this display d(d) denotes the convolution coefficient at integer d, not a divisor-counting function. Thus the claimed beta+epsilon bound holds for every epsilon>0 (larger exponents are harmless). Abel summation also proves

  sum_{n<=x}a(n)psi(n)n^(it)
      =O_{epsilon,psi}((1+|t|)x^(beta+epsilon))

uniformly for all real t. Any fixed number of log n factors costs x^epsilon after shrinking the original epsilon. Constants depend on the chosen outcome and fixed character; this is not a conductor-uniform theorem.

### M2. Exact continuation and complete Gaussian readout

Before the finite changes, E v_p=theta_p=p^(beta-1). The centered independent variables xi_p=v_p-theta_p have mean zero and variance at most1. Apply the same dyadic maximal proof to the sequence equal to xi_p on primes and zero on composites. Almost surely,

  S(x)=sum_{p<=x}xi_p=O_eta(x^(1/2+eta))

for every eta>0. Abel summation then defines

  Z(s)=sum_p xi_p p^(-s)=s integral_1^infinity S(x)x^(-s-1) dx

holomorphically on Re(s)>1/2. On every fixed closed vertical strip with left edge sigma0>1/2 it satisfies |Z(s)|<=C(1+|Im s|), after choosing eta<sigma0-1/2.

For Re(s)>1 the absolutely convergent Euler product D_a(s)=sum a(n)n^(-s)=product_p(1+v_p p^(-s)) satisfies

  D_a(s)=zeta(s+1-beta) H(s),

where H is the exponential of

  Z(s)
  +sum_p sum_{j>=2} (-1)^(j+1) v_p^j p^(-js)/j
  -sum_p sum_{j>=2} p^(-j(s+1-beta))/j.

Both double tails converge absolutely and locally uniformly on Re(s)>1/2: their leading prime exponents are2 Re(s)>1 and2(Re(s)+1-beta)>1. Hence H is holomorphic and nonvanishing there, with |H(s)|<=exp(C(1+|Im s|)) on every fixed closed vertical strip. The finitely many deletions or prescriptions multiply H by factors1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) or(1+v'_p p^(-s))/(1+v_p p^(-s)). They are analytic and nonzero on Re(s)>0, with bounded modulus on any such strip; the conclusions persist. Thus D_a has a simple pole at beta with nonzero residue H(beta). No supposition about zeta zeros is needed.

Normalize the fixed Gaussian by

  g_tau(u)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2*tau)),
  F_a(x)=sum_{n>=1}a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

Absolute convergence follows from |a(n)|<=1. Mellin inversion on any line Re(s)>1 gives

  F_a(x)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral e^(tau*s^2/2)D_a(s)x^s ds.

Shift to any fixed sigma in(1/2,beta). Zeta has at most polynomial growth on the fixed strip in question, for example by Euler--Maclaurin summation; H has the exponential bound above. The factor exp(-tau*t^2/2) therefore pays the entire infinite-height integral and both horizontal sides. The sole pole crossed is beta. This proves

  F_a(x)=e^(tau*beta^2/2)H(beta)x^beta+O_sigma(x^sigma).

The leading constant is nonzero. This is the complete Gaussian, with no height truncation or omitted tails. The same proof permits fixed derivatives. As x tends to zero, the original absolutely convergent sum is smaller than every positive power of x: for each A>1 use g_tau(log(n/x))<=C_A(x/n)^A. This pays the other end of later Mellin transforms.

### M3. Fixed affine correlations, including conjugation

Take fixed positive-slope affine forms L_i(n)=A_i n+B_i, integer coefficients, A_i>0, with A1 B2-A2 B1!=0. Finitely many n for which a form is nonpositive may be discarded. First change only a fixed finite set F of prime values; include primes of q. Write Q=product_{p in F}p and D=2^{|F|}. On a nonzero term write L1(n)=d r, L2(n)=e s, with d,e|Q and r,s squarefree and coprime to Q. Any ramified or squareful zero is simply omitted.

After conditioning on all random values at primes in F, the remaining conjugated monomial is epsilon(r/s); the unconjugated monomial is epsilon(rs). Distinct positive rational ratios, respectively distinct positive integer products, are orthogonal under the remaining Steinhaus variables. For a fixed ratio r/s and fixed d,e, the equation L1(n)/L2(n)=(d/e)(r/s) has at most one n, because the determinant is nonzero. A monomial class therefore contains at most D^2 terms. For a fixed product rs and fixed d,e, the quadratic equation L1(n)L2(n)=de*rs has at most two n, giving at most2D^2 terms. Coefficients arising from finite prime values or fixed character weights have modulus at most1. Consequently, for either correlation sum C_N,

  E |C_N|^2 <= 2D^2 N+O_F(1).

Markov and Borel--Cantelli along N=j^2 show C_{j^2}/j^2 tends to zero almost surely; bounded summands fill the gaps, since(j+1)^2-j^2=O(j). Take the countable intersection over finite F, integer affine pairs, and fixed ordinary character weights. The estimate is uniform over conditioned finite prime phases, since only their moduli entered.

Now transfer to the infinite random set P. Truncate it at Y, along with the fixed prescriptions and primes of q. The infinite and truncated sequences can differ at a positive integer only if some p in P above Y divides it. For a fixed form A n+B, put the finitely many p|A into the truncation. Each remaining p has at most N/p+1 roots with n<=N and p<=C N. The density of exceptional n is therefore at most

  sum_{p in P,p>Y}1/p + O(#P(CN)/N).

The second term tends to zero by the bound O(N^b), b<1; the first tends to zero as Y tends to infinity. Products of two bounded terms change by at most2 on the union of their exceptional sets. First take N to infinity, then Y to infinity. Both asserted Cesaro correlations vanish. This argument is compatible with the probability-one events of M1 and M2 because the whole list is countable. It produces one fixed outcome, not a new sequence at each scale.

In particular, for every FIXED integer H>=1,

  (1/N) sum_{m<=N}|sum_{j=1}^H a(m+j)|^2 -> H d_q,

where d_q=product_{p|q}(1-1/p) product_{p not dividing q}(1-1/p^2)>0 is the squarefree coprime density. Off-diagonal terms vanish by M3; the diagonal follows by the elementary squarefree density computation. There is no uniformity for growing H. Ordinary Cesaro cancellation also implies the qualitative logarithmic fixed-form conclusions by partial summation, including long logarithmic intervals with length parameter tending to infinity. It does not establish every nonpretentiousness hypothesis of an outside theorem, nor its quantitative uniformities.

### M4. Finite masks and what the obstruction actually excludes

Every feasible fixed valuation pattern on a finite set of unramified primes has Dirichlet series D_a(s) multiplied by a product of factors1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) for valuation0 and v_p p^(-s)/(1+v_p p^(-s)) for valuation1. These factors are nonzero at beta. Every such individual masked complete Gaussian retains a nonzero beta mode. An arbitrary signed combination of masks can cancel that mode only by making its combined multiplier vanish at beta; a return to the original source must then repay the missing signal. The full exact recombination retains it. Patterns at ramified primes that require positive valuation are identically zero and are not called feasible.

This strengthens the relevant [private research revision] coarse calibrated countermodel by imposing genuine multiplicativity, exact natural zero support, arbitrary finite prime prescriptions, all fixed character-twist summatory bounds, and vanishing fixed affine correlations. W27 already constructed a multiplicative real-sign source with a prescribed finite prefix and poles inside the baseline strip; multiplicativity itself is therefore not new here. W27 explicitly left quantitative partial-sum/height calibration unproved. The addition here is the simultaneous proven calibration, fixed affine correlation cancellation, and forced growing-window energy lower bound, at the cost of allowing complex unit phases. This is not a strengthening in real-valuedness. It retains W24/W27's warning about global inversion. It is not a counterexample within the actual mu*chi family: at infinitely many unramified primes its unit value differs from -chi(p), and its Dirichlet convolution inverse is not the prescribed character source. Real-valuedness is also not asserted. Thus a proof using the global Möbius prime law, exact convolution inverse, or sufficiently uniform quantitative correlations can escape the obstruction. This is a scoped mathematical test of a proposed mechanism, not a general impossibility statement.

## Theorem B: exact complete offset-averaged short-window return

Let |a(n)|<=1 for positive integers, and extend a(n)=0 for n<=0. Fix tau>0, X>=1, and integer H>=1. Define

  B_H(k)=sum_{k-H<n<=k}a(n),
  w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4*tau)),
  E_a(X,H)=(1/H)sum_{k>=1}|B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

The sum includes every positive endpoint and all Gaussian tails. It is finite by the Gaussian decay; it is neither a projected rank nor an energy restricted to selected lag terms. Put ell=log2 and

  K_tau=exp(ell^2/(3*tau))
     *[exp(tau/3+4*ell/3)/sqrt(3*pi*tau)+1/(pi*tau)].

Then the complete uniform return is

  sup_{X<=x<=2X}|F_a(x)|
    <= sqrt(K_tau*(X/H+1)*E_a(X,H))+2H*g_tau(0).       (B)

### B1. Proof with all offsets, tails, and mixed terms

For each r in{1,...,H}, partition the integer line into blocks(k-H,k] whose positive right endpoints k are congruent to r modulo H, and use the zero extension on the initial partial block. Set

  V_r(x)=sum_{k>=1,k congruent r mod H} B_H(k)g_tau(log(k/x)).

The total variation of t -> g_tau(log(t/x)) on(0,infinity) is2g_tau(0). On one block, replacing each value at n by its right endpoint value costs at most H times the variation on that block. Summing disjoint blocks proves

  |F_a(x)-V_r(x)|<=2H*g_tau(0)

uniformly in x. This pays the complete replacement error, including the first block and both infinite tails; no summatory cancellation was used.

For u=log(x/X) in[0,ell] and v=log(k/X), the Cauchy weight quotient is

  g_tau(v-u)^2 / exp(-v^2/(4*tau))
    =(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp(-3v^2/(4*tau)+2uv/tau-u^2/tau).

As a function of t=k/X this is positive and unimodal. Its integral over t>0 equals

  exp(tau/3+4u/3+u^2/(3*tau))/sqrt(3*pi*tau),

and its supremum is exp(u^2/(3*tau))/(2*pi*tau). A positive unimodal function sampled on a grid of spacing H/X has sum at most(X/H) times its integral plus twice its supremum: split at the maximum and compare each monotone tail with adjacent grid integrals. Thus the quotient sum on every offset grid is at most K_tau*(X/H+1).

Writing E_r=sum_{k congruent r}|B_H(k)|^2w_X(k), Cauchy gives |V_r(x)|<=sqrt(K_tau*(X/H+1)*E_r). Average the identity F_a=V_r+error over all r and apply Jensen to sqrt(E_r). Since H^(-1)sum_r E_r=E_a, inequality(B) follows. This proves a supremum, so the log-shell L2 norm is also at most sqrt(log2) times its right side. No omitted cross terms are estimated as though positive.

For clarity the EXACT arithmetic content of E is

  E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_{|h|<H}
    sum_{n>=max(1,1-h)} a(n)conjugate(a(n+h))
    *sum_{j=max(0,h)}^{min(H-1,H-1+h)}w_X(n+j).       (L)

Indeed B_H(k)=sum_{j=0}^{H-1}a(k-j); write n=k-j and h=j-l in its square. All sums converge absolutely. Formula(L) includes every diagonal, both signs of every lag, and the exact moving weight. Replacing the inner weight by(H-|h|)w_X(n) would introduce an error not used or hidden here. A bounded exact check accompanies the report solely to guard these indices, not to certify the analytic theorem.

### B2. Exact arithmetic estimate needed for a gain

Choose theta in(0,1), H=floor(X^theta), and suppose that for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

  E_{mu*chi}(X,H) <<_{epsilon,chi,tau} X^(e+epsilon).   (A)

Then(B), after absorbing floors, yields the complete Gaussian estimate with every epsilon loss and limiting exponent

  gamma=max(theta,(1-theta+e)/2).

For a strict first gain over b6=.874861 it suffices that theta<b6 and

  e<2*b6-1+theta=.749722+theta.

At theta=.26, the limiting current threshold is e<1.009722. To reach gamma=.87449, c=.12551, it suffices to prove e=1.00898 with every epsilon loss. This is the upstream source analogue of the .000742 gap between the .249722 baseline and the .24898 target Gaussian moment, but(A) is a different, complete arithmetic estimate and must be proved in its own normalization.

The deliberately coarse square-root averaged energy E<<X^(1+epsilon) would give:

  theta=.26 -> gamma=.87, c=.13;
  theta=1/3 -> gamma=5/6, c=1/6;
  theta=1/2 -> gamma=3/4, c=1/4.

Even the weaker pair theta=.6, e=1.1 gives gamma=.75. These are conditional returns, not established candidates. The rigorous bound available without new arithmetic is only E<=H sum_k w_X(k)<<_tau XH+H, hence exponent e=1+theta. Comparing it with the strict first-gain threshold leaves the fixed power gap2*c6=.250278, independent of theta. Qualitative o(XH), if available in precisely this weighted setting, does not close that gap. The original summatory calibration alone does not give the needed high-frequency window energy; Theorem M makes that failure concrete rather than merely noting a missing proof.

### B3. Zero-exclusion return and family scope

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q, take literally a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including its natural zeros. Its Dirichlet series on Re(s)>1 is1/L(s,chi), so direct absolute Mellin interchange gives

  integral_0^infinity F_a(x)x^(-s) dx/x
    = e^(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

The x->0 estimate in M2 used only |a(n)|<=1 and applies here. If(A) holds, the dyadic-shell estimate gives F_a(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for all x>=1. For every fixed s with Re(s)>gamma, choose epsilon strictly below Re(s)-gamma. The Mellin integral therefore continues holomorphically to that half-plane, locally uniformly on compact subsets. The Gaussian transform is entire and nonzero. By identity with the usual meromorphic continuation, L(s,chi) has no zeros there. The principal-character pole at s=1 is compatible with a zero of1/L and is not a zero-exclusion violation; zero multiplicity causes no cancellation because the numerator never vanishes.

All heights are included by the Mellin transform and absolute x-integrability on compact subsets; no height cutoffs or finite numerical height data are substituted. The H parameter grows only inside the estimate; the returned F is the original fixed Gaussian, so no moving transform is analytically continued. Choose tau,theta,e and the intended strict target before character, scale, epsilon bookkeeping, or data-dependent selection. Constants may depend on the fixed ordinary character and tau. To assert the result for every q and character, hypothesis(A) is needed separately for each such character with the same theta,e. No uniform conductor constant is claimed. This is ordinary Dirichlet scope; no Hecke, arbitrary number-field, or nonordinary Eisenstein extension is inferred. The project's exact guide/root-L-function binding remains controller work; no proof-assistant activity is performed.

This architecture replaces the original source theorem and pays its own complete Gaussian return. It does not reuse old Gao moments, pretend the old29-family/109-child decomposition disappeared, or leave a shortening complement inside an asserted old theorem. Those objects remain valid and untouched in their own route. No extraction error, moving Euler factor, missing radical, physical K^(5/6), 9a exception, or descendant is silently promoted: none of the old local estimates is invoked to prove(A). If(A) is eventually derived from them, each of those costs must be transferred explicitly at that time. The separate full-H .004 requirement is also not met by this report.

## The quantitative obstruction to the selected bridge

Apply(B) to Theorem M's fixed sequence with H=floor(X^theta), theta<beta. Since F_a(X)=C_tau X^beta+O(X^sigma), C_tau!=0, the replacement error O(H) is smaller than the leading term. Therefore, for every sufficiently large X,

  E_a(X,H) >= c_{a,tau,theta} X^(2*beta-1+theta).     (O)

Thus an energy estimate E<<X^(1+delta+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 is impossible in this class when theta-delta>2(1-beta). This is a strict exponent comparison. Equality is not ruled out, and no equality/strict-reserve impossibility is asserted for the epsilon-loss endpoint problem.

Numerically choose gamma=.87449, beta=.8747 and a summatory calibration exponent .8748<b6. These choices all satisfy the theorem. At theta=.26 the proposed target energy exponent is1.00898, whereas(O) forces at least1.0094, a gap.00042. Yet for every fixed H the same sequence has the square-root Cesaro energy limit H*d_q proved in M3. The exact failed step is passing from every fixed-lag qualitative cancellation to a power-uniform assertion for H=X^.26 while retaining a coherent low-frequency mode. Calibration, multiplicativity and all finite masks do not cure it.

For ANY proposed first-gain exponent gamma<b6, choose beta strictly between gamma and b6 and then a calibration exponent strictly between beta and b6. The same obstruction works. It therefore tests nearer improvements as well as1/6 and1/4; it is not tied to one optimized parameter. Conversely it does not exclude using genuinely quantitative information about the actual mu*chi coefficients, their global inverse relation, or a new arithmetic moment.

## D33. Exact small-prime covariance and a rapidly cancelling detector with the wrong transform

### D33.1 Actual local signs and their complete-period law

For finite P containing 2 and excluding 3, let

    Q=product_(p in P)p,
    e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(-1)^(1_(p|n)),
    W_P(x)=sum_(n>=1)e_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

These are f3's ACTUAL local signs at the listed primes: every positive p-adic valuation gives -1. The function e_P is Q-periodic, including n=0 in a complete period. Chinese remainder factorization gives exactly

    Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2/p)=0,
    Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)e_P(n+h)
       =product_(p in P) c_p(h),
    c_p(h)=1 if p|h; c_p(h)=1-4/p otherwise.            (D33.1)

For p not dividing h exactly the two distinct residues n=0,-h contribute -1 and the other p-2 contribute +1; for p|h both signs are equal at each residue. This proves the formula with no heuristic independence of actual integers outside the completed period. The p=2 factor is -1 for odd h and +1 for even h. The natural p=3 exemption is literal. Both prime powers and h=0 are included.

For P={2,5,7}, all 70 shifts were checked exactly with rational arithmetic. This is an arithmetic periodic identity, not a bound for f3(n)f3(n+h): multiplying the true rough-prime factors before averaging changes the measure and destroys the completed-period factorization.

The marginal-only optimization has a complementary decisive test. Keep every small-prime divisibility pattern fixed, but permit a free hidden rough sign r(n) in {+1,-1}. Choosing r(n)=e_P(n) makes e_P(n)r(n)=1 while preserving ALL observed patterns. For a positive Gaussian Gram this attains the magnitude-only maximum; sum_n g_tau(log(n/x))=x exp(tau/2)+O_tau(1) has norm of order X. Those constraints cannot certify gamma<1. This assignment is NOT the actual arithmetic rough sign and need not obey its prime-deletion relations. Controlling that dependence is the missing arithmetic input. ### D33.2 Quantitative Gaussian cancellation for a growing model

    e_P(n)=sum_(k=1,...,Q-1) b_k exp(2pi i k n/Q),
    |b_k|<=1.

There is no k=0 term because of (D33.1). Poisson summation and m>=2 integrations by parts show

    |W_P(x)|
      <= C_(tau,m) x sum_(k=1,...,Q-1) sum_(j in Z)
                              |x(j-k/Q)|^-m
      <= C'_(tau,m) x^(1-m) Q^m.                      (D33.2)

The reindexing r=Qj-k runs over nonzero integers not divisible by Q; their absolute m-series is at most 2zeta(m). The constant is independent of Q,P,x. No arbitrary ell-dependent mask is inserted into G9; this is direct Poisson on the stated periodic coefficient sequence.

For sufficiently large X it includes 2. The elementary bound Q<=floor(z_X)!<=z_X^z_X gives Q<=X^(a+o(1)), without PNT. Uniformly on the CLOSED shell [X,2X],

    |W_(P_X)(x)| <= X^(1-m(1-a)+o(1)).                (D33.3)

Given any A0>0, choose one fixed m>(1+A0)/(1-a). Then W_(P_X)=O(X^-A0), after using a strict margin to absorb the o(1). This finite-prime model therefore passes every candidate Gaussian moment exponent, including gamma=3/4. That favorable result proves nothing about the full f3 field.

## Proposed growing-order source theorem: statement and exact algebra

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q, and tau>0. In this report convolution is Dirichlet convolution, while a(n)=mu(n)chi(n) is a pointwise product. Set

  F(x)=sum_n a(n) g_tau(log(n/x)),
  g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
  D=d/d(log x), r=K-1, phi_r(v)=(1+d/dv)^r g_tau(v).

Then F_r=(1-D)^r F is exactly sum a(n)phi_r(log(n/x)). For large X, write L=log X and allow EVERY integer

  (1/2)L^(1/3)<=K<=2L^(1/3), K>=2.

Let Y=floor(exp(L/(K-1/2))), V=L/(2K-1), W=V/2. Thus the unrounded cutoff is exp(2V). Put m(n)=a(n)1_(n<=Y) and u=a-m. The global arithmetic law is a*chi=delta_1, including ramified zeros. Its exact K-fold expansion is

  u^{*K}*chi^{*(K-1)}
    =a+sum_(j=1)^K (-1)^j binom(K,j)m^{*j}*chi^{*(j-1)}.       (N1)

The j=1 term has chi^{*0}=delta_1. There is no pairwise-coprime assumption, and repeated primes shared between factors remain. Formula(N1) is a classical higher inverse identity, not a claimed invention. It is precisely where the G71 surrogate's missing prescribed inverse matters.

Define the complete short-factor source

  C_(X,K)(x)=(-1)^(K+1)
     sum_(d_1,...,d_K<=Y) product_i a(d_i)
     sum_(ell_1,...,ell_(K-1)>=1) product_j chi(ell_j)
       phi_(K-1)(log(d_1...d_K ell_1...ell_(K-1)/x)).          (N2)

Every ordered tuple and every plain factor is retained. The source is absolutely convergent for each fixed X,K,x; the absolute coefficients are bounded by d_(2K-1)(n). Introduce C^bal by imposing just the additional PRODUCT restriction

  X exp(-W)<=d_1...d_K<=2X exp(W).                          (N3)

No plain factor is capped, and all its character zeros remain. Each surviving d_i satisfies exp(V/2)<=d_i<=Y: divide the lower product bound by Y^(K-1)<=X exp(-V). Hence all its Möbius data lie between exp(c L^(2/3)) and exp(C L^(2/3)), uniformly over the K-band. These are genuine subpower factor lengths, not X^constant/k with fixed k.

The claimed uniform conclusion, proved in the following sections, is that for every fixed A>0,

  sup_(X<=x<=2X)|F_(K-1)(x)-C^bal_(X,K)(x)|
       =O_(A,q,tau)(X^(-A)),                              (N4)

uniformly for every allowed K. This pays all lower faces, the full all-large source, and both removed product tails. It does not estimate the surviving complete signed source.

## 2. Development04: full energy bridge and exact fixed-modulus target

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including imprimitive characters with their natural zeros. Let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n) and M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), zero for x<1. Complete multiplicativity gives

    (a*chi)(n)=chi(n) sum_(d|n)mu(d)=delta_(n=1).       (R1)

The literal logarithmic energy is

    E(X)=integral_1^X |M(x)|^2 dx/x
        =sum_(m,n<=X)a(m)conjugate(a(n))log(X/max(m,n)).
                                                               (R2)

Each pair enters the integral precisely at max(m,n). The upper-endpoint weight is zero, not a half-weight. The whole log X term and both orientations of every complex pair are retained. This is a positive Gram kernel with signed/complex off-diagonal summands; it is not a sum of positive pair contributions.

Suppose, for a common0<gamma<1 and every fixed chi and epsilon>0,

    E_chi(X) <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)        (R3)

for all large real X. Dyadic X suffice because E is monotone. For sigma0>gamma, choose epsilon<2(sigma0-gamma). On [2^j,2^(j+1)], Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the absolute integral of M(x)x^(-s) against dx/x, after any fixed k derivatives in s, by

    O_(chi,epsilon,k,sigma0)(
         (j+1)^k 2^(j(gamma+epsilon/2-sigma0))).

Thus H(s)=integral_1^infinity M(x)x^(-s)dx/x is holomorphic locally uniformly on Re(s)>gamma. Initially Re(s)>1, absolute interchange and (R1) give sH(s)=1/L(s,chi). The meromorphic identity L(s,chi)sH(s)=1 continues throughout that half-plane. A zero of L there is impossible. The principal pole at1 corresponds to a removable reciprocal zero; it is not accidentally excluded. Since gamma>0, no issue at s=0 enters.

This proves the claimed ALL-FINITE-HEIGHT return without a vertical reciprocal-growth hypothesis or pointwise extraction. Constants and starting scales may depend on the fixed character. There is no moving-conductor claim. Pointwise M(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) does imply (R3), but the author correctly does not infer a same-exponent pointwise bound from energy using only bounded increments.

For ALL phi(q) characters of one FIXED modulus, finite orthogonality gives

    Ebar_q(X)=(1/phi(q))sum_(chi mod q)E_chi(X)
      =sum_(m,n<=X,(mn,q)=1,m==n mod q)
                       mu(m)mu(n)log(X/max(m,n)).        (R4)

This includes the principal and every imprimitive character. No conjugate or zero mask is dropped. Each nonnegative E_chi is at most phi(q)Ebar_q, so a common exponent for EVERY FIXED q gives the required common exponent for EVERY FIXED chi. Averaging only a selected character subfamily would not yield (R4).

The diagonal is D_q(X)=sum_(n<=X,(n,q)=1)mu(n)^2 log(X/n). To verify its scale, insert mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) into the unit count. Counting the remaining units with error O_q(1), and paying the d^-2 tail, gives

    Q_q(t)=d_q t+O_q(sqrt t),

Then D_q(X)=integral_1^X Q_q(t)dt/t=d_q X+O_q(sqrt X+1). For gamma>1/2 this diagonal is already below the target squared exponent.

The missing estimate is precisely the COMPLETE signed scalar

    OFF_q(X)=sum_(m!=n<=X,(mn,q)=1,m==n mod q)
                       mu(m)mu(n)log(X/max(m,n))
      <<_(q,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)                (R5)

as a one-sided upper bound, for every fixed q and all sufficiently large X. Its imaginary part is zero by paired symmetry. No absolute values may be put inside the sum without creating a stronger, unpaid problem. Conversely an energy bound implies the same upper bound because OFF=Ebar-D. At q=1 this already asks for the complete unsolved Mobius energy. The fixed-family rewrite supplies no automatic orthogonality cancellation between same-residue integers.
