## 3. Protected rare27: integrated logarithmic Hankel operator

Fix one ordinary chi and 0<a<1. Put M=M_chi, with M(x)=0 for x<1, and

    h_a(v)=exp(-a v)M(exp v), v>=0.

For each L>0 let Gamma_(a,L) be the integral operator on L2(0,L) with kernel
h_a(t+u). All original arithmetic is inside the one complete M. Its associated
complex BILINEAR form is

    B_(a,L)(f,g)=integral_0^L integral_0^L h_a(t+u)f(t)g(u)dtdu.

The bilinear supremum equals the usual operator norm (complex conjugation in
the Hilbert pairing changes no norm). There is no unintended conjugation of
chi or of h. Kernels are bounded on every finite square, so all finite operators
are well-defined.

### 3.1 A uniform complete norm excludes all right-hand zeros

Assume

    K_(a,chi):=sup_(L>0)||Gamma_(a,L)|| < infinity.            (H)

squared norm is1/(2Re(z)). The map z->E_z is holomorphic into L2 on that

Q(z)=B_a(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic and

    |Q(z)| <= K_(a,chi)/(2Re(z)).                            (27.1)

Initially Re(a+z)>1, Fubini is absolute, and the line t+u=v has length v:

    Q(z)=integral_0^infinity v M(exp v)exp(-(a+z)v)dv
        =-d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))] at s=a+z.                  (27.2)

The last identity follows directly from Abel summation, including the n=1
atom, since integral_0^infinity M(exp v)exp(-s v)dv=1/(sL(s,chi)) for Re(s)>1.
Both sides of(27.2) are meromorphic on Re(s)>a, while the left side is
holomorphic. The identity theorem forces the derivative of1/(sL) to have no
pole there. Every L-zero of order m>=1 would give1/(sL) a pole of order m and
its derivative a pole of order m+1, since s!=0. Hence no such zero exists.
The principal pole at1 is a zero of1/(sL), not an obstruction. No primitive
replacement, conductor growth, or height supremum has been introduced.

For a common gamma, it is enough to prove(H) for every fixed chi and every
a>gamma (one may restrict to a countable decreasing sequence tending to gamma).
The constants may depend on a and chi. Each individual zero with Re(rho)>gamma
then lies to the right of one such a. This is an all-finite-height conclusion.
There is no need to control one inverse norm uniformly as a approaches gamma.

This resembles the earlier W29 Sobolev-Hankel pole gate but changes the object:
W29 uses the atomic folded coefficient form and a Sobolev metric; here one
ordinary logarithmic primitive is built into the KERNEL and the input norm is
plain L2. The two contracts must not be identified without a proved operator
comparison. Neither supplies a bound for the other from terminology alone.

### 3.2 Pole, Hilbert-Schmidt and oscillation tests

For a literal one-mode kernel h(v)=R exp(lambda v), Gamma_L has rank1 and its
only nonzero singular value is

    |R| integral_0^L exp(2Re(lambda)t)dt
      =|R|(exp(2Re(lambda)L)-1)/(2Re(lambda)),

with value |R|L when Re(lambda)=0. Thus a low-rank approximation cannot throw
away the leading few singular modes without proving that a zero pole is not
among them. Finite computations at bounded L cannot settle the growing norm.
This calculation is a model calibration; it is not an unproved decomposition
of the full arithmetic source into independently bounded zero modes.

The exact Hilbert-Schmidt identity on a finite square is

    ||Gamma_(a,L)||_HS^2
      =integral_0^(2L) w_L(v) exp(-2av)|M(exp v)|^2 dv,
    w_L(v)=v for0<=v<=L, and2L-v forL<=v<=2L.             (27.3)

This follows by measuring each anti-diagonal. A finite full weighted moment
integral_0^infinity v exp(-2av)|M(exp v)|^2dv proves(H), but it essentially
reimports the old full signed energy and gives no new arithmetic saving.
The factor v is logarithmic in x and costs no fixed exponent.

Operator norm is nonetheless a strictly weaker functional target. For the
NONARITHMETIC example h(v)=exp(i v^2),

    Gamma f(t)=exp(i t^2) integral_0^infinity exp(2itu)exp(iu^2)f(u)du.

Extend exp(iu^2)f(u) by zero to the full real line. Plancherel for the Fourier
transform integral exp(i xi u) gives full-output squared norm pi||f||_2^2
after xi=2t; restricting t>=0 can only decrease it. Therefore every finite
compression has norm<=sqrt(pi), whereas its Hilbert-Schmidt norm equals L,
because the kernel has modulus1 on a square of area L^2. This is an exact
example of coherent oscillatory suppression missed by the positive HS price.
It is not a Mobius model and does not show that actual h has such oscillation.

### 3.3 Exact arithmetic target and coarse headroom

For compactly supported inputs, expanding the complete M gives

    B_a(f,g)=sum_(n>=1) mu(n)chi(n)
        integral_(t,u>=0,t+u>=log n) exp(-a(t+u))f(t)g(u)dtdu. (27.4)

Only finitely many n occur when both inputs are compactly supported. Every
coefficient, the threshold inequality and all q-unit zeros are literal. The
unproved estimate(H) is a uniform signed bound for this complete form. Taking
absolute values coefficient by coefficient would lose the proposed mechanism.

There is a complete finite-growth version that permits a much coarser bound
than(H) at the initial weight. Fix0<a<=gamma<1. It is sufficient that for every
epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large L,

    ||Gamma_(a,L)|| <<_(chi,epsilon)
          exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L).                       (H-growth)

Here is the full return, including every off-diagonal time rectangle. Write
I_j=[j,j+1), j>=0. The block of the a-weighted Hankel operator from I_j to I_i
is unitarily equivalent to its restriction with BOTH variables in
[(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1): translation balances the two coordinates while preserving
their sum. Thus its norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1), where
K_a(L)=||Gamma_(a,L)||. For sigma>a the sigma-weighted block is obtained by
multiplying the two slots by exp(-(sigma-a)t); its norm is consequently at most

    exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)) K_a((i+j)/2+1).                   (27.5)

If K_a(L)<=C exp(2eta L), eta>=0, summing EVERY block gives the finite bound

    ||Gamma_sigma|| <= C exp(2eta)
          [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2), sigma>a+eta.       (27.6)

The double geometric series converges in operator norm, agrees with the kernel
on compact inputs, and covers the whole quadrant. It does not discard mixed
blocks or assume that unequal side lengths behave like the longer side.
Choose eta=gamma-a+epsilon<sigma-a for any sigma>gamma. Then(H-growth) and the
already proved(H) bridge exclude all L-zeros to the right of gamma. Small L
are absorbed into C since finite kernels are bounded. At gamma=a the same
argument allows every subexponential K_a(L), not just a uniformly bounded one.

For the high-potential starting weight a=1/2, an ideal bounded operator would
have half-plane reach. A much weaker growth bound already suffices:

| Conditional target | Allowed L exponent in K_(1/2)(L), with every epsilon |
|---|---|
|First improvement over c11|strictly below .7497080728|
|gamma=.87485, c=.12515|.7497|
|gamma=5/6, c=1/6|2/3|
|gamma=3/4, c=1/4|1/2|

The elementary actual-source bound |M(exp v)|<=exp v gives only

    K_a(L)<=(exp(2(1-a)L)-1)/(2(1-a)), 0<a<1,             (27.7)

by dominating the kernel with the rank1 positive kernel
exp((1-a)t)exp((1-a)u). Thus at a=1/2 the proved elementary exponent is1,
while first gain needs below .7497080728. No part of that signed norm saving
is established here. More generally a PROVED pointwise envelope
|M(x)|<=C x^b would give the same rank1 upper bound with1-a replaced by b-a,
interpreted continuously at b=a. We do not infer such an envelope solely from
unquantified holomorphy or assign it to an unverified source contract.

These are coarse sufficient bounds: the constants can be arbitrarily large
and depend on chi and epsilon. No contraction or small norm is required.
The aspiration, quantitative loss allowance and missing arithmetic input are
therefore separate. Neither(H) at a new a nor(H-growth) at a new exponent has
been proved for the actual source.

The next mathematical action is to estimate the complete signed form(27.4)
using a specific oscillatory decomposition that preserves its cumulative
threshold, and to compare its cost to the inherited Sobolev gate. The HS route
does not reduce the arithmetic gap. Low-rank tail control alone misses a pole.

statement:
## 4. Development16: the exact cubical source retains harmonic parity

This was the purposeful high-ceiling construction. It was not discarded merely because its vocabulary differs from established analytic methods.

For one distinct prime p!=3 take the real two-term chain complex

    C_1=span(e_+,e_-), C_0=span(e_0),
    d(e_+)=d(e_-)=e_0.                                 (16)

Its Euler characteristic is1-2=-1. With the displayed orthonormal bases, Delta=dd*+d*d has eigenvalue2 on C_0, eigenvalues2 and0 on C_1, and harmonic vector h=(e_+-e_-)/sqrt2 in odd degree. Thus

    Str(exp(-t Delta))=e^-2t-(e^-2t+1)=-1              (17)

for all t>=0. A one-arrow complex with one even and one odd cell would instead have Euler characteristic0 and would destroy the source. The second odd cell is exactly what restores the actual sign and its survivor.

For n, take the graded tensor product of(16) over the DISTINCT primes p|n,p!=3. Repeated prime powers add no coordinate; prime2 is included and prime3 adds only a trivial even factor. For n=1 or a power of3 use the one-dimensional even complex. The signed tensor differential uses the usual preceding-degree sign, which can be checked directly to make d^2=0. Denote it C(n), and put k(n)=#{p|n:p!=3} only in this section (not the convolution coefficient k above).

The total dimension is3^k(n), the Laplacian is the sum of the commuting local Laplacians, and the only harmonic vector is the tensor of all h. It has degree k(n). Thus

    dim ker Delta_n=1,
    Str(exp(-t Delta_n))=(-1)^k(n)=f3(n),
    Str(P_n)=f3(n),                                    (18)

where P_n is the harmonic projection. The nonzero spectrum has gap2. There is a bounded homotopy h_n=d*Delta_n^-1 on the nonharmonic space, with norm<=1/sqrt2 and

    d h_n+h_n d=I-P_n.                                 (19)

There is NO homotopy with right side I: apply it to the nonzero harmonic vector. This obstruction is exact already at one prime. The favorable uniform gap and bounded complement homotopy are real facts, but concern the complement of the entire arithmetic sign.

On the direct sum of C(n), let W_x,chi act as scalar chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)) on C(n), and let Gamma give the degree sign. The Gaussian dominates every fixed polynomial in n, while3^k(n)<=n^2, so all the following weighted operators are trace class and limits/sums are justified by the same absolute majorant. We obtain the COMPLETE actual-source identity

    F(x)=Tr(Gamma W_x,chi exp(-t Delta))
        =Tr(Gamma W_x,chi P),                 every t>=0. (20)

All characters, zeros, repeated primes and tails remain. Sending t to infinity eliminates every nonharmonic state while leaving exactly F(x), unchanged. This is an exact new realization in this lane, not an arithmetic estimate and not a claimed new theorem of the literature.

The price of bounding the remaining harmonic trace absolutely is particularly clear:

    Tr(|W_x,chi| P)=sum_(n>=1,(n,q)=1)g_tau(log(n/x))
       =(phi(q)/q) exp(tau/2) x+O_(q,tau)(1).            (21)

To prove(21), write h(u)=g_tau(log u), set h(0)=0, and split the Riemann sum into the fixed residue classes modulo q. Its sum/integral error is bounded by a constant times the total variation of h; h has finite variation. The integral is integral_R g_tau(v)e^v dv=exp(tau/2). Thus the positive harmonic norm has exponent1. This is NOT a lower bound for |F| or its signed square moment. It states exactly why an absolute harmonic estimate cannot improve the accepted bound.

Could a differential joining different integers repair this? Only with a paid loss of commutation with W_x. The smallest exact model pairs one even and one odd state, with differential sqrt(lambda), lambda>0. Then Delta=lambda I and P=0, while

    Str(W)=w_+-w_-=
            integral_0^infinity lambda e^-lambda t (w_+-w_-)dt. (22)

Increasing the gap lambda does not reduce the weighted readout: the time integral cancels it exactly. If w_+=w_-, the pair cancels; otherwise the full difference is the boundary bill. The same identity follows in any finite complex from I=P+integral Delta exp(-tDelta)dt. A new cross-integer matching must estimate the complete signed weighted differences and any remaining harmonic term, not just make a large Laplacian gap. That returns to actual-source transport/filling with its full charge and Gaussian metric, already available in W44 and the W43 Hodge audit.

The next meaningful construction is a specific cross-integer differential or matching whose weighted commutator/residual can be bounded below exponent.874861 on every large shell. Prime-divisibility topology alone does not supply it. Natural character zeros may remove vertices; a proposed matching has to keep those holes, and complex character phases need an actual compatible intertwiner. The one-dimensional-per-n construction and the two-state defect are scoped obstructions to this exact homotopy strategy, not an impossibility theorem for arithmetic topology or for first gains.

## 4. Full square-prefix estimate, including every alias

This is the new quantitative source lemma. Put b0=3/2, k=6 and

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6), x in [X,2X],
    ||F||_j=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j).

For fixed periodic mean-zero beta of period Q0 and bounded amplitude, uniformly in every real A with 1<=A<=p X^alpha0 for any fixed 0<=alpha0<1, every shell-fixed endpoint R in[0,infinity], and X sufficiently large,

    ||sum_(1<=r<=R) beta(r) f_x(A r^2)||_2
       <<_(p,Q0,alpha0,||beta||inf) 1+X^(3/8) A^(-1/4).                 (4.1)

R may depend arbitrarily on X,A and a frozen cutoff; it must not depend on x. The infinite endpoint is allowed through the actual damping. The same bound holds in L1 by Cauchy-Schwarz. This lemma estimates the complete square row, not a selected low-frequency projection.

Proof. Let F=(X/A)^6 and choose a fixed small c0>0 depending only on Q0. Set R0=c0 F^(1/11). Since A<=p X^alpha0 and alpha0<1, R0 tends to infinity uniformly. Expand beta in its nonzero Fourier modes j/Q0, 1<=j<Q0. On r<=R0, their phase in the convention exp(2pi i Phi) is

    Phi_j(t)=jt/Q0-(A t^2/x)^6/(2pi),
    Phi_j'(t)=j/Q0-(6/pi)(A/x)^6 t^11.

Choose c0 sufficiently small that the second term is at most1/(4Q0) even up to R0+1, for every x>=X and all sufficiently large X. The derivative is monotone and stays separated from integers by a fixed multiple of1/Q0. Discrete summation by parts with (exp(2pi i(Phi(r+1)-Phi(r)))-1)^(-1), whose total variation is bounded on this arc, gives O_(Q0)(1) for every undamped prefix. Abel summation with the actual decreasing exp(-A r^2/x^(3/2)) pays the damped low prefix with the same bound. The endpoint min(R,R0) and integer floors are harmless; the finite initial X range enters the constant.

The remaining coefficients t_r=beta(r)1_(R0<r<=R) are bounded. Majorize the sharp x-shell by a fixed nonnegative smooth rho(x/X), supported in[1/2,3], which is at least1 on[1,2]. Expand the ENTIRE square. Its diagonal is

    << sum_r exp(-c A r^2/X^(3/2)) << X^(3/4) A^(-1/2).

For r!=s, two integrations by parts in u^(-6), u=x/X, give

    |K_A(r,s)| << exp(-c A(r^2+s^2)/X^(3/2))
       min(1,[F/|r^12-s^12|]^2).                     (4.2)

To see the uniform constant, each differentiated amplitude is bounded by a fixed polynomial in A(r^2+s^2)/X^(3/2) times its exponential; absorb that polynomial into a weaker exponential. Smooth rho removes boundary terms. Both off-diagonal orientations are included. For r>s>R0,

    r^12-s^12 >= r^11(r-s),
    sum_(h>=1) min(1,[F/(r^11 h)]^2) << F/r^11.

The last inequality holds also when F/r^11<1, since its square is then smaller. Thus the full absolute off-diagonal is

    << F sum_(r>R0) r^(-11) << F R0^(-10)
     << F^(1/11)=(X/A)^(6/11).

For A>=1 and X>=1, (X/A)^(6/11)<=X^(3/4)A^(-1/2), because the ratio is X^(-9/44)A^(-1/22). Taking square roots and adjoining the low prefix proves (4.1). Arbitrary R was never used to shorten the price: its high coefficients were bounded and the full infinite positive sum was paid. The low/high cross term is paid by the norm triangle inequality; no signed-subset monotonicity is assumed.

This proof is also valid for every fixed periodic mean-zero beta, not only (3.3), with its own fixed constants. No modulus or period is allowed to grow with X under this statement.

## 7. Fixed general phase compatibility (controller suggestion, checked here)

Root proposed this extension during this pass; it is additional to the fixed k=6 theorem. With the SAME v_G and frozen masks, replace f_x(n) by exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), for fixed b>1 and fixed integer k>2. The proof above gives

 ||B_G||_2 <<_(b,k,epsilon,B_0) X^epsilon
       [X/G+(X^(b/2)+X^(2k/(3k-2)))/sqrt(G)].            (LGK)

Here are all changed sums. In a comparable upper block H=X^k/N^(k-1). Equation(LG8) becomes, with the changed damping,

 exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)

## 2. D1 / R11: an actual ordinary-character source and exact realization

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural zero values. Put delta=1 for the principal character and 0 otherwise, r=delta*phi(q)/q, and

    A(x)=sum_(n<=x) chi(n),
    b(t)=A(exp(t))-r exp(t),  t>=0.

Periodicity gives |b(t)|<=q. No Mobius cancellation is used. For Re(s)>1, summation by parts gives

    H(s)=integral_0^infinity b(t) exp(-s t) dt
        =L(s,chi)/s-r/(s-1).                           (1)

The integral continues H holomorphically to Re(s)>0 because b is bounded. Define the pole-normalized source

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s.            (2)

For nonprincipal chi this is L/s. For principal chi the apparent singularity at 1 is removable, with F_chi(1)=r/2 !=0. On Re(s)>0, s and s+1 do not vanish; (2) has exactly the natural L zeros in that half-plane, with multiplicity. No artificial zero at 1 is added for nonprincipal characters.

Its literal causal inverse-Laplace source is

    f(t)=b(t)                                  if delta=0,
    f(t)=r exp(-t)+b(t)-2 integral_0^t exp(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                               if delta=1.       (3)

Indeed for delta=1, F=r/(s+1)+(s-1)H/(s+1). Thus F=Laplace(f) on Re(s)>0. In both cases |f(t)|<=C_q:=1+3q. The n=1 contribution is included in A; values at the isolated log(n) jumps do not affect these integrals. All imprimitive Euler factors remain in L. This is an ordinary-character construction; no number-field or changing-conductor transfer is asserted.

For principal chi, cancellation of the r terms in (3) gives the particularly concrete identity, with x=exp(t),

    f(log x)=(2/x)sum_(n<=x) n chi(n)-A(x).            (3a)

It follows from integral_1^x A(v)dv=sum_(n<=x)chi(n)(x-n). At q=1 and m=floor(x), this is m(m+1-x)/x, hence 0<=f<=1 at every x>=1. The zeta source is therefore a positive bounded staircase; one may replace C_q by 1 in its tail bounds. Positivity alone cannot establish the desired complex zero exclusion: the positive bounded source exp(-bt)+C exp(-b(t-T))1_(t>=T), with b>0,C>1, has transform (1+C exp(-sT))/(s+b) and zeros on Re(s)=log(C)/T>0. This toy only defeats a positivity-only inference; it says nothing adverse about the additional arithmetic structure in (3a).

Fix 0<gamma<1 and a=2-gamma, so a>gamma and the safe anchor is s0=gamma+a=2. Set

    s(z)=gamma+a(1+z)/(1-z),
    z(s)=(s-gamma-a)/(s-gamma+a),
    F(z)=F_chi(s(z)), F0=F(0)=F_chi(2) !=0.           (4)

The Euler product in Re(s)>1 proves F0!=0. The bound |F_chi(s)|<=C_q/Re(s) puts F in H-infinity of the disk, hence H2. Define, on L2(0,infinity),

    f_gamma(t)=exp(-gamma t)f(t),
    h(t)=sqrt(2a) integral_0^t exp(-a(t-u))f_gamma(u)du,
    Qv(t)=v(t)-2a integral_0^t exp(-a(t-u))v(u)du,
    ell0(t)=sqrt(2a)exp(-a t).                         (5)

Q is an isometry: after zero extension its Fourier multiplier is
(it-a)/(it+a), of modulus one. Q*ell0=0 by direct integration and ||ell0||=1. For any polynomial p, Laplace transformation of p(Q)h gives

    sqrt(2a)/(w+a) * p((w-a)/(w+a)) * F_chi(gamma+w).

The circle change of variable t=a cot(theta/2), followed by Fourier Plancherel, proves the exact identities

    ||p(Q)h||_L2^2 = ||p F||_H2^2,
    ||p(Q)h-F0 ell0||_L2^2 = ||p F-F0||_H2^2.         (6)

The factor is exact: dtheta/(2pi)=a dt/[pi(a^2+t^2)] in absolute orientation, and the Fourier Plancherel convention is ||v||_2^2=(1/(2pi))integral|vhat(t)|^2dt. Also <h,ell0>=F0 under the inner product linear in the first entry. These give a literal source, state update and positive output; no guessed finite-dimensional realization is substituted.

**First decisive control test.** A bounded positive metric mI<=P<=MI cannot make Q*PQ<=kappa P for any kappa<1: iteration would give m||v||^2<=kappa^n M||v||^2 while ||Q^n v||=||v||. Thus an equivalent-norm contraction of the complete state is impossible. This is not an obstruction to source-specific signed combinations p(Q)h. Their relevant information is the actual correlations <Q^j h,Q^k h>, not the unrestricted norm of Q. It refines the old source-versus-multiplier distinction with a fully formed ordinary-character source; it supplies no contraction estimate.

## [restricted research revision]-W2. Exact Newton correction has a support/feedback dichotomy

Write m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y), d_Y=delta-1*m_Y, with Dirichlet convolution,
and q_(Y,k)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))). Then exactly

    delta-1*q_(Y,k)=d_Y^(*k),
    d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y,
    d_Y^(*k)(n)=0 for n<(Y+1)^k.

Thus q equals mu on that longer prefix. Truncating q to the prefix merely
produces a longer ordinary Mobius truncation. In Dirichlet-series notation,
with Q=Q_tr+T and D=1-zeta M,

    1-zeta Q_tr=D^k+zeta T.

The tail feedback cannot be dropped. At a zeta zero, D=1 and Q=kM: the
finite correction is regular there, so small support error alone has lost
the original reciprocal pole signal.

For a Y-rough integer, d_Y=-1. On a product with exactlyk prime factors
counted with multiplicity, d_Y^(*k)=(-1)^k k!/product e_p!. For fixedk
and Y=X^theta, theta<=1/k gives a rough-sector absolute Gaussian mass
at least a constant times X/(log X)^k, using distinct primes. This is not
a lower bound on the entire signed defect. For theta>1/k, the full defect
Gaussian is O_A(X^-A) for everyA by future support and the divisor bound;
its missing zero feedback is still unpaid. Growingk requires uniform
constants, all tails and a surviving zero signal. Fixed ordinary character
twists preserve their natural zeros; no Eisenstein extension is inferred.

# [private research revision] independent review: literal f3 Gaussian rough-depth renewal

**Disposition: ACCEPT the frozen candidate's main term, sign, and exact-source scope.** The reciprocal smooth-core mass is exactly zero; the first surviving derivative is positive. Every prime power and the complete Gaussian can be retained and paid. This report independently proves the candidate for every fixed B>0, gives a stronger two-term expansion, and proves a uniform moving-threshold extension. It also derives the literal signed bands and their complete fixed-finite Gram, including the exact whole-complement mismatch interface.

This is an arithmetic estimate for a large partial field. It does not improve the full-field exponent or the accepted written c_G=.1251134. The new endpoint's independent kernel replay remains pending. The full-field convolution from G28 is used only where explicitly indicated; no masked-subfamily equivalence is imported through it.



## 1. Exact statement and a stronger proved range

Fix tau>0. Write

    g_tau(u)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)),
    f(n)=f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))),
    omega_z(n)=#{p>z:p divides n},
    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1) f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).       (F1)

The count is of DISTINCT primes. All their powers remain. Put

    L=log X, ell=log x, t=log z,
    P(z)=product_(5<=p<=z) (p-2)/(p-1),
    h_z=3 log(2)P(z)>0,
    D_z=-3 log(2)-log(3)
           +2 sum_(5<=p<=z) p log(p)/((p-1)(p-2)).       (F2)

The following assertions hold uniformly for the CLOSED shell X<=x<=2X and

    4 <= t <= L/(1000 log L).                           (F3)

All constants are independent of z,x,X. They can depend on the fixed tau and on fixed classical PNT constants. For all sufficiently large X,

    T_z(x)=h_z exp(tau/2) x/ell^2
            *[1-(2 tau+D_z)/ell+O_tau(t^2/L^2)].        (F4)

In particular,

    T_z(x)=3 log(2) exp(tau/2) P(z) x/(log x)^2
                      *[1+O_tau(t/L)].                (F5)

Here D_z=2t+O(1). For z=(log X)^B, with fixed B>0, one has t=B log L, eventually inside F3. Thus the candidate's POSITIVE main term is correct, with relative error O_(tau,B)(loglog X/log X). Its proposed coarser remainder also suffices at this fixed-B scope. The second term and F3 are separately proved reviewer extensions, not claims in the frozen candidate.

The upper range is z=exp(L/(1000 log L)), still subpower in X. At that endpoint the leading field has size comparable to X loglog X/(log X)^3. It still has exponent one. Nothing in this proof reaches a fixed power z=X^rho, rho>0.

## 2. Exact decomposition and local Euler factors

Let S(z) be the set of positive integers whose prime factors are <=z; it includes1 and retains all valuations. Since z>=exp(4)>3, every n admitted in F1 either lies in S(z), or has a UNIQUE representation

    n=r p^k,  r in S(z), p>z prime, k>=1.

For every k>=1, f(p^k)=-1, while f(3^k)=+1. Thus, exactly,

    T_z(x)=sum_(r in S(z)) f(r)g_tau(log(r/x))
         -sum_(r in S(z)) f(r)
              sum_(p>z,k>=1)g_tau(log(r p^k/x)).        (F6)

All sums converge absolutely before using signs: the Gaussian in log n dominates any fixed power and |f(n)|=1. There is neither a squarefree-core convention nor a discarded prime-power term in F6.

For Re s>0 the finite-prime geometric series give

    H_z(s)=sum_(r in S(z)) f(r)/r^s
      =(1-3^(-s))^(-1)
          product_(p<=z,p!=3) (1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s)).   (F7)

This infinite smooth-number series and its fixed derivatives converge absolutely on every compact subset of Re s>0. At p=2 its numerator vanishes at1. If

    A_2(s)=(1-2^(1-s))/(1-2^(-s)),
    J_z(s)=(1-3^(-s))^(-1)
             product_(5<=p<=z)(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s)),

then H_z=A_2 J_z,

    A_2(1)=0,  A_2'(1)=2log2,  A_2''(1)=-6(log2)^2,
    J_z(1)=(3/2)P(z).

Consequently,

    H_z(1)=0,  H_z'(1)=h_z,
    sum_(r in S(z)) f(r)log r/r=-h_z,                 (F8)
    H_z''(1)/H_z'(1)=D_z.

The last equality follows by differentiating the nonvanishing J factors:

    J_z'(1)/J_z(1)=-log3/2
                    +sum_(5<=p<=z) p log p/((p-1)(p-2)).

These exact identities independently verify both the factor3 and the main-term sign. The leading k=1 prime density has an outer minus sign in F6; its surviving signed log-r moment is negative. The two signs produce the positive coefficient in F5. The Gaussian's first tilted moment multiplies H_z(1) at the leading density order and therefore cancels.

## 3. Prime input, product size, and all-order Euler bounds

The only prime-distribution input is the fixed-order PNT already accepted in [private research revision] review §2:

    R(v)=pi(v)-li(v)=O_N(v/(log v)^N), v>=2,           (F9)

for each FIXED N. That review pins Johnston-Yang v2, Corollary1.3, to the stronger explicit bound 9.59v(log v)^.515 exp(-.8274 sqrt(log v)). This report uses F9 as that established primary input. No new provider call, short-interval relative PNT, or order N growing with X is used. N=10 suffices for the source approximation and is selected in advance; a separately chosen stronger fixed order gives any requested fixed rate in the prime-product asymptotic below.

Standard partial summation from F9 gives

    sum_(p<=z) log p/p <<t,
    p_z=product_(p<=z)(1-1/p)
          =(e^(-gamma_E)/t)[1+O_N(t^(-N))].           (F10)

For the stated rate, use a stronger fixed PNT order in the convergent error tail for sum1/p, exactly as in [private research revision] §2. Since

    (p-2)/(p-1)=(1-1/p)(1-1/(p-1)^2),

one has

    P(z)=3p_z product_(5<=p<=z)(1-1/(p-1)^2)
        =(kappa/t)[1+O_N(t^(-N))],
    kappa=3e^(-gamma_E)
                 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)>0.        (F11)

The remaining convergent-product tail is O(1/z). In particular P(z) is comparable to1/t throughout t>=4. Also partial summation gives sum_(p<=z)log p/p=t+O(1), and the difference between p/((p-1)(p-2)) and1/p is O(1/p^2), proving D_z=2t+O(1).

For POSITIVE smooth cores with full valuations use

    Z_z(s)=product_(p<=z)(1-p^(-s))^(-1),

not the squarefree product from RN. On |s-1|<=1/t and t>=4, Re s>=3/4 and p^(1/t)<=e for p<=z. All relevant denominator factors are bounded away from zero. The factors1-2p^(-s) are also bounded away from zero for p>=5, since2*5^(-3/4)<1. Integrating their logarithmic derivatives from1 to s gives

    |Z_z(s)|<=C Z_z(1)<=Ct,
    |J_z(s)|<=C J_z(1)<=C P(z).                        (F12)

Indeed each derivative sum is at most C sum_(p<=z)log p/p<=Ct, and the integration length is at most1/t. The logs have analytic branches on this disk; the p=2 zero is excluded from J_z rather than hidden in a logarithm.

Write H_z(s)=(s-1)V_z(s). The quotient A_2(s)/(s-1) is analytic and uniformly bounded on |s-1|<=1/4, so

    V_z(1)=h_z,  sup_(|s-1|<=1/t)|V_z(s)|<=C h_z.

Cauchy's estimate yields, SIMULTANEOUSLY for every integer j>=1,

    |H_z^(j)(1)|<=C h_z j! t^(j-1).                  (F13)

There is no unspecified growing O_j constant. The simple p=2 zero saves one power of t, which is crucial at the derivative-main-term scale.

The positive tilt Z_z(1-1/t)<=Ct and u^j<=j!e^u give, for all j>=0,

    sum_(r in S(z)) (log r)^j/r <=Ct j!t^j.           (F14)

If R_0=e^Q>=1, splitting the exponential between the power and the tail gives

    sum_(r>R_0,r in S(z)) (log r)^j/r
          <=Ct e^(-Q/(2t)) j!(2t)^j,                 (F15)
    sum_(r>R_0,r in S(z)) 1/r <=Ct e^(-Q/t).          (F16)

For F15, pointwise use 1_(log r>Q)(log r)^j <= e^(-Q/(2t)) j!(2t)^j exp(log r/t). Thus these estimates pay the completion of all signed moments even when the Taylor degree grows. This adapts the finite-Euler method to full valuations; it is not an application of RN's squarefree-core formula.

## 4. Complete Gaussian, smooth, and prime-power tails

A useful elementary bound is, uniformly for every y>0,

    sum_(m>=1) g_tau(log(m/y)) <=C_tau y.             (F17)

For y>=1 use the integrable function h(u)=g_tau(log u), u>0, extended flatly by0 at0, and its finite total variation: the Riemann-sum error is bounded by the variation, giving C(y+1)<=C'y. For0<y<1, g_tau(log(m/y))<=C_tau(y/m)^2, so the sum is O(y^2)<=O(y). The same proof applies to g_(2tau). Hence

    sum_(m>=1, |log(m/y)|>=W) g_tau(log(m/y))
              <=C_tau y exp(-W^2/(4tau)),             (F18)

because g_tau(u)1_(|u|>=W)<=sqrt(2)exp(-W^2/(4tau))g_(2tau)(u).

Use the FIXED cuts

    delta=1/100,  Q=delta L, R_0=X^delta, W=delta L.   (F19)

First, the entire fully smooth field in F6 is at most

    C_tau x^(1-1/t) Z_z(1-1/t)
              <=C_tau Xt exp(-L/t).                  (F20)

This follows from the bounded function exp((1-1/t)u)g_tau(u); its bound is uniform for3/4<=1-1/t<=1.

Second, every integer of the form p^k has a unique prime base and exponent. The positive sum over p>z,k>=1 is therefore bounded by the integer sum F17. ALL rough terms with r>R_0, including every k, have total absolute field at most

    C_tau X sum_(r>R_0,r in S(z))1/r
              <=C_tau Xt exp(-Q/t).                  (F21)

This is the needed full source tail, without an unproved signed majorant or a loss from repeating prime powers.

For r<=R_0 and k>=2 choose the FIXED sigma=3/4. The positive series

    sum_(p,k>=2)p^(-3k/4)<infinity

converges. The Gaussian exponential bound therefore gives

    sum_(p>z,k>=2)g_tau(log(p^k/y))<=C_tau y^(3/4).

Summing over the retained cores,

    sum_(r<=R_0,r in S(z)) sum_(p>z,k>=2)
                      g_tau(log(rp^k/x))
        <=C_tau X^(3/4)R_0^(1/4) Z_z(1)
        <=C_tau t X^(.7525).                          (F22)

Thus all higher powers are negligible at the asserted main-term scale, but they were not declared absent. No core product at Re s=3/4 is used; the factor R_0^(1/4) returns the core weight to1/r.

Finally retain only -W<log(rp/x)<=W in the k=1 term. F18 pays its entire omitted Gaussian tails by

    C_tau Xt exp(-W^2/(4tau)).                         (F23)

The boundary -W itself can be included in the discarded tail, so subsequent Stieltjes endpoint conventions are literal. The outer field still contains every original Gaussian term through these quantified error estimates.

## 5. Uniform sharp-endpoint PNT and the source integral

For retained r and x set y=x/r. The central prime interval is

    y e^(-W)<p<=y e^W.

Its endpoints lie in [X^.98,2X^1.01]. For all sufficiently large X this entire interval is above z throughout F3. Thus the condition p>z is automatic here AFTER the tails were paid. It is not removed in the original source by assertion.

Apply Stieltjes summation to w(v)=g_tau(log(v/y)) on the half-open interval (a,b], with a=ye^(-W),b=ye^W. The exact error is

    R(b)g_tau(W)-R(a)g_tau(-W)
       -integral_a^b R(v)g_tau'(log(v/y))dv/v.

For fixed N, F9 and the positive-power corridor bound this by

    C_(tau,N)y L^(-N)
       [e^Wg_tau(W)+e^(-W)g_tau(-W)
                           +integral_R e^u|g_tau'(u)|du]
                <=C_(tau,N)y L^(-N).                 (F24)

The bracket is uniformly bounded; tau is fixed. Both sharp endpoints remain in the formula, including when an endpoint is prime. Summing1/r over the retained cores with full valuations costs O(t). With N=10 fixed once and for all, F6 has become

    T_z(x)=-x integral_(-W)^W e^u g_tau(u)
           sum_(r<=R_0,r in S(z))
                   [f(r)/r]/(ell+u-log r) du + E_0,   (F25)

where

    |E_0| <=C_tau [Xt e^(-L/t)+Xt e^(-Q/t)
           +t X^(.7525)+Xt e^(-W^2/(4tau))+Xt L^(-10)]. (F26)

This proof uses ordinary PNT over a fixed power corridor, with a complete fixed Gaussian derivative integral. It has no short-interval prime-density premise and no growing-order PNT dependency.

## 6. Growing signed Taylor completion and main-term evaluation

Set

    K=floor(L/(16t)).

In F3, K grows at least like a positive multiple of log L, and eventually K>=4. For -W<=u<=W let a=ell+u, and for r<=R_0 let v=log r. Then

    a>=.99L,  a-v>=.98L,
    1/(a-v)=sum_(j=0)^(K-1) v^j/a^(j+1)
                         +v^K/[a^K(a-v)].             (F27)

Taking absolute values only on the last term and using F14 gives an integrated field error at most

    C_tau (xt/L) K!(t/(.99L))^K
               <=C_tau(xt/L)15^(-K),                 (F28)

since Kt/(.99L)<=1/15.84. The derivative order has an explicit price.

Complete EACH signed polynomial moment to all smooth cores before estimating it. F15 bounds the sum of completion errors by

    C_tau(xt/L)e^(-Q/(2t))
                    sum_(j<K)j!(2t/(.99L))^j
          <=C_tau(xt/L)e^(-Q/(2t)),                   (F29)

because consecutive terms have ratio at most2Kt/(.99L)<1/7. The completed moments are EXACTLY

    sum_(r in S(z)) f(r)(log r)^j/r=(-1)^j H_z^(j)(1).

The j=0 term vanishes. The j=1 term is -h_z, so the outer minus sign in F25 yields

    +x h_z integral_(-W)^W e^u g_tau(u)/(ell+u)^2 du.  (F30)

For F5, the j>=2 terms, by F13 and the same consecutive-ratio bound, have total absolute size at most C_tau x h_z t/L^3. The two required Gaussian integrals are

    integral_R e^u g_tau(u)du=exp(tau/2),
    integral_R u e^u g_tau(u)du=tau exp(tau/2).         (F31)

The finite tilted absolute moments and F18 give

    integral_(-W)^W e^u g_tau(u)/(ell+u)^2 du
       =exp(tau/2)ell^(-2)[1-2tau/ell+O_tau(L^(-2))]. (F32)

For precision, Taylor expansion in u is performed only on |u|<=W, where the denominator is bounded below by .99L; its remainder is at most C u^2/L^4. Extending its finitely many Gaussian moments to all real u has exponentially small error. This does not extend the rational denominator across its pole at u=-ell.

Keeping j=2 supplies

    -x H_z''(1) integral_(-W)^W e^u g_tau(u)/(ell+u)^3 du
      =-x H_z''(1)exp(tau/2)ell^(-3)
                                     +O_tau(x h_z t/L^4). (F33)

Here the absolute first tilted moment prices the replacement, and F13 gives |H_z''(1)|<=C h_z t. The j>=3 terms are bounded by C_tau x h_z t^2/L^4. Together F30--F33 give F4, provided the preceding absolute tails fit its relative O(t^2/L^2) error. They do, uniformly:

| Paid field error | Ratio to the positive main size x h_z/ell^2, up to fixed constants |
|---|---|
| Fully smooth F20 | L^2 t^2 exp(-L/t) |
| All large cores F21 | L^2 t^2 exp(-.01L/t) |
| Higher prime powers F22 | L^2 t^2 X^(-.2475) |
| Gaussian tail F23 | L^2 t^2 exp(-.0001L^2/(4tau)) |
| Fixed PNT F24 | t^2 L^(-8) |
| Taylor tail F28 | L t^2 15^(-K) |
| Moment completion F29 | L t^2 exp(-.005L/t) |

For example, after division by t^2/L^2 the largest relevant completion expression is

    L^3 exp(-.005L/t)<=L^3 exp(-5log L)=L^(-2).

The large-core expression becomes L^4 exp(-.01L/t)<=L^(-6). For the Taylor tail, K>=L/(16t)-1 and log(15)/16>.16, so L^3 15^(-K)<=15L^3 exp(-.16L/t), much smaller still. The other rows are immediate, with tau fixed. Thus every row is O_tau(t^2/L^2). There is no unpriced positive-to-signed mass loss: it appears explicitly as t^2 in this table because Z_z(1) is of order t while h_z is of order1/t.

This completes the independent proof of F4 and F5, including their x,z uniformity, the all-order constants, all valuations, and every tail. The numerical constants .01 and1/1000 were chosen for a transparent proof, not optimized.

## 7. Literal threshold bands and their signs

Let A_z(n)=1_(omega_z(n)<=1). If z_2>z_1 then A_z2>=A_z1, so

    T_z2-T_z1=sum_n f(n)[A_z2(n)-A_z1(n)]g_tau(log(n/x)) (F34)

is EXACTLY the field of the newly admitted coefficient set. No coefficient mask changes during x integration. At a prime threshold p,

    A_p(n)-A_(p^-)(n)=1_(p divides n, omega_p(n)=1),    (F35)

which retains every positive power of p. There is only one integer n here, so the two-original-factor shared-prime subtraction of RN is not this jump law. F35 gives no sign for an individual prime jump.

For fixed lambda>1 with t,lambda t in F3, and t tending to infinity, F5 and F11 give, for every fixed N,

    T_(z^lambda)(x)-T_z(x)
      =h_z exp(tau/2) x/ell^2
          *[lambda^(-1)-1+O_(tau,lambda,N)(t/L+t^(-N))]. (F36)

For lambda=2, explicitly require 4<=t<=L/(2000 log L), so BOTH t and2t lie in F3, and t tends to infinity. Then

    T_(z^2)=(1/2+o(1))T_z,
    T_(z^2)-T_z=(-1/2+o(1))T_z,                       (F37)

uniformly on the full shell. T_z is eventually positive, and the complete added band is eventually negative there. This is an actual signed arithmetic estimate for the full coefficient band, despite its selector being nonnegative. It is not a pointwise-in-prime-jump assertion. If lambda tends to1, the subtractive error still applies at any proved uniform parameter range but need not give a relative asymptotic for that small band; no such uniform moving-lambda assertion is claimed here.

There is no exact finite terminal threshold for the UNCAPPED Gaussian source: n is unbounded. For any increasing z_j tending to infinity, dominated convergence and the disjoint coefficient partition give the exact locally uniformly convergent identity

    F_6-T_z0=sum_(j>=1)(T_zj-T_z(j-1)).                (F38)

Indeed the sum of the absolute band fields is at most sum_n g_tau(log(n/x))<=C_tau x. F38 is an exact decomposition, not an asymptotic extrapolation of F36 outside F3. The remaining late flow cannot be evaluated by extending the factor lambda^(-1) to fixed-power thresholds or infinity.

## 8. Complete fixed-finite leading Gram

Use the physical inner product integral_X^(2X) overline(U(x))V(x)dx/x. Fix finitely many constants

    1=lambda_0<lambda_1<...<lambda_m,
    z_j=z^(lambda_j),

with all thresholds in F3 and t=log z tending to infinity. Define

    V_X(x)=h_z exp(tau/2) x/(log x)^2,
    N_X=||V_X||_2,
    epsilon_X=t/L+t^(-N),

where N>=1 is any fixed order. Direct integration gives

    N_X^2=h_z^2 exp(tau)
               integral_X^(2X) x dx/(log x)^4
         =(3/2)h_z^2 exp(tau) X^2/L^4[1+O(1/L)].      (F39)

The t/L term in epsilon_X is the analytic field error; t^(-N) is the separately priced prime-product ratio error. Neither is the power-small accepted-full-field error used in §9. Constants in this section may depend on the fixed collection, tau,N. The uniform field estimates imply

    ||T_zj-lambda_j^(-1)V_X||_2<=C epsilon_X N_X.      (F40)

For the literal DISJOINT components

    B_0=T_z,
    B_j=T_zj-T_z(j-1), 1<=j<=m,
    b_0=1, b_j=lambda_j^(-1)-lambda_(j-1)^(-1),

one therefore has

    ||B_j-b_j V_X||_2<=C epsilon_X N_X,
    <B_i,B_j>=[b_i b_j+O(epsilon_X)]N_X^2.            (F41)

This is the COMPLETE finite Gram, with every off-diagonal entry included. The prefix-band entries are negative in their leading term; the band-band entries are positive. For any fixed complex vector a, uniformly in that vector,

    ||sum_j a_j B_j||_2^2
       =N_X^2 |sum_j a_j b_j|^2
                       +O(epsilon_X N_X^2 (sum_j|a_j|)^2). (F42)

A vector that kills the displayed leading coefficient only obtains the proved field error O(epsilon_X N_X sum|a_j|), using F41. This upper bound still has exponent one; it is not a lower bound for the actual residual. The coarse scalar error F42 must not be read as a new power estimate when its leading term vanishes.

For complete source binding, if c_i(n)=f(n) times any of these disjoint masks, then

    <B_i,B_j>=sum_(n,r>=1) overline(c_i(n))c_j(r) K_X(n,r),
    K_X(n,r)=g_(2tau)(log(n/r))
          *integral_0^(log2)
                  g_(tau/2)(u-log(sqrt(nr)/X))du.     (F43)

This is exactly current-proof G22 for the literal F1 coefficients. Absolute convergence follows from F17, since the double absolute sum equals an integral bounded by C_tau X^2. For distinct partition pieces c_i(n)c_j(n)=0, so their same-integer diagonal is absent by the coefficient partition itself. Each own true diagonal is O_tau(X), by applying the same Gaussian lattice bound to g_tau^2. None of this deletes negative cross terms in the full signed expansion.

## 9. Actual whole complement, its stronger Gram, and exact mismatch

Put

    F=F_6=sum_n f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    R_z=F-T_z=sum_(omega_z(n)>=2) f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    a=||T_z||_2, b=||R_z||_2, d=||F||_2.             (F44)

The accepted full-field baseline supplies d=O(X^beta) for a fixed beta<1. The explicit inherited calibration beta=.8749 follows from G21 and G28; more generally one may use any actually accepted full-field bound at beta=1-c_G+eta<1 with fixed eta>0. This is the sole place where the existing whole-field result enters. The prefix proof F4 did not use it. The use of G28 here is legitimate for FULL fields and implies no masked transfer.

From F5,F39,

    a is comparable to X/(tL^2),
    eta_X=d/a=O(X^(beta-1)tL^2)=o(1),
    |a-b|<=d, hence b/a=1+O(eta_X).                  (F45)

The exact field identity R_z=F-T_z yields

    <T_z,R_z>=-a^2+<T_z,F>=-a^2+O(ad),
    b^2=a^2-2Re<T_z,F>+d^2=a^2+O(ad+d^2).            (F46)

Therefore, NORMALIZED BY THE ACTUAL a^2,

    a^(-2) Gram(T_z,R_z)
       = [[1,-1],[-1,1]]+O(eta_X+eta_X^2)             (F47)

entrywise, with the first diagonal entry exactly1. This power-small normalized error is stronger than a conclusion obtained by substituting an asymptotic formula for a. In particular the actual cross scalar is eventually negative. Since the two coefficient supports are disjoint, it is an actual off-diagonal signed f3 interaction. It is not a depth-by-depth positivity assertion and is not new cancellation beyond the accepted full-field baseline.

The exact cosine/mismatch identity is

    rho=Re<T_z,R_z>/(ab),
    d^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+rho),                           (F48)
    0<=1+rho=[d^2-(a-b)^2]/(2ab).

Consequently the baseline gives

    |a-b|/a << X^(beta-1)tL^2,
    0<=1+rho << X^(2beta-2)t^2L^4.                   (F49)

The one-sided cross ratio in F46 has the LINEAR rate beta-1; the cosine defect has the SQUARED rate2beta-2. Equivalently,

    2Re<T_z,R_z>/(a^2+b^2)
                     =-1+d^2/(a^2+b^2).

For any proposed full target d<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), with1/2<gamma<1, the following pair is necessary and together sufficient, after renaming epsilon:

    |a-b| <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+rho <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)t^2L^4.       (F50)

Necessity uses F48 and a,b comparable to X/(tL^2). Conversely the first bound makes b comparable to a, and F48 with the second bound gives the requested d estimate. For the already known baseline b is positive eventually; the same follows from the first proposed target when proving sufficiency without that baseline.

At beta=.8749 the linear/squared powers are -.1251/-.2502. The current c_G frontier gives -.1251134/-.2502268 with the chosen positive baseline buffer. At gamma=.87449 the powers required are -.12551/-.25102. These rate requirements are not established improvements. The polylog case has t=B loglog X, so its mismatch and cosine factors are respectively (log X)^2 loglog X and (log X)^4(loglog X)^2, up to fixed constants.

The ACTUAL difference a-b is mandatory in F48--F50. The available error bound after replacing either norm by a leading expansion is much larger than X^gamma for gamma<1. Even F4's second term leaves only an exponent-one remainder bound; no lower bound for that actual remainder is asserted. A leading rank-one Gram with a vanishing coefficient sum does not establish the exact small eigenvalue needed for a stronger whole-field norm.

For completeness, append R_zm to the fixed finite components in §8. Its leading coefficient is b_(m+1)=-lambda_m^(-1), since F is power-small compared with N_X. Then

    <C_i,C_j>=[b_i b_j+O(epsilon_X+d/N_X)]N_X^2,
    (C_0,...,C_(m+1))=(B_0,...,B_m,R_zm),
    sum_i b_i=0,  sum_i C_i=F.                        (F51)

This is the complete leading Gram INCLUDING the actual late complement. Its complement entries use the accepted full-field estimate; they are not separately proved depth estimates. Exact telescoping and F48 retain the residual that this leading Gram cannot measure.

## 10. Comparison with RN, pair02, and the open target

The inspected predecessors are close in method but different in source.

| Feature | [private research revision] RN / pair02 Max SP class | Literal f3 theorem here |
|---|---|---|
| Original labels | Ordered d,e,ell; mu(d)mu(e)b(ell), strict d,e>Y, profile and source-specific masks | One integer n, coefficient f_3(n), complete fixed Gaussian |
| Rough condition | At most one rough prime in EACH original factor, or the specified DA one-prime class | At most one DISTINCT rough prime in the completed n |
| Cores | Two squarefree cores; common primes allowed | One core with full valuations; all powers of2,3 and other primes retained |
| Signed reciprocal mass | p_z^2, nonzero | H_z(1)=0 exactly |
| First surviving arithmetic quantity | Core reciprocal mass | -sum f(r)log r/r=h_z=3log2 P(z) |
| Leading field | C_theta p_z^2 x/log X | 3log2 exp(tau/2)P(z)x/(log x)^2 |
| Fixed log-threshold ratio lambda | Prefix factor lambda^(-2) | Prefix factor lambda^(-1) |
| Doubling band | -3/4 times old prefix | -1/2 times old prefix |
| Terminal source | Finite literal SP cap permits exact terminal threshold | Uncapped Gaussian has no finite exact terminal threshold |

RN's finite-Euler signed-moment method is reused with a different Euler product and a vanishing local factor. Pair02 Max BR18--23 proves its own DA-to-SP mask comparison and fixed original-prime-cell Gram. It does not supply F4 by inheritance. W35 review explicitly left Gaussian rough-depth transfer open; the new contribution is the direct source-specific proof F6--F33 for the accepted G25 coefficient, together with its actual threshold bands.

The elementary compensation identity F48 and finite-component Gram algebra are established predecessor tools. Their fresh inputs are the literal f3 prefix, its different constant/logarithmic order, its exact coefficient complement, and the new derivative estimates retaining full valuations. No literature-priority claim or exhaustive absence claim is made.

Current-proof G28--G30 supplies exponent equivalence for FULL F_6,G_tau and the original coprime cell, after their paid reconstruction. The moving predicate omega_z(n)<=1 does not commute with those Dirichlet convolutions, and no estimate for a correspondingly restricted A-source, pair source, or SP field follows from this report. Every such projection would require its own comparison.

OPEN-F3 remains the complete signed off-diagonal target G31. The present theorem proves an exponent-one partial field and genuine negative threshold bands. The actual high-depth complement must cancel that partial field at the established baseline rate, and would have to improve BOTH F50 requirements to yield gamma<1-c_G. It supplies no new c and no endpoint formal verification.

## 11. Evidence and handoff

The frozen candidate was read in full and its supplied SHA256 matched. Current-proof G25--G31, the Gaussian definition/kernel/baseline, [private research revision] review §§2--3 plus the relevant source/band/mismatch sections, the complete maintained attempt index and pertinent [private research revision]/52 entries, pair02 Max BR19--23, and W35's source-scope statements were inspected. The mathematical checks here are independent derivations of the actual decomposition, Euler derivatives, uniform moment bounds, sharp-endpoint PNT, every Gaussian/core/power tail, growing Taylor constants, signs and Gram interfaces. No numerical sample is offered as asymptotic proof.

statement:
# W43: exact reciprocal amplification limits and finite Gaussian source compression

This is a bounded research report, not a new zero-free theorem. The written c5=7821/62500=.125136 and boundary .874864 are unchanged, relative to the pinned PR9/PR15 premises; their newer formal/kernel replay remains separate from old-c0 evidence. No full Gaussian/f3 exponent, original-prime H covariance, or growing-conductor/angular estimate is proved here.

The useful outputs are (i) an explicit failure of a proposed signed convolution algebra even for bounded coefficients, (ii) an exact actual-Mobius obstruction and support dichotomy for finite-order Newton reciprocal amplification, and (iii) a complete compression of the fixed Gaussian readout to O((log X)^(3/2)/loglog X) source moments with arbitrary power error. The last is a new concrete target relative to the inspected sources, not a cancellation estimate or a literature-priority claim. Its stronger positive coefficient-energy criterion is clearly separated from its equivalent full signed Gram criterion.

## 1. Frozen process and six first tests

The immutable recipe was used without redraw. The 30-card seed artifact was read back and hashed before the detailed proof/history intake or test outcomes. Seeds SHA256:39ff2974fe20ea779773f70e7991a97c66ab32ad0d6b222909063d3a485b3cef;19,286bytes. Recipe SHA256:ed5c956dd1010115db98997ffe1f3936d0083dd96a0bd9446d09e5cd7052b0e3. Root received the seed-only event before further work. The charter itself had historical summaries; incidental search snippets are disclosed in the frozen seed prefix.

The complete current-proof.md and attempt-index.md were read after freezing seeds, followed by relevant original source slices. Four exact duplicates were excluded before sampling:03/27 repeat current G36's complete opposite-source Gram condition;05 supplies no change beyond W37's largest-prime organization;09 repeats the [private research revision]/54 reciprocal Hankel architecture. The exclusions do not claim those mechanisms false. Remaining familiar families were retained when their proposed quantitative first test was distinct. No added free extras were sampled.

Every numerical pool file records all eligible unreserved IDs, labels and literal comparisons BEFORE its one local secrets.randbelow draw. Deliberate reservations02/15/30 were frozen first. All qualifying prompt groups participate. Files are never retrospectively reconstructed or rerolled.

| Slot | Selected card | First test and result |
|---|---|---|
| Strongest bridge |02, p=.08 | The signed summatory norm is not a bounded convolution algebra, even with both coefficient sequences bounded by1; Section2 gives an explicit family. The generic amplification premise fails; a source-specific stronger norm remains possible. |
| Highest reach |15, p=.009 | A k-step geometric/Newton inverse agrees exactly with the ordinary longer Mobius prefix before (Y+1)^k. Its rough k-prime layer has fixed sign and absolute Gaussian mass at least X/log^k X. Section3 develops the actual source, the complementary regime and the missing zero return. |
| Uniform p<.10 |19, p=.006; index11 of21 | With completed functional-equation partners f(s)=epsilon g(s), the vector (f,g) and its s derivative are proportional, so their antisymmetric determinant is identically0. Gamma normalization does not create a positive conserved flux. A shifted or genuinely independent state would be a different proposal. |
| Uniform p<.01 |20, p=.008; index0 of9 | PSD completion gives A-C B^dagger C* >=0, a lower bound for A, not an upper bound. Fix B=C=1; [[t,1],[1,1]] is PSD for every t>=1, with unbounded A=t. A controlled residual/common realization is missing; the H and Gaussian deficits cannot be added. |
| Most different |30, p=.0012 | For S in{+1,-1}, conditional bias energy E|E(S|T)|^2 is the right exact quantity. Mutual information alone is insufficient: a deterministic S has I(S;T)=0 but bias1. For the actual f3 statistic T=rad(n/3^v3(n)), S=mu(T) is determined, so conditional bias energy is exactly1. No compression gain follows from retaining that complete statistic. |
| Uniform remaining wildcard |06, p=.06; index2 of21 | Counting-space conditional expectation does not automatically commute with Gaussian readout. A polynomial extension of log-bin projection does, however, have an explicitly paid readout residual. Section4 is its protected development. |

The three developments are02,15,06. The calculations for19/20/30 are first tests only. The protected rare/high-reach card15 and wildcard06 received actual development; no unselected replacement was silently inserted.

For19, the standard primitive Dirichlet functional equation was checked at [NIST DLMF25.15.5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15#E5). After the usual completion it has a constant root-number factor. The zero determinant is derived here, not cited as a zero-free result. It is a narrow failure of the proposed two-dependent-state flux, not of all canonical-system or Hermite-Biehler methods.

For20, an honest sufficient replacement would first prove a source-exact identity F=T H+E in compatible spaces and scales, including the original H roots, both projectors, all ordered short pairs, phase and heights. Bounds ||H||<=X^(h+epsilon), ||T||<=X^(t+epsilon), ||E||<=X^(e+epsilon) would then give gamma=max(h+t,e), after epsilon allocation. Neither that map, the identification of X with H's scale, nor the residual estimate is supplied. A formal block matrix cannot manufacture it.

## 2. Development02: bounded-coefficient summatory norms are not an algebra

For a finitely supported real sequence a, let A(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n) and

    ||a||_[sigma]=sup_(x>=1) x^(-sigma)|A(x)|, 0<sigma<1.

**W43.1.** There is no constant C_sigma such that

    ||a*b||_[sigma] <= C_sigma ||a||_[sigma] ||b||_[sigma]

for all finite real a,b, even if |a(n)|,|b(n)|<=1 and both input norms are at most1. Thus a uniform Banach-algebra argument based only on the buffered Mertens exponent and bounded coefficients cannot justify the seed's reciprocal iteration.

Proof. Fix N>=2. Set A(d)=(-1)^(d+1)/2 for1<=d<=N and A(d)=0 for d=0 or d>=N+1; a(d)=A(d)-A(d-1). Then a is supported on1,...,N+1, its endpoint magnitudes are1/2 and its other magnitudes are1. In particular |a|<=1 and ||a||_[sigma]<=1/2.

Choose a large integer H with

    H>=4(N+1)^2,
    H^(1-sigma)>=16(N+1)^(2-sigma),
    t_d=floor(H/d), 1<=d<=N+1.

These t_d are distinct. Prescribe B(t_d)=sign(a(d))*t_d^sigma. On the real interval[0,2H], define B by linear interpolation through those points, B(0)=B(2H)=0, and set B=0 outside. The signed interpolation lies between the concave envelopes +/-t^sigma: its absolute value is bounded by the interpolation of the endpoint absolute values, which is at most t^sigma. Therefore |B(t)|<=t^sigma.

For consecutive d,d+1, the spacing is at least H/(4d^2), while the change in B is at most2(H/d)^sigma. Thus each inner slope has absolute value at most

    8 H^(sigma-1) d^(2-sigma) <=1/2.

The two outer slopes have absolute value at most1. Let b(n)=B(n)-B(n-1). It is finitely supported, |b(n)|<=1 and ||b||_[sigma]<=1. Dirichlet convolution and summation now give the exact positive alignment

    sum_(n<=H)(a*b)(n)
      =sum_(d<=N+1)a(d)B(floor(H/d))
      =sum_(d<=N+1)|a(d)|t_d^sigma.

Since t_d>=H/(2d), the last expression divided by H^sigma is at least

    2^(-sigma) sum_(d=2)^N d^(-sigma)
      >>_sigma N^(1-sigma).

This diverges with N, proving W43.1. The proof works with rounded-down peaks floor(t_d^sigma) as well, losing only an absolute factor for sufficiently large H. Rounded peaks permit entirely rational finite certificates when sigma=7/8, by computing the integer eighth root of t_d^7.

With H chosen of order N^((2-sigma)/(1-sigma)), this family has a convolution value of order at least H^(1/(2-sigma)). Since 1/(2-sigma)>sigma, even the input exponent is not preserved by this uniform norm argument. This is a family of finite sequences with uniform input constants; it is not a claimed asymptotic lower bound for one fixed infinite sequence, and neither sequence is claimed to be mu. At sigma=.874864 the comparison exponent is the exact62500/70321, not a QRH exponent.

**What this changes.** A signed reciprocal construction cannot invoke submultiplicativity merely because both inputs have partial sums O(x^sigma). It must estimate the actual convolution or use a genuinely stronger norm with its inclusion and complete zero return proved. Weighted coefficient l1 is a true algebra on its convergence half-plane, but moving from the signed norm into it pays the omitted absolute values and does not supply a new strip. This sharpens the generic bounded-coefficient failure; it does not refute source-specific Mobius convolution estimates.

Functional signature: finite bounded arithmetic sequences; interpolate opposite partial-sum peaks at hyperbolic sampling points; exact positive alignment under convolution; first unpaid input is a source-specific stronger convolution norm; quantitative output is an unbounded norm ratio, not a zero-free gain. Ancestry: W26's finite-Euler H-infinity obstruction and W35's absolute renewal failure concern different norms and coefficients. No literature novelty is asserted for the general nonalgebra fact.

## 3. Development15: actual inverse Newton iteration and its complete rough sector

Throughout, g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)), with tau>0 fixed. Let bold1(n)=1, delta(n)=1_(n=1), and let * denote Dirichlet convolution. For integer Y>=1 put

    m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y),
    d_Y=delta-bold1*m_Y,
    M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)n^(-s),
    D_Y(s)=1-zeta(s)M_Y(s).

The finite convolution m_Y is literal, including every zero coefficient. For fixed integer k>=1 define

    q_(Y,k)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))),
    Q_(Y,k)(s)=M_Y(s)sum_(j=0)^(k-1)D_Y(s)^j.

The k=2 step is precisely the proposed Newton inverse M(2-zeta M). Repeated Newton squaring corresponds to k a power of2. All identities are first coefficient identities or absolutely convergent series on Re(s)>1, then meromorphic identities away from the principal pole.

**W43.2 (exact support and length return).**

    delta-bold1*q_(Y,k)=d_Y^(*k),
    d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y,
    d_Y^(*k)(n)=0 for n<(Y+1)^k,
    q_(Y,k)(n)=mu(n) for n<(Y+1)^k.

The first line is the finite geometric identity. The second is mu*bold1=delta with all divisors below the original cutoff. The third follows because every nonzero convolution factor is at least Y+1. Multiply the first line by mu to obtain q_(Y,k)=mu-mu*d_Y^(*k), which proves the last line. Thus truncating q below (Y+1)^k produces exactly the ordinary longer Mobius prefix. This is an identity, not a faster estimate for that prefix. No assertion is made that the endpoint (Y+1)^k is always the first nonzero defect; natural Mobius zeros may delay it.

Let Q^tr be the Dirichlet polynomial obtained by truncating q to n<(Y+1)^k, and T=Q-Q^tr. The entire truncation feedback is

    1-zeta Q^tr = D_Y^k + zeta T.                  (N1)

It is not legitimate to omit zeta T because Q^tr is exactly the longer Mobius prefix. At any zeta zero rho in the open critical strip,

    D_Y(rho)=1, Q_(Y,k)(rho)=k M_Y(rho),
    1-zeta(rho)Q^tr(rho)=1.                       (N2)

Q and T are holomorphic at rho: they are finite polynomials in zeta multiplied by finite Dirichlet polynomials. The apparent formula Q=(1-D_Y^k)/zeta has a removable singularity there. This distinguishes the proposed observable from the actual Gaussian reciprocal detector, whose Mellin transform has a nonvanishing numerator over zeta. A small local smoothed defect has not inherited that pole return.

**W43.3 (all rough coefficients and a fixed-order absolute barrier).** Say n is Y-rough if every prime factor exceeds Y. For every Y-rough n>1, d_Y(n)=-1, because the only divisor admitted by m_Y is1. Hence, for every Y-rough n,

    d_Y^(*k)(n)=(-1)^k F_k(n),

where F_k(n) is the nonnegative number of ordered k-tuples of integers>1 whose product is n. In particular it vanishes for Omega(n)<k, and if Omega(n)=k then

    F_k(n)=k! / product_(p^e||n)e! .               (N3)

This includes prime powers; no squarefree surrogate or changed mask is used. For a fixed k and0<theta<=1/k, take Y=floor(X^theta) and the complete rough Gaussian subfield

    V_(Y,k)(x)=sum_(P^-(n)>Y) d_Y^(*k)(n)
                              g_tau(log(n/x)).

Its terms all have the one sign (-1)^k. Restrict just for a lower bound to products of k distinct primes in (X^(1/k),2X^(1/k)]. These primes exceed Y, and their products lie in[X,2^k X]. The Gaussian has a positive lower bound depending only on fixed tau,k for every such product and x in[X,2X]. The prime number theorem gives >>_k X^(1/k)/log X primes in that interval. Unique factorization and (N3) yield, uniformly on the whole shell,

    |V_(Y,k)(x)| >>_(tau,k) X/(log X)^k.          (N4)

Thus its norm is also >>X/(log X)^k. The same lower bound holds for the absolute value majorant of the complete d_Y^(*k) field. No fixed finite order k permits an absolute coarse estimate with norm exponent gamma<1 in this range. The PNT input is the standard asymptotic checked at [NIST DLMF27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2#E3); no moving modulus or short-interval theorem is used.

The full signed d_Y^(*k) field also contains nonrough terms. Their interaction can cancel (N4), so this is NOT a lower bound for that full field or for the actual f3/Gaussian detector. The complement is precisely what an improved signed argument must pay. The model resembles earlier semiprime obstructions at a conceptual level but the coefficients here are the exact Newton defect, not DP's E=-2 or the f3 critical rough field.

**W43.4 (opposite regime and missing bridge).** If theta>1/k is fixed, every d_Y^(*k) coefficient begins beyond (Y+1)^k=X^(k theta+o(1)), strictly to the right of the shell. Since |d_Y(n)|<=d_2(n), one has |d_Y^(*k)(n)|<=d_(2k)(n). The elementary divisor count sum_(n<=u)d_(2k)(n)<=u(1+log u)^(2k-1) and Gaussian tail integration give, for every fixed A>0,

    sum_n |d_Y^(*k)(n)| g_tau(log(n/x))
       <<_(A,tau,k,theta) X^(-A),  X<=x<=2X.      (N5)

Indeed the lower logarithmic distance is (k theta-1)log X-O(1); its negative quadratic Gaussian exponent dominates every linear exponent and fixed logarithmic factor. This is completely unconditional. It coexists with (N2) at any hypothetical zero because the defect is not a reciprocal pole detector and because its scale-dependent future tail is not discarded from a continued Mellin integral.

The dichotomy is consequential for the proposed high-ceiling mechanism: at fixed finite order with k theta<=1, absolute treatment fails at every gamma<1; with k theta>1, arbitrary local Gaussian smallness is automatic yet has no zero-exclusion implication. This rules out the particular advertised coarse-loss-budget route, not every nonlinear detector or growing-order scheme. Growing k changes divisor constants, prime counting, combinatorics and Mellin return; it is not covered by these fixed-k statements.

**Weakest honest return left.** A source-exact estimate |1-zeta(s)Q^tr(s)|<1 on the desired region directly excludes zeros there. N1 shows that it must retain zeta T. Alternatively, convergence of the longer actual inverse prefixes to an analytic reciprocal would suffice, but the usual hypothesis sum_(n<=x)mu(n)=O_epsilon(x^(gamma+epsilon)) is exactly a new arithmetic bound. A c=1/6 or1/4 endpoint would respectively need gamma=5/6 or3/4 (with appropriate open-strip buffers), and neither is supplied. Merely squaring D or proving (N5) does not weaken these complete obligations.

For a fixed ordinary character, complete multiplicativity gives d_(Y,chi)(n)=chi(n)d_Y(n) and the same exact truncation identity with L(s,chi). Natural zeros remain. The absolute rough-sector obstruction persists after excluding the finitely many conductor primes; no signed lower bound for a nonreal character is asserted. No Eisenstein-ideal analogue or growing-conductor uniformity is claimed from this rational-integer calculation.

Functional signature: literal truncated Mobius inverse; polynomial reciprocal iteration; formal defect-power cancellation followed by exact tail feedback; first unpaid estimate is the complete signed correction or an actual pointwise reciprocal bound; proved return is the support/rough-sector dichotomy and a failed zero-detection shortcut. This was the serious hard/upstream attempt. It achieved a useful negative result rather than a larger c.

## 4. Development06: a source-exact polylogarithmic Gaussian compression

This develops the viable wildcard instead of allowing all slots to become generic negative examples. It changes the representation of the full fixed Gaussian, not its coefficients or pole return.

Fix tau>0 and a bounded complex coefficient sequence |a(n)|<=1. In the intended application a(n)=f3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) from current G25/G31, including every prime power and its actual prime3 exception. Put

    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), L=log X.

Fix an arbitrary desired error power A>0. Let

    C=sqrt(2tau(A+2)),
    j_-=-ceil(C sqrt L), j_+=ceil(log2+C sqrt L)-1,
    N_X={n in N: j_-<=log(n/X)<j_++1},
    m=ceil(2(A+2)L/log L),
    I_j={n in N_X: j<=log(n/X)<j+1}.                (P1)

Endpoint conventions are literal: all outer and inner cuts are left closed/right open, and the outer cuts are aligned with complete unit log bins. This expands the nominal Gaussian window by less than one unit at either end; the complete tails are still paid below. Empty bins contribute no space. For each nonempty I_j let P_j be the orthogonal projection in the actual finite counting space ell2(I_j) onto the values of real polynomials in t_n=log(n/X)-j of degree<m. If a bin has fewer than m points, take its entire value space. No continuous-density replacement enters this definition. Put P_X=direct_sum P_j, a_X=a|_(N_X), and

    F_X^proj(x)=sum_(n in N_X)(P_X a_X)(n)
                                      g_tau(log(n/x)).

**W43.5.** Uniformly for all coefficient sequences |a|<=1 and x in[X,2X], for all sufficiently large X depending only on A,tau,

    |F_a(x)-F_X^proj(x)| <= C_(A,tau) X^(-A),
    rank(P_X)=O_(A,tau)(L^(3/2)/log L).              (P2)

All discarded source terms, all within-bin residuals and every cross-bin interaction are included in this approximation. It is not a hereditary submask inequality, an unrestricted infinite-column operator estimate, or a claim that the projected coefficients remain bounded by1.

Proof of tails. Below the lower cap, log(n/x)<=-C sqrt L; counting at most X exp(-C sqrt L) terms bounds that tail by X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). Above the upper cap, Gaussian integral comparison after n=x exp(v) gives the same exponent. Both are X^(-A-1+o(1)), hence O(X^-A) after a fixed buffer. The bound uses |a|<=1 and needs no arithmetic cancellation.

Proof of projection error. Let c be any real number. On a complex circle |z|=R,

    |g_tau(c+z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(R^2/(2tau)).

The negative real square has simply been dropped; the inequality is uniform in c. Cauchy's coefficient formula bounds the tail after degree m-1, for0<=t<1 and R=sqrt(tau m)>=2, by

    eps_(tau,m) <= 2(2pi tau)^(-1/2)
                           (e/(tau m))^(m/2).          (P3)

For u=log(x/X) in[0,log2], take c=j-u. The sampled Gaussian vector v_x(n)=g_tau(log(n/X)-u) has a degree<m polynomial approximant on every I_j with pointwise error eps_(tau,m). Since an orthogonal projection has the best ell2 error,

    ||(I-P_X)v_x||_2 <= sqrt(#N_X) eps_(tau,m).

Self-adjointness and ||a_X||_2<=sqrt(#N_X) now imply

    |sum_(N_X)(a_X-P_Xa_X)(n)v_x(n)|
       <= #N_X eps_(tau,m).                           (P4)

Complex coefficients cause no problem: conjugate the real Gaussian vector in the Hermitian pairing. Since #N_X<=2e X exp(C sqrt L) and

    log eps_(tau,m)=-(A+2)L+o(L),

(P4) is X^(-A-1+o(1)). There are at most2C sqrt L+O(1) nonempty bins, each of dimension at most m. This proves both parts of(P2).

**Complete finite target.** Choose any real orthonormal basis q_alpha of range(P_X), each basis vector supported on one original bin, and define the exact signed source moments and readouts

    c_alpha(X)=sum_(n in N_X)a(n)q_alpha(n),
    V_alpha(x)=sum_(n in N_X)q_alpha(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    Kproj_(alpha,beta)=integral_X^(2X)
                            V_alpha(x)V_beta(x) dx/x.

Then

    F_X^proj=sum_alpha c_alpha V_alpha,
    ||F_X^proj||_2^2=c* Kproj c.                       (P5)

Kproj is a finite positive Gram matrix, but the off-diagonal source contributions are still signed or complex. Equation(P5) retains all of them. For every fixed gamma>0, (P2) gives equivalence, with arbitrary epsilon allowances, between the full F_a norm bound O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) and the corresponding bound for c* Kproj c. The number of source moments is polylogarithmic; their sizes and correlated phases remain an arithmetic problem.

For literal f3 and fixed gamma>1/2, combine this equivalence with current G28/G29/G31, whose two absolutely summable convolution inverses and small-scale tails are already proved. A bound

    c* Kproj c <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon)

on every sufficiently large dyadic X excludes zeros in Re(s)>gamma by that exact existing return. No additional Gaussian/H saving is added. The explicit first-gain condition is gamma<.874864; the targets5/6 and3/4 remain available. This is a complete reformulation, not proof of its input.

**A simpler but stronger sufficient input.** The Hilbert-Schmidt estimate on the finite readout W_X gives

    ||W_X||^2 <= sum_(n in N_X)||v_n||_2^2
       <= (log2)/(2pi tau) #N_X = X^(1+o(1)).

Consequently it suffices to prove the positive source-moment bound

    E_X:=sum_alpha |c_alpha|^2=||P_Xa_X||_2^2
       <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-1+epsilon).                (P6)

This requires actual cancellation in every retained polynomial statistic and can be stronger than(P5), because it discards the favorable cross-bin readout interference. It is not claimed necessary. ### New exact alternative to the fixed-point search

At fixed target \(\kappa\) and its chosen \(\delta\), put
\[
D_\kappa=3R'/4-1/(24\kappa),\quad
H_0=-1/(2D_\kappa),\quad
H_1=-(1/2+1/(6\kappa))/D_\kappa.
\]
Then \(h=H_0+H_1\ell\). Let
\[
A_\kappa=(2H_0-1)/12,\qquad
B_\kappa=(2H_1-3)/12,\qquad
\ell_b=4(c-1/12).
\]
The simultaneous equations \(\ell=\ell_b-4\sigma\), \(\sigma=\alpha(y-x)/12\) solve exactly as
\[
\sigma=
\frac{\alpha(A_\kappa+B_\kappa\ell_b)}
{1+4\alpha B_\kappa}, \tag{A14.2}
\]
whenever the denominator is nonzero. All capacity and rectangle constraints still require separate verification. This removes the need for a monotonicity-assuming binary search and is a new exact diagnostic simplification.

The resonant-coset, Pólya–Vinogradov-shaped, and generic \((Q+Z)\) comparisons in GS §5 are at most bookkeeping comparisons under their displayed models. The coset bound is not reconstructed there with full coefficients; do not promote it to a new uniform arithmetic lemma. The explicit algebraic comparisons at \(4/33\) are correct.

## 1. What the collective evidence changes

The previous program spent substantial effort constructing usable currents and completions. That work now supplies actual objects to estimate. Repeating their synthesis, gamma amplification or qualitative continuation would not improve the main exponents. The useful next theorem must change a dominant arithmetic average, improve the complete physical/numerator budget, or enable a genuinely different detector.

There are several distinct ways to do that. A conductor-saving completed cubic mean and the signed cubic covariance share much arithmetic, but have different sufficient hypotheses; neither has been proved equivalent to the other. The reflected short-divisor hypothesis H and a bound on the full physical sextic covariance can lead to the same desired geometry, but no all-branch equivalence is available. The rational Möbius scale energy and the Eisenstein triple-theta scale energy have related Mellin content, but no norm comparison transfers a saving between them. These are reasons to share exact lemmas, not reasons to count every label as an independent discovery or to collapse unlike estimates into one campaign.

| Available now | Research consequence | Remaining obligation |
|---|---|---|
| T01–T02: fixed-factor division and direct common-completion selector | Work with the completion the current supplies; no angular nonvanishing theorem is needed on this route | A conductor-saving mean with the stipulated finite ray orbit and buffered-strip uniformity |
| T03–T04: cube-free lifting and actual inverse-prime-square bound | Order rows by \(q_aq_b^2\); concentrate effort on the ordinary-oriented core | Composite/mixed orientations and the ordinary-dominant boxes; prime-square descendants are not free |
| T05: physical cube-row Type I restriction | The complete principal-cube remainder can be compared with C–C, with a strictly affordable Type I correction | Improve C–C itself and control the nonprincipal remainder |
| T06–T07: all-descendant same-core square function and true-gcd tail | Study covariance of *different* cores with small true gcd, keeping actual prime slots | A full signed small-gcd bound, especially at gcd one |
| A01: coherent unembedded pair remainder after pairwise zero subtraction | One additional genuine sector is affordable | Nonprincipal characters, their sixth-power-frequency packets and mixed embeddings |
| T08: finite incidence, including common-completion equivalence | Trade row and divisor exponents separately | A finite-incidence estimate; its \(g=1\) part still contains an ordinary mean |
| T09: dyadic Möbius and compact-profile triple energies | Seek averaged signed correlations; avoid unnecessary uniform inverse Mellin factors | The new scale-energy estimates at every dyadic scale |
| A14: full-probe-saving certificates | A modest uniform improvement of the *actual probe* has a checked incremental payoff | The full-probe saving; a pair-dependent Gram label is not a vector projection |

**Important disagreement resolved.** The Grok brainstorming correctly stresses how far the pointwise conductor bound lies from a useful mean. It overstates the consequence when it closes every squarefree-source/current variant, leaves fixed Hecke division as unavoidable, or identifies H with the full physical covariance without a kernel theorem. Conversely, Gemini's completion-preserving idea was productive after exact selector verification; its automatic Deligne saving, prime-square identity and fixed numerical cutoff choices do not survive scrutiny. The rankings below use the corrected mathematics, not provider confidence.
