# [private research revision] independent review: calibrated multiplicative model and complete window return



## 1. Decision and exact limits

**Accept Theorems M and B as written mathematical results at their stated scope. Accept their combined quantitative obstruction. Do not credit an arithmetic energy improvement or any new zero-free constant.** The incumbent remains c6 = 125139/1000000, with b6 = 874861/1000000. The conditional returns to c = .13, 1/6 or 1/4 have a completely explicit missing hypothesis. They are not established endpoints.

I fully read the one frozen author packet: `report.md`, `check.py`, `receipt.json` and `freeze.json`. Its four byte bindings match the authorized handoff, and are independently recorded in `receipt.json` here. I did not execute or alter the author's helper. I reconstructed the arguments below rather than infer analysis from its finite arithmetic checks. No outside correlation theorem is needed for M or B.

The strongest relevant objection was simultaneous probability-one selection. An estimate uniform in a conditioned finite phase does not, by itself, license an uncountable intersection over every possible phase assignment. The stated theorem does not need such an intersection: finite prescriptions are fixed first; finite truncation sets, integer affine forms and ordinary character weights form countable collections. Section 3 below gives the complete selection argument, and a finite-basis strengthening if uniform finite-phase control is desired. Thus this is an explanation of the exact quantifier contract, not a fatal gap or a change to the theorem.

The model is genuinely multiplicative and has exactly the squarefree/coprime support. It permits complex phases. It does not have the actual global prime law a(p) = -chi(p), the prescribed global convolution inverse, or the real-valuedness of W27's model. Its fixed-H Cesaro energy limit is an averaged statement; it is not square-root cancellation in each individual interval. These distinctions are essential to the verdict.

## 2. Frozen inputs, ancestry and recovery record

The frozen author directory is `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/headroom-source/`:

| File | Bytes | SHA256 |
|---|---:|---|
| report.md | 28806 | 87668bea280aa2e24aeb4e39e38ad795ced2cdc15f439e26d7607be6bb89830d |
| check.py | 5097 | 99d378421360dbaf5dcff78e955ffac6425c82ece97778415fc1864e138740f4 |
| receipt.json | 5146 | e71774bd5485edc3d287f86478aeb5f9affc4e90745fa355c7c218e23a389843 |
| freeze.json | 1483 | e3e08691209c3cb7c9ac1c53648ce389a3e1a60d7c6fd196694bab9d7c9983be |



The author disclosed that its normal release failed from host/workspace binding drift after the outage. Its original claim remains untouched. The controller expressly authorized this separate read-only frozen intake while handling recovery. This report makes no claim that the author has released ownership. My own release result is a separate operational receipt after the mathematical freeze; no unconfirmed release is inferred from a status check.

For ancestry I read W27's construction at `[restricted mathematical source]`, lines 176-215, and targeted matches in the current attempt index and [private research revision] headroom-A. The exact current bytes still match the author's snapshot hashes; those bindings and read limits are recorded here. W27 already supplied a real multiplicative finite-prefix model with interior poles. Its line 210 explicitly left quantitative partial-sum/height calibration unproved. [private research revision] headroom-A supplied a calibrated but nonmultiplicative coarse model. M's useful additional package is simultaneous calibration, multiplicativity, fixed-form correlation cancellation and a growing-window lower bound. Multiplicativity alone is not new, and M is not a strengthening of W27 in real-valuedness.

I retained the author's primary-paper screen as motivation only. I did not freshly fetch or reverify the Tao or Matomaki--Radziwill--Tao--Teravainen--Ziegler papers in this provider-free review. Their conclusions are not premises of the accepted M/B arguments. No claim of literature priority follows from this review.

## 3. Independent proof and quantifier audit of M

Fix q >= 1, a finite set of prescribed unit values at primes not dividing q, and 1/2 < beta < b6. Fix the Gaussian parameter tau > 0. A target gamma, when used, is chosen below beta. The existence order is: fixed mathematical parameters and finite prescriptions; choose the probability space; intersect the required probability-one events; select one outcome; then let character, accuracy exponent, affine form and scale vary within the stated contract. A different beta or incompatible finite prescription may use a different sequence. There is no claim that one sequence realizes mutually incompatible prime prescriptions.

### 3.1 Rare replacements and all fixed-character calibration

Let epsilon_p be independent Steinhaus variables, and independently let I_p be Bernoulli with mean p^(beta-1). Initially set v_p = 1 if I_p = 1 and v_p = epsilon_p otherwise. Set

    a(n) = mu(n)^2 product_{p|n} v_p,

then delete primes dividing q and impose the finite prescribed values. The resulting function is multiplicative, a(1)=1, and

    |a(n)| = mu(n)^2 1_{(n,q)=1}.

It is not completely multiplicative. These are the actual natural zero conditions, not a squarefree replacement inside a completely multiplicative claim.

Write P = {p : I_p = 1}. For every b > beta,

    E sum_{p in P} p^(-b) = sum_p p^(-(b+1-beta)) < infinity.

A nonnegative random variable with finite expectation is finite almost surely. Intersect over rational b > beta; comparison then supplies every real b > beta. In particular, the reciprocal sum over P is finite. Choosing rational beta < b < 1 also gives

    # {p in P : p <= x} <= x^b sum_{p in P} p^(-b) = O_b(x^b).

For the unmodified source a0(n) = mu(n)^2 product epsilon_p, distinct squarefree integers give distinct Steinhaus monomials and hence are orthogonal in L2. Non-squarefree terms vanish. Multiplication by any fixed ordinary character psi preserves this orthogonality and does not increase the diagonal variances. The deterministic n=1 term is also orthogonal to all other monomials.

The dyadic maximal inequality used by the author needs no independence between the integer-indexed coefficients. Every initial segment of [1,2^k] is a disjoint union of at most k+1 standard dyadic blocks. Cauchy bounds its squared sum by (k+1) times the sum of squared sums over those blocks; enlarging to every block on every level has expected value at most (k+1)2^k. Therefore

    E max_{m <= 2^k} |sum_{n <= m} a0(n) psi(n)|^2
        <= (k+1)^2 2^k.

Markov at 2^(k(1/2+eta)) produces a summable series in k for every eta > 0. Borel--Cantelli and interpolation between dyadic endpoints prove

    sum_{n <= x} a0(n) psi(n) = O_{eta,psi}(x^(1/2+eta)).

Ordinary characters are countable: there are finitely many for each positive modulus. Intersect over all of them and rational eta > 0. Smaller rational eta recover every requested real accuracy exponent. No conductor-uniform constant is obtained or required.

The local quotient at a changed prime, with z = p^(-s), is exactly

    (1+v z)/(1+epsilon z)
      = 1 + sum_{j>=1} (v-epsilon)(-epsilon)^(j-1) z^j.

Its nonconstant coefficients have modulus at most 2. It defines a multiplicative convolution coefficient d with a = a0*d and, for b > beta,

    sum_n |d(n)| n^(-b)
      <= C_{b,F} product_{p in P} (1 + 2 p^(-b)/(1-p^(-b))) < infinity.

Finite deletions and prescribed changes multiply this by finitely many convergent factors for b > 0. Since an ordinary character is completely multiplicative, including its zero values,

    a psi = (a0 psi) * (d psi).

Choose 1/2+eta < b. Applying the preceding bound to x/m >= 1 and enlarging its exponent to b gives an upper bound C x^b sum_m |d(m)|m^(-b). For any epsilon > 0, choose b in (beta,beta+epsilon). Thus every fixed twist satisfies O_{epsilon,psi}(x^(beta+epsilon)). This supplies, in particular, any weaker summatory calibration exponent strictly between beta and b6. Abel summation also gives the claimed O((1+|t|)x^(beta+epsilon)) for the additional n^(it) twist, and fixed logarithmic derivatives cost another arbitrarily small power. This does not assert uniformity for a growing family of characters.

### 3.2 Exact pole and full-height Gaussian asymptotic

Before finite modifications, E v_p = p^(beta-1). Let xi_p = v_p - p^(beta-1). These are independent centered variables of variance at most 1. The same dyadic maximal argument, with zero coefficients off the primes, gives

    S(x) = sum_{p <= x} xi_p = O_eta(x^(1/2+eta))

on a probability-one event for every rational eta > 0. Hence

    Z(s) = s integral_1^infinity S(x) x^(-s-1) dx

is holomorphic on Re(s)>1/2. On any fixed closed vertical strip with left boundary sigma0>1/2, choose eta<sigma0-1/2. The integral is bounded by a constant times |s|, uniformly on that strip. In particular, |Z(s)| <= C(1+|Im(s)|).

Starting in Re(s)>1, the absolutely convergent Euler products and logarithmic series give

    D_a(s) = zeta(s+1-beta) H(s),

where the logarithm of H is

    Z(s)
    + sum_p sum_{j>=2} (-1)^(j+1) v_p^j p^(-js)/j
    - sum_p sum_{j>=2} p^(-j(s+1-beta))/j.

The signs follow directly by subtracting log zeta from log D_a. Both double tails converge absolutely and normally on Re(s)>1/2. The respective leading real prime exponents are 2 Re(s)>1 and 2(Re(s)+1-beta)>1; the second inequality uses beta<1. Thus H is an exponential of a holomorphic function there, is nonzero, and obeys |H(s)| <= exp(C(1+|Im(s)|)) on each fixed closed strip. Finite deletions or changes multiply H by

    1/(1+v_p p^(-s)), or
    (1+v'_p p^(-s))/(1+v_p p^(-s)).

For Re(s)>0 their denominators and numerators are nonzero; on a strip bounded away from zero their moduli are bounded. Consequently D_a has exactly the required simple pole at beta with nonzero residue H(beta). Zeta zeros create zeros, not extra poles, and cannot cancel the simple pole at argument 1.

For g_tau(u) = (2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)), direct Mellin inversion gives

    F_a(x) = (1/(2 pi i)) integral_{Re(s)=c}
                exp(tau s^2/2) D_a(s) x^s ds,   c>1.

Move this contour to any fixed sigma in (1/2,beta). On the finite horizontal width, ordinary zeta has polynomial vertical growth away from its isolated pole, H has at most exponential vertical growth, and the Gaussian has exp(-tau t^2/2) decay. Horizontal integrals tend to zero and both infinite vertical integrals converge absolutely. This is a full-height contour shift; there is no truncated-height remainder or data-dependent contour. The only crossed pole is beta, so

    F_a(x) = exp(tau beta^2/2) H(beta) x^beta + O_sigma(x^sigma).

The leading coefficient is nonzero. Every fixed derivative only inserts a polynomial in s and is paid by the same Gaussian decay. As x tends to zero, g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_A (x/n)^A for each A>1; summing yields O_A(x^A). This covers the other end of a later Mellin transform. None of these conclusions uses a zero-free hypothesis.

### 3.3 Fixed affine correlations and one outcome

Take L_i(n)=A_i n+B_i with integer A_i>0 and determinant A1 B2 - A2 B1 nonzero. Discard finitely many n with nonpositive arguments. First modify only a fixed finite prime set F, including primes dividing q. Let Q be its squarefree product, and D=2^|F|. On nonzero terms write L1(n)=d r and L2(n)=e s, where d,e divide Q and r,s are squarefree and coprime to Q. The coefficient contributed by primes in F, or by any fixed ordinary character weights, has modulus at most 1.

For the conjugated product, the remaining random monomial is epsilon(r/s). Distinct rational ratios are orthogonal. Holding d,e and r/s fixed determines L1/L2, hence determines at most one n by nondegeneracy. Every monomial class contains at most D^2 terms. For the unconjugated product it is epsilon(rs); distinct integer products are orthogonal. Holding d,e,rs fixed gives a quadratic equation for n, with at most two solutions, so classes have at most 2D^2 terms. Cauchy inside each class gives

    E |C_N|^2 <= 2D^2 N + O_F(1)

for either correlation sum. Shared prime factors in r,s are allowed: rational cancellation in the conjugated case and exponent 2 in the unconjugated case are exactly encoded by these monomials. There is no assumption that distinct n supply independent summands.

For each fixed positive rational epsilon, Markov at N=j^2 gives a summable O(epsilon^(-2)j^(-2)) failure probability. Borel--Cantelli implies C_{j^2}/j^2 -> 0. The O(j) omitted bounded terms fill the gaps to every N. Intersect over epsilon, finite F, affine forms and ordinary character weights; these are countable sets.

Conditioning on the finitely many original phases in F causes no problem: the estimate is uniform in their values, and Fubini gives a probability-one conclusion for the fixed prescribed modification under the original probability measure. There is no uncountable-intersection step. If the sentence about uniform finite phases is interpreted as uniform convergence across all phase assignments, it also has a direct proof: decompose C_N into its finitely many (d,e) components. Each component has the same orthogonality/multiplicity bound, independently of the phase coefficient. Take their finite probability-one intersection. The maximum over unit phase coefficients of |C_N|/N is bounded by the sum of the finitely many component magnitudes divided by N, which tends to zero. Zero-valued ramified components can simply be omitted.

Now restore the infinite Bernoulli replacement set P. Truncate it at Y, retaining the fixed prescriptions and q. Every realized finite truncation belongs to the countable finite-set family already handled, even though its identity depends on the Bernoulli outcome. A value at A n+B can differ from its truncation only if a prime p in P above Y divides that argument. Put the finitely many primes dividing A below Y. Each remaining p has at most N/p+1 such n up to N, and p <= C N apart from harmless initial terms. The exceptional proportion is at most

    sum_{p in P, p>Y} 1/p + O(#P(CN)/N).

The second term tends to zero because #P(x)=O_b(x^b) for some b<1. Take N to infinity first, then Y to infinity; the first term tends to zero by reciprocal summability. Products of bounded terms change by at most 2 on the union of the two exceptional sets. Both limiting correlations are zero. All calibration, prime-series and correlation events used above are countable intersections of probability-one events, so one fixed outcome has all the stated properties at all scales.

For every fixed integer H, expansion of the unweighted Cesaro window energy gives diagonal contribution H d_q, where

    d_q = product_{p|q}(1-1/p) product_{p not dividing q}(1-1/p^2)>0.

This follows from the ordinary squarefree/coprime density, proved by finite sieve and the convergent tail sum over p^2. The finitely many off-diagonal shifts have nonzero determinant and hence vanish by the pair result. The conclusion is

    (1/N) sum_{m<=N} |sum_{j=1}^H a(m+j)|^2 -> H d_q.

The order fixes H before N. No uniform rate in H follows. Partial summation turns C_N=o(N) into qualitative logarithmic fixed-form cancellation, including logarithmic intervals whose log-length tends to infinity: split at a fixed threshold, then use the arbitrary small bound |C_N|<=epsilon N above it. This does not establish an outside theorem's nonpretentiousness hypotheses or a growing-lag rate.

### 3.4 Finite masks and exact scope of the obstruction

For a feasible valuation 0 or 1 at a fixed unramified prime, the Dirichlet series is multiplied by 1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) or v_p p^(-s)/(1+v_p p^(-s)). Each is analytic and nonzero at beta. Their finite products preserve the pole and its nonzero Gaussian mode. A signed combination may kill the pole only when its combined multiplier vanishes at beta; an exact recombination back to the original source restores the original pole. A positive valuation at a ramified prime is infeasible and identically zero, not an exception to this assertion.

M therefore defeats a derivation of a better complete Gaussian bound from the listed coarse properties alone, even with these individual finite masks. It does not defeat arithmetic arguments using the actual global Mobius prime law or its global convolution inverse. For fixed prescribed ordinary chi, outside the finite prescribed set the random unit phases differ from -chi(p) at infinitely many primes almost surely. The model is not secretly in the actual mu*chi family. A finite alphabet restriction or reality condition may also exclude this model; no claim about those narrower classes is proved here.

## 4. Independent proof of B, including offsets and exact lags

Let |a(n)|<=1 for positive integers and a(n)=0 otherwise. Fix tau>0, real X>=1 and integer H>=1. Define

    B_H(k) = sum_{j=0}^{H-1} a(k-j),
    w_X(k) = exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4 tau)),
    E_a(X,H) = (1/H) sum_{k>=1} |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

The sum has every positive endpoint and both Gaussian tails; bounded coefficients guarantee absolute convergence. There is no dyadic support truncation. Put ell=log 2 and

    K_tau = exp(ell^2/(3 tau))
              [exp(tau/3+4 ell/3)/sqrt(3 pi tau) + 1/(pi tau)].

Then

    sup_{X<=x<=2X} |F_a(x)|
      <= sqrt(K_tau (X/H+1) E_a(X,H)) + 2H g_tau(0).       (B)

For a residue representative r in {1,...,H}, the intervals (k-H,k], with positive k congruent to r, partition all positive integers after zero extension at the initial block. Replace g_tau(log(n/x)) by its value at the block's right endpoint, giving V_r(x). The total variation of t -> g_tau(log(t/x)) on (0,infinity) is 2g_tau(0), because it increases from zero to its maximum and then decreases to zero. Each interval contains at most H integers, so the sum of absolute replacement errors is at most H times the total variation. This proves |F_a(x)-V_r(x)| <= 2H g_tau(0), including the first partial block and the infinite tails.

Set u=log(x/X) in [0,ell] and v=log(k/X). The Cauchy quotient is

    g_tau(v-u)^2 / w_X(k)
       = (2 pi tau)^(-1)
          exp(-3v^2/(4 tau) + 2uv/tau - u^2/tau).

As a function of t=k/X>0 this is positive and unimodal. Its supremum is exp(u^2/(3 tau))/(2 pi tau). Integrating in t introduces the Jacobian exp(v); completion of the square gives its integral

    exp(tau/3 + 4u/3 + u^2/(3 tau)) / sqrt(3 pi tau).

The independent helper checks both square-completion identities as polynomial identities over exact rational coefficients. A positive unimodal function sampled at spacing H/X has sum bounded by (X/H) times its integral plus twice its maximum: compare adjacent intervals on each monotone side of the peak, leaving at most two peak samples. Uniformly in u in [0,ell], this is at most K_tau(X/H+1). Thus, with E_r the unnormalized energy on one offset grid,

    |V_r(x)| <= sqrt(K_tau(X/H+1) E_r).

Average the approximations over r and use concavity of the square root. Since (1/H)sum_r E_r = E_a(X,H), this proves (B) with the asserted normalization. There is no lost factor H, and no sign assumption on cross terms. A logarithmic shell L2 norm is also bounded by sqrt(log 2) times the same supremum bound.

The exact expansion, retaining its moving weight, is

    E_a(X,H) = (1/H) sum_{|h|<H} sum_{n>=max(1,1-h)}
       a(n) conjugate(a(n+h))
       sum_{j=max(0,h)}^{min(H-1,H-1+h)} w_X(n+j).        (L)

Indeed, in B_H(k)conjugate(B_H(k)), write n=k-j and h=j-l. The restrictions 0<=j,l<=H-1 are equivalent to the displayed j bounds, and positivity of n,n+h gives the n bound. Then k=n+j. This is a bijection of summation indices, and absolute convergence permits rearrangement. It does not replace the inner weight by a fixed triangular coefficient. The helper independently preserves every symbolic monomial a_n conjugate(a_m) w_k in an offset/direct/lag spot check, but this general bijection is the proof.

## 5. Full conditional ordinary-character return

Fix tau>0, 0<theta<1 and e before scale or character selection. Let H=floor(X^theta). The missing arithmetic hypothesis is, for every fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi and every epsilon>0,

    E_{mu*chi}(X,H) <<_{epsilon,chi,tau} X^(e+epsilon)     (A)

for all sufficiently large dyadic X. Here mu*chi denotes the pointwise sequence mu(n)chi(n), not Dirichlet convolution. Its energy must have exactly the full support and weight in Section 4. Constants and the scale threshold may depend on the fixed character. A universal conductor constant is not needed for the resulting qualitative per-character assertion, but the same theta,e must be valid for every character being asserted.

For large X the floor gives H comparable to X^theta. Applying (B) yields, with every epsilon loss,

    F_{mu*chi}(x) << x^(gamma+epsilon),
    gamma = max(theta, (1-theta+e)/2).

Dyadic shells cover every x>=1. The factor 1/2 on the energy accuracy exponent is harmless because (A) holds for every epsilon. The O(H) replacement cost is part of gamma, not discarded. First improvement over b6 requires theta<b6 and

    e < 2b6-1+theta = .749722+theta.

For the literal ordinary-character sequence, absolute Euler products in Re(s)>1 identify its Dirichlet series with 1/L(s,chi). Direct absolute interchange gives

    integral_0^infinity F_{mu*chi}(x) x^(-s) dx/x
       = exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi),      Re(s)>1.

At x->0, bounded coefficients give O_A(x^A) for arbitrarily large A. At infinity, the returned bound with arbitrarily small epsilon makes the integral holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly on compact subsets, including its differentiated integrals. This supplies all imaginary heights. The nonvanishing entire Gaussian factor means the reciprocal L-function cannot have a pole there. Equivalently, after meromorphic continuation, L has no zero in this half-plane away from its principal pole. Nonprincipal s=1 is included; the principal pole at s=1 corresponds to a zero of the reciprocal and is compatible with the identity. The external theorem's explicit principal-(chi=1,s=1) exclusion should therefore remain.

This is an ordinary Dirichlet return for all positive moduli if (A) is supplied separately for all their characters. It is not a Hecke or number-field theorem. The exact external root-LFunction definition and its ordinary-function identification remain an external handoff obligation; they were not proved here. There is no moving Gaussian transform: the growing H occurs only in an estimate of the fixed F. No actual-supremum feedback is needed for this replacement route. Its source estimate directly implies the asserted conditional strip.

The architecture does not import any PR9/PR15 local moment bound in order to prove (A). Accordingly it does not constitute a cheaper version of the old shortening, 29-family/109-child, height, Euler-shift, 9a or physical K^(5/6) ledger. If an eventual proof of (A) uses that route, those costs must be paid in that proof. This review changes none of the accepted old source assumptions, and discharges none of their remaining import-independence or external kernel obligations.

## 6. Quantitative obstruction and exact arithmetic

Apply (B) to the single fixed model from M and set H=floor(X^theta), with theta<beta. The asymptotic at x=X gives |F_a(X)| >= c X^beta for every sufficiently large X, since its leading coefficient is nonzero. The O(H) replacement term is lower order. Because X/H+1 is comparable to X^(1-theta), squaring the remaining inequality yields

    E_a(X,H) >= c' X^(2beta-1+theta)                    (O)

for every sufficiently large X. The constants may depend on the fixed model and tau. This is not merely a subsequence lower bound.

Consequently an upper estimate E_a << X^(1+delta+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 is impossible when theta-delta > 2(1-beta). Choose epsilon strictly below the positive exponent gap. Equality is not excluded by this argument. More generally, if (A) would return a proposed exponent gamma<beta, then gamma>=theta and e<=2gamma-1+theta force e<2beta-1+theta, contradicting (O). The target must have gamma>=theta for the claimed return in the first place.

At theta=13/50, the exact comparisons are:

| Quantity | Exact value | Decimal |
|---|---:|---:|
| First-gain energy boundary | 504861/500000 | 1.009722 |
| Energy needed for gamma=.87449 | 50449/50000 | 1.00898 |
| Model beta | 8747/10000 | .8747 |
| Available weaker calibration | 2187/2500 | .8748 |
| Model's forced energy exponent | 5047/5000 | 1.0094 |
| Strict obstruction gap | 21/50000 | .00042 |

Here .87449 < .8747 < .8748 < b6. Thus the model satisfies the incumbent coarse summatory calibration and every fixed-H Cesaro energy limit, while blocking this growing-window target. For any proposed gamma<b6 in the meaningful range, choose beta between max(gamma,1/2) and b6 and a calibration exponent between beta and b6. This is a scoped obstruction to coarse-data proofs of a gain, not an impossibility for the arithmetic coefficients.

The conditional returns were also recomputed independently:

| theta | Assumed energy e | Returned gamma | Conditional c=1-gamma |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 13/50 | 1 | 87/100 | 13/100 |
| 1/3 | 1 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 1/2 | 1 | 3/4 | 1/4 |
| 3/5 | 11/10 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

Without new arithmetic, |B_H(k)|<=H gives E_a<=H sum_k w_X(k) <<_tau H(X+1). The generic exponent is therefore e=1+theta. Its gap to the first-gain boundary is exactly 2c6 = 125139/500000 = .250278, independently of theta. Qualitative o(XH) has no guaranteed fixed power saving and does not close this gap. This remains true even though the model has stronger fixed-form Cesaro cancellation than the qualitative logarithmic limits invoked as motivation.

## 7. Acceptance, repair status and useful next contract

No substantive mathematical repair is required for the stated M/B package. The finite-phase sentence should be read with the quantifier explanation in Section 3.3; a finite-basis proof is available if an explicitly uniform formulation is wanted. The statement must keep the complex-phase scope, fixed-data order, all-offset/full-tail energy, exact moving lag weight, theta<beta restriction in the obstruction, and strict exponent gap. It must not become a no-go theorem for real sequences, the literal mu*chi family, the equality case, arbitrary conductors uniformly, or Hecke sources.

The useful new source target is (A), or equivalently a quantitative bound for the complete signed moving-weight sum (L) with all |h|<X^theta. It must exploit arithmetic absent from M, such as the actual global Mobius prime law, its exact convolution inverse, or genuinely quantitative growing-lag information. A's HA17 is a valid further formulation at its stated scope.
With divisor-cell sizes D,D', E=N/D,E'=N/D', freeze t first and
rerun the positive JPS17 proof on v=t z. The remaining extracted
label z has size D/q_t; the actual quadratic column z e b has
length NG/(q_t q_f). The cubic coefficients at fixed z,b contain
the retained chi_Q(tz)^4 and are independent of live e and row k.
The fixed-t diagonal estimate is therefore

    Z^epsilon (D/q_t) G(K+NG/q_t) S(E,L) Omega_i,    (R33)

after the same complete f,Delta costs. One need not assert a
new JPS3 prime theorem at N/q_t: this is only a rerun of its
positive sieve proof, with all original product supports retained.

Cauchy between the two sides, then the signed t-transform with
absolute divisor weights, uses harmonic sum 1/q_t in the K term
and tail sum 1/q_t^2 in the NG term. It gives

    Z^epsilon sqrt(D D') G(K+NG/U)
       sqrt(S(N/D,L)S(N/D',L))
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                (R34)

This validates HA17, including the shortened label count.
Its main restricted application is already covered by R5.

Indeed, for every D>=1,

    D S(N/D,L)
       = N+D L+(NL)^(2/3)D^(1/3)
       >= N+L+(NL)^(2/3) = S(N,L).                 (R35)

Hence with the SAME original N on both sides,
sqrt(D D')sqrt(S(N/D,L)S(N/D',L)) >= S(N,L).
Up to the fixed dyadic comparison constants, R34 is dominated
by R5. It is a correct comparison to the proposed JPS30 scale,
not a second quantitative improvement over HA16/BGC1.
At the pressure cells with N/D,N/D'>=L^2 the two long factors
are comparable, explaining the matching scale there.

A's fixed-set formulation and B's union-of-cells argument use
the same bound |b_(i,t)|<=tau(m); no extra row-dependent selection
is permitted by either. A's r_W-support formulation is a convenient
generalization of the hypothesis, but it uses the same analytic

## Fixed multiples of the square-root threshold

Fix tau>0 and kappa>=1. Define the absolutely convergent profile

    J(v)=integral_v^infinity e^u(u-v)g(u)du,
    Phi(q)=sum_(r>=1) f(r)/r J(log(rq)), q>0.

Then, with z=kappa sqrt(X),

    R_z(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)+O_(tau,kappa)(X/L^3).

This theorem uses ordinary fixed-order PNT and absolute core estimates;
it uses no Mertens input, conditional reciprocal moment or bound for F.
For kappa^2>=2e^(3tau), the entire shell has q>=e^(3tau) and

    Phi(q)>=(3/4)J(log q)>0.

Thus the actual complement is positive of order X/L^2. The full band
T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X)), for any fixed rho_plus>1/2, has the
same positive leading profile and error, again without a bound for F.
A negative leading prefix T_z follows only after separately using the
accepted F(x)=O(X^beta). For other fixed kappa>=1 the profile formula
is proved, but this positivity criterion makes no sign assertion.

Here the core remains absolutely controlled because the threshold
forces a rapid Gaussian decay in log r. The central original source
has exactly two distinct rough primes as before. Cores above X^.01
and primes above X^.52 are complete Gaussian tails. Both finite
Stieltjes substitutions include both endpoints. The review proves the
continuous extension by the exact positive full-core expression

    x integral_(log a)^infinity e^u g(u)
       sum_(r<=e^u/a) (u-log(ar))/r du, a=kappa^2 X/x,

whose inner sum is O_kappa((1+u_+)^2). Every omitted set forces
u>=.01log X-O(1). This pays the extension before any cancellation.
After p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w, the global density error is bounded by
8(log v+log w)/L^3 and is absolutely integrable over all cores.
The unordered factor1/2 and leading density4/L^2 give exactly2.
Finally J(v+log r)<=r^-2 J(v) for v>=3tau; r=1 exceeds the total
r>=2 absolute contribution, at most J(v)/4. Neither kappa nor tau
moves with X in the admitted theorem.

### F04.N3 — New pass 1: merge paid sectors only through an exact common partition

There are two legal decompositions:

- Core decomposition: full physical energy = same-core square function + large-gcd off-core covariance + small-gcd off-core covariance.
- Frequency decomposition: full physical energy = complete zero mode + coherent-unembedded pairwise zero-subtracted remainder + all other pairwise zero-subtracted remainders.

These cannot be combined by declaring their overlapping “paid pieces” positive. A01 controls the coherent principal-good-character pair condition \(aA'/(bA)\in\mathcal I^6\), after subtracting each pair's zero contribution. It does not control a nonprincipal character evaluated on a sixth-power frequency. A15 shows that gcd masks need not preserve positive semidefiniteness, even on a two-column Gram.

The concrete new bookkeeping/lemma task is to express both decompositions on one finite pair index set, enumerate intersections, and price the resulting addbacks before removing truncation. A useful extension would transport the coherent divisibility-discrepancy proof to one mixed embedding: derive coherence after substituting the true rows \(e^2r,d^2r\), then prove the CRT/Jacobian/profile statement. Merely reusing the unembedded ratio is wrong. This is an enabling theorem worth a bounded attempt because it could remove an additional portion of CORE; it is not H or a full saving.

statement:
# Controller reconstruction of the literal f3 renewal theorem

11 October 2026. **Accept F4–F51 at their stated scopes**, after reading
the entire [independent report](f3-renewal/report.md), SHA-256
`55e58309d2c0db17eb43baf6ce14a905e96572c23806b73d5c9bcaf8272f7ee3`.
The controller proposed the frozen fixed-polylog candidate; the independent
reviewer supplied a complete proof and the stronger moving-threshold and
second-term statements. This note checks those added statements and their
use in the current proof. No complete-field improvement is asserted.

## Main term and all-order constants

The exact representation n=r p^k, with r z-smooth and p>z, is unique
when exactly one distinct rough prime occurs. Its coefficient is -f_3(r)
for every k>=1. The finite-prime smooth series has a simple zero from
prime 2 at s=1. Direct expansion gives A_2'(1)=2log2 and
A_2''(1)=-6(log2)^2. The prime-3 factor is 3/2. Thus

    H_z'(1)=3log2 P(z),
    H_z''(1)/H_z'(1)=-3log2-log3
           +2 sum_(5<=p<=z) p log p/((p-1)(p-2)).

The reciprocal smooth mass is zero; its logarithmic moment is negative.
The external minus sign in the prime term therefore makes the leading
field positive. The two second-order contributions have exactly the
minus signs in F4: the Gaussian tilted mean contributes 2tau, and the
second signed core moment contributes H_z''(1)/H_z'(1).

On the complex disk |s-1|<=1/t, t=log z>=4, prime 2 is removed before
taking logarithms of the nonvanishing factors. The other denominators
and p>=5 numerators stay away from zero. Their logarithmic derivatives
are O(t), so integration over a radius 1/t changes each complete
product by a bounded factor. Dividing H_z by s-1 and applying Cauchy's
estimate gives C h_z j!t^(j-1) simultaneously for all j. This prices
growing differentiation order; a bound with unspecified O_j constants
would not suffice for the claimed extension.

## Full tails and uniformity

The positive smooth-core product is O(t) at 1-1/t. The elementary
Gaussian lattice bound sum_m g(log(m/y))<=C y holds for every y>0.
Together they pay the complete large-core tail, with no squarefree
restriction and no lost prime-power multiplicity. The retained higher
prime powers have convergent norm at 3/4 and total cost
C t X^(.7525). The fully smooth field and the omitted Gaussian tails
are separately bounded; neither is declared absent.

For r<=X^.01 and |u|<=.01log X, both sharp prime endpoints are in
[X^.98,2X^1.01]. Ordinary fixed-order PNT therefore gives the complete
Stieltjes error, including both endpoint atoms, of size
C (x/r)(log X)^(-10). This needs no relative short-interval theorem.

With K=floor(L/(16t)), the unsigned Taylor remainder is at most
C xt/L *15^(-K). Signed moments are completed before their estimation.
The completion error is C xt/L *exp(-.005L/t); consecutive factorial
terms have ratio below 1/7. Under t<=L/(1000log L), its ratio to the
desired relative t^2/L^2 error is bounded by

    L^3 exp(-.005L/t) <= L^(-2).

The large-core ratio is at most L^(-6); the remaining listed tails
are smaller or directly polynomially negligible. These checks close
the stronger uniform statement rather than just the original fixed-B
case. The rational Gaussian denominator is expanded only where it
is bounded below by .99L; it is never extended across its pole.

## Signed bands and what the Gram proves

The monotone coefficient selectors give literal disjoint threshold
bands. Their local jump condition is p|n and omega_p(n)=1. The
asymptotic doubled-cutoff band requires both t and 2t inside the
proved range and t tending to infinity. Under those conditions it
is -1/2 times the old prefix to relative o(1). Individual prime
jumps are not assigned that sign.

The Gaussian remains uncapped, so its exact terminal reconstruction
is dominated infinite telescoping, not a finite threshold identity.
The shell norm has leading factor 3/2 because
integral_X^(2X) x^2 dx/x=3X^2/2. The finite Gram includes every
off-diagonal entry. Killing its leading vector yields only the
stated logarithmic field error, with no new power saving.

For the actual complement R=F-T, write a=||T||, b=||R|| and d=||F||.
The exact identity

    d^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+rho)

retains both norm mismatch and the cosine defect. Normalization by
the actual a^2 gives the power-small Gram error from the previously
accepted full-field bound. Normalization by a leading asymptotic
does not preserve that rate. F50 correctly requires improvement of
both terms and is equivalent to the requested full-field bound,
with epsilon renamed. No masked convolution transfer is used.

The result directly fills the missing literal f3 rough-depth estimate.
Its leading field has exponent one even at the largest proved cutoff.
The remaining signed cancellation, and therefore every larger c,
remains open. The source-relative accepted endpoint and its separate
formal-kernel evidence are unchanged by this theorem.

### A4. The self-improving local-set theorem

**Theorem W39-A (ordinary).** Fix tau>0, an ordinary Dirichlet character chi, 0<gamma<1, and 0<=kappa<1/2. Suppose for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer j there exists a measurable E_j subset [j,j+1] with

    |E_j| >= c_epsilon j^(-kappa),
    ess sup_(u in E_j) |sum_n mu(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u)|
        <= C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j).              (W39.13)

Then L(s,chi) has no zeros in Re s>gamma. Moreover the COMPLETE fixed Gaussian obeys |F(u)|<<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)u) at every large real u. The E_j may depend on chi, epsilon and j; their existence and bounds are arithmetic hypotheses, not selected from an observed favorable subsequence.

Proof. Put r=2kappa<1 and h_m=gamma+r^m(1-gamma). Initial W39.2 supplies b=1. A2 and A3 prove zero exclusion and the all-scale Gaussian bound at limiting exponent h_1. Inductively zero exclusion above h_m replenishes W39.4 for every b>h_m; apply A2 with suitably small fixed epsilon margins to get h_(m+1). For any requested sigma>gamma, choose a finite m with h_m<sigma and margins smaller than sigma-h_m. The Mellin return excludes every zero with Re rho>gamma. The same finite argument, or W39.12 on b in (gamma,gamma+epsilon), gives the final all-scale bound. No limit of constants or moving number of iterations is taken inside an estimate.

Any fixed positive interval length can replace1, by rescaling W39.3 and changing only fixed constants in W39.7. The coefficient2 in the SINGLE-STEP loss is proved, not asserted optimal. This method gives no improvement from kappa>=1/2. It neither proves a counterexample there nor excludes a stronger arithmetic observability theorem.

If a prior fixed buffered exponent B is already available, replace1 by B in h_m. With kappa=1/4, B approaching .874872 and gamma=.87449, the first limiting exponent is .874681; the limit is .87449. Starting only from1 gives h_m=.87449+2^(-m)*.12551, crossing .874872 at m=9. These are CONDITIONAL returns from W39.13, not newly proved constants. The same hypothesis at gamma=5/6 or3/4 supplies the corresponding all-height targets.

statement:
## 3. Complete coprime RR, long shifts, and the four distinct primes

Below z^3, an integer with at least two distinct primes exceeding z
has exactly two, both at valuation one. Thus it has the unique form
n=rpq, z<p<q, r<z, and f(n)=f(r). A third rough prime or a repeated
rough prime together with the other one would force n>z^3. Above
z^3 the difference between the literal and completed fields is
bounded with d_3(n) and R3 by O_A(X^-A). Hence

    R=V+S_core+O_A(X^-A),    |S_core|<=U.                    (R7)

Also, at every n, the absolute literal rough coefficient is bounded
by the number of representations n=rpq with p<q>z. Therefore its
positive field is bounded exactly by V+U, with no tail exception.

The original integer window is

    W_X=log 2+sqrt(24 tau L),
    I_X=[X exp(-W_X),X exp(W_X)].

If x is in the shell and n is outside this window, then
|log(n/x)|>=sqrt(24 tau L). R2--R3 show that the entire positive
original-pair mass with either integer outside I_X is O(X^-4).
This calculation uses bounded original coefficients: one factor has
mass O(X exp(-6L)), the other O(X), and the shell has bounded
logarithmic measure. The divisor-weighted completed-source tails
have already been paid separately. Eventually max I_X<z^3, and all
cores in the central source satisfy r<=exp(W_X)/kappa^2<z.

To prove the coprime lower bound one must subtract the whole signed
noncoprime contribution, not discard an unfavorable part of it. On
the central window split noncoprime rough pairs as follows.

If a rough prime p>z divides both integers, the total absolute mass
is at most

    sum_(p>z) integral_X^(2X)
                   [sum_(a>=1)g(log(pa/x))]^2 dx/x
       <= C X^2 sum_(p>z)p^-2 << X^(3/2).                    (R8)

This upper bound includes coincident primes, repeated valuations and
diagonal pairs; any overcount is positive and hence harmless.

If there is no common rough prime, any common divisor greater than
one is in the two cores. Both cores then exceed one. Their entire
absolute pair contribution is at most ||U||^2. Enlarging to all
completed positive cores is allowed for this upper bound. Together
with the original window tail,

    |sum_((m,n)>1)f(m)A_R(m)f(n)A_R(n)K_X(m,n)|
       <= ||U||^2 + C X^(3/2)+O(X^-4).                      (R9)

By R6--R7 the lower pointwise bound V-U-O_A(X^-A) is eventually
positive, so its square may be used in the lower bound for ||R||^2.
Subtracting R9 then cancels the U^2 term and gives

               >= (1/3)||V||^2-C X^(3/2),
    |C_1(R,R)| <= ||V+U||^2 <= (16/9)||V||^2,
    ||V||^2 asymp_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4.                       (R10)

the favorable r=1 family was only an ingredient of a bound that also
paid for every other core. The positive-subset fallacy does not occur.

For every integer h>=1 and every Y>0, R2 gives

    sum_(a>=1)K_Y(a,a+h) <= C_tau Y.                        (R11)

Use sup g on one factor and R2 on the other, then integrate over the
shell. This estimate is valid also for Y<1. Both integer orders in

there is no coprime diagonal. If C_1^H also restricts m,n to I_X,
m!=n, and |m-n|>H, then

    C_1^H(R,R)=C_1(R,R)+O(XH+X^-4).                         (R12)

At H=X/L^6 the removed mass is o(X^2/L^4), proving A4. Every
retained integer has two rough primes of valuation one, and
gcd(m,n)=1 forces all four rough primes in the pair to be distinct.

## G195. Every fixed low-chain sector under one common filter

Fix p not dividing q and integer J>=2, independent of x. Define

    Q=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p, v_J=Q^(*J),
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b=Q*chi=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)),
    f_t(n)=mu²(n)t^omega(n)chi(n), f_0=delta1.

b has period pq and mean zero, including principal/imprimitive characters.
Choose D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|); D=p²q suffices.

For any fixed bounded mean-zero periodic b, the full ordered hyperbola
identity proves

    |sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t),
    C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)².

Indeed each t-tuple of product<=x has a coordinate<=Y=x^(1/t).
In inclusion-exclusion with j<t short coordinates and m=t-j, induction
costs C_m x^(1-1/m)[sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^(-1+1/m)]^j,
at most C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t). For j=t the product cutoff is automatic:
the term is the bounded quantity(sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t. All overlaps and real
floors are retained. The recurrence and m!m^(t-m)<=t! prove the stated
constant bound.

The exact Euler correction is

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.

The local linear term vanishes. The absolute coefficient series
Gabs_t(sigma)=sum|g_t(n)|n^-sigma converges for every fixed t and sigma>1/2.
Consequently, for1<=t<=J,

    v_J*f_t=b^(*t)*v_(J-t)*g_t,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_t)(n)|
      <=C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma,
          sigma>1/2, sigma>=1-1/t.

Each finite p^a coefficient is evaluated at x/p^a; arguments below1
contribute zero. All colors on the left use the SAME filter v_J.

The independent review sharpens the two low endpoints without assuming
Euler convergence at1/2. For t=1, g_1 is supported on r² with coefficient
mu(r)chi(r)². For t=2, the local polynomial1-3z²+2z³ has absolute
coefficients dominated by(1-z²)^-3(1-z³)^-2. Thus

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_1)(n)|<=D(1+sqrt p)^(J-1)sqrt x,
    sum_(n<=x)|g_2(n)|/sqrt n
      <=zeta(3/2)²(1+0.5log x)³,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_2)(n)|
      <=3D²zeta(3/2)²(1+sqrt p)^(J-2)sqrt x(1+0.5log x)³.

The second inequality follows by writing the majorant as
sum_(a²c³=n)d_3(a)d_2(c): the c-series converges, and the a-series is
bounded by the cube of a harmonic sum. The periodic two-variable
hyperbola bound is3D²sqrt x. All p shifts remain in these bounds.

Set a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu²(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k). Finite differences
give the complete first-J chain combination

    L_J=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.

Combining ALL colors and their common filter proves, for every real x>=1,

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*L_J)(n)| <<_(p,q,J) x^(1-1/J), J>=3;
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_2*L_2)(n)| <<_(p,q) sqrt x log³(2x).

The exponent for J>=3 has no epsilon loss. This is a complete arithmetic
estimate of the low source, including principal characters.

Growing depth is not free. Splitting primes at t^(1/sigma) proves
logGabs_t(sigma)<<_sigma t^(1/sigma)log(2t) for fixed1/2<sigma<1.
The factorial hyperbola constant, finite p-shift factors and binomial
combination must all be paid, and sigma>=1-1/t still applies. These upper
prices establish no impossibility theorem for a better growing-depth proof.

## 3. Sharp-shell energy: signs, boundaries and the complete complement

For this subsection |a_n|<=1 may be arbitrary. Put N=X^b. Absolute
convergence of the damped square gives

    E(X)=sum_(n,m>=1) a_n conjugate(a_m) K_X(n,m),
    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                     exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k))du/u.

In particular K_X(m,n)=conjugate(K_X(n,m)); one must retain both orders
when estimating a real cross energy. Let A=(n+m)/N and v=u^(-k). The
kernel becomes the Fourier integral on [2^(-k),1] with positive amplitude

    B_A(v)=exp(-A v^(b/k))/(k v).

Its derivative is negative. Endpoint sum plus total variation is
2B_A(2^(-k))<=2^(k+1)/k. One integration by parts therefore proves

    |K_X(n,m)|<=C_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|), n!=m.       (R4)

The changing damping has been differentiated, not frozen. For n>m,

    n^k-m^k=(n-m)sum_(j=0)^(k-1)n^(k-1-j)m^j
             >=n^(k-1)(n-m).

For a real shell-fixed M>=2, the pairs outside n,m<=M are exactly those
with max(n,m)>M. Summing both orientations gives

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+D_>M(X)+O_(b,k)(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)),   (R5)
    D_>M=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n)>=0.

Indeed sum_(n>M)n^(1-k)sum_(h<n)1/h<<M^(2-k)log(2M).
There is no missing low/high strip, equality-boundary atom or distant
physical tail. For real M, n<=M and n>M partition integers exactly.
The summable majorant, since k>2, justifies passage from finite squares.
Also D_>M<<_b X^b by geometric summation before the u-integral.

Thus E_<=M<=E+O(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)), as well as the forward upper bound
in the author report. This use of D_>M>=0 is legitimate only after (R5).
The same off-diagonal argument restricted to n,m>M gives an actual tail
norm estimate. It is this tail estimate, not a pointwise truncation, that
pays the weaker L1 complement below.

For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^r, the error exponent is 6-4r and diagonal exponent
3/2. At r=19/16, 6-4r=5/4; M itself has exponent19/16<5/4. The author's
selected error budget is correct. The cutoff need not be optimized for
this statement to be valid.

## 3. Poisson, the genuine tail, and both true roots

Expand sixth-freeness by mu(a0) with a0^6|u and retain(a0,Hcol*x*y)=1. This restriction is legitimate before expansion because the omitted original terms are zero. Expand the E-hole completely with sum_(d|E,d|u/a0^6)mu(d), and put u=a0^6 d z. Write qa=N(a0), qd=N(d). As d is prime to kxy, its character value is a unit on the actual source. No natural zero is divided out.

Primitive Poisson at scale U/(qa^6 qd), using PR9 B3.5, has zero dual term for the nonprincipal primitive character in(2), and zero at every good conductor-sharing frequency. General CRT gives

    gamma(psi_k;k) gamma_e(x) gamma_-e(y)
       psi_k(xy) chi_x(ky)^e chi_y(kx)^(-e).                 (4)

The x-y factor is the fixed sextic reciprocity ray sign. The remaining interactions with k factor into an x function and a y function. The mixed normalized Gauss factor has modulus one and is not replaced by a fixed-order Gauss coefficient at k. The d twist separates in the same way. All frequency-dependent psi_k factors stay in the outer weight or its natural-zero restriction.

The residual inverse signs equal mu(x) and mu(y), times the fixed slot-count signs and original extracted collision coefficients. PR9 B1.10 gives the two accepted G185 orientations after defining a0(x)=conjugate(alpha(x))gamma_2(x). For e=-1 the residual Gauss factors are a0(x)conjugate(a0(y)) with chi_x(-1)conjugate(G(x))G(y); for e=1 they are conjugate(a0(x))a0(y) with G(x)conjugate(G(y))chi_y(-1). Fixed ray signs, nu corrections and all collision and slot coefficients remain. B1.11 later supplies the same within-column cubic cocycle in each orientation, conjugated as appropriate.

The genuine conductor norm is comparable to Q=Kc N0^2/(LR). Fix tau=1/1000, an ORIGINAL a0 dyad qa~A and a sufficiently large fixed support constant C_*. The retained cutoff is exactly

    Hc=C_* U^tau A^6 qd Kc N0^2/(U L R).                    (5)

It depends on original collision/hole labels and the original A, not on artificial f. Outside(5), the actual Schwartz argument exceeds c U^tau. The genuine one-pair prefactor is U/(qa^6 qd N0 sqrt(Q)). PR9 B3.4 gives a tail factor bounded by(1+qa^6 qd Q/U)U^(-tau(B-1)). Before extension there are O(N0^2 U^epsilon) original tuple pairs, O(U^(1/6)) possible a0, and divisor-many d. Since Q<<N0^2, the total raw price is at most

    H_J U^(1/6+epsilon)(U N0+N0^2)
                          U^(-tau(B-1))
       << H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1)).                  (6)

Choose finite B after this count. This includes the lattice-counting1, rather than assuming every dual scale is large. On a fixed fractional lattice, keep all points with N(ell)<=Hc; the empty-set threshold is its fixed least positive norm. Using N(Delta)Hc in a cleared-lattice energy only changes fixed comparison constants. No term is discarded merely because Hc<1.

Only after this tail is paid, extend the separated product formula to individually squarefree x,y prime to Hcol and insert the COMPLETE sum_(f|x,f|y)mu(f). It annihilates every artificially added noncoprime pair. Old collision predicates are held at their original labels; recomputing them on x,y would destroy this cancellation. The frequency cutoff and both core selectors are independent of f.

Allocate each f prime independently to its actual residual inverse color or surviving named slot on EACH copy. Slot coefficients and masks remain, with divisor-bounded multiplicity. With F=N(f), the residual product lengths are genuinely unequal:

    XL=N0/(L F), XR=N0/(R F).

The pair prefactor before normalized columns is U sqrt(LR)/(qa^6 qd N0^2 sqrt(Kc)). Restoring both unnormalized roots gives exactly

    U sqrt(LR)/(qa^6 qd N0^2 sqrt(Kc)) sqrt(XL XR)
                  =U/(qa^6 qd N0 sqrt(Kc) F).               (7)

In particular a true shared type(1,1) collision is NOT another artificial f. There is no extra reciprocal L or R in(7).

For fixed allocations a merged residual coefficient is a sum over original factorizations, of divisor-bounded multiplicity and bounded individual magnitude. The total number of permitted color/slot tuples is O(Xi U^epsilon) at its independently shortened scales. Hence its normalized squared mass is O(H_J U^epsilon). This proof uses the actual product slot family, not an arbitrary joint coefficient matrix. Truly empty scales stay empty; nonempty nominal scales below one are clipped only by bounded original annular ratios.

Fix all nominal norm boxes first, including a0,d,ell and collision norms. The kernel on the full ambient normalized box is the original Schwartz function of U N(ell)LR/(qa^6 qd Kc N(n)N(n')). Euler derivatives are bounded uniformly in its nominal positive scale. PR9 B3.3 therefore chooses one weighted Fourier measure before live labels. Real inverse roots occur once; new imaginary norm powers distribute multiplicatively through the original colors. Sharp masks remain outside the smooth separation. There is no f-dependent density or selector, and both original height seminorms remain.

Factorization can formally reintroduce x=y=1 when k=1. Subtract that rank-one block explicitly. For each diagonal coefficient its full absolute Poisson sum, including zero frequency, costs

    sum_(qa<<U^(1/6), d|E) [U/(qa^6 qd)+1]<<U^(1+epsilon).

The c_abs squared-mass bound then pays the entire correction, even with a frequency selection. Thus the factorized energy need not pretend its unit-core row is nonprincipal.

Finitely many exceptional pairs contribute a fixed bound.

A pair crossing x has distinct lower endpoint in [x-C_chi x^theta,x]; there are at most C_chi x^theta+1 such lower integers. Both-below pairs cancel exactly, not just in real part. Therefore

For all characters modulo a fixed q, opposite mu signs and equal reduced residue suffice. The example6 and11 modulo5 has coefficients1 and-1 for EVERY character mod5. ## 4. D33: periodic law, uniform smoothing, wrong detector and full complement

For finite P containing2, excluding3, define Q=product P and e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(-1)^(1_(p|n)). These are f3's exact local all-valuation signs on P. Their extension to all n by periodicity is a model obtained by omitting other primes; it is not f3 itself. CRT on the COMPLETE period gives zero mean from2, and

    Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)e_P(n+h)
       =product_(p in P)[1 if p|h, else 1-4/p].

The two negative residues for p not dividing h are n=0,-h. At2, odd h gives-1 and even h gives1; h=0 and n=0 in the completed period are included. No claimed independence of weighted arithmetic f3 pairs follows. Independent exact checks cover all236 shifts across four periods, including P={2}, {2,5}, {2,7,11} and {2,5,7}.

Let h_tau(t)=g_tau(log t), zero for t<=0. It is Schwartz/flat at0. The mean-zero DFT has Q-1 frequencies, coefficients of modulus<=1. Direct Poisson and m fixed integrations by parts give

    |W_P(x)| <= C_(tau,m)x^(1-m)Q^m, m>=2.

The apparent sum over Q frequencies does not add a further Q: r=Qj-k bijects onto the nonzero integers not divisible by Q; its m-series is bounded by2zeta(m). This is a real uniform bound, not an inherited G9 estimate with a forbidden ell mask. With z_X=a log X/loglog X,0<a<1, Q<=floor(z_X)!<=z_X^z_X<=X^(a+o(1)). On the whole closed shell, choose ONE fixed m>(1+A0)/(1-a), with a strict margin, to obtain O(X^-A0). The derivative constant depends on that fixed m/tau, not X/P. No PNT or random-sign hypothesis enters.

For Re s>1, the local coefficient series yields EXACTLY

    Mellin(W_P)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)zeta(s)product_(p in P)(1-2p^-s).

Prime2 cancels the pole at1. The entire transform has zeta zeros in its numerator. The Gaussian Mellin integral at fixed P is entire by rapid right decay and Gaussian left decay. This supplies no inverse-zeta zero exclusion; a zero of the transform is allowed.

The missing arithmetic source is retained pointwise:

    f(n)=e_P(n)r_P(n),
    F(x)=W_P(x)+E_P(x),
    E_P(x)=sum e_P(n)(r_P(n)-1)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    r_P(n)=product_(p|n,p not in P,p!=3)(-1).

All powers/signs and every full energy interaction reside in this identity. The only unconditional magnitude price for E_P is O_tau(x). For the moving sieve and any fixed gamma>0, the every-epsilon shell norm of E_(P_X) at exponent gamma is equivalent by two norm triangles to that of the fixed full F; W_(P_X) is arbitrarily power-small. For gamma>=1/2, with the true O(X) diagonal restored, this is the current complete OPEN-F3 moment/correlation contract. D33 neither pays that correction nor bounds F below.

The marginal obstruction is also correct at its declared relaxed scope: keep every observed small-prime divisibility pattern, but permit an unconstrained hidden rough sign. Choosing r(n)=e_P(n) makes the full coefficient identically1. The positive Gaussian Gram then attains its magnitude-only maximum, and S_tau(x)=e^(tau/2)x+O_tau(1) gives norm exponent1. These free hidden signs are not the actual arithmetic r_P and need not satisfy deletion/convolution relations. The result refutes marginal-only certification, not f3 cancellation or all conditional-expectation methods.

**Verdict:** ACCEPT D33.1--D33.5, rapid model theorem, scoped marginal extremum and full-complement equivalence. No OPEN-F3 payment or c gain. Functional signature: exact local signs; CRT/Poisson; prime-two zero mean; first unpaid complete rough correction; rapid periodic return with numerator zeros and the complete F equivalence.

[private research revision] gaussian-signed S24--S29 already proves actual all-valuation periodic divisibility laws, prime-two cancellation and fixed-order Gaussian Poisson, with S30 pricing its limited low-radical range. D33 is a different finite-prime SINGLE-field model and explicitly growing period plus a direct rough-complement diagnosis; it is not a newly discovered periodic/prime-two mechanism. ## 4. Independent strengthening: no upper restriction on D

For the same fixed phase and fixed mean-zero b, (R3) holds for EVERY finite real D>=1, with constants depending only on Q and ||b||inf. No alpha0 is required. This is not a different detector or a general-phase claim.

For the low output source, choose a fixed delta_Q>0 small enough. Rows m<=delta_Q X have the discrete derivative gap, including the last increment, by the same calculation as above with ml<=3X. Each costs O_Q(1). Rows m>delta_Q X can contribute only if m<=2X, and contain at most2/delta_Q positive l. Their trivial row cost is O_Q(1). Summing all low rows costs O(A min(D,X)), hence O(AD), uniformly for all X>=2.

On a high output block, m>4N gives an EXACTLY empty row, because l>=1 and w(ml/N)=0. Delete those empty rows before Poisson. The remaining dyadic block is now

    [M,2M) intersect[1,D] intersect[1,4N].                   (R16)

It is still a single frozen dyadic subinterval, so (R9)-(R11) are unchanged. Its m/N is at most4, which is all the nonstationary tail bound in Section3.3 needs. All near aliases and all transformed errors remain paid. Also M<=4N, so log(2+J)<<_Q log(2N) without any D-dependent constant. Hence (R15) holds on every nonempty block.

For each N, sum these blocks in norm. The sqrt N contribution gains at most log(2N); the M contribution sums to O(min(D,N)), with a fixed factor4 harmless. Therefore the full high source is bounded by a constant times

    A sum_(N=2^jX) e^(-cN/X^(3/2))
             [sqrt N log^2(2N)+min(D,N)log(2N)].             (R17)

The first sum is O(X^(3/4)log^2(2X)). The second is at most D times a damped logarithmic sum, O(D log^2(2X)), uniformly in every D. This proves the stronger version, with log^4 still more than sufficient. Arbitrarily large D introduces no log D: every active row block is bounded by its actual output support. Each X has a finite D; no infinite undamped coefficient bank is asserted.

This strengthening improves the theorem's analytic robustness and fixed-range uniformity. The actual rectangle uses D=X^gamma< X anyway, so it does not change the retained arithmetic exponent, the cofactor cap, the short-face constraints or c11.

statement:
## 3. Completion and the absence of a Type I main term

Write u=mu_(<=Y), v=mu_(>Y). Expanding v*v*1 and using
mu*1=e_1 gives v*v*1=mu-2u+u*u*1 exactly at every integer.
Convolving with kappa yields

\[
 A=2\kappa*u-u*u*b+v*v*b,\qquad
 b(\ell)=1-2\,1_{2\mid\ell}=(-1)^{\ell+1}.
 \tag{DPR7}
\]

Every convolution is a finite divisor identity. It contains
ordered d,e, all repeated/shared primes, their original
Mobius zeros, and every restoration label ell. In particular
no coprimality between d and e has been introduced.

For 0<delta<=delta0, the compact support of V_delta lies
uniformly away from zero. Its zero extension is smooth.
The chain rule gives
||V_delta^(j)||_1 <= C_j delta^(-j):
the maximal derivative size is O(delta^(-j-1)), and the
support length is O(delta). The j=0 bound is O(1).
Integrating by parts j times therefore proves DP23 with
constants independent of delta.

With the source Fourier convention, alternating Poisson is

\[
 \sum_{\ell\ge1}(-1)^{\ell+1}V_\delta(\ell t)
 =-\frac1t\sum_{\nu\in\mathbb Z,\ \nu\ {\rm odd}}
                  \widehat V_\delta\left(\frac{\nu}{2t}\right).
 \tag{DPR8}
\]

It follows by first extending the physical sum to every
integer, where the added terms are zero, and modulating
the integer lattice by exp(pi i ell). Its dual lattice
is the half-integer lattice. The leading minus sign
comes from (-1)^(ell+1), not from the Fourier convention.
There is no zero frequency. The dual series converges
absolutely for each positive t.

For 0<t<=delta, DP23 with B>=2 bounds the right side by

\[
 C_Bt^{-1}(t/\delta)^B
       \sum_{\nu\ {\rm odd}}|\nu|^{-B}
 \ll_B t^{-1}(t/\delta)^B.
 \tag{DPR9}
\]

The term 2kappa*u has support <=2Y=o(X), outside every
narrow profile on the entire enlarged shell for large X.
For d,e<=Y, t=de/x and delta=delta_X satisfy
t/delta<=e X^(-kappa0). Also t^(-1)=x/(de)<=2eX/(de).
Summing the absolute bound in DPR9 hence costs only

\[
 C_B X(CX^{-\kappa_0})^B
       \left(\sum_{d\le Y}\frac1d\right)^2.
 \tag{DPR10}
\]

There is no missing factor Y^2: the inverse t factor
leaves the two harmonic denominators. Selecting
B>(R+2)/kappa0, for example, makes the error O_R(X^(-R)).
This proves DP25--26 uniformly in the enlarged shell at
its frozen width. All derivative orders and constants
are fixed before the arithmetic labels vary.

The surviving support ell*d*e<=e^delta x, d,e>Y, implies
d,e<=C X/(Y+1) and ell<=C X/(Y+1)^2. Since Y tends to
infinity, its floor changes only fixed constants, proving
DP27. Long individual factors and a polynomial restoration
range remain; their cancellation is not supplied by the
vanishing Type I term.

## 1. Bind the actual family before applying the theorem

Write q_a=N(a), K=Q(omega), O=Z[omega]. Work on ideal columns avoiding the fixed S, containing primes above6 and the fixed conductors. The primary generator is congruent to1 modulo3. PR9 uses psi_u(b)=chi_b(u), including zero at every shared prime; phi_u=nu psi_u^e, e=+1 or-1. The fixed nu may have order not dividing6.

The imported bound for sixth-power-free ideal rows and columns is

    T(A,B)=A+B+A^(5/6)B^(1/3)+A^(1/3)B^(5/6),
    sum_a^(6) |sum_b^(6) lambda_b chi_a(b)|^2
      <<_(fixed data,epsilon) (AB)^epsilon T(A,B) sum_b|lambda_b|^2. (1)

Here chi_a is the family constructed with fixed n,K,S,ray modulus and representatives in the cited Sections2.3–2.5. In this class-number-one field choose the representative generators m_E to be their global primary generators. If a=(x)E g^6 with x=1 modulo the fixed ray modulus, choose a primary generator g_0 of the fractional ideal g. Then x m_E g_0^6 and the primary a_0 generate the same ideal and are both1 modulo3; their quotient is a unit congruent to1 modulo3, hence1. Therefore the defining residue symbol is exactly (a_0/b)_6 on coprime labels. Its prescribed zero extension agrees at every shared prime. This gives the PR9 orientation directly, without suppressing a reciprocity factor.

For a different permissible generator convention, splitting the finitely many S-unit classes modulo sixth powers gives fixed column twists; no growing conductor is hidden in them. Rows containing fixed S-primes are split into their valuation residues0,...,5 and sixth powers. Units give six fixed column phases. The fixed nu multiplies lambda_b. The opposite orientation is obtained by conjugating the entire inner sum and its coefficients, not by silently dropping nu. The reverse residue-symbol orientation, when needed, is handled by PR9's fixed modulo36 reciprocity sectors. These operations retain the natural zeros and cost only fixed constants or small powers.

The matrix theorem allows arbitrary fixed column coefficients. It does not allow an arbitrary array lambda_(a,b). Fixed row restrictions may be dropped only from the positive outer norm. Smooth rowwise heights are addressed separately below. Source family binding does not prove the external theorem or complete its definition/import/admission obligations.

## 1. An optimal finite-rank core still contains the full arithmetic problem

Use the literal source f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))), including all prime powers:
f(p^k)=-1 for p!=3 and f(3^k)=1. For sigma>1/2, the multiplicative Hankel
T(m,n)=f(mn)(mn)^(-sigma) is Hilbert--Schmidt with norm squared zeta(2sigma)^2.
At p!=3 its nonzero local block is

    H_p = [[1,-sqrt(R_p)],[-sqrt(R_p),-R_p]],
    R_p=p^(-2sigma)/(1-p^(-2sigma)).

Write lambda_p^+ for its positive eigenvalue and c_p=1/(lambda_p^++R_p).
Then 0<c_p<1 and 1-c_p=c_p(1+c_p)R_p. The p=3 block is rank one.
Retain p=2,3 exactly and the positive local eigenvector at every p>=5.
The resulting B_sigma is the optimal rank-two truncation in both operator
and Hilbert--Schmidt norm. The proof orders the local singular ratios
r_2>r_5>r_7>... and passes from finite prime-semigroup compressions using
Hilbert--Schmidt convergence. It does not assume a complete infinite tensor
eigenbasis or identify this source with W29's different local blocks.

Its first column is C_sigma b_sigma(n)n^(-sigma), C_sigma>0, where
b_sigma(2^k)=-1, b_sigma(3^k)=1 and b_sigma(p^k)=-c_p for p>=5.
For every fixed rho>1/2 there are exact inverse Dirichlet kernels a,d with

    b_sigma=a*f,  f=d*b_sigma,
    sum_n (|a(n)|+|d(n)|) n^(-rho) < infinity.           ([restricted research revision]-S1)

At p=2,3 both kernels are the identity. At p>=5 their local series are

    A_p(z)=(1-(1+c_p)z)/(1-2z),
    D_p(z)=(1-2z)/(1-(1+c_p)z).

The nonconstant absolute mass is O_(sigma,rho)(p^(-2sigma-rho)); small
prime factors are retained exactly. Consequently the complete Gaussian
fields of b_sigma and f have equivalent all-shell, every-epsilon power
norms for every gamma>1/2. Minkowski pays every shifted shell and both
small-scale tails. This is a transfer for complete fields, not a hereditary
estimate for signed submasks.

For each fixed ordinary character chi, including its ramified zeros,
multiplication of both kernels by chi gives the same equivalence. The
complex twisted operator uses left and right unitary multiplication;
it need not be self-adjoint. If 2 divides the modulus, the optimal retained
core has rank one. The literal Euler numerator W_chi is nonzero in
1/2<Re(s)<1, so the complete Gaussian bound has its own ordinary-character
zero-exclusion return. No ideal, angular or growing-conductor assertion is
inferred from this twist.

The physical readout has norm O(x^(sigma+1/2)). A column approximation
error epsilon_X therefore costs X^(sigma+1/2)epsilon_X. At sigma=3/4,
the current boundary requires epsilon_X=O(X^(-.375136)) before any strict
improvement. A fixed nonzero spectral residual does not decay with X.
The strongest consequence is that treating the optimal leading modes as
an easy main term is unjustified: their actual arithmetic field already
contains the full target exponent through ([restricted research revision]-S1). Signed cancellation
among retained and complementary modes remains a possible research input.

statement:
## 2. A continuation cone and its precise limitation

Write b0=1-c0. The accepted uniform reciprocal-L bounds give analytic
continuation of (R1), through a normally convergent AUXILIARY expansion,
to every compact buffered subregion of

\[
\boxed{\Re v<0,\qquad
\Re(s+v-\tfrac12)>b_0,\qquad
\Re(z+v-\tfrac12)>b_0.} \tag{R2}
\]

To prove this, expand L(1-v,bar eta) absolutely. Expand E using
disjoint squarefree d1,d2 with term
mu(d2) eta(d1 d2^2) q_d1^(-u) q_d2^(-(u+v)). Insert the COMPLETE
projector sum_(ell|(a,b)) mu(ell) and the finite unit-neutral projector.
After a=ell a', b=ell b', two masked Mobius Dirichlet series separate.
They retain all character zeros and deletions at ell d1 d2 S.
Subtract the a=b=1 term when replacing the restricted outer sum by
the product of these two series; it has already been separated above.
Each is a reciprocal finite-order Hecke L-function with deleted
Euler factors. The accepted buffered bounds cost only
(q_k q_d1 q_d2 q_ell)^delta, after rescaling delta to absorb the
fixed powers in the conductor.

Choose delta smaller than the compact region's margins. The k sum
converges since Re(1-v)>1; the remaining d1,d2,ell sums converge since

\[
\Re u>1,\qquad \Re(u+v)>1,\qquad
\Re(s+z+2v-1)>1.
\]

These inequalities follow from (R2) and 2b0>1. Initially the two
reciprocal series converge absolutely to the right of one. Ordinary
polynomial conductor bounds for L(v,eta), with s,z sufficiently far
right, give a bridge across v=0 from the original chamber. This
identifies the continued expression with Z. The explicitly separated
principal term is retained. Neither convergence of the original h sum
nor normal convergence of the raw double Mobius series in (R1) is
claimed throughout the new cone.

In the symmetric case Re s=Re z=sigma, (R2) requires
sigma>b0+1/2-Re v>1.374886647... . Its convex hull with the original
absolute chamber still has sigma>1. It does not reach the desired
central point sigma=1/2+epsilon, Re v<35/32. Nor is the reflected
sixth-order family identified with this same MDS.

There is a useful exact criterion for a future continuation argument.
At fixed w=1/2+epsilon+it the coefficients of Z(v;w,bar w), grouped by
the integer norm q_h, are nonnegative. The previously proved coarse
row bounds give a finite convergence abscissa. If its actual continuation
were holomorphic near EVERY real v>1+eta, Landau's positivity argument
would force that abscissa to be at most 1+eta. Indeed, Taylor expansion
leftwards from a real point just to the right of a hypothetical larger
abscissa has coefficients
sum_n a_n (log n)^j n^(-v0)/j! >=0. Tonelli then turns convergence of
the Taylor series across the abscissa into convergence of the original
positive Dirichlet series there, a contradiction.

If, in addition, Z(1+eta+delta;w,bar w) has polynomial height cost,
positivity gives (65) immediately. This implication needs no vertical-v
estimate. Both its central-continuation premise and its height bound
remain OPEN; (R2) proves neither.
