statement:
## 2. W40-20: a complete signed-boundary zero bridge

### 2.1 Exact disk theorem and strongest cheap counterexample

Let h be holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk and h(0)=1. Define normalized circle measure dm=dtheta/(2pi),

    u(theta)=Re h(exp(i theta)),
    B(h)=integral max(-u(theta),0) dm.

Write u=u_+-u_-. The mean-value identity gives integral u_+=1+B and integral u_-=B. For |z|=rho<1 the Poisson kernel obeys

    (1-rho)/(1+rho) <= P_z(theta) <= (1+rho)/(1-rho).

Consequently, with k_rho=(1-rho)/(1+rho),

    Re h(z) >= k_rho(1+B)-B/k_rho.                 (W40.1)

This is the full complementary return: the negative part is paid against the largest Poisson weight and the positive part against the smallest. It follows that

    B(h) <= b(r):=(1-r)^2/(4r)
       ==> Re h(z)>0 for every |z|<r.              (W40.2)

At |z|=r a strict hypothesis gives strict positivity; equality only gives nonnegativity there. The open-disk conclusion with non-strict B<=b(r) is valid because b(rho) is strictly decreasing for 0<rho<1. In particular h has no zero in |z|<r. No positivity of the original arithmetic coefficients was used.

For completeness the signed representation is also exact:

    h(z)=integral (exp(i theta)+z)/(exp(i theta)-z)
                       *u(theta) dm.              (W40.3)

Expand the kernel into1+2 sum_(n>=1)z^n exp(-in theta). The Fourier coefficients of Re h give half the positive Taylor coefficients; the constant is h(0)=1. Uniform convergence on compact subdisks proves the identity. This avoids assuming a positive Herglotz measure or an analytic logarithm of h.

The generic budget is sharp in the signed-measure closure. Put B>0 and

    h_B(z)=(1+B)(1+z)/(1-z)-B(1-z)/(1+z).

Its representing measure is (1+B)delta_1-B delta_-1, and h_B(0)=1. It has a zero at

    z=-r_B,
    r_B=(sqrt(1+B)-sqrt B)/(sqrt(1+B)+sqrt B),
    B=(1-r_B)^2/(4r_B).                             (W40.4)

Thus arbitrarily small total negative mass can create a zero arbitrarily close to the boundary. A claim that a small unweighted defect gives the ENTIRE disk is false. A positive collar is essential. The rational h_B has boundary poles, so it is not an equality example in the smooth-boundary class. To verify sharpness there, take h_B(tz), t<1, and choose r_B=tr. It is analytic beyond the unit circle and has its zero at-r. Its boundary real part is the signed Poisson smoothing of the two atoms. Its negative mass tends to b(r) as t increases to1: the two Poisson kernels concentrate on disjoint arcs, and their overlap mass tends to0. For a proposed larger budget at fixed r, first choose r'<r with b(r') below that budget, then use this approximation at r'. Its zero is now INSIDE the target disk. Thus no larger uniform open-disk budget follows in the smooth class either.

This first test corrects the unpriced seed: total negative mass is useful only with the explicit radius-dependent return W40.2. It does not by itself prove any arithmetic bound.

### 2.2 Actual ordinary and fixed Eisenstein L-functions

For an ordinary fixed Dirichlet character let P(s)=L(s,chi) if it is nonprincipal and P(s)=(s-1)L(s,chi) if it is principal. The factor removes the simple principal pole; it has a nonzero limiting value at1. Keep all finite imprimitive Euler factors. For a fixed finite-order, trivial-infinity-type Eisenstein Hecke member use the identical principal/nonprincipal definition with its PRESENTED fixed ray modulus and every conductor zero retained.

The needed analytic package is modest. Ordinary periodic character sums give A(x)=c x+O_q(1). For the Eisenstein family the fixed residue-lattice argument gives A(x)=c x+O_f(sqrt x+1): count complete fixed-conductor lattice cells in a norm disk and O_f(sqrt x+1) boundary cells, divide by the six units, and exclude the zero vector. In the nonprincipal case c=0. Abel summation gives meromorphic L on Re s>1/2 with only the principal pole at1, so P is holomorphic there. On Re s>1 the absolutely convergent Euler product is nonzero. These are the exact analytic inputs used in W39 A3/A5; this argument uses no W39 small-set theorem or new unintegrated f3 claim. Constants may depend on the fixed member. There is no angular or growing-conductor uniformity.

Fix outer radius R=7/5. For EVERY real t set

    h_t(z)=P(2+it+Rz)/P(2+it).                     (W40.5)

The closed disk lies in Re s>=3/5>1/2, with a positive analytic margin. The denominator is nonzero. For any fixed gamma in(3/5,1), put

    r_gamma=(2-gamma)/R,
    b_gamma=(1-r_gamma)^2/(4r_gamma).

**Conditional theorem W40-B.** If B(h_t)<=b_gamma for EVERY real t, then that fixed L-function has no zeros in Re s>gamma, excluding the principal pole by construction. Proof: a zero rho=beta+it with gamma<beta<=1 gives h_t((beta-2)/R)=0 at modulus<r_gamma, contrary to W40.2. The Euler product handles Re s>1. The same contradiction includes beta=1 if necessary. Every height is tested; no average or finite net is silently substituted.

Here are exact targets. They are hypothesis budgets, not proved endpoints:

| Prospective c | gamma=1-c | r_gamma | Sufficient all-height B budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| .125136 |54679/62500|70321/87500|295118041/24612350000, about .0119906|
| 1/6 |5/6|5/6|1/120|
| 1/4 |3/4|25/28|9/2800|

The first would exceed c4 by exactly .000001. The construction thus has an actual quantitative high-ceiling RETURN and a concrete first-gain budget. Section2.4 proves the bare hypothesis false for zeta, so these are not live unmodified proof targets. The return does not add the Gaussian .00075 gap to the separate H .004 deficit.

There is a legal height-adaptive variant. Let E_t(s) be ANY explicitly chosen finite Euler product

    E_t(s)=product_(p in a finite set depending on t)
                       (1-chi(p)N(p)^(-s)),

using rational primes or prime ideals as appropriate. Natural zero local characters give factor1. Each factor is nonzero on Re s>0. Replacing P by P E_t and normalizing at2+it preserves every zero in the disk. The same theorem holds if for each t there exists one such finite product satisfying its B budget. No common finite product is required, because this is a separately proved local-disk architecture, not an X-dependent Gaussian claimed to have one fixed Mellin transform. The actual product, all its derivatives and its boundary behavior must still be paid. Neither existence nor a uniform cost is proved.

### 2.3 Serious arithmetic test, failed coarse bound, and constructive error budget

This is not the old constant-corrected logarithmic derivative. W24-C proves that the latter fails positivity already in Re s>1. Here the object is the holomorphic P itself and its target zeros are never removed. The signed boundary measure exists unconditionally and can be computed; its small negative mass is the unpaid arithmetic hypothesis. SC25's pole-removing Cayley warning is also avoided: the principal pole is the only removed singularity, and a nonprincipal zero stays a zero of h_t.

The first available absolute arithmetic bound does NOT pay W40-B. From the preceding A(x)=c x+O(x^alpha), alpha=0 or1/2, Abel summation gives

    L(s)=c*s/(s-1)+s*integral_1^infinity
                         [A(v)-cv]v^(-s-1)dv,

on Re s>alpha. For nonprincipal c=0; multiply by(s-1) in the principal case. On the circle Re s>=.6 these bounds, divided by the Euler lower bound at2+it, give only

    sup_theta |h_t(exp(i theta))| <= C_fixed(1+|t|).

For principal P the numerator has apparent degree2, but the anchor factor |1+it| removes one degree. This coarse estimate is an UPPER bound, not evidence that B actually grows. Since

    B(h_t)=(integral |Re h_t| dm-1)/2
            <=(integral |h_t| dm-1)/2,

it yields no uniform small constant at high height. A finite Euler product adds further boundary/derivative costs; it does not fix this estimate for free. Thus the weakest sufficient missing arithmetic task is the actual signed negative-part integral, not a global modulus bound or a positivity assumption inferred from coefficients.

A finite-height test of a genuinely changed normalization can be made concrete without treating samples as proof. For one fixed finite Euler multiplier on a height interval I, write Q=P E and h_t(z)=Q(2+it+Rz)/Q(2+it). Suppose certified bounds on that interval and its circle give

    |partial_theta Re h_t(exp(i theta))| <= M_theta,
    |partial_t Re h_t(exp(i theta))| <= M_t.

For N equally spaced left-endpoint angles, let B_N(t) be their average negative part. The map v ->max(-v,0) is1-Lipschitz, hence

    |B(h_t)-B_N(t)| <= pi M_theta/N.                (W40.6)

If a height net has nearest-point distance at most delta/2, its additional error is M_t delta/2. Therefore

    B_N(t_j)+pi M_theta/N+M_t delta/2 <= b_gamma    (W40.7)

at all net points certifies the covered interval. Include quadrature/value interval errors additively. With |Q(anchor)|>=m>0, one may use

    M_theta = R sup_circle |Q'|/m,
    M_t = sup_circle |Q'|/m
             +sup_circle|Q| sup_anchor|Q'|/m^2.

These are explicit sufficient bounds, obtained by differentiating the quotient. Overlapping intervals may use different fixed E. All omitted heights still need a theorem or a certified covering; finite-height success would not increase c. No contour discretization or numerical L-function evaluation was promoted here. An optional mpmath availability check failed because that module is absent in the task Python; no installation or substitute numerical result is claimed.

### 2.4 A primary-source universality test rejects the bare arithmetic target

The further strongest-objection test is decisive, not merely a weak available upper bound. For the bare zeta choice P(s)=(s-1)zeta(s),

    sup_(t real) B(h_t)=infinity.                   (W40.21)

External input: Johan Andersson, *Lavrent'ev's approximation theorem with nonvanishing polynomials and universality of zeta-functions*, arXiv:1010.0386, Theorem2, PDF page2. The theorem states uniform vertical approximation to any continuous target on a compact subset of1/2<Re s<1 having empty interior and connected complement, on a positive-lower-density set of positive shifts. The primary [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.0386) was opened and its exact theorem inspected. Only that theorem is imported; it is not reproved here. Voronin's1975 original disk result was identified, but its full PDF fetch failed, so the argument binds to the accessible primary theorem above.

Here is the new application, including the anchor and principal-pole factors. Let R=7/5, delta=1/40, and

    K={2+R exp(i theta): |theta-pi|<=delta}.

This compact simple arc has empty interior and connected complement. Its real parts lie between.6 and.6+R delta^2/2<1, so it is strictly inside the universality strip. For any fixed M>=32, apply the cited theorem to the constant target-M with uniform error1. It gives arbitrarily large t with

    zeta(s+it)=-M+e(s), |e(s)|<1 for every s in K.

On the anchor line2 the absolutely convergent reciprocal series gives

    w_t=1/zeta(2+it),
    |w_t-1|<=sum_(n>=2)n^-2<3/4,
    Re w_t>1/4, |w_t|<7/4.

The elementary bound uses1/4+integral_2^infinity v^-2 dv=3/4; no unknown vertical phase is ignored. For s in K put k_t(s)=(s+it-1)/(1+it). If t>=40,

    |k_t-1|<=R/40=7/200,
    |w_t||k_t-1|<49/800<1/16,
    |w_t||k_t|<2.

Therefore the actual normalized P satisfies throughout the whole arc

    Re[k_t(s)w_t(-M+e(s))]
       <-M/4+M/16+2 <=-M/8.

Its negative boundary mass is consequently at least

    B(h_t)>= (2delta)/(2pi) * M/8 = M/(320pi).      (W40.22)

Since M is arbitrary, W40.21 follows. For any chosen finite budget, such bad heights even have positive lower density after discarding a bounded interval. The theorem does not produce a zero: zero-free analytic functions can have large real-part oscillation. It proves the proposed sufficient positivity condition is too strong for this bare normalization, independently of an off-line-zero assumption.

This is a distinct obstruction from W24's logarithmic-derivative phase witness. It uses actual zeta universality on a contour arc and explicitly pays division by zeta(2+it) and the(s-1) normalization. No result for a finite Euler multiplier, especially a height-adaptive one, is inferred: such a multiplier can rotate/change the arc and needs its own argument. The valid future question is whether a specified changed normalization both defeats this obstruction and has a small all-height negative-part estimate. An unspecified multiplier or finite successful samples do not supply that escape.

Functional signature: actual holomorphic pole-removed L; signed real-boundary decomposition; Poisson extremal weights; bare all-height hypothesis REFUTED by W40.21; changed-normalization estimate open; exact zero return W40-B retained. This is quantitative relative to F21/F22/F23 and SC25, not a literature-priority claim.

I read T10 in the [private research revision] consolidated proof and the
N28.C entry in the merged portfolio. T10 already
constructs discrete and continuous dilation criteria
for the actual Mertens function, identifies their
Mellin multipliers and proves the conditional
zero-exclusion bridge. N28.C develops their logarithmic
increment/overlap interpretation and explicitly keeps
the arithmetic cross-scale energy open.

DP's equality
F_(A,delta)(x)=F_(mu,delta)(x)-2F_(mu,delta)(x/2)
is the same broad dilation mechanism. The generic
shell-to-holomorphy proof is likewise old in that
record. In DP the extra local multiplier's zeros
lie on Re s=1, already outside the new target strip;
one fixed prime factor therefore suffices for the
qualitative bridge. This does not upgrade the
old open dilation energy to a theorem.

The specific checked combination is narrower:
an infinitely refinable compact probability kernel,
an exact frozen-width norm transfer, the fixed
arithmetic pole-killing factor, its fully folded
diagonal and the uniform alternating completion
with its capped reciprocal-frequency return.
Those particular identities and normalizations
are not furnished by the T10/N28 statements read.
The source correctly calls this a developed child
of that route, not a new portfolio family or a
literature-priority claim. The present acceptance
does not establish a broader novelty search.

# [private research revision] headroom: source replacement discovery and bounded development

Status: mathematical development complete, no new c; independent review pending. Current written c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, gamma11=.8748540364. Root owns canonical research, tracker and Git. Prior frozen scopes are untouched. No formalization or new packet.

## Compact current worklog

Objective: substantively develop a genuinely different higher-ceiling source mechanism, work backward to the weakest complete first-gain estimate and test a coarse rigorous bound. Discovery precedes the full index review. Completed: stable prefix, frozen problem/assignment, [restricted research revision] G170-G172 integration, relevant ownership/recovery policy, reservation and exact own claim. Completed mathematics: full square-prefix and cross-row estimates, complete changed-source return, exact variance, and a coarse logarithmic arithmetic test. Checks passed and source pins saved. Final readback/freeze are recorded in the manifest; independent review and the full signed power estimate remain OPEN. Accepted current mathematical obligations F0/positive-slot/external admission remain OPEN. Existing 29-family/109-child portfolio is retained.

## 1. Initial discovery comparison (before full-index intake)

A. Replace Mobius by the completely multiplicative Liouville twist. For a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h=chi, and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, a*h=s. The series of a*s is L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi), with numerator nonzero above1/2. Potential: collapse two long arithmetic signs exactly while paying square-supported short terms. Objection: those real square costs cannot be erased by reciprocal-L equivalence. SELECTED for development.

B. Polynomial-phase Type II cancellation on the nonlinear transition N>X. Potential: improve the complete coefficientwise tail. Objection: bounded phase variation at N~X leaves a genuine near-scale arithmetic range; changing fixed k alone is no estimate.

C. Combine fixed unramified Euler compensators before projection. Potential: remove an arithmetic stratum. Objection: fixed filters retain prime-power prices; growing filters must repay coefficients, periods, short sources and Mellin costs. No unpriced growing bank is used.

D. Nyman-Beurling type multiplicative approximation. Potential: an upstream direct zero detector. Objection: without a complete approximation-residual estimate this only renames an open reciprocal-L norm. Not selected.

The selection seeks a proved source estimate or a specific failed construction, not a conditional ceiling or separate-cell certificate.

## 2. Duplicate screen, selected repair and source status

The full current attempt index was consulted after the initial discovery. W24/round24-review Section 2 already pays a square-divisor remainder and shows that the crude buffered Mertens input does not improve the exponent. [private research revision] preserves the dormant Liouville/gcd option; [private research revision]/W49 Section 5 proves the complete prime-square mask and the two inverse square convolutions. Those identities and their exponent equivalence are inherited, not discoveries here. They do not contain the simultaneous ordinary/root compensation or the full square-row alias estimate below. [restricted research revision] supplies the complete nonlinear tail and Mellin machinery; [restricted research revision] and [restricted research revision] supply periodic mean-zero row completion and its exact complement. The separate signed-mixed worker's native divisor-projector correlations are not developed here.

The first attempted Liouville substitution exposed a real price: a*h is supported on squares, not at 1. Replacing those short terms by the old Mobius short terms is false. Bounding a square row absolutely loses its root length. Calling its entire infinite row nonstationary is also false: its nonlinear derivative eventually crosses every Fourier frequency. The repair uses TWO local factors and pays the full alias tail in L2 instead of removing it.

Outside primary ancestry: Peter Humphries, *The Distribution of Weighted Sums of the Liouville Function and Polya's Conjecture*, arXiv:1108.1524v2 (4 October 2012), JNT 133 (2013), 545-582, introduction pp.1-2, verifies the standard Euler product and reciprocal-zeta relation. Its distribution theorems assume RH and further hypotheses; none is imported. The twisted identities used here are proved directly below. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.1524v2), [author paper at UCL](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1569441/1/Humphries_the_distribution_of_weighted_sums_of_the_liouville.pdf).

Root's 20:54 steering reports [restricted research revision] published as 3535bdec01be9c59d4fe24be6a0d52ea717fe126. At that intake W62 was not yet accepted; neither it nor the later [restricted research revision] update is an input below. No hypothetical first-gain target is substituted for current c11.

## 3. A double compensated completely multiplicative source

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including its actual zero values, and one prime p not dividing q. All parameters and this character are fixed before X, epsilon and any target zero. Let * denote Dirichlet convolution and let delta_m be the unit mass at m. Define

    a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n),
    s(n)=1_(n=r^2 for an integer r>=1) chi(r)^2,
    q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g.

Prime powers give a*h=s, and hence a*a*b=v*a*s=c. Complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de) is literal, including nonunits; lambda has no artificial squarefree zeros. We do not identify this a with the original Mobius coefficient.

In Re(z)>1 the absolute Euler identities are

    D_a(z)=L(2z,chi^2)/L(z,chi),
    D_c(z)=P_p(z) J_p(z) L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z),
    J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2 p^(1-2z).                         (3.1)

J_p has all zeros on Re(z)=1/2. L(2z,chi^2) is holomorphic and nonzero for Re(z)>1/2 by its absolutely convergent Euler product; its possible principal pole at z=1/2 is on the excluded boundary. Thus this replacement has its own zero-detection numerator. It has no new zero above1/2 except P_p's familiar line Re(z)=1.

The ordinary cofactor b is periodic of period Q=p^3 q and has mean zero. Indeed b=q2*b1 with b1(n)=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)); b1 has period pq and zero mean, and its p^2-dilate does too. Explicitly

    b(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    |b(n)| <= (p+1)^2.                                (3.2)

For the square-supported short source put w=q2*s. It is supported at r^2 and

    w(r^2)=beta(r):=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)).              (3.3)

beta is periodic of period Q0=pq, bounded by p, and has mean zero. If chi^2 is nonprincipal both period sums vanish. ## 8. Complete reopening contract and ancestry

For the surviving joint arithmetic option, choose nested finite spaces V_j
spanned by specified original wavelets with q=2,3 (and, if desired, a fixed
finite original seed). Let r_j=1-P_(V_j)1, d_j^2=||r_j||^2, and let U_j be the
orthogonalized newly added block in V_(j+1) intersect V_j^perp. Then

    d_(j+1)^2=d_j^2-g_j,   g_j=||P_(U_j)r_j||^2.

Equivalently, for the block map A_j with orthogonalized columns spanning U_j,
its full Gram C_j=A_j^*A_j and
q_j=A_j^*r_j give g_j=q_j^* C_j^dagger q_j. The dagger respects the true
nullspace. A sufficient quantitative target is

    g_j>=delta_j d_j^2,   0<=delta_j<=1,
    sum_j delta_j=infinity.                              (R20)

Unless a residual has already vanished, iterating gives
d_j^2<=d_0^2 product_(i<j)(1-delta_i), tending to zero. All entries here are
the complete R1 Gram, including every later reciprocal cell and every ordered
cross-grid product. A sequence of independently restarted prefix fits is not
this compatible projection chain. Neither artificial-zero removal nor
separate grid conditioning supplies R20.

The alternative exact gate is o(1) of the source resolvent for the enlarged
dictionary, with positive summable weights fixed as part of that source and
with its zero atom included. Any vanishing rate would suffice. At
sigma=.874864 either complete gate would imply the first-gain zero exclusion;
at sigma=5/6 or 3/4 it would give the corresponding later target. These are
conditional returns, not achieved estimates.

The source comparisons establish the following scope and deduplication.

* **SW33–SW41:** SW34 is the exact q=2 dictionary studied here. SW38 proves one
  leakage shell; SW41 says the absolute future-tail bound diverges at
  sigma<=1 and explicitly leaves signed capture open. R5/R9/R10/R14 now rule
  out full signed capture of 1 by this dictionary, including any fixed finite
  starting arithmetic patch. That is stronger than the old majorant failure.
* **F08.A/N1/N2, F19.A, A08–A09:** These already supply the original source,
  heavy-tail Gram, capture and resolvent gates. Their arbitrary balanced
  differences n f_n-m f_m, including A09's varying m=2N, are larger families.
  The new restricted obstruction does not close those proposals. The spectral
  theorem by itself and the generic capture identity earn no new credit.
* **N28.D/C:** Two discrete dilations b=2,3 already avoid a common unwanted
  nonreal multiplier zero for Delta_b M=M(bx)-b^alpha M(x); continuum dilations
  already have quantitative calibration. Common scale 6 was not a contraction.
  The non-common-zero principle is therefore inherited. The present positive
  source floor, fixed-finite-seed obstruction, literal inverse coefficients
  and the specific B_q Gaussian conditioning are distinct statements about a
  different actual source, not a newly proved Mobius energy estimate.
* **The old SW two-grid theorem is different:** its shell-start set is
  {2^j,3*2^j}, with consecutive ratios 3/2 and 4/3, and it compares affine,
  Mertens and continuum energies under an inherited growth premise. These are
  overlapping shell grids, not the two arithmetic wavelet dilation families
  q=2 and q=3. Their energy equivalence cannot simply be substituted into R20.
* **W22/R22:** R22.4–R22.11 prove legitimate finite known-zero division for the
  actual divisible Hardy source and its changed target. They do not identify
  the arithmetic span with the ambient inner ideal or prove Gram capture.
  That result supplies no permission to divide out the present artificial
  lattice while leaving both the original target 1 and its norm gate unchanged.
  The Mellin transform of 1-W has value 1/s_k at every artificial zero, so it is
  not divisible there. Even a single such division would have a pole. Changing the
  target to make a division legal would require a new calibrated zero return.

For the user's simultaneous-detector idea, the exact useful analogy is narrow:
one wavelet grid has blind Mellin frequencies which the other grid sees, and a
common underlying signal admits the paid joint recovery R16–R19. The arithmetic
work is still to control that common signal or prove full joint capture. Pooling
separately bounded or separately fitted detector outputs supplies neither.
This review claims no literature novelty beyond the comparison with the exact
maintained local sources.

For j=0,1,

    |(d/dz)^j Z_r(Xz)| << (N/sqrt T)e^(-c rho).              (R12)

On the support of w or its derivative n_r is comparable to N and dn_r/dz=(6/5)n_r/z. All damping derivatives are absorbed by a weaker exponential. This also holds through the smooth support boundaries. For r!=s in the near window the phase difference has first derivative comparable to N|r-s|, since

    X^(6/5)(T/N)^(1/5)=N.

Its second derivative is a bounded multiple of the first. One integration by parts on the ACTUAL interval1<=z<=2, retaining both shell endpoint terms and the derivative of1/z, gives the Gram bound

    C (N^2/T)e^(-c rho) min(1,1/(N|r-s|)),                  (R13)

and the same scale with minimum1 on the diagonal. All distinct reduced fractions with denominators<=2M have spacing at least1/(4M^2). Ordering them gives the full row sum

    O(1+(M^2/N)log(2+J)), J<<M+M^2T/N.                     (R14)

Apply 2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 to the complete double sum, both orientations included. Combining (R11)-(R14), using log(2+J)<<_Q log(2N), gives

    ||whole stationary bank||_2^2
        <<A^2 e^(-c rho)(N+M^2)log^2(2N).                  (R15)

Add the full row error by norm triangle. Sum the whole blocks in norm over M and N, never by a signed-subset norm comparison. statement:
## 3. Reciprocal replenishment and the finite bootstrap

### R39-B. The Mellin identity gives actual zero exclusion

On Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F(y) exp(-s y)dy=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).  (R39.6)

If F(y)=O_epsilon(exp((h+epsilon)y)) for every epsilon>0,
the right tail integral is holomorphic on Re s>h. Each fixed
s-derivative introduces a power of y, still integrable on compact
subsets by choosing epsilon inside the real-part margin. The left
Gaussian tail pays negative y. Multiplication by the meromorphic L
continues the identity from Re s>1. Any zero in Re s>h would force
the nonvanishing exponential to vanish. The principal pole at 1
instead forces a zero in the reciprocal and causes no false claim.
This argument covers unbounded heights; it is not a sample of zeros
or a contour truncated at a moving height.

### R39-C. The fixed-line reciprocal bound is proved after that step

For nonprincipal ordinary chi, periodic partial sums A_chi(x) are
O_q(1), so Abel summation continues L=s integral_1^infinity
A_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt to Re s>0 and gives a polynomial upper bound.
For principal chi, write A_chi(t)=ct+E(t), E=O_q(1). Then

    L(s)=c*s/(s-1)+s integral_1^infinity E(t)t^(-s-1)dt.

Consequently P=L in the nonprincipal case and P=(s-1)L in the
principal case are holomorphic with polynomial upper growth on
every closed positive real-part strip. In the principal case
P(1)=c>0. All imprimitive factors remain; their zeros have real
part 0 and do not intrude on this domain.

Assume the zero-free conclusion already obtained above: Re s>h,
h>0. Fix h<b<2. At center 2+it choose outer radius
R_0=2-(h+b)/2 and inner radius r_0=2-b. The outer disk stays in
Re s>h; its positive gap is (b-h)/2. The regularized P is
holomorphic and nonzero there. Choose a local log f=log P whose
center imaginary part is in [-pi,pi]. The Euler product on Re s=2
bounds L above and away from zero. Together with the regularizing
factor this gives |f(2+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)). The polynomial upper
bound for P gives sup Re f=O(log(2+|t|)) on the disk.

Here is the quantitative log estimate. Choose positive
M>max(0,sup Re f), of size O(log(2+|t|)), and set g=M-f. Then Re g>0.
The map (g-g(center))/(g+conj(g(center))) takes the disk to the unit
disk and vanishes at its center. Schwarz's inequality bounds its
modulus by r_0/R_0 on the inner disk. Hence

    |g| <= (R_0+r_0)/(R_0-r_0) |g(center)|,
    |f| <= C_(h,b,q) log(2+|t|).

This proves |1/P(b+it)|<=C(2+|t|)^K. For principal chi multiply
by |b+it-1| to recover 1/L. Compact low heights are harmless.
The same fixed disks bound every point b<=Re s<=2, uniformly in
height. No Phragmen--Lindelof premise, conjectural reciprocal bound,
or conductor-uniform estimate has entered this argument. The
author's strip here must be understood as a fixed real-part strip
with all heights; the disk proof supplies exactly that bound.

Mellin inversion starts on Re s=2, where the Dirichlet series is
absolutely convergent. Shift to b. The integrand is holomorphic,
including at the principal pole's reciprocal zero. Horizontal sides
vanish because exp(-tau*t^2/2) beats the just-proved polynomial,
uniformly across b<=Re s<=2. Thus

    F(z)=(1/(2pi)) integral_R exp(tau*(b+it)^2/2)
                         exp((b+it)z)/L(b+it,chi)dt.     (R39.7)

For z=u+iv, completing the square gives
-tau*t^2/2-tv=-(tau/2)(t+v/tau)^2+v^2/(2tau).
The shifted Gaussian integral of (1+|t|)^K is bounded by
C_(tau,K)(1+|v|)^K. This proves R39.3 **for all v**, not just on
a fixed complex strip. It therefore supports the growing Cauchy
disks used in R39.4. All fixed derivatives follow by polynomial
factors of b+it under this same integral.

The possible circularity is resolved in the correct order:
interpolation first proves an improved real exponent; R39.6 first
proves the corresponding zero-free domain; only then does this disk
argument improve the complex bound for the next step.

### R39-D. Quantifiers in W39-A and protected audit E03

For W39-A take 0<gamma<1 and 0<=kappa<1/2 throughout.
Let P(h) mean the complete all-scale bound at h with every positive
exponent allowance. Write r=2kappa<1. The hypothesis supplies, for
every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large j, sets E_j of measure
at least c_epsilon j^-kappa and values at most
C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j). These constants may depend on
epsilon and the fixed character, but not on j.

Starting with the unconditional complex bound at b=1, the first
interpolation proves P(h_1), h_1=gamma+r(1-gamma). R39.6 and R39.7
then give R39.3 for every fixed b>h_1. The next interpolation, with
sufficiently small fixed input allowances and b-h_1, proves
P(h_2), h_2=gamma+r^2(1-gamma). In general

    h_m=gamma+r^m(B-gamma),                              (R39.8)

where B=1 initially, or a separately available prior limiting
exponent B>gamma. The word limiting means an arbitrary positive
buffer is taken before using R39.3; no estimate on the exact
boundary line is presumed.

For any requested output margin eta>0, choose a finite m with
r^m(B-gamma)<eta/3. Then choose the finitely many b/input margins
small enough that their total contribution is <2eta/3. The hypothesis
allows each such choice. The resulting constants and initial scale
may worsen, but are fixed. There is no interchange of an infinite
iteration and an estimate. For kappa=0 the first step already gives
P(gamma). This proves W39-A, its all-scale conclusion, and exclusion
of every zero with Re rho>gamma. It asserts nothing on Re rho=gamma.

Protected E03 is therefore **accepted through A02's developed
argument**, including its suggested single-step formula. Its
pre-outcome protection was warranted by a genuine open hypothesis
left by the old density examples, but it is the same-batch overlap
already acknowledged by the author, not a seventh selected test or
independent theorem discovery. The improvement from R39.5 to the
final exponent gamma uses the actual meromorphic L package. It is
not granted to every generic bounded-coefficient entire function.

A fixed positive interval length can replace 1: the interpolation
numerators and Taylor radius costs change by fixed factors, leaving
R39.5 unchanged after rescaling. Shrinking lengths or a sparse
subsequence of intervals require a new argument. Finitely many
point samples have measure zero and meet no stated hypothesis.

The frozen illustration at kappa=1/4 and gamma=.87449 is correct:
from B=1, h_8=.8749802734375 and h_9=.87473513671875. Nine steps
cross both the old .874872 and current .874867 boundaries, entirely
conditionally. With the current limiting B=.874867, the first
midpoint is .8746785; the author's .874681 is the historical c2
midpoint. These arithmetic illustrations prove no small-value set
and no new c.

Nothing about the merely x^(1/4) lower-end decay of a reflected V-sharp profile licenses arbitrary substitution into this primal statement. For a fixed finite list of smooth parameters, real powers, heights and scales, prove the same coefficient bounds for their derivatives. D1 is the existing exact prime split

    M_chi(X)=A_p(X)-chi(p)A_p(X/p)

    A_p(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n).

Squareful terms vanish and no character defect is dropped. Choosing chi(p)=1 removes the displayed interior term but supplies no estimate for B_p. G144 already retains this identity and its twist/gauge limitations.

Inside the finite squarefree q-unit set n<=X, a terminal prime p in(X/2,X] has exactly one distinct comparable vertex:1. It has no other divisor and no proper multiple within the cutoff. In any disjoint comparable-vertex pairing at most one terminal prime can be matched. Therefore the unmatched count is at least their number minus one. Character phase restrictions can only remove eligible pairs, so the bound survives them. For standard NONNEGATIVE fractional matching with vertex capacity1, the sum of the terminal primes' incident weights is at most the capacity of1; the same lower bound applies to residual mass. An unrestricted complex flow is not a fractional matching in that sense.

PNT gives terminal count~X/(2log X) for fixed q. No Morse acyclicity was used. The obstruction includes adaptive pivots and comparable pairs differing by several primes. It does not apply to arbitrary shared-vertex linear homotopies, noncomparable pairs, or partners beyond the finite cutoff. In particular it is not by itself a lower bound on the global future-partner cost of G150. The complete global M1 return and this finite graph statement must remain distinct.

## 9. Strongest surviving objection and next action

The polynomial phase is slow on n~X. Its difference over a unit n-step
there is O(1/X); increasing the fixed degree changes a constant, not that
power. The absolute Gram price or curvature alone therefore cannot create
the missing cancellation in the transition. The bounded-array example
proves the generic exponent2 cannot be improved by this method. It is not
a lower bound for actual Mobius, and it does not retire arithmetic routes.

The complete kernel for an actual signed core is still
mu(n)mu(m)chi(n)conjugate(chi(m))K_X(n,m), with both indices inside the
same sharp interval. A bilinear/nilsequence/inverse-theorem attack must
retain the sum's complete interactions. Merely improving the already paid
far-frequency tail repeats a solved component. Uniform logarithmic
polynomial orthogonality includes the zero polynomial; replacing its log
saving by a power would itself require much stronger arithmetic. The
specific moving polynomial here might admit a sharper argument, but no
such bound follows from the imported theorem.

The next decisive target is therefore the actual CORE1 at gamma=.8748
on X^.8748<n<=X^1.0626 over the ENTIRE shell, or a sufficient signed L2
bound there. Near gains remain preferable first tests;1/6 and1/4 are fully
priced, andSection8 keeps a precisely conditional larger ceiling visible.
No norm-equivalence, favorable review, finite calculation or generic
counterexample is counted as a numerical c increase.

statement:
## 5. Relative characters, complete coefficient mass and masked rows

For two columns l,l', let e_p be their valuation difference modulo6, in {0,...,5}. Define squarefree pairwise coprime ideals

    q1=product_(e_p=1 or5) p,
    q2=product_(e_p=2 or4) p,
    q3=product_(e_p=3) p,
    Q_i=Nq_i, Q=Q1 Q2 Q3, H=Q1 Q2^2 Q3^3.             ([restricted research revision])

At every good prime, nonzero powers of the primitive sextic character have conductor p, with orders6,3,2 respectively. The primitive relative conductor is q1 q2 q3 away from fixed data. Fixed ray factors alter it by a fixed factor; they cannot cancel a conductor prime outside S. The actual product of row phases is

    psi_u(l) conjugate(psi_u(l'))
       =xi_e(u) 1_((u,E_(l,l'))=1).                  ([restricted research revision])

E retains EVERY prime of ll' whose relative valuation is zero, plus the fixed omitted primes not already in the primitive conductor. Equal or sixth-power phases at such a prime do not remove that hole. Whole inverse orientation conjugates xi_e. q1=q2=q3=1 is exactly the same-sixth-power-class sector, apart from the already fixed ray/unit data. It is paid separately, not treated by a nonprincipal Gauss estimate.

### 5a. Extension of balanced-residue mass to the COMPLETE tail

For a fixed residue vector e, the actual coefficients (including the `Nc>U^(6/5)` projection if desired) satisfy

    sum_(l/l' congruent e mod sixth powers)
       |partial b_l(s) partial' b_l'(s)|
        << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H^(-1/2).     ([restricted research revision])

Here partial and partial' are any two of the finite required derivative operators. This proves cross-dyad as well as same-dyad control. To see it, put Nl in a dyad L and Nl' in a possibly different dyad L'. For each choice of signs of the actual nonzero valuation differences, write

    l=g a x^6,  l'=g b y^6,  (a,b)=1,
    N(ab)>=H.

At a prime of residue e, its exponent in ab is e or 6-e according to that sign. All additional multiples of six are in x,y. Taking g to be the actual gcd gives an exact representation; then allowing all x,y only overcounts. There are at most `2^omega(q1q2q3)` sign choices. For fixed a,b,x,y the number of g is at most

    min(L/[Na (Nx)^6], L'/[Nb (Ny)^6])
       <= sqrt(LL')/[sqrt(Nab) (Nx)^3 (Ny)^3].

If either upper cutoff is below one, the actual set is empty. Summing x,y uses the convergent ideal zeta series at3. Multiplying by (C7) gives the dyadic bound

    H_J U^((2sigma-1)v+epsilon)
       (LL')^(1/2-sigma) H^(-1/2).

Both L,L' start at `c0 U^(t+v)`. Since sigma>1/2, the TWO geometric tail sums converge with total

    [U^(t+v)]^(1-2sigma).

The slot power cancels, leaving exactly ([restricted research revision]). This step is what an invocation of the old single-annulus RM-A would omit. The cutoff has been merged before this decomposition; A_R is never triangle-expanded into individual divisor witnesses. Derivative logarithms are paid by a small decrease of sigma. The finite terminal support makes the sign count and all divisor factors subpower uniformly; no infinite sum of conductor dyads with a nondecaying bound is asserted.

On dyadic ranges of Q1,Q2,Q3 there are at most `(Q1Q2Q3)^(1+epsilon)` residue vectors. Thus their combined coefficient mass is

    << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] (Q1/Q3)^(1/2).     ([restricted research revision])

This already pays all q1=1 classes, including mixed quadratic/cubic characters of GLOBAL order6. Global order6 is not by itself the hard class.

### 5b. Actual row kernel, not an invented orthogonality

For a primitive nonprincipal relative character of conductor norm Q and a fixed smooth radial Phi, literal PR9 equation B3.5 gives

    |sum_w xi(w) Phi(Nw/V)| << min(V,sqrt(Q)).         ([restricted research revision])

The primitive dual zero frequency vanishes. The normalized Gauss sum has modulus one, and radial decay/lattice counting bound `A sum_(h!=0)|F Phi(A Nh)|` by a fixed seminorm. This proves the square-root-conductor branch. Ordinary lattice counting proves the V branch. For V below a fixed positive threshold the compactly supported original sum is empty; the same bound follows uniformly. Fixed ray restrictions are first expanded into their finite characters, retaining each phase and any additional fixed conductor holes.

To impose sixth-freeness, use its EXACT Möbius sum over b^6|u and put u=b^6 w. The relative sextic factor at b^6 is one when coprime, zero otherwise. A fixed ray factor from the finite expansion can leave a phase of modulus one, which is retained. Expand the remaining row hole by d|rad E. With d,b restricted by the actual nonempty scale, the absolute majorant is

    sum_(d|rad E) sum_b min(U/[(Nb)^6 Nd], sqrt Q)
      << U^(1/6) Q^(5/12)
                     product_(p|E)(1+(Np)^(-1/6)).

Split at `(Nb)^6=U/(Nd sqrt Q)`. Ideal counting below and the sixth-power tail above give the displayed power; if that split is below one the same upper bound follows from the whole convergent tail. The product is at most `(NE)^epsilon` for every fixed epsilon. E is in a fixed polynomial range, so its loss is preallocated. Natural shared-prime zeros therefore cost a subpower, not a lost radical factor.

Removing the fixed finite exceptional free rows changes the kernel by `O_fixed(1)`, absorbed since U,Q>=1. Thus for the stated clean natural family, with or without those rows,

    |K_e(l,l';U)|
      << H_J U^epsilon min(U, U^(1/6) Q^(5/12)).      ([restricted research revision])

This is uniform over the actual pair's holes. It does NOT apply after inserting an arbitrary high-bin or amplitude indicator. For a full raw-row variant, primitive Poisson gives min(U,sqrt Q); excluding a fixed list of sixth-power core families costs O_fixed(U^(1/6)). For Q<=U^2 both fit ([restricted research revision]), and for Q>U^2 the trivial U bound fits. This raw variant assumes precisely that fixed list and is not a statement about all physical child exclusions. The free family above is the primary proved contract.

statement:
## 5. New complete bound: choose the estimate before counting repetitions

Keep the ORIGINAL joint (f,k) norms R4 or R6. For fixed good ideal e, write k=a e^6 with a sixth-power-free. Let A=U/(Ne)^6. Every coefficient acquires the exact whole-index mask 1_((index,e)=1). It is fixed during both remaining averages, so both preceding proofs apply to this SAME masked source:

    F^(-1) sum_f w(f) sum_(a sixth-free,Na<<A)
                       |source_f(a e^6)|^2
       << H_J Z^epsilon min{T_6(A,X), A Z^L}.         (R9)

The first bound fixes f and uses R1, or R7 for the completed coefficients. The second fixes a and applies the cubic f sieve as in R8. There is no assertion that a signed subset has smaller norm: these are two bounds on exactly the same complete positive joint norm. Fixed e may share primes with f, the puncture, c,b or a; all masks remain in each proof. In particular no coprimality (a,e)=1 is assumed.

The decomposition of every good k is unique at each valuation, with the units and fixed-prime sectors restored as in Section1. On a dyad Ne~Z^y there are O(Z^y) ideals e and residual row exponent t=M-6y. Sum the smaller uniform bound R9 on that dyad, then sum the O(log Z) dyads. Finite dyadic endpoint constants are absorbed by a previously chosen epsilon. Therefore BOTH complete sources obey

    E << H_J Z^(E_mix(M,N,V)+epsilon),
    E_mix = sup_(0<=t<=M) {
        (M-t)/6 + min[C(t,N), t+L(N,V)] },            (R10)
    C(t,N)=max{t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6}.

The factor (M-t)/6 is the FULL e count, not a square root or a normalized measure. Fixed S-supported powers contribute logarithmic multiplicity; their shortening may be discarded because both bounds are monotone in A. The completed h extraction is already fully summed within R9, before this e count. This avoids exchanging an unproved pointwise signed bound with an outer count.

R10 can also be used with smooth row majorants: retain the original lower row ball, decompose only a rapidly decaying upper tail, and sum the complete ball bounds. Coupled smooth profiles use the common measure described in Section3; positivity and Minkowski retain the whole source before either sieve is selected. All uniformity is for fixed polynomial scale ranges, fixed arithmetic construction data and fixed finite slot systems.

### 5.1 Exact evaluation of the new envelope

For N,V>=0, 0<=L<=N. Define

    E0=min{C(M,N), M+L},
    P=(M+5N+L)/6.

Then

    E_mix=E0,
      unless L>=N/2 and N-L<=M;
    E_mix=max{E0,P} when both conditions hold.         (R11)

This is a continuous endpoint formula; including equality in either condition causes no jump. Here is a proof on the entire interval, not a numerical grid. For 0<=t<=N/2, C(t,N)=N. After the repetition count, the sieve branch is M/6+N-t/6, decreasing, while the label branch is M/6+5t/6+L, increasing. Their crossing is t=N-L. It lies in the actual interval precisely when the conditions in R11 hold, and its common value is P. The endpoint t=0 is no larger than the crossing if it exists; otherwise the minimum is increasing up to the relevant endpoint.

For N/2<=t<=N, C=t/3+5N/6; for N<=t<=2N, C=5t/6+N/3; for t>=2N, C=t. After adding (M-t)/6, these branches have slopes1/6,2/3,5/6, respectively. They and the label branch are increasing, so their minimum achieves its largest value at t=M whenever this portion is present. This gives E0 and proves R11, including truncated intervals M<N/2. The case N=0 follows by the same endpoint formula.

### 5.2 A strictly larger all-row canonical sufficient region

For M>0 and the literal target exponent N+V, R10-R11 give exactly the following boundary for THIS upper envelope:

    E_mix<=N+V  iff  V>=g(M,N),
    g(M,N)= M-N                    (0<=N<=M/2),
             5M/6-2N/3             (M/2<=N<=M),
             (2M-N)/6              (M<=N<=8M/7),
             M/7                   (N>=8M/7).         (R12)

The word "exactly" concerns this proved upper-envelope criterion, not a lower bound for the true energy. Equality is valid with the usual Z^epsilon loss; an induction needing a strict reserve must impose a strict padded inequality.

For N<=M, sufficiency follows from E_mix<=E_all. Necessity for the envelope comes from its t=M endpoint: C(M,N) reaches N+V only at the old boundary, while M+L<=N+V requires V>=max{M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4}, which is no weaker in these ranges.

For N>=M the proposed threshold is at most M/6. Check first 0<=V<=M/6; then L=N-V, t=N-L=V is present, and R11's crossing costs N+(M-V)/6. Paying it requires V>=M/7. The t=M endpoint has label branch M+N-V>N+V in this interval; its sieve branch requires V>=(2M-N)_+/6. Together these give max{M/7,(2M-N)/6}, with the switch at N=8M/7. At that threshold both branches are paid. Larger V only decreases E_mix and increases the target, proving sufficiency for every V. Smaller V fails one displayed envelope branch. This proves R12.

For example M=1,N=8/7,V=1/7 gives

    E_mix=9/7=N+V,
    E_all=55/42,
    E_label=2.

The gain over the previous sixth-order price is1/42, and the global label minimum alone gives no such gain. At N=2,V=1/7 the corresponding prices are15/7,13/6 and20/7. Common punctures of any fixed polynomial size are still allowed; this is genuinely outside the old V>=M/6 sufficient region, even when a large Q also defeats B3.7. No favorable puncture is selected after the row.

The mechanism is a valid complement payment: few repetitions are paid with the sixth-order sieve, many repetitions with the genuine label average, and EVERY intervening dyad is included by R10. It retains the original weights, characters, marks and natural zeros. It is not a theorem about freely conditioning coefficients on f. At V=0, L=N and R10 evaluates to E_all exactly. The repeated principal layers remain charged. In particular E_mix>N for every M>0: the unlabeled canonical target is still unpaid by this new family of estimates.

### 5.2 W40-29 — fixed phase-list occupancy cannot save a power

Give total positive weight V/2 to each phase+pi/3 and-pi/3. Every half-open arc of length pi/3 contains at most V/2, but the complex sum is V/2. Replicate or rescale all weights by any power of X: the same exponent survives. A fixed occupancy cap is thus at most a constant-factor input, not a power-saving theorem.

A precise stronger target is available. For a positive phase measure mu of total V let

    Delta=sup_(connected half-open circle arcs I)
          |mu(I)-V*length(I)/(2pi)|.

Then

    |integral exp(i theta)dmu|<=2 Delta.            (W40.18)

Proof: subtract uniform measure, write its cumulative function F on a cut circle, and note that the oscillation of F is at most Delta, since every interval difference is an arc discrepancy. Subtract the midpoint of its range, giving |F|<=Delta/2. Rotate so the desired integral is real. Stieltjes integration by parts against cos has no boundary term (total signed mass is0), and integral|sin|=4. This gives2Delta; atom endpoints are retained by half-open conventions or a limit of cuts avoiding them. The required arithmetic improvement is a POWER-small complete weighted discrepancy. No distribution law for actual H phases, including their signs/projectors, is proved.
title: 5.2 W40-29 — fixed phase-list occupancy cannot save a power

## Uniform squarefree mass, with a logarithmic refinement

Write Q*=rad(S+ Q), and D(Q*)=prod_(p|Q*)(1+q_p^-1)^(-1).
The G218(218.3) count, subtracted at2X and X, gives

    N_sf(X,2X;Q*)=kappa_R X D(Q*)/zeta_R(2)
          +O(sqrt(X)log(2X) S_1/2(Q*))              [K],
    N_sf(X,2X;Q*)=X D(Q*)/zeta(2)
          +O(sqrt(X) d(Q*))                       [Z]. (3)

The ideal version counts ideals, not associates. This uniform estimate
does not require q_Q<=X. Repeated Q factors do not create new holes.

To improve the candidate's X^(1-delta) lower count, use the exact identity

    D(Q*)^-1=sum_(d|Q*) q_d^-1
       <=sum_(q_d<=q_Q*)q_d^-1 << log(2q_Q*).             (4)

The last bound follows by partial summation from the elementary count
A_R(T)<<T. It uses no prime number theorem or new external input.
Because q_Q*<=C_(S,eta)X^A, (4) gives D(Q*)>>1/log(2X).
For any fixed delta>0, the prime-product argument already used in G219
gives S_1/2(Q*)<<_delta q_Q*^delta. The same elementary small/large-prime
split gives d(Q*)<<_delta q_Q*^delta over Z: each large-prime factor2
is at most q_p^delta, while the finitely many small-prime factors have
a fixed product. Choose delta=1/(4A). The errors in(3) are then
O_(S,eta,A)(X^(3/4)log(2X)), below its positive main term for all large X.
Consequently, uniformly in the entire allowed Q family,

    N_sf(X,2X;Q*) >> X/log(2X).                           (5)

For q_a and x in[X,2X], log(q_a/x) lies in[-log2,log2], where g has a
fixed positive minimum. Therefore

    W_Q(x):=sum_a |c_a| I_Q(a)g(log(q_a/x))
             >> X/log(2X),  every x in[X,2X].            (6)

Also W_Q(x)<=W_1(x)<<x by the complete Gaussian majorant. Both bounds
are uniform in Q. The natural zeros enter S+ once; no character value
of zero is replaced by a unit phase. All large-parameter thresholds
remain allowed to depend on the fixed presented character.
title: Uniform squarefree mass, with a logarithmic refinement

statement:
## 7. Independent extension: fixed bounded-variation profiles

The same proof extends C to any fixed nonzero right-continuous complex profile h of bounded variation, compactly supported inside (1,V). This includes fixed step corrections. It is useful because piecewise-constant quotient tables are a natural possible repair after the smooth-profile failure.

Let nu=dh be its finite distributional derivative measure, using the zero extension. With delta=p^(-r), exact right-continuous sampling gives

    h(m delta)-h((m-1)delta)=nu(((m-1)delta,m delta]).

Therefore (V8) and the smooth main term satisfy

    |sum_m s(m delta)nu(((m-1)delta,m delta])-integral s(v)dnu(v)|
       <=delta sup|s'| |nu|(R).                         (V12)

The uniform source error costs its supremum times |nu|(R). Stieltjes integration by parts, with the zero extension paying all endpoint atoms, gives

    integral v^(-1)(log v)^k dnu(v)=m_k-km_(k-1).

All subsequent Taylor and prime-band steps are identical. A finite first nonzero moment exists as before; right continuity rules out an isolated nonzero point invisible to all the Lebesgue moments. Thus (V11) holds for this larger fixed class. This does not apply with a total variation growing freely with N, nor with growing J, changing support, or uncontrolled endpoint atoms.

A concrete non-smooth mean-annihilator is

    h(v)=(5/9)1_[5/4,7/4)(v)-1_[7/4,9/4)(v).

It is right-continuous, bounded by 1, compactly supported away from the collar, and m0=0 exactly. Its positive and negative v^(-2)-masses are equal, with all positive mass below all negative mass, so m1<0. Its complete response at one prime is exactly

    -(5/9)S_ceil(5p^r/4)+(14/9)S_ceil(7p^r/4)
                      -S_ceil(9p^r/4).                 (V13)

The ceilings and the half-open endpoints are part of the formula. The resulting full response has the same order and coefficient pattern as (V10), with this profile's m1. Four initial rational cases all gave zero, so their evidentiary value was weak; they are retained. A fifth case (N,p,q,r)=(441,7,6,1) gives exactly 5/9 under the original coefficient sum, discrete summation by parts and (V13). These checks include grid-aligned and misaligned jumps and principal natural zeros. They do not prove the asymptotic, whose proof is (V12) and the imported fixed-order estimate.
title: 7. Independent extension: fixed bounded-variation profiles

statement:
## 4. Why this changes the live source contract

The old SW41 obstruction showed that absolute summation of all future repetitions diverges for sigma<=1; its text explicitly left signed arithmetic-wavelet capture open. B4-B6 go further for the exact fixed-q Haar frame: even optimal signed combinations cannot approximate the target, and a fixed finite arithmetic starting fit cannot repair it. This is a restriction of the broader F08.N1 proposal, which permits arbitrary balanced n f_n-m f_m. Those larger families and the full original f_n space are NOT ruled out.

Any finite family of dilation ratios that are powers of one integer base shares a nonreal lattice and has the same obstruction (replace q by that base in the annihilating lattice). Merely adding more dyadic widths or smoothing coefficients within the same frame does not help.

The weakest plausible repair is to introduce genuinely incommensurable integer dilation ratios at unbounded stages, for example 2 and 3. Their factors 1-2^(1-s) and 1-3^(1-s) have no common nonreal zero: a common zero would force 2^a=3^b for positive integers a,b. At s=1 the canceled factors have values eta_2(1)=log2 and eta_3(1)=log3. Zeta zeros remain common as required. Absence of artificial common zeros is only a necessary repair; it is not arithmetic closure. Adding only finitely many q=3 wavelets is still a finite arithmetic seed and is ruled out by B6, so the second family must grow.

The literal repaired extension is

 (W_(q,N)R)(k)=sum_(j>=1) b_q(j) R(floor(k/j)),
 b_q(j)=1-q 1_(q divides j),                                (B9)

obtained by replacing SW34 with sum_(n=N)^(2N) [R(n)-R(n-1)] w_(q,n). It retains every later repetition, including all q=2 versus q=3 mixed products in a combined energy. Prefix preservation and the first-shell equality still hold because b_q(1)=1. No common-grid tail or mixed Gram term is silently inherited.

OPEN REPAIR: prove a full signed compatible capture or source-resolvent estimate for such a genuinely enlarged arithmetic frame at a fixed sigma<.874865. In the capture formulation, exact successive orthogonal projections give d_(j+1)^2=d_j^2-g_j; a sufficient complete estimate is g_j>=delta_j d_j^2 with sum delta_j=infinity. No positive decay rate is intrinsically required, but every full-tail norm, every cross-grid interaction, and every step of the fixed arithmetic span must be included. The one-grid theorem proves that this condition cannot hold indefinitely for the unpatched fixed-q source.
title: 4. Why this changes the live source contract

## 3. A concrete simultaneous two-filter detector

The protected S42 audit derives, for the SAME actual f3*chi field,

    G_lambda(x)=F_chi(x)-lambda^beta F_chi(x/lambda),
    Mellin(G_lambda)(s)=(1-lambda^(beta-s)) Mellin(F_chi)(s).

Both complete filtered gamma moments, for lambda=2 and 3, exclude zeros in
gamma<Re(s)<1 except possibly one simple real zero at s=beta. Their only
common symbol zero is beta: a nonreal one would make log2/log3 rational.
Higher multiplicity at beta would still leave a pole. For zeta the real
exception is absent by positivity of its alternating series. For a general
fixed character it must be retained unless separately excluded, or beta<=gamma.
This proves a useful conditional joint return. The two arithmetic moment
hypotheses are OPEN; neither follows from filtering an incumbent bound.

Simultaneous Diophantine approximation also makes both symbols arbitrarily
small along unbounded heights. There is no fixed positive uniform gain.
This does not invalidate qualitative zero detection at each fixed zero.
Changing a counterterm with scale introduces an additional exact error:
to cancel a nonzero beta-mode down to gamma<beta requires coefficient
accuracy of order X^(-(beta-gamma)). A mere o(1) error is insufficient.

The uniform S22 audit supplies the sharp positive-range/readout price for
a signed realization. For v=(u,Ku), ||K||=kappa<1,

    ||v||^2 <= (1+kappa^2)/(1-kappa^2) * v*diag(I,-I)v.

For the actual readout d*u, the best constant is d*(I-K*K)^-1 d.
A signature count or small indefinite energy alone gives no positive bound.
The native Gaussian matrix remains its actual positive Gram; no arithmetic
graph-range condition or near-null alignment is proved by this finite audit.
title: 3. A concrete simultaneous two-filter detector

## 8. Paid portions of the small-gcd norm

All conductor ranges below are disjointly assigned: first Q<=U^(9/5), then its complement with Q1/Q3<=U^(8/5). There are only O((log U)^3) ranges because n,n' have polynomial support.

For total conductor Q<=V0, use `V>=Q` in (7.2). The number of oriented vectors per radical is divisor bounded. Partial summation of the linear ideal count gives

    sum_(Nq<=V0) (Nq)^(-1/2+5/12+epsilon)
      <<V0^(11/12+epsilon).

Thus this complete absolute off-diagonal contribution is at most

    H_J U^(1/6+epsilon) V0^(11/12),
    hence H_J U^(109/60+epsilon) at V0=U^(9/5).       (8.1)

The ratio sector follows from (7.3) and the trivial U branch of (7.5):

    H_J U^(1+epsilon) (U^(8/5))^(1/2)
      =H_J U^(9/5+epsilon).                         (8.2)

Both estimates are for the original signed expression after taking its absolute majorant on these sectors; their positivity is not assumed in the full norm. They include all Q2 values and shared columns, not merely coprime squarefree pairs.

The uniform coarse target floor is

    T_mix >=(17/25)(217/100)+19/54
           =3689/2500+19/54.                         (8.3)

Its gaps above 109/60 and 9/5 exceed 1/100; the diagonal exponent 1 has much larger reserve. Exact fractions are retained in the numerical receipt. Consequently the complete diagonal and the two paid off-diagonal sectors are bounded by `H_J U^[T_mix-1/200+epsilon]` after the same finite loss allocation. These coarse cuts are not asserted optimal and are not the main innovation of this report.
title: 8. Paid portions of the small-gcd norm

statement:
## G104. Actual finite character traces and their exact limitation

The squarefree prime polynomial P_X(z)=sum_(n<=X,(n,q0)=1)mu(n)z(n) has
torus norm squared Q_q0(X)=sum mu(n)^2 over the same support. Its evaluation
norm is sqrt(Q_q0(X)). The actual coefficients attain this loss at z_p=-1,
where P_X=Q_q0(X)=d_q0 X+O_q0(sqrt X).

Every prescribed finite set of real prime signs is realizable by an ordinary
character. CRT selects an odd D=1 mod4, coprime to q0 and every p<=X,
with the desired quadratic residues and D=1 or5 mod8 when2 is unramified.
Then chi(n)=1_((n,q0)=1)(n/D) has those signs and exactly the q0 zeros up toX;
the extra D zeros beyondX remain. Jacobi characters and composite reciprocity
license this construction without requiring D prime or squarefree.
[NIST DLMF27.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.9) records those facts.

Thus a conductor-independent phase trace of loss X^eta with eta<1/2 fails,
even for actual arithmetic coefficients with the full inverse identity.
The realizing character changes with X. This does NOT refute fixed-character
estimates whose constant and onset depend on chi. For a fixed q, the exact
character-average trace factor is instead sqrt(phi(q)), an allowed constant;
its ambient norm contains the full same-residue signed covariance of G103.
The earlier G71 fixed-sequence asymptotic countermodel has different scope.

For sqrt X<=y<=X the complete one-large-prime complement is exactly

    M_z(X)=S_y(X)-sum_(y<p<=X,p not dividing q0) z_p A(X/p),
    R_y(X)=sum_p |A(X/p)|,

where S_y is the entire smooth part and A depends only on fixed low-prime
values. Its maximal distance from S_y is R_y and its diameter is2R_y;
this does not assert that every point in a disk is attainable. For real low
values, opposite prime signs attain S_y+/-R_y and are realized by the CRT
characters above. The exact endpoint-sensitive price is

    R_y=sum_(1<=m<=floor(X/y)) |A(m)|
       [pi_q0(X/m)-pi_q0(max(y,X/(m+1)))].

If y<=X/2 the m=1 term is at least pi_q0(X)-pi_q0(X/2), asymptotic to
X/(2log X) for fixed q0 by the ordinary prime number theorem.
[NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) supplies that asymptotic;
the identities need no PNT. This prevents uniformly sublinear phase-blind
pricing, but fixed-q characters agreeing on all unramified primes<=q are
identical, by factoring each least unit representative. Once y>=q, the
independent tail is unavailable. Global character linkage remains a live
escape, not a disproof. All smooth terms, cofactors and later cross energies
must be retained.
title: G104. Actual finite character traces and their exact limitation

statement:
## 2. Exact algebra, natural zeros and compensation

Since a*h=delta1, define

    q_p=delta1-p chi(p) delta_p,
    b_p=q_p*h=chi(l)(1-p 1_(p|l)),
    c_p=q_p*a.

The identity for b_p uses chi(p)chi(l/p)=chi(l) when p divides l, including
ramified zero values. Its period is Q=pq. Over that period,

    sum_(l=1)^Q b_p(l)=p(1-chi(p)) sum_(a=1)^q chi(a)=0.

For a nonprincipal character the last character sum vanishes. For a
principal character chi(p)=1. A ramified p would leave the principal
mean nonzero, so that exclusion is essential. A smaller primitive
conductor is neither substituted nor needed.

Write m_U=a 1_(n<=U), u_U=a-m_U, and similarly for V. Expanding gives

    u_U*u_V*b_p
      =c_p-q_p*m_U-q_p*m_V+m_U*m_V*b_p.                 (R1)

This holds at each integer, with ordered d,e, common prime factors and
all l retained. In particular c_p(n)=a(n)-p chi(p)1_(p|n)a(n/p), bounded
by p+1, and it can be nonzero at squareful integers. Such terms are real
parts of this changed detector. At integers noncoprime to q all terms
still vanish. Also f_x(pn) is not f_(x/p)(n), because b>1.

For S=m_U*m_V*b_p and R=u_U*u_V*b_p the absolute coefficient bound
p d_3(n) holds uniformly in U,V. The elementary divisor bound gives
O_(p,eta)(n^eta) for every fixed eta>0. Local absolute convergence follows
from the actual exponential damping. The two complete short sources
have modulus at most (p+1)(U+V); neither one is zero by convention.
title: 2. Exact algebra, natural zeros and compensation

statement:
## 7. Numerical growing ranges and the exact remaining obligation

Put \(K=D^k\), restrict \(q_B,q_E\le D^\lambda\), and ask for every quadratic class with \(q_d\le D^\eta\). A sufficient uniform rectangular budget is

\[
\boxed{\eta+3\lambda\le 2-\kappa-k.}
\tag{MQ24}
\]

Indeed

\[
\Delta_\kappa(B,E)
=\frac{D^{2-\kappa}
 q_{\min(B,E)}^{\,3(\kappa-1)}}{K q_{\max(B,E)}^3}
\ge D^{2-\kappa-k-3\lambda}.
\]

The min/max notation in this formula refers to the two norms only. The sharper curved sector is still MQ22.

At the current cubic scale \(k=.87653\):

| Sector | Required arithmetic input | Bare-pair class cutoff | One uniform two-cube example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sixth-power-free away from \(S\) | I-C3CF | \(q_d\le D^{.12347}\) | \(q_d\le D^{.05},\ q_B,q_E\le D^{.024}\), reserve \(.00147\) |
| Every repetition | I-C3CF and I-HECKE at \(b=7/8\), so \(\kappa=11/10\) | \(q_d\le D^{.02347}\) | \(q_d\le D^{.01},\ q_B,q_E\le D^{.004}\), reserve \(.00147\) |

Both examples allow the original double-large-core restriction \(q_c,q_e>D^{1/4}\). Their nominal smallest core scales are \(D^{.928}\) and \(D^{.988}\), respectively. The bounds concern a growing set of genuine classes, not a fixed finite family whose constants are left uncontrolled.

For the all-repetition bare pair at \(b=7/8\), the endpoint class cutoff has \(\Delta=D^{.02347}\), \(H=D^{1.12347}\), and the balancing repetition cutoff is \(T=D^{1/10}\). The short-repetition term \(X\Delta T\) and the long Möbius term \(X^{3/4}(H\Delta)^{1/2}T^{-2}\) are both exactly of order \(H\). This makes the repeated-row cost explicit. Choosing the fixed buffer \(b=.8749\) instead gives \(\kappa=1.09992\) and bare-pair cutoff \(D^{.02355}\); the limiting available exponent as \(b\downarrow b_0\) is \(.023560682368028695\ldots\), with constants fixed only after selecting a positive buffer.

The squarefree diagonal \(d=n,\ a=1,\ q_d\asymp H\) is **not** paid. In the bare pair, MQ6 reaches only \(d\le H/D\), and MQ7 only \(d\le H/D^{\kappa_b}\). The original direct cubic-sieve estimate on squarefree rows still contains

\[
H+D+(HD)^{2/3}.
\]

After the actual \(D^2/H\) covariance normalization, its last term is

\[
D^{8/3}H^{-1/3}=D^2K^{1/3}
=D^{2.292176666666\ldots}
\quad(k=.87653).
\tag{MQ25}
\]

That is the remaining upper-budget gap in the dominant primitive range, not a lower bound for the actual Möbius moment. The present proof avoids that range by genuinely summing the smaller quadratic representatives with their shorter square-root row variables. It has not frozen a moving ramified twist, invoked a conductor-uniform separate UM theorem, or identified a row conductor with the indexing norm.

The exact residual remains the unselected double-large-core C--C Poisson contribution, including the moving squarefree diagonal and the other cube-pair/class ranges, **minus the original whole II**. No II frequency, continuation addback, or Type I residue is reassigned. Closing SR18 for that actual residual, or obtaining an equivalent signed covariance estimate with both masks and the complete projector, is still an additional arithmetic obligation.
title: 7. Numerical growing ranges and the exact remaining obligation

statement:
## 2. S28: an exact deletion channel whose inverse is affordable at a true size cutoff

For real X>=1 and fixed q let D_X be the squarefree q-unit integers n<=X, including1. This is a divisor downset. Coordinates outside it have value zero. Write k(n)=omega(n), K_X=max_(D_X)k(n), 0<rho<=1, lambda=1-rho, R_rho=(2-rho)/rho. Let B_rho delete each occupied prime independently with probability lambda:

    B_rho(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^k(d) lambda^(k(n)-k(d)), d,n in D_X.    (A1)

The 0^0 convention is1. This channel acts on a finite complex measure, not a claim that prime factors of an arithmetic integer are independent. Each column sums to1. No deleted prime value or size condition is replaced by a probabilistic approximation.

### A. Exact inverse and exact norm

The inverse is

    C_rho(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^(-k(n))(-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)).           (A2)
    ||B_rho||_(l1->l1)=1,
    ||C_rho||_(l1->l1)=R_rho^K_X.                               (A3)

For d|n every intermediate e with d|e|n is still in D_X. Expanding (CB)(d,n) factors over the primes of n/d and gives (lambda-lambda)^k(n/d), with coefficient1 for d=n; the other product is the same binomial cancellation. Thus the cutoff causes no missing intermediate state. The absolute column sum of C at n is rho^(-k(n))(1+lambda)^k(n)=R_rho^k(n); taking a maximal-degree column proves equality, not merely an upper estimate.

Every squarefree integer with k primes is at least (k+1)!. Consequently

    K_X <= (1+o(1)) log X/loglog X,
    fixed rho>0: R_rho^K_X=X^o(1).                             (A4)

The factorial lower bound and integral estimate for log(k!) prove the needed upper bound without a prime theorem. This corrects a possible full-cube objection: exp(const*pi(X)) is the wrong inverse price on D_X. The number of sites may be enormous, but a surviving column occupies at most K_X sites.

For moving retention, log R_(rho_X)=o(loglog X) still suffices for subpower loss. If rho_X=(log X)^(-b), fixed b>0, then the norm is X^(b+o(1)). Here equality uses K_X~log X/loglog X, obtained from the ordinary prime number theorem and primorial products, with only finitely many q-primes removed. This is a genuine debit: such increasingly severe deletion cannot be called exponent-neutral. The PNT input is [NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12); no growing-q uniformity is used.

### B. Literal arithmetic coefficients and readout

### M2. Exact continuation and complete Gaussian readout

Before the finite changes, E v_p=theta_p=p^(beta-1). The centered independent variables xi_p=v_p-theta_p have mean zero and variance at most1. Apply the same dyadic maximal proof to the sequence equal to xi_p on primes and zero on composites. Almost surely,

  S(x)=sum_{p<=x}xi_p=O_eta(x^(1/2+eta))

for every eta>0. Abel summation then defines

  Z(s)=sum_p xi_p p^(-s)=s integral_1^infinity S(x)x^(-s-1) dx

holomorphically on Re(s)>1/2. On every fixed closed vertical strip with left edge sigma0>1/2 it satisfies |Z(s)|<=C(1+|Im s|), after choosing eta<sigma0-1/2.

For Re(s)>1 the absolutely convergent Euler product D_a(s)=sum a(n)n^(-s)=product_p(1+v_p p^(-s)) satisfies

  D_a(s)=zeta(s+1-beta) H(s),

where H is the exponential of

  Z(s)
  +sum_p sum_{j>=2} (-1)^(j+1) v_p^j p^(-js)/j
  -sum_p sum_{j>=2} p^(-j(s+1-beta))/j.

Both double tails converge absolutely and locally uniformly on Re(s)>1/2: their leading prime exponents are2 Re(s)>1 and2(Re(s)+1-beta)>1. Hence H is holomorphic and nonvanishing there, with |H(s)|<=exp(C(1+|Im s|)) on every fixed closed vertical strip. The finitely many deletions or prescriptions multiply H by factors1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) or(1+v'_p p^(-s))/(1+v_p p^(-s)). They are analytic and nonzero on Re(s)>0, with bounded modulus on any such strip; the conclusions persist. Thus D_a has a simple pole at beta with nonzero residue H(beta). No supposition about zeta zeros is needed.

Normalize the fixed Gaussian by

  g_tau(u)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2*tau)),
  F_a(x)=sum_{n>=1}a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

Absolute convergence follows from |a(n)|<=1. Mellin inversion on any line Re(s)>1 gives

  F_a(x)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral e^(tau*s^2/2)D_a(s)x^s ds.

Shift to any fixed sigma in(1/2,beta). Zeta has at most polynomial growth on the fixed strip in question, for example by Euler--Maclaurin summation; H has the exponential bound above. The factor exp(-tau*t^2/2) therefore pays the entire infinite-height integral and both horizontal sides. The sole pole crossed is beta. This proves

  F_a(x)=e^(tau*beta^2/2)H(beta)x^beta+O_sigma(x^sigma).

The leading constant is nonzero. This is the complete Gaussian, with no height truncation or omitted tails. The same proof permits fixed derivatives. As x tends to zero, the original absolutely convergent sum is smaller than every positive power of x: for each A>1 use g_tau(log(n/x))<=C_A(x/n)^A. This pays the other end of later Mellin transforms.

## 4. Why finite-atlas uniformity is legitimate

The relevant order is: choose this numerical finite atlas; for a requested loss choose one common mesh and small positive budgets; then fix the finite original slot system and target arithmetic family; choose the final finite orders, constants and one eventual threshold; only then allow live scales, masks, subsets, rows, and independent heights.

The exact amplification interfaces quantify all original data and widths after their eventual threshold. Fixed sigma_j and common polynomial envelopes therefore do not produce a separate uncontrolled threshold for each live width. A maximum over fifty thresholds and four derivative-profile pairs is finite. Taking a maximum of finite height orders is also allowed. The smallest positive amplifier and the compact normalized geometry bound all representation constants and polynomial raw envelopes.

The atlas index is determined by fixed total selected-slot width and the outer M, not the row being summed or either plain scale in a scale-supremum rectangle. The classwise selection theorem in SS fixes the same subset throughout an amplitude class. Thus both the subset and j are fixed for the moment call, and differentiation does not cross atlas boundaries. Varying outer Euler shifts, selected subsets or dyads only selects among already simultaneous estimates. It creates no additional growing reconstruction label or density dictionary. A finite partition, if explicitly summed, costs a constant.

FM supplies Euler derivative bounds for `K(B product y_i^e_i)` uniformly for B>0 and one common Fourier majorant before labels. The Hilbert direct sum retains all first labels inside the norm. The diagonal contraction has norm at most one. The same reasoning applies to all four derivative pairs and all fifty radii without a `Z^(const*a_j)` seminorm loss.

The density's internal height exponent and the later external truncation exponent remain distinct. Fix the target's final density degree, then take external height exponent small enough for the common positive reserves; choose sufficiently high derivative/height orders backward through the finite graph and Fourier-tail orders afterward. Very large independent input heights are paid by a fixed polynomial height allowance and the common bounded raw envelope. Constants/orders/threshold may depend on the fixed family and finite slots, but the numerical reserve and mesh need not depend on the target dictionary.

In the endpoint `U=Z^d` with `d0<=d<=h+zeta0`, `d0=1/200`. A common U-threshold is reached for all d once `Z>=U0^(1/d0)`. A requested Z-loss is met by choosing the normalized U-loss no larger than that Z-loss divided by the fixed upper d bound. This explicitly pays the continuum of outer d values. No uniformity in an unbounded M range or moving conductor has been inferred.

statement:
## 8. Independent complete energy bound and its generic sharpness

For ANY fixed sequence |a_n|<=1 and fixed b>1, let V_b have the same
literal damping and phase. Then

    integral_X^(2X)|V_b(x)|^2 dx/x <<_b X^(b+1).         (R16)

This requires no Mobius identity, conductor information or epsilon.
Here is a direct proof retaining the infinite source and variable damping.
Set d=1/[2(2X)^b] and

    G(z)=sum_(n>=1)a_n exp(-dn)z^n.

It is analytic past the closed unit disk. For x in [X,2X], write
theta=1/x and Delta=x^(-b)-d. Then d<=Delta<=(2^(b+1)-1)d and
V_b(x)=G(exp(-Delta-i theta)). The subharmonic Poisson inequality,
which also follows from Cauchy--Schwarz in the Poisson representation,
gives

    |G(exp(-Delta-i theta))|^2
      <=(1/(2*pi)) integral_0^(2*pi) P_Delta(theta-phi)
                                         |G(exp(-i phi))|^2 dphi,
    P_Delta(t)=sinh(Delta)/(cosh(Delta)-cos t).

Since Delta is between d and C_b d, P_Delta(t)<=C'_b P_d(t)
uniformly in t for X large: increase the numerator to sinh(C_b d)
and decrease the denominator to cosh d-cos t. The ratio
sinh(C_b d)/sinh d is bounded by a b-dependent constant.

Now dx/x=dtheta/theta<=2X dtheta in absolute value. Integrate theta
over [1/(2X),1/X], enlarge that interval to one full period only in
the positive Poisson integral, and use its mass 2*pi. Parseval gives

    E_b(X)<=C_b X sum_n |a_n|^2 exp(-2dn)
            <=C_b X/d <<_b X^(b+1).

The Poisson domination, rather than an unproved substitution of fixed
damping, is what licenses this complete varying-profile estimate.

The exponent is sharp for uniform bounds over arbitrary bounded arrays
at a single scale. Take N=floor(X^b), x0=3X/2, and a_n=exp(in/x0)
for 1<=n<=N, zero otherwise. Where |1/x-1/x0|<=1/(4N), the real part
of every rotated term is positive and bounded below by a fixed constant;
the sum has size >>_b N. This interval lies in [X,2X] for large X and
has logarithmic measure comparable to X/N. Its energy is >>_b NX.
These coefficients depend on X and are not mu(n)chi(n). The example
only proves sharpness of the generic certificate, not of the arithmetic
source or of a theorem for a single preselected coefficient sequence.

At b=3/2, (R16) improves the author's unconditional energy statement by
removing epsilon, but carries NO arithmetic exponent gain. Its exponent
is 5/2, still far above 1.7497080728. The pointwise theorem (R10)
is not subsumed by (R16); converting the latter back to pointwise
control by the next section recovers only the trivial x^b exponent.
title: 8. Independent complete energy bound and its generic sharpness

statement:
## 5. A reusable comparison lemma, with its limits

Use section4's F and rectangle, with A,B,D0,C,C0,h positive. Suppose the
old fixed-h top boundary at ell0 and capacity C0 has

    b0-F0 >= [A(delta-delta0)^2+B(1/2-p)]/D0,

and an accepted endpoint ensures kappa<=kappa0. Keep h, increase ell by
L>0, decrease the probe boundary by L/4, and replace C0 by C<C0 with
h>4ell. On a patch [d_-,d_+] x [p_-,1/2] inside that rectangle, put
r=min(delta0-d_-,d_+-delta0)>0. Define

    deformation_all = L[3/4+(3/8)(1+2/C0)],
    deformation_patch = L[3/4+(d_+/2)(1+2/C0)],
    gain_patch = d_- p_- (h-4ell)/2 (1/C-1/C0),
    gap_outside = min(A*r^2,B*(1/2-p_-))/D0.

If gain_patch>deformation_patch and gap_outside>deformation_all, their
two positive differences give a uniform new top margin. The proof is
exactly E1-E3 and the complement disjunction; favorable gain outside
the patch is discarded. Endpoints can use strict enclosures of the
algebraic old parameters, as this packet does.

This certificate adds no moment or density estimate. Physical geometry,
shortening, supply, shifts, other rows and common-saving order must still
be proved. The fixed-h specialization need not optimize the endpoint.
