statement:
## 3. No illicit growing-conductor step

The moving coprimality in E3 can be controlled from a fixed-character M bound by an explicit finite Euler removal. If |M_chi(t)|<=C t^alpha for all t>=1 and some fixed alpha>0, then

    sum_(k<=T,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k)
       =sum_(r<=T, every prime of r divides m)chi(r)M_chi(T/r),

so its magnitude is at most

    C T^alpha product_(p|m)(1-p^-alpha)^-1.            (E8)

For fixed 0<alpha<1 and m<=N, that finite product is exp(O_alpha((log(2N))^(1-alpha))), hence N^o(1), uniformly in m. To see this without a prime asymptotic, split at L=log(2N). The small-prime contribution to sum_(p|m)p^-alpha is bounded by sum_(2<=n<=L)n^-alpha=O_alpha(L^(1-alpha)); the large-prime contribution is at most (log N/log2)L^-alpha. Also -log(1-p^-alpha)<=C_alpha p^-alpha. The exact removal is therefore sufficient for this specific induced-character family. It grants no uniformity over arbitrary growing primitive conductors.

Even E8 only gives an exponent1 total after summing the complete dual in absolute value. The elementary E7 already gives that exponent without an inherited zero-free premise. There is no unearned gain from using the accepted baseline on the short factors.
title: 3. No illicit growing-conductor step

statement:
## 4. Exact far and near reconstruction; proof of SF10

First regroup each linear block at the ORIGINAL integer norm m=q_n,
retaining the sum over all ideal labels of norm m. This is only a
regrouping of a finite sum, and does not treat an ideal as an integer.

For H>=0 integer, if H exceeds the maximum original norm difference,
the strict far set is empty. Otherwise H=O(N) in this common original
N dyad. Choose a containing power-of-two interval for x=m and y=m'+H;
it has width O(N), hence O(log(2N)) tree levels. For internal nodes J,

    1_(m>m'+H)
      = sum_J 1_(m in J_R) 1_(m' in J_L-H).          (R6)

For x>y the two values have one unique lowest common ancestor, with
x in its right child and y in its left. This is the unique contributing
node. For x<=y no node contributes. Thus (R6) is exact, including x=y
and all endpoints. On a given level the right-child intervals are
pairwise disjoint; the left-child intervals remain pairwise disjoint
after translation by -H.

The reverse condition `m'>m+H` has its OWN identical construction with
the two sides exchanged. For independent arrays it must not be silently
replaced by a conjugate or twice a real part. Adding the two exact
formulas gives `1_(|m-m'|>H)`. Both ideal orientations at equal rational
norm, and the actual diagonal, are absent. This is an exact exclusion,
not an estimate of only the pairs n=n'.

Now keep the original true short-core scalar. Its complete inversion is

    h((g,g')) = sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f),
    r_h(f) = sum_(a|f) mu(f/a)h(a),
    |r_h(f)| <= tau(f)                             (R7)

for |h|<=1. The core is still (g,g'), not a core recomputed from de.
Every original g window, rational-primitivity/opposite restriction,
finite phase, and perpendicular mask is retained. For active f,
q_f is O(G), and the number of original g divisible by f is O(G/q_f),
including bounded or unit ranges. Inactive f contributes zero.

At one fixed tree level and one f, let I_j,J_j be the paired disjoint
interval families in (R6). For a fixed pair g,g', put

    X_j(R)=xi(g)A_1(g)chi_R(g)^3 V_(I_j),1(R,g),
    Y_j(R)=xi(g')A_2(g')chi_R(g')^3 V_(J_j),2(R,g').

Every factor shown here is the original one. For any bounded normalized
row weight w, Cauchy in the JOINT finite coordinates (R,j) gives

    |sum_R,j w(R) X_j(R) conjugate(Y_j(R))|
      <= (sum_R,j |w(R)| |X_j(R)|^2)^(1/2)
         (sum_R,j |w(R)| |Y_j(R)|^2)^(1/2).          (R8)

There are O(K) original rows. Apply (R5) uniformly to each fixed R,g,
and use its independent counterpart on side two. Triangle over the
O(G/q_f) short labels on each side then gives

    << Z^epsilon K (G/q_f)^2 N
       ell_(side 1) ell_(side 2) sqrt(T T')
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                 (R9)

Here each side chooses the better completed d/e orientation, and each
ell is bounded by O(log(2N)). Equivalently one may first form each
short-source linear vector and use Minkowski in (R,j), as the report
does. The original common separated row weight permits that order.

For clarity, even if a bounded paired row weight depends on BOTH g,g',
one can put triangle over the ordered g,g' pairs BEFORE (R8), retaining
their individual weight inside (R8). This proves the identical bound
(R9) with no factorization assumption on that bounded short-pair row
weight. A new arbitrary mask depending jointly on live m,m' is NOT
covered by this clarification; only the original core and the exact
interval mask have been treated.

The zero of chi_R(f)^3 is present in the original X/Y until their
positive norms; no cancellation of that zero has occurred. Signs of
r_h are likewise present in (R7) until triangle is explicitly taken.
Summing the complete f expansion costs

    sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2 < infinity,

or the weaker allowed subpower factor. The convergence follows, for
example, by ideal counting and a divisor bound with any exponent <1.
There is no unreturned low/high-f remainder. Summing O(log(2N)) levels
and the two ordered orientations proves

    |C_far[h]| << Z^epsilon K G^2 N sqrt(T T')
                 sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig,       (R10)

with explicit additional interval overhead at most O(log^3(2N)). This
is SF11. Independent interval choices on the two sides cost no interval
count because (R8) pairs their vectors in the same node coordinate and
SF2 controls each entire disjoint family separately.

Finally, before any estimate the full complementary mask satisfies

    C_near = C_all - C_(m>m'+H) - C_(m'>m+H).         (R11)

C_all has the same bound from a single interval and the same full core
inversion; each strict orientation is paid above. Equation (R11) pays
ALL pairs with |m-m'|<=H, including distinct ideals of equal norm and
the diagonal. It is valid for independent arrays and both heights.
It gives no inherited estimate for an arbitrary submask of C_near.
The auxiliary near term `(H+1)L` in [private research revision] D6 is therefore unnecessary
at this restricted scope. The sharper original-prime near-graph theorem
remains separate and is not used on composites here.

statement:
### 2.2 Exact Poisson transform and uniform stationary term

Fix a high output block N and put T=(N/X)^k>=1. Remove exactly empty rows m>4N before transformation. Group the remaining m into frozen dyadic intervals [M,2M) intersect [1,D] intersect [1,4N]. Thus m/N<=4 and M<=4N. Extend the smoothly supported summand by zero to all real n and apply Poisson to the periodic Fourier expansion. With the appropriate periodic Fourier coefficients beta_h,

    sum_l h(l) w(ml/N) f_x(ml)
      =(1/m) sum_(h in Z) beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    beta_(Qj)=0,
    I_r(x)=int_0^infinity w(n/N)e^(-n/x^b)
                          exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^k]) dn.      (2.1)

The integer alias h here is distinct from the original periodic sequence h(l). Both alias signs and every nonzero Fourier residue occur. Mean zero deletes every beta_(Qj), not just the single zero alias.

For r>0 the unique critical point is

    n_r=(2pi r/(kQ))^(1/(k-1)) x^(k/(k-1)),
    Phi_r=(k-1)(2pi r/(kQ))^(k/(k-1)) x^(k/(k-1)),
    Z_r=sqrt(2pi/[k(k-1)]) x^(k/2) n_r^(-(k-2)/2)
                                      w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^b).

Fix a near range cT/N<=r<=CT/N, with constants depending only on Q,k, wide enough to contain every critical point meeting the smooth output support for all x in [X,2X]. Write x=Xz, n=Nt, rho=N/X^b and R=rN/T. The normalized phase is

    T psi_(R,z)(t), psi=2pi Rt/Q-t^k/z^k.

Here z in [1,2], R in a fixed positive compact interval, and the critical point t0 lies in another fixed positive compact interval. Its second derivative is negative and bounded away from zero there. Every fixed derivative of the damped amplitude w(t)e^(-rho t/z^b) is O_j(e^(-c rho)) on the positive support, with a smaller fixed c after absorbing powers of rho.

For completeness, choose a uniformly small smooth neighborhood of t0. Away from it, two integrations by parts give O(T^-2 e^(-c rho)). Near it, the one-dimensional Morse coordinate

    y=sign(t-t0) sqrt(psi(t0)-psi(t))

has uniformly bounded derivatives and inverse derivatives. The transformed compact amplitude B has the same derivative bounds and B(0)=a(t0)sqrt(2/|psi''(t0)|). Write B(y)=B(0)kappa(y)+y C(y), with a fixed even bump kappa equal to one near zero. The y C term is O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)) by one integration by parts; the kappa term is the Fresnel integral plus a smaller nonstationary error. This gives, after restoring N,

    I_r=Z_r exp(i Phi_r-i pi/4)
                  +O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^b)).                   (2.2)

The argument is uniform even when t0 crosses either endpoint of w's smooth support: the amplitude, extended smoothly by zero, remains in the same bounded family. No sharp output truncation was substituted inside a stationary formula. No derivative of the remainder is needed later.
title: 2.2 Exact Poisson transform and uniform stationary term

statement:
## 3. A dimension-four obstruction on the ACTUAL Jordan middle

This theorem permits arbitrary X-dependent quaternion directions, not merely one constant embedding. Fix the source above and gamma in (0,1). Let either I_X be all positive integers, or precisely the G215 retained set

    I_X={n: X^alpha<n<=2X log X},
    alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2).

For n in I_X put w_n=|a_n K(n/X)|. When w_n>0 put
xi_n=a_n K(n/X)/w_n, so |xi_n|=1. All original coefficient zeros stay zero. Choose ANY quaternions

    v_n=z_n+t_n j, z_n=xi_n, N(v_n)<=C^2, C>=1,       (12)

with C fixed independently of X; set v_n=0 when w_n=0. No arithmetic independence is assumed. The encoded field Q_X=sum_n w_n v_n has first complex channel exactly the complete Phi(X), or the exact retained Cmid(X), respectively. Hence the scalar square is at most N(Q_X).

Consider the particular positive certificate obtained by taking absolute values of the POINTWISE expanded quaternion Gram:

    B_+(X)=sum_(d,e in I_X) w_d w_e
                       |Re(v_d conjugate(v_e))|.      (13)

It includes both orientations and the diagonal. Then the unconditional bound is

    B_+(X) >= [sum_(n in I_X) w_n]^2/(4C^2).           (14)

Proof. Regard H as R^4 and form the positive matrix S=sum_n w_n v_n v_n^T. Its trace is at least sum w_n because (12) implies N(v_n)>=|z_n|^2=1. Its rank is at most 4, so tr(S^2)>=(tr S)^2/4. On the other hand tr(S^2)=sum w_d w_e (v_d dot v_e)^2, and |v_d dot v_e|<=C^2. Thus (13)>=tr(S^2)/C^2, proving (14). Finite truncation followed by monotone convergence proves the statement for the full infinite source; all sums converge since sum |a_n K(n/X)| is finite.

G216 supplies the ACTUAL, character-specific weighted squarefree asymptotic

    sum_n w_n=kappa_q X I_K+O(sqrt X),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1),
    I_K=integral_0^infinity |K(t)|dt>0.                (15)

For I_X equal to the retained middle, the removed absolute mass is O(X^gamma)+O(X^-1), so its sum is still kappa_q I_K X+o(X). Therefore for BOTH actual source choices,

    B_+(X)>=(kappa_q^2 I_K^2/(4C^2)+o(1))X^2.         (16)

Integrating the pointwise majorant over the complete real shell retains exponent 2. It cannot establish an energy exponent 2gamma<2 for any fixed gamma<1. This applies even though the diagonal alone has exponent 1 and is already affordable at gamma>1/2.

For the explicit principal q=1,r=2,m=0 source,

    K_0(t)=e^(-t)(1-e^(-t))/(1+e^(-t))^3>0,
    I_K=1/4, integral K_0^2=1/60,
    B_+(X)>=(1/(64C^2 zeta(2)^2)+o(1))X^2.            (17)

The diagonal of (13) is at most C^2[X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X)]. Thus a quadratic cost persists in the absolute OFF-diagonal price too. This is not a lower bound on N(Q_X), |Phi|^2, the actual signed cross form, or (7). Negative Gram entries can still cancel.

The reconstruction condition in (12) matters. If C=1, |z_n|=1 forces t_n=0: there is no second-channel freedom at all. For C>1 bounded, the rank proof shows why finite extra directions do not change this certificate's exponent. More generally, in real dimension d with a scalar/complex readout ell of norm L and ||v_n||<=C, exact ell(v_n)=xi_n gives

    L^2 B_+(X) >= [sum w_n]^2/[d(CL)^2].              (18)

Indeed ||v_n||>=1/L and the same trace proof applies. Rescaling the lift cannot hide a cost: CL is invariant under reciprocal rescaling of lift and readout. A necessary condition for this particular positive certificate to reach X^(2gamma+epsilon) is d(CL)^2 at least X^(2-2gamma-epsilon), up to constants. This is not sufficient. It leaves growing dimension, unbounded conditioning with a fully paid return, and source-specific signed comparisons eligible.

The scope is pointwise absolute Gram payment. Taking an absolute value only AFTER integrating a signed pair over x, or retaining a collective companion deficit such as (7), is a different certificate and is not excluded by (14). Nor is the full automorphic spinor space four-dimensional: four real quaternion coordinates at one point must not be confused with a function-space rank bound.
title: 3. A dimension-four obstruction on the ACTUAL Jordan middle

statement:
## 4. W47-26: what the Ward defect actually costs

For a finite prime set \(\mathcal P\), use the exterior basis S and supertrace (\operatorname{Str}Z=\sum_S(-1)^{|S|}Z_{SS}). With the ordering strings in the CAR creators,
\[
 Q=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}w_pa_p^*,\quad W=\sum_p|w_p|^2>0,
 \qquad Q^2=0,\quad QQ^*+Q^*Q=WI.
\]
For even Z, finite-dimensional supertrace cyclicity gives
\[
 \operatorname{Str}(Q^*[Q,Z])=W\operatorname{Str}Z. \tag{R10}
\]
For diagonal Z, mixed-prime traces vanish and **each individual prime term** is (|w_p|^2\operatorname{Str}Z). There is no square-root-of-prime-count cancellation among these terms.

Taking $Z_{SS}=\chi(n_S)g_\tau(\log(n_S/x))$, $n_S=\prod_{p\in S}p$, yields $\operatorname{Str}Z=U_{\mathcal P}(x)$, exactly the finite squarefree Gaussian field. Ramified χ makes corresponding entries zero. Taking Euler entries instead yields $\prod_p(1-z_p)$, with no zero for $|z_p|<1$; this is a finite-product diagnostic, not the physical zero theorem.

If $\mathcal P_X$ contains every prime up to $2X\exp(C\sqrt{\log X})$, every omitted squarefree n exceeds that cutoff. Direct summation of the bounded-coefficient Gaussian tail gives $|U-U_{\mathcal P_X}|\le X^{1-C^2/(2\tau)+o(1)}$ uniformly on the shell. Hence $D_X/W_X=U_{\mathcal P_X}$ has an exponent-equivalent return when this error is below γ. **Without division by W, raw defect exponents shift with its size.** Rescaling the weights already demonstrates why raw equivalence cannot be invariant. One may normalize $\sum|w_p|^2=1$, in which case the wording becomes literally valid.

The full boundary thus re-encodes the entire source; a spectral gap alone does not pay it. This scoped failure leaves room for a different differential with an independently cheaper total defect. Credit round31/T26's exterior supertrace and the related W46/Hodge defect now accepted in G74; neither their existence nor the current consensus proves a moment. The finite prime-subset U construction is not identical to W46's actual f3 channels.
title: 4. W47-26: what the Ward defect actually costs

## 4. Physical normalization and embedding sum

Multiply HC16 by \(\sqrt R\) from row Poisson and by the raw normalization \((Y_DY_E)^{-1}\). For a fixed radical this gives
\(Z^\epsilon(Y_DY_E)^{-1/3}\). PC9's physical factor is exactly
\[
\frac1{Q\sqrt{q_Dq_E}}.
\]
The fixed-\((D,E,\mathfrak r)\) bound is therefore
\[
Z^\epsilon\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|}
{QY^{2/3}(q_Dq_E)^{1/6}}. \tag{HC17}
\]
For the original fixed slot subsets,
\[
\sum_D\frac{|\omega_D|}{q_D^{1/6}}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon L^{5/6}.
\]
There are \(O(T)\) good radicals of norm at most \(T\); this proves HC1. For \(R=1\), use the discrepancy version of HC5-HC6 and the same mass calculation. In particular PC10 improves to
\[
\sum_{R=1}|C_{\lambda\mu}-Z_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\frac{L^{5/3}}{QY^{2/3}}.
\]
PC11 still supplies the absolute complete-zero bound \(Z^\epsilon/Y\), proving HC2.

The proof sums absolute atom-pair row covariances after each row sum. Hence arbitrary bounded row-independent masks, including true-gcd cutoffs and true gcd one, are permitted. It does not infer positivity for a gcd mask, allow arbitrary row-dependent masks, or define a pair-dependent vector projection.

statement:
# Independent review: compensated squarefree chains



## 1. Decision

**Accept the component theorems and conditional return, with the observation-norm clarification below.** The literal twisted squarefree Redheffer determinant, prime-cover exponential, all-depth positive-chain exponent, common-filter fixed-color payment, complete Newton remainder and every p-valuation survive independent reconstruction. The author has proved an arithmetic bound for a complete finite collection of chain sectors, including principal characters; the result is more than a change of notation for an unknown norm.

There is no proof of the full signed remainder estimate OPEN-RHCHAIN, no c gain and no improved Mertens exponent. The determinant and conditional return are exact source interfaces. The positive-chain and projected-prime lower prices apply only to their stated positive or projected objects. They do not lower-bound the complete signed determinant or filtered tail. The new source remains an ordinary fixed-character architecture; it does not acquire a native Hecke or Gao-source admission by analogy.

The review adds a modest complete endpoint improvement. For the same common fixed filter, the t=1 color costs O(sqrt x), the t=2 color costs O(sqrt x log^3(2x)), and the entire first J chain sectors cost **O(x^(1-1/J)) for every fixed J>=3**, without an epsilon loss. For J=2 the complete low-chain bound is O(sqrt x log^3(2x)). This follows from the actual Euler correction, not an unproved divisor-problem estimate. The proof is in Section5 and support.md. It changes no target c and does not control the remaining tail.

One sentence needs correction: author line376 calls an unspecified L2 condition stronger than the pointwise sharp-source hypothesis. For the usual multiplicative-shell L2 norm at the same exponent, the implication runs from the pointwise bound to L2. Section7 proves the weaker complete shell-L1 return directly, without changing the sharp source or discarding a complement. The author's actual pointwise implication remains correct; neither version's arithmetic input is proved.

Current source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and gamma11=.8748540364 are unchanged. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain open. Near .1252, 1/6 and 1/4 are conditional targets. Root owns acceptance and integration; this review makes no literature-priority claim.

## 2. The literal matrix source, including its characteristic polynomial

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, with its natural zero extension. For every real x>=1 take the actual finite divisor downset

    D_x={n<=x: mu^2(n)=1, (n,q)=1}.

Every divisor of an element remains in this set. Nonunits and nonsquarefree integers already contribute zero to mu(n)chi(n); excluding them changes neither M_chi(x) nor an endpoint convention. All matrix indices below are the increasing ordering of D_x. Let N=|D_x|, e be the coordinate of 1 and v=1-e. Define

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(n/d prime),
    P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.

No character value zero is inverted. The matrices B,P are strictly upper triangular. If d|n, the ratio n/d has distinct prime factors. A path of exactly k prime-cover edges exists precisely when omega(n/d)=k, and then all k! permutations of those factors lie inside the original downset. Their weights telescope to chi(n/d). Thus for k>=0,

    B^k(d,n)=k! chi(n/d)1_(d|n,omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z,
    exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).                  (2.1)

All exponentials are finite polynomials, so no limiting operator norm or analytic semigroup assertion is hidden here. Since det Z=1, the determinant lemma gives

    det R=1+e^T Z^(-1)v=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n).             (2.2)

The identity retains the closed cutoff n<=x and all ordinary natural zeros. It is the independently derived twisted squarefree specialization of the finite-poset construction. Wilf's Theorem2 supplies its classical ancestry, not the new arithmetic bounds below. [Wilf, pp.1-4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408263v1).

Let K=max_(n in D_x)omega(n). If K>=1, strict divisor chains give

    A_k=e^T P^k v=sum_(n in D_x,n>1)chi(n) k! S(omega(n),k),
    P^(K+1)=0.

Indeed a strict chain from 1 to n is an ordered partition of its distinct prime factors into k nonempty blocks. For y=lambda-1 and y!=0, the rank-one resolvent formula is

    det(lambda I-R)=y^N[1-e^T(yI-P)^(-1)v].

The k=0 resolvent coefficient vanishes because e^T v=0. Expanding the finite inverse, then using polynomial identity at y=0, proves

    det(lambda I-R)
      =y^(N-K-1)[y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k y^(K-k)].        (2.3)

At least N-K-1 eigenvalues are 1. The multiplicity may be larger if the twisted top coefficient A_K cancels. No full-integer exact-multiplicity theorem is imported. If K=0, D_x={1} and R=(1); this is handled separately. At y=-1, (2.3) agrees with det(-R)=(-1)^N det R, so the alternating chain sign is correct.

The product of j distinct primes is at least (j+1)!, giving K=O(log(2x)/loglog(3x)). This degree estimate does not bound the value at y=-1 or the product of the nontrivial roots. Vaughan's characteristic calculation is classical ancestry only; its full-integer spectral conclusions are not transferred to this altered support. [Vaughan, printed pp.283-286](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf).

## 3. The entire positive chain mass really has exponent one

Write F_0=1 and F_j=sum_(k=1)^j k!S(j,k) for j>=1. The map that orders each block internally, concatenates the blocks and records cuts injects ordered set partitions into permutations with cuts. Therefore F_j<=2^(j-1)j!.

Fix sigma>1. With w_p=p^-sigma, choose a finite prime cutoff Y so that R_sigma=sum_(p>Y)w_p<1/4. If r is the number of small primes, the elementary symmetric functions obey

    e_j(all)=sum_(a+b=j,0<=a<=r)e_a(small)e_b(tail),
    e_b(tail)<=R_sigma^b/b!.

For each fixed a, the complete contribution after multiplying by the bound for F_j is bounded by a fixed constant times

    sum_(b>=0)(2R_sigma)^b (a+b)!/b!.

The factorial ratio is a polynomial of fixed degree a; this converges. Summing the finite choices of a proves

    sum_(n squarefree) F_(omega(n)) n^-sigma < infinity.  (3.1)

The n=1 term is harmless and included. This argument pays ALL depths at once, including those increasing with x; it does not substitute a fixed-depth model. Rankin's inequality gives

    P_q(x):=sum_(n in D_x)F_(omega(n)) <<_(q,epsilon)x^(1+epsilon). (3.2)

For the principal character the actual Redheffer matrix is nonnegative. Every nonidentity cycle in a contributing permutation must contain 1, and it is exactly a strict divisor chain; all other coordinates are fixed points. Consequently P_q(x) is its permanent, and 1+sum_k|A_k|=P_q(x) for that character. For a twisted matrix it is an upper bound on the sum of absolute determinant terms and on 1+sum_k|A_k|. No norm or determinant lower bound is inferred after introducing phases.

The positive price is at least |D_x|. Directly expanding mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) and counting q-units yields

    |D_x|=delta_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    delta_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.    (3.3)

The O_q(sqrt x) pays every floor and the omitted tail of sum mu(d)/d^2. Hence log P_q(x)/log x tends to 1. This is the exact meaning of a sharp exponent-one positive price; no precise logarithmic asymptotic is claimed.

The claimed semigroup warning is also correct. On D_x, U=diag(chi(n)) is unitary and U B_chi U^(-1)=B_1. With J0=diag((-1)^omega(n)), J0 B_1 J0=-B_1. It follows that

    ||exp(-B_chi)||_(2->2)=||exp(B_1)||_(2->2).

The rank-one closing column transforms to Uv and retains the character. It cannot be dropped. Compressing the Hermitian part of -B_1 to the span of e and the normalized unramified-prime vector gives off-diagonal entries -sqrt(pi_q(x))/2; its largest eigenvalue is at least sqrt(pi_q(x))/2. Thus the proposed contraction fails at the time-zero derivative whenever the prime vector is nonempty. This is an exact operator obstruction for this proposed norm, not a lower bound for M_chi.

## 4. Common-filter arithmetic payment: full proof audit

For an integer t>=0 put f_t(n)=mu^2(n)t^omega(n)chi(n), using f_0=delta1. Fix p not dividing q and J>=2, independent of x. Let

    Q_p=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    v_(p,J)=Q_p^(*J), P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b_p=Q_p*chi=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)).                       (4.1)

At p^a, the literal filter coefficient is binom(J,a)(-p chi(p))^a for 0<=a<=J. The actual b_p has period pq and mean zero. For nonprincipal chi both period sums vanish; for principal chi the p unrestricted copies cancel the p-multiple contribution, since chi(p)=1. Imprimitive and ramified natural zeros remain. Hence its partial sums are bounded by a constant depending on p,q.

### 4.1 Periodic hyperbola induction with every overlap

For any fixed bounded periodic mean-zero b, set B_t(x)=sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n). For every fixed integer t>=1,

    |B_t(x)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t), x>=1.                       (4.2)

For t=1 this is bounded periodic partial sums. For t>1 let Y=x^(1/t). Every admissible ordered t-tuple has at least one coordinate <=Y. Inclusion-exclusion over these t events is exact. In a term with j<t designated short coordinates, put m=t-j and beta=1-1/m. Their product is at most Y^j<=x, so the remaining summation threshold is >=1 and the induction hypothesis applies. Bounding ONLY the designated short coefficients costs

    C_m x^beta [sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^-beta]^j
       <=C_m(Dm)^j x^beta Y^(j/m)
       =C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t),                             (4.3)

where D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|). The exponent equality follows from m=t-j. For j=t the product cutoff is automatic and the term is exactly (sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t, bounded by D^t. This last cancellation must not be replaced by Y^t. Every sign and overlap remains; real floors and empty initial intervals cause no error.

The resulting recurrence is

    C_1<=D,
    C_t<=D^t+sum_(m=1)^(t-1)binom(t,m)C_m(Dm)^(t-m).

Induction gives C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2: after division by this proposed bound and j=t-m, each summand is <=2^-j/j!, since m!m^j<=t!. Their sum is <e^(1/2)-1, and the remaining D^t ratio leaves a strict margin for t>=2. This is a valid explicit upper bound, not an optimality claim.

### 4.2 Exact squarefree Euler correction and all p shifts

On Re s>1 the literal f_t has Euler product

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.       (4.4)

The product is over primes. Each local polynomial has constant one and zero linear term. Its coefficients g_t therefore satisfy

    Gabs_t(sigma):=sum_n|g_t(n)|n^-sigma<infinity
                                      for every sigma>1/2, (4.5)

for each fixed t. This follows from the absolutely convergent product of the finite local absolute polynomials; ramified local factors are one. No nonvanishing claim about G_t is needed or implied.

For 1<=t<=J the exact coefficient identity is

    v_(p,J)*f_t=b_p^(*t)*v_(p,J-t)*g_t.                   (4.6)

This retains a COMMON filter on the left. It follows from Q_p^t*chi^(*t)=b_p^(*t); it is not a subtraction of estimates obtained with different filters. For t=0 the source is the finite sequence v_(p,J).

Take sigma>1/2 with sigma>=beta_t:=1-1/t. On every real x, (4.2), (4.5) and (4.6) give

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*f_t)(n)|
      <= C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma.    (4.7)

To justify every endpoint, sum only over p^a d<=x, use the bound at y=x/(p^a d)>=1, and replace y^beta_t by y^sigma. The finite shifts have weights binom(J-t,a)p^a and arguments x/p^a, giving exactly the displayed factor. Terms whose argument is below one are empty, not approximated. At t>=3 choose sigma=beta_t>1/2; at t=1,2 choose sigma=1/2+epsilon. This proves the author's individual-color bound and preserves all dependence on fixed J,p,q.

Define a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu^2(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k), k>=1. Finite differences give

    a_k=sum_(t=0)^k(-1)^(k-t)binom(k,t)f_t.

Summing (-1)^k for k<=J gives the exact low-chain combination

    L_J:=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.              (4.8)

Equations (4.7)-(4.8) prove the author's complete common-filter estimate

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*L_J)(n)|
         <<_(p,q,J,epsilon)x^(max(1/2,1-1/J)+epsilon).     (4.9)

It includes every first-J chain sector and every compensator term for all real x. It is a genuine arithmetic estimate, including principal characters; it is not an estimate of an arbitrarily selected signed subsource.

### 4.3 Explicit growth is accounted for but gives no growing-J theorem

The local coefficient c_(t,a) of (1+tz)(1-z)^t obeys

    |c_(t,a)|<=t^a(1/a!+1/(a-1)!), a>=2.

For fixed 1/2<sigma<1, split primes at Y=t^(1/sigma). The tail local logarithm is O(t^2 l^-2sigma), with a universal constant because t l^-sigma<1. Summing over all integers beyond Y costs O_sigma(t^(1/sigma)). On l<=Y, the absolute local polynomial is bounded by (1+t l^-sigma)(1+l^-sigma)^t. Summing its logarithm over all integers up to Y proves

    log Gabs_t(sigma)<<_sigma t^(1/sigma)log(2t).          (4.10)

Together with C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2 and (4.7), this confirms the author's explicit upper price, including all p shifts, all binomial coefficients in (4.8), and the t=0 bound (J+1)(1+p)^J. The condition sigma>=1-1/t must remain: a fixed target sigma cannot be used in (4.7) for arbitrarily large t. The factorial/Euler constants may also grow rapidly. These are failures of the available upper budget, not lower-bound impossibility theorems for a better growing-color argument.

## 5. Additional complete endpoint improvement

There is no need for an epsilon loss in (4.9) when J>=3. Here are the missing low endpoints explicitly, so this statement does not hide a limiting Euler product.

For t=1, G_1(s)=prod_l(1-chi(l)^2 l^-2s). Thus g_1(r^2)=mu(r)chi(r)^2 and it vanishes off squares. With B_1(y) uniformly bounded,

    |sum_(n<=x)(b_p*g_1)(n)|
       <=D sum_(r<=sqrt x)1 <<D sqrt x.

Every extra p shift is paid by (1+sqrt p)^(J-1), yielding O_(p,q,J)(sqrt x) for v_(p,J)*f_1.

For t=2, each local correction is 1-3z^2+2z^3. Its absolute coefficients are dominated coefficientwise by those of

    (1-z^2)^(-3)(1-z^3)^(-2).

The latter has constant one, coefficients three and two at powers two and three, and nonnegative coefficients elsewhere. Multiplying these coefficientwise inequalities over primes, including the ramified zeros, proves

    |g_2(n)|<=sum_(a^2 b^3=n)d_3(a)d_2(b).                (5.1)

Consequently

    sum_(n<=x)|g_2(n)|n^-1/2
      <=sum_b d_2(b)b^-3/2 sum_(a<=sqrt x)d_3(a)/a
      << log^3(2x).                                      (5.2)

The b series is zeta(3/2)^2, absolutely convergent. The a sum is at most (sum_(r<=sqrt x)1/r)^3 by dropping the positive product restriction. This proves the logarithm without invoking any prime-counting or zeta zero estimate. Applying (4.2) for t=2 and paying all remaining filter shifts gives

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*f_2)(n)|
       <<_(p,q,J)sqrt x log^3(2x).                       (5.3)

For each t>=3, (4.7) already allows sigma=1-1/t with no epsilon because the actual Gabs series converges there. Thus for fixed J>=3 every t>=3 term is O(x^(1-1/J)); the low bounds (5.2)-(5.3) are absorbed into that power with fixed constants. Combining ALL terms in (4.8),

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*L_J)(n)|
       <<_(p,q,J) x^(1-1/J),             J>=3,
       <<_(p,q) sqrt x log^3(2x),        J=2.              (5.4)

All statements hold for every real x>=1. This strengthening affects only the already paid low source. It does not improve the exponent 1 of the complete coarse tail estimate, supply OPEN-RHCHAIN, or enlarge the permitted growing-J scope.

## 6. The full Newton remainder and its literal valuation coupling

For j>=0 define

    W_J(j)=(-1)^j-sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)t^j,
    r_J(n)=mu^2(n)chi(n)W_J(omega(n)),                     (6.1)

using 0^0=1. The exact identity (4.8) gives

    mu chi=L_J+r_J.                                      (6.2)

Thus W_J(j)=0 for j<=J. This is a resummation of the entire finite chain expansion at each n, including every depth greater than J, not a truncation that drops its error.

Summing (6.1) as a formal generating series gives

    sum_(j>=0)W_J(j)z^j
      =(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)! z^(J+1)
                       /[(1+z)prod_(t=1)^J(1-tz)].       (6.3)

For a direct verification, the rational left side is 1/(1+z) minus the finite sum of binomial weights/(1-tz). Its first J+1 coefficients vanish. Its common-denominator numerator has degree at most J+1; the highest coefficient, from the t=0 term, is (-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. This proves (6.3) at every degree. Combining (1+z)(1-z)=1-z^2 yields

    W_J(J+1+h)=(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)![z^h]
                   1/[(1-z^2)prod_(t=2)^J(1-tz)].        (6.4)

For J>=2 all displayed coefficients are strictly positive, since the factor (1-2z)^-1 has positive coefficients at every nonnegative degree. Hence the principal unfiltered residual has one fixed sign on j>=J+1; its first coefficient is (-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. At J=1 the remaining factor 1/(1-z^2) gives the author's parity zeros, though the main statement uses J>=2.

The finite-color formula (6.1), independent of x, gives |W_J(j)|<=C_J J^j. Therefore |r_J(n)|<<_(J,epsilon)n^epsilon: only finitely many primes below J^(1/epsilon) require a fixed constant, and each remaining distinct prime pays J by its p^epsilon factor. This removes the factorial representation cost, but proves no saving in the signed summatory source.

Now define the literal complete sharp sources, for all real x,

    T_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*r_J)(n),
    S_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*mu chi)(n).

Equations (5.4) and (6.2) give the stronger complete transfer

    |S_(p,J)(x)-T_(p,J)(x)| << x^(1-1/J),         J>=3,
    |S_(p,2)(x)-T_(p,2)(x)| << sqrt x log^3(2x).           (6.5)

All constants retain p,q,J. The author's every-epsilon version follows. The finite filter terms whose shifted argument is below one are zero. No lower interval, p-valuation, chain depth or real endpoint is removed.

To verify all p-valuation signs, write n=p^a m, p not dividing m, with m squarefree. Set j=omega(m) and take binomial coefficients outside 0,...,J to be zero. In the convolution, r_J(p^(a-i)m) can be nonzero only for a-i=0 or1. These two terms are exactly

    (v_(p,J)*r_J)(p^a m)
      =chi(p)^a chi(m)[(-p)^a binom(J,a)W_J(j)
              +(-p)^(a-1)binom(J,a-1)W_J(j+1)].          (6.6)

The second term is absent at a=0. The a=J+1 term is retained; only a>J+1 vanishes. Nonsquarefree m or a ramified prime in m gives zero. The two coefficients are linked by the SAME W_J and must not be treated as independent signs. A source restricted to p-free integers is a projection of (6.6), not a valid signed upper bound for the whole source.

For principal chi choose a fixed product A of J distinct primes avoiding pq. On n=A*l with l prime avoiding Apq, the literal a=0 coefficient is the nonzero constant (-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. Ordinary pi(y)>>y/log y, unaffected by finitely many exclusions, gives an absolute projected summatory price >>_(A,J)x/log x. This arithmetic lower bound is valid and source-specific. It rules out paying every such projection separately with a power below one. It does not lower-bound T_(p,J), because all p-divisible cross-valuations and remaining prime counts still participate. The required prime lower bound follows from the unconditional ordinary prime asymptotic in [NIST DLMF 27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12); no RH-conditional or progression estimate is used.

## 7. Complete zero-exclusion return, and the weaker sufficient observation

Fix ONE gamma with 1/2<gamma<gamma11 before choosing characters or hypothetical zeros. Fix J>=2 with beta_J=max(1/2,1-1/J)<=gamma. For every fixed chi choose a fixed pair of distinct unramified primes as described below. The author's OPEN-RHCHAIN condition is

    |T_(p,J)(x)| <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon)x^(gamma+epsilon)

for each prime, every epsilon>0, and all sufficiently large REAL x. By (6.5), it is equivalent to the same pointwise bound for S_(p,J) in this exponent range. This is an exact paid source comparison, not a claim that the new bound is arithmetically easier.

Initially for Re s>1, absolute Dirichlet convergence and ordinary partial summation give

    P_p(s)^J/L(s,chi)
       =s int_1^infinity S_(p,J)(x)x^(-s-1) dx.            (7.1)

The n=1 coefficient is correctly included; the formula holds for the right-continuous sharp summatory function. The finite initial interval contributes an entire function. The assumed bound and an epsilon buffer give normal convergence, including s derivatives, on every compact subset of Re s>gamma. Thus (7.1) is holomorphic there. Ordinary Dirichlet-L meromorphy identifies this continuation with the original quotient; no reciprocal power bound has been imported.

Zeros of P_p lie on Re s=1. At a common nonzero-height zero for two different primes, each t log p/(2pi) is a nonzero rational number because chi(p) has finite order. Their ratio would make log p1/log p2 rational, impossible for distinct primes. For nonprincipal chi choose one prime with chi(p)!=1: factor a unit integer with nontrivial character value to find such a prime. This covers height zero. For a principal character, the pole of L at s=1 is the allowed exception and gives a zero of 1/L. The power J changes orders but not the numerator zero locations.

Consequently every hypothetical ordinary zero in Re s>gamma is visible for at least one fixed prime. All natural imprimitive Euler factors remain, and every finite height is covered. Constants may depend on the fixed character and primes; no growing-conductor or uniform-in-height estimate is required.

### 7.1 Correction and independent shell-L1 extension

For clarity define ||F||_(j,X)=(int_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j). A pointwise bound at exponent gamma implies a shell-L2 bound at that exponent, and shell L2 implies shell L1 by finite-measure Cauchy. Therefore author line376's statement that an L2 condition would be stronger is not valid for these usual shell norms. An absolute-coefficient bound would indeed be stronger. The undefined L2 wording should be removed or qualified; it does not damage the actual proved pointwise implication.

In fact the following WEAKER complete sufficient input has its own paid return:

    int_X^(2X)|T_(p,J)(x)| dx/x
          <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)           (OPEN-L1-CHAIN)

for both fixed covering primes, every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X. No subinterval or sample set is omitted; the underlying source remains the literal sharp summatory function. Equation (6.5) pays the entire comparison in shell L1 at the same exponent, including equality beta_J=gamma. On a compact set with Re s>=gamma+delta choose epsilon<delta/2. The absolute contribution of the dyadic shell to (7.1), and to each fixed s derivative, is bounded by

    C_K (log(2X))^m X^(-delta+epsilon).

The sum over dyadic X converges, proving normal holomorphy exactly as before. Hence OPEN-L1-CHAIN suffices for the SAME all-height ordinary-character zero exclusion, with the same principal exception and two-prime cover. Shell-L2 at the same exponent also suffices. No converse from zero exclusion, no pointwise recovery at exponent gamma, and no attained shell estimate are asserted.

This adjustment is an observation requirement, not an arithmetic gain. The complete new input remains open. It is consistent with earlier shell-observation returns but is proved here for this exact sharp source, with all finite filters and low-chain complements paid.

### 7.2 Calibration and full remaining price

The complete parameter rows remain:

| Prospective gamma | Fixed J | Paid low exponent | Conditional c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2187/2500=.8748 | 7 | 6/7 | .1252 |
| 5/6 | 6 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 3/4 | 4 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

For squarefree n, J^omega(n)=d_J(n). The complete residual obeys |r_J(n)|<=C_J d_J(n) on that support and zero elsewhere. Elementary repeated harmonic summation gives sum_(n<=x)d_J(n)<<_J x log^(J-1)(2x). Paying every filter term yields the entire bound

       <<_(epsilon,A_0,tau,a) X^(-A_0+epsilon).          (G20)

## 6. Independent proof of the actual-coefficient operator obstruction

Use exactly GC23: N=floor(B_X), a fixed real sigma>=0,

    L_sigma(c)_{n,m}=1_{m|n}c(n/m)(n/m)^(-sigma),
    W_X(v)(x)=sum_{n<=N}n^sigma v_n g_tau(log(n/x)).

Input norm is unweighted l2({1,...,N}); output norm is L2(dx/x)
on [X,2X]. The matrix product satisfies

    L_sigma(c)L_sigma(d)=L_sigma(c*d).                   ([restricted research revision])

Every intermediate divisor lies between m and n<=N, so finite
truncation removes no term. Hence all three finite identities in
GC24 follow from mu*1=delta_1, b*mu=q_2 and b*mu*mu=A. These
algebraic identities do not yet control W_X.

Let c_X be the literal W35 coefficient with d,e>Y, de>T and
de*ell=n<=N. It has the exact support property

    c_X(q)=0 for every integer q<=T.                    ([restricted research revision])

At e_1 the readout is the capped coefficient field. R35.17 pays
its difference from G_tau; the omitted A-tail is at most three
times the bounded-coefficient Gaussian upper tail. Thus

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]e_1||_2
       << X^(-A_0+o(1)),                               ([restricted research revision])

independently of sigma. The powers n^sigma and n^(-sigma) cancel
exactly at this input. This verifies GC25 including the A cap.

For the full operator define

    a_tau=2 exp(4tau),       b_tau=4 exp(4tau),
    M_X={m in N:a_tau X<=m<=b_tau X}.

For sufficiently large X, M_X is contained in {1,...,N}, because
B_X/X=2 exp(H) tends to infinity. Also, for m in M_X,

    mT >=2 exp(4tau) X^2 exp(-H)>2X exp(H)>=N           ([restricted research revision])

eventually; the sufficient inequality is log X+4tau>2H. Since
H=kappa sqrt(log X), this holds for all sufficiently large X.

If a nonzero c_X quotient contributed in column m, ([restricted research revision]) would
force q>T, so n=mq>mT>N. Therefore every such column of
L_sigma(c_X) is identically zero. This is an exact support
statement, not an estimate for a generic replacement sequence.

The A-column has readout

    W_X L_sigma(A)e_m
       =m^sigma sum_{q<=N/m}A(q)g_tau(log(qm/x)).        ([restricted research revision])

This equality checks the weighting: (mq)^sigma q^(-sigma)
=m^sigma, with no remaining q-weight. Put u=log(m/x). For all
m in M_X and X<=x<=2X,

    4tau<=u<=4tau+log 4.

For every q>=2 the exact Gaussian ratio is

    g_tau(u+log q)/g_tau(u)
      =q^(-u/tau)exp(-(log q)^2/(2tau))<=q^(-4).       ([restricted research revision])

Use the actual A(1)=1 and |A(q)|<=3. The remaining signed terms,
however truncated at N/m, have absolute sum at most

    3 sum_{q>=2}q^(-4)
       <=3[1/16+integral_2^infinity t^(-4)dt]
       =5/16.

Consequently ([restricted research revision]) is uniformly at least

    (11/16)m^sigma g_tau(u)
       >=(11/16)a_tau^sigma X^sigma
                           g_tau(4tau+log 4)>0.         ([restricted research revision])

Here sigma>=0 is used in the displayed lower bound, and tau,
sigma are fixed before X varies. The constant may be small as
tau varies; no uniformity in moving tau is claimed.

For large X, |M_X|>=a_tau X/2. The positive vector

    v_m=|M_X|^(-1/2)1_{m in M_X}

has l2 norm one. The c_X columns vanish, while all A readouts
have the same positive lower bound ([restricted research revision]) throughout the shell.
Thus

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]||_{l2->L2}
      >= c_(tau,sigma) X^(sigma+1/2),                   ([restricted research revision])

with one admissible explicit constant

    c_(tau,sigma)=(11/16)a_tau^(sigma+1/2)
                   g_tau(4tau+log 4)sqrt((log 2)/2)>0.

This independently proves GC26. The exact finite cap, original
prime-two coefficients, original product cut and zero modulation
height are all retained. No finite numerical experiment is needed
for this asymptotic lower bound; the eventual support inequalities
and Gaussian ratio provide the decisive calculation.

The difference between ([restricted research revision]) and ([restricted research revision]) is the point of the result.
The witness vector is supported at high indices, whereas the
actual arithmetic input is e_1. The result refutes only the claim
that the small error at e_1 can be promoted to a small unrestricted
l2-to-physical-L2 operator norm. It is not a lower bound for
G_tau, F_tau, P_Y, their scalar energies, or a domain restricted
by a separately proved arithmetic condition. It also does not
contradict the weighted all-dyad function-space bound GC13.

statement:
### 3.2 Exact pole and full-height Gaussian asymptotic

Before finite modifications, E v_p = p^(beta-1). Let xi_p = v_p - p^(beta-1). These are independent centered variables of variance at most 1. The same dyadic maximal argument, with zero coefficients off the primes, gives

    S(x) = sum_{p <= x} xi_p = O_eta(x^(1/2+eta))

on a probability-one event for every rational eta > 0. Hence

    Z(s) = s integral_1^infinity S(x) x^(-s-1) dx

is holomorphic on Re(s)>1/2. On any fixed closed vertical strip with left boundary sigma0>1/2, choose eta<sigma0-1/2. The integral is bounded by a constant times |s|, uniformly on that strip. In particular, |Z(s)| <= C(1+|Im(s)|).

Starting in Re(s)>1, the absolutely convergent Euler products and logarithmic series give

    D_a(s) = zeta(s+1-beta) H(s),

where the logarithm of H is

    Z(s)
    + sum_p sum_{j>=2} (-1)^(j+1) v_p^j p^(-js)/j
    - sum_p sum_{j>=2} p^(-j(s+1-beta))/j.

The signs follow directly by subtracting log zeta from log D_a. Both double tails converge absolutely and normally on Re(s)>1/2. The respective leading real prime exponents are 2 Re(s)>1 and 2(Re(s)+1-beta)>1; the second inequality uses beta<1. Thus H is an exponential of a holomorphic function there, is nonzero, and obeys |H(s)| <= exp(C(1+|Im(s)|)) on each fixed closed strip. Finite deletions or changes multiply H by

    1/(1+v_p p^(-s)), or
    (1+v'_p p^(-s))/(1+v_p p^(-s)).

For Re(s)>0 their denominators and numerators are nonzero; on a strip bounded away from zero their moduli are bounded. Consequently D_a has exactly the required simple pole at beta with nonzero residue H(beta). Zeta zeros create zeros, not extra poles, and cannot cancel the simple pole at argument 1.

For g_tau(u) = (2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)), direct Mellin inversion gives

    F_a(x) = (1/(2 pi i)) integral_{Re(s)=c}
                exp(tau s^2/2) D_a(s) x^s ds,   c>1.

Move this contour to any fixed sigma in (1/2,beta). On the finite horizontal width, ordinary zeta has polynomial vertical growth away from its isolated pole, H has at most exponential vertical growth, and the Gaussian has exp(-tau t^2/2) decay. Horizontal integrals tend to zero and both infinite vertical integrals converge absolutely. This is a full-height contour shift; there is no truncated-height remainder or data-dependent contour. The only crossed pole is beta, so

    F_a(x) = exp(tau beta^2/2) H(beta) x^beta + O_sigma(x^sigma).

The leading coefficient is nonzero. Every fixed derivative only inserts a polynomial in s and is paid by the same Gaussian decay. As x tends to zero, g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_A (x/n)^A for each A>1; summing yields O_A(x^A). This covers the other end of a later Mellin transform. None of these conclusions uses a zero-free hypothesis.

## 5. Rational frequency decomposition, including its ramified branch

For P prime, P not dividing q, and (a,P)=1, finite orthogonality gives
on P-units

    e(an/P)=1/(P-1) sum_(psi mod P)psi(a)tau(conjugate psi)psi(n).

For Re s>1 this yields the unit part of the additive Dirichlet series.
For n=Pm use mu(Pm)=-mu(m)1_(P not dividing m), multiplicativity of
chi, and e(am)=1. The complete result is therefore

    sum_n mu(n)chi(n)e(an/P)n^(-s)
     =1/(P-1)sum_psi psi(a)tau(conjugate psi)/L(s,chi psi)
        -chi(P)P^(-s)/L(s,chi psi0).                    (R11)

The coefficient psi(a), not its conjugate, follows from the condition
u=an in the orthogonality sum. The negative ramified correction includes
the absence of P^2 multiples and every chi zero. Since tau(psi0)=-1,
the principal numerator is -1/(P-1)-chi(P)P^(-s), and

    L(s,chi psi0)=(1-chi(P)P^(-s))L(s,chi).

Both signs and that Euler factor are correct. The independent exact check
uses P=3 and a complex mod-5 character, so the ramified factor chi(P) is
nonreal; it does not merely repeat the author's real-character example.

At x=P/(2*pi) the source's phase is e(-n/P). Hence an attempted proof
using rational-frequency expansions must retain the growing-modulus twists
and the correction above. Bounds with uncontrolled character-dependent
constants cannot simply be summed uniformly over that moving family.
Absolute Gauss-sum summation may lose sqrt(P); this is a property of
that certificate, not a lower bound for the signed source. Moreover,
(R11) at isolated x does not turn (R4) into a pointwise hypothesis.
Section 9 quantifies a valid observation consequence instead.

### A paid whole-shell nonprincipal-bank reduction

There is a useful stronger conclusion from the literal identity. Freeze
an unramified prime P comparable to X before varying x over [X,2X], and
put w_P(x)=x^(-b)+i(1/x-2*pi/P). For any ordinary eta let
F_eta(w)=sum_n mu(n)eta(n)exp(-nw), Re w>0. Apply finite character
orthogonality to e(-n/P), leaving exp(-nw_P(x)) as the COMMON profile.
Absolute convergence proves for EVERY real x in the shell

    V_b,chi(x)=G_(P,chi)(x)+B_(P,chi)(x),                (R20)
    G_(P,chi)(x)=1/(P-1) sum_(psi mod P,psi!=psi0)
           psi(-1)tau(conjugate psi)F_(chi psi)(w_P(x)),
    B_(P,chi)(x)=-F_(chi psi0)(w_P(x))/(P-1)
                    -chi(P)F_(chi psi0)(P w_P(x)).

In the second branch n=Pm, the phase exp(-i m(P/x-2*pi)) is exactly
the original exp(-i Pm/x). Thus this is not merely an identity at the
isolated rational point x=P/(2*pi). The P^2 deletion remains in psi0;
the character product and all other natural zeros are unchanged.

The elementary bound |F_eta(w)|<=1/(exp(Re w)-1)<=1/Re w gives

    |B_(P,chi)(x)|<=x^b/(P-1)+x^b/P<=3x^b/P
                                      <<_b X^(b-1).   (R21)

Both branches are therefore paid over the ENTIRE physical shell, even
where the residual imaginary part vanishes. No estimate uniform in a
growing character is needed for (R21). For fixed q, all sufficiently
large such P are unramified. This statement is for any chosen P comparable
to X; selecting one per dyadic shell changes only the exact auxiliary
representation, not the global source used in the Mellin return.

For gamma>=b-1, the every-epsilon complete L1 hypothesis for V_b is
equivalent to that for the coherent G_(P,chi); the same is true of the
L2-energy hypotheses by the triangle inequality for their square-root
norms. Constants require a fixed lower bound for P/X. Equality at
gamma=b-1 is allowed in the every-epsilon formulation. At b=3/2 all
three targets in Section 3 have gamma>1/2, so the principal and ramified
sectors are fully paid. The remaining bank has only nonprincipal psi,
and for (P,q)=1 its products chi psi are also nonprincipal.

This is a restricted payment and an exact remaining target, not a bound
for that bank. A further triangle inequality over its P-2 terms generally
loses the coherent signs and may cost sqrt(P) in Gauss weights. The
source-relative fixed-character endpoint alone supplies no uniform
growing-family substitute. The useful task is the WHOLE signed bank norm
with the common w_P(x), retaining every x in the shell.

statement:
## 3. Cheap decisive objection, and the surviving variant

The attractive initial thought was that a rank-three determinant removes the dense prime output and might therefore permit a crude absolute estimate. D5 decisively rejects that inference for the actual coefficients. The 2p channel has weights bounded below by a positive constant for all sufficiently large p, uniformly on I.

More precisely, for any sigma<=1,

    sum_n |h_delta(n)| n^(-sigma)=infinity                 (D6)

because its 2p subseries dominates a fixed positive multiple of sum_p p^(-sigma). Euler's divergence of sum_p 1/p suffices. Thus the absolute Gaussian field cannot satisfy an all-dyad power bound X^gamma with gamma<1: positive Mellin Fubini would then make D6 finite at some gamma<sigma<1. The same obstruction applies to the positive 2p field alone. This is an actual arithmetic obstruction, not an arbitrary-sign toy or a lower bound for the complete signed determinant field.

The viable variant keeps the whole signed field and averages its energy in a fixed real shift interval. That averaging has a precise purpose: a single cofactor can vanish at a hypothetical zero, while the analytic cofactor family cannot vanish identically. It does not assert random signs, a negative average energy, or cancellation among representations of the same squarefree output. The latter representations actually have the same sign by D4.
title: 3. Cheap decisive objection, and the surviving variant

### The cubic families used in T01–T05

Use good primary ideal indices in the Eisenstein field, one generator per ideal, and norm `q`. The fixed excluded set is `S`. Element units and valuations modulo three at fixed primes form additional finite components. A finite ray orbit must be closed under the switches in FD (3). Characters always retain their nonunit zero. Let
\[
D_h(s)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf,good}}\beta(c)\vartheta_c(h)q_c^{-s},\qquad
\beta(c)=\mu(c)\overline{\mathfrak G(c)},\quad |\beta(c)|=1.
\]
FD (1) gives, for squarefree good `g`,
\[
D_h^{(g)}(s)=\beta(g)\vartheta_g(h)q_g^{-s}D_{gh}(s).
\tag{T0}
\]
For an individual `A_{nu,h}` the right side switches `nu` to `nu R_g`; it is not legitimate to ignore that switch. FD (49) supplies separate holomorphy of the required uncompleted families for `Re s>1/2`; FD (59) supplies coarse, uniform polynomial row/height growth there. These are independent prerequisites, not conclusions inferred by division from a completed current.

statement:
## 17. Semidefinite Hermite–Biehler positivity and positive Fourier measure are insufficient

**Two generic countermodels.** The HB kernel of \(E_0=e^{-iz}\) is positive; multiplication by \(z^2+1\) preserves semidefiniteness but introduces the common upper zero \(i\) of \(E,E^\#\). Strict diagonal positivity or common-zero exclusion is essential. Positive Fourier measure also cannot reverse heat: \(H_t=2+e^t\cos z\), with \(\partial_tH_t=-\partial_z^2H_t\), has nonreal zeros before \(t=\log2\) and real zeros afterwards. Gaussian smoothing preserves the phenomenon, and frequency scaling makes the initial strip arbitrarily thin. An arithmetic xi theorem must use more than positivity. Fixed-degree eventual Jensen hyperbolicity likewise leaves an unbounded degree/shift range. [BB R12.a–b; A10; portfolio F23/F26.]

Its first-error coefficient is positive since, at the lower k boundary, `k/4-r/6=5r/12>0`; the other errors are larger. Also

`C-1-9k > 114773/86100 > 1.33`,

and `7k*.04<.065`. For the whole strict family, `a/M<.01` and `A/M<.9` give the simple high-derivative lower bound `50*(.94)/(3*(3.6)^2)-.9=1501/4860>0`. Positive terminal coefficients and sufficiently fine rounding therefore finish the same finite proof for each fixed C. Constants and the finite atlas may depend on that fixed C.

This validates the claimed **open strict-reserve family**. It does not provide the endpoint C=3791/861, a C changing with Z, or a theorem excluding the endpoint moment. In particular an arbitrary epsilon loss and an epsilon-dependent construction are logically different from requiring a strictly positive fixed reserve. The frozen report's `infimum_is_admissible:false` must be read only in the strict-reserve scope. The controller's integration should say **equality is unproved by this argument**, not that the actual moment at equality is impossible. No further tuning or endpoint construction is part of this review.

statement:
## Complete return theorem for the moving detector

Fix A>0, tau>0, and 1/2<a<b0. Suppose off-line zeta zeros have |Im rho|>T,
where T>=1-a is a fixed certified height. Define

    d(a,A,T)=A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2),
    gamma_crit(a,A,T)=a-d(a,A,T).                           (B5)

Assume d(a,A,T)<c0, gamma<=gamma_crit(a,A,T), and prove the actual norm

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |D_A(u)|^2 du
         <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon)                    (B6)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X. A,tau,a,T,gamma
are fixed before epsilon and X; constants may depend on those fixed
parameters. Then zeta has no zeros with Re s>a. This is a proved conditional
return, with B6 OPEN. Its conclusion gives c=1-a only when B6 is proved.

In fact the proof only needs the weaker first-moment hypothesis

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |D_A(u)|du
                    <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).         (B6-L1)

This is the weakest norm hypothesis used in this file; B6 is a convenient
stronger certificate that exposes the complete Gram. Neither is proved at
an improved exponent. No assertion of an optimal criterion among all
possible zero-detection methods is intended.

Proof of the analytic and zero accounting:

(i) Cauchy--Schwarz on logarithmic shells makes H(w) holomorphic for
Re w>gamma under B6, with every fixed w-derivative justified on compact
subsets by the same geometric summation. The finite initial u interval contributes an entire
function. No moving-X Mellin formula is being assumed.

(ii) F=Phi-E is meromorphic on the whole complex plane. Exchanging the two
algebraic roots leaves B3 unchanged, so it is single valued. At a collision
it is a symmetric divided difference, meromorphic in w, and holomorphic
when F is holomorphic at the collision. In the numerical cases below the
collisions occur at s=1+-sqrt(A), real positive points where zeta is
nonzero; the reciprocal is regular at 1 as well. Thus B3 defines a
meromorphic function R(w) throughout the plane. Image poles are locally
finite: the map is rational, zero preimages are discrete, and they cannot
accumulate at s=1. The identity theorem identifies H with R in the initial
right half-plane and then on Re w>gamma. R has no pole there. For a larger
A that puts a collision at a real trivial zero, symmetry still gives a
meromorphic expression; no example in this file needs that complication.
In particular, applying the symmetric expression to the entire left-tail
correction E gives an entire function of w; it contributes no hidden pole
or branch term.

(iii) Suppose a<Re rho<=b0. Put delta=1-Re rho, so c0<=delta<1-a. Its
paired root has

    Re rho*=1-A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)
             >=1-d(a,A,T)>b0.                             (B7)

Here T>=1-a makes delta/(delta^2+T^2) increasing on the required interval.
F is therefore holomorphic at rho*: no second pole can cancel the pole
at rho. Also rho is nonreal, so phi_A'(rho) cannot vanish. The coefficient
of F(rho) in B3 equals

    (1-rho)/(rho*-rho)=1/phi_A'(rho),

which is nonzero. A simple pole of F with residue R_rho produces a pole
of H at phi_A(rho) with the SAME residue. For a pole of order m, the leading
coefficient is multiplied by phi_A'(rho)^(m-1), also nonzero. Simplicity of
zeta zeros is not assumed.

(iv) On this delta interval and at height at least T,

    Re phi_A(rho)=1-delta-A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)
       > a-A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2) >= gamma.                 (B8)

The strict inequality follows from Re rho>a; for T>=delta the displayed
expression decreases strictly with delta. This contradicts (i)--(iii).
Zeros to the right of b0 were excluded by the accepted baseline, and
zeros of height at most T by the finite-height theorem. The Gaussian never
vanishes, and 1-2^(1-rho) is nonzero for 0<Re rho<1. Neither numerator
cancels a pole. No even correction, height range, reflected contribution,
or residual branch term has been dropped.

As an independent algebra check, for f(t)=exp(rho*t) on t>=0 one has
F(s)=1/(s-rho), and B3 simplifies exactly to

    [(1-s1)/(s1-rho)+(s2-1)/(s2-rho)]/(s2-s1)
                  =1/(w-phi_A(rho)).                     (B9)

Thus there is neither an extra Jacobian nor an unpriced second exponential
in the zero signal. This also checks the sign of A in the return.

There is also an explicit inverse identity, useful for auditing the
complement rather than merely asserting noncancellation. For
s*=1-A/(1-s), rearranging B3 gives

    F(s)=(1-A/(1-s)^2)*H(phi_A(s))
                         +A/(1-s)^2*F(s*).                (B9a)

On a<=Re s<=b0 and |Im s|>=T, the second term is already paid by the
accepted baseline: Re s*>=1-d>b0, |Im s*|<=A/T, and
|A/(1-s)^2|<=A/T^2. Choose the fixed baseline exponent
beta=(b0+1-d)/2. Then the defining integral for F gives

    |F(s*)| <= C_beta/(Re s*-beta)
              <=2*C_beta/(c0-d),                         (B9b)

up to an immaterial fixed initial-interval constant. This is uniform in
the entire height range, with positive fixed denominator c0-d. Thus the
second root has a quantified bounded correction, not an unpriced source
norm. B9a is consistent with the meromorphic argument even at a possible
pole, and provides another direct view of the return.

## 2. W47-01: scale drift and the actual diagonal

Put (y=\log x), (h>0), (a=e^{\gamma h}), (E_j=\int_{jh}^{(j+1)h}|U(e^y)|^2dy), and (D(y)=U(e^{y+h})-aU(e^y)). Direct expansion gives
\[
 E_{j+1}-a^2E_j=\int_{jh}^{(j+1)h}(|D|^2+2a\Re(D\overline U))dy. \tag{R5}
\]
A bound $E_{j+1}-a^2E_j\le C_\epsilon e^{(2\gamma+\epsilon)jh}$ on **every** j yields the corresponding upper bound for $E_j$ by the geometric recurrence; conversely an energy bound implies that one-sided drift bound because $E_j\ge0$. Finite initial shells and fixed-h/dyadic covers cost constants. Density-one j is insufficient. A pure faster exponential has positive normalized drift $e^{2\beta h}-e^{2\gamma h}$, independently of its imaginary frequency; this is a diagnostic, not an actual zero construction.

For the fixed modulus q of the zero-extended character (not merely its primitive conductor), elementary squarefree counting gives
\[
 \sum_{n\le t}\mu(n)^2\mathbf1_{(n,q)=1}=\kappa_qt+O_q(\sqrt t),\quad
 \kappa_q=\prod_{p\mid q}(1-p^{-1})\prod_{p\nmid q}(1-p^{-2}).
\]
This follows by (\mu^2(n)=\sum_{d^2\mid n}\mu(d)), imposing gcd conditions before counting the remaining multiples. Partial summation with the full squared Gaussian gives
\[
 \sum_n\mu^2(n)|\chi(n)|^2 g_\tau(\log n-y)^2
 =\kappa_q {e^{\tau/4}\over2\sqrt{\pi\tau}}e^y+O_{q,\tau}(e^{y/2}). \tag{R6}
\]
The integrated diagonal therefore has leading drift proportional to (e^h-e^{2\gamma h}<0) when γ>1/2. This calculation is correct, including ramified zeros. It is not a lower bound for the signed total square, and it does not bound the off-diagonal contribution to R5. This is an exact adaptation of the existing scale/Lyapunov family, not a new arithmetic estimate.
