# [restricted research revision] independent quartic boundary review

Written mathematical review; no formalization. Current accepted c5=.125136 and boundary .874864 are unchanged. This review accepts useful local definitions and algebra, but does not certify a coupled relative scattering matrix, a uniform arithmetic moment, or a new endpoint.



Recovery amendment: fourth stream failure `[private operational identifier omitted]` interrupted the completion suffix after the report and diagnostic source were saved. The controller preserved the original and first extended deadlines and authorized a final suffix through 2026-10-12 02:40 UTC. At 02:25 UTC the inspected independent diagnostic ran successfully. No mathematics or author source reads were restarted; only evidence, freeze, and exact own-claim release remained.

Final recovery amendment: fifth stream failure `[private operational identifier omitted]` interrupted freeze/release after the complete report readback and passing diagnostics. The 01:55 original and 02:25/02:40 recovery windows were missed; the controller authorized only the remaining freeze/readback/release suffix through 03:00 UTC. No mathematical work was reopened. The controller also reported an independently accepted c6 endpoint; c5 and .874864 in this review remain its historical calculation benchmark, not a claim that c5 is still the current project endpoint. This quartic review supplies no endpoint promotion.

## 1. Decision and evidence bindings

The frozen author report is `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/quartic-boundary/report.md`, 23823 bytes, SHA256 `7af7fc3b653ecfea1264ebf2a3ff472461d6d7fe761a8b092e2b98a42ccc3c5c`. Its single frozen followup was received and its complete report read in bounded slices. It was not inspected while changing. The author's manifest SHA256 is `9e2c4c679d89bf9115e0666f14d81a4f1d365e010ab284abd93a4feec850ac0d`.

The underlying merged consultation is `[restricted mathematical source]`, 311255 bytes, SHA256 `5998db643c6d3f477fcb9c06c6d349f6eae5c7505dc90e9ed7588a005aea4146`. Its relevant exact anchors are Q1–Q3, Q2R19–22, R3Q1–10, R4E1–5 and R4V. The canonical [restricted research revision] merged review and component index supplied the accepted scope. These are source evidence, not instructions.

**Verdict:** accept the author's geometry, identity-cell coefficient readout, phase residues, finite phase-span obstruction, and local cost calculation. Accept its displayed trilinear functional as a mathematically valid construction under its explicitly stated compatible-cover convention. Do not upgrade the conditional identification of those conventions with the actual global source. The author correctly reports the absence of the full coupled boundary map. Its partial result is useful and honestly scoped.

The independent additions here are the complete stabilizers and normal representations at all nine geometric strata, their incidence geometry and nonsimple boundary, explicit constants of both actual quartic sources at three specified cusps, and a finite-Schwartz-to-Hilbert phase limit showing precisely why pointwise boundary cancellation is insufficient. These strengthen the next definition task; they do not supply the missing arithmetic estimate.

## 2. Complete H-orbit calculation

Let F have characteristic different from 2, G=SL2, B the upper Borel, and a(t)=diag(t,t^-1). On G/B=P1 use z=Z/W, so B fixes infinity. Put

    H={(n(x)a(t), n(y)a(t), n(x+y)a(t))}.

The action in the finite chart is

    (z1,z2,z3) -> (t²z1+x, t²z2+y, t²z3+x+y).

Infinity patterns are invariant. In the all-finite chart d=z3-z1-z2 transforms to t²d. Translations kill z1,z2; over an algebraic closure scaling makes a nonzero d equal to 1. For one or two infinity coordinates, the remaining translations independently remove all remaining finite coordinates. This proves the following exhaustive list without importing a classification theorem. All stabilizers below are at the displayed representative. Normal weights are exponents of t, on the tangent space modulo the orbit tangent space.

| Orbit | Representative | Dimension | Stabilizer | Normal T weights |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| O_open | (0,0,delta), delta!=0 | 3 | x=y=0, t²=1 | none |
| O_0 | (0,0,0) | 2 | x=y=0, T | +2 |
| O_1 | (infinity,0,0) | 2 | x=y=0, T | -2 |
| O_2 | (0,infinity,0) | 2 | x=y=0, T | -2 |
| O_3 | (0,0,infinity) | 2 | x=y=0, T | -2 |
| C_12 | (infinity,infinity,0) | 1 | x+y=0, G_a semidirect T | -2,-2 |
| C_13 | (infinity,0,infinity) | 1 | y=0, G_a semidirect T | -2,-2 |
| C_23 | (0,infinity,infinity) | 1 | x=0, G_a semidirect T | -2,-2 |
| P | (infinity,infinity,infinity) | 0 | H | -2,-2,-2 |

At infinity, w=1/z transforms as w/(t²+a w), with derivative t^-2. At O_0 the transverse coordinate d has derivative t². These prove all listed weights. Stabilizer unipotents act trivially on these first-order normal quotients, though they can act on higher jets. The open stabilizer mu2 acts trivially on the underlying geometry; a chosen representation or density fiber can still have a central-character obstruction. In particular the odd unary archimedean component still requires the matching odd torus character.

For an odd nonarchimedean local field, O_open(F) splits into four H(F)-orbits indexed by F*/F*²; the other eight geometric strata each give one rational orbit. Thus there are twelve rational orbits. Over a finite field of odd order there are ten, since its square-class group has order two. Over C there is one open orbit. The effective algebraic quotient H/mu2 has a larger image on F-points than H(F): replacing t² by arbitrary r in F* would erase genuine rational-orbit information. The Fourier annihilator (nu,nu,-nu) and its square classes are compatible data, but their identification with these geometric d-orbits still requires an unfolding.

The product Bruhat decomposition has eight infinity patterns. Its all-opposite open chart is the all-finite chart, which contains both O_open and O_0. The distinguished all-opposite point w³B³=(0,0,0) is on O_0, while the all-identity point e³B³ is P. Consequently “identity/opposite cells” is not a two-orbit decomposition for H. Simultaneous ordinary Weyl action sends d to ((z1+z2)z3-z1z2)/(z1z2z3); it does not preserve d=0. These observations rule out a guessed two-germ basis, but do not determine the dimension of any actual equivariant-functional space.

## 3. Boundary incidence, weights, and density

There are four irreducible boundary divisors: D_i={z_i=infinity}, i=1,2,3, and D_0=closure(d=0). In homogeneous coordinates,

    D_0: Z3 W1 W2 - Z1 W2 W3 - Z2 W1 W3 = 0.

D_0 contains all three C_ij and P, but none of the O_i. D_i contains O_i, the two C_ij involving i, and P. D_i intersect D_j along the closure of C_ij. D_0 intersect D_i is the union of those same two curves. At each C_ij three boundary divisors meet in a two-dimensional normal space. Near C_12, with finite third coordinate z3, D_0 has equation z3 w1 w2-w1-w2=0. Near P it has equation

    w1 w2 - w1 w3 - w2 w3 = 0.

Its Hessian has determinant 2, so D_0 has an ordinary quadratic-cone singularity at P and is smooth elsewhere. The boundary is not simple normal crossings. At P its leading defining equation has weight t^-4; this is distinct from the three tangent-normal weights t^-2. Any boundary extension or resolution must retain these incidences and density changes. Counting four divisors neither proves a four-dimensional germ basis nor excludes resonant derivatives and higher-jet distributions.

Conjugation by a(t) on U' has Jacobian |t|_F^4. Left Haar measure on H is dx dy d* t/|t|_F^4, and its modular function in this convention is |t|_F^-4. On O_open the measure dz1 dz2 dd/|d|_F³ is H-invariant. This is not an invariant measure on G³/H: G³ is unimodular and H is not. At the complex place |t|_C is the squared ordinary modulus, so the square root of the conjugation Jacobian is ordinary |t|^4=X^-2 at t=X^-1/2. Normal weights alone cannot determine a spectral exponent before the source fibers, Mellin character, measure and chosen specialization are specified.

## 4. Primary-source constant terms and actual source slots

The primary formulas used here are the zero-frequency matrices immediately after (4.23) and the 24-cusp equation (4.28) in [DDHL v4](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.11875v4), and the definitions (6.11)–(6.15), square relation (6.18), and fourth-power periodicity (6.16) in [de Faveri–Dunn–Hoffstein v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07911v1). In particular (6.12) includes the actual constant 4pi Psi_ij(0) v^(3/4). These are residual quartic theta forms, not cuspidal forms.

Write lambda=1+i, let i1 denote cusp 0 and i2 cusp eta_c=lambda^4/(1+lambda^3), and put

    f=(V theta_i1, -V theta_i2),
    zeta_lambda(w)=zeta_Q(i)(w)(1-2^-w),
    R=Res_(w=1) zeta_lambda(w), C=pi R/zeta_lambda(2).

Here V is the source torus volume (16 in its convention). Direct residue calculation gives the following constant vectors, all multiplied by v^(3/4):

| Expansion cusp | Constant vector of f |
|---|---|
| infinity | (C,0) |
| 0=i1 | (2C,0) |
| eta_c=i2 | (0,-2C) |

For clarity, this table is a deduction, not an assumed symmetry of a complex-character matrix. DDHL's displayed columns have the common quotient R(xi)=zeta_lambda(4xi-4)/zeta_lambda(4xi-3); the self-cusp entry has multiplier 2/(2^(4xi-4)-1). At xi=5/4 that multiplier is 2, and the quotient residue is R/(4 zeta_lambda(2)). The other relevant column entries are R(xi) for the infinity/i1 pair and zero for the infinity/i2 and cross pairs. Where a row rather than the displayed column is required, zero-frequency double-coset inversion gives

    phi_ij(xi)=conjugate(phi_ji(conjugate(xi))).

Indeed gamma -> gamma^-1 swaps the two cusp double-coset sets, replaces the lower-left entry by its negative without changing its absolute norm, and inverts the unitary multiplier. The entries just used are real on the real initial convergence line, so their residues transpose as stated. Multiplication by the archimedean zero-mode factor 4pi and the signed V gives the table. This also avoids extending a formula stated only for nonzero Fourier index to index zero without proof.

Let r(nu0)=(a,b) !=0 and R0=|a|²+|b|². The literal ray sources are

    f_1=(conjugate(a) f1+conjugate(b) f2)/R0,
    f_eta=(conjugate(b) f1-conjugate(a) f2)/R0.

Each ray term uses its own f_ray in BOTH quartic slots. In general it is not theta_i1 tensor theta_i2. At infinity the constants of these two ray sources are C conjugate(a)/R0 and C conjugate(b)/R0; at 0 they are twice these; at eta_c they are -2C conjugate(b)/R0 and 2C conjugate(a)/R0. All cross terms arising from these expressions belong to the actual source. Since the two raw-source constants at 0 and eta_c form a nonsingular diagonal matrix, no nonzero linear combination in this two-dimensional global seed span is cuspidal at both cusps.

This obstruction is deliberately limited. The complete U' period imposes nu1=nu2=-nu3, and its odd unary theta has no zero Fourier coefficient. Thus every literal term containing a source constant disappears after the appropriate full unipotent average. Odd parity persists under Weil translation; its possible zero-index theta contribution comes only from m=0 and vanishes. Source constants must be retained while constructing or unfolding a boundary map, but their mere existence does not prove an uncancelled boundary in the final period. A cusp zero mode and a relative asymptotic germ are different functionals.

The two components above specify global cusps and bad-place ray data. Away from the level their source vectors are unramified. Neither cited primary formula declares them an independent two-dimensional good-prime scattering basis. No local Whittaker multiplicity-one or multiplicity-two claim is needed or proved here. In particular the 24-cusp global functional equation cannot simply be reduced to a guessed local two-by-two relative matrix.

## 5. The author's explicit local functional checks

The author makes a useful advance over an unnamed H-period. Let c=lambda^-4 nu0 be a good-place unit, use Whittaker characters psi(c x) for both source slots, and the Weil quadratic form -c x². Choose compatible torus sections with sigma4(x,b)²=sigma2(x,b) and

    gamma_q(xb)=gamma_q(x) gamma_q(b) sigma2(x,b),
    omega(a(b))phi(x)=gamma_q(b)|b|^(1/2)phi(bx).

For an unramified character chi the defined integral is

    Lambda_(s,chi)(W1,W2,phi)
      = integral_F* W1(a(x)) W2(a(x)) gamma_q(x)
                     chi(x) phi(x)|x|^(s-2) d*x.                 (L)

It is initially unproblematic for phi supported on finitely many nonzero valuation annuli. Right translation by (n(v1),n(v2),n(v1+v2)) multiplies the source product by psi(c(v1+v2)x²), canceled by the Weil factor. For common a(b), the two source cocycles contribute sigma2(x,b), so their product with gamma_q(x)gamma_q(b) is gamma_q(xb). Changing variable y=bx leaves precisely

    Lambda(T_delta(b)v)=|b|^(5/2-s) chi(b)^-1 Lambda(v).

The exponent and character direction are correct. Omitting gamma_q would be incorrect. This is a concrete H-equivariant distribution in a stated local convention, not a construction of its boundary scattering or adelic factorization.

The author's clean identity-ray normalization is also algebraically correct in its stated restricted setting. Choose a good primary split pi, sufficiently deep in the identity congruence ray to stabilize the fixed bad-place vectors, and use f_1 whose selected seed is nonzero. With Q=Npi, alpha=pi/|pi|, epsilon=(nu0/pi)_2, h=(nu0/pi)_4, g=conjugate(gamma4(pi)), set

    r_(2j)=1, r_(2j+1)=Q^-1/4 h g,
    h²=epsilon, g²=-alpha^-1.

The selected local Whittaker function, normalized at 1, has the required values

    W_i(a(pi^k))=Q^(-3k/4) r_k for k>=0;
    W_i(a(pi^k))=0 for k<0.                                (W)

The exponent follows by the rational diagonal move: the archimedean height becomes v/Q^k, the Fourier norm power contributes Q^(k/4), and the Bessel argument stays fixed. Other finite vectors remain fixed only under the stipulated congruence restriction. Negative valuations vanish by right n(O)-invariance and the nonintegral frequency c pi^(2k). Defining this W by the fixed global Whittaker functional restricted to local translates avoids an unjustified generic uniqueness theorem. It does not resolve all lift conventions by itself.

On units the quadratic Weil scalar is 1 in this good unramified convention. Torus-section unit factors of W1W2 cancel the corresponding gamma_q factor. Since the local field contains i, (-1/pi)_2=1, and gamma_q(pi^k)=gamma_q(pi)^k. Choosing

    chi(pi)=alpha epsilon/gamma_q(pi), chi|O*=1

in (L) yields the paired-annulus coefficients

    B_(2j)=(chi2(p)Q)^j, B_(2j+1)=-(chi2(p)Q)^j.              (B)

Specifically |pi^k|^(s-2) W1W2 gives Q^(k/2)Q^(-ks) r_k²; the angular/quadratic factor alpha^k epsilon^k gives (B). This checks both source copies and the non-Hermitian pairing. The other ray may have zero coefficient at the original seed, so normalizing it independently to 1 would be wrong; its actual U_[m] and ell_[m] transport must be retained.

The remaining qualification is material: (W), the rational-diagonal convention, the selected torus sections and chi must be bound to the SAME actual adelic source, including bad places and the odd archimedean character. The author explicitly leaves that binding open. Therefore accept the covariance calculation and conditional local realization, not an unconditional global source-normalized H-transform. A scalar character can specify the desired local orientation; it does not prove that the assembled idele-class character has it at all places.

There is an equivalent direct starting construction. With actual local Whittaker functionals lambda1,lambda2, the tensor lambda1 tensor lambda2 tensor ev_1 is U'-invariant by cancellation of its three phases. Torus averaging supplies (L) after its character and density are calibrated. Applying w³ changes this to a functional for the opposite unipotents. Comparison needs a map between these functional spaces. Right w-fixation of a chosen spherical vector and ordinary Fourier-fixation of one unary vector do not supply that map.

## 6. Identity readout, finite phase limits, and residues

Put A=chi2(p)Q, z=Q^-s and u=Q^(it). For radial integral inputs the actual normalized coefficient functional is

    J_s(phi)=sum_(k>=0) B_k z^k phi(pi^k).

It is absolutely convergent for bounded phi on O and Re(s)>1/2. Negative valuations are invisible to the two source slots by (W). The squarefree input gives J_s(1_O-1_pi²O)=1-z. Its Fourier-fixed exterior completion

    (1+Q^-2)1_O-1_pi²O-Q^-2 1_pi^-2O

has the same readout. Thus the existing exterior repair is genuinely exact at the coefficient level.

For a finite phase input

    a_(u,2J)=sum_(j=0)^(J-1) u^j(1_pi^(2j)O-1_pi^(2j+2)O),
    E(a)=a+Fourier(a)-(integral a)1_O,

every E(a_(u,2J)) is Schwartz, Fourier-fixed, and has value and integral zero. Fourier involution holds on these even radial functions; its value at zero is integral a, and integral Fourier(a)=a(0)=0. On O the Fourier term is constant integral a, hence E(a)|O=a. Consequently

    J_s(E a_(u,2J))=(1-z)sum_(j=0)^(J-1)(Au z²)^j.          (P_J)

These vectors converge in local L2 to E(a_u), where a_u(pi^k)=u^floor(k/2). For Re(s)>1/2 the displayed coefficient sums converge to

    J_s(E a_u)=(1-z)/(1-Au z²).                              (P)

The meromorphic continuation has poles at chi2(p)u Q^(1-2s0)=1, all on Re(s0)=1/2, with residues

    (1-Q^-s0)/(2 log Q).

They are nonzero, with absolute value between (1-Q^-1/2)/(2log Q) and (1+Q^-1/2)/(2log Q). At u=1 the Hilbert limit is 1_O, although every finite E(a_(1,2J)) has value zero at the origin. The point-value functional is not L2-continuous. This is an explicit reason that finite-stage boundary conditions and selected Hilbert-tensor convergence do not prove approximation-uniform limiting boundary cancellation. For u!=1, a_u has no specified pointwise limit at zero; assigning a point value to an L2 representative cannot fix that problem.

This counterexample concerns the defined arithmetic Mellin readout, not the still-undefined H-divisor germ. It neither proves that the latter survives nor that it vanishes. Its poles at 1/2 also do not prohibit a bound at .874864. The precise demand is a continuous or uniformly controlled actual germ map on the selected approximation space.

For u!=v, subtracting (P) gives

    (1-z)A z²(u-v)/((1-Au z²)(1-Av z²)).

The phase direction is nonzero, and its derivative at t=0 is i log(Q)(1-z)A z²/(1-Az²)². Distinct u have disjoint pole sets, so a finite linear combination with s-independent coefficients cannot cancel all their poles unless all coefficients vanish. In particular it cannot retain the constant coefficient 1 and become 1-z. Positive continuous scalar averaging achieves that only with Haar measure on the phase circle: all positive Fourier moments must vanish, their negative counterparts are conjugate, and Fourier uniqueness applies. Averaging Nth roots leaves (1-z)/(1-(Az²)^N). These claims concern local scalar recombination. They do not invalidate a retained phase vector with moving auxiliary numerator or prove finite rank impossible for a different relative map.

## 7. Source Euler data and quantitative costs

Factoring the primary zero-frequency quotient gives

    C_p(xi)=(1-Q^(3-4xi))/(1-Q^(4-4xi)).

Direct evaluation and differentiation give C_p(5/4)=1+Q^-1, C_p(3/4)=0, and C_p'(3/4)=-4 log(Q)/(Q-1). These match the author. Two raw source constant factors contribute C_p(xi1)C_p(xi2), before the actual cusp/ray linear combinations. At the forward residual point their scalar product is (1+Q^-1)². It cannot by itself erase the nonconstant identity phase direction. At the reflected point there are zeros, but substituting zero into an unspecified intertwiner is not a boundary theorem: transported Whittaker functionals, normalization and specialization order can have compensating poles. The principal-series intertwining integral is also different from right multiplication by the compact Weyl element.

The scalar factors are source constant-term Euler data, not verified entries in a relative matrix. Their unrestricted prime product is not absolutely convergent; it cannot be absorbed into the O(Q^-2) selected-vector convergence budget. Likewise the explicit cusp constants in section 4 do not replace an actual opposite-cell calculation.

For sigma=Re(s)>1/2 and r=Q^(1-2sigma), the difference formula gives

    (1-Q^-sigma)r|u-v|/(1+r)²
      <= |J_s(Ea_u)-J_s(Ea_v)|
      <= (1+Q^-sigma)r|u-v|/(1-r)².

Put q=Q^-2. Annulus integration for b=a_-1-a_1 gives ||b||²=4q/(1+q) and integral b=-2q/(1+q). The completion norm identity ||Eb||²=2||b||²-|integral b|² therefore gives

    ||Ea_-1-Ea_1||²=4q(2+q)/(1+q)².

The ratio of the readout difference to this Hilbert distance has size Q^(2-2sigma) for fixed sigma as Q grows. At sigma=.874864 the exponent is .250272. This is a genuine lower cost on the displayed local family, not an operator bound on all inputs, and not a license to multiply local lower bounds into a global impossibility claim.

The author's first phase derivative norm also checks: the annulus mass at floor(v/2)=j is (1-q)q^j, giving (log Q)² q(1+q)/(1-q)². Completion costs at most a factor 2 in squared norm. Fixed higher derivatives have q times a fixed logarithmic power, and their vacuum overlaps have the same summable order. Thus smooth selected Hilbert tensor families are plausible with these explicit estimates; moving restriction and relative distribution norms remain unpaid. No ambient-L2-to-moving-trace inference is made.

## 8. What identity and opposite operations actually define

| Object actually defined | Verified information | Missing information |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed cusp residue sources | Nonzero square coefficients, constants in section 4, ray functionals | A good-prime boundary basis and local Whittaker transport |
| Identity square-index readout | (B), J_s, primitive 1-z, phase (P) | Identification with each H-boundary germ |
| Explicit trilinear integral (L) | H covariance in its stated cover convention | Actual global normalization, bad-place binding and full unfolding |
| Unary Fourier/Weyl operation | Exact exterior completion and selected-vector symmetry | Coupled source-dependent relative Hankel/intertwining map |
| Ordinary source constant term | C_p(xi), exceptional zero/residue data | Opposite-cell matrix after both exceptional specializations |
| Global 24-cusp functional equation | Genuine source continuation/transport formula | A reduction to this H-model, its four divisors and phase family |

No phase-preserving coupled boundary matrix is defined by combining the entries in this table. The missing information is structural, not an uncomputed numerical coefficient. There is also no warrant for replacing a guessed 2x2 matrix by a guessed 9x9 or 4x4 one: orbit and divisor counts do not identify the actual space of equivariant boundary distributions.

A useful repaired next task is to fix the local modules and all torus lifts; define the H-equivariant functional and its density before exceptional specialization; construct restriction/asymptotic maps on D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3, including their intersections or a justified resolution; and explicitly transport the chosen Whittaker functionals under the relevant source intertwiners. Then evaluate the resulting maps on finite E(a_(u,2J)), including the phase derivative, with a bound uniform in J and the phase interval. A justified quotient could reduce the boundary coordinates, but that is a theorem to prove, not an input supplied by the two rays.

The first coefficient contract remains (P_J) and its primitive specialization 1-z. A new analytic gain requires a complete signed vector estimate, for the SAME arithmetic source and actual ray corrections, of the form

    integral_I ||F_t||_[X,2X]^2 dt <<_epsilon X^(2a+epsilon),
    a < .874864,

or a fully stated alternative norm that returns it with all losses paid. The physical relative field has the X^-5/2 normalization, so its corresponding norm must be O(X^(a-5/2+epsilon)). The common phase must remain until vector zero return; independent primewise scalar phase averaging simply recreates hard deletion. Finite-source limits, cross terms, tails, bad-place complements and nonzero detector multipliers remain in the contract. For the Q(i) source this controls zeta_Q(i), hence the ordinary zeta factor; it is not automatically a construction for every Hecke family in the project's larger fixed-family scope.

## 9. Author comparison and final status

| Author item | Independent disposition |
|---|---|
| Section 3 nine geometric/twelve odd-local/ten finite-field orbits | Accept; sections 2–3 above add all normal representations and incidences |
| Section 4 same f_ray in both slots | Accept; explicit cusp constants retain its seed-dependent cross terms |
| Equations (2)–(4), (7)–(8) | Accept their algebra and restricted identity-ray normalization; full adelic binding remains conditional |
| Equations (5)–(6) | Covariance proved in stated compatible-section convention; not a source-global scattering certificate |
| Equations (9)–(11) | Accept phase direction, poles and finite-span obstruction in the defined identity readout |
| Equations (12)–(13) | Accept source scalar factors and derivative; correctly not promoted to relative entries |
| Equations (14)–(16) | Accept scoped local estimates; no free global norm or restriction consequence |
| Full coupled boundary map and new endpoint | Unproved, as author states; no c promotion |

The independent finite diagnostic exhausts the H-action on (P1(F_q))³ for q=5,13, verifies all orbit and stabilizer sizes, and checks a bounded collection of exact rational phase identities and norm algebra. It is a transcription/error check. The arguments in this report, not finite samples, prove the geometric and analytic statements. No supplied-source code or author code was run. No formal proof code, provider changes, canonical edits, tracker changes or Git operations were performed. Prior [restricted research revision] source, detector and hybrid artifacts were preserved. Original PR9/Gao and consultation provenance remains unchanged.

The completion receipt binds the complete files and inputs after full byte readback. The independent review is a completed partial mathematical result: it precisely identifies what is defined and what is still absent, rather than claiming that the original full coupled-boundary objective has been proved.

# W57-23: exact divisor-check recovery and the terminal-row price

This development retains the actual Mobius coefficients, character phases and natural zeros. It gives an exact finite dual and its sharp exponent for independent row-error certificates. It does not bound the actual signed contraction below. Earlier G117 concerns a different all-scale finite-preconditioner operator; G118 concerns finite-prefix relaxations. Those warnings are compatible with, but do not supply, the finite all-row calculation here. General Dirichlet inversion and hyperbola methods are classical; no literature novelty is claimed.

## 1. Recovery on the squarefree unit set

Fix an ordinary chi modulo q, real X>=2, N=floor X, and 1<=Y<N. Let

    S={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1},
    E={n in S:n<=Y}, H=S minus E, a_n=mu(n)chi(n).

Values outside S are their actual zeros. The exact convolution a*chi=delta_1 gives, for each m in H,

    sum_(d in H,d|m) chi(m/d)a_d=b_m,
    b_m=-sum_(d in E,d|m) a_d chi(m/d).                (E1)

Write Z_(m,d)=chi(m/d)1_(d|m), m,d in H. Increasing numerical order makes Z triangular with diagonal1. Every interval d|k|m inside two endpoints of H lies in H: k>=d>Y, k<=m<=N, and k is a squarefree q-unit. Therefore its inverse is exactly

    (Z^-1)_(m,d)=mu(m/d)chi(m/d)1_(d|m).               (E2)

Proof: in the matrix product, the phase factors multiply to chi(m/d), while sum_(e|m/d)mu(e) is1 for m=d and0 otherwise. No entrywise absolute estimate or random model is used.

The unique row dual for the summatory functional on H is

    lambda_m=sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k).           (E3)

Here squareful/ramified k vanish by their natural coefficients. This follows by summing column m of Z^-1: all squarefree q-unit multiples are m*k with (k,m)=1. Thus

    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H)lambda_m b_m.         (E4)

The products in E4 are bilinear, without a complex conjugate. All right endpoints use <=; H uses the strict lower cutoff >Y. This is an exact identity for every finite N and fixed character.

For Y=floor(sqrt N), every lambda uses only k<=sqrt N+O(1), but has the genuine moving coprimality (k,m)=1. These cannot be replaced by one unconditioned short M sum. The b_m retain every exposed divisor, and the sum covers ALL of H, including m near N.

## 2. Exact independent-error norm: exponent1

Let eta_m be arbitrary independent complex errors in the right sides E1, and measure their maximum magnitude. The resulting scalar error is sum lambda_m eta_m. Hence its exact l_infinity-to-absolute-value norm is

    K_(N,Y,chi)=sum_(m in H)|lambda_m|.                (E5)

The upper bound is triangle; equality is attained by eta_m=conjugate(lambda_m)/|lambda_m| when lambda_m!=0. This is a linear error norm; the attaining errors are NOT asserted to be an actual Mobius perturbation, nor to preserve multiplicativity or coefficient bounds.

Every m in S with max(Y,N/2)<m<=N is terminal: it has no strict multiple <=N. For these rows lambda_m=1, literally for every chi. If Y<=N/2, the elementary squarefree-unit count therefore gives

    K_(N,Y,chi) >= kappa_q N/2-O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.  (E6)

On the other hand,

    K <=sum_(m<=N)floor(N/m)<=N(1+log N).              (E7)

Consequently this independent-error certificate has exponent exactly1, uniformly in Y<=N/2; there is no power saving even though all lambda arguments can be short. This is a statement about a dual norm, NOT a lower bound on M or on its actual signed right side.

The lower bound survives adding all convolution rows n<=N, including squareful rows, and all natural-zero information. A terminal squarefree unit m has a nonzero unknown-column entry only in row m, with coefficient1. Every exact linear dual recovering its contribution must assign coefficient1 to that row. Extra lower or squareful rows cannot reduce this price. More general nonlinear certificates using exact arithmetic correlations are not covered.

For errors bounded by weights w_m>=0, the analogous exact norm is sum|lambda_m|w_m. In particular a target O(N^gamma) requires sum_(terminal m)w_m=O(N^gamma). Coding redundancy alone cannot pay a constant error on a positive-density terminal set.

There is also an ACTUAL-coefficient obstruction, which does not use adversarial errors. Put P_N=sum_(m in H)|lambda_m b_m| and allow any chosen Y_N in[1,N/2]. For every unramified prime N/2<p<=N, E1 and E3 give b_p=-chi(p), lambda_p=1. Thus P_N is at least the number of those primes. For every gamma<1, P_N is NOT O_(chi,gamma)(N^gamma) for all large N. Otherwise, at N=2^j, each dyadic prime interval would contribute O(2^(-j(1-gamma))) to sum_p 1/p, forcing convergence. Euler's elementary argument gives divergence: if sum_p1/p converged, the products product_(p<=T)(1-1/p)^-1 would be bounded, whereas they dominate sum_(n<=T)1/n. Removing the finitely many primes dividing q does not change divergence.

At the same time, |b_m|<=tau(m), |lambda_m|<=N/m, and

    P_N<=N sum_(m<=N)tau(m)/m<=N(1+log N)^2.           (E7a)

Consequently limsup_(N->infinity) log(P_N)/log N=1 (with log0=-infinity), for any such cutoff sequence Y_N. This is a precise exponent1 obstruction to taking absolute values of the full actual dual contraction. It gives no pointwise linear lower bound and no signed lower bound. Cross-row cancellation is still fully allowed. The elementary prime argument is supplied here so this claim uses no unverified prime-counting theorem.

## 3. No illicit growing-conductor step

The moving coprimality in E3 can be controlled from a fixed-character M bound by an explicit finite Euler removal. If |M_chi(t)|<=C t^alpha for all t>=1 and some fixed alpha>0, then

    sum_(k<=T,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k)
       =sum_(r<=T, every prime of r divides m)chi(r)M_chi(T/r),

so its magnitude is at most

    C T^alpha product_(p|m)(1-p^-alpha)^-1.            (E8)

For fixed 0<alpha<1 and m<=N, that finite product is exp(O_alpha((log(2N))^(1-alpha))), hence N^o(1), uniformly in m. To see this without a prime asymptotic, split at L=log(2N). The small-prime contribution to sum_(p|m)p^-alpha is bounded by sum_(2<=n<=L)n^-alpha=O_alpha(L^(1-alpha)); the large-prime contribution is at most (log N/log2)L^-alpha. Also -log(1-p^-alpha)<=C_alpha p^-alpha. The exact removal is therefore sufficient for this specific induced-character family. It grants no uniformity over arbitrary growing primitive conductors.

Even E8 only gives an exponent1 total after summing the complete dual in absolute value. The elementary E7 already gives that exponent without an inherited zero-free premise. There is no unearned gain from using the accepted baseline on the short factors.

## 4. A complete signed target and its return

Choose Y=floor(sqrt N). Then the trivial bound |M_chi(Y)|<=sqrt N pays this entire exposed sector for every target gamma>1/2. It does not require the source-relative accepted beta. The remaining exact target is

    D_chi(N)=sum_(m in S, sqrt N<m<=N)lambda_m b_m,
    |D_chi(N)| <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon)       (E9)

for every fixed ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large integers N, with one common 1/2<gamma<.8748540364. The actual implementation uses Y=floor(sqrt N), equivalent to the displayed strict real cutoff for integral m. E4 then gives the desired full M bound at the same gamma. Real X follows by N=floor X. No exceptional m, prime-power corrections, coprimality or terminal rows remain outside E9.

The near target .8748, 5/6 and 3/4 all have room to pay sqrt N. A hypothetical model btilde must bound BOTH sum lambda*btilde and the full signed residual sum lambda*(b-btilde); an error norm with independent row errors has the E6 floor. A moving model is returned to M by E4 before any analytic continuation.

The first direct attempt was to pay the erased block through its many exact divisor checks and a short-dual bound. E6--E7 decisively reject the independent-row version: short lambda arguments do not suppress the terminal rows, which have lambda=1. The surviving task is signed cancellation among the actual b_m, with its coprimality-conditioned dual retained. This is an explicit new source contract in this draft, not a proof that the remaining arithmetic input is easier than M itself.

## 5. Zero exclusion from any proved E9

For completeness, if the resulting bound M_chi(X)<<_(chi,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon) holds for every epsilon>0, partial summation defines

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

holomorphically on Re(s)>gamma, uniformly on compact subsets, with all fixed derivatives. On Re(s)>1 it is the absolutely convergent series sum mu(n)chi(n)n^-s=1/L(s,chi). The identity L(s,chi)F_chi(s)=1 continues wherever L is holomorphic in that half-plane, so L has no zero there. For principal chi, its simple pole at1 is excluded from this multiplication argument; F has the corresponding zero, and there is no zero of L at the pole. For imprimitive chi induced from chi*, the factors 1-chi*(p)p^-s omitted at ramified primes have modulus bounded away from zero on each compact subset of Re(s)>0, since any of their zeros has Re(s)=0. Thus the ordinary-character formulation already includes the exact imprimitive factors. This is an all-height analytic identity, not a low-height numerical test.

The continuation just used is elementary in this half-plane: for nonprincipal chi, its periodic partial sums are bounded, so Abel summation continues L to Re(s)>0. For principal chi, L(s,chi)=zeta(s)product_(p|q)(1-p^-s), and zeta(s)=s/(s-1)-s integral_1^infinity {x}x^(-s-1)dx is meromorphic on Re(s)>0 with its single pole at1. These formulas suffice for the identity-theorem return above.

All E9 hypotheses remain OPEN. No value of c is increased by the identities or error-norm calculation above.

# [private research revision]: complete low-core and relative-conductor reduction

Accept G122–G124 below, from the frozen [author](completed-crossclass/report.md)
and [independent review](completed-crossclass-review/report.md). They reduce
the arithmetic input still needed for the completed detector. They do not
prove that input or raise the accepted written
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636. The source-relative F0/analytic ancestry,
original positive-slot uniformity and exact external L-function
definition/import/admission obligations remain OPEN.

The balanced-residue and masked-Poisson mechanisms come from the expert
[merged note, Section2.5](../external/gpt6-pro-20261011/QRH_merged_research_and_extensions.md),
RM-A/RM10. The new work extends them to the actual completed merged
coefficients with all original slots, proves a stronger radical-support
projection, and pays complete sectors against the current density envelope.
This is source-specific progress, without a literature-priority claim.

## Exact source and norm

Fix the original finite natural dictionary, excluded primes S, complete
orientation and admissible slot system. For ideal columns and element rows,
write phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n), psi_u(n)=chi_n(u)^(+/-1), including all natural
zeros. A fixed nu of order other than six stays in the coefficient. Whole
conjugation acts on every factor. All six units remain in the row family.

For the original row-independent prime pools and profiles,

    Q_u=U^(-v/2) sum_P alpha(P)psi_u(P), 0<=v<=1/20,

with NP comparable to U^v. The no-slot term is P=1,v=0. Common primes
between n and P remain allowed with their zero extensions. No arbitrary
coefficient version of UM/MI/MP is asserted.

Let R=U^t,Y=U^B, and use the actual V, equal to1 on[0,1] and0 on[2,infinity).
Set

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y).

The [accepted completion](../[private research revision]/joint-density-integration.md) gives
D_R,u(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)) at a zero of the same natural nonprincipal character.
The primitive inducing character must be nonprincipal; adding Euler holes
to a principal character does not suffice. The identity is a value
identity, not a claim that derivatives vanish at a zero.

First pay the genuine exponential tail Nn>U^(B+1), with all needed fixed
derivatives and cross terms. A crude polynomial bound on the retained
expression and arbitrarily small absolute tail error suffice. Fix raw
row/slot/height powers before the tail order, B and final threshold. Pair
classification then concerns a finite polynomially supported expression;
it never assigns a uniform subpower loss to unbounded conductors.

Merge equal nP=l with signs:

    F_u=D_R,u Q_u=sum_l b_l(s)psi_u(l),
    b_l=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l,Nn>R)
        A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y)alpha(P).

The finite terminal cutoff is understood. For each required derivative,
on a fixed compact real interval sigma>1/2,

    |partial b_l| << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)(Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l!=0 implies Nl>=L0=c0 U^(t+v).                 (1)

H_J contains fixed seminorms and a fixed height polynomial, not a live
arithmetic coefficient. Divisor multiplicities, logarithms and fixed
derivatives are absorbed into the requested loss before the threshold.

Choose a smooth positive radial Phi>=1 on the required row ball BEFORE
expansion. Use every nonzero sixth-power-free row, with the original
fixed-dictionary exclusions (or retain that finite set). PR15 proves those
exclusions finite from fixed prime support and valuations at most5.
For a fixed positive-width interval I whose lower edge is at least
(1+delta)/2-h0, 0<=h0<=10^(-5), put

    N(F)=sum_(u free,eligible) Phi(Nu/U)
        sum_(i,j in {0,1}) integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
        |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j F_u|^2 d tau d sigma.       (2)

Finite extra derivatives and orientations mean their finite sum. An
original positive row weight bounded by U^epsilon and its selected subset
are dominated on the FULL norm before expansion. This does not dominate
individual signed sectors or license amplitude-selected Poisson kernels.

## G122. Radical support and all low/high crosses

If n!=1 and N(rad n)<=R, every squarefree divisor lies inside the plateau
of V. Thus exactly, including the endpoint,

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|rad n) mu(d)=0.                     (3)

Consequently b_l!=0 implies N(rad l)>R. Write l=c a^6 with c sixth-free.
Since rad l divides ca, Nc Na>R. This is stronger than the support
inequality Na>(R/Nc)^(1/6). It requires the merged convolution, not a
separated divisor dyad.

Project the actual merged columns onto Nc<=C0=U^lambda<R. For each row
and every required derivative, (1) gives

    |partial F_lo,u|
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
         sum_(Nc<=C0) (Nc)^(-sigma)
         sum_(Na>R/Nc) (Na)^(-6sigma)
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon) R^(1-6sigma) C0^(5sigma).

The source's linear ideal count proves the inner convergent tail by
partial summation. The outer sum is bounded by the integral of
x^(5sigma-1), with constants uniform on the fixed real interval. Extending
both positive sums to all ideals is allowed. All roots, late scales,
shared slot primes and exceptional rows are included. Therefore

## 3. Proof with the actual endpoints and complete tails

### 3.1 Exact finite operator identity

On test functions on the positive integers define the forward average

    (T_H f)(n)=(1/H) sum_(j=0)^(H-1) f(n+j),
    Q_r(T)=sum_(j=0)^(r-1)(I-T)^j
          =sum_(k=0)^(r-1) (-1)^k binom(r,k+1) T^k.

The polynomial identity

    T Q_r(T)+(I-T)^r=I                                     (3)

is exact. The sum of absolute coefficients of Q_r is 2^r-1. Each T_H^k is a positive probability average of forward shifts between0 and k(H-1), with endpoints included. Thus every shift in Q_r lies between0 and (r-1)(H-1).

Set psi_x=Q_r(T_H)f_x and R_x=(I-T_H)^r f_x. Absolute summability and the zero extension give the exact adjoint relation

    F_a(x)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) B_H(k) psi_x(k)
                         +sum_(n>=1) a(n) R_x(n).          (4)

Indeed, replacing k by n+j in the first sum gives sum_n a(n)T_H psi_x(n). Terms with n<=0 vanish; no negative index or first-block correction is silently dropped. Equation (3) proves (4). The forward shifts, rather than backward shifts, are essential here.

### 3.2 The corrected main term uses the same energy

First restrict the main sum to k>=rH. Every shift j occurring in psi obeys0<=j<rH<=k. Write v=log(k/X). For X<=x<=2X,

    log((k+j)/x)=v+b,   |b|<=ell.

Consequently

    f_x(k+j)^2/w_X(k)
      =(2 pi tau)^(-1)
         exp([-3v^2/4-2bv-b^2]/tau)
      <=(2 pi tau)^(-1) exp(3ell^2/tau) exp(-v^2/(2tau)). (5)

The last inequality follows from 2|bv|<=v^2/4+4b^2. Using the absolute coefficient sum of Q_r, (5) applies to |psi_x(k)|^2 with the extra factor (2^r-1)^2.

For any positive unimodal function with maximum1, its positive-integer sum is at most its integral plus2. Substituting k=X exp(v) therefore gives

    sum_(k>=1) exp(-log(k/X)^2/(2tau))
       <=X sqrt(2 pi tau) exp(tau/2)+2 <=K_tau X.           (6)

Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, using the ENTIRE sum defining E and restricting only the test-function norm, now yields

    |(1/H) sum_(k>=rH) B_H(k) psi_x(k)|
          <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H)).               (7)

For the remaining indices1<=k<rH use |B_H(k)|<=H. Every positive argument of f_x in psi is <2rH<=X<=x, where f_x increases toward its maximum. Thus this whole part is at most

    rH (2^r-1) g(0) exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2tau)).           (8)

This is why the extremely small w_X(k) near k=1 causes no uncontrolled inverse-weight factor. Applying (5) indiscriminately there would be false for long windows. The explicit split pays that strongest endpoint objection.

### 3.3 Repeated differences pay the complete residual

For a nonnegative shift j,

    f(n)-f(n+j)=-integral_0^j f'(n+u)du.

Iterating this representation for (I-T_H)^r expresses R_x(n) as (-1)^r times the average, over j_1,...,j_r in {0,...,H-1}, of the integral of f_x^(r)(n+u_1+...+u_r) over0<=u_i<=j_i. No derivative is taken of a sharp arithmetic cutoff.

For every absolutely continuous integrable f with integrable derivative and every v>=0,

    sum_(n>=1) |f(n+v)| <= ||f||_(L1(0,infinity))
                                  +||f'||_(L1(0,infinity)). (9)

To prove (9), compare f(n+v) with f(t) on each interval[n+v-1,n+v], integrate, then sum the disjoint intervals. They all lie in[0,infinity). Applying (9) to f_x^(r), using the derivative scaling f_x^(r)(t)=x^(-r)h_tau^(r)(t/x), proves

    sum_(n>=1)|R_x(n)|
       <= ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r x^(1-r)+J_(r+1) x^(-r)]
       <= ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r X^(1-r)+J_(r+1) X^(-r)].        (10)

The coefficient ((H-1)/2)^r is the exact product of average shift lengths. This bound includes the whole positive integer line, hence the complete right tail. The smooth zero extension pays the left endpoint. Equations (7),(8),(10) prove (2). H=1 is included: the residual vanishes exactly and B_1=a.

## 18. Moving negative norms and actual-source transport

[private research revision]'s [complete W44 integration]([private research revision]/wild44-integration.md) adds:

- **G64:** for the full localized Gaussian W_X, its H^-rX bound X^eta
  returns the complete shell exponent eta+d/2, where
  d=limsup r_X loglog X/log X. The d=0 case is an exponent equivalence;
  positive d gives only the stated sufficient return. The full signed
  kernel and Gaussian high-frequency tail remain. First gain requires
  eta+d/2<.8748540364, with the actual fixed-character pole bridge.
- **G65:** exact Hilbert feature transport, including unmatched ghost
  charge and both tails, gives exponent (1+q+d)/2 from full cost X^q.
  First gain requires q+d<.7497080728. Known monotone matching gives cost
  X^(2beta-1) for buffered beta>.8748540364; better cost is still open.
- **G66:** the literal rough cutoff1-sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^-s has a real
  zero1-lambda*/log N+o(1/log N). Full omitted-prime inverse remainders
  retain their reciprocal pole; actual code fibres retain a nonzero
  conditional covariance. These are scoped failures, not full-field
  lower bounds or universal impossibility claims.

The [quartic boundary integration]([private research revision]/quartic-boundary-integration.md)
also defines all nine geometric strata and their normal representations,
four intersecting boundary divisors, actual cusp constants, and a conditional
local trilinear functional. A finite-to-Hilbert phase limit shows why
pointwise finite-stage cancellation does not price a limiting germ.
The actual coupled boundary map, global binding and arithmetic norm remain
open. No orbit count determines a scattering matrix size.

The [forward c6 proof]([private research revision]/formalizer-handoff/README.md) is independently
accepted as equivalent to the pinned analytic framework. Its constant/affine
local proof and exact finite endpoint certificate retain c=.125139 while
removing unnecessary intermediate endpoint premises. External import audit,
root-definition binding, formalization and independent admission remain
separate; no root or subagent formalization was performed.

Primary retained source: `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, SHA256 `2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8`, especially B0.35 at line508, B0.36, and B0.62 at line881. The ordinary-family dictionary, SHA256 `8ec443e21cd50b05eb4559895fd03b6ac9952acb4d206033d99cd798dcad7ccc`, checks one ideal term per nonzero ideal, removal of the factor six, and actual zeros for the presented modulus. It does not supply an angular or conductor-uniform estimate.

Fix K=Q(omega), one finite-order trivial-infinity character eta and the source's fixed finite S. All ideals/prime ideals below exclude S, or have the equivalent zero extensions. For a remaining prime ideal put Q=Np, t=Q^-1, D=a Q^-s, R=b Q^(3-6s), with

    a=eta(p), b=conjugate(alpha(p))^6 eta(p)^6, |a|=|b|=1.

The sixth power makes this phase insensitive to changing an associated generator by a unit. No estimate for an angular L-function is needed to define or bound this coefficient list. Literal B0.35 gives

    H_p=(1-t^2)/(1-R) * (1+t(D-R)/(1-D)),
    C_S=product_(p notin S)(1-Q^-2)>0,
    H=C_S h, h_p=N/((1-D)(1-R)), N=1-(1-t)D-tR.       (R42.1)

The lower-case physical residue constant c_S in B0.36 is different. Also keep the source's k: P_eta(x)=x^k f_eta(x). B0.36 itself defines this principal signal on an absolute Mellin line, and B0.62 confirms

    Mellin(P_eta)(s)=exp((s-5/6)^2) H(s)/L_K^S(s,eta). (R42.2)

Mellin means integral F(x)x^-s dx/x. The objects J_eta, J_eta-f_eta, the compensator, physical rows and the short-divisor hypothesis H are not identified with this P_eta or Euler H. This is the decisive scope boundary: the source normalization is exact, but no physical error estimate transfers merely by renaming it.

## 8. The remaining estimate and a sufficient actual mixed moment

The weakest new counting target needed for a source improvement is

    sum_(u in B_sep)|Q_u|^2
           <= H_J U^[E_K-xi+epsilon], xi>0,            (OPEN-SEP)

for every original fixed family, bin, profile/height list and slot subset in the displayed range. Together with F21 this gives a source density saving min(xi,1/2000), after the usual loss allocation. It is conditional until OPEN-SEP is proved. A physical return must still use that input in its actual licensed family before any numerical c increase.

A concrete stronger sufficient arithmetic theorem avoids selecting zero rows inside a transform. For every compatible pair of inverse profiles arising from F14 and all original slots, prove on the clean natural free-row majorant

    sum_u |M_-(U^r_-)|^2 |M_+(U^r_+)|^2 |Q_u|^2
       <= H_J U^[delta(r_-+r_+)+E_K-xi+epsilon],        (OPEN-MIX)

with the necessary rowwise real-power and the TWO independent inverse-height suprema recovered through the finite source Sobolev derivatives. The fixed-inducing rows already paid in Section7 may be excluded by their fixed source condition; no high-zero indicator is inserted. On B_sep the two inverse witness lower bounds F16 divide this estimate to give OPEN-SEP. The actual annular and complementary profile compatibility may be retained; arbitrary coefficient arrays or an independently selected pair of characters are not requested. Original slots and their relative phases remain. A theorem for all such clean profiles is stronger than needed but unambiguous.

OPEN-MIX is a specific separated-length mixed inverse moment, not supplied by the old MI. Merging the inverse factors produces coefficients of the form

    sum_(d1 d2=n)mu(d1)mu(d2)W_-(Nd1/D_-)W_+(Nd2/D_+),

with shared-prime terms. Even without weights, the squarefree n coefficient is mu(n)2^omega(n); at a prime square the mu*mu coefficient is1 although mu(p^2)=0. Separated dyadic scales do not prohibit a shared prime in d1 and d2. Thus neither divisor boundedness nor the separated lengths licenses B3.31 or B3.6 on the merged coefficient. This is an actual source-family obstruction; a new mixed theorem or direct compatible covariance argument is necessary.

The precise signed interference is visible already before witness selection. If T_< and T_> denote the two unsigned-cutoff sums in F14, then

    T_< + T_> =0

term by term in the nonunit product coefficient, for every row. Therefore their actual cross covariance is minus the positive norm of T_<. This is a dependence identity, not a new saving; taking two independent absolute moment estimates cannot exploit that negative sign. Any covariance estimate must retain the actual profiles and common divisor convolution. This is the stronger objection to multiplying marginal density savings.

### 2.2 Every higher prime power is relatively bounded

For gamma>1/2,

    C_gamma=sum_p sum_(j>=2)log p*p^(-j gamma)
       <=[1/(1-2^-gamma)]sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2gamma)<infinity. (3)

Translation by j log p on the causal half-line has norm1 after the displayed weight. Extend z by zero above R, retaining its entire past. Young's inequality, or Minkowski followed by Cauchy, gives

    |Q_2(R)|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z(y)|^2dy.

The negative half-line integral is finite unconditionally. For every eta>0, splitting the positive integral at a fixed sufficiently large Y yields

    |Q_2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_(eta,gamma,tau),                (4)

uniformly in R. The finite B uses only unconditional bounds for U on a fixed bounded interval and its Gaussian left tail. No unknown right-tail norm enters B. Character dependence is allowed, although the crude majorant need not use it.

For other rows the old boundary is

    G_old(d)=(1+delta)/2+13h/75-y/2-ell/2+ell q

It is convex in d and remains nondecreasing in kappa on the required

using R>=1-delta>=1/4. At d=h-.001 the old bound is at most
theta-19/400000. At d0=.005 the displayed source coarse bound is less
than theta-.1. Convexity pays every d between them, including d=y.

at the junction and has the proved top margin. Its positive slope is

The floor .51+h/3+.51ell is below theta-.01. The tiny-row relative
exponent 13h/75-y/2+63d0/50 is below -1/20. Far rows d>h+10^-10 use
the original raw exponent B0+(h+zeta)(1+epsilon)-zeta*v+epsilon with
v chosen after fixed zeta=10^-10; this pays arbitrary negative powers.
No near-top certificate is used as a surrogate for those branches.

## 5. A reusable comparison lemma, with its limits

Use section4's F and rectangle, with A,B,D0,C,C0,h positive. Suppose the
old fixed-h top boundary at ell0 and capacity C0 has

    b0-F0 >= [A(delta-delta0)^2+B(1/2-p)]/D0,

and an accepted endpoint ensures kappa<=kappa0. Keep h, increase ell by
L>0, decrease the probe boundary by L/4, and replace C0 by C<C0 with
h>4ell. On a patch [d_-,d_+] x [p_-,1/2] inside that rectangle, put
r=min(delta0-d_-,d_+-delta0)>0. Define

    deformation_all = L[3/4+(3/8)(1+2/C0)],
    deformation_patch = L[3/4+(d_+/2)(1+2/C0)],
    gain_patch = d_- p_- (h-4ell)/2 (1/C-1/C0),
    gap_outside = min(A*r^2,B*(1/2-p_-))/D0.

If gain_patch>deformation_patch and gap_outside>deformation_all, their
two positive differences give a uniform new top margin. The proof is
exactly E1-E3 and the complement disjunction; favorable gain outside
the patch is discarded. Endpoints can use strict enclosures of the
algebraic old parameters, as this packet does.

This certificate adds no moment or density estimate. Physical geometry,
shortening, supply, shifts, other rows and common-saving order must still
be proved. The fixed-h specialization need not optimize the endpoint.

## 6. The ordinary zero-free return

The unchanged probe has k=5/6-x/3-ell/6. Since5ell-1<0, its norm
boundary is k+x/2+(y-x)/12=theta. The principal double residue is the
inverse Mellin integral of exp((s-5/6)^2)H_eta(s)/L_K^S(s,eta), where
|H_eta-1|<=1/2 on Re(s)>=.87 after the target's fixed cutoff. Principal
remainders retain y/4,h/24 and mu_P>0. Our helper additionally checks
nearby box margins y/20-(1+h)/1000-1/4000>0 and
h/600-.001-1/4000>0. Prime approximation has common positive saving
below .87 times the least fixed slot width, only at its source locus.

Three independent frequencies, full w-inversion, buffered reciprocal
shifts and off-height tails remain the source operations. Raw polynomial
powers precede tail orders; height degrees precede external exponents.
Under mu=beta_*-theta>0 choose common real error budgets, mesh, finite
original slots, capacity decrements and Delta below fractions of mu and

Thus J_eta-f_eta=O_eta(Z^(beta_*-k-Delta)), while
J_eta=O_eta(Z^(theta-k+epsilon)). Taking epsilon<mu/4 gives a common
smaller saving for f_eta. Its Mellin transform continues the reciprocal
quotient to Re(s)>beta_*-Delta'>theta>.87; decay near zero follows from
the source's arbitrarily far-right initial line. Neither Gaussian nor
H_eta vanishes there. A zero sufficiently close to the defining supremum
contradicts holomorphy, without assuming that supremum is attained.

Restore only nonzero Euler factors in Re(s)>0. The exact Eisenstein norm
lift gives the ordinary Dirichlet product with quadratic twist, including
ramified/imprimitive factors. At1 inherit nonprincipal nonvanishing from
the accepted old theorem rather than multiplying a zero by a possible
pole. Exclude the principal pole throughout. Scope is the strict half-plane
for each fixed finite-order Hecke character of trivial infinite type over

or growing-parent-conductor theorem.

## 7. Corrections, qualifications and evidence limits

1. The packet's numerical local novelty claim must be read relative to
   its supplied [private research revision] baseline. In the present library it is P/W38
   reuse, and accepted [private research revision] subsumes its full local window. The new

   The note explicitly retains it in section 1.2. It is a row ball/dyadic
   source estimate with that support, not an infinite unweighted sum
   over all eligible k. Preserve that convention in any extracted theorem.
4. Positivity of Kphys and polynomial caps, independent profile heights,
   fixed original slot choices during differentiation, old MP0's individual
   U^2 cap and lower-row slot supply are necessary. The note invokes the

5. The all-height density proof uses an internal exponent selected after
   its initial moment degree; its returned final polynomial degree then

6. The finite audit does not establish high-row reconstruction, Poisson,

   Its 129,024 valuation checks are supplementary finite examples. The

No numerical repair is needed under these source conventions. No provider
