# [private research revision]: an actual large-common-divisor estimate for the separated inverse source



## 1. Result and exact boundary

There is a source-legal power saving for the part of the actual paired inverse polynomial in which its two squarefree indices have a common divisor of norm at least `U^(1/5)`. Exact divisor inversion exposes two shorter ordinary inverse polynomials. An explicit Euler convolution removes their new column masks before the old inverse moment is used. The estimate retains the actual signs, all prime collisions, natural zeros, original slots and two independent heights. It uses no moment for an arbitrary coefficient on an inverse column.

After all finite derivative and subpower losses, this component has a squared-norm saving `1/200` against the full G148 target throughout its separated-width box. This pays high rows on which that component carries a fixed fraction of the required signal. It does NOT pay every high row: the small-common-divisor component remains, with its full signed interference.

For that complement this report also identifies the complete sixth-power diagonal and gives a source-based, fully masked relative-conductor decomposition. Its diagonal, total-conductor range `Q<=U^(9/5)`, and then ratio range `Q1/Q3<=U^(8/5)` are paid with the same conservative saving. The surviving signed sum is written explicitly in Section 9. These latter estimates reuse the accepted balanced-residue/Poisson mechanism; they are not counted as a new Poisson theorem. The substantive new estimate is the earlier large-common-divisor bound on the actual paired coefficient.

OPEN-MIX and OPEN-SEP remain open. No new `c` follows. The current accepted source-relative value remains

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    theta11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364,
    K=28114053/6250000 (preceding-family input).

F0/base ancestry, the retained positive-slot uniformity obligations, and exact external root-definition/import/admission obligations remain open. No public verified-record claim is made. Credit remains with the original PR9 authors and Gao/AI PR15, the preceding [private research revision]--89 authors/reviewers, OpenAI, Hailey and Akash. The balanced-residue mechanism cited below was already present in external RM-A/RM7 and the [restricted research revision] review; it is not new credit for this pass.

## 2. Source contract and ambient mixed target

The literal primary input is PR9 commit `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`, retained `paper.md`: B0.3, B0.7--9 and B3.3--6. The source file is 198343 bytes with SHA256 `2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8`. Exact current source pins are in the companion receipt. The accepted written reduction is `[restricted mathematical source]`, especially G147--G148, with the independent [restricted research revision] corrections. The natural row/kernel convention and the complete hole estimate are also pinned to [restricted research revision] review Sections 5--7.

Fix the number field, its licensed generator/unit convention, one fixed natural coefficient dictionary and a whole orientation. Write

    phi_u(n)=nu(n) psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1),
    M_u(D;W)=D^(-1/2) sum_n mu(n) phi_u(n) W(Nn/D).

All sums use the actual source ideals/primary generators; unit multiplicities have fixed cost. Columns avoid the fixed excluded set S, as stated literally in PR9 B0.1. The symbol is zero at every original nonunit. Complete multiplicativity includes these zero values. `nu` is fixed; its order need not divide six. Its values stay in column coefficients during a row-kernel expansion. Whole conjugation conjugates every associated factor, rather than just `nu`.

The inverse profiles are common smooth profiles on fixed compact annuli, with bounded real powers and two independently varying heights. The common real parameter may also vary over its fixed compact interval. The original slot product is

    Q_u=prod_i [P_i^(-1/2) sum_(p in P_i)
                       a_i(p) phi_u(p) W_i(Np/P_i)],
    P_i=U^(z_i), v=sum_i z_i, 0<=v<=1/20.

The fixed original prime pools are disjoint across slots. They need not be disjoint from either inverse index. The relative slot coefficients remain the original row-independent coefficients; natural character zeros remain on the whole product. B0.3 expresses these slots with the same whole orientation. A fixed relative character is in `a_i`, not a new variable orientation. Zero slots are allowed. Absolute ideal counting gives

    sup_u |Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(v+epsilon).                 (2.1)

Here and below `H_J` denotes the finite product of the required common-profile seminorms and one fixed polynomial in all the independent heights. The exponent/order is selected before the live height and final threshold. A fixed number of derivatives has the same notation with enlarged orders.

The ambient rows are nonzero sixth-power-free rows in a fixed smooth enclosing ball of scale U, with their natural fixed ray restrictions. An annular assertion can be enlarged to this positive norm. Any original nonnegative divisor-bounded weight is dominated at its U^epsilon cost BEFORE pair expansion. The fixed finite inducing exceptions already handled in G147 may be retained or removed as stated below. No zero predicate, amplitude predicate, varying dictionary or signed physical projector is inserted into a Poisson kernel.

For any bounded scale E, literal B0.9 and its scale/height restoration give

    sum_(free u) Phi(Nu/U)|M_u(E;W)|^2
      << H_J U^epsilon [U+U^(1/6) E^(5/6)].            (2.2)

For a row ball use its dyadic annuli; the resulting `log U` is a subpower. The original B0.9 has an arbitrarily small slack from UM's `vartheta`; choose it before the requested final loss. Subunit nonempty scales have only boundedly many columns, and the expression is empty below a fixed positive scale. Fixed extra column punctures, when already present in the retained source, can be removed by the same explicit identity in Section 4; they are never hidden in a smooth seminorm. Their norm must remain polynomial in U, exactly as required by the source. No arbitrary new puncture family is admitted here.

Use the accepted coarse separated box

    17/25<=delta<=7/10,
    17/20<r<47/50, 33/25<s<141/100,
    s-r>3/8, 0<=v<=1/20, D1=U^r, D2=U^s.             (2.3)

The compatible plain lengths and common product-annulus equation from G147 remain imposed on an actual extracted witness. The new ambient estimates hold on the larger box (2.3), so do not require dropping that equation in the source construction. The two Fourier heights remain independent.

Set `B_u=M_u(D1;W1)M_u(D2;W2)`. With the preceding-family K fixed, define

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    G_K=min(3kv,a_K+b_Kv), E_K=rho+delta v-G_K.

The sufficient ambient mixed target has exponent

    T_mix=delta(r+s)+E_K.                              (2.4)

Only the elementary lower bound `E_K>=rho>=19/54` will be used: `G_K<=3kv` and `delta-3k=4delta^2/(5-2delta)>0`. Thus this report neither recalibrates K from c11 nor silently replaces it by the historical 9/2.

The internal buffered zero parameter is distinct from physical delta. It may exceed .70. G147 first obtains its true inverse lower bounds at that internal value, then weakens them to `|M(Dj)|^2>=U^(delta r_j-small)`. Physical slot prices and E_K still use physical delta. Both original and exponential-free profile families were frozen before the easy union, and both residual presentations were re-extracted on the same annulus. These accepted conventions are not changed here.

## 3. Exact projection by the two inverse indices' gcd

Let `G>=1`. Define the actual coefficient part

    B_{>=G,u}=(D1D2)^(-1/2)
       sum_(d1,d2; N(d1,d2)>=G) mu(d1)mu(d2)
            phi_u(d1d2) W1(Nd1/D1)W2(Nd2/D2),         (3.1)

and `B_{<G}=B-B_{>=G}`. The prime slots are not part of this gcd cutoff; they remain fully original. Equation (3.1) is a column restriction before merging and before expansion against another row coefficient. It is not a selector of high rows.

Define the signed ideal-divisor coefficient

    a_G(q)=sum_(d|q, Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Divisor convolution with 1 yields the exact finite identity

    1_(Ng>=G)=sum_(q|g) a_G(q).                       (3.2)

Indeed interchange d|q|g; the inner sum of `mu(q/d)` is zero unless d=g. Thus `a_G(q)=0` for `Nq<G`, and `|a_G(q)|<=d(q)`. Every q which contributes to (3.1) is squarefree because d1,d2 are squarefree. Put d1=qx, d2=qy. Then

    mu(qx)mu(qy)=mu(x)mu(y) 1_(x,q)=1 1_(y,q)=1

on squarefree q. This does NOT require (x,y)=1. The two natural factors `phi_u(q)` also remain, including their zeros.

Let `M_u^(q)(E;W)` be M with the extra column mask `(n,q)=1`. Central normalization gives the exact formula

    B_{>=G,u}=sum_(q squarefree, Nq>=G)
       a_G(q) phi_u(q)^2/(Nq)
       M_u^(q)(D1/Nq;W1) M_u^(q)(D2/Nq;W2).          (3.3)

The q sum ends at a fixed multiple of D1. All support constants are the fixed profile endpoints. Shared q/slot primes and shared q/row primes are retained. When a natural zero makes the outside phase vanish, it is zero rather than a reciprocal phase. The signs in a_G and mu remain exact in (3.3).

## 4. Removing the new masks without an illegal moment input

For every q and every original common profile W,

    M_u^(q)(E;W)
      =sum_(h supported on primes of q)
          phi_u(h)/(Nh)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nh;W).            (4.1)

The h sum is finite on the actual annulus. At each p|q, the local convolution of mu with the all-nonnegative-exponent sequence 1 is `1,0,0,...`; at p not dividing q it is mu. Thus its coefficient is exactly `mu(n)1_(n,q)=1`. Complete multiplicativity carries phi through this identity even at zero values. The normalizations in (4.1) multiply to E^(-1/2), so there is no missing h power. Substituting qh into the fixed normalized arguments changes the scale, not the common W.

The absolute restoration mass is bounded by

    sum_(h q-smooth) (Nh)^(-1/2)
      =prod_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1)
      <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.                       (4.2)

To prove the last inequality, fix epsilon first; each sufficiently large prime's factor is at most `(Np)^epsilon`, and the finite small primes supply a fixed constant. This is uniform in polynomial q. Derivatives in log scale merely change the common profile. If an alternative convention puts a norm-height factor outside W, differentiating its q,h phase supplies powers of log(qh), bounded by a further subpower on the nonempty support. The two independent heights are never identified.

For an already frozen polynomial puncture R0, replace the prime set by that of qR0 in (4.1)--(4.2). This explicit outer expansion is the required justification; one must not invoke B0.9 directly on a moving q-mask. Similarly, applying B3.6 to the merged coefficient `mu*mu` would be illegal. Neither shortcut occurs here.

## 5. Large-gcd mixed estimate and continuous saving

Write `||F||_U^2=sum_(free u) Phi(Nu/U)|F_u|^2`. Multiplication by a phase of modulus at most one is a contraction in this Hilbert norm; no division by a natural zero occurs. Apply Minkowski to the EXACT signed sum (3.3), then (4.1) separately to its two factors. Use the trivial annular estimate

    |M_u(E1;W1)| << H_J E1^(1/2)

on nonempty scales, with a fixed constant for bounded subunit windows. Use (2.2) for the second factor, and (2.1) for all original slots. The h sums have total subpower mass (4.2); their scales only decrease. Consequently for q of norm x,

    ||M_u^(q)(D1/x) M_u^(q)(D2/x) Q_u||_U
       << H_J U^(v/2+epsilon) (D1/x)^(1/2)
                [U+U^(1/6)(D2/x)^(5/6)]^(1/2).      (5.1)

Both terms decrease by a fixed positive power of x. In a dyadic q range x~X, the ideal count and divisor bound give `sum |a_G(q)|/(Nq)<<X^epsilon`. Summing the resulting geometric dyadic tail from G proves

    ||B_{>=G} Q||_U^2
      << H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/G)
                      [U+U^(1/6)(D2/G)^(5/6)].       (5.2)

This includes every q up to its genuine support endpoint; no single-prime approximation or missing middle regime is used. It also includes all shared primes between d1,d2 and the slots. The entire q label count was paid in Minkowski, not omitted through a spurious normalized average.

Take `G=U^(1/5)`. Since `s-1/5>1`, the second branch dominates and (5.2) has exponent

    E_gcd=v+r+(5/6)s-1/5.                            (5.3)

Against (2.4), throughout the closed coarse box,

    T_mix-E_gcd
      >=rho+(delta-1)r+(delta-5/6)s+1/5-v
      >=rho+(47/20)delta-393/200
      >=2809/273000 >1/100.                          (5.4)

For the last minimum, the derivative is `47/20-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]`, positive on `[17/25,7/10]`; its minimum is at 7/10. Substituting delta=17/25 gives the stated exact fraction. The companion rational receipt checks this continuous proof and its positive derivative floor; it is not a sampled grid. The slack above 1/100 is `79/273000`.

The inequalities have ample room for the fixed G147 endpoint pads and all subsequently requested subpowers. A conservative final statement is

    ||B_{>=U^(1/5)} Q||_U^2
       << H_J U^[T_mix-1/200+epsilon].               (5.5)

Choose all internal small losses below the algebraic slack between 1/100 and 1/200. Real/height derivatives, scale suprema and finite common-profile Fourier integrals obey the same result, as justified in Section 10. Constants and thresholds may depend on fixed source data and requested loss, not on the live row, zero, q, scale or height.

For counted separated rows, the two witness inequalities imply `|B|^2>=U^[delta(r+s)-small]`. On those rows where `|B_{>=G}|>=|B|/2`, positivity and (5.5) pay their original weighted slot mass with exponent `E_K-1/200+epsilon`, after losses. On the remaining rows `|B_{<G}|>=|B|/2`. This is a genuine further source restriction. It does not infer that most actual witnesses have large gcd, nor that any high-bin scalar saturation is arithmetically realized.

Alternatively,

    ||BQ||_U^2 <=2||B_{<G}Q||_U^2+2||B_{>=G}Q||_U^2. (5.6)

This handles every low/high cross term if a bound for the small-gcd norm is subsequently supplied. It does NOT prove that those cross terms individually have the large-gcd saving while the small-gcd norm is still open.

## 6. Merging the small-gcd coefficient: all sixth-power coincidences

Retain exactly `B_{<G}Q`, including both inverse profiles, all slot coefficients, signs and the condition `N(d1,d2)<G`. For fixed parameters merge a tuple into

    n=d1 d2 prod_i p_i,   N0=D1D2 prod_i P_i.

Its actual coefficient c(n) includes the normalization N0^(-1/2), `mu(d1)mu(d2)`, all fixed nu/relative phases and profile values, summed over the allowed tuple factorizations. The resulting row polynomial is

    B_{<G,u}Q_u=sum_n c(n) psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1).      (6.1)

This is an identity, not a claim that c is an allowed B3.6 coefficient. A common puncture remains in the tuple; it is never replaced by an unrelated coefficient family. Each column n has norm in a fixed annulus about N0. At a good prime,

    v_p(n) in {0,1,2,3}: two squarefree inverse
    appearances plus at most one original slot appearance.              (6.2)

Valuation 3 really is allowed: the same prime can occur in d1,d2 and one slot. None of those collisions is dropped. For two such n,n', their valuation difference lies in [-3,3]. It is a multiple of 6 exactly when it is zero. Hence the COMPLETE same-sixth-power ideal class is simply n=n'. There are no unequal ideal sixth-power roots in this finite paired source. Fixed units/primary generators contribute their original finite phases and can be separated into the licensed finite sectors; they do not create a growing root sum. This simplification is specific to (6.2), not applicable to the older completed A_R coefficient with unbounded powers.

The number of tuple factorizations of n is divisor bounded, even with named fixed slots. The normalized coefficient and its fixed derivatives therefore satisfy

    |c(n)|<<H_J N0^(-1/2) U^epsilon,
    sum_n |c(n)|^2<<H_J U^epsilon.                  (6.3)

For the second estimate one may use Cauchy inside the tuple factorization sum and the linear ideal count in every original annulus. Dropping the small-gcd restriction after absolute values only enlarges this majorant. Both heights remain inside c; no assertion of their equality or statistical independence is made.

After expansion the full diagonal is

    sum_n |c(n)|^2 sum_(free u) Phi(Nu/U)1_(u,n)=1
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon).                         (6.4)

Retained fixed holes can only decrease this positive diagonal. This is the whole diagonal, including every inverse/slot overlap. It is an upper bound on the diagonal contribution, NOT a lower bound for the entire norm; its off-diagonal can be negative.

## 7. Actual relative conductors and complete natural holes

For n!=n', put `e_p=v_p(n)-v_p(n')`. Up to the whole orientation, nonzero values are ±1, ±2, ±3. Let qj contain primes with |e_p|=j, and

    Qj=Nqj, Q=Q1Q2Q3, V=Q1Q2^2Q3^3.                 (7.1)

All qj are pairwise coprime radicals. The full oriented local vector, not just (Q1,Q2,Q3), specifies the relative character. At every nonzero good prime its local conductor is that prime. The fixed ray data can only alter the fixed S factor. Thus n!=n' supplies a nonprincipal relative character; principal relative rows have already been included in (6.4). The two signs of 3 specify the same sextic local phase but different integer ratios, a divisor-many multiplicity retained in the coefficient count.

Write n=g a, n'=g b with (a,b)=1. For a fixed oriented integer valuation vector, `Na Nb=V`. Their common annular support implies

    Ng<<N0/sqrt(V).

Every such g contributes a coefficient product of size at most `H_J N0^(-1)U^epsilon`; ideal counting therefore gives

    sum_(n,n' with that vector)|c(n)c(n')|
       <<H_J U^epsilon V^(-1/2).                    (7.2)

If the upper bound for Ng is below 1 there are no pairs; fixed annulus constants give the same estimate when it is bounded. Allowing all g overcounts but never removes natural restrictions. Divisor-many choices of signs and local allocations have subpower cost. Summing vectors in dyadic conductor ranges yields

    sum |c(n)c(n')|<<H_J U^epsilon (Q1/Q3)^(1/2).    (7.3)

This is the finite-product counterpart of the accepted [restricted research revision] weighted-gcd calculation. It is not a new claim of cancellation.

The actual row kernel is

    K(n,n';U)=sum_(free u) Phi(Nu/U)
              xi_e(u) 1_((u,E_(n,n'))=1),            (7.4)

with its licensed fixed ray/unit restrictions. E includes ALL primes in nn' at which the phase has canceled, and every retained frozen hole not already supplied by the primitive conductor. In particular equal powers at a common prime leave a zero at that prime. Fixed nu phases stay in c. The norm of E is polynomial in U on this finite product source.

Literal B3.5, with the original deleted zeros, and the [restricted research revision] derivation R16--R18 give uniformly

    |K(n,n';U)|<<H_J U^epsilon min(U,U^(1/6)Q^(5/12)). (7.5)

For completeness, primitive nonprincipal Poisson at scale X has prefactor X/sqrt(Q), normalized Gauss amplitude 1, dual argument X Nh/Q, and zero dual term zero. Decay and lattice counting bound it by sqrt(Q); ordinary counting bounds it by X. Expanding the sixth-free row indicator as `sum_(b^6|u)mu(b)` and the complete hole as `sum_(d|rad E)mu(d)` leaves scale U/[(Nb)^6 Nd]. Splitting the b sum at `[U/(Nd sqrt(Q))]^(1/6)` gives

    U^(1/6) Q^(5/12) prod_(p|E)(1+(Np)^(-1/6))
      <<U^(1/6+epsilon) Q^(5/12).

A split below 1 uses the whole convergent sixth-power tail and the same bound. Nonempty bounded/subunit windows have the fixed support interpretation of B0.8. Polynomial E pays the displayed product by a subpower. This is the existing full-mask argument, not a second clean-coprime-only transform. Every shared-prime zero remains present.

The fixed finite inducing free exclusions cost O_fixed(1) in each kernel and can be deleted since the right side of (7.5) is at least a constant. Alternatively retain them in the ambient norm, for which (5.2) and the same relative expansion hold. No unrestricted moving high-bin exclusion or varying physical projector is licensed. For a requested fixed finite list of raw core restorations, the inherited G147 absolute row payment remains available; arbitrary raw/positive-child transfer is NOT established by (7.5).

## 8. Paid portions of the small-gcd norm

All conductor ranges below are disjointly assigned: first Q<=U^(9/5), then its complement with Q1/Q3<=U^(8/5). There are only O((log U)^3) ranges because n,n' have polynomial support.

For total conductor Q<=V0, use `V>=Q` in (7.2). The number of oriented vectors per radical is divisor bounded. Partial summation of the linear ideal count gives

    sum_(Nq<=V0) (Nq)^(-1/2+5/12+epsilon)
      <<V0^(11/12+epsilon).

Thus this complete absolute off-diagonal contribution is at most

    H_J U^(1/6+epsilon) V0^(11/12),
    hence H_J U^(109/60+epsilon) at V0=U^(9/5).       (8.1)

The ratio sector follows from (7.3) and the trivial U branch of (7.5):

    H_J U^(1+epsilon) (U^(8/5))^(1/2)
      =H_J U^(9/5+epsilon).                         (8.2)

Both estimates are for the original signed expression after taking its absolute majorant on these sectors; their positivity is not assumed in the full norm. They include all Q2 values and shared columns, not merely coprime squarefree pairs.

The uniform coarse target floor is

    T_mix >=(17/25)(217/100)+19/54
           =3689/2500+19/54.                         (8.3)

Its gaps above 109/60 and 9/5 exceed 1/100; the diagonal exponent 1 has much larger reserve. Exact fractions are retained in the numerical receipt. Consequently the complete diagonal and the two paid off-diagonal sectors are bounded by `H_J U^[T_mix-1/200+epsilon]` after the same finite loss allocation. These coarse cuts are not asserted optimal and are not the main innovation of this report.

## 9. Exact remaining signed target and quantitative implication

Define R_mix to be the real ordered off-diagonal sum from the expansion of the actual positive norm of (6.1), restricted to

    n!=n', Q>U^(9/5), Q1/Q3>U^(8/5),                  (9.1)

using the actual merged coefficients c(n), the actual kernel (7.4), and no extra row predicate. Each c(n) still sums ONLY its tuple factorizations with `N(d1,d2)<U^(1/5)`; its conjugate does so independently. Do not replace this by the weaker condition on the merged gcd (n,n'), and do not discard slot collisions. On a tensor Sobolev norm the same definition is summed over the finite derivative list and integrated with its fixed positive parameter measure.

The OPEN estimate is the one-sided signed upper bound

    R_mix <=H_J U^[T_mix-xi+epsilon], xi>0,           (9.2)

uniformly in all source data fixed in Section 2. It is not an absolute pair bound and not an assertion that R_mix is nonnegative. If (9.2) holds, Sections 6--8 bound the complete small-gcd norm. Equation (5.6) and Section 5 then bound OPEN-MIX with the smaller of xi and 1/200 (with further small losses). Evaluating on the two inverse witnesses, without dividing by Q_u, bounds B_sep. Combining with G147's already paid exponent yields the smaller of that margin and 1/2000 for the original high-row density. Choose, for example, half of the smallest displayed positive margin before the final loss allocations; no equality endpoint is being spent.

This is a complete implication for the stated free natural source. A numerical c increase would additionally require the complete raw/positive-child and physical return: both signed coprimality projectors, original family reconstruction, clipped rectangles, root/slot holes, fixed-inducing and exceptional rows, physical radii and amplifier charges, all shortenings and Euler shifts, principal cases, and the common-Delta actual-supremum argument. None of those costs is supplied merely by (9.2), and this report neither spends the centered exceptional reserve nor changes the old descendant moments.

## 10. Profiles, two heights, tails and quantifier order

All estimates above are first for a fixed allowed parameter tuple. To dominate rowwise choices, apply the retained tensor Sobolev estimate in the common bounded real variable, both independent inverse heights, the independently allowed slot heights, and logarithmic scale coordinates. Leibniz produces finitely many products with the same arithmetic coefficients and the same column gcd selector. A derivative in log scale replaces W by `-W/2-yW'`; differentiating a norm twist adds a bounded number of logarithmic factors on polynomial supports. The proofs of (3.3)--(5.2) therefore apply to each derivative with a larger finite H_J. The derivative list is fixed before the live row and height. No Sobolev derivative of a rowwise chosen coefficient is taken.

For an actual coupled common product profile, use B3.3 on its FULL ambient box before current rows, q labels or live slots are selected. Multiply by the fixed larger individual cutoffs, Fourier separate, and integrate the resulting product-profile estimates with the absolutely integrable common Fourier measure. The independent Fourier coordinates do not become equal just because the presentations arose at the same zero. Substituting q,h changes the polynomial scales, not the pre-existing arithmetic coefficients or Fourier measure. The finite demanded child height orders determine the needed parent derivative orders backwards. All non-smooth gcd and hole restrictions remain explicit outside the smooth profile operation.

The G147 construction already completed the detector, retained the original H,V, removed the exponential only after locating the residual annulus, and re-extracted both pre-frozen profile families. Its genuine terminal/Fourier tails, prefix, easy witnesses and finite dictionary labels remain paid by its existing 1/2000 statement. This report does not reopen a truncated divisor identity or remove V from the full sum. Its new finite product expressions have compact annular supports and the q/h sums terminate there. If Fourier tails are used for the new common separation, choose their raw decay order after all finite requested derivative/height orders and before the final threshold, using B3.3--4 and the polynomial raw count. No hidden infinite pair tail remains in (7.2).

The order is: fix a requested positive reserve/loss, the fixed dictionary and finite original slot system/profile families; choose all finite derivative orders, relative-conductor cuts and G=U^(1/5); choose the small internal height power and buffer shares, raw tail orders as required by the retained dependency graph, then one sufficiently large threshold before live heights/scales/zeros are inspected. Large external heights use the retained absolute estimates with a larger fixed height polynomial. Constants may depend on the fixed family, not on a growing conductor dictionary. These are source-relative quantifiers, not an unproved uniformity extension.

## 11. Strongest obstruction and what was not proved

The saving in Section 5 comes from two actual shorter inverse scales after a common divisor is extracted. The large q label count is precisely canceled by the normalization 1/Nq before its shortened-scale saving is used. This is a legal use of an old moment on its original mu coefficient; it is not a scalar high-bin localization. It removes an actual nontrivial portion of the paired source before pair expansion and gives an explicit limiting complement. This cut is not the old low relative-conductor cut: factors d1=qa,d2=qb give n=q^2ab, while an independently factored n' can have large unique-prime support on both sides. The within-column q may be large while Q1 and Q1/Q3 are also large. This is a statement about permissible factor patterns, not a quantitative high-zero realization.

Small gcd includes the entirely coprime squarefree sector. With no slots and squarefree n, its merged coefficient has the exact form

    (D1D2)^(-1/2) mu(n) nu(n)
      sum_(d|n) W1(Nd/D1) W2(N(n/d)/D2),             (11.1)

with the two independent twists in their respective W factors and the retained dyadic supports. The identity `mu(d)mu(n/d)=mu(n)` does not remove this divisor-profile coefficient. At untwisted nonnegative profiles its divisor weight is nonnegative after the fixed phase `mu(n)nu(n)` is factored out; at independent heights it has a genuinely different divisor phase. Neither case makes it an admitted one-inverse B3.6 coefficient. Natural common-product dependence supplies no identity collapsing (11.1) to the old source moment.

The generic relative squarefree coprime n,n' sector has Q1 comparable to N0^2 and Q2=Q3=1. It survives both (9.1) cuts, and its underlying tuples can also have small within-column gcd. This is an algebraic admissible sector, not a claim that some actual high-zero row realizes its maximal norm. The proven absolute envelope there is `U N0` (up to a subpower), which is far larger than T_mix. This shows why the present positive bounds do not complete the task; it is not a lower bound on the true signed residual and not an impossibility theorem.

An attempted direct use of MI on `mu*mu`, or an average of the two independent witness heights as though they were the same variable, fails at the literal source contract. A common zero creates dependence, not independent rarity. Conversely the exact covariance identity of the two full annular inverse/plain presentations from G147 is retained but does not itself bound this inverse/inverse product. No target-unit cancellation or full norm lower bound is asserted here.

The next consequential estimate is (9.2) on the actual small-gcd, high-Q1 coefficient, or a source identity that genuinely changes that coefficient while paying its complementary terms. A further clean coprime Poisson transform alone retains the same absolute conductor loss and does not supply it. This report leaves that estimate OPEN rather than promoting a partial source gain to a new density or endpoint.

## 12. Evidence and status

The companion helper uses only exact rational/integer arithmetic. It records the continuous margin identities, the source envelope comparisons, finite diagnostics of divisor inversion and mask restoration, and the local valuation reason for the complete sixth-power diagonal. These finite diagnostics are not proofs of the infinite analytic moment. Sections 3--10 supply the written analytic derivation and its precise imported boundary.

All original source dates, commit pins and frozen ancestor bytes are retained in `source-pins.json`; no remote or provider call was made. Own artifacts will be fully read back, hashed and frozen before the single authorized review wake. Root and the independent reviewer decide acceptance. Current status: substantive restricted source estimate proposed; full signed complement open; c11 unchanged.

**W41-16 | Dirichlet passive realization | p=.025.** Realize a reciprocal L-object as the transfer function of a passive system whose energy estimate forbids poles. First test: does a finite Euler product admit a positive storage function with constants independent of the prime cutoff? Bridge: a quantitative limiting realization yields analyticity and nonvanishing. Danger: the energy inequality itself encodes the missing zero-free theorem. New invariant: minimum storage cost versus cutoff.

**W41-17 | balanced truncation of multiplicative Hankel | p=.015.** Form a multiplicative Hankel matrix from inverse coefficients and retain only directions with large singular value. First test: derive the exact tail bound and compare with an additive low-rank surrogate. Bridge: a certified operator tail plus a small inverse residual proves a Bezout identity in the target strip. Danger: translation from l2 operator control to pointwise evaluation is unbounded. Reach: 1/6 or 1/4 if the tail decays.

**W41-18 | pseudospectral continuation barrier | p=.08.** Track the smallest singular value of a finite coefficient convolution operator as sigma moves left; certify it cannot cross zero before the desired line. First test: distinguish finite triangular invertibility from a uniform infinite inverse. Bridge: bound finite-section inverses and tails in one evaluation-compatible norm. Danger: every finite section is invertible even when the infinite analytic function vanishes. Reach: precise no-go invariant or a new inverse proof.

**W41-19 | two-port scattering detector | p=.006.** Place the detector and its complement in a two-port scattering matrix; conservation makes the omitted sector an observable outgoing channel. First test: build a unitary dilation for a finite signed convolution and recover its defect formula. Bridge: a strict contraction at the zero witness contradicts conservation. Danger: unitary dilation adds exactly the missing loss and yields no strict contraction. Reach: systematic accounting of complement losses.

**W41-20 | observability of a zero mode | p=.055.** A zero corresponds to a hidden mode of a shift realization. Prove a coarse observability lower bound from arithmetic sampling that prevents hidden modes in a larger strip. First test: explicit exponential-polynomial toy system with one planted zero. Bridge: controllability/observability constants must be uniform in truncation and height. Danger: a planted mode can evade every finite sample. Reach: direct replacement zero exclusion.

## UR2. Actual determinant coefficients and the remaining prime channel

Put `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, with the ordinary character's natural zero extension, and `F(s)=1/L(s,chi)`. Initially `Re s>1`. For real delta>0 the Hankel matrix is

    sum_n a(n)n^(-s) v_n v_n^T,
    v_n=(1,n^(-delta),n^(-2delta))^T.

Cauchy--Binet for finite truncations gives the ordered triples `a<b<c`, each with coefficient `a(a)a(b)a(c) det[v_a,v_b,v_c]^2`. Absolute convergence permits passage to the infinite sum, since `|V_delta|<=1` and the unconstrained triple Dirichlet series converges. Squaring removes the immaterial orientation of the Vandermonde. This proves D3 with no analytic conjugation, no coprimality restriction and no deletion of shared primes.

On every nonzero tuple, each factor is squarefree and

    mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)=(-1)^(Omega(a)+Omega(b)+Omega(c))
                       =lambda(abc),
    chi(a)chi(b)chi(c)=chi(abc).

Thus D4 is exact even at squareful outputs. The coalesced weight `W_delta(n)` is nonnegative and `|h_chi,delta(n)|<=d_3(n)`. Distinctness is essential: a prime-power output has at most the two allowed squarefree labels 1,p, so its coefficient vanishes. At pq with distinct primes the sole admissible triple is `(1,p,q)`, proving D5.

For zeta, the `(1,2,p)` channel has a positive weight tending, uniformly on `I=[1/5,1/4]`, to `(1-2^(-delta))^2 2^(-2delta)`. Consequently D6 is correct: its positive absolute Dirichlet series diverges at every real sigma<=1. Positive Mellin Fubini then rules out an all-dyad sublinear power bound for the absolute Gaussian field, including an averaged-in-delta version. This does not lower-bound the full signed field.

The same obstruction extends to every fixed ordinary character: replace 2 by a fixed prime p0 not dividing the specified modulus, and let p vary over the other unramified primes. Then `|chi(p0 p)|=1`, the weights tend uniformly to a positive constant depending on p0, and removing finitely many ramified primes does not repair the divergent prime reciprocal sum. Original prime arithmetic therefore survives in a short-factor semiprime face. Prime-power annihilation alone does not pay D20.

## 5. Low/high branches, missing labels and all-height scope

Low indicators are imposed only after both transforms on positive allocated child energies. RC's `commonChild_energy` and `common_clipped_energy` permit the keep predicate. Use the actual moving child character with the original fixed anchor Q_*; do not insert that child into the anchor. In each fixed parent translate mask transport preserves the literal row gate and positive-real zeros. Whole-character conjugation reflects height; conjugating only its fixed factor would change the family.

A removed canonical slot of width dz costs squared exponent (7/10+O(buffer))dz in a low bin. Greedily remove slots until old 9/2 capacity holds or the slots run out. Drop the low indicator only after this payment and use the old full eligible family. Exhaustion uses unrestricted zero-slot input even if the plain sum exceeds the width. Bounded prime lengths are estimated directly; the large-length contour premise is not applied at length one.

Actual canonical width minus M', denoted d_*, can be negative after support cancellation; only d_*<=delta2 is known. For 0<=v<=1,

    d_*+v(F-d_*)_+ <=delta2+v F_+.

Use v=7/45 and nominal defect F<=g+6a+small losses. The low reserve is a/15-7g/45. On case j its normalized lower bound is exactly b_j/15000, with minimum 57/25000000. This pays frequency/support padding, one greedy overshoot, bin buffering and aggregate finite-slot losses by choosing a smaller common budget. The slot list is fixed before the final threshold; there is no growing count hidden in that aggregate budget.

For high bins delta in [7/10,3/4], set rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)]. The actual nonzero row is w=u0 e F_c G_c V h'. Active left/right residues are 1+t and 1-t modulo six, and a zero residue retains the natural puncture. Retain u0 among six fixed unit sectors. With canceled active radical width R0 and L_c=log_Z NF_c, L_c<=5(R-R0), and the actual support gives

    log_Z Nw<=W+small losses,
    W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a.

Every genuine second common prime and the first projector divides w. The missing first common radical has width <=p-R-E+R0. For fixed w and missing radical the remaining common labels, including arbitrary valuations, are divisor-many by the source Rankin product estimate. A finite valuation table alone would not prove this. The second residual projector need not divide w; its dyadic count is paid by the two extraction scalars and original priority allocation. A possibly zero extracted character value stays outside, and no new coprimality condition is imposed on quotient plains.

The fixed-dictionary density has a threshold before all heights and live norm bounds, and primitive conductor O_fixed(Nw). Polynomial Euler holes are separate from that conductor and dictionary size. Within the actual parent translate, the upper buffered zero maximum controls each surviving factor; a member of a fixed finite list realizes the lower maximum needed for density. A union over that fixed list costs a constant; a union over live arithmetic labels is not taken. Sixth-power lifting converges because rho>=2/7>1/6. Thus the joint count is

    Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+epsilon)(1+T)^J.

A slightly negative nominal W with a supported row is enlarged to its O(epsilon) supported bound. If the supported bound is negative, the range is empty. No nonempty integral row range is assigned a population bound below one.

The source pointwise factor and outside normalization yield this excess over the joint side target:

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)
    +(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c+rho L_c+R0
    +g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+small losses.

Using min(c,d)>=p>=R, L_c<=5(R-R0), rho+delta>1 and 5rho>1 bounds the middle line by

    (4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c <=-79p/270-E-B_c.

The last line is <=-delta b2-t2. The remaining normalized reserve is

    H_j(delta)=1-rho-delta A_j-k b_j(5-6rho),
    A_j=min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1)).

Its derivative is 50(1-6k b_j)/(3(5-2delta)^2)-A_j. The safe extrema a_max/M=309/25000 and A_max=4401/5000 give the uniform lower bound 188591/607500>0. Thus its minimum is at delta=.7, where

    H_j(.7)=35/54-(7/10)A_j-(26/9)k b_j.

The cap envelope is smaller for j=1,...,8 and the capacity envelope for j=9,...,30. The reserve decreases on the first segment by [7/10+(26/9)k]/5000 per step; it increases on the second by [(7/10)(C-1)-(26/9)k]/5000. The adjacent cases are

    j=8: A_8=4401/5000, H_8=967/4218750;
    j=9: A_9=275031/312500, H_9=40919/337500000.

The exact finite minimum is 40919/337500000 at case 9, including ceiling and cell-envelope rounding. The continuous crossing t=(1-2N)/C=37/1040 lies inside cell 8; it does not replace these finite bounds. Discarding the cap envelope at the same C,k gives high minimum -150029/67500000. The new original-source hypothesis is essential.

Bins crossing .7 stay in the buffered low branch. Its smaller reserve 57/25000000 pays the O(buffer) loss. Density is used only when its lower edge is at least .7, with no enlargement of range.

For all-height recovery, finite Euler factors and their reciprocals and fixed derivatives cost U^epsilon on a fixed positive-real strip and are nonzero there. Natural zeros remain in the coefficient identities. Profiles separate on a common ambient logarithmic box before live labels. Euler derivatives of K(B product y_i^e_i) are uniform in B>0, so larger a_j gives no hidden power in a smooth seminorm. The weighted Fourier integral is taken in the direct-sum Hilbert space of rows and labels and charges their count once. Coprimality, valuation and zero-bin indicators are never differentiated.

The density's internal detector exponents precede its finite height order. Choose a distinct small external height exponent afterward to fit (1+T)^J in the same reserve. Internal smooth orders are chosen backward through the fixed transform graph; external Fourier-tail orders follow raw polynomial bounds. Arbitrarily larger input heights use absolute polynomial U-bounds absorbed by a sufficiently large fixed polynomial in those input heights. This retains independent plain, slot and witness heights without selecting a detector anew for each row.

### 2.3 Complete return, thresholds and remaining arithmetic

For Re s>1 absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du
      =exp(tau s^2/2) D_chi(s),
    D_chi(s)=N_chi(s) H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi(s)=1-2chi(2)2^-s.                            (L7)

For z=chi(p)p^-s, the local H factors are (1-z)^-2 at p=2,3 and (1-2z)/(1-z)^2 at p>=5. At a ramified prime z=0 exactly. Both H and H^-1 converge absolutely on each fixed half-plane Re s>=sigma>1/2, because the large-prime factors start with z^2 and2/sqrt5<1. N has no zeros in1/2<Re s<1; if2 is ramified it is1. The fixed Gaussian exponential never vanishes.

Under L6 with gamma>1/2, the right u-tail makes L7 holomorphic for Re s>gamma. The left Gaussian tail is paid exactly as in G2, including all fixed s-derivatives on compacta. Multiply by L and continue the identity. Any zero with gamma<Re s<1 would force the nonzero numerator N H exp(tau s^2/2) to vanish, including multiple zeros. The known right edge supplies the remaining boundary. Each fixed character requires its own L6; no average over characters substitutes for it.

Thus the complete new input is the signed geometric-mean bound L6(i) for every large unit log interval. Any gamma<.874861 gives a first gain, gamma=5/6 gives c=1/6, and gamma=3/4 gives c=1/4. The analytic return loses only o(j), so a coarse upper bound on J_j/j below.874861 would suffice even in a route aspiring to3/4. No such arithmetic bound is proved. The trivial absolute Gaussian estimate gives J_j<=j+O(1); the accepted buffered calibration only reproduces the existing endpoint. A fixed empirical mean or an assertion that most signs are random pays none of the required gap.

The same analytic L1–6 lemma applies to any fixed complete ideal Gaussian for which an absolute norm series and its original pole bridge have separately been established. This is an analytic conditional interface, not an integer-CRT proof for ideals.

## G105. Exact continuation classes, reconstructed amplitudes and contours

The critic's protected13 audit factors every nonzero squarefree n<=N
as n=de, with prefix primes<=y and future primes>y. Store a(d) separately
and define V_d(z)=sum_(eligible e<=floor(N/d))a(e)z(e). Then

    M_chi(N)=sum_d a(d)V_d(1).

Distinct squarefree future monomials are independent on the prime torus
and Boolean sign cube. Therefore two normalized continuation laws are equal
exactly when their eligible future support sets agree. Equal integer
quotients suffice, and different quotients can merge if the intervening
range contains no eligible e. Parity/zero flags alone do not suffice.
There are at most2 floor(sqrt N) nonzero normalized states at one stage.
For r distinct nested supports, a triangular monomial matrix proves rankr
for arbitrary linear combinations of those laws. This is not a rank bound
for one fixed signed sum or for nonlinear/approximate encodings.

At N=21,y=5 for principal chi, histories2,3 have law1-z7 and total
amplitude-2; histories5,6,10,15 have law1 and amplitude2. The remaining
history1 has law1-z7-z11-z13-z17-z19. Reconstruction gives M(21)=-2.
For general classes C the exact contraction is sum_C W_C V_C(1), with
W_C=sum_(d in C)a(d). Its amplitudes and all cross terms are still unpaid.
O(sqrt N) states is neither a runtime bound nor square-root cancellation.
The closed quotient recurrence
S_j(m)=S_(j-1)(m)-chi(p_j)S_(j-1)(floor(m/p_j)), S_0(m)=1_(m>=1),
is an exact source organization with the same open signed final estimate.

Uniform17 retains the complete first-Riesz sum
R_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n)log(x/n), whose Mellin integral is
integral x^s/[s^2L(s,chi)] ds/(2pi i) on c>1. A finite rectangle gives
the left line, EVERY enclosed residue, both horizontals and right tail
at most zeta(c)x^c/(pi T). A zero rho of multiplicity m contributes
x^rho P_(m-1)(log x), with nonzero leading coefficient
m!/[L^(m)(rho)rho^2(m-1)!]. A winding-one local detour cannot erase it.
This is a local residue obstruction, not a lower bound for the full sum;
other terms may interfere. A complete all-scale Riesz bound atgamma returns
zero exclusion atgamma, but no low-resolvent arc alone supplies that bound.
G77 already contains the general full-contour principle. This supplies its
Riesz source and explicit truncation cost, not a new uncredited detector.

The other tests retain the literal native H isometric projection identity
with its entire complement, a generic reachable/unobservable-pole toy, and
the exact causal inverse convolution with its moving endpoint. They pay
neither H's fixed-u,v pressure nor its distinct.004 all-g deficit. Divergent
absolute norms and generic toys do not disprove source-specific signed work.

statement:
## 4. A matching diagonal obstruction in the comparison class

The author already supplies the lower price X/G for 1<=G<=c sqrt(X): retain a1=a2=b0=1, d=e=r, G<r<=2G, r^2 l<=X/2. All phases lie in a fixed positive real sector and there are at least c'X/G triples.

The second term has its own comparison-class obstruction. Let Y=floor(X^b), with X sufficiently large, and 1<=G<=c sqrt(Y) for a small fixed c. Retain only d=e=r, G<r<=2G, Y/2<r^2 l<=Y. Let

    A_n=#{r in (G,2G]: r^2 divides n}, Y/2<n<=Y.

Length minus one for each r gives sum_n A_n >>Y/G (choose c small so each Y/(2r^2) is at least four). Hence sum A_n^2>=sum A_n>>Y/G. Give every retained tuple of output n the same sign epsilon_n in {-1,1}; this is a permitted fixed mask. For independent equiprobable signs, at each real x in [X,2X],

    E |sum epsilon_n A_n f_x(n)|^2 = sum A_n^2 |f_x(n)|^2 >>Y/G,
    E |sum epsilon_n A_n f_x(n)|^4 <=3 (sum A_n^2 |f_x(n)|^2)^2.

The fourth-moment inequality follows by enumerating even index multiplicities and remains true for complex f_x(n). Holder yields E|sum epsilon_n z_n| >= (sum |z_n|^2)^(1/2)/sqrt(3). Here |f_x(n)|>=e^-1 on the retained range. Integrate this pointwise expectation over the full shell. Fubini is finite, so at least one fixed sign choice satisfies

    ||F_G||_1 >> X^(b/2)/sqrt(G),

and its L2 norm has the same lower bound up to the fixed measure constant. This is an existence proof; no numerical random draw or average-source theorem is used.

These examples attain each displayed scale as a lower price in the broad bounded-mask class in its stated range. At b=3/2 each scale dominates the other in a nonempty parameter regime, so both terms are needed there. For other b one upper term may be redundant; no universal optimality claim for every b is made. These examples do NOT lower-bound the actual signed Liouville source, its small-gcd residual, or every admissible mask.

statement:
## 3. Actual source identity, floor geometry and profile

Fix one positive modulus q, one ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q, and tau>0. Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), where this is pointwise multiplication; all stars below denote Dirichlet convolution. Complete multiplicativity of chi, including zero values, gives

    (a*chi)(n)=chi(n) sum_{d|n} mu(d)=delta_1(n).

For Y an integer put m=a 1_{n<=Y}, u=a-m. Expanding (a-m)^{*K} and canceling a against chi gives exactly

    u^{*K}*chi^{*(K-1)}
       = a + sum_{j=1}^K (-1)^j binom(K,j)m^{*j}*chi^{*(j-1)}.  (1)

The j=K case contains no a factor to cancel, and the j=1 case has chi^{*0}=delta_1. Solving (1) for a puts coefficient (-1)^(K+1) on its K-short-factor term. No coprimality condition between different factors is introduced. In particular, shared primes and squareful products are necessary parts of the identity. This actual global inverse law is absent from G71's surrogate.

Let L=log X, r=K-1,

    Y=floor(exp(L/(K-1/2))),  V=L/(2K-1),  W=V/2.

Use either band:

    I:  (1/2)L^(1/3) <= K <= 2L^(1/3),
    II: (2/5)sqrt(L)/log L <= K <= 2sqrt(L)/log L,

with K>=2. Completion itself permits odd K; the subsequent moment reduction uses even K. The following are exact, before asymptotics:

    Y^(K-1) <= X exp(-V),
    (Y+1)^K > X exp(V),
    Y^K <= X exp(V).

The strict middle inequality is why the floor causes no missing all-large endpoint. The balanced product condition is

    X exp(-W) <= d_1...d_K <= 2X exp(W),  d_i<=Y.          (2)

Dividing its lower bound by Y^(K-1) gives d_i>=exp(V-W)=exp(W). Thus every short factor is in [exp(W),exp(2V)]. The plain factors remain uncapped positive integers. In band I these lengths have logarithms comparable to L^(2/3); in band II they have logarithms comparable to sqrt(L)log L. Constants are uniform within the displayed bands, with q and tau fixed.

Normalize g(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)) and phi_r=(1+partial_v)^r g. Since D=d/d(log x) acts as -partial_v on g(log(n/x)),

    F_r=(1-D)^r F = sum_n a(n)phi_r(log(n/x)).

Cauchy's derivative formula on the unit circle centered at real v gives

    |g^{(j)}(v)| <= j! C_tau exp(-v^2/(2tau)+|v|/tau).

Indeed Re((v+z)^2)>=v^2-2|v|-1 on |z|=1. Summing binom(r,j)j! costs at most exp(O((r+1)log(r+2))). Completing a real square therefore gives, uniformly for every r,v,

    |phi_r(v)| <= exp(C_tau(r+1)log(r+2)) exp(-v^2/(4tau)). (3)

The same estimate for phi_r' follows by replacing j! with (j+1)!; it has the same logarithmic order in r. These explicit constants, rather than a fixed-order O_r symbol, are what permit the growing order.

statement:
# Ninth-cycle review: the ordinary row series and long-column costs

9 October 2026. Started from clean local revision
ec2f23f097c0b3eb9f2b5df03e3c8250afed2f57. The controller owns records,
Beads and Git writes; research and review agents are read-only.
The user-accepted c0=0.125113352960035869... remains the strongest
project zero-free constant. No stronger constant or complete arithmetic
approximate functional equation is proved in this cycle.

## 1. Exact row Dirichlet series

Use the manuscript's beta(c)=mu(c) conjugate(G(c)) and its cubic
characters, extended by zero on nonunits. All column labels are good
primary elements, coprime to the fixed S. Put

\[
D_h(s)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf}}\beta(c)\vartheta_c(h)q_c^{-s},
\qquad D_h^\#(z)=\overline{D_h(\bar z)},\qquad
Z(v;s,z)=\sum_{h\ne0}D_h(s)D_h^\#(z)q_h^{-v}.
\]

The second coordinate is holomorphic; the positive second moment is
Z(v;w,bar w). Rows include all elements, units and S-prime valuations.
Initially Re s, Re z, Re v>1, so every rearrangement below is absolute.
Write c=da and e=db, with d,a,b pairwise coprime and squarefree, and
eta=theta_a conjugate(theta_b). The common-core identity is

\[
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}
 \vartheta_c(h)\overline{\vartheta_e(h)}
=\beta(a)\overline{\beta(b)}\eta(d)
 1_{(d,h)=1}\eta(h).
\]

Summing the six associate rows kills eta unless its restriction to
mu6 is trivial. In that case eta is a finite-order Hecke character
of primitive conductor ab, and the row sum is
6 L_K(v,eta) product_(p|d)(1-eta(p)Q^(-v)). It is the FULL L-function:
deleting its S factors would remove rows that the target includes.
Consequently, with u=s+z,

\[
\boxed{
Z(v;s,z)=6\!\!\sum_{\substack{a,b\ {\rm sf},\ (a,b)=1\\
                         \eta|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\frac{\beta(a)\overline{\beta(b)}L_K(v,\eta)}
     {q_a^s q_b^z}E_{a,b}(u,v),\qquad
E_{a,b}(u,v)=\prod_{p\nmid abS}
\left(1+\eta(p)Q^{-u}-\eta(p)^2Q^{-(u+v)}\right).
}
\]

The negative local term retains the common-column/nonunit interaction.
A fixed column twist nu adds nu(a) conjugate(nu(b)); its two d factors
cancel. The only principal case is a=b=1. Its contribution is

\[
6\zeta_K(v)E_{1,1}(u,v),\qquad
E_{1,1}(u,1)=\prod_{p\notin S}(1+(1-Q^{-1})Q^{-u}).
\]

This gives the expected O_epsilon(X) smoothed diagonal for
Re u=1+2epsilon. Although E is uniformly bounded when Re u, Re v>1,
that bound alone does not continue the outer double Gauss series.

For ab>1 the ordinary Hecke functional equation is

\[
L(v,\eta)=A(v)(q_aq_b)^{1/2-v}\epsilon(\eta)L(1-v,\bar\eta),
\quad
A(v)=3^{1/2-v}(2\pi)^{2v-1}
             \frac{\Gamma(1-v)}{\Gamma(v)}.
\]

With the manuscript's additive character, CRT and cubic reciprocity give
epsilon(eta)=gamma2(a) conjugate(gamma2(b)). Therefore

\[
\beta(a)\overline{\beta(b)}\epsilon(\eta)
=\mu(a)\mu(b)\vartheta_a(\lambda)
                        \overline{\vartheta_b(\lambda)}.
\]

The a,b cross-character cancels on the retained coprime support.
The nonprincipal part of Z becomes

\[
6A(v)\!\!\sum_{\substack{a,b\ {\rm sf},\ (a,b)=1,\ ab>1\\
                         \eta|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\frac{\mu(a)\mu(b)\eta(\lambda)
 L(1-v,\bar\eta)E_{a,b}(u,v)}
 {q_a^{s+v-1/2}q_b^{z+v-1/2}}. \tag{R1}
\]

The [ordinary Hecke normalization](https://arxiv.org/html/1707.00091v3)
is the one used in the supplied manuscript. Here the root-number
cancellation is computed for the actual coefficient, rather than
inferred from a formal resemblance to a linear theta source.

## 2. A continuation cone and its precise limitation

Write b0=1-c0. The accepted uniform reciprocal-L bounds give analytic
continuation of (R1), through a normally convergent AUXILIARY expansion,
to every compact buffered subregion of

\[
\boxed{\Re v<0,\qquad
\Re(s+v-\tfrac12)>b_0,\qquad
\Re(z+v-\tfrac12)>b_0.} \tag{R2}
\]

To prove this, expand L(1-v,bar eta) absolutely. Expand E using
disjoint squarefree d1,d2 with term
mu(d2) eta(d1 d2^2) q_d1^(-u) q_d2^(-(u+v)). Insert the COMPLETE
projector sum_(ell|(a,b)) mu(ell) and the finite unit-neutral projector.
After a=ell a', b=ell b', two masked Mobius Dirichlet series separate.
They retain all character zeros and deletions at ell d1 d2 S.
Subtract the a=b=1 term when replacing the restricted outer sum by
the product of these two series; it has already been separated above.
Each is a reciprocal finite-order Hecke L-function with deleted
Euler factors. The accepted buffered bounds cost only
(q_k q_d1 q_d2 q_ell)^delta, after rescaling delta to absorb the
fixed powers in the conductor.

Choose delta smaller than the compact region's margins. The k sum
converges since Re(1-v)>1; the remaining d1,d2,ell sums converge since

\[
\Re u>1,\qquad \Re(u+v)>1,\qquad
\Re(s+z+2v-1)>1.
\]

These inequalities follow from (R2) and 2b0>1. Initially the two
reciprocal series converge absolutely to the right of one. Ordinary
polynomial conductor bounds for L(v,eta), with s,z sufficiently far
right, give a bridge across v=0 from the original chamber. This
identifies the continued expression with Z. The explicitly separated
principal term is retained. Neither convergence of the original h sum
nor normal convergence of the raw double Mobius series in (R1) is
claimed throughout the new cone.

In the symmetric case Re s=Re z=sigma, (R2) requires
sigma>b0+1/2-Re v>1.374886647... . Its convex hull with the original
absolute chamber still has sigma>1. It does not reach the desired
central point sigma=1/2+epsilon, Re v<35/32. Nor is the reflected
sixth-order family identified with this same MDS.

There is a useful exact criterion for a future continuation argument.
At fixed w=1/2+epsilon+it the coefficients of Z(v;w,bar w), grouped by
the integer norm q_h, are nonnegative. The previously proved coarse
row bounds give a finite convergence abscissa. If its actual continuation
were holomorphic near EVERY real v>1+eta, Landau's positivity argument
would force that abscissa to be at most 1+eta. Indeed, Taylor expansion
leftwards from a real point just to the right of a hypothetical larger
abscissa has coefficients
sum_n a_n (log n)^j n^(-v0)/j! >=0. Tonelli then turns convergence of
the Taylor series across the abscissa into convergence of the original
positive Dirichlet series there, a contradiction.

If, in addition, Z(1+eta+delta;w,bar w) has polynomial height cost,
positivity gives (65) immediately. This implication needs no vertical-v
estimate. Both its central-continuation premise and its height bound
remain OPEN; (R2) proves neither.

## 3. Poisson identifies the unpaid signed mean

Consider the actual central polynomial on a smooth column dyad
q_c comparable to D, with coefficients beta(c)q_c^(-1/2), and a
smooth radial row profile at scale X. Arbitrarily small central
buffers and profile derivatives have the stated small-power and
polynomial height costs. For q_d comparable to C put
L=D/C and H=D^2/(CX).

Common-core Poisson retains the dual coefficient

\[
\mu(ab)\sqrt{q_{ab}}\,c_d(k)\,
\vartheta_a(\lambda)\overline{\vartheta_b(\lambda)}
\overline{\vartheta_a(dk)}\vartheta_b(dk)
\]

and the ONE kernel
Phi_hat(X q_k/(q_d q_a q_b)). All coprimality and nonunit masks remain.
Here c_d is the corresponding Ramanujan sum. Resolving it and using
the existing cubic sieve after taking absolute values gives the
available upper-bound cost

\[
\mathcal M(X,D)\ll(XD)^\delta
 [X+D+X^{2/3}D^{2/3}+X^{1/3}D]. \tag{R3}
\]

An apparent diagonal of the dual positive Mobius norm is not a new
main term of the off-diagonal transform: its complete ell-projector
cancels by sum_(ell|a) mu(ell)=0 for a>1.

The accepted individual Mobius bounds pay the principal dual packet
at cost

\[
(XD)^\delta X^{2/3}D^{2b_0-4/3}. \tag{R4}
\]

For k=zj, z|d, principal induction requires dzj to be a cube outside
S. Thus j contains z(d/z)^2, leaving O((H/C^2)^(1/3)) rows up to
divisor and fixed-S losses. The common-core dyad has weight
C^(1-2b0+delta), which is summable. This is an upper-bound budget,
not a lower bound for the actual signed packet.

At D=X, (R3) costs X^(4/3), while (R4) costs
X^(1.0831066274...). At D=X^2 they cost respectively X^(7/3) and
X^(1.4995465882...). The target is X^(35/32); the latter two excesses
are 119/96 and 0.4057965882... . At D=X^2 the dual length is H=X^3.
Its nonprincipal signed bilinear target is X^(131/32+delta), whereas
the generic positive certificate costs X^(16/3+delta).
The principal packet also needs more at this longer scale.

## 4. The global reflection does not shorten the columns

Work in the ENTIRE fixed-level induced space, with compact-picture
bases f_j^+ and f_l^- and actual fixed-place intertwining matrix
M_S(w)f_j^+=sum_l m_lj(w)f_l^-. The four original norm selectors
need not form an invariant subspace. Define reflected arithmetic
coefficients by E^-_(r,l)(a_y;z)=J W^-(r,y,z) A^-_l(r,z).
This retains every fixed-place sector and row valuation; it does not
identify A^- with one of the four original Psi functions.

For r=h^4, kappa=2pi/sqrt(3), B=B_nu and xi=B^6, the established
Whittaker comparison and the
[KP global intertwiner and functional equation, II.1.2--II.1.3](https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/BF02698770.pdf)
give the meromorphic operator identity

\[
\Psi_j^+(h,w)=
\kappa\bar\alpha(r)(\kappa|r|)^{1-2w}
\frac{\Gamma(w)}{\Gamma(2-w)}
\frac{L^S(6w-3,\xi)}{L^S(6w-2,\xi)}
\sum_l m_{lj}(w)\mathcal A^-_l(r,1-w). \tag{R5}
\]

The two archimedean minus signs and J cancel. Reflection inverts
the inducing ratio B and preserves the center by the common B(det)
twist, trivial on SL2. The genuine epsilon remains the calibrated
one; it is not silently conjugated.

Multiplying by Lambda(6w-2,xi)/Gamma(w+1) gives the completed
coefficient. Its gamma factor is

\[
\frac{\Gamma_{\mathbb C}(6w+1)}{\Gamma(w+1)}
=C A^w\prod_{j=1}^{5}\Gamma(w+j/6).
\]

Thus the FORMAL conductor and balanced length are
q_h^4 T^10 and q_h^2 T^5, respectively. In particular
|h^4|^(1-2w)=q_h^(2-4w). A usable arithmetic approximate functional
equation still needs the normalized bad-place matrix, cancellation
or clearing of its apparent poles, arithmetic reflected coefficients
and coefficient-energy bounds, and row-map collision bounds for
squarefree extraction. A pointwise extraction l1 bound alone does
not transfer an all-row mean.

Even granting those missing inputs ideally, a central column dyad
of length M has squared coefficient mass O(M^(-2epsilon)).
The all-element sieve costs
[X+X^(1/3)M+(XM)^(2/3)] M^(-2epsilon), hence
X^(7/3-4epsilon) at M=X^2. Ideal cube-free extraction would reduce
this only to X^(2-4epsilon).

Unbalancing M=X^a, N=X^(4-a) gives the two costs
F(X,M)M^(-2epsilon) and X^(-8epsilon)F(X,N)N^(2epsilon).
For 0<epsilon<1/6, the direct long-column term when a>=2, or
the dual one when a<=2, has at least the balanced certificate's
exponent. This is a limitation of THESE upper-bound estimates,
not a lower bound on the actual mean. It supplies neither eta=3/32
nor a new zero-free constant.

## 5. Retaining the quadratic Jacobi variables

For coprime odd squarefree integer columns n,m, set q=nm,
chi=chi_n chi_m, and K_n(x)=chi_n(x(1-x)). The exact retained
auxiliary-variable transform is

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{r\bmod q}\sum_{x\bmod n,y\bmod m}
\chi_n(-r x(1-x))\chi_m(-r y(1-y))e_q(kr)\\
&\qquad=\mu(n)\mu(m)\tau_\chi\overline{\chi(k)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Indeed the r sum is the primitive Gauss transform, and
J_n(0)=chi_n(-1)mu(n) contracts the two constant-weight auxiliary
sums. No nonzero auxiliary Fourier frequency has been created.
For shared core g, n=ga,m=gb, the row character is instead
chi_ab(u) 1_((u,g)=1); expanding its mask gives every r|g branch
with row scale H/r and primitive conductor ab. The principal case
a=b=1 remains.

The [Blomer--Pascadi fixed-modulus theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24311v1#S1.SS1)
requires two interval arguments. Our exact Jacobi transform fixes
the first argument and puts squares in the second, so its balanced
saving is unavailable. At H=D^1.498 and q comparable to D^2 the
row-dual length would be q/H=q^0.251; this does not create two
independent interval arguments of length comparable to sqrt(q).

Decomposing every positive integer row u=v a^2, with v squarefree,
retains chi_n(u)=chi_n(v)1_((a,n)=1). Applying the
[quadratic large sieve](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3A[private operational identifier omitted])
to each v family therefore gives

\[
\frac1D\sum_{u\le H}
\left|\sum_{n\ {\rm odd}}\mu(n)\chi_n(u)W(n/D)\right|^2
\ll(HD)^\delta[H+D\sqrt H].
\]

This preserves the principal-square repetitions. At H=D^1.498 its
excess over H is D^0.251. The exact detector has not supplied a paid
transfer to two independent Kloosterman arguments or an improved CM2.

## 6. A stable first-shell inverse and its unpaid future tail

This is a distinct non-character test of agenda D1--D7. Set t=2sigma,
0<sigma<1, p_k=k^(-t)-(k+1)^(-t), and use
||F||_sigma^2=t^(-1) sum_k p_k |F(k)|^2. Let h_N be the agenda's
exact finite-prefix interpolant and r_N=1-h_N. For N<=n<2N put
b_n=n f_n-2N f_(2N). On N<=k<2N,

\[
b_n(k)=-n1_{k\ge n},\qquad
a_n=-\frac{r(n)-r(n-1)}n,\quad r(N-1)=0.
\]

This is the unique exact first-shell inverse; including n=N is
necessary. It satisfies sum|n a_n|^2<=4 sum|r(k)|^2. The weighted
version has a sigma-dependent constant since p_k is comparable
on the shell. This does not bound the correction's future repetitions.
For the actual residual,

\[
a_N=-S_{N-1}-\mu(N)/N,\qquad a_n=-\mu(n)/n\ (n>N),
\quad\boxed{c_N:=\sum a_n b_n=h_{2N}-h_N.} \tag{R6}
\]

Thus exact refitting produces the old interpolant at twice the scale.
One component is completely stable: B_N=2f_(2N)-f_N is the indicator
of alternating integer blocks [(2j+1)N,(2j+2)N). If
eta_alt(t)=sum_(j>=1)(-1)^(j-1)j^(-t), then
||B_N||_sigma^2=N^(-t)eta_alt(t)/t. Its first-shell mass is
N^(-t)(1-2^(-t))/t and its future mass is their difference.
The initial correction (N S_(N-1)+mu(N))B_N consequently has
controlled future-to-shell cost. The remaining increments are
the source of the unproved analytic estimate.

The complete future correction has the exact floor representation

\[
c_N(k)=\sum_{N\le n<2N}\mu(n)\lfloor k/n\rfloor
+NS_{N-1}\lfloor k/N\rfloor
-2NS_{2N-1}\lfloor k/(2N)\rfloor. \tag{R7}
\]

Let F_N be the squared residual norm restricted to N<=k<2N,
T_N the squared correction norm on k>=2N, and J_N the inner product
of r_N with c_N on k>=2N, all with weight p_k/t. Then

\[
\boxed{\|r_N\|_\sigma^2-\|r_{2N}\|_\sigma^2
       =F_N+2\Re J_N-T_N.} \tag{R8}
\]

Interpolation removes the first shell but need not decrease the
total norm. An independent exact expression for its future cost is

\[
\begin{gathered}
A_N(s)=\sum_{N\le n<2N}\mu(n)n^{-s}
       +N^{1-s}S_{N-1}-(2N)^{1-s}S_{2N-1},\\
T_N=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{|\zeta(\sigma+iu)A_N(\sigma+iu)|^2}{\sigma^2+u^2}\,du-F_N .
\end{gathered} \tag{R9}
\]

This follows directly from the Mellin transform
Mf_n(s)=zeta(s)(n^(-1)-n^(-s))/s and Plancherel. It uses no new
reciprocal bound. For b=b0+epsilon<1, the accepted Mertens estimate
and partial summation give S_(N-1)<<N^(b-1) and F_N<<N^(2b-2sigma).
The fractional-part expression gives |c_N(k)|<<N. Expanding the
floors in (R7) instead gives |c_N(k)|<<k N^(b-1). Splitting the
weighted tail at N^(2-b) proves

\[
T_N\ll_{\sigma,\epsilon}N^{\,2-2\sigma(2-b)}. \tag{R10}
\]

At sigma=0.8745 the limiting first-shell and future-tail exponents
are +0.000773294079928262 and +0.032176745672897265... .
These are insufficient upper-bound certificates, not lower bounds
or divergence results. The crude full-tail bound decays only for
sigma>1/(2-b0), approximately 0.8887993351.

A sufficient next lemma is the SIGNED capture inequality
F_(2^j)+2 Re J_(2^j)-T_(2^j)>=delta_j ||r_(2^j)||_sigma^2,
where 0<=delta_j<1 and sum_j delta_j diverges. No such inequality
is proved. Even first-shell convergence requires an improved
square-integral estimate for
N S_(N-1)+M(k)-M(N-1); good finite interpolation alone does not
provide it.

## 7. Evidence and next allocation

cubic_covariance derived the row series, root cancellation, auxiliary
continuation cone and direct Poisson budgets. review_cubic independently
checked them and the controller's Landau implication. Its review
required distinguishing normal convergence of the auxiliary expansion
from the raw double series and keeping the holomorphic second-coordinate
convention explicit.

sixth_order derived the full-space operator reflection and its
conductor budget. review_sixth checked the scalar, gamma normalization,
center-preserving twist and unbalancing. The integrated wording
distinguishes an available upper-bound cost from a lower bound on
the actual mean and retains the unfinished arithmetic-AFE obligations.

sextic_optimization tested the retained quadratic variables and the
fractional-part correction. review_sextic accepted both, retaining
the exact S_(N-1), S_(2N-1) endpoints, 0<sigma<1, the shared-column
masks and the distinction between coefficient stability and tail cost.
The controller verified (R6)
and its prefix/first-shell identities using exact rational arithmetic
in 4,914 cases (2<=N<=40, 1<=k<=6N). Exact fraction arithmetic also
checked the exponent gaps 23/96, 119/96 and 29/32. These finite checks
do not prove an analytic mean or tail-capture inequality.
Receipts are in ignored [restricted provenance path] mathematical source]

The ordinary mean (65) remains the main analytic target, with
eta<247/2506, for the complete finite-divisor transfer already proved
in [private research revision]. Further fixed-level AFE bookkeeping alone cannot make
the displayed generic bounds pay. A productive continuation of this
route needs a signed long-column estimate or actual central continuation
of the row series with polynomial height control. Both principal and
nonprincipal packets must be paid at length X^2.

The fractional-part route now has a concrete independent signed tail
covariance to test. Its finite inverse is no longer an open problem.
The compensated sextic short-divisor estimate remains an alternative;
the conditional c=0.12551 certificate is unchanged. Beads carries the
active plan. No route has yet crossed the zero-free milestone.
title: Ninth-cycle review: the ordinary row series and long-column costs

### The actual prime pool and slot gap

PR9 B3.7, manuscript lines 2356--2393, puts `ell_*=sigma/3`, requires mesh below `sigma/6`, and uses good primes in `(Z^(ell_*)/2,Z^(ell_*)]`. The exact source does not assume `sigma` tends to zero with the requested local epsilon:

```
eventually_original_amplification:
  sigma > 0, loss > 0, Mmax >= 0, profile upper endpoint b >= 0,
  eta_mesh < sigma/6;
  bounded masks R,s; retained dyadic row logarithm <= Mmax.
```

It then supplies the actual nonempty prime pool, its cardinality saving, source character families with conductor bounds, and the main/error energy inequality. The constant `(Mmax+2 sigma)/(sigma/6)` is a fixed multiplicity constant, not a new exponent. Any fixed positive sigma works. Polynomial mask sizes and row bounds can be enclosed uniformly on the compact local geometry. For `a=M/160`, choosing mesh below `a/10` is stronger than the required mesh below `a/2=sigma/6`. The finitely many original slots are smaller than every amplifier prime eventually. Removing support, row, mask, and first-projector primes omits only `O(log Z)` choices. There is no prime-supply or fixed-small-prime-cutoff obstruction.

This does **not** substitute `sigma=3M/160` into the old proof of the global `9/2` moment. In that proof, B3.10 (lines 2631--2656) chooses a small internal sigma so terminal costs `3 sigma + 5 sigma/3` fit an arbitrary epsilon. The new local proof calls the completed old theorem with its own chosen small loss, and therefore its own internal induction parameters. Its separate, fixed outer amplifier cost is paid by the local strict reserves. Conflating these two sigma choices would invalidate the extension; keeping them separate is legitimate and is what PLA already does for `M/2000`.

The main amplified term retains the original columns and coefficients. The amplifier prime does not become a new varying parent in its density dictionary. The three extracted errors do retain the appropriate moving-prime characters and conductor contribution; they are bounded by the old moment and the original extraction ledger, never by the fixed-parent density theorem.

## 5. Genuine embedding in the [restricted research revision] joint bank

For K, use the exact source-bound sextic symbol psi_k(a)=chi_a(k), with its zero extension and [restricted research revision] G212's global primary representatives. These representatives multiply on good ideals, so f0²e0⁶ represents f²e⁶ without an untracked unit. For good squarefree f and arbitrary good e,
    chi_a(f)^4 chi_a(f²e⁶)
           =1_((a,fe)=1).                            (5.1)
This holds even when f and e share primes, and when a shares one of those primes: both sides are then zero. No cancelled character power is replaced by1 at a nonunit.

For Z tending to infinity and x on a shell X=Z^N with fixed N>0, form the normalized joint source
    T_(f,k)(x)=X^(-1/2) sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)
       1_((a,S)=1) chi_a(k)chi_a(f)^4
                         g_tau(log(q_a/x)).            (5.2)
These are new coefficients, not the canonical Gauss coefficients or the old physical numerator. They are independent of live f,k and have the normalized squarefree column mass used by the generic sieves. (5.1) gives
    T_(f,f²e⁶)(x)=X^(-1/2)U_rad(fe)(x).                (5.3)
For each f, e->f²e⁶ is injective in ideals. Fix
    F=Z^V, E=Z^R, M=2V+6R, Urow=Z^M,
with fixed V,R>0 for the two-sided approximation; the V=0 one-sided
variant is defined below.
All selected k satisfy q_k<=4Urow. The exact selected pair count is N_F N_E, not N_F Urow. The full positive joint norm dominates its selected principal part, so
    B_(F,E)(X)
       <= C_S X Z^(-R) [ F^(-1) sum_(f) sum_(q_k<=4Urow)
                           integral_X^(2X)|T_(f,k)(x)|² dx/x ].
                                                               (5.4)
Constants account only for the exact F/E counts. This is lawful positive-norm restriction, not signed subset domination. Full Gaussian tails can be treated by annular decomposition and Gaussian summability; there is no sharp source cutoff or unpaid small scale.

[restricted research revision]'s generic proof uses arbitrary f,k-independent column coefficients. Conditional on its NAMED sextic and squarefree cubic sieve inputs, it therefore supplies the same normalized upper-envelope exponent
    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M)
        {(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L(N,V))},
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6),
    L(N,V)=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).                         (5.5)
It does not supply a new Möbius-specific cancellation estimate.

When V=0, take Fset={1}. The corresponding fixed detector has local weight
1-q_p^(-1), not(q_p-1)/(q_p+1); its sole cofactor error and the same
zero-free multiplier proof are given in support SectionB. Thus the V=0
price comparison below also belongs to a legitimate detector variant.

## 4. First transform, comparison and low-bin descendants

The equal-product comparison uses lengths M/4 and n1+n2-M/4, identical masks, whole character and profiles. Delete its exact extra mask and reflect only the long factor. Its old capacity is at most

\[
 M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+\xi=93M/100+\xi<M.
\]

The old nonempty or unrestricted empty-slot theorem applies. Whole-factor conjugation, redundant Euler coefficient mass, eligibility and two-scale supremum are retained.

For the centered difference, first-transform outside exponent is M-A-R/2-E. Keep first labels INSIDE Hilbert-space Cauchy. The C-side joint target is

\[
 \sum_\lambda\mathcal N_{C,\lambda}
 \ll Z^{p+A-c+R+E+B_c+\eta},\qquad
 B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6,                             \tag{7}
\]

with the exchanged D target. Here the local p is first radical width. Since B_c+B_d<=c+d-2p-R, their geometric mean times the outside factor has exponent

\[
 M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(B_c+B_d)/2+\eta\le M+\eta.
\]

No first-label count is added after that step.

At radius (6) the exact main child formulas are

\[
 M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-\omega-g_2+t_2,
\]
\[
 (A-c-c_2-M')-(A-M)
 =6a+\omega-\min(c,d)-(c_2-g_2)-t_2\le6a+\omega.
\]

The available inner allowance is M'+Delta with Delta=b2-p2+B_c+a>=a. Insert the low indicator only AFTER both transforms, on positive allocated child energy, for bins with upper parameter .7+O(e). It is never passed through Poisson or differentiated. Retain the full second projector and signed priority allocations.

Greedily remove original slots until the OLD 9/2 capacity holds or slots are exhausted. Squared pointwise price is .7+O(e) per removed width, hence r_low=7/45+O(e) per defect. Coefficient identities, anchor Q_*, relative characters, zeros and keep gate stay literal. Drop the low indicator only after pointwise payment. Exhaustion invokes the unrestricted old zero-slot estimate, with no invented condition on the sum of plain lengths.

Let d_* be actual canonical width minus M'. It can be negative. For d_*<=delta2 and 0<=s<=1,

\[
 d_*+s(F-d_*)_+\le\delta_2+sF_+.
\]

Applying this with s=r_low pays actual width and slot removal together by M'+(7/45)(g+6a)+eta. On interval j the reserve is

\[

### D26.2 Complete field approximation and cross terms

Let W_P be the fixed field at a specified prime cutoff P whose Mellin transform is

    Mellin(W_P)(s)=exp(s^2) E(s) Rcal_<=P(s)/L_K^S(s,eta). (3.5)

The fully corrected field W has the same transform with Rcal in place of Rcal_<=P. By (2.8), P_eta is exactly C_S exp(25/36) times W at the fixed dilation exp(-5/3). Thus no physical scale normalizer is lost.

Assume the inherited complete M_eta,2 bound ||M_eta,2||_beta<infinity for one fixed 2/3<beta<1. This is the source-level calibrated bound furnished by the accepted fixed-family zero-free premise with a positive buffer; it is not a new exponent. The coefficient convolution norm, uniform finite-product mass and (3.4) give

    ||W-W_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(4-6beta).               (3.6)

This holds for every X>0 and P>=2 with one constant for fixed eta,S,beta. It therefore remains valid at P_X=X^theta. Define q=beta-theta(6beta-4). Then the complete error is O(X^q).

If an actual source estimate proves

    ||W_(X^theta)||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)    (OPEN-W42)

for every large dyadic X, and q<gamma, (3.6) gives W, then P_eta and M_eta,2, the same gamma exponent. D02 supplies the fixed-family zero-exclusion return. Conversely a complete gamma bound for M gives OPEN-W42 because the weighted norms of E Rcal_<=P are uniformly bounded at each gamma+epsilon>2/3. In the stated range this remains an equivalent arithmetic target, not a weaker exponent theorem.

The full mixed energy is explicitly retained. For R_X=W-W_P,

    ||W||^2=||W_P||^2+2 Re<W_P,R_X>+||R_X||^2,
    | ||W||^2-||W_P||^2 |
       <=2 ||W_P|| ||R_X||+||R_X||^2.                  (3.7)

Under OPEN-W42 the right side is O(X^(gamma+q+epsilon)+X^(2q)); both terms are below the target 2gamma with a positive buffer. Using only the inherited beta bound would instead pay beta+q, which is coarser and is not needed for the norm implication. No negative cross term is dropped and no different detector savings are added.
