## Exact coefficient and valuation audit

For J=[U^eta,U^(2eta)), the ordered pair weight is sum_{p,q in J,pq|b} logNp logNq/(logNb)^2. At p=q it requires v_p(b)>=2 and counts that pair ONCE, regardless of higher valuation. Expanding the square of the radical logarithm removes precisely the v_p(b)=1 diagonal. Hence the author's (8) is exact. Since J is disjoint from the old closed band, omega<=ell_J(b)^2/(logNb)^2<=(1-theta)^2<=1-theta. This is a coefficient inequality only.

For every extracted L and d=pq, put h=d/gcd(d,L). At each prime the remaining divisibility requirement is max(v_p(d)-v_p(L),0), so d|Lc iff h|c. Substituting c=h c' preserves all remaining valuations and gives the exact phase phi(h), normalization (Nh)^(-1/2), and length E/Nh. It does not divide by a character. If p=q, h=p^2,p,1 for v_p(L)=0,1,>=2. If p!=q, h contains exactly the missing primes. Natural zeros are multiplicative through this substitution, even when primes occur simultaneously in L, the inverse puncture and the cofactor. The logarithmic profile is exact: NL*Nc=D*(Nc/E). This verifies author (15), including the most dangerous middle valuation.

A useful independent refinement is available without any new analytic input. Write s=(1+beta)/2, w_p=logNp/logD, I=sum_{p|L}w_p, V=sum_{p not|L}w_p(Np)^(-s). The EXACT positive pair mass after the shortened plain estimate is

  A_L=sum_{p,q in J} w_p w_q N(pq/gcd(pq,L))^(-s)
     =(I+V)^2-sum_{p in J,v_p(L)=1}w_p^2[1-(Np)^(-s)].

Proof: all distinct pairs factor as products of the single-prime weights; their diagonal removal is restored by p^(-2s) when v_p(L)=0, p^(-s) when v_p(L)=1, and1 when v_p(L)>=2. Thus only valuation1 differs from the diagonal of (I+V)^2. This identity includes p=q and every shared-prime equality. In particular A_L<= (I+V)^2; no extra diagonal loss is needed. It is a sharper label-specific absolute block mass, not a signed norm contraction or a new global power saving.

Nonempty support gives NL<=CD, so I<=1+O(1/logD). Ideal counting gives V<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2), A=U^(2eta). Therefore A_L<<U^epsilon A^(1-beta). The original whole profile contributes only its declared common derivative/height envelope. This re-proves the author's uniform (16), and clarifies that its SQUARED cost is A^(2(1-beta))=Y^(1-beta), once.

## 5. W60-28 and W60-26: what the native H packet actually permits

Freeze the literal finite packet and both independent heights before forming its matrix. The conventions in G75 give H=w*Tv, T=K^T. T contains the complete short-core sum, all original masks/projectors, both rooted mark factors, natural zeros, ray/CRT phases, and every original coefficient. The raw target remains G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]sqrt(Omega1 Omega2)P_orig; the outside factor N^-1 G^-2 is applied once. Nothing below estimates that target or its complementary branches.

**W60-28 first test: the proposed mark constraint is not source-valid.** In [restricted mathematical source] Section1 the native coefficients are a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n), xi(g)=alpha(g)^3eta(g)^3, and the two mark arrays u_i are independent original arrays. They are not the rational sequence mu(n)chi(n). A relation u(pn)=-chi(p)u(n) is therefore not available. When both indices are in an allowed support, the array assigning1 at the first and0 at the second already violates it. A support with no such pair supplies no constraint either. Copying the rational prime relation onto the native mark vector changes the admissible input class.

Upstream rational convolution constraints can be used only after deriving their exact map through the source construction, with roots, masks and boundary terms. The prior full-divisor SDP in W38 R38.7 already gives a valid rational-source certificate; this round does not rename it as new native H progress. W60-28 stops at the failed source test. An actual transported relation remains OPEN.

**W60-26 first test: a positive real auxiliary linearization is impossible for nonzero T.** For any real theta let

    A_theta=[[0,e^(i theta)T],[e^(-i theta)T*,0]],  x=(w,v).

Then x*A_theta x=2 Re(e^(i theta)H). Its nonzero eigenvalues occur as +s_j,-s_j for the singular values of T: if Tv=s w and T*w=s v, the vectors(e^(i theta)w,+/-v) verify this directly. Thus its realification B is indefinite whenever T!=0.

Suppose a positive probability measure, independent of y, and a real linear auxiliary coupling represented exp(y^T B y) as E exp(y dot F) on a neighborhood of0. The Hessian at0 of the logarithm of the right side is Cov(F), positive semidefinite; the left Hessian is2B, indefinite. This disproves that specified positive-real representation for the literal bilinear dilation. It is not a claim that every Gibbs/variational model is impossible.

The exact complex Gaussian alternative diagonalizes B and uses independent standard real Gaussians G_j:

    E exp(sqrt(2) sum_(lambda_j>0)sqrt(lambda_j)y_j G_j
          +i sqrt(2) sum_(lambda_j<0)sqrt(-lambda_j)y_j G_j)
       =exp(y^T B y).                                         (H1)

The formula follows from the one-dimensional Gaussian integral in each coordinate. Taking the absolute value INSIDE this expectation gives exp(y^T B_+ y), losing precisely the factor exp(y^T B_- y), where B_-=(-B)_+ and B=B_+-B_-. In the diagnostic B=diag(1,-1), y=(0,1), the exact value is e^-1 and the absolute expectation is1. The indefinite two-by-two off-diagonal block has the same eigenvalues. There is no unrecorded positive normalization or automatic phase gain. A useful estimate would retain the full imaginary-field cancellation with the physical source. This is an unpaid alternative, not an H estimate.

## 5. Development C / W49-06: exact prime-square deletion with a complete return

This wildcard changes the source to the completely multiplicative Liouville sign while preserving all omitted-square errors explicitly. Let lambda(n)=(-1)^Omega(n), and for an integer Y>=2 set

    a_(Y,chi)(n)=lambda(n)chi(n) product_(p<=Y)(1-1_(p^2|n)),
    A_(Y,chi)(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_(Y,chi)(n).                  (C1)

At small primes the valuations0,1 survive and all higher valuations are zero. At primes>Y every lambda power remains. Ramified character values are still zero. C1 equals mu(n)chi(n) unless n has a square prime divisor p^2 with p>Y and no smaller forbidden square. Therefore the COMPLETE difference, including all overlaps, obeys

    |A_(Y,chi)(x)-M_chi(x)|
      <=sum_(p>Y) floor(x/p^2)
      <=x sum_(m>Y)m^-2 <=x/Y.                            (C2)

The first inequality bounds an actual coefficient difference of modulus at most1, not an incorrectly counted signed inclusion-exclusion tail. The union bound may overcount overlaps, which is legitimate here. It is independent of chi.

Expanding the finite product gives a separate exact signed identity

    A_(Y,chi)(x)
      =sum_(d<=sqrt x, P^+(d)<=Y) mu(d)chi(d)^2
                         L_chi(x/d^2),
    L_chi(t)=sum_(m<=t)lambda(m)chi(m).                    (C3)

There is NO condition (d,m)=1. Products d of several small primes may be much larger than Y. The overlap for two distinct primes p,r is the positive term 1_(p^2 r^2|n) in the expanded indicator. Dropping it changes C1; all these terms are retained by C3. At n=p^2 r^2 the four local inclusion-exclusion coefficients are 1,-1,-1,+1, summing to zero.

Fix gamma in(1/2,1), a positive buffer eta, and delta=1-gamma+eta<1/2. For each dyadic X set Y_X=ceil(X^delta), fixed across that shell. C2 gives

    sup_(X<=x<=2X)|A_(Y_X,chi)(x)-M_chi(x)|
                          <=2X^(gamma-eta).              (C4)

Thus the EVERY-large-shell, EVERY-epsilon sup estimate for this moving source at exponent gamma is equivalent to Z1, in both directions. In particular the coarse complete complement permits:

| Conditional c | gamma | sufficient prime-square threshold exponent delta |
|---|---|---|
| .12514 | .87486 | .12514+eta |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1/6+eta |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1/4+eta |

Always take eta>0 small enough that delta<1/2. The target still includes the d=1 Liouville sum and the entire signed d-sum in C3. One interval or one character does not satisfy it. The moving source is first returned to FIXED mu*chi by C4; no Mellin transform is assigned to the changing prime mask. Z1 then pays all heights and imprimitive zeros. If a squared-norm variant is used, write A=M+E and retain 2 Re<M,E>+||E||^2, or use both norm triangle inequalities after C4; no cross term disappears.

The classical full square-divisor identities already give

    [lambda(n)chi(n)] = [mu(n)chi(n)] convolved with chi(d)^2 on squares,
    [mu(n)chi(n)] = [lambda(n)chi(n)] convolved with mu(d)chi(d)^2 on squares.

Both absolute square-kernel norms are finite at any weight gamma>1/2, bounded by zeta(2gamma). Hence the complete Liouville exponent is not automatically easier than the complete Mobius exponent. W24 already proves a stronger, different shrinking-window DP estimate for a cutoff d>D, and [private research revision] preserves the Liouville/gcd option. C1 uses the condition P^+(d)<=Y, rather than d<=Y; they must not be interchanged. The modest contribution here is the elementary sharp-sum moving-prime-mask contract C2–C4 with its explicit common-character return. It is a representation/complement payment, not a new arithmetic saving or replacement for W24.

Next action: estimate the full small-prime-square-excluded lambda sum in C1/C3 using its complete multiplicativity before enforcing the mask, and keep the signed square-divisor sum intact. No quantitative cancellation bound for it was obtained.

imported statements.

The actual source slots require care. If the signed source vector is
f=(V theta_i1,-V theta_i2)^T, then f_ray=ell_ray(f), with ell_ray defined
from the fixed seed r(nu0). The literal period uses f_ray(z1) f_ray(z2),
the SAME linear combination in both slots, and then sums the two ray terms.
It is not theta_i1(z1) theta_i2(z2). Below W1,W2 label the two slots, both
chosen from this f_ray. The raw source constant terms need not vanish.
Nevertheless R3Q1/A.1 proves that replacing centered sources by full sources
does not change the complete U' period: integrating the variable belonging
to any source constant kills the kernel, which has no zero frequency.
Keep those constants through an unfolding; their mere presence cannot prove
a surviving boundary in the final period.

## 3. Exact H-orbit geometry: what “both cells” does not specify

Write H elements as (x,y,t), acting in the affine chart by

    (z1,z2,z3) -> (t^2 z1+x, t^2 z2+y, t^2 z3+x+y).

Each infinity coordinate stays infinity. In the fully finite chart,
d=z3-z1-z2 transforms to t^2 d. Consequently the orbit list over an
algebraic closure is:

| Representative | Number of strata | Orbit dimension | Stabilizer |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| (0,0,1), d!=0 | 1 | 3 | t=+/-1, x=y=0 |
| (0,0,0), d=0 | 1 | 2 | T_delta |
| (infinity,0,0) and its other two placements | 3 | 2 | T_delta |
| Two infinities and one zero | 3 | 1 | T_delta with one unipotent dimension |
| (infinity,infinity,infinity) | 1 | 0 | H |

For example, with first coordinate infinity the independent translations
y and x+y set the other two coordinates to zero. With two infinities only
one translation condition remains. This proves completeness and distinguishes
all nine strata without a classification theorem.

Over the actual odd nonarchimedean field, the open finite-chart orbit splits
according to d in F^*/F^{*2}, which has four classes. This is a rational-orbit
distinction; it does not create four more geometric boundary divisors. The
other eight orbits do not split, so there are twelve F-rational orbits in all.
Over the finite residue field there are ten: two open square classes plus
those same eight closed orbits. The
selected Fourier line (nu,nu,-nu), nu=c m^2, fixes a square class on the
Fourier side. Identifying it with a particular d-orbit is still an unfolding
map to be supplied; equality of the two class counts is not that map.

The complement of the geometric open orbit has four irreducible divisors:
the closure of d=0, and z1=infinity, z2=infinity, z3=infinity. At their standard
representatives their stabilizer is T_delta. The normal coordinate of d=0
has weight t^2. Each infinity divisor has normal coordinate 1/zi of weight
t^-2. The tangent measure on each two-dimensional orbit has Jacobian |t|^4.
These normal characters, fiber characters and the chosen density line are
the inputs needed to define boundary distributions. Their multiplicities do
not collapse because two quartic source vectors happen to be equal.

Even the simultaneous ordinary Weyl action does not simply exchange the
affine incidence divisor and itself. Where all coordinates are nonzero,

    d after (z1,z2,z3)->(-1/z1,-1/z2,-1/z3)
      = ((z1+z2)z3-z1 z2)/(z1 z2 z3).

On d=0 its numerator is z1^2+z1 z2+z2^2, generally nonzero. Thus “apply
Fourier and exchange two cells” needs a specified correspondence, not just
this simultaneous group element.

## 4. Both source coefficients fix the identity-cell readout

Put alpha=pi/|pi|, epsilon=(nu0/pi)_2, h=(nu0/pi)_4 and
g=conjugate(gamma4(pi)). Then h^2=epsilon and g^2=-alpha^-1.
For the identity ray, normalize the selected nonzero seed coefficient to1.
Fourth-power periodicity and the square relation give

    r_j := selected residue at nu0 pi^(2j) / selected seed
         = 1                            if j=2r,
           Q^(-1/4) h g                 if j=2r+1.       (2)

Each actual source coefficient contributes Q^(j/4) r_j after the fixed
archimedean Bessel factor is removed. The nonconjugated product, multiplied
by the REQUIRED angular and quadratic correction alpha^j epsilon^j, is

    B_j = alpha^j epsilon^j Q^(j/2) r_j^2
        = A^r                 if j=2r,
          -A^r                if j=2r+1,
    A=alpha^2 Q=chi2(p)Q.                              (3)

The odd sign uses BOTH copies of h and g: epsilon*h^2=1 and
alpha*g^2=-1. Replacing the pairing by a Hermitian one would lose this
identity. For other good rays, applying the supplied ell_[m] and U_[m]
before squaring gives the same (3); treating the two ray entries as two
independent spherical sources is unnecessary and incorrect.

Define the normalized radial arithmetic functional, initially absolutely
convergent for Re(s)>1/2 on bounded radial f supported in O, by

    J_s(f)=sum_(j>=0) B_j Q^(-js) f(pi^j).              (4)

It has the multiplicative integral form
integral_(O minus0) B_(v(x)) |x|^s f(x) d^*x.
This is an exact coefficient readout derived from the coupled sources.
It is not yet the full relative scattering operator or an all-vector norm.

One can also specify a trilinear H-functional in an explicit compatible local
cover convention, which the actual adelic realization must match. Let W1,W2
be the source Whittaker functions
for psi(c x), and let gamma_q(x) be the Weil torus scalar in

    omega(a(b))f(x)=gamma_q(b)|b|^(1/2) f(bx).

Use compatible torus sections with sigma4(x,b)^2=sigma2(x,b) and
gamma_q(xb)=gamma_q(x)gamma_q(b)sigma2(x,b). For an unramified character chi
define, wherever convergent,

    Lambda_(s,chi)(W1,W2,f)
      = integral_(F^*) W1(a(x)) W2(a(x)) gamma_q(x)
                        chi(x) f(x) |x|^(s-2) d^*x.    (5)

This formula includes the Weil scalar; omitting it leaves a quadratic
cocycle in the torus change of variables. The two upper-unipotent source
characters cancel psi(-c(x1+x2)x^2) from the kernel. For simultaneous
a(b), the displayed cocycle identities and x->x/b give

    Lambda(T_delta(b) v)
       = |b|^(5/2-s) chi(b)^(-1) Lambda(v).            (6)

Thus (5) is a concrete H-equivariant distribution in its initial domain under
the stated compatible-section convention. This calculation proves covariance;
it does not independently verify that convention against every source lift.
Its torus degree matches the required 5/2 arithmetic normalization. Equality
with the actual global physical period still requires the named unfolding.
Covariance alone does not identify a normalized orbital integral in every
flag chart.

The source normalization required to identify (5) with (4) is explicit.
With W_i(1)=1, the clean identity-ray spherical values are

    W_i(a(pi^j))=Q^(-3j/4) r_j, j>=0,
    W_i(a(pi^j))=0, j<0.                              (7)

Here the actual slot is f_1, so ell_1(r(nu0))=1. No analogous normalization
is silently imposed on the other global ray at this same seed: its selected
coefficient can vanish. Outside the clean identity-ray calculation one must
retain the actual two-state ray transport before comparing local values.

The exponent -3j/4 follows directly by moving the rational diagonal to the
archimedean chart: height becomes v/Q^j, while N(nu0 pi^(2j))^(1/8)
contributes Q^(j/4); the Bessel argument is unchanged. The bad-place
stabilizer restriction above is needed for this move. Negative j vanishes
by unramified upper-unipotent invariance, since c pi^(2j) is nonintegral.
Equivalently W_p(g) can be defined by applying the fixed global seed
Whittaker functional after a right p-translate; this does not assume a
generic multiplicity-one theorem for quartic Whittaker models.
Here the diagonal lift is fixed by that rational-move convention. Transporting
to another chosen torus section rephases the Whittaker factors and the Weil
factor together; it cannot be omitted when matching (7) with (8).

At odd good places gamma_q is1 on units. Unit factors from W1 W2 cancel
those in gamma_q. Because -1 is a square, gamma_q(pi^j)=gamma_q(pi)^j.
These assertions follow from the unramified quadratic Gauss-sum formula:
the unit Weil index is1, the quadratic Hilbert symbol (pi,pi)_2 equals
(-1/pi)_2=1, and the displayed cocycle identity then handles all integer j.
Choose the local character line

    chi(pi)=alpha*epsilon/gamma_q(pi), chi|O^*=1.       (8)

Substitution of (7)–(8) into (5) gives exactly (3)–(4): the factor
|pi^j|^(s-2) supplies Q^(2j)Q^(-js). Formula (8), not a bare declaration
of odd parity, fixes the local angular/seed orientation.

At infinity the actual kernel has angular weight+1 and the two quartic
vectors have weight0. Under convention (6) the character must therefore
have angular weight-1. The fixed finite ray data must supply the compatible
global idele-class character and cover trivialization. The retained source
does not record that full adelic identification. Equations (5)–(8) give
the exact local convention it must meet, not a new certificate for arbitrary
bad places or a factorization of the global period.

## 5. The phase survives, and its identity-cell germ is nonzero

For a_u(x)=1_O(x)u^floor(v(x)/2), |u|=1, exterior completion E preserves
its interior values. Negative valuations are invisible to (4), by (7).
Summing paired annuli gives (1) exactly.

The difference of two phase readouts is

    J_s(Ea_u)-J_s(Ea_v)
      =(1-z) A z^2 (u-v)/[(1-Au z^2)(1-Av z^2)].       (9)

It is not identically zero when u!=v. In particular the t-derivative at0
is i log(Q)(1-z)A z^2/(1-Az^2)^2. This proves that the actual coefficient
constraints and the same H-character line do not force the phase to be
constant. Neither the already-known compact projection nor a new source
twist has been used.

The poles in the local Mellin variable satisfy

    chi2(p)u Q^(1-2s0)=1, Re(s0)=1/2,
    Res_(s=s0) J_s(Ea_u)=(1-Q^(-s0))/(2 log Q).        (10)

Their absolute residues lie between (1-Q^-1/2)/(2 log Q) and
(1+Q^-1/2)/(2 log Q). They are nonzero for EVERY |u|=1. Phase changes their
imaginary position, not their real part. These local poles at1/2 are not
hypothetical global zeta zeros and do not by themselves prohibit a bound
at exponent .874864 or smaller.

For finitely many distinct u_j, a linear combination of (1) with coefficients
independent of s has disjoint pole sets for the different j. Vanishing of every
geometric-series pole forces every coefficient to vanish. It cannot also retain
the normalized constant coefficient1. This is a finite phase-span obstruction
to becoming the primitive local space, not an obstruction to the Hilbert
vector return. The hard squarefree vector itself gives 1-z.
In particular these identity-cell meromorphic readouts span an infinite-
dimensional space as u varies. A proposed finite-rank boundary reduction must
explain what its additional transport does to this already visible family;
finite rank of the missing relative map is not disproved by this fact alone.

For a positive probability measure on the phase circle, exact scalar
primitive recovery requires integral u^r dnu(u)=0 for every r>=1. The
negative moments are conjugates, so Fourier uniqueness forces normalized
Haar measure. Finite positive quadrature cannot impose all those conditions.
For example averaging the Nth roots of unity yields

    (1-z)/(1-(A z^2)^N),                              (11)

which removes the first N-1 repeated-square levels but leaves a geometric
tail. Independent local phase averages reproduce hard deletion and expose
its original arithmetic energy; they are not the common scalar t-family's
signed cancellation estimate.

## 6. Both source constant-term factors: the exceptional point matters

Use xi for the Eisenstein parameter, distinct from the detector Mellin s.
The primary zero-frequency quotient supplies the good-prime factor

    C_p(xi)=(1-Q^(3-4xi))/(1-Q^(4-4xi)).               (12)

Algebraically its expansion is
1+(1-Q^-1) sum_(r>=1) Q^(4r(1-xi)) in its convergence region.
This is the source constant-term Euler factor, not a verified matrix entry
on the relative H-boundary. It is a necessary scalar normalization check for
any proposed spherical source intertwiner. The two ordinary source
constant-term expansions contain C_p(xi1)C_p(xi2). At the residue point,

    C_p(5/4)=1+Q^-1,
    C_p(3/4)=0,
    C_p(3/4+e)=-4 log(Q)/(Q-1)*e+O(e^2).              (13)

Multiplying (9) by just the forward scalar factors at5/4 cannot erase its
nonconstant direction: their product is (1+Q^-1)^2. This does not describe
the full intertwiner action on Whittaker functionals. The reflected exceptional
point has zeros. It is not legitimate to insert a scalar0 from (13) and
declare the opposite boundary absent: one must specify the inducing
representations, maps on the selected Whittaker functionals, normalized
intertwiners, and order of taking the two exceptional specializations.
Dividing by that zero changes the normalization and requires a limit.

Thus this calculation locates actual scalar data and the actual singular
parameter issue. It does not identify a two-by-two relative matrix. The
global 24-cusp functional equation and its special bad-place factors do
not provide that identification, either. The two prescribed source vectors
cannot simply be substituted for the two basis vectors of a guessed matrix.
In particular the seed-dependent linear combinations of the cusp coefficients
must remain attached to these Euler factors; a particular combined constant
term can vanish. No uncancelled global period boundary follows from (13).

There is a further exact distinction between two meanings of Weyl action.
The compact representative w is in K_p and fixes each unramified source
vector. On the unary factor its action is Fourier, up to the stated fixed
unit Weil scalar, so the completed selected tensor is also fixed after that
normalization. But w H w^-1 has lower rather than upper unipotents and is
not H. This vector symmetry is not a relative scattering formula. Nor is
right translation by w the principal-series intertwining integral M(xi),
which changes the inducing parameter and transports Whittaker functionals.
Both source intertwiners still require that transport before specialization.

## 7. Quantitative cost of retaining the phase direction

Let sigma=Re(s)>1/2 and r=Q^(1-2sigma)<1. Equation (9) gives

    (1-Q^-sigma)r |u-v|/(1+r)^2
       <= |J_s(Ea_u)-J_s(Ea_v)|
       <= (1+Q^-sigma)r |u-v|/(1-r)^2.               (14)

The selected Hilbert tensor remains inexpensive, but its relative readout
does not have that same cost. For u=-1 and v=1, exact annulus integration
and the E norm formula give

    ||E a_-1-E a_1||_2^2
       =4 Q^-2(2+Q^-2)/(1+Q^-2)^2.                  (15)

Consequently the readout-to-Hilbert-norm ratio for these actual phase
directions is of order Q^(2-2sigma), for fixed sigma>1/2 as Q grows.
At the limiting current target sigma=.874864 this is Q^.250272;
at5/6 it is Q^(1/3), and at3/4 it is Q^(1/2). This is a scoped lower cost
for this readout on the displayed phase directions. It is not a global
impossibility result or a license to multiply local lower bounds.

Parameter smoothness also has an explicit paid local bound:

    ||partial_t a_(Q^it)||_2^2
      =(log Q)^2 Q^-2(1+Q^-2)/(1-Q^-2)^2,
    ||partial_t E a_(Q^it)||_2^2 <= 2 times that.       (16)

All fixed higher derivative orders have the same Q^-2 times a fixed
logarithmic power summability. Together with the known O(Q^-2) vacuum
deviation this permits a smooth selected Hilbert tensor family. It does
not imply bounded point restriction or a uniform distribution norm.
For this tensor assertion the derivative vacuum overlaps are also paid:
the kth derivative of (1-Q^-2)/(1-Q^-2 u) is O_k(Q^-2(log Q)^k), uniformly
on the phase circle. They are absolutely summable, while the orthogonal
derivative components have the preceding square-summable bounds.

The source scalar product (1+Q^-1)^2 in (13) is a separate normalization
issue; its unrestricted prime product is not absolutely convergent. An
adelic residue/scattering normalization must account for it explicitly.
One cannot absorb it into the O(Q^-2) selected-vector convergence argument.

The complete vector arithmetic target remains

    integral_I ||F_t||_[X,2X]^2 dt <<_epsilon X^(2a+epsilon),
    a<.874864 for first gain; a=5/6 or3/4 for1/6 or1/4.

Its relative-period norm is X^(a-5/2+epsilon): strictly below
X^(-1.625136+epsilon), or the limiting -5/3 and -7/4 targets. All finite
source approximations, ray/bad-place complements, phase crosses and shifted
scale tails remain. The conditional fixed-denominator vector zero return
from [private research revision] survives; this report supplies no such global estimate.
This conditional return concerns zeta_K and hence ordinary zeta; extending
it to the accepted project's entire Hecke family needs its own construction.

## 8. The exact next object to construct

A meaningful continuation must provide the following single compatible
package, rather than a formal scalar Weyl substitution:

1. The p-local source modules and normalized Whittaker functionals realizing
   (7), with the actual chosen seed/ray sections and all torus lift scalars.
2. The H-equivariant distribution with normalization (5)–(8), together with
   the global ray/angular binding and the map from the selected Fourier
   square class to an H-orbit. The positive real slice must recover X^-5/2.
3. A boundary-coordinate basis including the four divisors above, or a
   proved quotient reducing them. Give the intertwining/scattering map on
   this basis BEFORE specializing both source parameters to5/4; then take
   the specified specialization with (12)–(13) retained.
4. Its action on the finite valuation approximants to E a_u, as a function
   of u, with uniform errors and a distribution norm on a named Mellin line.

The currently known identity cell, source scalar factors and unary Fourier
operator do not determine item3: they say nothing about the map from the
remaining boundary coordinates into the selected character line. Assigning
arbitrary entries would manufacture the answer. Conversely the missing
definition does not prove that no useful coupled transform exists.

The cheapest decisive check is now narrower: construct the normal-germ
maps for the d=0 and each source-infinity divisor in the actual exceptional
Whittaker model, verify their compatibility with (8) and (12), and determine
whether they force a nonzero bad component on the phase derivative (9).
Only a specified map can answer whether that direction survives ALL coupled
constraints. The exact partial calculation proves survival of the constraints
already defined, and locates the ones not yet defined.

## 9. Evidence boundary

All supplied-source code remains unexecuted. A small independent script
checks the orbit classification over three prime fields, the rational
source factors, and exact finite phase identities. It verifies algebra,
not adelization, functional-equation transport, or arithmetic cancellation.
The analytic orbit and residue arguments above are the proofs; sample
counts are only independent error checks. Independent review is reserved
by the controller. New endpoint formalization/replay remains pending, and
PR9/Gao/source credits remain unchanged.

# G173-G175: a paid prime-flux reduction and exact returned sources

The main new reduction pays every higher prime power, a growing small-prime
range and the exact same-output diagonal in the Gaussian logarithmic
equation. What remains is a strict signed off-diagonal estimate. It is
unproved. The written source-relative constant stays

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364.

Root accepts the restricted statements below after reading the [author
proof](wild62/report.md), [independent review](wild62-review/report.md),
both helpers, receipts and relevant ancestry. The [retention
manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds 28 original artifacts and sixteen
source bindings from each side. Source hashes, semantic read extents and
historical versions remain distinct. Independent reviewer additions are
identified explicitly. No finite diagnostic proves an asymptotic bound.

## G173. The complete hard-prime off-diagonal criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, principal or
imprimitive allowed, tau>0 fixed, and 1/2<gamma<1. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    g(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=exp(-gamma y)U(y).

The unit, prime2, squareful zeros and character zeros are literal.
Gaussian majorants justify local absolute convergence and derivatives;
the entire left tail is bounded by a polynomial times a Gaussian.
Coefficientwise logarithmic differentiation of a*chi=delta gives

    a(n)log n=-sum_(d|n)a(n/d)chi(d)Lambda(d),
    tau U'+yU+K1 U+K2 U=0,
    K1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K2 U=sum_(p,j>=2)chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

The last two surviving local terms cancel at squareful n. Deleting higher
prime powers would change the source. This identity has W35/G118 ancestry.
In z coordinates each delay d has coefficient chi(d)Lambda(d)d^(-gamma).
For every R>=0 define

    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Qj(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(Kj,gamma z)(y)dy.

The exact energy equation, including the initial value, is

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2. (1)

Three full payments leave a more precise arithmetic problem.

First, the sum of absolute higher-power coefficients is finite:

    C_gamma=sum_(p,j>=2)log p p^(-j gamma)
      <=(1-2^(-gamma))^(-1)sum_(n>=2)log n n^(-2gamma).

Truncate z only above R, retaining its whole past. Translation contraction,
Minkowski and Cauchy give |Q2|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z|^2. The past
is unconditionally finite. Split the positive integral at a fixed large Y;
for every eta>0 this proves

    |Q2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                  (2)

B_eta uses only a fixed bounded interval and the Gaussian left tail, not
an unknown future norm. This is a relative form bound, not prime-power
cancellation.

Second, the author pays p<=(2+y)^A whenever A(1-gamma)<1. The reviewer
enlarges that region to the exact monotone cutoff

    Y_gamma(y)=((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^(1/(1-gamma)), y>=0.        (3)

Equality belongs to the small sector. Elementary binomial prime counting
gives theta(t)<=4(log2)t. Partial summation yields

    sum_(p<=Y)log p p^(-gamma)
      <=[4log2/(1-gamma)]Y^(1-gamma).

Thus the row sum for (3) is O_gamma((2+y)/log(e^2+y))=o(y).
For large y, log p<=y/2 on this sector, so v=y-log p belongs to[y/2,y].
In the second half of 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, change variables
separately for every p. Since y<=2v, the column is bounded using
p<=Y_gamma(2v) and is o(v). Also v<=R. The bounded initial region has
finitely many primes and a fixed bounded input interval. Therefore

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta                              (4)

for every eta>0. Both row and column are paid. Formula (3) is larger
asymptotically than every fixed subcritical power (2+y)^A. It does not
transfer an assumed residual estimate between different masks for free.

Third, expand the hard-prime contribution with p>Y_gamma(y) before taking
absolute values. Its literal summand is

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))chi(p)a(m)] log p exp(-2gamma y)
          *g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),

over all m,n>=1 and 0<=y<=R. For n=pm its coefficient is +1 exactly when
pm is a squarefree q-unit, otherwise zero. For fixed n the retained prime
log-weights sum to at most log n. The exact whole-line integral is

    int exp(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =exp(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi tau)).

Consequently the exact diagonal D_R is nonnegative and bounded by the
fixed finite constant obtained by summing log n n^(-2gamma). Define
H_R=Q_hard-D_R, precisely the complete n!=pm form. Every sign, phase,
infinite source sum and the complementary prime mask remains inside it.

**OPEN-PF.** For one common gamma in(1/2,1), suppose every fixed ordinary
chi admits delta_chi>0, B_chi and R0_chi such that

    H_R <= (1-delta_chi)I_R+B_chi, every R>=R0_chi.           (5)

Take eta=delta_chi/4 in (2) and (4) and absorb the finite initial range.
Then (1) gives, for all R>=0,

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'_chi.  (6)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma y)) on every sufficiently large real y. The
bilateral transform F(s)=int U(y)exp(-sy)dy is holomorphic on Re s>gamma,
locally uniformly with all derivatives. On Re s>1 absolute Fubini gives

    F(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Continue L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau s^2/2). Its right side never vanishes, so
there is no ordinary L-zero in Re s>gamma at any finite height or
multiplicity. The principal pole at1 is allowed and forces a zero of F;
imprimitive factors and natural zeros were never removed. The standard
continuation and Euler-product conventions are those of [DLMF
25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15). No height-uniform lower bound for the
Gaussian multiplier, unsmoothing theorem or native-H adapter is needed
for this one-way return.

The gamma is common to all fixed characters; margins, constants and
onsets may depend on chi. Neither gamma=1/2 nor growing-conductor
uniformity is supplied. Conditional c=.12515 would improve c11 by
.0000040364; 1/6,1/4 and values below1/2 remain conditional possibilities.
None has (5) proved. Even if a bound U(y)=O(exp(beta y)), gamma<beta<1,
is GRANTED, absolute prime summation gives the coarse flux exponent
1+beta-2gamma, against I's exponent2beta-2gamma. The gap1-beta remains.
This failed upper-budget trial is not a signed lower bound, and the
granted U bound is not inferred from a bare zero-free statement.

W35/G79/G118 retain credit for Gaussian renewal, energy drift and the full
logarithmic identity. The increment is the combined complete payments,
the enlarged moving cutoff and its exact residual criterion. No strict
coercivity follows from the equation alone.

## G174. Actual cutoff boundaries and the price of a positive observation

Let S_N be the squarefree q-units n<=N. On its orthonormal basis define
B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) when p does not divide n and pn<=N, zero otherwise.
Distinct insertions commute: their product exists in both orders exactly
when prn fits. The divisor-closed cutoff does not create noncommutative
independence. Ordered fermionic boundaries are different operators.

For p!=r the mixed adjoint commutator is exactly

    C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^*,
    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))chi(r)e_(rm),
    m squarefree, (m,qpr)=1,
    N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r),                                (7)

and zero elsewhere. The lower endpoint is strict and upper endpoints
inclusive. It is a phased negative partial isometry, norm1 if its domain
is nonempty. For a_N=sum_(S_N)mu(n)chi(n)e_n, every character phase cancels:

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#domain(7).

With profile f, the exact contraction is instead
-sum_m conjugate(f(rm))f(pm). Complex profiles cannot be replaced by
positive counts. For the k unramified primes in(N/2,N], the sum over

### Full zero return and scope

The bilateral transform F(s)=int_(-infinity)^infinity U(y)e^(-s*y)dy is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly with all derivatives, by (R5) and the Gaussian left tail. On Re(s)>1, absolute summation gives

    F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Thus L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) as a meromorphic identity on Re(s)>gamma. The right side never vanishes. A zero of L at any finite height is impossible there. The principal pole at 1 is allowed and forces the corresponding zero of F; it is not an L-zero. Natural zeros and imprimitive factors were present in a from the start. No uniform lower bound for the Gaussian multiplier as height tends to infinity is needed for this pointwise nonvanishing argument, and no reciprocal-growth or unsmoothing theorem is silently imported. The standard character Euler product and principal-pole distinction agree with [DLMF 25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15).

The exponent gamma is common to the family, while delta, constants and onset may depend on fixed chi. This proves an all-height ordinary-character return if PF holds for every such chi. It says nothing about a moving modulus, an Eisenstein Hecke family, or the physical H branches. The endpoint gamma=1/2 is not supplied because both positive payments diverge there. Conditional targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4,.5001 in the author are in range; none has its arithmetic premise established.

The inherited bound U(y)=O(e^(beta*y)) and absolute prime summation give a generic flux envelope with exponent 1+beta-2gamma, whereas I has exponent 2beta-2gamma. The gap 1-beta explains why that absolute route cannot prove PF. An upper envelope is not a signed lower bound or proof that PF fails.

    A=integral_0^(1/q)|Phi(u)|^2du>0,
    B=||Phi||_infinity, L=a global Lipschitz constant.

A>0 follows from the nonzero continuous value Phi(0). For 1<=a,b<=1+eta,

    |integral_0^(1/q)Phi(au)conj(Phi(bu))du-A|
       <=BL eta/q^2.

Choose a fixed eta>0 small enough that this is at most A/2. Then for N<n,m<=(1+eta)N,

    Re K_N(n,m)>=A/(2N), hence |K_N(n,m)|>=A/(2N).

The actual squarefree integers coprime to q in that interval number delta(q)eta N+O_q(sqrt(N)). At most O(N^2/G) ordered pairs have gcd>=G. Therefore, whenever G->infinity and T eventually exceeds (1+eta)N,

      |a(n)a(m)|(nm)^(-r)|K_N(n,m)| >>_(chi,r) N^(1-2r). (R14)

This includes imprimitive, principal, even, odd and complex characters with fixed q. It lower-bounds the absolute price, not the signed core or arc energy. All natural zeros are counted through the coprime squarefree density. Thus paying the localized kernel pairwise absolutely fails for each fixed character, rather than only for the principal test case. No uniform lower constant as q grows is asserted.

## 6. Uniform ordered prime density with sharp endpoints

Set \(u=Y/D,\ v=Y/E,\ Z=x/(DE)\). On the retained cores all contributing
prime variables lie in a fixed corridor \(X^{\theta-o(1)}\) through
\(X^{1-\theta+o(1)}\). Eventually this is contained, for example, in
\([X^{.49},X^{.51}]\). Therefore a fixed PNT order has uniform constants
over all cores, the full shell, and endpoints which happen to be primes.

Stieltjes summation in the second prime variable keeps
\(-R(v)K(pv/Z)\), and bounds the error by
\[
 C_NL^{-N}
 \left(v|K(pv/Z)|+
       \int_v^\infty t(p/Z)|K'(pt/Z)|\,dt\right)
 \le C_N(Z/p)L^{-N}.
\]
The sum over \(1/p\) in the positive-power corridor is \(O(1)\).
For the resulting continuum function
\[
 J(s)=\int_v^\infty K(st/Z)\frac{dt}{\log t}
\]
one has \(|J(s)|\ll Z/(sL)\), \(|J'(s)|\ll Z/(s^2L)\).
The outer Stieltjes step retains \(-R(u)J(u)\).
Its integral uses \(\int_u^{eZ/v}ds/s=O(L)\);
choose a stronger fixed PNT order before the calculation. Thus
\[
 \sum_{p>u,\ q>v}K(pq/Z)
  =Z\int_0^\infty K(r)h_{u,v}(Zr)\,dr+O_N(ZL^{-N}), \tag{RNR15}
\]
where \(h_{u,v}(T)=0\) for \(T\le uv\), and otherwise
\[
 h_{u,v}(T)=
 \frac1{\log T}\log
 \frac{(\log T-\log u)(\log T-\log v)}
      {\log u\,\log v}.                             \tag{RNR16}
\]
Indeed this is the antiderivative of
\(ds/[s\log s\log(T/s)]\) from \(u\) to \(T/v\).
The factor two in the eventual constant is correct.
This is an ordered sum including \(p=q\), not a distinct-prime sum
with an unpriced diagonal.

Choose fixed \(\eta=.004<1-2\theta\).
For \(r\ge X^{-\eta}\), \(Zr/(uv)=xr/Y^2\to\infty\), independently of
the cores. With
\[
 c=(\log x+\log r)/L,\quad y=\log Y/L,\quad
 a=\log D/L,\quad b=\log E/L,
\]
RNR16 is \(L^{-1}\mathcal F_{c,y}(a,b)\), where
\[
 \mathcal F_{c,y}(a,b)=
 \frac{\log(c-y-a)+\log(c-y-b)-\log(y-a)-\log(y-b)}
      {c-a-b}.                                     \tag{RNR17}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(X\), we may use
\(.995\le c\le1.01\) and \(.494\le y\le.495\).
This is a uniformly analytic family on, for example, the closed
bidisc \(|a|,|b|\le1/100\), with an absolute fixed bound.
All logarithms stay in the right half-plane and the denominator
is bounded away from zero. This explicitly supplies the bidisc
hypothesis of RNR8 without any growing derivative of \(K\).

On its whole support the actual density is \(O(1/L)\).
The region \(r<X^{-\eta}\), including its true product boundary, has
arbitrarily small fixed power after using fixed-order flatness of \(K\).
Its integral remains negligible after multiplying by \(h_z^2\ll t^2\).
There is no extension across the product boundary before this payment.

Apply RNR8 for each remaining \(r\), before taking absolute values
of the core sum. The main field is
\[
 \frac{x p_z^2}{L}
 \int_{X^{-\eta}}^e K(r)\,
       \frac2c\log\frac{c-y}{y}\,dr.                 \tag{RNR18}
\]
The integrated core-lemma error is at most
\(C(xp_z^2/L)(t/L)\int|K|\), plus \(O_A(XL^{-A})\).
The prime error is at most \(C_NXt^2L^{-N}\);
increase the **fixed** \(N\) to absorb \(t^2\le L^2\).
No PNT order depends on the Taylor degree.

The factor \(2c^{-1}\log((c-y)/y)\) is uniformly Lipschitz here.
Since
\[
 c-1=\{\log(x/X)+\log r\}/L,\qquad
 y-\theta=O(X^{-\theta}/L),
\]
the fixed absolute first logarithmic moment of \(K\) replaces it in
RNR18 by \(2\log((1-\theta)/\theta)\) at cost \(O(1/L)\).
RNR10 gives exactly \(C_\theta\).
Since \(t\ge\ell_0^2\), this is absorbed in \(O(t/L)\).

This also proves that the claimed error is genuinely **relative**.
Uniformly \(p_z\asymp1/t\), \(x\asymp X\), and \(t\le L\), so
\[
 \frac{x p_z^2}{L}\frac tL\asymp\frac{X}{L^2t}
 \ge c\,\frac X{L^3}.
\]
Any fixed \(O(XL^{-4})\) remainder suffices. The preceding prime,
core-tail and small-\(r\) bounds allow that order with all constants
fixed in advance. RN3 therefore holds in its full claimed range;
no narrowing or unsupported growing-order input is needed.

statement:
# Full-cutoff positive moment: a direct return without the baseline

Controller candidate, 12 October 2026 UTC. Independent review requested from the existing headroom critic. This is written mathematics, not formalization. It does not prove the open moment or increase c.

Use the headroom author's notation, with fixed ordinary character chi, fixed tau>0, 1/2<sigma<gamma<1, eta=gamma-sigma>0, and even K=2m. Let

    P_Y(t)=sum_(n<=Y) mu(n)chi(n)n^(-sigma-it),
    Q_(K,Y)=integral_R exp(-tau*t^2/4)|P_Y(t)|^K dt.

Assume, for every epsilon>0, uniformly for ALL sufficiently large real X and every allowed even K in [(log X)^(1/3)/2,2(log X)^(1/3)], that

    Y=floor(exp(log X/(K-1/2))),
    Q_(K,Y) <= C_epsilon X^(eta+epsilon).                 (R1)

The all-real-X quantifier is essential to this proof. A merely dyadic X subfamily is not silently filled in: gaps between its Y cutoffs can have positive-power absolute price.

For any large integer Y choose K=2 ceil(sqrt(log Y)/2) and set X=Y^(K-1/2). The cutoff equals Y exactly and K/(log X)^(1/3) tends to1, so it is allowed. Write A=|P_Y(0)|. The elementary derivative bound

    |P'_Y(t)| <= C_sigma Y^(1-sigma)log Y = D_Y

holds for every real t. Also A<=C_sigma Y^(1-sigma); choosing the constant larger if necessary ensures w=A/(2D_Y)<=1. If A=0 the desired bound is immediate. Otherwise |P_Y(t)|>=A/2 for |t|<=w, and the Gaussian is bounded below on [-1,1]. Therefore

    Q_(K,Y) >= c_tau 2^(-K) A^(K+1)/D_Y.

Combining with R1 gives

    A <= [C_epsilon C_sigma/c_tau]^(1/(K+1)) 2^(K/(K+1))
         (log Y)^(1/(K+1))
         Y^(((K-1/2)(eta+epsilon)+1-sigma)/(K+1)).

For every fixed delta>0, choose epsilon<delta/2 and then Y sufficiently large. The constant, logarithm and O(1/K) exponent are absorbed to get

    |sum_(n<=Y) mu(n)chi(n)n^(-sigma)| <<_delta Y^(eta+delta)

for every integer Y (enlarge the constant for the finite initial range). With B(u) equal to this weighted partial sum, Abel inversion is exact:

    sum_(n<=Y) mu(n)chi(n)
       = Y^sigma B(Y)-sigma integral_1^Y u^(sigma-1)B(u)du.

Since gamma>0 this proves M_chi(Y)<<_delta Y^(gamma+delta). No previously accepted subunit Mertens estimate was used. Its Dirichlet series is then holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma, agrees with 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1, and excludes zeros of L there by analytic continuation of the product. At the principal pole1, multiply by s-1 first; no nonzero claim for the pole itself is made. All fixed-character quantifiers remain literal.

Conversely M_chi(u)<<_delta u^(gamma+delta) implies, by Abel summation, |P_Y(t)|<<_delta(1+|t|)Y^(eta+delta). Gaussian integration of its Kth power costs exp(O_delta(K log(K+2))). Because log Y=log X/(K-1/2)+o(1), K log K=o(log X), and K/(K-1/2)=1+o(1), this gives R1 after allocating epsilon. Thus the full-cutoff moment is exponent-equivalent to the original ordinary-character Mertens bound, with every positive epsilon loss.

The author's paid diagonal, ratio tail and large-gcd estimates also show that its one-sided Core bound is equivalent to this Q bound at the same exponents: Core=Q-diagonal-remaining sectors; the removed signed sectors have the proved absolute price, and the nonnegative diagonal is X^o(1). Keep its threshold G=X^(1-gamma+kappa), 0<kappa<gamma-1/2, and all coefficients unchanged. In the reverse implication Core<=Q+absolute price of removed off-diagonal sectors suffices; it does not require Core to be positive.

Consequently this explicit full-cutoff Q/Core route has a direct return that removes the author's baseline N11 premise. The separate dyadic balanced-source-to-field future-integral route still has that premise as stated. Neither equivalence makes the arithmetic hypothesis weaker or supplies its missing estimate. At sigma=3/4 the nearest open eta=.124860 would imply c=.125140 for every fixed ordinary character for which R1 holds; no Eisenstein extension follows from this argument.
title: Full-cutoff positive moment: a direct return without the baseline

### Natural holes at the new frequency

At a prime dividing n or n', the primitive finite Fourier transform is zero when that prime divides ell. There is no factor sqrt((ell,nn')) or other gcd size: the character is primitive at every good conductor prime, with exponent1 or5. When slots are conditioned on below, a slot prime dividing ell simply kills that term. Fixed S factors have only the original fixed-modulus price.

To remove the remaining mutual coprimality, first define (3.1), its full profile and formal product conductor on all individually squarefree columns, retaining all individual zeros. THEN insert the complete identity

    1_((n,n')=1)=sum_(f|n,f|n') mu(f).

No Poisson formula is asserted for the artificial noncoprime conductors. The full Möbius sum annihilates precisely those artificial pairs. On n=f m,n'=f m', squarefreeness gives (m,f)=(m',f)=1, and

    a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m) chi_m(f)^4.                        (3.2)

The extracted frequency factor is chi_f(ell) conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((ell,f)=1). It is a contraction; it is NOT replaced by a gcd magnitude or divided out. All remaining factors involving ell stay separately on m and m'.

statement:
## 2. Complete positive-core bounds needed for A3

The following bounded-coefficient version of the accepted critical
PNT argument is proved here to avoid a masked-transfer assumption.
For arbitrary coefficients |c(r)|<=1 define the COMPLETED source

    S_c(x)=sum_(r>=1)c(r)sum_(z<p<q)g(log(rpq/x)).

Uniformly over such c and the closed shell,

    S_c(x)=2x/L^2 sum_(r>=1)c(r)/r J(log(r z^2/x))
                                      +O_(tau,kappa)(X/L^3), (A6)
    J(v)=integral_v^infinity exp(u)(u-v)g(u)du.

This is a linear prime-density estimate with an absolute error; it
asserts no arithmetic cancellation for arbitrary c. Here are the
complete bounds establishing its applicable uniformity.

Choose delta=1/100 and P_X=X^(.52). Terms with r>X^delta force
rpq>kappa^2 X^(1+delta); terms with p or q>P_X force
rpq>kappa X^(1.02). Their total, with |c|<=1 and all representation
multiplicities, is a complete divisor-weighted Gaussian upper tail,
O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A. This follows from d_3(n)<<_epsilon
n^epsilon and the Gaussian tail bound proved below in (A11).

On r<=X^delta and z<p,q<=P_X replace the unordered pair by half the
ordered pair and subtract its actual p=q diagonal. Even with all r,
that diagonal has positive cost

    sum_(p>z)sum_(r>=1)g(log(rp^2/x))
       <=C_tau x sum_(p>z)p^-2 <= C_(tau,kappa)sqrt(X).

For each fixed N, the PNT input is pi(v)-li(v)=O_N(v/log^N v).
Use N=10 before X varies. Stieltjes summation for fixed r,q on
(z,P_X] gives BOTH endpoint terms and the derivative integral, each
bounded by C x/(rqL^N). Indeed p g(log(rpq/x)) is bounded by Cx/(rq),
and the derivative integral is at most
(x/(rq))integral exp(u)|g'(u)|du. The lower endpoint is excluded
correctly even when z is prime. Summing errors over retained r,q
costs at most two harmonic factors O(L^2). Replace the other prime
sum inside the already continuous first-prime integral; the same
bound and both endpoints give a second O(X/L^8) error. There is no
unpriced product of PNT errors.

Extend the continuous integral to all r,p,q by an ABSOLUTE bound.
Put a=z^2/x in [kappa^2/2,kappa^2]. After dropping denominators
log p,log q>=1, the full positive expression is exactly

    x integral_(log a)^infinity exp(u)g(u)
            sum_(r<=exp(u)/a)(u-log(ar))/r du.

The inner sum is at most C_kappa(1+u_+)^2. Every term added by an
omitted core or prime endpoint forces u>=.01L-O_kappa(1), so the
whole continuous extension is O_A(X^-A). This explicitly pays the
infinite core, not only a finite-core rectangle.

Finally scale p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w, with v,w>=kappa>=1. Globally,

    |1/[(L/2+log v)(L/2+log w)]-4/L^2|
                       <=8(log v+log w)/L^3.

The sum over all r of the resulting positive error integral is
finite uniformly in x/X in [1,2]. With u=log(rvw/(x/X)), a fixed
Gaussian exponential majorant bounds each core integral by C_B r^-B
for any chosen B>1. The leading integral for that core is exactly
(x/(Xr))J(log(rz^2/x)). The factors unordered 1/2, Jacobian X and
density 4/L^2 give the coefficient 2x/L^2. This proves (A6), uniformly
in all bounded c, using only absolute errors at this stage.

Take c=1_(r=1) and c=1_(r>=2), respectively. Put

    q_x=z^2/x,   V_0(x)=2x/L^2 J(log q_x).

Then

    V=V_0+O(X/L^3),
    U=2x/L^2 sum_(r>=2)r^-1 J(log(rq_x))+O(X/L^3).   (A7)

For v>=3tau, completing the Gaussian square in J gives, for b>=0,

    J(v+b)/J(v)
       <= exp(-(v-tau)b/tau-b^2/(2tau)) <= exp(-2b).

Since q_x>=exp(3tau), the entire r>=2 main term is at most V_0/4:

    sum_(r>=2)r^-1 J(log(rq_x))
       <=J(log q_x)sum_(r>=2)r^-3 <=(1/4)J(log q_x).  (A8)

The last numerical bound follows from 1/8+integral_2^infinity t^-3dt
=1/4. J is continuous and strictly positive on the fixed compact
q_x interval, so V_0 is uniformly comparable to X/L^2. Consequently

    0<=U(x)<=V(x)/3,
    V(x) asymp_(tau,kappa) X/L^2                     (A9)

for all sufficiently large X, uniformly on the closed shell. The
constant 1/3 deliberately leaves room for the O(1/L) density errors.
No new logarithmic profile is claimed as the lane's result: (A6)--(A9)
are the positive-core estimates needed for the coprime obstruction.

## 3. Transforms, supports, projectors and normalization

The first transform's prefactor is
\(H/[X N(e)\sqrt{N(r)}]\). It follows from the Poisson factor \(H/[N(e)N(r)N(a)N(b)]\), three Gauss roots and the original squared central factor \(X^{-1}\). The inverse column roots and the central normalizers of the two Gauss norms cancel in the Cauchy conversion. With the source first targets

\[
 \mathcal N_C\ll Z^{A-c+\widetilde q+B_c-s_0+\epsilon},
 \quad \widetilde q=q+R+E,
 \quad B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6,
\]

the outside exponent plus both targets and the first-label cost is exactly

\[
 M-S/2,\qquad
 S=c+d-2p-R-B_c-B_d\ge0.
\]

The inequality S>=0 is PR9 B3.56's primewise balance. It is a genuine available saving; the new proof spends it once at the final Cauchy return.

For the second transform, put \(a_0=A-c-w\). Direct expansion of B1.14-B1.15 gives the prefactor \(Z^{K+g-\ell-a_0}\), the inverse roots \(1/\sqrt{N(u)N(v)}\), and the literal correlation \(F(u,v;j)\). B1.19 then gives

\[
 F(D_2a,E_2b;j)=F(D_2,E_2;j)
 R(a,E_2)R(b,D_2)R(a,b)\chi_a(j)\overline{\chi_b(-j)}.
\]

Thus the two second children of a *fixed first side* have whole character \(\tau_1(n)\chi_n(j)\), up to fixed ray/unit twists. Their good-prime residues agree. A whole-character conjugation must also conjugate its fixed factor and reflect its height; no inversion of j on just one child is available.

The literal ledger is

\[
 -a_0+(K+g-a_0)-\ell+(p_2-s_0)+(g_2-t_2)+(a_0-b_2).
\]

Subtracting it from
\(\Lambda_c=a_0+\widetilde q+w_o+w+B_c-s_0\)
gives

\[
 M'+\Delta,\quad
 M'=M+J-g-g_2+t_2,\quad
 \Delta=b_2-p_2+w+B_c+\ell,
\]

where \(J=d-c+(K_0-K)-2w+w_o\). This independently checks the density and normalizers: neither \(-\ell\) nor either central factor can be omitted.

All disjointness needed by the new count is present **before** any positivity enlargement. Old moving-support primes and all first common primes puncture all surviving factors. An allocation meeting an old zero has zero frozen scalar and is discarded as zero. Hence genuine second common primes are disjoint from old and first supports. The auxiliary amplifier prime is chosen outside frozen supports, and its extraction punctures the residual factors. It cannot later be a genuine second common prime. Fixed dictionary conductor primes belong to the fixed excluded set S, so none is a new good common prime.

Both coprimality projectors must be the complete sums. At the first one, s divides both subsequent full columns and hence their genuine second common support; this justifies p2-s0. At the second one, an individual artificial t term does **not** make its primes genuine second common primes or frequency divisors. Extracting a selected plain divisor leaves an unrestricted quotient. The author retains these distinctions. Such an extraction changes a frozen scalar, not the whole row character whose forced residues are counted. A zero scalar remains zero. Bounding the genuine partition by one admits more rows, but every admitted exceptional row still obeys the same row-character congruences.

The retained row ball is \(N(h')\le Z^{m'+\delta_2}\), where
\(m'=2a_0-K-g-g_2-V\), \(0\le\delta_2<\xi\). A negative supported upper length is empty. The notation \(M'+\delta_2\) is a valid declared full-support enclosure; it must not erase the c6 correction that the actual canonical width can be smaller after cancellation. This refinement counts rows directly and does not need to identify those two widths. Nonexceptional imports still retain forward (2.16)/Gao (LA.9).

The first zero frequency, the added zero Gauss row, and the genuine second diagonal are separate. No new gain has been proved for any of them.

### 2.1 Exact equation and energy, with no deleted prime powers

Coefficientwise Dirichlet convolution gives

    a(n)log n = -sum_(d|n) a(n/d)chi(d)Lambda(d).

This follows by differentiating a*chi=delta, or by checking each prime exponent. At a squareful n the terms with the last two p-powers cancel; deleting those terms would change the source. Since tau U'(y)+yU(y)=sum a(n)log n g(log n-y), the EXACT equation is

    tau U'(y)+yU(y)+K_1 U(y)+K_2 U(y)=0,                 (1)
    K_1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K_2 U=sum_p sum_(j>=2)chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

Ramified terms vanish. This specializes the existing Gaussian commutator/renewal ancestry; it is not credited as a new identity. In z coordinates, each delay d has coefficient chi(d)Lambda(d)d^-gamma. For R>=0, multiply (1) by exp(-2gamma y)conjugate(U(y)), take real parts and integrate:

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)
      +I_R+tau*gamma*E_R = Q_1(R)+Q_2(R),              (2)
    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Q_j(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(K_j,gamma z)(y)dy.

All boundary terms and signs are retained. There is no finite-height restriction.

statement:
### 4.2 Source-sensitive obstruction at shrinking height

For each fixed1/2<sigma<1 and sufficiently large P, R2 instead grows faster than EVERY power of P. The obstruction occurs at heights t approximately pi/log P, which approach0, so Gaussian frequency suppression does not help.

For p>=5 the uniformly convergent local logarithm gives

    log|(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)|=-Re(p^-s)+O_sigma(p^-2sigma).

The sum of errors is bounded independently of P and small t. The finite p=2,3 factors are bounded above and away from zero near t=0 for fixed sigma in(1/2,1). Hence

    log|E_P(sigma+it)|=-Re sum_(p<=P) p^(-sigma-it)+O_sigma(1). (R4)

The ordinary PNT, verified in [Johnston–Yang, arXiv:2204.01980v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), supplies pi(y)~y/log y. Stieltjes partial summation or the substitution y=P exp(-v) gives, uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6],

    sum_(p<=P) p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =(P^(1-sigma)/log P)[exp(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o_sigma(1)]. (R5)

For completeness, one may first restrict y>=P^b for fixed b in(0,1), where the PNT error is uniform; the omitted y<=P^b is O(P^(b(1-sigma))) and is negligible. In the main integral, v=log(P/y) has limiting density exp(-(1-sigma)v); a/log P tends to0 uniformly, which yields R5 by a bounded tail split. No zero-free conjecture is used.

Since cos a<=-sqrt3/2 on that interval, R4–5 imply for all sufficiently large P and all those t=a/log P,

    log|E_P(sigma+it)| >= [1/(2(1-sigma))] P^(1-sigma)/log P. (R6)

The t-interval has length pi/(3log P) and its Gaussian factor tends uniformly to1. Consequently

    ||exp(-sigma u)V_P||_2
      >= c_(sigma,tau)(log P)^(-1/2)
           exp([1/(2(1-sigma))]P^(1-sigma)/log P).    (R7)

For rigor one can reduce the positive constant in R7 slightly when absorbing finite factors; the stated R6 already has fixed slack relative to sqrt3/2. Every polynomial allowance in R3 fails for this uncut global norm, including the large c=1/4 budget. This is an ACTUAL f3 finite-prime/Gaussian-source obstruction, stronger than a generic operator-norm example. It does not lower-bound the true full field on x~P: the global norm can be dominated by remote smooth-number scales. It does not disprove a causal, physically restricted signed resolvent.

## 5. The other three first tests, with exact scope

**R16, sieve trellis.** A state recording only coarse parity/residue cannot determine the remaining support. At N=21, y=5, the normalized future laws for histories 2 and 3 are 1-z7; for 5,6,10,15 they are 1; history 1 has 1-z7-z11-z13-z17-z19. Signed reconstruction gives M(21)=-2. Keeping amplitudes distinct from normalized laws is essential. This repeats G105, including its O(sqrt N) lawful-state count and open complete signed contraction. It does not establish complexity or square-root cancellation. No extra development credit is requested.

**F04, rare free-group holonomy.** For true sharp prefixes, V_p V_q e_n=V_q V_p e_n=e_(pqn) exactly when pqn<=N, and both vanish otherwise. Thus the proposed prime-shift holonomy is zero; zero curvature supplies no norm gain. The diagonal projector onto numbers whose primes are <=y also commutes with the diagonal size projector, so merely comparing those two diagonal filtrations does not produce an anomaly. Non-divisor-closed masks can fail to commute but owe the omitted source. This is the exact Sol04 S09/G69 ancestry. Adjoints, noncausal transports, and a different paid boundary remain live; they were not developed here.

**X30, divisor simplex.** On one unramified prime p, the augmented simplex has e_p in degree one and e_empty in degree zero, with d(e_p)=e_empty. Weighting by chi(p) and 1 is a chain map only if chi(p)=1. Its putative weighted Euler trace 1-chi(p) can therefore be nonzero even though this augmented complex is acyclic. For chi(p)=-1 it is 2. Thus the weighted arithmetic parity sum is not automatically a homology trace. A product cutoff introduces the same unpaid weighted boundary; the principal case needs the reduced Euler characteristic with its empty face. This repeats A-SIMPLICIAL and the Sol04 topology audit, and does not rule out a different coefficient-exact complex with a genuinely cheaper signed boundary.

`checks.py` and `checks.json` retain exact finite determinant, inverse-interpolation, continuation, prefix and weighted-chain calculations. `tail-checks.py` and `tail-checks.json` add exact periodic decompositions for principal, nonprincipal and complex-character components, plus isometry-vector checks and a separately labeled numerical tail diagnostic. ## 9. Exact remaining estimate and limitations

The useful new ingredient is (XM25)--(XM34), not a claim that the squarefree-source \(H_0/\sqrt Y\) bound already held for all sources. At \(\rho=0\), the refined fixed-\(u\) calculation would give \(H_0/(\sqrt Y R_u)\). For \(u=b^6\), \(R_u=1\); its sum is not subpower. The forced row scale supplies \(U^{-\rho}\), and (XM24) prices precisely what is needed. It incurs the explicit \(Q^\rho\) cost. Thus the sharper all-source \(H_0/\sqrt Y\) estimate remains open.

FR resolves the same local principal-power sparsity issue in a different aggregate. Its normalized local kernel
\[
q^{a/2}1_{p^a\mid r}-q^{a/2-1}1_{p^{a-1}\mid r}
\]
is the normalized form of (XM14) with its forced \(p^{a-1}\) support. FR multiplies two such kernels and combines shared divisors by their maximum. Here there is one source Gauss kernel and one completed character, so the single-source counting and the optimum interpolation endpoint are different.

No relative-conductor inclusion suitable for PC follows from one small active conductor. For example, take coprime good cores \(A=p,A'=q\) and outer labels \(a=pw,b=qw\), with \(w\) coprime to \(pq\). Both individual active conductors can be \(\operatorname{rad}(w)\), arbitrarily large, while their relative conductor is one. Conversely one small active conductor can pair with a large one and leave large relative conductor. Calibration cancels against its conjugate in the covariance, whereas it remains nonprincipal in the linear row calculation.

Accordingly neither (XM34) nor (XM37) proves a new sector of PC's atom-pair covariance beyond the current FR theorem. The target
\[
\mathcal C_{<,\,R>(QY)^{4/9}}
\ll Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon
\tag{OPEN-XM-COV}
\]
at small true core gcd remains unproved here. T07's true-gcd conductor and its I-HECKE-dependent tail are unchanged.

There is instead an exact alternative linear residual: with \(B_{\rm tar}=P_a^{1/12}\), retain in every branch
\[
h_{{\rm act},D}>Q_D^{10/11}P_a^{1/11},
\qquad
q_J\lesssim (ZLY/(QP_a^{1/12}))^{2/5},
\tag{OPEN-XM-LIN}
\]
with the original source/core/cube repetitions, marks, phases, profiles and all heights. Bounding that remaining signed linear sum by
\(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}P_a^{1/12}\) would complete this alternative estimate for the probe. The present argument does not bound it. No lower bound for a completed-row norm and no arbitrary independent coefficient replacement has been used.

## 1. Gcd-one and large-shift obstruction

Write C1(U,V) for the bilinear Gaussian sum restricted to gcd(m,n)=1.
This is not a positive semidefinite form. The positive core-one prime-pair
field V and the absolute nontrivial-core majorant U satisfy, eventually,

    V(x) asymp X/L^2 on X<=x<=2X,       U(x)<=V(x)/3.

The fixed critical profile is

    J(v)=integral_v^infinity exp(u)(u-v)g_tau(u) du,
    S_c(x)=(2x/L^2) sum_r c(r)/r J(log(r z^2/x))+O(X/L^3).

The hypothesis on kappa gives J(v+log r)<=r^-2 J(v); the absolute core
sum uses sum_(r>=2) r^-3<=1/4. The proof pays both prime endpoints,
the prime-square representation diagonal, the entire Gaussian tails and
the denominator replacement. In the logarithmic window
I_X=[X exp(-W),X exp(W)], W=log 2+sqrt(24tau log X), the outside-pair
cost is O(X^-4). Below z^3 the literal form is n=rpq, with r<z and the
two rough prime valuations equal to one. The noncoprime portion costs
at most ||U||^2+O(X^(3/2)), which is subtracted from the FULL rough norm.
Consequently

    (1/3)||V||^2-O(X^(3/2)) <= C1(R,R) <= (16/9)||V||^2,
    C1(R,R) asymp X^2/L^4.                                  ([restricted research revision]-F1)

Removing |m-n|<=H costs O(XH). Thus H=X/L^6 still leaves the same
order. In particular, four distinct large primes, gcd one and large
shifts do not make the complete rough self-correlation power-small.

For f_d(n)=product_(p|n,p not dividing 3d)(-1), the exact identity
f(dn)=f(d)f_d(n) is retained. Its convolution majorant B_d(beta) is
O_(beta,delta)(d^delta) for every fixed delta>0, and the full field is
bounded by C B_d(beta)y^beta for ALL y>0, including d>X in y=x/d.
The frozen proof uses a historical buffered exponent beta>.874872;
it does not claim the unbuffered endpoint or silently replace that
premise by the later c4 boundary.

For any original one-variable mask 0<=A_X<=1, absolute convergence of
the gcd expansion gives

    C1(F,f A_X)=O(X^(1+beta)).                                ([restricted research revision]-F2)

Only one factor is masked. This is not a two-mask, arbitrary pair-mask
or hereditary signed-subset estimate. Applied to the rough mask, with
the same shift removal, it yields

    C1^H(T,R)=C1^H(R,T)=-C1^H(R,R)
                         +O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C1^H(T,T)=C1^H(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4).                ([restricted research revision]-F3)

The sign pattern +,-,-,+ explains why separate absolute bounds lose
the cancellation. It is not a positive lower bound for the full energy.

## 7. Quantitative cost of retaining the phase direction

Let sigma=Re(s)>1/2 and r=Q^(1-2sigma)<1. Equation (9) gives

    (1-Q^-sigma)r |u-v|/(1+r)^2
       <= |J_s(Ea_u)-J_s(Ea_v)|
       <= (1+Q^-sigma)r |u-v|/(1-r)^2.               (14)

The selected Hilbert tensor remains inexpensive, but its relative readout
does not have that same cost. For u=-1 and v=1, exact annulus integration
and the E norm formula give

    ||E a_-1-E a_1||_2^2
       =4 Q^-2(2+Q^-2)/(1+Q^-2)^2.                  (15)

Consequently the readout-to-Hilbert-norm ratio for these actual phase
directions is of order Q^(2-2sigma), for fixed sigma>1/2 as Q grows.
At the limiting current target sigma=.874864 this is Q^.250272;
at5/6 it is Q^(1/3), and at3/4 it is Q^(1/2). This is a scoped lower cost
for this readout on the displayed phase directions. It is not a global
impossibility result or a license to multiply local lower bounds.

Parameter smoothness also has an explicit paid local bound:

    ||partial_t a_(Q^it)||_2^2
      =(log Q)^2 Q^-2(1+Q^-2)/(1-Q^-2)^2,
    ||partial_t E a_(Q^it)||_2^2 <= 2 times that.       (16)

All fixed higher derivative orders have the same Q^-2 times a fixed
logarithmic power summability. Together with the known O(Q^-2) vacuum
deviation this permits a smooth selected Hilbert tensor family. It does
not imply bounded point restriction or a uniform distribution norm.
For this tensor assertion the derivative vacuum overlaps are also paid:
the kth derivative of (1-Q^-2)/(1-Q^-2 u) is O_k(Q^-2(log Q)^k), uniformly
on the phase circle. They are absolutely summable, while the orthogonal
derivative components have the preceding square-summable bounds.

The source scalar product (1+Q^-1)^2 in (13) is a separate normalization
issue; its unrestricted prime product is not absolutely convergent. An
adelic residue/scattering normalization must account for it explicitly.
One cannot absorb it into the O(Q^-2) selected-vector convergence argument.

The complete vector arithmetic target remains

    integral_I ||F_t||_[X,2X]^2 dt <<_epsilon X^(2a+epsilon),
    a<.874864 for first gain; a=5/6 or3/4 for1/6 or1/4.

Its relative-period norm is X^(a-5/2+epsilon): strictly below
X^(-1.625136+epsilon), or the limiting -5/3 and -7/4 targets. All finite
source approximations, ray/bad-place complements, phase crosses and shifted
scale tails remain. The conditional fixed-denominator vector zero return
from [private research revision] survives; this report supplies no such global estimate.
This conditional return concerns zeta_K and hence ordinary zeta; extending
it to the accepted project's entire Hecke family needs its own construction.

statement:
## 2. Literal completion, including characters at ramified primes

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Write
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), and write h(n)=chi(n), so a*h=delta1. Choose a prime
p not dividing q, FIXED before any shell parameter. Put

    q_p=delta1-p*chi(p)*delta_p,
    b_p=q_p*h,
    b_p(l)=chi(l)(1-p*1_(p|l)),
    c_p=q_p*a.

In particular |b_p(l)|<=p and b_p is periodic modulo Q=pq. Its mean is
zero: the sum over a period is p(1-chi(p))*sum_(a mod q)chi(a), which
vanishes for nonprincipal chi by orthogonality, and for principal chi
because chi(p)=1. Choosing p ramified would destroy this argument for a
principal character and is explicitly forbidden. No primitive-character
replacement or conductor-uniform bound is used.

The new global source is

    C_p(x)=sum_(n>=1)c_p(n)f_x(n),
    f_x(t)=exp(-t/x^b-i(t/x)^k).

It is literal: c_p(n)=a(n)-p*chi(p)*1_(p|n)*a(n/p). Every underlying mu
and chi value, including zero values, is retained. Compensation can create
nonzero coefficients at some squareful n; these are part of c_p and may
not be discarded. The coefficients satisfy |c_p(n)|<=p+1. Absolute local
convergence follows from the damping. The second term is f_x(pn), not
f_(x/p)(n): those damping factors differ when b>1.

For real U,V>=1 define m_U(n)=a(n)*1_(n<=U), u_U=a-m_U, and similarly
at V; the displayed indicator multiplication is pointwise. Direct
convolution expansion using a*h=delta1 gives, at EVERY positive integer,

    c_p=q_p*m_U+q_p*m_V-m_U*m_V*b_p+u_U*u_V*b_p.          (2.1)

This is the old alternating completion in a new kernel and with its exact
unramified-character factor. It is not claimed as a new algebraic identity.
The new question is whether its full small-divisor term can be bounded
at a useful power for this nonlinear source. Shared prime factors, both
ordered d,e roles, all l, and strict versus closed cutoffs remain literal.

Write S_p,U,V(x) for the source with coefficients m_U*m_V*b_p and
R_p,U,V(x) for the source with coefficients u_U*u_V*b_p. The short two
terms in (2.1) have absolute value at most (p+1)(U+V). Both S and R have
coefficient modulus at most p*d_3(n), uniformly in U,V. In particular
they converge absolutely with f_x, and for each fixed eta>0 their
coefficients are O_(p,eta)(n^eta). The familiar divisor bound follows
elementarily by absorbing each prime-power factor (e+1)(e+2)/2 in
p^(eta e), with only finitely many small-prime constants.

statement:
## G119. Anchored one-sided pressure has an exact zero-exclusion return

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q with its natural ramified zeros.
Let delta be1 for principal chi and0 otherwise. For Re s>0 define

    J_y(s)=integral_2^y u^(-s)/log(u) du,
    H_y(s)=delta J_y(s)+sum_(p<=y)log(1-chi(p)p^(-s)),
    Q_y(s)=exp(H_y(s)).

Each logarithm means its fixed local power series, including every prime
power. No unknown prime sum is subtracted in J_y. On Re s>1 the complete
Euler expansion gives Q_y -> exp(delta J_infinity)/L(s,chi). The function

    B(s)=(s-1)exp(J_infinity(s))

extends to an entire nonvanishing function because
B'/B=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1) is entire, including its removable value log2.
Fix the multiplicative constant at one real point>1. The optional series
in the source agrees with [NIST 6.6.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/6.6.E2);
the derivative proof suffices without that formula. The identity to extend is

    (s-1)^delta L(s,chi) Q(s)=B(s)^delta.                 (80.1)

For principal chi the first factor at s=1 is product_(p|q)(1-1/p),
nonzero. Finite imprimitive Euler factors have zeros only at Re s=0.
Thus a holomorphic limit Q satisfying (80.1) excludes all L-zeros in its
domain, while treating the principal pole explicitly.

For0<a<1, suppose for every compact K in Re s>a and every epsilon>0,
eventually for every integer k,

    integral_K (Re H_(2^k)(s))_+ dA <= C_(K,chi,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).
                                                               (LP_a)

This is an area estimate on the complete dyadic sequence. A countable
rectangle exhaustion suffices. The subharmonic area mean inequality
gives local upper bounds on Re H. At one real b>1, the actual logarithms
are uniformly bounded as complex numbers. Borel-Caratheodory in the safe form

    sup_(D(c,R/2))|h| <=3|h(c)|+2 max(0,sup_(D(c,R))Re h)

propagates this anchor through a fixed finite disk chain. Hence H_(2^k)
is locally O(2^(k epsilon)) for every epsilon. Its increments f_k are
O_b(2^(-k(b-1))) on Re s>=b>1 by the integer tail majorant.

Choose overlapping inner/middle/outer disks with radii r,2r,4r inside
Re s>a. Three-circle interpolation propagates a decay exponent d_j by
d_(j+1)=(d_j-epsilon)/2. For N fixed steps, epsilon<d_0/2^(N+1)
makes every resulting exponent positive. Centers at distance<=r let
the previous middle disk cover the next inner disk. Finite covers handle
any compact. Therefore sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly, H_(2^k)
has a holomorphic limit H and Q=exp(H) is nonzero. The identity theorem
extends (80.1). This is an all-height return: every alleged finite-height
zero lies in a suitable compact. Constants may depend on chi and K.

For this exact anchored sequence, LP_a is EQUIVALENT to local uniform
convergence of H_(2^k): the reverse follows from local boundedness. For
a>1/2 the higher-prime-power logarithm converges absolutely, so LP_a is
also equivalent to local convergence of the centered DYADIC prime sum
sum_(p<=2^k)chi(p)p^(-s)-delta J_(2^k)(s). This is not an equivalence
with bare zero exclusion or a claim about every intermediate cutoff.
It refines the one-sided sufficient input without providing cancellation.

A separate global-height hypothesis gives a numerical loss budget. Suppose
a>0,kappa>=0,a+kappa<1, and for every epsilon>0 there are fixed A,C with

    |H_y(a+it)| <= C(1+|t|)^A y^(kappa+epsilon)

for every dyadic y and real t. Apply three-lines to f_k(s)/(s+D)^m,
D>1,m>A, on a<=Re s<=b with b>1. Each finite source is bounded in height;
the denominator pays the horizontal boundary. The resulting exponent is

    E=[(kappa+epsilon)(b-sigma)+(1-b)(sigma-a)]/(b-a).

At epsilon=0 its zero is
r_b=a+kappa+kappa(1-a-kappa)/(kappa+b-1). For each compact to the right
of a+kappa choose finite b large enough, then epsilon small enough.
Geometric convergence and (80.1) return Re s>a+kappa. For kappa=0 the
same argument uses a positive epsilon buffer. A_y growing with cutoff,
or an estimate on finitely many heights, does not meet this contract.

At a=3/4 the current first-gain threshold is
kappa<312135091/2500000000=.1248540364. The conditional choice
kappa=78/625 returns c=.1252, gain135091/2500000000 over c11.
Choices (a,kappa)=(3/4,1/12) and (2/3,1/12) return1/6 and1/4.
All these inputs remain open. The actual direct bound is y^(1-a),
giving a+kappa=1. Synthetic h_k=sum_(j<=k)2^(j(a+kappa-s))/j shows
the strict abstract boundary cannot improve for free: its exponential
limit has a pole at a+kappa. This model is not an arithmetic L-source.
