## G213. Average the true cubic label before counting repetitions

In (4) fix k and use the order-three character chi_n(f)^4 in the actual
squarefree f,n variables. The old squarefree cubic sieve B2.25 gives,
after dividing by F and counting all k,

    Elabel=M+L,  L=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).              (8)

For (6), fix b first:
chi_(c b^3)(f)^4=chi_c(f)^4 1_((b,f)=1).
The b phase has modulus at most1. Remove its natural f-hole only after
taking the fixed-b positive norm. Its coefficient mass is bounded by
q_b^(-2) times logarithms, and its c-length is X/q_b^3.
Minkowski sums q_b^(-1) for the constant-in-length term (a logarithm);
the positive column-length terms converge. Thus (8) holds for the full
theta source as well. This requires the coefficients, marks, puncture
and common profile to be independent of f. Arbitrarily conditioning them
on the label would invalidate the cubic sieve.

The whole-norm minimum of (5),(8) does not enlarge the boundary for the
canonical target exponent N+V. The label-only gate is
V>=max(M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4), which is at least the old all-row gate.
There is nevertheless a stronger estimate BEFORE counting repetitions.

For each exact e in k=a e^6, both estimates apply to the SAME complete
positive joint norm in f and sixth-power-free a. The column mask
1_((A,e)=1) is fixed through both averages. Put Arow=U/q_e^6. Its bound
is the minimum of T6(Arow,X) and Arow Z^L, up to the same small loss
and height cost. The two methods do not select incompatible sources.
Counting EVERY e dyad q_e~Z^y, including both endpoints, with t=M-6y
therefore proves

    E << H_J Z^(Emix+epsilon),
    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M)
        [(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)],
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6).              (9)

This is valid for (4) and the complete (6). The dyadic count Z^y is
essential. No signed subsource monotonicity, invented f-average or
discarded principal layer occurs.

For completeness, a continuous evaluation of (9) gives

    E0=min(C(M,N),M+L),  P=(M+5N+L)/6,
    Emix=E0, except that
    Emix=max(E0,P) if L>=N/2 and N-L<=M.             (10)

Indeed C(t,N) has successive affine pieces
N,t/3+5N/6,5t/6+N/3,t, with breakpoints N/2,N,2N.
On the first piece its contribution after subtracting t/6 decreases,
whereas the label contribution increases. Their sole crossing is
t=N-L. Because0<=L<=N, it lies in the first piece and in[0,M]
exactly under the condition in (10). The value there is P.
On each later piece both branches increase: their respective slopes
after counting are1/6,2/3,5/6 and5/6. Their minimum increases as well.
Thus the endpoint t=M and that one crossing give the entire maximum.
This also covers a truncated first interval; M=0 or N=0 is immediate.

For M>0, the precise boundary of THIS proved upper envelope is

    Emix<=N+V iff V>=g(M,N),
    g(M,N)= M-N                   (0<=N<=M/2),
             5M/6-2N/3            (M/2<=N<=M),
             (2M-N)/6             (M<=N<=8M/7),
             M/7                  (N>=8M/7).        (11)

Here is the proof of necessity as well as sufficiency for the envelope.
For N<=M, (9)<=Eall proves sufficiency at the first two thresholds.
At t=M, the sieve branch reaches the target only at that threshold,
while the label branch requires the stronger gate following (8).
For N>=M the proposed threshold is at most M/6. In0<=V<=M/6,
L=N-V and the crossing t=V is present. Its price is
N+(M-V)/6, so it is paid exactly when V>=M/7.
The t=M label price exceeds N+V throughout this interval; the sieve
branch requires V>=(2M-N)_+/6. Their maximum switches at N=8M/7.
These conditions suffice by (10). Larger V decreases Emix and increases
the target; a smaller V fails a displayed envelope branch.
Equality has the usual Z^epsilon loss. Applications needing a strict
reserve must choose a padded inequality. This is no lower bound on the
true arithmetic energy.

At (M,N,V)=(1,8/7,1/7), the new price9/7 equals N+V, while Eall=55/42
and Elabel=2. At (1,2,1/7), they are15/7,13/6,20/7.
The gain over Eall is1/42 in each example. Polynomial-size common
punctures remain uniform; the improvement need not satisfy PR9 B3.7's
older sufficient Q gate. Conversely at V=0, L=N and C(t,N)<=t+N.
Equation (9) becomes EXACTLY Eall. In particular Emix>N for every
M>0. The complete unlabelled canonical target remains unpaid.

## 3. An all-character repair with its literal coefficients

Choose a fixed prime r not dividing q and set

    kappa=delta_1-r chi(r)delta_r,
    c=kappa*a,
    c(n)=mu(n)chi(n)-r chi(r)1_(r|n)mu(n/r)chi(n/r),
    b=kappa*1_chi,
    b(ell)=chi(ell)-r chi(r)1_(r|ell)chi(ell/r).       (H5)

The coefficient r is essential. This is a declared changed source, not c=a. Ramified zeros remain; c can be nonzero at some squareful integers, exactly as the displayed second term prescribes. Nothing silently discards those coefficients.

For every chi, b is periodic with period qr and mean zero. Write
C_chi(y)=delta_(chi principal)(phi(q)/q)y+E_chi(y), |E_chi(y)|<=q.
The principal main terms cancel because chi(r)=1 in that case; the nonprincipal main term is already zero. Thus

    B(y)=C_chi(y)-r chi(r)C_chi(y/r),
    |B(y)| <= q(1+r)=:C_b.                            (H6)

Convolving H1 with kappa gives the full identity

    c=2kappa*a0-a0*a0*b+a1*a1*b.                     (H7)

Let T_(Y,L)=Gamma[a1*a1*b]_(a,L). H2--H3 and the exact atomic mass of kappa give

    | ||Gamma[c]_(a,L)|| - ||T_(Y,L)|| |
       <= (2/a)(1+r^(1-a))A_Y(a)+(C_b/a)A_Y(a)^2
       <<_(a,q,r) Y^(2(1-a)).                         (H8)

In T the actual cumulative kernel is

    exp(-av) sum_(d,e>Y,de<=exp(v))
          mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e) B(exp(v)/(de)),
    v=t+u in [0,2L].                                 (H9)

Equivalently it is the full ordered d/e/ell sum with de ell<=exp(v). Exact bounds are d,e<=X/(Y+1), ell<=X/(Y+1)^2. Both inequalities and every cofactor label are retained. Removing ell=1, shared-prime terms or a selected prime class would change H9.

Initially Re(s)>1, sum c(n)n^-s=m_r(s)/L(s,chi), with m_r(s)=1-chi(r)r^(1-s). The G149 full-rectangle argument applies to this integrated source because its coefficients are bounded by 1+r. Its exponential test gives

All zeros of m_r have Re(s)=1. If the full Gamma[c] growth is O_(chi,epsilon)(exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L)) for every epsilon, G149 makes Q holomorphic to Re(s)>gamma. Any L zero in gamma<Re(s)<1 produces an uncancelled pole in H10. ## What the density calculation really proves

The unsmoothed model is f_0(u)=exp(u)/u, u>0. Although it grows at the
boundary exponent 1, its B1 integral converges absolutely: use
|J_1|<=1 at large v, leaving O(v^(-3/2)) after the factor 1/(u+v).
The identity 1/(u+v)=integral_0^infinity exp(-r(u+v))dr and B0 give

    D_A f_0(u)=exp(u)*integral_0^infinity exp(-u*r-Au/r)dr
      =2sqrt(A)*exp(u)*K_1(2sqrt(A)*u)
      ~sqrt(pi)*A^(1/4)*u^(-1/2)*exp((1-2sqrt(A))*u).       (B11)

Absolute Fubini in the preceding double integral follows from the same
v^(-3/2) bound; no exchange of a merely formal asymptotic series occurs.
For fixed h instead of Au the corresponding leading expression is
sqrt(pi)*h^(1/4)*u^(-3/4)*exp(u-2sqrt(h*u)), only subpower suppression.

A fixed Gaussian does not invalidate the model, but one cannot simply
apply a fixed number of terms in its 1/u expansion when the filter order
grows. Here is the complete Gaussian density calculation. Set l=log 2,

    P_cont(u)=integral_l^infinity exp(y)/y*g_tau(y-u)dy.

Choose a fixed R>2sqrt(A). Splitting the representation 1/y=int_0^infinity
exp(-r*y)dr at R, and then completing the Gaussian square, gives

    P_cont(u)=integral_0^R exp(tau*(1-r)^2/2)*exp((1-r)*u)dr
                 +E_R(u),
    |E_R(u)| << exp((1-R)*u)+exp(-c_tau*u^2),   u>=1.      (B12)

Indeed the r>=R part is the original density integral with exp((1-R)y)
in place of exp(y), and y>=l keeps its denominator bounded. The missing
Gaussian integration range y<l in the compact-r part is superpower small
uniformly for r in [0,R]. Applying B1 to this error costs at most
O((1+u)exp((1-R)u)) plus a Gaussian tail, since 1-R<1.

The main term transforms exactly to

    integral_0^R exp(tau*(1-r)^2/2)
                  *exp(u*(1-r-A/r))dr.

The saddle r=sqrt(A) is interior. Laplace's method, with second derivative
2/sqrt(A) for r+A/r, proves

    D_A P_cont(u)
      ~exp(tau*(1-sqrt(A))^2/2)*sqrt(pi)*A^(1/4)*u^(-1/2)
                            *exp((1-2sqrt(A))*u).          (B12a)

The E_R exponent is smaller because R>2sqrt(A). Thus the model suppression
survives the actual fixed smoothing, with its exact leading constant. This
calculation is proved for the continuous density and NOT for primes.

The exact even correction should also be preserved in this diagnostic.
If the underlying mu source is restricted to its prime terms, its model
after q_2=delta_1-2delta_2 is

    -P_cont(u)+2P_cont(u-log 2).

In the compact-r calculation this replaces the amplitude by
(2^r-1)*exp(tau*(1-r)^2/2). Hence its transformed leading constant is
the B12a constant multiplied by 2^sqrt(A)-1, which is strictly positive.
The exponent 1-2sqrt(A) survives the actual numerator. This is only the
q_2 image of the prime part of mu, not a claim that it equals the old
two-rough-prime source or the full A(n) field. The rest of mu's coefficients
remain present in B1 and B14.

For example, even granting a strong pointwise prime-density remainder
P_actual(u)-P_cont(u)=O(exp(bu)), with b>b0 fixed and b<1, the elementary
Bessel estimate only bounds its transformed remainder by
O((1+u)exp(bu)). This exceeds each desired gamma. A classical subpower PNT
remainder cannot supply the required fixed power either. Therefore B12a
does not contradict [private research revision]'s actual signed-core prime asymptotic, which
concerns its original fixed profile and sharp source. It supplies no new
asymptotic for that source. Moving-order uniformity is a real new demand.

## Group 1: free invention, no cap

- **01. Two-witness convex duality** (p=.18; R/H/U). Object: a zero must satisfy two normalized detector witness constraints in one arithmetic Hilbert space. Bridge: the minimal cost of their simultaneous constraints is the inverse of their exact Gram matrix; a joint upper bound could beat either detector. Test: derive the two-constraint variational inequality with complex phase and cross term. Objection: the two detectors may not admit a common witness or comparable normalization.
- **02. Paid low-rank transfer** (p=.14; R/H). Object: approximate the hard detector coefficient map by a bounded map applied to the easier detector plus a residual. Bridge: transfer a proven norm estimate with explicit operator norm, residual norm and cross term. Test: derive the optimal quadratic transfer inequality and identify the required source identity. Objection: the residual may contain the entire arithmetic difficulty.
- **03. Local-moment support surgery** (p=.22; R/H). Object: partition the exact local moment into low multiplicity and collision-rich support. Bridge: use the newer local estimate only on the collision-poor region and count its complement. Test: symbolic exponent budget at the support cut. Objection: the known improvement may already optimize this partition, or the exceptional set dominates.
- **04. Prime-power quotient detector** (p=.08; R/U). Object: quotient the detector coefficient space by the span of prime powers, keeping exact prime contributions. Bridge: inverse Gram correction preserves the zero witness while shrinking variance. Test: finite exact coefficient projection and its witness leakage. Objection: removing prime powers may also remove the detectable zero signal.
- **05. Resonant mixed energy** (p=.12; H/U). Object: multiply rather than add the Gaussian and H detector witnesses on a common zero. Bridge: fourth or mixed moments constrain simultaneous largeness. Test: derive the mixed-moment exponent needed to exceed c5. Objection: multiplication increases length and forces an unproved cross-correlation estimate.

# [private research revision] headroom: complete large-common-factor source estimate

Status: mathematics and bounded checks complete; independent review pending; no new c. Final freeze/release status is recorded in the handoff. Current source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, gamma11=.8748540364. All prior scopes remain frozen; root owns canonical/tracker/Git. No formalization, packet, child or model-provider contact.

## Compact worklog

Objective: discover distinct higher-ceiling mechanisms and test a complete first-gain requirement. Completed: discovery/index/source audit, primary BSZ criterion check, exact large-root collision proof, complete nonlinear masked-gcd estimate, inherited-source transfer and explicit failed power test. Completed also: one exact identity run and source pins. Readback, final integrity, own release/absence and the sole reviewer wake are recorded in freeze.json and the native handoff. Original29-family/109-child library, all prior frozen scopes, and F0/positive-slot/external obligations remain intact. Source/evidence pointers: Sections3-6, source-evidence.json and checks.json. Root owns canonical integration; the sole writer scope and native claim are identified above.

## 1. Initial discovery comparison

A. Higher cyclotomic completely multiplicative sources. The Liouville choice is the order-two case. For a primitive r-th root omega, convolve the r-1 functions omega^(j Omega(n))chi(n). The Euler product suggests a numerator L(rz,chi^r)/L(z,chi), hence r-th-power rather than square-supported completion and more sparse complementary terms. Potential: retain multiplicative layers and obtain much cheaper physical support. Strong objection: the individual complex layers can have artificial branch singularities at z=1; their separate norms may be intrinsically too large. Develop the actual coupled and separated source contracts before any absolute-value step. Provisional selection.

B. Katai/prime-dilation bilinearization of the actual Liouville source. Complete multiplicativity permits exact prime factor extraction; oscillation could enter cross-prime correlations before absolute values. Strong objection: near n~X the nonlinear phase has bounded variation, and close prime dilations remain correlated. Prime coverage and the rough complement are real costs. This requires a source-exact argument, not a generic multiplicative orthogonality slogan.

C. Increasing the reciprocal-L pole order by convolution before applying a detector. A zero then produces a higher-order singularity and a larger logarithmic signal. Potential: trade amplification against a coarse arithmetic bound. Strong objection: the actual divisor coefficients and factorial normalization also grow; fixed-order logarithms never give a power, and growing order must be uniform throughout the return.

D. Signed unique-prime organization of the accepted four-cross-gcd residual. A prime assigned to only one variable may couple parity with the exact Gaussian correlations. Potential: retain arithmetic cancellation in the remaining all-small-gcd form. Strong objection: independent heights, all15 intersections, and actual Hecke/projector marks cannot be compressed to arbitrary four bounded sequences or identified with OPEN-LC. Read the source before deciding whether a distinct usable identity exists.

The pass will retain an actual complete estimate or a precise actual-source obstruction after substantive construction; a changed name for an open norm will not count as a gain.

## 2. Development checkpoint and inherited credit

The initial cyclotomic selection was rejected as a separated-layer argument after the W22/W35 duplicate check. Its coupled identity remains valid and is retained below. At22:12 a different survivor was saved: an exact large-root collision count combined with W24's interval multiplicity estimate and the [restricted research revision] whole-kernel method. The initial collision-only payment suggested X G^(-5/6); the complete local-count argument improves this to X/G. Sections4-6 give the full proved restricted theorem, its exact source transfer and the failed complete first-gain test. This is distinct from the separately assigned Hecke R4 lane. W24's count, [restricted research revision]'s kernel and small-multiplier collision method are credited inputs, not relabeled discoveries. The new large-root collision identity and its full masked-gcd source application are proved here. No literature-priority claim is made.

## 3. Final discovery dispositions and outside primary check

A was tested at the coefficient level. For r>=3 and omega=exp(2pi i/r), let a_j(n)=omega^(j Omega(n))chi(n), 1<=j<r. The exact coupled source A_r=*_(j=1)^(r-1)a_j has local series (1-t)/(1-t^r), t=chi(p)p^(-z). Consequently A_r=(mu chi)*s_r, A_r*chi=s_r, and D_(A_r)(z)=L(rz,chi^r)/L(z,chi), where s_r(m^r)=chi(m)^r. Its nonzero prime-power coefficients are chi(p)^nu for nu=0 mod r and -chi(p)^nu for nu=1 mod r. This valid coupled construction is retained; no separate-layer norm is licensed.

For the principal character modulo1, each separated layer has D_(a_j)(z)=zeta(z)^(omega^j)H_j(z), with H_j analytic and nonzero near1: the logarithm of its Euler correction starts at prime powers of order2 and converges normally there. A nonzero finite Euler filter Q has integer order m at1, so QD_(a_j) has local factor (z-1)^(m-omega^j). For a noninteger omega^j this cannot be a single-valued holomorphic function near1. The same fixed nonlinear Mellin return used below would force such holomorphy if this separate source had a full L1 shell bound X^(gamma+epsilon), gamma<1. Thus that proposed separate payment fails already for q=1. Even r may contain the exceptional j=r/2 layer; the other noninteger layers still prevent this separated argument. This is the existing W22/W35 branch obstruction in a new notation, not new credit. Coupling the layers cancels the branch but loses the single completely multiplicative Liouville merge. Indeed a completely multiplicative a with (a*chi)(p)=0 has a(p)=-chi(p), forcing (a*chi)(p^2)=chi(p)^2, so it cannot give pure r-th powers for r>2. The coupled construction remains a possible different source, with a missing complete arithmetic estimate.

The primary outside check was [Bourgain-Sarnak-Ziegler, arXiv:1110.0992v1, Theorem2, p2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1110.0992). It requires bounded multiplicative weights and small correlations of distinct prime dilations, at fixed small accuracy before the large-length limit. Its parameter range and thresholds do not supply a uniform polynomial saving for a shell-dependent profile. Its proof and [Tao's criterion and proof](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/11/21/the-bourgain-sarnak-ziegler-orthogonality-criterion/) motivated testing B's actual transition profile rather than assuming decorrelation. For F_X(n)=1_(n<=X) exp(-n/X^(3/2)-i(n/X)^6), fixed distinct primes p,q and m<=X/max(p,q), the phase difference has modulus<=1. Thus the real part of the entire dilation correlation through this endpoint is at least cos(1)exp(-2/sqrt(X))floor(X/max(p,q)). It is of the full length. This does not refute an argument exploiting the actual signed source and other regions; it refutes the direct uniform small-correlation input for this specific profile. Those other regions and their cross terms cannot be discarded. No BSZ theorem is imported into the survivor.

[De la Breteche-Tenenbaum, arXiv:2010.12929v8](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.12929v8), metadata/abstract, also confirms the complex zeta-power setting of A. No Selberg-Delange asymptotic is imported; the branch calculation above is elementary. Source access and exact local pins are in source-evidence.json.

C does not change an exponent with a fixed reciprocal-pole order: it changes the finite logarithmic polynomial associated with that pole. A growing-order construction still needs uniform coefficient, normalization and return estimates, which were not derived. D is now explicitly assigned to the independent R4 lane and was not developed here. The selected E combines the valid unused LARGE-root collision calculation with W24's interval count and [restricted research revision]'s whole-kernel method. Its new content is the uniform complete estimate in Section4 and the literal source restriction in Section5; the inherited counts/kernel ancestry retain their credit.

## 4. Completed restricted theorem: all large common factors, full norm

**Theorem LG.** Let X>=2 and G>=1 be real. Let |a_1(d)|,|a_2(e)|<=1 and |b(l)|<=B_0, with B_0 fixed. For EACH X and G choose any complex tuple weights theta_(X,G)(d,e,l), of modulus<=1, before real x varies. They may contain arbitrary strict or closed arithmetic cutoffs, natural zeros, independent coefficient phases and n-dependent support; they must be independent of live x. Define the literal ordered coefficient and full damped source

 v_G(n)=sum_(d e l=n, gcd(d,e)>G) a_1(d)a_2(e)b(l)theta_(X,G)(d,e,l),
 B_G(x)=sum_(n>=1)v_G(n)exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6).

For every epsilon>0,

 ||B_G||_(L^2([X,2X],dx/x))
   <<_(epsilon,B_0) X^epsilon [X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)].             (LG1)

The same bound holds in L1. Constants are independent of G, all sequences and all frozen masks within these bounds. In particular there is no need for a polynomial upper cap on G. The physical applications below use G=X^(1-gamma). Absolute local convergence follows from the divisor bound and the damping. The theorem does not assert a pointwise bound at this strength.

### 4.1 Full collision and local multiplicity, with endpoints

Let r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2|n}. Its first moment is <=2Y/G. The exact second-moment identity is

 sum_(n<=Y)r_G(n)^2
  =sum_(r,s>G)floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G, Y>=1.               (LG2)

Every sum on the left and the nonzero part on the right is finite. In the inequality write r=g u,s=g v,(u,v)=1. The condition is g>G/min(u,v). For every t>0, sum_(g>t)g^(-2)<=2/t. Thus the right side is at most (2Y/G)sum_(u,v>=1)min(u,v)/(u^2v^2). The last series is <=2sum_u u^(-1)sum_(v>=u)v^(-2)<=4sum_u u^(-2)<8. This proves the stated constant16 without discarding collisions. Nonintegral Y/G, r=s and repeated/shared prime powers are included. Equality r=G, if integral, remains in the good source.

For fixed c,C>0, an interval I subset[cN,CN] of length h satisfies

 sum_(n in I)r_G(n) <<_(c,C) h/G+E_N,
 E_N=min(N^(1/3),N/G^2),                                (LG3)

whenever 1<=G<=sqrt(CN). If G>sqrt(CN) the sum is zero. To verify the inherited W24 count: if G<=N^(1/3), sum G<r<=N^(1/3) with count<=h/r^2+1. For larger r, reverse the summation to l=n/r^2<=CN^(1/3). The real root interval for each l has length O(h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l))); length plus one gives O(h/N^(1/3)+N^(1/3)). If G>N^(1/3), reverse all roots and use l<=CN/G^2, giving O(h/G+N/G^2). This is a PAIR count (r,l), with multiplicities. Closed endpoints and h<1 are paid by the length-plus-one terms; if the block is nonempty N/G^2>=1/C, so no unpriced isolated endpoint remains. The global mass is O(N/G), by (LG2)'s first-moment version.

Writing d=r u,e=r v with r the EXACT gcd assigns every original ordered tuple once. At a given r^2|n, its remaining number of factorizations is at most d_3(n/r^2). Hence for every fixed eta>0

 |v_G(n)| <= B_0 d_3(n)r_G(n) <<_(eta,B_0) n^eta r_G(n),
 sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| << Y^(1+eta)/G,
 sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 << Y^(1+2eta)/G.                    (LG4)

No coprimality was inserted between r,u,v,l beyond the defining (u,v)=1, and this last condition was only dropped in a POSITIVE upper bound. All tuple masks remain literal; the majorant counts every possible root, not only its largest or prime root. This is coefficient domination, not norm monotonicity under a signed subset.

### 4.2 Whole nonlinear kernel and the low/high split

Choose one nonnegative smooth w supported in[1/2,3], w>=1 on[1,2]. The weighted shell kernel K_X(n,m)=integral w(x/X)f_x(n)conj(f_x(m))dx/x obeys

 |K_X(n,m)| << exp(-c(n+m)/X^(3/2))
                    min(1,(X^6/|n^6-m^6|)^2),           (LG5)

with the minimum set to1 on the exact diagonal. Substitute x=Xu and integrate by parts twice in the nonstationary phase -(n^6-m^6)/(X^6u^6). Its derivative has no zero on the fixed support. Derivatives of the damping cost a fixed polynomial in (n+m)/X^(3/2), absorbed into a slightly weaker exponential. Compactly supported w removes boundary terms. This proves (LG5) on the full shell, not a sampled x grid.

Split B_G=B_lo+B_hi at the CLOSED cutoff n<=X. By (LG4), |B_lo(x)|<<X^(1+eta)/G throughout the support of w. All low/high interactions are paid by the norm triangle inequality, so no unconditional small scalar mixed term is asserted. It remains to bound the entire norm of B_hi, n>X. Expansion is justified first for finite truncations and then by local absolute convergence.

Partition every ordered upper pair into comparable pairs (ratio between1/2 and2) and far pairs. A bounded-overlap dyadic covering puts every comparable pair in [N/2,4N]^2 for some N>=cX. Let H=X^6/N^5. On this block |n^6-m^6| is bounded below by a fixed multiple of N^5|n-m|. The kernel is bounded by exp(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,(H/|n-m|)^2), including its diagonal.

Using (LG3), the weighted r_G mass about ANY integer center n is O(H/G+E_N): divide distances into |m-n|<=H and successive doubling rings. For H>=1, local count gives a geometric sum H/G+E_N. For H<1, use |m-n|<=H for the possible diagonal and doubling rings beginning at H; empty subunit rings contribute nothing, and the same upper bound follows (or begin off-diagonal rings at1 with weight O(H^2)). Intersecting a ring interval with [N/2,4N] costs at most two intervals with the same fixed constants. Multiplying by the complete block mass O(N/G) gives the positive pair majorant

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)
                      [X^6/(G^2 N^4)+(N/G)E_N].        (LG6)

Separately, the unweighted integer-kernel row sum is O(1+H): the off-diagonal sum over nonzero integer distances is O(H) for H>=1 and O(H^2)<=O(H) for H<1. Apply 2|v_G(n)v_G(m)|<=|v_G(n)|^2+|v_G(m)|^2 and (LG4) on [N/2,4N]. This bounds THE SAME positive pair majorant by

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)(N/G)(1+H).             (LG7)

The global l2 density alone would leave the larger HN/G cost near N~X. It is (LG6), retaining the local square-divisor count, that closes this loss. Taking the minimum of the two valid bounds for the same complete block, and using min(A+B,C+D)<=A+C+min(B,D), gives

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)
       [X^6/(G^2 N^4)+(N/G)(1+min(N^(1/3),H))].        (LG8)

Constants/exponentials are first made common. Both ordered orientations, exact coincidences, all distinct roots giving the same output, and all masks were included before taking this minimum.

Sum (LG8) over dyadic N>=cX. The first term is O(X^(2+2eta)/G^2). Actual damping pays the isolated1 term by O(X^(3/2+3eta)/G). The remaining sum is bounded without damping by

 (1/G)sum_(N dyadic>=cX)N^(1+2eta)min(N^(1/3),X^6/N^5)
       <<_eta X^(3/2+9eta/4)/G, 0<eta<1.               (LG9)

Indeed its increasing term N^(4/3+2eta) and decreasing term X^6N^(-4+2eta) meet at N=X^(9/8). Their geometric tails converge. This argument uses every high block, not only an average block or a low-frequency range. Blocks with G>sqrt(4N) are empty and may be kept as zero.

For far pairs take n~N, X<m<n/2, and include the reverse orientation. The gap is bounded below by a constant times N^6. The absolute coefficient shell and cumulative masses from (LG4) are each O(N^(1+eta)/G). Thus their complete total is

 <<sum_(N dyadic>=cX) X^12 N^(-12) N^(2+2eta)/G^2
 << X^(2+2eta)/G^2.                                    (LG10)

Damping can only improve this bound. There is no omitted large/small cross pair: both entries here belong to B_hi; B_lo/B_hi were paid earlier by triangle. Combining (LG8)-(LG10), the low bound and norm triangle gives

 ||B_G||_2^2 <<_(eta,B_0) X^(2+2eta)/G^2+X^(3/2+3eta)/G.

Choose eta>0 after the requested epsilon, for example eta=min(epsilon/4,1/4), to prove (LG1). L1 follows by Cauchy-Schwarz on logarithmic measure log2. This completes the theorem uniformly for every G>=1 and every stated frozen mask.

### 4.3 What the strongest uniform obstruction actually says

The first term X/G cannot be improved in this broad bounded-mask class by cancellation of the kernel alone. Choose a_1=a_2=b=1 and retain just d=e=r with G<r<=2G and r^2 l<=X/2. For 1<=G<=c sqrt(X), with a sufficiently small fixed c, there are >>X/G such ordered triples. Their phases for every x in[X,2X] lie between -1/64 and0; damping is bounded below. Therefore ||B_G||_1,||B_G||_2 >>X/G. This is an example in the explicitly quantified comparison class, not in the actual signed Liouville core. It establishes sharpness of this general method's first term and no impossibility theorem for the actual signs. In particular it does not rule out the endpoint exponent, an epsilon-loss bound, or any structured arithmetic improvement after restriction.

## 5. Literal application to the accepted compensated source

This section imports exactly [restricted research revision] G176-G178; it does not replace the pinned PR9/Gao analytic ancestry or enlarge a Hecke family. Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a positive integer q, naturally zero off the units, and fixed unramified p. Write a=lambda chi, h=chi, s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 with s zero off squares. Retain

 q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
 q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
 b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g=a*a*b.                              (LC1)

In particular q2's coefficient is -p chi(p)^2, not -p^2 chi(p)^2. The original b is bounded by (p+1)^2 and has zero mean and period p^3q. The root sequence beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)) has zero mean and period pq. Their compensations and all their cross terms remain unchanged. The Euler series is

 D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
 P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).       (LC2)

For a fixed 3/4<=gamma<1 set L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4), Q=p^3q, eta0=1/(6000Q), B(n)=min(L,eta0 X^6/n^5). Choose tau in the CLOSED range

 max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= (11gamma-3)/8,             (LC3)

before live real x; U(n)=B(n)^tau, V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau). The original exact decomposition is c=Q_U+Q_V-S_tau+R_tau, with

 Q_U(n)=sum_(de=n,d<=U(n))a(d)(v*s)(e),
 S_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l),
 R_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l).

Q_V is the other ordered short slot. The full source is C(x)=sum c(n)f_x(n). The old complete core is T=sum_(L<n<=M)R_tau(n)f_x(n).

Now define G=X^(1-gamma) and impose ONE additional literal tuple condition:

 T_small(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) f_x(n)
     sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n),gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b(l). (LC4)

The difference T-T_small is precisely Theorem LG with the frozen mask
1_(L<de l<=M)1_(d>U(de l))1_(e>V(de l)). It includes every cofactor, squareful output and multiplicity admitted by that mask. No averaging of the gcd, merged-output truncation or live-x-dependent mask has been substituted. By (LG1),

 ||T-T_small||_j << X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2,             (LC5)

because X/G=X^gamma and X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)=X^(1/4+gamma/2)<=X^gamma. All constants are uniform in tau satisfying (LC3), since the mask theorem is uniform.

For clarity, the COMPLETE difference C-T_small is the sum of the two full short-slot sources, minus the full small-double source, plus the original R_tau at n<=L, its entire damped tail n>M, and the new finite-core large-gcd source. The inherited short-slot estimate is

 ||Q_D||_2^2 << D^2+X^(6/11)D^(16/11)+X^(3/4)D^(1/2)
                    +min(X^(3/5)D^(7/5),X^(15/16)D^(1/2)).

At D=X^alpha and alpha<= (11gamma-3)/8, its four norm exponents are all <=gamma. Both ordered slots therefore cost X^gamma. The small-double source is paid by the actual zero-mean b, its period Q, and the unchanged derivative-gap cutoff eta0. Its treatment has not been reapplied to the gcd-restricted source, where that periodicity might be broken. The old low core uses |R_tau(n)|<=(p+1)^2d_3(n). The full high core has squared norm O(X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon)); its two exponents are <=2gamma for gamma>=3/4. The new source costs (LC5). These complete-source estimates and norm triangle give

 ||C-T_small||_(L^j([X,2X],dx/x))
        <<_(p,q,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2. (LC6)

Every low/high, short/plain, two-short and good/bad interaction is paid at the norm level. No unconditional scalar energy-error formula is asserted. Equality at each exponent boundary is allowed because the theorem is stated for every epsilon. An intermediate strict-reserve failure would not prove impossibility at equality.

The retained merged coefficient is exactly

 R_small(n)=sum_(m l=n)a(m)D_(U(n),V(n);G)(m)b(l),
 D_(U,V;G)(m)=#{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G}.   (LC7)

Complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de) holds for shared primes and natural zeros; it is used only for Liouville in (LC7). No unrestricted Mobius merge is inferred. Every common factor up to G, every squareful m, and both orderings remain. All exact gcds greater than G were paid, including composite products of small common primes. The result does not impose primality or pairwise coprimality with l. It is a new restriction inside the oscillatory core, not an improvement only to its already paid far tail.

The coarse absolute finite-core sum would cost M/G up to X^epsilon and require delta=log_X G >= (3/2)(1-gamma). The collision-only intermediate bound in Section2 would require delta>=(6/5)(1-gamma). The full local-count-plus-collision proof permits delta=1-gamma. These comparisons are bounds for this SAME within-source integer gcd, not the physical Hecke cross-copy gcd of [restricted research revision]. No independent-height/projector theorem is imported into an arbitrary coefficient class; (LG1) has its own elementary proof. Natural unitary coefficient twists can occur in its bounded weights, but the analytic return below concerns a fixed ordinary character.

| calibration/target | gamma | delta in G=X^delta | earlier absolute delta | remaining L1 exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| current c11 | 2187135091/2500000000 | 312864909/2500000000 | 938594727/5000000000 | gamma |
| conditional c=.1252 | 2187/2500 | 313/2500 | 939/5000 | gamma |
| conditional c=1/6 | 5/6 | 1/6 | 1/4 | gamma |
| conditional c=1/4 | 3/4 | 1/4 | 3/8 | gamma |

This table establishes only paid complements. In particular the first row checks the actual current gamma=.8748540364, not just the illustrative .8748. The allowed tau corridor is unchanged, including [1/8,7/8] at gamma=3/4. No endpoint or numeric c is promoted.

## 6. Weakest complete first-gain target, return, and actual failed test

The remaining sufficient estimate is the COMPLETE (LC4) L1 bound

 integral_X^(2X)|T_small,p,chi,tau_X(x)| dx/x
    <<_(p,chi,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)            (OPEN-LCG)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, for every fixed ordinary character chi and each member of a fixed covering pair of unramified primes. One common gamma<gamma11 must be chosen BEFORE chi and a putative zero. The choices tau_X may depend on epsilon, chi, p and the shell, but lie in (LC3) and are frozen before x. G is fixed as X^(1-gamma); all original source cuts remain literal. Constants and scale thresholds may depend on these fixed data. A full L2 bound at the same exponent suffices; a selected block, average over characters, finite height range, fixed positive epsilon loss, or a few sampled x do not.

By (LC6), this every-epsilon complete norm hypothesis is equivalent to the same full L1 bound for C. This equivalence is inherited norm-triangle logic, not claimed as a new theorem saying the problem is intrinsically easier, nor as an equivalence to zero exclusion. The new arithmetic input is (LG1), which permits a smaller actual retained gcd.

The complete conditional return stays the accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] return. The shell bound makes H_p(z)=integral_0^infinity C_p,chi(1/t)t^(z-1)dt holomorphic for Re z>gamma. Small x is paid by the actual exponential damping; derivatives introduce logarithmic factors absorbed locally in the fixed strip. Initially on Re z>3/2, clockwise contour rotation gives

 H_p(z)=A0(z)P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi)+E_p(z),
 A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6.                       (RET)

The unchanged coefficient-integral remainder is O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)), locally with derivatives, so E_p is normally holomorphic on Re z>1/2. The source, detector, damping, finite p factors and error were not replaced by the gcd-restricted object in this identity. The restriction is used only through the proved full norm transfer (LC6).

A0, J_p and L(2z,chi^2) have no zeros on Re z>1/2. P_p has zeros only on Re z=1. Two distinct fixed unramified primes have no common nonzero-height P zero: finite character values are roots of unity, whereas log p1/log p2 is irrational. For nonprincipal chi choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1 to cover height zero; p2 is distinct. The principal pole at1 is the specified exception. Thus (OPEN-LCG) excludes every finite-height zero with Re z>gamma. This uses local holomorphy around each height, not an unproved uniform conductor/height estimate. Imprimitive factors, natural zeros and fixed inducing-character data remain exactly as in the ordinary source. All external root-LFunction binding, F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot and admission qualifications remain OPEN in the project; no formalization was attempted.

The near conditional target gamma=2187/2500 would give c=.1252, exceeding c11 by135091/2500000000. The same complete statement is available at gamma5/6 and3/4. These are conditional targets, not achieved bounds.

**Coarse complete test actually performed.** The full source coefficients obey the accepted variance bound sum_(n<=Y)|c(n)|^2<<_(p,q)Y. The complete kernel estimate then gives ||C||_2<<X, which transfers by (LC6) to ||T_small||_2<<X+X^(gamma+epsilon); no power below1 follows. The stronger already accepted fixed-degree arithmetic input (Green-Tao plus the exact square expansion, with its full square tail paid) gives for each fixed D

 ||C||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D).

It transfers to the whole T_small by (LC6), with the additional X^(2gamma+epsilon) term. This remains above every fixed exponent2gamma<2 eventually; choosing a fixed larger D does not change that conclusion. No new nilsequence or growing-degree estimate was imported or rerun. Direct positive counting of the retained source gives coefficient bound (p+1)^2d_3(n), and the same full-kernel split at n=X costs X^(1+epsilon); the gcd restriction does not itself provide a power saving for the ubiquitous gcd-one factorizations. The exact merged sign a(m), ordered divisor multiplicity and periodic b(l) remain in (OPEN-LCG). A lower bound for one selected positive/semiprime part would not lower-bound its signed full norm, so none is claimed.

The useful redirect is now quantitative: try arithmetic cancellation in (LC7) with original gcd(d,e)<=X^(1-gamma), retaining all cofactors and both orientations, or prove a further legitimate source decomposition of that exact object. The all-large-gcd complement is already paid at the sharp uniform-mask main-term scale. Improving it alone will not establish (OPEN-LCG). This pass proves a restricted actual-source estimate and a complete changed-core criterion; it does not produce a new c.

## 7. Fixed general phase compatibility (controller suggestion, checked here)

Root proposed this extension during this pass; it is additional to the fixed k=6 theorem. With the SAME v_G and frozen masks, replace f_x(n) by exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), for fixed b>1 and fixed integer k>2. The proof above gives

 ||B_G||_2 <<_(b,k,epsilon,B_0) X^epsilon
       [X/G+(X^(b/2)+X^(2k/(3k-2)))/sqrt(G)].            (LGK)

Here are all changed sums. In a comparable upper block H=X^k/N^(k-1). Equation(LG8) becomes, with the changed damping,

 exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)
   [X^k/(G^2 N^(k-2))+(N/G)(1+min(N^(1/3),H))].

Its first sum from N>=cX is O(X^(2+2eta)/G^2); the diagonal sum is O(X^(b+2b eta)/G). The remaining increasing N^(4/3+2eta) and decreasing X^k N^(2-k+2eta) terms meet at N=X^(3k/(3k-2)), and sum to O(X^(4k/(3k-2)+6k eta/(3k-2))/G. Choose eta<(k-2)/4 after epsilon so the decreasing tail converges. Far pairs give X^(2k)sum N^(2-2k+2eta)/G^2=O(X^(2+2eta)/G^2). The complete low piece still costs X^(1+eta)/G, and triangle pays its entire cross term. This proves(LGK), uniformly in all G>=1. No parameter grows with X.

With G=X^(1-gamma), the additional complement conditions are exactly

 gamma>=b-1, and gamma>=(k+2)/(3k-2).                    (LGK2)

This is compatible with the ALREADY accepted [restricted research revision] general Liouville architecture for each fixed1/2<gamma<1. Choose fixed1<b<=2gamma and then a sufficiently large fixed integer k>=6 such that b>=2k/(2k-1) and r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b. Its weaker short-source corridor is alpha<=(4gamma-b)/3, nonempty even at balanced tau=1/2. Keep its generalized derivative-gap cuts and every original source term. Then(LGK2) holds: b-1<=2gamma-1<gamma and (k+2)/(3k-2)<=1/2. Thus the same additional small-gcd condition is paid in that general core as well.

The inherited return must retain ALL fixed K shifts D_c(z+(b-1)j), j<K, with K fixed so1-(b-1)K<gamma; the j-th factor is (-1)^j Gamma((z+bj)/k)exp(-i*pi*(z+bj)/(2k))/(k j!). The remainder is holomorphic to the required line. Finite strip descent from Re z>1 treats shifted reciprocals first, then solves for the unshifted term using A0 and the covering primes. It does not discard shifted poles or claim a height-uniform constant. [restricted research revision] review Sections7-8 and [restricted research revision] Section8 are the retained contract; (LGK) changes only the proved complement. At gamma=3/5, b=11/10,k=12,K=5,r=27/25 meet all conditions and permit G=X^(2/5). This remains conditional arithmetic reach. There is no boundary gamma=1/2 result, no uniform limiting argument and no achieved gain.

## 8. Evidence, disposition and handoff scope

The fresh helper check.py was read in full before its one execution. It checks49 exact large-root collision identities,400 local-count diagnostics (including singleton intervals),18 actual compensated Liouville source/mask cases for q=1,4,5 and three tau values, three generic Mobius tuple-map cases, and four exact rational calibration/target rows. All assertions passed. It retains the natural character zeros, ordered factorizations, strict bad-gcd endpoints and row-dependent B(n). The local-count diagnostics and finite coefficient checks are not proofs of (LG1), its uniformity or (OPEN-LCG); the proofs are Sections4-7. No numerical quadrature or arbitrary norm sample is offered as arithmetic evidence. The helper writes only adjacent checks.json and must not be rerun in frozen author scope.

Exact local source paths, hashes and read extents are in source-evidence.json. W24's square-divisor interval count and the [restricted research revision] review's short-source collision method retain their original credit. The [restricted research revision] physical true-gcd and [restricted research revision] Hecke cross-copy gcd sources have different variables/projectors; neither was imported into this ordinary theorem. Novelty is relative to the inspected project index and these sources, with no literature-priority assertion.

Surviving result: an unconditional full masked large-common-factor source estimate, and its exact paid reduction of the accepted nonlinear Liouville core to gcd(d,e)<=X^(1-gamma), with fixed general-phase compatibility. Unresolved: the complete signed (OPEN-LCG) estimate. Current c11 and all external/F0/positive-slot qualifications are unchanged. The proof does not authorize arbitrary canonical-moment coefficients, a selected-subset norm comparison, a new Hecke scope or formalization. Independent review is required before controller acceptance.

statement:
## 1. One fixed smooth test detects every zero in the right half-plane

For u>0 put

\[
V(u)=e^{-u-1/u},\qquad
\phi(u)=(uV(u))'=(1-u+u^{-1})e^{-u-1/u},\qquad
S_\phi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\phi(n/x). \tag{V1}
\]

Extend phi by zero to u<=0. It is a real Schwartz function, flat
at zero, with integral zero. Its entire Mellin transform is

\[
\Phi(s)=\int_0^\infty\phi(u)u^{s-1}\,du
       =2(1-s)K_s(2). \tag{V2}
\]

Integration by parts gives the factor 1-s. Substituting u=e^t
in the remaining integral gives the usual integral representation
of K_s; see [NIST DLMF 10.32.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.32.E9).
This standard identity does not by itself assert nonvanishing.

**Nonvanishing in the order variable.** If K_s(2)=0, set
f(t)=K_s(2e^t), t>=0. The
[modified Bessel equation](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.25.E1) gives

\[
-f''+4e^{2t}f=-s^2f,\qquad f(0)=0.
\]

For fixed complex s, the
[large-argument expansions](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.40.E2)
and their derivative show
K_s(x)~sqrt(pi/(2x)) exp(-x). Thus f, f', and e^t f lie in L2,
the boundary term at infinity vanishes, and f is not identically
zero. Integration by parts gives

\[
0<
\int_0^\infty\left(|f'|^2+4e^{2t}|f|^2\right)\,dt
=-s^2\int_0^\infty|f|^2\,dt. \tag{V3}
\]

Consequently -s^2 is positive real and s is purely imaginary.
In particular K_s(2) is nonzero when Re s>0. Hence Phi is
nonzero in that half-plane except at s=1.

**Proved conditional criterion.** Let 0<a<1. If for every
epsilon>0, at every sufficiently large INTEGER N,

\[
|S_\phi(N)|\ll_\epsilon N^{a+\epsilon}, \tag{V4}
\]

then zeta has no zeros in Re s>a.

Indeed, absolute differentiation and a Schwartz envelope give
|S_phi'(x)|<=x^(-1) sum_n |(n/x)phi'(n/x)|<<1 for x>=1.
Integer bounds therefore give the same real-scale bound.
As x tends to zero, S_phi(x) is exponentially small.
For Re s>1, absolute integration and u=n/x give

\[
\int_0^\infty S_\phi(x)x^{-s-1}\,dx
       =\frac{\Phi(s)}{\zeta(s)}. \tag{V5}
\]

The left side continues holomorphically to Re s>a under (V4).
Multiplying by (s-1)zeta(s) and continuing the identity excludes
every zero there by (V2)--(V3). The point s=1 is zeta's pole,
not a possible zero. This argument does not require a uniform
lower bound for Phi on vertical lines, a zero-dependent profile,
simple zeta zeros, or a finite-height verification.

### 4.1 The deliberately coarse complete first-gain test

Take the balanced cuts and gamma>6/7, covering gamma11 and .8748. To test a bounded-coefficient bilinear estimate, first remove the gcd cutoff from the WHOLE finite core using G182, paying X^(gamma+epsilon). Decompose its finite original d,e,l,n ranges dyadically; O(log^4 X) labels suffice. There is no continuum sampling. On a cell n~N>=X, d~D,e~E, DE l~N, relabel the two original colors if needed so D>=E. Both are at least a fixed multiple of X^(gamma/2). Keep the sharp product cutoff N<del<=2N (intersected with the actual M endpoint) and both lower inverse cuts.

For fixed l and x, Cauchy in d leaves the exact signed e-correlation with an inner d sum. For e'=e+h, the difference-phase derivative in d has size

 T h/(DE), T=(N/X)^6,

and is monotone. Its maximum is O(T/D). Since N<=M and gamma>6/7,

 T<=X^(3(1-gamma))=o(X^(gamma/2))<=o(D).

The discrete first-derivative bound therefore gives

 |K_(e,e+h)| <<min(D,DE/(T h)).                               (23)

The d interval is the intersection of the two original product intervals and the fixed dyadic/lower-cut interval, hence one interval or empty. Its endpoints are kept. Summing all h and both orders, and retaining the diagonal, yields

 |sum_(d,e in cell) a(d)a(e)f_x(del)|
  <<DE [E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))],                       (24)

up to harmless bounded-variation partial summation for the actual damping. On these cells n<=M<X^(3/2), the damping and its first needed variations are uniformly bounded. More explicitly it may be kept inside K and the original Cauchy amplitudes; the same Abel bound holds. No estimate for signed Liouville correlations was used in obtaining (24).

Summing |b0(l)| with DE~N/l and all dyadic labels gives the full n~N contribution bounded by

 X^epsilon [N X^(-gamma/4)+X^3/N^2].                          (25)

The first exponent over N<=M is r-gamma/4=3/2-3gamma/4, <=gamma exactly when gamma>=6/7. The second is <=X^gamma only when N>=X^((3-gamma)/2)=M. Thus the coarse test pays the diagonal throughout but fails on the interior transition, returning O(X^(1+epsilon)) when all N>=X are summed. Outputs L<n<X also cost at most X^(1+epsilon) by the actual coefficient bound. The paid gcd complement adds X^(gamma+epsilon). This is a complete failed first-gain calculation, not a claim that an unproved bilinear bound succeeds.

statement:
## 2. A: exact Gaussian source and the moving-order return

Fix `tau,kappa>0`, the actual sequence `a(n)`, and a fixed `B>0` with `C_B=sum |a(n)|n^-B<infinity`. Ideals can replace integers only with the same explicit norm-weighted absolute hypothesis. Put

    F(x)=sum_n a(n) g_tau(log(n/x)),
    W_X(v)=g_kappa(v) F(X exp(v)),
    sigma=tau+kappa, nu=tau*kappa/sigma, alpha=kappa/sigma,
    w_n=log(n/X), b_n=g_sigma(w_n).

Completing the square gives exactly

    g_kappa(v)g_tau(w-v)=g_sigma(w)g_nu(v-alpha*w).       (R1)

The prefactors agree because `kappa*tau=sigma*nu`. The v², vw and w² coefficients respectively give `1/kappa+1/tau=1/nu`, `alpha/nu=1/tau` and `1/sigma+alpha²/nu=1/tau`. There is no missing normalization or X-power. With Fourier transform `hat f(t)=integral f(v)e^(-itv)dv`,

    hat W_X(t)=e^(-nu*t²/2) sum_n a(n)b_n e^(-i alpha*t*w_n),
    sum_n |a(n)|b_n <= C_B X^B e^(sigma*B²/2)/sqrt(2pi*sigma).
                                                               (R2)

This is an absolutely justified formula at every real Fourier height. It comes from the original convergent coefficient sum, not an assumed reciprocal continuation. For fixed real/complex compact windows, Gaussian decay also justifies the differentiations used here.

For every real `r>=0`, define `N_r²=(2pi)^-1 integral (1+t²)^-r |hat W_X(t)|² dt`. Splitting at any `T>=1` and applying R2 to the **unweighted W tail** proves

    ||W_X||_2 <= (1+T²)^(r/2) N_r(X)
                  + C X^B e^(-nu*T²/2).                (R3)

The inverse Sobolev factor does not multiply the high-frequency tail. This is the decisive response to the general objection that a negative norm conceals high frequencies. The inequality would be false without an envelope of this kind for arbitrary functions.

If `d=limsup r_X loglog X/log X<infinity`, choose the fixed cutoff constant `M>2(B+A)/nu` and `T²=M log X`. Then

    (1+M log X)^(r_X/2) <= X^(d/2+epsilon)

eventually for every epsilon>0, while the tail is `O(X^-A)`. Hence an every-epsilon bound `N_(r_X)(X)<<X^(eta+epsilon)` on **every sufficiently large dyadic shell**, with constants independent of X, gives

    ||F||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) << X^(eta+d/2+epsilon).      (R4)

The division by the fixed positive minimum of `g_kappa` on `[0,log2]` costs only a constant. The kernel parameters, source, B and buffers are fixed before X; r may move as stated. Good subsequences or a finite screen are insufficient.

The converse is correctly proved at the **unshifted** exponent eta: since `N_r<=||W_X||_2`, decompose the v-line into intervals `[k log2,(k+1)log2]`. The shell moment assumption controls the field there at scale `X2^k`; the summation over k is finite after Gaussian weighting. For small scales x<=1,

    |F(x)| <= C exp(-(log x)²/(2tau)),

because `(log n-log x)² >= (log n)²+(log x)²` and the remaining weighted coefficient sum is finite by C_B. Compact scales are handled by normal convergence. Thus there is no missing left-tail or shifted-shell assumption. This proves the stated equivalence when `d=0`. For positive d, the report supplies only R4 and that unshifted converse; it proves neither a shifted equivalence nor sharpness of the loss on actual arithmetic sources.

### Exact scalar and zero return

The Gamma integral yields, for r>0,

    E_(r,nu)(z)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity
       q^(r-1)e^-q g_(2(nu+q))(z)dq,
    E_(0,nu)(z)=g_(2nu)(z).

Its Fourier multiplier is exactly `e^(-nu*t²)(1+t²)^-r`, with the `(2pi)^-1` inversion factor already in the Gaussian. Consequently

    N_r² = sum_(n,m) a(n)conj(a(m)) b_n b_m
               E_(r,nu)(alpha log(n/m)).               (R5)

The double series converges absolutely since `E(z)<=E(0)<=g_(2nu)(0)` and `sum |a|b<infinity`. All ordered pairs, powers and natural character zeros remain. E is positive, but this does not make the coefficient products nonnegative or authorize removal of negative cross terms. For bounded coefficients the true diagonal is `O(X)` uniformly in r; divisor-bounded coefficients permit the stated epsilon allowance. The diagonal can be paid below `X^(2eta)` only with the corresponding eta>1/2 buffer; positivity is not a substitute for cancellation at smaller eta.

For `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)` the character twist is pointwise. The symbol `*` in later coefficient identities denotes Dirichlet convolution. Mellin Fubini first on Re s>1 gives

    integral_0^infinity F(x)x^-s dx/x = e^(tau*s²/2)/L(s,chi).

R4 plus dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz gives absolute locally uniform Mellin convergence on `Re s>gamma=eta+d/2`; the small-x Gaussian bound handles zero. Multiplying the meromorphic identity by L excludes any zero in that half-plane. A principal pole at 1 is handled by the usual cancelling zero of the reciprocal, not treated as an L-zero. This proof covers arbitrarily large finite heights without requiring an unproved uniform reciprocal growth estimate on a continued line. No X-dependent source was Mellin transformed.

For the literal f3 twist, an explicit scope check is useful. Its prime-power values are `f3(p^j)=-1` for p!=3,j>=1, and `f3(3^j)=1`. With `z_p=chi(p)p^-s`, the numerator in `D_(f3 chi)=W_chi/L(s,chi)` is

    W_chi = (1-2z_2)/[(1-z_2)²(1-z_3)²]
               product_(p>=5) (1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)².        (R6)

Zero-extended ramified factors mean z_p=0. The p>=5 product converges normally and is nonzero for Re s>1/2; the p2 factor can have zeros on Re s=1, not in `1/2<Re s<1`. Thus the paid f3 return is valid in the open target strip, with the already known right boundary retained. One must not claim that W_chi is nonzero everywhere on the line Re s=1. This qualification agrees with the established G28/G53 source returns and requires no modification to A's useful claim.

For the original ideal Möbius coefficient, the analogous Mellin identity has numerator 1 and its own Hecke L-function. A separately proved full ideal moment is required; an ordinary f3 estimate does not imply it. Fixed ordinary characters and the originally specified fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke family are the available scopes. No angular, growing-conductor, or generic-character uniformity follows from notation alone.

**Verdict A:** accept R1–R6 and A1–13/A10 as a conditional analytic interface. The exact complete R5/A13 arithmetic bound remains open. Fixed-order negative norms and Gaussian spectral localization are prior; the useful increment here is the exact localized source, arbitrary moving order and explicit `d/2` budget, not a new negative-norm mechanism or a proved weaker arithmetic exponent. The Sol01 S45 norm was on a raw finite atomic measure over the full line; it is not this already smoothed and localized norm.

## 4. Complete norm proof and continuous margin

Multiplication by `phi_u(q)^2`, or by either h phase, is a contraction of the positive row Hilbert norm. Apply Minkowski first to R6 and then to both exact R7 expansions. Bound the first ordinary inverse trivially and the second by R4:

    |M_u(E1;W1)|<<H_J E1^(1/2),
    ||M^(q)(D1/x)M^(q)(D2/x)Qslots||_U
      <<H_J U^(v/2+epsilon)(D1/x)^(1/2)
                         [U+U^(1/6)(D2/x)^(5/6)]^(1/2).         (R9)

The trivial bound holds uniformly on nonempty subunit scales by their fixed lower support bound. The restored scales only decrease, so R8 bounds both h sums. The q-sum has its full cost:

    sum_(Nq in [X,2X]) |a_G(q)|/(Nq) << X^epsilon.

This follows from linear ideal counting and the divisor bound. The shortened factors in R9 then decrease by fixed positive powers of X. The dyadic tail from G is geometric, proving R1 including every q and every slot collision. It is not an unpriced normalized average over q or h, and no joint arithmetic independence is used.

At `G=U^(1/5)`, `s-1/5>=28/25>1`, so the long-inverse branch dominates. Its exponent is

    Egcd=v+r+5s/6-1/5.

On the whole closed coarse box,

    T-Egcd >=rho+(delta-1)r+(delta-5/6)s+1/5-v
            >=rho+(47/20)delta-393/200
            >=2809/273000 >1/100.                              (R10)

Both width coefficients are negative, so upper r,s and upper v are the worst case. The derivative of the middle expression is `47/20-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]`, positive on the entire delta interval; hence its minimum is at 17/25. Independently, `60(5-2delta)^2` times that derivative is the polynomial `2525-2820delta+564delta^2`. Its exact Bernstein coefficients on `[17/25,7/10]` are

    542621/625, 105958/125, 20684/25,

all strictly positive. This is a continuous certificate, not a sample grid. The excess over 1/100 is `79/273000`.

For an explicit conservative loss ledger, reserve at most 1/1000 for the cumulative exponent change from fixed geometric pads, and at most 1/500 for all new subpower, internal-height, fixed-derivative and witness-signal losses combined. After retaining margin 1/200, R10 still has reserve `5/2184>0`. Endpoint pads are chosen small enough for the first aggregate bound by continuity on a compact box. The number of auxiliary losses is fixed; choose their individual epsilons and the internal height power after their finite orders are known. This ledger applies to this new source estimate. G147's smaller existing counting margin 1/2000 retains its own separately chosen loss allocation.

On an actual witness, `|B|^2>=U^[delta(r+s)-eta]`. Where `|B_{>=G}|>=|B|/2`, positivity, R1 and the above allocation bound the original weighted slot mass by `U^[E_K-1/200+epsilon]`. No division by a possibly zero slot product occurs. On the other rows, `|B_{<G}|>=|B|/2` by the triangle inequality. Alternatively

    ||BQslots||^2<=2||B_{<G}Qslots||^2+2||B_{>=G}Qslots||^2.     (R11)

This latter implication handles all low/high cross terms once the complete small-gcd norm is bounded. It does not independently save each cross term before that missing bound exists.

## 7. Protected critic audit S22: complete scattering return on native H

This audit was selected before outcomes for its potential to pay the entire far-gap operator and its complementary channels. Here is an exact realization and its inverse cost, without replacing H by the ordinary-character source.

### Literal source contract

Use the Eisenstein field's original primary, fixed-ray, six-unit and fixed bad-place conventions. Long prime ideals pi,pi' occupy the original windows, have distinct rational norms, and exclude both equal-norm orientations. Retain both ordered good squarefree rationally primitive short ideals g,g', including g=g', the actual bounded complex core h((g,g')), and the rational gcd screen on their norms. The native coefficient is

    a_H(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3.

Every term keeps the original phases/profiles/masks, both projectors 1_(P,Rg)=1 and 1_(P',Rg')=1, and both independent separating heights. Put v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'); each root occurs once, ||v||^2=Omega1 and ||w||^2=Omega2. With the entire signed short-source sum folded into the scalar matrix K, set T=K^transpose so that the literal finite packet is H=w^*Tv. No positive divisor child replaces the common core. No extra opposite-coprimality screen is inserted.

The raw target is B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), where

    B0=G K0 [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] P_orig.

K0 denotes the original K scale, and P_orig retains the original kernel coefficients and weighted profile seminorms. The physical outside N^(-1)G^(-2) is applied exactly once afterward. The original range/collision restrictions and every other physical branch remain obligations. The following finite identities are uniform in the entries, so apply at each pair of heights; an arithmetic bound must still have the required uniform constants.

### Cayley realization, reflected state and residual

For any r>0, even without r>=||T||, set A=[[0,T^*],[T,0]]. Its Cayley transform C_r=(A-irI)(A+irI)^(-1) is unitary because A is self-adjoint. Writing G0=T^*T, D=(G0+r^2I)^(-1), its input-reflection and input-to-output blocks are

    R=(G0-r^2I)D,  J=-2ir T D,
    R=R^*, R^2+J^*J=I, I-R=2r^2D.

The exact returned input is x=(I-R)^(-1)v. Direct substitution gives

    Tv=ir Jx,
    ||Tv||^2=r^2(||x||^2-||Rx||^2)
             =r^2(2Re<x,v>-||v||^2).                          (R13)

The inner product is conjugate-first. Thus global ||T||<=r is equivalent to R<=0. At the actual v, ||Tv||<=r||v|| is equivalent to Re<x,v><=||v||^2. The latter is a sufficient condition for the raw bilinear bound against every w of its allowed mass; it is stronger than controlling one particular scalar pairing. At r=B0>0 it returns the desired raw target exactly. The degenerate B0=0 requires the zero pairing directly.

This is a finite source-preserving identity, not an arithmetic estimate for x. On a singular mode of T with singular value sigma,

    R=(sigma^2-r^2)/(sigma^2+r^2),

    (I-R)^(-1)=(sigma^2+r^2)/(2r^2).

For sigma much larger than r, transmission is small while the inverse grows quadratically. Hence unitary scattering or small J alone cannot imply a small original T.     |H|<=[r/2+B^2/(2r)] ||v|| ||w||,

Optimizing r merely recovers the known B bound. It creates no improvement.

For an approximate returned state xhat define d=v-(I-R)xhat. The COMPLETE scalar is

    H=ir w^*J xhat+w^*T d.                                    (R14)

No favorable truncated scattering term controls the original form without its residual channel. This explicit formula also governs a proposed iterative or blockwise implementation; the source-sensitive error must be paid in the actual native T.

beta_U(d) and Lambda(e)/log N, with its exact prime support and
cutoffs; the bounded factor log N/log(q_de) stays in the profile.
Define the linear block, with n=de retained as the original label,
by

    V_(R,g) = sum_P u(P)/sqrt(q_P) 1_(P,Rg)=1
              sum_(d~D,e~E) c(d)b(e)a(d)a(e)
                 chi_d(e)^4 chi_R(de)^3 chi_P(de)^4
                 C(de) 1_(de,g)=1 1_(de,bar(g))=1.   (D1)

All original good/ray/deletion restrictions remain, and
xi(g)A(g)chi_R(g)^3 is applied on the outside, including its zero
at (R,g)>1. Natural character zeros impose the
required coprimalities; no inverse is used at a zero. Fixed ray
conditions on de can be separated by their finite characters.
Original norm heights split as (q_d q_e)^(it) on each side, with
the two heights still independent. C(de) has the actual product
endpoints, not a substituted window on e or on a new mark.

For an exactly separable normalized norm profile put

    T(D,E;L)=min{S(E,LD), S(D,LE)}.

Then for EACH original R,g, including their collisions,

    |V_(R,g)|^2 << Z^epsilon N T(D,E;L) Omega.        (D2)

The same bound holds with the original smooth common-profile
seminorm and a subpower logarithmic factor for its sharp product
endpoints. This uniformity is justified below; no rapidly
oscillating additive product phase is included in this assertion.
In contrast to JPS24, D2 does not assert uniformity for an arbitrary
additional bounded function of n. Its scope is the actual separated
smooth norm profiles, sharp product intervals and independent norm
heights just specified.

Proof of D2. First use the orientation t=P d. The surviving
chi_P(d)^4 forces (P,d)=1, so t is a squarefree ideal. Put

    A_(R,g)(t)=sum_(P d=t) u(P)/sqrt(q_P) c(d)a(d)
                       chi_R(d)^3 chi_P(d)^4
                       1_(P,Rg)=1
                       1_(d,g bar(g))=1,              (D3)

retaining the actual P,d supports, fixed deletions and their
separable profile factors. The remaining e coefficient is
b(e)a(e)chi_R(e)^3 1_(e,g bar(g))=1 with its original support.
Because chi_P(e)^4 chi_d(e)^4=chi_t(e)^4, the exact inner sum in
D1 is sum_e B(e) sum_t A(t)chi_t(e)^4. The character zero at
(e,t)>1 includes both the original (e,P) and (e,d) exclusions.
The original projector (P,Rg)=1 is still inside A; no residual
coprimality was inserted or removed. In particular this proof
does not require an incomplete Delta expansion.

For each t there are at most tau(t) pairs P,d. Thus

    sum_t |A_(R,g)(t)|^2
       << Z^epsilon sum_P |u(P)|^2/q_P sum_(d~D)|c(d)|^2
       << Z^epsilon D Omega.                         (D4)

The mark root in D3 is STILL q_P^(-1/2). Replacing it by
q_t^(-1/2) changes the original form; its compensating factor
q_d^(1/2) is exactly what restores the D in the mass bound D4.
The mark-side coefficient is not being asserted to satisfy the
original H contract at the new t length.

Cauchy in e and the squarefree-IDEAL cubic sieve, with its actual
exponent 4 character, give

    |V_(R,g)|^2
      <= (sum_e |B(e)|^2) sum_e |sum_t A(t)chi_t(e)^4|^2
      << Z^epsilon E S(E,LD) D Omega.

Even reciprocity gives chi_d(e)^4=chi_e(d)^4 in the fixed source
conventions. Reversing d,e therefore proves the other orientation
S(D,LE). All unit, angular and native Gauss factors were kept until
the displayed norm. The proof actually allows any source-only
divisor-bounded c,b, so the actual Lambda coefficients are covered.
No ordinary Hecke or scalar cuspidal replacement has occurred.

Here the original label remains n=de everywhere in D1. This is an
upstream bilinear calculation with R fixed; it does not perform a
quadratic Cauchy step on a shortened n and does not apply the
original cubic mark theorem C1 at length E. Its new cubic input is
proved directly with the transformed coefficient and mass D4.
That distinction is necessary to respect the original H contract.

**Product endpoints.** For a bound A on the integer norm q_de,
first evaluate its exact strict/non-strict convention on integers.
There is a smooth cutoff in x=log(q_de/N), agreeing with the
resulting indicator on EVERY attainable integer norm, whose
transition is centered between the two adjacent integers and has
width comparable to 1/N. On the fixed annular x support its Fourier
transform is bounded by

    O(min(1, |t|^(-1), N |t|^(-2))).

This follows respectively from its L1 bound, its derivative's L1
bound O(1), and its second derivative's L1 bound O(N), by integration
by parts. Its Fourier L1 norm is O(log(2N)). Each Fourier component
is q_d^(it)q_e^(it) times a unit scalar; D4 and the cubic sieve are
uniform in t. Lower and upper cuts, and the original smooth
profile, are treated together or by a fixed number of products.
Only logarithmic factors are lost. The existing common-profile
integral is then paid with its original seminorms and height mass.
This is not an AG12 contour shift with a hidden high-derivative
cost; the sieve bound here is uniform for every unit norm height.

**The additive-phase objection.** The cyclic phase used by JPS to
impose a far mask is exp(2 pi i ell q_d q_e/M). It does NOT in
general split into a d factor and an e factor. Its cross ratio on
(d_1,d_2) and (e_1,e_2) is

    exp(2 pi i ell (q_d1-q_d2)(q_e1-q_e2)/M).          (D5)

For ideal norms 7,13 and 19,31, ell=1, M=1031, the cross ratio is
exp(2 pi i 72/1031), not 1. All four products are squarefree and
M exceeds twice their norm range. Thus multiplying D1 by that
phase cannot be waved through D3 as independent coefficients.
This is an explicit algebraic failure of that proposed adapter.
These finite labels test the claimed factorization identity; they
are not claimed to lie in every frozen ray or deletion set.

The exact far mask can nevertheless be paid by subtracting its
ENTIRE near band after the bilinear estimate, at a stated cost.
Let C_(D,E;D',E')^far[h] denote the literal ordered covariance of
two D1 blocks with DE,D'E' comparable to N and the two original
mark arrays. Then

    |C_(D,E;D',E')^far[h]|
      << Z^epsilon K G^2 N
          [sqrt(T(D,E;L) T(D',E';L))+(H0+1)L]
                      sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.   (D6)

For the complete covariance before the gap, invert the original
short core h((g,g'))=sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f), |r_h(f)|<=tau(f).
At f there are O(G/q_f) possible original g values. Triangle in
that linear vector, D2, and Cauchy between the two independent
arrays give K (G/q_f)^2 N sqrt(T T') sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2).
The original row norm contains O(K) ideals; its exact sharp row
window and bounded normalized weight have not been extended by a
new row theorem. Sum f using sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2<infinity (or the
permitted subpower loss). The original xi(g), finite signs, all
perpendicular masks, and fixed squarefree/rational-primitive
restrictions remain in every child until this positive estimate.

For the near band regroup each block at ORIGINAL n=de. Its source
coefficient is divisor-bounded and its native factor is a(n).
The number of ideals of integer norm m is at most tau(m), by the
two-prime factorization law in this quadratic field. Therefore
there are O(Z^epsilon N(H0+1)) pairs with |q_n-q_n'|<=H0.
Cauchy on the exact original mark sum gives pointwise squared
mass at most O(L Omega_i), with its root q_P^(-1/2). Count O(K)
rows and O(G^2) short pairs and use |h|<=1. This bounds the near
band by the second term of D6. It includes BOTH equal-norm
orientations, not just n=n'. Subtracting this entire band gives
the original strict far condition. There is no signed-form
monotonicity step and no unsupported near-prime theorem applied
to the auxiliary composites.

D6 is therefore an exact, restricted covariance bound with its
common core, marks, endpoints and gap paid. The complete scalar
return of this bound multiplies by N^(-1)G^(-2), exactly as before;
the introduced bilinear indices do not create an extra physical
normalization. C2 remains a second bound on the same piece after
regrouping its divisor-bounded coefficient at n, so the smaller
of these two available bounds may be used for that piece.

**Pressure calculation and failure.** For every factor split DE=N,
both alternatives in T contain the term (NL)^(2/3). The best
balanced choice for the first orientation has E=LD, namely
D=sqrt(N/L), E=sqrt(NL), giving T of order (NL)^(2/3) for NL>=1.
The best certificate supplied by D6 consequently has, relative to
the desired raw GKN scale, the sizes

    G(NL)^(2/3),             G(H0+1)L.                (D7)

At the frozen pressure point their exponents are respectively

    .673880911641069319333...,  .221813789153867993...

The mixed cubic term is already much worse than the incumbent's
.004 deficit; compared to that incumbent its surplus exponent is
.669880911641069319333.... This is a lower bound on this PARTICULAR
positive certificate, not on the true covariance. Even free
near-band removal would not repair it. Restrictions imposed by
U,V can only make the optimized D7 certificate worse, not better.

For perspective the bound is a real arithmetic improvement over
the old G^2 N^2 term in the different range
K L^(2/3)<N^(1/3) with the near term also smaller. It does not pay
GKN there and it does not apply that different range to the frozen
pressure point. The mark absorption puts the mark-count cost
inside S(E,LD). In the mixed-term range it saves L^(1/3) against
estimating each mark separately; it does not remove every L cost.
That saving is insufficient here. The unit Type-I block D=1,
E~N has T~N in the actual L range and also remains unpaid.

This ends the tested bilinear route: two cutoff choices cannot
repair a mixed cubic term independent of those choices. An
improvement must retain joint row cancellation before the K row
count or exploit the signed I/II covariance before separate
positive estimates. Neither has been proved in this draft.

Even a hypothetical removal of the cubic sieve's mixed term would
leave min{E+LD,D+LE}>=2sqrt(NL), up to fixed dyadic constants.
After the same row count and short-source triangle the target ratio
would still be at least of certificate size G sqrt(NL), exponent
.5056606837308019895 at the pressure point. Thus replacing just
that cubic sieve constant by its conjectured two linear terms
cannot fix this particular argument. This is again a statement
about the argument's cost, not a lower bound for its true sum.
