# [private research revision]: countable detector banks and their endpoint return

The accepted written constant stays c10=3128649/25000000=.12514596.
G109 removes an unsupported way to improve it: a fixed positive summable
bank of scale differences has no uniform lower frame bound on its common
critical line, even after discarding every bounded height interval.
The exact buffered constant, its boundary law and a corrected endpoint
return survive. The latter permits gamma=beta in an every-epsilon
arithmetic hypothesis; it does not assert an inverse at the exact line.

This accepts the [Sol High author](sol04/report.md), [shared Sol High
review](sol-review/report.md) and [independent Astra Max
review](astra-review/report.md) at the scopes below. Their complete
proofs are in the three support files. All ordinary characters are fixed
in each estimate and retain their natural zero extension. A family result
requires one common exponent, while constants and onset may depend on chi.
No actual improved signed moment, new c, literature priority or formal
kernel result is claimed. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot
uniformity and external root-definition/import/admission remain OPEN.

## G109. Fixed countable banks, exact buffering and the complete source

Let lambda_j>1, w_j>0 and 0<W=sum_j w_j<infinity be fixed. Write
ell_j=log(lambda_j), r_j=exp(-delta ell_j), for delta>=0, and

    F_delta(t)=sum_j w_j |1-r_j exp(-it ell_j)|^2,
    A(delta)=sum_j w_j (1-r_j)^2.

Both sums converge uniformly in real t by domination with 4w_j. Exactly

    F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      =2 sum_j w_j r_j (1-cos(t ell_j)) >=0.             (75.1)

For any finite head of length r and integers H,L>=1, divide the unit
r-torus into H^r boxes. Two of the H^r+1 points nL(ell_1,...,ell_r)/(2pi)
modulo1 lie in the same box. Their difference gives t=Lq with
L<=t<=L H^r and distance(t ell_j/(2pi),Z)<=1/H for every j<=r.
Consequently, uniformly for delta>=0,

    0<=F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      <=4pi^2 W_head/H^2+4W_tail.                      (75.2)

Given any fixed T>=0, first take L>=max(1,ceil(T)), then a sufficiently
small full tail and sufficiently large H. Equations75.1-2 prove

    inf_(t>=T) F_delta(t)=A(delta).                    (75.3)

This uses no independence assumption on the logarithms. It keeps every
channel and never changes character to manufacture adverse phases. The
principal character modulo1 already defeats a shortcut required for all
ordinary characters. Arbitrarily prescribed complex target phases on
related scales are outside this identity-target recurrence proof. The
large bound L H^r gives no useful arithmetic power estimate in height.

At delta=0 the infimum is zero. At delta>0 it is positive and also equals
F_delta(0). Dominated convergence gives A(delta)->0 as delta decreases
to zero. Furthermore,

    A(delta)/delta^2 -> sum_j w_j (log lambda_j)^2,

where the limit may be +infinity. For a finite second log moment use
dominated convergence; otherwise arbitrarily large finite partial moments
force the liminf to infinity. Summability alone does not supply a finite
quadratic coefficient or a universal decay rate. For lambda_j=2^j,
w_j=2^-j, j>=1, the exact checks are A(1)=10/21 and second log moment
6(log2)^2.

On the global space L2(R_+,x^(-2sigma) dx/x), put sigma=beta+delta and
D_j V(x)=V(x)-lambda_j^beta V(x/lambda_j). The unitary logarithmic change
f(u)=exp(-sigma u)V(exp u), Tonelli and Plancherel give

    sum_j w_j ||D_j V||_global^2 >= A(delta)||V||_global^2.

Continuity of the uniformly convergent symbol and localized Fourier
packets show sharpness, also near arbitrarily high near-minimizers.
These are unrestricted test functions, not arithmetic sources. A single
point frequency is not a nonzero L2 extremizer. The theorem is not an
exact constant for a joint physical-shell norm, nor for a sum of separate
shell suprema. Those distinctions from G52/Sol03 remain essential.

### Formation is paid for the actual Gaussian source

Fix tau>0 and the normalized Gaussian g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)
exp(-v^2/(2tau)). Let

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), U(y)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/y)).

For any A>max(1,beta), the elementary bound |a(n)|<=1 proves for all y>0

    |U(y)|<=C_A y^A,
    C_A=zeta(A)(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(tau A^2/2).

Indeed n^A g_tau(log(n/y)) is at most y^A times the supremum of
exp(Av)g_tau(v), and sum_n n^-A=zeta(A). Hence |D_j U(x)|<=2C_A x^A
uniformly in j, since lambda_j^(beta-A)<=1. In particular

    sum_(j>r) w_j |D_j U(x)|^2 <=4C_A^2 x^(2A) W_tail.

The entire bank is therefore well defined locally and on every finite
shell, with its complete tail paid. This closes the source-formation
qualification in the shared review. It supplies only an exponent A>1;
the desired subtrivial arithmetic moment remains OPEN.

### Endpoint correction: gamma=beta is admissible

Suppose the COMPLETE bank obeys, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently
large dyadic X,

    sum_j w_j integral_X^(2X) |D_j U(x)|^2 dx/x
      =O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(2gamma+epsilon)),
    0<gamma<1, beta<=gamma.                            (75.4)

Choose one fixed channel with positive weight. For every sigma>gamma,
choose epsilon<2(sigma-gamma). Dyadic covering, finite initial shells
and the preceding all-y bound give its finite N_sigma norm, where
N_sigma(V)=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||V||_[X,2X]. Since sigma>beta, its causal
inverse converges geometrically, with cost

    w_j^(-1/2)/(1-lambda_j^(beta-sigma)).

The K-th telescoping remainder is lambda_j^((K+1)beta)
U(x/lambda_j^(K+1)), bounded by C_A x^A
lambda_j^(-(K+1)(A-beta)); it tends to zero. Thus (75.4) returns the
same every-epsilon exponent gamma for U, INCLUDING gamma=beta.
The inverse constant may diverge as sigma approaches beta; that is
permitted in an every-epsilon conclusion. No inverse at sigma=beta is
asserted. This corrects the shared review's unnecessarily strict beta<gamma.

The direct Mellin check gives the same result: the numerator of this
channel is (1-lambda_j^(beta-s)) exp(tau s^2/2), which has no zero in
Re(s)>gamma when gamma>=beta. Its transform is holomorphic there under
the complete shell hypothesis and the paid left tail, so the reciprocal-L
identity excludes every zero in that half-plane. For gamma<beta one
channel leaves numerator zeros on Re(s)=beta. Two multiplicatively
independent scales leave a possible simple real zero at beta; the existing
G47 exception must still be addressed. No automatic stronger family
theorem follows.

The live alternatives outside the obstruction are height-dependent or
nonsummable banks, different critical lines, signed cross-channel forms,
and estimates restricted to the actual arithmetic source. Each owes its
own definition, complete costs and zero-exclusion return. Chaining or
simultaneous use remains eligible when it supplies actual new arithmetic
control; additional fixed positive channels alone supply no critical gap.

## Preserved interfaces and scoped audits

These are useful exact contracts and corrections, not new arithmetic
savings or claims of novelty over their recorded ancestry.

**D12, full logarithmic primitive.** Put
B(x)=sum_(n<=x) a(n) log(x/n)=integral_1^x M(t)dt/t, zero below1.
Its Mellin transform is 1/(s^2 L(s,chi)) for Re(s)>1. A complete
dyadic B energy O(X^(2gamma+epsilon)), 0<gamma<1, makes that transform
and every fixed derivative holomorphic in Re(s)>gamma by shell
Cauchy-Schwarz and locally uniform summation. The meromorphic identity
s^2 L H=1 excludes all zeros there. It retains imprimitive factors and
the principal pole; no conductor-uniform constants are assumed.

In logarithmic variables b''=sum_n a(n)delta_log(n), INCLUDING the n=1
atom. The Gaussian return is U(exp v)=integral b(u)g_tau''(u-v)du, with
both integrations by parts and tails paid. Its complete weighted kernel
cost is at most exp(tau sigma^2/2)(sigma^2+2/tau). Hence no loss in
gamma is required for zero exclusion. The separate pointwise sharp
finite-difference route B=O(x^beta) -> M=O(x^((beta+1)/2)) is valid but
unnecessary for this purpose. The differential-kernel mechanism is
standard [restricted research revision] ancestry; its original rational coefficient source differs.
No improved B estimate is supplied.

**D22, exact prime operator and its actual source.** For finite
unramified P, product_(p in P)(I-chi(p)D_p)1_(x>=1) equals
sum_(d|product P,d<=x) mu(d)chi(d). With every unramified prime<=N it
is M(x) throughout x<=N; N>=2X pays a full physical shell. Ramified
factors are identity. No fixed Mellin identity is assigned to a moving P.

For coefficient shifts S_p e_n=p^-sigma e_(pn) with the cutoff pn<=N,
each T_p=I-chi(p)S_p is unit triangular. Its determinant1 gives no
contraction. A two-state singular value is (sqrt(4+r^2)+r)/2>1,
r=p^-sigma. On a full tensor box 0<=k_p<=K, coefficients
product_p(-chi(p))^k_p give the projected squared ratio

    product_(p in P) [1+K(1+p^-sigma)^2]/(K+1).

The finite witness requires N>=(product P)^K. Letting K tend to
infinity for FIXED P proves the infinite coefficient-space norm
product_p(1+p^-sigma); it does not assign that limit to a growing finite
matrix. For 0<sigma<=1 the product diverges as P grows, but this is not
a specified power of N or an obstruction to every affordable restricted
moving-prime regime. The actual e1 column has bounded weighted l2 norm
for sigma>1/2, while its sharp readout costs X^(sigma+1/2)>X.
Neither unrestricted witness lower-bounds the actual signed Mertens sum.
The independent complex chi mod5 box check gives 451/162. Pair02/W38
are direct ancestry; the all-power f3 source of G69 is different.

**S09, true prefixes commute.** Truncated shifts V_p,V_q both map e_n
to e_(pqn) exactly when pqn<=N; both intermediate indices then fit.
They commute for every N. The non-divisor-closed mask {1,2,6} can fail
commutation, but it omits the real n=3 source and must restore that
complement. This does not exclude every other projected construction.

**S38, ordinary trace is not the sharp readout.** For N>=pX,

    [P_X,chi(p)V_p]e_n
      =-chi(p)1_(X/p<n<=X)e_(pn).

This strictly raises indices, so its product on either side with any
finite Dirichlet-convolution matrix has ordinary trace zero. Inserting
the exact inverse-convolution matrix does not create a Mertens detector.
The actual coordinate sum on the coefficient source is instead
-chi(p)[M(X)-M(X/p)]. With quartic chi mod5, p=2,X=4,N=8, it equals1
while the trace is0. A complete signed difference bound at exponent
gamma>0 would return M by telescoping with cost1/(1-p^-gamma); that
window estimate is unpaid. Adjoints, noncausal operators or a different
trace are eligible only with their full new identity and costs.

Other preserved tests include the correct prime recurrence
M=R_p-chi(p)R_p(./p) and its full inverse; finite absolute Euler prices
do not uniformly bound an infinite bank for gamma<=1. The one-prime
weighted topological trace 1-chi(p) is not an ordinary chain-map trace
unless the weight commutes with the boundary. The principal scalar uses
minus the REDUCED Euler characteristic, including the empty face.
Unrestricted Gaussian Gram bounds cost X^2 and do not lower-bound
the signed arithmetic energy. All are scoped, with their live escapes
retained; no untested card is relabeled impossible.

## Calibration, allocation and evidence

For complete ordinary-character B/U energy or a valid bank with beta<=gamma,
first gain requires gamma<.87485404, hence limiting energy exponent
below1.74970808. Targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 would give respectively
c=.12515,1/6,1/4 if their COMPLETE arithmetic inputs were proved. None is
proved here. These raw energies are not the normalized PR9 local moment.

All60 author cards and probabilities survive: ten first tests
01/12/22/31/16/58/43/54/51/26; three developments12/22/43;
50 author-untested cards. The author reserved01/12,22/31,51 and used
literal all-group numerical pools for five immutable draws. Seed and
pool commitments preceded entropy. Shared priority order34/38/41/36/17/46
was frozen before author conclusions. Its optional uniform attempt
failed a size assertion before persistence/view; no completed uniform
commitment or replacement draw is claimed. Astra priorities followed
author outcomes but preceded shared conclusions; its later protected38
and uniform09 audits were selected after both outcomes and are not blind.
48 cards remain outside author tests and those two critic audits.

The author's countable extension and boundary law, Sol's uniform
finite-head estimate and infinite-moment extension, and Astra's source
formation proof and endpoint correction receive distinct credit.
The three reports total 77575 bytes; their support files total40195
bytes. These byte counts describe review material, not tokens, latency,
cost or measured cache use.

This is the fourth comparable accepted post-[private research revision] Sol batch, the FIRST
since the [private research revision] reassessment. It offers a useful obstruction and a
review-derived prerequisite removal, mostly alongside duplicate interfaces;
it proves no new arithmetic exponent. Keep the smaller Sol High lane
and selective actual-source Sol Max policy. This one batch does not trigger
the three-further-batch reassessment or DSPy. No extra Sol batch is
allocated on the W54 pass while endpoint/W52/headroom intake occupies
the controller. The Astra lane continues. DeepSeek/Grok remain inactive
under their exact unresolved gates, not a model-quality judgment.

The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds41 byte-preserved
research files and all43 original file/manifest pins. Two files containing
host-local claim snapshots remain in their original ignored locations;
their mathematical artifact lists and hashes are preserved without
copying claims. All three owners stopped and released their own scopes.
Root read every report and support in full. Finite checks verify signs,
cutoffs and formulas only; the written arguments carry the infinite claims.
The full29-family/109-child portfolio and all historical baselines survive.

## 6. Both opposite-column masks and the residual core coprimality

In the exact DC7 expression, write
\[
c=su,\qquad e=rv,\qquad r\mid e,\quad s\mid c.
\]
The exact restrictions become
\[
(r,s)=(\ell,rs)=1,\qquad
(u,rs\ell)=(v,rs\ell)=1,\qquad (u,v)=1.
\]
The condition `(ell,rs)=1` comes from the original `(ell,ce)=1` and
is retained here; it can be dropped only in the positive outer bound
at (BC16). All these variables are squarefree where forced by their
core factorizations. There is no own-column exclusion. The signs obey
\[
\mu(c)\mu(e)\mu(r)\mu(s)=\mu(u)\mu(v).
\tag{BC14}
\]
Retain the outside phases
`xi(r) bar xi(s) chi_mathfrak_n,u0(s) bar chi_mathfrak_n,u0(r)`
before bounding their magnitudes by one.

Open `(u,v)=1` with its complete Möbius projector and write the common
divisor in a projector term as `g`. The residual sums run separately
over `u/g` and `v/g`; their natural zeros and masks at `rs ell g`
are retained. Apply (BC13) to both. The outside `g^(2h)` and the two
rescaled lengths leave
\[
\sum_gq_g^{-2b+O(\delta)}\ll1,
\tag{BC15}
\]
because `b>1/2` and the preliminary loss is sufficiently small. With
fixed component twists, the extra `g` phase has modulus at most one.

This is an actual coprimality expansion of the coefficient-specific
Möbius product. It does not require a new Hecke moment assumption.

# Gao's local moment and the new accepted analytic endpoint

Controller disposition,11October2026: **accept the written analytic proof,
relative to the pinned PR9 framework, of c_G=0.1251134**. Equivalently,
theta_G=4374433/5000000=.8748866 is a zero-free boundary: Re(s)>theta_G
for every finite-order Hecke L-function of trivial infinite type over
Q(sqrt(-3)), and every ordinary Dirichlet L-function, including zeta.
The principal pole at1 is excluded. This is an open half-plane statement;

The advance is **Zhongpai Gao's, with AI assistance**, from

# W67: signed boundary reconstruction and its actual price

The useful output is a set of exact reconstruction identities and scoped obstructions. No new arithmetic power saving, zero-free constant, native Hecke estimate or public-record claim is established. The accepted source-relative c remains .1251459636, with its stated ancestry and admission obligations. Three developments below retain S02, the protected high-ceiling S27, and the rare draw S24. S11, S15 and wildcard S21 receive distinct first tests. The serious upstream tests concern the signed source representation itself, before falling back to finite diagnostics.

The fourth stream failure left only the original final author window. The mathematical derivations and saved checks below are retained; further asymptotic development is explicitly incomplete. No deadline was reset and no frozen sample was replayed.

## 1. Frozen experiment and source scope

The initial 30 cards were frozen before detailed history intake at 00:19:54 UTC, in initial-seeds.json, SHA256 a25fea116a0371f6f457dd320930342de36103bf2303259e735367f2b4b195b9. Root received only that path/hash for blind preparation. The complete maintained attempt index was subsequently read. Relevant exact contracts include G105, G121, G68, G175, G189 and the Gaussian G25-G29 source. All seed cards, including the incoherent entropy-only S30 and its explicit alternative, remain unchanged.

Deliberate choices S02/S27/S15 and eight explicit duplicate exclusions were frozen before OS entropy. Every threshold pool covered all six groups. The complete pool sizes were 18,10,17; accepted independent bytes db/7e/1d selected S11/S24/S21. There were no rejected bytes, empty strata or rerolls. The first pool includes eligible rare cards from uncapped groups; the wildcard includes every eligible remaining card regardless of p. sampling-receipt.json SHA256 0d2e133d65b2ce77abf150ffa6fc5e60c4ee5ff46b85b0acf7beb47d175ddc6d binds the originals. p means generation typicality only.

The controller expressly corrected the assignment's retained wild66 transcription errors: sole writer wild67, reserved review wild67-review. Original assignment bytes/hash remain intact. W66 was untouched. Root owns the only final critic wake after the older review backlog and W67 blind preparation.

These are three different arithmetic objects. The ordinary Liouville core G189 has a=lambda*chi, including shared primes, and MUST NOT acquire a squarefree/coprimality zero from this report. The Gaussian coprime source G25 really has mu(d)mu(e)1_((d,e)=1,(de,6)=1). The inverse-matrix source below is a newly specified finite ordinary-character representation of the full Mertens sum; its own return is proved, rather than borrowed from G189 or the native Hecke source.

## 2. D1 / S02: an exact inverse exposes what the boundary must reconstruct

Fix N>=1 and an ordinary character chi modulo q. Let S={a<=N:mu(a)!=0,(a,q)=1}, ordered increasingly and including1. This is divisor closed. Put E_(a,d)=1_(d|a), M=diag(mu(a)). Elementary divisor inversion gives

    E^(-1)=M E M.

Indeed its (a,b) entry in the product is the sum of mu(d/b) over b|d|a, equal to delta_(a,b). Define the coprimality matrix C and its signed version K by

    C_(a,b)=1_((a,b)=1)=sum_(d|a,d|b)mu(d),
    C=E M E^T,             K=M C M=(mu(ab))_(a,b).

Every shared-prime zero is literal. Since E is triangular with unit diagonal, C and K are invertible of full rank |S| and determinant product_(a in S)mu(a). Their real inertia is the number of positive and negative mu(a), by congruence. In particular their signature equals sum_(a in S)mu(a); this is an identity, not an estimate for that sum.

The COMPLETE inverse of K is especially revealing:

    (K^(-1))_(a,b)=sum_(d in S; lcm(a,b)|d)mu(d).          (1)

Proof: invert M E M E^T M and substitute E^(-1)=M E M; the result is E^T M E. Thus (K^(-1))_(1,1) is the full principal-character Mertens sum with precisely the q zeros. This is an actual arithmetic inverse, not an arbitrary-matrix counterexample. At N=2,q=1 it is zero although K is invertible; the nuisance block indexed by a>1 is zero. Therefore eliminating that block by an assumed invertible Schur complement already fails in an actual smallest source.

For a general character the simple phase gauge diag(chi(a)) K diag(chi(a)) does NOT put the twisted Mertens sum in its (1,1) inverse entry: that entry stays the untwisted sum. A different ambient matrix is required. Define

    A_chi=E diag(mu(d)conj(chi(d))) E^T,
    (A_chi)_(a,b)=product_(p|(a,b))(1-conj(chi(p))).

Only unramified squarefree labels occur; hence every diagonal factor inverted has modulus1. Exact inversion gives

    (A_chi^(-1))_(a,b)
      =mu(a)mu(b) sum_(d in S; lcm(a,b)|d)mu(d)chi(d),
    (A_chi^(-1))_(1,1)=M_chi(N):=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n).   (2)

This twisted matrix has changed local entries: it is not the original coprimality projector when chi(p)!=1. In particular it is generally complex symmetric, not Hermitian. No Hermitian inertia or positivity assertion is made for it.

Here is its quantitative bridge. If for every fixed chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, one common 0<gamma<1 satisfies

    integral_1^X |(A_(chi,floor t)^(-1))_(1,1)|^2 dt/t
       <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon),              (3)

then ordinary L(s,chi) is zero free in Re(s)>gamma, with the principal pole at1 permitted. By (2) this is exactly the G103 complete Mertens-energy hypothesis. On each dyadic shell Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the integral of |M_chi(t)|t^(-sigma)dt/t by O(X^(gamma-sigma+epsilon)); summing proves locally uniform holomorphy for sigma>gamma, with derivatives. Initially on sigma>1,

    1/L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt.

Continuation of the product with L gives the conclusion at every finite height. Constants may depend on the fixed character. This includes natural imprimitive zeros; it asserts no growing-conductor estimate. First gain needs gamma<.8748540364; gamma=5/6 and3/4 give the prospective1/6 and1/4 targets. Equation (3) is wholly OPEN and is exactly as difficult as that scalar energy, not a new proof.

Two cautions distinguish exact memory from useful approximation. On m distinct unramified prime labels, K=J_m-I_m, so its rank is m and singular values are m-1,1,...,1 (m>=2). Yet the rank-one approximation J_m has error operator norm1. For arbitrary boundary vectors u,v its omitted scalar is -u^T v, bounded by ||u||_2||v||_2. Thus a large exact state count does NOT rule out a useful paid approximation; the diagonal correction may be inexpensive. This is a genuine escape from an overstated rank obstruction.

On a complete k-prime divisor cube, the unsigned local gate B=[[1,1],[1,0]] has eigenvalues phi and -1/phi, phi=(1+sqrt5)/2. Tensoring gives eigenvalues (-1)^j phi^(k-2j), multiplicity binomial(k,j), all nonzero. The signed gate is T=D B D, D=diag(1,-1), so its singular values agree exactly. This local spectrum was already recorded in W01/W09. The useful addition here is the full divisor-closed inverse (1)-(2), the corrected twisted construction, and the explicit distinction between exact rank and scalar residual cost. No literature priority is claimed; classical divisor inversion and Redheffer-type matrix representations are ancestors. Vaughan's primary paper documents a different determinant representation and does not supply a bound for (3): https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf .

## 3. D2 / S27: the collective dual transform retains the whole mask

This protected high-ceiling mechanism remains an exact open target after a decisive failure of the cheap version. Use the actual principal Gaussian coprime source, not a changed Liouville source. Fix tau>0, Y=floor(X^.495), and B_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)), with fixed C>0. Index a Boolean cube by ALL primes 5<=p<=B_X. Let d(u)=product p^(u_p) and write

    K(u,v)=(-1)^(|u|+|v|)1_(u&v=0),
    W_x(u,v)=1_(d(u)>Y,d(v)>Y,d(u)d(v)<=B_X)
       *sum_(1<=l<=B_X/(d(u)d(v))) (-1)^(l+1)
                   g_tau(log(d(u)d(v)l/x)).

The finite scalar Z_X(x)=sum_(u,v)K(u,v)W_x(u,v) is precisely the output-truncated G25 source. The prime2,3 exclusion, both strict cuts, repeated-factor zeros, ordered copies, alternating cofactor, exact product cap and every boundary are retained. Impossible cube states have W=0; the full cube is an algebraic ambient space, not an asserted efficient algorithm.

For k cube sites use the UNNORMALIZED Walsh transform in both variables:

    hat F(a,b)=sum_(u,v)(-1)^(a.u+b.v)F(u,v).

Finite character orthogonality proves the exact collective identity

    Z_X(x)=2^(-2k)sum_(a,b)hat K(a,b)hat W_x(a,b).         (4)

No conjugation is required because the Walsh matrix is real and the original contraction is bilinear; the identity remains valid for complex W. Locally H T H=[[-1,1],[1,3]], H=[[1,1],[1,-1]]. Hence hat K is the tensor product of this FULL local matrix. Changing basis has made the three-entry coprimality gate into four nonzero entries. The signs survive; there is no sparse-dual saving from the gate alone. Any sparse support must be proved for the complete transformed arithmetic W, whose product cutoff couples the sites.

The bridge has explicit complements. The original d3 output-tail majorant gives, uniformly for x in[X,2X],

    |P_Y(x)-Z_X(x)| <= X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).            (5)

This bounds the actual omitted labels de*l>B_X, not an independently chosen mask. Choose C so that the exponent in(5) is strictly below a fixed gamma>1/2. G27 separately pays P_Y-F6 at X^(.495+delta), with delta small enough. G28's two fixed Euler convolution inverses have absolute weighted sums finite for every fixed sigma>1/2; they transfer all-shell F6 and G_tau norms in both directions. Their separate prime2,3 factors and each shell's frozen Y remain mandatory. Thus a full all-shell L2 bound of the signed RIGHT SIDE OF(4) by X^(gamma+epsilon) would return the original Gaussian G3 and zeta zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. It gives no ordinary-character or Hecke result without an additional source-specific extension. The new transform is not assigned an independent Mellin transform as X changes.

The remaining arithmetic hypothesis is the complete signed sum in(4), including both copies when squaring. Replacing it by the sum of absolute terms, estimating only a favorable dual block, or interpreting cube sites as independent arithmetic variables does not establish that hypothesis. The number of cube sites is enormous; the expression is not a computational saving by itself.

A useful retained boundary condition is therefore: supply a family of dual coefficients or compressed states and prove BOTH its whole signed output estimate and the entire omitted signed field norm below gamma. This is a concrete mechanism change with a paid projection back, but no such arithmetic family has been found here. G68 already owns a different biased-Walsh degree truncation with paid CRT error; G121 owns cutoff rectangle rank. Neither licenses deletion of modes in(4). G175 already contains the parity-syndrome blindness example, so that example is not recounted as a new result.

## 4. D3 / S24: a lossless ambient system must pay scale and defect return

For any finite operator A, an exact representation A=alpha P U Q with U unitary and P,Q contractions necessarily has alpha>=||A||. Conversely, alpha=||A|| is achievable by the standard Halmos dilation of C=A/alpha (the zero operator is trivial):

    U_C=[[C,(I-CC*)^(1/2)],[(I-C*C)^(1/2),-C*]],
    P U_C Q=C.                                         (6)

The intertwining C(I-C*C)^(1/2)=(I-CC*)^(1/2)C makes block multiplication prove unitarity. This is standard, not a new dilation theorem; Robinson's primary manuscript gives the construction: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.09329 , Theorems1-2. The application is that the least possible contractive projection normalization is exactly the original operator norm, not an omitted constant. For the actual k-prime coprimality cube it is phi^k. Character diagonal unitary gauges preserve that singular-value cost; ramified zero sites must be removed, not inverted.

A second, different loss arises if one recycles the same finite ambient system. If C is selfadjoint, D=(I-C^2)^(1/2), then U_C=[[C,D],[D,-C]] satisfies U_C^2=I. Therefore

    P U_C^2 Q=I,             C^2=I-D^2.                 (7)

The returned defect channel D^2 is exactly the missing difference. The one-step dilation does NOT preserve powers. In a multiscale interpretation, either keep the full returning defect, insert intermediate physical projections, or construct a genuine power dilation. A fresh-ancilla realization of a product retains the product of all original normalizations; saying that each enlarged step is unitary does not remove it. These statements concern the proposed architecture, not a claim that every larger-system method fails.

For an approximate reconstruction A_tilde with ||A-A_tilde||<=delta, the complete scalar boundary error obeys

    |u* (A-A_tilde)v|<=delta||u||_2||v||_2.              (8)

For a general coefficient/mask matrix W the alternative complete bound is |tr((A-A_tilde)W)|<=||A-A_tilde||_F||W||_F. In either case the ACTUAL W contains all source masks and phases; a low-rank factorization of one gate alone does not estimate W. A source-restricted estimate could be much cheaper and remains eligible. Equations(6)-(8) give a constructive finite representation with its full error budget, but no new detector power.

This rare draw is retained as a useful repair condition. The next substantive step would be an actual source-specific boundary alignment or a cancellation estimate for the entire returning defect channel. Merely refining a one-step unitary realization has no arithmetic benefit. G175's native Cayley work and the earlier indefinite-observer contracts retain their separate source ancestry.

## 5. Other first tests, including the wildcard

S11 (p<.10 draw): for the literal local gate, T=D B D. Thus the signed gate and its absolute gate have the SAME spectral radius phi and singular values. The hoped-for local spectral-radius improvement is absent already for the principal arithmetic signs. A signed scalar may still cancel through its boundary vector. General nonnormality is not needed to make this narrower diagnosis.

S15 (most different): the exact real symmetric matrix J=[[-2,-1],[-1,2]] obeys T^T J T=-J. Thus alternating the boundary metric gives a conserved indefinite flux; T^2 is J-unitary. But v=(phi,-1) has v^T J v=0 and T^(2m)v=phi^(2m)v. The first-coordinate observation grows without bound while flux is zero. A positive observed norm therefore needs a proved bound on admissible states relative to the null cone. This is a toy transfer built from the actual local gate, not a construction of an arithmetic source state following that growing trajectory. The broad Krein-space warning already appears in W29 and the Sol pilot; only this explicit gate/metric is supplied here.

S21 (uniform wildcard): for ANY finite selfadjoint K, including the real coprime matrix above, its Cayley transform V=(K-iI)(K+iI)^(-1) is unitary, and

    K=i(I+V)(I-V)^(-1),
    (I-V)^(-1)=(I-iK)/2,
    ||(I-V)^(-1)||=sqrt(1+||K||^2)/2.                   (9)

The inverse projection restores the full large-eigenvalue bill. Unitarity by itself supplies no smaller norm. For the complex twisted A_chi of(2), selfadjointness is absent and the assertion that this Cayley transform is unitary is not licensed. A holomorphic family needs its own spectral/contour justification. This wildcard survives only as the explicit inverse-error obligation in a larger realization; it is not an analytic-continuation proof.

## 6. All 30 dispositions and ancestry

Tested/developed: S02 D1; S27 D2 (protected high ceiling, exact return OPEN); S24 D3 (protected rare draw). Tested: S11 signed-gauge failure; S15 indefinite-flux failure without observability; S21 Cayley inverse bill. None is a new arithmetic power estimate.

Screened before entropy, retained as duplicates at the specified first-test scope: S03 proper-marginal parity (W36/W38/G175); S04 generic Schur (U-VARIATIONAL/G108/G163); S05 square-species identity (G176-G178); S06 collective determinant (D3/Hankel); S10 triangular compensation (G92/G105/G108); S23 Hankel reconstruction (G135/G149); S25 generic Jordan warning (U-VARIATIONAL); S30 entropy-only draw and full-phase alternative (U-FILTRATION/W36). statement:
## 2. D1 / S01: fully paid reduction to a hard-prime off-diagonal form

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including principal and imprimitive characters. Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with all squareful and nonunit zeros literal. Fix tau>0 independently of scale, and write

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1) a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=exp(-gamma y)U(y).

For every fixed real y all sums and derivatives below converge absolutely. The coefficient majorants are at most powers of log n times a Gaussian. For y<=0, U and each fixed derivative have a polynomial times Gaussian bound. No old cancellation premise is needed for these facts.

### 2.1 Exact equation and energy, with no deleted prime powers

Coefficientwise Dirichlet convolution gives

    a(n)log n = -sum_(d|n) a(n/d)chi(d)Lambda(d).

This follows by differentiating a*chi=delta, or by checking each prime exponent. At a squareful n the terms with the last two p-powers cancel; deleting those terms would change the source. Since tau U'(y)+yU(y)=sum a(n)log n g(log n-y), the EXACT equation is

    tau U'(y)+yU(y)+K_1 U(y)+K_2 U(y)=0,                 (1)
    K_1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K_2 U=sum_p sum_(j>=2)chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

Ramified terms vanish. This specializes the existing Gaussian commutator/renewal ancestry; it is not credited as a new identity. In z coordinates, each delay d has coefficient chi(d)Lambda(d)d^-gamma. For R>=0, multiply (1) by exp(-2gamma y)conjugate(U(y)), take real parts and integrate:

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)
      +I_R+tau*gamma*E_R = Q_1(R)+Q_2(R),              (2)
    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Q_j(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(K_j,gamma z)(y)dy.

All boundary terms and signs are retained. There is no finite-height restriction.

### 2.2 Every higher prime power is relatively bounded

For gamma>1/2,

    C_gamma=sum_p sum_(j>=2)log p*p^(-j gamma)
       <=[1/(1-2^-gamma)]sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2gamma)<infinity. (3)

Translation by j log p on the causal half-line has norm1 after the displayed weight. Extend z by zero above R, retaining its entire past. Young's inequality, or Minkowski followed by Cauchy, gives

    |Q_2(R)|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z(y)|^2dy.

The negative half-line integral is finite unconditionally. For every eta>0, splitting the positive integral at a fixed sufficiently large Y yields

    |Q_2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_(eta,gamma,tau),                (4)

uniformly in R. The finite B uses only unconditional bounds for U on a fixed bounded interval and its Gaussian left tail. No unknown right-tail norm enters B. Character dependence is allowed, although the crude majorant need not use it.

### 2.3 A moving small-prime sector is also fully paid

Choose A>0 with alpha=A(1-gamma)<1 and split K_1 at

    p<=(2+y)^A for y>=0; the hard sector has p>(2+y)^A. (5)

The threshold is real, with equality in the small sector. Write Q_small and Q_hard for the exact corresponding pieces of Q_1. For sufficiently large y, A log(2+y)<=y/2. Thus every small-prime delay v=y-log p has y/2<=v<=y. Its weighted row sum is bounded by

    sum_(p<=(2+y)^A)log p*p^-gamma
      <=C_(A,gamma)(2+y)^alpha log(2+y).                (6)

This deliberately coarse estimate sums over ALL integers. For a column v from that large-y region, y<=2v, so the same bound holds with p<=(2+2v)^A and a changed fixed constant. Apply 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, sum and change variables in the second term. Since (2+v)^alpha log(2+v)=o(v), for every eta>0

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_(eta,A,gamma,tau),           (7)

uniformly in R. The bounded initial y region has finitely many primes and input v in a fixed interval, so its full bill is part of B. The upper endpoint y<=R implies v<=R; no future values of z or unpriced transfer occur. This is a quadratic-form relative bound on the actual delayed source, not an operator contraction on arbitrary growing functions.

### 2.4 The exact hard-prime same-output diagonal costs only a constant

Expand the full hard-prime integrand BEFORE taking absolute values:

    Q_hard(R)=-Re int_0^R exp(-2gamma y)
      sum_(p>(2+y)^A)sum_(m,n>=1)
       conjugate(a(n))*chi(p)*a(m)*log p
       g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y)dy.                       (8)

There is no cutoff of m or n. The n=pm terms are nonzero only for squarefree q-units pm, so p does not divide m and

    -conjugate(a(pm))*chi(p)*a(m)=|a(m)|^2=1.

The exact diagonal D_R is therefore nonnegative. At a fixed squarefree n, its retained prime log-weights sum to at most log n. The whole-line Gaussian integral is exact:

    int_(-infinity)^infinity exp(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
       =exp(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi tau)).

Consequently, for gamma>1/2,

    0<=D_R<=B_diag
      =exp(tau gamma^2)/(2sqrt(pi tau))
         *sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2gamma)<infinity.         (9)

Natural zeros only lower this positive majorant. Define H_R=Q_hard(R)-D_R: it is precisely (8) restricted to n!=pm. All p,m,n signs and phases remain inside H_R. This same-output diagonal is different from deleting a signed subset of a completed physical form.

### 2.5 Complete criterion and quantitative zero return

**Proposition, conditional arithmetic input.** Fix one common gamma in(1/2,1), and A>0 satisfying A(1-gamma)<1. Suppose that for every fixed ordinary chi there are delta_chi>0 and B_chi<infinity such that, for all sufficiently large R,

    H_R <= (1-delta_chi) I_R+B_chi.                    (OPEN-PF)

Then every L(s,chi) has no ordinary zero with Re s>gamma. Constants and onsets may depend on chi; the common gamma does not.

Proof: choose eta=delta_chi/4 separately in(4),(7); absorb the bounded initial R range. Insert (9) and OPEN-PF into(2). For every R>=0,

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R
       +tau*gamma*E_R<=B'_chi.                         (10)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma y)) for y>=0. The left Gaussian tail and this right bound make F(s)=int_(-infinity)^infinity U(y)exp(-sy)dy holomorphic on Re s>gamma, including all compact-uniform derivatives. Absolute Fubini on Re s>1 gives

    F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Continue L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2). Its right side is never zero. At every regular zero of L in the half-plane the left side would vanish. The principal pole at1 is allowed and forces F to vanish there; imprimitive Euler factors were already retained through chi's natural zeros. All complex heights and all zero multiplicities are covered. The ordinary continuation, pole and imprimitive-factor conventions were checked against [NIST DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15), specifically25.15.1-4. This is a replacement source's complete return, with no borrowed native-H projectors, no unsmoothing and no fixed-height gap.

|Desired c|gamma|One allowed A|alpha=A(1-gamma)|Status|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
|.12515|.87485|7|.87605|Conditional gain .0000040364 over c11|
|1/6|5/6|5|5/6|Conditional|
|1/4|3/4|3|3/4|Conditional|
|.4999|.5001|1|.4999|Conditional high ceiling; gamma=1/2 is NOT covered|

The strongest objection is substantive: OPEN-PF is an unproved signed source-specific inequality. The full logarithmic equation lets its negative hard-prime correlation carry an entire hypothetical bad mode, so the identity alone cannot supply strict delta. A deliberately coarse trial does not close it. Even GRANTING an input |U(y)|<=C exp(beta y) for y>=0, gamma<beta<1, triangle and the full Gaussian left tail only give sum_p log p|U(y-log p)|<=C exp(y)(1+y). For p<=exp(y), sum over all integers p^-beta log p; for p>exp(y), use the Gaussian left tail and split into fixed log intervals. Thus the absolute flux budget has exponent1+beta-2gamma in R, whereas the available I_R budget has exponent2beta-2gamma up to logarithms. The unresolved exponent gap is1-beta. This is failure of that upper-bound trial, not a lower bound on the signed flux; the granted U input is not silently inferred from a bare zero-free assertion. The near,1/6 and1/4 targets therefore receive no arithmetic credit from the coarse test.

The proposition is an explicit localization of that gap, with actual complete paid sectors, not a proof of a new exponent or a claim that the remaining estimate is easy. W35 owns the Gaussian renewal sign; G79 owns general drift ideas; G118 owns the full logarithmic source identity. The incremental claim is the combined relative payment(4),(7),(9) and the exact prime-only off-diagonal criterion. Novelty elsewhere in the record or literature is not asserted beyond the inspected sources.

### 3.2 The weighted norm and small-index objection

For k>=rH, every shift j in Q_r lies below rH<=k. Write v=log(k/X), b=log((k+j)/k)+log(X/x), so |b|<=ell. Then

    f_x(k+j)^2 / w_X(k)
      =(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp((-3v^2/4-2bv-b^2)/tau)
      <=(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp(3ell^2/tau) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)).

The underlying difference after replacing ell^2 by b^2 is (v/2+2b)^2>=0. This directly verifies the exponent and constant, rather than invoking an unpriced change of Gaussian width. The unimodal sum satisfies

    sum_(k>=1) exp(-log(k/X)^2/(2*tau)) <= K_tau X.

Its integral is X sqrt(2*pi*tau)exp(tau/2), and comparison to the integral costs at most 2. The absolute coefficient sum of Q_r and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz now give the first term of (R1):

    (1/H) sqrt(sum |B_H|^2 w_X) sqrt(sum |psi|^2/w_X)
       <= C_(tau,r) sqrt(X E/H).

For 1<=k<rH, the preceding ratio estimate is not available uniformly. Instead |B_H(k)|<=H, every test argument is <2rH<=X<=x, and the Gaussian is monotone there. Summing at most rH indices gives exactly the last term of (R1). This pays the strongest inverse-weight objection; applying the large-index ratio everywhere would be invalid.

### A1. Original signed recurrence

For t>=1 and y>=1, define

    R_chi(t,y)=sum_(n<=t, P^-(n)>y) mu(n)chi(n),

with P^-(1)=infinity. Partition every squarefree n>1 by its least prime p; its remaining factor has all primes strictly greater than p. This proves the finite identity

    R_chi(t,y)=1-sum_(y<p<=t) chi(p)R_chi(t/p,p).             (A1)

All primes dividing q have coefficient zero. The n=1 term is essential; repeated-prime states are excluded by strict increase rather than by silently changing mu. If t<=y, R=1. In particular M_chi(x)=R_chi(x,1). This is the classical signed least-prime partition, with U-FUGACITY/RN/G81 ancestry; ordering by least rather than largest prime is not itself a new cancellation theorem.

Let F(t,y) be any proposed approximation on the finite state set reachable from one root (x,1). Its **actual recurrence defect** is

    Delta(t,y)=F(t,y)-1+sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)F(t/p,p).           (A2)

Writing E=F-R gives E=Delta-T E, where T is the displayed increasing-prime transition. Each path terminates, and expanding the finite triangular inverse gives exactly

    E(x,1)=sum_(d<=x) mu(d)chi(d)
                  Delta(x/d,P^+(d)),  P^+(1):=1.           (A3)

Indeed a path consists of a uniquely ordered list p1<...<pk, d=p1...pk; its transition sign is (-1)^k=mu(d). Distinct squarefree products give distinct x/d and hence distinct reached states. Every partial product is <=d<=x, so no additional hidden path constraint occurs. There are no missing boundary, squareful or ramified terms. A3 is a complete signed scalar, not a sum of independently estimated depth magnitudes.

The thirteen collision types are the pairs(a,b) with a+b>=2. Let h_ab be the squarefree ideal formed from primes of that type. All h_ab are pairwise coprime and their complete original-site incidences remain attached. Define

    Lc=product h_ab^a, Rc=product h_ab^b,
    L=N(Lc), R=N(Rc), D=LR,
    k=product_(a!=b)h_ab, Kc=N(k),
    E=product_(a=b>=1)h_ab, Hcol=product h_ab.

Every actual pair is uniquely n=Lc*x, n'=Rc*y, where x,y are squarefree, mutually coprime, and prime to Hcol. Their primes occur in exactly one original site. The nonunique sector is exactly Hcol!=1. The six gcd cuts depend only on these actual collision ideals and their site incidences, not on residual singleton primes.

On every row, including conductor primes,

    chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e)
       =psi_k(u) chi_x(u)^e conjugate(chi_y(u)^e)
                                                 1_((u,E)=1),
    psi_k=product_(a!=b)chi_p^(e(a-b)).                       (2)

The nonzero exponent e(a-b) lies in{+/-1,+/-2,+/-3}. It has order6,3 or2 and is nonprincipal primitive at that good prime. Equal positive valuations cancel phase but preserve the unit indicator. Thus the primitive good conductor is kxy, while E is a genuine canceled-phase hole. The fixed nu factors stay in the source coefficients; they are not assumed to have order six.

The full relative principal case kxy=1 forces x=y=1 and all collision valuations equal, hence n=n'. Conversely the complete merged diagonal has that form, up to the retained fixed unit/ray conventions. Its row cost is O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)) using c_abs. Pay it before invoking zero frequency vanishing. A fixed ray expansion may have nontrivial fixed-place pieces; this does not erase the whole diagonal payment or remove any original principal/inducing family.

The support bounds used later are valid:

    N(h20),N(h02) << G P0;   N(h11)<<N0;
    N(h11^(ij))<Hij.                                        (3)

For the first, write a column d1=gx,d2=gy with squarefree pairwise-coprime g,x,y and squarefree slot product P. Its defect n/rad(n) equals g times a divisor of P, hence is <C G P0. A type(2,0) prime divides the left defect and type(0,2) the right. For the second, h11 divides both original merged columns. For the last, the indicated type(1,1) prime set divides the ORIGINAL inverse gcd on edge ij. Strict original endpoints and fixed annular constants remain; relaxing a positive majorant to a closed upper support is harmless.

## 3. Large plain square divisors, including their complete intersection

Define A_H(k) by(8) with H in place of G. Since k|s_2(b) iff k^2|b,

    1_(N s_2(b)>=H)=sum_(k^2|b) A_H(k).                 (13)

Unlike the gcd divisor q, k need NOT be squarefree. Define the actual plain
part S_bad(D) with this indicator. Multiplicativity gives

 S_bad(D)=sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi_u(k^2)/(Nk)
                         S_u(D/(Nk)^2).

Using(2) BEFORE triangle and ideal counting afterwards yields the uniform
pointwise bound on the same buffered rows

    |S_bad(D)| << H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2) H^(-beta).
                                                               (14)

All prime powers, equality at H, terminal nonempty scales and fixed holes remain.
Consequently ||M S_bad Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)H^(-2beta).
This alone does NOT license deleting the intersection with B_g from a signed
source. We pay that intersection next.

Let B_gs restrict to BOTH N(a,b)>=G and N s_2(b)>=H. Expand(8),(13) simultaneously.
For squarefree q, put L=[q,k^2]=q k^2/(q,k). Then a=qc,b=Ld, and EXACTLY

 B_gs(u)=sum_(q sf,k;Nq>=G,Nk>=H)
    A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi_u(qL)/(Nq NL)^(1/2)
                    M_u^(q)(R/Nq) S_u(D/NL).           (15)

This formula includes q/k intersections of every valuation. It is not obtained
by incorrectly replacing lcm(q,k^2) by qk^2. Restore M^(q) by(10). The coefficient
mass left after(2),(3) is

 sum_(q,k) tau(qk)^(O(1)) (Nq)^(-1/2)(NL)^(-(1+beta)/2).

Primewise, put i=v_p(q) in{0,1}, j=v_p(k)>=0. Then
v_p(L)=max(i,2j)=i+2j-min(i,j). Thus its non-divisor weight equals
q^(-1-beta/2) k^(-1-beta) (q,k)^((1+beta)/2) in norm notation.
For i=1,j>=1 its local factor is exactly
(Np)^(-1/2-j(1+beta)); the shared prime is not counted twice.
For i=1,j=0 it is (Np)^(-1-beta/2), and for i=0 it is
(Np)^(-j(1+beta)). These exhaust all valuation cases, including holes.

Writing d=(q,k), k=de, and dropping only positive coprimality restrictions gives

 sum_(Nk>=H) (Nk)^(-1-beta) N(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
       << U^epsilon H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) (Nd)^((beta-1)/2)
       << U^epsilon H^(-beta) tau(q).                  (16)

For Nd<=H, sum the e tail from H/Nd. For Nd>H, its complete sum is bounded;
(Nd)^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)(Nd)^((beta-1)/2). Thus BOTH ranges satisfy(16).
The strict compact upper bound beta<1 is used, and all divisor losses fit the
arbitrarily small U^epsilon. Summing q then proves

    ||B_gs Q||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).
                                                               (17)

Finally B_s=M S_bad-B_gs. Hilbert triangle and G>=1 prove the second part of(5).
No signed subset monotonicity or independent signs have entered. The three
pieces in(4) are exhaustive, and every low/high cross term is paid by the
same Hilbert triangle when a complete norm is needed.

## Exact band consequences and limitations

For any fixed rho_plus>1/2, every coefficient of R_(X^rho_plus) has
n>X^(2rho_plus), so its full Gaussian field is O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A.
For fixed admissible kappa, X^rho_plus>kappa sqrt(X) eventually. Exact
coefficient subtraction, without using F or any full-field bound, gives

    T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X))
      =R_(kappa sqrt(X))-R_(X^rho_plus)
      =2x/L² Phi_tau(kappa²X/x)+O(X/L³)>0.                      (CT8)

This is a complete actual positive band of order X/L² derived using only
ordinary PNT and absolutely convergent core estimates. It is not a
pointwise-prime-jump sign assertion. It also differs from the negative
fixed-power-late-to-terminal band, which crosses this critical range.

Only if one separately uses the accepted full-field bound F=O(X^beta),
beta<1, does T_(kappa sqrt(X))=F-R acquire a negative leading term from
CT1. That prefix conclusion uses the accepted baseline; CT1 and CT8 do
not. Neither conclusion improves the full-field exponent or c. No
arbitrary mask, low-gcd subfamily, Hecke twist, or inherited convolution
transfer is claimed. The uncapped Gaussian and every prime power remain
in the source through the paid tails above.

STOP candidate writing after full readback and hash. Independent reviewer
must particularly challenge CT3 tail multiplicity, the second Stieltjes

## G110. The canonical amplitude-conditioned theorem

Fix the original canonical ray-character family, genuine good-prime pool,

and one physical high bin delta in[17/25,7/10]. The accepted [private research revision]
re-anchoring permits the witness presentation to differ from the original

Minkowski. Arbitrary MI coefficients or prime subsets are not thereby
admissible in MP. Both inverse and plain witnesses come from one actual
zero, at the same character, real part and height. Slot heights remain
independent. The physical bin supplies upper slot prices; a larger internal
height-box maximum is never substituted for that upper price.

Normalize the row width W to1 temporarily and write v=z/W<=1/20. Fix
positive squared-amplitude grades 0<=q_i<=delta with
sum_i q_i z_i<=qv, delta-.01<=q<=delta. This is a bound on positive
grades, not merely a product bound that lets tiny factors offset large
ones. Amplitude classes and one greedy original slot subset are fixed
before each class/dyad moment. One fractional-slot loss and all mesh,
height and profile losses are paid. No division by a possibly zero slot
is used. With witness cutoff t fixed before witnesses, the source gives
r<=t, r+m>=t, 0<=m<=1/2 and squared witnesses at least
Z^(delta r), Z^(delta m), up to preallocated small losses.

Partial inverse marking minimizes the actual amplified inverse moment
plus the full complementary slot price. Since 2x<=r for the permitted
marked width and r>=1/2, its third capacity term is dominated. The exact
piecewise bound is

    I(r)=1-delta r+q[v-(1-r)/2]_+    (r<=1),
    L(r)=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+qv        (r>=1),
    P(m)=1-2delta m+q[v-(1-2m)/(9/2)]_+.

The factor2 in the plain term is its fourth power. I and P decrease,
while L increases; I remains continuous through its kink. This removes
the previous nonbinding transition hump without adding a new moment
theorem. Bounded/zero plain witnesses use the old unrestricted no-slot
theorem; all finite dyads and derivative-profile pairs retain common
thresholds.

Put h_delta=5-2delta, e_delta=5-6delta and
D=135delta-54delta^2-20q. Balancing the short crossing against L(t)
gives the weighted-density exponent

    E_delta,q(W,z)=rho W+max(4delta q z/h_delta,-aW+bz),
    rho=1-10delta/(3h_delta),
    a=2delta q e_delta^2/(3h_delta D),
    b=3delta q(15+18delta-8q)/D.                         (76.1)

The switch is v0=2e_delta/(135-54delta-24q). The two cutoffs are
(5-6qv)/h_delta and
(135delta-20q-12delta q-108delta qv+24q^2v)/D.
Their short crossings are respectively2t/3 and
[(18delta-4q)t+2q-9qv]/(27delta-4q).
Eleven entire cleared polynomial inequalities, with194 positive rational
Bernstein coefficients, verify all denominators, cutoff/witness ranges,
inverse kink gates and a<1/500 on the FULL delta/omega/v box, where
omega=delta-q in[0,.01]. At q=delta this is exactly the previously
accepted nonlinear envelope, not an additional gain counted twice.

The first branch has partial_q E/W>=68v/91. On the second branch,
a'_q>0 and v>=v0 give partial_q E/(Wv)>=b'_q-a'_q/v0>=7/10;
its entire cleared numerator is among the positive certificates.
Continuity across the switch and integration prove

    E_delta,delta(W,z)-E_delta,delta-omega(W,z)
       >=(7/10)omega z,  0<=omega<=.01.                (76.2)

For raw w=u b^6 keep the actual root holes, freeze b and put
s=log_Z Nb, V=W-6s. The main range V>=20W/21 decays at rate
6(rho-a)-1>0. In the tail, the old unmarked density with the actual
conditioned slot price pays the entire gain<=3k(delta)z, where
k=rho+delta-1 and z<=W/21: rho-1/6-3k(.68)=818/61425>0.
Bounded free windows and fixed-inducing free cores retain their raw
population O(Z^(W/6+qz+small)); they are not declared finite raw sets.

The additional saving can be applied after the two transforms to their
positive child energies if each actual live list satisfies the condition.
For empty common support, trivial projectors and no clipping, both live

An original deficit is NOT transported through arbitrary signed mask
removal or discarded slots. No theorem here forces any such deficit.

The retained scalar extremizer shows only that the stated one-witness

statement:
### A whole-field replacement with every difference and tail paid

Let a(n) be ANY fixed complex sequence with |a(n)|<=1. Later take
a(n)=f3(n), or f3(n)chi(n) with its actual zero extension. For an
integer B>=1 define right-closed blocks ((j-1)B,jB], j>=1,

    b_B(j)=sum_((j-1)B<n<=jB)a(n),
    V_B(x)=sum_(j>=1)b_B(j)g_tau(log(jB/x)),
    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

All these infinite sums converge absolutely on compact x-ranges
by the Gaussian majorant; b_B(j) has modulus at most B. Put
k_x(t)=g_tau(log(t/x)), t>0. Its total variation on(0,infinity)
is exactly2g_tau(0). On one block,

    sum_(n in block)|k_x(n)-k_x(jB)|
       <= B integral_((j-1)B)^(jB)|k_x'(t)|dt.

Indeed every segment[n,jB] lies in the block and at most B
integer segments cover a point. At t=0 the Gaussian is flat and
has limit0, so the first block has no omitted endpoint. Summing
ALL blocks yields the uniform, coefficient-preserving bound

    |F_a(x)-V_B(x)|<=2B g_tau(0), x>0.                 (D48.2)

This prices every within-block signed detail, including the infinite
high-n tail, with no exceptional or unmatched class deleted. It is
not an estimate of a positive submask. Squaring afterwards retains
all ordered block interactions; norm triangle has paid both mixed
terms and the difference square at the field level.

For every parent dyadic X fix B_X=floor(X^theta),0<=theta<gamma,
and use that same B_X for ALL x in[X,2X]. D48.2 implies the exact
every-epsilon equivalence

    ||F_a||_[X,2X]<<X^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff ||V_(B_X)||_[X,2X]<<X^(gamma+epsilon).         (D48.3)

Use a smaller epsilon than gamma-theta. No Mellin continuation of
the MOVING block source is inferred; the fixed source is recovered
by D48.2 first. All n and their signs/zeros occur once in b_B.

For actual f3, B=2 makes the arithmetic coefficient explicit:

    b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)+(1-2*1_(2 not dividing j))f3(j).    (D48.4)

This preserves f3's valuation rule: multiplying by2 flips its sign
only if2 was absent. Thus even the pair source is not an independent
random-sign source or a squarefree source. With a fixed chi,
b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)chi(2j-1)+f3(2j)chi(2j); all ramified zeros remain.

There is also a direct fixed-B pole-preserving transform. Write
e_B(n)=B ceil(n/B) and initially on Re s>1 let

    D_B(s)=sum_(j>=1)b_B(j)(jB)^-s,
    E_B(s)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)[n^-s-e_B(n)^-s].             (D48.6)

Since0<=e_B(n)-n<B, the integral of the derivative of t^-s gives
|n^-s-e_B(n)^-s|<=|s|B n^(-Re s-1). Thus E_B converges absolutely
and locally normally on Re s>0, including fixed s-derivatives
(their extra log powers are summable). Coefficient rearrangement
on Re s>1 gives D_B=D_a-E_B. For fixed ordinary chi this becomes

    L(s,chi)D_B(s)=W_chi(s)-L(s,chi)E_B(s).           (D48.7)

If the fixed-B Gaussian block field has a complete moment exponent
gamma>.5, its Mellin transform continues D_B to Re s>gamma.
At a hypothetical L-zero rho there, D48.7's left side and its
second right term vanish, while W_chi(rho) does not. This proves
the direct fixed-B zero return; additive holomorphic error, rather
than an Euler-product guess, preserves the reciprocal poles. At
B=2 the source uses exactly b_2 from D48.4. Moving B_X still uses
D48.2--3 before continuation, so no changing transform is invented.

The pair difference sector alone is O_tau(1). Its complete signed
sum mode b_2 remains the entire arithmetic problem. Large B reduces
the number of block coordinates in a paid finite Gaussian window
to X^(1-theta+o(1)), but b_B(j) can be as large as B. No complexity
or amplitude reduction is asserted from coordinate count alone.

### 3.1 A uniform complete norm excludes all right-hand zeros

Assume

    K_(a,chi):=sup_(L>0)||Gamma_(a,L)|| < infinity.            (H)

The compatible forms extend from compactly supported functions to a bounded
bilinear form B_a on L2(R_+) by density. For Re(z)>0 put E_z(t)=exp(-zt). Its
squared norm is1/(2Re(z)). The map z->E_z is holomorphic into L2 on that
half-plane by exponential domination of every local derivative. Therefore
Q(z)=B_a(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic and

    |Q(z)| <= K_(a,chi)/(2Re(z)).                            (27.1)

Initially Re(a+z)>1, Fubini is absolute, and the line t+u=v has length v:

    Q(z)=integral_0^infinity v M(exp v)exp(-(a+z)v)dv
        =-d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))] at s=a+z.                  (27.2)

The last identity follows directly from Abel summation, including the n=1
atom, since integral_0^infinity M(exp v)exp(-s v)dv=1/(sL(s,chi)) for Re(s)>1.
Both sides of(27.2) are meromorphic on Re(s)>a, while the left side is
holomorphic. The identity theorem forces the derivative of1/(sL) to have no
pole there. Every L-zero of order m>=1 would give1/(sL) a pole of order m and
its derivative a pole of order m+1, since s!=0. Hence no such zero exists.
The principal pole at1 is a zero of1/(sL), not an obstruction. No primitive
replacement, conductor growth, or height supremum has been introduced.

For a common gamma, it is enough to prove(H) for every fixed chi and every
a>gamma (one may restrict to a countable decreasing sequence tending to gamma).
The constants may depend on a and chi. Each individual zero with Re(rho)>gamma
then lies to the right of one such a. This is an all-finite-height conclusion.
There is no need to control one inverse norm uniformly as a approaches gamma.

This resembles the earlier W29 Sobolev-Hankel pole gate but changes the object:
W29 uses the atomic folded coefficient form and a Sobolev metric; here one
ordinary logarithmic primitive is built into the KERNEL and the input norm is
plain L2. The two contracts must not be identified without a proved operator
comparison. Neither supplies a bound for the other from terminology alone.

# [private research revision]: paid detector overlap and consultation library

The user supplied three GPT6-Pro consultation files and asked whether the
detectors can help each other, both through transfers and simultaneous use.
The answer is yes at the analytic-interface level. Several exact bridges and
a complementary-numerator family are now available. Their missing arithmetic
estimates remain explicit. No consultation component increases the accepted
written **c5=7821/62500=.125136** from the separate
[affine-window argument](gao-affine-window-integration.md).
Its formalization and independent kernel replay remain pending. Original
PR9/Gao credit and fixed-family scope are unchanged.

The user's subsequent request to combine chaining and simultaneous use is
handled by the [hybrid construction](hybrid-detector-integration.md): retain
the phase vector through smoothing, split/recombine a2/3 filter bank with
explicit causal costs, and harvest bounds for fixed pieces in different
representations. Its new arithmetic input remains open.

The exact user files and extracted endpoint package are retained under the
[source manifest](../external/gpt6-pro-20261011/source-manifest.json).
The [Concrete review](expert-concrete-review/review.md) covers all219 numbered
tags in55 components; its [component index](expert-concrete-review/component-index.json)
also names three further developments. The
[merged review](expert-merged-review/report.md) and
[110-row map](expert-merged-review/component-index.json) cover all4912 source
lines. A source's claimed proof and our independently checked proof retain
different labels. The merged A/B originals and named supplements were absent;
we certify the supplied bytes, not the undocumented merge operation.
Embedded instructions are source content, not authority.

## 1. Transfers between fixed smoothers

For the SAME coefficient sequence a(n), write

    F_k(x) = sum_n a(n) k(log(n/x)),
    M_k(s) = integral_R k(u) exp(su) du.

The geometric compact kernel k_o is the convolution of uniform densities on
[-2^-j,2^-j], j>=1. The new compact kernel k_n uses normalized positive widths
asymptotic to1/[(j+1)log(j+1)^rho], rho=1+eta/4>1. Let g_tau be the fixed
Gaussian. Their Mellin multipliers are nonzero in Re(s)>0. Section4 of the
Concrete review proves

    F_new(x) = integral h_no(v) F_old(x exp(v)) dv,
    F_Gaussian(x) = integral h_gn(v) F_new(x exp(v)) dv,
    integral |h(v)| exp(gamma v) dv < infinity  (every fixed gamma>0).

The quotients are M_n/M_o and M_g/M_n, in that direction. The lower bounds
exp(-C log²(2+|t|)) and exp(-C(1+|t|)log(2+|t|)) for the two compact
multipliers, combined with the stronger decay in each numerator, justify
inversion and weighted integrability. All shifted shells and small-scale tails
are paid. Therefore complete dyadic norm estimates pass along

    geometric compact --> near-log compact --> Gaussian

without a loss of power, for each fixed positive growth exponent and its
epsilon buffers. The same argument applies to a Hilbert-valued coefficient
sequence with the corresponding polynomial coefficient-mass bound.

The opposite multiplier quotients are unbounded: Gaussian smoothing cannot
be undone as a bounded general weighted-L2 operation. For the actual ordinary
arithmetic field there is another, logically different route back: a complete
every-epsilon bound gives zero exclusion, buffered zero exclusion gives
polynomial reciprocal-zeta growth, and contour shifting gives a bound for a
different fixed kernel. This does not transfer a submask, local component,
conductor-uniform family, or an unproved Hecke numerator condition.

The merged review adds a bridge for the actual rational coefficient
A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2). If R(y)=F2(exp y), where
F2(x)=sum_(n<=x)A(n)(1-n/x)^2, then

    D(D+1)(D+2)R = 2 sum_n A(n) delta_(log n),
    G_tau(exp y) = [.5 D(D+1)(D+2)g_tau] * R(y).

The convolution kernel has every exponential L1 weight. Thus the Riesz field
also transfers to Gaussian with every shell/tail paid. This is not an
identification of the rational A(n) source with the different ideal-Mobius
source over Q(i).

## 2. What the new compact detector changes

The Concrete review's [restricted research revision]-C2 removes the old55-prime smooth-part selector
entirely. Keep the exact both-rough decomposition, the bounded product mask
independent of the restoration index, and its complete deletion error. With
Y=floor(X^.495), B=2e³X, the unpruned source is

    C_X(n)=sum_(de ell=n; d,e>Y) mu(d)mu(e)b(ell)P_X(d,e),  n<=B,
    Z_X(x)=sum_n C_X(n) k_n(log(n/x)).

On the complete physical interval [X/e,2eX], both sup and dyadic norm errors
are O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A. The decomposition has
O_eta(log X loglog X) rectangles; restoration requires only
O_eta(log X (loglog X)^(1+eta/2)) terms and heights
O_eta(log X (loglog X)^(1+eta)). Coefficient mass is at most
B(1+log B)^2. All ordered cross terms and both height tails remain.

This removes the old .87407 selector error floor, so this compact route has
no such obstruction to1/6 or1/4. Gaussian uses fewer bins/lower heights but
a larger exp(O(sqrt(log X))) restoration range; near-log compact has compact
physical support and a shorter restoration. Which exposes useful arithmetic
cancellation is still unknown. At line a=3/4 the current strict component
moment target is omega<.249728 with paid positive buffer. Targets1/6 and1/4
correspond to limiting omega=1/6 and0 respectively; the complete scalar norm
can be weaker than separate component bounds.

## 3. Simultaneous detectors can cover numerator zeros

The genuinely different simultaneous opportunity is the unprojected quartic
phase family over K=Q(i). For fixed excluded primes and a fixed bounded
positive-length interval I,

    F_t(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1+it) F_K(X/Nd²),
    Mellin(F_t)(s)=M(s)L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2)/zeta_K^S(s).

The squarefree part c and square part d need not be coprime. The denominator
is fixed, while the auxiliary numerator moves with t. Assuming the fixed
profile M is nonzero in the target half-plane, the full estimate

    integral_I ||F_t||_[X,2X]^2 dt <<_epsilon X^(2a+epsilon)

excludes every zero of zeta_K^S in Re(s)>a: at a hypothetical zero, the
L2(I)-valued numerator cannot vanish identically, by the identity theorem for
the fixed L-function. All multiplicities are covered. The original merged
profile was stipulated, not specified; choosing the geometric or reviewed
near-log profile supplies nonvanishing but requires the actual arithmetic
estimate for that profile. This is a Q(i), hence ordinary-zeta, return; it is
not automatically the project's whole fixed ordinary/Eisenstein-Hecke scope.

There is quantitative capture on any fixed compact height window using
m0=min_s max_t|N_s(t)|>0 and a derivative bound. There is no supplied numerical
all-height lower bound. For arithmetic energy, O_A(log X) positive Gauss
quadrature samples of the phase approximate the full fixed-I norm to any
X^-A error, since the phase bandwidth is O(log X). Their nodes move with X;
this is not a finite fixed list known to cover all zeros. The d,e crosses
inside each sampled energy remain fully present.

The overlap cost is decisive. Direct absolute transfer from F_K at exponent
a to F_t costs sum_(Nd<=sqrt X) Nd^(1-2a), losing X^(1-a) and leaving only X.
Attenuating by Nd^(-2tau) makes both the convolution and its Dirichlet inverse
bounded when **a+tau>1**, with constants at most zeta_K^S(2a+2tau-1).
At the current boundary this requires tau>.125136. This safe family is
equivalent to the original norm problem. The unattenuated family may have
better coupled source geometry, but its complete arithmetic estimate is open.

Projection can destroy the reason for using the family. At a good odd local
place, compact averaging with the first two source vectors fixed sends every
unary vector to its one-dimensional spherical projection. The resulting
phase family is A(t) times one vector with the SAME arithmetic L numerator;
A(t)=zeta_K^S(2-it)/zeta_K^S(2) is nonzero. Thus that projected family cannot
cover each other's numerator zeros. The unprojected family must be retained
through the needed estimate.

## 4. Other simultaneous returns already available

The [reviewed library](reviewed-library-integration.md) retains literal2/3
filtered f3 returns: their only possible common filter zero is the designated
real beta. Zeta has no real exceptional zero there; a general real character
can retain a simple exception. This is a qualitative return, not a uniform
all-height multiplier lower bound or an arithmetic gain.

The [wavelet review](headroom-b-review/report.md) supplies a quantitative
example. For the SAME source V and B_q(s)=(1-q^(1-s))/(s-1),

    |B_2|²+|B_3|² >= exp(-2|t|)/(4(1+|t|)²),

and a positive Gaussian width gap pays the inverse condition number with
cost4 exp(Delta+4/Delta). Equal widths do not give a bounded arbitrary-source
inverse. Independently fitted source lists are not the common V needed for
this identity. Full joint arithmetic capture remains open.

Stacking scalar smoothers of the same A does not create new numerator
coverage when each multiplier is already nonzero. A sum of positive energies
also does not cancel either energy. A mixed signed scalar readout may cancel,
but its cross terms and surviving numerator must be proved explicitly.

## 5. Further library components and exact reopening conditions

| Shifted rank-two finite-field kernel | Literal holes, local monodromy, homothety classification, fourth moments;1/40 bilinear saving at .4/.6 lengths. | Actual signed inverse/plain source, composite/nonunit complements, legal profiles and heights. |
| Balanced inert-prime estimate | Eisenstein lattice/extension-field transfer with1/2400 saving. Required repair excludes the at-most2ell zero-stalk values omitted by a direct FKMS import; each costs O(q²). | Complete source transfer; large residue characteristic and all support restrictions remain. |
| Weighted CRT fibers | Phi_r(alpha)=sum_a(sum_(d=a mod r)|alpha_d|)^2 yields the full independent signed local-pairing bound before worst-fiber replacement. | Prove favorable fibers for actual coefficients; arbitrary joint masks and principal factors are not included. |
| Inverse/plain stencils | Exact shifted-profile distinction, Poisson phase cancellation and UM-weighted remainder. | Direct local insertion needs delta>=3/8 at nominal JM, far beyond1/40; P19 signed term and all complements are open. |
| Fourier-fixed exterior vector | E(a)=a+Fourier(a)-(integral a)1_O; norm2||a||²-|integral a|²; radial uniqueness and arithmetic invisibility at finite stages. | BOTH coupled relative boundary germs with actual source intertwiners, then the moving restriction bound. Unary symmetry and small Hilbert residual do not pay it. |
| Centered Mayer operator | Exact block at a zeta zero; next feedback is an absolutely convergent triple mixed difference for Re(s)>0. | Exclude BOTH eigenvalues+1 and-1 at all heights Re(s)>a/2; Schur inverse and parabolic/complex-height costs must be paid. |
| Factorial flux | Full forward-cell energy, sharper first-cell inequality and exact allowed bad-time fraction. | Actual signed flux for every fixed power of8 and9; no density-model substitution. |
| Adaptive true-gcd | Contractive tail with finite head lengths1,2,4 for near,1/6,1/4 targets. | An actual arithmetic weight rule estimating the entire retained core. |
| Coherent hook model | Partial inverse/plain convolution equals one Schur hook; exact Haar norm is1 or0 according to partition length. | Fixed-order sextic monodromy, natural-zero/ray restrictions and number-field transfer; generic character-family averages do not suffice. |
| Growing-depth Liouville | Fixed-depth nonlocal inverse and subpower inverse constant at proposed depth. | Same fixed-depth source on every past/future scale; depth-uniform completion and moving contour costs. |
| Older c=.125123 packet | Valid source-relative return; alternative whole-domain patch/complement certificate. | Local improvement duplicates [restricted research revision]/W38 and is subsumed; any reuse needs its own complete endpoint ledger. |

Every local theorem keeps its literal characters, masks, signs, exceptional
terms and normalizations. The detailed maps also retain scoped failures,

full29-family/109-child portfolio is preserved without renumbering or deletion.

The first useful next test for the phase/exterior route is one good prime's

## 3. The disappearing main returns in the complementary tail

For this step retain MO's explicit **I-HECKE** input: the supplied
whole-family finite-order Hecke zero-free/reciprocal hypothesis in
every buffered half-plane \(\Re v\ge b>b_0=1-c_0\). The step below
uses only its principal \(\mathbb K\)-character instance, not ordinary
Riemann-zeta nonvanishing. Fix \(b_0<b<1\).

MO7--MO19 may be applied with cutoff R in place of \(S_0\), retaining
the auxiliary-height powers instead of absorbing them into Z.
Take \(X=\lfloor R\rfloor+1/2\), Perron height \(2X^3\), and choose
the reciprocal-height losses independently. For every
\(\eta>0\), this gives

\[
|\mathcal M_\sigma(R)|
\ll_{b,\eta,\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
Z^\epsilon\mathcal B R^{b-1+\eta},\qquad R\ge2.
                                                               \tag{SC6}
\]

The source feature norms and MO17 remainder bound have no R cost;
the displayed \(R^\eta\) pays the contour-height powers and ideal
norm counts. The horizontal and sharp-truncation errors decay more
rapidly. There is no residue at the apparent Perron pole: the finite
source Dirichlet series has the common factor \(F_D(v)\), so it
vanishes at \(v=1\), while all its other Euler factors are regular
there. This is the exact MO union/intersection factorization.

Choose \(\eta<1-b\). Then \(\mathcal M_\sigma(R)\to0\). Combining
SC3--SC6 shows that the ordered limit
\(\mathcal C_\sigma(\infty)=\lim_{R\to\infty}\mathcal C_\sigma(R)\)
exists and satisfies

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal M_\sigma(S_0)=
\mathcal C_\sigma(\infty)
+\mathcal E_\sigma(\infty)-\mathcal E_\sigma(S_0),
\qquad
\mathcal M_\sigma(S_0)
=\mathcal C_\sigma(\infty)
+O_{\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}\!\left(
Z^\epsilon\sqrt K B S(N,L)\right).}
                                                               \tag{SC7}
\]

The fixed \(A_+^{-1/2}\) in \(1/S_0\) is part of the original
endpoint constant. A finite and quantitatively priced version is

\[
|\mathcal M_\sigma(S_0)-\mathcal C_\sigma(R)|
\ll Z^\epsilon\left(
\mathcal H/S_0+\mathcal B R^{b-1+\eta}\right).
                                                               \tag{SC8}
\]

This is an actual-source identity and estimate, with beta unchanged.
In the definition of \(\mathcal C_\sigma\), first sum all h0,t for
each fixed s,z, then take the s-cutoff limit. It supplies no license
to reverse those operations or sum separate SQ principal parts over
all h0. Completing s kills the selected main only in a **different**
selected sector; its difference from the physical sector is exactly
the complementary tail in SC7.

## R42.9. Protected parked audit24: exterior response and a sourced repair

The original card asks whether two zero-induced scalar constraints force a nonzero wedge of coefficient witnesses. They do not. In a Hilbert space let a nonzero linear functional ell satisfy ell(u)=1. For arbitrary prescribed scalar responses alpha,beta, take A=alpha u, B=beta u. Both constraints hold but

    ||A wedge B||^2=||A||^2||B||^2-|<A,B>|^2=0.       (R42.18)

This is a complete counterexample to that implication, not an invented arithmetic counterexample. Even when actual A,B are independent, the constraints alone supply no quantitative lower Gram determinant. For D02 both meromorphic fields are scalar analytic multipliers of the same F(s)=exp(s^2)/L(s), so a simple zero supplies a rank-one pole response. The hypothesis of two independent responses remains unpaid. A bound on the exterior norm by marginal norms does not repair the missing lower signal.

A derivative determinant is a different, explicit alternative worth retaining. With G=hF,

    F G'-F' G=h' F^2.                                (R42.19)

The zeros of h' are not controlled, so this pair does not give a globally nonzero numerator. If h' vanishes to order m at a zero of L of order k, the possible pole order is2k-m. No claim that m<2k has been proved.

One can instead choose a fixed dilation a0>1 of the actual ideal field: V(x)=U_eta,2(x/a0), whose Mellin transform is G=a0^-sF. Then the determinant is exactly

    F G'-F' G=-(log a0)a0^-s exp(2s^2)/L(s)^2.        (R42.20)

Its numerator never vanishes. The exact physical field with transform a0^-s exp(2s^2)/L^2 is

    Q_eta(x)=sum_c (mu_K*mu_K)(c)eta(c)
                         g_4(log(a0 Nc/x)).           (R42.21)

All S zeros remain. The convolution coefficients are1,-2,1,0,... at each prime power. Gaussian integral convolution of the two fields proves R42.21 directly; the physical field corresponding to determinant R42.20 is -(log a0)Q. Absolute convergence on Re s>1 justifies differentiating and composing. This is not an identification with the original Hilbert-space wedge norm; it is a changed detector with a paid source formula and a new complete moment obligation.

If the complete signed Q norm is O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)) on every large dyad, its Gaussian left tail and Mellin continuation exclude every original L-zero with Re rho>gamma, since the pole order in R42.20 is2 ord_rho L. No height cutoff or assumed simple zero is needed. A common family return needs this hypothesis for each fixed eta. The full physical energy of Q contains **all four original ideal indices** from the two convolutions, with every collision and signed cross term; a product of two diagonal estimates does not estimate it.

Conversely an original U every-epsilon gamma bound implies a Q bound at that level. For sigma>gamma, dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz makes integral |U(y)|y^-sigma dy/y finite, including the Gaussian left tail. Weighted Minkowski for U*V then pays Q at sigma. Thus this explicit nonlinear representation does not create an improved exponent from existing marginal bounds. Its useful retained content is an unconditional nonzero numerator for a changed derivative-determinant detector. The tensor/product mechanism has W29/F16 ancestry; only this exact ideal coefficient and return calculation is claimed here as a reviewer refinement.
