statement:
### 3.3 Fixed affine correlations and one outcome

Take L_i(n)=A_i n+B_i with integer A_i>0 and determinant A1 B2 - A2 B1 nonzero. Discard finitely many n with nonpositive arguments. First modify only a fixed finite prime set F, including primes dividing q. Let Q be its squarefree product, and D=2^|F|. On nonzero terms write L1(n)=d r and L2(n)=e s, where d,e divide Q and r,s are squarefree and coprime to Q. The coefficient contributed by primes in F, or by any fixed ordinary character weights, has modulus at most 1.

For the conjugated product, the remaining random monomial is epsilon(r/s). Distinct rational ratios are orthogonal. Holding d,e and r/s fixed determines L1/L2, hence determines at most one n by nondegeneracy. Every monomial class contains at most D^2 terms. For the unconjugated product it is epsilon(rs); distinct integer products are orthogonal. Holding d,e,rs fixed gives a quadratic equation for n, with at most two solutions, so classes have at most 2D^2 terms. Cauchy inside each class gives

    E |C_N|^2 <= 2D^2 N + O_F(1)

for either correlation sum. Shared prime factors in r,s are allowed: rational cancellation in the conjugated case and exponent 2 in the unconjugated case are exactly encoded by these monomials. There is no assumption that distinct n supply independent summands.

For each fixed positive rational epsilon, Markov at N=j^2 gives a summable O(epsilon^(-2)j^(-2)) failure probability. Borel--Cantelli implies C_{j^2}/j^2 -> 0. The O(j) omitted bounded terms fill the gaps to every N. Intersect over epsilon, finite F, affine forms and ordinary character weights; these are countable sets.

Conditioning on the finitely many original phases in F causes no problem: the estimate is uniform in their values, and Fubini gives a probability-one conclusion for the fixed prescribed modification under the original probability measure. There is no uncountable-intersection step. If the sentence about uniform finite phases is interpreted as uniform convergence across all phase assignments, it also has a direct proof: decompose C_N into its finitely many (d,e) components. Each component has the same orthogonality/multiplicity bound, independently of the phase coefficient. Take their finite probability-one intersection. The maximum over unit phase coefficients of |C_N|/N is bounded by the sum of the finitely many component magnitudes divided by N, which tends to zero. Zero-valued ramified components can simply be omitted.

Now restore the infinite Bernoulli replacement set P. Truncate it at Y, retaining the fixed prescriptions and q. Every realized finite truncation belongs to the countable finite-set family already handled, even though its identity depends on the Bernoulli outcome. A value at A n+B can differ from its truncation only if a prime p in P above Y divides that argument. Put the finitely many primes dividing A below Y. Each remaining p has at most N/p+1 such n up to N, and p <= C N apart from harmless initial terms. The exceptional proportion is at most

    sum_{p in P, p>Y} 1/p + O(#P(CN)/N).

The second term tends to zero because #P(x)=O_b(x^b) for some b<1. Take N to infinity first, then Y to infinity; the first term tends to zero by reciprocal summability. Products of bounded terms change by at most 2 on the union of the two exceptional sets. Both limiting correlations are zero. All calibration, prime-series and correlation events used above are countable intersections of probability-one events, so one fixed outcome has all the stated properties at all scales.

For every fixed integer H, expansion of the unweighted Cesaro window energy gives diagonal contribution H d_q, where

    d_q = product_{p|q}(1-1/p) product_{p not dividing q}(1-1/p^2)>0.

This follows from the ordinary squarefree/coprime density, proved by finite sieve and the convergent tail sum over p^2. The finitely many off-diagonal shifts have nonzero determinant and hence vanish by the pair result. The conclusion is

    (1/N) sum_{m<=N} |sum_{j=1}^H a(m+j)|^2 -> H d_q.

The order fixes H before N. No uniform rate in H follows. Partial summation turns C_N=o(N) into qualitative logarithmic fixed-form cancellation, including logarithmic intervals whose log-length tends to infinity: split at a fixed threshold, then use the arbitrary small bound |C_N|<=epsilon N above it. This does not establish an outside theorem's nonpretentiousness hypotheses or a growing-lag rate.

### The exact same-output diagonal and the remaining form

Expand Q_hard before absolute values. Its summand is

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))*chi(p)*a(m)] log p
      *exp(-2*gamma*y)g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),

over p>(2+y)^A, all m,n>=1, and 0<=y<=R. The equality n=pm contributes only when pm is a squarefree q-unit; then -conjugate(a(pm))*chi(p)*a(m)=1. The total retained log-prime weight at fixed n is at most log n. Exactly,

    int_(-infinity)^infinity exp(-2*gamma*y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =exp(tau*gamma^2)n^(-2*gamma)/(2*sqrt(pi*tau)).

Thus the actual hard same-output diagonal D_R obeys

    0<=D_R<=exp(tau*gamma^2)/(2*sqrt(pi*tau))
                 *sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2*gamma)<infinity.          (R4)

This bound includes all cutoff changes and both infinite source sums. It gives no positive domination for arbitrary signed subcollections. Set H_R=Q_hard-D_R, literally the complete n!=pm form with its signs and moving mask.

The proposed arithmetic premise OPEN-PF is: for every fixed chi there exist delta_chi>0, B_chi and R0_chi such that

    H_R<=(1-delta_chi) I_R+B_chi for every R>=R0_chi.             (PF)

Take eta=delta_chi/4 in each of (R2),(R3), use (R4), and absorb the finite initial interval. Equation (R1) implies

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R+tau*gamma E_R<=B'_chi.       (R5)

## HC3. Exact signed reciprocal atoms at prime-square frequency

For a term of HC2.3, its integer frequency label is

    r=product_(j=1)^3 n_j^(alpha_j+beta_j).

Absolute grouping gives

    H_(delta,theta)(x)=sum_(r>=1) r^(-delta)B_r(x)exp(-i theta log r).

B_r retains every permutation sign, character phase and Gaussian output weight. The five possible sorted exponent patterns are

    (0,2,4), (0,3,3), (1,1,4), (1,2,3), (2,2,2).                (HC3.1)

Let p be the least prime not dividing the specified modulus. It is also the least integer n>1 with a(n) nonzero. The smallest live integer frequency is p^2. It occurs only for the tuple (1,p,c), c>p, with exponent 4 on 1, 2 on p and 0 on c. The permutations are identical, hence their product sign is +1. All-positive patterns use two distinct nonunit live labels at least p and q>p, so give r>=pq>p^2. The (0,3,3) pattern gives r>=p^3. The (0,2,4) pattern attains p^2 only in the stated assignment.

Consequently the coefficient is the COMPLETE signed reciprocal field with precisely two labels removed:

    B_(p^2)(x)=a(p)[M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))],       (HC3.2)
    B_(p^2)(s)=a(p)p^(-s)[F(s)-1-a(p)p^(-s)].                  (HC3.3)

No prime number theorem, zero-free premise, random signs or common-divisor payment enters. The free c runs over every live integer, including squarefree composites divisible by p. This is not a positive semiprime subseries.

In fact HC3.2--HC3.3 hold for EVERY unramified prime p, not only the least. If r=p^2, every positive-exponent label must be a power of p. A live label is squarefree, so can only be 1 or p. Three distinct labels require one zero exponent. HC3.1 then forces exactly the same (4,2,0) assignment with free c distinct from 1,p. Now c can be smaller than p, but the M formula already includes it. In all cases the median of (1,p,c) is at most p.

Finitely many deleted theta-frequency channels therefore cannot remove all these reciprocal copies: select another unramified prime whose square was not deleted. This statement concerns specified frequency deletion, not a prohibition on genuinely new arithmetic cancellation.

statement:
## 3. Independent proof and quantifier audit of M

Fix q >= 1, a finite set of prescribed unit values at primes not dividing q, and 1/2 < beta < b6. Fix the Gaussian parameter tau > 0. A target gamma, when used, is chosen below beta. The existence order is: fixed mathematical parameters and finite prescriptions; choose the probability space; intersect the required probability-one events; select one outcome; then let character, accuracy exponent, affine form and scale vary within the stated contract. A different beta or incompatible finite prescription may use a different sequence. There is no claim that one sequence realizes mutually incompatible prime prescriptions.

### 3.1 Rare replacements and all fixed-character calibration

Let epsilon_p be independent Steinhaus variables, and independently let I_p be Bernoulli with mean p^(beta-1). Initially set v_p = 1 if I_p = 1 and v_p = epsilon_p otherwise. Set

    a(n) = mu(n)^2 product_{p|n} v_p,

then delete primes dividing q and impose the finite prescribed values. The resulting function is multiplicative, a(1)=1, and

    |a(n)| = mu(n)^2 1_{(n,q)=1}.

It is not completely multiplicative. These are the actual natural zero conditions, not a squarefree replacement inside a completely multiplicative claim.

Write P = {p : I_p = 1}. For every b > beta,

    E sum_{p in P} p^(-b) = sum_p p^(-(b+1-beta)) < infinity.

A nonnegative random variable with finite expectation is finite almost surely. Intersect over rational b > beta; comparison then supplies every real b > beta. In particular, the reciprocal sum over P is finite. Choosing rational beta < b < 1 also gives

    # {p in P : p <= x} <= x^b sum_{p in P} p^(-b) = O_b(x^b).

For the unmodified source a0(n) = mu(n)^2 product epsilon_p, distinct squarefree integers give distinct Steinhaus monomials and hence are orthogonal in L2. Non-squarefree terms vanish. Multiplication by any fixed ordinary character psi preserves this orthogonality and does not increase the diagonal variances. The deterministic n=1 term is also orthogonal to all other monomials.

The dyadic maximal inequality used by the author needs no independence between the integer-indexed coefficients. Every initial segment of [1,2^k] is a disjoint union of at most k+1 standard dyadic blocks. Cauchy bounds its squared sum by (k+1) times the sum of squared sums over those blocks; enlarging to every block on every level has expected value at most (k+1)2^k. Therefore

    E max_{m <= 2^k} |sum_{n <= m} a0(n) psi(n)|^2
        <= (k+1)^2 2^k.

Markov at 2^(k(1/2+eta)) produces a summable series in k for every eta > 0. Borel--Cantelli and interpolation between dyadic endpoints prove

    sum_{n <= x} a0(n) psi(n) = O_{eta,psi}(x^(1/2+eta)).

Ordinary characters are countable: there are finitely many for each positive modulus. Intersect over all of them and rational eta > 0. Smaller rational eta recover every requested real accuracy exponent. No conductor-uniform constant is obtained or required.

The local quotient at a changed prime, with z = p^(-s), is exactly

    (1+v z)/(1+epsilon z)
      = 1 + sum_{j>=1} (v-epsilon)(-epsilon)^(j-1) z^j.

Its nonconstant coefficients have modulus at most 2. It defines a multiplicative convolution coefficient d with a = a0*d and, for b > beta,

    sum_n |d(n)| n^(-b)
      <= C_{b,F} product_{p in P} (1 + 2 p^(-b)/(1-p^(-b))) < infinity.

Finite deletions and prescribed changes multiply this by finitely many convergent factors for b > 0. Since an ordinary character is completely multiplicative, including its zero values,

    a psi = (a0 psi) * (d psi).

Choose 1/2+eta < b. Applying the preceding bound to x/m >= 1 and enlarging its exponent to b gives an upper bound C x^b sum_m |d(m)|m^(-b). For any epsilon > 0, choose b in (beta,beta+epsilon). Thus every fixed twist satisfies O_{epsilon,psi}(x^(beta+epsilon)). This supplies, in particular, any weaker summatory calibration exponent strictly between beta and b6. Abel summation also gives the claimed O((1+|t|)x^(beta+epsilon)) for the additional n^(it) twist, and fixed logarithmic derivatives cost another arbitrarily small power. This does not assert uniformity for a growing family of characters.

### 3.2 Exact pole and full-height Gaussian asymptotic

Before finite modifications, E v_p = p^(beta-1). Let xi_p = v_p - p^(beta-1). These are independent centered variables of variance at most 1. The same dyadic maximal argument, with zero coefficients off the primes, gives

    S(x) = sum_{p <= x} xi_p = O_eta(x^(1/2+eta))

on a probability-one event for every rational eta > 0. Hence

    Z(s) = s integral_1^infinity S(x) x^(-s-1) dx

is holomorphic on Re(s)>1/2. On any fixed closed vertical strip with left boundary sigma0>1/2, choose eta<sigma0-1/2. The integral is bounded by a constant times |s|, uniformly on that strip. In particular, |Z(s)| <= C(1+|Im(s)|).

Starting in Re(s)>1, the absolutely convergent Euler products and logarithmic series give

    D_a(s) = zeta(s+1-beta) H(s),

where the logarithm of H is

    Z(s)
    + sum_p sum_{j>=2} (-1)^(j+1) v_p^j p^(-js)/j
    - sum_p sum_{j>=2} p^(-j(s+1-beta))/j.

The signs follow directly by subtracting log zeta from log D_a. Both double tails converge absolutely and normally on Re(s)>1/2. The respective leading real prime exponents are 2 Re(s)>1 and 2(Re(s)+1-beta)>1; the second inequality uses beta<1. Thus H is an exponential of a holomorphic function there, is nonzero, and obeys |H(s)| <= exp(C(1+|Im(s)|)) on each fixed closed strip. Finite deletions or changes multiply H by

    1/(1+v_p p^(-s)), or
    (1+v'_p p^(-s))/(1+v_p p^(-s)).

For Re(s)>0 their denominators and numerators are nonzero; on a strip bounded away from zero their moduli are bounded. Consequently D_a has exactly the required simple pole at beta with nonzero residue H(beta). Zeta zeros create zeros, not extra poles, and cannot cancel the simple pole at argument 1.

For g_tau(u) = (2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)), direct Mellin inversion gives

    F_a(x) = (1/(2 pi i)) integral_{Re(s)=c}
                exp(tau s^2/2) D_a(s) x^s ds,   c>1.

Move this contour to any fixed sigma in (1/2,beta). On the finite horizontal width, ordinary zeta has polynomial vertical growth away from its isolated pole, H has at most exponential vertical growth, and the Gaussian has exp(-tau t^2/2) decay. Horizontal integrals tend to zero and both infinite vertical integrals converge absolutely. This is a full-height contour shift; there is no truncated-height remainder or data-dependent contour. The only crossed pole is beta, so

    F_a(x) = exp(tau beta^2/2) H(beta) x^beta + O_sigma(x^sigma).

The leading coefficient is nonzero. Every fixed derivative only inserts a polynomial in s and is paid by the same Gaussian decay. As x tends to zero, g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_A (x/n)^A for each A>1; summing yields O_A(x^A). This covers the other end of a later Mellin transform. None of these conclusions uses a zero-free hypothesis.

For the unconjugated product it is epsilon(rs); distinct integer products are orthogonal. Holding d,e,rs fixed gives a quadratic equation for n, with at most two solutions, so classes have at most 2D^2 terms. Cauchy inside each class gives

    E |C_N|^2 <= 2D^2 N + O_F(1)

for either correlation sum. Shared prime factors in r,s are allowed: rational cancellation in the conjugated case and exponent 2 in the unconjugated case are exactly encoded by these monomials. There is no assumption that distinct n supply independent summands.

For each fixed positive rational epsilon, Markov at N=j^2 gives a summable O(epsilon^(-2)j^(-2)) failure probability. Borel--Cantelli implies C_{j^2}/j^2 -> 0. The O(j) omitted bounded terms fill the gaps to every N. Intersect over epsilon, finite F, affine forms and ordinary character weights; these are countable sets.

Conditioning on the finitely many original phases in F causes no problem: the estimate is uniform in their values, and Fubini gives a probability-one conclusion for the fixed prescribed modification under the original probability measure. There is no uncountable-intersection step. If the sentence about uniform finite phases is interpreted as uniform convergence across all phase assignments, it also has a direct proof: decompose C_N into its finitely many (d,e) components. Each component has the same orthogonality/multiplicity bound, independently of the phase coefficient. Take their finite probability-one intersection. The maximum over unit phase coefficients of |C_N|/N is bounded by the sum of the finitely many component magnitudes divided by N, which tends to zero. Zero-valued ramified components can simply be omitted.

Now restore the infinite Bernoulli replacement set P. Truncate it at Y, retaining the fixed prescriptions and q. Every realized finite truncation belongs to the countable finite-set family already handled, even though its identity depends on the Bernoulli outcome. A value at A n+B can differ from its truncation only if a prime p in P above Y divides that argument. Put the finitely many primes dividing A below Y. Each remaining p has at most N/p+1 such n up to N, and p <= C N apart from harmless initial terms. The exceptional proportion is at most

    sum_{p in P, p>Y} 1/p + O(#P(CN)/N).

The second term tends to zero because #P(x)=O_b(x^b) for some b<1. Take N to infinity first, then Y to infinity; the first term tends to zero by reciprocal summability. Products of bounded terms change by at most 2 on the union of the two exceptional sets. Both limiting correlations are zero. All calibration, prime-series and correlation events used above are countable intersections of probability-one events, so one fixed outcome has all the stated properties at all scales.

For every fixed integer H, expansion of the unweighted Cesaro window energy gives diagonal contribution H d_q, where

    d_q = product_{p|q}(1-1/p) product_{p not dividing q}(1-1/p^2)>0.

This follows from the ordinary squarefree/coprime density, proved by finite sieve and the convergent tail sum over p^2. The finitely many off-diagonal shifts have nonzero determinant and hence vanish by the pair result. The conclusion is

    (1/N) sum_{m<=N} |sum_{j=1}^H a(m+j)|^2 -> H d_q.

The order fixes H before N. No uniform rate in H follows. Partial summation turns C_N=o(N) into qualitative logarithmic fixed-form cancellation, including logarithmic intervals whose log-length tends to infinity: split at a fixed threshold, then use the arbitrary small bound |C_N|<=epsilon N above it. This does not establish an outside theorem's nonpretentiousness hypotheses or a growing-lag rate.

### 3.4 Finite masks and exact scope of the obstruction

For a feasible valuation 0 or 1 at a fixed unramified prime, the Dirichlet series is multiplied by 1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) or v_p p^(-s)/(1+v_p p^(-s)). Each is analytic and nonzero at beta. Their finite products preserve the pole and its nonzero Gaussian mode. A signed combination may kill the pole only when its combined multiplier vanishes at beta; an exact recombination back to the original source restores the original pole. A positive valuation at a ramified prime is infeasible and identically zero, not an exception to this assertion.

M therefore defeats a derivation of a better complete Gaussian bound from the listed coarse properties alone, even with these individual finite masks. It does not defeat arithmetic arguments using the actual global Mobius prime law or its global convolution inverse. For fixed prescribed ordinary chi, outside the finite prescribed set the random unit phases differ from -chi(p) at infinitely many primes almost surely. The model is not secretly in the actual mu*chi family. A finite alphabet restriction or reality condition may also exclude this model; no claim about those narrower classes is proved here.

# [private research revision] independent review: reciprocal Hankel determinant and its exact return

Verdict: **PASS as an analytic reduction and conditional zero-exclusion theorem. The finite signed moment D20 remains OPEN.** The exponent `1.74898+epsilon` in D20, with all of its stated character and scale quantifiers, does imply the conditional constant `c=.12551`. The complete median/product complement, every mixed error term, multiple zeros, principal poles, and the exceptional shift parameters are accounted for below. The separate fixed-shift inverse has norm strictly below 20 in the claimed weighted dilation algebra. None of these results establishes D20 or an increased c.



Current worklog: source bound and read in full; exact new ownership acquired; determinant, tails, parameter selection, pole return and inverse independently reconstructed; independent finite arithmetic passed. This report gives the final mathematical verdict. The remaining mathematical work is D20 itself. Handoff requires full readback/hash, explicit STOP and release only this review claim.

## UR1. Frozen source and dependencies

Main source: `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/upstream/report.md`, 27,589 bytes, SHA256 `b2f1f25b3751d9ff670b270aba98eeac7049380755130b48c81a9b0dacb2dede`, explicitly matched against the parent packet. Its equation labels D1--D26 are used below. Adjacent source evidence, also read:

- `check_exact.py`, 3,389 bytes, SHA256 `71717d30e44f009c0d005fa4988bff5074ddfc92b8db682c75ee2d64f8700ee0`.
- `exact-receipt.json`, 2,237 bytes, SHA256 `e74777a27523be5853dcb2522422c8dff89f4c5d3d01494aafb00fc14795886d`.

The ancestry is narrower than a proved arithmetic estimate. `[restricted mathematical source]`, section R36.10 and equation R36.24, gives an abstract adjugate-residue escape, explicitly leaving arithmetic reconstruction, nonvanishing and the nonlinear norm open. Its read snapshot hash is `73b3f2ed29c3059a337fe97cb1fb957393035a93f0a916afb0657cc323b7c86c`. The new report supplies a concrete correlated reciprocal matrix and a complete conditional return, so it is not simply the old abstract determinant example.

`[restricted mathematical source]`, read snapshot SHA256 `c4864ef57197ae30da6b32e9484ab061cd28b122c20296f69ec4330488bd4692`, supplies the accepted research premise `c_G=.1251134`, with new endpoint/kernel replay pending separately from the old c0 receipt. It also explicitly uses the buffered zeta Mertens calibration `beta=.8749`. That calibration is needed only for the optional scalar comparison D21. The proof D20 => zero exclusion below does not assume any Mertens estimate or the accepted zero-free boundary.

Other inspected context: the stable research prefix, `[restricted mathematical source]`, and the [private research revision] high-ceiling discovery/review's warnings about unrelated multiplicative-Hankel readouts. Here the physical field is constructed from the actual determinant coefficients and has its own Mellin identity; no unrelated operator norm is substituted.

## UR2. Actual determinant coefficients and the remaining prime channel

Put `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, with the ordinary character's natural zero extension, and `F(s)=1/L(s,chi)`. Initially `Re s>1`. For real delta>0 the Hankel matrix is

    sum_n a(n)n^(-s) v_n v_n^T,
    v_n=(1,n^(-delta),n^(-2delta))^T.

Cauchy--Binet for finite truncations gives the ordered triples `a<b<c`, each with coefficient `a(a)a(b)a(c) det[v_a,v_b,v_c]^2`. Absolute convergence permits passage to the infinite sum, since `|V_delta|<=1` and the unconstrained triple Dirichlet series converges. Squaring removes the immaterial orientation of the Vandermonde. This proves D3 with no analytic conjugation, no coprimality restriction and no deletion of shared primes.

On every nonzero tuple, each factor is squarefree and

    mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)=(-1)^(Omega(a)+Omega(b)+Omega(c))
                       =lambda(abc),
    chi(a)chi(b)chi(c)=chi(abc).

Thus D4 is exact even at squareful outputs. The coalesced weight `W_delta(n)` is nonnegative and `|h_chi,delta(n)|<=d_3(n)`. Distinctness is essential: a prime-power output has at most the two allowed squarefree labels 1,p, so its coefficient vanishes. At pq with distinct primes the sole admissible triple is `(1,p,q)`, proving D5.

For zeta, the `(1,2,p)` channel has a positive weight tending, uniformly on `I=[1/5,1/4]`, to `(1-2^(-delta))^2 2^(-2delta)`. Consequently D6 is correct: its positive absolute Dirichlet series diverges at every real sigma<=1. Positive Mellin Fubini then rules out an all-dyad sublinear power bound for the absolute Gaussian field, including an averaged-in-delta version. This does not lower-bound the full signed field.

The same obstruction extends to every fixed ordinary character: replace 2 by a fixed prime p0 not dividing the specified modulus, and let p vary over the other unramified primes. Then `|chi(p0 p)|=1`, the weights tend uniformly to a positive constant depending on p0, and removing finitely many ramified primes does not repair the divergent prime reciprocal sum. Original prime arithmetic therefore survives in a short-factor semiprime face. Prime-power annihilation alone does not pay D20.

## UR3. Pole cofactor: exact expansion, nontriviality and multiplicities

Direct expansion of the 3 by 3 determinant gives

    D_delta=C_delta F+E_delta,
    C_delta=F(s+2delta)F(s+4delta)-F(s+3delta)^2,
    E_delta=-F(s+delta)^2F(s+4delta)
            +2F(s+delta)F(s+2delta)F(s+3delta)
            -F(s+2delta)^3.

This agrees with D7, including all three complementary terms. A second two-column Cauchy--Binet identity yields

    C_delta(s)=sum_(m<n) a(m)a(n)(mn)^(-s-2delta)
                                      (m^(-delta)-n^(-delta))^2.

Let rho be fixed with sigma=Re rho>4/5, and let p be the least prime not dividing the specified modulus. It is also the least integer n>1 with a(n) nonzero. For real delta tending to infinity, the `(1,p)` summand is

    -chi(p)p^(-rho-2delta)(1-p^(-delta))^2.

It dominates the entire remaining series, not only finitely many initial terms. For `(1,n)` with n>=p+1, divide the elementary tail bound

    sum_(n>=p+1) n^(-sigma-2delta)
      <=(p+1)^(-sigma-2delta)
                       [1+(p+1)/(sigma+2delta-1)]

by the leading magnitude. The result tends to zero geometrically. For m>=p, the remaining sum is bounded by

    1/(sigma+2delta-1) sum_(m>=p) m^(1-2sigma-6delta).

After division by `p^(-sigma-2delta)`, this is at most

    p^(1-sigma-4delta)/(sigma+2delta-1)
                 [1+p/(2sigma+6delta-2)]

for sufficiently large delta, up to the factor `(1-p^(-delta))^(-2)` tending to one. It also tends to zero. These estimates permit constants depending on the fixed p and rho; no height-uniform lower bound has been inferred.

As a function of complex delta, `C_delta(rho)` is analytic in the connected half-plane where `Re(rho+j delta)>1`, j=2,3,4. This domain contains I and all sufficiently large positive real delta. The preceding asymptotic proves that it is not identically zero. Its real zeros on I are isolated, hence measure zero. This works for imprimitive characters with their specified modulus, not just their primitive conductor.

The only useful wording precision is to express the pole statement by its leading Laurent term. If

    F(s)=b_(-m)(s-rho)^(-m)+O((s-rho)^(-m+1)), b_(-m)!=0,

then, when `C_delta(rho)!=0`, D has leading term

    C_delta(rho)b_(-m)(s-rho)^(-m).

This is the exact multiple-zero statement. It does not identify the complete residue of a higher-order pole with that one factor; derivatives of C may affect lower Laurent coefficients. This precision requires no change in the author's theorem or exponent.

## UR4. The averaged all-height zero-exclusion bridge is valid

For fixed tau>0 let

    H_delta(x)=sum_n h_chi,delta(n) g_tau(log(n/x)).

The d3 bound gives local uniform convergence. For x<=1, writing u=-log x>=0, `(log n+u)^2 >=(log n)^2+u^2` gives a uniform Gaussian left tail. Polynomial factors from differentiation are harmless. Thus integration over x near zero gives an entire Mellin contribution.

For `Re s>1`, absolute Fubini and the substitution v=log(n/x) give exactly

    integral_0^infinity H_delta(x)x^(-s) dx/x
                           =exp(tau*s^2/2)D_delta(s).

In particular the Gaussian multiplier is `exp(+tau*s^2/2)`, never zero. No determinant of physical Gaussian fields has been used.

Suppose D11 holds for one fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0 on all sufficiently large dyadic X, at a fixed `4/5<gamma<1`. For any fixed sigma0>gamma, choose epsilon<2(sigma0-gamma). Summing the weighted dyadic bounds gives

    integral_I integral_1^infinity
                   |H_delta(x)|^2 x^(-2sigma0) dx/x ddelta < infinity.

The finitely many initial shells are finite by local convergence. Tonelli supplies finite weighted L2 norm for almost every delta. Cauchy--Schwarz, with the remaining factor `x^(-(Re s-sigma0))`, gives absolute Mellin convergence and holomorphy for `Re s>sigma0`; logarithmic factors needed for all complex derivatives are integrable on compact sub-half-planes. Intersecting over one countable sequence sigma0 decreasing to gamma gives one full-measure set of fixed delta with a holomorphic transform on `Re s>gamma`.

Independently, the zeros of the nonzero meromorphic function L form a countable set. For each zero rho in `Re rho>gamma`, UR3 excludes only a null set of shifts. The union of these sets is null. Choose delta outside that union and the previous L2 exceptional set. This single delta, selected after the all-scale summation, is valid for every zero and every height.

Because `gamma+1/5>1`, all shifted entries occurring in C and E are holomorphic throughout `Re s>gamma`. D is meromorphic there through the identity `D=CF+E`. Its Mellin identity continues meromorphically from `Re s>1`; the left side is holomorphic and the exponential is nonvanishing. A zero of L of any multiplicity would give the uncancelled leading pole from UR3, a contradiction.

For principal characters, the pole of L at one is a zero, not a pole, of F. It creates no missing residue or obstruction. For imprimitive characters, the natural coefficients and the specified modulus have been retained throughout. Finite Euler-factor zeros at Re s=0 lie outside the asserted region in any case. A theorem for each ordinary chi at the same gamma proves a common constant without conductor-uniform implicit constants. If desired, the full-measure shift sets can be intersected over the countable family of ordinary characters; this is not needed for the individual conclusion.

Thus the bridge is valid at all heights, with an open boundary `Re s>gamma`. A finite-height sample, a bound on a subsequence of X, or a bound for only one selected delta would not be the stated hypothesis. None is being substituted here.

## UR5. Complete median and product tails

For `a<b<c` and delta>0, monotonicity gives

    0<=V_delta(a,b,c)^2<=a^(-4delta)b^(-2delta).

There is a constant K_tau such that

    sum_(n>=1) g_tau(log(n/y)) <= K_tau y, y>0.

For completeness, partition log(n/y) into `[j,j+1)`. Each interval contains at most `exp(j+1)y` positive integers. Summing that bound times the Gaussian supremum over the interval gives a convergent bilateral series, independent of y. This also handles y<1 without an extra unpriced constant.

For the ENTIRE median complement b>Y, discard signs and character phases but retain the Vandermonde decay. Summation over c gives

    |H_(b>Y),delta(x)|
      <=K_tau x sum_a a^(-1-4delta) sum_(b>Y) b^(-1-2delta)
      <=(5/2)K_tau zeta(9/5) x Y^(-2/5), delta in I.

The integral comparison is `sum_(b>Y) b^(-1-2delta)<=Y^(-2delta)/(2delta)`. With `Y=floor(X^(63/200))`, Y is at least half of `X^.315` for large X. Uniformly on x in `[X,2X]`, this is `O(X^(437/500))=O(X^.874)`. Integration over the fixed measures `dx/x` and ddelta preserves that exponent. No median-sector boundary or unbounded c-tail is absent.

For product tails, the positive tuple counting measure satisfies

    A_delta(t):=sum_(abc<=t; a<b<c) |a(a)a(b)a(c)|V_delta^2
       <= t sum_a a^(-1-4delta) sum_b b^(-1-2delta)
       <= t zeta(9/5)zeta(7/5).

The same upper bound holds when the coefficient sequence has character zeros. Set tau=1, `L=log X`, `A_X=X exp(-2 sqrt L)`, `B_X=2X exp(2 sqrt L)`. For n<A_X and x>=X the Gaussian is increasing as a function of n and at most a constant times `exp(-2L)`. Therefore the lower tail is at most

    O(A_X exp(-2L)) = O(X^(-1) exp(-2 sqrt L)).

For n>B_X and x<=2X the logarithmic separation is at least `2 sqrt L`. Stieltjes integration against `A_delta(t)<=Ct` bounds the upper tail by a constant times its endpoint term and

    x integral_(2 sqrt L)^infinity e^v (1+v)g_1(v) dv
                                       = X^(-1+o(1)).

Here completing the square in `-v^2/2+v` gives the exponent explicitly. These bounds are uniform in delta and chi. The lower cap is strict for the discarded tail and the finite field includes equality; likewise at the upper and median caps. The intersection of discarded sectors only reduces the triangle bound.

Thus D19 is valid in the joint Hilbert space `L2(I x [X,2X], ddelta dx/x)`:

    ||H-Z_X|| <= C X^.874 + X^(-1+o(1)).

This compares the moving finite field Z_X with ONE fixed H. It never takes the Mellin transform of a field whose definition changes with X. The small-factor faces, including `(1,p0,c)`, remain; the derived lower bound on c is `X^.37 exp(-2 sqrt L)`, and neither a nor b receives an artificial lower cutoff.

## UR6. The finite scalar, every interaction, and exact exponent return

For the exact finite tuple set, the coefficient is `chi(n)lambda(n)w_delta,X(n)` with real nonnegative w. Expanding its Hilbert norm gives D20 exactly:

    Q(X)=sum_(n,m in [A_X,B_X])
       chi(n)conjugate(chi(m))lambda(nm) K_X(n,m)
                                 integral_I w_delta,X(n)w_delta,X(m) ddelta.

No source pair, ordered mixed term or repeated product representation is omitted. The entire scalar is real and nonnegative because it is a squared norm; individual summands need not be positive or even real. For complex characters, conjugation on the second output is indispensable. Averaging the individual energies in delta is the definition of this norm, so no cross-delta term belongs to it.

Completing the square in the product of the two g1 factors gives

    K_X(n,m)=g_2(log(n/m))
       *integral_0^(log 2) g_(1/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X))du.

Both the exponent and normalization agree: the product prefactor is `1/(2 pi)`, as is that of g2 times g_(1/2). The parameter integral is exactly the signed sum of the 1296 permutation-pair terms obtained from two squared Vandermondes. For each resulting integer r it uses `(r^(-1/5)-r^(-1/4))/log r`, with continuous value `1/20` at r=1. This is a finite identity, not a positive-sieve replacement for the signed moment.

Now assume the full D20 estimate `Q(X)<<_(chi,epsilon) X^(1.74898+epsilon)` for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X. Put

    gamma=87449/100000=.87449,
    q=437/500=.874,
    gamma-q=49/100000=.00049.

Taking square roots and using UR5 gives

    ||H|| <= O(X^(gamma+epsilon/2))+O(X^q)+X^(-1+o(1)).

Thus `||H||^2<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)` for every epsilon>0. One may directly use `(u+v+w)^2<=3(u^2+v^2+w^2)`. If expanded instead, the largest target-tail cross term has exponent `gamma+q+epsilon/2=1.74849+epsilon/2`, and the median square has exponent `2q=1.748`; both lie below `2gamma+epsilon=1.74898+epsilon`. All cross terms with the product-tail norm are much smaller. Mixed terms between the three discarded sectors are also included in UR5's norm triangle inequality and its square. Every mixed contribution is paid below the claimed target exponent.

UR4 then excludes all zeros of the specified ordinary L-function in

    Re s>.87449,

so `c=1-gamma=.12551` follows CONDITIONALLY. For the family conclusion the same D20 hypothesis is required separately for every ordinary character. A zeta-only D20 theorem yields only the zeta conclusion.

The optional inherited-calibration computation D21 also checks. If the full H norm has exponent `beta=.8749` and R=H-Z has exponent q=.874, then

    | ||H||^2-||Z||^2 | <=2||H||||R||+||R||^2
                      <<X^(1.7489+epsilon)+X^(1.748+epsilon).

Its largest exponent is below 1.74898 by `1/12500=.00008`; choose the arbitrary calibration buffer correspondingly small when a strict comparison is wanted. This includes both ordered mixed terms and the error square. The direct norm implication does not need this smaller calibration margin.

The E_delta field is also correctly priced in D12--D13: each of its three products has every shift at least delta, giving `|e_delta(n)|<=4d_3(n)n^(-delta)`, hence a uniform weighted absolute norm at `4/5+epsilon` and a Gaussian field `O(x^(4/5+epsilon))`. E is already included in H's actual coefficients and in D20; it is not silently removed in the moment target. The cofactor absolute coefficient norm at beta>3/5 likewise follows from beta+2delta>1. These facts validate the optional baseline calibration but supply no new signed estimate.

The diagonal is `X^(1+o(1))`: w<=d3, `d3(n)^2<=d9(n)`, `K_X(n,n)<=constant`, and `B_X=X^(1+o(1))` give this by `sum_(n<=t)d9(n)<=t(1+log t)^8`. The coefficient inequality can be seen prime by prime: any pair of weak three-part compositions of k is the row/column margin pair of a nonnegative 3 by 3 integer matrix of total k. Choose one such matrix deterministically; different margin pairs give different matrices. Counting matrices gives `binom(k+2,2)^2<=binom(k+8,8)`, and multiplicativity finishes. Therefore the true remaining estimate concerns the complete signed off-diagonal, not an omitted diagonal or analytic tail.

## UR7. Fixed delta=2: norm 20 and the complete inverse readout

This argument is separate from small-shift D20. It applies to any coefficient sequence with `|a(n)|<=1`, a(1)=1 and `|a(2)|=1`. At delta=2 the `(1,2)` cofactor coefficient is

    c2=(9/256)a(2),
    C2(s)=c2 2^(-s)(1+R(s)),

where R has dilation arguments `r=mn/2>=3/2`. If coefficients with a repeated product coalesce, taking the sum of their absolute tuple weights remains an upper bound. On Re s=-1,

    sum_r |R_r|r
      <= [sum_(m<n) (mn)^(-3)(m^(-2)-n^(-2))^2]/(9/128)-1.

The denominator is exactly the first `(1,2)` term. Expanding the square and pairing `(m,n)` with `(n,m)` gives the exact positive sum `zeta(3)zeta(7)-zeta(5)^2`. There is no dropped factor of two. Integral bounds on the zeta tails at cutoff 32 give the rational upper bound in D23. The independent script recomputes it with exact fractions and verifies

    q_R <= .9468750294472809... <19/20,
    1/(1-q_R)<20.

The displayed decimal is diagnostic only; the comparison is exact rational arithmetic. Since `r^(-Re s)<=r` for Re s>=-1,

    |C2(s)| >= |c2|2^(-Re s)(1-q_R)
                    >=(9/5120)2^(-Re s).

The cofactor is therefore nonzero throughout that entire half-plane at all heights.

In the weighted discrete measure algebra with norm `sum|b_r|r`, multiplicative convolution is submultiplicative. Hence

    nu=sum_(j>=0)(-R)^(star j),
    sum_r |nu_r|r <=1/(1-q_R)<20.

All nonidentity atoms have r>=3/2. Repeated labels are coalesced by signed summation, never deleted. Local finiteness of the inverse support is genuine: if a product of atoms is at most X, every atom is at most X, its integer numerator mn is at most 2X, and there are at most `log X/log(3/2)` factors. Thus the sum over r<=X is finite.

Let `M_tau(x)=sum a(n)g_tau(log(n/x))`. The cofactor multiplication means

    H2(x)-E2^g(x)=c2 [(1+R)*M_tau](x/2),

where `[R*M](y)=sum R_r M(y/r)`. Applying nu therefore gives the exact direction of the dilation in D25:

    M_tau(x)=c2^(-1)sum_r nu_r [H2(2x/r)-E2^g(2x/r)].

Absolute convergence can be checked without a formal inversion argument: M has at most linear growth, H2 at most polynomial/logarithmic growth, and their Gaussian left tails are uniform on bounded positive intervals. On `0<t<=T`, each is bounded by `C_T t^(-1)`. Thus at fixed x the nu field sums are bounded by a constant times `sum|nu_r|r`, and the double convolution is absolutely convergent by the product of the corresponding weighted norms. Inserting the coefficient identity for `nu*(1+R)` is legitimate.

For the finite version, `|e2(n)|<=4d3(n)n^(-2)` gives `E2^g(t)=O_epsilon(t^(-1+epsilon))` for every t>0. For 0<epsilon<1,

    sum_r |nu_r| |E2^g(2x/r)|
       <<x^(-1+epsilon) sum_r |nu_r|r^(1-epsilon)
       <<X^(-1+epsilon), X<=x<=2X.

For the omitted H2 part r>X, the argument t=2x/r lies below 4; the Gaussian left tail gives `|H2(t)|<=C/t` on `(0,4]`. Consequently

    sum_(r>X)|nu_r| |H2(2x/r)|
                     <=C/(2x) sum_(r>X)|nu_r|r=O(X^(-1)).

This proves D26 with its entire infinite complement. The r cutoff is applied to the fixed source H2, not to a source whose cutoff is frozen at the wrong x scale.

For odd-modulus ordinary characters the condition `|a(2)|=1` is automatic. For even moduli, the explicit repair a(2):=-1 changes F by the entire function `(chi(2)-1)2^(-s)=-2^(-s)`, retaining every pole and its principal part. The corresponding original physical field differs by one Gaussian atom, which is smaller than any power of X on `[X,2X]`. The repaired coefficients generally are not `mu(n)chi(n)` and their determinant must not use the unmodified D4 factorization; the author makes this distinction. The small-shift theorem and D20 use the original ordinary characters, without repair.

This anchor is an invertible filter of the original Gaussian arithmetic, not a proof of an improved moment. For example, at any fixed gamma>-1, a global power bound on H2 (with its harmless left tail) transfers to M through `sum|nu_r|r^(-gamma)<=20` and the paid E term. Conversely a bound on M transfers to H2 through the absolutely summable cofactor coefficients. An inverse formula alone cannot supply either improved bound, and delta=2 cannot be substituted for the required interval `[1/5,1/4]` without a new argument.

## UR8. Independent evidence, disposition and remaining work

The new `check_independent.py` computes the determinant by its six-term Leibniz expansion, independently of the author's three-term cofactor assembly, and compares it with the ordered Vandermonde convolution through output 120 at delta=2. It uses exact Gaussian rational numbers for the order-four character modulo 5 with chi(2)=i, retaining natural zeros at multiples of 5. It checks a nonreal output coefficient and prime-power annihilation. The zeta case is also checked. The same script recomputes the strict rational cofactor bound and all exponent margins; it records the frozen source hashes.

## 5. Unpaid arithmetic, objections and novelty relative to the record

The surviving explicit energy is

\[
 \int_{e^{-1}X}^{2eX}
 \left|
   \sum_{\substack{d,e>Y\\de\le8X}}\mu(d)\mu(e)
       \sum_{\ell\ge1}(-1)^{\ell+1}
                   V_{\delta_X}(\ell de/x)
 \right|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 \ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}.
 \tag{DPR16--OPEN}
\]

It is exactly OPEN-DP in its completed form, with the
arbitrarily small DP26 error removed in norm. Every
ordered cross term of the displayed square is still
present. The finite product cap is inserted before
Poisson; an equally valid remaining object is DP28
with all odd frequencies through its paid DP29 cutoff.
Neither object is bounded in this review.

The stated examples have the following actual ranges:
with eta=.20, kappa0=.02, the factor cap is X^.61,
restoration length X^.22 and folded diagonal X^1.20;
with eta=.70 and the same kappa0, the caps become
X^.86, X^.72 and X^1.70. Both parameter choices satisfy
eta+kappa0<1 and the diagonal inequality eta<.74898
at a=.87449. These arithmetic ranges, including the
very long individual factors, are genuine costs.

For comparison with the derivative construction, take
the ordinary zero-mass profile
psi_delta=(1+u d/du)V_delta. Direct calculation gives

\[
 \int_0^\infty \psi_\delta(u)^2du
   =\delta^{-3}\int_{-1}^1
        (k'(v)+\delta k(v))^2e^{\delta v}dv
   \asymp\delta^{-3}
 \quad(\delta\longrightarrow0).
 \tag{DPR17}
\]

Here ||k'||_2>0 because a nonzero smooth compactly
supported probability density cannot be constant.
This independently verifies the normalization cost
used in DP's comparison; it is not an appeal to an
unreviewed construction. By contrast, the fixed
coefficient factor has the paid diagonal DPR6.

The quoted existing Mertens bound gives
sum_(n<=z) A(n)=M(z)-2M(z/2)=O(z^b).
Partial summation through V_delta costs its total
variation O(delta^(-1)), giving O(X^b/delta) on
the shell. This computation is correct and provides
no new exponent sufficient for DPR16--OPEN.
It is not a claim that this elementary bound is the
best possible one under every extra structural use
of the baseline.

The strongest objections I attempted were:

- **The probability transfer might hide an inverse width.**
  DPR2 exhibits the exact weight 0<=w_X<=1. It uses the
  same delta_X throughout the expanded shell. A theorem
  only for the varying width delta_y would not suffice
  without a further comparison, but it is not the
  hypothesis asserted in OPEN-DP.
- **The master multiplier could lose zeros at high heights.**
  DPR1--3 establish that M has no zero in Re s>0.
  Its possible small size there does not affect the
  qualitative holomorphic contradiction. No bounded
  inverse multiplier or quantitative high-height
  reciprocal-zeta estimate is claimed.
- **Folding could erase exact 2-adic resonances.**
  DPR4--5 retain the cross-density 4/(3zeta(2)), in
  addition to the direct density 3/zeta(2). The
  resulting 13/(3zeta(2)) is the correct constant.
  The natural zeros at valuation at least three
  and at odd square factors remain.
- **The Type I sum could recover a main term or a Y^2 cost.**
  DPR8 has only half-integer dual frequencies, and
  DPR10 retains both harmonic denominators. Fixed
  high derivative order prices the whole Type I
  sum uniformly. It does not give a bound for the
  surviving Type II energy.
- **The reciprocal expression could discard large
  factors or frequency tails.** DPR11 freezes a cap
  that contains every original physical term on
  the whole shell. DPR12--14 sum every omitted
  frequency and every ordered pair, including
  physically zero pairs added by the fixed cap.
  There is no unpriced cutoff dependence on x.
- **A positive kernel could turn its diagonal into
  a whole-energy lower bound.** A(N)A(M) has both
  signs. The diagonal calculation is a component
  cost; no lower bound on OPEN-DP's whole energy
  is used or accepted.

None produces a mathematical repair to DP1--30.
The surviving objection is substantive but already
acknowledged by the source: the new signed arithmetic
estimate is still hard and entirely unproved. Removing
a derivative normalization and the Type I zero-frequency
term does not control the complete long-factor energy.

### Comparison with T10 and N28

I read T10 in the [private research revision] consolidated proof and the
N28.C entry in the merged portfolio. T10 already
constructs discrete and continuous dilation criteria
for the actual Mertens function, identifies their
Mellin multipliers and proves the conditional
zero-exclusion bridge. N28.C develops their logarithmic
increment/overlap interpretation and explicitly keeps
the arithmetic cross-scale energy open.

DP's equality
F_(A,delta)(x)=F_(mu,delta)(x)-2F_(mu,delta)(x/2)
is the same broad dilation mechanism. The generic
shell-to-holomorphy proof is likewise old in that
record. In DP the extra local multiplier's zeros
lie on Re s=1, already outside the new target strip;
one fixed prime factor therefore suffices for the
qualitative bridge. This does not upgrade the
old open dilation energy to a theorem.

The specific checked combination is narrower:
an infinitely refinable compact probability kernel,
an exact frozen-width norm transfer, the fixed
arithmetic pole-killing factor, its fully folded
diagonal and the uniform alternating completion
with its capped reciprocal-frequency return.
Those particular identities and normalizations
are not furnished by the T10/N28 statements read.
The source correctly calls this a developed child
of that route, not a new portfolio family or a
literature-priority claim. The present acceptance
does not establish a broader novelty search.

### 5.1 W40-11 — the proposed full operator bound fails for the actual critical split

For a Hermitian block M=[[a,z],[conj(z),d]],

    M<=lambda I iff lambda>=a,d and
                    |z|^2<=(lambda-a)(lambda-d).    (W40.17)

This follows directly from the two principal minors of lambda I-M, including equality cases. Its largest eigenvalue is(a+d+sqrt((a-d)^2+4|z|^2))/2. Improving only the a-sector cannot pay d or the cross block.

Use the canonical actual split F=T_z+R_z of [private research revision], with z=kappa sqrt X, fixed tau and kappa^2>=2exp(3tau). The accepted critical profile gives ||R_z||_[X,2X] comparable to X/(log X)^2. The actual two-vector Gram matrix has d=||R_z||^2, so its largest eigenvalue is at least d, of order X^2/(log X)^4. A whole-matrix bound O(X^(2gamma)) for any gamma<1 is impossible for this actual matrix, even though the particular direction(1,1) can be much smaller. This conclusion uses the canonical unmasked profile, not the unintegrated gcd-one result or a hereditary mask transfer.

The surviving source target is precisely the directional cancellation already retained in [private research revision]: both ordered TR and RT terms and the amplitude mismatch. The frozen f3 A29b further diagnoses the all-g hard mask, but is evidence for independent review and is not newly accepted here. Repackaging the full matrix as a Schur complement does not lower its norm. This is a useful rejection of this stronger implementation, not a new obstruction to every directional dual certificate.

## DQ3--DQ5. Exact Type-I addback and a coefficient obstruction

Use the actual source decomposition

`I_Y=-m_Y*m_Y*1`, `m_Y=mu 1_(q<=Y)`, `C=J[mu]`.

The CP21 source identity is

\[
 J[v]_k(cB^3)=q_B\xi(B)\overline{G(c)}\theta_c(k)
 \sum_{t\mid B}w_t v(ct^3)1_{(t,k)=1},
 \qquad w_t=q_t^{-1/2}\overline\xi(t).
\]

For `t|B,u|E` define

`r(t,u)=product_(p|tu,p not dividing ce) p`,
`Delta_r(z;eta)=product_(p|r)(1-eta(p)q_p^(-z))`.

The exact Mellin coefficient for the II addback is

\[
 \mathcal I_Y(c,e;B,E;z)=
 \sum_{t\mid B,\ u\mid E}
 w_t\overline{w_u}\,I_Y(ct^3)I_Y(eu^3)
 \Delta_{r(t,u)}(z;\eta).
 \tag{DQ3}
\]

Primes of `tu` dividing `ce` already have natural zero and do not require a
second deletion. Own-column overlaps remain allowed. These factors are
`Delta_r(z;eta)` on the original row line, not guessed factors at `1-z`.

Let `W_D(c,e;B,E)` be the two balanced core selectors times
`bar(W0(q_c q_B^3/D)) W0(q_e q_E^3/D)`. The ordinary FE is

`L(z,eta)=A(z)(q_c q_e)^(1/2-z) epsilon(eta)L(1-z,bar eta)`,

where

`A(z)=3^(1/2-z)(2 pi)^(2z-1) Gamma(1-z)/Gamma(z)`.

The exact Gauss cancellation is
`beta(c) bar(beta(e)) epsilon(eta)=mu(c)mu(e)eta(lambda)`.
Consequently the fixed-class projection of the original signed CC-minus-II
kernel, on `0<a<2/3`, is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(a)}&\widetilde R(z)A(z)(K/D^2)^z q_d^{z-1}\!
\sum_{\substack{c,e>1\ {\rm sf},\ (cB^3,eE^3)=1\\
                 \eta|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\sqrt{q_cq_e}(q_Bq_E)^{1+3z}\xi(B)\overline\xi(E)\,
W_D(c,e;B,E)\\
&\qquad\times\psi_d(c)\overline{\psi_d(e)}Z_{ce}(3-3z)
\left[\mu(c)\mu(e)-\mathcal I_Y(c,e;B,E;z)\right]\,dz.
\end{aligned}
\tag{DQ4}
\]

The core powers follow exactly from
`(ce)^(1/2-z)(c B^3/D)^z(e E^3/D)^z
=sqrt(ce)D^(-2z)(B E)^(3z)`.
There is one row Mellin variable. This formula applies the same class
projector to both signed terms. It does not import the whole-II bound into a
restricted dual-class theorem, nor identify this analytic class with a physical
cube-row projection.

There is an immediate coefficient counterexample to universal CC--II
identification. Take `B=E=1`, `c=pq`, `e=r`, with distinct primes all beyond
the Type-I cutoff, in permitted unit-neutral ray sectors. Then

\[
 I_Y(c)=I_Y(e)=-1,\qquad
 \mu(c)\mu(e)-I_Y(c)I_Y(e)=-2.
 \tag{DQ5}
\]

Such columns can be taken in balanced norm ranges whenever the cutoff permits
two rough factors in one column, as in the intended application. More generally
the local coefficient identity already holds independently of a range choice.
For `d=lambda`, `psi_d(c)=1` on good cores, so the same discrepancy occurs in
the principal fixed-ray class. It persists in the class pole coefficient.
This disproves a termwise or universal coefficient/pole equality with II. It
does not disprove a separate aggregate signed cancellation theorem.

Test the literal ordinary reciprocal source before abstract chain language. Let S be all primes <=Y, `m_S(n)=mu(n)1_(all prime factors of n lie in S)`, and let `1(n)=1`. Then

    (1*m_S)(n)=1_(P^-(n)>Y),
    e_S=delta_1-1*m_S=-1_(n>1, P^-(n)>Y).              (R15)

The first identity is inclusion–exclusion over the S-primes dividing n. It retains all rough prime powers and products, not only singleton primes. For a fixed ordinary character replace the two coefficient sequences by chi and `m_S chi`; the error becomes `-chi(n)1_(n>1,P^-(n)>Y)`, with literal zeros. Multiplicativity of chi proves the identity without removing a ramified term by hand.

In the convolution Banach algebra with norm `sum |a(n)|n^-sigma`, the exact error norm is

    ||e_S||_sigma=product_(p>Y)(1-p^-sigma)^-1-1       (R16)

when sigma>1, and is infinite for every sigma<=1. For fixed Y, the divergence needs no new PNT: the progression `n=1 mod product_(p<=Y)p` is rough and has positive density. For a fixed character also use `n=1 mod q` so its absolute value is 1. Thus no small absolute coefficient norm exists in the desired strip. Even a growing cutoff `Y<=N/2` leaves a finite-prefix lower bound

    ||e_S 1_(n<=N)||_sigma >= sum_(N/2<p<=N, p>Y)p^-sigma
       >> N^(1-sigma)/log N,                           (R17)

for fixed sigma<1 and sufficiently large N when Y<=N/2, by PNT. Fixed conductor exclusions remove only finitely many primes. This blocks that specific Neumann norm at the target exponents; it is not a lower bound for a signed physical field or every operator norm.

For every finite K, form the exact convolution polynomial

    v_K=m_S*(delta_1+e_S+...+e_S^(*K-1)).
    1*v_K=delta_1-e_S^(*K),
    mu=v_K+mu*e_S^(*K).                                (R18)

Twisting every coefficient by chi gives the identical character formulas. All omitted-prime interactions occur in the remainder. Initially on Re s>1, `M_S=product_(p<=Y)(1-chi(p)p^-s)` and `E=1-L M_S` give

    V_K=M_S sum_(j=0)^(K-1)E^j=(1-E^K)/L.             (R19)

At any hypothetical L-zero rho with Re rho>0, M_S(rho) is nonzero and E(rho)=1. The finite approximation is holomorphic there, with `V_K(rho)=K M_S(rho)`; its apparent reciprocal pole is cancelled. The remainder `E^K/L` retains the pole. Thus neither finite exact inversion nor a nilpotent finite divisor matrix supplies zero exclusion. Gaussian smoothing R18 is legitimate for fixed S,K by absolute coefficient bounds, but its complete remainder must still be controlled on every physical shell. A moving S or K additionally needs uniform constants and tails.

There is also a precise functional-space warning: in a unital Banach algebra of analytic functions with continuous evaluation at rho, multiplicativity of that evaluation gives `r_spectral(E)>=|E(rho)|=1`. A genuine submultiplicative norm with `||E||<1` throughout a region would already exclude such a zero; it cannot be assumed as free input. This does not prohibit a newly proved source-restricted contraction.

The finite check independently verifies all coefficients of R15/R18 through n=240, for Y=5, K=1,2,3,4, both untwisted and with the zero-extended character mod3. It proves only those finite identities; R15–19 have the written general proofs above. The geometric identity and lost-pole test overlap W43's actual Möbius Newton result; absolute inverse warnings and physical readout costs are already G32/MM-[restricted research revision]/W26/W36. The added audit makes this seed's full rough residual and intended norm explicit. **Disposition:** the default absolute perturbative inverse fails; a quantitatively paid different norm/physical contraction remains untested. ## R2. Exact block optimum and the actual-source isolation lemma

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q and put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), including its squareful and nonunit zeros. Let ell be the all-ones column. The certificate condition is the **global matrix inequality** P >= ell ell*. P may depend on the actual source, N and chi. This already implies P >= 0. Requiring the inequality only on a separately established reachable-state class is a different problem and is not ruled out here.

For a partition B_j, let b_j=sum_(n in B_j) a_n and B=sum_j |b_j|. The claimed block-diagonal optimum is correct:

    inf a*Pa = B^2, over block-diagonal P >= ell ell*.

For a lower bound, multiply each block of a by a unimodular scalar aligning its block sum. Its energy is unchanged while the global readout has modulus B. For the upper bound with every b_j nonzero, the block matrix (B/|b_j|)ell_j ell_j* has the required global majorant by weighted Cauchy, and energy B^2. If some b_j=0 and B>0, give the zero-sum blocks a total reciprocal-weight share delta>0 and scale the other blocks by 1/(1-delta); then let delta decrease to zero. If all b_j=0, sufficiently large finite block weights give energy zero. This validates the infimum formulation without inventing universal attainment or invertibility.

Now let I be squarefree q-units, of size K, isolated from every other nonzero source coordinate by the permitted off-diagonal support of P. Then P_II is diagonal and all actual I-to-complement cross terms vanish. The principal inequality P_II >= ell_I ell_I* gives

    sum_(n in I) P_nn >= K^2.

Since |a_n|=1 there and the complementary principal block is PSD,

    a*Pa >= K^2.                                      (R2.1)

No signs of the isolated coefficients were assumed to agree. Positivity was used for the complementary **quadratic form**, not as a claim that omitted signed Mertens terms are nonnegative. The same proof holds on the support-only coordinate space. Original integer labels must still determine bandwidth and offsets.

This is a certificate obstruction, not |M_chi(N)| >= K. The dense admissible P=ell ell* has energy exactly |M|^2; it can use all distant cross terms. A source-only inequality or a nonlocal signed observer can therefore escape (R2.1).

### T09a. One fixed Möbius profile

Let
\[
V(u)=e^{-u-u^{-1}},\quad
\phi(u)=(uV(u))',\quad
S_\phi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\phi(n/x).
\]
For \(0<a<1\), suppose for every \(\epsilon>0\) and every sufficiently large dyadic \(X\),
\[
\int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\,\frac{dx}{x}
\ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}. \tag{T09.1}
\]
Then \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>a\).

Indeed, on \(\Re s\ge a+\delta\), Cauchy bounds the Mellin contribution of one shell by \(X^{-\delta+\epsilon/2}\). Taking \(\epsilon<2\delta\) makes the dyadic sum and every fixed complex derivative converge locally uniformly. At zero the function is exponentially small. Thus
\[
F(s)=\int_0^\infty S_\phi(x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
\]
is holomorphic for \(\Re s>a\). Initially \(F(s)=\Phi(s)/\zeta(s)\), where [restricted research revision] proves
\[
\Phi(s)=2(1-s)K_s(2).
\]
For completeness, a zero \(K_s(2)=0\) would give \(f(t)=K_s(2e^t)\), \(t\ge0\), with Dirichlet boundary and
\[
\int_0^\infty(|f'|^2+4e^{2t}|f|^2)\,dt
=-s^2\int_0^\infty|f|^2\,dt>0.
\]
Hence such \(s\) is purely imaginary. Therefore \(\Phi\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>0\) except \(1\). Continue
\[
(s-1)\zeta(s)F(s)=(s-1)\Phi(s).
\]
Any proposed zeta zero in \(\Re s>a\) contradicts the nonzero right side. No uniform lower bound for \(\Phi(\sigma+it)\) is used.

The exact positive scale kernel is
\[
\int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
=\sum_{m,n}\mu(m)\mu(n)
\int_1^2\phi(m/(Xt))\overline{\phi(n/(Xt))}\frac{dt}{t}.
\]
The arithmetic coefficients retain signs and all shared primes.

### All ten exact first tests

**S04: small-prime conditioning.** For finite P contained in primes>=5, let f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) and f_P(n)=f(n)1_(gcd(n,product P)=1). The exact Dirichlet-convolution multiplier that reconstructs f from f_P has local series 1-z-z^2-z^3-..., not 1-z. Thus every eliminated prime power is retained. Its positive reconstruction price is product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)^-1. A moving P is affordable in a strict subpower range, but its source estimate must keep the parent cutoff frozen on cofactor shells. **Pass as a source-specific conditional bridge; developed D04.**

**S15: central covariance plus absolute complement.** Current-proof G23 already proves the full actual-f3 far-pair bound X^(2-r^2/(4tau)+o(1)) outside |log(n/m)|<=r sqrt(log X). To pay this below a target 2gamma-eta, choose r^2>=4tau(2-2gamma+eta). The true diagonal is O(X). This merely specializes G23; central signed energy is still open, and no H saving can be added. **Duplicate quantitative split, not a new survivor.**

**S45: weak negative Sobolev proposal.** For the finite actual coefficient measure nu=sum c(n)delta_(log(n/X)), r>1/2 gives

    ||g_tau*nu||_(L2(R))^2
       <= M_(tau,r) ||nu||_(H^-r(R))^2,
    M_(tau,r)=sup_t exp(-tau*t^2)(1+t^2)^r < infinity.

This follows directly from Fourier multipliers. The proposed rational frequency weight is a *stronger sufficient all-height estimate* than the Gaussian weight; it is not a weakening of the needed arithmetic cancellation. It also controls the full line, whereas the original energy is shell-local. A fixed smoothing or primitive multiplier nonzero at s=rho does not change the growth exponent of an e^(rho u) mode. **Valid conditional organization, existing D-GREEN/A-GRAPH ancestry; no new arithmetic norm or relaxed input. Parked after first test.**

**S51: Koszul detector.** Contraction d by the all-one covector and exterior multiplication h by a chosen generator obey dh+hd=I: the augmented complex is acyclic. A sharp mask introduces [d,P]. W37 T15/D28 already supply this obstruction and a paid-boundary repair; finite Euler zeros cannot replace the infinite reciprocal limit. **Duplicate failure.**

**S31: divisor Stokes boundary.** For n=pq with distinct primes p,q<=Y<pq, sum_(d|n,d<=Y)mu(d)=1-1-1=-1. The full Boolean rectangle adds mu(pq)=+1 and sums to zero. Truncation leaves exactly the omitted top face. For the actual Gaussian d,e,ell source W37 D28 supplies the stronger fixed-total-product boundary identity, including the masks. **Exact boundary failure duplicates U-PRIME-CHAIN/W37; no new saving.**

**S33: finite marginal LP.** Retain the actual local sign (-1)^(1_(p|n)), including p=2 and excluding p=3. Chinese-remainder independence on one complete period gives exact pair correlations, but the single-field average is identically zero because of prime 2. Gaussian smoothing makes that periodic field rapidly small. The full f3 field is not that finite local model. **Pass as a restricted source-specific calculation and failure diagnosis; developed D33.**

**S37: complex saddle contour.** For 0<r<1, averaging log|1-r exp(it log p)| over its full height period gives zero, by the absolutely convergent logarithmic series. A fixed imaginary shift leaves this average unchanged. Thus avoiding the finite Euler factor's zeros alone cannot provide a strictly smaller modulus at all heights, even in the one-prime test. An adaptive contour would still need its exact source integral, Jacobian, growth and residue payments. **Scoped failed free-contour gain; broader arithmetic saddle estimates remain untested.**

**S54: smallest missing-prime involution.** The cut top face from S31 survives. A source-compatible pivot is fixed as a function of d*ell and preserves de*ell. W37 D28.6 permits ANY odd-prime pivot, already including “smallest.” **Duplicate boundary mechanism.**

**S57: arithmetic differential forms.** Each d log(1-chi(p)p^-s) is a multiple of ds, so its wedge with another is zero. Independent formal prime coordinates require a new paid diagonal readout. **Scalar wedge fails; broader multivariable constructions remain open.**

**S06: contour index.** B_a(z)=(z-a)/(1-a z), 0<a<1, has a zero, B_a(1)=1 and |B_a|=1 on the whole circle. Winding one coexists with the constant function's boundary L2 norm. statement:
## 3. Exact two-prime source in the Gaussian central range

Put `z=X^rho` and choose

    nu=(3rho_0-1)/2>0,       U=X^(1+nu).

For every rho in the compact range, U<z^3. If n<=U and omega_z(n)>=2,
then n has EXACTLY two distinct prime factors p<q above z, each with
valuation one. A third occurrence of a rough prime, including a repeated
one, would force n>z^3. Write n=rpq. Then

    r<=U/z^2<z,

so r automatically has no prime factor above z, and p,q do not divide r.
Since z>3 for all sufficiently large X,

    f(rpq)=f(r)f(p)f(q)=f(r).

This keeps every valuation in r; it is not a squarefree-core reduction.
Consequently, for n<=U, the original coefficient in R_z is EXACTLY

    sum_(p<q, p,q>z, pq|n) f(n/(pq)).                ([restricted research revision])

Extend the right side to the full Gaussian and define

    S_z(x)=sum_(z<p<q) sum_(r>=1) f(r)g(log(rpq/x)). ([restricted research revision])

The completion beyond U is paid, not asserted exact. For each n, the
number of selected prime pairs is at most omega(n)^2, hence at most a
fixed multiple of `(1+log n)^2`. The original coefficient is bounded
by one. Since `log(U/x)>=nu L-log2`, the complete Gaussian tail with
this polynomial/logarithmic multiplicity is O_A(X^(-A)) for any fixed
A>0, uniformly on the closed shell. For example, bound the multiplicity
by n^epsilon, dominate half of the Gaussian by its value beyond
`nu L/2`, and sum the other half with its finite tilted lattice moment.
The resulting fixed power of X times `exp(-c_(nu,tau)L^2)` is smaller
than every prescribed power. Thus

    R_z(x)=S_z(x)+O_A(X^(-A)).                       ([restricted research revision])

This accounts for all extra rough primes, all repeated rough prime
powers, and all labels introduced by extending ([restricted research revision]). There is no
uncapped finite-terminal assertion: the full tail is present in ([restricted research revision]).

The finite helper records explicit failures of ([restricted research revision]) ABOVE its range:
at z=5, n=7^2*11 and n=7*11*13, the global two-prime completion has the
wrong coefficient. Those are exactly the configurations priced by
([restricted research revision]), not silently ignored algebraic exceptions.

statement:
## 1. Exact universal collision count

For real D>=1 let W_D(n)=#{d<=D: n/d is an integer square}. Then, uniformly
for Y>=1,

    sum_{n<=Y} W_D(n)^2 << sqrt(Y D).                    (I1)

The implicit constant is absolute. To prove this, write every pair of
possible physical multipliers with the same squarefree kernel as
d1=a u^2,d2=a v^2, a squarefree. Their common square multiples are
n=a l^2 with l a multiple of lcm(u,v). Thus the exact identity is

    sum_{n<=Y} W_D(n)^2
      = sum_{a squarefree; a<=D} sum_{u,v<=sqrt(D/a)}
          floor(sqrt(Y/a)/lcm(u,v)).                    (I2)

Pairs with different squarefree kernels have no common square multiple.
Using floor(t)<=t and then interchanging the nonnegative sums gives

    LHS <= sqrt(Y) sum_{u,v>=1} gcd(u,v)/(uv)
                  sum_{a<=D/max(u,v)^2} a^(-1/2)
        <= 2sqrt(YD) sum_{u,v>=1} gcd(u,v)/(uv max(u,v)).

The last series converges. Write u=g h,v=g k with gcd(h,k)=1 and drop
that last restriction: it is bounded by

    (sum_g g^(-2)) 2 sum_{k>=1} k^(-2) sum_{h<=k} h^(-1),

which is finite by H_k<=1+log k. This proves (I1), including all repeated
physical multipliers, exact diagonal collisions and nonintegral cutoffs.
It imports no arithmetic cancellation or outside counting theorem.
title: 1. Exact universal collision count

## R7. Exact counted reduction and all complements

Let B_hi be the original physical high-row set, with its fixed natural family and actual slot weights. If enlarged internal bins are required, their finite labels are included according to R3. Let B_sep be the subset that, after the preceding fixed easy-union removal, admits the compatible witnesses R6 and R11--R12 with the exponential-free annular profiles. Then, for every requested final epsilon>0 and the source's finite seminorm/polynomial-height factor,

    sum_(u in B_hi)|Q_u|^2
       <<H_J U^(E_K(delta,v)-1/2000+epsilon)
          +sum_(u in B_sep)|Q_u|^2.                  (R16)

The first term pays the whole prefix, every easy inverse or plain witness in either presentation and both profile families, all too-long annuli, genuine terminal and Fourier tails, finite dictionary/internal-bin labels, dyadic and scale-supremum costs, real/height Sobolev derivatives, and nonempty bounded subunit windows. The aggregate exponent losses, including buffers and padded boundaries, are less than eta/2. The unspent eta is not reported as the final margin.

For the natural free family, exceptions supported entirely on the fixed bad-prime set have only finitely many valuation-mod-six and unit sectors. Their absolute slot mass is O_fixed(H_J U^(v+epsilon)), including the principal unit presentation. This is affordable because G<=3kv and

    delta-3k=4delta^2/(5-2delta)>0,
    E_K>=rho>=19/54.

If the original restoration has a fixed finite list of such raw free cores, its sixth-power roots have O(U^(1/6)) possibilities, so U^(1/6+v+epsilon) is also strictly below the paid exponent; the helper certifies rho>1/6+1/20+eta. This does not extend R16 to arbitrary raw moving-support families. Their actual root holes, normalization and child-width restrictions must still be established before a raw density statement. No unit row is declared oscillatory or removed from a negative-power target.

No squarefree substitute for A_R(n), no arbitrary row selector in Poisson, and no absolute replacement of the full signed detector is used. R16 is a counted necessary-condition reduction. It is not a theorem about an independently selected signed cross-class pair slice. ## 6. Reviewer addition: bounded variation suffices without fixed J

Here is the completed refinement from the pre-deadline proof reconstruction.
Let J=J_X be any finite number, keeping sum lambda_j=1 and
sum |lambda_j|<=Lambda with Lambda fixed. Retain the same principal-character
source, fixed gamma,k,p,q, and moving-cut definition. There is a selection
of semiprimes in the literal core for which the bank projection still has
norm >>_{gamma,Lambda,k,p,q} X/log X, uniformly in J_X and the bank data.

Proof. Use F,delta,m from Section 5. Define a positive endpoint measure

    nu=sum_j |lambda_j|(delta_{t_j}+delta_{t_j+c}
                            +delta_{gamma-t_j}+delta_{1-t_j}).

Its total mass is at most 4Lambda. For any two arguments the change in F
is bounded by the nu-mass between them, including endpoints. If
kappa=log(n/X)/log X, the actual coefficient G(alpha,kappa) is obtained by
shifting each of the two upper endpoints by kappa. Hence, for |kappa|<=h,

    |G(alpha,kappa)-F(alpha)| <= nu([alpha-h,alpha+h]).

Choose h=c^2/(4096Lambda^2) and a fixed grid of cells of length h. Discard
the terminal strip [1/2-m/4,1/2] and the at most two partially intersecting
boundary cells of [delta,1/2-m/4]. Mark a full grid cell bad when the nu-mass
of its enlargement by h on both sides is greater than c/8. A point belongs
to at most four such closed enlarged cells. Therefore the sum of these
masses is at most 16Lambda, there are at most 128Lambda/c bad cells, and
their total length is at most c/(32Lambda)=m/4.

The good set E={alpha in [delta,1/2]: Re F(alpha)>=c/2} has measure at least
m. The discarded and bad portions have total length at most m/2+2h<m.
There is therefore a full good grid cell I containing some alpha_0 in E.
For every alpha in I the variation of F is at most c/8, and for every
|kappa|<=h the additional displacement error is at most c/8. Thus

    Re G(alpha,kappa)>=c/4,   |G(alpha,kappa)|<=2Lambda.

Choose a fixed a in (0,1/4] so small that (2a)^k<=c/(64Lambda). For all
sufficiently large X and n in [aX,2aX], one has |log(n/X)|/log X<h and
B(n)=L. For every x in [X,2X], theta=(n/x)^k satisfies
theta<=c/(64Lambda), and

    Re[G exp(-i theta)] >= c/8-2Lambda theta >= c/16.

The damping has a fixed positive lower bound. Select primes r with
log r/log X in I and s in (aX/r,2aX/r]. The cell has fixed length h and
is contained in [delta,1/2-m/4], so r<s for large X and each product has
a unique selected factorization. Ordinary PNT, followed by partial
summation for sum 1/r, gives >> X/log X such products uniformly in the
location of I. Removing the finitely many primes dividing pq is harmless.
All selected integers satisfy X^gamma<n<=X^r for large X. Their complete
merged bank coefficients have the positive real part just established.
The real part of the resulting projected sum is >> X/log X at every x
in the shell, proving both norm bounds.

No coefficient was made positive by replacing it with its absolute value.
The projection can depend on X and on the bank. The proof uses a fixed
coarse grid and bounded variation, not a fixed number of breakpoints.
It therefore rules out improving the separated positive-cell budget merely
by using more normalized cuts at bounded total variation. It does not rule
out cancellation with the complementary signed cells, unbounded variation,
or the different compensator used next. This addition has not undergone a
separate critic pass; its exact proof is supplied for root review.
title: 6. Reviewer addition: bounded variation suffices without fixed J
