statement:
## 2. D02: literal Euler correction and two-way norm transfer

### D02.1 Frozen source and normalization

Let K=Q(omega), and use PR9's primary-generator/ideal dictionary (one representative per nonzero ideal, no extra factor six). Fix one finite-order, trivial-infinity Hecke character eta and the source's finite exclusion S, including its conductor and primes above 6. All ideals below are coprime to S; equivalently coefficients are zero on every excluded prime power. Constants may depend on this fixed data. No growing-conductor or angular-family theorem is asserted.

For each remaining prime ideal p, let Q=Np, alpha(p)=p/|p| in the source's primary-generator convention, t=Q^-1, and, temporarily, z=Q^-s. Write

    a=eta(p), b=conjugate(alpha(p))^6 eta(p)^6,
    D=a z, R=b Q^3 z^6,     |a|=|b|=1.

PR9 B0.35 is exactly

    H_p(s)=(1-t^2)/(1-R) * (1+t(D-R)/(1-D)).                 (2.1)

Let C_S=product_(p notin S)(1-Q^-2)>0 and normalize H=C_S h. Then

    h_p = [1-(1-t)D-tR]/[(1-D)(1-R)].                       (2.2)

This scalar C_S is unrelated to PR9's physical residue scalar c_S in B0.36. Neither is suppressed by normalization. PR9's k is also retained: define P_eta(x)=x^k f_eta(x). Its transform is

    Mellin(P_eta)(s)=exp((s-5/6)^2) H_eta(s)/L_K^S(s,eta).   (2.3)

This is the **principal signal**. The physical probe J_eta, its compensator, all nonprincipal rows and their moment estimates are different objects.

### D02.2 Absolute coefficient and inverse budgets

For sigma>2/3 put d=Q^-sigma and r=Q^(3-6sigma). Since r<Q^-1 and d<Q^-2/3, the local Dirichlet-series weighted coefficient norms satisfy

    ||h_p-1||_sigma <= [r+t(d+r)/(1-d)]/(1-r) =: B_p^+,
    ||h_p^-1-1||_sigma
       <= [t d+(1-t)r+d r]/[1-(1-t)d-t r] =: B_p^-.       (2.4)

The first bound follows from (2.1) after removing 1-t^2. For the second, subtract 1 from (1-D)(1-R)/(1-(1-t)D-tR); the numerator is -tD-(1-t)R+DR. Its denominator is expanded in its actual convergent geometric series. Indeed

    (1-t)d+t r <= Q^(-2/3)+Q^-2 <= 2^(-2/3)+1/4 <1.

No local zero is hidden in the inverse. Both B_p^+ and B_p^- are

    O_sigma(Q^(-1-sigma)+Q^(3-6sigma)).                    (2.5)

Ideal counting N_K(T)=O_K(T) implies convergence of their sums. Therefore there are multiplicative, exact ideal coefficients h(a), j(a), with h*j=delta_1 and

    A_sigma=sum_a |h(a)| Na^-sigma <infinity,
    B_sigma=sum_a |j(a)| Na^-sigma <infinity.              (2.6)

For example A_sigma<=product(1+B_p^+) and B_sigma<=product(1+B_p^-). The products converge locally uniformly for Re s>2/3. Thus **the literal H_eta and its reciprocal are holomorphic and nonzero there**, with this coefficient proof; the source's previously used .87 half-plane is not the limit of this Euler correction. This does not extend the physical contour boxes, source moments or PR9 endpoint argument.

There is a real boundary to this absolute method. The exact sixth coefficient is

    h(p^6)=t a^6+(1-t)b Q^3.                              (2.7)

Its magnitude is at least (1-Q^-1)Q^3-Q^-1. The prime-ideal harmonic series diverges (equivalently, use the source's prime ideal theorem), so sum |h(a)|Na^-sigma diverges for sigma<=2/3. This only obstructs the stated absolute coefficient norm. It is not a lower bound on the signed Gaussian field or a universal c<=1/3 barrier.

### D02.3 Exact fixed-field identity

Set

    M_eta,tau(x)=sum_a mu_K(a) eta(a) g_tau(log(Na/x)),
    g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)).

The source zeros at S and the Möbius squarefree zeros remain exact. Absolute convergence and Gaussian tails justify all coefficient identities. For Re s>1,

    Mellin(M_eta,tau)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L_K^S(s,eta).

Since exp((s-5/6)^2)=exp(25/36) exp(-5s/3) exp(s^2), (2.3) gives

    P_eta(x)=C_S exp(25/36)
                  sum_a h(a) M_eta,2(exp(-5/3)x/Na),
    M_eta,2(x)=C_S^-1 exp(-25/36)
                  sum_a j(a) P_eta(exp(5/3)x/Na).          (2.8)

The real shift, width 2, scalar and original ideal coefficients are all necessary. These are absolutely convergent field identities, first checked on an absolute Mellin line and then by unique inversion. Polynomial coefficient growth follows already from any fixed absolute line, so the Gaussian also supplies direct locally uniform convergence. Composing the two series is justified on that line and by the same positive majorants.

For real-shell norm

    ||F||_[X,2X]=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^2 dx/x)^(1/2),
    ||F||_sigma=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||F||_[X,2X],

Minkowski gives the paid estimates

    ||P_eta||_sigma <= C_S exp(25/36-5sigma/3) A_sigma ||M_eta,2||_sigma,
    ||M_eta,2||_sigma <= C_S^-1 exp(-25/36+5sigma/3) B_sigma ||P_eta||_sigma. (2.9)

Every x/Na shell has its own scale. No moving arithmetic cutoff is kept at an incorrect parent scale. Gaussian left tails pay bounded/small shells; at most two adjacent dyadic shells cover a real shell. Thus the complete all-dyad moments for P_eta and M_eta,2 are equivalent at every exponent gamma>2/3, also with the usual every-positive-epsilon quantifier. At gamma=2/3 the every-epsilon version follows by using (2.9) at sigma=gamma+epsilon; no exact-power endpoint norm is asserted.

A bound for M_eta,2 with exponent gamma makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on Re s>gamma by dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz, including derivatives on smaller half-planes. Its Gaussian left tail pays zero. The multiplier never vanishes, so every zero of the same L_K^S in that region is excluded; its possible pole at 1 is allowed. This supplies the complete conditional zero return, independently of an unproved covariance claim. To recover a common boundary for the original entire fixed-family scope, the proposed moment hypothesis must hold for **each** fixed target with the same gamma and every positive epsilon; constants, exclusions and large-X thresholds may depend on the target. A result for one eta alone excludes zeros only for that target.

### D02.4 An explicit ordinary-Dirichlet return, with a paid width change

Here is a concrete bridge to the rational Gaussian architecture, rather than an identification of different coefficient lists. Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi with its actual zero extension, set psi=chi*chi_-3, and let eta(a)=chi(Na). Euler factors give

    L_K(s,eta)=L(s,chi)L(s,psi).                          (2.10)

At a split rational prime the two ideal factors equal the two same-sign Dirichlet factors; at an inert prime the product is (1-chi(p)^2 p^-2s)^-1; at 3 only the chi factor survives. Zeros at primes dividing the presented modulus persist on both sides. This proves the identity without an inferred primitive reduction.

First restore the fixed excluded ideal primes in M_eta,2 by the finite polynomial product_(p in S)(1-eta(p)Np^-s). Its inverse is the corresponding finite product of geometric series, absolutely summable at every positive weight. Thus the restoration has fixed cost and leaves the exponent unchanged. Call the resulting complete field M_eta,2^full.

Fix any delta>0 and put B(s)=1-2^(1-s). Define the **actual periodic** sequence and fixed field

    d_psi(n)=psi(n)-2*1_(2|n) psi(n/2),
    K_psi,delta(y)=sum_(n>=1) d_psi(n) g_delta(log(n/y)).

If psi has period q, d_psi has period 2q and total sum zero over that period, including when psi is principal. Poisson summation of the zero-extended Schwartz function g_delta(log t) on each residue class gives K_psi,delta(y)=O_A(y^-A) for every fixed A as y tends to infinity; the zero Fourier mode vanishes. Its left tail is Gaussian. Equivalently, m integrations by parts bound it by C_(m,q,delta)y^(1-m), with m fixed after A. Consequently

    I_(gamma,psi,delta)=integral_0^infinity |K_psi,delta(y)| y^-gamma dy/y <infinity (2.11)

for every fixed real gamma. The Mellin transform of K is exp(delta*s^2/2)B(s)L(s,psi), first on Re s>1; pole cancellation at s=1 is literal, not asserted away.

The multiplicative integral convolution therefore satisfies

    integral_0^infinity M_eta,2^full(x/y) K_psi,delta(y) dy/y
       = sum_n [mu(n)chi(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2)chi(n/2)]
                    g_(2+delta)(log(n/x)) =: G_chi,2+delta(x).             (2.12)

This numerator is B(s), not 1-2chi(2)2^-s; the second coefficient is written explicitly to avoid that error. It reduces exactly to current G1 when chi=1, at the permitted fixed width 2+delta. Minkowski and (2.11) give

    ||G_chi,2+delta||_gamma <= I_(gamma,psi,delta) ||M_eta,2^full||_gamma.   (2.13)

All convolution tails and shell dilations are paid. The new width is fixed before X. No inverse heat operation or estimate at width 1 is inferred. Since B has no zero in 0<Re s<1, this is a full conditional ordinary-Dirichlet zero return. The ideal result already covers each fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke target. It does not create a growing-conductor assertion.

This comparison shows a legitimate way easier **complete** estimates from the old principal signal could help the new detector. It says nothing that permits transplanting PR15 local moments to G13, F3 or the short-divisor H form without their missing arithmetic source adapters.

`ell` or divisor phases have bounded magnitude. Hence (UC5)--(UC11)
hold componentwise. The argument does not move a deleted Euler
product with conductor depending on the core or row.

For fixed-place row refinements, retain the exact local factors and

nontrivial good conductor `e`. Fixed-place factors are bounded on each
fixed strip `Re z>=delta>0`; fixed-prime valuation progressions have

good character. All fixed-prime row valuations and natural zeros are
therefore accounted for. This assertion covers the required fixed

No Mellin root of the original common profile has been moved or

## T08. Two-exponent finite-incidence transfer

**Status:** proved conditional implication relative to the inherited coefficient identities, holomorphy, tail estimates, common-profile separation, and completed-current criterion. The finite mean hypothesis remains open.

Let \(\mathbf D_h(s)\) be the complete finite ray/unit/deletion orbit required by FD, with its component norm. For squarefree good \(g\), the exact extraction identity is
\[
\mathbf D_h^{(g)}(s)
=\beta(g)\vartheta_g(h)q_g^{-s}\,
 U_{g,h}\mathbf D_{gh}(s),
\]
where \(U_{g,h}\) is unitary on the finite component orbit whenever the natural character is nonzero. A shared prime of \(g,h\) makes the entire term zero. Write
\[
\mathcal T(K,G;s)=
\sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm squarefree,good}\\q_g\le G}}
\sum_{0<q_h\le K}\|\mathbf D_h^{(g)}(s)\|^2.
\]
Suppose \(u,v\ge0\), \(3u+v<1\), and, for every fixed positive central buffer \(e\), every arbitrarily small loss \(\delta>0\), and every required fixed component/deletion family,
\[
\mathcal T(K,G;\tfrac12+e+it)
\ll (KG)^\delta K^{1+u}G^v(1+|t|)^A. \tag{T08.1}
\]
The constants may depend on the fixed data, buffers and specified profile seminorms; \(A\) cannot depend on moving \(K,G,t\). This is a finite trace, never an infinite \(G\)-limit.

Then the inherited current satisfies, for \(1\le K,G\le D\),
\[
|\mathfrak Q(D,K)|
\ll_\rho(DK)^\rho
\left(
 DK^{1+u}G^v+DK+
 D^2K^{1/3}G^{-1}
 +D^{5/3}K^{2/3}G^{-2/3}
\right). \tag{T08.2}
\]
Consequently,
\[
k_*=\frac{1+v/2}{1+u+v},\qquad
c_{u,v}=\frac{k_*-1/2}{3}
       =\frac{1-u}{6(1+u+v)}. \tag{T08.3}
\]
The zero-free conclusion concerns the open half-plane. For any proposed zero inside it, use a strict interior row exponent \(k<k_*\). No boundary-line assertion is needed.

### Proof of the energy implication

For the whole completed column FD (68) gives
\[
S_h^{(g)}(w)=L^S(3w-1,\xi)
\sum_{d\mid g}x_{g/d}(w)
\prod_{p\mid d}(1-x_p(w))D_h^{(d)}(w),
\quad x_a(w)=\xi(a)q_a^{1-3w}.
\]
This selector includes primes shared by a squarefree core and its outside cube. At \(\Re w=1/2+e\),
\[
|x_a|^2=q_a^{-1-6e},\qquad
\prod_{p\mid d}(1+|x_p|)\ll q_d^\delta.
\]
Divisor Cauchy therefore reduces the finite whole-column trace to (T08.1) with cutoff \(G/q_a\le G\), followed by an absolutely convergent \(a\)-sum. The angular factor is incorporated into the original radial cube profile \(\Phi_V\) of FD (69), whose nonzero angular type makes its lower endpoint rapidly decreasing. It is not divided out. Finite Mellin shifts use inherited independent holomorphy and polynomial height bounds. Squaring costs \(D^{1+2e}\); choose \(e\) and preliminary losses sufficiently small in terms of final \(\rho\). This gives the first term of (T08.2).

FD (71)–(72) supplies the unchanged large-divisor energies. The three resulting weights are
\[
\frac{DK}{q_dq_aq_j},\quad
\frac{D^2K^{1/3}}{q_d^2q_a^4q_j^4},\quad
\frac{D^{5/3}K^{2/3}}{q_d^{5/3}q_a^3q_j^3}.
\]
Their sums over \(q_aq_d>G\), with the original finite supports, are the final three terms in (T08.2). The natural core-divisor and \(j\)-overlap conditions remain intact.

Finally, FD §19.3 separates the original common product kernel before applying positive Cauchy in the same divisor/row indices. This step preserves the signed coprime covariance, all original total-column profiles, radial norm twists and both separately paid zero terms. It does not apply a signed estimate to an arbitrarily partitioned profile.

Set \(G=\max(K^{1/3},KD^{-1/2})\). If \(K\le D^{3/4}\), the first term is at most
\[
D^{7/4+3u/4+v/4},
\]
which is strictly below \(D^2\) by \(3u+v<1\). If \(K=D^k\), \(k\ge3/4\), its exponent is
\[
1-v/2+k(1+u+v)<2
\]
for \(k<k_*\). Both tails are at most \(D^2\), and \(DK\le D^2\). Exact equality in a tail is harmless: M (2.18) asks for \(D^{2+\epsilon}\), with arbitrarily small loss. It does not require a power saving below \(D^2\) in every term. This proves the conditional current criterion and (T08.3).

### Exact incidence and what it selects

The extraction identity gives
\[
\mathcal T(K,G;s)=
\sum_{q_k\le KG}\|\mathbf D_k(s)\|^2
\sum_{\substack{
g\mid\operatorname{rad}_{=1}(k)\\
q_g\le G,\ q_k/q_g\le K}}
q_g^{-2\Re s}. \tag{T08.4}
\]
The radical contains only primes of valuation exactly one. This is an equality after summing the full finite orbit: the component switches are permutations/unitary phases. For \(G\le K\), prime rows above \(K\), pure prime squares above \(K\), and pure cubes above \(K\) receive zero weight. A positive ordinary mean through \(KG\) charges rows absent from this incidence. Conversely \(g=1\) still requires an ordinary mean through \(K\); counting divisors alone cannot prove the desired trace.

### New merge corollary: common-completed finite incidence is equivalent

Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal T}(K,G;s)=\sum_{g,h}\|F(s)\mathbf D_h^{(g)}(s)\|^2\), with exactly the same finite index set as \(\mathcal T\). On every buffered strip, (T08.1) is equivalent, up to arbitrary losses and a polynomial height factor, to its version for \(\widetilde{\mathcal T}\). In one direction multiply by the fixed polynomially bounded \(F\). In the other, apply T01 to the single finite holomorphic vector \((\mathbf D_h^{(g)})_{g,h}\); its estimate is dimension-free, and neighboring lines give the required local bound. Moving finite deletions cost at most \((KG)^\delta\). Thus no arithmetic exponent is lost by a **common scalar completion** of this finite incidence.

This completes a merger of T01 with the two-exponent transfer. The symbol \(F\mathbf D_h^{(g)}\) means completion of the forced squarefree-core series. It is not the whole-column selector \(S_h^{(g)}\), which additionally counts primes in the outside cube through T02. Nor does formal multiplication by \(F\) establish a missing current-period realization or align differently completed ray components. Those obligations remain exactly as stated in T01–T02.

### New merge corollary: only the actual divisor corridor is needed

It is enough to assume (T08.1), uniformly in all scales and fixed data, only for
\[
1\le G\le C K^\gamma,\qquad
\gamma=\frac{1-u}{2+v}
      =1-\frac1{2k_*}>\frac13, \tag{T08.5}
\]
where a fixed multiplicative constant \(C\) is harmless. This closes the profile obligation left open in BA's prototype corridor.

For annular equal-length columns, if \(K\le D^k\) and \(k<k_*\), then
\[
K^{1/3}\le K^\gamma,\qquad
KD^{-1/2}\le K^{1-1/(2k)}\le K^\gamma.
\]
The chosen selector split therefore never leaves (T08.5). The cube-selector formula only shortens \(G\).

For the original unbounded profiles, retain the exact common-kernel separation of FD §19.3. On a block of column lengths \(D_1,D_2\) and effective row length \(K'\), first set
\[
D_*=\max\{2,D_1,D_2,(K')^{1/k}\}.
\]
Use one common cutoff
\[
G=\max\{(K')^{1/3},K'D_*^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Then \(K'\le D_*^k\) and \(G\le(K')^\gamma\). Both positive column energies are bounded using the common larger scale \(D_*\); any support rescaling costs only fixed polynomial factors in \(D_*/D_i\), exactly of the kind allowed in the inherited positive profile bounds. Since \(K\le D^k\) and \(K'\) is the original row dyad times \(D_1D_2/D^2\),
\[
\frac{(K')^{1/k}}D
\ll \left(
\text{row-dyad factor}\,\frac{D_1}{D}\frac{D_2}{D}
\right)^{1/k}.
\]
Thus \(D_*/D\), and every rescaled-seminorm cost, is polynomial in the original scale ratios and their inverses. More explicitly, with \(r_i=D_i/D\) and normalized row-dyad factor \(R_{\rm row}\),
\[
 D_*/D\ll 1+r_1+r_2+(R_{\rm row}r_1r_2)^{1/k}.
\]
The retained rapid column tails and the rapid upper row Fourier tail sum these costs. Below \(R_{\rm row}=1\), this enlargement introduces no adverse negative power of \(R_{\rm row}\); the nonempty dyads with \(K'\ge1\) cost at most a logarithm in the scales. Effective row lengths below one use M §2.4's original Fourier-decay estimate. All epsilons are fixed before summing, and \(k\) is fixed strictly below \(k_*\). The full-profile conclusion therefore follows from the corridor hypothesis.

For \((u,v)=(1/8,1/32)\), the exact corridor is \(G\le CK^{28/65}\), and the conditional constant is \(14/111\). A slogan such as “control \(G\) near \(K^{.43}\)” is insufficient: (T08.5) requires every divisor cutoff below that boundary, all components and all height/profile uniformities.

### Exact numerical transfers and an off-central version

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
(u,v)&c_{u,v}\\ \hline
(\eta,\eta)&(1-\eta)/(6(1+2\eta))\\
(1/8,1/32)&14/111\\
(1/8,1/64)&28/219\\
(1/8,0)&7/54\\
(1/10,1/12)&9/71
\end{array}
\]
At \(c=.1255=251/2000\),
\[
c_{u,v}>.1255\iff1753u+753v<247.
\]
At \(u=1/8\) this is \(v<223/6024\). The general range \(3u+v<1\) extends BB's unnecessarily restricted \(0\le v\le u<1/4\).

If a mean is available only on the fixed line \(1/2+e\), do not hide the cost \(D^{2e}\) in an arbitrary epsilon. A finite trace \(K^{1+u}G^v\) on that line instead gives
\[
k_{*,e}=\frac{1-2e+v/2}{1+u+v},\qquad
c_{u,v,e}=\frac{1-u-4e}{6(1+u+v)},
\]
provided \(8e+3u+v<1\). In the ordinary-mean deduction \(v=(u-2e)_+\), this is exactly BB R05.b's two cases.

SB §6's exact interior example is correct: at \(\eta=3/32\), \(k=8813/10000\), \(g=1907/5000\), the four exponents are
\[
639897/320000,\quad18813/10000,\quad57371/30000,\quad29999/15000.
\]
Their margins below two are \(103/320000,1187/10000,2629/30000,1/15000\). The prefactor loss \(\rho=10^{-6}\) costs \(18813/10^{10}\), less than each margin. This proves exponent feasibility after the missing mean only.

**Sources:** BA D5; BB R05.a–b and R01; SB §6; FD (65)–(73); M (2.14)–(2.18). Corridor closure (T08.5) is original to the merge and was independently checked in the mathematical merge.

## Development14: exact cover, weighted defect and reconstruction

Let chi be any fixed ordinary Dirichlet character modulo q, with its natural zeros. Work on the augmented squarefree q-unit cutoff complex: a face S has product n<=X and degree |S|=omega(n), including the empty face in degree0. Its oriented deletion differential is d. Let D_chi e_n=chi(n)e_n. Then Str(D_chi)=M_chi(X), where M_chi(X)=sum_(n<=X) mu(n)chi(n). This convention fixes the reduced-chain sign shift.

The exact commutator is

    [D_chi,d] e_n
      = sum_(p|n) orientation(p,n) chi(n/p)(1-chi(p)) e_(n/p).

For distinct deletions the target faces are distinct. A local deletion coefficient that commutes with the character insertion must therefore vanish whenever chi(p)!=1. Ordinary weighted deletion cannot silently become a chain map for this insertion.

The author's proposed full residue cover does not solve that issue. Its basis is (S,g), g in G=(Z/qZ)^*, and deletion of p sends (S,g) to (S\{p},gp), with the usual orientation. The conserved coordinate h=g*product(S) conjugates this differential to d tensor I_G. Thus the cover is a trivial direct sum after a relabeling. In the Fourier sector sum_g chi(g)^(-1)e_(S,g), the differential has coefficient chi(p); it is D_chi^(-1)dD_chi. Every such sector has one vector per face and the same Euler index M_chi0(X), not M_chi(X).

This is an actual source discrepancy, not a dimensional slogan: for q=3, the nonprincipal chi and X=5, the allowed faces are1,2,5. The Euler index is1-1-1=-1, whereas M_chi(5)=1+1+1=3. Inserting chi(h) on the complete conserved register commutes but has trace0 for nonprincipal chi. Anchoring the register to g=1 recovers chi(n) but breaks the chain condition. The statement is restricted to this full regular-residue cover and this readout; it excludes no different nonlocal construction.

The paid repair is correct. Let ell be the least prime not dividing q. The subcomplex formed by ell-free faces of product<=X/ell and their ell-cones is contractible. Every boundary face of a critical ell-free face in (X/ell,X] lies in that cone: all its prime factors exceed ell. Let h insert ell on eligible ell-free faces, with positive insertion sign, and vanish otherwise. On the cone, dh+hd=I. On a critical face set P e_S=e_S-hd e_S; set P=0 on the cone. Directly, P^2=P, dP=Pd=0 and dh+hd=I-P. The author's projection is not merely the diagonal indicator of critical faces; the correction is necessary.

Graded cyclicity now gives the complete identity

    Str(D_chi) = Str(D_chi P) + Str([D_chi,d]h).

Writing A(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,ell∤n) mu(n)chi(n), B(X)=A(X)-A(X/ell), and c=chi(ell), its two terms are exactly B(X) and (1-c)A(X/ell). Hence

    M_chi(X) = B(X) + (1-c) sum_(j>=1) B(X/ell^j).

All sums terminate below1. A uniform all-scale bound B(X)=O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)), gamma>0, therefore returns M with the explicit geometric cost 1+|1-c|/(ell^(gamma+epsilon)-1), after paying a finite head. Conversely A(X)=sum_(j>=0)c^j M_chi(X/ell^j), so a full M bound gives the same B exponent. This is an exponent-equivalent source target, not a weaker arithmetic input. It includes principal, complex and imprimitive ordinary characters, with fixed-chi constants allowed.

Unsigned ranks remain too large. For r fixed,

    Q_r(X)=#{n<=X: n squarefree, (n,r)=1}
          = kappa_r X + O_r(sqrt X),
    kappa_r=(phi(r)/r) product_(p∤r)(1-p^(-2)) > 0.

The elementary proof uses mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counts integers coprime to r, and pays the convergent square-divisor tail. Thus the critical rank is kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X), including the principal q=1 value2X/pi^2. Bounding the scalar by this complete unsigned rank cannot establish M cancellation.

The sampled13 annular extension follows from the long exact sequence: total relative reduced Betti mass is at least b(K_X)-b(K_(X/Y)). It is linear for fixed Y>1. For any finite filtration, including a different finite filtration at each X, the sum of its relative masses telescopes to at least final mass minus initial mass. If initial mass=o(X), refining annuli cannot lower the complete unsigned price below order X. This does not reject signed pairings across annuli or pretend that D_chi commutes in a twisted index.

## Development23: source coefficients, exact dual and the surviving signed target

Set N=floor X, S={n<=N: mu(n)!=0, (n,q)=1}, E={n in S:n<=Y}, H=S\E, with1<=Y<=N/2. The unknown actual coefficients are a_d=mu(d)chi(d), d in H. The convolution a*chi=delta, with natural character zeros and all integer rows, gives on m in H

    sum_(d in H,d|m) chi(m/d)a_d = b_m,
    b_m = -sum_(d in E,d|m) mu(d)chi(d)chi(m/d).

The set H is order-convex inside divisor intervals: if d,m in H and d|k|m, then k in H. Consequently the square matrix Z_(m,d)=chi(m/d)1_(d|m) has the literal inverse W_(m,d)=mu(m/d)chi(m/d)1_(d|m): its product entry is chi(m/d)sum_(d|k|m)mu(k/d), equal to delta_(m,d). An arbitrary principal submatrix need not inherit an inverse; interval convexity supplies the justification here.

Its unique scalar dual is

    lambda_m = sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1) mu(k)chi(k),
    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H) lambda_m b_m.          (R1)

The final pairing is bilinear, with no complex conjugation. The conjugate enters only the adversarial norm witness below. Squarefreeness removes k sharing a prime with m; chi removes every ramified prime. No correction is hidden in those masks. For Y=floor(sqrt N), every lambda argument is short, but the number, dependence and terminal values of the duals still matter.

There are two distinct unconditional price results.

1. Independent row errors eta_m in the square system have scalar norm sum_H|lambda_m| from ell-infinity to C. Equality is attained by eta_m=conj(lambda_m)/|lambda_m| when lambda_m!=0. Every squarefree q-unit m>N/2 has lambda_m=1. Thus the norm is at least kappa_q N/2+O_q(sqrt N) and at most N(1+log N). Its exponent is1, uniformly for Y<=N/2. Adding all squareful convolution rows up to N cannot remove the terminal price: a variable a_m with m>N/2 appears only in row m. Any exact linear certificate for the scalar sum must assign coefficient1 to that row. This conclusion concerns independent equation errors and the specified full-row linear formulation; it does not allow errors in the actual arithmetic source or exclude nonlinear restrictions on them.

2. On the actual source, define P_N=sum_H|lambda_m b_m|. Every unramified prime N/2<p<=N has lambda_p=1 and b_p=-chi(p), so P_N is at least the number of those primes. Also |b_m|<=tau(m), |lambda_m|<=N/m, giving P_N<=N(1+log N)^2. If P_N were O(N^alpha) for any fixed alpha<1 on all large N, its values at N=2^j would force convergence of sum_p1/p, a contradiction. This proves limsup_(N->infinity) log P_N/log N=1, uniformly against any choice of Y_N in [1,N/2]. It does not prove a pointwise order-N lower bound for every N, and it does not lower-bound the signed right side of (R1).

The possible growing-conductor objection is explicitly paid for the particular omissions at hand. For any m,

    lambda_m(T)=sum_(r<=T, p|r => p|m) chi(r) M_chi(T/r).  (R2)

All powers of primes dividing m occur in r; omitting them would be false. A fixed-character bound |M_chi(t)|<=C t^alpha, with fixed0<alpha<1, implies

    |lambda_m(T)| <= C T^alpha product_(p|m)(1-p^(-alpha))^(-1).

For m<=N the product is exp(O_alpha((log(2N))^(1-alpha)))=N^o(1). Split primes at log(2N), majorize small primes by all integers, and bound the number of large prime factors by log N/log2. The estimate is uniform in m; it uses no theorem uniform over arbitrary growing primitive moduli. This correct paid estimate still does not beat either complete absolute-price obstruction.

The author's OPEN-E9 is the full signed sum in (R1), with Y=floor(sqrt N), bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0, every fixed ordinary chi, and all sufficiently large N, with one common1/2<gamma<theta11. Neither exceptional dual rows nor cross terms can be dropped. This equivalence holds at the near-endpoint,5/6 and3/4 targets; none is proved.

For completeness the all-height return is valid without an unpriced reciprocal-growth hypothesis. A full M bound gives

holomorphically on Re s>gamma, locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives. On Re s>1 it equals1/L(s,chi). ## Other first tests and scope boundaries

Card26 correctly prices the unordered integer fiber in the full free-word lift. An integer with k distinct prime factors has k! word representatives, all with the same arithmetic phase. The evaluation norm sqrt(k!) cancels the minimum lift norm1/sqrt(k!). The complete weighted version is the existing G117 fiber Cauchy floor, not a new cancellation theorem. It does not prohibit beneficial correlations between different integers.

Card16 correctly applies inertia only under invertible congruence of the principal signed form. Cancelling positive/negative planes leaves the unproved imbalance |M|. A complex-character matrix cannot be treated as that same Hermitian signature. Its standard Hermitian dilation has signature0 regardless of the original trace: the actual q=3,N=5 example has coefficient matrix I_3, trace3, but balanced dilation signature. Card20's formal second-order cutoff polymer calculation is correct:

               -sum_(p<r,pr>X) z_p z_r + terms of degree>=3.

Repeated powers here are cumulants, not new squareful Mobius coefficients. The restricted high-prime clique has Z=1+sum z_p.              -sum_(sqrt X<p<=X) chi(p)M_chi(X/p).

Every n<=X has at most one such prime; its cofactor is below sqrt X and automatically coprime to p. Both complete signed sectors remain. This is the retained largest-prime/renewal mechanism, not an unpaid new bridge.

## Protected independent audit30: which commutator survives evaluation?

The original rare card proposes isolating a noncommutative/free contribution and paying the commutative error. Its first missing contract is the choice of word space. Two natural choices have different answers. Neither is safely replaced by a generic assertion about commutators.

In the full finite free-word space, retain every ordering of distinct unramified primes of product n<=N. Abelianization E maps each word to e_n. Adjacent-transposition differences span exactly the zero-sum hyperplane in each k! fiber: the adjacent-transposition graph on permutations is connected, and differences along a spanning tree have rank k!-1. Hence ker E is precisely the full within-fiber commutator span. The hard product cutoff preserves entire fibers. Integer summation annihilates those commutators identically; reducing their norm cannot change M_chi. This is a scope-specific zero, not a claim that all noncommutative models have zero commutator readout.

For arbitrary positive word weights w_v, let beta_n=sum_(Ev=e_n)1/w_v. The minimum squared norm of a lift of actual a_n is sum_n|a_n|^2/beta_n, and the scalar evaluation's squared norm is sum_n beta_n. Their product is at least (#S)^2 because |a_n|=1 on the squarefree q-unit set S. This is G117's exact orthogonal-fiber price, with the original masks retained.

The outputs of T^r for different input words are disjoint. Therefore ||T^r||^2<=S_sigma^r/r!, where S_sigma=sum_(p∤q)p^(-2sigma)<infinity. The Neumann series for (I+T)^(-1) converges in operator norm even if ||T||>=1, and its vacuum vector is exactly

    (v_sigma)_n=mu(n)chi(n)n^(-sigma).                  (A30.1)

This operator construction and coefficient identity are the retained matched-Max B22, not a new family. For p<r, A_p A_r=0; A_r A_p can be nonzero. With commutator convention [A,B]=AB-BA, the complete ordered commutator is

This infinite sum is paid: for finite prime cutoffs C_P=T_P^2, while ||T-T_P||^2<=sum_(p>P)p^(-2sigma), so C_P converges in operator norm to T^2. No rearrangement of a merely conditionally convergent series is used. For a hard integer cutoff N, intermediate products never exceed the final product, so the identical two-step formula holds on the compressed finite space too.

Let Lambda_(N,sigma)(u)=sum_(n<=N)n^sigma u_n. From (I+T)v_sigma=e_1 follows T^2v_sigma=v_sigma-e_1+T e_1. Thus the literal source return is

    M_chi(N)=1-sum_(p<=N)chi(p)+Lambda_(N,sigma)(C v_sigma). (A30.3)

The final term is exactly the contribution of integers having at least two distinct prime factors, with every sign and character factor correct. It need not be small; it must cancel the prime term. An all-scale N^(gamma+epsilon) bound for the COMPLETE scalar in (A30.3), for each fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon, returns the M bound and the all-height zero exclusion already proved above. ## Uniform independent audit28: fractional regularity pays the boundary

This audit concerns the specific B22 sorted-Fock source (A30.1), not an unspecified fractional space. The sharp cutoff evaluator has ordinary Hilbert norm

    ||Lambda_(N,sigma)||^2 = sum_(n in S,n<=N)n^(2sigma)
      ~ kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/(2sigma+1).

The source norm is finite and independent of N. Generic Cauchy therefore gives exponent sigma+1/2>1; letting fixed sigma approach1/2 reaches the exponent1 boundary, not theta11. This existing B22 obstacle is retained rather than rediscovered as a new result.

Define the natural fractional logarithmic graph scale for fixed real s by

    ||u||_s^2=sum_n (1+log n)^(2s)|u_n|^2.

The actual v_sigma belongs to every such fixed space because2sigma>1. The exact evaluator norm is

      ~ kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/((2sigma+1)(log N)^(2s)).   (A28.1)

Partial summation against Q_q(x)=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x) proves this for every fixed real s; the error is lower by a positive power of N, up to logarithms. Fractional logarithmic order changes a logarithm, not the power needed. There is a stronger exact diagonal-weight statement. For arbitrary positive weights w_(n,N), even chosen separately at each cutoff, whenever the indicated norms are finite,

    (sum_(n in S,n<=N)w_(n,N)|v_sigma(n)|^2)^(1/2)

       >= sum_(n in S,n<=N)|v_sigma(n)|n^sigma
        = #S ~ kappa_q N.                              (A28.2)

A full infinite source norm is at least its truncated value, so it cannot evade this floor. Complex phases and ramified zeros are explicitly accounted for by S and |chi|=1 there. The complete missing input can be stated as |Lambda_(N,sigma)(v_sigma)|=O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(gamma+epsilon)) at all N, equivalently the M bound. ### 7.1 Correction and independent shell-L1 extension

For clarity define ||F||_(j,X)=(int_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j). A pointwise bound at exponent gamma implies a shell-L2 bound at that exponent, and shell L2 implies shell L1 by finite-measure Cauchy. ## B. Both detectors: the numerator-moving vector and paid transfers

### The family really preserves the denominator

For K=Q(i), fixed excluded primes S and chi2((d))=alpha(d)^2, let F_K(X)=sum_c mu_K(c) k(log(Nc/X)). Then the source's family is exactly

    F_t(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1+it) F_K(X/Nd²),
    Mellin F_t(s)=M(s) L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2)/zeta_K^S(s).

Every ideal has unique m=c d² with c squarefree; c and d need NOT be coprime. At squarefree m, d=1 and the coefficient is unchanged. This is not an ordinary Hecke twist of the whole denominator.

The return assumes M(s) is nonzero on the required Re(s)>a. Merged lines48–54 stipulate the inherited profile and its zero-free range without reproducing that profile or proof; I have not identified it with another detector merely by notation. This remains an explicit input, including for a=3/4. A possible fully specified replacement is the infinite convolution of uniform probability densities on [-2^-j,2^-j], j>=1: it is C-infinity, supported in [-1,1], with M(s)=product_j sinh(2^-j s)/(2^-j s), nonzero for Re(s)>0. Normal convergence follows from sum_j 2^-2j<infinity; arbitrarily many box factors give arbitrary Fourier decay. Using this replacement requires the actual period and arithmetic estimate for this fixed profile, not transfer of an unspecified profile's bound.

For a fixed positive-length bounded I, a bound

    int_I ||F_t||²_[X,2X] dt << X^(2a+epsilon)

gives an L2(I)-valued holomorphic Mellin transform for Re(s)>a, by dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz. Continue the multiplication identity with zeta_K^S(s). At any hypothetical zero rho with Re(rho)>a, its left side is zero; its right side is the vector

    N_rho(t)=M(rho)L_K^S(2rho-1-it,chi2).

This vector is nonzero: the fixed L-function cannot vanish on a vertical interval without vanishing identically, and M is nonzero by the explicit profile hypothesis above. This handles arbitrary finite multiplicity and proves the strict half-plane without dividing by a scalar numerator. The arithmetic moment, including all d,e and ideal/source cross terms, is still open.

### Uniform readout, finite parameters, and actual costs

At a fixed rho, set m_rho=max_(t in I)|N_rho(t)| and D_rho=max_(t in I)|N'_rho(t)|. If D_rho>0, a one-sided interval of length

    ell=min(|I|/2,m_rho/(2D_rho))

has |N_rho|>=m_rho/2. Hence ||N_rho||²>=ell*m_rho²/4. If D_rho=0 the exact lower bound is |I|m_rho². These are positive quantities; no claimed numerical all-height lower bound is hidden.

For a fixed compact strip/height window K0 lying in the relevant half-plane, m0=min_(s in K0)max_I|N_s|>0 and D0=max_(K0 x I)|N'_s|<infinity. The same formula gives a uniform compact-window bound. A grid with mesh <=m0/(2D0) then captures at least m0/2 at one node for every s in K0; equal-weight squared readout costs at worst m0²/(4N). This is an effective prescription only once certified bounds for m0,D0 are supplied. The consultation supplies no explicit bound as the height window tends to infinity. Its qualitative pole contradiction does not need one. A quantitative contour or resolvent argument WOULD need that additional height cost.

Parameter order matters:

* Fix I before the scale X. The continuum norm is a complete sufficient target.
* A single unspecified generic t already avoids simultaneous masking at every zeta_K zero: each fixed rho has a discrete bad-t set, and their union is countable. This is an existence statement, not a certified named phase or an estimate for that phase. Fubini applied to all rational positive epsilon values can extract an almost-everywhere scalar return from the continuum norm.
* A preselected finite explicit list has no established global noncommon-zero guarantee here. On each fixed compact window a finite list exists by the preceding bound. Growing the height window requires renewing its capture certificate.
* Finite moving quadrature can approximate the continuum ARITHMETIC energy cheaply. On x in [X,2X], the compact kernel gives Nd<=sqrt(2eX), so F_t is an exponential polynomial with frequencies in [0,Lambda], Lambda=.5 log(2eX), and total coefficient mass O(X log X). Thus |F_t|² has frequencies in [-Lambda,Lambda]. An N-node Gauss rule on I is exact to degree2N-1 and has positive weights summing |I|. Taylor's integral remainder gives error at most

      C_I X² log²X [e Lambda |I|/(4N)]^(2N).

  Taking N=C_A log X with a sufficiently large fixed C_A pays any prescribed X^-A error, uniformly in x; integrate dx/x afterwards. This is O(log X) parameter samples with no exponent loss. Nodes depend on X; they approximate the fixed interval norm and are not a claim about finitely many fixed detectors. All within-sample square-divisor cross terms remain.

### The exact obstruction to a free overlap transfer

Using the same physical weighted shell norm as current-proof G28, absolute Minkowski on F_t costs

    sum_d Nd^(1-2a),

which diverges for every a<=1. Truncating at Nd<=sqrt(X) costs X^(1-a), cancelling the gain X^a and yielding only X (logarithms at the boundary). Uniform local Hilbert norms do not remove this arithmetic restriction cost. A scalar phase has correlations int_I exp(it log(Nd/Ne))dt, a sinc kernel, not independent-prime orthogonality. Equal norms are fully coherent, and nearby log norms have large overlap.

There is a stable attenuated equivalence, which identifies precisely the easy case. Put

    F_(tau,t)(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1-2tau+it) F_K(X/Nd²).

For fixed a+tau>1, both this convolution and its Dirichlet inverse are bounded on the global weighted shell norm. Their absolute constants are at most

    sum_d Nd^(-(2a+2tau-1))=zeta_K^S(2a+2tau-1),

with the inverse using mu_K(d)chi2(d)Nd^(1-2tau+it). These bounds are uniform for real t. They also hold for a Hilbert-valued t-family. Their Mellin numerator lies in Re(2s-1+2tau)>1 for Re(s)>a. Thus the attenuated family has a safe numerator but the same arithmetic exponent problem as F_K. Strictly crossing the threshold costs tau>c; equality is not covered. This is an exact counterpart of the older W26 shifted-reciprocal safe-region equivalence, with a different square-dilation exponent.

For the unattenuated phase family the denominator-only return is a real addition to F25.E/N28's noncommon-multiplier idea: it moves an auxiliary arithmetic L-function without moving the zeta denominator. The sufficient moment is not weaker in its required power. It may permit a better coupled period estimate; it does not inherit one.

### Rational Riesz/Gaussian connection

The factorial detector uses precisely the current rational coefficient A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2). Let R(y)=F2(e^y), with F2(x)=sum_(n<=x) A(n)(1-n/x)^2. Distributionally,

    D(D+1)(D+2)R=2 sum_n A(n) delta_(log n),  D=d/dy.

Therefore the fixed Gaussian is exactly

    G_tau(e^y)=h_tau * R(y),
    h_tau=.5 D(D+1)(D+2)g_tau.

Every exponentially weighted L1 norm of h_tau is finite. Shell Minkowski gives a paid Riesz-to-Gaussian transfer at any fixed growth exponent with the usual left-tail/neighbor-shell treatment. The naive reverse multiplier contains exp(tau*t²/2) on a vertical line and is unbounded; a reverse arithmetic implication would need a zero-return/contour argument, not bounded Gaussian deconvolution.

This rational identity does not identify Q(i)'s F_K with A(n). zeta_K= zeta L(.,chi_-4), and ideal coefficients are a Dirichlet convolution of the two reciprocal coefficient sequences; they are different arithmetic fields. No Gaussian/compact component mask, signed subset, or current f3 bound is inherited by the quartic period. The other review owns the direct compact-to-Gaussian hierarchy.

Stacking Gaussian with a scalar compact smoother of the same A has no independent numerator benefit when each multiplier already is nonzero. A positive sum of their complete energies is at least either component energy; mixed scalar readouts need all cross terms and a calibrated nonvanishing numerator. The phase family above is the specific genuinely complementary-numerator opportunity.

Cheapest decisive test: compute the one-prime COUPLED relative boundary germ on E(a_(p,t)) as an identity in u=Q^(it), not only at t=0. Then seek one uniform finite-prime/finite-valuation L2(I x [X,2X]) estimate with all crosses. The local vector norm bound and this report's quadrature pay approximation costs, but not the moving relative restriction. There is no independent arithmetic cancellation assumption.

## DQ12. The dominant primitive band remains after removing cubes

The natural reflected row length in the balanced bare-cube sector is
`H=D^2/K`. Applying all three terms of the legitimate all-row sieve yields

\[
D^2+D^3H^{-2/3}+D^{8/3}H^{-1/3}
=D^2+D^{5/3}K^{2/3}+D^2K^{1/3}.
\tag{DQ12}
\]

At `K=D^.87653` the two loss exponents are `2.25102` and
`2.292176666666...`. The last term is already present for `kappa=1` and
squarefree `d~H`, so these rows have primitive conductor `q_d~H`. Removing
perfect cubes, or any fixed finite collection of cube classes, does not
remove this large-sieve loss.

The precise remaining task is a coefficient-specific primitive-row estimate
for the original two coprime Möbius columns, all their opposite-column masks,
fixed components, same-complex-variable profiles, and original signed II
subtraction. In the primitive band `d~H` the needed covariance budget before
the physical `H^(-1)` normalization is `H D^2`. The current cross-sieve
term loses

`D^(2/3) H^(-1/3)=K^(1/3)`.

This is an upper-bound obstruction, not a lower bound for the actual moment.
The fixed-class polar calculation proves neither that loss is necessary nor
that II cancels it. The actual residual remains the double-large-core CC
contribution minus the original whole II term. T05 pays its physical cube-row

## G103. Complete unsmoothed energy and fixed-modulus covariance

For a fixed ordinary character chi, with its natural zeros, put
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n). Complete multiplicativity gives
a*chi=delta. Direct finite integration gives the exact positive energy

    E_chi(X)=integral_1^X |M(x)|^2 dx/x
      =sum_(m,n<=X)a(m)conj(a(n))log(X/max(m,n)).

The terminal weight is zero; all signed off-diagonals and both orientations
remain. If, for every fixed chi and epsilon>0, E_chi(X)<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)
at all large dyadic X with one common0<gamma<1, positivity extends it to all
large X. On each dyadic interval, Cauchy--Schwarz gives locally uniform
convergence of integral M(x)x^(-s)dx/x and all its s derivatives for
Re(s)>gamma. Initially s times that integral equals1/L(s,chi). The identity
continues meromorphically and excludes all L zeros in that half-plane;
the principal pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero. This avoids lossy
pointwise extraction from the energy. Constants and thresholds depend on
the fixed character; no growing-conductor bound is claimed.

For ALL characters of one fixed modulus q, orthogonality gives

    Ebar_q=(1/phi(q))sum_(chi mod q)E_chi
      =sum_(m,n<=X,(mn,q)=1,m=n mod q)mu(m)mu(n)log(X/max(m,n)).

Since each energy is nonnegative, E_chi<=phi(q)Ebar_q. The literal diagonal
is d_q X+O_q(sqrt X+1), where
d_q=(phi(q)/q)product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0. This follows by inserting
mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) and counting units, then integrating. For gamma>1/2
it is already below the target. The entire signed off-diagonal upper bound
OFF_q(X)<<X^(2gamma+epsilon), for every fixed q and all large X, is the
remaining arithmetic input. There is no absolute value inside this sum.
At q=1 it already includes the unsolved complete Mobius energy.

At current c10, first gain requires gamma<.87485404, squared exponent
2gamma<1.74970808 and saving>.25029192 from the elementary exponent2.
Targets1/6 and1/4 require squared exponents5/3 and3/2. No part of these
arithmetic gaps is paid here. The general weak/energy continuation principle
is existing F01/W27/W35 ancestry; the value is this complete source contract.

### D04.2 The coarsest sufficient moving-source hypothesis used here

Fix 1/2<gamma<1, 0<sigma<gamma, A>0 and 0<delta<1 such that

    A(1-sigma)<1,
    q_head:=sigma+delta(1-sigma)<gamma.                  (D04.3)

For every large dyadic X, put z_X=(log X)^A and

    P_X={p prime:5<=p<=z_X, p does not divide q}.

This parent X and P_X stay frozen while the argument x varies over [X,2X] and while every cofactor shell is estimated. Assume, for every epsilon>0,

    ||V_(P_X,chi)||_(L2([U,2U],dx/x))
       <= C_epsilon U^(gamma+epsilon)
    for ALL real U with X^delta<=U<=X,                  (OPEN-D04)

with constants independent of X,U. This includes the complete norm of the signed rough source; it is not a norm of only primes or one rough depth. No conclusion is drawn from V_(P_U,chi) at its own changing cutoff. The latter is a different field and is not the premise.

**Conditional return theorem.** OPEN-D04 and (D04.3) imply, for every epsilon>0,

    ||F_chi||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (D04.4)

Proof of the price: for fixed 0<sigma<1, p>=5 implies

    log W_(P_X)(sigma)
       <= C_sigma sum_(p<=z_X) p^-sigma
       <= C'_sigma z_X^(1-sigma)
       =O((log X)^(A(1-sigma)))=o(log X).               (D04.5)

Comparison with ALL integers suffices; no prime-distribution estimate, calibrated random sign or external cancellation claim enters. Thus W=X^o(1), uniformly in the parent X.

Split (D04.1) at R=X^(1-delta), without rounding ambiguity: short r satisfy r<=R, long r satisfy r>R. For r<=R the exact real cofactor shell U=X/r lies in [X^delta,X]. Minkowski and OPEN-D04 give

    ||sum_(r<=R) a(r)V(./r)||_[X,2X]
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)
                       sum_(r<=R)|a(r)|r^(-gamma-epsilon)
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) W_(P_X)(sigma).

The last inequality uses gamma+epsilon>sigma and r>=1. For each arbitrarily small output epsilon, apply the premise with a smaller epsilon and absorb (D04.5).

For r>R, t=x/r<=2X^delta. The positive Gaussian integer sum satisfies

    sum_(n>=1)g_tau(log(n/t)) <<_tau t, t>=1,
    sum_(n>=1)g_tau(log(n/t)) <<_(tau,sigma) t^sigma, 0<t<1.

For the first bound compare the positive profile with its integral and bounded maximum; integral equals t exp(tau/2). For the second use Gaussian left-tail decay (or multiply by t^-sigma and take the bounded supremum on (0,1]). Consequently, uniformly for 0<t<=2X^delta,

    |V_(P_X,chi)(t)|
       <= C_(tau,sigma) X^(delta(1-sigma)) t^sigma.

This estimate uses ONLY coefficient modulus <=1 and includes every small-scale term and every character zero. Hence the entire long-r head is bounded pointwise by

    C X^(delta(1-sigma)) x^sigma
                  sum_(r>R)|a(r)|r^-sigma
       <= X^(q_head+o(1)).                              (D04.6)

The shell has fixed logarithmic length, so this also bounds its L2 norm. Equation (D04.3) gives a fixed positive margin below gamma. Norm triangle proves (D04.4). If the full energy is expanded afterwards, every r,r' interaction is retained; the triangle proof has already paid both mixed terms and the head square. No positivity deletion, inherited masked moment, height truncation, projector commutation or baseline-beta scalar shortcut is needed.

This coarse head price is not optimal or an equality impossibility. It removes the bounded-x source hypothesis at the stated delta/sigma cost.
title: D04.2 The coarsest sufficient moving-source hypothesis used here

```
<X,Y>_U = sum_u Phi(Nu/U) X_u overline(Y_u),   ||X||_U^2=<X,X>_U.
```

The rows are the original nonzero sixth-power-free free rows in a fixed nonnegative smooth enclosing ball. Original divisor-bounded row weights are dominated before expansion. No zero, amplitude, moving-row or signed physical-projector selector enters the moment or Poisson transform. `H_J` retains finite seminorm and height factors.

The sole cancellation input below is the licensed canonical single-inverse moment, with its actual coefficients:

```
||M(E;W)||_U^2 << H_J U^epsilon J(E),
J(E)=U+U^(1/6)E^(5/6).                                      (R1)
```

UM slack is chosen first. For nonempty subunit scales, the fixed profile endpoint bounds the scale away from zero; smaller scales are empty. The direct bound `|M(E)|<<H_J sqrt(E)` therefore holds uniformly on all nonempty windows after enlarging the fixed constant. Polynomially bounded moving punctures are repaired by the exact identity

```
M_u^(R)(E)=sum_(h R-smooth) phi_u(h)/(Nh)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nh),
sum_(h R-smooth) (Nh)^(-1/2)
 = product_(p|R)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (NR)^epsilon. (R2)
```

Each original annulus sum is finite; allowing the full positive mass only enlarges its bound. No zero value of `phi` is divided out. R1 is never applied directly to a merged divisor-profile coefficient or an arbitrary projected coefficient.

The physical parameter box is exactly

```
17/25<=delta<=7/10, 17/20<r<47/50, 33/25<s<141/100,
s-r>3/8, 0<=v<=1/20.
```

Keep `K=28114053/6250000` from the preceding c10 family. With `h=5-2delta`,

```
rho=1-10delta/(3h),  k=rho+delta-1,  D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,a_K+b_K v),
T=delta(r+s)+E_K.                                          (R3)
```

Thus `E_K>=rho>=19/54` and `T>=123353/67500`. These exact quantities are not recalibrated. G147's actual witness also has the same-zero/common-annulus/compatible plain-complement restrictions. Enlargement to this box is only for an upper bound. Extract the signal at the internal buffered parameter before weakening to physical delta; that internal parameter may exceed `.70` and does not replace physical delta in R3 or slot pricing.

## 4. Reconstruction of the author's crucial S10 estimate

Keep the original ordered inverse and slot tuple labels, even if their merged ideal agrees. Set `G=U^(1/5)`. Let `F_>` retain `N gcd(d1,d2)>=G` and `F_<` retain its strict complement, so `F=F_<+F_>` as tuple polynomials. For squarefree ideals `q1,q2`, let `P_(q1,q2)F` insert `q1|d1,q2|d2`. This is linear coefficient projection on the original tuples, not a row projection or an orthogonal projection in the row norm.

For fixed integer `A>=2`, write `w_A(q)=tau(q)^A` and

```
D_A(X)=sum_(q1,q2 squarefree) w_A(q1)w_A(q2)
                         ||P_(q1,q2)X||_U^2.              (R4)
```

All label sums have one fixed global cap covering the scale box, with empty terms zero. This energy is not assumed bounded by `||X||^2`.

Finite divisor inversion gives, for any real `H>=1`,

```
a_H(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=H) mu(q/d),
sum_(q|g) a_H(q)=1_(Ng>=H),
|a_H(q)|<=tau(q),  a_H(q)=0 if Nq<H.                        (R5)
```

Retaining signs and normalization, G155's extraction is

```
F_> = sum_f a_G(f) phi_u(f)^2/(Nf)
              M_u^(f)(D1/Nf) M_u^(f)(D2/Nf) Q_u.           (R6)
```

Only squarefree `f` can occur. For fixed f put `E_i=D_i/Nf`, write `d_i=f x_i`, and decompose `q_i=g_i h_i`, where `g_i=gcd(q_i,f)|f` and `(h_i,f)=1`. The condition `q_i|d_i` is exactly `h_i|x_i`; its projected inverse is

```
mu(h_i) phi_u(h_i)/(Nh_i)^(1/2)
                   M_u^(f h_i)(E_i/Nh_i;W_i).             (R7)
```

No coprimality between `h1,h2`, no restriction on their overlap with slots, and no character inversion are introduced. The `g_i` label weights cost `sum_(g|f)tau(g)^A << (Nf)^epsilon`. For fixed `h1,h2`, the first inverse is bounded trivially with its actual mask, the second by R2 then R1. Their squared row norm, before slot cost, is

```
<< H_J U^epsilon E1/(Nh1)^2
       [ U/(Nh2) + U^(1/6) E2^(5/6)/(Nh2)^(11/6) ].        (R8)
```

The divisor-weighted `h1^-2` and `h2^(-11/6)` sums converge after arbitrarily small auxiliary losses. The finite `h2^-1` sum costs subpower, not a reciprocal cutoff. Including Q and the f-divisor weights, the vector for fixed f in the full row x q1 x q2 Hilbert space has squared norm `<<H_J U^(v+epsilon) E1 J(E2)`.

Now use Minkowski in that entire space on R6, including the row multiplier `phi_u(f)^2`, whose modulus is at most one. On `Nf~X`, `sum |a_G(f)|/Nf << X^epsilon`. The square root bound decreases like a positive power of X; the dyadic tail starts at G. After factoring out `H_J^(1/2) U^(v/2+epsilon)`, its two terms are bounded by constants times

```
sqrt(D1 U) G^(-1/2+epsilon),
sqrt(D1) U^(1/12) D2^(5/12) G^(-11/12+epsilon).
```

Squaring proves, for every fixed A,

```
D_A(F_>) << H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/G) J(D2/G).               (R9)
```

This reconstruction pays the apparent extra q-label bill. Replacing R9 by the unprojected G155 norm would not justify later cuts. Its dominant exponent is `v+r+5s/6-1/5`, with raw gap

```
T-(v+r+5s/6-1/5)
 >=rho+(47/20)delta-393/200 >=2809/273000>1/100.            (R10)
```

The finite diagnostic in Section 11 checks R7 with actual ideal Möbius signs and natural zeros. R8-R10 are analytic arguments, not consequences of that diagnostic.

## 5. Reconstruction of the author's same-index cuts

The author's thresholds are `H11=D1/U^(1/2)` and `H22=D2/U^(3/4)`. For `X=F_<`, R5 turns the paired events `N gcd(d1,d1')>=H11` and `N gcd(d2,d2')>=H22` into

```
[restricted research revision](X)=sum_q a_H11(q)||P_(q,1)X||^2,
[restricted research revision](X)=sum_q a_H22(q)||P_(1,q)X||^2,
[restricted research revision],22(X)=sum_(q1,q2) a_H11(q1)a_H22(q2)||P_(q1,q2)X||^2.
```

The union is exactly `[restricted research revision]+[restricted research revision]-[restricted research revision],22`, and these signed scalar quantities need not be positive. On full F, the corresponding positive envelopes have bounds

```
H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/H11) J(D2),
H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D2/H22) J(D1),
H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/H11)
                         [U+U^(1/6)(D2/H22)^(5/6)].
```

For the last bound, `sum_(Nq2>=H22) tau(q2)^O(1)/Nq2` is a finite harmonic sum. It supplies no extra `H22^-1`. The source's bound correctly retains this U term. Their exponents are respectively `v+1/2+e(s)`, `v+3/4+e(r)=v+7/4`, and `v+3/2`, where `e(t)=max(1,1/6+5t/6)`. Their raw gaps are at least `30607/1365000`, `1853/67500`, and `4682/16875`.

For each positive envelope, linearity `PX=PF-PF_>` gives a bound by twice its full-F envelope plus `2D_A(F_>)`. R9 therefore retains both original within-column cuts in the correlation. The author's S22 follows with margin `1/200` after the stated loss allocation. No missing intersection or illicit signed-subset monotonicity was found in this step.

## 6. Additional tail projection energies

The following stronger envelopes efficiently pay all overlaps involving opposite indices. Define for `i=1,2`

```
E_i^A(H;X)=sum_(q1,q2 sf; Nq_i>=H) tau(q1)^A tau(q2)^A
                                  ||P_(q1,q2)X||_U^2.     (R11)
```

For full F the exact extraction is

```
P_(q1,q2)F = mu(q1)mu(q2) phi_u(q1)phi_u(q2)/sqrt(Nq1 Nq2)
             M_u^(q1)(D1/Nq1;W1) M_u^(q2)(D2/Nq2;W2) Q_u.
```

Shared primes between q1,q2 and slots are allowed. The first inverse trivial bound and the second repaired moment give precisely R8 with `E1=D1,E2=D2,h_i=q_i`. Summing q1 from H yields `H^(-1+epsilon)` from its power 2. Summing the other coordinate has harmonic/convergent subpower cost. Reversing which inverse is bounded trivially gives

```
E_1^A(H;F) << H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/H) J(D2),
E_2^A(H;F) << H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D2/H) J(D1).               (R12)
```

The masked factor receiving R1 is repaired by R2 in each orientation. All estimates hold for each fixed A; the constant and arbitrarily small auxiliary losses may depend on A. Empty tails are zero. For the actually needed X=F_<, the positive Hilbert inequality yields

```
E_i^A(H;F_<) <=2E_i^A(H;F)+2E_i^A(H;F_>)
             <=2E_i^A(H;F)+2D_A(F_>).                     (R13)
```

This is the only transfer across the within-column cut. It is a proved bound for a positive projection energy, not a norm assertion about a selected signed pair sum.

## 7. Literal four-edge identity, conjugation and lcm payment

Use left original inverse indices `(d1,d2)` and right indices `(d1',d2')`. The edges are `11,12,21,22`, with thresholds

```
H11=D1/U^(1/2), H22=D2/U^(3/4), H12=H21=Hcross=U^(3/5).
```

For a nonempty subset E of these four edges, let `C_E(X)` be the exact ordered pair contribution in `<X,X>_U` with `N gcd(d_i,d_j')>=H_ij` for every `ij in E`. Every original slot tuple is independently summed in each copy. No other pair selector is applied yet.

For labels `q_ij` on edges in E set

```
l_i=lcm(q_ij: ij in E),  r_j=lcm(q_ij: ij in E),
```

where the lcm over no incident edge is 1. On the left the index i is fixed; on the right j is fixed. Repeated divisor inversion gives the literal identity

```
C_E(X)=sum_(q_e sf, e in E) [product_(e in E) a_H_e(q_e)]
                       <P_(l1,l2)X, P_(r1,r2)X>_U.        (R14)
```

To specify heights and conjugation before any Cauchy step: the first entry contains the original `W1(sigma,t1;Nd1/D1)`, `W2(sigma,t2;Nd2/D2)` and `Q_u` on its original indices. The second entry contains those SAME two separately parameterized profiles evaluated at `d1',d2'`, and the same full slot polynomial on its own slot indices. The entire second entry is conjugated by the definition of the inner product. A 12 edge changes only divisibility conditions `q12|d1` and `q12|d2'`; it does not exchange W1 and W2, replace t2 by t1, or conjugate a lone inverse factor. All mu signs, fixed dictionary factors and zeros remain inside their respective projections.

Individual opposite-edge/intersection terms in R14 may be complex. If `E^t={ji:ij in E}`, then `C_(E^t)=overline(C_E)` because H12=H21. The full inclusion-exclusion union and its complement are real. No positivity is asserted for either signed subset.

Here is the complete label bill. Put `b(q)=product_e |a_H_e(q_e)|`. Fix the left lcm pair l. Each edge label incident at vertex i divides l_i; the vertex degree is at most two. Hence the number of assignments is at most `product_i tau(l_i)^(deg_i)`. Since `|a_H(q)|<=tau(q)<=tau(l_i)`, their total absolute coefficient mass is at most

```
sum_(q: left lcm=l) b(q) <=tau(l1)^4 tau(l2)^4.            (R15)
```

The actual lcm constraint only decreases this bound. This allows all shared primes between edge labels; no disjointness assumption is inserted. The same argument applies to the right lcm pair.

Choose ANY one edge `i0 j0` in E. Nonzero `a_H(q_i0j0)` implies `Nq_i0j0>=H_i0j0`, so `Nl_i0>=H_i0j0` and `Nr_j0>=H_i0j0`. Apply weighted Cauchy in the direct sum of the ORIGINAL row Hilbert spaces indexed by the edge-label assignments, and then group by left and right lcms using R15. This proves

```
|C_E(X)| <= [E_i0^4(H_i0j0;X) E_j0^4(H_i0j0;X)]^(1/2).  (R16)
```

In detail the two squared factors before grouping are `sum_q b(q)||P_l X||^2` and `sum_q b(q)||P_r X||^2`. R15 bounds those exact original tuple projections. No claim such as `||a sharply restricted pair sum||<=||F||` appears. R13 and the proven A=4 case of R9 then control X=F_<.

For E containing an opposite edge, choose that edge and use Hcross in R16. For E containing only same-index edges, choose 11 or 22; R12-R13 already suffice. The author's sharper dedicated intersection calculation remains valid but is not needed to pay the other twelve intersections. Thus every one of the fifteen nonempty terms is accounted for by an explicit original-source energy.

## 8. Continuous exponent margins and simultaneous removal

At Hcross the two full-F energy exponents are

```
b1=v+r-3/5+e(s),   b2=v+s-3/5+e(r)=v+s+2/5.
```

The deliberately coarse bound `b1<=1039/600` and the unchanged T floor give

```
T-b1 >=123353/67500-1039/600=12931/135000>1/20.             (R17)
```

For b2 a coarse independent maximum would lose useful dependence. Keep delta and the sign of `delta-1`:

```
T-b2 >=rho+(113/50)delta-93/50 >=9229/170625>1/20.          (R18)
```

The first inequality uses r's lower endpoint, s's upper endpoint, and `v<=1/20`. The derivative of the right side is `113/50-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]`, bounded below by `5917/6075>0` on the whole interval. Its minimum is therefore at delta=17/25. This is an exact interval calculation, not a grid experiment.

For H11, R12's first energy has the author's short-index exponent; for H22, R12's second has its long-index exponent. Section 5 records their gaps. In every case R13 adds the R9 term, whose smaller raw margin is `2809/273000`. R16 thus pays every intersection with the same worst margin. Finite sums, square roots and the fifteen-term inclusion-exclusion constant introduce no additional power of U.

Reserve at most `1/1000` for all fixed geometric endpoint pads and at most `1/500` for ALL auxiliary powers combined, including A=4 divisor weights, mask restorations, finitely many dyadic counts, fixed Sobolev derivatives and profile separation. The finite list of losses is set before allocating their individual epsilons. With retained margin `1/200`, the limiting unused reserve is exactly

```
2809/273000-1/1000-1/500-1/200=5/2184>0.                  (R19)
```

Fixed constants enlarge the eventual threshold. The result is the source-relative estimate

```
sum_(empty != E subset {11,12,21,22}) |C_E(F_<)|
                    << H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon).            (R20)
```

The union of the four large cross-gcd events is exactly `sum_E (-1)^(|E|+1) C_E`. Equation R20 bounds the sum of the fifteen absolute scalar contributions; it does NOT bound the sum of absolute values of all arithmetic pair terms.

## 9. New residual, actual additional scope, and open return

First expand the original tuple polynomial F_< and remove the four-event union by R20. On the remaining pairs use the merged ideals `n=d1 d2 product slots`, `n'=d1' d2' product slots'` only to apply the unchanged G156 sectors. Do not discard the factorization labels defining the six gcd restrictions.

The full tuple absolute multiplicity `c_abs(n)` satisfies `c_abs(n)<<H_J N0^(-1/2) U^epsilon` and `sum_n c_abs(n)^2<<H_J U^epsilon`, where `N0=D1D2P0`. It majorizes the absolute contribution of ANY remaining pair subset by `c_abs(n)c_abs(n')`. Thus the complete ideal diagonal, the `Q<=U^(9/5)` sector, and the remaining `Q1/Q3<=U^(8/5)` sector retain their G156 absolute bounds. Their powers are respectively `1`, `109/60`, and `9/5`. This is an absolute tuple-multiplicity argument, not an inherited norm bound for a signed restriction.

G156's full natural-hole row kernel remains `<<H_J U^epsilon min(U,U^(1/6)Q^(5/12))`, with `Q=Q1Q2Q3`; its canceled-prime holes are not removed. G157's actual support restrictions remain: each column is `A^3 B^2 C` with A,B,C pairwise coprime squarefree, `N(n/rad n)<C G P0`, and `Q2 Q3^2<C U^(2/5+2v)`, `Q3<=C U^(2v)`, with the source's fixed endpoint constants and pads.

Define R4 as the original ordered signed sum on pairs satisfying ALL of:

* `N gcd(d1,d2)<G` and `N gcd(d1',d2')<G`;
* `N gcd(d1,d1')<H11` and `N gcd(d2,d2')<H22`;
* `N gcd(d1,d2')<U^(3/5)` and `N gcd(d2,d1')<U^(3/5)`;
* `n!=n'`, `Q>U^(9/5)`, and `Q1/Q3>U^(8/5)`, with all original G157 support restrictions, slots, roots, phases, profiles and holes.

Use the same finite derivative sum and positive common-profile measure as the source when a Sobolev envelope is required. Pair transposition preserves this whole set, so R4 is real. It need not be positive. The exact expansion and paid removals give

```
||F_<||_U^2 = R4 + O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).             (R21)
```

The useful new restrictions remove source configurations not removed by the author's two cuts. For example take zero slots, r=.9, s=1.35, and pairwise coprime squarefree ideal factors q,a,e,b,f with norm exponents `.7,.2,1.35,.9,.65`. Put `(d1,d2,d1',d2')=(qa,e,b,qf)`. Both within gcds and both same-index cross gcds are 1. The 12 gcd has exponent `.7`, so the new cut removes it. The merged columns each have exponent 2.25 and common factor exponent .7, giving relative `Q1` exponent 3.1 and `Q2=Q3=1`; the old conductor sectors do not remove it. Its transposed pattern is handled by edge 21. These are admissible factor patterns, not realized zero configurations or norm lower bounds; fixed annuli are handled with the retained endpoint pads.

The next missing arithmetic theorem is the ONE-SIDED estimate

```
R4 <= H_J U^(T-xi+epsilon) for some fixed xi>0,              (OPEN-R4)
```

uniformly in the licensed data, independent heights and actual suprema. An absolute bound is stronger but unnecessary. R21, R9 and `||F||^2<=2||F_<||^2+2||F_>||^2` would then prove free OPEN-MIX with any strict margin below `min(xi,1/200)`. Divide by BOTH actual G147 inverse-witness lower bounds, never by a possibly zero slot; add G147's counted prefix. This yields the corresponding weighted residual count only with margin strictly below `min(xi,1/200,1/2000)`, after witness, height and buffer losses.

That conditional count still does not complete zero exclusion. Both signed physical coprimality projectors, full family reconstruction, root and slot holes, fixed inducing and exceptional rows, physical `6a/9a` radii and `K_phys`/`5/6` amplifier prices, clipped rectangles, every shortening and Euler shift, extracted errors, principal branches, the common mesh and actual-supremum/common-Delta return still require their complete licensed accounting. The centered reserve remains unspent. No numerical map from xi to an improved c has been proved here. The physical parameter box cannot simply be extrapolated to the `delta=2/3` or `delta=1/2` target lines.

## 10. Strongest obstruction, ancestry and next mathematical action

The author's failed common-cofactor sign idea is correctly scoped. In the zero-slot squarefree case with nonnegative profiles and zero heights, write

```
c(n)=N0^(-1/2) mu(n)nu(n) A(n),
A(n)=sum_(d|n) W1(Nd/D1) W2(N(n/d)/D2)>=0.
```

For `n=g a,n'=g b`, with g squarefree and coprime to ab and `(a,b)=1`,

```
c(ga) overline(c(gb))
 =N0^(-1) mu(a)mu(b)nu(a)overline(nu(b)) |nu(g)|^2 A(ga)A(gb).
```

The `mu(g)` sign squares away. The relative row character retains the natural zero `1_((u,g)=1)`. At equal nonzero heights there is only the common quotient phase; at distinct heights the divisor-profile phases need not be positive. This is not an obstruction theorem for all signed approaches and is not a lower bound for the full norm.

The strongest objection to R20 was that opposite indices and retained within cuts might require an unjustified norm bound for a selected signed subset, or an unpriced family of lcm labels. R14 states the literal conjugation and heights; R15 pays every label; R13/R9 preserve both within cuts. The affordable exact diagnostic then checks all fifteen overlaps with shared primes and zeros. This resolves that objection for the stated reduction.

The strongest remaining obstruction is unchanged: fully coprime squarefree pair columns can have all six tuple gcds equal to 1 and `Q1` of size `N0^2`, with `Q2=Q3=1`. They survive every new cut, and the available absolute envelope `U N0` is too large. Merging produces the actual two-divisor-profile coefficient, outside B3.6's canonical coefficient permission. Same-zero coupling does not create independence. Neither another clean Poisson bound nor the absence of a common factor establishes OPEN-R4.

[private research revision] MG, especially its MG21-MG30 incidence decomposition and four-edge union, is direct conceptual ancestry. Its result has the form `|Q_bad(H,R;X)|<<X^(2b+epsilon) R^(1-2b)` with accepted Mertens exponent `b=7/8`, for the separate rational smooth completed source using four singleton Abel summations. It preserves both internal gcd cuts and all four cross events. That theorem is not imported into the present Hecke norm: unequal scales, original mu coefficients, independent heights, slots and natural holes are established here by R1-R16 instead. Credit the existing generic four-gcd mechanism; retain the source-specific projection-energy extension as useful record progress. This corrects the pinned draft's narrower [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]-only ancestry discussion.

The next mathematical action is to write the exact squarefree, six-gcd-small residual by relative prime supports while retaining its two divisor profiles and distinct height variables, and seek a signed bilinear estimate in the UNIQUE relative supports. A proposed estimate must pay the full original profile coefficient and natural holes, then dominate OPEN-R4 with fixed xi. First test its generic coprime-column subclass: a mechanism which still leaves the `U N0` envelope there does not close this route. Do not count the removal of another already shared-factor sector as a complete saving.

## 11. Independent diagnostics and uniformity limits

`verify.py` was written independently; the author's helper was read as evidence and was not imported or rerun. Its exact arithmetic uses `Z[omega]`, `omega^2+omega+1=0`, and actual sextic residues at four split prime ideals of norms 7,13,19,31, with omega residues 2,3,7,5. Ideal masks carry true squarefree Möbius signs, gcd/intersection and lcm/union. The fixed dictionary factor is principal, optionally with the norm31 inducing puncture; the row1 case includes a principal residue character. Two separately assigned nonconstant complex profile value tables, both orientations, fixed and row-induced natural holes, and two disjoint original slot pools are retained. Slots may meet the inverse indices. Common positive normalizations cancel in the finite identities. Finite profile tables test the algebra for separate complex factors; they are not an assertion that independent analytic height dependence has been numerically exhausted.

The receipt records: all 15 graph identities in each of two cases, with eight nonreal individual intersections in each; 3,596 grouped lcm-mass checks; 8,192 R7 extraction identities; natural zeros; transpose-conjugation; inclusion-exclusion and weighted Cauchy. One surviving signed residual is `-322299` in the diagnostic's normalization, concretely exposing the danger of assuming positivity. Exact rational arithmetic checks R10, R17-R19 and the monotonic derivative floor. The helper exited 0. The host's known Python launcher warning did not affect execution; no environment repair was attempted.

These finite tests certify the stated finite identities for their test inputs. They do not certify R1, an infinite arithmetic saving, the full analytic parameter family, a physical return or a zero-free endpoint. The analytic work is the source-relative proof above.

For uniformity, choose the existing common geometric mesh/buffer before the eventual dictionary and slot count; freeze nominal U,D1,D2 cells and their arithmetic thresholds before taking actual parameter suprema. Use one global label cap, with empty terms zero. Do not differentiate G or H_ij. Freeze the finite derivative orders backward through the existing dependency graph. Tensor Sobolev keeps the common real coordinate, BOTH inverse heights, all original slot heights and log scales. Scale derivatives replace a normalized profile by `-W/2-yW'`; other derivatives retain twists and add fixed log factors. Extracted label phases contribute only logarithms of polynomially bounded labels. Every resulting finite derivative product obeys the same R7-R20 argument. Common-profile Fourier measures are fixed on the whole ambient box before labels or rows, and their two inverse coordinates remain distinct. Fourier decay follows the fixed raw label counts and height orders. Genuine G147 detector tails remain paid by that source and are not replaced by a formally truncated divisor identity.

All fixed inducing/ray/unit exclusions remain at R1's licensed scope. The proof neither creates a growing-character moment nor deletes principal or exceptional physical branches. The qualifications in Sections 1 and 9 are therefore part of the result. Root review and integration, rather than this report or its favorable diagnostics, determine any accepted record change.

## 0. Integration disposition and source boundaries

The checkout at import was exactly the packet's frozen revision
`c06e952f6512f78a15016c97533c104551acaef8`. The ZIP's mathematical advances

entries were verified against its manifest; the ZIP SHA-256 is

unique original child IDs, 21 original constructions and seven geometry
branches. The independent integration map found exact child/crosswalk
agreement and no broken relative Markdown links in the eight documents.
These are preservation checks, not mathematical proof by metadata.

holomorphic matched families (T01/T02), and the actual physical cube-row
Type I restriction (T05). Historical cycle records and original supplied

## 5. First arithmetic tests: what the weaker input does and does not buy

**Available calibration.** Take any fixed buffered beta>gamma4 from the accepted premise. Abel summation of the complete mu*chi coefficients against the Gaussian and its first derivative gives both |F(u)| and |F'(u)| bounded by C_beta exp(beta*u) in the existing ordinary-character scope. This is the same complete-source calibration used in the living proof; no masked estimate is inferred. With the requested gamma<gamma4, its direct bound on E_k is still exp(beta*k), exceeding the A4 target by exp((beta-gamma)k). Taking a smaller observation set does not turn an upper bound into cancellation.

Even GRANTING an exact real zero in every unit interval, that derivative bound only guarantees a neighborhood of width of order exp(-(beta-gamma)k) on which |F|<=exp(gamma*k). Its negative logarithm has order k, not o(sqrt(k)). This test does not upper-bound the actual small-value measure; it proves that the available zero-plus-first-derivative argument falls short. Section6 gives a rigorous Gaussian counterexample with exact natural coefficient zero support, so analytically produced valleys alone cannot fill the missing arithmetic estimate.

**Short-interval cancellation.** The Matomaki--Radziwill theorem compares normalized short averages of a real bounded multiplicative function to its long average, with an explicit logarithmic error. Theorem1 in <https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.04585> (v4, 15 October2017) retains that long average and the error C' loglog(h)/log(h). With h<=X this supplied error is not a negative power of X. Even a hypothetical direct Gaussian reconstruction with no additional loss would leave X times that normalized error, not X^gamma. Moreover a bound for local increments is not a bound for the complete Gaussian's long-average component. This primary theorem therefore does not establish A15; its arithmetic exceptional-set theorem is not being relabeled as observation sets for F. Complex/Hecke cases need their own stated extensions and are not inferred here.

The current original f3 rough/prefix identity must also remain complete: root's accepted [private research revision] source proves a large RR term and opposite restoration in the full hard mask. No small value of one chosen threshold piece supplies A4 for their sum. I used that result only to reject deletion of the restoration, not as a new leading-log obstruction or a new estimate.

The useful change is therefore at the exact input contract: future arithmetic work may now aim for very narrow valleys, or sparse but locally well-distributed valleys under A12. It need not prove W39's kappa<1/2 geometry. There is still no established arithmetic reason that these valleys exist at a new gamma. The next decisive arithmetic calculation is a lower bound for the measure of {u in[k,k+1]: |F(u)|<=exp((gamma+epsilon)k)} for the COMPLETE mu*chi or f3 field, at a threshold satisfying A4; sign-change counting alone is inadequate.

## 6. W60-25: the natural two-prime torsion loses the Euler product

This rare card was tested on its simplest exact realization, rather than replacing it after the draw. Put a=1-chi(p)p^(-s), b=1-chi(r)r^(-s), with Re(s)>0 and unramified distinct primes; then a,b are nonzero. The one-prime two-term based complex has differential a and torsion a or a^-1 depending on convention. Tensoring the two complexes gives

    C2=C, C1=C^2, C0=C,
    d2=(-b,a)^T, d1=(a,b), d1 d2=0.                           (T1)

It is acyclic. Choose boundary b0=a e0 with lift e_p, and boundary b1=(-b,a) with lift e_pr. The middle change-of-basis determinant is -a, so the alternating determinant ratio is a/(-a)=-1, or its inverse; up to the standard sign ambiguity, the torsion is1. It is not the desired reciprocal Euler polynomial ab. At p=2,r=3, principal chi,s=2, ab=(3/4)(8/9)=2/3.

The definition/alternating determinant convention was checked in the author's published primary source, [Michael Hutchings, *Reidemeister torsion in generalized Morse theory* (2002), AppendixA, DefinitionA.1 and PropositionA.2](https://math.berkeley.edu/~hutching/pub/rt3/rt3.pdf). The two-prime calculation above is independent and contains the whole claim; no infinite tensor-torsion theorem is invoked.

A direct sum of the one-prime complexes has torsion product a_p, but that simply stores the finite Euler product and introduces no cutoff interaction. Truncating the two-prime square before pr enters leaves C1=C^2->C0=C with one-dimensional H1, so an acyclic scalar torsion is no longer the proposed object. A choice of homology readout or a different complex could be investigated, but its arithmetic return and normalization must be derived. This disproves the literal tensor-complex repair, not every possible torsion detector.
