statement:
## 3. Development B: the exact variance price of a signed path

This executes C04's one/two-prime test and gives a useful scoped obstruction. Let a finite signed or complex sum be Z=sum_(alpha in A) w_alpha, with all zero weights removed. A one-path importance estimator picks alpha with probability p_alpha>0 and returns W=w_alpha/p_alpha. It is unbiased and

    E|W|^2=sum_alpha |w_alpha|^2/p_alpha >= V^2,
    V=sum_alpha |w_alpha|,
    E|W-Z|^2 >= V^2-|Z|^2.                              (W39.17)

This is Cauchy--Schwarz applied to |w|/sqrt p and sqrt p. Equality holds exactly for p_alpha=|w_alpha|/V. It is the optimum over ALL sampling laws, not merely independent prime laws. If N independent paths are averaged, the exact optimum mean-squared error is (V^2-|Z|^2)/N. This is an RMS/variance assertion, not an information-theoretic bound for every algorithm or every high-probability estimator.

For a finite set of primes P, z_p=chi(p)p^(-s), the exact Euler reciprocal expansion has w_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)z_p. Every subset, including the empty subset and repeated cross terms in the square, is retained. Then

    Z=product_(p in P)(1-z_p), V=product_(p in P)(1+|z_p|).

The optimizing law factorizes with inclusion probability |z_p|/(1+|z_p|). For ONE prime, the two outcomes are1/(1-r) and -z/r and

    E|W|^2=1/(1-r)+|z|^2/r >=(1+|z|)^2.                 (W39.18)

For TWO primes, independence under the optimum law gives

    E|W|^2=(1+|z_p|)^2(1+|z_q|)^2,
    |Z|^2=|1-z_p-z_q+z_pz_q|^2.                        (W39.19)

The negative one-prime terms and positive two-prime term have not been replaced by independent mean-zero noise. For principal chi at real s, 0<z_p<1, the relative second moment is product((1+z_p)/(1-z_p))^2. Already the finite law can have large phase cancellation; a formal random representation is no variance bound.

There is a direct ACTUAL Gaussian application. For fixed ordinary chi of modulus q, choose weights

    w_n=mu(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-y), n>=1.

They are absolutely summable. Monotone truncation extends W39.17 to this countable law, and V(y)=sum_(squarefree n,(n,q)=1) g_tau(log n-y). Elementary squarefree counting gives

    count_(n<=X)(mu(n)^2 1_(n,q)=1)
       =d_q X+O_q(sqrt X), d_q>0.                      (W39.20)

To verify it, use mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), impose (d,q)=1 and count the remaining integers coprime to q by their fixed periodic density; the O_q(1) error over d<=sqrt X and the convergent1/d^2 tail each cost O_q(sqrt X). The density equals (phi(q)/q) sum_((d,q)=1)mu(d)/d^2>0 by its absolutely convergent Euler product. Gaussian Stieltjes summation consequently gives

    V(y)=d_q exp(tau/2)e^y+O_(q,tau)(e^(y/2)),           (W39.21)

using the exact Gaussian integral and its derivative. Natural zeros of chi and mu are included; this is not random-Möbius modeling.

If the desired actual cancellation has |F(y)|<=e^(gamma y), gamma<1, then the optimum independent sample mean needs at least order exp(2(1-gamma)y) samples to achieve RMS absolute error at most a fixed multiple of exp(gamma y). Indeed insert W39.21 into W39.17 and divide by N; for large y the |F|^2 term is lower order. This statement is conditional on the desired small mean, not evidence that it holds. For a relative RMS tolerance delta when F!=0, the exact requirement is N>=(V^2/|F|^2-1)/delta^2.

A control variate with a known exact sum changes the residual weights to r_alpha. The same proof gives residual variance at least (sum|r_alpha|)^2-|sum r_alpha|^2. Thus merely changing the positive sampling law cannot remove the sign cost. A useful deterministic grouping or control variate must establish a genuinely smaller residual total variation (or use a method outside the independent one-path estimator class). No bound on every randomized algorithm, no Monte Carlo experiment, and no impossibility for arithmetic control variates is claimed. W38's exact Gaussian occupation representation is credited as related normalization work; W39.17 supplies the specific optimum/variance price, not a new phase-cancellation estimate.
title: 3. Development B: the exact variance price of a signed path

statement:
## 7. The signed band and the stopped-prefix obstruction

For fixed \(\lambda>1\), with \(t_2=\lambda t_1\) and both thresholds in
the admitted range, RNR2 and the fixed-order rate in RNR3 imply
\[
 P_{z_2}(x)-P_{z_1}(x)
 =C_\theta p_{z_1}^2\frac{x}{L}
 \left\{\lambda^{-2}-1+
 O_{\lambda,N}(t_1/L+t_1^{-N})\right\}.              \tag{RNR19}
\]
The difference is exactly the original-label band
\(\Psi_{z_2}-\Psi_{z_1}\), including every common-prime intersection
from RNR9. It is nonnegative as a selector; its resulting signed
field has a strictly negative leading term. For \(\lambda=2\),
\[
 P_{z_2}-P_{z_1}=(-3/4+o(1))P_{z_1},\qquad
 P_{z_2}=(1/4+o(1))P_{z_1},
\]
uniformly on \(J_X\). Eventual positivity of \(P_{z_1}\) follows
from RNR2, not positivity of the restored kernel.

This is a genuine estimate of a complete signed band. The number
of primes above the first threshold in a factor admitted by the
second threshold is not bounded uniformly in \(X\).
It is not a pointwise law for a single prime jump. When \(\lambda\)
tends to1, the subtraction formula with its displayed errors remains
valid, but it need not give a relative asymptotic for the small band.

Set \(n_1=C_\theta p_{z_1}^2X/L\), \(b_\lambda=\lambda^{-2}-1\), and
\[
 K_J=\int_{1/e}^{2e}u^2\,du/u=(4e^2-e^{-2})/2.
\]
The common physical leading profile is \(x/X\), so
\[
 \|P_{z_1}\|_2^2=(1+o(1))K_Jn_1^2,\quad
 \|P_{z_2}-P_{z_1}\|_2^2=(b_\lambda^2+o(1))K_Jn_1^2,
\]
\[
 \Re\langle P_{z_1},P_{z_2}-P_{z_1}\rangle
                 =(b_\lambda+o(1))K_Jn_1^2.        \tag{RNR20}
\]
All fields are real, with inner product conjugate-linear in the
first slot. No cross term has been inferred from separate upper
bounds on the positive norms.

At the author's endpoint \(t_*=L/(\ell_0m^2)\),
\[
 P_{z_*}(x)\sim C_\theta c_M^2\frac{x\,\ell_0^2m^4}{L^3},
\quad
 \|P_{z_*}\|_2^2\sim
 K_JC_\theta^2c_M^4\frac{X^2\ell_0^4m^8}{L^6}.      \tag{RNR21}
\]
Thus the entire signed sweep to this threshold still leaves a
prefix of field exponent1 and energy exponent2. This is an
actual-source obstruction to separately paying that prefix at
the OPEN-SP rate, not a lower bound for \(S\).
Its literal complement consists of labels with at least two
primes \(>z_*\) in **one** original factor. Nothing requires the
other factor to be prime or to have a fixed rough depth.
The source's terminal identity gives that complement exactly as
\(P_{\sqrt{B/Y}}-P_{z_*}\).

statement:
# S22 protected development: exact ordering and the cutoff CAR boundary

Status: finite identities and a scoped positive-certificate obstruction. No new Mertens estimate, H estimate, or zero-free constant. This was the first developed lane, before the other five first tests.

## Literal source and two correct encodings

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q. Its source is a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including zero for nonsquarefree n and (n,q)>1. Let P=(p_1<...<p_r) be finite unramified primes, containing every unramified prime <=N. On the orthonormal basis e_S indexed by subsets S of P, put n_S=product_(p in S)p. Missing integers in the embedding e_S->e_(n_S) have coefficient ZERO, not one.

Define commuting hard-core creation b_j e_S=1_(p_j notin S)e_(S union {p_j}) and fermionic creation

    c_j e_S=(-1)^(#{i<j:p_i in S}) b_j e_S.

Then b_i b_j=b_j b_i, b_j^2=0, while c_i c_j+c_j c_i=0 and c_i^* c_j+c_j c_i^*=delta_ij I. The diagonal parity string Z_<j satisfies b_j=Z_<j c_j. These are the standard occupation-basis relations; see Bravyi–Kitaev, Eqs.(1)–(2), https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0003137. They are also verified directly on each basis vector here.

With z_j=-chi(p_j), the exact coefficient vector is

    v=product_(j=1..r)(I+z_j b_j)e_empty
     =(I+z_1 c_1)...(I+z_r c_r)e_empty.                (F1)

The displayed operator order matters: the largest index acts first, so no previously occupied smaller index supplies a parity sign. This corrects an overly broad possible objection: bare fermions DO give a correct fixed ordered encoding. What fails is replacing that ordered product by a function of d=sum z_j c_j, since d^2=0, or treating reorderings as identical.

Let v_pi=(I+z_(pi(1))c_(pi(1)))...(I+z_(pi(r))c_(pi(r)))e_empty. Its S coefficient is z_S times the sign of the induced ordering of S relative to increasing order. Hence

    (1/r!)sum_pi v_pi=e_empty+sum_j z_j e_{p_j}.       (F2)

For |S|>=2 the induced order is uniform on all |S|! permutations and its signs cancel; for degrees zero and one the sign is one. This is an EXACT removal of every squarefree composite coefficient. It is not cancellation of the original arithmetic source. With Pi_N=1_(n_S<=N), its missing scalar for an arbitrary readout h(n) is exactly

    sum_(n<=N,squarefree,(n,q)=1,omega(n)>=2) mu(n)chi(n)h(n). (F3)

No norm or signed estimate of F3 follows from F2. A diagonal correction D_pi with these same ordering signs satisfies D_pi v_pi=v identically. Thus correctly compensated order randomization has constant output; the correction and source are perfectly dependent. This leaves other source-specific joint observations open.

Any common invertible similarity preserves [b_i,b_j]=0, so it cannot turn all b_j into CAR creation operators while preserving their nonzero two-prime products. On the square e_empty,e_p,e_q,e_pq, the two arithmetic insertion paths have equal sign and the fermionic paths opposite sign. A diagonal gauge cannot change this path-product ratio. This obstruction does not deny F1's single prescribed order.

## The exact cutoff defect is a positive boundary Gram

Let w_j be arbitrary complex weights, W=sum|w_j|^2>0, d=sum w_j c_j. Write Pi=Pi_N, Q=I-Pi, D=Pi d Pi and B=Q d Pi. The cutoff is divisor-closed: Q d^* Pi=0 and Pi d Q=0. Consequently

    D^2=0,
    D^*D+DD^*=W Pi-B^*B,       0<=B^*B<=W Pi.          (F4)

Proof: expand the full CAR identity d^*d+dd^*=WI between Pi's. The missing lowering term Pi d Q d^* Pi is zero. The other missing term is precisely B^*B. The same divisor-closure proves D^2=Pi d^2 Pi=0. No orthogonality between distinct boundary insertion paths is asserted: B^*B retains their signed off-diagonal overlaps.

Put Gamma e_S=(-1)^|S|e_S, Str(T)=Tr(Gamma T), and T_chi e_S=chi(n_S)e_S on Pi's range. Finite-dimensional cyclicity and the oddness of D give

    W M_chi(N)=Str(T_chi B^*B)+Str([T_chi,D^*]D).       (F5)

Indeed Str(T_chi(D^*D+DD^*))=Str((T_chi D^*-D^*T_chi)D). The diagonal version of F5 is the fully explicit formula

    W M_chi(N)=sum_(p in P)|w_p|^2 [
      sum_(N/p<n<=N,p not|n) mu(n)chi(n)
      +(1-chi(p))sum_(n<=N/p,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n)].      (F6)

Each bracket separately equals M_chi(N), by splitting the p-free and p-divisible terms. The strict lower bound and inclusive upper bound are exact even when N/p is integral. In the principal case the bulk term vanishes. For nonreal or negative chi(p) it generally does not. Ramified primes were removed from P; their original source coefficients remain zero. Character-dependent weights may be chosen, but neither term may be discarded.

The classical squarefree-complex/Euler-characteristic interpretation is not new: Bjorner's https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704 studies that complex and its Betti numbers. [restricted research revision] G79 already records an exterior Ward identity; [restricted research revision] G118 retains all parity layers; [restricted research revision] retains the twisted prime-toggle bulk. The newly integrated [restricted research revision]/G144 also explicitly owns the character-gauge/cone correction; G145 retains the complete prime/composite readout. F1–F6 isolate the ordering correction and positive cutoff Gram in this proposal; their familiar cores receive no new arithmetic or literature-novelty credit.

There is an additional exact scope check. For all characters of one presented modulus q, the unramified state space is the same, T_chi is unitary, and

    d_chi=sum_p chi(p)w_p c_p=T_chi d T_chi^*,
    D_chi=T_chi D T_chi^*,   E_chi=T_chi E T_chi^*.      (F6a)

Thus simply putting character phases on the differential preserves every singular value, Laplacian eigenvalue and Betti dimension. It does not turn M_chi into a character-sensitive spectral index. The source dependence is the inserted observable T_chi and its commutator in F5. This is not an obstruction to a bound uniform over characters of fixed q; it identifies what a bare spectral calculation has omitted.

Weights supported only on primes with chi(p)=1 make the character commutator vanish. That legitimate specialization still has the full positive boundary price below; the bulk term is not claimed unavoidable for every choice of weights.

## A uniform coarse price, including moving weights

The diagonal of E=B^*B is

    E_(S,S)=sum_(p notin S, p*n_S>N)|w_p|^2.

Let kappa_q=product_(p|q)(1-1/p) product_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2)>0. For every fixed q, elementary square-divisor expansion gives

    #{n<=x:squarefree,(n,q)=1}=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x).  (F7)

For a fixed unramified p, the number C_p(N) of source states crossed by p is

    C_p(N)=kappa_q (p-1)/(p+1) N+O_(q,p)(sqrt N).     (F8)

To prove the needed UNIFORM lower bound for all p, first handle the finitely many p<4/kappa_q using F8. For every larger p, count squarefree q-units in (N/2,N] and remove at most N/p multiples of p. Every retained n crosses the cutoff because pn>N. Therefore, once N exceeds a q-dependent threshold,

    (kappa_q/8) N <= C_p(N) <= N    for EVERY p not|q,
    (kappa_q/8) WN <= Tr(E) <= WN.                    (F9)

Primes p>N are allowed in this statement: every represented n then crosses. Thus arbitrary nonnegative weighting, moving prime blocks, or normalization by W cannot make this particular positive boundary-trace certificate sublinear. Its normalized exponent is one, missing the near, 5/6 and 3/4 targets. It is NOT a lower bound on |Str(T_chi E)+Str([T_chi,D^*]D)|, M_chi, a Gaussian moment or native H.

F7 follows by writing mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counting q-unit multiples of d^2 with O_q(1) error and completing the d^-2 sum. For F8 use the same count with modulus qp and subtract endpoints N and N/p; its density is kappa_q p/(p+1). This supplies an elementary proof rather than a reliance on a prime number theorem.

## Stronger exact calculation: the full-strength boundary eigenspace

Let p_* be the SMALLEST prime with w_(p_*)!=0; weights at smaller primes may be zero. The multiplicity of the eigenvalue W of E=B^*B is EXACTLY

    h_N=#{n:squarefree,(n,q)=1,p_* not|n,N/p_*<n<=N}.
    Therefore ||E||=W whenever h_N>0.                 (F10)

This is uniform in arbitrary weights on the other primes and in a moving active prime set. It strengthens F9 for this ambient spectral certificate: at least (kappa_q/8)N eigenvectors have full boundary loss for every sufficiently large N. It still says nothing below about the signed arithmetic readout.

Proof without a spectral approximation. Let U be the span of the states counted in h_N. Every active prime is >=p_*, so D kills U. In the quotient by U, each p_*-free state with n<=N/p_* is paired with its p_*-multiple. The p_* part of D gives an invertible coefficient w_(p_*) between each pair; all other active creation operators anticommute with p_* annihilation. Thus the quotient complex is contractible, with homotopy w_(p_*)^-1 c_(p_*)^*, taken modulo U. Equivalently it is the mapping cone of w_(p_*) times the identity on the lower p_*-free complex. No creation from U can return under the cutoff. The short exact sequence of these finite complexes gives H(D)=U as graded vector spaces. Finite-dimensional orthogonal decomposition gives dim(ker D intersect ker D^*)=dim H(D)=h_N. By F4 this is exactly ker(W Pi-E) inside Pi's range, proving F10. If p_*>N, the quotient is empty and D=0, which gives the same formula.

For q=1 and p_*=2 this is the familiar squarefree-complex critical-cell count in Bjorner's Theorem3.1. [restricted research revision]/G144 already includes the q-unit least-prime critical rank and its filtration price. The present statement keeps arbitrary zero/nonzero moving weights, their least ACTIVE prime, and the exact boundary-Gram eigenvalue. This is a useful explicit specialization/extension in this record, not a claim of a new topological theorem in the literature. A proposed spectral-gap shortcut below W fails on these actual cutoff states. Source-sensitive graded cancellation among those states remains entirely eligible.

## Conditional arithmetic return and the unresolved H adapter

If, for one specified allowed sequence of prime sets and nonzero weight vectors for each chi, every epsilon>0 and all large integers N, the COMPLETE right-hand side of F5 has modulus <=C_(chi,epsilon) W N^(gamma+epsilon), with one common gamma<.8748540364, then the ordinary Mertens bound follows exactly. It returns zero exclusion at every finite height by

    1/L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

first on Re(s)>1 and then on Re(s)>gamma. The integral is holomorphic there after a positive buffer; multiplying by meromorphic L gives the identity 1. A principal pole is not a zero, and imprimitive factors introduce no omitted positive-real-part zero. This is an exact CONDITIONAL return, not the needed signed bound. Sample targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 correspond to c=.12515,1/6,1/4.

For any already-defined finite source matrix H and embedding J, the literal lift is J^*HJ, retaining every entry, mask and phase. If H acts between different source spaces, use its two corresponding embeddings. This is an identity, not an estimate. No equality between the ordinary integer coefficient vector above and the native Eisenstein H tensor has been established. Native H still needs its actual rooted mark arrays, both projectors, signed short core, CRT/angular factors, natural zeros, height measures and once-only outside factor. S22 therefore supplies no native-H transfer or pressure saving; [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] contracts remain intact.

Next mathematical action: seek a bound on the COMPLETE graded boundary/character-bulk correlation in F5, or on a source-specific off-diagonal observation of B^*B that returns it. Optimizing only its trace is conclusively the wrong sufficient estimate. The hard signed trace survives and is not claimed easier merely because it is a boundary observable.

# W62: prime-flux localization, cutoff insertion algebra, and a coding obstruction

Completed author report for independent review; freeze/readback is recorded separately. No increase in c is proved. Current c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and its source obligations remain unchanged. The accepted c0 is a premise. No formalization, new proof packet or public-priority claim is made.

The proposed useful increment is a complete **prime-only, off-diagonal logarithmic coercivity criterion** for the actual ordinary-character source. All higher prime powers, a moving polylogarithmic small-prime sector and the exact same-output diagonal can be paid without any assumed Mobius cancellation. The first two payments are relative form bounds absorbed inside the conditional energy proof, not independent arithmetic power savings. The remaining hard-prime signed form is OPEN. Two other developments give exact arithmetic obstructions to particular operator/coding shortcuts. These are evidence for independent review, not automatic theorem acceptance.

## 1. Generation, sampling and first tests

Thirty cards in six groups of five were frozen in seeds.json, SHA-256 f2f96dbf0099ffc849ed7810094a595e6c0019fb2ca2b5a6ec0c6b2394a2481c. Groups1/2 are uncapped,3/4 have p<.10,5/6 have p<.01; p labels subjective generation typicality, never validity or success. The seed-only path/hash was sent to root before selections. A broad prefix-path discovery query inadvertently exposed limited older pilot excerpts before freeze; the exact exposure qualification remains in the immutable seed record. No fully unprimed claim is made.

After the freeze I read the attempt index, coherent proof and exact relevant sources. S01/S13/S16 were deliberately reserved, with no screen exclusions. Three independent OS eight-byte rejection draws used every eligible unreserved card in all six groups under literal thresholds; each complete pool was written before its entropy, and all draws froze before first tests. No reroll or substitute occurred.

|Role|Card|First test and disposition|
|---|---|---|
|Strongest credible bridge|S01|Derive the actual Gaussian logarithmic equation and price prime powers in a weighted norm. The identity has W35/G118 ancestry; the complete localized one-sided form below is the proposed incremental return. Develop D1.|
|Protected high ceiling|S13|The two-prime exterior complex with cutoff N=5 has one odd homology class after the6-face is removed. Its positive-gap shortcut fails. Exact W27 and the broader frozen W59 moving-weight spectrum already cover the mechanism. Duplicate at this realization, not a new topology theorem; no unsigned homotopy gain.|
|Most different|S16|A uniform syndrome can coexist with completely determined parity. On the actual source, observing all primes<=sqrt(N) leaves a nearly pure negative terminal-prime cell. Develop D3 with its complete quantitative certificate floor.|
|Uniform p<.10|S21|Actual un-ordered squarefree insertions commute even after the divisor-closed cutoff. Mixed insertion/deletion commutators survive and have a coherent all-character boundary contraction. Develop protected rare D2.|
|Uniform p<.01|S25|The full Schatten-fourth target is valid only with every native-H contraction. Rank alone gives no upper singular-value bound. Exact G80/G163 ancestry; no native arithmetic submatrix was numerically evaluated or invented. Parked duplicate, with literal H bill retained below.|
|Uniform remaining|S07|The character-orbit tensor is diagonal in the character basis; finite Fourier orthogonality reproduces G103's full same-residue covariance, including q=1. No new pointwise character saving. Parked duplicate.|

Pool sizes23/14/25, zero-based indices13/8/5 produced S21/S25/S07. Complete selection SHA-256 ec2f958cea571cbee8159239c443a76834464194b1718fdee133e0b1d6e1ca13. Original pools, entropy, limits and zero rejections remain immutable. Protected S13 received the substantive cutoff/homology test before being parked for exact ancestry. S21 preserves a rare high-ceiling exploration through a full actual-source calculation; its initial noncommutative-independence hope fails, while its signed boundary target remains available. D1 retains possible c arbitrarily near1/2, conditional on its genuinely unproved estimate.

## 2. D1 / S01: fully paid reduction to a hard-prime off-diagonal form

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including principal and imprimitive characters. Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with all squareful and nonunit zeros literal. Fix tau>0 independently of scale, and write

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1) a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=exp(-gamma y)U(y).

For every fixed real y all sums and derivatives below converge absolutely. The coefficient majorants are at most powers of log n times a Gaussian. For y<=0, U and each fixed derivative have a polynomial times Gaussian bound. No old cancellation premise is needed for these facts.

### 2.1 Exact equation and energy, with no deleted prime powers

Coefficientwise Dirichlet convolution gives

    a(n)log n = -sum_(d|n) a(n/d)chi(d)Lambda(d).

This follows by differentiating a*chi=delta, or by checking each prime exponent. At a squareful n the terms with the last two p-powers cancel; deleting those terms would change the source. Since tau U'(y)+yU(y)=sum a(n)log n g(log n-y), the EXACT equation is

    tau U'(y)+yU(y)+K_1 U(y)+K_2 U(y)=0,                 (1)
    K_1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K_2 U=sum_p sum_(j>=2)chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

Ramified terms vanish. This specializes the existing Gaussian commutator/renewal ancestry; it is not credited as a new identity. In z coordinates, each delay d has coefficient chi(d)Lambda(d)d^-gamma. For R>=0, multiply (1) by exp(-2gamma y)conjugate(U(y)), take real parts and integrate:

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)
      +I_R+tau*gamma*E_R = Q_1(R)+Q_2(R),              (2)
    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Q_j(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(K_j,gamma z)(y)dy.

All boundary terms and signs are retained. There is no finite-height restriction.

### 2.2 Every higher prime power is relatively bounded

For gamma>1/2,

    C_gamma=sum_p sum_(j>=2)log p*p^(-j gamma)
       <=[1/(1-2^-gamma)]sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2gamma)<infinity. (3)

Translation by j log p on the causal half-line has norm1 after the displayed weight. Extend z by zero above R, retaining its entire past. Young's inequality, or Minkowski followed by Cauchy, gives

    |Q_2(R)|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z(y)|^2dy.

The negative half-line integral is finite unconditionally. For every eta>0, splitting the positive integral at a fixed sufficiently large Y yields

    |Q_2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_(eta,gamma,tau),                (4)

uniformly in R. The finite B uses only unconditional bounds for U on a fixed bounded interval and its Gaussian left tail. No unknown right-tail norm enters B. Character dependence is allowed, although the crude majorant need not use it.

### 2.3 A moving small-prime sector is also fully paid

Choose A>0 with alpha=A(1-gamma)<1 and split K_1 at

    p<=(2+y)^A for y>=0; the hard sector has p>(2+y)^A. (5)

The threshold is real, with equality in the small sector. Write Q_small and Q_hard for the exact corresponding pieces of Q_1. For sufficiently large y, A log(2+y)<=y/2. Thus every small-prime delay v=y-log p has y/2<=v<=y. Its weighted row sum is bounded by

    sum_(p<=(2+y)^A)log p*p^-gamma
      <=C_(A,gamma)(2+y)^alpha log(2+y).                (6)

This deliberately coarse estimate sums over ALL integers. For a column v from that large-y region, y<=2v, so the same bound holds with p<=(2+2v)^A and a changed fixed constant. Apply 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, sum and change variables in the second term. Since (2+v)^alpha log(2+v)=o(v), for every eta>0

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_(eta,A,gamma,tau),           (7)

uniformly in R. The bounded initial y region has finitely many primes and input v in a fixed interval, so its full bill is part of B. The upper endpoint y<=R implies v<=R; no future values of z or unpriced transfer occur. This is a quadratic-form relative bound on the actual delayed source, not an operator contraction on arbitrary growing functions.

### 2.4 The exact hard-prime same-output diagonal costs only a constant

Expand the full hard-prime integrand BEFORE taking absolute values:

    Q_hard(R)=-Re int_0^R exp(-2gamma y)
      sum_(p>(2+y)^A)sum_(m,n>=1)
       conjugate(a(n))*chi(p)*a(m)*log p
       g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y)dy.                       (8)

There is no cutoff of m or n. The n=pm terms are nonzero only for squarefree q-units pm, so p does not divide m and

    -conjugate(a(pm))*chi(p)*a(m)=|a(m)|^2=1.

The exact diagonal D_R is therefore nonnegative. At a fixed squarefree n, its retained prime log-weights sum to at most log n. The whole-line Gaussian integral is exact:

    int_(-infinity)^infinity exp(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
       =exp(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi tau)).

Consequently, for gamma>1/2,

    0<=D_R<=B_diag
      =exp(tau gamma^2)/(2sqrt(pi tau))
         *sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2gamma)<infinity.         (9)

Natural zeros only lower this positive majorant. Define H_R=Q_hard(R)-D_R: it is precisely (8) restricted to n!=pm. All p,m,n signs and phases remain inside H_R. This same-output diagonal is different from deleting a signed subset of a completed physical form.

### 2.5 Complete criterion and quantitative zero return

**Proposition, conditional arithmetic input.** Fix one common gamma in(1/2,1), and A>0 satisfying A(1-gamma)<1. Suppose that for every fixed ordinary chi there are delta_chi>0 and B_chi<infinity such that, for all sufficiently large R,

    H_R <= (1-delta_chi) I_R+B_chi.                    (OPEN-PF)

Then every L(s,chi) has no ordinary zero with Re s>gamma. Constants and onsets may depend on chi; the common gamma does not.

Proof: choose eta=delta_chi/4 separately in(4),(7); absorb the bounded initial R range. Insert (9) and OPEN-PF into(2). For every R>=0,

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R
       +tau*gamma*E_R<=B'_chi.                         (10)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma y)) for y>=0. The left Gaussian tail and this right bound make F(s)=int_(-infinity)^infinity U(y)exp(-sy)dy holomorphic on Re s>gamma, including all compact-uniform derivatives. Absolute Fubini on Re s>1 gives

    F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Continue L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2). Its right side is never zero. At every regular zero of L in the half-plane the left side would vanish. The principal pole at1 is allowed and forces F to vanish there; imprimitive Euler factors were already retained through chi's natural zeros. All complex heights and all zero multiplicities are covered. The ordinary continuation, pole and imprimitive-factor conventions were checked against [NIST DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15), specifically25.15.1-4. This is a replacement source's complete return, with no borrowed native-H projectors, no unsmoothing and no fixed-height gap.

|Desired c|gamma|One allowed A|alpha=A(1-gamma)|Status|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
|.12515|.87485|7|.87605|Conditional gain .0000040364 over c11|
|1/6|5/6|5|5/6|Conditional|
|1/4|3/4|3|3/4|Conditional|
|.4999|.5001|1|.4999|Conditional high ceiling; gamma=1/2 is NOT covered|

The strongest objection is substantive: OPEN-PF is an unproved signed source-specific inequality. The full logarithmic equation lets its negative hard-prime correlation carry an entire hypothetical bad mode, so the identity alone cannot supply strict delta. A deliberately coarse trial does not close it. Even GRANTING an input |U(y)|<=C exp(beta y) for y>=0, gamma<beta<1, triangle and the full Gaussian left tail only give sum_p log p|U(y-log p)|<=C exp(y)(1+y). For p<=exp(y), sum over all integers p^-beta log p; for p>exp(y), use the Gaussian left tail and split into fixed log intervals. Thus the absolute flux budget has exponent1+beta-2gamma in R, whereas the available I_R budget has exponent2beta-2gamma up to logarithms. The unresolved exponent gap is1-beta. This is failure of that upper-bound trial, not a lower bound on the signed flux; the granted U input is not silently inferred from a bare zero-free assertion. The near,1/6 and1/4 targets therefore receive no arithmetic credit from the coarse test.

The proposition is an explicit localization of that gap, with actual complete paid sectors, not a proof of a new exponent or a claim that the remaining estimate is easy. W35 owns the Gaussian renewal sign; G79 owns general drift ideas; G118 owns the full logarithmic source identity. The incremental claim is the combined relative payment(4),(7),(9) and the exact prime-only off-diagonal criterion. Novelty elsewhere in the record or literature is not asserted beyond the inspected sources.

## 3. D2 / S21: exact cutoff insertion algebra and coherent boundary

This section concerns the ordinary squarefree source, not the Eisenstein native-H tensor. Let S_N={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, with orthonormal basis e_n. For each unramified prime p define

    B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) if p does not divide n and pn<=N; otherwise0.

Distinct B_p,B_r COMMUTE: if prn<=N and gcd(n,pr)=1 both orders give chi(pr)e_(prn), and otherwise both vanish. The divisor-closed cutoff cannot manufacture a noncommutative insertion effect. Fermionic ordering changes the operator and requires its own readout; the exterior construction of S13 cannot be substituted silently.

For p!=r the mixed commutator C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^* has the exact action

    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))*chi(r)e_(rm)
      if mu(m)^2=1,(m,qpr)=1,
         N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r); otherwise0.            (11)

At the lower endpoint equality gives zero because both paths exist. The upper endpoints are included. The proof compares the two paths: insertion first needs prm<=N, while deletion first needs only pm,rm<=N. No term with a square or nonunit is restored. C_pr is a phased negative partial isometry, so its norm is1 when this exact domain is nonempty and0 otherwise.

Let a_N=sum_(n in S_N)a(n)e_n. With the usual conjugate-first inner product,

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#{m in the domain of(11)}.           (12)

Indeed a(pm)=-chi(p)a(m), a(rm)=-chi(r)a(m), and every character phase cancels. This is an actual all-fixed-character coherence result, including complex and imprimitive chi, not an arbitrary phase model or a changing-conductor construction. With a general scalar profile f, replace a(n) by a(n)f(n); the contraction is exactly

    -sum_(m in domain)conjugate(f(rm))*f(pm).            (13)

For a real nonnegative profile it has one sign. General profiles must retain their products; this is not a signed-subset inequality.

In particular take the k unramified primes in(N/2,N]. On their span each C_pr is -conjugate(chi(p))*chi(r)|r><p|. Therefore the sum over ordered distinct p,r is unitarily conjugate to -(J_k-I_k), with eigenvalue -(k-1) on the ACTUAL source vector(-chi(p))_p and eigenvalue1 on its orthogonal complement. Its operator norm is k-1 for k>=2. The actual quadratic value is -k(k-1), not a square-root-size random fluctuation. A phase gauge changes neither this value nor the norm if it transports the source too.

This rejects the literal independence/orthogonality shortcut for this boundary algebra. It does not bound M_chi below, does not reject indefinite or source-specific compensation across other sectors, and does not establish a native-H phase value. The complete source return remains

    a_N=product_(p<=N,p not|q)(I-B_p)e_1,
    M_chi(N)=<sum_(n in S_N)e_n,a_N>.                   (14)

Every prime occurs once, insertion products commute, and the n<=N cutoff is exact. A proved bound |(14)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon) for every fixed chi/all large N gives zero exclusion through s int_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx, with the same principal/imprimitive/all-height argument as above. No such readout estimate follows from(11)-(13). This is the unpaid full complementary term; a bound only on commutators is insufficient.

Ancestry: W27/W59 cover the exterior cutoff/homology mechanism; G145 covers free-word abelianization and SORTED creation commutators with a different operator. Here B_p permits insertion at every absent prime and its mixed adjoint boundary is given explicitly by(11). G160's other all-character phase obstruction and G162's terminal-prime matching cut are related; neither is asserted to be this operator identity. This distinction, not a claim of a new broad family, is the proposed incremental record value.

## 4. D3 / S16: how much a small-prime syndrome can certify

Two elementary tests distinguish a probabilistic coding analogy from actual arithmetic.

First, on {0,1}^k let a syndrome be any linear map H over F2 whose row span does not contain the all-ones parity vector. Uniform measure on the even-parity hyperplane and uniform measure on the odd-parity hyperplane have exactly the SAME uniform syndrome distribution on im H; their parity biases are+1 and-1. Each syndrome fiber has equally many extensions of both parities before conditioning, because parity is independent of the rows of H. Their syndrome entropies and all statistics of that syndrome coincide. Thus entropy or a uniform syndrome alone does not control a missing parity character. This is a finite model obstruction, not an arithmetic lower bound.

For an ACTUAL arithmetic obstruction fix a principal character modulo q, let N grow, set y=sqrt(N), and partition S_N by the complete set of unramified prime divisors<=y. Let C0 be the cell with empty set. Since two primes>sqrt(N) have product>N,

    C0={1} union {p:sqrt(N)<p<=N,p not dividing q}.

Write L=#(C0 minus{1}), Q=#S_N. The signs in C0 are+1 at1 and-1 at each of its L primes, so its mass is L+1, signed sum1-L and conditional mean(1-L)/(L+1). Define the exact conditional square norm of any partition P by

    E(P)=sum_(C in P) |sum_(n in C)a(n)|^2/|C|,
    |M_chi(N)|<=sqrt(Q*E(P)).                          (15)

For this partition, and every REFINEMENT of it, conditional Cauchy gives

    E(P)>=(L-1)^2/(L+1)=L-3+4/(L+1).                  (16)

Refinement cannot reduce the conditional square norm. This allows all cancellation in every other cell; no unproved assumption about rough-number parity is made.

Elementary square-divisor counting gives Q=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N), kappa_q>0. An elementary prime-count lower bound suffices for L>>N/log N: binomial(2m,m)>=4^m/(2m+1), while each prime contributes at most2m to its factorization, so binomial(2m,m)<=(2m)^pi(2m). Use m=floor(N/2) and subtract pi(sqrt N)<=sqrt N plus finitely many ramified primes. No prime-distribution hypothesis is used. Therefore the NUMERIC RIGHT SIDE of the norm certificate(15) is at least

    sqrt(Q*E(P)) >>_q N/sqrt(log N).                   (17)

It cannot prove any fixed exponent gamma<1 by estimating E(P) from above. The target E(P)<<N^(2gamma-1+epsilon) is false for this observation, because(16) already has exponent1. For current gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 those putative E exponents are .74970,2/3,1/2. All fail for this particular positive conditional-square certificate.

This is NOT a lower bound for |M|. Coarsening cells so that terminal primes interact with other small-prime patterns, retaining cross-cell signed terms, or choosing an unrelated syndrome lies outside the obstruction. An arbitrary linear syndrome need not refine the small-prime pattern; the first toy and the second arithmetic test have distinct scopes. For every ordinary chi, a successful complete scalar reconstruction with |M_chi(N)|<<N^(gamma+epsilon) would have the full all-height reciprocal return already proved above; the principal case alone prevents this proposed universal norm route.

G103/G117/G145 own full energy, fiber/readout and positive diagonal-price warnings; G105 owns exact future-support merging. The narrow proposed addition is the explicit actual empty-syndrome cell after complete small-prime revelation, allowing arbitrary cancellation elsewhere and any further refinement. No literature novelty for the sieve parity problem or conditional expectation is claimed.

## 5. The other three tests keep their exact source obligations

S13's two-prime basis at cutoff5 is(1,2,3), with oriented deletion d e_2=d e_3=e_1. The degree2 vector e_6 is absent, so ker d in degree1 has dimension1. In the full cutoff6 complex it is killed by d e_6=e_3-e_2. This is the first decisive calculation, then exact W27/W59 source inspection identifies the duplicate and the general linear homology floor. The classical squarefree-complex/Betti ancestor was checked at [Bjorner's original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5704), submitted29January2011. Character insertion is not automatically a chain map. No unseen boundary is dropped and no new exterior development is claimed.

S25 preserves the native-H contract from [restricted research revision]/G163. With v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'), put H=w*Tv with T the TRANSPOSE of the scalar coefficient matrix. T retains the entire signed short-source sum/core, both projectors, natural zeros, phases, profiles, original masks, excluded equal-norm orientations and two independent heights. The raw target is B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), B0=G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig. N^-1 G^-2 is paid exactly once afterward. A bound tr((T*T)^2)<=B0^4 suffices since ||T||^4<=tr((T*T)^2); it keeps every four-cycle and diagonal and is G163 reuse. Knowing rank r or a favorable subset of singular values gives no upper bound on the largest singular value: diag(M,1,...,1) has fixed full rank and arbitrarily large norm. No arithmetic rank, random matrix replacement, scalar source identification with(14), or completed H saving is inferred. The protected serious upstream test was not replaced by this easy algebra check.

S07: for fixed q, orthogonality over all characters yields the exact averaged energy of M_chi as the signed same-residue sum. Every individual energy is at most phi(q) times that average, a permitted fixed-q factor. The unresolved principal q=1 component is still the whole signed Mobius energy. This is exactly G103; neither a tensor basis change nor the number of character coordinates pays it.

# [private research revision] independent headroom review: large common factors in the actual Liouville source

Decision: accept the author's complete large-gcd estimate and its literal changed-core reduction at the stated ordinary-character scope. The general-phase estimate is also valid, and admits the independent strengthening proved in support.md. No arithmetic power estimate for the retained signed core, new zero-free constant, Hecke transfer or growing-conductor statement is proved.



The current accepted source-relative calibration remains

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364.

F0/analytic ancestry, the original positive-slot uniformity and exact external root-definition/import/admission obligations remain open. The new elementary source theorem does not discharge those project obligations or imply record admission.

## 1. What this review accepts and adds

For literal ordered tuples, arbitrary shell-fixed bounded masks, every real G>=1, and f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6), the author proves

    ||sum_n f_x(n) sum_(d e l=n,gcd(d,e)>G)
                    a1(d)a2(e)b0(l)theta(d,e,l)||_(L1 or L2)
      <<_epsilon X^epsilon [X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)].        (R1)

Here |a1|,|a2|<=1, |b0|<=B0 fixed, |theta|<=1, and the norm is on every real x in [X,2X] with dx/x. Constants are uniform in the sequences, masks and G. All tuple phases, shared primes, natural zeros and strict endpoints are retained. This is a complete source norm bound, not just a diagonal estimate or a signed-subset comparison.

It pays the part of the accepted [restricted research revision] core with gcd(d,e)>X^(1-gamma), for 3/4<=gamma<1, while keeping every previous complement. Thus the retained signed core can impose the exact closed condition gcd(d,e)<=X^(1-gamma). This is a useful source restriction inside the previously unpaid interval, not merely an improved far-tail estimate. It is still equivalent, through paid norm differences, to the unproved complete source bound.

The independent addition is stronger for general fixed phases. Under the same tuple hypotheses, for every fixed b>1 and integer k>=4,

    ||sum_n v_G(n)exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k)||_(L1 or L2)
      <<_(b,k,epsilon,B0) X^epsilon[X/G+X^(b/2)/sqrt(G)]. (R2)

The proof retains the local error N/G^2 that the author's final block bound weakens to N^(1/3). It thereby pays the complete non-diagonal block sum by X^2/G^2. The coefficient epsilon is absorbed using the damping, so this improvement remains uniform for arbitrarily large G. It includes the closed degree endpoint k=4. The author's extra term X^(2k/(3k-2))/sqrt(G) is unnecessary in this range; its bound itself is not false.

The first term in (R2) already has the author's positive-mask lower example. Section 4 of support.md adds a finite random-sign existence proof of the second term's lower price in the broad mask class. Neither example is a lower bound for the actual signed Liouville core. These scoped obstructions identify what cannot be saved by a method treating its masks as arbitrary.

## 2. Intake, exact sources and novelty

The complete frozen author report was read in two bounded outputs (b0963f,67503a), its full helper and source-evidence in 23b121, and its full raw checks in e5719e. Its full manifest had been read in 73923b. The five pins were independently verified by the sole review helper run:

| Author file | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| report.md | 32271 | 8b2bcb6b2ce7c58315b5a05ddba196b7504c56b1f343eb1a0c08e32b02ce4eb8 |
| check.py | 8607 | 034e2c2f00d30d7b5d5c9d2bc975fad2d4f294efd78865df4a4356706f7248d9 |
| checks.json | 15750 | 52ff1d3a6cd4a3e3f80914a60d5bc6f6c1f03572f4e992ecf9231a14042e8c14 |
| source-evidence.json | 6843 | f0e10e32a8fa3b71097d055d793839384975fdc83f75a3e1133a5b2b81919814 |
| freeze.json | 2986 | 9558675f4625039cf135ba6f19863d7aedf6f45a308c85e2be3ee9967aafe84e |

The complete current attempt index, lines 1–388, was read in 4e1eba,246ff8,63b8bf. Current-proof's opening calibration/source qualifications were read in effd9a. The [restricted research revision] square-source integration was read in full in 8c070a. A wrapper truncated the middle of the [restricted research revision] Hecke integration; the missing parts were explicitly recovered in 63b8bf and dbd5bb. No complete read is inferred from a truncated wrapper alone.

The exact W24 R24.3 local multiplicity proof and endpoints were read in dbd5bb. [restricted research revision]'s fixed-source Mellin/two-prime/general-shift contract and [restricted research revision]'s general complete-tail/finite-descent contract were read in 63f95f. The R35 branch obstruction and its W22 credit were located and reviewed in effd9a. The full earlier [restricted research revision] independent proof remains retained in this same review context. Eleven author-listed local source pins were unchanged at the independent check; the receipt distinguishes pinning from mathematical reading. Not every historical source was reread wholesale this pass.

Novelty is relative to these inspected project sources. W24 owns the interval count; [restricted research revision] owns the nonlinear shell kernel and finite-shift return; [restricted research revision] owns the square collision method, Liouville completion and its paid short-source/core range. The author's large-root collision application is a new complete estimate for this literal within-source gcd. The independent (R2) is a further quantitative sharpening of that proof. No literature-priority claim is made. The original Hecke cross-copy gcd/projector problem accepted in [restricted research revision] has different coefficients and variables; neither its mixed-moment permission nor its physical zero return is imported here.

## 3. Reconstructing the author's unconditional estimate

The actual positive counting object is

    r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2 divides n}.

It counts every possible square divisor, including products of smaller primes and distinct roots producing the same output. It is not an indicator of one large repeated prime. The identity

    sum_(n<=Y) r_G(n)^2
       =sum_(r,s>G)floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G            (R3)

is valid, uniformly for real G>=1. Setting r=gu,s=gv with (u,v)=1 gives g>G/min(u,v), not a maximum. The g tail contributes at most 2min(u,v)/G; the resulting absolutely convergent double series has bound below eight. Thus the author's constant sixteen is safe. The first moment is at most 2Y/G. Diagonal r=s, nonintegral cutoffs and the strict r>G convention are all included.

At each actual tuple, r is the unique exact gcd(d,e), with d=ru,e=rv and (u,v)=1. Dropping this last condition only in a positive upper bound leaves at most d3(n/r^2)<=d3(n) factorizations. Hence

    |v_G(n)| <<_(eta,B0) n^eta r_G(n),
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| <<Y^(1+eta)/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 <<Y^(1+2eta)/G.                 (R4)

This proof survives every admissible complex tuple mask. It does not require the actual signed merged coefficient to retain an unsigned number of factorizations. In particular it is not an invalid norm monotonicity assertion.

W24's count gives, for intervals I in [cN,CN] of length h,

    sum_(n in I)r_G(n) <<h/G+min(N^(1/3),N/G^2).         (R5)

The reciprocal count h/G+N/G^2 is valid for all G by reversing n=r^2 l; there are at most CN/G^2 cofactors l and each real root interval has length O(h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l))). The +1 in each count pays closed endpoints and intervals shorter than one. If G>sqrt(CN), the sum is empty. The N^(1/3) alternative is the usual small-root split. No prime distribution or arithmetic cancellation is used in either estimate.

The smooth enclosing-shell kernel follows by two integrations by parts:

    |K_X(n,m)| <<exp(-c(n+m)/X^(3/2))
                   min(1,[X^6/|n^6-m^6|]^2),           (R6)

with diagonal factor one. After x=Xu, the phase derivative never vanishes on the fixed positive support. Derivatives of the true damping create only fixed polynomials in (n+m)/X^(3/2), absorbed into a weaker exponential. This is uniform over every real x in the shell at the norm level; an x grid is irrelevant.

Split exactly at n<=X. The whole low source costs O(X^(1+eta)/G). For every comparable ordered high pair use a bounded-overlap block n,m~N>=cX, and put H=X^6/N^5. Local annuli, (R5), and the full mass O(N/G) give the author's LG6. The integer row sum O(1+H), inequality 2|v_n v_m|<=|v_n|^2+|v_m|^2 and (R3) give LG7 for the SAME positive absolute pair sum. Thus taking their minimum is lawful. The diagonal at H<1 is paid by the local +1 contribution; off-diagonal distances begin at one, with weights O(H^2).

The author's resulting bound

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2))N^(2eta)
      [X^6/(G^2N^4)+(N/G)(1+min(N^(1/3),H))]

sums to O(X^(2+2eta)/G^2+X^(3/2+3eta)/G). In the last minimum, N^(4/3) and X^6 N^-4 meet at N=X^(9/8), with squared cost X^(3/2)/G. The isolated diagonal uses the actual infinite damping. No high block is discarded.

For far pairs, n~N and X<m<n/2, the gap has size N^6. The shell and cumulative masses from (R4) yield X^12 N^(-10+2eta)/G^2; summing from N~X gives X^(2+2eta)/G^2. The reverse ordered orientation contributes the same bound. The entire low/high interaction is paid by norm triangle, rather than an unjustified scalar cross-term error. Taking square roots and choosing eta after epsilon proves (R1), and finite-measure Cauchy-Schwarz gives L1.

These checks resolve the strongest cheap objections: collisions are counted, local density is not replaced by a support indicator, H<1 retains its diagonal, both far orientations survive, arbitrary frozen phases cause no change, and no polynomial upper bound on G was inserted.

## 4. Independent general-phase strengthening and its honest scope

The full proof is in support.md; this is its decisive calculation. For fixed b>1, integer k>=4 and H=X^k/N^(k-1), retain the N/G^2 version of (R5). The comparable block has both bounds

    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)[HN/G^2+N^2/G^3],
    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)(N/G)(1+H).

Their minimum is at most the common factor times

    X^k/(G^2N^(k-2))+N/G
                     +min(N^2/G^3,X^k N^(2-k)/G).      (R7)

Absorb N^(2eta) into the actual damping at the cost X^(2b eta). This is essential at k=4 and for G not bounded by a power of X; using G^eta<=X^epsilon would be false. The last two branches meet at N_*=XG^(2/k). Their complete geometric sum is

    O_k(X^2 G^(4/k-3)) <=O_k(X^2/G^2), k>=4.            (R8)

The first term sums from N>=cX to X^2/G^2, while damping pays the isolated N/G term by X^b/G. Both far orientations sum to X^(2+2eta)/G^2; low/high triangle remains unchanged. This proves (R2).

Consequently the additional large-gcd complement with G=X^(1-gamma) is paid whenever gamma>=b-1, for every k>=4. The author's additional condition gamma>=(k+2)/(3k-2) is a sufficient condition extracted from its weaker displayed general bound, not a necessary restriction of this complement. All old square-source, derivative-gap and full-tail conditions remain required separately. This review does not obtain a new complete architecture merely by lowering k.

Two scoped lower examples clarify the result. The author's mask retaining d=e=r, G<r<=2G and r^2 l<=X/2 has full positive real part and norm at least cX/G for G<=c' sqrt(X). For the damped diagonal, put Y=floor(X^b), retain d=e=r, G<r<=2G and Y/2<r^2 l<=Y. Its output multiplicities A_n have sum A_n^2>=sum A_n>>Y/G for G<=c' sqrt(Y). Assign each output n an independent sign epsilon_n, common to all its tuples. The second and fourth sign moments give

    E|sum epsilon_n z_n| >=(sum |z_n|^2)^(1/2)/sqrt(3).

Since |f_x(n)|>=e^-1 throughout the shell, integrating this finite expectation proves that some ONE frozen sign mask has L1 norm at least cX^(b/2)/sqrt(G), and hence the same L2 lower price. This is a deterministic existence consequence of a finite probability calculation, with no sampled signs or average over actual arithmetic. It says nothing about a lower bound for the real Liouville signs. The broad-class condition gamma>=b-1 cannot generally be dropped for gamma>1/2.

The refinement is useful analytic progress in a paid component. It supplies no power saving in the retained small-gcd sum. Improving the already paid large-gcd component again would not settle the research target.

## 5. Source identity and the complete changed-core transfer

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q with its natural zeros, and a fixed prime p not dividing q. Let a=lambda chi, h=chi, and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 with zero extension off squares. Prime-power multiplication gives a*h=s. Keep exactly

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g=a*a*b.                           (R9)

The p^2 coefficient is -p chi(p)^2. It is not -p^2 chi(p)^2. The complete ordinary cofactor and root cofactor are

    b(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)).

Their periods are p^3q and pq; sums over one full period vanish by grouping multiples of p. Natural zeros are preserved without division by a character value. The two physical root rows from q1 keep coefficients 1 and -p chi(p). The Euler series on Re z>1 is

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).  (R10)

For 3/4<=gamma<1 set L=X^gamma, M=X^r with r=(6-2gamma)/4, Q=p^3q and eta0=1/(6000Q). Put

    B(n)=min(L,eta0 X^6/n^5),
    U(n)=B(n)^tau, V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau),
    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau))<=(11gamma-3)/8.          (R11)

The parameter tau is fixed before x varies. At each n separately the cuts U(n),V(n) are frozen, so the indicator identity on the ordered d,e slots gives

    c(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n),
    Q_U(n)=sum_(d e=n,d<=U(n))a(d)(v*s)(e),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l).    (R12)

Q_V is the other full ordered short slot. The identity remains true even where B(n)<1, when both short slots vanish. Nothing is differentiated through a cutoff. The total C(x)=sum c(n)f_x(n) is fixed independently of the shell.

[restricted research revision]'s complete short-source inequality is

    ||Q_D||_2^2 <<D^2+X^(6/11)D^(16/11)+X^(3/4)D^(1/2)
                   +min(X^(3/5)D^(7/5),X^(15/16)D^(1/2)).

Its norm exponents at D=X^alpha are alpha,(3+8alpha)/11,3/8+alpha/4 and min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4). All are <=gamma under (R11). Each moving short root cut is a prefix because B(e d r^2) is nonincreasing in r, so the actual uniform-prefix theorem applies to both slots. The original full small-double source is O(X^gamma), using the nonzero periodic Fourier modes of b and the derivative-gap cut eta0. This argument is applied before the gcd restriction; the restricted b mask need not be periodic.

Define the smaller finite core

    T_small(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) f_x(n)
       sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n),gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b(l),
    G=X^(1-gamma).                                     (R13)

The difference from the old finite core is EXACTLY the source in (R1) with its original n,d,e mask and |b|<=(p+1)^2. Its two norm costs have exponents gamma and 1/4+gamma/2, the latter <=gamma. Strict gcd>G is paid; equality gcd=G stays in (R13). Uniformity in all masks implies uniformity throughout the allowed closed tau corridor.

The complete difference C-T_small consists of BOTH short sources, minus the full small-double source, the original R_tau prefix n<=L, the entire damped R_tau tail n>M, and the finite-core large-gcd part. The prefix uses |R_tau(n)|<=(p+1)^2 d3(n). The full tail costs squared norm X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon); gamma>=3/4 pays its diagonal and the choice of r pays its off-diagonal. Every mixed term is covered by norm triangle. Therefore

    ||C-T_small||_(Lj([X,2X],dx/x))
       <<_(p,q,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.  (R14)

There is no unproved scalar energy-error statement and no deletion of a signed subset. The entire arithmetic cofactor range and both orderings remain. Complete multiplicativity, including common primes, gives the exact merged form

    R_small(n)=sum_(m l=n) a(m)D_(U(n),V(n);G)(m)b(l),
    D_(U,V;G)(m)=#{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G}.

No analogous unrestricted Mobius merge is used.

## 6. Precise OPEN estimate and every-height zero return

The remaining sufficient input is the full signed L1 estimate for (R13): one common gamma<gamma11 chosen before chi and any candidate zero, such that for each fixed ordinary character chi and each of a fixed covering pair of unramified primes, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    int_X^(2X)|T_small,p,chi,tau_X(x)| dx/x
        <<_(p,chi,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).      (OPEN-LCG)

The choices tau_X may depend on epsilon, chi,p,X, but must satisfy (R11) and be fixed before live x. Constants and scale thresholds may depend on these fixed data. The pair of primes is chosen before the height and shell. A full L2 bound at the same exponent is stronger and sufficient. A fixed positive epsilon loss, selected block, sampled x, finite height band or character average is insufficient.

By (R14), this all-shell hypothesis is equivalent to the full L1 bound for the fixed source C. This norm equivalence is not arithmetic progress by itself and is not asserted to be an equivalence to zero exclusion.

The complete return can be reconstructed directly. Put

    H_p(z)=int_0^infinity C_p,chi(1/t)t^(z-1)dt.

Shell summation with epsilon smaller than Re z-gamma gives holomorphy on Re z>gamma, also after any fixed number of derivatives on every finite height compact set. Polynomial coefficient bounds and exp(-n/x^(3/2)) pay the other endpoint x near zero. Absolute Fubini initially requires Re z>3/2, with a sufficiently small divisor-exponent buffer.

For each coefficient integral, set v=nt and rotate clockwise through fixed 0<theta<min(pi/3,pi/12). On the sector, Re(v^(3/2))>0 and the oscillatory factor is nonincreasing in modulus; damping kills the large arc for each n and Re z>0 kills the small arc. On the ray exp(-iv^6) has exponential decay. The one-term Taylor remainder in exp(-n^(-1/2)v^(3/2)) is thus bounded by a compactly integrable constant times n^-1/2. It follows that

    I_n(z)=A0(z)n^-z+O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6.

Derivatives have only the corresponding logarithmic factors. Summing with |c(n)|<<_delta n^delta gives a normally holomorphic E_p on Re z>1/2. Hence

    H_p(z)=A0(z)P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi)+E_p(z). (R15)

The Mellin identity uses the original complete C, not the shell-dependent restricted core. That is why the paid transfer (R14) is indispensable.

A0 is finite and nonzero for Re z>0. J_p has zeros only on Re z=1/2. The Euler product makes L(2z,chi^2) finite and nonzero for Re z>1/2; its possible pole at 1/2 is outside the domain. P_p zeros lie on Re z=1. Two distinct fixed unramified primes have no common P zero at nonzero height, since such a zero would make log p1/log p2 rational using finite-order character values. For nonprincipal chi, choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1 to cover height zero; such a prime exists by factoring an integer with nontrivial character value. For principal chi the pole at one is the specified exception. Thus (R15) excludes each finite-height zero with Re z>gamma. No maximum zero height, rightmost attained zero or height-uniform constant is assumed. Natural imprimitive Euler factors remain present; no growing-conductor conclusion follows.

For general fixed b>1 and integer k, retain every term j<K:

    H_p(z)=sum_(j<K) A_j(z)D_c(z+(b-1)j)+E_(p,K)(z),
    A_j(z)=(-1)^j Gamma((z+bj)/k)
                   exp(-i pi(z+bj)/(2k))/(k j!).

Choose fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. The remainder is normally holomorphic on Re z>max(0,1-(b-1)K). Start above one, where the Euler reciprocal is holomorphic, and descend by finitely many strips of width b-1. Every positive shift is already holomorphic before solving for the unshifted reciprocal, with the same two-prime cover. The factors L(2w,chi^2), J_p(w) and the principal pole retain exactly the preceding scope for w in this domain. No finite shift is omitted.

The inherited full architecture for each fixed gamma>1/2 chooses fixed 1<b<=2gamma and sufficiently large k with b>=2k/(2k-1), r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b and the old short corridor alpha<=(4gamma-b)/3. Then (R2) pays its new gcd complement because gamma>=b-1. For example gamma=3/5,b=11/10,k=12,K=5,r=27/25 is compatible. All of this is conditional on its complete signed core norm. There is no boundary gamma=1/2 or uniform limiting-parameter theorem.

## 7. Quantitative targets, actual failed test and discovery audit

The gcd thresholds for the unchanged k=6,b=3/2 architecture are:

## 6. Complete fixed-detector Mellin return

For these literal coefficients, initially in Re z>1,

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z),
    J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).                            (6.1)

Natural imprimitive Euler factors are included in each L function. Define H_p(z)=int_0^infinity C_p(x)x^(-z) dx/x. Initial absolute Fubini holds on Re z>3/2 with a divisor-loss buffer. After t=1/x and u=nt, the individual transform is

    n^(-z) int_0^infinity e^(-n^(-1/2)u^(3/2)-iu^12)u^(z-1)du.

Rotate clockwise to a fixed ray of angle -alpha, where 0<alpha<min(pi/3,pi/24). Principal powers are fixed throughout. Both damping real parts have the correct sign there; the degree12 term supplies exp(-c|u|^12). The original damped integral permits the rotation for each n. On the ray,

    |e^(-n^(-1/2)u^(3/2))-1|<=n^(-1/2)|u|^(3/2).

Subtracting one leading term therefore leaves O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)) locally uniformly on each compact K in Re z>0, including z derivatives with their logarithms. With |c(n)|<<_eta n^eta, the summed remainder is normally holomorphic in Re z>1/2, choosing eta after the compact's distance from that boundary. The leading rotated gamma integral is exactly

    A0(z)=Gamma(z/12)exp(-i pi z/24)/12.

Thus meromorphic continuation of the initial identity gives

    H_p(z)=A0(z)D_c(z)+E_p(z),
    E_p holomorphic on Re z>1/2.                         (6.2)

This detector has b=3/2, so ONE Taylor term suffices above gamma=5/6. No positive finite-shift term is silently discarded. The gamma factor is holomorphic and nonzero in Re z>0.

The sufficient source hypothesis is: for every fixed ordinary chi, both primes of a fixed covering pair, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    ||T_(p,chi,X)||_1 <<_(chi,p,epsilon) X^(5/6+epsilon).   (OPEN12)

The coefficients c and detector C_p are fixed across shells, even though the core cuts depend on X. By (4.4), OPEN12 bounds that fixed C_p on every shell. Choosing epsilon below Re z-5/6 makes the dyadic Mellin integral normally convergent in Re z>5/6. Its small-x end is exponentially convergent. Hence H_p is holomorphic there, and (6.2) continues D_c there.

For Re z>1/2, J_p and L(2z,chi^2)^2 are finite and nonzero. The possible zero of P_p has Re z=1. Two distinct unramified primes cannot share such a zero at nonzero height: their finite-order character phases would force log(p1)/log(p2) rational, contradicting unique factorization. For nonprincipal chi choose one covering prime with chi(p)!=1; such a prime exists by factoring a unit integer on which chi is nontrivial. It covers height zero. For principal chi the pole at z=1 is the stated exception, rather than a zero to exclude.

Every hypothetical ordinary zero in Re z>5/6 is therefore detected by at least one fixed member of the pair. This is an all-height conditional implication: no bound uniform as height or conductor grows has been assumed or inferred, and compact local holomorphy suffices at each finite height. It would give c=1/6 if OPEN12 were established. OPEN12 and (OG12) remain unproved, so c11 is unchanged.

### Uniform readout, finite parameters, and actual costs

At a fixed rho, set m_rho=max_(t in I)|N_rho(t)| and D_rho=max_(t in I)|N'_rho(t)|. If D_rho>0, a one-sided interval of length

    ell=min(|I|/2,m_rho/(2D_rho))

has |N_rho|>=m_rho/2. Hence ||N_rho||²>=ell*m_rho²/4. If D_rho=0 the exact lower bound is |I|m_rho². These are positive quantities; no claimed numerical all-height lower bound is hidden.

For a fixed compact strip/height window K0 lying in the relevant half-plane, m0=min_(s in K0)max_I|N_s|>0 and D0=max_(K0 x I)|N'_s|<infinity. The same formula gives a uniform compact-window bound. A grid with mesh <=m0/(2D0) then captures at least m0/2 at one node for every s in K0; equal-weight squared readout costs at worst m0²/(4N). This is an effective prescription only once certified bounds for m0,D0 are supplied. The consultation supplies no explicit bound as the height window tends to infinity. Its qualitative pole contradiction does not need one. A quantitative contour or resolvent argument WOULD need that additional height cost.

Parameter order matters:

* Fix I before the scale X. The continuum norm is a complete sufficient target.
* A single unspecified generic t already avoids simultaneous masking at every zeta_K zero: each fixed rho has a discrete bad-t set, and their union is countable. This is an existence statement, not a certified named phase or an estimate for that phase. Fubini applied to all rational positive epsilon values can extract an almost-everywhere scalar return from the continuum norm.
* A preselected finite explicit list has no established global noncommon-zero guarantee here. On each fixed compact window a finite list exists by the preceding bound. Growing the height window requires renewing its capture certificate.
* Finite moving quadrature can approximate the continuum ARITHMETIC energy cheaply. On x in [X,2X], the compact kernel gives Nd<=sqrt(2eX), so F_t is an exponential polynomial with frequencies in [0,Lambda], Lambda=.5 log(2eX), and total coefficient mass O(X log X). Thus |F_t|² has frequencies in [-Lambda,Lambda]. An N-node Gauss rule on I is exact to degree2N-1 and has positive weights summing |I|. Taylor's integral remainder gives error at most

      C_I X² log²X [e Lambda |I|/(4N)]^(2N).

  Taking N=C_A log X with a sufficiently large fixed C_A pays any prescribed X^-A error, uniformly in x; integrate dx/x afterwards. This is O(log X) parameter samples with no exponent loss. Nodes depend on X; they approximate the fixed interval norm and are not a claim about finitely many fixed detectors. All within-sample square-divisor cross terms remain.

## 5. Primary arithmetic import and what its uniformity buys

The operative source is Green--Tao, *The Mobius function is strongly
orthogonal to nilsequences*, Annals of Mathematics175(2012),541--566,
[Theorem1.1, printed542--543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf).
I independently read the complete theorem across those pages through the
primary web PDF text. It gives arbitrary fixed logarithmic decay for
bounded Lipschitz functions on fixed rational nilmanifold data, uniformly
in polynomial sequences of fixed degree; constants are ineffective.

Use the circle with a degree-six abelian filtration (G_0=...=G_6=R,
and G_j trivial for j>=7), and fixed sine/cosine
functions. Their complex combination gives

    sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)e(P(n)) <<_A Y(log(2Y))^(-A), deg P<=6,

uniformly in the REAL coefficients of P, with A fixed in advance. A fixed
two-dimensional torus with a dummy coordinate is an equivalent realization.
There is no equidistribution hypothesis in this final theorem. No
growing-degree or growing-A uniformity is imported.

Literal finite Fourier expansion of chi is

    chi(n)=sum_(ell=0)^(q-1)c_ell e(ell n/q),
    c_ell=q^(-1)sum_(a mod q)chi(a)e(-ell a/q).

It preserves the zero values and has sum|c_ell|<=q. The polynomial for
each mode is P(n)=ell n/q-n^6/(2*pi*x^6), so all real x are covered.
For prefixes Y<=M, Y<sqrt M costs sqrt M; otherwise log(2Y) is comparable
to log M. The supremum of these prefixes is O_(q,A)(M(log M)^(-A)).
Abel summation with the actual positive decreasing exp(-n/x^(3/2)) has
uniformly bounded endpoint-plus-variation cost, for every x>0. Hence

    |W_<=M(x)| <<_(q,A) M(log M)^(-A).

With M=X(log X)^B, the author's B=(D+2)/4 and
A=B+(D+2)/2 give core logarithmic exponent -D-2 and complete sharp
off-diagonal exponent -D-1. Therefore

    E(X)<<_(q,D)X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D)                  (R12)

for every fixed D>0. This genuinely uses arithmetic, but the exponent2
exceeds 2theta11 by .2502919272. Cauchy--Schwarz yields the actual full
L1 bound X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D), after using2D in(R12); its power gap is
c11. D depending on X would invalidate the import and these constants.

The independently inspected [Gao--Zhao v2 Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09241v2)
explicitly assumes GRH and averages a quadratic-character family. It is
correctly excluded from the argument. Its theorem is on PDF page index1
(printed page2). The Green--Tao GRH power-decay remark is likewise unused.
No local PDF binary or image-byte inspection/hash is claimed; primary
theorem text was available through web reads.

## 2. Exposed prime bits and the remaining full covariance

For a finite prime set P containing 2 and excluding 3, let
Q=product_(p in P)p, a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)), and
r_P(n)=f(n)a_P(n). The actual source is on all integers. Its occupancy
probabilities are 1/p, whereas the squarefree law in W38 uses 1/(p+1).
The zero mean at p=2 is essential.

For every fixed delta>0 and any moving family with Q<=X^(1-delta),
periodic Gaussian Poisson summation gives F_P(x)=O_A(X^-A) on [X,2X]
for every A. It also gives the entire occupancy-pattern law in L1 to
arbitrary power accuracy; summing at most 2^|P|<=Q patterns is paid.
This uses the actual Gaussian measure mu_x(n)=g(log(n/x))/Z(x),
Z(x)=e^(tau/2)x+O_A(x^-A).

The exact remaining identity is

    F(x)=Z(x) Cov_mu_x(a_P,r_P)+F_P(x) E_mu_x[r_P].       ([restricted research revision]-S2)

Thus the complete exponent gamma is equivalent to the all-shell squared
covariance target X^(2gamma-2+epsilon). Every conditional tail mean,
including rare patterns, remains. Exposed-bit independence does not bound
this covariance. Credit [private research revision] S24--29 and Sol D33 for the prior mechanism;
W41 adds the full-pattern L1 statement and explicit normalized covariance
form, not a new finite-prime cancellation discovery.

statement:
## 6. Actual coefficient variance and the coarse complete arithmetic test

The added square factor need not be paid by a pointwise divisor bound in the FULL source. For g=a*s, its exact local coefficient is

    g(l^nu)=chi(l)^nu (-1)^nu (floor(nu/2)+1)

at each prime l. For all n,

    |g(n)|^2=1_((n,q)=1) sum_(d^2|n) d_2(d^2),        (6.1)

where d_2 is the ordinary divisor function. At l^nu, the right side is sum_(j=0)^(floor(nu/2))(2j+1)=(floor(nu/2)+1)^2; multiplicativity proves the formula, with the ramified zero unchanged. Hence

    sum_(n<=Y)|g(n)|^2 = C_chi Y+O_q(sqrt(Y)log^2(2Y)),
    C_chi=(phi(q)/q) sum_((d,q)=1) d_2(d^2)/d^2 >0.    (6.2)

Indeed the coprime count is phi(q)Y/(q d^2)+O_q(1). The errors and omitted main tail follow from sum_(d<=Z)d_2(d^2)<<Z log^2(2Z), since d_2(d^2)<=d_3(d), and dyadic partial summation. The constant series converges absolutely. The finite convolution by v and weighted Cauchy-Schwarz then give

    sum_(n<=Y)|c(n)|^2 <<_(p,q) Y.                    (6.3)

All cross terms of the finite compensator are included by Cauchy-Schwarz; (6.3) is not an asserted exact diagonal formula for c. In particular the COMPLETE damped source diagonal is O_(p,q)(X^(3/2)), with no logarithmic or epsilon loss.

For clarity, (6.3) also gives a useful exact-power full-source tail. With the same smooth shell majorant, for n>=M>=X the off-diagonal row sum of the squared-decay kernel is

    sum_(m>M,m!=n) min(1,[X^6/|n^6-m^6|]^2) << X^6/n^5.

Split n/2<m<2n, where |n^6-m^6| is bounded below by a constant times n^5|n-m|, and its two complements. On those complements their sum is O(X^12/n^11)<=O(X^6/n^5) because n>=X. The inequality 2|c_n c_m|<=|c_n|^2+|c_m|^2 pays both orientations. Partial summation in (6.3) yields

    ||sum_(n>M)c(n)f_x(n)||_2^2
        <<_(p,q) X^(3/2)+X^6 M^(-4), M>=X.           (6.4)

Damping is retained on the diagonal and can be dropped only in the already convergent off-diagonal. This is an actual full-source estimate, not a price for just its squarefree part. At M=X, combine (6.4) with sum_(n<=X)|c(n)|<<X from (6.3):

    ||C_p,chi||_1 <= (log2)^(1/2)||C_p,chi||_2 << X.  (6.5)

Thus the deliberately coarse COMPLETE test yields exponent1, short by c11 in the norm power. There is no hidden gain from the Euler numerator or the source change.

One can transfer the known logarithmic arithmetic input without inventing a power. Green--Tao, published Theorem1.1, pp.542-543, gives every fixed logarithmic Mobius saving for fixed-degree polynomial nilsequences, uniform in the polynomial coefficients; constants are ineffective. As in [restricted research revision], use a fixed torus with degree-k filtration, a dummy coordinate if needed, and fixed sine/cosine functions. Expand the actual finite periodic chi to retain its zeros. The resulting input is

    sum_(m<=Y) mu(m)chi(m)e(P(m)) <<_(q,A,k)
                                      Y(log(2Y))^(-A),

uniformly over real polynomials of fixed degree k. No GRH remark, growing degree or X-dependent logarithmic strength is imported. [Published primary theorem](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf).

Since a=(mu chi)*s, where (mu chi)(m)=mu(m)chi(m) is pointwise, the exact source g=(mu chi)*s*s has expansion

    g(n)=sum_(r^2 m=n) d_2(r)chi(r)^2 mu(m)chi(m).      (6.6)

There are no gcd conditions. For the polynomial prefix sum of g, split r at (log(2Y))^B with fixed B. Below that cutoff the inner length Y/r^2 has logarithm comparable to log Y, and the displayed arithmetic theorem applies to P(r^2 m), still of fixed degree. Sum its bound using the convergent sum d_2(r)/r^2. The entire remaining r-sum costs

    Y sum_(r>(log(2Y))^B) d_2(r)/r^2
       << Y log log(3Y)/(log(2Y))^B.

Choosing B after the desired fixed logarithmic power proves the same all-polynomial prefix estimate for g, then for c by its FOUR fixed v dilations. This is a transfer of [restricted research revision]'s arithmetic input, not a new power-cancellation theorem for Liouville.

Partial summation against the actual decreasing damping gives the bound M(log M)^(-A) for C restricted to n<=M, uniformly in x; split small prefix lengths at sqrt(M) to justify the common logarithm. Taking M=X(log X)^B in (6.4), and choosing fixed A,B large enough for each fixed D>0, proves

    ||C_p,chi||_2^2 <<_(p,q,D) X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D),
    ||C_p,chi||_1 <<_(p,q,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D).    (6.7)

Equation (5.6) then gives every fixed logarithmic saving for the complete finite T as well (its X^(gamma+epsilon) error is smaller for a sufficiently small fixed epsilon). But no fixed D turns (6.7) into X^(gamma+epsilon) for gamma<1. This is the strongest completed coarse arithmetic test in this pass, and it fails the first-gain power threshold honestly.
