# [private research revision] headroom: adaptive completion on the actual phase surface



Written incumbent c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, gamma11=.8748540364.
All F0/positive-slot/external admission qualifications remain OPEN. No
new c is proved by the current partial work. Ordinary fixed characters,
all natural zeros, every real shell point and complete signed sources
are retained. No formalization, children, provider jobs or shared writes.

## 1. Discovery before selection

Three distinct mechanisms were compared before the full index read.

1. A larger finite mean-zero compensator bank could couple the terminal
   prime/cofactor cells. Its immediate difficulty is algebraic: if a
   convolution compensator v has v(1)=1, then (v-v*chi)(r)=-chi(r)
   for every prime r, independently of v(r). Simply adding normalized
   compensators therefore does not remove the prime cofactor source.
   A vanishing first coefficient only moves the first nonzero source.
   This is a test of finite compensators, not a no-go for all banks.
2. Exact prime extraction or higher completion could redistribute the
   long Mobius variable before absolute values. Primary work on Ramare
   identities and short intervals keeps a genuine restricted cofactor,
   prime-square correction and extraction error. The available stated
   theorems supply logarithmic savings; they cannot be substituted for
   the desired power. A paid source-specific extraction remains viable.
3. Change the *geometry of completion*, not its scalar parameters.
   The accepted proof uses a rectangular cutoff chosen for the worst
   physical product M. A cutoff depending on the physical integer n
   can retain the discrete Fourier gap separately on every row. The
   key issue is whether the moving cutoff still leaves an interval in
   each cofactor row and whether the short terms remain affordable.
   Both appear to hold for the explicit decreasing phase surface below.

Selected mechanism3: develop a nonrectangular exact completion, then
test a signed cutoff bank rather than treating the resulting region
reduction as an arithmetic saving. Potential conditional reach remains
near gains,1/6,1/4 (and fixed gamma>1/2 with the earlier finite-shift return).

The complete current attempt index was read after this comparison.
Relevant ancestry is R35 completion, G140-G142 nonlinear tail/return,
and the full independently reviewed G152-G154 asymmetric completion.
The latter review was read in full. No novelty is claimed for those
identities or for a mere equivalent-norm restatement. The proposed new
piece is the uniformly paid curved cutoff, allowing a longer actual
Mobius prefix in the difficult n~X region.

## 2. Saved mathematical prefix: adaptive one-Mobius cutoff

Fix chi modulo q and prime p not dividing q, as in G152. Write
a=mu*chi pointwise, h(n)=chi(n), q_p=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
b_p=q_p*h (Dirichlet convolution), c_p=q_p*a, and h_p=q_p-b_p.
Thus h_p(1)=0, h_p(p)=-chi(p), and the remaining h_p(j) are
-chi(j)(1-p 1_(p|j)). The exceptional coefficients stay present.

Let f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), x in the FULL interval[X,2X].
Fix gamma>1/2, integer k>2 with u=2gamma-r>0, b<=2gamma,
r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), M=X^r, eta0=1/(100kpq).
Provisional new cutoff:

    A_X(n)=min(X^gamma, eta0 X^k/n^(k-1)).

At each integer n, use the exact asymmetric completion with the literal
real cutoff A_X(n); this is coefficientwise, so dependence on n is legal.
The small source is

    S_ad(n)=sum_(d|n, d<=A_X(n)) a(d)b_p(n/d).

For fixed d<=X^gamma, its cofactor condition is the single prefix

    1<=l<= (eta0 X^k/d^k)^(1/(k-1)).

The phase derivative correction on that prefix is at most k eta0/(2pi).
The accepted nonzero Fourier-mode argument thus bounds every row by
O_(p,q,k)(1), including actual damping and sharp endpoints. The total
small source costs O(X^gamma), without choosing a worst-case cutoff at M.
The short q_p*m_(A_X(n)) source is supported in n<=p X^gamma and is
bounded in absolute sum by O_p(X^gamma). The extra q_p term is finite.
The remaining source is sum_(d|n,d>A_X(n))a(d)h_p(n/d).

The following sections complete this prefix. The complete remaining
signed core is still OPEN. The current next action is independent review
of the adaptive proof and the bounded-bank obstruction; no numerical
endpoint promotion is requested.

## 3. A uniformly paid adaptive completion theorem

All convolutions below are Dirichlet convolutions; a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)
is a pointwise product. Fix 1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, and
1<b<=2gamma. Put

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), L=X^gamma, M=X^r,
    eta=1/(100kpq), B_X(n)=min(L,eta X^k/n^(k-1)).

No u>0 hypothesis is needed for this theorem; it is useful when
comparing to the earlier constant-cut core. Fix tau in[0,1], or allow
tau=tau_X in that interval with its choice frozen before x varies.
Define U_X(n)=B_X(n)^tau and V_X(n)=B_X(n)^(1-tau).
At tau=0 or1 use the literal convention B^0=1, even if B<1.
All comparisons against these positive real numbers are literal.

For each n, let m_{U(n)}(d)=a(d)1_(d<=U(n)); define m_V likewise.
This notation describes a family of coefficientwise finite identities,
not convolution by one global sequence with a moving index. Set

    Q_U(n)=sum_(d e=n) q_p(e)a(d)1_(d<=U(n)),
    Q_V(n)=sum_(d e=n) q_p(e)a(d)1_(d<=V(n)),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l).

Then, at EVERY positive integer n,

    c_p(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n).       (3.1)

Proof: for that n alone freeze both real cutoffs and apply
(a-m_U)*(a-m_V)*b_p=c_p-q_p*m_U-q_p*m_V+m_U*m_V*b_p.
This uses a*h=delta1, including all character-zero values. Freezing
separately at each n proves (3.1); replacing it by a global convolution
identity with a moving cutoff would not be valid. The formula remains
true when one or both cutoffs are below1. Every ordered factor pair,
shared prime and squareful compensation term is retained.

Claim (new restricted estimate): uniformly over tau in[0,1] and every
real x in[X,2X],

    |sum_n S_tau(n)f_x(n)| <<_(p,q,k) X^gamma,    (3.2)
    sum_n (|Q_U(n)|+|Q_V(n)|) <<_p X^gamma.      (3.3)

The sums in (3.2)-(3.3) have finite support for fixed X. For (3.3),
d<=U(n)<=L^tau whenever d>=1 is admissible (U may be below1),
and q_p is supported at1,p. Thus the Q_U support has n<=pL^tau,
and its absolute sum is at most(p+1)floor(L^tau); the V estimate is
the same with exponent1-tau. This proves (3.3), including endpoints.

For (3.2), fix an admissible pair d,e. It has
d<=L^tau and e<=L^(1-tau), so there are at most L pairs. For
0<tau<1 put W=max(d^(1/tau),e^(1/(1-tau))). The further condition
is B_X(de*l)>=W, hence the allowed l form exactly the single prefix

    1<=l<= (eta X^k/W)^(1/(k-1))/(de).           (3.4)

No rounding replacement is made. At tau=0 require d=1 and take W=e;
at tau=1 require e=1 and take W=d. Empty and one-term rows are allowed.
In every case de<=W, because d<=W^tau,e<=W^(1-tau).
If the row is nonempty, its whole real interval satisfies

    de (de*t)^(k-1) <= eta X^k.                 (3.5)

The exact Q=pq periodic sequence b_p has zero mean and Fourier
expansion sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j exp(2pi i jl/Q), with
sum|beta_j|<=pQ. In the j-th mode the phase is

    F_j(t)=jt/Q-(de*t/x)^k/(2pi).

It has a decreasing derivative; its correction from j/Q is at most
k eta/(2pi)<1/(2Q) by (3.5), uniformly on the FULL real shell.
Thus its derivative and each integer increment between row atoms lie
in[1/(2Q),1-1/(2Q)]. The elementary discrete summation argument of
G152 (or the identity g(v)=1/(exp(2pi iv)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v)
followed by summation by parts) bounds every prefix by O(Q).
The total variation of cotangent on this interval supplies the bound;
there is no continuous-integral substitute at an integer resonance.
Abel summation against the ACTUAL decreasing exp(-de*t/x^b) costs
at most twice this prefix bound. Each complete row is O_(p,q,k)(1).
At most L rows prove (3.2). There is no unpriced stationary region:
it belongs to R_tau under (3.1), not to this source.

This is different from replacing the old scalar u by gamma in a
rectangular certificate. The physical upper endpoint in (3.4) moves
with the pair d,e. The full small source is proved pointwise; it does
not acquire an unbounded row above M and does not need a tail repair.

## 4. Complete complements and the remaining finite source

Throughout, ||F||_j=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j), j=1,2.
Define

    T_tau,p,chi,X(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) R_tau(n) f_x(n). (4.1)

For every tau, |R_tau(n)|<=p d_3(n)<<_(p,delta)n^delta, uniformly
in X and tau. The closed low prefix n<=L costs O_(delta)(L^(1+delta))
in both shell norms. For the full strict n>M tail, use the accepted
divisor-bounded nonlinear tail (G152/R2):

    ||sum_(n>M) v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      << A_delta^2[X^(b(1+2delta))+X^k M^(2-k+2delta)], (4.2)

valid for |v_n|<=A_delta n^delta, 2delta<k-2. Its proof applies to
these X-dependent arrays with uniform divisor constants. It majorizes
the complete positive square on a fixed C2 enlargement of the shell,
then pays BOTH orientations and every internal pair by the twice
integrated kernel min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2). The damped diagonal is
retained. No signed off-diagonal is discarded. The exponents
b<=2gamma and k+(2-k)r=2gamma allow delta to be chosen after epsilon.
L1 follows by Cauchy-Schwarz on the shell of measure log2. A triangle
inequality for whole functions pays all interaction with the core.

Combining (3.1)-(4.2), for j=1,2 and EVERY epsilon>0,

    ||C_p-T_tau,p,chi,X||_j <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), (4.3)
    C_p(x)=sum_n c_p(n)f_x(n).

The constants are uniform for tau_X in[0,1]. They may depend on the
fixed ordinary character, p,b,k,gamma and epsilon. All masks, original
character zeros and physical endpoints in (4.1) are part of the source.
This is not a growing-conductor estimate. L1 and L2 equivalences are
separate; an L2 estimate is sufficient, not necessary, for the L1 return.

At tau=1 the e-cut is exactly1, so complete convolution over e,l gives
the one-Mobius form

    T_ad,p,chi,X(x)=sum_(d>B_X(n),j>=2,L<n=dj<=M)
                          mu(d)chi(d)h_p(j) f_x(n), (4.4)

where h_p=q_p-b_p includes its exceptional values at1,p. This collapse
is done coefficientwise BEFORE the physical mask. The cofactor obeys

    j < n/B_X(n)=max(n/X^gamma, n^k/(eta X^k)).   (4.5)

The strict inequality follows from d>B_X(n); it is not replaced by a
unit-constant exponent cutoff. The complete coefficient bound here is
(p-1)d_2(n), and (4.3) applies with the same paid complements.

The transition is n*=eta^(1/(k-1)) X^s, s=(k-gamma)/(k-1).
Below n*, the Mobius cutoff is X^gamma. Above n*, it is the decreasing
phase surface. At n comparable to X the cofactor cap is O(X^(1-gamma));
at n=M it is O(X^(r-u)), u=2gamma-r. Thus the old worst-case cap is
needed only near the upper end, rather than throughout the core.
At n=X^nu the exponent in (4.5) is max(nu-gamma,k(nu-1)); fixed
constants remain as written. This gives a genuinely smaller actual
remaining region near the transition n~X.

Whenever u>0, the old asymmetric cut A0=floor(eta X^u) satisfies
A0<=B_X(n) throughout n<=M for sufficiently large X. The new core
therefore removes an explicit set of old factor labels. Its signed
difference from the old core is paid by (4.3) and G153, including all
other labels; no norm domination by deletion is asserted.

## 5. Full conditional return and weakest first gain

For clarity the precise new OPEN input is the following: choose ONE
of the adaptive tau_X families (or the normalized bounded bank below),
and write T_* for that chosen core or bank (in particular T_ad for
tau=1). For each fixed ordinary chi and a fixed covering pair p1,p2, prove
for every epsilon>0 the WHOLE L1 norm bound

    ||T_*,p,chi,X||_1 <<_(chi,p,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon) (OPEN-AD)

on every sufficiently large dyadic shell, for a common gamma<gamma11.
The pair p1,p2 is fixed before X, epsilon and any proposed zero. It
consists of distinct unramified primes; for a nonprincipal character
choose chi(p1)!=1. Such a prime divides an integer on which chi!=1.
For a principal character any distinct unramified pair suffices.

(4.3) transfers OPEN-AD to C_p. For b=3/2,k=6,gamma>=3/4, the
accepted all-height Mellin calculation is

    integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(z-1)dt
      = A0(z)P_p(z)/L(z,chi)+E_p(z),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6,
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z),                         (5.1)

with E_p holomorphic for Re z>1/2, locally uniformly at every finite
height. Initially absolute interchange holds for Re z>b. Dyadic
summation of the every-epsilon full-shell premise continues the left
side holomorphically to Re z>gamma, with derivatives on compacta.
The x down to zero end is bounded by(p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1), including
all required logarithmic factors. A0 has no zero on Re z>0.

The two P_p have no common zero in this half-plane except possibly the
allowed principal point z=1: their zeros have real part1; a common
1+it with t!=0 would make log(p1)/log(p2) rational, since character
values are roots of unity. At t=0 the nonprincipal choice rules it out.
For a principal character z=1 is its L pole, not a zero. This excludes
every ordinary L zero with Re z>gamma. Actual imprimitive Euler factors
remain; their zero-real-part holes are not replaced by a primitive L.
No native H, Gaussian f3 or positive-slot estimate is inferred.

For any fixed gamma>1/2, choose fixed k>2,1<b<=2gamma and K with
1-(b-1)K<gamma. The same accepted contour calculation retains ALL
terms A_j(z)P_p(z+(b-1)j)/L(z+(b-1)j,chi), j<K, with a normally
summable remainder on Re z>max(0,1-(b-1)K). Finite-strip descent from
Re z>1, using the nonzero A0, pays each shift. This gives the same
conditional return. No k,K or character conductor grows with X.

Exact near and stretch targets, using b=3/2,k=6:

| conditional c | gamma | r | old u | new transition s | new cofactor at n~X |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|.1252|2187/2500|5313/5000|687/1000|64065/62500|313/2500|
|1/6|5/6|13/12|7/12|31/30|1/6|
|1/4|3/4|9/8|3/8|21/20|1/4|

The first conditional target improves c11 by135091/2500000000.
Its transition exponent is1.02504. The old uniform cofactor exponent
.3756 becomes .1252 near n~X and then rises along (4.5); the upper
cap .3756 is retained. None of these rows is an accepted endpoint.
The weakest complete gain is OPEN-AD at ANY fixed gamma<gamma11,
with every source and return cost just described.

## 6. Actual coarse estimate: what still fails

The adaptive reduction does not itself prove OPEN-AD. In (4.4), for
example, ignoring signs bounds a coefficient by(p-1)d_2(n). Split the
whole source at n=X. Its prefix costs X^(1+epsilon). Apply (4.2) with
M=X to the tail: it costs X^(1+epsilon), because b<2. Thus the full
coarse L1/L2 estimate is X^(1+epsilon), still short by a fixed power.
The same calculation with p d_3 handles general tau. It includes the
entire infinite source rather than discarding n>M and its interactions.
G142's already accepted fixed-strength logarithmic arithmetic estimate
also transfers through (4.3); it remains logarithmic, not a new gain.

For principal chi and tau=1 the old terminal prime cell survives:
n=p d with d prime in(X/(4p),X/(2p)]. Here B_X(n)=X^gamma for large X,
d>B_X(n), h_p(p)=-1, and mu(d)=-1. Its full merged coefficient is+1.
Consequently its separate norm is comparable to X/log X by ordinary
PNT and the small phase on n/X in(1/4,1/2]. This is the actual
strongest objection to paying cofactor rows separately. It does not
lower-bound the full signed core.

Taking 0<tau<1 removes that fixed prime cell for large X but leaves
semiprimes in a different factor band. The next section tests whether
SIGNED combinations of cutoffs can remove all those bands at once.

## 7. A bounded signed cutoff bank cannot remove every semiprime cell

This is a new exact obstruction for the enlarged adaptive family,
not an arbitrary coefficient countermodel. Fix gamma in(1/2,1), J>=1
and Lambda>=1. For each X choose at most J parameters tau_j,X in[0,1]
and complex weights lambda_j,X with

    sum_j lambda_j,X=1, sum_j |lambda_j,X|<=Lambda. (7.1)

They may vary with X but are fixed before real x varies. For one fixed
p, form T_bank=sum_j lambda_j T_tau_j,p,chi,X. Equation (4.3) gives
the complete unconditional comparison

    ||C_p-T_bank||_ell <<_epsilon Lambda X^(gamma+epsilon), ell=1,2. (7.2)

Thus this is a legitimate extension of OPEN-AD, not an unpriced
averaging operation. For the obstruction in the rest of this section
take chi to be PRINCIPAL; (7.2) itself holds for every fixed chi.
Write c=1-gamma and t_j=gamma tau_j. At an
integer n=r s with distinct large primes r,s not dividing pq,
n in(X/4,X/2], the adaptive product is exactly X^gamma. Both cutoff
complements exclude1, even when one cutoff equals1. The ONLY residual
factorizations are(r,s,1) and(s,r,1). If alpha=log r/log X and one
temporarily replaces log s/log X by1-alpha, the coefficient profile is

    F_X(alpha)=sum_j lambda_j[
       1_(t_j<alpha<t_j+c)+1_(gamma-t_j<alpha<1-t_j)]. (7.3)

Endpoint equalities will be avoided by fixed margins, not rounded away.
For all alpha in[0,1], F_X(1-alpha)=F_X(alpha), |F_X|<=2Lambda, and
the exact integral identity is

    integral_0^1 F_X(alpha)dalpha =2c.             (7.4)

Each of the two intervals for a single t_j has length c and lies
inside[0,1]. This proves (7.4), including endpoint cutoffs. In
particular no normalized signed bank can annihilate every semiprime
profile. The conclusion does not require weights to be nonnegative.

Here is the quantitative actual-arithmetic form. Set delta=c/(4Lambda).
Discarding alpha in[0,delta] and[1-delta,1] removes at most c from
the integral of Re F_X. By symmetry,

    integral_delta^(1/2) Re F_X(alpha)dalpha >= c/2.

The portion where Re F_X<c/2 contributes at most c/4 to this upper
half-length interval. Since Re F_X<=2Lambda, the subset on which
Re F_X>=c/2 has measure at least c/(8Lambda). The at most4J endpoints
of (7.3) cut the interval into at most4J+1 constant open pieces.
At least one such piece I has length

    |I|>=ell0=c/[8Lambda(4J+1)], and Re F_X|I>=c/2. (7.5)

Trim one quarter from each end. The remaining [alpha_X,beta_X] has
length at least ell0/2; its endpoints are uniformly separated from
0,1/2 and all relevant breakpoints by at least a fixed positive amount
depending only on c,J,Lambda. (If I abuts1/2, the trim supplies that
margin.) For large X, |log(n/X)|/log X<=log4/log X is smaller than
the breakpoint margin. Thus for primes

    X^alpha_X<r<=X^beta_X,
    X/(4r)<s<=X/(2r),                             (7.6)

the ACTUAL merged bank coefficient equals the SAME complex number
z_X=F_X|I, without a limiting approximation. In particular |z_X|>=c/2.
The primes are distinct and automatically avoid fixed pq for large X.
The core lower/upper physical cuts hold because gamma<1<r (the latter
r here denotes the exponent from Section4, not the prime variable).

Ordinary PNT uniformly for arguments at least a fixed positive power
of X gives, for each prime r in (7.6), at least C X/(r log X) eligible
s, for a uniform C>0. Partial summation of the same PNT yields
sum_(X^alpha_X<r<=X^beta_X, r prime)1/r
=log(beta_X/alpha_X)+o(1), uniformly on the compact allowed endpoint
range. Since beta_X-alpha_X>=ell0/2, the resulting distinct integers
in (7.6) number at least C_(gamma,J,Lambda) X/log X. This invokes no
short-interval or progression-uniform prime theorem: the s intervals
have fixed ratio2, and all endpoints stay polynomially large.

Let B_bank,X be the arithmetic projection of T_bank onto precisely
these integers, retaining their ENTIRE merged coefficients z_X. Rotate
by the unit complex number conjugate(z_X)/|z_X| only for the norm
calculation. For all real x in[X,2X],

    Re[conj(z_X)/|z_X| B_bank,X(x)]
      >=|z_X| exp(-X^(1-b)/2) cos(2^(-k)) # (7.6).

Both its L1 and L2 norms are therefore

    ||B_bank,X||_1, ||B_bank,X||_2 >> X/log X.     (7.7)

This is uniform over every bank satisfying fixed J,Lambda. It covers
moving cut choices and complex signed weights, not only a fixed
positive average. It refutes an argument that pays every arithmetically
selected semiprime cell separately at X^(gamma+epsilon), epsilon<c.
It does NOT lower-bound T_bank, C_p, an unselected factor box, or a
bank with unbounded J or Lambda. Full signed cancellation against the
complement remains possible and necessary. A mask selecting (7.6)
cannot be inserted for free into (7.2); that would be exactly the
invalid norm-monotonicity step exposed by (7.7).

The concrete redirect is to couple these cells with their composite
partners BEFORE a triangle or positive-square budget, or to prove a
new estimate for a genuinely growing bank with its operator and return
costs. A bounded normalized cutoff bank alone cannot remove the need.

## 8. Attempted escape: a zero-sum compensator bank really deflates cells

Section7 is not a theorem against every compensator bank. In particular
normalization sum lambda=1 is essential when using cutoffs of the SAME
source. A zero-sum combination of DIFFERENT compensators need not have
zero Mellin signal. I tested the simplest such escape explicitly rather
than silently extending the obstruction to it.

For any fixed integer K>=0 put

    v_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*q_p,
    b_K=v_K*h,
    c_K=v_K*a,
    h_K=v_K-b_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*h_p.    (8.1)

For K>=1, v_K=q_(p^(K+1))-q_(p^K), where
q_m=delta1-m chi(m)delta_m. In particular its coefficient at1 is
zero. Explicitly

    b_K(j)=chi(j)[p^K 1_(p^K|j)-p^(K+1)1_(p^(K+1)|j)]. (8.2)

This is periodic of period Q_K=p^(K+1)q and has mean zero. The principal
mean cancels because p^K/p^K=p^(K+1)/p^(K+1); nonprincipal complete
character sums vanish. The unramified hypothesis remains essential.
All squareful support in this changed detector is retained.

The adaptive theorem applies verbatim with q_p replaced by v_K,
b_p by b_K, and eta_K=1/(100k Q_K). Its constants now depend on the
FIXED K,p,q. The short sources have absolute price at most
(p^K+p^(K+1)) times their cutoff lengths. The cofactor sum has a
nonzero-frequency gap1/Q_K, and the full residual has the uniform-in-X
divisor bound p^(K+1)d_3(n). Thus every complement in (4.3) is still
paid for each fixed K; none is erased by support notation.

At tau=1 the remaining h_K cofactor is zero at every prime j for K>=1.
For j prime this also follows directly from
(v-v*h)(j)=-v(1)chi(j)=0. On the region B_X(n)>=1 this also excludes
the long-variable label d=1, while h_K(1)=0 excludes d=n. Hence its
WHOLE semiprime projection, including squares of large primes, is
exactly zero. If u=2gamma-r>0 (as in all three target rows), B_X(n)>=1
throughout the finite core for sufficiently large X, so the whole-core
claim applies. Without that hypothesis it is a statement only on the
specified region; the possible d=1 upper complement must be retained.
This is a real escape from the semiprime profile in Section7.

It also preserves the zero return: the numerator of c_K is

    chi(p)^K p^(K(1-z)) P_p(z),                   (8.3)

and the extra factor never vanishes. The same fixed two-prime bank,
all-height local uniformity, finite-shift descent and ordinary-character
scope therefore apply for fixed K. This is no claim about K growing
with X. In fact (8.1) is precisely a fixed multiplicative dilation of
the original compensated source, so deflation alone gives no new
arithmetic exponent. It is credited as an attempted repair, not as an
independent new detector or an additional conditional c gain.

The next actual arithmetic cell is explicit. For principal chi take
n=p^(K+1)d, with d prime in

    X/(4p^(K+1))<d<=X/(2p^(K+1)).                (8.4)

For fixed K and large X, d>B_X(n)=X^gamma. The term with long variable
d has coefficient mu(d)h_K(p^(K+1))=(-1)(-p^K)=p^K. The possible
long variable pd has h_K(p^K)=0, and any higher p-adic power in that
variable has Mobius coefficient0. Every other long-variable label is
excluded or zero. Hence the ENTIRE merged coefficient is+p^K.
Its selected full-shell norm is comparable to

    p^K X/[p^(K+1) log X] = X/[p log X].         (8.5)

Thus eliminating all semiprimes has shifted the positive cell to a
fixed valuation; it has not reduced its power price. This pays the
exceptional p-adic terms rather than discarding them after deflation.

There is also a precise limited growing-K diagnostic. Fix delta>0
with delta<1-gamma and allow p^(K+1)<=X^(1-gamma-delta).
Then the primes d in (8.4) still exceed X^gamma by a power. Ordinary
PNT is uniform because d is at least a fixed positive power of X.
With eta_K as above, B_X(n)=X^gamma throughout (8.4) for large X:
eta_K X is at least a constant times X^(gamma+delta).
The same exact merged-cell calculation therefore gives a uniform
lower bound of constant times X/log X. This concerns that selected
arithmetic cell only. It does NOT import (4.3) uniformly in growing K.
Indeed the elementary row constant is at most a fixed multiple of
p^(K+1)Q_K^2, and the short-term absolute budget contains p^K X^gamma.
Those costs grow as powers when K is proportional to log X. Beyond
this diagnostic range the cell can leave the long-variable support,
but the growing source, short terms and all-height return must then be
proved afresh. These are limitations of the proved upper budgets, not
lower bounds for the full short source or an impossibility theorem for
growing banks. The fixed-K theorem provides no permission to omit them.

## 9. Sources, comparison and exact limitations

The full current attempt index and operative recombination policy were read.
The principal source contract is the complete independently reviewed
G152-G154 record, especially its asymmetric formula and retained
h_p(1),h_p(p) corrections. G140-G142 supplies the smooth full-tail
kernel and locally uniform Mellin expansion. The proof above derives
the new cutoff geometry directly; no old positive-slot theorem is used
as an arithmetic bound for this changed source.

A useful outside primary comparison is Helfgott and Thompson,
*Summing mu(n): a faster elementary algorithm*, Research in Number
Theory9,6(2023), published8December2022,
[publisher article](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40993-022-00408-8).
The publisher's Section2 gives the Mobius completion identity with its
support hypothesis. Section3 reorganizes a truncated divisor sum using
a product-dependent cutoff. Those are computational identities, not
estimates for this nonlinear phase; algorithmic running-time exponents
are not cancellation exponents. They establish relevant ancestry for
adaptive divisor geometry. The new claimed estimate is specifically
(3.2) on the curved nonresonance surface with all its short terms paid.

The primary Ramare-Zuniga Alterman preprint *Mobius function and primes:
an identity factory with applications*, arXiv2312.05138, was opened as
an alternative exact-identity lead; no theorem from it is invoked.
Likewise the earlier Matomaki-Teravainen short-interval theorem is
motivation with the already recorded restrictions, not an imported
power bound. The prime-cell lower bounds use only ordinary PNT and
its elementary partial-summation consequence for sums1/p. The fixed
ratio prime intervals and polynomially large endpoints in the proofs
state the required uniformity; no AP or short-interval upgrade occurs.

Novelty within the retained library, not a priority claim: (3.2)-(4.5)
pay a strictly larger actual nonlinear small-product region near n~X;
(7.4)-(7.7) obstruct every bounded-cardinality, bounded-total-variation
normalized signed moving-cut bank from removing all separately priced
semiprime cells. Section8 tests a real escape, proves its exact source
deflation/return, and retains the next valuation cell and growth costs.
The completion, contour return, fixed dilation and tail lemmas are
inherited components, not new arithmetic cancellation claims.

No full signed power estimate is proved. OPEN-AD still requires the
joint Mobius/cofactor cancellation across all retained cells. The new
region and the bank obstruction materially specify what that estimate
must do; neither asserts that the full signed source has exponent1.
All29 original families/109children, near targets,1/6 and1/4 remain
available. The independent reviewer should assess usefulness and
source novelty as well as correctness before root integration.

## 10. Verification and final worklog

The owned helper was read completely before its one execution. The
successful run, native chunk4a4895, exit0, checks sixteen exact adaptive
identities through n=600 for four actual characters, including a complex
quartic character and natural zeros. It checks1024 whole row-prefix
memberships, including B<1 and strict equality controls; nine exact
signed-bank profiles; eight shifted-compensator coefficient cases; and
the three rational target rows. Arithmetic uses rational numbers and
integer pairs for complex values. The complete receipt is checks.json.
These finite checks do not prove any asymptotic, PNT, contour argument,
or OPEN-AD. The mathematical proofs are Sections3-8.

Six source paths are byte-hashed in that receipt. The cycle-specific
mathematical sources are immutable ancestor records. The attempt index
and assignment pin are read-time evidence, not a claim that controller
files cannot subsequently change. Primary outside-source evidence is
text inspection in the web tool; no downloaded PDF/HTML binary hash or
rendered-image inspection is claimed. Exact provenance is retained in
source-evidence.json.

Completed: discovery and full index comparison; full predecessor review;
adaptive exact identity and complete small-source estimate; full finite
core/ordinary-character return; bounded moving-bank obstruction; a
source-exact zero-sum compensator repair and its actual valuation cell;
one meaningful exact diagnostic run. Remaining: the complete signed
OPEN-AD arithmetic estimate, independent review, and any root admission.
The whole task remains source-relative at the incumbent c11; no new c,
old-source admission, physical positive-slot saving or formal result is
certified.

statement:
# Independent review: fixed-phase cofactor theorem and degree12 source



## 1. Verdict and scope

**Accept the fixed-phase Hbk theorem and the complete degree12 application at their stated conditional scope.** I independently reconstructed the changed stationary phase, all signed Poisson aliases, reduced-frequency energy, arbitrary finite row cutoff, actual general-phase square-short estimate, complete complements, and Mellin return. I found no mathematical gap in these claims. The proof below supplies the uniform details needed at smooth stationary support crossings and real shell endpoints; the square-short import is reconstructed from its full retained proof rather than inferred from a compact summary.

The concrete unconditional additions are a complete analytic estimate for every fixed b>1 and integer k>=4, and a paid bilinear diagonal for the actual degree12 ordinary-character source at gamma=5/6. The source has smaller high-end cofactor exponent 1/5, compared with 1/4 for degree6 at the same gamma. This is a comparison of two independently justified detectors, not a signed-subset comparison between their norms.

The full signed core and its sufficient one-sided Gram estimate remain **OPEN**. At n comparable to X the available absolute Gram price still misses a squared factor X^(1/3). No c gain follows. Current source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 remains unchanged; F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity, and external definition/import/admission obligations remain open. No native Hecke or growing-conductor conclusion is licensed.

A useful additional consequence is the precise fixed-degree threshold gamma_*(k)=4k/(5k-2) for the balanced diagonal budget; strict inequality also pays the non-aliasing condition in the elementary off-diagonal test. Thus degree11 already suffices at gamma=5/6, whereas the stated degree12 gives slightly smaller cofactors and more reserve. This method's diagonal threshold tends to 4/5, not 3/4. These are properties of this particular sufficient Cauchy budget, not lower bounds for the complete signed source.

All shell norms below use dx/x on the whole real interval [X,2X]. Constants may depend on fixed b,k,Q, the fixed periodic coefficients, chi,p and epsilon where applicable. They never assert uniformity as these arithmetic or phase parameters grow. Every coefficient bank and arithmetic cut is fixed before live x varies.

## 2. Full fixed-phase theorem

Let b>1, integer k>=4, and bounded mean-zero Q-periodic h be fixed. For any finite real D>=1 and any complex |A_m|<=A, frozen before x, put

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k),
    H_D(x)=sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1) h(l) f_x(ml).

Then, uniformly in D and the entire bounded bank,

    ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2 << A(D+X^(b/2)) log^4(2X).            (H)

There is no arbitrary joint mask in (m,l), live-x bank, growing period or undamped infinite bank in this statement. Divisor losses become X^epsilon only when the relevant m range is bounded by a fixed power of X.

### 2.1 Exact output partition and low source

Choose a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi equal to one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity), and set w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t). For every n>0,

    1=phi(n/X)+sum_(N=2^j X,j>=0) w(n/N).

This is an exact telescoping identity, with w supported in [1,4]. For each finite D all rearrangements first follow from the original exponential damping. The final bounds also prove summability of the block norms.

On the low part, expand h(l)=sum_(1<=j<Q) beta_j exp(2pi i j l/Q). For m<=delta X, the phase derivative in l is

    j/Q - (k/(2pi))(m/x)^k l^(k-1).

On the entire low support ml<=2X, including an extra integer for the last discrete increment, its correction is O_k(m/X). Choose fixed delta sufficiently small relative to Q,k. The derivative is monotone, lies between two consecutive integers with a fixed gap, and the reciprocal discrete-increment factor has bounded total variation. Discrete summation by parts gives O_(Q,k)(1) for every undamped prefix. Abel summation with phi(ml/X) exp(-ml/x^b), a bounded monotone weight, pays the actual damped low row. For m>delta X any nonempty low row has m<=2X and at most 2/delta terms. Hence the entire low source costs O(A min(D,X))<=O(AD). No D<X hypothesis was used.

### 2.2 Exact Poisson transform and uniform stationary term

Fix a high output block N and put T=(N/X)^k>=1. Remove exactly empty rows m>4N before transformation. Group the remaining m into frozen dyadic intervals [M,2M) intersect [1,D] intersect [1,4N]. Thus m/N<=4 and M<=4N. Extend the smoothly supported summand by zero to all real n and apply Poisson to the periodic Fourier expansion. With the appropriate periodic Fourier coefficients beta_h,

    sum_l h(l) w(ml/N) f_x(ml)
      =(1/m) sum_(h in Z) beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    beta_(Qj)=0,
    I_r(x)=int_0^infinity w(n/N)e^(-n/x^b)
                          exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^k]) dn.      (2.1)

The integer alias h here is distinct from the original periodic sequence h(l). Both alias signs and every nonzero Fourier residue occur. Mean zero deletes every beta_(Qj), not just the single zero alias.

For r>0 the unique critical point is

    n_r=(2pi r/(kQ))^(1/(k-1)) x^(k/(k-1)),
    Phi_r=(k-1)(2pi r/(kQ))^(k/(k-1)) x^(k/(k-1)),
    Z_r=sqrt(2pi/[k(k-1)]) x^(k/2) n_r^(-(k-2)/2)
                                      w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^b).

Fix a near range cT/N<=r<=CT/N, with constants depending only on Q,k, wide enough to contain every critical point meeting the smooth output support for all x in [X,2X]. Write x=Xz, n=Nt, rho=N/X^b and R=rN/T. The normalized phase is

    T psi_(R,z)(t), psi=2pi Rt/Q-t^k/z^k.

Here z in [1,2], R in a fixed positive compact interval, and the critical point t0 lies in another fixed positive compact interval. Its second derivative is negative and bounded away from zero there. Every fixed derivative of the damped amplitude w(t)e^(-rho t/z^b) is O_j(e^(-c rho)) on the positive support, with a smaller fixed c after absorbing powers of rho.

For completeness, choose a uniformly small smooth neighborhood of t0. Away from it, two integrations by parts give O(T^-2 e^(-c rho)). Near it, the one-dimensional Morse coordinate

    y=sign(t-t0) sqrt(psi(t0)-psi(t))

has uniformly bounded derivatives and inverse derivatives. The transformed compact amplitude B has the same derivative bounds and B(0)=a(t0)sqrt(2/|psi''(t0)|). Write B(y)=B(0)kappa(y)+y C(y), with a fixed even bump kappa equal to one near zero. The y C term is O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)) by one integration by parts; the kappa term is the Fresnel integral plus a smaller nonstationary error. This gives, after restoring N,

    I_r=Z_r exp(i Phi_r-i pi/4)
                  +O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^b)).                   (2.2)

The argument is uniform even when t0 crosses either endpoint of w's smooth support: the amplitude, extended smoothly by zero, remains in the same bounded family. No sharp output truncation was substituted inside a stationary formula. No derivative of the remainder is needed later.

### 2.3 Every alias remainder is paid

Put H_m=mT/N. The near integer bank has O(1+H_m) aliases, and if nonempty then H_m is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. Thus the sum of (2.2)'s remainders after the original factor 1/m is O(e^(-cN/X^b)). This includes the case of an empty near bank.

For nonstationary positive aliases below the near range, at most O(H_m) terms occur, each bounded by O(N T^-2 e^(-cN/X^b)). Negative aliases have the stronger bound O(N(T+N|h|/m)^-2 e^(-cN/X^b)); summing them after 1/m costs O(T^-1 e^(-cN/X^b)). The full positive tail above the near range costs

    e^(-cN/X^b) (m/N) sum_(h>cH_m,h>=1) h^-2
       << e^(-cN/X^b)(T^-1+m/N).

Because m/N<=4, every complete row remainder is O(e^(-cN/X^b)), uniformly in the original finite D. Summing the entire row-block error costs O(AM e^(-cN/X^b)) in either norm. Its interaction with the stationary bank is paid by the norm triangle, before any Gram estimate.

### 2.4 Complete reduced-frequency bank and shell Gram

Reduce the positive near alias r=h/m=u/v, (u,v)=1. Since the ENTIRE Z_r and Phi_r depend only on r,N,x, exact grouping gives

    C_(u/v)=sum_(vj in the original row block) A_(vj) beta_(uj)/(vj).

It is frozen before x, includes every collision and Fourier zero, and satisfies |C_(u/v)|<<A/v by summing 1/j on the truncated ratio-two interval. Moreover u>=1 and r<=CT/N force the essential lower denominator floor v>=N/(CT). Consequently

    sum_r |C_r|^2
      << A^2 sum_(max(1,N/(CT))<=v<=2M) (vT/N+1)/v^2
      << A^2 (T/N) log(2M).                               (2.3)

If the lower floor exceeds 2M, the bank is empty. If the floor is at most one, T/N is already bounded below, so the +1 count still has the stated price. Dropping this floor would introduce an unpaid term.

On the fixed real z interval, the explicit amplitudes satisfy

    |Z_r|+|dZ_r/dz| << (N/sqrt(T))e^(-cN/X^b).

By the mean value theorem and the near-range bounds,

    |d_z(Phi_r-Phi_s)| is comparable to N|r-s|,
    |d_z^2(Phi_r-Phi_s)| << |d_z(Phi_r-Phi_s)|.

One integration by parts in the entire sharp shell, retaining both endpoints and the weight 1/z, therefore bounds the full inner product by

    (N^2/T)e^(-cN/X^b) min(1,1/(N|r-s|)).                 (2.4)

The diagonal uses minimum one. Distinct reduced fractions with denominators <=2M are separated by 1/(4M^2). Their number is J<<M+M^2T/N, and log(2+J)<<_k log(2N) since M<=4N, X>=2 and k is fixed. The complete positive kernel row sum is O(1+(M^2/N)log(2N)). Applying 2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 to every pair and using (2.3) yields

    ||whole (M,N) block||_2^2
      << A^2 e^(-cN/X^b)(N+M^2) log^2(2N).               (2.5)

This includes the already paid entire row error by norm triangle. No diagonal, close frequency, or either off-diagonal orientation is omitted.

### 2.5 Infinite completion and arbitrary D

Sum WHOLE block norms. For fixed N there are O(log(2N)) row blocks; the M terms sum to O(min(D,N)). Thus the high source is bounded by

    A sum_(N=2^jX) e^(-cN/X^b)
           [sqrt(N)log^2(2N)+min(D,N)log(2N)].

For each fixed b>1 the first sum is O(X^(b/2)log^2(2X)); the second is O(D log^2(2X)). The tail beyond N comparable to X^b is exponentially summable, with all differentiated damping already absorbed. Adding the low source proves (H), with the stated conservative log^4. This norm-triangle completion pays all cross terms between low/high sources, distinct row blocks and distinct output blocks. Finite-measure Cauchy gives L1. Arbitrarily large finite D creates no log D because rows m>4N were removed exactly first.

## 3. Independent reconstruction of the actual square-short input

The relevant accepted source is [restricted research revision]'s FULL single-square proof (author Section4, reviewer Section4), with its explicit fixed-phase continuation (author Section8, reviewer final discussion). It is not the specialized degree6 collision bound alone.

For fixed mean-zero Q0-periodic beta, 1<=a0<=pX^alpha0 with fixed alpha0<1, and every frozen root prefix R in [0,infinity], set F=(X/a0)^k and R0=c0 F^(1/(2k-1)). On r<=R0 each nonzero Fourier phase has derivative

    j/Q0 - (k/pi)(a0/x)^k r^(2k-1).

Choose c0 fixed so the correction stays below 1/(4Q0), including the final increment. R0 tends to infinity uniformly; a finite initial X range enters the constant. Discrete first derivative and Abel summation pay the complete low prefix by O(1), using the actual exp(-a0 r^2/x^b) and the exact endpoint min(R,R0).

For the entire remaining root prefix, a smooth nonnegative majorant of the original x shell and two integrations by parts give the full kernel

    exp(-c a0(r^2+s^2)/X^b)
       min(1,[F/|r^(2k)-s^(2k)|]^2).

The diagonal is O(X^(b/2)a0^-1/2). For r>s>R0, the difference is at least r^(2k-1)(r-s); summing all positive gaps and then r costs

    F sum_(r>R0) r^(-(2k-1)) << F^(1/(2k-1)).

Both orientations, all high roots and the low/high cross term are paid. Arbitrary prefix R only restricts a positive absolute upper bound; it is not a signed norm monotonicity claim. If b>=2k/(2k-1), then for a0>=1 this high off-diagonal price is at most the diagonal price. Therefore

    ||sum_(r<=R) beta(r) f_x(a0 r^2)||_(1,2)
        << 1+X^(b/4)a0^-1/4.                             (3.1)

At b=3/2,k=12 the condition is 3/2>=24/23. The literal source has beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p 1_(p|r)), period pq, mean zero, natural zeros retained. It has physical multipliers d and pd with coefficients 1 and -p chi(p), respectively. Applying (3.1) to BOTH rows and summing d<=D gives

    ||Q_D||_(1,2) << D+X^(3/8)D^(3/4).                  (3.2)

Every required root prefix, including infinity, is permitted. For D=X^(5/12), the two exponents are 5/12 and 11/16, both below 5/6. No assertion f_x(pn)=f_(x/p)(n) is used; that scaling would be false for b>1.

## 4. Literal degree12 source and all complements

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural zero extension, and a fixed unramified prime p. Let a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), pointwise. Put h0=chi and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, zero off squares. With Dirichlet convolution *, define

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h0, c=a*a*b0=v*a*s,
    b0(l)=chi(l)[1-p1_(p|l)-p1_(p^2|l)+p^2 1_(p^3|l)].

In particular the q2 coefficient is -p, not -p^2. The identities follow from a*h0=s and preserve shared primes, all ordered factors and natural character zeros. The actual b0 is bounded, periodic of period p^3q, and mean zero. Also v*s=q1*(q2*s), explaining the exact two square-root rows in Section3.

Use b=3/2,k=12,gamma=5/6 and freeze

    L=X^(5/6), U=V=X^(5/12), G=X^(1/6), M=X^(31/30).

Write a_U=a 1_(n<=U) and similarly for V. The complete ordered identity is

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_U*(v*s), Q_V=a_V*(v*s),
    S=a_U*a_V*b0, R=(a-a_U)*(a-a_V)*b0.                  (4.1)

The entire S has frozen coefficients A_m=sum_(de=m,d<=U,e<=V)a(d)a(e), supported m<=UV=L and bounded by d2(m). Apply (H), choosing its fixed divisor loss after epsilon: S costs X^(5/6+epsilon). This is a complete source estimate; no output mask is inserted into H. Section3 pays both complete Q faces.

Every R tuple has de>UV=L, hence n=del>L. The low output prefix n<=L is identically empty, even for nonintegral real cutoffs. Coefficients of R are bounded by a fixed multiple of d3(n), uniformly in X,U,V. The FULL divisor-bounded tail, proved by the smooth-shell kernel and all integer gaps, gives

    ||sum_(n>M) R(n) f_x(n)||_2^2
      <<_epsilon X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^12 M^(-10+epsilon)
      <<_epsilon X^(5/3+epsilon).                        (4.2)

This import is [restricted research revision]'s fixed b>1,k>2 theorem, not its obsolete small-product cap. Its kernel is exp(-c(n+m)/X^b)min(1,[X^k/|n^k-m^k|]^2), with diagonal, both orientations and complete infinite damping. A sufficiently small divisor exponent chosen after epsilon pays the displayed losses. It needs no M<X^b assumption.

Next use [restricted research revision] G182 with the literal bounded mask d>U,e>V,L<del<=M. Its fixed b>1,k>=4 theorem pays all tuples with gcd(d,e)>G by

    X^epsilon[X/G+X^(b/2)/sqrt(G)]
      =X^epsilon[X^(5/6)+X^(2/3)].                       (4.3)

This theorem allows the exact joint mask; no mean-zero estimate is applied after gcd restriction. Strict gcd>G and closed retained gcd<=G are complementary for every real G. There is no extra coprimality with l.

Define the COMPLETE retained core

    T_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) f_x(n)
       sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G) a(d)a(e)b0(l),
    C_p(x)=sum_(n>=1)c(n)f_x(n).

Then for every epsilon>0,

    ||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_1+||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_2
                         <<_(chi,p,epsilon) X^(5/6+epsilon). (4.4)

Norm triangle applied to (4.1)-(4.3) pays every cross term, including both tail/core orientations. All physical output endpoints and ordered tuples survive. Since de>L and n<=M, each retained l satisfies l<M/L=X^(1/5), strictly. Within this fixed degree12 detector, (4.4) makes its every-epsilon full core norm hypothesis equivalent to the corresponding full C_p norm hypothesis. It is not asserted equivalent to zero exclusion or to a different phase detector's norm.

## 5. Paid diagonal, exact open Gram, and the failed coarse test

First remove the entire finite-core gcd restriction using the already proved (4.3). Partition the resulting WHOLE ordered source into output cells n comparable to N, dyadic inverse cells d comparable to D,e comparable to E, and the original cofactor labels l. Orient D>=E using the symmetry of these balanced cuts, retaining all ordered cells with bounded multiplicity. Both inverse scales are at least a fixed multiple of X^(5/12). The exact d range for a given e is the intersection of its dyadic interval, d>U and L<del<=M with the chosen output cell. Any two such ranges intersect in one interval or are empty.

Cauchy in d uses |a(d)|<=1. Its diagonal is O(DE). The precise off-diagonal is

    B_(l,x)=2 Re sum_(e<e') lambda(ee')chi(e)conj(chi(e'))
       sum_(d in I_e intersect I_e') exp(-d(e+e')l/x^(3/2))
                 exp(-i[(del/x)^12-(de'l/x)^12]).          (5.1)

The natural e zeros remain. Cauchy has discarded the d weights through their absolute bound; (5.1) is the resulting exact Gram, not a claim of independent arithmetic signs. It retains both signed cross orientations and actual damping factors. Before any arithmetic hypothesis, the complete cell obeys

    |cell|^2 <= C D [C DE+B_(l,x)].                       (5.2)

For N>=X put T=(N/X)^12. If e'=e+h, the difference derivative in d is comparable to T h/(DE), monotone on the intersected interval. Its upper bound, including a last discrete increment, is O(T/D). Since N<=M,

    T/D << X^(12(31/30-1)-5/12)=X^(-1/60).

Thus sufficiently large X gives a uniform gap from nonzero integer aliases. Discrete first derivative and Abel summation with the decreasing damping give

    |K_(e,e+h)| << min(D,DE/(T h)).

Include the diagonal, every h and both pair orders. The WHOLE cell costs

    DE[E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))].                  (5.3)

Summing all l and all original inverse cells, using DE comparable to N/l, gives the complete high output block bound

    X^epsilon[N X^(-5/24)+X^6/N^5].                      (5.4)

The first exponent at N=M is 31/30-5/24=33/40, below 5/6 by 1/120. The second term is paid at N=M, but costs X at N comparable to X. The low output interval L<n<X also has only the available trivial X^(1+epsilon) bound. Consequently this entire coarse argument supplies no power gain.

A sufficient OPEN input is the one-sided inequality

    B_(l,x)<=C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (L/N)^2             (OG12)

for EVERY original finite-core cell, EVERY retained cofactor label and EVERY real x in the shell. It includes cells below X and the transition N comparable to X. The diagonal already fits because

    E >= c X^(5/12), (N/L)^2 <= X^(2/5).

The ratio has reserve X^(1/60). Combining (OG12) with (5.2) gives DE X^epsilon L/N, and the whole l sum costs only harmonic factors. This would prove a pointwise full core bound and hence the required L1 bound, but is stronger than necessary. Negative B helps; taking its absolute value would demand more.

For N>=X the available absolute off-diagonal price relative to (OG12) is

    T^-1 (N/L)^2 = X^(31/3)/N^10 = (M/N)^10.

For L<N<X, the corresponding trivial ratio is (N/L)^2. At N comparable to X both are X^(1/3). The actual products lambda(e(e+h))chi(e)conj(chi(e+h)) have been exposed, not estimated. No selected positive cell is treated as a lower bound for the signed source.

## 6. Complete fixed-detector Mellin return

For these literal coefficients, initially in Re z>1,

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z),
    J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).                            (6.1)

Natural imprimitive Euler factors are included in each L function. Define H_p(z)=int_0^infinity C_p(x)x^(-z) dx/x. Initial absolute Fubini holds on Re z>3/2 with a divisor-loss buffer. After t=1/x and u=nt, the individual transform is

    n^(-z) int_0^infinity e^(-n^(-1/2)u^(3/2)-iu^12)u^(z-1)du.

Rotate clockwise to a fixed ray of angle -alpha, where 0<alpha<min(pi/3,pi/24). Principal powers are fixed throughout. Both damping real parts have the correct sign there; the degree12 term supplies exp(-c|u|^12). The original damped integral permits the rotation for each n. On the ray,

    |e^(-n^(-1/2)u^(3/2))-1|<=n^(-1/2)|u|^(3/2).

Subtracting one leading term therefore leaves O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)) locally uniformly on each compact K in Re z>0, including z derivatives with their logarithms. With |c(n)|<<_eta n^eta, the summed remainder is normally holomorphic in Re z>1/2, choosing eta after the compact's distance from that boundary. The leading rotated gamma integral is exactly

    A0(z)=Gamma(z/12)exp(-i pi z/24)/12.

Thus meromorphic continuation of the initial identity gives

    H_p(z)=A0(z)D_c(z)+E_p(z),
    E_p holomorphic on Re z>1/2.                         (6.2)

This detector has b=3/2, so ONE Taylor term suffices above gamma=5/6. No positive finite-shift term is silently discarded. The gamma factor is holomorphic and nonzero in Re z>0.

The sufficient source hypothesis is: for every fixed ordinary chi, both primes of a fixed covering pair, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    ||T_(p,chi,X)||_1 <<_(chi,p,epsilon) X^(5/6+epsilon).   (OPEN12)

The coefficients c and detector C_p are fixed across shells, even though the core cuts depend on X. By (4.4), OPEN12 bounds that fixed C_p on every shell. Choosing epsilon below Re z-5/6 makes the dyadic Mellin integral normally convergent in Re z>5/6. Its small-x end is exponentially convergent. Hence H_p is holomorphic there, and (6.2) continues D_c there.

For Re z>1/2, J_p and L(2z,chi^2)^2 are finite and nonzero. The possible zero of P_p has Re z=1. Two distinct unramified primes cannot share such a zero at nonzero height: their finite-order character phases would force log(p1)/log(p2) rational, contradicting unique factorization. For nonprincipal chi choose one covering prime with chi(p)!=1; such a prime exists by factoring a unit integer on which chi is nontrivial. It covers height zero. For principal chi the pole at z=1 is the stated exception, rather than a zero to exclude.

Every hypothetical ordinary zero in Re z>5/6 is therefore detected by at least one fixed member of the pair. This is an all-height conditional implication: no bound uniform as height or conductor grows has been assumed or inferred, and compact local holomorphy suffices at each finite height. It would give c=1/6 if OPEN12 were established. OPEN12 and (OG12) remain unproved, so c11 is unchanged.

## 7. Additional bounded consequences

The accompanying support.md proves the exact threshold gamma_*(k)=4k/(5k-2), the degree11 alternative, the limitation of this particular diagonal budget at gamma<=4/5, and a broader complete analytic transfer under 2k/(2k-1)<=b<=2gamma. It also explicitly retains every finite Mellin shift needed when b changes. None supplies an arithmetic estimate or an attained c.

## 8. Evidence and next action

Exact pins are in source-evidence.json; support.md records read extents, provenance and method limits. No old helper was rerun. The new rational ledger checks transcription, not the analytic proof. Novelty is limited to this research record.

The next mathematical action is the COMPLETE signed Gram near n comparable to X, or another full-core norm argument avoiding its absolute price. The missing squared saving remains X^(1/3). No c is increased; root owns integration.

## 7. Sum the forced opposite incidences and preserve the tails

Put
\[
X=(D/C)^{1/3},\qquad Y=(D/E)^{1/3},\qquad X\ge Y,
\qquad H_A(x)=\min(x^A,x^{-A}).
\]
For fixed `r,s,ell,g`, the first angular argument depends smoothly on
`q_c/C` as `X/(q_ell q_r) (q_c/C)^(-1/3)`, and the second depends
smoothly on `q_e/E` as `Y/(q_ell q_s) (q_e/E)^(-1/3)`. The original
CS8 bounds and their Euler derivatives therefore supply the same
`H_A` envelopes to the seminorms in (BC13). The factors with imaginary
norm exponent cost only fixed powers of `T`.

After the two Möbius estimates, the remaining positive budget is
\[
\begin{aligned}
(CE)^{b+1/2-a+O(\delta)}
\sum_\ell q_\ell^2
&\sum_rq_r^{1-b}H_A\!\left(\frac X{q_\ell q_r}\right)\\
{}\times&\sum_sq_s^{1-b}H_A\!\left(\frac Y{q_\ell q_s}\right),
\end{aligned}
\tag{BC16}
\]
up to polynomial height and arbitrarily small norm powers. For
example, the outside `q_s^(1+h)` and the `u`-length power
`(C/q_s)^(b+h)` leave `q_s^(1-b)`. The `r` calculation is identical.
Thus neither opposite deletion has been replaced by a free divisor
count. Dropping the remaining restrictions on these positive outer
sums only enlarges them.

Ideal counting gives
\[
F_b(U):=\sum_rq_r^{1-b}H_A(U/q_r)
\ll
\begin{cases}
U^{2-b},&U\ge1,\\
U^A,&U<1.
\end{cases}
\]
For `X>=Y`, it follows that
\[
\sum_\ell q_\ell^2F_b(X/q_\ell)F_b(Y/q_\ell)
\ll X^{2-b}Y^{1+b}E_N(C/D)E_N(E/D).
\tag{BC17}
\]
For `Y>=1`, the range `q_ell<=Y` costs
\[
(XY)^{2-b}\sum_{q_\ell\le Y}q_\ell^{2b-2}
\ll (XY)^{2-b}Y^{2b-1}.
\]
The factor `Y^(2b-1)` is included. For `Y<q_ell<=X`, use the
small-argument bound in the second factor; for `q_ell>X`, use it
in both. These give the same budget when `A>b+1`. When `Y<1`, take
`A>=b+1+3N` to supply the displayed arbitrary upper-tail power.
When also `X<1`, the same choice supplies both tails since `b>1/2`.
Arbitrarily small outer norm powers are absorbed by increasing the
endpoint exponents and decreasing the preliminary losses.

The powers in (BC16)--(BC17), before the small `a,delta` losses, are
\[
(CE)^{b+1/2}(D/C)^{(2-b)/3}(D/E)^{(1+b)/3}
=D C^{4b/3-1/6}E^{2b/3+1/6}.
\]
Together with (BC11), this proves (BC6).

## 4. C/S10: protected rare signed renewal development

This test keeps the actual global prime law rather than an independent-jump model. Let Lambda be von Mangoldt and use Dirichlet convolution. Differentiating the absolutely convergent reciprocal Euler series in Re(s)>1 gives the coefficient identity

    (a log)(n)=-(a*(Lambda chi))(n).                     (C1)

It also follows directly from the prime-power divisor identity, so every prime power, natural zero and endpoint is present. Set

    R_chi(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M_chi(x/d).

Finite summation and Abel integration give exactly

    M_chi(x)log x = int_1^x M_chi(t)dt/t - R_chi(x),
    M_chi(x)=1-R_chi(x)/log x
                  -int_2^x R_chi(t)dt/[t(log t)^2], x>=2. (C2)

The second formula uses R_chi(2-)=0 and a(1)=1. In particular a complete bound R_chi(x)=O(x^gamma log x), gamma>0, gives M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma). Conversely M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma) gives that R bound by the first formula. These statements remain equivalent with every-epsilon losses. Thus the exact signed renewal input is explicit and returns the same exponent, but it is not intrinsically weaker than the original problem.

The attempted positive contraction fails on the full source. On the weighted space |M(x)|<=x^gamma, the absolute discrete renewal kernel has mass

    sum_(d>=2)Lambda(d)|chi(d)|d^(-gamma),                (C3)

which is infinite for gamma<=1. At gamma=1 this follows elementarily from

    sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)floor(X/d)=log(floor X!),
    sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)/d >= log(floor X!)/X -> infinity.

Removing the finitely many prime-power rays dividing q changes the gamma=1 sum by a finite amount; for0<gamma<1 the weights are larger. No stochastic minorization exists after pretending this infinite signed measure is a probability distribution. Dividing the finite Volterra equation by log x does not supply a fixed subunit norm: the gamma=1 lower ratio approaches1, and the known positive prime-density asymptotic makes the gamma<1 ratio grow. The infinite-mass result alone suffices to reject a scale-independent absolute-kernel small-gain certificate.

A deliberately coarse complete estimate is |R_chi(x)|<=sum_(n<=x)log n<=x log x, using its exact value -sum a(n)log n. It returns only exponent1. Replacing M by an inherited exponent beta on the right of the first C2 does not bootstrap, because the signed correlation still needs new control. On the other hand the true signs in R can cancel; (C3) is not a lower bound for R or M. The viable residual is a complete signed prime-power/Mobius correlation estimate, including all d and every covariance if squared. This is renewal/Dirichlet-inverse ancestry (G78/G81/G92/G112), not a new arithmetic theorem or an impossibility result for signed renewal.

This is the promised hard/upstream/high-ceiling attempt before settling on the easier A and B refinements. It actually reaches the native arithmetic convolution and computes its full positive budget. It fails to supply the required cancellation, and that failure is retained without a replacement random draw.
