statement:
# W61: actual isolated-source costs, prime-graph control, and a compact certificate ladder

Author conclusions for independent review. No increased zero-free constant is proved. The current source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and gamma11=.8748540364 are unchanged; the inherited analytic, positive-slot and external-admission obligations remain open. The accepted baseline is a premise, not something this report re-proves.

The main proposed new result in our record is an actual-arithmetic obstruction to **short additive bandwidth or small translation-bank positive certificates**, including a quantitative bill for a nonlocal correction. It strengthens the earlier diagonal-certificate obstruction without becoming a lower bound for Mertens sums. A protected prime-flow construction has a complete source and a sharp anchored-control formula, but its harmonic readout still contains the original signed sum. The uniform wildcard yields an explicit, sound compact zero-exclusion algorithm; its all-compact success remains unproved. These are written arguments, not a new theorem acceptance or public priority claim.

## 1. Frozen generation and six first tests

Thirty initial cards were frozen at 18:22:05 UTC on 2026-10-12, before detailed mathematical history intake. `initial-seeds.json` has SHA-256 `49802ef767daf7551a80271aab498fe3f00e827856bad5c70340f39a31ca9817`. The exact four recipe combinations and every card remain. No incoherent draw was silently replaced; all four semantic combinations admitted a concrete initial formulation, with their likely obstructions recorded in the cards.

The deliberate choices were S04 (strongest credible bridge), S29 (protected high ceiling), and S13 (most different). The complete all-group literal p<.10 pool had 22 cards and selected S11; the subsequent p<.01 pool had 12 and selected S26; the uniform remaining pool had 25 and selected S23. No screen exclusions other than already selected cards were used. Independent eight-byte OS entropy, rejection thresholds, all attempts, complete pools and timestamps were saved before the first tests. The numbers p describe subjective generation typicality, not truth or success.

| Test order | Card | Decisive calculation and disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | S29 | The actual sorted-prime transfer is already bounded and quasinilpotent for sigma>1/2. Thus the proposed essential-spectrum obstruction is not the right diagnosis in this realization. Its sharp output remains expensive. Develop the complete prime-graph observation contract below; do not claim a new spectral gap. |
| 2 | S04 | Exact inverse-convolution output is established ancestry. The affordable new calculation is the optimum block-diagonal terminal metric and an actual squarefree-isolation witness against every short-band metric. Develop sections 2-3. |
| 3 | S13 | For the explicitly defined cutoff complex, the unweighted torsion ratio is either identically 1 or a power whose exponent is the entire unknown principal Mertens sum. A character insertion is not a chain map in general. The literal proposal fails; retain the precise calculation in section 5. |
| 4 | S11 | Fixed-prime contraction gives the already paid G144 boundary identity, with the character commutator and full reconstruction factor. No saving appears. Duplicate at the tested scope; different nonlocal pairings remain untested. |
| 5 | S26 | One prime's exact cutoff flux is a full signed interval of M, and ordinary causal matrix trace is zero. Telescoping pays reconstruction but supplies no interval estimate. This repeats the Sol04/G144 interface. Keep cross-tile signed estimates open; do not relabel transport as mixing. |
| 6 | S23 | A normalized actual-character Laplace source gives an explicit tail-plus-grid certificate on any compact set. This repairs the raw principal global-polynomial obstruction, but finite success is not all-height success. Develop the wildcard in section 4. |

Three survivors are developed: S04, protected S29, and the uniformly selected rare wildcard S23. The serious countable-prime/upstream test preceded the easier source-formation construction. S13/S11/S26 failures remain visible, and the other 24 cards are untested rather than refuted.

## 2. S04: a quantitative actual-source obstruction to short-range positive metrics

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural nonunit zeros. Put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), 1<=n<=N, and let ell be the all-ones column. A global terminal certificate is a Hermitian matrix P satisfying

    P >= ell ell*, so |M_chi(N)|^2 <= a* P a.                 (1)

The inequality is a matrix inequality on all input vectors. All statements in this section also hold after deleting the forced-zero coordinates and restricting P and ell to S={n<=N:a_n!=0}; bandwidth is still measured in the original integer labels. The proofs use only that support and N as an upper bound on dimension. A certificate required only on a separately proved reachable class is a different, potentially weaker condition. P may depend arbitrarily on N, chi and the actual coefficients. No independence or ignorance restriction is imposed.

### 2.1 Exact block optimum

For any partition into nonempty coordinate blocks B_j, write b_j=sum_(n in B_j)a_n and B=sum_j|b_j|. Then

    inf_(P block diagonal, P>=ell ell*) a*Pa = B^2.           (2)

For the lower bound, multiply a by one scalar phase on each block so that its block sums align. The quadratic energy of a block-diagonal P is unchanged, while its required readout majorant becomes B^2. For the upper bound when every b_j!=0, take block P_j=(B/|b_j|)ell_j ell_j*. Weighted Cauchy gives P>=ell ell* because sum_j |b_j|/B=1, and its actual energy is B^2. Zero block sums are handled by assigning them an arbitrarily small share of this reciprocal-weight budget and taking a limit. If every b_j=0, any sufficiently large finite block weight attains energy zero. Thus (2) is an infimum; no invertibility or false universal attainment is assumed.

This is an exact signed-block target. Optimizing a positive block metric cannot improve on the complete sum of absolute block sums. It extends G129's singleton/diagonal optimum; it does not estimate those block sums.

### 2.2 Isolated squarefree coefficients force a banded price

Let h>=1 be an integer. Call n in [h+1,N-h] isolated if n is squarefree, n=1 mod q, and every n+r with 0<|r|<=h is nonsquarefree. Let I be any set of such indices and K=|I|. If P in (1) has half-bandwidth h, namely P_nm=0 when |n-m|>h, then

    a*Pa >= K^2.                                            (3)

Indeed, |a_n|=1 for n in I, every other actual nonzero source coordinate is more than h away from it, and distinct members of I are more than h apart. Hence the actual cross terms between I and its complement vanish, and P_II is diagonal. The principal submatrix inequality P_II>=ell_I ell_I* implies, by evaluation on ell_I, sum_(n in I)P_nn>=K^2. The remaining principal block is PSD. Its actual energy is nonnegative, so (3) follows. This proof retains all squareful and nonunit zeros; no cancellation outside I is discarded as an assertion about M.

Here is a completely elementary supply of such indices. For each r in {-h,...,-1,1,...,h}, choose a distinct prime p_r>h not dividing q. Set

    Q=q product_r p_r^2,
    n=1 mod q,     n=-r mod p_r^2 for every r.                (4)

CRT gives one residue a0 modulo Q and gcd(a0,Q)=1: p_r cannot divide r, and the q-residue is 1. Every shifted n+r is squareful. Count squarefree n in this residue. The exact expansion mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), with only gcd(d,Q)=1 contributing, gives uniformly in Q and a0,

    #{n<=N:n=a0 mod Q, mu(n)^2=1}
      = (N/Q) product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^-2)+O(3 sqrt N),
      >= N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N,       N>=4.                        (5)

For completeness, truncate d at floor(sqrt N). Each compatible congruence modulo Qd^2 costs at most 1 in its count, hence at most sqrt N total. The omitted main sum costs at most 2 sqrt N/Q. Its Euler product is at least 1/zeta(2)>1/2, using sum_(n>=2)n^-2<1. Take I to be the resulting squarefree indices in [h+1,N-h]. Deleting the at most 2h endpoint integers leaves

    K >= max(0, N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N-2h).                         (6)

Neither a prime distribution theorem nor a hypothesis about mu cancellation is needed for (3)-(6).

The primes in (4) can be chosen <=C_q h log(2h). One elementary proof of the needed supply uses

    4^m/(2m+1) <= binom(2m,m) <= (2m)^pi(2m).

Each prime contributes at most 2m to the binomial's factorization, since every term of its valuation sum is 0 or 1. This gives pi(x)>>x/log x. Choosing C_q large supplies 2h distinct primes above h and outside the fixed ramified set. Consequently

    log Q <= log q+4h log(C_q h log(2h))
           =(4+o(1))h log h                    as h->infinity. (7)

For any h_N=o(log N/loglog N), (6) gives K=N^(1-o(1)). Every matrix in (1) with that bandwidth therefore has

    sqrt(a*Pa) >= N^(1-o(1)).                                (8)

For h_N=floor(kappa log N/loglog N), fixed 0<kappa<1/8, it instead gives

    K >= N^(1-4kappa-o(1)),
    sqrt(a*Pa) >= N^(1-4kappa-o(1)).                         (9)

The restriction kappa<1/8 is the range in which the explicit AP main term dominates the sqrt N error. Fixed h gives the stronger K>>_(q,h)N. These are all-large-N certificate statements with fixed q; the constants do not purport to be uniform as q grows.

Thus a bound a*Pa <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(2gamma+epsilon) through this class requires kappa>=(1-gamma)/4 in the regime of (9). This is only a necessary width, never a sufficient arithmetic saving.

| Proposed source exponent gamma | Desired c=1-gamma | Necessary kappa for this bandwidth class |
|---|---:|---:|
| A strict gain below .8748540364 | >.1251459636 | >.0312864909 |
| .8748 | .1252 | >=.0313 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | >=1/24 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | >=1/16 |

These tests deliberately include a coarse near gain, 1/6 and 1/4. None is obtained.

### 2.3 Pay the nonlocal correction instead of silently deleting it

Suppose P=D+E>=ell ell*, D>=0 has half-bandwidth h, E=E*, and ||E||<=eta in Euclidean operator norm. With the same K isolated actual coefficients,

    a*Pa >= K^2-eta(K+N).                                  (10)

The principal inequality gives sum_I D_nn>=K^2-eta K. Actual cross terms of D involving I vanish, its complementary energy is nonnegative, and a*Ea>=-eta||a||^2>=-eta N. This proves (10), including every correction term. If h=o(log N/loglog N), reducing the full root cost to a fixed exponent gamma<1 requires a nonlocal correction of norm at least N^(1-o(1)) along the lower-bound scale. Small entrywise errors are not enough unless their complete operator cost is also paid.

Scope: (3)-(10) do not lower-bound |M_chi(N)|. Distant isolated terms may cancel against other signed terms. Nonlocal metrics, signed debts and source-only inequalities escape this class. Prime-dilation edges are often long in additive distance, so the bandwidth theorem does not exclude them.

### 2.4 Arbitrary finite translation banks, including large shifts

More generally let D_N be any symmetric set of nonzero integer shifts with |r|<=N-1, and suppose P_nm=0 off the diagonal unless m-n is in D_N. Put k=|D_N|. For each r choose a distinct prime p_r not dividing qr, and impose n=1 mod q and n=-r mod p_r^2. The same CRT argument gives a coprime residue modulo Q=q product_r p_r^2. Every allowed neighbor that actually lies in [1,N] is squareful; neighbors outside that interval are irrelevant. No endpoint deletion is needed. Equation (3) holds for P with this support; (10) holds when its PSD part D has this support and the full E is paid. For the constructed set,

    K>=max(0,N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N).

The prime choices can be bounded uniformly in the actual shifts. At each choice, at most k-1 previously used primes and omega(q)+floor(log_2 N) divisors of qr are forbidden. The first J=k+omega(q)+floor(log_2 N)+1 primes therefore suffice. The elementary prime bound used above gives

    log Q <= log q+2k log(C J log(2J)).

Hence k=o(log N/loglog N) forces Q=N^o(1) and root certificate cost N^(1-o(1)), regardless of how large or data-dependent the allowed shifts are. If k~kappa log N/loglog N with 0<kappa<1/4, the cost is at least N^(1-2kappa-o(1)). A target gamma requires kappa>=(1-gamma)/2 in that range. This counts the TOTAL distinct allowed offsets, not the degree of each row; an arbitrary sparse graph with many different offsets is not covered. The near-local correction still has the full operator bill (10). A finite shift bank cannot escape the obstruction merely by moving its offsets far away.

## 3. Protected S29: a stable prime state still needs a signed observation theorem

### 3.1 The exact countable realization and the first-test correction

On the Hilbert space of squarefree q-units with increasing prime labels, for sigma>1/2 let

    T_sigma e_n=sum_(p>P+(n), p not dividing q)
                         chi(p)p^-sigma e_(np),   P+(1)=1.

Distinct parents have disjoint k-step descendants. Therefore, with S_sigma=sum_(p not dividing q)p^-2sigma<infinity,

    ||T_sigma^k||^2 <= S_sigma^k/k!,
    v_sigma=(I+T_sigma)^-1 e_1,
    v_sigma(n)=mu(n)chi(n)n^-sigma.                           (11)

The Neumann series converges in operator norm; T is quasinilpotent. This is B22/G145 ancestry, not a new theorem or an essential-spectrum failure. It directly answers the first affordable question in the protected seed. The actual squareful and nonunit coefficients are zero because those vertices are absent, not replaced by free signs.

The physical output is

    M_chi(N)=Lambda_(N,sigma)v_sigma,
    Lambda_(N,sigma)u=sum_(n<=N)n^sigma u_n.

Squarefree q-unit counting and partial summation give
||Lambda||^2 ~ kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/(2sigma+1), with kappa_q>0. Thus the naive norm price has exponent sigma+1/2>1. G117/G145 already rule out repairing this by arbitrary positive diagonal reweighting. Section 2 now covers much more than diagonal weights: under the congruence W=diag(n^sigma), a banded terminal majorant for Lambda becomes precisely a banded majorant for ell on the physical a=Wv. The cost is unchanged. This is a source-sensitive refinement of the observation obstruction, not a saving from the stable state.

### 3.2 An exact prime-graph storage identity, including the harmonic part

Here is a concrete alternative that uses the long multiplicative edges rather than a short additive metric. Let S={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}. Use all edges n--np with p not dividing nq and np<=N, with arbitrary positive weights w_e. This graph is connected through divisors to 1. Let L be its ordinary weighted graph Laplacian and U=diag(a_n) on S. Then |a_n|=1, and

    L_a=U L U*,
    x*L_a x=sum_(n--np) w_e |x_(np)+chi(p)x_n|^2,
    L_a a=0.                                                (12)

Every edge relation is the literal arithmetic one. Squareful and nonunit vertices contribute zero to the original output and are not assigned artificial inverse equations here. The complete graph and all its retained endpoints are specified.

For lambda>0 and eta>0 define the anchored storage

    H=lambda L_a+eta e_1 e_1*.

It is positive definite, and its actual source energy is exactly a*Ha=eta. A successful global majorant H>=ell ell* would therefore prove |M_chi(N)|^2<=eta. Its full criterion, however, is

    H>=ell ell*  iff  |M_chi(N)|^2/eta+E_N/lambda <=1,
    E_N=f_R* (L_RR)^-1 f_R,  f=U*ell, R=S minus {1}.        (13)

E_N>=0 includes the entire signed Green contraction. For N=1 it is zero. To prove (13), use the rank-one criterion ell*H^-1ell<=1 and conjugate by U. Solve (lambda L+eta e_1e_1*)x=f. Summing all coordinates gives x_1=(sum f)/eta. Writing x=x_1 ell+y with y_1=0 gives y_R=(L_RR)^-1 f_R/lambda. Consequently

    f*x=|sum f|^2/eta+f_R*(L_RR)^-1 f_R/lambda,

and sum f=conjugate(M_chi(N)). No off-diagonal Green terms or zero mode have been removed.

If M!=0, feasibility requires lambda>E_N and

    eta >= |M_chi(N)|^2/(1-E_N/lambda).                      (14)

If M=0, lambda>=E_N suffices for any eta>0, with equality allowed. If lambda<E_N no eta works. These edge cases prevent treating the complementary Green cost as a free or strictly contractive term.

A graph gap may help bound E_N. It cannot remove the first term of (13): the actual arithmetic vector is exactly the harmonic state. This supplies a sharp finite version of the older G74 harmonic-mode warning, now with the literal squarefree ordinary-character graph, an explicit positive complement and arbitrary edge weights. It is a legitimate high-ceiling architecture only if a noncircular method proves the complete majorant at eta<<N^(2gamma+epsilon). The formula does not provide that method. It is not a claim that all prime graphs, indefinite storage or source-restricted observers fail.

For gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 the necessary complete storage exponents are respectively 1.7496,5/3,3/2 (allow every epsilon). Mere boundedness of (I+T)^-1, a graph gap, vanishing edge defects or finite numerical feasibility does not establish any of these targets. The next mathematical action is to estimate nonlocal signed observation structure, or a proved reachable-state class that avoids the global majorant, while retaining the full Green/harmonic reconstruction.

## 4. Uniform wildcard S23: an explicit compact certificate algorithm and its exact limit

This replacement goes upstream to the actual periodic character, using the G128 normalization. Let delta=1 for a principal character and 0 otherwise, r=delta phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), and b(t)=A(e^t)-r e^t. Periodicity gives |b|<=q. The actual function

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s                  (15)

has exactly the ordinary L zeros in Re s>0, with multiplicity. At the principal pole its removable value is r/2, which is nonzero. A nonprincipal character receives no extraneous s-1 factor. All imprimitive factors and all heights are retained.

Its causal Laplace source is explicit:

    f(t)=b(t)                                      nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r e^-t+b(t)-2 integral_0^t e^(-(t-u))b(u)du principal,
    |f(t)|<=C_q=1+3q,
    F_chi(s)=integral_0^infinity e^(-st)f(t)dt, Re s>0.       (16)

The algebra follows from L(s)/s=r/(s-1)+Laplace(b). It is also the exact source already proved in G128. No arbitrary Mobius tail is substituted for a fixed character.

For T>0 let F_T be the integral in (16) through T. On Re s>=sigma0>0,

    |F-F_T|<=C_q e^(-sigma0 T)/sigma0,
    |F'(s)|<=C_q/sigma0^2.                                 (17)

Both follow directly by integrating the full absolute tail or t e^(-sigma0 t). Let a compact rectangle K lie in Re>=sigma0. Cover it with finitely many cells of center z_j and radius at most d_j, with the segment from z_j to each point of its cell lying in K. Suppose certified numerical values v_j obey |v_j-F_T(z_j)|<=epsilon_j. Then the entirely finite test

    |v_j| > epsilon_j+C_q e^(-sigma0 T)/sigma0
                         +(C_q/sigma0^2)d_j    for every j   (18)

proves that F, hence L, has no zeros anywhere in K. This pays source truncation, point evaluation and interpolation, not just the sampled points. The finite integrals can be bounded from the literal character period and its known jumps at log n; interval evaluation supplies the epsilon_j. No efficiency claim is made about the number of terms through e^T.

If F is nonzero on K, its minimum modulus m_K is positive. Refine d_j and epsilon_j to zero and increase T until the three terms in (18) are small compared with m_K. Uniform convergence ensures that this finite certificate eventually succeeds. If K contains a zero, the sound test cannot succeed. This is a semidecision algorithm for the zero-free compact property, not a proof that its inputs satisfy that property.

For one common 0<gamma<1 take the increasing exhaustion

    K_m={gamma+1/m<=Re s<=m+2, |Im s|<=m}, m>=1.

Successful certificates for every K_m exclude every zero in Re>gamma. This is a complete all-height logical bridge, with no interchange of a height supremum and a pointwise limit. The missing input is a theorem that these certificates succeed for **every m** at some gamma<.8748540364. The adaptive procedure alone does not prove termination of all stages; finitely many completed rectangles cannot certify the entire half-plane.

Given an independently established lower margin m_K, a sufficient source cutoff is T>=sigma0^-1 log(8C_q/(sigma0 m_K)), and a sufficient cell radius is <=m_K sigma0^2/(8C_q), with point error <=m_K/8. Then |v_j|>=3m_K/4 while the test's right side is <=3m_K/8. Those budgets identify the unknown margin. They do not conjure it from finite data. A fixed character's finite period determines the entire function; the synthetic finite-prefix pole completions of G118 are therefore not counterexamples within this actual-character class. They only explain why a weaker finite-relaxation argument would be insufficient.

The normalized compact procedure is compatible with G130's obstruction to raw principal finite-polynomial global contraction. It supplies a correct constructive algorithm and error bill at a narrower scope. It is mostly a concrete composition of G128 and elementary compactness, not a new arithmetic estimate. No numerical rectangle was run here because that would not address the unresolved all-m premise or improve c.

## 5. Preserved torsion, cone and flux failures

For S13 define the augmented cutoff complex K_X with one basis vector e_S for each finite set of unramified primes with product<=X, including the empty set. Its parity is |S|, deletion is the usual oriented d, and Delta=dd*+d*d. The set is downward closed, so d^2=0 with no omitted boundary. Let Gamma be parity. The odd operator d+d* maps the positive lambda-eigenspaces of Delta bijectively between parities, by division by sqrt(lambda). Thus, with det_even/det_odd,

    sdet(I+z Delta)=1,
    sdet(z I+Delta)=z^(Str I)=z^(M_chi0(X)).                 (19)

The first ratio's logarithmic derivative is zero; the second is M_chi0(X)/z. The entire signed principal source sits in the zero-mode power. A gap does not bound that exponent. This is a specified finite determinant realization answering the earlier undefined-torsion objection, not an impossibility theorem about every regularized torsion.

For a general character, D_chi e_S=chi(product S)e_S has Str D_chi=M_chi(X), but

    [D_chi,d]e_S=sum_(p in S) orientation(p,S)
                    chi(product(S)/p)(1-chi(p))e_(S minus p).

It is not generally a chain map. Even the weighted first Laplacian trace keeps its complete edge defect:

    Str(D_chi Delta)=sum_(n,p: np<=X, mu(n)^2=1,
                                      (np,q)=1,p not|n)
                          mu(n)chi(n)(1-chi(p)).             (20)

Each edge contributes its lower and upper diagonal incidences. This is not the original source unless a separate normalization and complementary return is proved. For a principal character it is zero, consistently with (19). No hidden weighted determinant is identified with 1/L.

S11's actual fixed-prime cone, for p not dividing q, yields A(X)=sum_(n<=X,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n), B(X)=A(X)-A(X/p), and

    M(X)=B(X)+(1-chi(p))sum_(j>=1)B(X/p^j).                 (21)

The complete positive-exponent reconstruction factor is 1+|1-chi(p)|/(p^gamma-1). This is G144 ancestry, including its character commutator; a small geometric boundary rank is not supplied.

For S26 the causal prime shift and physical projection satisfy

    [P_X,chi(p)V_p]e_n=-chi(p)1_(X/p<n<=X)e_(pn).

Its ordinary trace, also after multiplication by a finite causal divisor-convolution matrix, is zero. Its actual coordinate readout is -chi(p)[M(X)-M(X/p)]. A complete bound for that interval returns M by telescoping with factor 1/(1-p^-gamma), gamma>0. This is already Sol04's S38 calculation. Signed boundary transport is retained, but no contraction follows from the identity. General vector fluxes remain eligible with a new full return.

## 6. Complete zero-exclusion return and limits

For any of the actual-source storage/block routes, a common gamma with every fixed chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large real x satisfying M_chi(x)<<_(chi,epsilon)x^(gamma+epsilon) gives

    R_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx.

Choose epsilon with room on each compact subset of Re s>gamma. The integral and all fixed derivatives converge locally uniformly there. For Re s>1 it equals 1/L(s,chi), by Abel summation of the literal mu chi coefficients. Continuation of L R=1 excludes every L zero in Re>gamma at every height. At the principal pole the reciprocal has the appropriate zero. Fixed imprimitive Euler factors, squareful zeros and nonunit zeros are never dropped. Integer N bounds extend by floors. This is the established G116/G143 return, not a new detector gain.

For a squared storage estimate with every epsilon exponent 2gamma+epsilon, split the epsilon before taking square roots. A constant-factor or logarithmic reduction at exponent 1 does not give the required gamma. Equations (1)-(21) prove no complete signed power estimate at .8748,5/6 or3/4. The compact replacement has its own exact ordinary-zero bridge in (15)-(18), but the all-m arithmetic lower-margin premise is also open.

The strongest objection was tested directly: short-range positive geometry cannot manufacture cancellation of isolated actual coefficients; the prime graph's zero residual cannot erase its exact harmonic readout; and a finite analytic margin does not extend itself to unbounded height. The open escapes are nonlocal signed source geometry, a justified reachable-state inequality, or a proved all-compact arithmetic margin. No supplied baseline or finite experiment settles them.

## 7. All thirty dispositions and source credit

U means author-untested, not false. D means developed above. T means one of the six first tests. The index and exact integrations were read only after the seed freeze. Nearby history is evidence, not a blanket rejection of a broader card.

statement:
## G143. Divisor-erasure recovery with literal coprimality and two prices

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. For integer N
and 1<=Y<=N/2 let S be the squarefree q-units through N, E={n in S:n<=Y},
H=S minus E, and a_n=mu(n)chi(n). The other integers retain their actual
squareful/nonunit zeros. The full convolution a*chi=delta_1 gives

    sum_(d in H,d|m) chi(m/d)a_d=b_m,
    b_m=-sum_(d in E,d|m)mu(d)chi(d)chi(m/d),  m in H.

H is convex inside every divisor interval between two of its elements.
Consequently the triangular matrix Z_(m,d)=chi(m/d)1_(d|m) has inverse
mu(m/d)chi(m/d)1_(d|m). Its matrix product reduces to
chi(m/d)sum_(e|m/d)mu(e); no general principal-submatrix inversion is used.
Summing the inverse columns gives the unique scalar dual

    lambda_m=sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k),
    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H)lambda_m b_m.          (88.1)

This final contraction is bilinear, with no conjugate. The moving
coprimality is forced by squarefreeness of the multiple mk. At
Y=floor(sqrt N) every dual has short argument, but the entire m range
through N and every exposed divisor in b_m remain.

For independent row errors bounded by1, the exact scalar norm is
K_(N,Y)=sum_H|lambda_m|. Triangle gives the upper bound; errors
conj(lambda_m)/|lambda_m| attain it. Every m in S with m>N/2 has
lambda_m=1. The elementary square-divisor count

    Q_q(x)=#S_x=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0

therefore gives kappa_q N/2-O_q(sqrt N)<=K_(N,Y)<=N(1+log N).
Adding all convolution rows through N, including squareful rows and
known zeros, does not remove this terminal price: the column of an
unknown m>N/2 occurs only in its own row, with coefficient1. Every exact
linear certificate must assign1 to that row. Weighted independent errors
w_m have exact price sum_H|lambda_m|w_m, including all terminal weights.
This result concerns that linear error formulation, not multiplicative
perturbations of the source or nonlinear arithmetic constraints.

There is a separate actual-source result. Put P_N=sum_H|lambda_m b_m|
and permit any cutoff sequence1<=Y_N<=N/2. Each unramified prime
N/2<p<=N has lambda_p=1 and b_p=-chi(p). Thus P_N dominates the number
of those primes, while

    P_N<=N sum_(m<=N)tau(m)/m<=N(1+log N)^2.

If P_N=O(N^alpha) for some alpha<1 at all large N, dyadic intervals
N=2^j would make sum_p1/p converge. Euler's elementary finite-product
argument forbids that: bounded product_(p<=T)(1-1/p)^-1 would dominate
the divergent partial harmonic sums. Removing finitely many ramified
primes changes nothing. Hence

    limsup_(N->infinity) log P_N/log N=1                (88.2)

for every such cutoff sequence, with log0=-infinity. This is neither a
pointwise linear lower bound nor a lower bound on the signed sum(88.1).
It rules out the full absolute-payment strategy on the actual source.

The particular moving prime omissions can be paid without a fictitious
growing-conductor theorem. For any m and T,

    sum_(k<=T,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k)
      =sum_(r<=T, p|r implies p|m)chi(r)M_chi(T/r).     (88.3)

Every power of a prime dividing m is included in r. If the fixed-character
bound |M_chi(t)|<=Ct^alpha is available,0<alpha<1, its price is

    CT^alpha product_(p|m)(1-p^-alpha)^-1
      <=CT^alpha exp(O_alpha((log(2N))^(1-alpha)))

uniformly for m<=N. Split at log(2N), bound the small primes by all
integers and the number of large prime divisors by log N/log2. This is
N^o(1), but summing absolute prices still cannot beat(88.2).

The surviving OPEN-E9 target is the complete signed sum in(88.1), with
Y=floor(sqrt N), bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0, every
fixed ordinary chi and all large N, with one common1/2<gamma<theta11.
The exposed sector costs at most sqrt N. Thus this target is exponent-
equivalent to the full M bound; it is not claimed to be a weaker premise.
Targets gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 all have room for that exposed sector.
Any model must bound its own complete contraction and the full signed
model residual, with terminal rows, coprimality and phases retained.

A proved full M bound defines
F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx holomorphically on
Re s>gamma, locally uniformly with every fixed derivative. Initially
Re s>1 it is1/L(s,chi). Periodic partial sums continue nonprincipal L
to Re s>0; the elementary zeta integral gives the principal simple pole.
Continuation of LF=1 excludes all zeros at every height in Re s>gamma.
At the principal pole F has the appropriate zero; omitted imprimitive
Euler factors have zeros only on Re s=0. This return is conditional on
the complete all-scale fixed-character estimate, which is OPEN.
